When true, includes records that have been soft-deleted in Salesforce (i.e., moved to the Recycle Bin) in the source data pulled by this AppFlow flow.
The name of the Salesforce object (e.g., Account, Contact) from which the AppFlow flow source reads data.
This object defines the source-specific properties for the SAPOData connector in AWS AppFlow, such as the OData path representing the entity collection from which the flow retrieves data.
The object path within the SAP system (such as an OData entity or report path) that the AppFlow flow reads data from when using SAPOData as the source.
Specifies the maximum number of records to retrieve in a single page when reading data from the SAPOData source in the flow.
Specifies the maximum number of parallel requests that AppFlow can make to the SAP OData source during a flow run.
Specifies the ServiceNow-specific source connector properties, including the ServiceNow object (e.g., Incident or Problem) that the flow retrieves data from.
The ServiceNow object name (such as a table) whose records are retrieved by this AppFlow source connector.
Contains the source configuration specific to the Singular connector, such as the Singular object from which the flow reads data, when Singular is selected as the source connector.
Specifies the Singular object (data entity) from which AppFlow reads data in the source step of the flow.
Configures the Slack source connector properties, defining the Slack object (e.g., 'Channel' or 'Message') that the flow reads data from.
Specifies the name of the Slack object (e.g., a conversation or channel) that the flow will pull data from as its source.
An object that specifies the request parameters for a Trend Micro source connector in AppFlow, including the Trend Micro object name to be used as the data source.
Specifies the Trend Micro object name that the source connector queries to fetch records.
This object defines the Veeva-specific source connector settings, including the Veeva object to retrieve data from and optionally the document type, when Veeva is the flow's source.
The document type used to filter which Veeva documents are pulled by the flow, such as 'All' or a specific Veeva document type.
When set to true, includes all historical versions of Veeva document objects in the source flow; when false, only the latest version is included.
Specifies whether to include renditions (alternate versions of documents) from Veeva in the flow.
Specifies whether AppFlow includes source files (attachment files) from the Veeva object in the data that is transferred by the flow.
The name of the Veeva CRM object (e.g., Account, Contact) that the AppFlow flow reads data from as a source.
Specifies the Zendesk source connector properties for the AppFlow flow, including the Zendesk object (such as 'tickets' or 'users') from which data is retrieved.
The name of the Zendesk object (such as Ticket, User, or Organization) that this flow reads data from.

aws_app_flow_flow.tags.value.text: The value string of a tag attached to the AppFlow flow, used to store custom metadata that helps identify and manage the flow.

aws_app_flow_flow.tasks.connector_operat.text: Specifies the connector-specific operation (e.g., PROJECTION, EQUALITY, GREATER_THAN) that Amazon AppFlow applies to the source fields when executing this task.
For the Amplitude connector, specifies the operation (e.g., EQUAL_TO, GREATER_THAN, LESS_THAN, or BETWEEN) that AppFlow applies to the source data in the task.

The operator to be applied for a custom connector in an AppFlow flow task, which is a string value defined by the custom connector's schema and controls the data transformation operation (e.g., projection, comparison) performed on the field.
Selects the Datadog-specific connector operator (a string value from the set supported by AppFlow's Datadog connector) that defines the operation performed on the data for this flow task.
Specifies the Dynatrace connector operator (e.g., PROJECTION or EQUAL_TO) that this task applies to data when processing via AppFlow, as one of the enumerations supported by the Dynatrace connector.
Defines the operator applied to Google Analytics records in a flow task, such as EQUAL_TO or BETWEEN, used when the flow's source or destination is Google Analytics.
Specifies the Infor Nexus-specific operator (e.g., PROJECTION, EQUAL_TO) applied to the source field in this AppFlow flow task's connector operator configuration.
Determines the Marketo connector-specific operation applied to the task's source field, such as EQUAL_TO, BETWEEN, or MASK_FIRST_N.
The connector-specific operator for the Pardot connector, which determines how the task processes source fields (e.g., PROJECTION for selection or EQUAL_TO for filtering).
Determines the S3 connector operator to apply to source fields in this AppFlow task, controlling operations such as field projection, filtering, or masking when the flow interacts with Amazon S3.
The Salesforce-specific operator to apply to the source data for this task within an AppFlow flow, such as PROJECTION, EQUAL_TO, or BETWEEN.
Specifies the SAPOData operation to apply to source data, such as PROJECTION, LESS_THAN, GREATER_THAN, or BETWEEN, when the flow uses an SAPOData connector.
The ServiceNow-specific operator for the flow task, determining the type of operation (such as PROJECTION or EQUALITY) that AppFlow performs when processing data through the ServiceNow connector.
Specifies the Singular connector operation (e.g., PROJECTION or EQUALITY) to apply to the data in this AppFlow flow task.
Specifies the operator (such as PROJECTION) applied to Slack data for this task when Slack is the connector type.
Specifies the Trend Micro connector operator (e.g., PROJECTION) that determines how source data is projected or filtered in the flow task.
Configures the Veeva-specific operator for the flow task, determining the operation applied to the data (e.g., PROJECTION, EQUAL_TO) when the connector is Veeva.
Specifies the Zendesk-specific operator (such as PROJECTION or EQUAL_TO) that this task uses to filter or transform Zendesk data during the AppFlow flow.

aws_app_flow_flow.tasks.destination_fiel.text: The destination field in the target connector (e.g., Salesforce, S3, or other AppFlow-supported service) where the mapped source data is written during task execution.

aws_app_flow_flow.tasks.source_fields.text: Defines the list of source fields from the source connector that the task applies to, such as fields used for mapping, filtering, or transformation operations.

aws_app_flow_flow.tasks.task_properties.text: The list of task property objects that provide task-specific configuration, such as source and destination data type mappings for map tasks or the write operation type for connector writes.

aws_app_flow_flow.tasks.task_properties..text: The key of a task property, which names the specific setting (e.g., SOURCE_DATA_TYPE, DESTINATION_DATA_TYPE, or CONCAT_FORMAT) that configures how the AppFlow flow task processes data.
The value for a task property key, used to configure task behavior such as data transformation or filtering thresholds in the AppFlow flow.

aws_app_flow_flow.tasks.task_type.text: Specifies the type of transformation operation (e.g., Map, Filter, Aggregate) that this task performs on the data flowing through the AppFlow flow.

aws_app_flow_flow.trigger_config.trigger.text: Specifies whether the scheduled flow pulls only incremental data (Incremental) or all data (Complete) on each scheduled run.
The Unix timestamp (in seconds) that defines the earliest time at which the scheduled AppFlow flow's first execution can start, after which the schedule takes effect.
The number of consecutive flow execution errors that must occur before AppFlow automatically deactivates the flow when using a scheduled trigger.
The end time (as epoch seconds or timestamp) that defines the upper bound of the scheduling window for the AppFlow scheduled trigger, after which the flow no longer runs on the defined schedule.
The cron expression that defines the schedule for the scheduled trigger, such as 'cron(0 12 * * ? *)', determining when the flow runs.
The schedule offset, in minutes, that shifts the flow's scheduled trigger execution time relative to the schedule expression, useful for accommodating data source delays.
The timestamp (in seconds since epoch) that defines the earliest time the scheduled flow can begin running, used as the start boundary for the schedule.
Specifies the IANA time zone (e.g., 'America/New_York') in which the scheduled trigger's cron or rate expression is evaluated; if omitted, the default is UTC.
Specifies whether the AppFlow flow is started on a schedule, in response to an event, or on demand by a manual invocation, and is required in the trigger configuration.

aws_app_integrations_application.applica.text: Specifies the operational scope of contact handling (the only supported value is DRIVE) for the AppIntegrations application, meaning the app acts as the primary interface during a contact.
Configures the external URL for the AppIntegrations application, specifying the access URL and the list of approved origins.
The URL that users are redirected to when they access the application from the AppIntegrations UI.
Specifies a list of allowed origins for the external URL of the AppIntegrations application, enabling CORS access from those domains.

aws_app_integrations_application.iframe_.text: Iframe configuration for the application, specifying the AccessUrl to embed and the ApprovedOrigins list that controls which domains can host the iframe.
Defines the list of allowed origins that are permitted to embed this AppIntegrations application in an iframe.

Defines the sandbox permissions for the iframe used to display the application, where each string in the list corresponds to a token such as 'allow-scripts' or 'allow-same-origin' that controls what the iframe content can do.

aws_app_integrations_application.tags.va.text: The tag value for a key-value pair attached to the AWS AppIntegrations application, used to organize, identify, and manage the application resource within AWS.

aws_app_integrations_data_integration.sc.text: Defines the schedule for data integration runs, specifying a cron expression for the schedule, the first execution timestamp, and the owner of the source data object.

aws_app_integrations_event_integration.e.text: Specifies the source of the events that this EventIntegration subscribes to, determining which events are routed into the associated EventBridge bus.

aws_app_integrations_event_integration.t.text: The key of a tag attached to the Amazon AppIntegrations Event Integration, used for identifying and organizing the resource.
The value component of a tag for the AWS App Integrations Event Integration, storing arbitrary metadata paired with the tag key for resource organization, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the App Mesh gateway route, which uniquely identifies this gateway route within AWS.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.gateway_route.text: The name of the gateway route, which must be unique within the virtual router and is used as an identifier for the route in AWS App Mesh.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.id.text: The unique Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to the AWS App Mesh gateway route.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.mesh_name.text: The name of the App Mesh service mesh that contains the virtual gateway and gateway route, identifying the mesh in which this gateway route is defined.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.mesh_owner.text: The AWS account ID of the mesh owner that owns the App Mesh mesh to which this gateway route belongs.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.resource_owne.text: The AWS account ID of the gateway route's owner, as provided by the App Mesh service in the resource metadata.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.spec.text: Defines the route specification for the gateway route, containing the HTTP or gRPC routing rules and the target action for the gateway.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.spec.grpc_rou.text: The gRPC route configuration for the gateway route, defining how to match and route gRPC traffic to a target virtual service.
Defines the target virtual service and, optionally, the port number to which matched gRPC traffic is forwarded by the gateway route.
Specifies the rewrite settings (currently only hostname rewriting) applied to requests matched by this gRPC gateway route before forwarding.
Specifies the hostname rewrite for the gRPC gateway route action, replacing the original request hostname with the default target hostname of the route's destination virtual service.
When enabled, rewrites the hostname of incoming gRPC requests to the default target hostname (the hostname of the target virtual service).
Specifies the destination virtual service (and optional port) for traffic forwarded by this gRPC gateway route action.
Specifies the port on the target virtual service that the gateway route sends traffic to, overriding the default listener port when provided.
The virtual service that receives traffic for this gRPC gateway route action.
Specifies the name of the App Mesh virtual service to which the gateway route's gRPC action forwards matched traffic.

Defines the gRPC match criteria for the gateway route, specifying the required service name and optional port and metadata conditions that incoming gRPC requests must satisfy to be routed to the target virtual service.
Configures how the gRPC gateway route matches the request's hostname, allowing an exact hostname or a suffix-based match.
Specifies the exact hostname value that the gateway route matches against in the request's Host header for gRPC traffic.
Specifies the suffix that the request's hostname must end with for the gateway route to match.

Defines a list of metadata entries from the incoming gRPC request that the gateway route matches against, with each entry specifying a metadata key and an optional match condition such as exact value, prefix, suffix, range, or presence.
Determines whether the gRPC route metadata match condition is inverted, causing the route to match when the actual metadata value does NOT satisfy the specified match criteria.
Defines how to match the value of a specific gRPC route metadata key, using exact, prefix, suffix, or range criteria.
Specifies the exact value that must appear in the gRPC request metadata (header) for the match to succeed.
Specifies the prefix string that the gRPC gateway route metadata value must start with for the route to match.
Defines the inclusive start and end values used to match a gRPC request metadata entry by range in the gateway route.
The end value (inclusive) of the numeric range that a gRPC metadata value must fall within for the gateway route matching to apply.
Specifies the inclusive lower bound of the numeric range used to match a value in the gRPC route's metadata when the match type is range.
Specifies a regular expression pattern that the gateway route uses to match the metadata key value in a gRPC route's match criteria.
The suffix of the gRPC metadata value that the gateway route matches on for this metadata entry.
Specifies the name of the gRPC request metadata entry that the gateway route matches on.
The destination port number of the incoming gRPC request that this gateway route matches on; if omitted, the route matches requests on any port.
The fully qualified domain name of the gRPC service to match in the incoming request, used to route traffic to the appropriate virtual service in an App Mesh gateway route.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.spec.http2_ro.text: Specifies the HTTP/2 routing configuration for the gateway route, including how incoming HTTP/2 requests are matched and forwarded to a target virtual service.
Specifies the routing action for HTTP/2 requests handled by this gateway route, primarily defining the target virtual service where matching traffic is forwarded.
An object that defines the hostname and path prefix rewrites to apply to matched HTTP/2 requests before forwarding them to the gateway route's target action.
Configures rewriting of the request hostname for an HTTP/2 gateway route, where setting `defaultTargetHostname` to true replaces the original hostname with the target virtual service's hostname.
Indicates whether the gateway route rewrites the hostname of incoming HTTP/2 requests to the default hostname of the target virtual service.
Specifies the exact path to which HTTP/2 gateway route requests are rewritten, based on the App Mesh HttpGatewayRoutePathRewrite property.
Specifies the exact path value that the gateway route will use to rewrite the request path in the HTTP/2 route action.

Specifies the path prefix rewrite behavior for an HTTP/2 gateway route, allowing the matched request path prefix to be replaced with a custom value or reset to the default prefix before the request is forwarded.

In an AWS App Mesh GatewayRoute HTTP2 route action, the `default_prefix` field under `prefix` rewrite specifies either `/` to rewrite the matched request prefix to the root path or `disabled` to disable the prefix rewrite.
The new prefix that replaces the matched prefix in the request path when App Mesh rewrites the path for a gateway route's HTTP/2 action.
Defines the virtual service and traffic weight to which matched HTTP/2 gateway route traffic is forwarded.
Specifies the destination port on the target virtual service for HTTP2 gateway route traffic, allowing override of the virtual service's default port.
Specifies the target virtual service for the HTTP/2 gateway route action, where the route's matching traffic is forwarded.
The name of the target virtual service to which matching HTTP/2 traffic is forwarded by this gateway route action.

Specifies the matching criteria (including prefix, headers, query parameters, method, and protocol) that incoming HTTP/2 requests must satisfy for the gateway route to route them to the target service.

Defines the HTTP headers to match on for the gateway route's HTTP/2 traffic, where each entry specifies a header name (e.g., 'Content-Type') and its matching condition (such as exact value, prefix, suffix, regex, or presence) to determine which requests are routed.
When set to true, this inverts the header matching condition for the http2 route, so the gateway route matches if the specified header condition is not satisfied.
Specifies the matching criteria (exact, prefix, suffix, regex, or range) for an HTTP/2 gateway route header value.
For the gateway route's HTTP/2 header match, this exact value is the literal string that the header value must equal for the request to match.
Specifies the prefix that the header value must begin with for an HTTP/2 request to match this gateway route header condition.
Specifies the inclusive start and end bounds of a header value range that an HTTP/2 request header must fall within to satisfy the gateway route's header match condition.
The end value of the numeric range that the gateway route uses to match an HTTP/2 header value, with the range being inclusive of this end.
The starting value of the numeric range used to match a header in an HTTP/2 gateway route, defining the lower bound of acceptable values.
Specifies the regular expression pattern that a header value must match when the header match type is set to REGEX for this HTTP2 gateway route.
Specifies the exact suffix of the header value to match for the HTTP/2 gateway route header match.
The name of the HTTP header to match against when routing HTTP/2 traffic through the App Mesh gateway route.
Specifies the hostname match for the HTTP/2 gateway route, defined as an object containing a Suffix that the request's hostname must end with.
Specifies the exact hostname value that the gateway route must match in the request's Host header.
Specifies the suffix of the hostname to match for the gateway route, so that any incoming request whose hostname ends with this exact suffix is matched.
Specifies the HTTP method (e.g., GET, POST, PUT) that the gateway route matches for HTTP/2 traffic.
Specifies an exact path or regular expression pattern used by the HTTP/2 gateway route to match the incoming request path.
The exact URL path that an HTTP/2 request must use for the gateway route to match.
Defines the regular expression that the request path must match for an HTTP/2 gateway route to apply.
Specifies the destination port number that HTTP/2 traffic must use for the gateway route's match criteria.
When a gateway route uses HTTP/2 matching, this prefix specifies the path prefix that the incoming request URL must start with for the route to apply.

A list of query parameters for the HTTP/2 gateway route match, where each entry specifies a parameter name, value, and optional match type (exact, prefix, or regex) to determine if a request matches the route.
Specifies the matching criteria for a query parameter's value in an HTTP/2 gateway route, which can be an exact string, a prefix, a suffix, or a regular expression pattern.
The exact string value that a query parameter must match for the HTTP2 gateway route rule to apply.
The name of the HTTP/2 query parameter to match in the gateway route's match criteria.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.spec.http_rou.text: Configures the HTTP routing behavior for the gateway route, defining match criteria (such as prefix, headers, and query parameters) that determine which requests are routed, along with the action to forward matching traffic to a specified target virtual service.
Defines the action for the HTTP gateway route, specifying the target virtual service that receives matching traffic.
Specifies how to rewrite the hostname and path prefix of the incoming request before it is forwarded to the target virtual service for an HTTP gateway route action.

Specifies the hostname rewrite settings for an HTTP gateway route action, which determines whether to replace the incoming request's host header with the target virtual service's hostname by setting the default_target_hostname flag.
Specifies the default target hostname to which incoming HTTP request hostnames are rewritten for this gateway route, used when no hostname is specified in the request.
Configures the path rewrite in an HTTP gateway route action by specifying the exact path to rewrite the original request path to.
The exact path string that the gateway route rewrites the HTTP request path to before forwarding.
Specifies the rewrite rule for the HTTP gateway route's path prefix, either using the default '/' or replacing it with a custom value before forwarding the request.

Specifies the default prefix that replaces the original request path prefix when the gateway route's HTTP action rewrites the path before forwarding to the target, with an empty value preserving the original prefix.
The actual prefix string that replaces the matched prefix in the request path; if empty, the matched prefix is removed.
Defines the target virtual service (and optionally a port) to which the gateway route forwards matching HTTP traffic.
Specifies the port number on the target virtual service or virtual node that this gateway route forwards HTTP traffic to; when omitted, App Mesh uses the target's default listener port.
For an HTTP route action in an AWS App Mesh gateway route, this object specifies the virtual service (by name within the mesh) that receives traffic matching the route's match criteria.
The name of the App Mesh virtual service that this gateway route's HTTP action forwards matching traffic to, serving as the target of the route action.
Specifies the HTTP request matching criteria (such as path prefix, method, headers, query parameters, and port) that determine which requests are routed to this gateway route.
Defines a list of HTTP header match criteria used to determine whether incoming requests match this gateway route.
When true, the gateway route matches requests where the specified HTTP header does not match the given criteria, inverting the normal header match behavior.
Defines the matching criteria for a single HTTP header in the gateway route's HTTP route, specifying values such as exact, prefix, range, or regex patterns.
Specifies the exact value that the HTTP request header must match for the gateway route's HTTP route to apply.
Defines the literal string prefix that the HTTP header value must begin with to satisfy the match condition.
Specifies the inclusive start and end integer values for matching a header's numeric value in an HTTP gateway route.
Specifies the upper bound (end) of a numeric range used to match an HTTP header value in the gateway route's traffic.
The inclusive lower bound of the numeric range used to match the HTTP header value in the gateway route's HTTP route match criteria.
The regular expression pattern that the header value must match for the gateway route's HTTP header match condition to be satisfied.
Specifies the suffix string that the header value must end with for the gateway route's HTTP match to apply.
The name of the HTTP header to match in the gateway route's HTTP route match criteria.
Specifies the hostname criteria for matching inbound HTTP traffic to this gateway route, supporting an exact hostname or a suffix-based match.
Specifies the exact hostname that a request's Host header must equal for the gateway route's HTTP match to apply.

The suffix field, when specified, matches incoming HTTP requests whose hostname ends with the given string (for example, suffix 'example.com' matches 'api.example.com'), providing a way to route based on a trailing domain portion.
Specifies the HTTP request method (like GET, POST, or PUT) that the gateway route must match for the route to take effect.
Specifies the path matching condition for the HTTP gateway route, allowing an exact path or a regular expression pattern to determine which requests match the route.
Specifies the exact request path that must match the path in the gateway route's HTTP route match.
Specifies a regular expression pattern used to match the request path for the gateway route.
Specifies the port number of the gateway listener that incoming HTTP requests must target for this route to match.
The URL path prefix that an incoming HTTP request must begin with for this gateway route to match and route traffic.

Specifies a list of query parameter matching criteria, each defining a query string parameter name and its match condition (e.g., exact, prefix, or suffix) that must be satisfied for the HTTP request to match the gateway route.
Specifies the matching rule (exact, prefix, regex, or suffix) for a query parameter value, used to determine whether an incoming request matches the gateway route's HTTP route match.
Specifies the exact string value that the gateway route matches against the query parameter in the HTTP request.
The name of the query parameter in the HTTP request that this gateway route's match condition checks for.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.spec.priority.text: Specifies the priority of the gateway route, which determines the order in which gateway routes are evaluated, with higher values evaluated first.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.tags.text: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) to attach to this App Mesh gateway route, used for organizing and identifying the route.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.tags.key.text: The key of a key-value tag that can be applied to an AWS App Mesh gateway route for resource identification and management.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the App Mesh gateway route, used for categorizing, filtering, and managing the route through metadata such as cost allocation or access control.

aws_app_mesh_gateway_route.virtual_gatew.text: The name of the AWS App Mesh virtual gateway that this gateway route is attached to, identifying the parent resource for the routing rules.

aws_app_mesh_mesh.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the App Mesh mesh.

aws_app_mesh_mesh.id.text: The computed `id` field contains the name of the App Mesh mesh, which serves as the unique identifier for the resource within AWS and in Terraform's state, and is also the primary key used when importing the resource.

aws_app_mesh_mesh.mesh_name.text: The name of the App Mesh service mesh; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name, and this name serves as the mesh's resource identifier.

aws_app_mesh_mesh.mesh_owner.text: The AWS account ID that owns the mesh, automatically assigned by AWS and read-only.

aws_app_mesh_mesh.resource_owner.text: The AWS account ID of the mesh owner, which is the account that created the App Mesh mesh resource.

aws_app_mesh_mesh.spec.text: Defines the mesh's EgressFilter and optional IpPreference settings, which govern outbound traffic handling and IP protocol preference for the mesh.

aws_app_mesh_mesh.spec.egress_filter.text: Specifies the egress filter type that controls whether outbound traffic from the mesh to external services is allowed (ALLOW_ALL) or blocked (DROP_ALL).

aws_app_mesh_mesh.spec.egress_filter.typ.text: Specifies the egress filter type for the service mesh, either allowing all outbound traffic (ALLOW_ALL) or dropping all outbound traffic (DROP_ALL).

aws_app_mesh_mesh.spec.service_discovery.text: Defines mesh-wide service discovery settings, specifically the IP preference (IPv4 or IPv6) used for DNS resolution of virtual service endpoints.
Determines the IP preference for DNS service discovery in the mesh, controlling whether DNS queries return only IPv4 addresses, only IPv6 addresses, or prefer one type when both are available.

aws_app_mesh_mesh.tags.text: Specifies the tags (key-value metadata) to attach to the AWS App Mesh mesh resource.

aws_app_mesh_mesh.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS App Mesh mesh, used for resource grouping and identification.

aws_app_mesh_mesh.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the App Mesh mesh, used for categorizing, cost allocation, and IAM-based access control of the mesh resource.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the virtual gateway in AWS App Mesh.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.id.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to the virtual gateway.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.mesh_name.text: The name of the AWS App Mesh service mesh that this virtual gateway belongs to.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.mesh_owner.text: The AWS account ID that owns the service mesh, required when the virtual gateway is being created in a mesh shared from another account.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.resource_ow.text: The AWS account ID of the account that owns the virtual gateway, which is useful when the gateway is shared across AWS accounts.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.spec.text: Defines the configuration for the App Mesh virtual gateway, including its listeners, backend defaults, and logging settings.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.spec.backen.text: Defines the default client policy (including TLS settings) that the virtual gateway applies to all outgoing traffic to its backend services.
Specifies the client policy for all backend traffic from the virtual gateway, defining TLS settings such as validation and certificate requirements when connecting to backend services.

Configures the TLS settings (such as validation context, trusted CA certificates, and TLS negotiation mode) for the default client policy that the virtual gateway uses when connecting to backend services, applying unless a more specific policy overrides it.
Specifies the client certificate the virtual gateway presents to backend services for mutual TLS authentication under the default client policy for all backends.
Specifies the client policy TLS certificate to be sourced from a file on the virtual gateway, including the paths to the certificate chain and private key.
The file system path to the certificate chain file used for the TLS certificate in the client policy for backend defaults in the App Mesh virtual gateway.
Specifies the file path to the private key used for TLS client authentication in the virtual gateway's backend default client policy.

Configures the virtual gateway's backend-default client TLS certificate to be sourced dynamically through Envoy's Secret Discovery Service (SDS), where the secretName property identifies the secret containing the certificate and private key.
The name of the secret in the Secret Discovery Service (SDS) that provides the TLS certificate for the client policy applied to backend defaults of the virtual gateway.
Indicates whether the TLS client policy is enforced for the virtual gateway's backend defaults, rejecting connections that do not comply with the policy when set to true.
Specifies the destination port numbers for which the TLS client policy applies to traffic from the virtual gateway to its backends, with an empty list meaning the policy applies to all ports.
Specifies the TLS trust validation configuration (ACM or file-based trust chain) used by the virtual gateway to validate backend certificates in the client policy.
Specifies the subject alternative names (SANs) required in the server certificate for TLS validation when the virtual gateway's default client policy is applied to backend connections.
Defines the exact subject alternative names (SANs) that must be present in the certificate presented by a backend for the virtual gateway's default TLS client policy validation to succeed.
Specifies the exact subject alternative names that must be present in the peer certificate for the TLS validation to succeed.
Defines the TLS validation trust for the virtual gateway's backend defaults, specifying how the client certificate chain is trusted via ACM, a file, or SDS.
Specifies the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Private Certificate Authority trust settings used by the virtual gateway to validate client certificates for TLS backend connections.

The Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the AWS Certificate Manager Private Certificate Authority certificates used to validate the client certificate for mutual TLS in the virtual gateway's backend defaults.
Defines a file-based trust store for TLS certificate validation in a virtual gateway's backend defaults, specifying the path to a certificate file used as the trusted CA.
Path to the file containing the certificate chain for validating client certificates in the backend default client policy TLS trust file configuration.

Defines the SDS (Secret Discovery Service) trust configuration for validating the TLS peer certificate in the virtual gateway's backend default client policy, where the secret name holds the CA certificate.

The name of the secret in the Secrets Discovery Service (SDS) that contains the trusted CA certificate used to validate the client TLS certificate's trust chain for the virtual gateway's backend defaults.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.spec.listen.text: Defines the listeners for the virtual gateway, specifying each listener's port mapping (port and protocol) and optionally its health check and TLS settings for incoming traffic.
Defines the connection pool settings for a virtual gateway listener, specifying the maximum number of connections or requests for protocols like HTTP, HTTP/2, gRPC, and TCP.
Defines the gRPC-specific connection pool settings for a virtual gateway listener, which includes the maximum number of concurrent requests allowed to the virtual gateway.
Specifies the maximum number of concurrent in-flight gRPC requests allowed in the connection pool for a virtual gateway listener.
Specifies the HTTP connection pool settings for the virtual gateway listener, including the maximum number of active connections and pending requests.
Sets the maximum number of outbound connections that the virtual gateway can create to a backend service for the HTTP connection pool.
The maximum number of pending HTTP requests that can be queued in the virtual gateway's HTTP connection pool before new requests are rejected.
Configuration for the HTTP/2 connection pool of the virtual gateway listener, specifying limits such as the maximum number of requests and pending requests.
Specifies the maximum number of in-flight HTTP/2 requests that the virtual gateway allows in its connection pool for a listener.

Specifies the health check settings used by the virtual gateway listener to determine if the target virtual services or virtual nodes are healthy, enabling the gateway to route traffic only to healthy backends.
The number of consecutive successful health checks required before a virtual gateway listener target is considered healthy.
The time in milliseconds between each health check attempt for the virtual gateway listener.
The URL path for an HTTP or HTTP/2 health check request sent by the virtual gateway listener to determine target health, such as '/ping'.
The destination port on the virtual gateway listener to send health check requests to.
Specifies the protocol used for the virtual gateway listener's health check, which can be grpc, http, http2, or tcp.
Specifies the timeout, in milliseconds, for each health check request sent by the virtual gateway listener; if no response is received within this period, the target is considered unhealthy.
The number of consecutive failed health checks that must occur before the virtual gateway listener is marked unhealthy.
Specifies the network port and protocol (such as HTTP, HTTP2, or GRPC) on which the virtual gateway listener receives traffic.
The port number on which the virtual gateway listener accepts traffic.
Specifies the protocol for the virtual gateway listener's port mapping, which determines how incoming traffic is handled and can be one of grpc, http, or http2.

Specifies the TLS configuration for the virtual gateway listener, including the TLS mode (e.g., STRICT, PERMISSIVE) and the certificate (from AWS Certificate Manager or a local file) used for server-side TLS termination.
Specifies the TLS certificate used by the virtual gateway listener for TLS termination, which can be an ACM certificate or a file certificate containing the certificate chain and private key.
Specifies the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate used for TLS termination on the virtual gateway listener, identified by its Amazon Resource Name (ARN).
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate used for TLS termination on this virtual gateway listener.
Specifies the file path to a TLS certificate and private key stored on the local file system, used to terminate TLS traffic on the virtual gateway's listener.
The file path to the TLS certificate chain used by the virtual gateway's listener when the certificate is sourced from a local file.
The path to the private key file on the disk that is used by the virtual gateway's TLS certificate for listener traffic.

This object configures the Secret Discovery Service (SDS) as the source for the TLS certificate on the virtual gateway listener, using a named secret from the Envoy's SDS configuration to provide the certificate and private key.
Specifies the name of the Envoy secret that holds the TLS certificate when the virtual gateway listener's TLS certificate is obtained via SDS (Secret Discovery Service).
Specifies the TLS mode for the virtual gateway listener, either STRICT (requires TLS for all connections) or PERMISSIVE (allows both TLS and plaintext connections).
Defines the TLS validation trust settings (such as ACM private certificate authority or file-based trust) used to validate client certificates for the virtual gateway listener.
Specifies the list of subject alternative names (SANs) that must be present on the peer's TLS certificate for it to be considered valid during the virtual gateway's TLS validation.
Specifies the exact subject alternative name (SAN) values that the peer certificate must match for TLS validation to succeed for the virtual gateway listener.
This field specifies a list of exact Subject Alternative Names (SANs) that must match the SANs in the peer certificate for the virtual gateway's TLS validation to succeed.

Specifies the TLS validation context trust for the virtual gateway listener, defining how the listener trusts client certificates via either an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) trust or a file-based trust.
Configures the file-based trust object that specifies the path to a certificate chain on the file system used for validating the TLS peer certificate.
The file path to the certificate chain file used by the virtual gateway's listener to validate client certificates for TLS.
Specifies the TLS validation trust source as a secret obtained from Envoy's Secret Discovery Service (SDS), identified by the secret name for the virtual gateway's listener TLS configuration.
The name of the secret stored in the secret management service that the virtual gateway uses to validate client certificates when TLS trust is configured via Secret Discovery Service (SDS).

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.spec.loggin.text: Configures access logging for the virtual gateway, specifying the destination for access logs (a file or stdout).
Defines the destination for the virtual gateway's Envoy access logs, supporting either a local file path or a mesh-based endpoint for log delivery.
Specifies configuration for writing virtual gateway access logs to a file, including the file path and optional format.
Specifies the format of the access log entries written to the file, either as a JSON structure or as a custom text string with placeholders, for the virtual gateway's file access logging.
Specifies a list of key-value objects that define the JSON format for the virtual gateway's access log file, where each object contains a key and value to determine what information is logged.
Specifies the JSON key name in a key-value pair that defines the format of the virtual gateway's file access log, where the paired value provides the data to be logged.
Sets the value for a key-value pair in the JSON access log format, which can be a literal string, a request header name, or a predefined expression such as `%CLIENT_IP%` or `%METHOD%`.
Specifies the text format string for the virtual gateway's access log file, using Envoy access log format placeholders to define which request and response data is recorded.
The absolute file path on the Envoy container where the virtual gateway's access logs are written.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs (each with Key and Value) to associate with the virtual gateway for metadata and resource management.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.tags.key.text: The tag key for a tag attached to the AWS App Mesh virtual gateway, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.tags.value.text: The user-defined value for a tag on the App Mesh virtual gateway, used to attach arbitrary metadata such as environment, owner, or cost center to this gateway for operational management.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.uid.text: The universally unique identifier (UID) assigned to the virtual gateway by AWS App Mesh, distinct from the ARN and used for internal tracking.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_gateway.virtual_gat.text: The name of the virtual gateway, which must be unique within the mesh; if omitted, AWS CloudFormation generates a unique name for the virtual gateway.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the virtual node, uniquely identifying it within AWS App Mesh.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.mesh_name.text: The name of the App Mesh service mesh that this virtual node belongs to, scoping the virtual node within the specified mesh.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.mesh_owner.text: The AWS account ID of the service mesh owner, used when the mesh belongs to a different account than the virtual node.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.resource_owner.text: The AWS account ID that owns this virtual node, used for access control and resource ownership tracking.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.spec.text: The desired configuration for the virtual node, defining its listeners, service discovery, backends, and logging settings.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.spec.backend_d.text: Defines default client policy settings (such as TLS validation) that apply to all backends of the virtual node unless a backend explicitly overrides them.

Defines the default client policy, including TLS encryption and certificate validation settings, applied to outbound traffic from the virtual node to all backends that do not have their own explicit client policy.
Specifies the TLS settings for the client policy that applies to all backends of the virtual node by default, including certificate validation trust configuration.

The default client TLS certificate presented by this virtual node when establishing TLS connections to backend services, which can be defined as either a file-based certificate or an SDS (secret discovery service) certificate.
The file-based client TLS certificate configuration, providing the file paths for the certificate chain and private key used for mutual TLS authentication with backend services.
Specifies the file path to the certificate chain used for TLS client authentication when the certificate is provided as a file in the virtual node's backend default client policy.
The file path to the PEM-encoded private key used by the client policy's TLS certificate when validating traffic to backend defaults.
Specifies that the TLS certificate is sourced dynamically through Envoy's Secret Discovery Service (SDS), enabling delivery and rotation of secrets without restarting the Envoy proxy.
The name of the secret that Envoy retrieves from the Secret Discovery Service (SDS) to obtain the TLS client certificate for the virtual node's backend defaults.
Determines whether TLS is strictly enforced for connections from this virtual node to its backends when a backend TLS client policy is configured; when false, TLS is offered but not required.
Specifies the list of destination port numbers for which the TLS client policy is enforced when the virtual node communicates with backend services.

Configures how the Envoy proxy validates the TLS certificate presented by backend services for this virtual node's default client policy, specifying a trusted certificate authority (via AWS Certificate Manager or a local file) and optional subject alternative name checks.
Specifies the subject alternative names (SANs) that the peer certificate must match for TLS validation of backend defaults.
Specifies the exact or wildcard subject alternative names that must match the peer certificate's SANs for TLS validation to succeed in the backend defaults client policy.
Specifies the exact subject alternative names (SANs) that the presented certificate must contain for TLS validation of backend traffic to succeed.
Defines the trust source used to validate the TLS certificate from the backend service, such as an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate, a local file, or the Envoy proxy's built-in trust store.
Specifies the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Private Certificate Authority ARNs used to validate client certificates for TLS against backend defaults in the virtual node.
Specifies the ARNs of ACM Private Certificate Authority certificates used to validate the peer certificate for TLS when the trust is configured with ACM.
An object representing a file-based trust store that specifies the file path to the certificate chain used to validate peer certificates for TLS.
The file path to the certificate chain on the virtual node's filesystem that the backend defaults client policy uses to validate peer certificates when the TLS trust type is 'file'.

Configures the TLS validation trust for backend defaults to use a secret from AWS App Mesh's Secret Discovery Service (SDS), defining the secret name and optional subject alternative names used to validate peer certificates.
The name of the secret in AWS Secrets Manager (used by the Envoy Secret Discovery Service) that contains the trusted CA certificate for validating peer TLS certificates in backend defaults.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.spec.backends.text: Specifies the list of virtual services (backends) that this virtual node can communicate with, defining the services to which traffic from the node can be routed.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.spec.backends..text: Identifies the App Mesh virtual service used as a backend for this virtual node, including the required name of the virtual service and an optional client policy for outbound traffic.
Specifies the TLS client policy, including certificate validation and enforcement, used when the virtual node communicates with the backend virtual service.

TLS configuration for the client policy applied when this virtual node communicates with the specified virtual service backend, controlling enforcement mode, ports, client certificate, and validation of the backend's TLS certificate.
Specifies the client certificate (from a file or SDS) that the virtual node presents to the backend virtual service for mutual TLS authentication.

The file object in the TLS client policy certificate specifies the local file paths to the certificate chain and private key that the virtual node uses to present a client certificate during mutual TLS handshakes with the backend virtual service.
The filesystem path to the certificate chain file used by the client policy for TLS when the virtual node communicates with the specified virtual service backend.
The file path to the private key used for the TLS client certificate presented to the backend virtual service in AWS App Mesh.

This object defines the Secret Discovery Service (SDS) configuration for the TLS certificate used by the virtual node's client policy, specifying the secret name from which Envoy retrieves the certificate.
Sets the name of the secret stored in the Secret Discovery Service (SDS) that Envoy uses to obtain the TLS client certificate for the virtual node's backend virtual service connection.
If true, the virtual node enforces TLS for traffic to the backend virtual service, requiring the connection to use TLS; if false, TLS is used if available but not required.

The ports field in a TLS client policy of an App Mesh virtual node backend specifies the destination ports over which the TLS settings are applied, allowing the policy to be scoped to specific ports on the virtual service.
Defines the TLS validation context, including the trust chain and subject alternative names, used by the virtual node when establishing a TLS connection to the specified virtual service backend.
Specifies the subject alternative names (SANs) that the server certificate must contain for TLS validation to succeed when the virtual node connects to the backend virtual service.

Specifies the exact or prefix values that the subject alternative names (SANs) on the server certificate must match for the TLS client policy validation to succeed when the virtual node connects to this virtual service backend.
Specifies the exact subject alternative names (SANs) that must be present in the peer certificate for the backend virtual service's TLS client policy validation to succeed.
Specifies the source of trust (ACM, file, or SDS) used to validate the TLS certificate presented by the backend virtual service during client policy TLS validation.
Configures TLS validation trust for backend virtual service client policies using AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) private certificate authority ARNs.

The list of ARNs of AWS Certificate Manager Private Certificate Authorities that are trusted to validate the TLS certificate presented by the backend virtual service, as configured in the client policy's TLS validation trust for ACM.

Specifies the file-based TLS validation trust for a virtual node's client policy, which provides the path to a certificate chain file (certificateChain) used to validate the TLS certificate of a backend virtual service.
The file path to the certificate chain used to validate the TLS certificate presented by the backend virtual service when using file-based trust for TLS validation.
Specifies the Secret Discovery Service (SDS) trust configuration for TLS validation, including the secret name used by the proxy to obtain trusted certificates from Envoy's SDS server.
The name of the secret in the Secret Discovery Service (SDS) from which the trusted CA certificate is retrieved to validate the TLS certificate presented by the backend virtual service.
Specifies the name of the virtual service to which this virtual node's backend routes traffic.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.spec.listeners.text: Specifies the list of inbound listeners for the virtual node, each defining the port and protocol (HTTP, HTTP/2, gRPC, or TCP) along with optional health-check settings used to determine if the listener is healthy.

Defines the connection pool settings for the virtual node's listener, specifying protocol-specific limits such as maximum connections, pending requests, and idle timeouts for HTTP, HTTP/2, gRPC, or TCP traffic.
Configures the gRPC connection pool for the virtual node listener, allowing you to set the maximum number of concurrent requests (maxRequests) that the connection pool can handle.
The maximum number of simultaneous in-flight gRPC requests allowed in the connection pool for this virtual node listener.
Defines HTTP connection pool settings for the listener, including the maximum number of outbound connections and maximum pending requests.
The maximum number of outbound TCP connections that the virtual node can establish to the backend from this HTTP connection pool.
Sets the maximum number of pending requests allowed in the HTTP connection pool for the virtual node's listener, controlling how many requests can wait for an available connection.
Specifies the HTTP/2 connection pool limits for the virtual node listener, including the maximum number of concurrent requests, pending requests, and connections to the backend.
Specifies the maximum number of in-flight HTTP/2 requests allowed in the connection pool before App Mesh rejects new requests.
Defines the TCP connection pool settings for a listener using the TCP protocol, controlling the maximum number of open connections and the connection timeout for TCP traffic.
Defines the maximum number of concurrent TCP connections that a virtual node's listener will accept, capping the connection load to the backend.

Specifies the health check policy for the virtual node's listener, defining the protocol, port, path, healthy/unhealthy thresholds, timeout, and interval used by AWS App Mesh to determine target health.
The number of consecutive successful health check responses required before the virtual node listener is marked as healthy in AWS App Mesh.
The time interval in milliseconds between each health check performed on the virtual node's listeners.
The destination path for the health check request, used only when the health check protocol is HTTP or HTTP2, where the mesh endpoint will probe this path to determine the virtual node's health.
The port number the health check uses to communicate with the virtual node, which defaults to the listener's traffic port if not specified.
Sets the protocol (http, http2, grpc, or tcp) used by the health check to determine the health of the virtual node listener.
Specifies the amount of time in milliseconds that the health check waits for a response before considering the target unhealthy.
Specifies the number of consecutive failed health checks that must occur before the virtual node listener is marked unhealthy and removed from traffic routing.

Configures outlier detection for a virtual node listener, defining thresholds and durations for ejecting unhealthy hosts from the load balancing pool (e.g., max errors, base ejection duration, and interval).
The base ejection duration sets the base amount of time a host is ejected from the load balancing set before being re-included, as part of outlier detection for the virtual node listener.
The unit of time for the base ejection duration, either 'ms' (milliseconds) or 's' (seconds), used by App Mesh outlier detection to determine how long a host is ejected before retrying.

Specifies the numeric value of the base ejection duration, combined with a companion unit field, that determines how long an unhealthy host is ejected before being retried in App Mesh outlier detection.
Specifies the time interval, in duration format such as '10s', between ejection sweeps where the proxy evaluates consecutive 5xx errors to decide whether to eject hosts from the load balancer.
The unit of time for the outlier detection interval, which is either 'ms' (milliseconds) or 's' (seconds).
Specifies the numeric value of the time interval (with the unit defined by the sibling 'unit' field) between outlier detection ejection sweeps for this listener of the virtual node.
Sets the maximum percentage of healthy virtual node hosts that can be ejected from the load balancing pool during outlier detection, helping to prevent excessive removal of replicas.

Specifies the maximum number of HTTP 5xx server error responses that the virtual node listener will tolerate from an endpoint before the endpoint is ejected as unhealthy by App Mesh outlier detection.
Specifies the port and protocol (such as HTTP, TCP, or gRPC) that the virtual node listener uses to accept incoming traffic.
The port number (1-65535) that the virtual node listener uses to receive traffic, as part of the listener's port mapping.
Specifies the protocol (grpc, http, http2, or tcp) used for the listener's port mapping, determining how traffic is routed to the virtual node.
Configures the idle and per-request timeout settings for the virtual node's listener traffic, which apply to the protocols (e.g., HTTP, HTTP/2, gRPC, TCP) supported by the listener.
Defines the idle and per-request timeout values for gRPC traffic on the listener, controlling how long connections and requests may remain active before being terminated.
Specifies the idle timeout configuration for gRPC connections on the virtual node listener, setting the maximum duration a connection can remain idle before being terminated.
Specifies the time unit (such as ms or s) for the idle timeout duration of a gRPC listener on the virtual node.
Specifies the numerical value of the idle timeout for gRPC connections on this virtual node listener, interpreted according to the accompanying `unit` field.
Configures the maximum time a gRPC request is allowed to complete on the virtual node listener before it is terminated, as part of the gRPC timeout settings.
Specifies the unit of time (e.g., 'ms' for milliseconds or 's' for seconds) for the per-request timeout on gRPC listeners of the virtual node.
Specifies the numeric duration for the per-request timeout on gRPC connections to this virtual node's listener, after which an individual request is terminated.
Specifies the idle and per-request timeout settings for HTTP traffic on this listener, controlling how long connections or requests can remain idle or pending before termination.
The idle timeout for HTTP connections on the virtual node's listener, specifying the maximum amount of time a connection can remain idle (no data sent or received) before being terminated.
Specifies the unit of time (milliseconds or seconds) used for the idle timeout of an HTTP listener on the virtual node.

Specifies the numeric value of the idle timeout duration for HTTP listeners on this virtual node, interpreted according to the sibling unit (e.g., ms or s) to determine how long a connection can remain idle before it is timed out.

Defines the maximum duration allowed for a single HTTP request to complete on the virtual node's HTTP listener, configured as a numeric value with an associated time unit (e.g., seconds or milliseconds).
The unit of time for the per-request HTTP timeout duration (e.g., 'ms' or 's'), used to specify how the timeout value is interpreted.
The numeric magnitude of the per-request timeout for HTTP listeners on the virtual node, interpreted with the sibling `unit` field (e.g., seconds) that determines the actual duration.
Specifies the HTTP/2 protocol-specific timeout settings for the virtual node listener, including idle timeout and per-request timeout durations.
Specifies the idle timeout for HTTP/2 connections on the virtual node listener, configured as a duration object that controls how long a connection can remain idle before it is terminated.
The unit of time (e.g., 'ms' or 's') for the HTTP/2 idle timeout duration specified for the virtual node listener.

The numeric amount of the idle timeout for HTTP/2 connections on the virtual node listener, interpreted together with the sibling `unit` field to define how long a connection may remain idle before being closed.
Defines the per-request timeout for HTTP/2 traffic on the App Mesh virtual node listener, specifying a duration value and its unit (e.g., seconds or milliseconds).
The unit of measure (milliseconds or seconds) for the HTTP/2 per-request timeout on a virtual node's listener.

Specifies the per-request timeout in milliseconds for HTTP/2 traffic on this virtual node's listener, defining the maximum duration allowed for a single request to complete before the connection is closed.
Specifies the TCP-specific timeout settings for a listener in AWS App Mesh, including the idle timeout for TCP connections.
Configures the idle timeout duration for TCP traffic on this virtual node listener, using a Duration object that defines how long the connection may remain idle before App Mesh closes it.
Specifies the unit of measurement (e.g., 'ms' or 's') for the idle timeout duration of a TCP listener on the virtual node, controlling how long a connection may remain idle before being terminated.

The numeric value of the idle timeout duration for TCP connections to the virtual node listener, which is paired with the unit field (e.g., 'ms' or 's') to set how long a connection may sit idle before being closed.
The TLS configuration for a listener on the virtual node, defining the certificate and mode (DISABLED, PERMISSIVE, or STRICT) for securing traffic.

Specifies the TLS certificate used by the virtual node listener to terminate TLS, either a certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) or a local file containing the certificate chain and private key.
The ACM certificate reference containing the ARN of the certificate to use for TLS termination on the virtual node listener.
ARN of an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate used to provide TLS certificates for the virtual node's listener.
Specifies the local file paths for the TLS certificate chain and private key used to terminate TLS connections on the virtual node listener.
Specifies the path to the certificate chain file used for the TLS certificate when the certificate is provided from a file on the virtual node.
The file path to the private key of the TLS certificate stored on the virtual node's file system, used by the listener for TLS termination.
Configures the TLS listener to use a certificate obtained from a Secret Discovery Service (SDS), specifying the secret name Envoy will reference.
Specifies the name of the secret retrieved from the Secrets Discovery Service (SDS) that contains the TLS certificate and private key for the virtual node's listener.

Specifies the TLS mode for the virtual node's listener, which controls whether the listener enforces encrypted connections (ENFORCED), permits both encrypted and plaintext traffic (PERMISSIVE), or disables TLS (DISABLED).

Defines the TLS certificate validation settings for the listener, specifying the trust chain (from a file or AWS Certificate Manager) and optional subject alternative names used to verify the peer certificate during TLS handshake.
Specifies the subject alternative names (SANs) that must match the certificate presented by the peer for TLS validation to succeed in the virtual node's TLS listener.
The match object defines the exact or suffix matching criteria for the subject alternative names (SANs) that the virtual node's TLS listener validation will accept for peer certificates.
Specifies the exact subject alternative names (SANs) that must match the certificate presented by the backend for the TLS validation to succeed.

Specifies the source of trust (an AWS Certificate Manager Private Certificate Authority or a local file containing the certificate chain) used to validate the peer certificate during TLS handshakes for the virtual node's listener.
This object defines the file-based trust configuration for TLS certificate validation, specifying the path to a file containing the trusted certificate chain in its `path` property.
The path to the certificate chain file on the file system that is used to validate the peer certificate for TLS in the virtual node listener.
Specifies the SDS (Secret Discovery Service) configuration used by the TLS validation trust, including the name of the secret that holds the certificate chain to validate the client.

The name of the secret in the Secret Discovery Service (SDS) server that provides the validation context for verifying the client certificate presented during TLS handshake on the virtual node's listener.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.spec.logging.text: Defines the access logging configuration for the virtual node, including the file path or format for Envoy access logs.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.spec.logging.a.text: The access log configuration for the virtual node, specifying how Envoy access logs are recorded, such as through a file path.
Configuration for sending virtual node access logs to a file, specifying the destination path and optional log format.
Configures the format of the access log written to the file, choosing between a structured JSON format with defined fields or a simple text format.
Specifies the list of key-value pairs that define the structured JSON fields for the virtual node's access log file, where each object contains a 'key' and 'value' to include in the log entry.
Defines the key name in a key-value pair within the JSON-formatted access log file configuration, specifying the field label emitted in the App Mesh virtual node's access log output.
The value to associate with the corresponding key in a JSON-formatted access log entry, typically an HTTP header name or a supported predefined value.
Specifies the text format string for the access log file, allowing you to define custom log output using variables such as %START_TIME%, %HOSTNAME%, and %REQUEST_ID% to include request metadata.
The file path on the Envoy container where the virtual node's access logs are written.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.spec.service_d.text: Configures how the virtual node's service endpoints are discovered in App Mesh, either via AWS Cloud Map (with namespace name, service name, and optional attributes) or via DNS (with a hostname).

Defines AWS Cloud Map-based service discovery for the virtual node by specifying the Cloud Map namespace name, service name, and optional attributes used to register and discover the virtual node's endpoints.
A list of key-value pairs (attributes) used to filter the AWS Cloud Map service instances that this virtual node discovers during service discovery.
The attribute key that, together with the corresponding value, is used to filter AWS Cloud Map service instances for service discovery of the virtual node.
Specifies the value of the key-value pair that AWS Cloud Map uses to match service instances for the virtual node's service discovery.

Specifies the IP version preference for AWS Cloud Map service discovery (IPv4_PREFERRED, IPv6_PREFERRED, IPv4_ONLY, or IPv6_ONLY), controlling whether the virtual node resolves service endpoints using IPv4, IPv6, or both with a preferred order.
The name of the AWS Cloud Map namespace that the virtual node uses for service discovery to locate backend service instances.
The name of the AWS Cloud Map service that the virtual node uses for service discovery.

Specifies the DNS-based service discovery method for the virtual node, including the DNS hostname that App Mesh resolves to locate the service and an optional response type that controls whether the proxy returns endpoints or a load balancer address.
The fully qualified DNS hostname (e.g., my-service.namespace.svc.cluster.local) that App Mesh uses for DNS-based service discovery to resolve the virtual node's endpoints.
Specifies the IP version preference (IPv4 or IPv6) used when resolving the DNS hostname for service discovery, with allowed values such as IPv4_PREFERRED, IPv6_PREFERRED, IPv4_ONLY, or IPv6_ONLY.

Specifies the DNS response type for the virtual node's DNS service discovery, where `ENDPOINTS` returns the IP addresses of the virtual node's tasks and `LOAD_BALANCER` returns the DNS name of the associated load balancer.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.tags.key.text: Specifies a tag key for the AWS App Mesh virtual node, used to categorize and manage the resource in AWS.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS App Mesh virtual node, used for resource organization and identification.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_node.virtual_node_n.text: Specifies the name of the virtual node, which must be unique within the service mesh and is used to identify the virtual node in App Mesh APIs and configuration.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_router.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the virtual router.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_router.id.text: The AWS-assigned unique identifier for this App Mesh virtual router, which is its Amazon Resource Name (ARN).

aws_app_mesh_virtual_router.mesh_name.text: The name of the service mesh in which the virtual router is defined.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_router.mesh_owner.text: Specifies the AWS account ID of the mesh owner when creating a virtual router in a shared App Mesh mesh owned by another AWS account; if omitted, the mesh is assumed to be in your current account.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_router.resource_own.text: The AWS account ID of the account that owns the virtual router, as returned by the App Mesh API in the resource metadata.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_router.spec.text: Specifies the virtual router's desired configuration, primarily its Listener property that defines the port mapping and protocol for traffic received by the virtual router.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_router.spec.listene.text: Defines the port mappings (port and protocol) that the virtual router listens on for traffic from virtual services.
Specifies the port number and protocol (such as http or tcp) that the virtual router listener uses to receive incoming traffic.
Specifies the port number that the virtual router listener uses to receive incoming traffic, as part of its port mapping configuration.
Specifies the protocol (grpc, http, http2, or tcp) for the listener's port mapping on the virtual router.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_router.tags.text: Tags are key-value pairs you can assign to an AWS App Mesh virtual router to organize, identify, and manage access to it through IAM policies, following the standard AWS resource tagging model.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_router.uid.text: The unique identifier (UUID) assigned by AWS to the virtual router, used to uniquely reference it within the App Mesh service.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_router.virtual_rout.text: The name of the virtual router, which must be unique within the AWS App Mesh service mesh it belongs to.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_service.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the virtual service, generated by AWS App Mesh and used to uniquely identify this resource.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_service.id.text: The ARN of the App Mesh virtual service.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_service.mesh_name.text: The name of the App Mesh service mesh in which this virtual service is defined.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_service.mesh_owner.text: The AWS account ID of the mesh owner, used when creating a virtual service in a shared mesh owned by another account.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_service.resource_ow.text: The AWS account ID that owns the App Mesh virtual service, returned as a computed read-only attribute.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_service.spec.text: Defines the service discovery and routing configuration for the virtual service, specifying either a virtual node or virtual router as the provider.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_service.spec.provid.text: Specifies the virtual node or virtual router provider that the virtual service routes traffic to, defining how the service is realized in the mesh.
Specifies the virtual node that backs this virtual service, enabling traffic routing to that node's endpoints.
Specifies the name of the virtual node that acts as the service provider for this virtual service, to which the virtual service routes traffic.
Configures this virtual service to use a specific virtual router as its provider, directing traffic to the named virtual router within the mesh.
Specifies the name of the virtual router that acts as the provider for this App Mesh virtual service, routing traffic to the chosen virtual router.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_service.tags.text: A list of custom key-value tags to apply to the App Mesh virtual service, enabling cost tracking, resource grouping, and tag-based access control with IAM.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_service.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag (key-value pair) attached to the App Mesh virtual service, used for metadata and resource categorization.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_service.uid.text: The unique identifier (UUID) that AWS App Mesh assigns to the virtual service when it is created.

aws_app_mesh_virtual_service.virtual_ser.text: The DNS-compliant name of the virtual service, which acts as the service discovery identifier used within the App Mesh for routing traffic.

aws_app_runner_auto_scaling_configuratio.text: The key of a tag to apply to this AWS App Runner auto scaling configuration, used for resource organization and cost allocation.
The value of a tag attached to the App Runner auto scaling configuration, which is a user-defined key-value pair used for labeling and managing the resource.

aws_app_runner_observability_configurati.text: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the App Runner observability configuration, used to categorize and identify the resource.

aws_app_runner_service.instance_configur.text: The ARN of an IAM role that grants the App Runner service permissions to access other AWS services on behalf of the service's instances.

aws_app_runner_service.source_configurat.text: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS App Runner assumes to access the source code repository or image registry specified in the service's source configuration.
The name (key) of a runtime environment secret, which becomes the environment variable name that App Runner injects into the service's runtime environment.
The AWS Secrets Manager secret ARN or Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter name whose value is exposed as the runtime environment secret to the App Runner service.
Specifies the environment variables to pass to the App Runner service runtime, as a list of key-value pairs where each object contains the variable name and value.
The name (key) of a runtime environment variable that App Runner sets in the service's environment when it launches.
The value of a runtime environment variable defined for the App Runner service's source code configuration.
The name of the environment variable to set in the App Runner service container, whose value is sourced from an AWS Secrets Manager secret.

The value of a runtime environment secret entry, which is the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the secret stored in AWS Secrets Manager that gets injected into the App Runner service's runtime environment.

Specifies a list of key-value pairs, each containing a Name and Value, that define runtime environment variables passed to the App Runner service's container when it uses an image from an image repository.
The name (key) of a runtime environment variable to be passed to the App Runner service's container when using an image repository configuration.
Defines the value of a runtime environment variable (the key is given by the corresponding `name` field) that App Runner injects into the service's container when the image is started.

aws_app_runner_service.tags.text: This is a list of tag objects (Key and Value) that attach metadata to an AWS App Runner service, used for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization.

aws_app_runner_service.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to an AWS App Runner service, used to organize and manage the service resource.

aws_app_runner_vpc_connector.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag that can be attached to the AWS App Runner VPC connector for identification and resource management.

aws_app_runner_vpc_connector.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key-value pair that can be assigned to the App Runner VPC connector for resource organization, access control, and cost tracking.

aws_app_runner_vpc_ingress_connection.ta.text: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) that are applied to the AWS App Runner VPC Ingress Connection to help identify, categorize, and manage this resource.

aws_app_stream_app_block.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AppStream 2.0 app block.

aws_app_stream_app_block.created_time.text: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the AppStream App Block was created.

aws_app_stream_app_block.description.text: The description of the AppStream 2.0 AppBlock, a user-defined string that provides human-readable details about the application bundle stored as an app block.

aws_app_stream_app_block.display_name.text: The display name of the app block, which is the user-friendly name shown in the AppStream 2.0 console and to end users.

aws_app_stream_app_block.name.text: The unique name for the app block, used as an identifier in AppStream 2.0.

aws_app_stream_app_block.packaging_type.text: Defines the packaging format (either 'CAB' or 'ZIP') used to compress and store the application source files for this AppStream 2.0 app block.

aws_app_stream_app_block.post_setup_scri.text: Specifies the details of a script that runs after the AppStream app block setup process, including the script path, any executable parameters, and the allowed execution timeout.
Specifies the path to the executable that runs the post-setup script for the AppStream 2.0 application block.
The S3 location (bucket and key) of the post-setup script that AppStream 2.0 runs on the streaming instance after the AppBlock application is installed.
Specifies the name of the S3 bucket that contains the post-setup script for this AppStream AppBlock.
The S3 object key (path) of the post-setup script within the S3 bucket specified by script_s3_location, which AppStream 2.0 downloads and executes after setting up the app block.
Specifies the maximum time, in seconds, that the post-setup script can run before it is considered failed.

aws_app_stream_app_block.setup_script_de.text: Specifies the details of the setup script that runs on streaming instances when the app block is deployed, including the script location, executable path, parameters, and timeout.
Specifies the command-line arguments to pass to the setup script executable when the app block is provisioned.
The path to the executable file that runs the setup script for the app block.
The Amazon S3 location of the setup script that runs when the app block is provisioned.
The name of the S3 bucket where the setup script for this AppStream app block is stored.
The S3 object key (file path) of the setup script within the specified S3 bucket, which AppStream 2.0 uses to retrieve and run the script when setting up the app block.
