Specifies the list of CloudWatch alarm metrics to monitor for the process, enabling custom alarm-based health monitoring for each process in the Application Insights application's component configuration.
The name of the metric (e.g., CPU Utilization, Memory) to monitor for the process's alarm, used to define alarm metrics in the default component configuration.
The name of the application process to be monitored under the custom component's configuration details.

This object configures the SQL Server Prometheus exporter, specifying settings such as the exporter's listening port and Prometheus endpoint path used by Application Insights to collect SQL Server metrics.
The port number on which the SQL Server Prometheus exporter listens to expose metrics for collection by Application Insights.
The name of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the SQL Server credentials (username and password) used by the Prometheus exporter to connect to the SQL Server database.
Specifies the list of Windows Event Log configurations (including event type, event levels, and log group name) that Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights monitors for the component.
Specifies the Windows event log levels (such as ERROR, WARNING, INFO) to monitor for the given Windows event in Application Insights.
The name of the Windows Event Log (e.g., Application, System, or Security) to monitor for the component's configuration details.
The name of the Windows Event Log (e.g., Application, System, Security) that Application Insights monitors for the component when using this default overwrite configuration.
Specifies a regular expression pattern set used to filter Windows event messages for Application Insights monitoring.

Specifies a list of monitoring configurations for individual sub-component types (e.g., AWS::EC2::Instance) that override the base default configuration contained in the parent DefaultOverwriteComponentConfiguration.
Specifies the alarm metrics and log configurations that define how to monitor a specific sub-component type when the component's default configuration is overwritten.
Specifies the list of alarm metrics that define the CloudWatch alarms to monitor for the sub-component.
Specifies the name of the CloudWatch metric that Application Insights monitors and uses to create an alarm for the component.
Defines the log configurations (e.g., log group names or paths) to be monitored for this sub-component type in the Application Insights application.
Specifies the encoding format (e.g., UTF-8) that Application Insights uses to read the log file for this sub-component's log configuration.

The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group whose events Application Insights collects and analyzes for the specified sub-component type, enabling anomaly detection and metric generation from those logs.
The file system path on the application host to the log file or directory that Application Insights monitors for this sub-component type (e.g., /var/log/myapp or C:\logs\app.log).
Specifies the type of logs to monitor, such as SQL_SERVER, IIS, APPLICATION, or CUSTOM, for this sub-component configuration.

For a given log in a sub-component's configuration, pattern_set specifies custom log patterns (typically one per line) that Application Insights uses to match and highlight specific events in that log, overriding the default pattern set.

Specifies the list of process names to be monitored for the sub-component type configuration, enabling Application Insights to track operating system-level processes under the default overwrite component monitoring settings.
Specifies the CloudWatch metrics to monitor for the processes defined in the sub-component type configuration, where each object in the list identifies a metric name to be used for creating alarms.
The name of the CloudWatch metric that the alarm monitors for the process (for example, CPU or memory usage).
The name of the process to be monitored as part of the sub-component configuration for this application component's monitoring settings.

Specifies the Windows event logs to monitor for the sub-component, where each entry defines an event name (e.g., Application, System) and optionally its log group, event levels, and pattern set to determine which events are collected.
The list of Windows Event Log levels (e.g., ERROR, WARNING, INFO) to monitor for the specified Windows Event in the sub-component configuration.
The name of the Windows Event Log to monitor, such as Application, System, or a custom log name, when overriding configuration for a sub-component type.
Specifies the CloudWatch Logs log group name where the Windows Event Logs are collected for monitoring by Application Insights.
The comma-separated list of Windows Event Log patterns (e.g., 'Application', 'System') used to filter which Windows events are monitored for this sub-component.

Identifies the AWS resource type of the sub-component (e.g., AWS::EC2::Instance or AWS::DynamoDB::Table) so that the accompanying sub-component configuration details can be applied to that specific resource type when overwriting default monitoring settings.
The tier property specifies the application tier (e.g., DOT_NET_CORE, JAVA_JMX, MYSQL) that defines which monitoring settings apply to the component.

aws_application_insights_application.cus.text: The user-defined name for the custom component that groups related resources for monitoring in the Application Insights application.
Defines the list of AWS resources, specified by ARN or resource identifier, that are grouped together into this custom component for monitoring by Application Insights.

aws_application_insights_application.log.text: Defines the list of log patterns within a log pattern set, where each pattern specifies a regular expression (Pattern), a name (PatternName), and a rank for evaluation order.
The regular expression pattern used to match log lines for this custom log pattern in Application Insights.
The name to assign to this log pattern within a log pattern set, used to identify the pattern in the configuration.
A numeric value that sets the priority order of this log pattern within its log pattern set, where lower ranks are evaluated first.
The name of a log pattern set in AWS Application Insights, which groups a collection of log patterns to detect specific issues in application logs.

aws_application_insights_application.tag.text: The value of a tag associated with the Application Insights application, used to categorize and manage the resource within AWS.

aws_application_signals_grouping_configu.text: Specifies the fallback value used to group telemetry under a particular application or service when the source attribute defined by this grouping attribute definition is missing from the telemetry data.
The name of the grouping attribute (used as the key in a grouping attribute definition) that identifies how telemetry is grouped in Application Signals, such as an environment or service name.

Specifies the list of source telemetry attribute keys (e.g., service.name, environment) that are combined to derive the value of the corresponding grouping attribute in this grouping attribute definition, determining how Application Signals groups telemetry into applications or services.
The timestamp of when the grouping configuration was last updated, as set by the AWS service.

aws_application_signals_service_level_ob.text: The length of the look-back window, in minutes, over which the burn rate is evaluated for this burn rate configuration.
The reason or annotation for excluding this time window from the SLO's evaluation, commonly used to document planned maintenance or expected anomalies.
Defines the recurrence schedule (cron or rate expression) for a time window during which the service level objective's evaluation is excluded.
The cron expression that defines the recurring schedule for this exclusion window, during which the SLO is not evaluated.

Defines the start of an exclusion window, a time period during which the SLO's evaluation is paused so that planned maintenance or other excluded events do not affect the objective's availability calculation.
This object specifies the start and end times of the exclusion window, during which the SLO's attainment metric is not evaluated.
The duration in minutes of the exclusion window, during which the SLO's metric data is excluded from evaluation.
The unit of time (such as Days or Hours) for the numeric duration of the exclusion window, determining how long the service level objective evaluation is paused.
Configures the request-based SLI as a composite SLI, which aggregates multiple underlying service level indicators into a single SLI metric for the SLO.
Defines the list of individual SLI components (each with its own SLI metric configuration and weight) that are combined to calculate the composite SLI metric for this service level objective.
The name of the specific operation (e.g., an HTTP endpoint or API call) that this composite SLI component uses to evaluate performance against the SLO.
Defines which underlying service level indicators (SLIs) are selected and combined to calculate the composite SLI for the SLO.
A string specifying the boolean formula (e.g., `${sl1} AND ${sl2}`) that determines how the referenced individual SLIs are combined to form the composite service level objective.
Determines the selection mode for a composite SLI, using 'ANY' to require that at least one of the selected operations meets the SLO, or 'ALL' to require that every selected operation meets the SLO.
The AWS account ID that owns the CloudWatch metric used as the bad count metric for the monitored request count in the SLO, typically needed when the metric is in a different account.
The CloudWatch metrics expression that defines the bad count metric used to calculate the service level objective.
The unique identifier assigned to this bad-count metric definition within the request-based SLI, used to reference the metric in the SLO's monitored request count configuration.

This object defines the CloudWatch metric statistic (including namespace, metric name, dimensions, period, and statistic) that is used to count the number of bad requests for the request-based SLI's monitored request count metric in the SLO.
The CloudWatch metric that defines the bad count metric, including its namespace, metric name, and dimensions, used to calculate the number of bad requests for the request-based SLI.

Defines the CloudWatch metric dimensions (name-value pairs) that identify the bad count metric used in the request-based SLI's monitored request count metric, enabling the SLI to track unsuccessful requests.

Specifies the name of a CloudWatch metric dimension (for example, 'ServiceName' or 'Operation') that, together with the dimension value, identifies the bad count metric used in the request-based SLO's monitored request count metric.
The value of a dimension that identifies the CloudWatch metric used to count bad requests for the request-based SLO.
The name of the CloudWatch metric that represents the count of bad or failing requests used to calculate the service level objective's request-based SLI.

Specifies the CloudWatch namespace of the metric used as the bad request count for the monitored request count metric in the request-based SLI, identifying the service or application that emits the metric.

The period, in seconds, for the CloudWatch metric statistic that collects the bad count metric, which is used as part of the monitored request count metric in the request-based SLI for this Service Level Objective.

The statistic (e.g., Sum, Average) to apply to the metric data for the bad request count metric in the request-based SLI's monitored request count metric, used to evaluate requests that do not meet the SLI objective.

The unit of the CloudWatch metric statistic (e.g., Count, Bytes, Seconds) that defines the bad request count metric used in the monitored request count metric for this request-based service level objective.

Controls whether the value of the bad count metric is returned in the CloudWatch metric math expression that defines this request-based SLI, where 'true' surfaces the bad count data as an output and 'false' uses it solely as an intermediate calculation step.
The AWS account ID of the CloudWatch metric that counts good (successful) requests, used to compute the request-based service level objective.

The CloudWatch metric math expression string that defines the good count metric for the request-based SLI, used to calculate the number of successful requests counted against the service level objective.

The unique identifier (Id) of the CloudWatch metric data definition used as the good count metric within the monitored request count metric for a request-based SLO, enabling the metric to be referenced in SLI expressions and burn-rate calculations.

The metric_stat object defines the CloudWatch metric and statistic (e.g., metric name, namespace, dimensions, statistic, period) used to obtain the count of good (successful) requests for the request-based SLO calculation.
Specifies the CloudWatch metric (namespace, metric name, and dimensions) that defines the 'good' count for the request-based SLO's monitored request count metric.
A list of dimension key-value pairs that define the scope of the CloudWatch metric used as the good count metric in the request-based service level objective's monitored request count metric.
The name (key) of a CloudWatch metric dimension that, along with its value in the corresponding 'value' field, identifies and filters the good count metric referenced in the request-based SLI.
The value of a dimension on the CloudWatch metric that counts good (successful) requests for this request-based service level objective, used to identify or filter the metric.
The CloudWatch metric name for the metric that provides the count of good requests, used as the numerator in the request-based SLI's availability calculation for the service level objective.

The CloudWatch namespace (such as 'AWS/ApplicationELB' or a custom namespace) that identifies the metric used as the good count metric in the request-based SLI's monitored request count for this service level objective.

Specifies the evaluation period in seconds for the CloudWatch metric statistic of the good count metric, determining the time granularity over which the request-based SLI's good request count is aggregated.
The CloudWatch statistic (e.g., Sum, Average) applied to the good count metric to evaluate the number of good requests for the request-based SLI.

Specifies the unit of measurement for the metric statistic (e.g., Count, Bytes, Seconds) that defines the good count of monitored requests in the request-based SLO's metric, enabling CloudWatch to correctly interpret and compare metric values.

Whether the metric data from this good count metric is returned and included in the calculated good count for the request-based service level objective, matching the CloudWatch MetricDataQuery ReturnData behavior.
The AWS account ID that owns the CloudWatch metric used for the total request count metric in the request-based SLI; if omitted, defaults to the current account.
Specifies the CloudWatch metrics insights expression that calculates the total request count for the request-based service level objective's metric.
The unique identifier for the total request count metric, used to reference this metric in the SLO's metric data queries and math expressions.
Defines the CloudWatch metric statistic (metric name, dimensions, period, stat, and unit) for the total request count metric used to calculate the request-based SLI.
CloudWatch metric definition (namespace, metric name, and dimensions) that identifies the metric whose value represents the total number of requests for the request-based SLI.
Defines the list of CloudWatch metric dimension name-value pairs that uniquely identify the metric used for the total request count in the request-based service level objective metric.
Specifies the name of a dimension that, combined with a corresponding dimension value, identifies the CloudWatch metric used for the total request count in the request-based service level objective.

Specifies the value for a metric dimension (such as an operation name or resource identifier) that, together with the corresponding dimension key, uniquely identifies the total request count metric used in the request-based SLI's metric statistic.
The name of the CloudWatch metric that measures the total request count, used as the source for the metric_stat in the request-based service level objective's SLI.
This field specifies the CloudWatch namespace of the metric used to measure the total request count for the request-based SLO.
The period (in seconds) over which the total request count metric is aggregated or evaluated, defining the granularity of the metric stat used for the request-based SLI.
The CloudWatch statistic (for example, 'Sum') used to aggregate the total request count metric over the evaluation period for the service level objective.

The unit of measurement for the CloudWatch metric used as the total request count in the request-based SLI, such as 'Count' or 'Bytes', which must be consistent with the metric's actual unit to compute the SLO correctly.
Indicates whether the total request count metric data query returns its data for inclusion in the request-based service level objective calculation.
Specifies the composite SLI configuration, which lets you combine multiple service level indicators using boolean AND/OR operators to evaluate the overall SLI for the service level objective.
The list of component service level indicators that are combined to compute the composite SLI, where each component contains its own SLI metric configuration and optional weight.

The name of the service operation (e.g., a specific API action like 'GetItem' for DynamoDB) for which this component's metric is defined, used to filter the CloudWatch metric contributing to the composite SLO.
Specifies the metric selection criteria (service, operation, and metric type filters) used to determine which underlying metrics are aggregated into the composite service level indicator.
Specifies whether the composite SLO requires all selected member SLOs to meet their objectives (ALL) or at least one (ANY).
Specifies the AWS account ID that the metric data query will query metrics from, enabling cross-account metric retrieval for the SLO's SLI metric evaluation.

The CloudWatch Metrics Insights or metric math expression that defines the service level indicator metric, enabling calculations such as SUM(METRICS()) or arithmetic over the referenced metric data queries.
A short name that uniquely identifies this metric data query within the SLI's metric data queries list, so that other queries or metric math expressions can reference it.

Specifies the CloudWatch metric to use for this query, including the metric namespace, metric name, dimensions, period, and the statistic (e.g., Average, Sum) to compute for the SLO's service level indicator.
Defines the CloudWatch metric (namespace, metric name, and optional dimensions) that is used in the metric statistic for this SLO's metric data query.
Specifies the CloudWatch metric dimensions (as name-value pairs) that identify the specific metric used in this metric stat of the SLI's metric query.
Specifies the dimension key (name) for a CloudWatch metric dimension that identifies the metric used in the service level objective's SLI metric query.
The value of the dimension, paired with the dimension name, identifies the specific metric dimension for the metric used in the service level objective's SLI metric data query.
The name of the CloudWatch metric that the metric stat uses for this metric data query in the SLO's SLI metric definition.
Specifies the CloudWatch namespace of the metric used in the metric statistic for the service level objective's SLI metric.

The period (in seconds) specifies the granularity of the metric used in the SLI metric stat, determining the time interval over which the metric values are aggregated for the service level objective calculation.
Specifies the CloudWatch metric statistic (e.g., Sum, Average, Minimum, Maximum, SampleCount) to use for the SLI metric in the service level objective.

The unit of measurement (e.g., Count, Milliseconds, Bytes) for the metric statistic used in the service level objective's metric data query, which specifies the unit that the SLO calculation applies to the metric value.

Specifies whether the results of this metric data query are returned for use as the service level objective's metric, where queries with ReturnData set to false are used only as intermediate inputs to other queries (such as math expressions) and are not directly evaluated as the SLI metric.
Specifies the key of a tag to attach to the service level objective, enabling you to categorize and manage SLOs by metadata such as environment, team, or cost center.
The value of a tag attached to the Application Signals Service Level Objective, used to store arbitrary user-defined metadata.

aws_aps_anomaly_detector.configuration.text: Configures the anomaly detector with a PromQL-based metric definition and optional dimension filters that determine which metric time series are analyzed for anomalous behavior.

aws_aps_anomaly_detector.configuration.r.text: Defines the configuration for the Random Cut Forest algorithm used by this anomaly detector to identify anomalous patterns in Prometheus metric data.

Controls the Random Cut Forest anomaly detection sensitivity by specifying whether to ignore data points that are close to the expected value from above, reducing false positives for minor upper-side deviations.

When enabled, this parameter instructs the Random Cut Forest anomaly detector to ignore deviations that are below but very close to the expected value, preventing them from being flagged as anomalies.
The PromQL query that selects the time series data to be analyzed for anomalies by the random cut forest algorithm in the anomaly detector.

In the Random Cut Forest configuration of an AWS APS anomaly detector, sample_size specifies the number of data points from the input time series used to train the model, balancing training accuracy against computational cost.
The number of consecutive time series data points grouped into a single shingle (feature vector) that the Random Cut Forest model considers when evaluating anomalies.

aws_aps_anomaly_detector.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus anomaly detector, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_aps_anomaly_detector.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag applied to the Amazon Managed Prometheus anomaly detector, used for resource categorization, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_aps_rule_groups_namespace.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus rule groups namespace, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_aps_rule_groups_namespace.tags.value.text: The value for a tag assigned to the AWS Prometheus rule groups namespace, used to organize, identify, and manage the resource through cost allocation and operational metadata.

aws_aps_scraper.scraper_logging_configur.text: Specifies the list of scraper components (such as target allocation or scrape loop) for which logs are enabled and forwarded to the configured log destination for the Amazon Managed Prometheus scraper.
The type of scraper component (APISERVER, SCRAPER, or TARGET) for which logging is enabled in the scraper logging configuration.

aws_aps_scraper.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag that can be assigned to an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus scraper for organizational and identification purposes.

aws_aps_workspace.query_logging_configur.text: Specifies the CloudWatch Logs log group that receives query logs from the Amazon Managed Prometheus workspace.
The ARN of the CloudWatch Logs log group to which the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace sends its query logs.

aws_aps_workspace.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key applied to an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace, used to categorize and manage the workspace for purposes such as environment, team, or cost allocation.

aws_aps_workspace.workspace_configuratio.text: Defines the list of label names (e.g., ["job", "team"]) that group time series into sets, and the workspace configuration applies the associated maximum active series limit per unique set of label values.
The name of a label set in the workspace configuration's limits_per_label_sets section, used to identify a group of labels for applying per-label-set series limits in Amazon Managed Prometheus.
The maximum number of active time series allowed for the label set defined in this Amazon Managed Prometheus workspace configuration limit, enforced per label set.
Specifies the query limits (for example, maximum number of samples and maximum query time) applied to a particular label set within the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace configuration.

The maximum number of unique time series (combinations of metric name and label values) that a per-label-set limit allows to be active in the workspace, beyond which incoming samples for that label set are rejected and the limit is enforced.

aws_arcregion_switch_plan.associated_ala.text: A list of ARNs or names of CloudWatch alarms associated with the region switch plan; when any of these alarms enters the ALARM state, the switch plan is automatically executed to perform the region failover.

aws_arcregion_switch_plan.execution_role.text: The IAM role that AWS Application Recovery Controller (ARC) assumes to execute the region switch plan, granting permissions to update routing controls and perform the crossover of traffic between regions.

aws_arcregion_switch_plan.primary_region.text: Specifies the AWS region that is considered the primary or active region, which is the source from which traffic is switched to the secondary region during a region switch plan execution.

aws_arcregion_switch_plan.recovery_time_.text: The target recovery time objective (RTO) in minutes for the switch plan, specifying the maximum acceptable time to resume operations after a failover or region switch.

aws_arcregion_switch_plan.report_configu.text: The AWS account ID of the owner of the destination S3 bucket, used by the service to verify bucket ownership before writing the report output to prevent accidental writes to unintended buckets.

aws_arcregion_switch_plan.route53_health.text: The list of Amazon Route 53 health check IDs that the switch plan monitors to assess the health of the active region, helping determine whether a region failover should be initiated.
This field specifies the Route 53 hosted zone IDs associated with the health checks, which the ARC region switch plan uses to update the corresponding DNS records when a failover occurs.

aws_arcregion_switch_plan.triggers.condi.text: The name of the Amazon CloudWatch alarm that must be in ALARM state to satisfy this trigger condition and initiate the switch plan.

aws_arcregion_switch_plan.workflows.step.text: Defines the AWS regions and the associated ARC routing control identifiers (such as ARNs or names) that the execution block configures to implement the region switch.
Configures the auto scaling behavior (e.g., min/max capacity or scaling policy) for Aurora Provisioned clusters when this workflow execution block is run.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an IAM role that allows the execution block to perform Aurora provisioned scaling actions in a different AWS account, enabling cross-account failover or scaling operations.
The external identifier that must be supplied when assuming an IAM role to perform Aurora provisioning and scaling actions, used as a safety measure to prevent the confused deputy problem.
Specifies the identifier of the Aurora global cluster to which this provisioned scaling configuration applies.
Defines the set of Amazon Aurora instance ARNs that the provisioned scaling configuration applies to during an execution block, limiting scaling actions to those instances.
Specifies the Amazon Aurora database cluster ARNs within the region that this provisioned scaling configuration targets during a workflow execution block.
The ARN of an IAM role in the target AWS account that is assumed to perform Aurora Serverless scaling operations during a region switch.
Specifies the Aurora global cluster identifier (the global database) that this serverless scaling configuration is associated with during the execution step of an ARC region switch workflow.

Specifies a list of Amazon Aurora Serverless database cluster ARNs in the target region whose compute capacity will be scaled according to the Aurora Serverless scaling configuration during this execution step of the switch plan.
Specifies the maximum time in minutes to allow for an Aurora Serverless database to complete a scaling adjustment during an execution step's blocking configuration.
The ARN of the IAM role that the custom action Lambda function assumes to access or modify resources in another AWS account during the workflow step.

The external identifier (ExternalId) that the Lambda function uses when assuming an IAM role for the custom action, helping prevent the confused deputy problem by ensuring the role trust policy requires it.
The AWS Region in which the Lambda function for the custom action is invoked during this step of the region switch plan.
The number of minutes to wait before retrying the custom action Lambda function after a failed execution step in the workflow.
This field specifies the Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the Amazon DocumentDB clusters that the execution block configuration in this workflow step operates on during the region switch.
Specifies the identifier of the Amazon DocumentDB global cluster that the execution step's DocumentDB configuration targets during the region switch workflow.
Configuration for increasing the EC2 Auto Scaling Group capacity as part of a step's execution block, used to pre-scale compute resources during a region switch workflow.
Specifies the list of Auto Scaling Groups targeted for capacity increase during this execution block step's capacity increase configuration.
The ARN of the EC2 Auto Scaling group whose desired capacity will be increased as part of this execution block step in the region switch plan.
The IAM role ARN assumed in the account that owns the Auto Scaling group to perform the capacity increase action for this step.
Specifies the maximum time in minutes that the execution block waits for the EC2 Auto Scaling group capacity increase to reach its target before the step is considered failed.
The ARN of the Amazon ECS cluster that the ECS service belongs to, used to target the service for capacity increase during the execution block of the workflow step.
The cross-account IAM role assumed to increase the desired capacity of this ECS service in another AWS account during the region switch capacity increase step.
The ARN of the ECS service that will be targeted for a capacity increase when the execution block runs.
The target capacity percentage to set for the ECS service or cluster when this execution block's capacity increase action is executed.
The maximum time, in minutes, allowed for the ECS capacity increase to complete during this execution block step before the step is considered failed.

The minimum success percentage required for an ungraceful ECS capacity increase execution step to be considered successful, used to validate that enough capacity was added during the switch plan workflow.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon EKS cluster that the scaling configuration targets, identifying the specific cluster to be scaled during the region switch execution step.
The ARN of the IAM role to assume in the target account owning the EKS cluster, used by the region switch execution to perform scaling changes on that cluster.
Specifies the Kubernetes API version (e.g., 'v1', 'apps/v1') of the resource type to be scaled, matching the apiVersion used in the resource manifest.
Specifies the Kubernetes resource kind (e.g., Deployment, StatefulSet) that the scaling configuration targets for EKS resource scaling.
Specifies the minimum percentage of EKS resources that must successfully complete scaling for the ungraceful step to be considered successful.
The ARN of an IAM role assumed by the switch plan to access and manage the Amazon Aurora global database in a different AWS account during this execution step.
The database_cluster_arns field specifies the list of Amazon Aurora Global Database cluster ARNs that this execution block will target for switching during the region switch plan.
The Aurora global cluster identifier that the execution block's step uses to target the specific global database across regions during a region switch.
Maps each AWS region to the Lambda event source mapping identifiers that should be enabled or disabled when this region switch execution block runs.

This object specifies how the execution step should handle an Amazon Neptune global database during a region switch, including the target global database and the failover action to promote a secondary cluster in the destination region.
The ARN of an IAM role that the switch plan assumes to perform Neptune Global Database configuration changes in a different AWS account.
The identifier of the Neptune global database that this execution block configuration targets during the region switch plan workflow step.

Specifies the Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the Neptune DB clusters (one per AWS region) that form a Neptune global database, used by the switch plan execution step to coordinate failover or management of the global database.
Specifies the maximum time in minutes that the Neptune global database configuration execution block is allowed to run before timing out in a region switch plan step.
Configuration for creating a cross-region read replica of an RDS database instance as part of the execution block of this workflow step.
The IAM role ARN to be used for cross-account permissions when creating the RDS cross-region read replica, allowing the operation to be performed in another AWS account.
Maps the ARNs of source RDS DB instances to the configuration specifying how their cross-region read replicas should be created when this execution block is run during a switch plan step.
The maximum time in minutes to wait for the RDS cross-region read replica creation to complete before the step times out and is marked as failed.
Specifies the configuration for promoting an Amazon RDS read replica to a standalone DB instance during the execution block of a step in the region switch workflow.
The ARN of an IAM role to assume when the recovery step performs the cross-account promotion of an RDS read replica.
A mapping of the ARNs of the existing primary RDS database instances to the ARNs of the corresponding read replicas in the secondary Region that should be promoted as part of the region switch step.
The ARN of the IAM role that the switch plan assumes in the target account to execute the region switch actions.
The external ID that the region switch plan provides when assuming an IAM role in the target account, used to establish trust and authorize the region switch operation.
Specifies the IAM role that the switch plan assumes to access the Route 53 health check when it resides in a different AWS account.
This field specifies the ID of the Amazon Route 53 hosted zone associated with the health check, enabling Route 53 to resolve and route the health check's DNS records.
The fully qualified domain name (e.g., app.example.com) that the Route 53 health check monitors to assess the health of the target endpoint during the execution block of a region switch plan.

Identifies the specific Route 53 record set (among multiple with the same name and type, e.g., for weighted or failover routing) that this health check configuration applies to within the switch plan's execution block.
The AWS Region of the Route 53 record set that this health check configuration monitors, used to control failover routing during a region switch execution block.
The maximum number of minutes that an execution step will wait for a Route 53 health check to reach the desired status before the step times out and is considered failed.

aws_arczonal_shift_autoshift_observer_no.text: Specifies whether the autoshift observer notification for the account is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED).

aws_arczonal_shift_zonal_autoshift_confi.text: Defines the practice run configuration for zonal autoshift, specifying blocking windows/dates and the outcome alarms that must clear for a practice run to be considered successful.
A list of dates in YYYY-MM-DD format on which zonal autoshift practice runs are blocked and cannot occur.
A list of cron expressions in UTC that define recurring time windows during which the service will not start a practice run for this zonal autoshift configuration.
Specifies the list of CloudWatch alarms that, when in ALARM state, block the practice run from starting (or continuing) for the zonal autoshift configuration.
The identifier (ARN or name) of a CloudWatch alarm that, when in ALARM state, blocks or stops zonal autoshift practice runs.

Specifies whether the CloudWatch alarm in the blocking alarms list is a 'BLOCKING' type (as opposed to 'OUTCOME'), which is required for blocking alarms to prevent zonal autoshift when the alarm enters ALARM state.
Specifies the CloudWatch alarms used to evaluate the outcome of zonal autoshift practice runs, where an alarm entering the ALARM state during a practice run marks it as failed.
The CloudWatch alarm name or ARN that identifies an alarm used to evaluate the outcome of a zonal autoshift practice run.
Specifies the type of the outcome alarm control condition, which must be either 'CLOUDWATCH_ALARM' or 'CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_MULTI', to evaluate the success or failure of a zonal autoshift practice run.
The identifier (such as an ARN) of the resource for which the zonal autoshift configuration is set, enabling automatic traffic shifting away from an Availability Zone for that resource.
Sets the desired zonal autoshift status for the configuration, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.

aws_athena_capacity_reservation.capacity.text: Specifies the list of Athena workgroup names assigned to this capacity reservation for query processing.

aws_athena_capacity_reservation.status.text: The current lifecycle state of the Athena capacity reservation (e.g., PENDING, ACTIVE, CANCELLING), updated automatically by AWS and not settable by the user.

aws_athena_capacity_reservation.tags.val.text: Specifies the value of an arbitrary user-defined tag key assigned to an AWS Athena capacity reservation, allowing metadata-based management and categorization of the reservation.

aws_athena_data_catalog.tags.text: Specifies the key-value tags to attach to the Athena data catalog for metadata management, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_athena_data_catalog.tags.value.text: The value string of a user-defined tag attached to the Athena data catalog, used for resource organization and access control.

aws_athena_work_group.tags.text: Specifies the tags to attach to the Athena work group, which can be used for cost tracking, resource organization, and IAM-based access control.

aws_athena_work_group.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the Athena work group, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_athena_work_group.tags.value.text: The user-defined value string paired with a tag key on the Athena work group, used for organizing, cost allocation, and tag-based access control.

aws_athena_work_group.work_group_configu.text: The computed work group configuration object that defines the query execution settings for this Athena work group, including the result location, encryption, and CloudWatch metrics publishing behavior.
Determines whether this workgroup uses Athena's managed query results bucket to automatically store query results.
Whether to remove the customer content encryption configuration from the Athena work group during an update.
When set to true, this removes the existing ACL (access control list) configuration from the workgroup's result settings during an update.
Indicates whether to remove the encryption configuration for the query results settings of the Athena work group.
Whether to remove the expected bucket owner setting from the Athena work group's result configuration for query results, so that the bucket owner check is no longer enforced.
This boolean flag, when set to true, removes the previously configured S3 output location for query results in the Athena work group as part of a result configuration update.

aws_audit_manager_assessment.assessment_.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS Audit Manager to the assessment.

aws_audit_manager_assessment.delegations.text: The unique identifier of the AWS Audit Manager assessment that this delegation is associated with, linking the delegation record to its parent assessment.
The name of the AWS Audit Manager assessment that this delegation belongs to.
Specifies an optional comment that the delegating administrator can include when delegating the assessment to another administrator, providing context or instructions for the delegation.
The unique identifier of the control set that is delegated to a reviewer within the assessment.
The IAM user or role that created this delegation of the assessment.
The creation time of the delegation, represented as a Unix epoch timestamp in seconds.
The unique identifier of the delegation, as assigned by AWS Audit Manager, which allows the assessment to be administered by a different AWS account.
The epoch timestamp indicating when the delegation entry within the assessment was last updated, reflecting changes to the delegation's details or status.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the assessment is delegated to.
The type of IAM role (ADMIN or OWNER) assigned to the delegated role for the assessment, controlling the level of permissions granted.
The current workflow state of a delegation, indicating whether the delegated control set assessment is in progress, under review, or complete.

aws_audit_manager_assessment.roles.role_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that is associated with the assessment, used to define the roles that have access to the assessment in AWS Audit Manager.
Specifies whether the role is a `PROCESS_OWNER`, who owns the overall assessment process, or a `RESOURCE_OWNER`, who owns a specific resource within the assessment.

aws_audit_manager_assessment.scope.aws_a.text: The email address of the AWS account that is included in the assessment's scope, used to identify the account for audit purposes.
The AWS account ID of an AWS account included in the assessment scope.
The name of the AWS account that is included in the scope of the assessment.

aws_audit_manager_assessment.scope.aws_s.text: The name of an AWS service (e.g., 'S3', 'IAM') that is included in the assessment's scope of audited services.

aws_audit_manager_assessment.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag attached to the AWS Audit Manager assessment, used to label or categorize the assessment for organizational purposes.

aws_audit_manager_assessment_framework.c.text: Specifies the list of controls for each control set in the assessment framework, where each control entry includes its name, source type, and mapping details so the framework can evaluate evidence against them.
The identifier (ARN) of the AWS Audit Manager control to include in the control set of the assessment framework.
Name of the control set within the assessment framework, identifying a group of related controls.

aws_audit_manager_assessment_framework.t.text: The key (name) of a tag attached to the AWS Audit Manager assessment framework, used to identify and categorize the resource.
In AWS Audit Manager, this is the value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to the assessment framework, used for custom metadata and resource identification/filtering.

aws_auto_scaling_auto_scaling_group.auto.text: The ARN (Amazon Resource Name) that uniquely identifies the Auto Scaling group, automatically assigned by AWS and exposed as a read-only computed value.

aws_auto_scaling_auto_scaling_group.capa.text: Lists the IDs of the Capacity Reservations that the Auto Scaling group targets when launching instances, enabling the group to use multiple specific reservations.
Specifies a list of ARNs of resource groups that have EC2 Capacity Reservations, which the Auto Scaling group targets when launching instances to use those reserved capacity resources.

aws_auto_scaling_auto_scaling_group.life.text: Specifies the action (either 'CONTINUE' or 'ABANDON') that the Auto Scaling group takes when the lifecycle hook times out or if an unexpected failure occurs.
Specifies the maximum time, in seconds, that an instance can remain in a waiting state before the lifecycle hook times out and the Auto Scaling group proceeds with the action.
The name of the lifecycle hook, which must be unique within the Auto Scaling group and is used to identify the hook for lifecycle actions and CloudWatch events.
The lifecycle transition type (autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING or autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING) that triggers the lifecycle hook.
The optional metadata string that AWS includes in the notification sent to the SNS topic or Lambda function when the lifecycle hook triggers.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic or Amazon SQS queue that Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling sends lifecycle hook notifications to when an instance enters a wait state.
The ARN of the IAM role that the Auto Scaling group assumes to publish lifecycle hook notifications to the specified notification target (e.g., SNS topic or SQS queue).

aws_auto_scaling_auto_scaling_group.metr.text: Specifies the granularity (currently only '1Minute') at which CloudWatch metrics are collected for the Auto Scaling group as part of a metrics collection configuration.
The list of Auto Scaling group metrics to collect (such as GroupMinSize, GroupMaxSize, GroupInServiceInstances, etc.) when this metrics collection is enabled.

aws_auto_scaling_auto_scaling_group.mixe.text: Specifies the AMI ID to use for the override, letting you run different instance types with different Amazon Machine Images within the same Auto Scaling group.

Specifies a set of instance requirements (such as vCPU count, memory, storage, and network performance) that Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling uses to select suitable instance types for the mixed instances policy, rather than a fixed instance type.
Defines the minimum and maximum number of accelerators (such as GPUs or FPGAs) that an instance type must have to be considered for the mixed instances policy launch template overrides.
Specifies the maximum number of accelerators (GPUs) that an instance type must have to be eligible for the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy.
The minimum number of accelerators (such as GPUs) that an instance type must have to be eligible for the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy override.

Specifies the list of hardware accelerator (GPU) manufacturers (e.g., 'nvidia', 'amd', 'xilinx') that instance types must have to satisfy the instance requirements for the mixed instances policy launch template override.
Specifies the names of GPU accelerators (e.g., a100, v100) that instance types must have, used to filter which instance types satisfy the requirements.
The range of total GPU accelerator memory (in MiB) that an instance must have to match the instance requirements for this Auto Scaling group's mixed instances launch template override.
The maximum total accelerator memory, in MiB, that an instance type must have to be included in the Auto Scaling group's instance type selection.

The minimum total memory, in MiB, of all GPU accelerators on an instance, which the Auto Scaling group uses to filter allowed instance types when applying the mixed instances policy's instance requirements.
The kinds of hardware accelerators (such as GPU or FPGA) that must be present on the instance types considered for this launch template override in the mixed instances policy.

Specifies the list of instance types that the Auto Scaling group is allowed to use when launching instances, restricting the selection to only these types within the instance requirements of a launch template override.

Specifies whether bare metal EC2 instance types are included, excluded, or required when Auto Scaling selects instance types for the mixed instances policy, filtering eligible instance types by the bare metal attribute.
The minimum and maximum baseline EBS bandwidth in Mbps an instance must support to be included in the auto scaling group's instance requirements overrides.
The maximum baseline EBS bandwidth in Mbps that an instance type must have to be selected for the mixed instances policy overrides.
Specifies the minimum baseline EBS bandwidth in Mbps that an instance must meet to be considered for the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy.
Defines the baseline performance factors (such as CPU and memory) that instance types must meet when selected through the mixed instances policy's instance requirements.
Defines the baseline CPU performance threshold used by the Auto Scaling group's instance requirements to filter eligible instance types, ensuring instances meet a minimum CPU performance level.

Specifies a list of CPU performance factor references (such as Amazon vCPU) used by Auto Scaling to define baseline CPU performance requirements when selecting instance types for the mixed instances policy launch template overrides.
Specifies an EC2 instance family (such as 'c5' or 'm5') to use as a CPU baseline performance reference when the Auto Scaling group evaluates candidate instance types for the mixed instances policy.
Specifies whether the Auto Scaling group's instance requirements include burstable performance instance types (such as T2 and T3), accepting values like 'included', 'excluded', or 'required'.

Restricts the eligible instance types to those using the specified CPU manufacturer(s) (e.g., 'intel', 'amd', or 'amazon-web-services') when the Auto Scaling group evaluates instance requirements for mixed instances.

Specifies a list of instance types to explicitly exclude from the set of instance types that satisfy the instance requirements for the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy launch template override.

Specifies which instance generations (current or previous) are accepted for the instance types Auto Scaling may choose from when launching instances under the mixed instances policy, accepting values 'current' and 'previous'.

Determines whether the selected instance types must have local instance storage (values: 'included', 'excluded', 'required', 'optional'), influencing which EC2 instance types are eligible for use in this Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy.
Filters the eligible instance types for the launch template's instance requirements to those with the specified local storage types, such as 'hdd' or 'ssd'.

Specifies the maximum price you are willing to pay for a Spot Instance as a percentage of the optimal On-Demand price, filtering eligible instance types in the mixed instances policy's instance requirements.

Specifies the memory-per-vCPU constraints (in GiB) for instance types allowed by this override, expressed as an object with optional Min and Max values that filter eligible instances for the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy.
Specifies the maximum amount of memory per vCPU (in GiB) that an instance type must have to be eligible under the instance requirements for the Auto Scaling group.

Specifies the minimum memory size in GiB per vCPU that an instance must have to be eligible for the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy, used as a lower bound when selecting instance types from the launch template overrides.
Specifies the minimum and maximum memory size in MiB that an instance must have to be considered for use in the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy.
The maximum amount of memory, in MiB, that an instance must have to satisfy the instance requirements in the mixed instances policy's launch template override.
The minimum amount of memory, in MiB, that an instance type must provide to be considered eligible when using instance requirements in the mixed instances policy.
Specifies the minimum and maximum network bandwidth in Gigabits per second (Gbps) that an instance type must meet to be eligible for the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy.
The maximum network bandwidth in gigabits per second (Gbps) that an instance must not exceed to satisfy the instance requirements for the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy.
The minimum network bandwidth in Gbps that an instance type must provide to match the instance requirements in the mixed instances policy launch template override.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of network interfaces that instance types must support, used to filter eligible instance types in the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy.
The maximum number of network interfaces that an instance type must support to be considered for the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy when using instance requirements.
The minimum number of network interfaces that an instance type must have to qualify for use in the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy, as part of the instance requirements override.

Sets the maximum price you are willing to pay for On-Demand Instances as a percentage above the lowest-priced instance type that satisfies the instance requirements, filtering out instance types whose on-demand price exceeds that threshold.
Indicates whether eligible instance types must support EC2 hibernation, so that only instances capable of hibernation are considered for the Auto Scaling group.

Specifies the maximum price you are willing to pay for a Spot Instance, as a percentage over the lowest price for the instance type, which controls the Spot Instance types selected for the Auto Scaling group.
Sets the minimum and maximum total local storage (in GB) for instance types eligible in the mixed instances policy, derived from the instance requirements of each launch template override.
The maximum amount of local storage, in GB, that an instance type can have to be considered for the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy.
The minimum total local storage in GB that an instance must have to qualify for the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy when using this launch template override.
Defines the required vCPU count range (minimum and maximum) that an instance type must meet to be considered when using instance requirements to select instance types for the mixed instances policy.
The maximum number of vCPUs that an instance type can have to be considered for the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy, used to filter instance types by compute capacity.
The minimum number of vCPUs that an instance type must have to be considered in the Auto Scaling group's mixed instances policy instance requirements.
Specifies an EC2 instance type to include as an override in the mixed instances policy, so the Auto Scaling group can launch instances of that type in addition to the launch template's default type.
Specifies the launch template and version to use for each override in a mixed instances policy, letting different instance types or instance requirements reference different launch templates.
The ID of the launch template to use for this specific override in the mixed instances policy, allowing a different launch template for a given instance type.

Specifies the name of the launch template to use for this specific override in the mixed instances policy, allowing the Auto Scaling group to launch instances with a particular template from the overrides list.
Specifies the version of the launch template to use for this instance type override in the mixed instances policy, such as a specific version number, $Default, or $Latest.

Specifies the relative capacity that this instance type contributes to the Auto Scaling group's desired capacity when using a mixed instances policy, allowing you to scale proportionally across instance types.

aws_auto_scaling_auto_scaling_group.noti.text: The list of Auto Scaling event types (e.g., autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE) that trigger the notification to be sent.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SNS topic that receives Auto Scaling notifications for the group's scaling events, such as instance launch and terminate activities.

aws_auto_scaling_auto_scaling_group.skip.text: When set to `true`, this flag skips the Auto Scaling group's validation that checks whether its Availability Zone configuration is eligible for zonal shift, allowing the group to be created or updated even if it doesn't meet the zonal shift prerequisites.

aws_auto_scaling_auto_scaling_group.tags.text: The key (name) of a tag to associate with the Auto Scaling group, which can be automatically propagated to instances launched by the group.
Indicates whether to propagate the tag to instances launched by the Auto Scaling group.
The value portion of a tag attached to the Auto Scaling group, used to categorize or identify the resource.

aws_auto_scaling_auto_scaling_group.traf.text: The identifier of the traffic source to attach to the Auto Scaling group, which is the load balancer name for Classic Load Balancers and the ARN for Application, Network, or Gateway Load Balancers and VPC Lattice target groups.

The type of the traffic source identifier, indicating the kind of load balancer or target group (e.g., 'elb' for Classic Load Balancer, 'elbv2' for Application/Network Load Balancer, or 'vpc-lattice' for VPC Lattice) that the Auto Scaling group is attached to; it must be used together with the corresponding Identifier to fully specify the traffic source.

aws_auto_scaling_plans_scaling_plan.appl.text: Defines the application source for the scaling plan, including either CloudFormation stack names or tag filters that identify the resources to scale.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudFormation stack whose resources define the application for the scaling plan, used when the application source is a CloudFormation stack.
Specifies tag-based filters that identify the AWS resources (such as EC2 instances) to include in the scaling plan from the source application.
The tag key used in a tag filter to identify resources that belong to the application source for the scaling plan.
The tag values to match for the associated tag key; when specified, only resources whose tag value for that key equals one of these values are included in the application source.

aws_auto_scaling_plans_scaling_plan.id.text: The Terraform resource identifier for an Auto Scaling Plan, set to the scale plan's unique name used for state tracking and import.

aws_auto_scaling_plans_scaling_plan.scal.text: Specifies the scaling instructions for the resources to be managed, including the service namespace, resource ID, scalable dimension, minimum and maximum capacities, and target tracking configurations.
Defines a custom load metric (metric name, statistic, dimensions, and unit) used for predictive scaling within this scaling instruction, tracking application load to forecast capacity.
Specifies the CloudWatch metric dimensions (key-value pairs) that uniquely identify the custom load metric used by AWS Auto Scaling for load forecasting.

Specifies the dimension name (key) used to define a metric dimension (such as LoadBalancerName or TargetGroup) for the customized load metric specification in the scaling plan's predictive scaling configuration.
The value that corresponds to the dimension key for the custom load metric, used to fully identify the metric in CloudWatch for the scaling plan's load forecasting.
The name of the CloudWatch metric used as the customized load metric for predictive scaling, specified in a scaling instruction's customized load metric specification.
The CloudWatch namespace of the custom load metric used for predictive scaling, such as 'AWS/SQS' or a custom namespace, which is required to identify the metared in CloudWatch.
The statistic of the customized load metric, such as Sum or Average, that AWS Auto Scaling uses to calculate load capacity for the scaling plan.
The unit of measure for the customized load metric (e.g., Count, Percent, Bytes) that AWS Auto Scaling uses to evaluate the metric values when predicting capacity requirements.
When true, disables dynamic scaling for the resources targeted by this scaling instruction, so that capacity will not be automatically adjusted in response to load.
The maximum capacity that the scalable resource can reach, used by the scaling plan to limit scale-out activities for the resource defined in this scaling instruction.
Defines the minimum capacity of the scalable resource, so that the scaling plan does not scale the resource below this value.

Specifies the predefined load metric configuration for predictive scaling within a scaling instruction, identifying the load metric type (such as ASGTotalCPUUtilization or ALBRequestCountPerTarget) used to calculate the forecast load.
The type of predefined load metric (e.g., ASGTotalCPUUtilization, ALBTargetGroupRequestCount) that the scaling plan uses to track resource load for predictive scaling.

This field specifies the resource identifier (such as an Application Load Balancer target group ARN) that the predefined load metric applies to, required only when the predefined_load_metric_type references a resource-specific metric like ALBTargetGroupRequestCount.

Determines how the maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group is set when predictive scaling is active, with allowed values such as SetForecastCapacityToMaxCapacity, SetMaxCapacityToForecastCapacity, and SetMaxCapacityAboveForecastCapacity.
The maximum capacity buffer, expressed as a percentage, that predictive scaling can exceed the forecasted capacity to accommodate forecast inaccuracies in each scaling instruction.
Determines whether predictive scaling only generates forecasts (ForecastOnly) or also uses those forecasts to scale capacity (ForecastAndScale).
Specifies the identifier of the resource to scale, formatted as the resource type followed by a colon and the resource's unique name (for example, autoScalingGroup:my-asg for an Auto Scaling group).
The scalable dimension that the scaling instruction applies to, such as an Auto Scaling group's desired capacity or an ECS service's desired count.

Determines whether AWS Auto Scaling keeps or replaces existing scaling policies on the target resource when the scaling plan is applied, with allowed values KeepExternalPolicies and ReplaceExternalPolicies.
Specifies the buffer time (in seconds) that AWS Auto Scaling waits before applying a scheduled scaling action, to account for latency in resource initialization.

The AWS service namespace (e.g., autoscaling, dynamodb, ecs, etc.) that identifies the service or resource type to which this scaling instruction applies, determining which scalable targets are configured.

In each scaling instruction, defines the list of target tracking configurations that specify a metric and target value, causing the scaling plan to adjust capacity when the metric deviates from the target.
Defines the custom CloudWatch metric specification used for target tracking scaling, allowing you to specify a metric name, namespace, dimensions, and statistic instead of using a predefined metric.
Defines the CloudWatch metric dimensions (as name-value pairs) that filter the customized metric used for target tracking scaling within the scaling plan's instructions.
The name of a CloudWatch metric dimension (key) used to scope the customized scaling metric for the target tracking configuration.
Specifies the value of a CloudWatch metric dimension key–value pair that identifies the metric used in the customized scaling metric specification for target tracking in the AWS Auto Scaling Plan.
The name of the CloudWatch metric that AWS Auto Scaling Plans uses to monitor the resource for target tracking scaling.
The CloudWatch metric namespace (such as AWS/EC2) that the customized scaling metric belongs to.
The statistic to apply to the custom scaling metric, with allowed values including Average, Sum, Minimum, Maximum, and SampleCount.
The unit of measure for the custom scaling metric, such as 'Percent' or 'Count', used in the target tracking configuration for the scaling plan.
When set to true, this target tracking configuration prevents scale-in actions, meaning the Auto Scaling group will only scale out based on the metric, not scale in.

Specifies the estimated time, in seconds, until a newly launched instance can contribute to the CloudWatch metrics used for target tracking scaling, preventing premature scaling actions based on instances that are still warming up.

Defines the predefined CloudWatch metric (such as DynamoDBReadCapacityUtilization or DynamoDBWriteCapacityUtilization) that the target tracking scaling policy uses to track utilization, including an optional resource label to identify the specific resource dimension.
The type of predefined metric that the target tracking scaling policy uses, such as ASGAverageCPUUtilization or DynamoDBReadCapacityUtilization.

The resource label identifies the specific AWS resource (such as a DynamoDB table name or Aurora DB cluster name) whose predefined metric is used for target tracking scaling, and it is required for predefined metric types that are not EC2 or Application Auto Scaling metrics.
The amount of time, in seconds, after a scale-in activity completes before another scale-in activity can start.
The amount of time, in seconds, after a scale-out activity completes before another scale-out activity can start for the target tracking configuration.
The target value for the metric that the scaling policy will maintain, such as a CPU utilization percentage or a request count per target, used to trigger scaling actions.
The name of the scaling plan, which uniquely identifies it within the AWS account and is used to reference the plan in AWS Auto Scaling APIs and other resources.
The version number of the scaling plan, which must be provided on updates to ensure you are modifying the latest version of the plan.

aws_auto_scaling_scaling_policy.policy_n.text: The name of the scaling policy, automatically assigned by Auto Scaling and returned as a read-only attribute.

aws_auto_scaling_scaling_policy.predicti.text: Defines the predictive scaling policy configuration for the Auto Scaling group, which uses machine learning to forecast future load and provision capacity in advance to minimize scaling latency.
Determines how the predictive scaling policy handles forecasted capacity that exceeds the maximum, either honoring the maximum capacity (HonorMaxCapacity) or increasing it (IncreaseMaxCapacity).
The percentage of capacity that the predictive scaling policy can use to scale out beyond the maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group.

Specifies the list of metric specifications, including load/scaling metrics and target utilization values, that Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling uses for predictive scaling forecasts and scheduled scaling actions.

This object defines a customized capacity metric for predictive scaling by specifying metric data queries that Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling uses to measure the group's actual capacity, which is one of the metrics used to calculate the predictive scaling model.
Specifies the metric data queries (CloudWatch metrics and expressions) that define the customized capacity metric for the predictive scaling policy.

A math expression that derives the capacity metric value from one or more metric data queries in the same customized capacity metric specification, using CloudWatch metrics math syntax (e.g., a sum, average, or arithmetic combination of returned metrics).

A short name that uniquely identifies this metric data query within the customized capacity metric specification, and can be referenced by other queries' 'Expression' fields to combine data from multiple metrics.
The label provides a human-readable name for the metric data query, used to identify and reference the query's results within the predictive scaling customized capacity metric specification.

This object specifies the metric statistics (such as the CloudWatch metric, statistic, period, and unit) for a single metric data query used to define a custom capacity metric for the predictive scaling policy.
Specifies the CloudWatch metric (namespace, metric name, and dimensions) used in the metric statistic for the customized capacity metric data query of the predictive scaling policy.

Specifies the CloudWatch metric dimensions (name/value pairs) that identify the custom capacity metric used in the predictive scaling policy's metric data query, scoping the metric data to the specified dimension values.
The name of a dimension for the metric used in the customized capacity metric specification of a predictive scaling policy.

The value of a CloudWatch metric dimension that, together with the dimension name, identifies a specific resource (such as an Auto Scaling group or instance) for the customized capacity metric used in predictive scaling.
The name of the CloudWatch metric used in the metric data query for the customized capacity metric specification of the predictive scaling policy.
The namespace of the CloudWatch metric that defines the customized capacity metric for the predictive scaling policy.

The statistic to apply to the specified metric (such as Sum, Average, Minimum, Maximum, or SampleCount) within a metric data query for the customized capacity metric specification of a predictive scaling policy.
Specifies the unit of measure for the metric used in the customized capacity metric specification (e.g., 'Percent', 'Count', 'Bytes'), which CloudWatch uses for the predictive scaling model.

Indicates whether this metric data query returns the actual capacity value for the customized capacity metric in predictive scaling; only the query that provides the capacity should set this to true, while supporting queries (e.g., used in math expressions) set it to false.
Defines the customized load metric specification for a predictive scaling policy, including the metric data queries that supply the load metric used to forecast future capacity requirements.
A list of CloudWatch metric data queries that define the customized load metric used for predictive scaling, specifying one or more metrics or mathematical expressions to represent application load.

Specifies the math expression that is evaluated to derive the custom load metric value for predictive scaling, using CloudWatch metrics and functions such as SUM, AVG, or IF to combine the metric data returned by the query's metric stat.
The short name that identifies this metric data query, used to reference it within the metric expression of a customized load metric specification for an Auto Scaling predictive scaling policy.
A human-readable name for the metric data query, used to identify the returned time series in the customized load metric specification.
Defines the specific CloudWatch metric and statistic (such as Sum or Average) that the metric data query uses to compute the custom load for predictive scaling.

Defines the source CloudWatch metric (metric name, namespace, and dimensions) that is used as the basis for the metric statistic in the customized load metric specification of a predictive scaling policy.
The dimensions (name/value pairs) of the CloudWatch metric used as the customized load metric for predictive scaling, which uniquely identify the metric within its namespace.
The name (key) of a CloudWatch metric dimension that identifies the customized load metric used for predictive scaling.
The value of a dimension key-value pair that identifies a specific metric in the custom load metric specification for predictive scaling, used to match the metric's dimensions in CloudWatch.
The name of the CloudWatch metric used as the custom load metric for the predictive scaling policy.
Specifies the namespace of the CloudWatch metric used as the custom load metric for predictive scaling, identifying the service or custom application that the metric belongs to.
The statistic to use for the specified metric (for example, Sum or Average) when calculating the customized load metric for the predictive scaling policy.
The unit of measure for the CloudWatch metric used in a customized load metric specification for predictive scaling, such as Count, Bytes, or Percent.

Indicates whether the metric data for this query is included in the customized load metric specification used by the predictive scaling policy, enabling or suppressing its use in the metric evaluation.
Defines the customized scaling metric specification for a predictive scaling policy, using metric data queries to specify the load metric.

A list of metric data queries that define the custom metrics used for predictive scaling, allowing you to specify CloudWatch metrics or math expressions for the customized scaling metric specification.
Expression defines the mathematical expression to apply to the metric data query, referencing the Ids of other queries in the same customized scaling metric specification for predictive scaling.

A unique short label that identifies this metric data query within the predictive scaling customized metric specification, and that can be referenced in the metric expression to combine or transform the data.

A human-readable label for the metric data query that provides context for the metric in the predictive scaling policy's customized scaling metric specification, typically displayed in the console for identification.
Specifies the CloudWatch metric and statistic (such as Average, Sum, Minimum, Maximum) used to evaluate a metric data query in a customized predictive scaling metric specification.
Specifies the CloudWatch metric (namespace, metric name, and dimensions) that serves as the source for the metric statistic in a customized predictive scaling metric data query.
Specifies the list of CloudWatch metric dimensions (key-value pairs) that uniquely identify the metric used in the metric stat of a customized scaling metric specification for predictive scaling.

The name of a CloudWatch metric dimension (e.g., AutoScalingGroupName or InstanceId) that, together with the dimension value, uniquely identifies the metric used in the customized scaling metric specification for predictive scaling.
The value of a dimension that, together with the dimension name, identifies a CloudWatch metric for a customized predictive scaling metric specification.
The name of the CloudWatch metric that this metric data query references for the customized predictive scaling metric specification.
The namespace of the CloudWatch metric used in the customized predictive scaling metric specification, identifying the service or application that emits the metric.
Specifies the CloudWatch statistic (e.g., Sum, Average, Minimum, Maximum, SampleCount) to use for the custom metric in the predictive scaling metric specification.
The unit of measure for the metric statistic, such as Count, Percent, or Bytes, used in the customized scaling metric specification for the predictive scaling policy.
Indicates whether this metric data query's result is included when the customized scaling metric is calculated, typically true for the primary metric and false for intermediate helper queries.
Specifies the predefined load metric for predictive scaling, including the metric type and an optional resource label to identify the specific load balancer or resource being used.

Specifies the predefined load metric type (for example, ASGTotalCPUUtilization, ASGTotalNetworkIn, or ASGTotalNetworkOut) that the predictive scaling policy uses to measure the load on the Auto Scaling group.

The resource label uniquely identifies the specific resource, such as an Application Load Balancer target group, that the predefined load metric is associated with, required for metrics like 'ALBRequestCountPerTarget'.

Defines a predefined metric pair specification, which uses the ASGCPUUtilization metric type to pair CPU utilization and memory utilization metrics for the predictive scaling policy's metric specification.
Specifies the name of a predefined metric pair (for example, ASGCPUUtilization, ASGNetworkIn, or ASGNetworkOut) that the predictive scaling policy uses to determine the load and scaling metrics.

A label (typically the ARN) identifying the Application Load Balancer target group from which the predefined metric pair, such as ALBRequestCountPerTarget, derives its request count data for predictive scaling.

This object defines a predefined scaling metric specification for predictive scaling, selecting the metric type (e.g., ASGAverageCPUUtilization) and optionally a resource label for the target resource.
The predefined metric type (such as ASGAverageCPUUtilization, ASGAverageNetworkIn, or ALBRequestCountPerTarget) that specifies which scaling metric the predictive scaling policy uses for forecasting.

The resource label that uniquely identifies the specific AWS resource (such as an Application Load Balancer target group) to which the predefined scaling metric applies, required when the metric is `ALBRequestCountPerTarget`.
The target value for the predictive scaling metric, which the model uses to determine the capacity to add for predicted load.
Specifies whether predictive scaling will actually scale capacity based on forecasts ('ForecastAndScale') or only generate forecasts without taking action ('ForecastOnly').
The amount of time, in seconds, that the predictive scaling policy can use to execute scaling actions in advance of the forecasted load, with a default of 300 seconds.

aws_auto_scaling_scaling_policy.step_adj.text: Defines the lower bound for the difference between the alarm threshold and the CloudWatch metric, determining the metric interval that triggers this step's scaling adjustment.
Specifies the upper boundary of the CloudWatch metric value range for a step adjustment, determining the maximum metric threshold at which the corresponding scaling adjustment is triggered.
The number of instances to add (positive value) or remove (negative value) when the alarm breach falls within the bounds of this step adjustment.

aws_auto_scaling_scaling_policy.target_t.text: Specifies the target tracking configuration for the scaling policy, defining the metric to track and the target value that the Auto Scaling group maintains.

Defines the customized CloudWatch metric specification (namespace, metric name, dimensions, and statistic) that the target tracking policy uses to compute the scaling metric rather than using a predefined metric.
Specifies the CloudWatch metric dimensions (key-value pairs) used to identify the customized metric for the target tracking scaling policy.
The name of the dimension key for the customized CloudWatch metric used in the target tracking policy, such as 'InstanceId' or 'AutoScalingGroupName'.
Specifies the value of a dimension for the custom metric that the target tracking scaling policy monitors.
The name of the CloudWatch metric to be used for target tracking scaling.
