Specifies a list of metric data queries that define the custom metric (including metric math expressions) used for target tracking scaling.

The CloudWatch metrics math expression that AWS Auto Scaling evaluates to derive the target metric value for the target tracking policy; it can combine multiple metric data queries referenced by their Id.
A short name that uniquely identifies this metric data query within the list, allowing other queries to reference its returned data in their expressions.
The label is a human-readable name for a metric data query in the customized metric specification, used for display in CloudWatch when the target tracking policy is active.
Specifies the CloudWatch metric and its statistic (such as Average or Sum) used by this metric data query in the customized target tracking scaling policy.
Specifies the CloudWatch metric (including metric name, namespace, and dimensions) whose value is used in the metric stat for this customized target tracking scaling policy.
Specifies the dimensions of the custom metric used with the target tracking scaling policy, where each dimension is a name-value pair that identifies a particular metric.
The name of the CloudWatch metric dimension, which combines with the dimension value to uniquely identify a specific metric for the target tracking policy.
The specific value for the CloudWatch metric dimension (e.g., an instance ID or instance type) that, combined with the dimension name, identifies the metric used for the target tracking policy.
The name of the CloudWatch metric to use for the custom metric specification in the target tracking scaling policy.

The namespace of the custom metric referenced in the metric stat, used to identify the metric (e.g., 'AWS/EC2' or a custom namespace) that the target tracking scaling policy will use for scaling decisions.
The period (in seconds) over which the specified statistic is applied to the customized metric in the target tracking scaling policy, defining the metric's data granularity for CloudWatch.
The statistic (e.g., Average, Sum, Minimum, Maximum, SampleCount, or a percentile such as p99) to apply to the custom metric for the target tracking scaling policy.
Specifies the unit of measure for the metric's value (such as Percent, Count, or Bytes) that Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling uses when evaluating the target tracking policy.

Specifies the period (in seconds) over which CloudWatch aggregates the metric data for the corresponding metric query in the custom metric specification used by this Auto Scaling target tracking policy.
Indicates whether this metric data query's result should be included in the target tracking metric evaluation; set to false for intermediate query results used only in expressions.
Specifies the CloudWatch namespace of the customized metric used by the target tracking scaling policy, identifying the source or service that published the metric.
The statistic to apply to the custom CloudWatch metric in the target tracking policy (e.g., Average, Sum, Minimum, Maximum, SampleCount).
The unit of measure for the custom CloudWatch metric specified in the target tracking configuration, such as 'Count' or 'Percent', which is used by the scaling policy to interpret the metric's value.
When set to true, the target tracking scaling policy does not scale in (terminate) instances in response to the target metric, restricting actions to scale-out only.

Specifies the predefined Auto Scaling metric type (such as ASGAverageCPUUtilization or ALBRequestCountPerTarget) that the target tracking policy will track, and optionally a resource label for metrics that apply to a specific resource.

Specifies the name of the predefined Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling metric (e.g., ASGAverageCPUUtilization, ASGAverageNetworkIn, ASGAverageNetworkOut, or ALBRequestCountPerTarget) that the target tracking policy will use to scale the Auto Scaling group.

For the ALBRequestCountPerTarget predefined metric, this label identifies the Application Load Balancer target group (e.g., app/my-alb/1234567890abcdef/targetgroup/my-tg/1234567890abcdef) that the scaling policy tracks request count per target for.
The target value for the CloudWatch metric that the scaling policy tracks; Auto Scaling adjusts capacity to keep the metric at or near this value.

aws_auto_scaling_warm_pool.auto_scaling_.text: The name of the Auto Scaling group for which the warm pool is configured.

aws_auto_scaling_warm_pool.instance_reus.text: Configures the instance reuse policy for the warm pool, which controls whether instances removed during scale-in are reused when the Auto Scaling group scales out.
When true, instances that are scaled in from the Auto Scaling group are returned to the warm pool for reuse instead of being terminated.

aws_auto_scaling_warm_pool.max_group_pre.text: Specifies the maximum number of instances that can be in the warm pool and the Auto Scaling group together, defaulting to the group's maximum capacity if not provided.

aws_auto_scaling_warm_pool.min_size.text: Specifies the minimum number of instances to maintain in the warm pool.

aws_auto_scaling_warm_pool.pool_state.text: Specifies whether instances in the warm pool are stopped (Stopped, so they do not incur instance charges) or running (Running, so they incur instance charges).

aws_b2_bi_capability.capability_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the B2Bi capability, automatically assigned by AWS when the capability is created.

aws_b2_bi_capability.capability_id.text: The unique identifier that AWS assigns to this B2BI capability when it is created.

aws_b2_bi_capability.configuration.text: The configuration object contains the EDI transformation settings for the B2Bi capability, specifying the EDI type, input/output document locations, and the transformer that processes interchange data.

aws_b2_bi_capability.configuration.edi.text: The configuration.edi field holds the EdiConfiguration for the B2Bi capability, specifying the EDI standard (such as X12), the input and output Amazon S3 locations for EDI documents, and the transform options applied.

aws_b2_bi_capability.configuration.edi.c.text: Specifies whether this EDI capability handles inbound or outbound EDI documents, using the value 'INBOUND' or 'OUTBOUND'.

aws_b2_bi_capability.configuration.edi.i.text: The S3 location (bucket and key) where inbound EDI documents are stored for processing by this AWS B2Bi capability's EDI configuration.
The name of the S3 bucket where input EDI files are stored for this capability's EDI configuration, serving as the input location for document exchange.
The Amazon S3 object key (file name) within the input bucket where the source EDI document is located for the B2Bi capability's EDI configuration.

aws_b2_bi_capability.configuration.edi.o.text: For the EDI configuration of a capability, this object specifies the Amazon S3 location (bucket and key) where AWS B2Bi stores the output files after performing the EDI transformation.
The name of the S3 bucket where processed EDI output documents are stored, as specified in the output location of the EDI configuration for this B2B capability.
The S3 object key prefix under the output bucket where the transformed EDI documents are stored for this capability.

aws_b2_bi_capability.configuration.edi.t.text: The transformer_id specifies the AWS B2Bi transformer used to process EDI documents for this capability, defining how incoming or outgoing EDI files are mapped and converted according to the transformer's configured settings.
Specifies the EDI standard type (e.g., X12) and its associated details, such as transaction set and version, for the EDI configuration of this AWS B2BI capability.
Specifies the X12-specific settings, such as the transaction set identifier and version, for the EDI capability when the EDI type is X12.
Specifies the X12 transaction set (such as X12_850 or X12_810) for which the EDI capability is configured, determining the exact business document standard handled by this capability.
The X12 version for the EDI capability (e.g., VERSION_4010, VERSION_5010), determining the transaction set standard used for EDI document parsing and validation.

aws_b2_bi_capability.created_at.text: The timestamp indicating when the capability was created in AWS B2B Data Interchange.

aws_b2_bi_capability.instructions_docume.text: Lists the Amazon S3 locations of instruction documents that provide supplemental guidance for this capability in AWS B2B Data Interchange.
The S3 bucket name where the instructions document for this B2BI capability is stored.
The S3 object key of an instructions document located in the bucket specified by the parent instructions_documents block, used to provide supplemental EDI processing instructions for the capability.

aws_b2_bi_capability.modified_at.text: The timestamp indicating when the B2B capability was last modified.

aws_b2_bi_capability.name.text: A user-specified name for the AWS B2BI capability, which is required when creating the resource and serves as a human-readable identifier for the capability in the AWS B2BI service.

aws_b2_bi_capability.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag to associate with the AWS B2B Data Interchange capability.

aws_b2_bi_capability.type.text: The type of the B2BI capability, which determines the document exchange protocol, with 'edi' currently the only supported value.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.capabilities.text: The list of EDI capability identifiers (e.g., X12 850 or X12 810) that this partnership supports, determining the business document formats and transformations that can be exchanged with the trading partner.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.capability_options.text: Specifies the EDI capability options for the partnership, including the outbound EDI envelope configuration (X12 functional group and transaction set headers) applied to generated EDI documents.
For an AWS B2Bi partnership, this object configures how inbound EDI documents are processed, specifying the EDI type identifier (such as X12_4010) and whether to apply default X12 settings.
Defines the X12 EDI handling parameters for inbound EDI messages arriving through this partnership, setting how X12 documents are parsed and validated.
Configures whether an acknowledgment (such as an X12 997) is required for inbound X12 EDI documents received under this partnership.
Specifies whether a functional acknowledgment (e.g., a 997) is supported or required for inbound X12 EDI transactions, where the value must be either SUPPORTED or REQUIRED.
Determines when AWS B2Bi sends a technical acknowledgment (TA1) for inbound X12 EDI, based on the accepted or rejected status of the interchange.
Specifies the EDI type (e.g., X12) and version (e.g., 4010) to apply to outbound EDI documents exchanged through this partnership.
This object specifies the X12 EDI version and transaction set used for outbound EDI documents in this partnership's outbound capability.
This object defines the common X12 envelope settings for outbound EDI, including the interchange (ISA/IEA) and functional group (GS/GE) header and trailer segment values used by the partnership.
Defines the starting interchange, group, and transaction set control numbers used to generate unique numbers for outbound X12 EDI documents in the partnership.
The starting value for the functional group control number sequence used in outbound X12 EDI interchange segments, ensuring each functional group is uniquely numbered.
Specifies the starting interchange control number (ISA13) used for outbound X12 EDI interchanges, allowing the partnership to begin numbering from a specific value.
Sets the initial value for the transaction set control number (ST02) in outbound X12 EDI envelopes, which AWS B2BI increments for each subsequent transaction set in the interchange.

Specifies the delimiter characters (e.g., data element separator, component separator, segment terminator, repetition separator) used when constructing outbound X12 EDI documents for this partnership.

Specifies the single character used to separate components within composite data elements in outgoing X12 EDI interchange envelopes for this partnership, such as '>' or ':', controlling how the segment structure is parsed.
Specifies the character (such as '*') that separates individual data elements within each segment of an outbound X12 EDI document for this partnership.
Sets the character that marks the end of each X12 segment in outbound EDI transmissions for this partnership, such as '~' or a newline.

Configures the functional group header (GS) segment for outbound X12 EDI, defining how its control fields (e.g., functional ID code, sender/receiver codes, group control number) are set or mapped from source data.
Specifies the application receiver code (GS03) to include in the functional group header of outbound X12 EDI documents.
Specifies the application sender code (GS02) that appears in the functional group header (GS segment) of outbound X12 EDI documents, identifying the sender of the group.
Defines the responsible agency code for the functional group header (GS02) in outbound X12 EDI, identifying the standards agency (e.g., X for ASC X12) that assigned the transaction set codes.
Specifies whether the GS05 time in the X12 functional group header is formatted as HHMM or HHMMSS, controlling the precision of the timestamp for outbound EDI.
Configures the interchange control header (ISA segment) for outbound X12 EDI documents, including sender and receiver identifiers, qualifiers, and control numbers used at the envelope level.

For outbound X12 EDI, this sets the interchange acknowledgment request code (ISA14) in the interchange control header, indicating whether a TA1 interchange acknowledgment is requested from the trading partner.
The receiver identifier (ISA-08) in the X12 interchange control header for outbound EDI, specifying the trading partner that receives the interchange.
Specifies the qualifier code that identifies the type of value used in the receiver ID (e.g., DUNS, EAN, etc.) for the X12 interchange control header of outbound EDI documents in the partnership.
The single character used as the repetition separator in the X12 interchange control header (ISA segment) for outbound EDI, separating repeated data element occurrences.
The sender_id specifies the sender's identification code (ISA06) in the interchange control header for outbound X12 EDI documents in the B2B partnership.

Specifies the qualifier for the sender ID in the interchange control header (ISA) of outbound X12 EDI documents, indicating the type of identifier used for the sender (e.g., DUNS number, SCAC code, or mutually defined).
Indicates whether the interchange contains test, production, or information data, corresponding to the ISA15 usage indicator in the X12 interchange control header.
Whether to validate outbound X12 EDI documents against the X12 standard and the partnership's configured validation rules before transmission.
Specifies the envelope wrapping configuration for outbound X12 EDI interchanges, including whether to include the ISA/IEA segments around the payload.
Specifies the maximum number of characters per line used when wrapping X12 EDI output in the outbound partnership capability.
Specifies the line terminator character (such as '\n') used to separate lines in the wrapped X12 EDI payload for outbound transmissions.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.created_at.text: The timestamp indicating when the partnership was created, returned in ISO 8601 format by the AWS B2BI service.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.email.text: The email address associated with this partnership, which AWS B2B Data Interchange uses for sending notifications and coordinating EDI transactions.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.modified_at.text: The date-time timestamp indicating when the partnership was last updated.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.name.text: Specifies the name of the partnership, used as a human-readable identifier for the B2B trading relationship within the AWS B2B Data Interchange service.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.partnership_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the B2B Data Interchange partnership, assigned by AWS when the partnership is created.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.partnership_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this B2B data interchange partnership.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.phone.text: The phone number for the primary contact associated with the B2Bi partnership, used as part of the partnership's contact information.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.profile_id.text: Specifies the unique identifier of the profile that this partnership is associated with, which links the partnership to a specific B2B integration profile in AWS B2BI.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.tags.text: A list of key-value tags to associate with the partnership, which can be used for organizing, searching, and managing access to the partnership resource.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the AWS B2B Data Interchange partnership, used to label and categorize the resource for management and cost tracking.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS B2BI partnership resource, used for organizing and identifying the partnership.

aws_b2_bi_partnership.trading_partner_id.text: The AWS-generated unique identifier of the trading partner associated with this B2Bi partnership, returned after the partnership is created.

aws_b2_bi_profile.business_name.text: The name of the business organization that this B2BI profile represents, used to identify the company in B2B EDI interchanges.

aws_b2_bi_profile.created_at.text: The timestamp indicating when the B2B Data Interchange profile was created, returned as a read-only string.

aws_b2_bi_profile.email.text: The email address associated with the AWS B2Bi profile, used for service notifications and communications.

aws_b2_bi_profile.log_group_name.text: The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group that AWS B2B Data Interchange automatically creates for the profile's activity and error logs.

aws_b2_bi_profile.logging.text: Determines whether CloudWatch logging is enabled for the profile, with valid values ENABLED or DISABLED, governing the capture of API activity and transaction events.

aws_b2_bi_profile.modified_at.text: The timestamp indicating when the B2B Data Interchange profile was last modified.

aws_b2_bi_profile.name.text: Sets a human-readable name for the AWS B2Bi profile, used to identify it in the AWS console and API operations.

aws_b2_bi_profile.phone.text: The phone number associated with the AWS B2Bi profile, a required contact detail used for the profile's business contact information.

aws_b2_bi_profile.profile_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the B2BI profile, assigned by AWS and used for cross-service references and IAM policies.

aws_b2_bi_profile.profile_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the B2Bi profile, generated upon creation and used to reference the profile in subsequent API operations and CloudFormation resources.

aws_b2_bi_profile.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the AWS B2B Data Interchange profile, used for cost allocation, organizing resources, and access control.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.created_at.text: The date and time when the transformer was created.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.edi_type.text: Defines the EDI interchange format and version (X12 or EDIFACT) that the transformer uses for parsing or generating EDI documents.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.edi_type.x12_detai.text: Specifies the X12 EDI transaction set and version (e.g., 850, 00401) that the transformer is configured to parse or convert for this EDI type.
Specifies the X12 transaction set identifier (e.g., X12_850) that this transformer is configured to process, defining the specific EDI document type for B2B data interchange.
The X12 version of the EDI standard (for example, V5010) that the transformer uses for parsing or generating X12 transactions.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.file_format.text: Specifies the output file format (either JSON or XML) that the transformer generates when converting EDI documents.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.input_conversion.text: Specifies how the source (input) data is interpreted, including the data format (e.g., CSV or X12) and any format-specific options, prior to applying the transformer's mapping.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.input_conversion.a.text: This nested object holds X12-specific advanced settings for the transformation's input conversion, enabling fine-grained control over how incoming X12 EDI messages are parsed and interpreted.
Defines how the transformer splits an incoming X12 envelope into separate processing units, such as by transaction set, during input conversion.
Specifies whether the inbound X12 document is split into separate transactions by transaction set or by functional group.
Adds the specified X12 codes to the allowed code list that this validation rule enforces during input conversion, permitting those codes to pass code-list validation.
Specifies a list of X12 codes to exclude from the allowed code list during validation, causing those codes to be treated as invalid and trigger a validation error when present in the EDI document.
Specifies the X12 data element identifier (such as a segment's data element number) to which this code list validation rule applies in the transformer's input conversion X12 validation settings.

This X12 validation rule checks whether incoming EDI data element values conform to the maximum length defined for their element type, and when enabled, causes the transformer to flag or fail validation for non-conforming values during input conversion.
The X12 data element identifier (e.g., the element's numeric position or reference code within the X12 transaction set) for which the element length validation rule is defined.
Defines the maximum number of characters allowed for an X12 data element in the transaction set, so that elements exceeding this length fail the element length validation rule.
Specifies the minimum allowed character length for an X12 data element when the element-length validation rule is applied.
Specifies the sequential position of the X12 data element within its segment that the element-requirement validation rule applies to.
Sets the expected element requirement level (e.g., Required, Optional, NotUsed) that the X12 validation rule enforces for the specified element.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.input_conversion.f.text: Specifies format-specific options for the input conversion, such as the X12 transaction set and version, used when converting the incoming EDI data.
Defines the X12 EDI format options that the transformer uses when parsing an incoming X12 document, including how EDI segments and elements are interpreted during input conversion.
Specifies the X12 transaction set identifier (such as 850, 810, or 997) that the input EDI document should match for the transformer to process the conversion.
The X12 version (such as VERSION_4010 or VERSION_5010) used for the incoming EDI interchange when the input format is X12.
Defines the EDI standard of the incoming document (such as X12 or EDIFACT) that the transformer will convert from.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.mapping.text: This field defines the mapping template that specifies how input EDI data is transformed into the output format (such as JSON or XML) for the AWS B2BI transformer.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.mapping.template.text: The XSLT template content that defines how the transformer converts input documents into the desired output format.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.mapping.template_l.text: Defines the template language (e.g., XSLT or JSONata) used by the mapping template to transform input EDI documents into the desired output format.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.modified_at.text: The date and time when the transformer was last modified, returned as a string timestamp.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.name.text: Specifies the name of the AWS B2Bi transformer, a required field that provides a human-readable identifier for the resource within the B2Bi service.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.output_conversion.text: Specifies the target format (e.g., JSON, XML, or TEXT) and any format-specific conversion options for the document output by the AWS B2Bi transformer when transforming between EDI and non-EDI formats.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.output_conversion..text: A map of advanced options that customize the output conversion format, allowing you to set format-specific parameters like delimiters and character sets for the transformed EDI document.
Configuration options that determine whether the X12 transformer output is split into individual transaction sets or functional groups, rather than being kept as a single interchange.
Specifies the level at which to split the X12 output, such as by transaction set or functional group, when converting the output.

This object defines the X12 EDI validation checks (such as detecting duplicate control numbers and enforcing transaction set validity) that the transformer applies when generating converted X12 output.
Specifies a list of validation rules, each with a rule name and value, that control how AWS B2Bi validates the X12 output document during transformation to enforce EDI compliance.

This object defines the configuration for a code list validation rule, which verifies that a specified X12 element's code value is contained within a defined list of allowed codes during output conversion.
Specifies additional X12 codes to add to the allowed code list for this code list validation rule, so that these codes are treated as valid during EDI validation.

The codes_to_remove field under the code list validation rule specifies a list of X12 codes to exclude from the valid code set during output conversion validation, thereby overriding the standard allowed values.
The X12 data element reference number (e.g., element ID like '305') that identifies which segment element the code list validation rule applies to for output conversion.
Controls the validation of X12 data element lengths, ensuring that element values fall within their defined minimum and maximum length ranges during output conversion.

The X12 data element identifier (such as an element number within a segment) that this element-length validation rule targets, ensuring the element's length conforms to the specified constraints during output conversion.
Specifies the maximum number of characters that an X12 data element may contain in an outbound document, used by the element length validation rule to flag violations.

Defines the minimum number of characters permitted for the value of a data element when the element_length_validation_rule is applied during X12 output conversion, used to flag values shorter than this threshold.
This object defines the element requirement validation rule for the X12 output conversion, which determines whether missing mandatory EDI segments cause the document to fail validation.
Specifies the position of the element within the X12 segment that the element requirement validation rule applies to, used to identify the exact data element being validated.
Specifies whether the X12 data element must be present (Required), may be absent (Optional), or its presence depends on other data elements (Conditional) for the element requirement validation rule.
The X12-specific format options for the transformer's output conversion, which let you control whether leading zeros and whitespace characters are preserved in the converted output.
The X12 transaction set code (e.g., '850' for a purchase order or '810' for an invoice) that identifies the type of EDI document produced by the output conversion in the AWS B2Bi transformer.
Specifies the X12 version (e.g., VERSION_4010 or VERSION_4030) to apply when converting the transformer's output to X12 format.
The target format to which the input EDI document is converted, such as JSON or XML.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.sample_documents.text: Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket and object keys that contain sample EDI documents used to generate the transformer's mapping.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.sample_documents.b.text: The name of the S3 bucket that stores the sample input document used to test this transformer.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.sample_documents.k.text: Specifies the list of Amazon S3 object keys within the sample documents bucket that the transformer uses as sample input data for defining its mapping and conversion logic.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.status.text: Specifies whether the transformer is active or inactive, determining whether it can process EDI documents.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.tags.text: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the B2BI transformer resource for managing, identifying, and controlling access to it.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.tags.key.text: Defines the key portion of a tag attached to the B2B transformer resource for cost allocation and resource organization.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS B2BI transformer resource.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.transformer_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS B2BI transformer.

aws_b2_bi_transformer.transformer_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this transformer when it was created.

aws_backup_framework.framework_controls..text: Specifies the input parameters for a control within an AWS Backup framework, such as the retention period threshold that the control evaluates.
Specifies the name of an input parameter for a control in an AWS Backup framework, such as requiredRetentionDays, which is passed to the control to customize its behavior.

Specifies the value assigned to a control input parameter, customizing the framework control's behavior by providing configuration data such as thresholds, identifiers, or other control-specific settings.

The name of the backup framework control, which identifies the specific compliance rule (for example, BACKUP_RECOVERY_POINT_MANUAL_DELETION or BACKUP_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN) that this framework control evaluates.
Specifies the resource types and tags that determine which backup resources the framework control applies to.
The list of resource IDs (such as ARNs) that the control scope explicitly includes for compliance evaluation in the AWS Backup framework.
The list of AWS resource types (e.g., 'AWS::Backup::RecoveryPoint') to which the Backup framework control's compliance scope applies, filtering which resources are evaluated by the control.
Specifies the tag key-value pairs that AWS Backup uses to scope the control, so that only resources matching these tags are included in the framework's compliance evaluation.
The tag key used to define the resource tag scope for a backup framework control, filtering which tagged resources the control applies to.
The value of a tag used in the control scope, which restricts the framework control's evaluation to backup resources that carry that tag key-value pair.

aws_backup_framework.framework_tags.key.text: The key of a tag that can be attached to an AWS Backup framework to help identify, organize, or classify the resource.

aws_backup_gateway_hypervisor.host.text: Specifies the hostname or IP address of the on-premises VMware hypervisor (such as vCenter Server or ESXi) that AWS Backup Gateway connects to for backup operations.

aws_backup_gateway_hypervisor.hypervisor.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the hypervisor created by AWS Backup Gateway.

aws_backup_gateway_hypervisor.kms_key_ar.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the hypervisor.

aws_backup_gateway_hypervisor.log_group_.text: The ARN of the Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group where the hypervisor's logs are delivered.

aws_backup_gateway_hypervisor.name.text: An optional friendly name for the hypervisor, used to identify the on-premises VMware environment within AWS Backup Gateway.

aws_backup_gateway_hypervisor.password.text: The password used to authenticate to the hypervisor management interface (for example, vCenter Server) when registering the on-premises hypervisor with AWS Backup Gateway.

aws_backup_gateway_hypervisor.tags.text: A list of key-value tags to assign to the AWS Backup Gateway hypervisor for resource management, identification, and cost allocation.

aws_backup_gateway_hypervisor.tags.key.text: The key component of a tag assigned to an AWS Backup Gateway hypervisor, used to label and categorize the resource for management and cost allocation.

aws_backup_gateway_hypervisor.username.text: The username used to authenticate with the on-premises hypervisor (for example, VMware vCenter) that AWS Backup Gateway manages.

aws_backup_legal_hold.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag to attach to the AWS Backup legal hold, used for organizing, categorizing, and controlling access to the resource through IAM tag policies.

aws_backup_logically_air_gapped_backup_v.text: The access policy is a JSON resource-based policy that controls which IAM principals can perform actions (such as creating, deleting, or restoring backups) on this logically air-gapped backup vault.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to the logically air-gapped backup vault, used to reference the vault in other AWS Backup operations.
The name of the logically air-gapped backup vault, which uniquely identifies it within an AWS account and region and must be provided when creating the vault.
Specifies the key-value tags to assign to the backup vault, enabling you to organize and manage the logically air-gapped vault in AWS Backup.
Specifies the AWS KMS key ARN used to encrypt the backups stored in this logically air-gapped backup vault, allowing you to control encryption with a customer-managed key.
Specifies the maximum retention period in days for backups that can be stored in this logically air-gapped backup vault.
The minimum number of days that backups in this logically air-gapped vault must be retained before they can be deleted, enforcing a locked retention floor.

The ARN of the IAM approval team that must authorize the deletion of this logically air-gapped backup vault, enabling multi-party approval (MPA) as a safeguard against accidental or malicious removal.
Configures an optional SNS topic and a list of backup vault event types (such as BACKUP_JOB_COMPLETED or RESTORE_JOB_FAILED) that trigger notifications for this logically air-gapped backup vault.

Specifies the list of backup vault event types (e.g., BACKUP_JOB_STARTED, BACKUP_JOB_COMPLETED, RESTORE_JOB_STARTED) that trigger an SNS notification when they occur for this logically air-gapped backup vault.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic that AWS Backup uses to send notifications for events related to this logically air-gapped backup vault.
The current lifecycle state of the logically air-gapped backup vault (e.g., CREATING, AVAILABLE, FAILED), indicating whether it is ready to store recovery points.
The type of the backup vault, which for this logically air-gapped resource is set to LOGICALLY_AIR_GAPPED_BACKUP_VAULT to indicate its immutable, WORM-compliant storage behavior.

aws_backup_plan.backup_plan.text: Provides the backup plan configuration, including the plan name and the set of backup rules that define the backup schedule, lifecycle, and vault.

aws_backup_plan.backup_plan.advanced_bac.text: Specifies backup options for specific resource types, such as enabling Windows VSS for EC2 instances, by associating a resource type with backup option key-value pairs.

Specifies the key-value pairs that configure advanced backup settings for the associated resource type, such as enabling Windows VSS for Windows workloads via a key like `WindowsVSS` set to `enabled`.
Specifies the AWS resource type (such as EC2, RDS, or DynamoDB) to which these advanced backup settings apply.

aws_backup_plan.backup_plan.backup_plan_.text: The user-defined name for the backup plan, used to identify it in AWS Backup and required when creating the plan.
Specifies the list of backup rules, each defining the backup schedule, lifecycle (transition to cold storage or expiration), and target backup vault for the AWS Backup plan.
Specifies the time window, in minutes, within which the backup job must complete; if the job exceeds this duration, AWS Backup cancels it.
Configures the copy actions, each of which copies a backup created by this rule to a separate destination Backup vault (optionally applying a different lifecycle).
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the backup vault to which the backup copy is sent when a backup rule's copy action is executed.

For each copy action in a backup plan rule, this lifecycle object specifies when the copied recovery point transitions to cold storage (MoveToColdStorageAfterDays) and when it expires and is deleted (DeleteAfterDays).
For a copy action in a backup plan rule, this specifies the number of days after the copied recovery point is created before it is permanently deleted.
For each copied recovery point, the number of days after creation when AWS Backup moves it to cold storage.

When set to true, this boolean opts the backup copy created by this copy action into transitioning to the archive storage tier for supported resources, based on the lifecycle's archive-after days setting.
Specifies whether to enable continuous backup for the rule, which provides point-in-time recovery (PITR) with a retention window of up to 35 days.
Configures backup indexing for the rule by specifying the resource types whose backups will be indexed, enabling fast search and query of backup contents.
Defines the AWS resource types to index for backup search (for example, S3), enabling item-level querying and recovery from the backup.
Defines when backups expire and optionally move to cold storage, via DeleteAfterDays and MoveToColdStorageAfterDays settings for the rule.
Specifies the number of days after creation that a recovery point is automatically deleted.
Specifies the number of days after creation that a backup recovery point is moved to cold storage, allowing cheaper storage for older backups.
When set to true, this boolean enables automatic archiving of backups to cold storage for resource types that support archiving, as part of the backup plan rule's lifecycle configuration.
Specifies the key-value tags that AWS Backup applies to recovery points created by this backup plan rule.
A human-readable name for the backup rule that uniquely identifies it within the backup plan.
Enables or disables the malware scan action on backups created under this backup plan rule.
Specifies the mode for scanning backups, with value 'ON' to enable malware scanning or 'OFF' to disable it for the associated backup rule.
Defines the schedule for the backup rule using a cron or rate expression, such as `cron(0 5 * * ? *)` or `rate(12 hours)`.
Specifies the timezone (e.g., America/New_York or Etc/UTC) in which the backup rule's schedule expression is evaluated, determining when the backup is scheduled to run.
The number of minutes before the scheduled backup start time that AWS Backup can wait before starting the backup, providing a window to accommodate resource availability or conflicts.
The name of the backup vault in which the backups created by this rule are stored.
The ARN of the logically air-gapped backup vault that this backup plan rule targets, causing backups to be stored in an immutable, ransomware-protected vault for the rule's retention period.

aws_backup_plan.backup_plan.scan_setting.text: Specifies the scanning configuration used by AWS Backup to run malware detection on supported backup resources (such as S3) when backups are created under this backup plan.

Indicates whether AWS Backup malware scanning is enabled for the backup plan, with accepted string values 'TRUE' or 'FALSE' that determine if newly created backups are scanned for potentially malicious software.
Lists the AWS resource types (e.g., 'Aurora', 'RDS') that are selected for malware scanning under the backup plan's scan settings.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Backup uses to scan backups for sensitive data, typically via Amazon Macie, when vault scanning is enabled.

aws_backup_plan.backup_plan_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the backup plan, uniquely identifying the resource across AWS, such as arn:aws:backup:region:account:backup-plan:plan-id.

aws_backup_plan.backup_plan_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS Backup when the backup plan is created.

aws_backup_plan.backup_plan_tags.text: Tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the backup plan for cost allocation, access control, and resource management in AWS Backup.

aws_backup_plan.version_id.text: The version identifier of the backup plan, which changes each time the plan is updated.

aws_backup_report_plan.report_plan_tags..text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Backup report plan, used to categorize and manage the resource.
The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the AWS Backup report plan, used for identifying and organizing the report plan.

aws_backup_restore_testing_plan.recovery.text: Defines the recovery point selection criteria for the restore testing plan, including the selection algorithm (e.g., latest or random within a window) and optional filters on resource types and backup vault names to narrow which recovery points are tested.

Specifies the algorithm used to select recovery points for restore testing, where `LATEST_WITHIN_WINDOW` picks the most recent recovery point within the selection window and `RANDOM_WITHIN_WINDOW` picks a random recovery point from that window.
Specifies the names of backup vaults whose recovery points are excluded from the restore testing plan selection, preventing those vaults' recovery points from being used in restore tests.
Specifies the names of backup vaults to include in the recovery point selection, so that only recovery points from these vaults are considered for restore testing.
Specifies the types of backup recovery points to include in the restore testing plan, such as 'CONTINUOUS' or 'SNAPSHOT', determining which recovery points are eligible for testing.
Specifies the number of days prior to the current date from which recovery points are eligible for selection in the restore testing plan, restricting tests to recently created recovery points.

aws_backup_restore_testing_plan.restore_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the restore testing plan, assigned by AWS when the plan is created.
The name of the restore testing plan, which must be unique within your AWS account and is used to identify the plan in AWS Backup.

aws_backup_restore_testing_plan.schedule.text: Defines the cron or rate expression that determines when the restore testing plan automatically initiates restore tests, such as 'cron(0 12 * * ? *)' or 'rate(1 day)'.
Specifies the IANA timezone (in Area/Location format, e.g., 'America/New_York') used to evaluate the restore testing plan's schedule expression, enabling the test schedule to run at a local time.

aws_backup_restore_testing_plan.start_wi.text: Defines the number of hours after the scheduled time that the restore testing plan is allowed to begin its restore test, providing a time buffer for the test to start within that window.

aws_backup_restore_testing_plan.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs that assign tags to the AWS Backup restore testing plan, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the plan through cost allocation and access control.

aws_backup_restore_testing_plan.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Backup restore testing plan, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the resource.

aws_backup_restore_testing_selection.iam.text: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Backup assumes to perform restore testing for the resources included in this restore testing selection.

aws_backup_restore_testing_selection.pro.text: The ARNs of the protected resources to include in the restore testing selection.
Defines the key-value conditions (StringEquals and StringNotEquals) on protected resource attributes, such as tags, to filter which resources are included in the restore testing selection.
Specifies key-value pairs for tag-based filtering, where a protected resource must have a tag whose key and value exactly match a pair in this list to be included in the restore testing selection.
Specifies the AWS resource tag key (e.g., Environment) that the string_equals condition requires to be present with a matching value on a protected resource for the restore testing selection.

The value that a protected resource's attribute or tag (identified by the corresponding key in the enclosing StringEquals key-value pair) must equal for the resource to match this restore testing selection condition.

A list of conditions where each specifies a resource attribute (such as a tag key) and a value, and the condition is satisfied when the resource's attribute value does not equal that value, thereby excluding matching protected resources from the restore testing selection.
The tag key used in a StringNotEquals condition to match protected resources whose value for that key is not equal to the specified value in the restore testing selection.

For a string_not_equals condition on a protected resource tag, this value is the tag value to compare against; a protected resource is excluded from the restore testing selection if its tag value for the specified key equals this value.
Specifies the AWS resource type (e.g., 'EBS', 'S3', or '*') that determines which protected resources are included in the restore testing selection.

aws_backup_restore_testing_selection.res.text: A map of restore metadata overrides used to customize the restore job parameters for a restore testing selection.
The name of the AWS Backup restore testing plan that this selection is associated with.
The name of the restore testing selection, which must be unique among all restore testing selections in the same restore testing plan.

aws_backup_restore_testing_selection.val.text: The number of hours in the validation window, starting from the beginning of the restore test, within which the restore test must complete successfully or it is considered failed.

aws_backup_selection.backup_plan_id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS Backup plan to which this backup selection belongs.

aws_backup_selection.backup_selection.text: Specifies the resources to be backed up, including the selection name, the IAM role AWS Backup uses to authenticate, and the resource lists or tags that define which resources are included or excluded from the backup plan.

aws_backup_selection.backup_selection.co.text: Defines condition expressions (such as StringEquals or StringLike) evaluated against resource attributes like tags to determine which resources match this backup selection.
Specifies tag key-value pairs that resources must match exactly to be included in the backup selection, where each object contains a key and a value that must equal the resource's tag value.
Specifies the tag key that must match for resources to be included in the backup selection when using a StringEquals condition.
The value that must exactly match the specified condition key (for example, a resource tag's value) for a resource to satisfy this string-equals condition and be included in the backup selection.
A list of tag-based conditions that select resources for the backup plan when the value of a specified tag key matches the given pattern, supporting wildcard characters such as * and ?.
Defines the tag key (e.g., aws:ResourceTag/Environment) or resource attribute used as the condition key in a string-like match to determine which resources are included in the backup selection.
The value that the resource tag key (specified by condition_key) must match, using wildcard matching, for the resource to be included in the backup selection.
Defines a list of key-value pairs that must not equal the resource's tag values for the resource to be included in the backup selection.
Specifies the tag or resource attribute key to compare in a StringNotEquals condition, excluding resources whose value for this key equals the specified condition value from the backup selection.
The value that the resource attribute (such as a tag) must not equal for the backup selection condition to match, used in a StringNotEquals condition within the AWS Backup selection.
Defines a list of key-value conditions that match backup resources whose value for the specified key is not similar to the given pattern, used to exclude resources from the backup selection.

The condition key (typically a tag key like `aws:ResourceTag/Environment`) that the `string_not_like` operator evaluates, so that resources with a matching value pattern are excluded from the backup selection.

For a StringNotLike condition, this is the string pattern (supporting wildcards such as * and ?) that the tag value identified by the condition key must not match, so the resource is excluded from the backup selection when it matches.

aws_backup_selection.backup_selection.ia.text: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Backup assumes to perform backup and restore operations, giving it permissions to access the resources being backed up.

aws_backup_selection.backup_selection.li.text: Specifies a list of tag conditions that determine which resources are included in the backup plan, each condition requiring a tag key, a tag value, and a match type such as STRINGEQUALS.
The tag key to match when selecting resources based on tag conditions.

Specifies how the tag condition is evaluated for a resource, and in AWS Backup this must be STRINGEQUALS, meaning the resource must have a tag whose key and value exactly match the specified condition key and value.
The tag value (or wildcard pattern) that the backup selection uses to match AWS resources by tag, paired with a tag key in the same tag condition.

aws_backup_selection.backup_selection.no.text: Specifies a list of resource ARNs to exclude from the backup selection, refining which resources are included in the backup plan.

aws_backup_selection.backup_selection.re.text: Specifies the list of resources (by ARN or resource ID) that this backup selection selects for backup, such as EC2 instances or DynamoDB tables.

aws_backup_selection.backup_selection.se.text: A user-defined name for the backup selection that identifies the set of resources assigned to an AWS Backup plan.

aws_backup_selection.id.text: The unique AWS-generated identifier assigned to the backup selection when it is created, used to reference the selection in AWS Backup and IAM policies.

aws_backup_selection.selection_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS Backup to the backup selection, used internally to reference the selection within a backup plan.

aws_backup_tiering_configuration.backup_.text: The name of the AWS Backup vault to which this tiering configuration is applied.

aws_backup_tiering_configuration.last_up.text: The timestamp of the most recent update to this AWS Backup tiering configuration.

aws_backup_tiering_configuration.resourc.text: The number of days after a backup is created that it should be moved to the cold storage tier, controlling the lifecycle transition for the selected resources.

aws_backup_tiering_configuration.tiering.text: The name that identifies this tiering configuration, which defines when backups transition to the cold storage tier within an AWS Backup plan.

aws_backup_vault.access_policy.text: Specifies a resource-based policy (in JSON) that defines which IAM principals can perform actions on the backup vault and its recovery points, such as viewing, creating, or deleting backups.

aws_backup_vault.backup_vault_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the backup vault, which uniquely identifies it within AWS.

aws_backup_vault.backup_vault_name.text: The name of the backup vault, which must be unique within the account and region.

aws_backup_vault.backup_vault_tags.text: Specifies the tags to attach to the backup vault as key-value pairs.

aws_backup_vault.encryption_key_arn.text: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt backups stored in this backup vault.

aws_backup_vault.lock_configuration.text: Specifies the configuration for AWS Backup Vault Lock, including minimum and maximum retention durations (in days) and the period (in days) during which the lock settings can still be modified, enabling an immutable backup vault.

aws_backup_vault.lock_configuration.chan.text: Specifies the number of days after the backup vault lock is applied during which the lock configuration can still be changed or removed, after which the vault lock becomes permanently immutable.

aws_backup_vault.lock_configuration.max_.text: Specifies the maximum number of days that the backup vault lock will retain recovery points before they are permanently deleted, enforcing an upper bound on retention for the vault.

aws_backup_vault.lock_configuration.min_.text: The minimum number of days that recovery points in the backup vault must be retained, enforced by the vault lock configuration.

aws_backup_vault.notifications.text: Specifies the Amazon SNS topic and the backup vault events (such as BACKUP_JOB_STARTED or BACKUP_JOB_COMPLETED) that trigger notifications for this backup vault.

aws_backup_vault.notifications.backup_va.text: Specifies the list of backup vault event types (e.g., BACKUP_JOB_STARTED, BACKUP_JOB_COMPLETED) that trigger the SNS notification to the configured topic.

aws_backup_vault.notifications.snstopic_.text: The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic to which AWS Backup publishes event notifications for this backup vault, as configured for the vault's notification events.

aws_batch_compute_environment.compute_en.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS Batch compute environment, assigned by AWS when the resource is created.

The name for the AWS Batch compute environment, which must be unique within the region and can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores; if omitted, AWS CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_batch_compute_environment.compute_re.text: The resolved configuration of EC2 compute resources (instance types, min/max vCPUs, subnets, security groups) that AWS Batch uses to run jobs in the managed compute environment.

Specifies the strategy used by AWS Batch to select which compute resources (e.g., instance types) to use for the compute environment, such as BEST_FIT, BEST_FIT_PROGRESSIVE, or SPOT_CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED.
The percentage of the On-Demand price that you are willing to pay for Spot Instances in the compute environment's Spot Fleet, influencing the maximum bid price for Spot capacity.
Sets the desired number of vCPUs for the managed EC2 compute environment, which AWS Batch automatically scales between the minimum and maximum vCPU limits based on job queue demand.
Defines EC2 configuration settings for the compute resources, including AMI overrides and image type (e.g., ECS or EKS) used for the Batch compute environment's instances.
Specifies a custom Amazon Machine Image (AMI) ID that overrides the default ECS-optimized AMI used for the EC2 instances in the AWS Batch compute environment.

This field sets the Kubernetes version for the Amazon EKS optimized AMI used in the EC2 configuration of an AWS Batch compute environment, enabling the compute instances to run a specific Kubernetes minor version.
Specifies the ECS-optimized AMI type (e.g., ECS_AL2 for Linux, ECS_AL2_NVIDIA for GPU) used for EC2 instances in the compute environment.
The name of the Amazon EC2 key pair used to enable SSH access to the EC2 instances that AWS Batch launches in the compute environment.
The AMI ID used for the EC2 instances in the compute environment; when omitted, AWS Batch automatically selects an appropriate Amazon ECS-optimized AMI.
The ARN of the IAM role that the compute environment's EC2 container instances assume to enable the ECS agent to make AWS API calls on your behalf.
The EC2 instance types that the compute environment may use for its compute resources; if not specified, AWS Batch chooses default instance types based on the allocation strategy.
Specifies an Amazon EC2 launch template that defines the instance configuration for the compute resources of the AWS Batch compute environment.
The ID of the Amazon EC2 launch template to use for the compute resources in this AWS Batch compute environment.
The name of the EC2 launch template that AWS Batch uses to launch instances for the compute environment's compute resources.

The overrides list inside the launch template configuration lets you assign different launch templates to specific EC2 instance types used in the compute environment, so those instance types use their own launch template instead of the base one.
A list of EC2 instance types that override the instance types specified in the launch template used for the AWS Batch compute environment's compute resources.
Determines whether the override user data is provided as plain text (TEXT) or as a base64-encoded string (BASE64) when overriding the EC2 launch template's user data for AWS Batch compute resources.

The version of the AWS EC2 launch template to use for the compute resources of the Batch compute environment, where you can specify a specific version number or use the special values $Latest or $Default to automatically use the latest or default edition of the launch template.
Configures the provider for managed compute instances in the AWS Batch compute environment, allowing selection between EC2 instances and EC2 Fleet and specifying their provisioning details.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Batch assumes to launch and manage the EC2 instances in a managed compute environment that uses the managed instances provider.

Specifies the capacity option (such as ON_DEMAND or SPOT) for instances launched from the provided launch template in the managed instances provider, determining whether the compute environment purchases instances on demand or as spot capacity.

Specifies the capacity reservation targeting configuration (such as the specific Capacity Reservation ID or the open/reserved preference) for EC2 instances launched by the compute environment's managed instance provider using the given launch template.
The ARN of the resource group that contains the EC2 Capacity Reservations to be used when launching instances in the managed compute environment.

Sets the capacity reservation preference for instances launched via the launch template used by this AWS Batch managed compute environment, where 'open' uses any matching open Capacity Reservation and 'none' skips capacity reservations entirely.
The ARN of the IAM instance profile that is attached to the EC2 instances launched for the AWS Batch managed compute environment.
Enables the use of FIPS (Federal Information Processing Standards) compliant endpoints on EC2 instances launched from this launch template within the AWS Batch managed compute environment.
Specifies whether to enable propagation of instance tags to the instance metadata service (IMDS) for instances launched via the launch template in this AWS Batch compute environment.
Defines the instance requirements (such as vCPU count, memory, and CPU architecture) used to select EC2 instance types for the managed instances in the AWS Batch compute environment.
Limits the pool of EC2 instance types that the compute environment can launch to only those explicitly listed in this allowed instance types list.

Determines whether detailed CloudWatch monitoring is enabled for the EC2 instances launched from this launch template, controlling the granularity of metrics collected (1-minute vs 5-minute intervals).
Specifies the security group IDs to assign to the EC2 instances in the AWS Batch managed compute environment when the launch template's network configuration is used.
Specifies the subnets in which the managed compute environment instances are launched, as part of the network configuration of the EC2 launch template referenced by the managed instances provider.

Specifies the size in GiB of the storage volume (e.g., an Amazon EBS volume) attached to the managed instances when launched using the specified launch template in the AWS Batch compute environment's managed instances provider.
When set to true, the tags of the AWS Batch compute environment are propagated to the EC2 instances launched for the managed instances provider.
Maximum number of vCPUs that the compute environment can scale out to, capping the total vCPU capacity of the managed compute resources.
The minimum number of vCPUs that the compute environment will maintain, defining the lower bound for the managed EC2 compute environment's auto-scaling group.
The name of an EC2 placement group to associate with the compute resources, which controls the physical placement strategy of the launched instances and may affect job performance.

This is a list of VPC security group IDs that AWS Batch assigns to the compute resources' EC2 instances (or Fargate tasks) in the managed compute environment, defining the firewall rules for network access.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that AWS Batch assumes to launch and manage Spot Fleet instances in the compute environment.
The VPC subnet IDs where the Batch compute resources (EC2 instances or Fargate tasks) are launched.
The compute resources type (e.g., EC2, SPOT, FARGATE, or FARGATE_SPOT) that determines the infrastructure on which this AWS Batch compute environment runs jobs.
When enabled, AWS Batch updates the compute environment's instances to the latest Amazon ECS-optimized AMI version (including the ECS container agent) when the environment is updated.

aws_batch_compute_environment.eks_config.text: Specifies the Amazon EKS cluster and optional Kubernetes namespace that the Batch compute environment uses when it is of type EKS.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon EKS cluster that this compute environment uses to run Batch jobs.
Specifies the Kubernetes namespace on the Amazon EKS cluster where the AWS Batch compute environment runs its job pods.

aws_batch_compute_environment.replace_co.text: Specifies whether the compute environment is replaced with a new one when updating this resource, allowing changes to properties that require replacement to take effect.

aws_batch_compute_environment.service_ro.text: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Batch assumes to make calls to other AWS services on your behalf when creating and managing the compute environment (required for managed compute environments).

aws_batch_compute_environment.state.text: Specifies whether the compute environment is enabled for job submission, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.

aws_batch_compute_environment.type.text: Specifies whether the compute environment is managed or unmanaged by AWS Batch, with valid values being MANAGED or UNMANAGED.

aws_batch_compute_environment.unmanagedv.text: The number of vCPUs to allocate to the unmanaged compute environment, used when the compute environment type is set to UNMANAGED.

aws_batch_compute_environment.update_pol.text: Configures the update policy for the compute environment, controlling whether in-progress jobs are terminated and the maximum time to wait for jobs to finish before an update is applied.
The maximum time in minutes that a job in the compute environment can run before AWS Batch terminates it when the compute environment's update policy is applied.
If true, AWS Batch terminates running jobs in the compute environment whenever the compute environment is updated.

aws_batch_consumable_resource.created_at.text: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when AWS Batch created the consumable resource.

aws_batch_job_definition.consumable_reso.text: Defines a consumable resource, including its name and the quantity the job requires from a shared pool, so that concurrent access to the resource can be limited across jobs in the same job queue.

The list of consumable resources that the job definition specifies, with each item identifying a resource name and the amount to be acquired from the job queue's pool of that resource before the job can run.
The name of the consumable resource that the job must acquire from a shared resource pool before it can run, used to enforce limits on concurrent consumption of that resource.
The number of units of the consumable resource named in the list item that the job requires to be allocated for its execution.

aws_batch_job_definition.container_prope.text: Defines the container configuration for the job, including the Docker image, vCPU and memory requirements, command, environment variables, and other runtime settings.
The command to pass to the container, as an array of strings, which overrides the default command specified in the container image.
Enables the Amazon ECS Exec feature for this container, allowing you to run interactive commands inside the running container of the Batch job.
Defines the environment variables to pass to the container, where each object specifies a variable name and its value.
In the AWS Batch job definition's container properties, this is the environment variable name for each entry in the environment list, which is paired with a value to set inside the container.
The value assigned to the environment variable key in the container's environment for the AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies the size in GiB of the ephemeral storage available to the container, used for temporary data during the job.
Defines the size in GiB of the ephemeral storage volume mounted for use by the container in the AWS Batch job definition.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon ECS uses to manage the container, including pulling container images from Amazon ECR and sending logs to Amazon CloudWatch.
Specifies the platform version to use for the Fargate container, such as 'LATEST' or a specific version like '1.4.0'.
Specifies the version of the AWS Fargate platform (e.g., LATEST or a specific version like 1.4.0) used to run the job's containers when the job definition uses Fargate resources.
The Docker image used to launch the container for the Batch job, specified as a string (e.g., a public image like 'amazonlinux:2' or a private Amazon ECR image URI).
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the container in the Batch job will assume to make AWS API calls.
Defines Linux-specific runtime parameters for the container in the job definition, such as shared memory size, tmpfs mounts, device mappings, and swap settings.
Specifies a list of host devices to expose to the container in the job's container properties.
Specifies the path inside the container where the host device is mounted for use by the container process.
Specifies the absolute path of the device on the host instance that is exposed to the container.
Specifies the access permissions (such as READ, WRITE, or MKNOD) granted on a host device mounted into the container for an AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies whether to run an init process inside the container that reaps zombie processes and forwards signals to the main process, analogous to Docker's --init flag.
The maximum amount of swap memory (in MiB) the container can use, which is only supported for jobs that run on Fargate resources.
Specifies the size (in MiB) of the /dev/shm volume for the container's shared memory, letting you increase the default shared memory available to the container.

Specifies the swappiness value (0–100) for the container's Linux memory-swapping behavior, where 0 disables swapping and 100 maximizes swap aggressiveness, as part of the LinuxParameters of the AWS Batch job definition's container properties.
Specifies the tmpfs mounts (container path, size in MiB, and mount options) to mount into the container's filesystem for the job's container properties.
The absolute file path inside the container at which the tmpfs volume is mounted.
Specifies the mount options (such as read-only, noexec, or size) that will be passed to the tmpfs mount when creating the temporary file system in the container.
Specifies the size (in MiB) of the tmpfs volume mounted at the container path defined by the corresponding tmpfs entry.
Specifies the logging configuration for the container, including the log driver (such as awslogs for CloudWatch Logs), driver-specific options, and any secret options for sensitive values.
The logging driver used by the container to send logs, such as 'awslogs' for CloudWatch Logs, 'fluentd', or 'splunk', controlling where container output is delivered.
A map of key-value pairs that configure the selected log driver for the container, such as setting the awslogs group or region when using the awslogs driver.

This is a list of secret objects that specify sensitive data from AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store to be passed to the container's log driver configuration for the AWS Batch job definition's container log configuration.

Specifies the name of the secret that is passed to the container's log configuration, where the corresponding secret value is retrieved from AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager via the sibling `valueFrom` field.

The ARN of the secret (for example, an AWS Secrets Manager secret) from which AWS Batch retrieves the value to pass to the log driver under the key specified by the `name` field in the same `secret_options` object.
Specifies the amount of memory (in MiB) to reserve for the container running in the AWS Batch job.
Defines the list of volumes to mount into the container, specifying the source volume name, the container path where it is mounted, and whether the mount is read-only.
The absolute path inside the container where the selected source volume is mounted, for example /mnt/data.
Indicates whether the container should use the mounted volume in read-only mode, preventing writes from the container to the volume.
The name of the volume to mount from the host, which must match a volume name defined in the container properties' volumes attribute.
Specifies whether the job's containers receive a public IP address by setting the AssignPublicIp property (ENABLED or DISABLED) in the Batch container's network configuration.
Indicates whether the job's container network interface should receive a public IP address when running in a VPC, set to 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED' (default).
Indicates whether the container runs in privileged mode, granting it access to all host devices and elevated permissions similar to Docker's --privileged flag.
When true, the container's root file system is mounted as read-only, preventing write operations to the root filesystem.
Configures authentication for pulling a private container image by specifying the Secrets Manager secret (via its credentialsParameter property) that contains the registry credentials.
Specifies the ARN or name of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that holds the credentials used to authenticate to a private container image repository.
Specifies a list of resource requirements for the job container, such as the amount of vCPUs, memory, or GPUs, where each item defines a type (e.g., VCPU, MEMORY, GPU) and its corresponding value.

The type of the resource requirement, which must be either MEMORY, VCPU, or GPU (if supported), indicating whether the paired value specifies the container's memory limit, number of vCPUs, or number of GPUs.
The quantity of the computing resource specified by the accompanying 'type' property (e.g., number of vCPUs or memory in MiB) for this container resource requirement in the AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies the operating system family and CPU architecture (e.g., LINUX, X86_64/ARM64) for the container, determining the runtime platform on which the job runs.
Specifies the CPU architecture for the container, such as X86_64 or ARM64, to select the appropriate runtime platform for the job definition's container properties.
Specifies the operating system family (e.g., LINUX or WINDOWS_SERVER_2019_CORE) for the container running on a Fargate runtime platform in an AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies the list of secrets to expose to the container, where each secret defines a name and a valueFrom that references an AWS Secrets Manager secret or an SSM Parameter Store value.
The name of the environment variable that will be injected into the container, with its value sourced from the AWS secret or SSM parameter specified in the corresponding valueFrom property.
Specifies the ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that provides the secret value to the container environment variable defined by the corresponding Name in this secrets entry.
Specifies a list of ulimits to set for containers in the job, each defining a resource limit name along with its hard and soft limits for the container process.
The hard limit value for the ulimit entry, specifying the maximum resource limit (e.g., number of open files) that the container can reach for the associated ulimit name.
The name of the ulimit, such as `cpu` or `nofile`, that identifies the resource limit to set for the container.
The soft limit for the resource specified by the ulimit name, which is the value enforced by the kernel and can be raised by a process up to the hard limit.
The user parameter specifies the user name or numeric UID to use for running the container's main process, overriding the default user specified in the container image.
Specifies the number of vCPUs to reserve for the container, which AWS Batch uses to allocate compute resources for EC2-based job definitions.
A list of volume definitions for the container, each specifying a volume name and its host path or EFS configuration to be mounted into the container, analogous to Docker bind mounts or volumes.
Configures the Amazon EFS file system to mount as a volume in the Batch container, including the file system ID, root directory, and encryption settings.
Defines the authorization configuration for the EFS volume, including the EFS access point ID and whether to enable IAM authorization for the mount.
The ID of the Amazon EFS access point to use for this volume, providing an application-specific entry point into the EFS file system.
Specifies whether to enable IAM authorization for the EFS volume, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
The ID of the Amazon EFS file system to be mounted as a volume in the container, which identifies the file system used for the EFS mount point.
Sets the directory within the Amazon EFS file system that AWS Batch mounts as the root directory for the volume inside the container.
Specifies whether to enable Amazon EFS transit encryption for data in transit between the container and the file system, with valid values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Specifies the TCP port used for encrypted (TLS) connections to the Amazon EFS file system when transit encryption is enabled, allowing you to override the default port of 2992.
Defines the host-side source path on the EC2 instance for the volume to be mounted into the container.
The host path on the Amazon ECS container instance (or EC2 host) that is mounted into the container as a volume for the AWS Batch job definition.
The name of the volume, used to reference it from the container's mountPoints.
This object configures an S3 files volume for the container, specifying the S3 bucket name, object key prefix, and mount point so the container can access files from S3 as a volume.
The ARN of the S3 access point that defines which S3 bucket and prefix is mounted as a volume in the container for this job definition's S3 files volume configuration.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 file system that is mounted as a volume in the container of the AWS Batch job definition, specified within the S3 files volume configuration.
Sets the subdirectory within the specified S3 bucket that is mounted as the root of the volume in the container, controlling which portion of the bucket is exposed to the job's container.
The port number used for TLS transit encryption when communicating with the S3 endpoint for this mounted S3 volume, typically 443 when transit encryption is enabled.

aws_batch_job_definition.ecs_properties.text: Configuration block for the ECS-specific properties of the job definition, holding a list of task properties that define the container images, commands, volumes, and other ECS scheduler settings.

aws_batch_job_definition.ecs_properties..text: Specifies a list of ECS task properties, each defining the container definitions, volumes, and other task-level settings used by AWS Batch to run a multi-container job.

Defines the list of containers that run in the ECS task for this AWS Batch job definition, where each container specifies its Docker image, command, environment variables, and resource allocation (CPU/memory) within the task.
Specifies the command to pass to the container, which overrides the default command provided in the container image.

Specifies dependencies of this container on other containers in the same task, using a list of objects that each contain a container name and a condition (such as START or COMPLETE) which determines when this container may start.
Specifies the state (e.g., START, COMPLETED, SUCCESS, or HEALTHY) that the dependency container must reach before the current container can start.

The name of the container within the same task definition that the current container depends on, as used to define container dependencies in the dependsOn list for an Amazon ECS task in an AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies a list of environment variables to pass to the container, where each object contains 'name' and 'value' keys.
The name of an environment variable to pass to the container in the ECS task.
Specifies the value for an environment variable passed to a container in the AWS Batch job definition's ECS task properties.
Indicates whether the container is essential to the task; if an essential container exits or fails, the entire task stops.
Specifies the FireLens configuration for the container's log routing, including the log router type (fluentd or fluentbit), its options, and optional S3 configuration for delivering logs.

A map of key-value options that configure the FireLens log router, such as enabling the log router's own log forwarding or setting custom configuration keys for the chosen Fluentd or Fluent Bit log driver.
Specifies the Firelens log router type for the container, which must be either 'fluentd' or 'fluentbit', in the ECS task properties of the Batch job definition.
The Docker image used to launch the container for this task in the Batch job's ECS task definition.

`linux_parameters` specifies Linux-specific container runtime options such as kernel capabilities to add or drop, whether to run an init process, shared memory size, tmpfs mount configurations, and swap memory settings for each container in the Batch ECS task definition.
Specifies the host devices to expose to the container inside the ECS task, where each device includes a host path, optional container path, and permissions.
The path inside the container where the device is mounted, making the host device accessible at that container path.
For each device specified in the container's Linux parameters, this field gives the absolute path of the device on the host that is passed through to the container.
For each device in the linuxParameters.devices list, this specifies the permitted device access modes for the container, with valid values of read, write, and mknod.
When set to true, the container runs an init process as PID 1, enabling it to reap zombie processes and forward signals to the main process.
