The maximum amount of swap memory (in MiB) that the container can use; a value of 0 disables swap, and if omitted, the container runtime's default is used.
The size (in MiB) of the /dev/shm shared memory volume for the container, used to adjust the container's shared memory allocation.

The swappiness value (0-100, default 60) controls the kernel's swapping behavior for the container in the Linux parameters of each container in the ECS task properties of the AWS Batch job definition.
Defines tmpfs mounts for the container, each specified by container path, size (in MiB), and optional mount options, used to provide volatile in-memory storage.
The absolute path inside the container where the tmpfs volume is mounted.
Specifies the mount options for the tmpfs volumes in the container, such as 'nosuid', 'nodev', 'noexec', which control permissions and behavior on the temporary file system.
The size of the tmpfs mount for the container, specified in MiB.
Specifies the logging configuration for the container, including the log driver (e.g., awslogs, splunk, json-file) and its options, as well as any secret options for the log driver.
Specifies the log driver to use for the container, such as awslogs or splunk, which determines how container logs are delivered.
The options map specifies the key-value configuration parameters passed to the container's log driver, such as awslogs-group, awslogs-region, and awslogs-stream-prefix for the awslogs driver.

Specifies the secret options that inject sensitive data, such as credentials, from AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store into the container's log driver configuration for the AWS Batch job definition.
The name of the log driver option in the container's log configuration that is populated with the secret value referenced by the `valueFrom` field.

The ARN or full Systems Manager parameter name of the secret (from AWS Secrets Manager or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store) that provides the value for the corresponding secret option (named in the sibling `name` field) used by the container's log driver configuration in the AWS Batch job definition.

Mount points for the container, specifying the volumes to mount into the container, including source volume, container path, and read-only flag, for each container defined in the ECS task properties of the Batch job definition.
The absolute path inside the container where the named volume is mounted, as defined in the mount point configuration for a task container in the AWS Batch job definition.
Whether the container has read-only access to the volume mounted at this mount point.
The name of the volume to mount, which must reference a volume defined in the job definition's `volumes` section.
Specifies the name of the container within the ECS task definition, used to identify the container and required to be unique among all containers in the task.
Specifies whether the container runs in privileged mode, granting it extended capabilities and access to host devices, analogous to Docker's --privileged flag.
When true, the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only, preventing the container from writing to any part of the root filesystem while still allowing writes to mounted volumes.

Specifies the private registry authentication credentials for the container, referenced by the ARN of a Secrets Manager secret or Systems Manager parameter that stores the credentials, used when pulling a private container image.
Specifies the ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the credentials for a private container registry, allowing the task to pull the container image.
Specifies the type and amount of a resource (e.g., GPU or memory) to reserve for the container, where each item in the list contains a Type and Value pair.
Specifies the type of resource being requested for the container (e.g., GPU, MEMORY, or VCPU) within the resource requirements list of an AWS Batch job definition's ECS container properties.
The value of the resource requirement, such as the number of GPUs or the memory limit in MiB, expressed as a string.

Specifies a list of secrets to expose to the container, where each item references an AWS Secrets Manager secret or SSM parameter via its valueFrom ARN, allowing sensitive data to be injected as environment variables or mounted as files.
The name of the environment variable that will be set in the container to hold the secret value from the referenced secret.
The ARN or full name of the secret in AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store from which the container retrieves the secret value.
The timeout in seconds allowed for the container in the ECS task to start before the job is considered failed.
Specifies the amount of time (in seconds) to wait for the container to stop before it is forcibly killed, with a minimum of 60 seconds and a maximum of 1800 seconds.

Specifies the ulimit settings for each container in the ECS task defined in the job definition, allowing you to set resource constraints such as the maximum number of open files (nofile) or processes (nproc) with corresponding soft and hard limits.
The hard limit is the maximum value for the container resource limit, beyond which the system prevents any further increase, even for privileged processes.
The name of the ulimit setting, identifying the system resource being limited for the container, such as core, cpu, data, nofile, or nproc.
The soft limit (lower bound) for the ulimit resource limit configured on the container, paired with the hard limit and ulimit name in the container's ulimits array.
Specifies the user name or numeric UID (and optionally group) used to run the container's main process inside the ECS task, such as 'user' or 'uid:gid'.
Specifies whether to enable the Amazon ECS Exec feature, which allows you to run interactive commands directly inside the containers of the task for debugging and troubleshooting.
Specifies the ephemeral storage configuration for the ECS task, allowing you to set the amount of temporary storage in GiB that will be available to the containers running in the task.
The amount of ephemeral storage, in GiB, to attach to each task's containers; valid values are between 21 and 200 GiB.

The ARN of the IAM execution role for the ECS task, which grants the container agent permissions to pull container images from Amazon ECR and access other AWS services like Secrets Manager and CloudWatch Logs for the Batch job's containers.
Sets the IPC mode for the containers in the task, controlling the inter-process communication namespace (e.g., 'host', 'task', or 'none').
Specifies the network configuration for the task, such as whether to assign a public IP and which security groups to use.
Determines whether the task's elastic network interface is assigned a public IP address when using the awsvpc network mode, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.

Specifies the network mode for the task's containers (e.g., 'awsvpc', 'host', 'bridge', or 'none'), controlling whether the task receives its own elastic network interface or shares the host's networking.
Sets the PID namespace mode for containers in the task, allowing either 'host' for sharing the host's PID namespace or 'task' for a dedicated PID namespace.

Specifies the version of the ECS platform on which the task runs, such as LATEST or a specific version like 1.4.0, which affects the runtime environment and capabilities available to the container within the AWS Batch job.
This object specifies the operating system family and CPU architecture (e.g., LINUX, X86_64) for the container, matching the ECS task definition's RuntimePlatform parameter.

Specifies the CPU architecture (such as X86_64 or ARM64) for the AWS Batch job definition's ECS task runtime platform, determining whether the container runs on an Intel/AMD or ARM-based compute environment.
Specifies the operating system family (such as LINUX) for the container runtime, which must match the underlying ECS compute environment's OS.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM task role that the ECS task in this job definition uses, allowing its containers to make AWS API calls.

Defines the list of data volumes for the task, where each volume has a name and either a host path or an empty-directory configuration, and can be mounted into containers via the container's mountPoints.
Configures an Amazon EFS file system for use as a volume in a container, specifying the file system ID, root directory, transit encryption, and optional IAM authorization settings.
Specifies the Amazon EFS authorization configuration for the volume, including the EFS access point ID and whether IAM authorization is enabled.
The ID of the Amazon EFS access point to use when mounting this volume in the task.
Specifies whether Amazon EFS uses IAM authorization for the file system access, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
The ID of the Amazon EFS file system (e.g., fs-12345678) to mount as a volume in the ECS task.
Specifies the path on the EFS file system to mount as the root directory for the task's containers.
Specifies whether to enable Amazon EFS transit encryption (TLS) for the mounted file system, with valid values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Specifies the port that Amazon EFS uses for transit encryption, which is typically 2049.
Specifies the host filesystem path on the EC2 instance that is mounted into the container for a bind-mounted volume in the AWS Batch job definition's ECS task properties.
Specifies the absolute path on the container instance (host) that is mounted into the container as a volume for the Batch job.
Specifies the name of the volume, which uniquely identifies it within the task properties and is referenced by the container definitions' mountPoints sourceVolume property.
Configures an Amazon S3 bucket as a volume to mount into the container for an AWS Batch ECS task volume, specifying details such as the S3 bucket name, path, and mount options.
The ARN of the S3 Access Point that the container uses to mount and access the S3 bucket for this volume.
Specifies the ARN of the S3 bucket that is mounted as a volume for the container's task.
The absolute path inside the container where the S3 bucket is mounted for this volume.
Specifies the network port used for encrypted transit communication with S3 (e.g., 443) when transit encryption is enabled for the S3 file volume.

aws_batch_job_definition.eks_properties.text: Specifies the Amazon EKS pod properties for this job definition, including the pod template, container specifications, volumes, and other Kubernetes-specific settings.

aws_batch_job_definition.eks_properties..text: Specifies the pod properties for an Amazon EKS-based job, including container definitions, volumes, and pod-level metadata such as service account name and labels.
The list of containers that run in the EKS pod defined by these pod properties.
Specifies the arguments to pass to the container's entrypoint, overriding the default arguments in the container image.
Specifies the command to run in the container, which overrides the default command defined in the container image (equivalent to the Docker CMD).
List of environment variables to pass to the EKS container, each specifying a name and value for the container's environment.
The name of the environment variable to set for the container in the EKS pod.
The value for the environment variable named in the corresponding `name` field within the same `env` list, applied to the container's pod on the EKS cluster when this AWS Batch job definition runs.
The container image used to launch the EKS pod's container for the AWS Batch job.
Specifies the Kubernetes image pull policy for the container, such as Always, IfNotPresent, or Never, which controls when the container image is pulled from the registry.
Specifies the name of the container within the Kubernetes pod, which must be unique within the pod and match the container name as defined in the pod spec.
Specifies the Kubernetes compute resource requirements for the container, such as CPU and memory, defining optional limits and requests as key-value pairs.
Specifies the maximum CPU and memory resources (in the form of key-value pairs like cpu and memory) that the EKS container in the Batch job definition is allowed to use.
Defines the minimum amount of compute resources (e.g., CPU and memory) requested by the EKS container, specified as a map of Kubernetes resource names to quantity strings.

This object specifies the Kubernetes security context for the container, including settings such as runAsUser, runAsGroup, privileged, and readOnlyRootFilesystem, which govern container-level permissions and security constraints within the EKS pod.
Indicates whether a container is allowed to escalate privileges, matching the Kubernetes securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation setting for the containers in the pod.
When true, the container runs in privileged mode, granting it extended capabilities and access to host devices as defined by Kubernetes security context.
When set to true, the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only, preventing writes to the root filesystem and allowing writes only to mounted volumes.
The group ID (GID) that the container's main process runs as, overriding the default group from the container image.
Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user, as defined in the Kubernetes security context for the EKS pod.
Sets the numeric user ID (UID) used to run the container's main process, overriding any image default.
Specifies the volume mounts for each container in the EKS pod, mapping pod-defined volumes to mount paths inside the container's filesystem.
Mount path inside the container where the referenced volume is mounted, as defined for each EKS pod container's volume mount in the AWS Batch job definition.
The name of the volume to mount, which must correspond to a volume defined in the pod's volumes list.
Specifies whether the volume mount is mounted as read-only inside the EKS container.
The path within the referenced volume to mount instead of the volume's root, allowing a single volume to be shared by multiple mounts at different directories.
Sets the Kubernetes DNS policy for the EKS pod in the job, controlling how DNS resolution is handled (e.g., Default, ClusterFirst, ClusterFirstWithHostNet, or None).
Indicates whether the pod should share the host's network namespace, allowing it to use the host network directly.
Specifies a list of image pull secrets (each with a name) used to authenticate with private container registries when pulling the container image for the EKS pod in the job definition.
The name of the Kubernetes secret to use as an image pull secret for the EKS pod.
Specifies the list of init containers that run before the main container in the EKS pod for the AWS Batch job definition.
The list of arguments passed to the init container's entrypoint command in the EKS pod specification for the AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies the command to execute in an init container of a Batch EKS pod, provided as a list of argument strings that overrides the container image's entrypoint.
Defines the list of environment variables passed to the init container of the Amazon EKS pod in the AWS Batch job definition.
The name of an environment variable to set in the init container of the EKS pod for this AWS Batch job definition.
The value of the environment variable for an init container in the EKS pod properties of the Batch job definition.
The container image to launch for each init container in the EKS pod of the Batch job definition.
The image pull policy for the init container, determining when Kubernetes pulls the container image (Always, IfNotPresent, or Never).
The name of the init container, which is required and must be unique within the pod.
Defines the CPU and memory resource limits and requests for the init container within the EKS pod properties of the AWS Batch job definition.
Limits the maximum amount of CPU and memory resources each init container in the EKS pod can consume, using Kubernetes-style resource names and quantities.
Specifies the minimum amount of compute resources (such as cpu and memory) that each init container in the EKS pod requires, which Kubernetes uses for scheduling and resource reservation.
Defines the security context for an init container in the EKS pod, including settings like runAsUser, runAsGroup, Linux capabilities, and read-only root filesystem behavior.

For an init container defined in the EKS pod properties of the job definition, this boolean controls whether the container's processes can gain more privileges than its parent process, corresponding to the Kubernetes `allowPrivilegeEscalation` security context setting.
Indicates whether the init container runs in privileged mode within the EKS pod, granting it access to all devices and extended security capabilities as defined by the Kubernetes security context.

Indicates whether the root filesystem of the init container is mounted as read-only, preventing any writes to the root filesystem, within the Kubernetes security context for the init container in the EKS pod properties of the AWS Batch job definition.
Sets the GID (group ID) that the init container's processes will run with, overriding the pod-level runAsGroup if specified.
Indicates whether the init container in the EKS pod must run as a non-root user, enforcing that the container's security context prevents root execution.
Sets the numeric user ID (UID) that the init container's main process runs as, overriding the user specified in the container image.
Defines volume mounts for an init container in an Amazon EKS pod, specifying the volume name and the mount path within the container.
The absolute file system path inside the init container where the referenced volume is mounted, corresponding to the Kubernetes volumeMounts mountPath for that container.
In the EKS pod specification of an AWS Batch job definition, this is the name of the Kubernetes volume to mount into the init container, which must match a volume declared in the pod's volumes list.
When true, the volume is mounted read-only inside the init container, preventing any write operations to that volume.
The subPath field specifies a subdirectory or file within the referenced volume to mount to the container's mountPath, enabling selective mounting of a portion of the volume.
Defines the Kubernetes metadata (labels and annotations) applied to the pod running the EKS job, used to identify or group the pod within the cluster.

The annotations are arbitrary key-value pairs attached to the Kubernetes pod, used to store non-identifying metadata that can be consumed by tools or AWS Batch integrations, distinct from labels which are used for pod selection.
Defines the Kubernetes labels (key-value pairs) to attach to the pod metadata for an Amazon EKS job definition.
The Kubernetes namespace in which to run the EKS pod for the job definition.
The name of the Kubernetes service account assigned to the pod, which enables IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA) to grant AWS permissions to the pod.
Enables sharing the same process namespace across all containers in the EKS pod, equivalent to the Kubernetes `shareProcessNamespace` pod setting.
Specifies the list of volumes available for mounting into containers in the EKS pod, defining sources like emptyDir or hostPath that correspond to the pod's volumeMounts.

This object configures an emptyDir volume for an EKS pod in an AWS Batch job definition, creating a temporary, initially empty directory that persists only for the pod's lifetime and can optionally set the medium (e.g., memory) and size limit via nested fields.
Specifies the storage medium for the emptyDir volume in the pod; set to 'Memory' to use a RAM-backed tmpfs volume, or omit it (empty string) to use the default ephemeral disk storage.
The maximum storage size for the emptyDir volume in the EKS pod, specified as a Kubernetes quantity string such as '128Mi'.
Defines a hostPath volume for the EKS pod, which mounts a specified directory from the node's filesystem into the container; the nested `path` property sets the host directory path.
Specifies the path on the host machine that is mounted into the pod as a hostPath volume.
The name of the volume, referenced by containers in their volumeMounts to mount this volume.
Specifies a Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) volume source for the Batch EKS pod, including the claim name and read-only flag to mount the claim into the container.
Specifies the name of the Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) in the pod's namespace that this volume references, which the AWS Batch EKS pod will mount.
When set to true, mounts the referenced PersistentVolumeClaim as read-only inside the EKS pod for this AWS Batch job definition.
Configures a Kubernetes secret volume source for the pod, specifying the secret name and optionally the keys (items) from that secret to expose as files.
Specifies whether the referenced Kubernetes secret must exist before the pod starts; when set to true, the secret is optional and its absence does not prevent the pod from starting.
The name of the Kubernetes secret to mount as a volume in the pod, referencing a secret that must exist in the same EKS cluster namespace.

aws_batch_job_definition.job_definition_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies the name of the job definition; if you omit it, AWS Batch generates a unique name for you.

aws_batch_job_definition.node_properties.text: Specifies the properties for a multi-node parallel (MNP) job, including the number of nodes, the main node index, and the container properties for each node range.
Defines the node index (starting at 0) that is designated as the main node in a multi-node parallel job definition, which runs the coordinating task.

Defines the per-node-range configuration for a multi-node parallel AWS Batch job, mapping a range of node indices to the container properties and instance types (and optional ECS configuration) used for those nodes.
Defines how much of a named consumable resource (e.g., GPU) a node range consumes in a multi-node AWS Batch job definition, specifying the resource name and quantity.

Defines the list of consumable resources (each with a name and quantity) that jobs in this node range will reserve and consume from the shared pool, enabling capacity-aware scheduling in multi-node AWS Batch jobs.
Defines the name of a consumable resource that the job's nodes can consume, used for coordinating resource allocation across multi-node jobs.

Specifies the required quantity of the named consumable resource for this node range in a multi-node parallel AWS Batch job, which the scheduler uses to limit how many jobs can concurrently consume the same shared resource.
Defines the container properties (such as image, command, environment, and resource requirements) for the node range in a multi-node parallel AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies the command to run in the container, passed as an array of strings that overrides the container image's default command for this AWS Batch job definition's node range.
When enabled, allows you to use ECS Exec to start an interactive shell or run commands inside the container of a multi-node AWS Batch job, which is helpful for debugging running jobs.
Defines the environment variables (as a list of objects with name and value keys) that are passed to the container when jobs run for this node range in a multi-node AWS Batch job definition.
The name (key) of an environment variable to pass to the container in this node range of the AWS Batch job definition.

Specifies the string value of an environment variable (paired with its `name`) that is injected into the container running on each node within the node range of an AWS Batch multi-node job definition.
Specifies the ephemeral storage configuration for the container, defining the size in GiB of temporary storage provisioned beyond the default.
The size, in GiB, of the ephemeral storage volume that is mounted to the container for scratch data in the multi-node batch job.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that AWS Batch assumes so the container can pull images and publish logs, required for Fargate-based job definitions.
Specifies the Docker image used to run the container for the job defined by this node range property.
Specifies the Amazon EC2 instance type to launch for the container that runs on this range of nodes in the multi-node AWS Batch job definition.
The ARN of the IAM role that the container in a node range of a multi-node AWS Batch job can assume to make API calls to AWS services.

Defines Linux-specific container parameters (such as shared memory size, init process enablement, swap settings, devices, and tmpfs mounts) for the Batch container in this node range of a multi-node job definition.
Specifies the list of host devices to expose to the container, including their host path, container path, and permissions.
The path inside the container where the host device is exposed when mounting a device for a Linux container in an AWS Batch job definition.
The host path of the device on the container instance, used to map a host device into the container.
Specifies the device permissions (READ, WRITE, MKNOD) that the container is granted for the corresponding host device when the job's container runs, controlling access to that device.
This field, when set to true, enables the init process inside the container, which forwards signals and reaps zombie processes for proper process lifecycle management.
Specifies the total amount of swap memory (in MiB) that the container can use, with a value of 0 disabling swap memory.
Sets the size (in MiB) of the container's shared memory (/dev/shm) volume, controlling the amount of shared memory available to the container's Linux processes.
Sets the swappiness kernel parameter (0-100) that controls how aggressively the container's kernel will swap anonymous memory pages to disk.

Defines a list of tmpfs mounts to be mounted in the container, where each item specifies a container path, mount size in MiB, and optional mount options (e.g., 'noexec', 'size=') that control the mount behavior.
Specifies the absolute file path inside the container where the tmpfs volume is mounted, such as /run or /tmp.
Specifies the list of mount options (e.g., 'noexec', 'nosuid') to apply to the tmpfs volume in the container's Linux parameters.
The size (in MiB) of the tmpfs volume mounted at the specified container path for a container in an AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies the logging configuration for the container, such as the log driver (e.g., `awslogs` to send logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs) and its options.
Specifies the log driver for the container, such as awslogs for Amazon CloudWatch Logs or fluentd, which determines how container logs are captured and delivered.
Specifies the log driver options (key-value pairs) for the container's log configuration, such as awslogs-group and awslogs-region when using the awslogs log driver.

Specifies a list of secrets from AWS Secrets Manager or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to be injected as environment variables into the container's log driver configuration, with each entry containing a `name` and a `valueFrom` reference.
The name of the secret option, which identifies the key or environment variable name that the log driver will reference, as specified in the container's log configuration secret_options.
The ARN of the secret in AWS Secrets Manager or the Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter that supplies the secret value for the log driver option identified by the corresponding name.
Sets the hard memory limit (in MiB) for the container of jobs in this node range.
Defines the mount points for volumes mounted into the container, specifying the container path, source volume, and whether the mount is read-only.
The absolute path inside the container where the volume is mounted for this mount point entry.
Specifies whether the container has read-only access to the mount point; if true, the container cannot write to the mounted volume, and if false, it can read and write.
Specifies the source volume name that must correspond to a volume configured in the container's `volumes` list, defining which storage volume is mounted at the container's mount point path.
Indicates whether the container runs in privileged mode (Docker --privileged), which grants it elevated permissions on the host, such as access to devices and kernel capabilities.
Specifies whether the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only, preventing writes to the root filesystem.
Provides the credentials required to authenticate with a private container registry, referencing the AWS Secrets Manager secret that holds the repository authentication parameters.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the private repository credentials for authenticating to the container registry.
Specifies the types and amounts of compute resources (such as vCPU, memory, and GPU) that the container in this node range requires for the job to run.
Specifies whether the resource requirement for the container in a node range applies to vCPUs (VCPU) or memory (MEMORY).
In the container definition for a node range in a multi-node Batch job, the string value giving the amount of the resource type (such as '2' for vCPUs or '2048' for MiB of memory) required.
Specifies the operating system and CPU architecture (e.g., 'LINUX' and 'X86_64') for the container, allowing the job to run on a compatible Amazon ECS or EKS compute environment.
Specifies the CPU architecture (x86_64 or arm64) for the container's runtime platform in the AWS Batch job definition's node range properties.
Specifies the operating system family (e.g., LINUX or WINDOWS_SERVER_2019_CORE) that the container in this node range property should use.

Defines a list of sensitive data (secrets) to pass to the container as environment variables, where each entry specifies a secret name and the ARN or full name of the AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store resource from which to retrieve the value.
The name of the environment variable that will be set in the container from the referenced secret.
Specifies the ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter whose value this container environment variable is populated from for jobs in the node range.
Defines the ulimit resource limits (e.g., the maximum number of open files) applied to each container in a node range, where each entry consists of a name, a hard limit, and a soft limit.
The hard limit for the resource specified in the ulimit, representing the maximum value that the process can reach under the Batch container's ulimits configuration.
Specifies which ulimit (resource limit) to apply to the container, such as 'nofile' or 'nproc', within the node range container ulimits list of the Batch job definition.
The soft limit of the ulimit setting for the container, which defines the resource ceiling the container process may use before the kernel enforces throttling or restriction.
Specifies the user name or numeric UID that the container process runs as inside the job's container, overriding the default user defined in the container image.
Defines the number of vCPUs to reserve for the container that runs on each node in this node range of the multi-node parallel AWS Batch job definition.
This is the list of Docker volumes available to the container for jobs in the node range, each specifying a host source path and volume name to be mounted via the container's mount points.

The EFS volume configuration for a container volume, specifying the Amazon EFS file system to mount, including the file system ID, root directory, transit encryption settings, and IAM authorization options.
Defines the authorization details for the Amazon EFS volume, including the EFS access point ID and whether to use IAM authorization for accessing the file system.
Sets the EFS access point ID (fsap-...) to use for the EFS volume when mounting it in the container, as part of the authorization configuration.
Specifies whether to enable IAM authorization for the Amazon EFS volume, with valid values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
The ID of the Amazon EFS file system that the container mounts as a volume.
The path on the EFS file system to mount as the root directory inside the container.
Specifies whether to enable encryption in transit for the Amazon EFS volume, with valid values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Specifies the port to use when connecting to the Amazon EFS file system using TLS for transit encryption.
Specifies the source path on the host for a volume that is mounted as a bind mount from the container instance filesystem into the container.
The absolute path on the host (EC2 instance) that the container volume is mounted from, used to give the container access to a specific directory on the underlying compute resource.
The name of the volume, used as a key to reference it in the container's mountPoints so that the container can mount the defined storage.

Defines the S3 source and mount settings (bucket, optional object keys/prefix, and container mount point) used to mount an Amazon S3 location as a filesystem volume inside the container for an AWS Batch job definition.
The ARN of the S3 access point that the container mounts as an S3 file volume, enabling access to the underlying S3 bucket through that access point.
The path inside the container where the S3 file volume is mounted, defaulting to the container's root directory ('/').
Specifies the network port to use for transit encryption when AWS Batch mounts this S3 volume in the container.
Specifies the ECS task properties (such as task definition, container overrides, and resource requirements) that apply to the nodes in this range of the multi-node AWS Batch job definition.
Defines the list of ECS task properties (each containing container definitions, volumes, and network settings) for the AWS Batch job definition's ECS properties within a node range.

For each node range in a multi-node AWS Batch job definition, this list defines the containers that run as part of the ECS task specified by the parent task properties, with each entry containing the container image, command, environment variables, and resource requirements.
Specifies the command (as an array of strings) passed to the container, overriding any default command defined in the container image; if omitted, the image's default command is used.

Specifies the container dependencies for a container in the task, where each entry identifies another container that must reach a given condition (such as START, COMPLETE, SUCCESS) before this container can start.
The condition that determines when the container can start relative to the dependency container, such as START or COMPLETE.
Specifies the name of a container in the same ECS task that this container depends on, controlling its start or run condition when multiple containers are defined in an AWS Batch job definition.
A list of environment variable objects (name and value) passed to the container when it runs, configured in the ECS task properties of a Batch job definition's node range properties.
The name of the environment variable in the key-value pair that is set for the container in the ECS task configuration.
The value part of an environment variable (key-value pair) that is injected into the container running in the ECS task for the specified node range in an AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies whether this container is essential to the task; if an essential container fails or exits, the entire Batch job task stops and all other containers are terminated.
Configures FireLens log routing for the container, specifying the log router type (fluentd or fluentbit) and its options, to enable custom log routing to destinations.

A map of key-value pairs that specifies optional configuration for the Firelens log router, such as enabling ECS log metadata (`enable-ecs-log-metadata`) or providing a custom configuration file via `config-file-type` and `config-file-value`.
Specifies the Firelens log router type to use, either 'fluentd' or 'fluentbit', for the container's log routing.
Specifies the container image (Docker image URI) that the ECS container in the Batch job task will run.
Specifies Linux-specific container settings such as kernel capabilities, device mappings, shared memory size, tmpfs mounts, and swap configuration for each container in the job.
Defines a list of host devices to expose inside the container, each specifying the host path, the container path, and optionally the access permissions.
The path inside the container where the host device is mounted, as part of a device mapping for Linux containers in an AWS Batch job's ECS task properties.
Specifies the host-side device path (e.g., `/dev/sda`) that the container's LinuxParameters exposes at the corresponding `container_path` for device access.
Permissions granted to the container for the device, such as read, write, or mknod.
When set to true, this enables the init process (PID 1) to run inside the container, ensuring proper signal handling and zombie process reaping as defined by the ECS container's LinuxParameters.
The maximum amount of swap memory (in MiB) the container can use, where 0 disables swap and a positive value must also specify swappiness.
Specifies the size in MiB of the container's shared memory (/dev/shm), overriding the default limit.
Sets the swappiness behavior for the container's kernel, a value from 0 to 100 that controls how aggressively the kernel swaps process memory to disk.
Specifies the tmpfs mounts for the container, where each entry defines the container path, the size in MiB, and optional mount options (such as ro, rw, or noexec) for the tmpfs filesystem.
Specifies the path inside the container where the tmpfs volume is mounted.
Specifies the mount options (e.g., 'ro', 'nosuid', 'size=') that control the behavior of the tmpfs volume mounted in the Linux container within the ECS task of this AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies the size of the tmpfs mount in MiB for the container's Linux parameters.
Specifies the log configuration for the container, including the log driver (e.g., awslogs, splunk) and its options, which control how container logs are sent to a logging service.
Specifies the log driver (e.g., awslogs, fluentd, json-file) that the container should use to send log information to.
Specifies the key-value pairs for the container's log driver configuration (such as awslogs-group, awslogs-region, and awslogs-stream-prefix) used by the AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies a list of secret options that define sensitive data (such as credentials) to pass to the container's log driver, referencing AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store values.
The name of the log driver option (e.g., awslogs-group or a custom key) that receives the secret value from the referenced secret ARN in the log configuration secret options.

The full ARN or name of an AWS Secrets Manager secret or Systems Manager parameter that supplies the secret value for this container log driver option in the AWS Batch job definition's ECS task properties.
Defines the container's volume mount points, specifying the source volume name, the path inside the container, and whether the mount is read-only.
The path inside the container where the volume is mounted, as specified for a mount point in the ECS task containers of a Batch job definition's node range properties.
Indicates whether the container mount point is read-only, preventing write access to the mounted volume from within the container.
The name of the volume in the ECS task definition that is mounted to the container at the specified container path.
The name of this container within the ECS task definition, used to uniquely identify it among the containers in the task and to reference it from other containers or logging configurations.

When set to true, the container runs in privileged mode, granting it access to all host devices and extended kernel capabilities beyond standard container isolation, mirroring the Docker privileged flag in ECS task definitions.
Specifies whether the container's root file system is mounted as read-only, so the container cannot write to its root filesystem.
Specifies the secret that contains the credentials for pulling a container image from a private repository, typically referencing an AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store secret.
The ARN or name of the AWS Secrets Manager secret or Systems Manager parameter that stores the private repository credentials for the container image.
Specifies the resource requirements (e.g., vCPU and memory) for each container in a task, defined as a list of objects each containing a resource type and value.
Specifies the type of additional resource the container requires, such as a GPU or an inference accelerator.
The value (as a string) specifying the amount of the resource (such as CPU units or MiB of memory) requested for the container, matched to the corresponding resource type in the same requirement.
Specifies the list of secrets to inject into the container as environment variables, referencing AWS Secrets Manager secrets or SSM Parameter Store parameters by their ARNs.

The name of the environment variable that will be set in the container to expose the secret value referenced by the corresponding valueFrom field in the ECS task properties of the AWS Batch job definition.
The full ARN of the secret in AWS Secrets Manager or the parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store from which the container's secret value is retrieved.
Specifies the maximum time, in seconds, AWS Batch will wait from the moment a container is launched until it transitions to a running state, after which the job is considered failed.
The number of seconds to wait for the container to stop before the system forces it to stop, applied when the container is stopped in the ECS task.
Defines the list of resource limits (e.g., nofile, nproc) with soft and hard values applied to each container in the ECS task for the specified node range in a multi-node Batch job definition.
The hard limit for the ulimit, specifying the maximum resource value a container process can reach for the named resource (e.g., file size or open files).
Specifies the name of the POSIX ulimit (e.g., core, cpu, memlock, nofile, nproc) to set for the container in the ECS task.
The soft limit for a container's ulimit value, which the process can dynamically raise up to the hard limit.
The user name or numeric UID to run the container's main process as, overriding the default user specified in the container image.
Enables ECS Exec (execute command) for the task's containers, allowing you to run interactive commands and debug the job's containers while they are running.
The ARN of the IAM role that the ECS task in this Batch job node range uses to make AWS API calls (e.g., pulling container images from Amazon ECR).
Specifies the IPC mode of the ECS task container(s) in the Batch job definition, which can be 'host', 'task', or 'none' to control the IPC namespace.
Specifies the PID (process ID) namespace mode for the containers in the task, either 'host' to share the host's PID namespace or 'task' to give each task a private namespace.
Specifies the IAM role that the ECS task container(s) can assume for AWS API calls, controlling permissions granted to the containers within the task.
Specifies the data volumes that can be mounted by containers in the ECS task, allowing persistent storage via EBS volumes or bind mounts from the host.
Configures an Amazon EFS volume to be mounted in the container, specifying the filesystem ID, root directory, transit encryption, and optional authorization configuration (access point or IAM).
Defines the EFS authorization configuration, including the access point ID and whether IAM authorization is enabled, for the Amazon EFS volume mounted in the task.
Specifies the ID of the Amazon EFS access point to use when mounting the EFS volume for the task.
Indicates whether IAM authorization is used to control access to the Amazon EFS volume, with allowed values ENABLED or DISABLED.
Specifies the Amazon EFS file system ID that the volume mounts, used in the EFS volume configuration for an ECS task in an AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies the path on the EFS file system to mount as the root directory for the volume when it is mounted into the container.
Indicates whether to enable encryption for data in transit between the container and the Amazon EFS file system, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Specifies the port to use for EFS transit encryption when connecting to the file system, used in the volume configuration for an AWS Batch job's ECS task properties.

Specifies the host volume configuration for a volume in the AWS Batch job definition's ECS task properties, which defines the source directory on the container instance that gets mounted into the container.
Specifies the host filesystem path on the container instance to be mounted into the container as a volume, used as the source for a bind-mounted host volume.
The name assigned to the volume, which is used to reference it in container mount points within the task definition.
Specifies the configuration for an S3 volume mount, including the S3 bucket, prefix, and optional transfer settings, for a container task in an ECS job definition.
The ARN of the S3 access point through which the container mounts the S3 bucket for this volume.
The ARN of the Amazon S3 access point that defines the file-system endpoint for the S3 volume mounted by this task's containers.
Specifies the root directory in the container where the S3 volume is mounted, determining the container filesystem path under which the S3 bucket's objects are made available.
Specifies the custom port to use for encrypted data transfer (TLS/HTTPS) when the S3 volume's transit encryption is enabled, with a default of 443.
The EKS properties for the job definition, specifying the EKS pod template and container properties used when running the job on Amazon EKS.
Specifies the Kubernetes pod configuration for the EKS job, including its containers, init containers, volumes, host network settings, and pod metadata such as labels and annotations.
Defines the container specifications for the EKS pod in this node range, including image, command, arguments, environment variables, and resource limits for each container in the pod.
Specifies the arguments to pass to the container's entrypoint, overriding the default CMD defined in the container image.
Specifies the entrypoint command for the EKS container, overriding the ENTRYPOINT instruction defined in the container image.
The list of environment variables to set for the container in the EKS pod.
The name of the environment variable that AWS Batch sets inside the container for the EKS pod when the job runs.
The value to assign to the environment variable specified by the 'name' field for a container in the EKS pod properties of an AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies the Docker image (with tag) that the EKS pod container runs, as defined in the Batch job definition's EKS pod properties.
Controls when the container runtime pulls the container image for the EKS pod, accepting Kubernetes-style values like Always, IfNotPresent, or Never.
The name of the container within the EKS pod, which must match the container name defined in the pod specification and is used to identify the container inside the pod.
Specifies the CPU and memory resource requests and limits for the container, analogous to Kubernetes container resource requirements.
Specifies the maximum amount of compute resources (such as cpu and memory) that the EKS container is allowed to use, expressed as a map of Kubernetes resource names to quantity values.
Specifies the minimum amount of CPU, memory, and other compute resources requested for the container, used by the Kubernetes scheduler to place the pod.
It specifies the security context settings for the EKS container, such as privileged mode, read-only root filesystem, and the user and group IDs under which the container runs.

Whether a container's process is allowed to gain more privileges than its parent process (e.g., via setuid or setgid binaries), corresponding to the Kubernetes security context's allowPrivilegeEscalation setting in the AWS Batch EKS pod properties.
When enabled, this flag runs the EKS container in privileged mode, giving it full access to the host node's devices and kernel capabilities.
When true, this makes the container's root filesystem read-only for the EKS pod running the Batch job, as defined by the Kubernetes security context.
The GID (group ID) that the container's main process should run as, matching the Kubernetes security context runAsGroup setting for EKS pods in the Batch job definition.
Specifies whether the container is required to run as a non-root user (with a UID other than 0), preventing it from running with root privileges.
Sets the numeric user ID (UID) that all processes in the container run as, overriding the image's default user for this EKS pod.
The list of volume mounts that specify which volumes to mount into the container and their mount paths.
Specifies the path within the container where the volume is mounted, following Kubernetes volumeMount mountPath semantics.
The name of the Kubernetes volume to mount into the container, which must correspond to a volume defined in the pod's volumes specification.
Indicates whether the mounted volume is read-only, so the container can only read from the volume and cannot write to it.
Specifies the sub-path inside the referenced volume to mount at the container's mount path, allowing a single subdirectory of the volume to be exposed rather than the entire volume.
Sets the Kubernetes DNS policy for the EKS pod (e.g., 'Default', 'ClusterFirst', or 'None'), determining how DNS queries are resolved for containers in the pod.
When true, the pod uses the host's network namespace instead of a dedicated pod network.
Specifies a list of Kubernetes secrets (each with a `name` key) that AWS Batch uses to authenticate with private image registries when pulling the container image for the EKS pod.
Specifies the name of the Kubernetes secret referenced in the imagePullSecrets list to provide credentials for pulling container images for the EKS pod in the AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies a list of init containers that run before the main containers in the EKS pod, allowing pre-work such as fetching secrets or setting up permissions before the primary job container starts.
The list of command-line arguments passed to the entrypoint of each init container, matching the Kubernetes container args field.
The command to execute in the init container of the EKS pod, overriding the image's default entrypoint, specified as a list of strings.
Defines environment variables for each init container in the EKS pod, where each object specifies a variable name and its value or a value-from source as per Kubernetes pod specification.
Specifies the name of an environment variable assigned to an init container within the EKS pod configuration of the Batch job definition.

Specifies the value assigned to the environment variable (with the key defined in the sibling `name` field) for an init container in the EKS pod properties of the AWS Batch job definition's node range.
Specifies the container image to use for an init container within the EKS pod properties of the node range properties in an AWS Batch job definition.
The image pull policy for the init container in the EKS pod, controlling when Kubernetes pulls the container image, with allowed values such as Always, IfNotPresent, or Never.
The name assigned to an init container within the EKS pod specification, which must be unique among all containers in the pod.
Defines the compute resource requirements (e.g., CPU and memory requests/limits) for the init container inside the EKS pod, mirroring Kubernetes container resource specifications.

Specifies the maximum amount of compute resources (such as CPU and memory) that an init container in the EKS pod is allowed to use, expressed as a key-value map of resource names to quantities (e.g., cpu: "1", memory: "512Mi").
Specifies the minimum compute resources (such as cpu and memory) that the init container in an Amazon EKS pod must have scheduled, as part of the Batch job definition's EKS pod properties.
Defines the Kubernetes security context for the init container, specifying privilege and access control settings such as run-as user/group, Linux capabilities, and privileged mode.
Controls whether the init container's processes can gain more privileges than their parent (e.g., via setuid or setgid binaries), with false preventing privilege escalation.

When true, the init container runs in privileged mode with extended Linux capabilities inside the EKS pod used by the AWS Batch job definition, matching the Kubernetes pod security context field of the same name.
When set to true, this makes the init container's root filesystem read-only, preventing writes to the container's filesystem layer.
Specifies the Linux group ID (GID) that the init container's processes run as in the EKS pod.
Specifies whether the init container must run as a non-root user, corresponding to the Kubernetes Pod security context field runAsNonRoot for EKS pods in an AWS Batch job definition.
Specifies the numeric user ID (UID) to run the init container's process as, overriding the image's default user in the Kubernetes security context.
Specifies the volume mounts for the init containers in the EKS pod, defining how volumes are mounted into the container's filesystem at specific mount paths.
The absolute path inside the init container where the volume is mounted.
The name of the Kubernetes volume to mount into the init container, matching a volume defined in the pod's volumes list.
In the AWS Batch job definition's EKS pod init containers, this boolean indicates whether the volume mount is mounted as read-only, mirroring the Kubernetes volumeMount readOnly field.
Specifies a sub-path inside the referenced Kubernetes volume to mount into the container, rather than the volume root.
Metadata for the Kubernetes pod, including optional labels and annotations, that are applied to the pod specification.

Provides the annotations, a set of key-value pairs attached to the Kubernetes pod metadata for EKS-based jobs in the batch job definition, used to attach arbitrary non-identifying metadata to the pod.
Specifies the Kubernetes labels to attach to the pod metadata for the EKS job.
Specifies the Kubernetes namespace in which the EKS pod for the Batch job will run, allowing you to isolate pod resources within the cluster.

Specifies the Kubernetes service account name attached to the EKS pod, which determines the pod's identity for Kubernetes API access and enables IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA) to grant AWS permissions.
Indicates whether all containers in the EKS pod share a single process namespace, so they can see and signal each other's processes.
Defines the list of Kubernetes-style volumes available to the EKS pod's containers, supporting types such as emptyDir, secret, configMap, and hostPath for providing storage or data to the job.

Configures an emptyDir volume for a pod in the EKS job definition, creating a temporary directory that is initially empty and persists only for the pod's lifetime, allowing containers in the pod to share data.
Specifies the storage medium for the emptyDir volume in an Amazon EKS pod; set to 'Memory' to back the volume with tmpfs (RAM) or leave empty for disk-backed storage.

The maximum storage size for the emptyDir volume in the EKS pod properties, specified as a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., '1Gi'), which limits the amount of local storage the emptyDir volume can consume.
Defines the hostPath volume source for an EKS pod in an AWS Batch job definition, specifying the host node's directory path and optional type.
Specifies the host node filesystem path that is mounted into the pod for a hostPath volume in an Amazon EKS pod definition used by the AWS Batch job.
The unique name of the Kubernetes volume within the pod, referenced by container volume mounts.
Defines a pod volume backed by a Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaim, including the PVC name and whether it is mounted read-only.
The name of the Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaim that this EKS pod volume references, which must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Indicates whether the referenced persistent volume claim (PVC) is mounted into the EKS pod as read-only, instead of the default read-write access.
Configures a Kubernetes secret volume that mounts a named secret into the EKS pod, allowing the pod to access sensitive data such as credentials as files.

Indicates whether the Kubernetes secret referenced by this volume must exist before the pod starts; if true, the mount succeeds even when the secret is missing, and if false, the secret must be present.
The name of the Kubernetes secret to mount as a volume in the EKS pod.
Specifies the EC2 instance types (or instance families) allowed for the nodes in this node range, overriding the default instance types of the compute environment.
Specifies the range of node indices (e.g., '0:5' or '1:') that this node range property applies to within a multi-node AWS Batch job definition.
Defines the total number of nodes in a multi-node parallel AWS Batch job, determining the required compute resources across the node group.

aws_batch_job_definition.parameters.text: Specifies a map of key-value pairs that define default parameters, which can be referenced within the container's command using the `Ref::` syntax.

aws_batch_job_definition.platform_capabi.text: Specifies the platform capabilities (EC2, FARGATE, or FARGATE_SPOT) required for the job to run, determining whether the job uses EC2 or Fargate computing resources.

aws_batch_job_definition.propagate_tags.text: Indicates whether tags from the AWS Batch job definition are propagated to the Amazon ECS task that runs the job.

aws_batch_job_definition.resource_retent.text: The resource_retention_policy configures the retention of compute resources after a job completes, specifying the number of completed jobs for which AWS Batch will retain resources to aid in troubleshooting.
When set to true, this Boolean field tells AWS Batch not to deregister the current job definition revision when an update creates a new revision, leaving the old revision available for use.

aws_batch_job_definition.retry_strategy.text: Defines the retry strategy for the job, including the maximum number of retry attempts and the conditions under which a job should be retried based on its exit status.

aws_batch_job_definition.retry_strategy..text: Specifies the total number of attempts (including the original) that AWS Batch will make for the job before considering it failed, with a valid range of 1 to 10, so an attempts value of N allows up to N-1 retries on failure.
Lists conditions that trigger specific actions (like retry or mark as failed) based on a job's exit code, status reason, or reason, controlling the retry behavior of the Batch job.
The action to take when the condition in this evaluate_on_exit rule is satisfied, which is either 'RETRY' to rerun the job or 'EXIT' to end the job's execution.
The job exit code (or a range of exit codes, e.g., '1-10' or '*') that must be matched for the corresponding retry action to be taken in an AWS Batch job definition's retry strategy.

Specifies the job's status reason string that triggers this evaluate-on-exit action when matched, such as a specific failure reason like 'CapacityError', causing the job to be retried according to the retry strategy.
Specifies a status reason string to match against the job's status reason, triggering the corresponding retry action when the job exits with that status reason.

aws_batch_job_definition.scheduling_prio.text: The scheduling priority for jobs using this job definition, which determines the order in which they are started when multiple jobs share the same job queue, with higher values given higher priority.

aws_batch_job_definition.timeout.text: The timeout configuration for the job definition, specifying the maximum duration (attemptDurationSeconds) that the job's container can run before it is forcibly terminated.

aws_batch_job_definition.timeout.attempt.text: The timeout duration in seconds for a single job attempt; after this time elapses, AWS Batch terminates the attempt.

aws_batch_job_definition.type.text: Specifies whether the job definition runs as a container job or a multinode job, using the value 'container' or 'multinode'.

aws_batch_job_queue.compute_environment_.text: Defines the ordered list of compute environments for the job queue, where each entry assigns a priority (order) to a compute environment and AWS Batch schedules jobs to the first available environment in that order.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the compute environment that is associated with this entry in the job queue's compute environment order.
Integer that determines the relative priority of the compute environment within the job queue, where lower values are attempted first.

aws_batch_job_queue.job_queue_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Batch job queue, assigned by AWS when the queue is created.

aws_batch_job_queue.job_queue_name.text: Specifies the name of the job queue, which must be unique within the AWS account and Region; if not provided, CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_batch_job_queue.job_queue_type.text: Specifies the type of the job queue, either 'COMPUTE' (the default) for running jobs or 'PLAYBACK' for replaying jobs from another queue for testing/debugging.

aws_batch_job_queue.job_state_time_limit.text: List of actions that automatically cancel jobs stuck in a specified state (e.g., RUNNABLE) for a configurable maximum time before they are deemed too old.
The action to take when a job in the specified state exceeds the time limit, such as CANCEL or CANCEL_AND_RESTART.
Specifies the maximum time in seconds that a job can remain in a given state before the associated action (such as CANCEL) is triggered for that job.

The reason to record for the job when this state time limit action is triggered, providing context for why the action (such as cancellation) was taken after the job exceeded the maximum time in the specified state.
Specifies the job state (only RUNNABLE is valid) that triggers the time limit action when a job remains in that state longer than max_time_seconds.

aws_batch_job_queue.priority.text: The priority of this job queue relative to other job queues in the same account and region, where higher values cause the queue to be considered earlier when scheduling jobs.

aws_batch_job_queue.scheduling_policy_ar.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the scheduling policy that controls the prioritization and placement of jobs in the AWS Batch job queue.

aws_batch_job_queue.state.text: Specifies whether the job queue is enabled to accept new jobs (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED), with the default being ENABLED.

aws_batch_scheduling_policy.fairshare_po.text: The percentage (0-99) of compute resources reserved for this scheduling policy's jobs, guaranteeing a minimum level of capacity even when shares are low.
The amount of time in seconds used to calculate the decay factor for the fair share policy, controlling how quickly the share of resources for a job family decreases over time based on its age.

Identifies an individual share within the fair share policy's share distribution list, used by AWS Batch to calculate each share's proportional allocation of compute resources based on its assigned weight factor.
The relative weight assigned to a share in an AWS Batch fairshare scheduling policy, controlling the proportional amount of vCPUs or resources allocated to that share compared to others.

aws_batch_service_environment.capacity_l.text: Specifies the unit of measure (for example, vCPU or memory) used to interpret the capacity limit value in the AWS Batch service environment's capacity limits configuration.

aws_bcm_dashboard.name.text: A user-specified unique name for the AWS Billing and Cost Management dashboard, used to identify and display the dashboard in the console.

aws_bcm_dashboard.tags.value.text: Specifies the value of a tag attached to the AWS BCM dashboard, allowing you to associate custom metadata with the dashboard for resource organization and cost allocation.

aws_bcm_dashboard.updated_at.text: The `updated_at` attribute is a read-only timestamp that records when the AWS Billing and Cost Management dashboard was last updated, automatically set by the service.

aws_bcm_dashboard.widgets.text: This required list contains the widget definitions—each specifying a visual block like a chart or KPI tile—that together form the content of the BCM dashboard.

aws_bcm_dashboard.widgets.configs.displa.text: The graph field defines the chart type and display options for the widget's visualization of cost and usage data within the AWS Billing and Cost Management dashboard.
Provides the table-specific display configuration for a widget in a BCM dashboard, defining the tabular layout of cost data.

aws_bcm_dashboard.widgets.configs.query_.text: Specifies the cost and usage query parameters for the widget, such as the time period, granularity, and metrics to display.
This filter object defines the criteria (e.g., service, region, tag, or cost category) that restrict which cost and usage data is returned and displayed in the dashboard widget.
A list of filter expression objects that must all evaluate to true (logical AND) for a cost and usage record to be included in the dashboard widget's underlying Cost Explorer query.
Maps Cost Category names to lists of Cost Category values in the widget's cost-and-usage query filter, so that the dashboard only includes data matching those Cost Categories.
The cost category key (dimension) that the dashboard widget's cost and usage query filters on, used to include or exclude data based on matching cost category values.
Specifies the matching criteria (such as EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, or CONTAINS) used to compare the cost category values in the filter for this dashboard widget's cost and usage query.
The list of cost category values to include in the cost and usage filter for the dashboard widget.
Specifies dimension filters (such as SERVICE, REGION, or USAGE_TYPE) and their allowed values to restrict the cost and usage data returned for the dashboard widget.
The name of the AWS Cost Explorer dimension (e.g., SERVICE, REGION, LINKED_ACCOUNT) that the cost-and-usage filter applies to within the dashboard widget's query parameters.

Specifies the matching strategies (e.g., EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, CONTAINS) used to compare the filter's dimension values against actual cost and usage data, controlling which results appear in the dashboard widget.
Specifies the list of dimension values (such as a set of AWS services or regions) to use when filtering cost and usage data in the dashboard widget query.
Defines a logical NOT operator that negates the evaluation of a nested cost-and-usage filter expression within the dashboard widget's query parameters.
A list of cost and usage filter expressions that are combined with logical OR, so that a resource or usage line item is included if it matches any of the contained filter conditions.
The tag key used to filter cost and usage data in the dashboard widget's query parameters.
Specifies the match options (e.g., EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, CASE_SENSITIVE) used to evaluate tag values in the cost and usage filter for a dashboard widget.
Specifies the list of tag values used to filter the cost and usage data displayed in the dashboard widget, applied to the tag key defined in the parent tags filter object.
Specifies the time granularity (e.g., DAILY or MONTHLY) for the cost and usage data displayed in the dashboard widget.

Specifies the list of grouping definitions (e.g., by service, linked account, or region) that control how cost and usage data is aggregated in the widget, mirroring the GroupBy parameter of an AWS Cost Explorer query.
Specifies the dimension name (e.g., 'AZ', 'SERVICE', or 'LINKED_ACCOUNT') by which the cost and usage data is grouped in the dashboard widget.
Specifies the type of grouping dimension (e.g., DIMENSION, TAG, COST_CATEGORY) used when aggregating cost and usage data for this widget's query.
Specifies the list of Cost Explorer metric names (e.g., BlendedCost, UnblendedCost, UsageQuantity) to be included in the widget's cost-and-usage query and displayed on the dashboard.

Specifies the end boundary of the time range used to filter cost and usage data for the widget's query, as an object containing a timestamp or date expression (such as '2024-12-31') that defines the upper limit for reported metrics.
The end date/time value of the time range used by the cost-and-usage query for the widget, defining the upper bound of the data period.
Defines the start of the custom time window (as an ISO 8601 timestamp) for which the cost and usage data is retrieved in the widget.

Specifies the start time (as a date/time string) for the time range used in the cost and usage query parameters of a BCM dashboard widget, determining the earliest data point included in the widget's display.

This object specifies the query parameters that determine how the dashboard widget calculates and displays reservation coverage, showing the percentage of AWS usage covered by Reserved Instances and Savings Plans.
Specifies the cost explorer query filter criteria (such as services, accounts, regions, or tags) used to narrow the reservation coverage data displayed by the corresponding dashboard widget.
The cost category filter for the reservation coverage query, mapping each cost category name to a list of values used to include or exclude matching reservation coverage data.
The name of the cost category used as the key in the cost_categories filter for the reservation coverage query parameter in the dashboard widget.
Specifies the match options (e.g., EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, CONTAINS) used to compare the cost category filter values in the reservation coverage query parameters of the dashboard.
Defines the list of cost category values used to filter the reservation coverage data, matching reservations that belong to any of the specified cost category values.
Defines a map of dimension names (e.g., REGION, INSTANCE_TYPE) to lists of allowed values, which filters the reservation coverage data displayed in the widget based on those dimension criteria.
The name of the AWS cost dimension (e.g., AZ, INSTANCE_TYPE, REGION) to use for filtering reservation coverage data in the dashboard query.
Specifies the matching options (such as exact, contains, or prefix matching) applied to the dimension values in the reservation coverage filter of a dashboard widget's query parameters.
Specifies the list of dimension values (e.g., region, instance type, usage type) that the reservation coverage filter includes for the given dimension in the dashboard widget's query parameters.
The NOT logical operator that negates a nested filter expression for the reservation coverage query, so results exclude resources that match the inner filter condition.
A map of tag keys and values that filter the reservation coverage data displayed in the dashboard widget, ensuring only resources matching those tags are included in the coverage metrics.
Specifies the tag key used in the reservation coverage query filter to narrow dashboard results to resources associated with that tag.
Specifies the matching options (e.g., EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, CONTAINS) applied to the tag filter when filtering reservation coverage data in the BCM dashboard widget.
Specifies the list of tag values used to filter reservation coverage data in the widget, paired with the tag key defined in the same `filter.tags` object.
Specifies the time granularity (e.g., DAILY, MONTHLY, HOURLY) for the reservation coverage data displayed in the widget.
Specifies the dimensions (such as LINKED_ACCOUNT, REGION, or INSTANCE_TYPE) by which reservation coverage data is grouped in the widget's Cost Explorer query.
Specifies the grouping dimension (e.g., AZ, INSTANCE_TYPE, PLATFORM) for reservation coverage query results in the dashboard widget.
Specifies the grouping dimension type (such as DIMENSION, TAG, or COST_CATEGORY) used to aggregate reservation coverage data in the widget's query parameters.
Defines the time range (e.g., start and end dates) for which reservation coverage metrics are aggregated and displayed in the dashboard widget.
Specifies the end time of the time range for the reservation coverage query in the widget configuration, defining the boundary until which coverage data is fetched and shown.
The end timestamp for the time range used to query reservation coverage data in the dashboard widget.
Specifies the start time of the time range used to query reservation coverage data for the dashboard widget.
Defines the format of the start time for the reservation coverage widget's time range, indicating whether the value is an absolute date-time or a relative period from the current time.
Specifies the start time (as a string) for the time range filter used by the reservation coverage query within the dashboard widget's configuration.
Defines the expression that filters which reservation utilization data (e.g., by account, service, region, or tags) is displayed in the widget's chart.
Specifies a list of filter conditions that are logically ANDed together to refine the reservation utilization data shown in the dashboard widget.

Specifies the cost categories and their values used to filter the reservation utilization data for this dashboard widget, matching the Cost Explorer filter structure for cost category-based inclusion or exclusion.
The key of the Cost Category used to filter reservation utilization data, matching the name of the Cost Category in AWS Cost Explorer.
Specifies the match operators (such as EQUALS or ABSENT) that determine how the selected cost category values are compared in the reservation utilization widget's filter.
The list of cost category values used to filter reservation utilization query results, restricting the dashboard widget's data to resources matching these cost category dimension values.

The dimensions object specifies the cost dimension filter (such as AZ, INSTANCE_TYPE, or LINKED_ACCOUNT) for the reservation utilization query, containing a dimension key and the list of values to match.
The dimension name (e.g., SERVICE, INSTANCE_TYPE, AZ) used in the filter to group or refine reservation utilization data in this dashboard widget query.
A list of match operators (e.g., EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, CONTAINS) applied to the dimension values when filtering reservation utilization data in the BCM dashboard widget's query configuration.
Specifies the dimension values (e.g., region, instance type, or linked account) that the reservation utilization widget's filter matches to include only the corresponding cost data in the dashboard.
Defines a negation filter for the reservation utilization query, excluding results that match the nested filter condition.
Defines a set of tag key-value pairs that act as a filter, narrowing the reservation utilization data displayed in the widget to only those resources that have the specified tags.
The tag key used to filter reservation utilization data in the dashboard widget's query parameters.
The list of tag matching options (e.g., EQUALS, STARTS_WITH) applied to the tag key/value filters when querying reservation utilization data in the dashboard widget.
The list of tag values to match when filtering reservation utilization data by a specific tag key in the BCM dashboard widget's query configuration.
Specifies the granularity of reservation utilization data displayed in the widget, such as DAILY or MONTHLY.
Specifies the dimensions or tags by which to group the reservation utilization data in the dashboard widget, such as instance type, region, or linked account.
Specifies the dimension or tag key (such as 'INSTANCE_TYPE', 'AZ', or a cost allocation tag) by which reservation utilization metrics are grouped in the dashboard widget.
Specifies whether the reservation utilization group-by is based on an AWS Cost Explorer dimension (e.g., INSTANCE_TYPE, LINKED_ACCOUNT) or a user-defined tag, with valid values 'DIMENSION' or 'TAG'.
Specifies the time interval (e.g., a preset like 'last 3 months' or custom start/end dates) for which reservation utilization metrics are queried and displayed in the widget.

Specifies how the end time of a reservation utilization widget's time range is expressed, such as an absolute date or a relative time period, which determines how the end_time value should be interpreted.
Specifies the end time of the time range for the reservation utilization query parameter in the dashboard widget's configuration, as a string timestamp.
In a BCM dashboard widget configuration, this field sets the start timestamp of the period over which reservation utilization metrics are aggregated and displayed.
Sets the start timestamp (date/time) of the reservation utilization query's time range in the dashboard widget configuration, defining the beginning of the usage period reported.
Specifies the query parameters for displaying Savings Plans coverage data in a BCM dashboard widget, allowing you to customize what coverage information is included.

In an AWS BCM dashboard widget that visualizes Savings Plans coverage, this object specifies the filter criteria (e.g., by account, service, or tag) that determine which coverage data is included in the widget's query.
Specifies a list of filter expressions that are combined with a logical AND to include only savings plans coverage data that satisfies all the given conditions in the widget's query.
Filters the savings plans coverage widget's data to include only the specified AWS Cost Categories and their values, allowing you to scope the dashboard view to selected cost category dimensions.
The key of the cost category used as the filter dimension for Savings Plans coverage data in the dashboard widget, matching the Cost Category name to filter on.
The list of match options (such as EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, or CONTAINS) that determine how cost category values are matched in the savings plans coverage filter for this dashboard widget.
The list of Cost Category values to match in the filter for the savings plans coverage dashboard widget's query.
Specifies the dimension key-value pairs (e.g., SERVICE, REGION, LINKED_ACCOUNT) used to filter savings plans coverage data for the dashboard widget.
The dimension name (such as 'REGION' or 'LINKED_ACCOUNT') used as the filtering key for savings plans coverage data in the dashboard widget's query parameters.
Specifies the match options (e.g., EQUALS, STARTS_WITH) used to filter dimension values within the savings plans coverage query for a dashboard widget.

Specifies the list of values for a dimension (such as REGION, SERVICE, or LINKED_ACCOUNT) to filter the Savings Plans coverage data displayed by the dashboard widget, narrowing results to the selected dimension values.
Negates the nested savings_plans_coverage filter criteria so that resources matching the enclosed conditions are excluded from the dashboard's coverage data.
