A map of tag keys to lists of tag values that filters the savings plans coverage data, showing only results for resources that match the specified tags.
The tag key used to filter savings plans coverage data in the widget, so only resources with this tag key are included in the displayed coverage metrics.
Specifies the matching options (such as EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, or CONTAINS) that determine how tag values are compared when filtering savings plans coverage data in the dashboard widget.
Specifies the time granularity (for example, DAILY or MONTHLY) used by the widget's Savings Plans coverage query.
This list of group-by objects determines the dimensions (e.g., REGION, INSTANCE_TYPE, or USAGE_TYPE) used to aggregate Savings Plans coverage data in the dashboard widget.
The name of the dimension (e.g., INSTANCE_TYPE, REGION, LINKED_ACCOUNT) by which the Savings Plans coverage data is grouped in the dashboard widget's query.
Specifies the grouping type (e.g., 'DIMENSION' or 'TAG') for the savings plans coverage query, determining how the group-by key is interpreted in the Cost Explorer data.
Defines the list of savings plan coverage metrics (such as 'Coverage' and 'Utilization') to display in the dashboard widget.
Specifies the time range (e.g., start and end dates or a relative period) used to filter the savings plans coverage data shown in the widget.
The end_time specifies the end of the time range for which Savings Plans coverage data is reported in the dashboard widget's query.
Specifies the end time of the time range for the Savings Plans coverage query parameter in the dashboard widget, determining the final date/time boundary for the coverage data returned.
Specifies the starting timestamp of the time range for which the dashboard widget queries Savings Plans coverage data, determining the earliest period included in the metric.
Defines how the start time for the savings plans coverage widget's time range is specified, such as an absolute date or a relative offset.
Defines the beginning of the time range (as a date/time string) used to query Savings Plans coverage data for this dashboard widget.
The filter object defines the conditions (such as account, region, service, or tag dimensions) used to narrow the savings plans utilization data displayed by the widget.

A list of filter conditions (each evaluating a dimension such as service, region, or usage type) that must all be true for the savings plans utilization data query, equivalent to a logical AND operation in AWS Cost Explorer filters.

In the widget's savings-plans utilization query, this object maps AWS Cost Category names to selected values, filtering the displayed utilization data to only include costs that match those category values.
The name of the cost category dimension used to filter Savings Plans utilization data in the dashboard widget's query.
Specifies the match options (such as EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, or CONTAINS) used to evaluate cost category values in the savings plans utilization filter.
The list of cost category values used to filter the savings plans utilization data shown in the widget, so only data matching those values is included.

The `dimensions` object defines a filter on cost dimensions for Savings Plans utilization data, specifying a dimension key (such as REGION or SERVICE) and the corresponding values that the queried utilization data must match to appear in the dashboard widget.
The name of the dimension (e.g., SERVICE, REGION, or LINKED_ACCOUNT) used to filter savings plans utilization data in the widget.

Specifies the matching operators (e.g., EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, CONTAINS) used to evaluate whether a dimension value qualifies when filtering Savings Plans utilization data in the dashboard widget's query.
Specifies a filter expression that must not match for the Savings Plans utilization data to be included in the dashboard widget's query results.
Specifies cost allocation tag key-value pairs used to filter the savings plans utilization query results for this dashboard widget.
The key of a tag filter applied to the savings plans utilization widget query, restricting the displayed data to resources that carry a tag with that key.
Specifies the match options (such as EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, or CONTAINS) applied to tag values when filtering savings plans utilization data in the dashboard widget.
A list of tag values to match when filtering savings plans utilization data for the widget, so only resources with any of these tag values are included in the dashboard view.
Specifies the time granularity (e.g., DAILY, MONTHLY, or HOURLY) for the savings plans utilization query used by this dashboard widget.
Configures the time interval (start and end dates) for which savings plans utilization metrics are queried and displayed in the dashboard widget.
Contains the end timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) that defines the end of the time range for the Savings Plans utilization query in the dashboard widget.

The value for the start time of the time range applied to the Savings Plans utilization query in the dashboard widget, specifying the beginning of the period for which savings plans utilization metrics are shown.

aws_bcm_dashboard.widgets.height.text: In an AWS BCM Dashboard, the height of a widget defines its vertical size on the dashboard grid, expressed in grid units.

aws_bcm_dashboard.widgets.title.text: The title text that is displayed on the widget in the AWS BCM (Billing and Cost Management) dashboard.

aws_bcm_dashboard.widgets.width.text: The width of the widget in grid units on the BCM dashboard, determining how many columns of the dashboard's layout the widget occupies.

aws_bcm_pricing_calculator_bill_scenario.text: The computed time interval (with start and end timestamps) that delineates the billing period the bill scenario analyzes, automatically populated by the AWS BCM Pricing Calculator service.
The start of the billing interval for the bill scenario, defining the beginning of the period over which AWS costs are estimated.
Controls whether the bill scenario is shared with all AWS Organizations groups (ALL) or not shared (NONE), restricting visibility to the creator account only.
The current lifecycle state of the bill scenario, such as whether it is active, being created, or failed, as determined by the AWS BCM Pricing Calculator service.
A user-defined key for a tag attached to the AWS BCM Pricing Calculator bill scenario, used to categorize and track the bill scenario for cost allocation.
The value part of a key-value tag on the AWS BCM Pricing Calculator bill scenario, used for categorizing and managing the resource.

aws_bcmdata_exports_export.export.text: The computed export object contains the full definition of the BCM data export, including its name, description, data query (query statement and table configurations), destination configuration (S3 bucket, prefix, region, and output settings), and refresh cadence.

aws_bcmdata_exports_export.export.data_q.text: Defines the SQL query statement and table configurations that determine which cost and usage data is included in the export.
The SQL query statement that specifies the cost and usage data to include in the export, such as selecting specific columns from a billing or cost report table.
Defines per-table configuration settings for the data query as a map of table names to property maps, enabling options such as the identity table's 'IncludeLinkedAccounts' flag.

aws_bcmdata_exports_export.export.descri.text: Specifies a user-defined description for the BCM data export, providing a human-readable label for the export's purpose or contents.

aws_bcmdata_exports_export.export.destin.text: Defines the Amazon S3 destination for the exported cost and usage data, specifying the bucket, prefix, and output format such as CSV or Parquet.
The S3 destination configuration specifies the Amazon S3 bucket (and optional prefix, region, and KMS key ARN) where the BCM data export output files are delivered.
The name of the S3 bucket to which the BCM Data Export's output files are delivered.
Specifies the AWS account ID of the owner of the S3 bucket where the cost and usage data export is delivered.
Specifies the output configuration for the S3 destination, controlling the compression, format, and output type of the exported data files.
Specifies the compression format (for example, GZIP) applied to the exported data files written to the S3 destination.
Specifies the output file format for the export's S3 destination, which must be either CSV or PARQUET.
Specifies whether the export's S3 output uses the original AWS Cost and Usage Report schema (ORIGINAL) or a custom schema (CUSTOM) defined in the export.
Specifies whether an export job overwrites existing files in the Amazon S3 destination (e.g., 'OVERWRITE') or preserves them and writes new files (e.g., 'NOT_OVERWRITE').
The S3 object key prefix prepended to exported files written to the destination bucket, used to organize the export output under a specific folder path.
The AWS region where the destination S3 bucket is located, used to configure where the BCM data export is delivered.

aws_bcmdata_exports_export.export.export.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the data export, returned after the export is created.

aws_bcmdata_exports_export.export.name.text: The user-defined unique name for the data export, required when creating an AWS BCM Data Exports export resource.

aws_bcmdata_exports_export.export.refres.text: Defines the refresh schedule for the export, using a `frequency` attribute that must be either `SYNCHRONOUS` to refresh data in real time or `ASYNC` to refresh on a preconfigured schedule.
Determines whether the data export is refreshed synchronously (on demand) or asynchronously (on a recurring schedule), with allowed values SYNCHRONOUS and ASYNCHRONOUS.

aws_bcmdata_exports_export.export_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the created BCM data export.

aws_bcmdata_exports_export.tags.text: Defines the customer-managed tags (key-value pairs) to associate with the BCM data export resource, allowing you to categorize, identify, and filter exports for billing and cost management.

aws_bcmdata_exports_export.tags.key.text: The tag key (left side of a key-value pair) applied to the BCM data export, which can be used for cost allocation and resource filtering in AWS Cost Management.

aws_bcmdata_exports_export.tags.value.text: The value assigned to a tag key on the BCM data export, allowing you to categorize and filter exports by custom metadata.

aws_bedrock_agent.action_groups.action_g.text: Specifies the executor of an action group, which is either the ARN of a Lambda function that the agent invokes for the action group's logic or a custom control mode (like RETURN_CONTROL) that determines whether the agent hands control back to the caller.

Determines the custom control mode for the action group executor; when set to the string value 'AMAZON_USER_INPUT', the agent returns action group invocation results to the calling application for execution rather than invoking a Lambda function.
The ARN of the AWS Lambda function that serves as the executor for this action group in the Bedrock agent.
The name of the action group, required to be unique among all action groups defined for the agent and used to reference it in the agent configuration.
Indicates whether the action group is enabled or disabled, with allowed values ENABLED and DISABLED.

aws_bedrock_agent.action_groups.api_sche.text: The API schema object for the action group, which provides an S3 location or an inline OpenAPI-compatible payload that defines the operations the agent can invoke.
The inline OpenAPI schema (JSON or YAML) string that defines the API operations for the action group, used when the schema is provided directly rather than via an S3 object.
Specifies the S3 bucket, key, and optional version for the OpenAPI schema that defines the action group's API.
The name of the S3 bucket that contains the OpenAPI schema file defining the API for this action group.
The S3 object key of the OpenAPI schema file stored in the S3 bucket specified by the sibling s3BucketName, used to define the API schema for this action group.

aws_bedrock_agent.action_groups.descript.text: A free-form text field that describes the purpose or functionality of the action group, which defines the set of APIs or tools the agent can invoke.

aws_bedrock_agent.action_groups.function.text: Specifies the schema of functions available to the agent within this action group, defining the function signatures and parameters that the agent can invoke to interact with external systems.
Defines the list of functions (each with name, description, and parameters) that the Bedrock agent can invoke through this action group.
Describes the function's purpose so that the Amazon Bedrock Agent can evaluate when to invoke it.
The name of the function defined in the function schema for an action group of an Amazon Bedrock agent, which the agent uses to invoke the function.
Defines the parameters for each function in an agent's action group function schema, including each parameter's name, type, description, and required flag for the function invocation.
Specifies whether the agent requires user confirmation before invoking this function, with valid values being ENABLED or DISABLED.

aws_bedrock_agent.action_groups.parent_a.text: Specifies the unique identifier (signature) of a parent action group when this action group is defined as a sub-action group, establishing a hierarchical relationship between the action groups within the Bedrock agent.

aws_bedrock_agent.action_groups.skip_res.text: This boolean controls whether the action group's deletion skips the AWS resource-in-use check, allowing the action group to be removed even if it is still considered in use by the agent or other AWS resources.

aws_bedrock_agent.agent_collaborators.ag.text: Specifies the agent ID and alias ARN that identify the collaborator agent in a multi-agent collaboration, allowing the current Bedrock agent to invoke and delegate to that sub-agent.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the alias of the collaborator agent that this agent can invoke.

aws_bedrock_agent.agent_collaborators.co.text: The instruction that the main agent uses to determine how to delegate tasks or queries to this sub-agent collaborator.
The name of the collaborating agent that this Bedrock agent can call during multi-agent collaboration, used to identify the sub-agent within the agent_collaborators list.

aws_bedrock_agent.agent_collaborators.re.text: Determines whether the conversation history is relayed to the collaborator agent, with values such as TO_COLLABORATOR or DISABLED.

aws_bedrock_agent.knowledge_bases.descri.text: The description of a knowledge base attached to the Bedrock agent, which provides a free-form text explanation of the knowledge base's purpose and is stored as part of the agent's knowledge base configuration.

aws_bedrock_agent.knowledge_bases.knowle.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Bedrock knowledge base that the agent uses to retrieve information for response generation.
Defines the runtime state of the connected knowledge base, allowing you to enable or disable its use by the Amazon Bedrock agent, with valid values of ENABLED and DISABLED.

aws_bedrock_agent.prompt_override_config.text: Specifies a JSON object of additional inference parameters that are passed through to the foundation model, beyond the standard inference configuration, when the prompt is invoked.

Provides the base prompt template string for this prompt configuration, which contains the instructions and placeholder variables that the Bedrock agent uses when generating the prompt for the corresponding prompt type.
The Amazon Bedrock foundation model ID (e.g., 'anthropic.claude-v2') used for this prompt configuration in the agent's prompt override settings.
Specifies the inference parameters (such as temperature, top P, and maximum length) for a particular prompt configuration in the agent's prompt override settings.
Specifies the maximum number of tokens the model is allowed to generate in its response for this prompt configuration.
Specifies a list of stop sequences (strings) that cause the model to halt token generation when any of them is encountered in the output.
Specifies the sampling temperature for the model's inference, controlling the randomness of generated responses for this prompt's configuration, where higher values yield more diverse outputs.

The top_k sampling parameter specifies the number of most-likely tokens to consider for each generation step, controlling the randomness and diversity of the model's responses within the prompt's inference configuration.
Sets the nucleus sampling probability threshold for the foundation model, such that only tokens whose cumulative probability mass reaches this top_p value are considered during response generation.
Specifies the parsing mode for the prompt configuration, indicating whether the agent uses the default parser (DEFAULT) or an overridden parser prompt (OVERRIDE) to interpret the model's output.
Specifies whether the prompt configuration uses the default Bedrock prompt or a custom override, with valid values PROMPT_CREATION_MODE_DEFAULT and PROMPT_CREATION_MODE_OVERRIDDEN.
Determines whether this prompt override configuration is active (ENABLED) or inactive (DISABLED), controlling whether the custom prompt is used for the associated agent step.
Specifies which step in the agent's orchestration flow this prompt override applies to, such as PRE_PROCESSING, ORCHESTRATION, POST_PROCESSING, or KNOWLEDGE_BASE_RESPONSE_GENERATION.

aws_bedrock_agent_alias.agent_alias_hist.text: The timestamp indicating when the agent alias stopped being associated with the agent version that the history event describes.
The routing configuration at the time of this history event, listing the agent versions to which the alias directed traffic.
The version of the Bedrock agent (for example, 'DRAFT' or a numeric version) that the routing configuration entry associated with this alias history event directs traffic to.
The timestamp indicating when the alias version associated with this history event began serving as the alias's active version.

aws_bedrock_agent_alias.routing_configur.text: Specifies the version of the Bedrock agent (such as 'DRAFT' or a numeric version) that this routing configuration entry directs alias traffic to.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_browser_custom.br.text: If set to true, enables browser signing, which allows the agent to use an authenticated browser session to access websites during execution.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_browser_custom.ce.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the certificate (and optionally its private key) for the custom core browser's certificate location, used by the Bedrock agent for secure connections.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_browser_custom.en.text: The S3 bucket that contains the enterprise policy document used by the Bedrock agent's core browser configuration.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_browser_custom.re.text: The name of the S3 bucket to which the agent's recorded browser sessions are uploaded.
The S3 object key prefix within the S3 bucket where the browser session recordings are stored.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_capacity_provider.text: Specifies the device name (e.g., /dev/sdb) for an ephemeral volume in the EC2 launch template configuration used by the Bedrock agent core capacity provider.

Configures the Amazon EBS volume settings (such as size, volume type, and encryption) for an ephemeral volume attached to EC2 instances launched using the launch template in the Bedrock agent core capacity provider's compute configuration.
Indicates whether the EBS volume is encrypted at rest; when true, the volume is encrypted using an AWS KMS key.
Specifies the provisioned IOPS (input/output operations per second) for the EBS volume defined in the launch template's block device mapping.

The KMS key ID used to encrypt the ephemeral EBS volumes attached to the EC2 instances launched for the Bedrock agent's compute capacity, enabling customer-managed encryption for these temporary storage volumes.
Specifies the EBS snapshot ID used to initialize the ephemeral EBS volume attached to EC2 instances launched for this Bedrock agent core capacity provider.

The throughput (in MiB/s) for the EBS volume attached as an ephemeral volume to the compute instances launched by the capacity provider's launch template, determining the sustained I/O performance of that volume.
Specifies the size of the EBS ephemeral volume in GiB within the EC2 launch parameters for the core capacity provider's compute configuration.

Sets the virtual device name (e.g., 'ephemeral0') for an ephemeral instance-store volume in the EC2 launch template's block device mapping used by the Bedrock agent core capacity provider's compute configuration.
The ARN of an AWS License Manager license configuration that is applied to EC2 instances launched from this launch template.

Specifies the Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume configuration, including settings like volume size, volume type, and IOPS, for a volume attached to the EC2 instances in the capacity provider's compute configuration.
The provisioned IOPS (input/output operations per second) for the EBS volume defined in the EC2 compute configuration of the Bedrock agent core capacity provider.
Specifies the ID of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the EBS volume defined in the EC2 configuration of the Bedrock Agent Core capacity provider's compute configuration.
The name field provides a unique logical identifier for the EBS volume within the compute configuration, which is used to reference the volume when attaching or mounting it to the EC2 instances.
The size of the Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume, in GiB, used by the EC2 compute configuration for this Bedrock agent core capacity provider.
The ID of the EBS snapshot from which the volume is created, used to initialize the volume with data when configuring the EC2 compute resources for the Bedrock agent capacity provider.

Specifies the throughput (in MiB/s) for the EBS volumes attached to the EC2 instances in the compute configuration of the Bedrock agent core capacity provider, controlling the I/O performance of the storage.
Specifies the EBS volume type (e.g., gp3, io2) to use for the volumes attached to the EC2 instances in the compute configuration of the Bedrock agent core capacity provider.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_code_interpreter_.text: The certificate_location property of each certificate specifies the S3 URI of the certificate file that is mounted into the custom core code interpreter container to establish trust for secure connections.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the certificate for a custom certificate location, used by the AWS Bedrock Agent Core code interpreter custom resource to secure TLS connections.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_dataset.tags.valu.text: The value of a user-defined tag applied to the Amazon Bedrock Agent Core Dataset, used to help identify, organize, and manage this dataset resource.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_evaluator.evaluat.text: Defines the list of categorical rating options (each with a name and description) that the LLM-as-a-judge evaluator uses to score model responses.
Specifies the textual definition/description for a category in the categorical rating scale, which instructs the LLM-as-a-judge on how to interpret and score model outputs.
The label is the human-readable name assigned to a category in a categorical rating scale, used by the LLM-as-a-judge evaluator to identify the category in prompts and results.
Provides the numeric rating scale for the LLM-as-judge, where each item defines a score point (e.g., 1 through 5) and its textual description, used to evaluate agent responses.
Provides a textual description that defines the meaning of a specific numerical rating value in the LLM-as-judge rating scale, guiding the judge model's evaluation criteria.
The numeric score assigned to a particular rating level in the numerical rating scale used by the LLM-as-judge evaluator for the Bedrock agent core evaluation.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway.authorize.text: Specifies the list of allowed audience values (the 'aud' claim) that a JWT must contain to be accepted by the custom JWT authorizer for this Agent Core Gateway.
Specifies the list of JWT scopes that must be present in the token's claims for the custom JWT authorizer to allow the request through the core gateway.
Specifies the value that a custom claim in the JWT token must match for the request to be authorized by the Bedrock Agent Core Gateway's custom JWT authorizer.

Determines the comparison operator (e.g., equals) used when evaluating whether a custom JWT claim's value matches the configured authorizing claim match value in the JWT authorizer of the Bedrock agent core gateway.

Defines the exact value that a custom claim in the incoming JWT token must match to authorize the request to the Bedrock agent core gateway, used by the custom JWT authorizer's custom claims configuration.
The exact string value that the specified custom claim must match for the request to be authorized.

For the custom JWT authorizer on the Bedrock Agent Core Gateway, this field determines whether the value of the inbound token claim is interpreted as a single string or an array of strings when extracting custom claims.

This field specifies the OIDC discovery URL (e.g., https://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration) that the custom JWT authorizer fetches to obtain the JWKS (JSON Web Key Set) used to validate the JWT tokens presented to the agent's core gateway.
Defines the managed VPC configuration (VPC ID, subnet IDs, security group IDs) used by the private endpoint of the custom JWT authorizer in the Bedrock Agent Core Gateway resource.
Specifies the IP address type (IPv4 or IPv6) for the managed VPC endpoint used to privately access the custom JWT authorizer.
The security group IDs to attach to the managed VPC resources that back this private endpoint, controlling network traffic for the custom JWT authorizer.
Specifies the list of subnet IDs in the managed VPC used for the private endpoint of the custom JWT authorizer, determining where the endpoint resources are placed for network connectivity.
The ID of the VPC in which the managed VPC resource for the private endpoint is provisioned.
The unique identifier of the Amazon VPC Lattice resource configuration that the custom JWT authorizer's private endpoint uses to route requests to the self-managed lattice resource.
Specifies the type of authorizer that the Bedrock Agent core gateway uses to authenticate and authorize incoming API requests before invoking the underlying agent.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway.intercept.text: Specifies a list of interceptor configurations that attach Lambda-based hooks to the agent core gateway for monitoring, modifying, or short-circuiting requests and responses between clients and the agent.
Whether the original request headers are included and passed through to the interceptor Lambda when the agent intercepts an invocation.

This object defines the payload filter for the interceptor's input configuration, specifying a matching pattern and type that determine which parts of the incoming payload are allowed through to the agent for processing.
Specifies the name of a field in the input payload that should be excluded from the payload sent to the interceptor as part of the payload filter's exclude list.
Specifies the agent lifecycle stages (such as PRE_PROCESSING and POST_PROCESSING) at which the interceptor Lambda function is invoked to intercept requests and responses.
Specifies the interceptor to be invoked by the core gateway, including its ARN and interception type (e.g., request or response).
Defines the Lambda function configuration used by the interceptor to hook into and process requests and responses flowing through the Bedrock agent core gateway.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway.kms_key_a.text: The ARN of the customer-managed AWS KMS key used to encrypt the Bedrock agent core gateway's data at rest, providing control over encryption.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway.protocol_.text: Determines whether the agent discovers tools from the MCP server via exact tool-name matching or semantic search.
Specifies the maximum duration in seconds that an MCP session remains active before timing out, controlling the lifespan of Model Context Protocol server connections used by the agent's core gateway.
Configures streaming behavior for MCP (Model Context Protocol) communication, including whether MCP messages are streamed between the agent and the core gateway.
This boolean enables response streaming in the MCP streaming configuration of the agent core gateway, allowing data to be delivered incrementally rather than as a single complete payload.
Specifies the list of MCP (Model Context Protocol) versions, such as '2024-11-05', that the gateway supports when communicating with connected MCP servers.
Defines the communication protocol used by the core gateway, with supported values of 'APPLICATION' for application-to-agent traffic and 'AGENTS' for agent-to-agent traffic.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway.role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that the Bedrock Agent Core Gateway assumes to invoke Amazon Bedrock agents and access related AWS services.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_rate_limi.text: The timestamp at which this Bedrock agent core gateway rate limit was created.
The sustained request rate in requests per second that the core gateway allows for this connection when the agent routes traffic through the specified rate limit entry.
The time window, expressed as an ISO 8601 duration string (e.g., 'PT1M' for one minute), over which the request rate limit is enforced for this rate-limit entry.

Defines the duration (such as seconds or an ISO 8601 period) over which tokens are replenished for a rate limit entry on the Bedrock agent core gateway, controlling how frequently tokens are refilled in the token bucket.
The unique identifier of the Bedrock Agent core gateway to which this rate limit is applied.
The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when this core gateway rate limit was last modified.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_rule.acti.text: Specifies the weighted routing override for an action within the core gateway rule's configuration bundle, controlling the proportional share of traffic directed to that action relative to others.

Defines the weighting rules that determine how traffic is distributed among the configuration bundles in the weighted override, with each list entry representing a target bundle and its relative weight.

Provides a human-readable note about this traffic split entry, used within a weighted override of an action's configuration bundle to document the purpose of routing a portion of traffic to a particular agent configuration in the core gateway rule.
Specifies the name of the static route's target, which identifies the destination (such as an action group or function) that the Bedrock agent core gateway uses to direct the action.

Specifies a weighted routing strategy that partitions traffic for this action among multiple target resources by assigning each target a numeric weight, so the proportion of requests sent to each target matches its weight relative to the total.
A description for this individual traffic split entry, allowing you to annotate the purpose or intended target of the portion of traffic routed through this weighted route path.

In the weighted route action of a Bedrock core gateway rule, this field provides a human-readable name for each traffic split, distinguishing the multiple targets (such as agents or agent versions) that receive a portion of the request traffic.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_rule.cond.text: A list of conditions that are evaluated against the incoming request or context to determine whether this core gateway rule should trigger its associated actions.

In an AWS Bedrock Agent Core Gateway Rule, the `any_of` list within `match_paths` contains path patterns and the condition is satisfied when the incoming request path matches any of the specified patterns.
Specifies a list of principal objects to match, such that the condition is satisfied when the incoming request principal matches any one of the listed principals.

Within the `any_of` list of a Bedrock Agent Core Gateway rule's `match_principals` condition, this object specifies an IAM principal (e.g., by ARN, account ID, or service) that the calling principal must match for the condition to apply.
The ARN of the IAM principal that the condition matches against, within an 'any_of' list in the match_principals block of the gateway rule.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_rule.gate.text: The unique identifier of the Bedrock agent core gateway to which this rule is attached, used to apply the rule's routing behavior to that gateway's traffic.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_target.au.text: Specifies the OAuth 2.0 authorization parameters (such as the token endpoint and client credentials) that the core gateway uses to obtain an access token for authenticating requests sent to the target API.
The authorization URL of the OAuth2 configuration that the Bedrock agent core gateway target uses to redirect users for authentication and consent.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_target.cr.text: Configures the API key credential provider for the Bedrock agent core gateway target, typically referencing a Secrets Manager secret to retrieve the API key and an optional header name for authentication.
Specifies the location, typically the ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret, where the API key credential used to authenticate requests to the target endpoint is stored.
Specifies the name of the secret or parameter (e.g., in AWS Secrets Manager) that holds the API key used by the credential provider for the Bedrock agent's core gateway target.
For a core gateway target, this region specifies the AWS Region where the IAM role is assumed by the function executor's credential provider, enabling cross-region access to resources.

Specifies additional key-value pairs to be sent as custom parameters in the OAuth token request to the credential provider's token endpoint, allowing provider-specific fields beyond standard OAuth parameters.
The default redirect URI to which the OAuth authorization server sends users after successful authentication, used by the OAuth credential provider for this agent core gateway target.
The OAuth 2.0 grant type used to request the access token from the token endpoint, such as client_credentials.
The list of OAuth 2.0 scopes that the credential provider requests when obtaining an access token for calling the core gateway target.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_target.me.text: Specifies the list of metadata attribute keys that are allowed to be used as query parameters when the agent performs queries against the associated knowledge base.

Specifies the list of HTTP request header names that are allowed to be forwarded or processed as metadata by the Bedrock Agent core gateway target, restricting which incoming request headers are included in the gateway's metadata configuration.
Determines the HTTP response headers that the agent core gateway target is permitted to include in its responses, configuring the metadata allowed in the gateway output.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_target.pr.text: Defines the VPC private connection configuration (such as a VPC endpoint ID) that the Amazon Bedrock core gateway uses to securely route requests to a target resource that is not publicly accessible.
Defines the Amazon resource inside the Bedrock-managed VPC that the core gateway target's private endpoint is attached to.
Specifies the IP address type (IPv4, IPv6, or dualstack) used for the private endpoint connection within the managed VPC resource.
Specifies the DNS domain name used for routing requests through the private endpoint to the managed VPC resource.
The subnet IDs within the managed VPC resource where the private endpoint's elastic network interfaces are placed, determining the network availability and routing for the endpoint.
Specifies the tags to apply to the AWS-managed VPC resource provisioned for the private endpoint of this Bedrock agent core gateway target.
The identifier (typically the ARN) of the VPC Lattice resource configuration that the self-managed lattice resource uses as the target for the Bedrock agent core gateway private endpoint.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_gateway_target.ta.text: Specifies the HTTP target configuration for the Bedrock agent core gateway, including the endpoint URL and HTTP method used to forward requests.
Specifies the version qualifier (e.g., an agent alias or 'DRAFT') used by the agent core runtime to select which version of the Bedrock agent the gateway target routes requests to.
Specifies the inline OpenAPI schema payload for the AgentCore runtime HTTP target's schema source, providing the API definition directly as a string rather than referencing an S3 location.
Defines the S3 bucket and object key that point to the API schema file (e.g., OpenAPI specification) used by the HTTP agent core runtime target.
The AWS account ID of the owner of the S3 bucket that contains the agent runtime schema, used to verify bucket ownership and authorize access when fetching the schema.
The S3 URI pointing to the schema definition file for the agent core runtime, used as the source schema for the gateway target's HTTP configuration.
The endpoint URL to which the gateway forwards HTTP requests when using passthrough mode.
This object specifies the S3 bucket and object key that contain the schema definition used for the HTTP passthrough request/response payload of the gateway target.
The AWS account ID that owns the S3 bucket containing the schema file specified as the source for the HTTP passthrough configuration.
The URI of an S3 object that contains the API schema (OpenAPI or JSON schema) defining the HTTP operation and data structures for the passthrough configuration of the target.
The duration in seconds for which a client session remains pinned to the same target in the HTTP passthrough stickiness configuration, after which the sticky session expires.
Specifies the model identifier or Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for an inference operation within the provider's models configuration for this gateway target.
Defines the Model Context Protocol (MCP) configuration for this Bedrock agent core gateway target, specifying how the agent connects to an external MCP server to access its tools.
The API Gateway configuration for the MCP server target, including the endpoint URL and required authentication parameters for the Bedrock agent to invoke tools.
Specifies tool filters for the API Gateway-hosted MCP server, defining include or exclude patterns for tool names to control which tools the agent can access.
Specifies the JSON path used to filter which MCP tools from the API Gateway are available to the Bedrock agent core gateway target, restricting the tool set exposed to the agent.
Filters the exposed API Gateway tool operations to only those whose HTTP method (e.g., GET, POST) is included in this list.

Specifies a list of overrides for the API Gateway tool definitions, letting you customize individual operations such as renaming tools or changing their descriptions before they are made available to the agent.

In the tool_overrides of the MCP API gateway tool configuration, the description field specifies the custom description that will replace the tool's original description when exposed to the agent model.
Specifies the name of the MCP tool whose settings are being overridden in this API Gateway tool configuration for the Bedrock agent core gateway target.
The API Gateway resource path that overrides the default tool endpoint path for the MCP tool configuration when invoked through the Bedrock agent's core gateway target.
The unique identifier of the Amazon API Gateway REST API that serves as the MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoint for this target configuration.
The API Gateway stage name (such as 'prod' or 'dev') that identifies the specific deployment stage of the API Gateway endpoint used as the MCP server for this Bedrock agent core gateway target.

Defines the MCP (Model Context Protocol) server connector configuration, specifying the connection details such as the server name and URI, that the Bedrock agent core gateway target uses to reach an external MCP endpoint.
Provides a human-readable description of a specific MCP connector configuration entry, used to document and identify the purpose of that configuration within the Bedrock Agent core gateway target.
Overrides the default parameter values of the MCP connector configuration used by the Bedrock agent's core gateway target, allowing custom values for keys such as endpoint or authentication settings.

The identifier of the MCP (Model Context Protocol) connector that serves as the source for the target configuration, specifying which connector's data or tools the Bedrock Agent core gateway target should route to.
The lambda configuration block that defines the AWS Lambda function used as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server endpoint for this core gateway target.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function that serves as the MCP (Model Context Protocol) target for the Bedrock Agent core gateway configuration.
The tool schema for the Lambda-backed MCP server, defining the tools' input and output structures so the Bedrock agent can invoke them.
Defines the inline list of tool schema objects for the Lambda-backed MCP target, specifying the tools' names, descriptions, and input schemas for the agent.
Provides a human-readable description of the tool within the inline JSON schema of the Lambda-based MCP tool configuration, which the Bedrock agent uses to determine when to invoke the tool.

The JSON Schema object that defines the structure, types, and validation rules for the input parameters of the tool exposed via the MCP Lambda target, enabling the agent to generate and validate tool arguments.
Provides a human-readable description of the input JSON schema that defines the parameters expected by the MCP tool's Lambda function.

Defines the JSON schema for each element of an array-valued input property within the tool's inline input schema, specifying the expected type and structure for array items passed to the MCP Lambda tool.
Specifies the list of property names that must be present in the tool's input payload, as defined by the JSON schema in the inline payload.
Defines the root JSON Schema type (commonly 'object') for the input schema of the MCP tool associated with the Lambda target configuration.
The name of the tool defined in the inline JSON schema for the MCP server's Lambda tool configuration, which the agent uses to invoke the appropriate function.
Defines the JSON schema that describes the expected structure and data types of the tool's output, which Bedrock Agents uses to validate and interpret the response from the MCP tool.
Provides a human-readable description of the output schema that defines the structure of the data returned by the Lambda-based MCP tool.

Specifies the JSON Schema definition for the items (elements) of an array-typed output value within the output_schema of the MCP Lambda tool's inline payload, which Bedrock Agent uses to validate the tool's response.
Specifies the properties map of the output JSON Schema for the MCP tool, where each property key maps to a schema definition describing the shape of the tool's response data.
The list of property names that must be present in the tool's output data, as specified by the JSON Schema output schema for the MCP Lambda tool.
The JSON Schema type (e.g., 'object') that defines the data type of the output schema for the tool exposed through the Lambda-backed MCP server in the Bedrock agent's target configuration.

For an MCP server backed by AWS Lambda, this object defines the S3 bucket and key from which the tool schema is retrieved, allowing the agent to discover the tools exposed by the Lambda-based MCP server.
Specifies the AWS account ID of the S3 bucket owner that contains the tool schema for the Lambda-backed MCP server, enabling cross-account access to the schema object.
The S3 URI (e.g., s3://bucket/key) of the JSON schema file that defines the tool schema for the Lambda-based MCP server in the agent's core gateway target.
Defines the MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that this core gateway target points to, including its endpoint or ARN.
The endpoint URL of the MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that the core gateway target connects to for accessing external tools and data sources.

The JSON Schema that defines the input parameters for each tool exposed by the Amazon Bedrock agent's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, enabling the agent to invoke those tools with correctly formatted arguments.
Specifies the inline JSON schema payload that defines the MCP tool's input and output structure for the core gateway target.
Specifies the AWS account ID of the owner of the S3 bucket that contains the MCP tool schema file, used to confirm bucket ownership when accessing the schema.
The S3 URI (s3://bucket-name/key) that points to the JSON schema document defining the tools exposed by the MCP server.
The OpenAPI schema for an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that defines the API operations and tools available to the Bedrock agent when targeting this MCP configuration.
Specifies the S3 bucket, key, and optional version of the OpenAPI schema object that defines the MCP endpoint's API contract for this core gateway target.
The AWS account ID of the owner of the S3 bucket that stores the OpenAPI schema for the MCP integration, used to enable access when the bucket belongs to a different account.
The S3 URI of the OpenAPI schema file that defines the MCP server's API, used by the Bedrock agent's core gateway target to connect to the MCP server.
The Smithy model (as an object) that defines the tools and operations exposed by the MCP server configured as the target, enabling the Bedrock agent to integrate and invoke those tools.
Specifies the inline Smithy model payload (a string) that defines the API schema for the MCP server configuration of the Bedrock agent's core gateway target.
Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket and object key where the Smithy model file defining the MCP server's tools and schema is stored, used as part of the core gateway target's MCP configuration.
Specifies the AWS account ID of the S3 bucket owner, enabling the service to validate that the bucket holding the Smithy model is owned by the expected account before retrieving it.
The S3 URI that locates the Smithy model file used to define the MCP server's API interface for the Bedrock agent core gateway target.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.authorize.text: This is the list of allowed audiences (the `aud` claim) for the JWT token, and the token must contain one of these values in its audience claim to be accepted by the custom JWT authorizer.
Specifies the list of client IDs that are permitted to access the API through this custom JWT authorizer, restricting authorization to known OAuth2 clients.
Lists the OAuth 2.0 scopes that must be present in the JWT token for the custom JWT authorizer to allow the request, restricting access to tokens with the required scope claims.
Specifies the expected value or match condition for a custom claim when using a custom JWT authorizer, allowing the agent to authorize requests based on token claims.
Specifies the comparison operator used to evaluate whether the value of a custom claim in the JWT matches the configured authorizing claim match value.
Specifies the expected claim value that must be matched for the custom JWT authorizer to authorize requests to the Bedrock agent core harness.
Specifies the exact string value that a custom claim in the JWT token must match for the authorizer to grant access.
This list defines the set of allowed string values that the corresponding JWT claim must contain (when the claim is a string list) for the request to be authorized by the custom JWT authorizer.

Specifies the expected data type (e.g., string, number, boolean) for the value of an inbound JWT claim, enabling the custom JWT authorizer to correctly parse and validate that claim during request authorization.
The discovery URL that the custom JWT authorizer calls to obtain the OpenID Connect configuration and JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) used for verifying JWT tokens.
Determines the IP address version (IPv4 or IPv6) assigned to the private endpoint of the managed VPC resource used by the custom JWT authorizer to access the agent core harness.
Specifies the domain name used for routing traffic to the custom JWT authorizer's private endpoint inside the managed VPC.
The security group IDs to attach to the managed VPC that backs the private endpoint for the custom JWT authorizer.
Specifies the subnet IDs inside the managed VPC where the private endpoint for the custom JWT authorizer is deployed, allowing the endpoint to be attached to those subnets.
The tags to assign to the AWS-managed VPC resource that hosts the private endpoint for the custom JWT authorizer, enabling resource identification and cost tracking.
The ID of the VPC in which the managed VPC resource for the private endpoint is provisioned, enabling network isolation for the custom JWT authorizer.
The identifier of the VPC Lattice resource configuration that defines the self-managed lattice resource used as the private endpoint for the custom JWT authorizer.

Specifies a list of private endpoint overrides that tell the custom JWT authorizer how to reach a JWT issuer or JWKS endpoint through private network routes (such as VPC endpoints) instead of the public internet, so token validation can occur within a private environment.
Specifies the IP address type (ipv4, ipv6, or dualstack) used by the managed VPC resource's private endpoint that connects to the custom JWT authorizer.
Specifies the routing domain name used for the private endpoint within the managed VPC to direct requests to the custom JWT authorizer.
Specifies the list of security group IDs for the managed VPC resource that backs the private endpoint override used by the custom JWT authorizer configuration.
The subnet IDs within the managed VPC where the private endpoint for the custom JWT authorizer is deployed, ensuring the endpoint is accessible from those subnets.
Tags to assign to the managed VPC resource that provides the private endpoint override for the custom JWT authorizer.
The ID of the VPC in which the managed VPC resource for the custom JWT authorizer's private endpoint is provisioned.
The unique identifier (such as an ARN) of the VPC Lattice resource configuration that exposes the self-managed private endpoint used by the custom JWT authorizer for private API access.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.environme.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Elastic File System (EFS) access point used by the Bedrock agent core harness to mount the filesystem in the agent's runtime environment.

Defines the absolute directory path within the agent's runtime container where the specified Amazon EFS access point filesystem is mounted, making the filesystem available at that location for the agent to read from or write to.
Defines the S3 access point configuration for a file system mount, specifying the access point ARN (and optionally a mount path) through which the Bedrock agent accesses files stored in S3.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 access point that the agent's core runtime environment uses to access files in the configured S3 filesystem.
Specifies the directory or mount point within the attached filesystem where the agent core's session data is stored and persisted across operations.
The absolute filesystem path inside the agent runtime environment where the session storage volume is mounted, determining where session state and temporary data are persisted across invocations.
Specifies the maximum duration, in seconds, that an idle agent runtime session can remain open before the agent core environment automatically terminates it to free up resources.
The list of VPC subnet IDs in which the agent core runtime environment is deployed, defining the network subnets for the harness when configured for VPC-based networking.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.memory.ag.text: Configures the agent's core memory behavior in the harness, including enabling or disabling memory and specifying the memory type (such as session summary) used by the agent.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the memory resource that the agent core uses to store and recall session context, required when configuring agent core memory.
Defines the retrieval configuration for the agent's core memory, such as the retrieval type (SEMANTIC or HYBRID) and the number of results to return when the agent recalls past interactions.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.model.text: Specifies the foundation model configuration (e.g., model ID or inference profile) that the Bedrock agent uses to process prompts and generate responses.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.model.bed.text: Specifies the Amazon Bedrock model configuration for the core harness, including the model ARN and inference settings, to define the model used to test the agent.
Specifies the API format (e.g., `INVOKE_MODEL` or `CONVERSE`) used to invoke the underlying foundation model in the agent's bedrock model configuration.
Configures the maximum number of tokens the Bedrock model is allowed to generate in a single response, effectively capping the output length.
The identifier of the Amazon Bedrock foundation model (e.g., anthropic.claude-v2) that the agent core harness uses to generate responses.

Sets the sampling temperature for the Bedrock foundation model in the agent's model configuration, where lower values produce more deterministic and focused responses and higher values increase randomness and creativity.

In the Bedrock model configuration for the agent's core harness, `top_p` sets the nucleus sampling probability threshold (0 to 1) controlling how many top tokens accumulate to that probability mass during response generation.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.model.gem.text: Specifies the Gemini-specific inference configuration (e.g., temperature, topP, and token limits) for the foundation model used by the agent core harness.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the API key used to authenticate calls to the Gemini model configured for this agent.
The maximum number of tokens the Gemini model can generate in a single response when used by the Bedrock agent core harness.
Specifies the identifier of the Google Gemini foundation model that the Bedrock agent core harness uses for generation.
Specifies the sampling temperature to apply to the Gemini model, controlling the degree of randomness in generated responses.
Sets the top-k sampling parameter for Gemini model inference, which limits the model to consider only the k most likely tokens at each generation step.

Specifies the top_p (nucleus sampling) parameter for the Gemini model configuration within the agent core harness, controlling the cumulative probability threshold for token selection during text generation.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.model.lit.text: The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the API key required to authenticate with the LiteLLM model endpoint.
The maximum number of tokens the LiteLLM model is allowed to generate in a single response.
The model identifier string required by LiteLLM to route requests to the underlying provider, typically formatted as 'provider/model-name' (e.g., 'openai/gpt-4').

The temperature parameter controls the randomness of the model's generated responses, with lower values making the output more deterministic and focused, and higher values increasing creativity and variability.
Specifies the top-p (nucleus sampling) value for the LiteLLM model configuration, determining the cumulative probability cutoff for token selection during generation.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.model.ope.text: Specifies the OpenAI API format (e.g., 'chat' or 'responses') the agent uses when invoking this model via the OpenAI-compatible model configuration.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the OpenAI API key used to authenticate requests for the OpenAI model configured in this core harness agent.
Specifies the maximum number of tokens the OpenAI-compatible model can generate in a single response for the Bedrock agent core harness, controlling output length.
The unique identifier of the OpenAI-compatible model to use in the core harness's OpenAI model configuration, such as a model name or endpoint ID.

Sets the sampling temperature for the OpenAI model used by the agent core harness, controlling the randomness of generated responses (lower values are more deterministic, higher values are more creative).
Sets the top_p nucleus sampling parameter for the OpenAI model, controlling output diversity by capping the cumulative token probability mass considered during generation.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.skills.gi.text: Defines the Git-based source repository that provides the skill's implementation, allowing the harness to pull the skill code from version control.
Specifies the authentication credentials (such as a username, password, or personal access token) used to access the private Git repository that contains the skill's source code.
This field specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a secret in AWS Secrets Manager that holds the authentication credentials for accessing the Git repository defined for the skill.
The username used for Git authentication when the agent's skill fetches its source from a Git repository.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.system_pr.text: The text of the system prompt that defines the agent's behavior and instructions for the AWS Bedrock agent core harness.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.tags.key.text: The key of a tag (key-value pair) attached to the AWS Bedrock Agent Core Harness, used to categorize or identify the resource within AWS.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.tools.con.text: Defines the authentication settings that the agent core gateway uses when making outbound calls to external tools or APIs.

Specifies the AWS IAM configuration used to authenticate outbound requests from the agent core gateway to external tool endpoints, typically including an IAM role ARN for signing and authorizing API calls.
When set, the `none` field under outbound_auth selects the 'no authentication' scheme, meaning outbound requests from the agent core gateway are sent without any authentication credentials.
The `oauth` object under `outbound_auth` specifies the OAuth 2.0 configuration (such as client credentials and token endpoint) used by the agent core gateway to authenticate outgoing requests.
Specifies additional key-value pairs to be included in the OAuth 2.0 token request for outbound authentication of the agent core gateway.

Specifies the default redirect URI that the OAuth authorization server will call back to after successful authentication, used as the return location when the agent core gateway requests OAuth tokens for outbound API access.
Specifies the OAuth 2.0 grant type used by the agent core to authenticate outbound requests through the agent core gateway.

Specifies the list of OAuth 2.0 scopes to request from the authorization server for the Agent Core gateway's outbound authentication, controlling the permissions granted when invoking the configured tool.
Specifies a description of the inline function, which the agent uses to understand when and how to invoke the tool.
Defines the JSON Schema that declares the input parameters an inline function tool expects, used for tool invocation validation in the Bedrock agent core harness.
Contains the endpoint URI and optional HTTP headers for connecting the tool to a remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
Specifies the HTTP headers, such as authorization or accept headers, to include when connecting to the remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server defined in this tool configuration.
Specifies the URL endpoint of a remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, which the agent's tool configuration connects to in order to discover and invoke the tools exposed by that server.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.tools.typ.text: Specifies the type of a tool in the agent's tools list, such as ACTION_GROUP, KNOWLEDGE_BASE, or FUNCTION, which determines how the agent invokes the tool.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_harness.truncatio.text: The maximum number of recent conversation messages to retain when the sliding window truncation strategy is applied.
The number of most recent conversation messages to preserve in their original form (i.e., exclude from summarization) when the agent core harness truncates conversation history via summarization.
Specifies the system prompt the agent uses to generate a summary of past conversation turns when the chat history exceeds the configured truncation limit.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_memory.created_at.text: The time, as an ISO 8601 string, at which this agent core memory object was created in AWS Bedrock.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_memory.failure_re.text: The failure reason reported by AWS Bedrock when a core memory operation (such as creating or updating the core memory) fails, providing details about why the operation was unsuccessful.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_memory.indexed_ke.text: Specifies the name of a memory key that the agent indexes in its core memory, enabling structured retrieval of stored information for the Bedrock agent.

Defines the data type of each key in the core memory's indexed_keys list (e.g., string, number), determining how that key's value is validated and interpreted when indexing and querying core memory entries.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_memory.memory_str.text: Defines the configuration for a custom memory strategy, allowing the Bedrock agent to use a tailored memory implementation instead of a predefined strategy.

The `episodic_override` object configures custom settings for episodic memory in the Bedrock agent's custom memory strategy, including the time-to-live for retaining recent conversation sessions and flags for enabling episodic memory processing.
Specifies the text to append to the prompt used during the consolidation phase of episodic memory in the custom memory strategy, enabling customization of how the agent summarizes past interactions.
The unique identifier (such as a model ID or ARN) of the Amazon Bedrock foundation model used to consolidate episodic memory entries in the custom memory strategy's episodic override.

Specifies the extraction configuration for the episodic memory override, which determines how the agent extracts and processes episodic memories from conversation history via a custom prompt template.
Adds a custom instruction string to the end of the prompt used during episodic memory extraction for the custom memory strategy.
The ARN or ID of an Amazon Bedrock foundation model used to extract and summarize episodic memories from conversation history.

In the aws_bedrock_agent_core_memory resource, this string is appended to the prompt used when generating reflections for episodic memories, allowing you to inject custom guidance into the reflection process.

Specifies the JSON schema object that defines the structure and validation constraints for memory records produced by the reflection step of the episodic override in a custom memory strategy for an AWS Bedrock Agent Core Memory resource.
Defines the metadata schema for memory records by specifying a list of metadata fields (such as name and type) used by the reflective episodic memory in the custom memory strategy.
Determines how metadata for the memory record is extracted from the input data, specifying either a foundation model prompt or a regex pattern to populate the metadata schema fields.
Configures how the LLM extracts metadata fields for the reflection memory record schema, specifying the model and prompt template to use for extraction.
The definition field contains the prompt or instruction text that guides the LLM to extract the relevant metadata fields from the memory record according to the specified metadata schema.
The instruction provided to the LLM that guides how metadata fields are extracted from conversation turns into the metadata schema for the episodic memory reflection.
Defines the validation configuration for metadata extracted by the LLM, ensuring that extracted values conform to expected formats or rules before being saved to the memory record.
Specifies the maximum numeric value allowed for a metadata field that is validated as a number during LLM-based extraction, enforcing an upper bound on the extracted value.

Defines the lower bound (minimum value) that a validated numeric metadata field extracted by the LLM must satisfy, used in the number validation rules for the memory record schema's metadata extraction configuration.
Defines validation rules for string-list values extracted by the large language model during metadata extraction for memory records.
Specifies the list of allowed string values that the extracted metadata must match for the LLM extraction string list validation to be considered valid.
The maximum number of items allowed in a string list that is extracted as metadata for an episodic memory record, used to validate the length of list-valued metadata fields during LLM extraction.
Defines validation parameters for string metadata values during LLM extraction, specifying required status, minimum and maximum length, and a regex pattern.

Specifies the list of exact string values that the LLM is allowed to extract for this metadata field, so that during memory record extraction any value not appearing in this list is treated as invalid and fails validation.
Defines the name (key) of a metadata attribute in the schema for episodic memory records, used to structure the metadata stored with each memory.
Specifies the JSON Schema type (e.g., 'object') for the metadata schema associated with a memory record schema in the reflection configuration of an episodic override for a custom memory strategy.
The Amazon Bedrock foundation model ID used to generate reflective insights or summaries from episodic memory in the custom memory strategy.

Specifies the list of namespaces that the reflection process uses to group and consolidate episodic memories within the custom memory strategy's episodic override configuration, enabling the agent to synthesize and retrieve across those namespaces.

Configures the self-managed vector store (typically Amazon OpenSearch Serverless) used by the agent's custom memory, including connection details like the collection ARN, vector index name, and field mappings for storing and retrieving conversation memory.
Specifies the number of recent conversation turns retained as historical context for the self-managed memory strategy in the Bedrock agent core memory.
Specifies the invocation configuration for the self-managed memory strategy, including the AWS Lambda function ARN and method used to execute memory fetch and update operations.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket to which the payload from the custom memory strategy's Lambda invocation is delivered for processing.
The ARN of the SNS topic to which the Bedrock agent publishes memory events for a self-managed custom memory strategy.
Specifies the message-based trigger condition for a self-managed custom memory strategy, defining when an incoming agent conversation message triggers memory extraction or storage.
Specifies the number of messages that must be exchanged in the session before the message-based trigger fires and the custom memory strategy captures or updates memory.

The time_based_trigger specifies a recurring schedule (using rate or cron expressions) that determines when the self-managed memory extraction is automatically run, controlling how often session data is captured into the core memory.
The number of seconds of session inactivity after which the time-based trigger condition fires, causing the self-managed custom memory strategy to run its memory consolidation action.
Configures the token-based trigger condition for the self-managed memory strategy, determining the token count threshold at which the agent's core memory is updated.
The token count threshold that, when reached in the conversation, triggers the self-managed custom memory strategy operation.
Specifies the Amazon Bedrock model or inference profile ID used to consolidate semantic memories when the semantic override consolidation is enabled.

Specifies the extraction configuration (such as prompt templates or extraction rules) used by the custom semantic memory strategy to identify and extract memory-relevant facts and relationships from conversation transcripts when semantic override is enabled.
Appends a custom string to the prompt used during semantic extraction of agent memory, adding instructions for how memories should be derived from conversation.
The ID or Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the foundation model used to perform semantic extraction, overriding the default model for deriving memories from conversations in the custom memory strategy.

Specifies a custom prompt and token limits that override the default summary generation for the core memory custom strategy, enabling you to control how conversation sessions are summarized into memory.

Specifies a custom text string that is appended to the prompt used during the consolidation step of the custom memory strategy, allowing you to influence how the agent summarizes and consolidates stored session memory.
The unique identifier of the Amazon Bedrock foundation model used by the consolidation step to summarize and merge stored memory observations in a custom memory strategy.
The unique identifier of the Bedrock model used to consolidate and summarize session memories when the user preference override is enabled for the custom memory strategy.

In the custom memory strategy of an AWS Bedrock Agent Core Memory, this extraction configuration defines the instruction or template that tells the agent how to parse and save user preferences from interactions, overriding the default preference extraction behavior.

The text to append to the prompt that instructs the agent on how to extract user preferences from the conversation, providing additional customization for the user preference override in the custom memory strategy.
Specifies the Amazon Bedrock model ID used for extracting user preferences from conversation history when the custom memory strategy's user preference override is enabled.
The creation timestamp of the custom memory strategy, indicating when it was first configured.
The description of the custom memory strategy, which provides a human-readable explanation of the strategy's purpose and configuration within the Bedrock agent's memory settings.
Defines the JSON Schema that specifies the structure and fields of each memory record stored by the custom memory strategy.
Defines the list of metadata fields (each with a field name and data type) that are stored as metadata for each memory record in the custom memory strategy.
Defines how the metadata fields of a memory record are populated, specifying whether extraction is performed by an AWS Lambda function or the Bedrock agent itself.
Configures the large language model (LLM) and its prompt used to extract metadata field values from agent conversations for a custom memory strategy.
The definition is a natural-language instruction that tells the LLM exactly which metadata fields to extract from the conversation and how to populate them for the memory record.

Specifies the natural language instruction that guides the large language model to extract the metadata values from a conversation and populate the fields defined in the metadata schema of the custom memory strategy.
Specifies validation constraints for number-typed metadata fields extracted from memory, such as minimum and maximum allowed values, ensuring numeric extractions fall within the defined range.
Specifies the maximum numeric value allowed for a metadata field during LLM-based extraction validation, so that any extracted number exceeding this threshold is rejected.
Specifies the minimum numeric value permitted for a metadata field that undergoes LLM extraction and numeric validation.
Defines the list of permitted string values that an extracted metadata field must match for LLM-based extraction validation to succeed.
Sets the maximum number of string elements permitted in a metadata value that the model extracts, so that validation fails if the extracted string list exceeds this count.

Configures the validation constraints for string-type metadata fields in the custom memory record schema, including minimum and maximum length and a regular expression pattern that the extracted value must match.
The list of permitted string values that an extracted metadata string must match for validation to pass in the LLM extraction config.
Determines whether the agent extracts the metadata field's value directly from the user's input (e.g., EXTRACT) or infers it from the conversation context (e.g., INFER) when creating a memory record.
The key identifies the name of a metadata field in the metadata schema that defines the structure of custom memory records for the agent's core memory strategy.
Sets the JSON Schema data type for the metadata schema within a custom memory strategy, typically 'object' to define a structured metadata object.
Specifies a unique name for the custom memory strategy so the agent can store and recall custom memory records within its core memory.
Defines the namespace templates for the custom memory strategy, where each string can include dynamic placeholders like $[sessionId] to generate scoped namespaces for storing memories.
Defines the list of namespace strings used to isolate and organize memory entries within the custom memory strategy, so each namespace acts as a separate memory domain for the agent.
Indicates whether the custom memory strategy is enabled or disabled for the Bedrock Agent's core memory, with values typically 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
The unique identifier for a custom memory strategy within an agent's core memory configuration, used to reference the strategy when managing memory operations.
The type field of a custom memory strategy specifies the concrete backend implementation (for example, an Amazon S3 table store) that the Bedrock agent will use to store and retrieve memory data.
This read-only attribute provides the timestamp of the most recent update to the custom memory strategy within the AWS Bedrock agent core memory configuration.
Configures the episodic memory strategy for the Bedrock agent, determining how past conversation histories are stored and used for recall during future interactions.

The description field provides an optional, user-defined explanation for the episodic memory strategy, which stores and recalls past conversation context to help the agent maintain continuity and relevance in its responses.

For the Bedrock agent's episodic memory strategy, this object specifies the record schema that defines the fields (name and type) for each stored memory entry, enabling the agent to store and recall structured interaction data.

Defines the list of metadata attributes (each with name and type) that can accompany episodic memory records, enabling structured storage and retrieval of additional context alongside each memory entry.

Specifies how metadata fields in the episodic memory record's schema are automatically extracted from conversation traces, including the extraction method (e.g., a Bedrock model) and the field selection mode (e.g., ALL or SUBSET).
Defines the configuration for using a large language model to automatically extract metadata fields from memory records within the episodic memory strategy's metadata schema.

Defines the natural-language instructions that guide the LLM in which metadata fields to extract from a conversation and how to populate them for an episodic memory record, following the specified metadata schema.
A natural-language instruction that guides the LLM on which metadata fields to extract from a memory record and how to map them into the schema defined by the metadata_schema.
The validation object specifies a regular expression pattern that the LLM-extracted metadata value must match to be considered valid for storage in the episodic memory record.
Defines validation rules for numeric metadata values extracted by an LLM, such as specifying minimum and maximum allowable numbers.
The upper bound for numeric validation of LLM-extracted metadata values, used to reject numbers above this maximum when validating against the memory record schema.
Defines the minimum numeric value that an LLM-extracted number must meet to pass validation for the metadata schema in the episodic memory strategy.
Defines validation rules for a string-list metadata field, specifying an allowed set of strings that the extracted list must match after LLM-based extraction.

Specifies the definitive list of permissible string values that the LLM-extracted metadata field must match during memory record validation, constraining the episodic memory's metadata to a controlled vocabulary.

Sets the maximum number of items allowed in a string list value within the memory record metadata schema when the metadata is extracted and validated using LLM extraction in the episodic memory strategy.
Restricts the LLM-extracted metadata value to one of the listed string values, enforcing an allowed-values constraint during validation.

Determines whether the metadata schema for episodic memory records is automatically populated by the agent (AUTO) or defined through custom configuration (CUSTOM), controlling how metadata fields are extracted and stored.
The key that names a single metadata attribute within the episodic memory record's metadata schema, used to identify and store custom metadata on each memory record.
Specifies the JSON Schema type (e.g., 'OBJECT') for the metadata schema in the episodic memory strategy, determining the structure of metadata attached to each memory record.

For the Bedrock Agent Core Memory resource, this field defines the list of namespaces used by the episodic memory strategy to partition memories into distinct logical scopes for targeted storage and retrieval.
Configures how often the agent reflects on past episodes and the maximum number of reflection summaries to retain, enabling episodic memory to distill insights from prior interactions.
Specifies the schema, as a set of named fields with associated data types, that defines the structure of memory records stored by the agent's episodic memory reflection configuration.
Defines the list of field objects (name and data type) that constitute the metadata schema for each episodic memory record, allowing structured filtering of memories.

This object configures the LLM-based metadata extraction process for the episodic memory strategy, specifying the prompt and model settings used to extract structured metadata fields from memory record content.
Defines the natural-language prompt that instructs the LLM to extract metadata fields from the conversation to populate the record's metadata schema.
