The instruction string that tells the large language model which metadata fields to extract from an episodic conversation or interaction for inclusion in the memory record schema.
Defines numeric validation rules (such as minimum and maximum allowed values) for a metadata field extracted by the LLM during memory reflection in the Bedrock Agent Core Memory configuration.

The maximum numeric value permitted for a number-typed metadata field extracted by the LLM extraction configuration, used to validate extracted values before storing them in the episodic memory record.
The minimum numeric value that an extracted metadata field must satisfy to pass validation when the metadata schema specifies a number type.
Specifies the allowable string values that the LLM extraction can assign to a metadata list field, ensuring any extracted value matches one of these permitted strings.
Specifies the maximum number of items allowed in a list of strings when validation uses the 'string_list_validation' rule in the LLM extraction configuration for memory metadata.
Specifies the validation rules (such as pattern matching or length limits) applied to string values in the metadata extracted from memory for the LLM-based extraction configuration.

Defines the permitted string values that the extracted metadata field must match when the LLM-based extraction configuration applies string validation to the metadata schema of the episodic memory strategy's reflection configuration.
The metadata field name (key) for a single entry in the memory record's metadata schema, defining which custom metadata attribute is stored for episodic memory records.
Lists the namespaces that the episodic memory reflection configuration is scoped to, restricting which memory entries the agent considers when generating reflections.
Indicates whether the episodic memory strategy is enabled or disabled for the agent's core memory.
The type of the episodic memory strategy, which must be set to the value 'EPISODIC_MEMORY' for the agent to use episodic memory.
Configures the semantic memory strategy for the agent's core memory, specifying how the agent stores and retrieves semantic memories using a vector index.
The timestamp indicating when the semantic memory strategy was created.
A user-supplied description for the semantic memory strategy that explains how the agent's core memory captures and uses semantic knowledge.
Defines the JSON schema that specifies the structure of memory records stored by the semantic memory strategy, including field names and data types.
Defines the JSON schema that specifies the structure and allowed fields of the metadata that can be attached to each memory record in the semantic memory strategy.
Defines how the metadata fields of a semantic memory record are automatically populated by a model from the conversation, such as specifying the extraction prompt and inference model.
Configures the LLM used to automatically extract metadata from memory records, specifying the model ARN and prompt template for extraction.
Specifies a natural-language description that instructs the large language model how to extract metadata fields from each memory record stored in semantic memory.
Specifies the instruction text that guides the large language model on what metadata fields to extract from the memory content to populate the metadata schema.
Defines numeric constraints such as minimum and maximum allowed values for a number-type metadata field extracted by the LLM during semantic memory record validation.
Specifies the maximum value allowed for a numeric metadata field when validating extracted values during LLM extraction for a Bedrock agent's semantic memory record schema.
Defines the minimum numeric value that an extracted number field must equal or exceed to pass LLM extraction validation.
Specifies validation rules for string list metadata fields extracted by the LLM during semantic memory extraction, including constraints like allowed values and maximum number of elements.
Defines the fixed set of string values that the LLM-extracted metadata value must be restricted to, ensuring the extraction output matches one of the allowed options.
Sets the maximum number of items permitted in a string list that the LLM can extract for a metadata schema field, enforcing a size limit for list values during semantic memory extraction.
Specifies the validation constraints for string fields in the metadata schema extracted by the LLM, enforcing rules like allowed patterns and length restrictions.
The list of permitted string values that a metadata field must match to be considered valid during LLM extraction.
Defines the method used to extract metadata values for semantic memory records, controlling whether metadata is parsed automatically from the record content or derived from a predefined schema.
This key defines the field name (attribute name) for an entry in the metadata schema of a semantic memory record, specifying the key under which metadata values are stored in the memory strategy.
The name of the semantic memory strategy configuration, used to identify this strategy within the agent's memory setup.

In the semantic memory strategy for an Amazon Bedrock agent, this list defines the namespace templates used to partition and organize memory entries into distinct semantic namespaces, so that memories can be scoped and retrieved by the generated namespace.
Specifies the list of vector store namespaces used to scope the storage and retrieval of semantic memory entries for this strategy in the Bedrock agent's core memory configuration.
Specifies whether the semantic memory strategy is enabled, with valid values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.

The user-defined unique identifier for the semantic memory strategy, used to reference and manage this strategy within the agent's core memory configuration, such as when updating or deleting its associated memory data.
Specifies the vector store provider (such as AMAZON_BEDROCK, OPENAI, PINECONE, or REDIS) used for semantic memory in the agent's memory strategy.
The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the agent's core memory semantic memory strategy was last modified, useful for auditing changes to the memory settings.

Configure the summary memory strategy for a Bedrock agent, specifying the summary length (short, medium, or long) and the number of recent conversation tokens to use when generating session summaries.
Defines the structure of the memory records that the summary memory strategy stores, by specifying a list of fields (each with a name and data type) that make up each memory record.
Specifies the list of metadata field definitions for memory records stored under a summary memory strategy, where each object represents a metadata attribute's name and data type.
Configures how the agent extracts the metadata fields defined in the parent metadata schema from conversation content when using the summary memory strategy.
Configures the large language model and its inference settings used to extract metadata fields for summary memory records from the conversation input.
Specifies the natural-language prompt/instructions that guide the LLM to extract metadata fields from the conversation for inclusion in the memory record's metadata schema.
Specifies the natural language instruction provided to the large language model to guide how it should extract and populate the metadata fields defined in the metadata schema for a memory record.
Defines validation rules for the metadata extracted by the LLM, such as requiring fields to be present or non-empty, ensuring the extracted output conforms to the memory record schema.
The inclusive maximum numeric value allowed for a validated number when the LLM extraction config applies number validation.
The minimum numeric value that a number in the metadata field must meet to be considered valid during LLM-based extraction for the memory record schema.
Configures validation rules for extracted metadata fields that are expected to be a list of strings, specifying constraints such as minimum and maximum list length and allowed string values.
Specifies the allowed values for a string list metadata field, restricting the LLM extraction to only these strings.

Specifies the maximum number of items allowed in a string list value for the metadata schema, enforced during validation in the LLM extraction configuration for the summary memory strategy's memory record schema.
Defines validation constraints for string fields in the extracted memory metadata, such as minimum/maximum length and regex pattern requirements.

Defines the set of allowed string values for a string-validated metadata field in the LLM extraction configuration of the metadata schema for a summary memory strategy, so that extracted metadata values outside this list are considered invalid.
The key (property name) of an entry within the metadata schema for the summary memory strategy, defining a structured metadata field that accompanies each memory record.
Specifies the JSON Schema type (such as 'object') for the metadata schema, which dictates the shape of metadata attached to memory records in the summary memory strategy.
The user-defined name that uniquely identifies this summary memory strategy within the agent's core memory configuration, used to reference the strategy when storing or retrieving memories.
The namespaces field specifies the memory namespaces in which the summary memory strategy stores and retrieves summaries for the agent's conversation memory.
Controls whether the agent's summary memory is active, with allowed values ENABLED or DISABLED.
A customer-defined unique identifier for this summary memory strategy, used to reference and manage the strategy within the agent's memory configuration.

Specifies the type of conversation summary memory to use, with allowed values 'RECENT' (maintains a summary of the most recent conversation segments) or 'LONG_TERM' (maintains a comprehensive summary across the entire conversation history).
The timestamp indicating when the summary memory strategy configuration was last updated, reflecting changes to the summary prompt template or other strategy settings.
Configures the user preference memory strategy, which enables the Bedrock agent to store and utilize user preferences across sessions for personalized responses.
Provides a human-readable description of the user preference memory strategy that the Bedrock agent uses to retain and recall user preferences across sessions.
Defines the JSON schema that specifies the structure and data types of user preference memory records stored by the agent, including valid keys and value types.
Defines how metadata fields are extracted from user interactions for the memory record, specifying either the agent's built-in prompt or a custom prompt to perform extraction.

Defines the settings for LLM-based extraction of metadata from user conversations, including the prompt template that instructs the model how to map conversation content to the memory schema's metadata fields.
Defines the natural language instruction that tells the LLM what metadata to extract from the conversation for storage in the user preference memory.
The instruction text that guides the LLM to extract user preference memory records from conversations, specifying what to identify and how to format the extracted preferences.
Specifies the minimum and/or maximum allowed values for a numeric metadata field when extracted by the LLM in a user preference memory strategy.
Specifies the maximum numeric value that a metadata field extracted by the LLM must not exceed when number validation is applied.
The minimum numeric value allowed for a number extracted by the LLM when validating metadata fields in user preference memory.

Defines allowed values and item count constraints for string list metadata fields, which the LLM extraction configuration uses to validate extracted values before storing them in the memory record's metadata.
Specifies the allowed values that the extracted string list must match, ensuring metadata list values are constrained to this defined set.
Specifies the maximum number of items allowed in a string array extracted from user input for memory record creation.

The `string_validation` object specifies the validation constraints for string-type metadata fields within the user preference memory strategy, defining allowed values or a regular expression pattern that the extraction config applies when validating LLM-extracted metadata.
The list of allowed string values that the LLM extraction must choose from when populating a metadata field, enforcing that the extracted value matches one of these permitted strings for validation.
Specifies the extraction approach for metadata in the user preference memory record schema, determining how the agent populates metadata values from conversation context.
Specifies the name of a metadata field in the memory record schema for user preference memory, defining how user preference context is stored and retrieved.
Specifies the schema type of the metadata schema used to store user preferences within the Bedrock agent core memory's user preference memory strategy.
The list of namespaces that scope user preference memory to specific application domains, allowing the agent to store and retrieve user preferences separately for each namespace.
Determines whether the user preference memory strategy is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for the Amazon Bedrock agent.
The unique identifier for this user preference memory strategy, which the agent uses to reference and manage how user preferences are stored and recalled during interactions.
Specifies the memory strategy type as USER_PREFERENCE, which enables the agent to record and use user preferences across sessions.
The timestamp of when the user preference memory was last updated.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_memory.stream_del.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Kinesis Data Stream that serves as the destination for streaming core memory events from the Bedrock agent.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_memory.updated_at.text: The read-only timestamp, in ISO 8601 format, indicating when the agent core memory was last updated.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_oauth2_credential.text: This is the client identifier assigned by Atlassian to the OAuth2 application, used by the Bedrock agent to initiate the OAuth2 authorization flow.
The client secret for the Atlassian OAuth2 application, used to authenticate the Bedrock agent's credential provider with Atlassian services such as Jira or Confluence.

Specifies the source of the Atlassian OAuth2 client secret, typically an AWS Secrets Manager secret ARN, which the Bedrock agent uses to retrieve the client secret for the OAuth2 provider configuration.
The domain name that overrides the default endpoint for the custom OAuth2 provider when using a private endpoint, typically pointing to an internal VPC hostname.
Specifies the VPC ID and subnet IDs for the private endpoint of the OAuth2 credential provider, allowing secure access through a managed VPC.
Specifies whether the private endpoint uses an IPv4 or IPv6 address type within the managed VPC resource.
The domain name used to route requests through the managed VPC's private endpoint to the custom OAuth2 provider.
Specifies the list of security group IDs to attach to the managed VPC resource that backs the private endpoint for the custom OAuth2 credential provider, controlling network access to that endpoint.
The list of subnet IDs for the managed VPC resource used by the private endpoint override, determining the subnets where the private endpoint for the OAuth2 credential provider is placed.
The ID of the VPC in which the managed VPC resource for the private endpoint is provisioned.
The identifier (such as an ARN) of the Amazon VPC Lattice resource configuration that this self-managed lattice private endpoint override uses for routing traffic.
The client ID of the GitHub OAuth application used to authenticate with GitHub.
The client secret issued by GitHub when creating the OAuth2 application, which is used to authenticate the credential provider when exchanging tokens with GitHub's OAuth2 endpoints.
The client ID issued by Google for the OAuth2 application, used to authenticate AWS Bedrock Agent's requests to Google services.
The client secret issued by Google for the configured OAuth2 application, used to authenticate the Bedrock agent when obtaining an access token for Google APIs.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the Google OAuth2 client secret, used as the source for the OAuth2 credential provider configuration.
The client identifier (client_id) issued by the OAuth2 authorization server to identify the Bedrock agent application when it requests access tokens.
The OAuth2 client secret that the agent uses to authenticate with the external application's authorization server.
The client ID (application identifier) assigned by LinkedIn to the OAuth2 application, used by the Bedrock agent to authenticate when connecting to LinkedIn.
The client secret from the LinkedIn application used to authenticate with LinkedIn's OAuth2 API for this credential provider.
Specifies the source of the LinkedIn OAuth2 client secret, such as an AWS Secrets Manager reference, that Bedrock Agent uses when authenticating to LinkedIn.
The client_id specifies the application (client) ID of the Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) app registration used by this OAuth2 credential provider to request tokens.
The client secret for the Microsoft OAuth 2.0 application used to authenticate the Bedrock agent when requesting access tokens for Microsoft services.
Specifies the source of the Microsoft OAuth2 client secret, such as indicating that the secret is referenced from AWS Secrets Manager rather than provided directly in the configuration.
The client ID of the Salesforce OAuth2 application used to authenticate requests from the Bedrock agent.
The client secret used by the Bedrock agent to authenticate against Salesforce during the OAuth2 token exchange.
Specifies the source from which the Salesforce OAuth2 client secret is retrieved, commonly an AWS Secrets Manager secret reference.
The OAuth2 client ID for the Slack application used to authenticate the Bedrock agent when connecting to Slack.
The client secret for the Slack OAuth2 application, used by the Bedrock agent to authenticate with Slack's APIs.
The client identifier (client ID) that the Bedrock agent core uses when authenticating to the OAuth2 authorization server, returned as part of the provider's output configuration.
Specifies the domain name used by the private endpoint override for the OAuth2 provider, allowing connections to be routed to a custom VPC endpoint instead of the provider's public endpoint.
Specifies the IP address type (such as IPv4 or IPv6) for the private endpoint's network interfaces within the managed VPC resource of the OAuth2 credential provider.
The routing domain associated with the managed VPC resource, used to resolve and route requests to the OAuth2 provider through the private endpoint.
Specifies the list of security group IDs to attach to the managed VPC resource for the private endpoint, controlling network access to the OAuth2 credential provider's private endpoint.
This field specifies the subnet IDs inside the managed VPC that the private endpoint for the OAuth2 credential provider will be associated with.
Tags (key-value pairs) to assign to the managed VPC resource used for the private endpoint override, enabling you to categorize, manage, and track this VPC resource.

The unique identifier of the AWS-managed VPC that hosts the private endpoint for the OAuth2 credential provider's output configuration, enabling connectivity to the OAuth2 provider over a private network.

The identifier (such as the resource configuration name or ARN) of the AWS VPC Lattice resource configuration that backs this self-managed lattice resource, used to route private endpoint traffic for the OAuth2 credential provider.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_online_evaluation.text: Provides the string to match in a rule filter for the Bedrock Agent Core online evaluation configuration, when the filter's value type is STRING, to determine which interactions are evaluated.
The key of a tag attached to the Bedrock agent core online evaluation configuration, used to organize and identify the resource by custom metadata such as environment or project.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_payment_connector.text: The ARN of the credential provider (e.g., an AWS Secrets Manager secret or IAM role) that supplies the API credentials used by the Bedrock agent to authenticate with Coinbase CDP for payment operations.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_payment_manager.a.text: The list of allowed audience values that the JWT token's audience claim must match for the custom JWT authorizer to authorize requests.
Defines the list of OAuth 2.0 scopes that must be present in the JWT token's scope claim for the custom JWT authorizer to grant access.
Specifies the exact string value that the custom JWT authorizer expects for a configured claim in a token, which must be matched to authorize a payment-related request.
Specifies the expected data type (such as string, number, or boolean) of the inbound JWT token's claim value for this custom claim, enabling the authorizer to correctly parse and validate it.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_runtime.agent_run.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Bedrock agent core runtime resource.
Configures the container image and runtime parameters used to execute the agent's code artifact within the Bedrock Agent Core Runtime.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_runtime.authorize.text: The ARN that uniquely identifies a hosting environment permitted to handle requests for the allowed workload configuration of the custom JWT authorizer.
The expected value against which the specified custom JWT claim is compared to determine if the request is authorized.

Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, CONTAINS) used to evaluate the JWT custom claim's actual value against the expected match value in the Bedrock agent core runtime custom JWT authorizer.
Defines the comparison type (e.g., EQUALS, CONTAINS) and the value that a custom JWT claim must match for the authorizer to authorize the request.
Specifies the string value that the custom JWT claim must match for the authorizer to authorize the request.
Defines a set of allowed values for a custom JWT authorizer claim; the token's corresponding claim must match one of the strings in this list to be authorized.
The name of the claim in the incoming JWT token that should be extracted and passed as a custom claim to the agent's runtime context.

Defines the data type to which the value of the JWT claim in the incoming token is cast before it is delivered to the custom authorizer Lambda function (supported values include STRING, NUMBER, and BOOLEAN).
Specifies whether the managed VPC endpoint for the custom JWT authorizer's private endpoint uses IPv4, IPv6, or dual-stack IP addressing.
The routing domain is the DNS domain name used to route requests to the private endpoint's managed VPC resource, which hosts the custom JWT authorizer for the Bedrock agent core runtime.

The list of security group IDs to attach to the managed VPC resource used as the private endpoint for the custom JWT authorizer configuration, controlling which network traffic can reach the endpoint.
The subnet IDs in the managed VPC where AWS deploys the VPC endpoint for the private endpoint configuration of the custom JWT authorizer in the Bedrock Agent Core Runtime.
The ID of the VPC in which AWS creates the managed VPC resource (e.g., an elastic network interface) to privately connect the Bedrock agent runtime to the custom JWT authorizer's private endpoint.
The identifier (ARN) of the Amazon VPC Lattice resource configuration that serves as the private endpoint for the custom JWT authorizer.
Overrides the domain name of the private endpoint that the custom JWT authorizer uses to validate tokens, allowing the authorizer to reach a different service endpoint than the default.

This object specifies the private endpoint host and path used to override the default public endpoint for the custom JWT authorizer, enabling the agent to reach the authorizer within a private network.
Defines the AWS-managed VPC resource that serves as the private endpoint for the custom JWT authorizer's private endpoint override in the Bedrock agent core runtime.

This field specifies the IP address type (IPv4, IPv6, or dual-stack) for the managed VPC private endpoint used to reach the custom JWT authorizer in the Bedrock agent core runtime, overriding the default endpoint IP configuration.
Specifies the custom DNS domain name used to route traffic to the private endpoint of the JWT authorizer within the managed VPC.
Specifies the list of security group IDs to attach to the private endpoint inside the managed VPC for the custom JWT authorizer's private endpoint overrides.
This field specifies the subnet IDs within the managed VPC where the private endpoint for the custom JWT authorizer is deployed, enabling private network access to that authorizer.
A map of key-value tags to apply to the managed VPC resource that backs the private endpoint override for the custom JWT authorizer.
Defines the self-managed AWS VPC Lattice resource that the private endpoint override points to for the custom JWT authorizer, enabling traffic to be routed to a customer-controlled lattice endpoint.

Specifies the identifier (such as the ARN or name) of the Amazon VPC Lattice resource configuration that the self-managed lattice resource for this custom JWT authorizer's private endpoint override uses, allowing the Bedrock agent core runtime to route requests to the authorizer through the configured private endpoint.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_runtime.created_a.text: The creation timestamp of this Bedrock agent core runtime, returned as a read-only string.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_runtime.filesyste.text: Specifies the Amazon EFS access point that the Bedrock Agent Core Runtime uses when reading from or writing to the configured EFS filesystem.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the EFS access point that the Bedrock agent core runtime uses to mount the associated EFS filesystem, enabling the agent to access files through that access point.
The directory path in the agent's runtime environment where the EFS file system is mounted when the agent uses the specified access point.
This object specifies the S3 access point configuration for the agent's file system, providing the access point ARN and the S3 path or prefix that the agent will use to access files in S3.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 access point that grants the Bedrock agent access to the associated S3 file system.
The mount path (e.g., /mnt/data) where the S3 access point is mounted inside the agent's runtime filesystem, enabling the agent to access S3 objects as local files under that path.
Defines the session storage configuration for the agent's file system, specifying the Amazon S3 bucket and optional AWS KMS key used to persist session data and state.

Specifies the file system mount path within the Bedrock agent runtime environment where the session storage volume is mounted, enabling the agent to persist and access session data across invocations.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_runtime.network_c.text: Provides the VPC configuration (security group IDs and subnet IDs) used by the agent's core runtime to access resources within a private network.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_runtime.role_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM service role that the Bedrock agent core runtime assumes to access AWS services and resources on behalf of the agent.

aws_bedrock_agent_core_runtime_endpoint..text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Bedrock agent core runtime endpoint, automatically assigned by AWS to uniquely identify the endpoint for agent invocation.
The version of the Bedrock Agent runtime to use for the endpoint, which controls the runtime behavior and feature set available when invoking the agent through this core runtime endpoint.

aws_bedrock_application_inference_profil.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the inference profile, assigned by AWS when the profile is created.
The AWS-generated unique identifier for the Bedrock application inference profile, used to reference the profile in subsequent API calls.
The name of the inference profile, which must be unique within the AWS account and Region, used to identify the profile when submitting inference requests.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an existing Bedrock inference profile to copy from; when this is set, the new application inference profile inherits the model configuration of that source profile instead of specifying a model ARN directly.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a foundation model or an existing inference profile that is included in the application inference profile's list of models, allowing the profile to invoke that model.
The key of a tag assigned to the Bedrock application inference profile, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the resource within AWS.
The value of a user-defined tag key attached to the Bedrock Application Inference Profile, used to store arbitrary metadata for resource identification, filtering, and cost allocation.

aws_bedrock_automated_reasoning_policy.d.text: An optional, human-readable explanation of the purpose or contents of the automated reasoning policy.

aws_bedrock_automated_reasoning_policy.p.text: Provides a human-readable explanation of a specific value defined within a type in the automated reasoning policy, giving the model additional context for interpreting that value.

aws_bedrock_automated_reasoning_policy.t.text: A list of key-value tags to associate with the AWS Bedrock automated reasoning policy.

aws_bedrock_data_automation_library.tags.text: The key of a tag to attach to the Bedrock Data Automation Library, used for identifying and categorizing the library.

aws_bedrock_data_automation_project.cust.text: Specifies the list of blueprint configurations that the custom output uses to define how Bedrock Data Automation extracts and structures data from the input documents.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the blueprint that defines the custom extraction schema applied to the data automation project's output configuration.
Specifies the stage of the blueprint (e.g., DEVELOPMENT or LIVE) to use for data extraction within the project's custom output configuration.
Sets the version identifier of the blueprint that defines the data extraction schema for this output configuration.

aws_bedrock_data_automation_project.over.text: Specifies the language (such as ENGLISH or MULTI_LANGUAGE) to apply when processing audio files in the data automation project, determining how speech is transcribed and analyzed.

Specifies the language code used for generative AI output when processing audio content in the project's override configuration, such as the language for summaries or insights generated from the audio.
Specifies the list of languages expected in the audio input, which the data automation project uses to process and extract information from the audio.
Specifies the audio modality processing configuration, letting you choose between automatic processing of audio data or overriding it with a custom blueprint ARN.
Specifies whether audio modality processing is enabled or disabled for this Bedrock data automation project, overriding the default audio processing configuration.
The types of sensitive data (e.g., PII categories) that Bedrock Data Automation will detect in the audio content.

Specifies the configuration for detecting and redacting specific PII entity types (such as names, credit card numbers, or addresses) in audio data processed by the AWS Bedrock data automation project, enabling selective redaction of sensitive information.
Specifies the list of personally identifiable information (PII) entity types to detect and redact in audio content, overriding the project's default sensitive data configuration for audio.
Configures the document modality processing type (e.g., extraction or summarization) applied when overriding the project's default document processing settings.
When set, determines whether the document modality processing is enabled or disabled for the project's override configuration.

Controls how sensitive data (such as personally identifiable information) is handled when processing documents in this Bedrock Data Automation project, typically to enable or configure automatic redaction of such content in the extraction output.

Defines the detection scope for sensitive data in documents by listing the specific sensitive data types (e.g., credit card numbers, bank account numbers) that should be detected, overriding any default scope set at the project level.

This object defines the PII entities configuration for document sensitive data handling, specifying which PII entity types to detect and the action to take on them (e.g., redact or mask) when processing documents in the data automation project.

Specifies the list of personally identifiable information (PII) entity types (such as NAME, EMAIL, or PHONE_NUMBER) that the Bedrock data automation project should detect and apply the configured sensitive data handling to for document processing when this override is used.
Specifies how detected PII entities are redacted, either by replacing them with a fixed mask character or by substituting the entity type label.
Configures the document splitter for the Bedrock data automation project, determining how uploaded documents are segmented (e.g., by page or semantic sections) before extraction.
Determines whether the document splitter component is enabled or disabled in the override configuration for this Bedrock data automation project.
Specifies the override settings for how image data is processed in the data automation project, including the extraction type used when extracting content from images.
Specifies whether image modality processing is enabled or disabled in the override configuration, controlling if the data automation project processes image content.

Configures how sensitive data (such as PII) is handled during image extraction in this Bedrock Data Automation project, overriding the project-level default sensitive data settings for image modality.
This object configures which PII entity types are detected or redacted in images as part of the sensitive data configuration override for the Bedrock Data Automation project.
Specifies the list of PII entity types (e.g., NAME, EMAIL, PHONE) to detect or redact in images when the sensitive data configuration is enabled under the image override settings.
Specifies how PII entities detected in images are masked during redaction, with options such as replacing them with their entity type, a generic label, a hash, or a redaction box.

When set, this field maps the MP4 media type to a specific Amazon Bedrock Data Automation blueprint ARN for the project's override configuration, so MP4 video inputs are processed using that blueprint instead of the project's default routing.
Overrides the default data automation configuration for video content in the project, specifying settings for the video extraction stage and splitter stage.

Specifies the video-specific processing settings within the override configuration of the Bedrock data automation project, allowing customization of how video content is handled during data automation.
Determines whether the video modality processing override is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for the data automation project's video processing configuration.
Configures sensitive data detection (such as PII) for video processing in this project's override configuration, letting you adjust which sensitive data rules are applied to video content.
Specifies which categories of sensitive data to detect in video content when overriding the blueprint's sensitive data configuration.

Defines which PII entity types are detected in video content and the redaction action (such as BLOCK or REDACT) applied to each, as part of the sensitive data configuration in the override settings for this Bedrock Data Automation project.
Determines the specific PII entity types (e.g., EMAIL, PHONE) that the data automation project will detect or act on within video content under the given override configuration.
Specifies how redacted PII entities in video content are masked, determining whether the output uses a placeholder or the entity type as the mask.

aws_bedrock_data_automation_project.stan.text: Defines the output settings for audio generated by the data automation project, including the audio file format and sample rate.
Specifies the audio extraction settings, such as the types of transcripts or analysis to include, for the project's standard output configuration in AWS Bedrock Data Automation.
Specifies whether the audio extraction category is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) in the standard output configuration for the AWS::Bedrock::DataAutomationProject resource.

Provides category-specific configuration for the selected audio extraction type (such as transcript or sentiment), with its nested fields varying based on the category's 'type' value, to tailor how that category is extracted from the audio input.
Configures the labeling of audio channels in the transcript data, so that extracted transcripts can identify which audio channel each speech segment belongs to.

Specifies whether channel labeling, which identifies and separates different audio channels or speakers in transcribed audio, is enabled or disabled for this transcript extraction category configuration in the audio standard output.
This object configures speaker labeling (speaker diarization) for the audio transcript, controlling whether distinct speakers are identified and labeled in the output.
Specifies the state (e.g., ENABLED or DISABLED) of speaker labeling for transcript extraction within the audio standard output configuration of the Bedrock Data Automation project.

In the audio standard output configuration, this object defines a custom generative field—specified by a name and description—that AWS Bedrock Data Automation will attempt to generate from the processed audio.
Specifies whether generative field extraction is enabled (e.g., ENABLED) or disabled (e.g., DISABLED) for audio in the standard output configuration of the Bedrock Data Automation project.
Specifies the list of generative field types to be produced for audio data in the standard output configuration of the AWS Bedrock data automation project.
Defines the standard output format for document processing, including the output type (such as plain text or structured data) and optionally a data automation blueprint to use.

This object defines the document extraction settings for the project's standard output configuration, controlling whether extraction is enabled and which structured data types (e.g., KEY_VALUE_PAIRS, TABLES) are extracted from documents.
Determines whether bounding box coordinates are extracted from documents, and which granularity of bounding boxes (such as word or line) are included in the standard output configuration.
Determines whether bounding box extraction is enabled for documents in the standard output configuration, with accepted values typically ENABLED or DISABLED.

Configures the granularity level for document extraction in the standard output configuration, controlling whether extracted document data is returned at the document, page, or element level for the Amazon Bedrock Data Automation project.
Specifies the granularity levels (such as document or page) at which document extraction results are produced in the standard output configuration of the Bedrock Data Automation project.

Defines a generative field for document output in AWS Bedrock Data Automation, specifying the field name, data type, and the prompt or instructions that guide the model to generate the field's value from the document's content.
Specifies whether the generative field is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for the document standard output configuration in the Bedrock data automation project.

Specifies the output format for documents in the standard output configuration, determining the text format preset and any additional file formats (such as CSV or JSON) for generated extraction output.

This object configures whether Amazon Bedrock Data Automation generates an additional output file format for documents (such as CSV) alongside the primary format, with a state property that enables or disables this extra file.
Specifies whether the additional file format for document output is enabled or disabled in the standard output configuration of the Bedrock data automation project.
This object configures the text format types (such as plain text, markdown, or HTML) that the Bedrock data automation project will output for document extraction.
Specifies the types of text output formats (e.g., plain text or Markdown) that the Bedrock Data Automation project will generate for extracted document content.
Defines the output configuration for images processed by the data automation project, controlling how image-derived data is extracted and formatted in the standard output.
Defines the extraction configuration for image files in the standard output configuration, specifying which extraction types (e.g., text extraction) are enabled for the data automation project.

Specifies the configuration for bounding box extraction from images in the standard output of a Bedrock Data Automation project, typically including an enable/disable setting that controls whether bounding box coordinates are generated.
Specifies whether bounding box extraction is enabled or disabled in the image extraction standard output configuration, where the required value is typically 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.

Specifies whether the image extraction category is enabled or disabled (as `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`) for the project's standard output configuration, controlling whether results from that category are generated.
Whether generative field extraction from images is enabled or disabled, with valid values ENABLED and DISABLED.
Lists the types of generative fields to extract from images in the standard output configuration, with valid values including OCR, Form, Table, and KeyValue.
Specifies the standard output configuration for video files in the AWS Bedrock data automation project, controlling which extraction types (e.g., transcript, caption) are produced from videos.

Configures how video files are analyzed and extracted into structured data for the standard output format, specifying the extraction types (such as text, key-value pairs, or entities) to apply to video content.
This configuration object controls whether bounding box annotations for objects detected in video frames are generated and included in the standard output of the Bedrock Data Automation project.
The state of bounding box extraction for video in the standard output configuration, controlling whether it is enabled or disabled.

Required mapping that defines which video extraction categories (such as transcription, text detection, or content moderation) are enabled and their configuration for the standard output of the Bedrock data automation project.
Defines whether the specified video extraction category is enabled for processing within the project's standard output configuration, typically set to 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
The list of category types to extract from the video, controlling which categorical outputs are generated in the standard output configuration.

Configures the generative AI field extraction for video standard output, defining the specific text fields (with associated prompts) that the Data Automation project will automatically generate from video content.
Indicates whether the generative field for video output is enabled or disabled in the standard output configuration, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.

Specifies the list of generative field types (for example, VIDEO_SUMMARY, VIDEO_CHAPTERS, and VIDEO_HIGHLIGHTS) that the data automation project will produce from the video as part of the standard output configuration.

aws_bedrock_data_automation_project.stat.text: The current lifecycle state of the data automation project, such as Creating, Active, Updating, Deleting, or Failed.

aws_bedrock_data_automation_project.tags.text: Specifies the value of a tag attached to the Bedrock Data Automation project, enabling arbitrary metadata such as cost centers or ownership labels.

aws_bedrock_data_source.data_source_conf.text: List of pattern strings that identify Confluence objects (e.g., pages or files) to exclude from being crawled and ingested into the Amazon Bedrock data source.
Specifies a list of string patterns that determine which Confluence objects are included during the crawl when using the pattern object filter.
The type of Confluence object (e.g., 'Space' or 'Page') to which the filter pattern applies in the Bedrock data source crawling configuration.
Specifies a list of regular expression patterns for Salesforce object names to exclude from being crawled, so that matching objects are filtered out of the Bedrock data source ingestion.
Specifies a list of regular expression patterns that match Salesforce object names to include during crawling, so only matching objects are ingested into the knowledge base.
The Salesforce object type name (e.g., Account, Contact) that this filter pattern applies to, determining which Salesforce objects are included or excluded when crawling the data source.
Specifies a list of object name patterns to exclude from being crawled in the SharePoint data source.
Defines a list of regex patterns that determine which SharePoint objects (e.g., files or folders) are included during the crawl, where an object must match at least one pattern to be ingested.
Specifies whether the filter pattern applies to files (OBJECT) or directories (FOLDER) within the SharePoint site being crawled.
The URL of a web page to use as a seed (starting point) for the web crawler in the Bedrock data source's web configuration, which the crawler will visit and follow links from to index content.

aws_bedrock_data_source.vector_ingestion.text: The maximum number of tokens allowed per chunk at the corresponding level within the hierarchical chunking configuration for the Bedrock data source.

Determines whether the custom transformation runs after chunking (POST_CHUNKING) or after chunks are written to the index (POST_INDEXING), controlling the point in the ingestion pipeline where the transformation is applied.
Defines the AWS Lambda function (via its ARN and optionally S3 code location) that Bedrock calls to perform the custom transformation on each data source content during ingestion.

Contains the configuration for the AWS Lambda function used as the custom transformation function, including the Lambda function ARN and optionally the S3 bucket where the function code is stored, for transforming documents during ingestion into the Bedrock data source.
The ARN of the AWS Lambda function that performs custom data transformation during ingestion into the Bedrock knowledge base.

aws_bedrock_flow.definition.connections..text: Configuration for a flow connection, where for conditional edges it holds the condition expression that determines whether the flow traverses this connection.
Defines the conditional configuration for a connection between nodes in a Bedrock flow, specifying the condition expression that determines whether the flow traverses this connection.
The name of the condition defined in the flow's conditions configuration that must evaluate to true for the flow to traverse this conditional connection.
In an AWS Bedrock Flow connection, this field specifies the name of the output from the source node that is mapped to the corresponding input of the target node.
The name of the input field on the target Flow node that this connection's data is sent to.
A required unique name that identifies this connection within the Bedrock flow definition, used to reference the connection and distinguish it from other connections in the flow graph.
The name of the source node in a Bedrock flow connection, indicating which node's output feeds into the connection's target node.
Specifies the identifier of the destination node in the flow that this connection links to, defining the graph edge's target.
Specifies the type of the connection between nodes in the flow, indicating whether it represents a data flow ('Data') or a control flow ('Control').

aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.config.text: Holds the node-type-specific settings for a single node in the Bedrock flow, such as the prompt template for a prompt node or the condition logic for a condition node.
Configuration for a Bedrock flow node of type 'Agent', specifying the agent alias to invoke and an optional prompt template to customize the agent's behavior.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Bedrock agent alias that this node uses to invoke the agent.
Configures a Collector node in the Bedrock flow, specifying the upstream node outputs to aggregate into a single array for use by downstream nodes.

This object specifies the branching condition for a Bedrock Flow condition node, containing the logical expression (and its evaluation type) that determines which outgoing connection the flow follows.

Defines the list of evaluation rules for a Bedrock Flow condition node, where each rule contains an expression (e.g., a comparison using flow variables) and a unique name that determines which outgoing branch the flow takes.
The Boolean expression that is evaluated for this condition in a Condition node, using the flow's variable syntax and expression grammar to determine whether the condition is met.
Specifies the unique name of an individual condition within a condition node, which the flow uses to route execution based on the evaluated expression.
Defines the script that is executed directly by the Bedrock flow node, enabling custom processing without referencing an external Lambda function.
The source code (such as JavaScript) to execute for the flow node, provided inline in the flow definition instead of referencing an external file.
Specifies the programming language (for example, Python) used to interpret and run the inline code in a flow node's inline code configuration.

For an input node in a Bedrock flow, this field defines the schema of the flow's input data, including its type (e.g., 'String') and, for structured objects, a list of named properties with their types.
Defines the configuration for an iterator node in the Bedrock flow, specifying the collection to iterate over and optional limits such as maximum items to control looping.
Specifies the Amazon Bedrock knowledge base and its retrieval configuration, such as the knowledge base ID and query settings, for a Knowledge Base node in the flow.
Configures the guardrail applied to the inference responses from this knowledge base node, referencing the guardrail's unique identifier and version.
The unique identifier (ARN) of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail that governs the knowledge base node's responses in the flow.
Specifies the version of the guardrail to apply to the knowledge base, such as 'DRAFT' or a specific numeric version.
Defines the inference parameters (e.g., temperature, topP, topK, maximumLength) applied when the knowledge base node in a Bedrock flow queries the underlying foundation model.

The `text` object under `inference_configuration` specifies the generation parameters (such as max tokens, temperature, and stop sequences) for text responses from the underlying model of the knowledge base node.
The maximum number of tokens the model can generate in the text response produced by the knowledge base node's inference configuration in the Bedrock flow.
Specifies the stop sequences (strings) that signal the model to halt text generation when encountered in the output of the knowledge base node's inference configuration.
Sets the temperature for text generation in the knowledge base node's inference configuration, controlling the randomness and creativity of the generated responses.

Specifies the top-p (nucleus sampling) probability threshold used by the knowledge base node's text inference configuration, limiting generation to the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds this value.
The unique identifier of the Amazon Bedrock knowledge base that this flow node uses to retrieve and ground responses.
Specifies the unique identifier of the Amazon Bedrock foundation model used by the knowledge base node to generate responses based on retrieved information.
Specifies the maximum number of retrieved knowledge base results to include in the prompt when the flow node queries the connected knowledge base.
Specifies additional inference parameters (such as temperature or topP) to send to the foundation model when the knowledge base node performs orchestration.
Specifies the inference parameters (such as temperature, topP, maxTokens) used by the model invoked during knowledge base orchestration in this Bedrock flow node.

In the AWS Bedrock Flow definition, this field specifies the text generation inference parameters (such as temperature, maximum tokens, and stop sequences) for the knowledge base node's orchestration configuration.
The maximum number of tokens that the orchestration model is allowed to generate in its text response for the knowledge base node's inference configuration.
Specifies a list of custom token sequences that stop the model's text generation in the knowledge base node's orchestration configuration.
Controls the randomness of text generation in the knowledge base orchestration step, where higher values yield more creative or varied responses.

The top_p nucleus sampling value that restricts token selection to the smallest set whose cumulative probability exceeds this threshold, applied to the knowledge base orchestration text inference configuration in the Bedrock flow.
This object configures retrieval performance for the knowledge base node, including the number of results to return and the vector search type (e.g., HYBRID) used during orchestration.
Sets the latency optimization tier (e.g., STANDARD or OPTIMIZED) for knowledge base retrieval in the flow node's orchestration, controlling the trade-off between response speed and query accuracy.
Defines the prompt template used by the model to orchestrate knowledge base retrieval and response generation within the flow's knowledge base node.
Specifies the prompt template text used by the knowledge base node's orchestration step to instruct the model how to formulate the final response based on the retrieved context and the user's query.
Specifies a prompt template for the knowledge base node, used to construct the query sent to the model with placeholders for user input and retrieved context.

Provides the plain-text prompt template for the knowledge base node, used to formulate the query that is sent to the knowledge base, typically containing a placeholder for the user's input such as `{{query}}`.
Configures how retrieval results from the knowledge base are reranked, including the reranking model ARN and the number of top results to keep after reranking.
Defines the Amazon Bedrock managed reranking model for this knowledge base node, specifying the model ARN and additional fields in modelConfiguration and the number of reranked results to return.

Specifies the metadata configuration for the Bedrock reranking model, such as whether to treat metadata as structured or unstructured and which additional metadata fields to include when reranking knowledge base results.
Determines whether all metadata fields or only a selected subset are passed to the Bedrock reranker for reranking, with values such as 'SELECTIVE' or 'ALL'.
Defines selective mode settings for the reranking metadata configuration, allowing you to specify which metadata fields should be used by the Bedrock reranker when reranking knowledge base results.
Specifies the metadata fields to exclude from consideration when reranking knowledge base results in selective metadata mode, preventing these fields from influencing reranking scores.
The name of a knowledge-base metadata field to exclude from the reranking process when using selective metadata configuration.
Specifies the metadata fields (each containing a field name and type) to include when reranking uses selective mode, so only the listed document metadata is considered for reranking decisions.
The name of a document metadata field to include in the metadata passed to the Bedrock reranking model when using selective mode.
Specifies the Bedrock model configuration for the reranking step, including the model ARN and any additional model request fields to pass to the reranking model.

Specifies additional model-specific request fields (as key-value pairs) to be passed to the reranking model, allowing customization of inference parameters such as top_n or return_documents for the Bedrock reranking operation.
The ARN of the Amazon Bedrock reranking model used to re-rank the knowledge base retrieval results.
Within a knowledge base node's reranking configuration, this number specifies how many of the top retrieved results are sent to the configured reranking model.
Specifies the reranking model type for the knowledge base node, indicating whether the reranker is an Amazon Bedrock built-in reranker or a Cohere reranker.
Specifies the AWS Lambda function to invoke for a Lambda function node in the flow, including the function's ARN and an optional JSON payload to pass to the function.
The ARN of the AWS Lambda function that this node invokes when the flow executes.
Configuration for an Amazon Lex node in the flow, defining which Lex bot alias to invoke and the locale for conversational interactions.
The ARN of the Amazon Lex bot alias that this node invokes to handle the conversational interaction within the flow.
The locale ID (e.g., en_US) of the Amazon Lex bot configured for this node in the Bedrock flow, which determines the language and regional variant used for the bot's interactions.
Configuration for a loop node within the flow, specifying the child nodes that form the loop body and the condition node used to determine when to exit the loop.
The inline definition of the sub-flow that the loop node iterates over, specifying the nodes and connections that constitute the repeated workflow body.
Defines the loop control parameters for a Bedrock Flow loop node, including the array of items to iterate over and optional maximum iteration count.
Specifies the condition that determines whether the loop continues to the next iteration, evaluated after each pass through the loop node's body.
The expression, written in Amazon Bedrock Flow expression syntax, that is evaluated to a boolean to determine whether the loop controller should repeat the iteration.
The name of the condition that determines whether the loop controller node in the flow continues to the next iteration.
Specifies the maximum number of iterations the loop node can execute before the flow terminates the loop, preventing infinite loops.
Defines the input for a loop node in the flow, specifying the flow variable or expression that the loop iterates over.
Defines the output configuration for an Output node in a Bedrock flow, specifying the data type and optional name of the flow's output.
Defines the prompt settings for a prompt node, including the prompt template, model selection, and inference configuration.
Defines the Amazon Bedrock guardrail applied to the prompt node, specifying the guardrail's unique identifier and version to filter or moderate content.
The Amazon Bedrock guardrail ARN that this prompt node uses to apply content filters and safeguards to the prompt and the model's response.
The version of the guardrail to apply to the prompt node, such as a specific numeric version or 'DRAFT' for the unpublished version.
Specifies the source of the prompt for the prompt node in the Bedrock flow, which can be either inline text configured directly or a reference to an existing prompt resource.

Specifies the inline definition of the prompt, including the model ID, template type (e.g., TEXT), template configuration, and optional inference settings, used directly within the flow node rather than referencing an external prompt resource.
Configures the model inference parameters for the inline prompt source, such as temperature, maximum tokens, and stop sequences, used when the prompt node invokes a model in the Bedrock flow.
Specifies the text inference configuration (e.g., temperature, topP, maxTokens, and stopSequences) for the inline prompt's model invocation.
Specifies the maximum number of tokens that the model is allowed to generate in the response for the inline prompt's text inference configuration, capping the length of the generated output.
Specifies a list of string sequences that, when generated by the model, cause it to stop generating further output tokens.

Controls the randomness of the model's text output in this prompt's inference configuration, where higher values produce more varied and creative responses and lower values produce more focused and deterministic responses.
The top_p value for nucleus sampling, controlling the cumulative probability mass of tokens considered for generation in the text inference configuration of the prompt node.
Specifies the Amazon Bedrock foundation model ID used by the inline prompt configuration for this prompt node in the flow.
Specifies the template type (TEXT or CHAT) and the actual prompt template content for an inline prompt source in a Bedrock flow node.
Defines the textual prompt template used for the prompt node when the source is configured inline, supporting variable placeholders for dynamic inputs.
Defines the list of input variables for the inline text prompt template, where each variable's name is declared so it can be referenced as a placeholder in the template text.
The name of the input variable that is referenced within the prompt template text and substituted with a runtime value when the flow node executes.
Specifies the actual prompt text used in the inline prompt template, which can include Bedrock prompt variables such as {{variableName}} for dynamic content.
This field specifies the prompt template format (such as TEXT or CHAT) for an inline prompt source in a Bedrock Flow prompt node, determining how the prompt content is structured and parsed.
For a prompt node within a Bedrock flow, this object specifies the source configuration to reference an existing Amazon Bedrock prompt resource by its ARN rather than defining the prompt inline.
The Amazon Bedrock prompt ARN that supplies the prompt text or prompt template for this node's prompt source configuration.
Configures a retrieval node in an Amazon Bedrock flow by specifying the knowledge base to query and the retrieval settings used to fetch relevant information for downstream processing.
Configuration for the retrieval service used by the retrieval node, specifying the knowledge base (and optionally model settings) that the node queries to fetch relevant information.
Specifies the Amazon S3 data source for the retrieval node's service configuration, with properties such as the S3 bucket name and an optional object key prefix.
Specifies the name of the S3 bucket from which the retrieval node in this Bedrock flow retrieves data.
Specifies the configuration for a storage node in the Bedrock flow, including the S3 location where the flow's input data should be saved.
Defines the S3-specific settings for the storage node's service configuration, including the bucket name and optional object key prefix where the flow output will be written.
The name of the S3 bucket used by the flow node's S3 storage service configuration, defining the bucket from which the node reads or to which it writes data.

aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.inputs.text: Specifies the input parameters that a node in an Amazon Bedrock Flow consumes from the flow's initial inputs or from outputs of preceding nodes, enabling data to be passed into the node's processing logic such as a prompt or condition.

Specifies the source category of a node input in a Bedrock flow definition, such as `FLOW` for a flow-level parameter or `NODE` for a reference to another node's output, which determines how the flow engine resolves the input's `value` field.
Specifies the expression that resolves the value for this input, commonly referencing outputs of other nodes using ${...} syntax in Amazon Bedrock flows.
The name of the input, which uniquely identifies it within the node and is used as the reference key for accessing the input's value in expressions and for wiring connections between nodes.
Specifies the data type of the node input, such as String, Number, Boolean, Object, Array, or Reference.

aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.name.text: A unique name for the node within the flow, used to identify the node when defining connections to and from other nodes in the flow definition.

aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.output.text: Specifies the list of outputs for a node, where each output includes a name, data type, and an expression that determines the value exposed to downstream nodes in the flow.
The name of this node output, which uniquely identifies it within the node and is used to reference it in downstream node expressions.
Specifies the data type of the node output (e.g., String, Number, Boolean) so downstream nodes can interpret the value correctly.

aws_bedrock_flow.definition.nodes.type.text: Specifies the type of the node (for example, Input, Output, Prompt, or Condition) in the Amazon Bedrock flow, which determines the node's behavior and required properties.

aws_bedrock_flow.validations.message.text: The message field of a validation object provides a human-readable description of a validation issue found in the flow's definition.

aws_bedrock_flow_alias.concurrency_confi.text: The concurrency configuration type for a Bedrock flow alias, which can be set to SINGLE to restrict the alias to one active flow invocation at a time or PARALLEL to allow multiple concurrent invocations, controlling how the alias handles runtime requests.

aws_bedrock_flow_alias.routing_configura.text: The version of the Amazon Bedrock flow (such as a numeric version or 'DRAFT') that this alias routes traffic to.

aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.conn.text: Defines the type-specific settings for a connection between two flow nodes, such as mapping the source node's output fields to the target node's input fields for data connections, or the condition expression that triggers the connection for conditional connections.

Defines the conditional configuration for a flow connection, specifying the condition expression that must evaluate to true for the flow to follow this connection from the source node to the target node.
Defines the expression evaluated at a conditional node that, when true, causes the flow to traverse this connection, using Amazon Bedrock's expression syntax.
Specifies the data flow configuration for a connection, defining which output of the source node connects to which input of the target node.
The name of the output from the source node that this connection uses to pass data to the target node.
The target input field name in the destination node that receives data from the source output when this data connection is used in the flow definition.
The name that uniquely identifies a connection between a source node and a target node in a Bedrock flow definition.
The name of the source node from which this connection originates in the flow definition.
The name of the target node in the Bedrock flow to which this connection routes data from the source node.
Specifies the connection type as either 'Data' for regular node-to-node data flow or 'Conditional' for a condition-based edge in the flow graph.

aws_bedrock_flow_version.definition.node.text: For each node in a Bedrock flow's definition, this object holds the node-type-specific configuration (e.g., prompt, knowledge base, Lambda, or condition settings) that defines the node's behavior.
Defines the configuration for invoking an Amazon Bedrock agent at this flow node, including the agent ID, alias, and the mapping of inputs and outputs between the flow and the agent.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Bedrock agent alias that this agent node uses to invoke the agent within the flow.
This field specifies the configuration for a collector node in a Bedrock flow, which aggregates multiple upstream outputs into a single list for downstream processing.
Defines the branch condition for a condition node in the flow, including the boolean expression and the list of conditions that determine which downstream node to invoke.
The list of condition rules that a Condition node in the flow evaluates against the flow's data to decide which outgoing branch to follow.

In an Amazon Bedrock flow's condition node, this expression is a Boolean-valued string that evaluates flow variables (e.g., using comparison or logical operators) to determine whether the corresponding condition is met and the flow should follow that branch.

Specifies the name of an individual condition within a condition node in a Bedrock flow, used to identify and route execution to the corresponding branch when that condition's expression is evaluated.
The inline code configuration for a node of type 'inline_code' in the flow definition, specifying the source code that the node executes.
The source code to be executed by the inline code node within the Bedrock flow, typically written in JavaScript or Python.
Specifies the programming language of the inline code (e.g., Python, JavaScript) executed by the code node in the Bedrock flow.
This field specifies the configuration for an Input-type node in a Bedrock flow version, marking it as the flow's entry point and defining the flow's input variable or schema.

The `iterator` configuration block for an Iterator node in an Amazon Bedrock flow specifies the collection expression to iterate over (typically referencing an upstream node's array output) so the flow can loop through items.
Specifies the knowledge base configuration for a node in an Amazon Bedrock flow, including the knowledge base ID and retrieval settings used to query information during flow execution.
Configures the guardrail used by the knowledge base node in the flow, specifying the guardrail identifier and version to apply.
The unique identifier or ARN of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail applied to this knowledge base node, used to filter or moderate content during flow processing.
The version of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail (e.g., 'DRAFT' or a numeric version like '1') to apply to the knowledge base node within the flow version.
Specifies the model inference parameters (such as temperature, topP, maximum tokens, and stop sequences) for the knowledge base node's response generation in the flow.
Specifies the text inference configuration for the knowledge base node, including parameters like temperature, maximum tokens, and stop sequences.
The maximum number of tokens the model can generate in text inference for a knowledge base node in an Amazon Bedrock flow.
Specifies the list of character sequences that, when produced by the model, cause text generation to stop early within the knowledge base node's inference configuration.
Temperature controls the randomness of text generation in the knowledge base node's inference configuration, where lower values produce more deterministic and higher values more creative output.

Sets the nucleus sampling top-p probability threshold for the text generation model in the knowledge base node, controlling the cumulative probability mass of token candidates considered during sampling.
The unique identifier of the Amazon Bedrock knowledge base that this flow node is configured to query for information.
The identifier of the foundation model used by the knowledge base node in this flow version to synthesize answers from the retrieved knowledge base context.
Specifies the maximum number of results (chunks) to retrieve from the knowledge base when this flow node executes a query.

Specifies additional model invocation parameters (as a dynamic map of key-value pairs) to pass to the underlying model when the knowledge-base orchestration step runs, allowing fine-grained control beyond the standard configured fields.

Specifies the inference configuration for the knowledge base node's orchestration, such as temperature, top-p, and max output tokens, that control how the underlying foundation model generates responses from retrieved context.
Sets the text generation inference settings (e.g., temperature, topP, maxTokens) for the knowledge base node's orchestration step in the flow version.
The maximum number of tokens to generate in a text response when the knowledge base node's orchestration invokes the foundation model for text inference.
A list of strings that define the stop sequences for text generation in the knowledge base orchestration configuration, causing the model to halt generation when it encounters any of these sequences.
The temperature parameter for the text inference configuration of the knowledge base orchestration node, which controls the randomness or creativity of the model's generated responses.

Sets the top-p nucleus sampling probability for text generation in the knowledge base orchestration step of a Bedrock flow, restricting the model to tokens whose cumulative probability mass reaches this threshold.
The latency mode (e.g., 'STANDARD' or 'OPTIMIZED') that controls the response-time vs. accuracy trade-off for the knowledge base orchestration.

Provides the prompt template (as an object) that the knowledge base node's orchestration configuration uses to construct the model prompt, formatting how the retrieved context and the user's query are combined, typically via placeholders like {{context}} and {{query}}.
The text of the prompt template used by the knowledge base node to formulate queries or generate responses, supporting placeholders like {{query}}.

Specifies the prompt template for the knowledge base node, which can be provided as inline text or as a reference to a stored prompt, and is used to instruct the model on how to incorporate retrieved knowledge base context into its response.
Defines the text of the prompt template that the knowledge base node in a Bedrock flow uses to generate the search query for retrieval.
Configures how retrieved knowledge base results are reranked for this flow node, including the reranker model to use for reordering query results.

Specifies the Bedrock reranker model configuration for knowledge base retrieval reranking, including the model ARN and optionally the number of results to return, used when the reranking configuration type is BEDROCK.
Specifies the metadata selection configuration for the Bedrock reranker, defining whether all or specific metadata fields from the retrieved documents are passed to the reranking model.
Determines whether all metadata fields are included in the reranking request or only a specified subset, using values ALL or SELECTIVE.
Configures selective-mode metadata selection for the Bedrock reranking model, including the list of metadata fields to exclude during reranking.

Specifies the list of metadata fields to exclude from consideration when the reranker scores retrieved knowledge base chunks, so those fields are ignored in the reranking process under selective mode.
Defines the name of a metadata field to exclude from the reranking process when selective mode is configured for the knowledge base's reranking step.
Specifies the list of metadata fields to include when the reranking metadata configuration is in selective mode, ensuring that only these fields are used for reranking.
The name of a metadata field to include in the selective metadata configuration used for reranking a knowledge base node's responses in the Flow Version.
Specifies the configuration for the reranking model used by the knowledge base node, including the model ARN and optional additional model request fields passed to the reranking model.

A map of additional model request fields to include in the inference request sent to the Bedrock reranking model specified in the model configuration, allowing customization beyond the default parameters.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Bedrock reranking model used to reorder knowledge base retrieval results.
Specifies the number of top retrieval results to be returned after reranking by the Bedrock reranking model in the knowledge base node's reranking configuration.
Specifies whether reranking is disabled or performed using a Bedrock reranking model for knowledge base retrieval in this flow node.
Specifies the AWS Lambda function to invoke for a Lambda node in the Amazon Bedrock flow, including its ARN and related invocation settings.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Lambda function that this Lambda function node in the Bedrock flow invokes.
Configuration for a flow node that invokes an Amazon Lex bot, specifying the bot alias ARN and locale ID.
The ARN of the Amazon Lex bot alias that this Lex node in the Bedrock flow definition uses to interact with the specified Lex bot.
The locale ID (e.g., en_US) of the Amazon Lex bot that this flow node interacts with, used to select the appropriate language/locale for the Lex conversation.
Configuration for a loop node in an Amazon Bedrock flow version, specifying the child nodes to execute repeatedly and the condition that controls when the loop ends.
Specifies the loop body definition for a loop node, including the sequence of nodes to execute on each iteration and the condition that terminates the loop.
Configures the loop controller for a Loop-type node in the Bedrock flow, specifying the maximum number of iterations the loop can execute.
Defines the condition that is evaluated after each iteration of a Bedrock Flow loop node to determine whether the loop should continue to the next iteration or terminate.
The expression string that defines the condition evaluated after each loop iteration to determine whether the loop should continue iterating in the flow version.
The logical name of the continue condition used by the loop controller to determine whether to proceed with another loop iteration.
Specifies the maximum number of iterations that the loop node's controller can run in the Amazon Bedrock flow version definition before the loop terminates.
In the configuration for a Loop node within a Bedrock flow definition, this field specifies the variable or expression that supplies the list of items the loop will iterate over.

The prompt object within a node's configuration defines the prompt settings for a prompt-type node in the Bedrock flow, including the prompt template and the model configuration for generating responses.
Configures the Amazon Bedrock guardrail (by identifier and version) to be applied to the prompt in this node, providing content filtering and privacy controls during flow execution.
Specifies the ARN or identifier of the Bedrock guardrail applied to this prompt node to enforce content moderation and safety policies.
