Specifies the version of the guardrail attached to this prompt node, used to select which guardrail policy set is enforced during prompt processing in the flow.
Specifies the source of the prompt for a prompt flow node, either referencing an existing Bedrock prompt resource by ARN or defining the prompt inline with text or chat configuration.
Contains the inline prompt definition used by a prompt node in the Bedrock flow, specifying the actual prompt text and related model inference settings.
Specifies the inference parameters (such as temperature, top P, and maximum tokens) applied when the inline prompt in this prompt node is invoked.
Specifies the text model inference parameters (such as temperature, max tokens, top P, and stop sequences) applied when the prompt node generates text output.
Sets the maximum number of tokens the model can generate in the response for this prompt configuration.
Specifies the custom text sequences that cause the model to stop generating further output when encountered during inference for the prompt.
The temperature setting for text generation in the inline prompt's inference configuration, controlling the randomness and creativity of the model's output.

Specifies the top_p (nucleus sampling) value, a number between 0 and 1, that controls the cumulative probability threshold for token selection in the text inference configuration of the prompt node's inline source.
The unique identifier (model ID or ARN) of the Amazon Bedrock foundation or custom model used to run the inline prompt in a prompt node.

Specifies the prompt template configuration for the inline source of a prompt node, holding the template text (including placeholders for prompt variables) that Amazon Bedrock uses to generate the prompt when the flow version executes.
Specifies the prompt template text used by an inline prompt node's source configuration in the Bedrock flow version definition.
Defines the list of input variables for the inline text prompt template, where each variable supplies a name and value substituted into the template at flow runtime.
The name of an input variable defined for an inline text prompt template in a prompt node within a flow version, which the prompt template references to substitute the variable's value at runtime.
Defines the prompt text template used by the inline prompt configuration in the Bedrock flow node.

Determines the format of the inline prompt template for a prompt node in the flow, where TEXT specifies a single plain-text prompt and CHAT specifies a chat-style prompt with conversation turns and role-based messages.
Defines the Amazon S3 resource that supplies the prompt text for the prompt node, containing the S3 URI of the prompt file.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Bedrock prompt that serves as the source for this prompt node's configuration in the flow version definition.
Configuration for a 'retrieval' node in a Bedrock flow, specifying the knowledge base to query when the node executes.
This object specifies the retrieval service (either Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base or Amazon S3) and its configuration for the retrieval node in the Bedrock flow definition.
This object specifies the S3 bucket and object prefix configuration used by the retrieval node in the Bedrock flow definition to fetch data from Amazon S3.
The name of the S3 bucket from which the Bedrock flow's retrieval node retrieves data when its service configuration is set to S3.
Specifies the service configuration for a storage node in the Bedrock flow version, such as the Amazon S3 bucket and prefix used for reading or writing data.
Specifies the S3 bucket and optional key prefix used as the storage destination for a Storage node in the Bedrock flow version's definition.
The name of the S3 bucket used for the storage configuration of this node in the Amazon Bedrock flow version.

Defines the list of input bindings for each node in the flow, where each input maps an expression (like a literal or a reference to another node's output) to a named input expected by the node's configuration.
A string expression that resolves to the value of this node input at runtime, typically referencing other nodes' outputs using the Bedrock flow expression syntax.
The name of this input to the flow node, which identifies the input variable that the node consumes and references in its configuration.
Specifies the name of a node in the flow definition, which must be unique within the flow and is used as the identifier for the node in connections and other flow elements.
Defines the list of output definitions (name and data type) for a node in the Bedrock flow version, enabling downstream nodes to reference these outputs by name.
The name of a node's output in the Bedrock flow definition, which downstream nodes use to reference the output data in expressions.
Specifies the data type of the output produced by a node in the Amazon Bedrock flow, such as String, Number, or Boolean, affecting how downstream nodes process the value.
Specifies the type of node within the flow definition, determining what operation the node performs (for example, Input, Output, KnowledgeBase, or Prompt).

aws_bedrock_guardrail.content_policy_con.text: Specifies whether the guardrail's content filter blocks or allows the matched content type in user input prompts, accepting values like 'BLOCK' or 'NONE'.
Specifies whether this content filter is enabled for user inputs (prompts) processed by the guardrail.
Specifies the input modalities (e.g., TEXT or IMAGE) that the content filter applies to, allowing the filter to target specific types of content entering the guardrail.
Specifies the strength of the content filter applied to user input prompts, controlling how aggressively the guardrail filters content for the input direction (e.g., NONE, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH).
Determines whether content matching the filter category is blocked (BLOCK) or allowed (NONE) when it appears in model-generated output.
Determines whether the content policy filter applies to generated model outputs, enabling or disabling the evaluation and filtering of the guardrail's responses for the specified filter category.
Specifies the output modalities (such as TEXT or IMAGE) to which this content filter applies for generated responses.

The strength (e.g., NONE, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) applied when filtering the model's generated (output) content for the specified content policy filter type, determining how aggressively the guardrail blocks or moderates that content.
The category of harmful content that this guardrail filter targets, such as SEXUAL, VIOLENCE, HATE, INSULTS, MISCONDUCT, or PROMPT_ATTACK.

aws_bedrock_guardrail.contextual_groundi.text: Specifies whether the contextual grounding filter blocks the request (BLOCK) or allows it (NONE) when the filter's check fails.
Boolean that enables or disables this specific contextual grounding filter (e.g., grounding or relevance) within the guardrail's contextual grounding policy.

The confidence threshold (between 0 and 1) for a contextual grounding filter (of type GROUNDING or RELEVANCE), which sets the minimum score the model's response must meet to be considered grounded or relevant, and responses scoring below this threshold are blocked.
The type of the contextual grounding filter, which must be either GROUNDING or RELEVANCE, controlling whether the filter checks factual grounding or query relevance.

aws_bedrock_guardrail.sensitive_informat.text: In an AWS Bedrock Guardrail's sensitive information policy, the `action` property for each PII entity config determines the enforcement response when that type of personally identifiable information is detected, with valid values such as `BLOCK` to deny the input or output, or `ANONYMIZE` to replace it with a placeholder.

Defines how the guardrail responds to detected personally identifiable information (PII) in an end-user prompt, allowing values like 'BLOCK' to deny the request or 'ANONYMIZE' to replace the PII with a placeholder before processing.
Indicates whether the PII filter for this entity type is enabled on input (prompt) text in the guardrail's sensitive information policy.
Specifies the action (e.g., BLOCK or ANONYMIZE) the guardrail applies when the configured PII entity type is detected in the model's output.
Specifies the type of PII entity (e.g., EMAIL, PHONE, SSN) to be filtered by the guardrail's sensitive information policy.
Determines whether a regex-pattern match triggers blocking (BLOCK) or anonymization/masking (ANONYMIZE) of the detected sensitive information in guarded content.
A user-defined textual description that explains the purpose or context of this custom regex pattern in the guardrail's sensitive information policy.
Defines the action (BLOCK or ANONYMIZE) the guardrail takes when a regex pattern in this configuration matches sensitive information in the prompt (input).
Indicates whether this regex pattern in the guardrail's sensitive information policy is applied to model inputs (prompts) as opposed to only model outputs (responses).
The name of the custom regex pattern defined in the guardrail's sensitive information policy, used to identify and reference the regex-based filter.
Specifies whether a matched regex pattern in the model's output is blocked or anonymized when detected by the Bedrock guardrail.
Indicates whether the regex pattern for this sensitive information filter is enabled on model output; when false, the pattern is only applied to input.
The regular expression pattern used to detect sensitive information in the guardrail's sensitive information policy.

aws_bedrock_guardrail.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to apply to the Bedrock guardrail, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_bedrock_guardrail.topic_policy_confi.text: In the topic policy of an Amazon Bedrock guardrail, each topic's definition provides a natural-language description of the specific subject matter that the guardrail should identify and block or deny in model responses.
Specifies a list of sample phrases that illustrate the topic, used to improve the accuracy of the guardrail's detection of the topic.
Specifies the action the guardrail takes when user input matches this topic, such as BLOCK or ALLOW.
The user-defined name of a topic configured in the guardrail's topic policy, used to identify a specific subject (e.g., 'investment advice') that the model is instructed to avoid discussing.
Specifies the action taken on the output when a user query or model response matches the topic, with allowed values 'BLOCK' to deny the content and 'NONE' to allow it.
Specifies whether the topic is defined as a denied (DENY) or allowed (ALLOW) topic in the guardrail's topic policy.

aws_bedrock_guardrail.word_policy_config.text: Determines the action applied to the input when a word from the managed word list is detected, with values such as BLOCK to block the input or NONE to allow it.
Enables or disables the managed word list (e.g., profanity) filter for user input prompts in the guardrail.

For each managed word list configured in the guardrail's word policy, this field determines the action taken when a word from that list is detected, with allowed values of 'BLOCK' (block the content) or 'NONE' (allow the content).
Indicates whether the managed word list (e.g., profanity) is applied to filter the model's output text.
Specifies the managed word list category to apply to the guardrail, with the supported value PROFANITY for filtering profane language.
Determines whether a word in this list is blocked when it appears in the user prompt (input) text, with `BLOCK` filtering it out and `NONE` permitting it.
Indicates whether this custom word in the word policy is filtered from the input (user prompt) traffic, as opposed to output (model response) traffic.
Specifies the action the guardrail takes when a model output contains the configured word, with BLOCKED causing the word to be blocked and NONE allowing it to pass through.
Indicates whether the word is enabled for output filtering, meaning that when true, the guardrail prevents the word from appearing in model-generated responses.
The word or phrase that the guardrail's word policy will filter or block in model responses.

aws_bedrock_intelligent_prompt_router.mo.text: The ARN of a Bedrock foundation model that the intelligent prompt router can select among, defining a candidate model in the router's `models` list for routing prompts.

aws_bedrock_intelligent_prompt_router.ro.text: The minimum difference in predicted response quality between the larger and smaller models that the intelligent prompt router uses as a threshold to decide whether to route the prompt to the larger model.

aws_bedrock_knowledge_base.knowledge_bas.text: Configures how audio content is split into segments for embedding generation, including segmentation strategy and segment duration, when creating a knowledge base in Amazon Bedrock.
Specifies the fixed duration in seconds for splitting audio into segments for embedding in the Bedrock knowledge base.
Defines how uploaded videos are divided into discrete segments (e.g., segment length and overlap) so the embedding model processes each segment separately for the knowledge base.
The duration in seconds of each fixed-length segment into which the video is divided before being embedded, used when the video segmentation configuration specifies a fixed-length segmentation mode.
The natural language phrasing of a curated example query, representing the user's question or intent that the corresponding SQL statement is meant to answer.
The SQL query string of a curated query that serves as an example to guide the model's SQL generation for the Redshift-based knowledge base.
Specifies the list of columns for each table in the query generation context, where each column object defines the column name and data type used by the model to generate SQL queries.
Provides a natural-language description of a column in the table context, used by Bedrock to generate accurate SQL queries against the Redshift database.
Specifies whether the column is included in the generation context for query generation in the Redshift configuration of the SQL knowledge base.
Specifies the name of a column in a Redshift table that the knowledge base uses as context for generating SQL queries.
Provides a human-readable description of the table to help the query generation model understand its purpose and contents for generating SQL queries.
Specifies whether the listed Redshift table is included in or excluded from the query generation context, using an enum value such as 'INCLUDE' or 'EXCLUDE'.
The name of the Redshift table that is included in the query generation context, allowing the knowledge base to reference this table when generating SQL queries.
Defines the AWS Glue Data Catalog settings (catalog ID, database name, and table name) that identify the Redshift data source to use for the knowledge base's SQL configuration.
The list of table names in the AWS Glue Data Catalog that the Redshift SQL knowledge base will use for querying and retrieving data.
Defines the Amazon Redshift connection details for one storage configuration in an Amazon Bedrock SQL knowledge base, including the Redshift server and authentication parameters.
Specifies the name of the Redshift database that the Amazon Bedrock knowledge base uses to store and query data within the configured Redshift cluster.
Specifies the storage format for the Redshift table in the knowledge base's SQL configuration, with allowed values 'ROW' or 'COLUMNAR'.
Configures how audio files are split into segments for embedding generation, such as the duration of each audio segment, when using a Bedrock embedding model with audio support.
When the audio segmentation strategy is set to FIXED_LENGTH, this property defines the duration (in seconds) of each audio segment before embedding.
This object specifies how input videos are segmented into smaller pieces before the embedding model processes them, controlling the granularity of video embeddings in the knowledge base.
Specifies the fixed segment duration (in seconds) used to split a video into chunks before generating embeddings for a Bedrock knowledge base.
The S3 location (bucket and key prefix) that specifies where supplemental data files for the knowledge base are stored, used alongside the vector index for retrieval.
The S3 URI (e.g., s3://bucket-name/object-key) of a supplemental data storage location where additional data for the Bedrock vector knowledge base is stored.
Specifies whether the supplemental data storage location is an Amazon S3 bucket (S3) or in-memory storage (IN_MEMORY) for the Bedrock knowledge base.

aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.additional_m.text: Defines additional model request fields as key-value pairs that are passed through to the underlying foundation model for this prompt variant, augmenting or overriding standard inference parameters.

aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.gen_ai_resou.text: Specifies the Amazon Bedrock agent to associate with the prompt variant, identified by the agent's ARN.
The identifier of the Amazon Bedrock agent that serves as the generative AI resource for this prompt variant.

aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.inference_co.text: Configures the inference settings for the prompt variant, controlling response generation parameters such as temperature, topP, and maximum token count.
Represents the text inference configuration for the prompt variant, specifying generation parameters such as temperature, topP, maximum tokens, and stop sequences that guide the model's text output.
Sets the maximum number of tokens the model can generate for text responses in this prompt variant's inference configuration, capping the output length.
Specifies a list of character sequences that will cause the model to stop generating further text when any of them is encountered in the output.

In the Bedrock prompt variant's text inference configuration, temperature controls the randomness of generated text, with lower values yielding more deterministic outputs and higher values increasing creative diversity.
Controls nucleus sampling by setting the cumulative probability threshold for token selection in the text generation inference configuration of the prompt variant.

aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.metadata.key.text: In the metadata map of a Bedrock prompt variant, this key defines the name of a user-specified attribute whose value is a string, enabling you to attach custom labels or annotations to the variant.

aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.model_id.text: The Amazon Bedrock foundation model ID (e.g., anthropic.claude-v2) that this prompt variant uses for generating responses.

aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.name.text: The name of the prompt variant, used to uniquely identify and reference this specific variant within the AWS Bedrock prompt.

aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.template_con.text: Specifies the prompt template configuration for this variant, defining the text or chat template structure and how input variables are substituted in the prompt.

The chat object defines the prompt template configuration for chat-based interactions, including the required list of messages (each with a role and content) and an optional set of system prompts used by the Bedrock prompt variant.
Defines the list of named variables used in the chat prompt template configuration, each containing a name that corresponds to placeholders substituted with runtime values when invoking the model.
The name of an input variable that serves as a placeholder within the chat prompt variant's template, replaced by a concrete value when the prompt is invoked.
Specifies the chat messages (each with a role like user or assistant and content) that define the chat prompt template for this variant.
The list of content blocks (such as text or image) that make up the body of a message in a chat prompt template for the prompt variant.

Defines a cache point within a chat message content block, used to enable prompt caching in Amazon Bedrock by marking a position in the conversation where the prompt can be cached for subsequent requests.
Specifies the type of the cache point marker within a message's content, which must be set to 'default' to indicate that the preceding content should be cached for subsequent prompt invocations.
Specifies the literal text of a message content block within a chat prompt template for a Bedrock prompt variant, defining the actual wording of a user or assistant message.
Specifies the conversational role of the message in the chat prompt template, such as 'user' or 'assistant', which determines how the message is positioned in the prompt for the model.
Defines the system content blocks for the chat prompt template, containing the high-level instructions and context provided to the model before the conversation messages.

Defines a cache point block (with type and optional label) in the system prompt of a chat template, specifying where prompt caching begins so that repeated system-prompt prefixes are cached across API requests to reduce cost and latency.
Defines the cache point type for a prompt-caching break in a chat system prompt, with the only supported value being 'default'.
The text of the system prompt included in the chat template for this prompt variant.
Specifies the list of tools (functions) the model may call in a chat prompt variant, along with optional tool choice settings.
Determines how the model selects which tool to invoke when multiple tools are available, supporting automatic, any-of, or a forced specific tool choice.
When specified under tool_choice, this property instructs the model to select and invoke at least one available tool in the current turn, rather than allowing an automatic or no-tool choice.
When enabled (e.g., set to true or an empty object), this property sets the tool choice to auto, allowing the model to autonomously decide whether to call a tool and, if so, which one.
Specifies the particular tool the model must use, defined by the tool's name within the configured tool list, when the tool choice strategy is set to a specific tool.
The name of the tool to select when the prompt's tool configuration specifies a specific tool choice rather than auto or any.
Specifies the list of tools available to the model in the chat tool configuration of the prompt, where each tool object defines its name, description, and input schema for invocation.

The cachePoint property defines a cache point in the tool configuration, enabling the prompt up to this point to be cached, and its 'type' field (e.g., 'default') specifies the kind of cache point to use.
Specifies the cache point type for a tool in a Bedrock prompt's chat tool configuration, where the value 'default' enables prompt caching for that tool's definition.
Defines the tool's specification, including its name, description, and a JSON schema that describes the expected input parameters for the model to invoke it.
Provides a description of the tool that the model uses to understand its purpose and decide when to invoke it.
The JSON schema that defines the expected input parameters for the tool, used by the model to construct valid function calls.
Defines the JSON schema that specifies the input parameters expected by the tool, used by the model to understand how to call the tool.
The name of the tool (function) that the model can invoke, as defined in the tool specification for the chat configuration of this prompt variant.
This block configures the text prompt template for the variant, containing the prompt text and optional input variables that are substituted into the template.
Defines a cache point in the text prompt, with a type that chooses between caching the entire prompt ('default') or only the final portion ('final') to optimize prompt caching during inference.
Specifies the cache point type in the prompt template, which must be `default` to enable caching of the preceding prompt content for reuse across invocations.
Defines the list of placeholder variables (e.g., `{{name}}`, `{{age}}`) used in the text prompt template of this variant, each specifying a name and data type that get substituted at invocation time.
The name of the input variable that is used as a placeholder within the prompt template text, which will be replaced with actual values at runtime.
The string content of the text prompt template configured for this Bedrock prompt variant.
Specifies the Amazon S3 object location (bucket, key, and optionally version) from which this text prompt variant's template text is loaded, instead of being supplied inline in the text field.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that contains the prompt template text file for this variant's text configuration.
The S3 object key of the text prompt template stored in Amazon S3, used as an alternative to inline text for the prompt variant's text template configuration.
The version field specifies the version ID of the S3 object containing the prompt template text, enabling retrieval of a specific version of the object from Amazon S3.

aws_bedrock_prompt.variants.template_typ.text: Specifies the format of the prompt template for this variant, where 'TEXT' indicates a plain-text prompt and 'CHAT' indicates a chat-message-style prompt.

aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.addi.text: For each prompt variant in the Bedrock prompt version, additional_model_request_fields is a JSON object containing extra inference parameters (such as top_k or stopSequences) that are passed through to the model's API request.

aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.gen_.text: Defines the Amazon Bedrock GenAI resource attached to the prompt variant, encapsulating the resource type and its ARN so the prompt version can target that specific agent or model resource.
Configures the Amazon Bedrock agent that this prompt variant is linked to, holding the agent's unique identifier (such as its ARN) in the AgentIdentifier property.
Identifies the Amazon Bedrock agent to which this prompt version's variant is attached, so the prompt is used with that agent.

aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.infe.text: Configures the inference parameters (such as temperature, top-p, and max tokens) applied when the model runs the prompt for this variant.
Specifies the text-specific inference parameters (temperature, topP, maxTokens, and stop sequences) for a prompt variant in the AWS Bedrock prompt version.
Sets the maximum number of tokens the model is allowed to generate in the response for this variant's text inference configuration, effectively capping the output length.
List of character sequences that stop the model from generating further output when encountered in the generated text.
Controls the randomness of the model's text generation, where lower values produce more deterministic and focused outputs and higher values produce more creative or varied outputs.
Specifies the top_p (nucleus sampling) probability threshold for the text inference configuration, determining the cumulative probability mass from which tokens are sampled.

aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.meta.text: The `variants.metadata` field lists the metadata entries (as key-value pairs) attached to each prompt variant in the prompt version, allowing you to store arbitrary additional information (such as author or notes) for a specific variant.
The key of a metadata entry for a prompt variant, representing a user-defined string key in the variant's metadata map.

aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.mode.text: The unique identifier of the foundation model used by this variant of the prompt version.

aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.name.text: The name that uniquely identifies this variant within the prompt version's set of variants.

aws_bedrock_prompt_version.variants.temp.text: Defines the prompt template configuration for a variant, specifying whether it uses a text or chat template along with its content and input variables.
The chat template configuration for a prompt variant, defining the structured conversation messages (with user/assistant roles) and optional system prompts that shape the model's responses.
Defines the list of input variables for the chat template configuration, allowing a prompt variant to reference variable names that are substituted with values at runtime.
The placeholder name for an input variable in the chat prompt template, which is substituted with a value when the prompt is invoked.
Defines the ordered list of chat messages (each with a role and content) that form the conversation template for a variant in this prompt version, providing the model input for chat-style prompts.
Defines the individual content blocks (such as text) that make up a chat message's content within the Bedrock prompt version's chat template configuration.
Configures a cache point in the message content, marking a location in the conversation where Bedrock can cache and reuse the preceding context to reduce inference cost and latency.
Specifies the cache point type as 'default', which instructs Bedrock to cache the preceding message content in the prompt for reuse across subsequent model invocations.
The text of the chat message content block within the prompt template's chat configuration, used as the message body when the prompt is invoked.
The role of the chat message in the prompt template, such as 'user' or 'assistant'.

Specifies the list of system content blocks (each containing text) that define the system prompt for the chat template configuration of a prompt variant, providing high-level instructions to the model.
Specifies a cache point within a system prompt for a chat prompt template, allowing prompt caching to be applied from that point onward in the conversation.
Specifies the type of cache point marker within the system block of the chat template configuration, where the only supported value is 'default' to mark where prompt caching begins.
Specifies the text of a system prompt in the chat template configuration for a prompt variant, which defines the model's behavior and context before user messages are processed.
Specifies the tool configuration for the chat template, defining the tools (e.g., function schemas) available for the model to call during prompt execution.
Specifies how the model should select which tool to use during chat prompt processing, with options for automatic selection, requiring a tool, or forcing a specific named tool.
When present in tool_choice, this empty object instructs the model to invoke any one of the available tools from the chat tool configuration.
Specifies the tool selection as automatic (Auto), letting the model choose the most appropriate tool from the configured tool list rather than forcing a specific tool or allowing any tool.
This object specifies the exact tool the model is required to use, identified by the tool's name within the prompt's tool configuration when the tool choice is set to a specific tool.
The name of the specific tool that the model is directed to use when the tool_choice type is set to 'tool'.
A list of tool definitions that the chat model can invoke, where each tool includes its name, description, and input schema.
Defines a cache point on a tool within the Bedrock prompt version's chat tool configuration, allowing the tool's definition to be cached for prompt-caching efficiency.
In an AWS Bedrock prompt version's tool configuration, this string specifies the cache point type; the only supported value is 'default'.
Defines the tool specification for a tool available to the model, containing its name, description, and the JSON schema for its input parameters.
The description of the tool, which is passed to the model to help it understand the tool's purpose and decide when to invoke it.
The JSON Schema object that defines the input parameters expected by the tool, including their types, constraints, and required fields, which the model uses to format tool invocation arguments.
The JSON schema that defines the input parameters for the tool, specifying the structure and validation constraints for the tool's invocation.
The name of the tool, which is the unique identifier the model uses to invoke the tool during inference.
In each variant of the Bedrock prompt version, this object specifies the text prompt template configuration, defining the prompt text and its input variables for use during model invocation.

Specifies a cache point within the text prompt template configuration, marking a location in the prompt where Bedrock will cache the preceding content to reuse across requests with the same prefix, reducing latency and cost.
Specifies the type of cache point, which enables caching of intermediate results in the prompt; the only supported value is 'default'.
A list of input variables for the text prompt template, each specifying a variable name that can be used as a placeholder within the template text.
Specifies the name of the input variable that is referenced as a placeholder within the prompt template text, which will be substituted with an actual value when the prompt is invoked.
The prompt text content for the text template configuration of this variant in a Bedrock prompt version.
Indicates the type of prompt template used by this variant, either TEXT, CHAT, or IMAGE, which determines how the variant's prompt is structured and processed.

aws_bedrock_session.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Bedrock session, used to assign metadata for organizing, filtering, and managing the session.

aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.acco.text: Specifies the linked accounts (by their account IDs) that are grouped together in this AWS Billing Conductor billing group for consolidated billing and custom pricing.
When enabled, accounts in the organization that are not already associated with another billing group are automatically added to this billing group.
Identifies the AWS accounts that are members of this billing group by their linked account IDs, determining which accounts are billed together under the group's pricing rules.

aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.comp.text: Specifies the cost computation preference for the billing group, referencing the pricing rule ARN that determines how the group's billed amounts are calculated.

aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.desc.text: An optional string that supplies a human-readable explanation of the billing group's purpose or contents, limited to 1024 characters.

aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.name.text: The user-defined name of the billing group, which must be unique within the AWS account and is used to identify the billing group in the Billing Conductor console and APIs.

aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.stat.text: This read-only field indicates the current lifecycle status of the billing group, such as ACTIVE, in the AWS Billing Conductor service.
The reason for the current status of the billing group, providing contextual details when the group is not fully active (e.g., why it failed or is in a transient state).

aws_billing_conductor_billing_group.tags.text: A list of tag objects that define key-value pairs to attach to the billing group, enabling you to categorize and manage billing groups within AWS Billing Conductor.
The key of a user-defined tag assigned to an AWS Billing Conductor billing group, used to organize and identify the group for cost tracking and management.

aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.b.text: The range of billing periods during which the custom line item is active, defined by an inclusive start and exclusive end billing period.

The exclusive_end_billing_period sets the cutoff billing period, in YYYY-MM-DD format, after which the custom line item is no longer applied, with the range being exclusive so the item remains active through the end of the previous billing period.
The inclusive start billing period that defines the first billing period in the range for which the custom line item is applied.

aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.c.text: The ISO currency code (e.g., 'USD') that denominates the custom line item's charges, automatically set to the currency of the associated billing group.
Defines the billing charge type (fee or credit) and the associated flat or percentage amount details for the custom line item.
Specifies the flat-rate charge details for the custom line item, defining a fixed monetary amount (charge_value) that is applied to the associated billing group's usage.
The required fixed amount (in USD) that AWS Billing Conductor charges for the custom line item when its charge type is set to FLAT.
A list of filters that specify which underlying billing line items the custom line item charge applies to, based on matching attributes such as the AWS service, usage type, or operation.
Specifies the billing line item attribute (e.g., LINE_ITEM_TYPE, OPERATION, or USAGE_TYPE) that the filter's value is matched against to determine whether the custom line item is applied.
The list of attribute values that the line item filter matches against, determining which billing line items are selected for the custom line item's charge calculations.
Determines whether the line item filter should match all, any, or none of the specified filter values, with valid values including MATCH_ALL, MATCH_ANY, NOT_MATCH_ALL, and NOT_MATCH_ANY.
Defines the list of matching values (e.g., specific line item types or product names) for the line item filter key, determining which billing line items the custom charge is applied to.
The percentage-based charge configuration for the custom line item, which defines the percentage of the associated billing group's usage that is charged and optionally includes child resources.

Specifies a list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the associated resources that the percentage-based custom line item charge applies to; if omitted, the percentage applies to all resources in the billing group.
The percentage of the custom line item charge, expressed as a numeric percentage (e.g., 10 for 10%).
The type of custom line item charge, which determines whether the line item is a fee (FEE) or a credit (CREDIT) applied to the customer's bill.

aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.d.text: An optional, user-defined text description that provides additional context about the custom line item, aiding identification in billing reports.

aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.n.text: The descriptive name assigned to the custom line item, which appears in billing reports to identify the charge.

aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.p.text: Specifies the customer-facing presentation of the custom line item, including its display name and whether it is visible or hidden on the customer's invoice.
Specifies the AWS service (e.g., AmazonS3, AmazonEC2) that the custom line item's charge applies to, as displayed in the customer's billing presentation.
The unique AWS-generated product code that identifies the custom line item in billing reports and invoices.

aws_billing_conductor_custom_line_item.t.text: Assigns a set of AWS resource tags (key-value pairs) to the custom line item for cost allocation, billing group identification, and resource management.
The key of a user-defined tag attached to the custom line item, used for organizing, categorizing, and filtering billing resources in AWS Billing Conductor.
Specifies the value of a tag attached to the custom line item, enabling you to categorize and track this item in AWS Billing Conductor for cost allocation and management.

aws_billing_conductor_pricing_plan.name.text: The user-defined name for the pricing plan, required when creating the plan in AWS Billing Conductor and used for identification and display.

aws_billing_conductor_pricing_plan.prici.text: The ARNs of the pricing rules to associate with this pricing plan.

aws_billing_conductor_pricing_plan.tags..text: The key portion of a user-defined tag assigned to the AWS Billing Conductor pricing plan, used to identify and categorize the plan within the resource's tag set.
The value of a user-defined tag key-value pair attached to the AWS Billing Conductor pricing plan, used to organize, track, or control access to the plan.

aws_billing_conductor_pricing_rule.tags.text: Specifies a list of tags, each with a Key and Value, to associate with the pricing rule for labeling and cost management.

aws_billing_conductor_pricing_rule.tieri.text: Whether the free tier is activated for this pricing rule, enabling the first set of units to be billed at zero when set to true and disabling the free tier allowance when false.

aws_billing_view.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Billing billing view.

aws_billing_view.data_filter_expression.text: DataFilterExpression selects which cost and usage records are included in the billing view by specifying dimension filters such as service, region, record type, or linked account.

aws_billing_view.data_filter_expression..text: The dimensions property of the data filter expression specifies dimension filters (such as service or region) that restrict the billing view to only include matching billing data.
The name of the billing dimension to filter on (for example, 'SERVICE' or 'REGION'), which along with the dimension values determines which data is included in the billing view.

Specifies a list of dimension values (such as AWS service names or linked account IDs) that the billing view's data filter expression will match against when selecting which cost and usage data to include in the view.
Specifies tag key-value pairs used by the data filter expression to include only resources that have those tags in the billing view.
The tag key used by the billing view's data filter expression to match cost items associated with resources that have a tag with this key.
Defines the list of tag values that the billing view's data filter expression uses to match resources with a specific tag key, thereby including only matching cost and usage data in the view.

aws_billing_view.description.text: An optional user-provided text that gives a human-readable explanation or context for the billing view, helping to distinguish it from other views.

aws_billing_view.name.text: The name of the AWS Billing view, which is required to uniquely identify the view within your account.

aws_billing_view.owner_account_id.text: The AWS account ID of the account that owns the billing view, which is set automatically at creation and cannot be modified.

aws_billing_view.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a tag attached to this billing view, used for cost allocation and management in AWS Billing.

aws_braket_spending_limit.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag key-value pair attached to the AWS::Braket::SpendingLimit resource, used to categorize and manage the spending limit with arbitrary metadata.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.text: The budget object defines the essential budget configuration, including the budget name, type (COST or USAGE), amount limit, time unit, and optional cost filters and cost types.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.auto_adjust_da.text: Configuration for automatic budget limit adjustment, where AWS adjusts the budget's limit based on historical usage or a forecast, including the autoAdjustType (HISTORICAL or FORECAST) and the corresponding adjustment period options.
Indicates whether the budget's automatic adjustment is based on a forecast of future spend (FORECAST) or on historical spending patterns (HISTORICAL).
Specifies the number of historical budget periods (months) of past spending that AWS Budgets uses to calculate the automatically adjusted budget amount.
Specifies the number of months of historical spending data that AWS Budgets uses to automatically calculate the adjusted budget amount.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.billing_view_a.text: Specifies the ARN of an AWS Billing view that the budget is scoped to, allowing the budget to track costs only for the accounts and usage associated with that billing view.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.budget_limit.text: Specifies the cost or usage threshold for the budget, defined by an amount and unit (for example, '100.0' and 'USD').

aws_budgets_budget.budget.budget_limit.a.text: The numerical amount of the budget limit, representing the maximum cost or usage allowed by the budget.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.budget_limit.u.text: The three-letter currency code (e.g., USD) that defines the monetary unit for the budget limit amount and must match the currency of the AWS account.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.budget_name.text: The name of the budget, which acts as a unique identifier within the AWS account for the specified budget type; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name (e.g., the logical ID).

aws_budgets_budget.budget.budget_type.text: Specifies the type of budget, such as COST, USAGE, RI_UTILIZATION, RI_COVERAGE, SAVINGS_PLANS_UTILIZATION, or SAVINGS_PLANS_COVERAGE, which determines the metric and dimensions used to track your AWS spend or usage.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_filters.text: A map of cost filter dimension names (such as Service, LinkedAccount, Region, or TagKeyValue) to lists of values that restricts the budget to matching AWS costs, analogous to the CostFilters property in the AWS Budgets API.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.text: Specifies the CostTypes object that controls which AWS cost types (such as taxes, subscriptions, recurring charges, support, discounts, credits, and upfront fees) are included or excluded when calculating the budget's actual and forecasted costs.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.inc.text: Specifies whether credits (such as promotional AWS credits) are included when calculating the costs covered by this budget.
Determines whether discounts are included in the cost amounts tracked by this budget.
Controls whether the budget includes other non-recurring subscription costs, such as one-time fees for services like Amazon QuickSight.
Whether the budget includes recurring costs (such as monthly subscription or recurring service fees) when calculating actual spend against the budget.
Indicates whether the budget includes refunds when calculating costs.
Specifies whether the budget includes subscription costs (such as AWS Support) when determining actual and forecasted spend.
Determines whether AWS Support charges (such as subscription fees for AWS Support plans) are included when calculating the costs tracked by this budget.
Specifies whether the budget includes taxes associated with your usage.
Specifies whether to include upfront fees, such as the one-time payment for Reserved Instances, in the budget's cost calculations.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.cost_types.use.text: In AWS Budgets, this boolean flag in the budget's cost types controls whether the budget includes amortized costs, which spread upfront reservation or savings plan charges over the term of the commitment.
A boolean flag that indicates whether the budget includes blended costs, which are calculated by mixing the effective rates of on-demand and reserved-instance usage.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.filter_express.text: Specifies a logical expression of key-value filters (such as service, tag, or account) and an operator (AND or OR) that determines which cost and usage data is included in the budget.

Specifies a list of filter expressions that must all be satisfied (logical AND) for a cost or usage item to be counted in the budget, enabling combined dimension-based filtering (e.g., service and region together).

Maps cost category names to lists of values within the budget's filter expression; only actual costs that match at least one of the listed values for each configured cost category are counted toward the budget.
The name of the AWS Cost Category to use as a filter key for this budget.
Specifies the matching options (such as EQUALS, STARTS_WITH) that apply to the cost category values in the budget's filter expression.
Defines the specific values of the chosen cost category that the budget filter matches, restricting the budget to only include costs associated with those cost category values.
Defines the AWS cost dimensions (like SERVICE or REGION) and their allowed values that this budget's filter expression uses to match and track specific cost and usage.
Specifies the dimension name (e.g., SERVICE, REGION, or AZ) that the budget's filter expression uses to filter cost or usage data.
Specifies a list of match options (such as EQUALS or STARTS_WITH) that determine how the dimension values in the filter are matched against actual budget costs.
The list of specific values for the dimension in the budget's filter expression, such as service names (e.g., AmazonS3) when the dimension is SERVICE.
The `not` field holds a nested filter expression that is logically negated, so the budget applies only to costs that do not match the nested criteria.
A list of filter sub-expressions that are combined using OR logic, so that a cost is included in the budget if it matches any of the listed sub-expressions.
Defines the tag-based filters (tag key and list of values) that restrict the budget's cost scope to matching tagged resources in the budget filter expression.
The tag key used in the budget's filter expression to scope the budget to costs associated with that tag.

Defines how the cost allocation tag key-value pairs in the budget filter expression are matched (e.g., using EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, or CONTAINS) against the tags applied to your resources, controlling which resource usage is included in the budget.
Specifies the list of tag values to match when the budget's filter expression filters by a tag key, limiting the budget's coverage to costs from resources tagged with any of these values.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.planned_budget.text: Specifies budget limits for future cost budget periods, mapping each period's start date (YYYY-MM-DD) to a budget limit amount and unit for that period.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.time_period.text: Specifies the start and end dates that determine the period covered by the budget.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.time_period.en.text: The end date of the budget time period, indicating the last day the budget is active; if omitted, the budget period is open-ended.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.time_period.st.text: The start date and time of the budget's coverage period, expressed in UTC (usually ISO 8601 format), which determines the beginning of the time window over which costs are evaluated against the budget.

aws_budgets_budget.budget.time_unit.text: The time unit (DAILY, MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, or ANNUALLY) that defines the period over which the budget tracks costs or usage and resets.

aws_budgets_budget.id.text: The budget name, which uniquely identifies the budget within the AWS account and is used as the resource's primary identifier.

aws_budgets_budget.notifications_with_su.text: Specifies the budget notifications and the email or SNS subscribers to receive alerts when the budget threshold is exceeded.

Defines the notification configuration for a budget, including threshold value, comparison operator (e.g., GREATER_THAN), threshold type (PERCENTAGE or ABSOLUTE_VALUE), and notification type (e.g., ACTUAL or FORECASTED), which triggers an alert to the subscribed SNS topics or email addresses.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., GREATER_THAN, LESS_THAN, EQUAL_TO) used to evaluate the budget's actual or forecasted value against the notification threshold.
Specifies whether the budget notification is triggered by actual spending or a forecasted spend amount.
The numeric threshold value that, when compared against the actual or forecasted budget cost or usage using the notification's comparison operator, triggers the budget notification.

Specifies whether the budget notification threshold is expressed as a percentage of the budget limit or as an absolute value (e.g., a dollar amount or usage quantity), corresponding to the PERCENTAGE or ABSOLUTE_VALUE enum values for the budget alarm.
Specifies the list of subscribers (email addresses or SNS topic ARNs) that receive the budget notification.
The email address or SNS topic ARN that receives the budget notification for the associated subscriber type.
The subscription channel type used by the subscriber to receive budget notifications, such as SNS or EMAIL.

aws_budgets_budget.resource_tags.text: Specifies a list of resource tag key-value pairs (with Key and Value properties) that are attached to this AWS Budgets budget to help categorize and manage it for cost allocation and filtering.

aws_budgets_budget.resource_tags.key.text: The key of a resource tag (a key-value pair) applied to the budget, used to categorize or identify the budget for cost allocation and management.

aws_budgets_budget.resource_tags.value.text: The value of a tag entry in the resource_tags map, used to attach metadata to the budget resource for identification and organization.

aws_budgets_budgets_action.action_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this budget action, returned as a read-only attribute after creation.

aws_budgets_budgets_action.action_thresh.text: Defines the threshold (a numeric value and type, either absolute dollar amount or percentage) that triggers the budget action when the actual or forecasted budget usage exceeds it.
Determines whether the threshold value is interpreted as an absolute dollar amount or as a percentage of the budget.
The numeric threshold value that triggers the budget action, interpreted according to the sibling threshold type (e.g., as a percentage of the budget limit or as an absolute monetary amount).

aws_budgets_budgets_action.action_type.text: Specifies the type of budget action to execute when a budget threshold is exceeded, such as APPLY_IAM_POLICY, APPLY_SCP_POLICY, or RUN_SSM_DOCUMENT, which determines whether the action applies an IAM policy, a service control policy, or runs an SSM document.

aws_budgets_budgets_action.approval_mode.text: Defines whether the budget action executes automatically or requires manual approval after it is triggered (valid values: AUTOMATIC or MANUAL).

aws_budgets_budgets_action.budget_name.text: The name of the AWS Budgets budget that this action is associated with.

aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.text: The definition object specifies the budget action's type and its configuration, including the action type (such as APPLY_IAM_POLICY or RESET_IAM_POLICY) and the corresponding details like the IAM policy ARN or target account for the action.

aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.ia.text: This object specifies the IAM action definition for a budget action, including the IAM policy ARN and the IAM roles, groups, or users to which the policy is applied.
Specifies a list of IAM group names to which the budget action's IAM policy will be applied, allowing the action to modify permissions for those groups.
The ARN of the IAM policy that the budget action attaches to or detaches from the specified IAM role, user, or group when the action is triggered.
The list of IAM roles to which the budget action applies the IAM policy defined in the IamActionDefinition.
The list of IAM user ARNs to which the budget action's IAM policy will be applied.

aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.sc.text: Configuration for a budget action that applies a service control policy (SCP), specifying the SCP policy ID and target account IDs.
The unique ID of the service control policy (SCP) that this budget action applies to when the budget threshold is exceeded.
The list of AWS account or organizational unit IDs to which the service control policy is applied by this budget action.

aws_budgets_budgets_action.definition.ss.text: The SSM action definition under 'definition' that specifies the target instance IDs, AWS Region, and subtype (such as STOP_EC2_INSTANCES or STOP_RDS_INSTANCES) used to execute the associated Systems Manager automation document as a budget action.
Specifies the list of EC2 instance IDs on which the SSM action (such as stopping or terminating instances) is executed when the budget action is triggered.
The AWS Region where the target EC2 instances for the Systems Manager (SSM) budget action are located.
The subtype of the Systems Manager action, specifying whether to stop Amazon EC2 instances or Amazon RDS instances.

aws_budgets_budgets_action.execution_rol.text: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Budgets assumes to execute the budget action, such as applying a policy or sending a notification.

aws_budgets_budgets_action.notification_.text: The type of budget notification that triggers the action, either ACTUAL (fired when actual spending exceeds the threshold) or FORECASTED (fired when spending is projected to exceed the threshold).

aws_budgets_budgets_action.resource_tags.text: Specifies the list of resource tags to apply to the budget action, enabling you to add metadata for identification, cost allocation, and management of the action resource.
The key of a resource tag attached to this AWS budget action, used to label and organize the action with custom metadata.
The value of a resource tag key-value pair assigned to the AWS Budgets action.

aws_budgets_budgets_action.subscribers.text: The list of subscribers to notify when the budget action is triggered, where each subscriber defines the notification method (email address or SNS topic) and the corresponding address.

aws_budgets_budgets_action.subscribers.a.text: The email address or SNS topic ARN that serves as the destination for the budget action notification sent to this subscriber.

aws_budgets_budgets_action.subscribers.t.text: Specifies the notification channel for a budget action subscriber, either SNS or EMAIL, which determines how the subscriber receives the alert or action notification.

aws_cases_case.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag attached to the AWS Cases case, used to store user-defined metadata for organizing, searching, or managing the case.

aws_cases_case_rule.rule.hidden.conditio.text: Within an Amazon Connect Cases case rule, this list contains the conditions under which the rule will hide the designated case fields from the case view.
Defines an equality condition for a hidden case rule, matching when the value of the referenced case field exactly equals the configured value.

This object is the first operand of an equality condition within the hidden conditions of an Amazon Connect Cases rule, specifying the source value (such as a case field reference or literal) to be compared against the second operand.
Specifies the unique identifier of the case field that acts as the first operand in an equal-to condition used to determine whether the hidden rule action applies.

Defines the second operand (typically a literal value or field reference) in an equality condition of an AWS Cases case rule, specifying what the first operand must match for the condition to be true.
The Boolean value to which the case field is compared in the equal_to condition, determining when the hidden rule action applies.
The double_value specifies the numeric floating-point value that operand_two must hold on a case for the equal_to condition to match during evaluation of the rule's hidden conditions.
When set, this field indicates that the second operand of the 'equals' condition is an empty value, causing the rule to trigger when the specified case field is empty.

For an `equal_to` condition in an AWS Cases case rule's hidden condition set, this field holds the second operand's string literal, which is compared against the first operand (typically a case field) to determine when the rule's action is triggered.
This object specifies a 'not equal to' comparison condition that, when true, contributes to hiding the associated field in an AWS Cases case layout.
Specifies the first operand to be compared in a 'not equal to' condition within the hidden conditions of the AWS Cases rule, which can reference a case field by ID or a literal value.
The unique identifier of the case field used as the left operand in a 'NotEqualTo' condition, evaluated within the rule's hidden conditions to determine if the rule is hidden.
Defines the second operand (either a case field reference or a fixed value) that the first operand is compared against in a 'not_equal_to' condition within a hidden rule of an AWS Cases case rule.
Specifies the Boolean value to compare a Boolean field against in a 'not equal to' rule condition, triggering the rule when the field's value does not equal this boolean.
In AWS Cases case rules, this number is the double-precision value used as the second operand in a 'not equal to' condition, serving as the literal that the evaluated case field is compared against.
When present in operand_two of a 'not_equal_to' condition in an AWS Cases case rule, this empty_value object indicates that the rule evaluates whether the specified field's value is not empty.
The string value of the right-hand side operand in a 'not equal to' comparison within a condition of a hidden rule for an AWS Cases case rule.

aws_cases_case_rule.rule.hidden.default_.text: Determines whether the field is hidden by default when the hidden rule's condition does not evaluate to true (or when no condition is specified).

aws_cases_case_rule.rule.required.text: Defines the required-field criteria for the rule, specifying which case fields must be present or carry a particular value for a case to comply with the rule.

aws_cases_case_rule.rule.required.condit.text: Specifies an equality comparison condition that must be met for the AWS Cases rule to trigger, evaluating whether a case field equals a defined value.
Defines the first operand of an equality condition in a case rule, which is compared against the second operand to determine whether the condition matches and triggers the rule's action.
The identifier of a case field whose value is compared to the second operand in an equal-to condition within an AWS Cases case rule.
The second operand of this 'equal to' condition, which can be a reference to a case field or a static value, used alongside the first operand to evaluate whether the rule's condition is satisfied.
In the 'equal_to' condition of a case rule, this boolean value specifies the second operand's literal value, matching when the evaluated field equals that boolean (true or false).
Specifies the double-precision floating-point value to which a case field is compared in an 'equal_to' condition within a rule's required condition set.
When set to an empty object, this indicates that the second operand of the 'equal to' rule condition is the empty value, so the condition matches when the case field is empty.
Specifies the literal string value of the second operand in an equal-to condition, used to compare against the first operand (a case field's value) to determine whether the rule's condition is met.
Specifies the boolean value to set on the target field when the equal-to condition in this AWS Cases case rule is satisfied.

Specifies the left operand for a 'not equal to' comparison in an Amazon Connect Cases rule condition, containing either a case field reference or a literal value that is compared against the second operand to trigger the rule action.
The field_id of operand_one is the unique identifier of a case field whose value is used as the left operand in the not_equal_to condition.
The second operand in a 'not equal to' condition of an Amazon Connect Cases rule, which holds the value (or field reference) that the first operand must not equal for the condition to match.
The boolean value that serves as the second operand for the 'not_equal_to' comparison in a case rule condition.
The double-precision numeric literal for the second operand of the 'not equal to' condition, representing the value the rule expects the field (first operand) to not match.
Indicates that the second operand of the `not_equal_to` condition is treated as an empty value, causing the rule to match when the source field is not empty.

Defines the string literal for the second operand (the comparison value) in a NotEqualTo condition, so that the rule condition is satisfied only when the selected case field's value does not equal this string.

aws_cases_case_rule.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the AWS Cases case rule, used for organizing, filtering, and managing the rule resource.

aws_cases_domain.tags.key.text: The tag key for a tag attached to the AWS Cases domain.

aws_cases_domain.tags.value.text: The value string of a key-value tag applied to the Amazon Connect Cases domain, used to store metadata such as environment or cost center for the resource.

aws_cases_field.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Cases field, used for metadata and resource management.

aws_cases_layout.content.basic.text: The basic layout configuration for the case layout, defining how case panel and additional information sections are arranged on the page.

aws_cases_layout.content.basic.more_info.text: The 'more_info' object configures the 'More Info' section of a basic layout, defining which case fields are displayed in that additional, separate area of the AWS Cases layout.
Specifies the list of sections that make up the 'More Info' area of a basic layout in an AWS Cases layout, where each section can contain text or a reference to a case field.
Defines a field group within a section of the 'More Info' area of the basic case layout, containing the ordered list of field items to be displayed together.
Specifies the list of case fields to display in this field group within the 'More info' section of the basic layout.
The id of a field within a field group in the 'more info' section of a layout's basic content, referencing the unique identifier of the Amazon Connect Cases case field to display at that position.
The display name of the field group, shown as a heading in the case layout section to visually group related case fields.

aws_cases_layout.content.basic.top_panel.text: Specifies the top panel of the basic layout, defining the sections and field items displayed at the top of the case view.
Specifies the ordered list of sections in the top panel of the basic layout, where each section groups a set of case fields with an optional title for display in the case details view.
Defines the field group for a section in the top panel of the basic layout, including the group name and the list of case fields to display in that section.
Defines the list of fields included in this field group for the layout, each referencing a field from the case template by its identifier.
The unique identifier of the case field to display, referencing an existing field in the case domain.
The name of the field group, which serves as the display label for the set of fields grouped within the top panel section of the case layout.

aws_cases_layout.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Cases layout, used to store arbitrary metadata for the layout.

aws_cases_template.required_fields.field.text: The identifier of the case field that must be included when creating a case using this template.

aws_cases_template.rules.case_rule_id.text: Specifies the unique identifier for a rule within the AWS Cases template, used to reference the rule when defining conditional field requirements.

aws_cases_template.rules.field_id.text: The unique identifier of the case field in Amazon Cases that this rule applies to, matching a field defined in the associated domain.

aws_cassandra_keyspace.replication_speci.text: Specifies the replication strategy (single or multi-Region) and the list of Regions for a multi-Region Amazon Keyspaces keyspace.
A list of AWS regions where the keyspace is replicated for Multi-Region Replication, enabling data availability across those regions.
Specifies the replication strategy for the keyspace, either SINGLE_REGION for single-region replication or MULTI_REGION for replicating data across multiple AWS regions.

aws_cassandra_keyspace.tags.text: Assigns a list of key-value metadata tags to the Cassandra keyspace, which can be used for categorization and cost tracking.

aws_cassandra_table.auto_scaling_specifi.text: When true, disables auto scaling for the table's read capacity, reverting to the fixed read capacity units configured on the table.
The maximum number of read capacity units (RCUs) that the table's read capacity can scale up to when auto scaling is enabled.
Sets the minimum number of read capacity units for the table's read capacity auto scaling policy in Amazon Keyspaces.
When true, prevents the target tracking scaling policy from reducing (scaling in) the table's read capacity.
The amount of time in seconds after a scale-in activity completes before another scale-in can begin for the read capacity of the Cassandra table's auto scaling target tracking policy.

The amount of time, in seconds, after a scale-out (increase) activity completes before another scale-out activity can start, used in the target tracking scaling policy for read capacity auto scaling of an Amazon Keyspaces (Cassandra) table.
The target value, expressed as a percentage, for read capacity utilization that the auto scaling policy maintains.
Disables automatic scaling of write capacity for the Amazon Keyspaces table, preventing CloudFormation from adjusting provisioned write capacity based on traffic.
The maximum number of write capacity units that the AWS Keyspaces table can scale up to when auto scaling is enabled for write capacity.
Specifies the minimum number of write capacity units that the table can scale down to when write capacity auto scaling is enabled.
Specifies whether scale-in (reducing write capacity) is disabled for this target tracking scaling policy, so the policy can scale out but not automatically scale in.
The cooldown period in seconds after a scale-in activity completes before the write capacity auto scaling policy can trigger another scale-in operation for the Cassandra table.
The number of seconds to wait after a scale-out activity completes before another scale-out activity can start for write capacity auto scaling on the Cassandra table.
The target utilization percentage (e.g., 50 for 50%) that the Amazon Keyspaces write capacity target tracking scaling policy aims to maintain for auto scaling.

aws_cassandra_table.billing_mode.text: Specifies the billing mode for the Cassandra table, choosing between on-demand and provisioned capacity, and when provisioned, includes the read/write capacity settings.

aws_cassandra_table.billing_mode.provisi.text: The number of read capacity units to provision for the Cassandra table when billing mode is set to provisioned.
Specifies the number of write capacity units (writes per second) that this Cassandra table can sustain when using provisioned billing mode.

aws_cassandra_table.clustering_key_colum.text: Specifies the name and type of a single column that is used as the clustering key, determining the sort order of rows within a partition in the Cassandra table.
The name of the clustering key column that defines the sort order of rows within each partition of the Cassandra table.
The Cassandra data type of the clustering key column (e.g., 'text', 'int', 'uuid').
Specifies the sort order (ASC or DESC) for this clustering key column, determining how rows are stored and queried in the Cassandra table.

aws_cassandra_table.partition_key_column.text: The name of a column that is part of the table's partition key, determining how rows are distributed across partitions in the Cassandra table.
The Cassandra data type (e.g., TEXT, INT, UUID, TIMESTAMP) assigned to this partition key column in the AWS::Cassandra::Table resource, matching the supported column types for Cassandra tables.

aws_cassandra_table.regular_columns.colu.text: The name of a regular (non-partition-key and non-clustering) column in the Cassandra table, defining the column's identifier in the table schema.
The Cassandra data type for the regular column, such as text, int, or timestamp, as defined in the regular_columns list of the table.

aws_cassandra_table.replica_specificatio.text: Defines the AWS Regions and optional provisioned read/write capacity settings for each replica in a multi-Region Amazon Keyspaces table.
Configures the auto scaling settings for read capacity of an Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) table replica, including enablement, minimum and maximum capacity units, and target utilization.
When true, disables automatic scaling of read capacity for the replica, requiring you to specify fixed read capacity instead.
The maximum number of read capacity units that the table can scale up to under automatic scaling.
Specifies the minimum read capacity (in read request units per second) that Amazon Keyspaces can scale down to for the corresponding replica in this table.
Defines the target tracking scaling policy configuration (e.g., target utilization and scale-in/out behavior) for the read capacity auto scaling of the Cassandra table replica.
Specifies the target tracking scaling policy configuration, including the target value and scale-in behavior, used for read capacity auto scaling on this replica.
When true, this target tracking scaling policy will not scale in (reduce provisioned read capacity) in response to low utilization, allowing only scale-out actions.

The amount of time, in seconds, after a scale-in activity completes before the read capacity target tracking policy can initiate another scale-in, used to prevent rapid repeated scaling down for a Cassandra table replica.
The cooldown period (in seconds) that elapses before a scale-out activity can start, preventing rapid increases in read capacity for the replica.
The target utilization percentage for read capacity that the auto scaling policy aims to maintain, triggering scaling adjustments to keep provisioned read capacity in line with the workload.
The number of read capacity units provisioned for this specific replica of the Cassandra table in its designated AWS region.
Specifies the AWS Region where the Cassandra table replica is created, enabling multi-Region replication.

aws_cassandra_table.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a tag assigned to the Cassandra table.

aws_cassandra_table.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag assigned to the Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) table, used for cost allocation and resource management.

aws_cassandra_table.warm_throughput.read.text: Number of warm read capacity units per second for the table's warm throughput configuration.

aws_cassandra_table.warm_throughput.writ.text: The number of write capacity units per second allocated for throughput on warm data stored in the Amazon Keyspaces table.

aws_cassandra_type.fields.field_name.text: The name of a field within a user-defined Cassandra type in Amazon Keyspaces, defining the structure of the type.

aws_cassandra_type.fields.field_type.text: The Cassandra data type assigned to this field within the custom type definition, specified as a string such as 'int' or 'text'.

aws_ce_anomaly_monitor.monitor_specifica.text: A JSON-formatted string that defines the custom monitoring criteria for the cost anomaly monitor, such as filtering by services, linked accounts, or cost categories, used when the monitor type is CUSTOM.

aws_ce_anomaly_monitor.monitor_type.text: Specifies whether the anomaly monitor is a DIMENSIONAL monitor (which watches a specific dimension like service or linked account) or a CUSTOM monitor (which uses a custom threshold on the anomaly score).

aws_ce_anomaly_monitor.resource_tags.key.text: The tag key for a resource tag applied to the Cost Explorer anomaly monitor, used for identifying and organizing the monitor among AWS resources.

aws_ce_anomaly_monitor.resource_tags.val.text: The value of a resource tag attached to the AWS Cost Explorer anomaly monitor, used for tagging and cost allocation.

aws_ce_anomaly_subscription.resource_tag.text: The key of a resource tag attached to the AWS Cost Explorer anomaly subscription, used to identify or categorize the subscription within a key-value pair.
Specifies the value of a key-value tag applied to the AWS Cost Explorer anomaly subscription, used for organizing, filtering, and controlling access to the subscription resource.

aws_ce_anomaly_subscription.subscribers..text: The email address or Amazon SNS topic ARN that receives notifications for this anomaly subscription.
The subscription status of the subscriber, indicating whether the subscriber has confirmed or declined the anomaly alert subscription.
Specifies the type of AWS Cost Explorer anomaly subscription subscriber, either EMAIL or SNS_TOPIC.

aws_ce_cost_category.name.text: The name of the cost category, which must be unique within your AWS account and is used to identify the cost category in the AWS Cost Management console and APIs.

aws_ce_cost_category.rule_version.text: Specifies the version of the cost category rule syntax, which must be set to 'CostCategoryExpression.v1' for the rule expressions.

aws_ce_cost_category.tags.key.text: The key portion of a tag applied to the AWS Cost Category.

aws_ce_cost_category.tags.value.text: Specifies the value portion of a user-defined tag (key-value pair) applied to the AWS Cost Category, used to categorize and track cost allocation.

aws_certificate_manager_account.account_.text: The AWS account ID that owns this ACM account-level configuration, automatically derived from the account in which the resource is deployed.

aws_certificate_manager_account.expiry_e.text: Configures the day-based threshold (DaysBeforeExpiry) at which AWS Certificate Manager emits certificate expiration events, enabling EventBridge notifications for upcoming renewals.
Specifies the number of days before certificate expiration when ACM begins emitting expiry-related events, allowing you to adjust the notification lead time.

aws_certificate_manager_certificate.doma.text: The domain name for which certificate validation options are specified, corresponding to one of the domains in the certificate's Subject Alternative Names.
The ID of the hosted zone in Route 53 where the DNS validation record for this domain will be created.
The domain that AWS Certificate Manager will use for validation (e.g., email or DNS checks), which can be a different domain than the one being certified.

aws_certificate_manager_certificate.tags.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Certificate Manager certificate, used for metadata, cost allocation, and resource organization.

aws_chatbot_custom_action.action_name.text: A unique, human-readable name for the custom action, used to identify and invoke it within AWS Chatbot (e.g., in Slack or Teams slash commands).

aws_chatbot_custom_action.alias_name.text: Specifies the alias for the custom action, allowing users to invoke the action with a shorter or alternate name in chat.

aws_chatbot_custom_action.attachments.bu.text: The text displayed on the button within the message attachment for the AWS Chatbot custom action.

aws_chatbot_custom_action.attachments.cr.text: The `criteria` list holds filter conditions that determine whether a given notification or command invocation should use this attachment, restricting the custom action to matching events.

The operator in an attachment criteria condition for an AWS Chatbot custom action, specifying the comparison method (e.g., 'CONTAINS' or 'EQUALS') used to match message attachment key/value pairs when determining whether the action can be invoked.

The value that AWS Chatbot compares against the event attribute specified by the sibling 'key' field using the sibling 'operator' logic, to decide whether the attachment should be included for a custom action invocation.
