Specifies the name of a notification message variable that this attachment criterion evaluates (together with an operator and value) to decide whether the corresponding custom action is presented for that notification.

aws_chatbot_custom_action.attachments.no.text: Specifies the type of AWS notification (such as a CloudWatch alarm state change) that this attachment associates with the chatbot custom action.

aws_chatbot_custom_action.attachments.va.text: Defines the map of variable names to values that are substituted into the custom action's command when this attachment is used.

aws_chatbot_custom_action.custom_action_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the custom action in AWS Chatbot, assigned by AWS when the resource is created.

aws_chatbot_custom_action.definition.text: Defines the custom action by providing the command text (CommandText) that the AWS Chatbot runs when the action is invoked.

aws_chatbot_custom_action.definition.com.text: The command text that defines the custom action's behavior, such as a shell command or script, which is executed when the action is triggered.

aws_chatbot_custom_action.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs that can be attached to the AWS Chatbot custom action to help identify, organize, and manage the resource, with each object containing a Key and Value property.

aws_chatbot_custom_action.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Chatbot custom action, used to identify and categorize the resource for management and cost tracking.

aws_chatbot_microsoft_teams_channel_conf.text: The user-defined key for a tag attached to an AWS Chatbot Microsoft Teams channel configuration, used for organizing, filtering, and cost-tracking the resource.
The tag value for a key-value pair applied to the AWS Chatbot Microsoft Teams channel configuration resource.

aws_chatbot_slack_channel_configuration..text: The key of a tag assigned to an AWS Chatbot Slack channel configuration, enabling cost allocation tracking and resource categorization within AWS.
The value component of a key-value tag that can be attached to the AWS Chatbot Slack channel configuration for resource organization and cost allocation.

aws_chime_app_instance.tags.key.text: The key of a tag that is attached to the Amazon Chime AppInstance resource for identification and organization.

aws_chime_app_instance.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to the Chime AppInstance, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_chime_app_instance_bot.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AppInstanceBot, used to categorize and manage the resource (e.g., environment, project) in AWS Chime.

aws_chime_app_instance_bot.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined metadata tag attached to the Amazon Chime App Instance Bot.

aws_chime_app_instance_user.app_instance.text: The ARN of the Amazon Chime AppInstance in which this user is created, uniquely identifying the parent app instance for the user.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AppInstanceUser, assigned by AWS when the user is created.
The client-supplied unique identifier for the user within the specified Amazon Chime AppInstance, which is required at creation and is used to form the user's ARN.

aws_chime_app_instance_user.expiration_s.text: Configures automatic deletion of the AppInstanceUser after a specified number of days from its creation timestamp, using an expiration criterion and day count.
Specifies whether the expiration date for the AppInstanceUser is calculated from the user's creation timestamp (CREATED_TIMESTAMP) or their last activity timestamp (LAST_ACTIVE_TIMESTAMP).
The number of days after which the Amazon Chime AppInstanceUser account automatically expires and is deleted.

aws_chime_app_instance_user.metadata.text: An optional user-defined metadata string (up to 1000 characters) attached to the AppInstanceUser for app-specific information.

aws_chime_app_instance_user.name.text: Sets the display name for the AppInstanceUser, which is used to identify the user within the Amazon Chime app instance.

aws_chime_app_instance_user.tags.text: Specifies a list of tags to associate with the App Instance User, used for organizing and managing the user in AWS Chime.

aws_chime_app_instance_user.tags.key.text: The key of a key-value tag attached to the Amazon Chime AppInstanceUser, used to label and categorize the resource.

aws_chime_app_instance_user.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag attached to an Amazon Chime AppInstanceUser, used to add user-defined metadata to the identity for management and tracking.

aws_chime_channel_flow.processors.config.text: Defines the configuration for a processor in the channel flow, specifying the Lambda function ARN and the invocation role ARN used when the processor type is Lambda.
The configuration block for a Lambda processor in a Chime channel flow, specifying the Lambda function ARN and the IAM role ARN used to invoke it.
Specifies whether the Lambda function is invoked asynchronously (ASYNC) or synchronously (SYNC) for this processor in the channel flow.
The ARN of the AWS Lambda function that the Amazon Chime channel flow invokes to process messages for this processor.

aws_chime_channel_flow.processors.execut.text: The integer execution order of this processor within the channel flow, which determines the sequence in which processors are invoked during message processing.

aws_chime_channel_flow.processors.fallba.text: The action to execute if the processor's primary action fails, such as 'SEND' or 'DELETE'.

aws_chime_channel_flow.processors.name.text: The user-defined name that identifies this processor within the channel flow's processor list, used for configuration and runtime reference.

aws_chime_channel_flow.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Chime ChannelFlow resource.

aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.analys.text: The default value to use for the analysis parameter when a value is not provided at runtime.
Specifies the name of an analysis parameter in the analysis template, which is used as a placeholder in the template's SQL query.
Defines the SQL data type of the parameter (e.g., INT, STRING, BOOLEAN) used to enforce type-checking when the analysis template is run in a Clean Rooms collaboration.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this analysis template, returned after creation.

aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the analysis template in AWS Clean Rooms.

aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.collab.text: The ARN of the collaboration that this analysis template belongs to.
The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that this analysis template belongs to, which is assigned by AWS and cannot be changed.

aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.descri.text: Specifies a user-provided description for the analysis template to help identify its purpose.

aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.error_.text: Specifies the custom error message (including subject and body) that AWS Clean Rooms returns to users when a query based on this analysis template is denied or fails.
Indicates the type of error message delivery mechanism; when set to 'S3', error messages from the analysis template are written to an Amazon S3 bucket configured in the accompanying S3 property.

aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.format.text: Specifies the query language of the analysis template, with valid values being 'SQL' or 'PYTHON'.

aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.member.text: The ARN of the AWS Clean Rooms membership associated with this analysis template, automatically assigned by AWS.
The unique identifier of the membership that owns this analysis template.

aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.name.text: The name of the analysis template, used to identify and reference the template within the collaboration.

aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.schema.text: Specifies the referenced tables (via an AnalysisSchema object) that the analysis template's SQL query is allowed to access.
The list of table names in the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that the analysis template's SQL query is permitted to reference, restricting the query's data access.

aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.source.text: The source object defines the SQL query content for the analysis template, containing the query text that will be executed against the collaboration data.
The S3 URIs of the analysis artifacts (such as SQL query files) that make up the source of the Clean Rooms analysis template.
Specifies additional artifacts (as objects containing artifact URIs) to be included with the analysis template's source, enabling the analysis to use supporting files beyond the primary SQL query.
Specifies the S3 location (bucket and key) of an additional artifact, such as a supporting file or script, that is part of the analysis template's source artifacts.

The S3 bucket name that stores an additional artifact (such as a custom analysis script or supporting file) for the AWS Clean Rooms analysis template's source, as specified in the source's artifacts list.
The Amazon S3 object key (file name) of an additional artifact that is part of the analysis template's source artifacts.
The entry_point object specifies the S3 location of the main Python script that serves as the starting point for the analysis in an AWS Clean Rooms analysis template.
The S3 location of the entry point query file, specified as an object with a bucket and key that identify the SQL script in Amazon S3.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that stores the entry-point artifact (the primary analysis file) for the analysis template's source artifacts.
The S3 object key within the specified S3 bucket that identifies the entry point file (e.g., a SQL script) for the analysis template's source artifacts.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS Clean Rooms read access to the S3 objects in the source artifacts location.
The SQL query text that defines the analysis template's source, used as the basis for the analysis.
Maps artifact names to their S3 URI locations, defining the source code artifacts for the analysis template within the source_metadata block.
Specifies the SHA-256 hash of an additional artifact file that is part of the source metadata for the analysis template.
The SHA256 hash of the entry point artifact (SQL script) in the analysis template's source metadata, used to verify the integrity of the source code.

aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.synthe.text: Configures the generation of synthetic data based on the analysis template's schema, including the desired row count, for testing analysis queries without using real data.
Configures the machine learning model parameters for generating a differentially private synthetic dataset from the analysis template's query results.

Specifies the per-column classification (such as categorical or numeric) applied when generating ML synthetic data from the analysis template's underlying dataset, controlling how each column is modeled by the synthetic data generator.
The name of the source column that is assigned a classification in the column mapping for generating ML synthetic data in the analysis template.

The semantic type assigned to the mapped column (for example, categorical, numeric, datetime, or free_text) that AWS Clean Rooms uses to guide the ML synthetic data generation process for the analysis template.

Indicates whether this column is classified as a predictive feature (input variable) for the machine learning model when generating synthetic data in AWS Clean Rooms, so the service preserves its relationship to the training label.
Specifies the privacy loss budget (epsilon) for the differentially private synthetic data generation, where lower values produce more private but less accurate data.

The maximum acceptable membership inference attack score for synthetic data generated for machine learning, providing a privacy threshold to limit the risk of inferring original data membership from the synthetic dataset.

aws_clean_rooms_analysis_template.tags.k.text: The user-defined key of a tag attached to the AWS Clean Rooms analysis template, used to categorize, organize, and identify the resource.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.allowed_re.text: Limits the AWS Regions where members of the collaboration can write query results, restricting result outputs to the specified regions.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.analytics_.text: Specifies the analytics engine for the collaboration, which must be either `CLEAN_ROOMS_SQL` (the default) or `SPARK`, and controls the query engine used by members of the collaboration.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the Clean Rooms collaboration.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.collaborat.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the collaboration.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.creator_di.text: Specifies the display name of the member who creates the collaboration, which is visible to other members in the collaboration.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.creator_me.text: Defines the set of abilities (e.g., CAN_QUERY, CAN_RECEIVE_RESULTS) that are granted to the creator of the collaboration, determining what actions the creator can perform within the Clean Rooms collaboration.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.creator_ml.text: This object specifies the machine learning abilities granted to the creator member of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration, determining which custom and standard ML member operations (such as receiving model output or trained models) the creator is permitted to perform.

Specifies a list of custom machine learning member ability names to be granted to the creator member of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration, defining customized ML permissions beyond the default standard abilities.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.creator_pa.text: Determines how the collaboration creator is compensated for query compute costs, including whether the creator accepts responsibility for those costs and the number of query credits provided to collaborating members.
Specifies how the collaboration creator pays for compute resources used by members when running jobs (as opposed to interactive queries) within the clean rooms collaboration.
Specifies whether the collaboration creator is responsible for paying for job compute costs in the collaboration.
Specifies the configuration for whether the collaboration creator is responsible for costs incurred by machine learning queries, typically by setting a status like ENABLED or DISABLED.
Configures the payment responsibility for machine learning model inference in the collaboration, indicating whether the collaboration creator is responsible for the resulting charges.
Indicates whether the collaboration creator is responsible for the costs incurred by machine learning model inference.
Configuration specifying whether the collaboration creator is responsible for the costs of training machine learning models.
Indicates whether the creator of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration is responsible for the cost of training machine learning models under the creator payment configuration.

Defines the payment configuration for the synthetic data generation capability under machine learning settings, specifying how the collaboration creator is billed for using this feature in an AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.
Indicates whether the collaboration creator is responsible for the costs associated with synthetic data generation.
Specifies the payment configuration for query compute in the collaboration, determining whether the collaboration creator pays for query compute usage.
Indicates whether the creator of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration is responsible for the query compute costs.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.data_encry.text: Specifies the data encryption metadata for the collaboration, controlling whether clear text is allowed, duplicate rows are permitted, joins on columns with different names are allowed, and how null values are preserved.
Indicates whether encrypted tables in the collaboration are allowed to contain cleartext (unencrypted) data.
Specifies whether this collaboration permits query results to contain duplicate rows under the configured encryption metadata.
Controls whether a query in the collaboration can join tables on columns that have different names across different members' datasets.
This required Boolean value determines whether nulls in the underlying data remain as nulls when encrypted in the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration, rather than being encrypted into a non-null value.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.descriptio.text: The user-provided description of the collaboration, which helps identify its purpose and can be updated after creation.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.is_metrics.text: Whether the collaboration collects metrics about query activity (such as query counts and latency), enabling you to monitor and analyze usage patterns.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.text: Defines the AWS accounts that participate in the collaboration, each with an account ID, display name, and the abilities (such as CAN_QUERY or CAN_RECEIVE_RESULTS) granted to that member.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.ac.text: The AWS account ID of the member being added to the Clean Rooms collaboration.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.di.text: The friendly, human-readable name assigned to a member's AWS account, used to identify that member within the Clean Rooms collaboration.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.me.text: Specifies the list of allowable operations (e.g., CAN_QUERY, CAN_RECEIVE_RESULTS) that this collaboration member is permitted to perform.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.ml.text: Specifies the ML-specific abilities for the member, such as whether they can query ML-protected data and receive results from ML queries.

Specifies the list of custom machine learning (ML) member abilities granted to this member in the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration, allowing them to perform additional ML operations beyond the predefined ML member abilities.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.members.pa.text: Configures how the member pays for query compute in the collaboration, specifically indicating whether the member is responsible for query compute costs via the query_compute.is_responsible property.

The `job_compute` object within a member's `payment_configuration` specifies which party pays for the compute used when this member runs analysis jobs, with its `type` field indicating either `MEMBER` (the member pays) or `COLLABORATOR` (the collaboration creator pays).
Indicates whether this member is responsible for paying the compute costs for job compute queries in the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.
Determines how this member pays for machine learning tasks (model training and inference) within the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.

Specifies the payment configuration for machine learning model inference activity, typically including the payment amount (in USD) that a collaboration member pays for each model inference operation run in the collaboration.
Indicates whether this member is the payer (responsible party) for costs incurred from machine learning model inference queries in the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.
Payment configuration for machine learning model training, indicating whether the member is responsible for the costs of model training in the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.
Indicates whether this member is responsible for paying for the costs associated with training the machine learning model in the collaboration.
An object that specifies whether this collaboration member enables synthetic data generation jobs and which party (the collaboration creator or the member) is responsible for paying for those jobs.
Indicates whether this collaboration member is responsible for payment for synthetic data generation under the machine learning payment configuration.
Specifies whether this collaboration member is responsible for paying the compute costs for queries run in the collaboration.
Indicates whether this member is responsible for paying the query compute costs incurred by the collaboration.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.name.text: The name of the collaboration, a user-defined friendly identifier that must be unique within the AWS account and can be up to 128 characters.

aws_clean_rooms_collaboration.query_log_.text: Determines whether query logs are enabled for the collaboration, accepting the enum values ENABLED or DISABLED.

aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.allowed.text: Specifies the list of column names from the underlying AWS Glue table that are allowed to be used in analyses using this configured table, restricting which columns are accessible to collaborators.

aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.analysi.text: Specifies the analysis method for the configured table, which determines how queries can be executed against the data (supported value: DIRECT_QUERY).
Defines the analysis rules for the configured table, specifying the allowed analysis types (such as aggregation or list) and the associated policy constraints that govern how the data can be queried.
Configures the analysis rule policy, which defines the rule type (aggregation, list, or custom) and its specific settings such as aggregate columns, join columns, and allowed operations.
The analysis rule policy version 1 object, which contains the aggregation or list rule settings (such as join columns and aggregate columns) that govern how members can query the configured table.

Specifies the aggregation analysis rule policy, controlling how aggregate queries can be run on the configured table within AWS Clean Rooms, including allowed aggregation functions, join requirements, and output constraints.
Controls whether the output of queries run under this aggregation analysis rule can be used as input to additional analyses, accepting values of 'ALLOWED' or 'REQUIRED'.
Defines the columns that queries are allowed to aggregate under this aggregation analysis rule, along with the permitted aggregation functions (e.g., SUM, AVG, COUNT) for each column.
The list of column names that are allowed to be used as aggregate columns in the aggregation analysis rule of this AWS Clean Rooms configured table.
Specifies the aggregation function (e.g., SUM, AVG, COUNT) applied to the column names in this aggregate column definition of the aggregation analysis rule.
Specifies which join operators (such as AND, OR, or NOT) are permitted in queries against the configured table when using this aggregation analysis rule.
Specifies the columns of the configured table that can be used as grouping dimensions in aggregate queries under this analysis rule.
Lists the column names that can be used as join keys in aggregation queries when this analysis rule's policy is applied to the configured table.
Specifies whether queries using this aggregation rule must include a join condition on the configured table's join columns.

A list of output constraints, each specifying a column name and the minimum number of distinct values that must appear in that column for an aggregation query to produce output, preventing re-identification.

Specifies the name of a column that must appear in the aggregated query output, where each distinct value in that column must occur at least the specified minimum number of rows to satisfy the analysis rule's privacy constraint.
Specifies the minimum allowable value for the aggregated output column, enforcing a privacy floor (e.g., to prevent revealing small counts) in the aggregation query results.
Defines the allowed aggregate function (such as COUNT, SUM, or AVG) for the associated output column in the aggregation analysis rule, restricting how that column can be aggregated in queries.
The list of scalar SQL functions (e.g., UPPER, ROUND) that are permitted to be used in aggregation queries under this analysis rule's aggregation policy.
Defines the custom analysis rule policy, which lists the SQL queries (allowed analyses) and related settings that collaboration members can use when querying the configured table.
Specifies whether the results of a query executed on this configured table can be used in subsequent additional analyses, with allowed values ALLOWED, REQUIRED, or NOT_ALLOWED.
A list of allowed analysis template identifiers (such as ARNs) that are permitted to run against the configured table under this custom analysis rule.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the analysis providers that are permitted to run analyses on the configured table under this custom analysis rule.

Specifies the differential privacy configuration for the custom analysis rule, including the list of protected columns and the epsilon value that controls the privacy-accuracy trade-off for query results.

Specifies the list of columns in the configured table to which differential privacy protection is applied, causing query outputs over these columns to be perturbed and tracked against a privacy budget for Clean Rooms analyses.
The name of a column that is included in the differential privacy policy of the custom analysis rule, specifying which configured table column is protected by the differential privacy aggregation.
Specifies the list of column names that must be excluded from the output of queries run under this custom analysis rule policy, preventing collaborators from viewing those columns.
Defines the list-based analysis rule policy for the configured table, specifying the columns that can be used in list queries and any associated constraints or parameters.
Specifies whether additional analyses may be run on the output of list queries governed by this list analysis rule, typically with enum values like ALLOWED or NOT_ALLOWED.
Specifies the allowed join operators (e.g., EQ, NEQ, LT, LE, GT, GE) that can be used when this configured table is joined with other tables in list-type analyses under the policy analysis rule.
The join_columns attribute specifies the list of column names in the configured table that can be used in JOIN operations when running queries under the 'list' analysis rule policy.
Specifies the list of columns in the configured table that are allowed to appear in the results of a list query under this analysis rule.
Specifies the type of analysis rule (e.g., AGGREGATION, LIST) that governs how query results are computed and displayed for the configured table.

aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the configured table.

aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.configu.text: The unique identifier (such as an ARN) that AWS assigns to the configured table upon creation.

aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.descrip.text: A free-form text description of the configured table that helps identify its purpose or contents.

aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.name.text: The name of the configured table, which is a required, user-defined identifier for the table within AWS Clean Rooms.

aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.selecte.text: Specifies the list of allowed analysis methods (such as DIRECT_QUERY or ADDITIONAL_ANALYSES) that can be used against the configured table, defining the permitted query types in its analysis rule policy.

aws_clean_rooms_configured_table.table_r.text: Defines the source AWS Glue table (via its database name and table name) that this configured table references.
Defines the Amazon Athena table that the configured table references, specifying the database name, table name, and optionally the workgroup where the table resides.
The name of the Athena data catalog that contains the table referenced by this configured table.
The name of the Athena database that contains the table referenced by this configured table for querying in AWS Clean Rooms.
The name of the Athena table that this configured table references for analysis in AWS Clean Rooms.
The name of the Athena workgroup in which the referenced table resides for this AWS Clean Rooms configured table.
The 'glue' object in 'table_reference' specifies the AWS Glue table that the configured table references, including the database name and table name.
The name of the AWS Glue database in the Data Catalog that contains the table referenced by this configured table.
The AWS Region where the referenced AWS Glue table is located.
The name of the AWS Glue table used as the data source for this configured table in AWS Clean Rooms.
Specifies the Snowflake table reference properties, including the account identifier, database name, schema name, and table name, to identify the source table for the configured table.
The Snowflake account identifier that uniquely identifies the Snowflake account hosting the source table referenced by this configured table.
The name of the Snowflake database that contains the table referenced by this configured table.
The name of the Snowflake schema that contains the table referenced by this configured table.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the Snowflake credentials used to connect to the Snowflake data source for this configured table reference.
The name of the Snowflake table that this configured table references.
Specifies version 1 of the column schema for the referenced Snowflake table, where each object in the list defines a column's name, data type, and nullability.
The name of a column within the Snowflake table schema that AWS Clean Rooms uses to define the configured table's column list.
Specifies the data type of a column in the Snowflake table schema that defines the table reference for the AWS Clean Rooms configured table.

aws_clean_rooms_configured_table_associa.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the configured table association, assigned by AWS when the association is created.

Configures the analysis rules for the configured table association, specifying the permitted analysis types (e.g., list, aggregate, custom) and their policy constraints for querying the associated configured table within a collaboration.

This object specifies the policy for an analysis rule attached to a configured table association, defining the type of analysis (e.g., aggregation, list, or custom) along with the detailed constraints and parameters (such as aggregation columns, join conditions, and output limits) that govern queries run by collaboration members on the associated table.

Specifies the versioned analysis rule policy for a configured table association, containing the v1 policy that defines allowed aggregation columns, join columns, or custom SQL templates used to constrain queries in the collaboration.

Specifies the aggregation analysis rule policy parameters for the configured table association, including the allowed aggregate columns, dimension columns, join requirements, and permitted aggregation operators.
Specifies which additional analyses (such as CORRELATION or REGRESSION) are permitted on the output of aggregation queries governed by this configured table association's aggregation analysis rule.
The list of collaboration member account IDs (or member ARNs) allowed to receive query results from aggregation queries run against this configured table association.

The custom analysis rule policy (version v1) for this AWS Clean Rooms configured table association, defining the allowed SQL operations such as joins, aggregations, and output columns that members can use when querying the associated table.

This field specifies the additional types of analyses (e.g., SQL, Python) that are permitted to be run on the configured table when using a custom analysis rule policy, extending the set defined in `allowedAnalyses`.
Specifies the list of member account IDs that are allowed to receive query results when this custom analysis rule is used.
Configures the list analysis rule for the configured table association, defining the allowed columns that members can select in list queries.
Specifies the list of additional analysis types (such as AGGREGATE or CUSTOM) that are permitted for queries on the configured table association when the base analysis rule is of type LIST.
Specifies the list of allowed result receivers (e.g., AWS account IDs or IAM roles) that may receive query results when a LIST analysis rule is applied to the associated configured table.
Specifies the type of analysis rule for the configured table association (e.g., AGGREGATION or LIST), which defines the privacy-enforcing query operations allowed on the associated table.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the configured table association within the membership.
The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms configured table that this association links to a membership for collaborative analysis.
An optional free-form description of the configured table association, used to provide additional context or identity for the association within the AWS Clean Rooms membership.
The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms membership for which this configured table association is created, linking the configured table to that membership.
A unique, user-provided name for the configured table association, used to identify and manage the association within the AWS Clean Rooms membership.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Clean Rooms assumes to access the underlying data referenced by the configured table when the associated table is used in analyses.
Specifies the value of a tag key attached to the AWS Clean Rooms configured table association, used to classify and manage the resource.

aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Clean Rooms ID mapping table in AWS.

aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.collabo.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that contains this ID mapping table, automatically assigned by AWS.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the collaboration that contains this ID mapping table.

aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.descrip.text: An optional user-defined description that provides context or identification for the ID mapping table in AWS Clean Rooms.

aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.id_mapp.text: The system-generated unique identifier (such as the Amazon Resource Name) of the AWS Clean Rooms ID mapping table, used to reference the table within the service.

aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.input_r.text: Configures the input reference for the ID mapping table, specifying the ARN of the source data or entity resolution resource and whether AWS Clean Rooms manages the resource policies.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the input reference data source (such as an Amazon S3 bucket) that contains the records used to create the ID mapping table in AWS Clean Rooms.

A Boolean flag that indicates whether AWS Clean Rooms automatically manages the resource policies for the input reference (the underlying AWS resource) so that the ID mapping table can access it; if set to true, Clean Rooms handles required policy changes, and if false, you are responsible for managing them.
The computed inputReferenceProperties object contains the resolved list of input reference column/table pairs that define how the ID mapping table maps identifiers across its referenced tables.
Specifies the S3 data source(s) that AWS Clean Rooms reads to build the ID mapping table, with each item providing an input source ARN.
The unique identifier of the ID namespace association that serves as the input source for this ID mapping table, linking the ID namespace to the collaboration.
Specifies whether the associated input source ARN represents the source or target for the ID mapping table, with allowed values SOURCE or TARGET.

aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.kms_key.text: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the ID mapping table data.

aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.members.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Clean Rooms membership that owns this ID mapping table.
The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms membership that owns this ID mapping table.

aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.name.text: The user-defined name of the ID mapping table, used to identify and reference it within the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.

aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.tags.text: The list of tags to apply to the ID mapping table, where each tag consists of a required key and an optional value.

aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.tags.ke.text: The key (name) of a user-defined tag (key-value pair) attached to the AWS Clean Rooms ID mapping table, used for metadata organization and resource identification.

aws_clean_rooms_id_mapping_table.tags.va.text: The value of a user-defined tag associated with the AWS Clean Rooms ID Mapping Table, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_clean_rooms_id_namespace_association.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this ID namespace association within AWS Clean Rooms.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the collaboration that this ID namespace association belongs to.
The unique identifier of the collaboration to which this ID namespace association belongs.
An optional free-text field for storing a human-readable note about the AWS Clean Rooms ID namespace association, helping to indicate its business purpose or configuration context.
Configures the ID mapping behavior for this ID namespace association, specifying whether the namespace acts as a source or target in AWS Clean Rooms ID mapping.
When set to true, allows the ID namespace to be used as a dimension column in AWS Clean Rooms queries and analyses.
The unique system-generated identifier for this Clean Rooms ID namespace association.

Defines the input reference for the ID namespace association, specifying the ARN of the underlying data source (such as an AWS Glue table) and whether AWS Clean Rooms manages resource policies on that source.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the entity reference data that the ID namespace association uses to resolve identities, as specified in the input reference configuration.

A Boolean flag that, when true, indicates AWS Clean Rooms automatically manages the resource policies for the referenced input resource (such as an S3 bucket) to allow access for the ID namespace association, and when false, requires the user to manage those policies manually.

The read-only InputReferenceProperties object that AWS returns for a Clean Rooms ID namespace association, specifying the ID namespace type (e.g., SOURCE or TARGET) and the member columns used as the input reference for ID matching.

A list of ID mapping workflow types (e.g., UseProvidedSource or UseProvidedTarget) that this Clean Rooms ID namespace association supports, determining which matching workflows can be run with the associated namespace.
Specifies whether the associated ID namespace functions as a SOURCE or TARGET in the Clean Rooms collaboration's matching workflow.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the membership that contains this ID namespace association.
The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms membership that this ID namespace association belongs to.
A required, user-specified name for the ID namespace association, used to identify and manage the association within an AWS Clean Rooms collaboration.
Specifies the list of tag key-value pairs to assign to the ID namespace association, enabling cost allocation and resource metadata organization.
The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Clean Rooms ID namespace association, used to organize, filter, and manage this resource.
The value of a tag attached to the AWS Clean Rooms ID namespace association, used to store arbitrary metadata for resource categorization and management.

aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.analy.text: Defines the analysis constraints that govern how members can query the intermediate table, including the allowed analysis methods and their configurations.

Defines the custom analysis rule variant within the V1 analysis rule policy, specifying which SQL analyses (e.g., SELECT) are allowed and any restrictions on analysis providers or output columns for the table.
This field specifies the ARNs of additional analyses that are allowed to be run on the intermediate table under the custom analysis rule policy.
Specifies the list of allowed analysis template names (strings) that collaborators may run on the configured table under this custom analysis rule, restricting which analyses are permitted.

This list of strings defines the AWS account IDs that are authorized to act as analysis providers for the custom analysis rule, restricting which accounts can run SQL queries against the intermediate table.
Specifies the list of member account identifiers that are allowed to receive the results of queries run under this custom analysis rule policy.
Defines the differential privacy settings for the custom analysis rule, specifying the privacy budget and noise injection mechanism applied to prevent re-identification of individual records.
Specifies the columns in the AWS Clean Rooms intermediate table that are protected by the differential privacy policy within this custom analysis rule.
The name of the column in the configured table to which the differential privacy policy is applied.

Specifies the list of column names from the intermediate table that are prohibited from being included in the output of any query executed under this custom analysis rule, preventing sensitive data from being exposed.

aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.colla.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration in which the intermediate table is defined.
The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that this intermediate table belongs to.

aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.inter.text: The system-generated unique identifier assigned by AWS Clean Rooms to this intermediate table, used to reference and manage the table resource.

aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.kms_k.text: Specifies the AWS KMS key ARN used to encrypt the intermediate table, enabling customer-managed server-side encryption for the table's data.

aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.membe.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Clean Rooms membership that owns or contains the intermediate table, provided as a read-only identifier.
The unique identifier of the membership within the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that this intermediate table belongs to.

aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.popul.text: The sql_parameters object provides named values for the placeholders defined in the SQL query of the population analysis configuration, enabling the analysis to be customized with different parameter values at execution time.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the analysis template that the SQL parameters in this block are associated with, used to identify which template's parameters are being configured for the population analysis.
The SQL query text that defines the population analysis logic for generating the intermediate table in AWS Clean Rooms.

aws_clean_rooms_intermediate_table.tags..text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Clean Rooms intermediate table, serving as the identifier for the tag's metadata label.

aws_clean_rooms_membership.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Clean Rooms membership.

aws_clean_rooms_membership.collaboration.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that this membership is associated with.
The `collaboration_creator_account_id` attribute returns the AWS account ID of the account that created the collaboration to which this Clean Rooms membership belongs.
The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that this membership is associated with.

aws_clean_rooms_membership.default_job_r.text: Specifies the default configuration for storing query results, including the S3 output location and the IAM role used to write results for jobs run by this membership.
Specifies the S3 bucket (and optional key prefix) that serves as the default destination for query results when running jobs in this membership.
The S3 output configuration for the default job result configuration, specifying the Amazon S3 bucket (and optional key prefix) where analysis job results are delivered.
The name of the S3 bucket where the default job results are delivered, as part of the membership's default job result output configuration.
The S3 key prefix under which the default analysis job result objects are stored in the specified output S3 bucket.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Clean Rooms assumes to write query results to the S3 location configured in the default job result configuration.

aws_clean_rooms_membership.default_resul.text: Specifies the default output configuration (such as the S3 bucket and IAM role) used to write query results for the membership.
Specifies the Amazon S3 destination (bucket and optional key prefix) used to store the default query results for this Clean Rooms membership.
Specifies the S3 bucket and optional key prefix where query results for this Clean Rooms membership are stored.
The name of the S3 bucket to which the default result configuration delivers query results for this AWS Clean Rooms membership.
The S3 object key prefix that is applied to the output files when the Clean Rooms membership's default result configuration writes query results to the specified S3 bucket.
Specifies the file format (CSV or PARQUET) for query results written to the S3 bucket and key prefix in the membership's default result configuration.
Determines whether the default result configuration writes query output to a single S3 file (true) or multiple files (false).
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Clean Rooms assumes to write query results to the default output location configured for the membership.

aws_clean_rooms_membership.is_metrics_en.text: Whether query metrics are enabled for the Clean Rooms membership, which if true enables Amazon CloudWatch metrics for queries run within the membership.

aws_clean_rooms_membership.membership_id.text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for this AWS Clean Rooms membership.

aws_clean_rooms_membership.payment_confi.text: Configures the payment details for the membership, including the mode that determines which member is billed for query compute in the clean room.
Specifies the payment configuration for job compute in the membership, indicating which party (the 'MemberWhoPays' value) is responsible for paying for compute jobs run under the collaboration.
Indicates whether this Clean Rooms membership is responsible for paying the compute costs for analysis jobs run in the collaboration.

Configures which party (the member or the collaborator) is responsible for paying for machine learning operations within the AWS Clean Rooms membership, as part of the overarching payment configuration.
Specifies the payment configuration for machine learning model inference jobs in the Clean Rooms membership, including which member is responsible for associated costs.
Indicates whether the member associated with this Clean Rooms membership is responsible for the costs of machine learning model inference under this payment configuration.
Defines the payment responsibility for machine learning model training in the membership's payment configuration, indicating whether the membership is responsible for the associated costs.
Indicates whether the membership owner is responsible for covering the costs incurred by machine learning model training in the collaboration.
Configures synthetic data generation for Clean Rooms ML by providing an IsEnabled flag that determines whether the feature is active and thus billing for it is incurred.
Indicates whether the membership is responsible for the costs of synthetic data generation queries in the machine learning payment configuration.
This configuration block indicates whether this Clean Rooms membership is responsible for the compute costs associated with running queries in the collaboration.
Indicates whether this membership is responsible for paying the query compute costs incurred by queries in the collaboration.

aws_clean_rooms_membership.query_log_sta.text: Specifies whether query logging is enabled for the Clean Rooms membership, with valid values ENABLED or DISABLED to control retention of query activity records.

aws_clean_rooms_membership.tags.key.text: The key portion of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Clean Rooms membership, used to categorize and identify the resource.

aws_clean_rooms_membership.tags.value.text: A user-defined tag value attached to the AWS Clean Rooms membership, providing metadata that can be used for categorization, cost allocation, or access control.

aws_clean_rooms_ml_configured_model_algo.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the configured model algorithm.
An optional, human-readable description that identifies the configured model algorithm and explains its purpose within the AWS Clean Rooms ML resource.
Specifies the container configuration, including the Amazon ECR image URI and optional environment variables, for running inference with this configured model algorithm.
The URI of the container image (stored in Amazon ECR) that hosts the model inference code for this configured model algorithm.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the configured model algorithm data.

The required name for the configured model algorithm, which uniquely identifies it within an AWS account and Region and is used as the resource identifier when referencing it in Clean Rooms ML operations.

The ARN of the IAM role that grants the configured model algorithm the necessary permissions to access customer data and other AWS resources during analysis within an AWS Clean Rooms ML collaboration.
The key of a tag assigned to this AWS Clean Rooms ML configured model algorithm, used to organize, identify, and manage the resource through metadata.
Configures the Docker container (e.g., image URI and runtime parameters) that runs the training algorithm for this configured model algorithm in AWS Clean Rooms ML.

The `arguments` field of the training container configuration for an AWS Clean Rooms ML configured model algorithm is a list of strings that specify command-line arguments to be passed to the training container when it runs.
Specifies the entrypoint command (as a list of strings) that the training container executes when started, overriding any image default entrypoint.
Specifies the Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) image URI of the container that runs the model training job for this configured model algorithm.
Defines the metrics (e.g., loss, accuracy) to capture from the training container's logs by specifying a name and a regular expression pattern to extract each metric value.
Specifies the name of a metric to extract from the training container's output logs, enabling CloudWatch monitoring of that metric during model training.
The regular expression pattern used to extract the metric value from the training container logs for this metric definition.
The identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration that contains this configured model algorithm association, used to scope the association to a specific collaboration environment.
The ARN of the configured model algorithm that this association links to the configured model.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the configured model algorithm association.
The description field is an optional, user-defined text string that describes the configured model algorithm association, allowing you to identify its purpose or context within AWS Clean Rooms ML.
The unique identifier (UUID) of the AWS Clean Rooms membership that this configured model algorithm association is created within and scoped to.
The name of the configured model algorithm association, which provides a required identifier for the association within AWS Clean Rooms ML.

Defines the privacy policies for the configured model algorithm association, including the direct analysis privacy budget template and output configuration constraints that govern how query results are protected in the collaboration.
Defines the policy for exporting trained models from the configured model algorithm association, specifying the allowed S3 destinations and any restrictions on where model artifacts may be written.
The list of file names that are allowed to be exported from the trained model when this trained model exports policy is applied in the privacy configuration.
Limits the maximum size of a trained model export allowed by the privacy policy, preventing the export of models larger than the specified threshold.
The maximum size, in bytes, allowed for a trained model export as part of the privacy configuration's trained model exports policy.
Specifies the privacy policy for trained model inference jobs on this configured model algorithm association, governing how inference job outputs are handled and where they may be sent.
Lists the AWS account IDs permitted to access the container logs produced during trained model inference jobs, as configured in the association's privacy policy.

The filter pattern defines a pattern (e.g., a CloudWatch Logs-style filter) used to select which container log lines are captured or recorded for trained model inference jobs under this privacy policy.

Defines the redaction settings applied to container logs from trained model inference jobs, ensuring sensitive data is removed before logs are stored or processed, as part of the privacy configuration for the configured model algorithm association.
Configures custom entities for log redaction in trained model inference jobs, defining the names and regular expression patterns used to redact sensitive data from container logs.

Specifies the list of custom data identifier patterns (regular expressions) used by the log redaction configuration to detect and redact sensitive custom entities in container logs from trained model inference jobs for this configured model algorithm association.
Specifies the list of sensitive data entity types that should be redacted from the container logs of trained model inference jobs in this configured model algorithm association.
Defines the maximum output size cap for trained model inference jobs, enforcing privacy constraints by limiting the volume of data that can be returned.
The unit of measurement for the maximum output size of a trained model inference job, with the only valid value being GB (gigabytes).
The numeric value of the maximum output size allowed for a trained model inference job, enforced by the privacy configuration's policy for the Clean Rooms ML configured model algorithm association.

Defines the trained models policy within the privacy configuration, specifying how trained models generated from the associated configured model algorithm can be accessed and used by collaboration members.

Defines the list of container log configurations (each specifying a CloudWatch Logs log group ARN and a log type) that are permitted for the trained model container as part of this algorithm association's privacy policy.
Defines the list of AWS account IDs permitted to access container logs for trained models, as part of the privacy configuration's trained models policy.

Specifies a pattern (likely a CloudWatch Logs filter pattern) applied to container logs of trained models to exclude sensitive information as part of the privacy configuration in the AWS Clean Rooms ML algorithm association.
Configures how sensitive data in the container logs of trained models is redacted, including the patterns to match and the redaction method to apply.
Specifies the list of custom data identifiers used by the custom entity configuration to redact matching sensitive data from the trained model's container logs.

Specifies the list of sensitive data entity types (e.g., personal identifiers) that are redacted from the container logs of the trained model, under the log redaction configuration of the privacy policy.

The noise level (HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW) that sets the amount of differential privacy noise added to container metrics for trained models, balancing privacy protection against metric utility in the Clean Rooms ML association.
Sets the maximum size limit for trained model artifacts in the privacy configuration, expressed as an object with a numeric size and a unit, to prevent overly large models from being exported.
The unit of measurement for the maximum size of a trained model artifact, such as MB or GB.
Specifies the numeric component of the maximum trained model artifact size, which the privacy configuration uses to limit the size of model outputs that can be shared.

aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.desc.text: A user-provided free-form description of the training dataset in AWS Clean Rooms ML, used to annotate and identify the dataset's purpose or contents.

aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.name.text: The name of the training dataset, which must be unique within the AWS account and Region.

aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.role.text: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Clean Rooms ML assumes to read your training data from the configured data source, granting the necessary permissions for dataset access.

aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.stat.text: The current status of the training dataset (e.g., ACTIVE or INACTIVE), indicating whether it is available for use.

aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.tags.text: The value of a tag key attached to the AWS Clean Rooms ML Training Dataset, used to organize, identify, and manage the dataset through metadata labels.

aws_clean_rooms_ml_training_dataset.trai.text: The list of training data configurations, each specifying a data source (such as a Glue table) and its column schema, that the Clean Rooms ML training dataset uses to define the input for model training.
Specifies the input configuration for the training dataset, including the S3 data source location and the list of column names that make up the schema.
Specifies the S3 location (URI) and type of the data source that provides the training input data for the Clean Rooms ML training dataset.
This object defines the AWS Glue table that supplies the training data for this Clean Rooms ML training dataset.
The AWS account ID of the Glue Data Catalog that contains the table used as the training data source for the Clean Rooms ML training dataset.
The name of the AWS Glue Data Catalog database containing the source table for the training dataset input.
The name of the AWS Glue table that contains the training data for the Clean Rooms ML training dataset.
Defines the schema of the training data input by listing column objects, each specifying a column name and its data type for the Clean Rooms ML training dataset.
Specifies the name of a column in the training data schema, which maps to a column in the configured data source for the Clean Rooms ML training dataset.
Specifies the data type (e.g., INTEGER, STRING) for each column in the training dataset schema, used by AWS Clean Rooms ML to interpret the input data.
Defines whether the training data for this Clean Rooms ML training dataset is sourced from an Amazon S3 bucket or an AWS Glue table.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Clean Rooms ML training dataset.

aws_clean_rooms_privacy_budget_template..text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the privacy budget template.
Indicates whether the privacy budget template automatically refreshes at the end of each allocation period, with valid values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the collaboration that this privacy budget template is associated with, assigned by AWS when the template is created.

collaboration_identifier is the unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms collaboration to which this privacy budget template belongs, automatically assigned by AWS and used as a read-only part of the resource's identity.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the membership that this privacy budget template belongs to, which is automatically assigned by AWS Clean Rooms.
The unique identifier of the AWS Clean Rooms membership that this privacy budget template is associated with.
Defines the differential privacy parameters for the privacy budget template, specifically the epsilon value and the maximum number of aggregation queries allowed.
Indicates whether the privacy budget template automatically refreshes the privacy budget on a recurring schedule (e.g., daily or monthly) to renew the querying allowance without manual intervention.
The maximum number of privacy budget units allocated to a parameter, determining how much aggregate data can be exposed while preserving differential privacy.
Defines the kind of privacy budget parameter (currently supported value: DIFFERENTIAL_PRIVACY) that determines how the analysis rule enforces differential privacy limits in the template.
Specifies the epsilon value for the differential privacy budget, which limits the amount of privacy loss allowed for queries using this template.
The number of users' worth of noise added to each query in the privacy budget template, controlling the level of differential privacy applied to query results.
The AWS-assigned unique identifier for this privacy budget template, used to reference the template in Clean Rooms operations.

The privacy budget type, either 'DIRECT' or 'DIFFERENTIAL_PRIVACY', determines whether the template enforces a direct query budget or a differential-privacy-based budget with noise for members' queries in the collaboration.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Cloud9 EC2 development environment.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.automatic_sto.text: The number of minutes of inactivity after which AWS Cloud9 automatically stops the environment's EC2 instance, shutting down the environment when this time is reached.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.connection_ty.text: Specifies whether AWS Cloud9 connects to the environment's Amazon EC2 instance via SSH (CONNECT_SSH, the default) or AWS Systems Manager (CONNECT_SSM).

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.description.text: An optional description that provides additional non-identifying context about the Cloud9 environment.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS Cloud9 to the environment, such as 'env-1234567890abcdef0'.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.image_id.text: The image_id specifies the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) ID used to launch the Amazon EC2 instance that hosts the Cloud9 environment.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.instance_type.text: Specifies the EC2 instance type (e.g., t2.micro, m5.large) that the AWS Cloud9 environment runs on, determining the compute and memory resources available.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.name.text: Specifies the name of the Cloud9 development environment.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.owner_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the environment owner; if not specified, the environment is owned by the user who created it.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.repositories.text: A list of repositories to clone into the environment, each containing the repository URL and the path component where it should be cloned.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.repositories..text: The relative path component within the AWS Cloud9 environment where the source repository will be cloned, serving as the directory name for the repository.
The URL of the source code repository to clone into the Cloud9 environment when the environment is created.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.subnet_id.text: The ID of the subnet in which the Cloud9 environment's EC2 instance is launched, allowing the environment to reside in a specific VPC and network configuration.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.tags.text: Specifies a list of tag key-value pairs to associate with the Cloud9 EC2 environment.

aws_cloud9_environment_ec2.tags.value.text: Specifies the value for a tag key on the AWS Cloud9 EC2 environment, allowing you to add arbitrary metadata for identifying or organizing the environment.

aws_cloud_formation_custom_resource.serv.text: The maximum amount of time (in seconds) that AWS CloudFormation waits for the custom resource provider to respond before considering the resource operation failed.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Lambda function or Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) topic that implements the custom resource's provisioning logic.

aws_cloud_formation_guard_hook.options.text: Specifies the Guard hook options, including the RuleStack property that gives the Amazon S3 location of the Guard rules file CloudFormation uses to apply policy validation.

aws_cloud_formation_guard_hook.target_fi.text: Specifies the list of stack operations (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE) for which the Guard hook is invoked on the targeted resources.
The invocation points of the target filter, which are the stack lifecycle events (such as BEFORE_CREATION or BEFORE_UPDATE) at which the Guard hook runs for the matched resources.
Specifies the list of AWS resource type names (for example, 'AWS::S3::Bucket') that this Guard hook evaluates for violations during CloudFormation operations.
Defines the resource targets that the Guard hook applies to, using include and exclude patterns based on resource type and resource identifiers.
Specifies whether the Guard hook should be invoked (INVOKE) or skipped (SKIP) for resources matching the target in this target filter.
The invocation point for a target in the Guard hook's target filter, indicating which CloudFormation resource lifecycle event (CREATE, UPDATE, or DELETE) triggers the hook for that target.
The name of a target resource type (for example, AWS::S3::Bucket) that this Guard hook filter matches so the hook is invoked only for resources of that type.

aws_cloud_formation_hook_version.logging.text: Configures the logging destination for the hook version, specifying the CloudWatch Logs log group and IAM role where the hook's execution logs are sent.

aws_cloud_formation_lambda_hook.target_f.text: Specifies the list of CloudFormation change actions (e.g., Create, Update, Delete) that trigger the Lambda hook invocation.
Specifies the list of CloudFormation hook invocation points (such as BEFORE_CREATE, BEFORE_UPDATE, BEFORE_DELETE) at which the Lambda hook is triggered for the matching target resources.
Specifies the list of AWS resource type names (e.g., AWS::S3::Bucket) that this Lambda hook targets, controlling which resource types trigger the hook.

The list of target objects that define which CloudFormation resources this Lambda hook is triggered for, where each target specifies a resource type (e.g., AWS::S3::Bucket) and optionally a specific resource name to narrow the hook's scope.
Specifies the CloudFormation action (e.g., CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE) that triggers the Lambda hook for the targeted resource types.

Specifies the invocation timing relative to the targeted CloudFormation operation (e.g., `BEFORE` or `AFTER`), determining whether the Lambda hook runs before or after the action on the matched resources.

The name of the resource type (e.g., AWS::S3::Bucket) or logical resource ID that the CloudFormation Lambda hook's target filter matches, depending on whether the target type is RESOURCE_TYPE or RESOURCE_NAME.

aws_cloud_formation_macro.description.text: The description field provides a human-readable summary of the macro's purpose or transformation logic, aiding users in understanding what the macro does.

aws_cloud_formation_macro.function_name.text: Specifies the name of the AWS Lambda function that AWS CloudFormation invokes to process template snippets when the macro is executed.

aws_cloud_formation_macro.id.text: The macro's name, which serves as its unique identifier within CloudFormation.

aws_cloud_formation_macro.log_group_name.text: The Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group where the macro function's execution logs are delivered.

aws_cloud_formation_macro.log_role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that CloudFormation assumes to send logs about the macro execution to the CloudWatch log group.

aws_cloud_formation_macro.name.text: Defines the name of the macro, used to reference it in CloudFormation templates and required to be unique within the account and region.

aws_cloud_formation_resource_version.log.text: Specifies the logging configuration for the resource type, including the CloudWatch Logs log group name and the IAM role ARN used to deliver logs from the resource provider.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.capabilities.text: A list of capability values (e.g., CAPABILITY_IAM, CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM, CAPABILITY_AUTO_EXPAND) that the stack operation requires to acknowledge creation or modification of IAM resources or to expand macros.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.change_set_id.text: The unique ID of the change set that was last executed to create or update the stack, useful for tracking which changes were applied.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.creation_time.text: The timestamp indicating when the CloudFormation stack was created, typically in ISO 8601 format.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.description.text: Provides a freely formed text description for the AWS CloudFormation stack, which is passed to the AWS CloudFormation service and helps identify the stack's purpose.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.disable_rollba.text: Disables rollback of the stack if stack creation fails, allowing the stack to remain in a failed state for troubleshooting.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.enable_termina.text: When set to true, enables termination protection on the CloudFormation stack, preventing the stack from being deleted until this setting is disabled.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.last_update_ti.text: The timestamp of when the CloudFormation stack was last updated, provided as a string.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.notification_a.text: The Amazon SNS topic ARNs to which CloudFormation sends stack event notifications, such as resource creation or deletion events.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.outputs.text: A list of the CloudFormation stack's output entries, each containing a key and value from the Outputs section of the stack template, as returned by AWS.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.outputs.descri.text: The description of a CloudFormation stack output, as defined in the stack template, providing human-readable context for the output value.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.outputs.export.text: The export name for a stack output, which makes the output value available to other CloudFormation stacks via Fn::ImportValue.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.outputs.output.text: Specifies the name of an output exported by the AWS CloudFormation stack, used to identify the corresponding output value within the stack's list of outputs.
The actual value of a CloudFormation stack output, returned after the stack has been created or updated.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.parameters.text: A map of input parameters to pass to the CloudFormation stack, matching the Parameters declared in the stack's template.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.parent_id.text: The unique identifier of the parent CloudFormation stack that this stack is nested within, or an empty string if this is a root-level stack.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.role_arn.text: ARN of the IAM role that AWS CloudFormation assumes to create, update, or delete the stack's resources.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.root_id.text: The root stack ID of a CloudFormation stack, which is the unique identifier of the top-level stack that this stack belongs to (equal to the stack's own ID for a top-level stack).

aws_cloud_formation_stack.stack_id.text: The unique Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to the CloudFormation stack by AWS when it is created.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.stack_name.text: The name of the CloudFormation stack, which must be unique within an AWS region and is used to identify the stack in operations.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.stack_policy_b.text: Specifies the JSON body of a stack policy, which defines permissions that protect stack resources from accidental updates or deletions during stack operations.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.stack_policy_u.text: The URL to the stack policy file, which restricts updates to specific resources within the CloudFormation stack during a stack update.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.stack_status.text: The current status of the CloudFormation stack as reported by AWS, such as CREATE_COMPLETE, UPDATE_COMPLETE, or DELETE_COMPLETE, and is read-only since it is determined by the service.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.stack_status_r.text: The reason provided by AWS CloudFormation for the stack's current status, such as why a create, update, or delete operation failed.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.tags.text: Specifies the list of key-value tags to associate with the CloudFormation stack, which are used to identify, organize, and manage the stack, and which are propagated to tag-supporting resources created by the stack.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.tags.key.text: The tag key to associate with the CloudFormation stack, used to organize and identify the stack for cost allocation and management.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the CloudFormation stack, used for cost allocation, access control, and organizing stack resources.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.template_body.text: The CloudFormation template body, in JSON or YAML format, that defines the stack's resources and properties; you can use this instead of providing a template URL.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.template_url.text: The URL of a file (typically in Amazon S3) that contains the CloudFormation template body, used instead of inline template_body.

aws_cloud_formation_stack.timeout_in_min.text: The maximum number of minutes that CloudFormation allows for the stack creation to complete before the stack creation fails.

aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.auto_deplo.text: Enables automatic deployment of stack instances to accounts added to the target organizational units or accounts, and optionally retains the stacks when an account is removed from the target scope.

aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.operation_.text: Specifies the maximum number of accounts per Region in which stack instance creation, update, or deletion can fail before CloudFormation stops the stack set operation in that Region.
The percentage of total stack instances in the stack set that can fail during an operation before CloudFormation stops the operation and considers it failed.
Specifies the maximum number of stack instances that can be operated on concurrently during a stack set operation, as an absolute count rather than a percentage.
Specifies the maximum percentage of accounts in the stack set that can be brought online or updated concurrently during stack operations, helping to limit the number of simultaneous deployments.
Specifies the custom order in which AWS Regions are traversed during stack set operations (create, update, or delete), controlling the sequence of stack instance deployments across those regions.

aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.parameters.text: The key of a parameter passed to the CloudFormation StackSet, which must match a parameter name declared in the stack template used by the StackSet.
The value to assign to a specific parameter key when provisioning stacks within the CloudFormation StackSet.

aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.stack_inst.text: DeploymentTargets specifies the target AWS accounts or Organizational Units (OUs) in AWS Organizations for stack instance deployment, including optional account list URL and account filter type.

Specifies how AWS CloudFormation filters accounts within an organization for stack set deployments: 'ALL' targets every account in the organization, while 'INTERSECTION' deploys only to accounts that appear in both the specified target accounts/OrganizationalUnitIds and the organization.
Specifies the list of AWS account IDs to which stack instances are deployed for this stack instances group in the StackSet.
The `accounts_url` field specifies a pre-signed Amazon S3 URL to a file containing a list of AWS account IDs that are the deployment targets for stack instances in the stack set group.
The list of organizational unit (OU) IDs in AWS Organizations to which the stack set deploys stack instances when using service-managed permissions.
Provides the parameter values that override the stack set's default parameters for the stack instances in this group, enabling different configurations per account/region group.
The key of a parameter override applied to the stack instances in this group, replacing the default parameter value from the stack set's template.
The value to assign to a stack template parameter for the stack instances in this group, overriding the default parameter value defined in the StackSet template.
The list of AWS Regions in which to create stack instances for this stack set instance group.

aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the CloudFormation stack set, used to organize, identify, and manage the stack set via cost allocation tags and IAM policies.

aws_cloud_formation_stack_set.tags.value.text: The value of the tag to assign to the StackSet, used for cost allocation, access control, and identifying the StackSet in the AWS Management Console.

aws_cloud_formation_type_activation.logg.text: Specifies the Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group name and IAM role ARN used to deliver logs for the registered resource type.

aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition.count.text: The number of success signals that must be received by the CloudFormation wait condition before it is considered complete, matching the Count property of the associated CloudFormation WaitCondition.

aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition.data.text: The map of data returned by the signaled resource or application once the wait condition is fulfilled, providing the payload sent via the signal URL.

aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition.handl.text: The handle property is the pre-signed URL (from the associated WaitConditionHandle) that a signal is sent to, marking the wait as complete and allowing CloudFormation to finish creating this WaitCondition resource.

aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition.timeo.text: The number of seconds to wait for the required number of signals to arrive before the wait condition times out.

aws_cloud_formation_wait_condition_handl.text: The unique identifier for the wait condition handle, which is a pre-signed URL used by external signals to notify CloudFormation of completion.

aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.anycast_.text: This field is the read-only list of IPAM CIDR configuration results for the CloudFront anycast IP list, reporting the allocated CIDR block and its allocation status for each specified IPAM configuration.
The anycast IP address allocated from the IPAM CIDR configuration for this CloudFront anycast IP list.
The CIDR block (e.g., '10.0.0.0/24') allocated from the IPAM pool for the anycast IP list, as reported in each IPAM CIDR configuration result.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IPAM pool associated with a CIDR configuration result for the CloudFront anycast IP list.
The lifecycle status of an individual IPAM CIDR allocation in the CloudFront anycast IP list, such as whether the CIDR is active and ready for use or still pending provisioning.

aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.etag.text: The entity tag (ETag) of the Anycast IP list, which is updated every time the list is modified and is used for conditional updates (e.g., If-Match requests).

aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.ip_addre.text: Specifies whether the anycast IP list contains IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, determining which type of IPs can be included in the IpList property.
