aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.ipam_cid.text: This computed attribute returns a list of objects, each representing the IPAM CIDR configuration result for a CIDR block associated with this anycast IP list, including details such as the CIDR and its allocation status.
The anycast IP address allocated from the IPAM pool, returned as part of the per-CIDR configuration result for this CloudFront anycast IP list.
The CIDR address range (e.g., 203.0.113.0/24) from an IPAM CIDR configuration result that is included in the CloudFront Anycast IP list's IP address inventory.
The ARN of the IPAM pool from which the CIDR block for this anycast IP list configuration result is allocated.
The provisioning status of each CIDR block returned in the IPAM configuration results for a CloudFront Anycast IP list, such as available, pending, or failed.
Specifies the IPAM pool CIDR allocations (each including an IPAM pool ID and netmask length) that define the IP address ranges CloudFront will advertise as anycast for this IP list.
The CIDR block, specified within an IPAM CIDR configuration, that determines the IP address range used for the CloudFront anycast IP list.
The ARN of the IPAM pool that supplies the CIDR block for this anycast IP list configuration in CloudFront.

aws_cloud_front_anycast_ip_list.tags.ite.text: The key (name) of a tag assigned to the CloudFront Anycast IP list, providing a user-defined label for the tag's value.
The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the CloudFront anycast IP list, used for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource.

aws_cloud_front_cache_policy.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS CloudFront to this cache policy, used to reference it in distributions and other resources.

aws_cloud_front_cache_policy.last_modifi.text: The timestamp (ISO 8601) of when the cache policy was last modified.

aws_cloud_front_cloud_front_origin_acces.text: The unique identifier assigned to the CloudFront origin access identity, which is used as the principal in S3 bucket policies and referenced in CloudFront distribution origin settings.
The canonical user ID associated with the CloudFront origin access identity, which you can use to grant the OAI permissions to access S3 objects via a bucket policy.

aws_cloud_front_connection_function.conn.text: The ARN of the CloudFront key value store to associate with the function, granting the function read access to that store's data during invocation at the edge.

aws_cloud_front_connection_function.crea.text: The date and time when the CloudFront function was created, as reported by AWS.

aws_cloud_front_connection_function.etag.text: Represents the current ETag version identifier of the CloudFront connection function, used for optimistic concurrency control during update/delete operations.

aws_cloud_front_connection_function.last.text: The date and time when the CloudFront function was last modified, returned by the API and updated automatically whenever the function's code or configuration changes.

aws_cloud_front_continuous_deployment_po.text: The HTTP header name that CloudFront inspects to route requests to the staging distribution in this continuous deployment policy.
The header value that CloudFront uses to route requests to the staging distribution in the continuous deployment policy.
Specifies the percentage of traffic to route to the staging distribution, with a value between 0 and 100, where 100 sends all traffic to the staging distribution.
The unique identifier that CloudFront assigns to the continuous deployment policy when it is created.
The date and time when the continuous deployment policy was last modified, returned as a string in ISO 8601 format.

aws_cloud_front_distribution.distributio.text: The HTTP methods (e.g., GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, POST, PATCH, DELETE) that CloudFront processes and forwards to the origin for this cache behavior.

The ID of the cache policy attached to this CloudFront cache behavior, which determines the time-to-live (TTL) settings and which HTTP headers, cookies, or query strings are included in the cache key.
Specifies which HTTP methods (such as GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, DELETE) CloudFront caches responses for in this cache behavior.
Indicates whether CloudFront automatically compresses files (such as HTML, CSS, or JavaScript) for this cache behavior when serving them to viewers.

Specifies the default time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for objects in the CloudFront cache for this cache behavior, controlling how long CloudFront retains an object before checking the origin for an updated version.
The ID of the field-level encryption configuration to apply to responses that match this cache behavior, enabling protection of sensitive data fields.
Specifies which query strings, cookies, and headers are forwarded to the origin and included in the cache key for requests that match this cache behavior.
Specifies how CloudFront forwards cookies from viewer requests to the origin for this cache behavior, controlling whether all, none, or a specific whitelist of cookies are forwarded.
Specifies which cookies to forward to the origin for this cache behavior: 'all', 'none', or 'whitelist' (the latter requires listing cookie names in 'whitelistedNames').
A list of specific cookie names that CloudFront includes in the origin request when forwarding cookies for this cache behavior, used when the cookie forwarding policy is 'whitelist'.
Specifies the list of HTTP header names that CloudFront includes in viewer requests forwarded to the origin for this cache behavior, alongside the default headers.
Specifies whether CloudFront forwards query string parameters to the origin; set to true to forward them (and optionally cache based on them) or false to not forward them.

The list of query string parameter names (keys) to include in the cache key for this cache behavior, controlling which query strings are used to determine cache hits when QueryString forwarding is enabled.
Associates CloudFront Functions with this cache behavior, specifying the function ARN and the event type (viewer-request or viewer-response) at which the function is invoked.
Specifies the CloudFront event type (such as viewer-request or viewer-response) that triggers the associated CloudFront Function for this cache behavior.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudFront function that is associated with the cache behavior to perform request and response manipulation.
Specifies whether gRPC is enabled for this cache behavior.
Whether gRPC is enabled for this CloudFront cache behavior.
Specifies the Lambda@Edge functions to invoke for a cache behavior, along with the CloudFront event type (such as viewer-request or origin-response) that triggers each function.
Specifies the CloudFront event that triggers the Lambda function, such as viewer-request, viewer-response, origin-request, or origin-response.
When true, includes the request body in the event passed to the associated Lambda function, allowing the function to inspect or modify the body for viewer-request or origin-request triggers.
The ARN of the Lambda function (Lambda@Edge) to associate with this cache behavior, which is invoked to process viewer or origin requests/responses for the specified path pattern.

The maximum time (in seconds) that objects are cached in CloudFront edge locations for this cache behavior, after which CloudFront will query the origin again regardless of the origin's Cache-Control headers.

Defines the minimum time in seconds that CloudFront retains objects in its cache for this cache behavior, ensuring that even if the origin provides a shorter Cache-Control max-age or Expires header, CloudFront still caches the object for at least this duration.
The unique identifier of the origin request policy attached to this cache behavior, which determines which headers, cookies, and query string parameters are forwarded from viewers to the origin.
Specifies the URL path pattern (e.g., /images/*) that determines which requests this cache behavior applies to, routing matching requests to the behavior's origin and caching settings.
Specifies the ARN of the real-time log configuration that determines which requests are logged in real time for this cache behavior.
Specifies the ID of the response headers policy that CloudFront attaches to HTTP responses for requests that match this cache behavior.
Indicates whether to enable Smooth Streaming support for this cache behavior, allowing CloudFront to properly serve Microsoft Smooth Streaming media content such as manifests and fragments.
The ID of the origin (from the distribution's origins) to which requests matching this cache behavior are forwarded.
Specifies the list of key group IDs whose public keys can be used to verify signed URLs or signed cookies for this cache behavior.
Specifies the AWS account IDs (or 'self') of trusted signers that are allowed to create signed URLs or signed cookies for this cache behavior, enabling access to private content.

Determines the protocol policy for viewer requests matched by this cache behavior, choosing between allowing HTTP and HTTPS ('allow-all'), enforcing HTTPS only ('https-only'), or redirecting HTTP to HTTPS ('redirect-to-https').
The minimum time (in seconds) that CloudFront caches the custom error response for a given error code before requesting the origin again, configured as part of each custom error response entry.
The HTTP status code (e.g., 400, 403, 404, 500) for which CloudFront should return the custom error response defined in this custom_error_responses block.
Sets the HTTP status code that CloudFront returns to the viewer for this custom error response, overriding the origin's status code.
The path to the custom error page that CloudFront returns for the corresponding error code in a custom error response.
Specifies the CloudFront event that triggers the associated function, such as `viewer-request` or `viewer-response`, for the default cache behavior.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudFront function to associate with the default cache behavior, executed on viewer request or viewer response events.
Specifies the CloudFront event that triggers the associated Lambda function, such as viewer-request, viewer-response, origin-request, or origin-response.
Indicates whether CloudFront includes the body of the request in the event payload sent to the Lambda function when the associated CloudFront event triggers.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function to associate with this cache behavior for Lambda@Edge processing.
Specifies the HTTP status codes that, when returned by the primary origin, trigger CloudFront to fail over to the secondary origin for the origin group.

Specifies the HTTP status codes (as an object containing a list of integer codes in `items` and a `quantity` count) that, when returned by the primary origin, trigger failover to the secondary origin for a CloudFront origin group.
The list of HTTP status codes from the primary origin that trigger CloudFront to fail over to the secondary origin in the origin group.
The number of HTTP status codes in the items list that trigger failover for the origin group when a response matches one of these codes.
A unique identifier for the origin group, used to reference the origin group when associating it with cache behaviors or in the origin groups' failover configuration.
Specifies the set of origins in this origin group, including the number of origins (Quantity) and the list of origin identifiers (Items) that CloudFront can fail over between.
Specifies the list of origin IDs that belong to this origin group, allowing CloudFront to perform failover between them based on the group's failover criteria.
The unique identifier of an origin that is a member of this origin group, referencing an origin in the distribution's Origin list to enable failover between origins.
The number of origins in the origin group; in CloudFront an origin group always consists of exactly two members (primary and secondary), so this quantity must be 2.
Specifies the number of times that CloudFront attempts to connect to the origin before giving up, accepting values from 1 to 3.
For a custom origin, this sets the connection timeout in seconds (1–10, default 3) that CloudFront allows for establishing a TCP connection to the origin server.
Configuration for a custom origin (non-S3) that defines the ports, protocol policy, and SSL settings used when CloudFront communicates with the origin.
Specifies the HTTP port that CloudFront uses to connect to the origin server.
The HTTPS port that CloudFront uses to connect to the custom origin, defaulting to 443 if not specified.
Specifies the IP address type (IPv4, IPv6, or IPv4 and IPv6) that CloudFront uses when connecting to the custom origin.
Specifies the duration in seconds that CloudFront should keep an idle connection to the custom origin open, with a default of 5 seconds and a valid range of 1–60 seconds.
Configures mutual TLS (mTLS) for the custom origin by specifying the S3 bucket container and the ARN of the client certificate that CloudFront presents to the origin.
The ARN of the client certificate, stored in AWS Certificate Manager, that CloudFront presents to this custom origin when using mutual TLS (mTLS).

Specifies the protocol policy that CloudFront uses to fetch files from the custom origin, allowing either HTTP only, HTTPS only, or matching the viewer's protocol (values: http-only, https-only, match-viewer).

Specifies the read timeout in seconds that CloudFront waits for a reply from a custom origin server before timing out, applicable only to custom (non-S3) origins and typically ranging from 1 to 60 seconds.
Specifies the SSL/TLS protocols that CloudFront may use to establish a secure connection with the custom origin.
Specifies the DNS domain name of the origin server (e.g., an S3 bucket website endpoint or custom HTTP server) from which CloudFront fetches content for this origin in the distribution.
The unique identifier for this origin within the distribution, used to reference it in cache behaviors and origin groups.
The ID of the origin access control (OAC) that is associated with this origin, which CloudFront uses to securely access the origin (e.g., an S3 bucket).
Specifies custom headers that CloudFront includes in requests it sends to the origin for this origin configuration.
The name of a custom header that CloudFront adds to requests sent to the origin.
The value of the custom header that CloudFront adds to requests it sends to the origin.

Specifies the directory path that CloudFront automatically appends to the origin's domain name for all requests forwarded to that origin, allowing content to be served from a subdirectory on the origin server.

Specifies the Origin Shield settings for this origin, including whether it is enabled and the AWS Region for the Origin Shield, to help reduce the load on your origin by caching and consolidating requests.
Specifies whether Origin Shield is enabled for this origin, adding an additional caching layer that can reduce load on the origin and improve availability.
Specifies the AWS Region where the CloudFront Origin Shield is located, providing an additional caching layer that reduces the load on the origin by aggregating requests from edge locations.
Specifies the maximum time, in seconds, that CloudFront waits for the origin to respond to a request before timing out (also known as the origin read timeout or response completion timeout).
Configures the S3 bucket origin settings for this origin, including the CloudFront origin access identity that CloudFront uses to access the bucket.

Specifies the CloudFront origin access identity (OAI) that CloudFront uses to access the S3 bucket, allowing you to restrict direct access to the bucket and only allow access through the distribution.
The number of seconds CloudFront waits for a response from the S3 origin, including the time to read the response headers, before timing out (allowed range 1-60, default 30).
Configures this origin to use a VPC origin (e.g., an Application Load Balancer or App Runner service) by specifying the VPC origin's ID and optionally the read and keepalive timeout durations.
The amount of time, in seconds, that CloudFront keeps an idle connection to the VPC origin alive before closing it, controlling connection reuse for the VPC origin configuration.
The amount of time (in seconds) that CloudFront waits for the VPC origin to respond to a request after it has been forwarded, before considering the request failed.
The AWS account ID that owns the VPC endpoint serving as the origin, required when the endpoint is in a different account than the distribution.
The identifier of the CloudFront VPC origin that this origin references, which points to a supported resource (such as an Application Load Balancer) inside a VPC.

Specifies whether viewer mutual TLS (mTLS) is enabled or disabled, where 'enabled' requires viewer requests to present a valid client certificate from the associated trust store and 'disabled' turns off mTLS enforcement.

aws_cloud_front_distribution.domain_name.text: The CloudFront distribution's automatically assigned domain name (e.g., d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net) that clients use to access content served by the distribution.

aws_cloud_front_distribution.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS CloudFront to the distribution, used to reference the distribution in other resources and APIs.

aws_cloud_front_distribution.tags.key.text: The key of a key-value tag applied to the CloudFront distribution, used for organizing and identifying the AWS resource.

aws_cloud_front_distribution_tenant.crea.text: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the CloudFront distribution was created.

aws_cloud_front_function.function_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CloudFront function, assigned by AWS upon creation.

aws_cloud_front_function.function_config.text: The ARN of the CloudFront KeyValueStore to associate with this function, enabling the function to read data from the key value store at runtime.

aws_cloud_front_function.stage.text: The CloudFront function's stage, which is read-only and indicates whether the function is in the 'DEVELOPMENT' or 'LIVE' lifecycle stage as managed by AWS.

aws_cloud_front_function.tags.key.text: The tag key (e.g., 'environment') assigned to the CloudFront function for metadata and cost allocation.

aws_cloud_front_key_group.id.text: The unique identifier assigned to the key group by CloudFront.

aws_cloud_front_key_group.last_modified_.text: The timestamp of the most recent change to this CloudFront key group's configuration, automatically set by AWS when the key group is created or updated.

aws_cloud_front_key_value_store.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CloudFront key value store.

aws_cloud_front_key_value_store.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this CloudFront KeyValueStore, used to reference the store in other resources such as CloudFront functions.

aws_cloud_front_key_value_store.status.text: The current status of the CloudFront KeyValueStore, such as CREATING or READY, indicating whether the store is ready for use.

aws_cloud_front_key_value_store.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the CloudFront key value store, used to identify the tag within the tag set.

aws_cloud_front_origin_access_control.id.text: The id is the unique CloudFront-assigned identifier for the origin access control, which is used when associating the OAC with a distribution's cache behavior.

aws_cloud_front_origin_request_policy.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by CloudFront to the origin request policy.

aws_cloud_front_origin_request_policy.la.text: The date and time when the origin request policy was last modified.

aws_cloud_front_public_key.created_time.text: The date and time when the CloudFront public key was created.

aws_cloud_front_realtime_log_config.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CloudFront real-time log configuration.

aws_cloud_front_realtime_log_config.end_.text: This object specifies the configuration for the Amazon Kinesis Data Streams destination of a real-time log endpoint, including the stream's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) and the IAM role ARN that CloudFront assumes to publish log records to the stream.
The ARN of an IAM role that CloudFront assumes to send real-time log data to the associated Kinesis data stream.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Kinesis data stream to which CloudFront delivers real-time log data.
Specifies the streaming service type for a real-time log configuration endpoint, and the only supported value is 'Kinesis'.

aws_cloud_front_response_headers_policy..text: The unique identifier assigned by CloudFront to this response headers policy, used to reference the policy in distributions.
The date and time when the response headers policy was last modified, returned as an ISO 8601 string.
The name of the HTTP response header that CloudFront adds to responses when using this policy.

Controls whether CloudFront overrides the value of the matching response header returned by the origin with the value specified in this custom header item; when false, CloudFront adds the custom header only if the origin does not already return a header with that name.
The value to be sent in the custom HTTP response header that CloudFront adds to responses for this policy.
The name of an HTTP response header that CloudFront removes from the response when the response headers policy is applied to a distribution.

aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.d.text: The domain name (such as d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net) that CloudFront assigns to the streaming distribution and that clients use to request content.

aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.i.text: The unique identifier assigned to the CloudFront streaming distribution by AWS, used as the distribution ID.

aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.s.text: The required configuration object for the CloudFront streaming distribution, specifying the S3 origin, enabled flag, optional aliases, comment, logging settings, and trusted signers for RTMP streaming.
List of alternate domain names (CNAMEs) that can be used to access the streaming distribution in addition to the default cloudfront.net domain name.
The required string comment that describes the CloudFront streaming distribution, which must be provided in the streaming distribution configuration.
Determines whether the CloudFront streaming distribution is enabled to accept and serve viewer requests.
Configures access logging for the streaming distribution, specifying whether logging is enabled, the S3 bucket where logs are stored, and the log file prefix.
The Amazon S3 bucket to which CloudFront delivers access logs for the streaming distribution.
Specifies whether CloudFront writes access logs for the streaming distribution to the S3 bucket named in the logging bucket property.
This string specifies the prefix that CloudFront adds to the beginning of the access log file names for this streaming distribution when it writes logs to the configured Amazon S3 bucket.

Specifies the price class for the CloudFront streaming distribution, which determines the geographic set of edge locations used and the associated pricing tier (e.g., PriceClass_100, PriceClass_200, or PriceClass_All).
Specifies the S3 bucket (domain_name) and CloudFront origin access identity used to authorize access for the streaming distribution's origin.
The domain name of the S3 bucket that acts as the origin for the CloudFront streaming distribution, typically formatted as `<bucket-name>.s3.amazonaws.com`.
The CloudFront origin access identity (OAI) to associate with the S3 origin for the streaming distribution, which permits CloudFront to access private S3 content.

Specifies the AWS account IDs (or 'self' for the owner account) that are permitted to create signed URLs for private content served by this CloudFront streaming distribution, including an Enabled flag indicating whether the trusted signer list is active.
Specifies the AWS account numbers of trusted signers (accounts with CloudFront key pairs) allowed to create signed URLs or signed cookies for this streaming distribution.

Indicates whether trusted signers are enabled for the streaming distribution, so that when true, the accounts in the AwsAccountNumbers list can create signed URLs, and when false, only the creating AWS account can create signed URLs.

aws_cloud_front_streaming_distribution.t.text: Configures the list of tag objects (each with a Key and Value) that are attached to the CloudFront streaming distribution for organization, cost tracking, and access management.
A tag key used to assign a custom metadata label to the CloudFront streaming distribution for organization, cost allocation, or access control purposes.

The value portion of a tag applied to the CloudFront streaming distribution, allowing you to associate arbitrary metadata such as environment or cost center with the resource for tracking and management.

aws_cloud_front_trust_store.etag.text: The entity tag (ETag) that represents the current version of the CloudFront trust store, used for optimistic concurrency control so that you can detect and avoid conflicting updates.

aws_cloud_front_trust_store.id.text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for the CloudFront trust store, used to reference the trust store when attaching it to a CloudFront distribution.

aws_cloud_front_trust_store.last_modifie.text: A read-only timestamp indicating the date and time when the AWS CloudFront trust store was last modified.

aws_cloud_front_trust_store.number_of_ca.text: The number of CA certificates currently contained in the CloudFront trust store.

aws_cloud_front_trust_store.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a user-defined tag applied to the CloudFront trust store, used to identify and categorize the resource for cost allocation and management.

aws_cloud_front_trust_store.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the CloudFront trust store, used for resource organization and metadata management.

aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.account_id.text: The account ID of the AWS account that owns the CloudFront VPC origin, automatically populated by CloudFront and read-only.

aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this CloudFront VPC origin, automatically generated by AWS upon creation and used to reference the origin in other AWS services and IAM policies.

aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.created_time.text: The date and time when the CloudFront VPC origin was created, returned as a read-only string.

aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the VPC origin, used to reference this origin when configuring CloudFront distributions.

aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.last_modified.text: The date and time when the CloudFront VPC origin was last modified.

aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.status.text: The current deployment status of the CloudFront VPC origin, such as 'InProgress' or 'Deployed', indicating whether the origin is fully provisioned and ready for use.

aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the CloudFront VPC origin, used for metadata and resource organization.

aws_cloud_front_vpc_origin.vpc_origin_en.text: Specifies whether the CloudFront VPC origin endpoint uses IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, with allowed values 'IPv4' or 'IPv6'.

aws_cloud_trail_channel.destinations.loc.text: The ARN of the destination resource (e.g., an event data store ARN) where the CloudTrail channel delivers events.

aws_cloud_trail_channel.destinations.typ.text: Specifies the type of destination for the CloudTrail channel, which can be either `EVENT_DATA_STORE` (for a CloudTrail Lake event data store) or `AWS_SERVICE` (for an AWS service such as Amazon S3, CloudWatch Logs, or EventBridge).

aws_cloud_trail_channel.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the CloudTrail channel for identification and management.

aws_cloud_trail_channel.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the CloudTrail channel, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the channel resource.

aws_cloud_trail_dashboard.created_timest.text: The timestamp, in ISO 8601 format, indicating when the CloudTrail dashboard was created, as returned by the CloudTrail DescribeDashboard API.

aws_cloud_trail_dashboard.refresh_schedu.text: Defines the automatic refresh frequency for the CloudTrail dashboard, expressed as a unit-value pair (e.g., HOURS with a value of 6 for a six-hour refresh interval).

aws_cloud_trail_dashboard.tags.text: A list of tag objects (each containing a key and value) to attach to the CloudTrail dashboard, enabling resource identification, cost allocation, and AWS resource management.

aws_cloud_trail_dashboard.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the CloudTrail dashboard, used to assign custom metadata for identifying, organizing, and controlling access to the dashboard (e.g., via IAM conditions and cost allocation tags).

aws_cloud_trail_dashboard.updated_timest.text: The timestamp indicating when the CloudTrail dashboard was last updated.

aws_cloud_trail_dashboard.widgets.query_.text: For each widget in an AWS CloudTrail dashboard, this list of strings supplies the query parameter values that are substituted into the widget's query to filter or scope the displayed data.
The SQL query statement that a widget in an AWS CloudTrail dashboard uses to fetch and display data from the CloudTrail event data store.

aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store.advance.text: Defines the list of field selectors within an advanced event selector that specify conditions on event fields, such as eventCategory or eventName, to determine which events are delivered to the event data store.
Matches events where the selected field's value ends with any of the specified string suffixes, defining a condition in the CloudTrail event data store's advanced event selector.

For each field selector in a CloudTrail event data store's advanced event selector, `equals` specifies the list of exact values that the named event field must match for an event to be delivered to the data store.
The name of the event attribute (e.g., eventCategory, readOnly, resources.type) that the field selector evaluates to filter which events are ingested into the event data store.
For each advanced event selector field, this list of suffixes defines a `not endsWith` condition: an event matches only if the field's value does not end with any of the specified suffix strings.
Defines a list of values that, if any matches the event field specified by the adjacent field selector, will cause the event to be excluded from the CloudTrail event data store.

For an advanced event selector on an event data store, this list contains string prefixes; events whose corresponding field value begins with any listed prefix are excluded from matching the selector.
Specifies a list of string prefixes that the value of the selected event field must start with for an event to match this advanced event selector and be included in the event data store.
Provides a friendly name for the advanced event selector, used to identify it when managing multiple selectors in the CloudTrail event data store.

aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store.created.text: The creation time of the CloudTrail event data store, reported by CloudFormation as a read-only timestamp string.

aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store.tags.text: Specifies the list of tags (key-value pairs) to associate with the CloudTrail event data store, enabling cost allocation, access control, and resource identification.

aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store.tags.ke.text: Specifies the key of a tag to assign to the CloudTrail event data store, which is a custom label used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store.tags.va.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the CloudTrail event data store, used to organize and identify the resource for governance and cost allocation purposes.

aws_cloud_trail_event_data_store.updated.text: The timestamp of the last update to the event data store, indicating when its configuration was most recently modified.

aws_cloud_trail_trail.advanced_event_sel.text: In an advanced event selector, this list defines which fields (e.g., eventCategory, resources.type, readOnly) and their matching values (equality or prefix matching) determine the data events that CloudTrail logs.
Restricts the advanced event selector to match events where the value of the specified field ends with any of the provided suffix strings.
Specifies the exact values that the field must match for a CloudTrail event to be logged, so only events whose field value equals one of the strings in this list are processed by the trail.
Specifies the event field name to filter on within a CloudTrail advanced event selector field selector, such as 'eventCategory', 'eventName', or 'readOnly'.
Matches data events where the value of the specified field does not end with any of the strings in this list, used to filter which events are delivered to the trail.

For CloudTrail advanced event selectors, this list of strings specifies field values that the event attribute must NOT equal for the selector to match (e.g., if Field is 'eventName', events with any event name not in this list are matched).
Specifies a list of strings that the value of the selected event field must not start with, so that events are included when the field value does not begin with any of these strings.
In an AWS CloudTrail advanced event selector's field selector, this list of string values defines prefixes that the event field's value must start with for the selector to match the event.
Defines a user-friendly name for an advanced event selector, such as 'Log all events', which helps identify the selector when managing trail event filtering settings.

aws_cloud_trail_trail.aggregation_config.text: Specifies the event category (e.g., Management, Data, Insight, or NetworkActivity) that this aggregation configuration applies to for a CloudTrail trail delivering events to a CloudTrail Lake event data store.

aws_cloud_trail_trail.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CloudTrail trail, automatically assigned by AWS when the trail is created.

aws_cloud_trail_trail.event_selectors.da.text: Specifies the S3 buckets or Lambda functions for which to record data events, where each data resource includes a resource type (e.g., AWS::S3::Object or AWS::Lambda::Function) and a list of ARNs or prefixes.
Specifies the AWS resource type (e.g., AWS::S3::Object or AWS::Lambda::Function) for which to log data events within the event selector.

Contains the list of ARNs (for example, S3 object or prefix ARNs in the form arn:aws:s3:::bucket/prefix, or Lambda function ARNs) that identify the specific data resources selected for the event selector.

aws_cloud_trail_trail.event_selectors.ex.text: For the trail's event selectors, this list specifies the event sources (such as kms.amazonaws.com) whose management events are excluded from being recorded.

aws_cloud_trail_trail.event_selectors.in.text: Indicates whether the trail includes AWS management events (such as CreateTrail or DeleteTrail) for the account; when false, only data events are logged for the selector.

aws_cloud_trail_trail.event_selectors.re.text: Specifies whether the trail records read-only, write-only, or all events (Allowed values: All, ReadOnly, WriteOnly) for the resources matched by this event selector.

aws_cloud_trail_trail.insight_selectors..text: Sets the list of event categories (either 'api' or 'insight') that control which CloudTrail Insights event types are captured for the trail, allowing you to log API activity insights and/or operational insights.
The type of CloudTrail Insights event to log, either ApiCallRateInsight for unusual API call rate or ApiErrorRateInsight for unusual API error rate.

aws_cloud_trail_trail.sns_topic_arn.text: The read-only Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SNS topic that CloudTrail uses to deliver notifications about log file delivery, populated automatically when the trail is configured with an SNS topic.

aws_cloud_trail_trail.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to this CloudTrail trail, used to categorize and identify the trail among resource groups and for cost allocation.

aws_cloud_trail_trail.tags.value.text: The value of an individual tag assigned to the CloudTrail trail, used for metadata, classification, or access control.

aws_cloud_trail_trail.trail_name.text: Specifies the name of the CloudTrail trail; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name, and trail names must start with a letter and may contain only lowercase letters, numbers, periods, underscores, and dashes.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CloudWatch alarm.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.dimensions.name.text: The name (key) of a CloudWatch metric dimension that, along with its value, is used to identify a particular metric or metric context for the alarm.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.dimensions.value.text: The value for a CloudWatch alarm metric dimension, which combines with the dimension name to uniquely identify a specific metric for the alarm to monitor.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.evaluation_window..text: The wall_clock_window within the evaluation_window configures a calendar-based evaluation window for CloudWatch anomaly detection, specifying the timezone and start/end times for when the band is computed.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.account_id.text: The AWS account ID associated with a metric data query, used to retrieve metrics from another account in a cross-account CloudWatch alarm.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.expression.text: A math expression string (e.g., 'm1 + m2') that defines a computed metric used in the alarm, referencing other metric queries in the same metrics list.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.id.text: A unique identifier for the metric within the alarm's metric configuration, used to reference it in metric math expressions.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.label.text: The label is a human-friendly name assigned to a metric or expression in a CloudWatch alarm's metric data query, which is displayed in the CloudWatch console and can be used to identify the metric in alarm graphs.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.metric_sta.text: Defines the specific CloudWatch metric and statistic to evaluate in this metric data query, including the metric's namespace, name, dimensions, period, and statistical aggregation (e.g., Average).
The metric that this statistic is based on, identified by its namespace, metric name, and optional dimensions.
Specifies the dimensions for the metric, each containing a name and value pair that uniquely identifies the metric within CloudWatch.
The name of the dimension, which is the key that, together with the dimension value, identifies a specific metric dimension within the metric's dimensions.
The value of the CloudWatch metric dimension, which combined with the dimension key uniquely identifies the metric's associated resource or scope.
The name of the CloudWatch metric to monitor, such as CPUUtilization or StatusCheckFailed, which must match a published metric in the specified namespace.
The namespace of the CloudWatch metric, such as AWS/EC2, that identifies the service or application emitting the metric in the metric stat of a composite alarm.
The length of time in seconds to aggregate the metric data for this alarm's metric statistic, defining the granularity of data points evaluated for the alarm.
The statistic to apply to the metric (for example, SampleCount, Average, Sum, Minimum, Maximum, or a percentile such as p99).
Specifies the unit of measure for the metric statistic (e.g., Count, Percent, Seconds, Bytes) that the alarm evaluates.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.period.text: The length of time, in seconds, used each time the specified metric is evaluated for the alarm (e.g., 60 for one-minute evaluation periods).

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.metrics.return_dat.text: Determines whether the time series data for this metric data query is returned in the CloudWatch alarm's metric math expression, and when the alarm uses multiple metric queries, exactly one query must have return_data set to true (typically the metric that drives the alarm).

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.tags.key.text: Specifies the key of a tag applied to the CloudWatch alarm, used to categorize and manage the alarm resource.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the CloudWatch alarm, used to categorize or identify the alarm for management and billing purposes.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm_mute_rule.tags.key.text: The key portion of a tag attached to the CloudWatch alarm mute rule, enabling you to categorize and filter the rule among your AWS resources.

aws_cloud_watch_alarm_mute_rule.tags.val.text: Specifies the value for a tag key on the CloudWatch alarm mute rule, allowing you to categorize or filter the rule in CloudWatch and AWS billing reports.

aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.configu.text: The configuration settings for the anomaly detector, specifying metric characteristics such as the period and evaluation periods (and optionally periodic spacing) that control how the detection model analyzes the metric.
Specifies the time ranges, defined by start and end times, during which CloudWatch Anomaly Detector will not perform anomaly detection on the associated metric(s).
Specifies the end time of the excluded time range, in ISO 8601 format, during which the anomaly detector ignores data.

The start time (in ISO 8601 format) of a time range to exclude from anomaly detection model training, marking the beginning of a period when the detector will not use data for learning the normal pattern.
Sets the IANA time zone (e.g., 'America/New_York') used by the anomaly detector to evaluate and display metric anomalies, overriding the default UTC.

aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.dimensi.text: A list of dimension key-value pairs that scope the anomaly detector to a specific metric, such as an instance ID or environment, and when omitted the detector applies to the metric without any dimensions.
The name of a dimension that, along with its value and other dimensions, uniquely identifies the CloudWatch metric for which this anomaly detector is configured.
The value of the dimension that, combined with the dimension name and metric name, identifies the specific metric for which the CloudWatch anomaly detector is configured.

aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.metric_.text: The metric_characteristics object specifies the period (in seconds) and timezone (e.g., 'UTC') used by the CloudWatch anomaly detector for evaluating the metric data.

When true, indicates that the metric is expected to have periodic spikes, causing the anomaly detector to adjust its band to be more tolerant of those recurring spikes rather than treating them as anomalies.

Defines the metric math expression anomaly detector configuration, including the metric data queries and the period (in seconds) that CloudWatch Anomaly Detector uses to establish a baseline for detecting anomalous behavior.
Specifies the list of metric data queries that define the metric math expression evaluated by this anomaly detector.
Specifies the AWS account ID containing the metric data for this query, enabling cross-account metric math within the anomaly detector's metric math expression.
The math expression (e.g., SUM(SEARCH('Namespace=...', 'Sum', 300))) that defines the metric data query used to calculate the anomaly detection band for the metric math anomaly detector.
A short name that uniquely identifies this metric data query within the anomaly detector's metric math expression, used to reference the query in the expression (e.g., 'm1' or 'e1').
A human-readable label for the metric or expression in the metric data query, which CloudWatch displays instead of the auto-generated label if provided.

Specifies the underlying metric and its statistic (e.g., Average, Sum, Minimum, Maximum, or percentile), along with the period and unit, for a metric data query used in the metric math expression of the anomaly detector.
Specifies the CloudWatch metric (including namespace, metric name, and dimensions) that the metric_stat for this metric data query uses to evaluate the anomaly detector.
Defines the dimensions (name-value pairs) for the target metric in the metric stat, which identify the metric in CloudWatch and scope the anomaly detection calculations.
The name of a CloudWatch metric dimension, which is the key in a key-value pair that identifies a specific attribute of the metric (e.g., 'InstanceId', 'LoadBalancerName').
Specifies the value of a CloudWatch metric dimension, which together with the dimension key and namespace uniquely identifies a metric used in the metric math anomaly detector's metric data query.
The name of the CloudWatch metric used in the metric stat for the metric math anomaly detector, identifying the specific metric to query.
Specifies the AWS namespace (e.g., AWS/EC2) of the metric referenced by the metric stat within the metric data query for this metric math anomaly detector.
The period specifies the length of time (in seconds) over which the metric data is aggregated for the metric stat used in the anomaly detector's metric math expression.
The statistic to apply to the metric (e.g., Average, Sum, Minimum, Maximum, SampleCount) within the metric data query used by the anomaly detector's metric math expression.
Specifies the unit of measure (e.g., Count, Percent, Seconds) for the metric statistic that contributes to the metric math expression used by this anomaly detector.
The time interval, in seconds, used to aggregate the metric data for the metric math expression that defines this anomaly detector.

Indicates whether the time series data for this metric data query should be returned in the anomaly detector's metric math evaluation, typically set to false for intermediate helper queries and true only for the final expression whose result is used for anomaly detection.
The name of the CloudWatch metric that the anomaly detector monitors, required when defining a single-metric anomaly detector.

aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.namespa.text: The CloudWatch namespace (e.g., AWS/EC2 or a custom namespace) that the anomaly detector applies to, identifying the metric's source.

aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.single_.text: Specifies the CloudWatch metric (namespace, metric name, dimensions, and stat) used to create an anomaly detection band for a single metric, as opposed to a metric math expression.
The 12-digit AWS account ID that owns the metric used by the anomaly detector, enabling cross-account anomaly detection.
Specifies the dimensions (name-value pairs) that define the metric for which this anomaly detector is created, used to identify the metric uniquely within the single metric anomaly detector.
The name (key) of a CloudWatch metric dimension that identifies the metric in the single-metric anomaly detector.
The value of a CloudWatch metric dimension, which together with its dimension name identifies a specific dimension for the metric used by the anomaly detector.
The name of the CloudWatch metric to be monitored by this single metric anomaly detector.
The CloudWatch namespace of the metric to monitor with the anomaly detector, such as AWS/EC2 or a custom namespace.
Specifies the CloudWatch statistic (such as Average, Sum, Minimum, Maximum, or SampleCount) applied to the metric in the single-metric anomaly detector configuration.

aws_cloud_watch_anomaly_detector.stat.text: The statistic (e.g., Average, Sum, Maximum) of the CloudWatch metric that this anomaly detector applies to, specifying which metric statistic the anomaly detection model analyzes.

aws_cloud_watch_composite_alarm.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the CloudWatch composite alarm, used to identify, categorize, and manage the alarm in AWS.

aws_cloud_watch_composite_alarm.tags.val.text: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the CloudWatch Composite Alarm, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the alarm resource.

aws_cloud_watch_dashboard.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the CloudWatch dashboard, used to identify and categorize the dashboard for resource management and cost allocation.

aws_cloud_watch_dashboard.tags.value.text: Specifies the value for a tag key applied to the CloudWatch dashboard for resource organization and identification.

aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.apply_on_tr.text: When set to true, this boolean indicates that the Contributor Insights rule evaluates logs after they have been processed by a CloudWatch Logs transformation, rather than the original raw logs.

aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CloudWatch contributor insights rule.

aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.rule_body.text: The JSON rule definition for the Contributor Insights rule, specifying the log filter, aggregation, and metric settings.

aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.rule_name.text: The name of the Contributor Insights rule, which must be unique within your AWS account and is used to identify and reference the rule in CloudWatch.

aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.rule_state.text: Specifies whether the Contributor Insights rule is enabled or disabled, with valid values ENABLED and DISABLED, controlling whether the rule continuously collects and aggregates log data for the specified metrics.

aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.tags.text: A list of key-value tags to attach to the CloudWatch Contributor Insights rule, enabling you to categorize and manage the rule across your AWS environment.

aws_cloud_watch_insight_rule.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the CloudWatch Contributor Insights rule, used for resource categorization, cost allocation, and access management.

aws_cloud_watch_log_alarm.tags.value.text: The value associated with a tag key applied to the CloudWatch alarm, which aids in identifying, organizing, and managing AWS resources and costs.

aws_cloud_watch_metric_stream.exclude_fi.text: The list of metric names within the specified namespace to exclude from the metric stream.
Defines the CloudWatch namespace (e.g., AWS/EC2) whose metrics are excluded from the metric stream when matched by this exclusion filter.

aws_cloud_watch_metric_stream.include_fi.text: The names of the metrics in the specified namespace to include in the metric stream; if omitted, all metrics in the namespace are included.
The namespace of the AWS service whose metrics must match this filter for them to be included in the metric stream (e.g., AWS/EC2).

aws_cloud_watch_metric_stream.statistics.text: Specifies additional statistics (such as percentiles like p99) to include in the metric stream for metrics that match the namespace and metric name of this statistics configuration.

Specifies the list of metrics (namespace and metric name) to which the corresponding statistics configuration's allowed statistics apply, controlling which metric streams include the configured statistics.
The name of the CloudWatch metric for which the specified additional statistics are included in the metric stream.

The name of the AWS service or custom application namespace (e.g., AWS/EC2, AWS/Lambda) whose metrics are included in this statistics configuration, filtering which metric namespaces are sent to the stream.

aws_cloud_watch_metric_stream.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the CloudWatch metric stream, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_code_artifact_domain.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to an AWS CodeArtifact domain, enabling custom metadata for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization.

aws_code_artifact_domain.tags.value.text: The free-form value of a user-defined tag attached to an AWS CodeArtifact domain, used to add custom metadata for organizing and managing the domain.

aws_code_artifact_package_group.origin_c.text: Configures the origin restrictions for the package group, controlling whether package versions can be published directly or pulled from upstream repositories.
Specifies the publishing and access restrictions for external and upstream origins to control how package versions are added or read within this package group.

Specifies the restriction mode (ALLOW or BLOCK) for whether package versions in this package group can be obtained from external upstream repositories, governing the origin of packages pulled into the repository.
Specifies the list of external upstream repository names to which the restriction mode (e.g., ALLOW or BLOCK) for 'external_upstream' applies in the package group's origin configuration.

This required string specifies the restriction mode for external upstream repositories (e.g., public registries) in the package group's origin configuration, with allowed values such as ALLOW, BLOCK, or ALLOW_SPECIFIC_REPOSITORIES.

Specifies the origin restriction settings for internal upstream repositories, controlling whether package versions can be pulled from other CodeArtifact repositories in the same domain via the `pull` mode (with allowed values `ALLOW`, `BLOCK`, or `ALLOW_OR_BLOCK`).

Specifies a list of CodeArtifact repository names that are allowed as internal upstream sources for this package group when the internal upstream restriction mode is set to ALLOW_SPECIFIC_REPOSITORIES.

Determines whether packages in this package group can be sourced from internal upstream repositories (upstream repositories within the same AWS CodeArtifact domain), with allowed values ALLOW, BLOCK, or ALLOW_SPECIFIC_REPOSITORIES to permit only specific repositories.
Configures the restriction mode for publishing package versions to this package group, controlling whether new package versions can be published directly to the repository associated with this group.
A list of repository ARNs that are allowed to publish packages to this package group when the publish restriction is set to ALLOW_SPECIFIC_REPOSITORIES in the origin configuration.
Controls the publish restriction mode for the package group, where ALLOW permits publishing, BLOCK denies all publishing, and READ_ONLY permits reading package metadata but blocks publishing.

aws_code_artifact_repository.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS CodeArtifact repository, used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_code_artifact_repository.tags.value.text: The value of a tag (key-value pair) applied to an AWS CodeArtifact repository, used to add metadata for organization and cost allocation.

aws_code_build_fleet.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CodeBuild fleet.

aws_code_build_fleet.base_capacity.text: The initial number of compute instances allocated to the CodeBuild fleet, serving as the baseline from which the fleet scales toward its maximum capacity.

aws_code_build_fleet.compute_configurati.text: Specifies the compute configuration for the CodeBuild fleet, including the disk size and machine type (e.g., General or ARM) used for build environments.
Specifies the amount of disk space (in GB) allocated to each compute instance in the code build fleet.
Specifies the EC2 instance type used by the compute fleet's compute configuration, such as m5.large or c5.xlarge, determining the underlying hardware for the build fleet.
The machine type of the CodeBuild fleet's compute configuration, which determines the processor architecture or GPU availability (e.g., GENERAL, ARM, GPU).
Defines the amount of memory allocated to each compute instance in an AWS CodeBuild fleet's compute configuration.
The number of virtual CPUs (vCPUs) to allocate to each compute instance in the CodeBuild fleet.

aws_code_build_fleet.compute_type.text: The compute type for the fleet's build instances, such as BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL or BUILD_GENERAL1_LARGE, which determines the CPU and memory allocated to each build.

aws_code_build_fleet.environment_type.text: The type of compute environment (e.g., LINUX_CONTAINER, WINDOWS_CONTAINER, ARM_CONTAINER) that the CodeBuild fleet uses for its build instances.

aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_proxy_configu.text: Specifies the proxy configuration for a CodeBuild fleet, including the default proxy address and HTTP/HTTPS proxy ports used to route outbound traffic from the fleet's compute instances.
Determines the default action (ALLOW_ALL or DENY_ALL) the proxy takes for traffic that does not match any ordered proxy rules.

Defines the ordered list of proxy rules (each specifying an app, domain, or IP type and a value) that control network access for the CodeBuild fleet's build environments, evaluated in the order listed.
The effect of the proxy rule, either ALLOW or DENY, determines whether traffic matching the specified entities and type is allowed or blocked.
The list of domain names or IP addresses that this ordered proxy rule matches for the CodeBuild fleet's proxy configuration.
Indicates whether the entities in this proxy rule are interpreted as URL patterns (e.g., 'URL') or as hostnames (e.g., 'HOST'), which controls how outbound traffic filtering is applied.

aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_service_role.text: The ARN of the IAM service role that the AWS CodeBuild fleet assumes to access necessary AWS resources such as source code repositories and build artifact storage.

aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_vpc_config.text: Specifies the VPC, subnets, and security group IDs that the CodeBuild fleet's compute instances use for network access.

aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_vpc_config.se.text: The security group IDs that AWS CodeBuild uses to control traffic to and from the network interfaces (ENIs) that the fleet launches in the specified VPC.

aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_vpc_config.su.text: Specifies the subnet IDs in the VPC where the CodeBuild fleet's compute instances run.

aws_code_build_fleet.fleet_vpc_config.vp.text: The ID of the VPC in which the CodeBuild fleet's compute resources are deployed.

aws_code_build_fleet.image_id.text: Specifies the container image (e.g., a managed CodeBuild image or a custom Docker image from Amazon ECR) that the fleet uses for its build environments.

aws_code_build_fleet.name.text: The name of the CodeBuild fleet, which serves as its identifier and is optional; if not provided, CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_code_build_fleet.overflow_behavior.text: Determines how builds are handled when the fleet's capacity is exhausted, either queuing them (QUEUE) or routing them to on-demand capacity (ON_DEMAND).

aws_code_build_fleet.scaling_configurati.text: Configures auto-scaling for the compute fleet by specifying minimum and maximum capacity and an optional target-tracking scaling policy that adjusts fleet size based on demand.
The maximum number of compute instances that the CodeBuild fleet can scale out to.
Determines the scaling strategy for the CodeBuild compute fleet, either TARGET_TRACKING_SCALING for dynamic auto-scaling or PAY_PER_REQUEST for on-demand capacity provisioning.
Specifies a list of target tracking scaling policies that automatically adjust the CodeBuild fleet's compute capacity to maintain a target value for a metric such as CPU or memory utilization.
Specifies the fleet utilization metric type (e.g., FLEET_UTILIZATION_RATE) that the target tracking scaling policy uses to determine when to adjust fleet capacity.
This field defines the target value for the target tracking scaling policy, which is the metric threshold (e.g., a percentage for CPU utilization) that triggers scaling of the CodeBuild fleet.

aws_code_build_fleet.tags.text: Assigns metadata as key-value pairs (tag key and tag value) to the CodeBuild fleet, enabling cost tracking, access control, and resource categorization.

aws_code_build_fleet.tags.key.text: The key portion of a tag attached to the CodeBuild fleet, used to categorize and filter the resource for management and cost tracking.

aws_code_build_fleet.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the AWS CodeBuild fleet, used to categorize and manage the fleet resource.

aws_code_build_project.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the CodeBuild project.

aws_code_build_project.artifacts.text: Defines where CodeBuild stores the build output, including artifact type (e.g., S3), location, path, packaging, and optional encryption settings.

aws_code_build_project.artifacts.artifac.text: Specifies an identifier for this output artifact so it can be matched against the artifact outputs declared in the project's buildspec when a build produces multiple artifact sets.

aws_code_build_project.artifacts.encrypt.text: Indicates whether encryption for the build output artifacts is disabled, allowing artifacts to be stored in S3 without server-side encryption.

aws_code_build_project.artifacts.locatio.text: Specifies the name of the S3 bucket where CodeBuild stores build output artifacts when the artifact type is set to S3.

aws_code_build_project.artifacts.name.text: The name of the build output artifact, which for S3 artifact type is the file name that CodeBuild writes to the output bucket.

aws_code_build_project.artifacts.namespa.text: Determines whether the build output artifacts are stored in a path that includes the build ID (as a subdirectory) or without it, affecting the S3 key structure for the artifact location.

aws_code_build_project.artifacts.overrid.text: When true, the name of the build output artifact is overridden by the artifact name specified in the buildspec (e.g., via the `name` property of the buildspec's `artifacts` section); otherwise, CodeBuild uses the project name and build ID as the artifact name.

aws_code_build_project.artifacts.packagi.text: Determines whether the build output artifacts are packaged into a ZIP archive (ZIP) or left as raw files (NONE) when uploaded to the artifact repository, such as an S3 bucket.

aws_code_build_project.artifacts.path.text: The path within the S3 bucket where the build output artifact is stored, relative to the bucket root; if omitted, the artifact is placed at the bucket root.

aws_code_build_project.artifacts.type.text: Specifies the type of build output artifact, which can be set to CODEPIPELINE to have CodePipeline manage the artifact, S3 to store the output in an S3 bucket, or NO_ARTIFACTS to not generate an artifact.

aws_code_build_project.auto_retry_limit.text: Sets the maximum number of times CodeBuild automatically retries a failed build as part of the project's batch build configuration.

aws_code_build_project.badge_enabled.text: Indicates whether the CodeBuild project has a build badge enabled, which provides an embeddable URL for showing the build's status in an external repository.

aws_code_build_project.build_batch_confi.text: Configures the batch build settings for the AWS CodeBuild project, including the service role, timeout, maximum number of builds, and restrictions for running builds in a batch.
Specifies how AWS CodeBuild generates test reports for batch builds, either as a single aggregated report for the entire batch or as separate reports for each individual build.
Whether to combine all build artifacts from the batch into a single artifact location.
Specifies the restrictions for a batch build, including the maximum number of builds that can run concurrently and the compute types allowed for the batch build.
Restricts the batch build to only use the compute types (e.g., BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL, BUILD_GENERAL1_MEDIUM) listed here for its individual builds; if the list is empty, all compute types are allowed.
Specifies the maximum number of builds that can be executed concurrently in a batch build for this CodeBuild project.
Specifies the ARN of the IAM service role that AWS CodeBuild assumes to run batch builds for this project.
The number of minutes after which a batch build is considered expired and is cancelled.

aws_code_build_project.cache.text: Configures the build cache for the CodeBuild project, allowing specification of either an S3 bucket for caching or a local cache with cache modes such as LOCAL_SOURCE_CACHE, LOCAL_CUSTOM_CACHE, and LOCAL_DOCKER_LAYER_CACHE.

aws_code_build_project.cache.cache_names.text: The cache namespace groups build output cache entries so that multiple build projects sharing the same namespace can reuse the same cache.

aws_code_build_project.cache.location.text: The S3 bucket path (e.g., 'bucket-name/path') where CodeBuild stores the cache when the cache type is S3.

aws_code_build_project.cache.modes.text: Specifies the local cache modes (e.g., LOCAL_SOURCE_CACHE, LOCAL_DOCKER_LAYER_CACHE, LOCAL_CUSTOM_CACHE) to enable for the build project when using a local cache type.

aws_code_build_project.cache.type.text: The type of cache to use for the build project, such as NO_CACHE, S3, or LOCAL, which determines how build outputs and dependencies are cached.

aws_code_build_project.concurrent_build_.text: Maximum number of concurrent builds that can run for this CodeBuild project.

aws_code_build_project.description.text: A short, optional description of the CodeBuild build project.

aws_code_build_project.encryption_key.text: The ARN of the AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) that CodeBuild uses to encrypt the build output artifacts; if not specified, the default AWS-managed key for Amazon S3 is used.

aws_code_build_project.environment.text: Specifies the build environment, including the compute type, container image, environment variables, and whether to use privileged mode for the CodeBuild project.

aws_code_build_project.environment.certi.text: The ARN of an AWS Certificate Manager certificate that AWS CodeBuild associates with the project's build environment to support cryptographic operations such as signing build artifacts.

aws_code_build_project.environment.compu.text: Specifies the compute resources for the build environment (for example, BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL or BUILD_GENERAL1_LARGE), determining the CPU and memory allocated to the build job.

aws_code_build_project.environment.docke.text: The list of security group IDs to associate with the Docker server used by the CodeBuild build environment, controlling network access to the Docker server.

aws_code_build_project.environment.envir.text: Defines custom environment variables passed to the build container, each specifying a name, value, and optional type such as PLAINTEXT, PARAMETER_STORE, or SECRETS_MANAGER.
The name of the environment variable to be set in the CodeBuild environment, used as the key to reference the variable in build commands.
The type of the environment variable, which can be PLAINTEXT, PARAMETER_STORE, or SECRETS_MANAGER, determining how the variable's value is interpreted and retrieved.

Specifies the value of the environment variable that is injected into the CodeBuild container at build time, which can be a plain string or, when the variable's type is PARAMETER_STORE, the name of a Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter whose value is resolved at runtime.

aws_code_build_project.environment.fleet.text: Specifies the compute fleet (via its ARN) that provides the compute resources for this CodeBuild project environment.
The ARN of the compute fleet to use for the build environment, enabling the build project to run on a specific managed or reserved capacity fleet.

aws_code_build_project.environment.image.text: The Docker image identifier (such as aws/codebuild/standard:5.0) that specifies the build environment for the CodeBuild project.
Controls whether CodeBuild uses the build project's Docker credentials (CODEBUILD) or the service role (SERVICE_ROLE) to authenticate when pulling a private container image.

aws_code_build_project.environment.privi.text: Enables running the build in privileged mode, which is required when building Docker images or using Docker-in-Docker inside the CodeBuild environment.

aws_code_build_project.environment.regis.text: Specifies the credentials, typically from AWS Secrets Manager, used to access a private Docker registry for the CodeBuild build environment.
The ARN or name of the credentials (such as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager) used to authenticate to a private Docker registry or other container image registry.
Specifies the service responsible for creating the registry credential, which must be set to SECRETS_MANAGER for AWS CodeBuild to retrieve the login credentials.

aws_code_build_project.environment.type.text: Specifies the type of build environment for the CodeBuild project, such as LINUX_CONTAINER, WINDOWS_CONTAINER, or ARM_CONTAINER.

aws_code_build_project.file_system_locat.text: Specifies the file system locations (such as Amazon EFS mount points) to mount to the build container during a build.

In an AWS CodeBuild project's file system location configuration, the identifier is a user-defined logical name that uniquely identifies the file system mount, used to reference and distinguish it among multiple file system locations.
The DNS name or path that identifies the file system to be mounted into the CodeBuild build environment, such as an Amazon EFS file system's DNS name (e.g., fs-12345678.efs.us-west-2.amazonaws.com).
Defines the mount options (for example, NFS options such as nfsvers, rsize, wsize, hard, timeo, and retrans) that are used when mounting the file system in the CodeBuild environment.
Mount point is the directory inside the CodeBuild container where the specified file system (e.g., Amazon EFS) is mounted, such as `/efs`.
Indicates the type of file system mounted in the CodeBuild project, which must be 'EFS' for an Amazon Elastic File System mount.

aws_code_build_project.id.text: The unique identifier for the AWS CodeBuild project, which is the project name as assigned when the project is created.

aws_code_build_project.logs_config.text: Configures log output for the build project, specifying CloudWatch Logs and/or S3 log settings such as status, group/stream names, path, and encryption key.

aws_code_build_project.logs_config.cloud.text: Defines the CloudWatch Logs settings for the build project's logs, including the status (enabled/disabled), the log group name, the stream name, and whether encryption using the default AWS-managed CMK is disabled.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs group to which CodeBuild publishes build logs.
Indicates whether CloudWatch Logs are enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for storing the build project's logs.
Specifies the name of the CloudWatch Logs log stream where the CodeBuild project's build logs are delivered, overriding the default build-ID-based stream name.

aws_code_build_project.logs_config.s3_lo.text: Defines how build logs are delivered to an S3 bucket, including the S3 bucket location and path, whether S3 logging is enabled, and whether encryption is disabled.
Indicates whether S3 build logs are encrypted; when set to true, the logs are stored unencrypted, whereas the default (false or omitted) enables encryption.
The ARN of the S3 bucket (and optional path prefix) where CodeBuild stores build logs when S3 logging is enabled.
Indicates whether S3 logging is enabled for the build project, with valid values being ENABLED or DISABLED.

aws_code_build_project.name.text: Specifies a unique, user-defined name for the CodeBuild build project, which cannot be changed after creation; if omitted, CloudFormation automatically generates a unique name.

aws_code_build_project.queued_timeout_in.text: Specifies the number of minutes a build can remain in the QUEUED state before CodeBuild times it out, after which the build is marked as failed.

aws_code_build_project.resource_access_r.text: The ARN of an IAM role that AWS CodeBuild assumes to access and manage resources in the VPC configured for the project, such as creating network interfaces.

aws_code_build_project.secondary_artifac.text: Specifies a list of additional build output artifacts (in addition to the primary artifact) that CodeBuild can produce, each configured with settings like type, location, path, namespace, packaging, and encryption.
A string that uniquely identifies this secondary artifact within the build project, used to reference it in build commands and to distinguish it from other secondary artifacts.
If set to true, the secondary build output artifact is stored unencrypted in S3, otherwise it is encrypted, typically using an AWS-managed or customer-managed KMS key.
Specifies the S3 bucket name (or the image/container path for other artifact types) where the secondary build artifacts are output.
The unique name for this secondary artifact, which must be distinct from other secondary artifact names in the project and is used to identify the artifact in build output.

Controls the directory structure of the secondary artifact in the output location, where the namespaceType value (NONE, BUILD_ID, or TIMESTAMP) determines whether the build ID or timestamp is included in the artifact path.

For secondary artifacts in an AWS CodeBuild project, setting this boolean to true overrides the default output artifact name with the value specified in the artifact's Name property, while false (or unset) lets the build spec determine the name.
Whether the build output artifact is packaged as a single ZIP file (ZIP) or left as-is without compression (NONE).

Specifies the directory path within the output S3 bucket where the build output for this secondary artifact is stored, with the final object key also influenced by the artifact's namespace type and name.
Specifies the type of the secondary artifact, such as S3 to store output in an S3 bucket or CODEPIPELINE to deliver it to AWS CodePipeline.

aws_code_build_project.secondary_source_.text: Specifies the source version (e.g., branch, tag, or commit ID) for each secondary source associated with the project, enabling the build to pull a specific revision of each additional repository.
Specifies the identifier of the secondary source (as defined in the project's secondary sources) that this particular source version applies to.

Specifies the version (such as a Git commit ID, branch name, or tag) of the secondary source that CodeBuild uses for the build, identified by the associated source identifier in the project's secondary source versions list.

aws_code_build_project.secondary_sources.text: Specifies a list of additional source repositories (such as GitHub, Bitbucket, S3, or CodeCommit) that CodeBuild uses for the build project, in addition to the primary source.

Specifies the authentication method for a Git-based secondary source (GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, or Bitbucket), including the authorization type (e.g., OAUTH or PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN) and the optional ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the credentials.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the OAuth token or personal access token used to authenticate to the secondary source repository.
Specifies the authentication type (e.g., OAUTH) used by CodeBuild to access the secondary source repository, as defined in the source's auth settings.
Specifies the buildspec file path or inline buildspec YAML/JSON content for this secondary source, allowing it to override the project-level buildspec for that source.
Specifies the context and target URL used for reporting the build status of this secondary source to the source repository provider.
The context string that identifies the build status entry for this secondary source in the repository's commit status (for example, a custom label displayed in GitHub or Bitbucket).
Specifies the URL of the repository that contains the source code, which is used as the target link for the build status report for this secondary source.
The number of commits to include in the Git clone for the secondary source, where a lower value speeds up the clone by fetching only the most recent commits.
Specifies whether git submodules are fetched for the secondary source repository in an AWS CodeBuild project.
Determines whether Git submodules are fetched for the associated secondary source repository in the AWS CodeBuild project.
Indicates whether the connection to the source repository is allowed to use insecure SSL (e.g., ignoring self-signed certificate errors).
Specifies the repository URL or source location (such as an S3 bucket path, GitHub repository, or Bitbucket) for the secondary source of the CodeBuild project.

For each secondary source, report_build_status controls whether CodeBuild reports build status information back to the source provider, which is only meaningful when that secondary source's type is GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, or Bitbucket.

The identifier that uniquely identifies this secondary source among all sources in the CodeBuild project, and is used to construct the environment variable names (e.g., `CODEBUILD_SOURCE_DIR_<identifier>`) that buildspec commands can use to reference the source's directory and version.
Defines the source provider type for this secondary source, such as CODECOMMIT, S3, BITBUCKET, GITHUB, or GITHUB_ENTERPRISE.

aws_code_build_project.service_role.text: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS CodeBuild assumes to perform the build, granting permissions for actions like fetching source code, publishing artifacts, and writing logs.

aws_code_build_project.source.text: Defines the source code repository for the build, including the repository type (e.g., S3, CodeCommit, GitHub, Bitbucket) and its location, along with optional settings like buildspec file path and git clone depth.

aws_code_build_project.source.auth.text: Specifies the authorization configuration for the source code repository, including the authentication type (such as OAuth) and optional resource ARN, enabling AWS CodeBuild to access the source.

aws_code_build_project.source.auth.resou.text: The resource field specifies the endpoint URL of the source provider (such as a GitHub Enterprise Server) when the auth type is PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, and is not used for OAuth-based authorization.

aws_code_build_project.source.auth.type.text: Specifies the authentication method to use when accessing the source repository, such as OAUTH, BASIC_AUTH, PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, or CODECONNECTIONS.

aws_code_build_project.source.build_spec.text: The build specification for the build project, either the name of a buildspec file or an inline YAML/JSON string that defines the build commands.

aws_code_build_project.source.build_stat.text: Determines how CodeBuild reports the build status back to the source provider (e.g., GitHub, Bitbucket, or CodeCommit) by setting the status context and a custom target URL for the status update.
The identifier string for the build status update, used to distinguish this build status from others in the source provider (such as a GitHub commit status context label).

Specifies the URL that AWS CodeBuild sends as the target link when reporting build status to the source control system (e.g., GitHub or Bitbucket), providing users with a direct link to the build details.

aws_code_build_project.source.git_clone_.text: Sets the depth of the git clone, limiting the number of commits fetched from the repository (default is 1) to create a shallow clone.

aws_code_build_project.source.git_submod.text: Configures Git submodules for the build source, with a 'FetchSubmodules' flag that determines whether submodules are fetched before the build runs.
Specifies whether to fetch git submodules for the build project's source repository.
