aws_code_build_project.source.insecure_s.text: Set to true to ignore SSL certificate warnings when connecting to the source repository, such as when it uses a self-signed certificate.

aws_code_build_project.source.location.text: The URL or location of the source repository (for example, an S3 bucket name, GitHub or Bitbucket repository URL, or CodeCommit ARN) that CodeBuild uses as the build input.

aws_code_build_project.source.report_bui.text: Indicates whether to report the build's start and finish status back to the source provider (e.g., GitHub, Bitbucket) for commits and pull requests, valid only for certain source types.

aws_code_build_project.source.source_ide.text: Assigns a logical identifier to the primary source that can be referenced in buildspec commands, enabling the build to distinguish this source when the project uses multiple sources.

aws_code_build_project.source.type.text: The type of source repository for the CodeBuild project, which determines how the build fetches source code (e.g., S3, CODECOMMIT, GITHUB, BITBUCKET, or NO_SOURCE).

aws_code_build_project.source_version.text: Specifies the version of the source code to build, such as a commit ID, branch, or tag for Git-based repositories (CodeCommit, GitHub, Bitbucket) or an object key/version ID for Amazon S3; if omitted, the default branch or latest source version is used.

aws_code_build_project.tags.text: Assigns a list of tag objects (key-value pairs) to the AWS CodeBuild project, used for cost allocation, access control, and identifying project resources.

aws_code_build_project.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to associate with the AWS CodeBuild project.

aws_code_build_project.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag attached to the CodeBuild project, providing arbitrary metadata for cost allocation or organization.

aws_code_build_project.timeout_in_minute.text: The number of minutes after which a build in this project is automatically stopped and marked as failed if it has not completed.

aws_code_build_project.triggers.text: Defines the webhook trigger configuration, including the build type and filter groups that control which repository events (e.g., branch pushes or pull requests) automatically initiate a build.

aws_code_build_project.triggers.build_ty.text: Specifies whether the project's webhook triggers should initiate a build, with a value of `BUILD` enabling builds and `NO_BUILD` disabling them for incoming source events.

aws_code_build_project.triggers.filter_g.text: Specifies a list of filter groups that determine which webhook events trigger a build, where each filter group is a list of webhook filters (e.g., event type, branch, file path) that must all match for the build to start.

aws_code_build_project.triggers.pull_req.text: Determines which pull requests trigger a build for the CodeBuild project's webhook: ALL builds every pull request, BRANCH builds only those targeting branches that match the filter pattern, and NON_BRANCH builds only those targeting branches that do not match the pattern.
A list of IAM role ARNs that can approve pull requests to trigger a build, defined within the project's pull request build policy for webhook-triggered builds.
Indicates whether an approval comment on a pull request is required to trigger the webhook build, so that builds only run when an authorized user comments with an approval phrase.

aws_code_build_project.triggers.scope_co.text: The domain of the Git repository hosting service (for example, 'github.com' or a GitHub Enterprise server hostname) that scopes the webhook trigger configuration for this CodeBuild project.
The name of the repository or organization (as determined by the associated scope) that this webhook filter applies to, restricting which source code events trigger the build.
Specifies whether the webhook trigger is scoped to an entire Bitbucket workspace ('WORKSPACE') or to a specific repository ('REPOSITORY').

aws_code_build_project.triggers.webhook.text: Determines whether the CodeBuild project's webhook is enabled, allowing builds to be automatically triggered by code changes pushed to the linked source repository (such as GitHub or Bitbucket).

aws_code_build_project.visibility.text: Specifies the visibility of the build project, with valid values PRIVATE, PUBLIC_READ, or PUBLIC, controlling whether unauthenticated users can view or trigger builds.

aws_code_build_project.vpc_config.text: Configures the build project to run in a customer-managed Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), specifying the VPC ID, subnet IDs, and security group IDs for the build environment.

aws_code_build_project.vpc_config.securi.text: This field specifies the security group IDs for the VPC configuration of the CodeBuild project, defining which security groups apply to the build's network interfaces.

aws_code_build_project.vpc_config.subnet.text: The list of subnet IDs within the VPC that AWS CodeBuild uses to run the build project's containers.

aws_code_build_project.vpc_config.vpc_id.text: The ID of the Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) in which the CodeBuild project's builds run.

aws_code_build_report_group.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CodeBuild report group, which uniquely identifies it within AWS.

aws_code_build_report_group.delete_repor.text: Indicates whether all reports associated with the report group are deleted when the CloudFormation stack deletes the report group.

aws_code_build_report_group.export_confi.text: Configures how test reports are exported from the report group, specifying either an S3 bucket destination or no export, including the S3 bucket, prefix, and encryption settings.
Specifies the type of export destination for the report group's raw test results, which is either S3 or NO_EXPORT.
Defines the S3 bucket and object path where CodeBuild exports the test reports generated by this report group.
The name of the S3 bucket where CodeBuild exports the report group's test results.
The AWS account ID of the S3 bucket owner, used to verify the bucket is owned by the specified account before writing report export artifacts.
When true, disables encryption for the S3 bucket where CodeBuild exports the report group's artifacts.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the exported test report's S3 objects; if omitted, CodeBuild uses the default AWS managed key for Amazon S3.
Specifies whether the report is packaged as a ZIP file or not when exported to the S3 destination, with valid values ZIP or NONE.
Specifies the path (prefix) within the S3 bucket where the raw data of the report is exported.

aws_code_build_report_group.id.text: This field is the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CodeBuild report group, which serves as the unique identifier and is generated by AWS when the report group is created.

aws_code_build_report_group.name.text: The name of the report group; if not provided, CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_code_build_report_group.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs to associate with the report group for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource, such as for cost allocation and access control.

aws_code_build_report_group.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS CodeBuild report group, which can be used to organize, categorize, or track costs and access for the resource.

aws_code_build_report_group.type.text: The type of report group, which can be either TEST or CODE_COVERAGE, determining the kind of reports this group contains.

aws_code_commit_repository.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this CodeCommit repository within AWS.

aws_code_commit_repository.clone_url_htt.text: The HTTP(S) clone URL for the AWS CodeCommit repository, which is used to clone the repository over HTTPS.

aws_code_commit_repository.clone_url_ssh.text: The SSH URL used to clone the CodeCommit repository over SSH.

aws_code_commit_repository.code.text: Defines the initial code to be committed to the repository, specifying the S3 source (bucket, key, and optional object version), target branch, and commit message.

aws_code_commit_repository.code.branch_n.text: The name of the branch in the repository to which the initial code (specified in the Code property) is committed when the repository is created.

aws_code_commit_repository.code.s3.text: The S3 location (bucket, key, and optional object version) from which AWS CodeCommit imports the code for the repository's initial commit.

aws_code_commit_repository.code.s3.bucke.text: The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that contains the source code to be committed to the CodeCommit repository when the repository is created.

aws_code_commit_repository.code.s3.key.text: The S3 object key (file path within the bucket) of a ZIP archive containing the initial code that the CodeCommit repository is populated with when the repository is created, as part of the 'code' configuration's 's3' block.

aws_code_commit_repository.code.s3.objec.text: Specifies the version ID of the S3 object that contains the initial code for the repository, enabling you to use a specific version when the object has multiple versions.

aws_code_commit_repository.id.text: The id is the repository name, which uniquely identifies the CodeCommit repository within AWS and is automatically populated from the repository name argument when the resource is created.

aws_code_commit_repository.kms_key_id.text: The ID of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the repository contents; if omitted, an AWS-managed key is used.

aws_code_commit_repository.name.text: The name attribute holds the repository name, which matches the RepositoryName property set at creation and is immutable afterwards.

aws_code_commit_repository.repository_de.text: Specifies the description of the CodeCommit repository, which is displayed in the AWS Management Console and can be up to 1,000 characters long.

aws_code_commit_repository.repository_na.text: Specifies the name of the AWS CodeCommit repository, which must be unique within the AWS account and region, and is used as the repository's identifier for clone URLs and API operations.

aws_code_commit_repository.tags.text: Defines a list of key-value tag objects to associate with the AWS CodeCommit repository, enabling you to categorize and filter the repository for cost tracking, access management, and resource organization.

aws_code_commit_repository.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to associate with the AWS CodeCommit repository, used for identifying and organizing the repository.

aws_code_commit_repository.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the AWS CodeCommit repository, used to store metadata associated with the corresponding tag key.

aws_code_commit_repository.triggers.text: Defines the list of SNS notification triggers for the repository, where each trigger specifies the SNS topic ARN, the repository events (such as 'all', 'update', 'create', or 'delete') that will fire the trigger, and optionally the branch names that restrict which events are published.

aws_code_commit_repository.triggers.bran.text: Specifies the list of branches in the repository for which the trigger's events (such as create, update, or delete) should trigger the associated action (e.g., an SNS notification); if the list is empty, the trigger applies to all branches.

aws_code_commit_repository.triggers.cust.text: The custom_data field of a trigger is an optional string that AWS CodeCommit includes in the SNS notification payload delivered to the trigger's destination ARN, allowing you to pass arbitrary metadata to downstream consumers.

aws_code_commit_repository.triggers.dest.text: The ARN of the SNS topic that receives push notifications from this CodeCommit repository when the trigger condition is met.

aws_code_commit_repository.triggers.even.text: Lists the CodeCommit repository events (for example, push, createBranch, deleteBranch, createTag, deleteTag, or updateReference) that activate the trigger.

aws_code_commit_repository.triggers.name.text: The name of an AWS CodeCommit repository trigger, which must be unique within the repository and is used to identify the trigger when configuring and managing repository events.

aws_code_connections_connection.tags.val.text: The value portion of a user-defined tag assigned to an AWS CodeConnections Connection, used to store arbitrary metadata for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_code_deploy_application.tags.value.text: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the CodeDeploy application.

aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.minimu.text: Defines the minimum number or percentage of healthy hosts that must remain available during a deployment, where the object specifies a type (HOST_COUNT or FLEET_PERCENT) and a numerical value.
Specifies whether the minimum healthy hosts value is an absolute number of instances (HOST_COUNT) or a percentage of the fleet (FLEET_PERCENT) that must remain healthy during a deployment.

The numeric value that defines the minimum number of healthy hosts (when type is HOST_COUNT) or the minimum percentage of the deployment fleet that must be healthy (when type is FLEET_PERCENT) during a CodeDeploy deployment.

aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.traffi.text: Configures how traffic is shifted from the original fleet to the replacement fleet during a deployment, such as a linear or canary strategy with a step percentage and interval.

The time_based_canary object inside traffic_routing_config for an AWS CodeDeploy deployment config specifies a canary-style traffic shift, moving a defined percentage of traffic to the new revision first and then the remaining traffic after a fixed time interval.
In a time-based canary deployment, this is the number of minutes to wait after shifting the canary percentage of traffic before shifting the remaining traffic.

The percentage of traffic to shift to the updated deployment group in the first (canary) increment of a time-based canary deployment, with the remaining traffic shifted in the second increment after the configured interval.

Specifies a time-based linear traffic routing configuration for a CodeDeploy deployment, which shifts a set percentage of traffic to the updated environment at regular time intervals until deployment completes.
The number of minutes to wait between each incremental shift of traffic during a time-based linear deployment, used with linear_percentage to control the pace of the rollout.
The percentage of traffic to shift to newly added instances at each interval in a time-based linear deployment configuration.

Specifies the traffic-routing strategy for the deployment — allowed values are AllAtOnce (all traffic shifted immediately), TimeBasedLinear (shift traffic incrementally at regular intervals), and TimeBasedCanary (shift a canary portion of traffic, then the remainder).

aws_code_deploy_deployment_config.zonal_.text: Configures zonal deployment behavior for the deployment config, including settings such as the first-zone monitoring duration, overall monitor duration, and the minimum number of healthy hosts required per zone.
The number of seconds AWS CodeDeploy waits to monitor the health of the first Availability Zone in a zonal ECS deployment before proceeding to the next zone.

Specifies the minimum number or percentage of healthy hosts that must be available in each Availability Zone during a CodeDeploy zonal deployment, configured via a type (HOST_COUNT or FLEET_PERCENT) and a value.
Specifies whether the minimum healthy hosts per Availability Zone is expressed as an absolute host count (HOST_COUNT) or as a percentage of the total fleet (FLEET_PERCENT).

Specifies the numeric threshold (as a host count or zone fleet percentage, determined by the associated 'type' property) for the minimum number of healthy instances that must remain available in each Availability Zone during a zonal deployment in AWS CodeDeploy.
The number of seconds that AWS CodeDeploy monitors the health of the first region after its deployment succeeds, before starting deployment to the next region in a zonal deployment.

aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.alarm_c.text: The name of a CloudWatch alarm that this CodeDeploy deployment group monitors to automatically stop a deployment if the alarm enters an alarming state.

aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.ec2_tag.text: The EC2 tag key (e.g., 'Environment') used to match instances for the deployment group's tag filter.
Specifies the tag filter type (KEY_ONLY, VALUE_ONLY, or KEY_AND_VALUE) used to match EC2 instances for the deployment group.
The tag value that the deployment group's EC2 tag filter matches against to select instances for deployment.

A list of EC2 tag filters (each with Key, Value, and Type) that collectively define a tag group; an instance must match all tags in this group to be included in the deployment group via this EC2 tag set list entry.
The tag key (name) of an EC2 tag filter used to match instances for inclusion in the CodeDeploy deployment group, where the filter belongs to a logical group within an EC2 tag set.
Specifies the tag filter type used to match EC2 instances in this tag group, with allowed values such as KEY_ONLY, VALUE_ONLY, and KEY_AND_VALUE.
The tag value to match for the EC2 instance tag group, used as a filter to select instances for the CodeDeploy deployment group.

aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.ecsserv.text: The name of the ECS cluster where the ECS service targeted by the CodeDeploy deployment group is running.
The name of the ECS service that the deployment group targets, as specified in the ECSServices configuration.

aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.load_ba.text: The name of the Classic Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) that CodeDeploy deregisters instances from and registers instances to during a deployment.
The name of an Elastic Load Balancing target group to associate with the CodeDeploy deployment group.

In an AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployment using paired target groups, prod_traffic_route specifies the listener ARN (or ARNs) on the load balancer that currently routes production traffic to the original (blue) target group, which CodeDeploy automatically updates to shift traffic to the replacement (green) target group during the deployment.

The ARNs of the Elastic Load Balancing listeners that route traffic to the production target group in a blue/green deployment, enabling CodeDeploy to shift production traffic to the replacement target group after deployment.

Specifies the list of target groups that make up a blue/green target group pair for an Application Load Balancer or Network Load Balancer, each containing the name or ARN of a target group used for the blue/green deployment traffic routing.
The name of the target group that is part of a target group pair used for load balancer traffic routing in a CodeDeploy blue/green deployment.

This traffic route object lists the target group ARNs that CodeDeploy sends test traffic to during a blue/green deployment, letting you validate the replacement environment before production traffic is shifted.
A list of Application Load Balancer listener ARNs that define the test traffic route used to shift traffic to the replacement environment during an AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployment.

aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.on_prem.text: The tag key used to match on-premises instances for the deployment group's on-premises instance tag filter.

The type of tag filter used to select on-premises instances for the deployment group, such as KEY_ONLY, VALUE_ONLY, or KEY_AND_VALUE, controlling whether matching is based on the tag key, the tag value, or both.
The tag value that an on-premises instance must match for the instance to be included in the deployment group when using tag-based instance selection.

Defines a list of on-premises instance tag filters (key, value, and match type) that constitute a single tag group within an on-premises tag set, used to select on-premises instances for the CodeDeploy deployment group.
The tag key used in an on-premises instance tag group to match and select on-premises instances for the deployment group.

The `type` field of an on-premises tag group in an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group specifies the tag filter matching mode, with valid values `KEY_ONLY`, `VALUE_ONLY`, or `KEY_AND_VALUE`, determining whether the filter matches on the tag key, value, or both when selecting on-premises instances.
The value of an on-premises instance tag (e.g., 'prod') that must match for an on-premises instance to be included in the deployment group when this tag group is used as a filter.

aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.tags.va.text: The user-defined value for a tag key attached to an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group, enabling resource categorization and metadata management.

aws_code_deploy_deployment_group.trigger.text: The list of CodeDeploy deployment or instance events (e.g., DeploymentSuccess, DeploymentFailure) that will trigger the SNS notification for this trigger configuration.
The name of a trigger configuration for the deployment group, used to identify this trigger among the configured CloudWatch Events or SNS triggers.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic that AWS CodeDeploy uses to send notifications when the deployment lifecycle events specified in the trigger configuration occur.

aws_code_guru_profiler_profiling_group.a.text: The unique identifier assigned by CodeGuru Profiler to an Amazon SNS notification channel used for anomaly detection, which references the channel within the profiling group's configuration.
The ARN of the SNS topic to which anomaly detection notifications are published for this profiling group.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the profiling group.

aws_code_guru_profiler_profiling_group.t.text: A key in the tags map of an AWS CodeGuru Profiler profiling group, used to attach custom metadata (such as environment or application name) to the profiling group for resource organization, cost allocation, and access control.
The value of a user-defined tag assigned to the profiling group, used for cost allocation, resource management, and access control in AWS.

aws_code_guru_reviewer_repository_associ.text: Specifies the value of a tag attached to the CodeGuru Reviewer repository association, using an arbitrary string for metadata or categorization.

aws_code_pipeline_custom_action_type.con.text: A short, user-facing description of the configuration property that is displayed to users in the CodePipeline console.
Indicates whether the configuration property is a key, which is used to uniquely identify the action instance within AWS CodePipeline.
The unique, human-readable identifier for a configuration property of the custom action type, used as the property key when specifying action configuration values in a pipeline.
Indicates whether the configuration property can be used as a filter (queryable) when listing or viewing pipeline executions in the AWS CodePipeline console.
Indicates whether the configuration property is required for the custom action type to be used in a pipeline.
Specifies whether the configuration property is a secret (such as a password) and should be hidden from view in the CodePipeline console.
Specifies the data type of the configuration property that the custom action accepts, such as 'String', 'Number', or 'Boolean', which determines how the property value is handled by the pipeline.

aws_code_pipeline_custom_action_type.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS CodePipeline to this custom action type upon creation.

aws_code_pipeline_custom_action_type.tag.text: The tag key (such as 'Environment') used to label and categorize this AWS CodePipeline custom action type for management and identification purposes.

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.artifact_stor.text: This object defines a single artifact store for the pipeline, specifying the S3 bucket name (location) and type, along with optional encryption key settings, used to store input and output artifacts for the CodePipeline.
Specifies the customer-managed AWS KMS key (by ID and type) that CodePipeline uses to encrypt the artifacts stored in the S3 bucket for this artifact store.
The AWS KMS key ID or ARN of the KMS key used to encrypt the S3 artifact store for the CodePipeline pipeline.
The type of encryption key used for the artifact store, which must be 'KMS' for an AWS KMS key or 'S3' for an Amazon S3-managed key.
The ARN or name of the S3 bucket that CodePipeline uses as the artifact store for the pipeline.
Specifies the type of the artifact store, which must be `S3` for the pipeline to use an Amazon S3 bucket for storing input and output artifacts.
The AWS region in which the S3 bucket that stores pipeline artifacts is located, enabling cross-region artifact stores.

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.disable_inbou.text: The user-provided reason explaining why inbound transition to the stage is disabled.
The name of a stage in the AWS CodePipeline pipeline for which inbound stage transitions are disabled, preventing automatic execution from preceding stages into this stage.

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.stages.action.text: Lists the actions that are part of a stage in the CodePipeline pipeline, where each action defines its type (e.g., Source, Build, Deploy), configuration, and run order within the stage.
Identifies the action type for a CodePipeline action by specifying its category, owner, provider, and version (e.g., Source, AWS, CodeCommit, 1).
The category of the action, such as Source, Build, Deploy, Test, Invoke, or Approval, which identifies the type of action and determines how it is executed in the pipeline.
The owner field specifies which entity provides the action type (AWS, ThirdParty, or Custom) used by the stage action in the CodePipeline pipeline.
The name of the service or action provider that performs the action, such as CodeDeploy, Lambda, or S3.
The version of the action type, which identifies the specific revision of the action provider (e.g., '1' for the default version of AWS-managed actions).
List of shell commands that the Command action runs when this stage action is executed in the CodePipeline pipeline.
Specifies the provider-specific configuration parameters for the CodePipeline action, such as Owner, Repo, and Branch for a GitHub source action, or other service-specific settings.

Specifies a list of environment variables, each defined by a name, value, and optional type (such as PLAINTEXT or PARAMETER_STORE), that are passed to the action's provider for use during its execution.
The name (key) of the environment variable defined for an action, which is used to reference it when the action runs in AWS CodePipeline.

The type of the environment variable, which can be PLAINTEXT, PARAMETER_STORE, or SECRETS_MANAGER, indicating whether the value is a plaintext string, a reference to an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter, or a reference to an AWS Secrets Manager secret.

Specifies the value of an environment variable passed to the action, which can be a static string or a reference to a CodePipeline variable expression (e.g., #{SourceVariables.CommitId}) for dynamic substitution.
Specifies the list of input artifacts for the action, where each artifact's Name property must match the name of an output artifact from a source or previous action in the pipeline.
The name of the artifact that this action consumes as an input, which must match an output artifact from an upstream action in the pipeline.
Specifies the name of the action, which must be unique within its stage and is used to identify the action in the pipeline.
Defines the variable namespace for the action, which is used to expose action variables to subsequent actions in the pipeline.
Specifies the list of artifacts that this action produces as outputs, making them available to downstream actions as input artifacts.
Specifies the list of file paths that the output artifact will contain, allowing you to select only the relevant files produced by the action for use by downstream actions.
The name of the output artifact, which downstream actions reference in their input artifacts to consume the output.
List of variable names that the action exports to the pipeline, allowing downstream actions to reference their values using the #{...} syntax.
The AWS region in which the action is executed; if omitted, the pipeline's region is used.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS CodePipeline assumes when performing the action, overriding the pipeline-level service role for this specific action.
The relative order in which this action runs within its stage, where actions with lower runOrder values execute first.
The number of minutes that AWS CodePipeline waits for the action to complete before considering it failed, overriding the action type's default timeout.

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.stages.before.text: Defines the before-entry conditions for a stage, which are rules that must be satisfied for the stage's actions to begin, enabling entry gates on the pipeline stage.
Specifies the list of conditions that must be satisfied before the stage is allowed to start, enabling entry gates based on variables, actions, or stage-level rules.
Specifies the outcome (e.g., 'ROLLBACK' or 'FAIL') that CodePipeline applies to the stage when the condition's rules are not satisfied.

Lists the rules that CodePipeline evaluates in the stage's before-entry conditions; each rule defines a command (such as a Lambda function or shell command) to run with an associated IAM role, and all rules must succeed for the pipeline to enter the stage.
A list of shell commands that the before-entry rule runs as part of the condition evaluation in a CodePipeline stage.

The configuration map of rule-provider-specific key-value pairs (schema determined by the rule's type) that CodePipeline passes to the rule when evaluating a stage's before-entry condition, controlling whether the stage is allowed to run.
Specifies the names of the artifacts passed to a rule within a stage's before-entry condition, providing the rule with the pipeline artifacts it needs to evaluate whether the stage can proceed.
The name of the artifact that the rule consumes as input, matching an artifact produced by an upstream stage in the pipeline.
The name of a rule in a before-entry condition for a stage, uniquely identifying the rule within that condition in the AWS CodePipeline pipeline.
Specifies the AWS region in which this rule of the stage's before-entry condition is evaluated, enabling the rule to run in a particular regional context.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS CodePipeline assumes to evaluate the rule as part of the before-entry condition of a pipeline stage.
Identifies the rule type by specifying its category, owner, provider, and version, determining which rule engine executes the condition check.
The category of the rule type identifier, which must be 'Rule' for rules used in CodePipeline stage conditions.
Specifies the owner of the rule provider, which can be AWS, a third-party partner, or a custom rule, indicating who authored and maintains the rule used in the stage's before_entry condition.
The provider name of the rule type (e.g., ImageScanningRule, DeploymentWindow) that identifies which rule service evaluates the before-entry condition for the pipeline stage.
Specifies the version of the rule provider invoked by CodePipeline when this condition rule runs, part of the rule type identifier.

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.stages.blocke.text: This is the list of blocker declarations for a pipeline stage, each with a name and a type (the only supported type is 'Schedule'), which act as manual gates that prevent the pipeline from proceeding past the stage until the blocker is removed or unblocked.
Specifies the name of the blocker, a user-defined gate that must be manually acknowledged or cleared before the stage can continue to run.
Specifies the type of a pipeline blocker, which in AWS CodePipeline is set to `Schedule` to define a time-based blocker that pauses the stage until a scheduled time is reached.

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.stages.name.text: The name of the stage, which uniquely identifies it within the pipeline and is used to reference the stage in pipeline configuration and execution.

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.stages.on_fai.text: Configures the failure behavior for the stage, including the condition that triggers the failure handling (e.g., ABORT, RETRY, ROLLBACK) and optional retry settings.

Specifies the list of conditions that must be satisfied for the stage's on-failure handling (such as rollback) to be triggered, where each condition includes a type like 'ExternalTrigger' and its configuration.
Specifies the stage execution result (either FAILED or ABORTED) that triggers the on-failure condition behavior for the stage in AWS CodePipeline.
Specifies the list of rule definitions that AWS CodePipeline evaluates when the stage's on-failure condition is triggered, including each rule's name, rule type ID, and optional configuration.
In an AWS CodePipeline stage's on-failure condition, this field specifies the list of shell commands executed by the rule to evaluate whether the condition is satisfied.

A dynamic map of key-value pairs that provides rule-specific configuration settings to the rule when the stage's on_failure condition is evaluated, where the allowed keys vary by the rule's provider and version (for example, for a Lambda rule the map may include FunctionName and UserParameters).
Lists the artifacts that the rule, defined under a stage's on-failure conditions, receives as input to evaluate whether the failure condition is satisfied.
Specifies the name of an artifact that serves as input to a rule within a stage's on-failure condition, referencing an artifact output from an upstream stage.
The name of the rule in the on-failure condition of a stage, used as a unique identifier for that rule within the condition.
Specifies the AWS Region in which the rule action is executed, allowing the rule provider (e.g., a Lambda function or managed rule resource) to be invoked in that designated regional scope.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS CodePipeline assumes to run the rule defined in the stage's failure condition, which determines when the stage transition fails.
Defines the rule type identifier (category, owner, provider, and version) that determines which AWS CodePipeline rule is invoked in the condition.
The category of the rule type, which must be 'Rule' for CodePipeline rules.
Identifies the owner of the rule type (e.g., AWS or a third-party/custom owner) for a rule used in a stage's on-failure condition, determining which provider's rule implementation is invoked.
The name of the provider that implements the rule, which together with the category, owner, and version identifies the rule type in AWS CodePipeline.
The version of the rule provider (e.g., '1' or '2') that identifies which implementation of the rule to use for this condition rule in the pipeline's on-failure stage.
Determines the pipeline behavior when a stage fails: set to FAILED to stop and fail the pipeline, or ROLLBACK to roll the stage back to its last successful checkpoint.
Specifies the retry configuration for a stage's on-failure behavior, including the retry mode (e.g., ALL_ACTIONS) that determines which failed actions are retried automatically.
Specifies whether retries on a stage failure apply only to failed actions (FAILED_ACTIONS) or to all actions in the stage (ALL_ACTIONS).

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.stages.on_suc.text: Specifies the success conditions for a stage in the pipeline, including a list of conditions and the evaluation rule (ALL or ANY) that determines whether the stage is considered successful before the pipeline proceeds.

Specifies the list of conditions evaluated when a stage completes, where each condition contains rules to be checked and a required result value (such as APPROVED) that determines whether the stage is considered successful and the pipeline proceeds to the next stage.
In a pipeline stage's on-success conditions, this field specifies the outcome (either ROLLBACK or FAIL) that occurs if the condition is not met.

The list of rules that AWS CodePipeline evaluates as part of the stage's on_success condition; each rule defines a command or condition that must be satisfied for the stage to be considered successfully completed.
For a Command-type rule within a stage's onSuccess condition, this list defines the shell commands that the rule executes.
The set of provider-specific configuration parameters for the rule, used by the rule provider to evaluate the stage's on_success condition (e.g., inputs or thresholds for the rule to succeed).
Specifies the artifacts from the stage's action outputs that are passed as inputs to the rule when evaluating the on-success condition.
The name of the artifact that the rule consumes as its input, which must match the artifact name declared by an upstream action's output artifact in the pipeline.
The name of a rule in an on-success condition for a stage in AWS CodePipeline, which identifies the rule and must be unique within the condition's rule list.
Specifies the AWS region in which the rule action for this on-success condition rule is executed, overriding the pipeline's default region.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS CodePipeline assumes to execute the rule defined in the on_success condition of the stage.
The rule type identifier that specifies the category, owner, provider, and version of the rule to evaluate in the success condition.
Specifies the high-level rule category (such as 'Rule' for AWS-managed CodePipeline rules) of the rule type used in the stage success condition.

Identifies the entity that owns the rule type, such as AWS for AWS-provided rules, Custom for custom rules, or a third-party provider, used to uniquely identify the rule within the pipeline's stage conditions.
Specifies the provider (such as 'AWS') of the rule type, identifying the service or partner that implements the rule in the pipeline condition.
Specifies the version of the rule provider (for example, '1') that identifies which iteration of the rule's logic to use when the rule runs.

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.tags.value.text: The value for a tag key attached to the AWS CodePipeline pipeline, used to organize and identify the pipeline for cost allocation and access control.

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.triggers.git_.text: Specifies the Git configuration for a trigger, including the source action name and the pull request and push event settings that determine when the pipeline runs.
Specifies the pull request filter rules for a Git-based source connection that determine which pull request events trigger the pipeline, based on branch and event criteria.
Specifies the branch filter criteria (include/exclude lists of branch names) that determine which pull request events trigger the pipeline.
Specifies the list of branch names to exclude from triggering the pipeline for pull requests, so pull requests from these branches will not start the pipeline.
Specifies the branch names or patterns for which pull requests trigger the pipeline, so that only PRs targeting these branches start an execution.
The pull request events (such as OPEN, UPDATED, or CLOSED) that cause the pipeline to run when they occur on the configured Git repository.
This field specifies a list of glob patterns for file paths that must be changed in a pull request to trigger the pipeline execution.
Specifies a list of file path patterns (glob-style) that, if matched by any changed file in the pull request, exclude the pull request from triggering the pipeline.
Specifies the glob patterns for file paths in the source repository that must be changed for the pull request trigger to invoke the pipeline.
Specifies a list of Git push filters, each defining branch and/or file-path patterns that control which code changes pushed to the connected source repository automatically trigger the pipeline.
Defines the branch names of the source repository that a push must occur on to trigger the pipeline execution, allowing you to limit the push trigger to specific branches.
A list of branch names or patterns that are excluded from triggering the pipeline when a push is made to those branches.
Defines the list of branch name patterns (e.g., 'main' or 'feature/*') that must match for a push event to trigger the pipeline run.
Defines the file-path filter criteria (with include/exclude glob patterns) that determines which changed files in a pushed commit trigger the pipeline.

This field defines a list of glob patterns for file paths that are excluded from push trigger evaluation, meaning changes to files matching these patterns will not start the pipeline even if they match the included patterns.
Specifies the file path patterns that must match for the push event to trigger the pipeline, so the pipeline runs only when commits change files matching any of these patterns.
Defines the inclusion and exclusion criteria for Git tags that are evaluated on push events to determine whether the pipeline should trigger.
A list of git tag names that, when matched on a push event, prevent the pipeline trigger from executing.
Specifies the list of Git tag names that must match the pushed tag in order for the push event to activate this trigger and start the pipeline.
The name of the source action in the pipeline that this trigger watches for Git events.

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.triggers.prov.text: Specifies the type of event source for the pipeline trigger, such as CodeStarSourceConnection for an external Git-based source connection or CloudWatchEvent for an Amazon EventBridge (CloudWatch Events) rule.

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.variables.def.text: The default value for a CodePipeline pipeline variable, which is used when the variable is not provided a value during a pipeline run.

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.variables.des.text: Provides an optional description that explains the purpose of a pipeline-level variable defined in the AWS CodePipeline pipeline.

aws_code_pipeline_pipeline.variables.nam.text: The unique name of the pipeline variable, used to reference the variable in pipeline configuration, actions, and within the execution environment.

aws_code_pipeline_webhook.filters.json_p.text: The JSON path in the event payload that this webhook filter rule uses to determine which events should trigger the pipeline.

aws_code_pipeline_webhook.filters.match_.text: The exact string value that the extracted payload at the filter's JSON path must match for the webhook to trigger the pipeline.

aws_code_pipeline_webhook.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS CodePipeline webhook, which acts as a custom label to identify, organize, and control access to the webhook resource.

aws_code_pipeline_webhook.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag attached to the CodePipeline webhook, providing user-defined metadata that can be used to organize and filter webhook resources.

aws_code_star_connections_connection.tag.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS CodeStar Connections connection, used to categorize and manage the resource.
Specifies the value of a tag attached to the AWS CodeStar Connections connection, which can be used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_code_star_connections_repository_lin.text: Specifies the value of a tag key associated with the AWS CodeStar Connections repository link resource.

aws_code_star_git_hub_repository.code.text: Specifies the S3 bucket, key, and optional object version of a ZIP file containing the source code to be initially committed to the GitHub repository.

aws_code_star_git_hub_repository.code.s3.text: Specifies the S3 bucket and object key (and optionally object version) of the source code archive that AWS CodeStar uses to populate the GitHub repository.
The name of the S3 bucket that contains the source code archive used to populate the GitHub repository.
The S3 object key (file path) of the source code archive in the specified S3 bucket that CodeStar uses to import the GitHub repository.

The object version identifier of the S3 object that contains the source code to be committed to the GitHub repository, used to reference a specific version of the object when multiple versions exist in the bucket.

aws_code_star_git_hub_repository.connect.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS CodeStar Connections connection used to authorize access to the GitHub repository.

aws_code_star_git_hub_repository.enable_.text: Whether to enable GitHub Issues (the repository's issue tracker) for the GitHub repository.

aws_code_star_git_hub_repository.id.text: The unique identifier for the AWS CodeStar GitHub repository, which CloudFormation returns as the GitHub owner and repository name combined with a slash (e.g., `owner/repo`).

aws_code_star_git_hub_repository.is_priv.text: Indicates whether the GitHub repository is private (true) or public (false).

aws_code_star_git_hub_repository.reposit.text: The GitHub personal access token used to authenticate with GitHub so AWS CodeStar can create and manage the repository on your behalf.
The description of the GitHub repository, which is displayed on the repository's main page.
The name of the GitHub repository to create or associate with this resource.
The GitHub user or organization that owns the repository.

aws_code_star_notifications_notification.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the notification rule.
The ARN of the IAM user or role that created the notification rule.
Specifies the level of detail included in the notifications, with BASIC providing only essential event information and FULL providing complete event details.

The list of event type IDs (e.g., codecommit-repository-comments-on-commits or codepipeline-pipeline-stage-execution-failed) that trigger the notification rule, each identifying a specific AWS service event that activates the notification.
The name of the notification rule, which identifies it in the AWS console and API operations.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS resource (such as a CodeBuild project, CodePipeline pipeline, or repository) that the notification rule is associated with.
Determines whether the notification rule is active, with valid values ENABLED and DISABLED (defaulting to ENABLED when omitted).
Tags (key-value pairs) that can be attached to the notification rule to help identify, organize, and manage it within AWS.
The ARN of the SNS topic or the client ID of the AWS Chatbot channel that receives notifications from this notification rule.

The list of targets that receive notifications from the notification rule, where each target specifies the target's address (such as the ARN of an SNS topic or AWS Chatbot configuration) and the target type.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the target (such as an SNS topic) that receives notifications from this notification rule.
Specifies the type of notification target (e.g., SNS for an Amazon SNS topic or AWSChatbotSlack for an AWS Chatbot) that the notification rule sends events to.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.allow_classic_.text: Determines whether the identity pool permits the classic authentication flow for unauthenticated identities, distinct from the enhanced flow; when false, only the enhanced flow is allowed.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.allow_unauthen.text: Indicates whether the identity pool allows unauthenticated identities to authenticate, enabling guest access for users not signed in to an identity provider.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.cognito_events.text: Maps Amazon Cognito event names (such as SyncTrigger) to Lambda function ARNs that invoke when those events occur for the identity pool.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.cognito_identi.text: Defines the list of external identity providers (such as Amazon Cognito user pools, social providers like Facebook/Google, or Amazon) that are enabled for the identity pool, including their client IDs and token-check settings.
The app client ID of the user pool that is configured as an identity provider for the Cognito identity pool.

The provider_name uniquely identifies the external identity provider (e.g., 'graph.facebook.com', 'accounts.google.com', or a Cognito user pool provider name) used in the identity pool's authentication flow.
Specifies whether the identity pool performs a server-side check of the token from the associated Cognito user pool provider, which validates the token with the user pool independently.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.cognito_stream.text: Configures Amazon Cognito event streaming to Amazon Kinesis for the identity pool, including the Kinesis stream name, IAM role ARN, and streaming status.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon Cognito assumes to publish identity pool events to the specified Kinesis stream.
The name of the Amazon Kinesis Firehose delivery stream that Cognito uses to deliver identity pool event data when streaming is enabled.
Indicates whether delivery of stream events from the Cognito identity pool to Amazon Kinesis is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED).

aws_cognito_identity_pool.developer_prov.text: Sets the developer provider name (a custom domain string) used to authenticate users via developer authenticated identities, enabling your backend to exchange its own tokens for AWS credentials through the Cognito Identity Pool.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.id.text: The unique identifier for the identity pool, a region-prefixed UUID string (e.g., 'us-east-1:12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012') assigned by AWS.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.identity_pool_.text: The name of the Amazon Cognito identity pool, which must be unique within the AWS region and account, and is used to identify the pool in the Cognito console and API.
The tag key part of a key-value pair used to label an Amazon Cognito identity pool for resource management, cost tracking, and IAM-based access control.
Specifies the value of a tag attached to the Amazon Cognito identity pool.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.name.text: The name of the Cognito Identity Pool, which either reflects the user-specified name or is automatically generated by AWS when the resource is created without one.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.open_id_connec.text: Specifies the list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) for the OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity providers that are trusted to authenticate users for the identity pool.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.push_sync.text: Defines the push synchronization settings for the identity pool, including the IAM role ARN (RoleArn) and SNS platform application ARNs (SnsPlatformApplicationARNs) that enable sending push notifications to client devices.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.push_sync.appl.text: A list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the SNS platform applications that can be used to send push notifications to devices for Cognito Sync in the identity pool.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.push_sync.role.text: The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon Cognito assumes to send push notifications to the app endpoints configured for the identity pool's push synchronization settings.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.saml_provider_.text: Sets the Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of SAML identity providers that the Cognito identity pool trusts for authenticating users and issuing AWS credentials.

aws_cognito_identity_pool.supported_logi.text: Specifies the mapping of external identity provider names (such as Facebook, Google, or Amazon) to their respective application IDs, enabling those providers as login mechanisms for the Cognito identity pool.

aws_cognito_identity_pool_principal_tag..text: The unique identifier of the Cognito identity pool to which these principal tags are associated.
The name of the identity provider (such as 'Facebook', 'Google', or a custom provider) that this principal tag configuration applies to.
A map of key-value pairs that define the principal tags to attach to the identity pool's principal for the specified identity provider.

Indicates whether to use the default principal tag mappings for the identity provider, causing Cognito to automatically apply its standard tags (such as 'role') instead of the custom principal tags you specify.

aws_cognito_identity_pool_role_attachmen.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Cognito identity pool that this role attachment configuration applies to.
The unique identifier of the Cognito identity pool to which this role attachment configuration applies.

Specifies the mapping of identity providers to role-mapping configurations, determining which IAM role a user authenticated through a given provider is assigned based on token claims or rule-based conditions.
Specifies a mapping of identity pool role types (such as 'authenticated' or 'unauthenticated') to the IAM role ARNs that define the permissions for users in each category.

aws_cognito_log_delivery_configuration.i.text: The unique identifier of the user pool to which this log delivery configuration belongs, acting as the resource's primary identifier.

aws_cognito_log_delivery_configuration.l.text: Specifies the list of log delivery configurations for the user pool, each defining the event source (e.g., userNotification, userAuthEvents), the log level (e.g., ERROR, INFO), and the destination CloudWatch log group to which Amazon Cognito delivers user activity logs.
Specifies the CloudWatch Logs log group (via its ARN) that receives Cognito user pool audit logs for the corresponding event source in the log delivery configuration.
The ARN of the CloudWatch Logs log group where Cognito user pool logs are delivered when CloudWatch Logs is the log destination.

Identifies which event source within the Cognito user pool (userNotification or userAuthEvents) this log configuration applies to, controlling which activity is delivered to the associated CloudWatch log group.
Specifies the Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream destination for a given log type, including the ARN of the delivery stream to which logs are delivered.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that receives the specified user pool log events for this log delivery configuration.
Determines the verbosity of logs (either ERROR or INFO) that are delivered to CloudWatch Logs for a specific event source in the user pool's log delivery configuration.
Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket destination (by bucket ARN) for delivering a particular log level from a Cognito user pool, used within one log configuration entry.
The ARN of the Amazon S3 bucket to which Amazon Cognito user pool logs are delivered for this log configuration.

aws_cognito_log_delivery_configuration.u.text: The ID of the Amazon Cognito user pool to which this log delivery configuration applies.

aws_cognito_managed_login_branding.asset.text: Specifies the list of image assets (such as logos, icons, and email graphics) to associate with the managed login branding, where each asset defines a category, resource identifier, and optional file URI.
Base64-encoded binary data for the brand asset, such as a logo, icon, or favicon, used in the Cognito managed login branding configuration.
Specifies the type of the managed login brand asset, such as FAVICON, LOGO, BACKGROUND, or CSS, which determines where and how the asset is applied to the user pool's managed login pages.
Indicates the display theme (light or dark) for which an asset in the managed login branding is intended, so the appropriate asset variant is served when the login page renders in that color mode.
The file extension (e.g., png, jpg, ico, svg) of a brand asset used in the managed login branding, indicating the image format of the asset's binary content.
The unique identifier for a custom branding asset (such as a logo or icon) within the Cognito managed login branding, used to reference or update that specific asset in subsequent operations.

aws_cognito_managed_login_branding.clien.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Cognito app client to which this managed login branding is applied.

aws_cognito_managed_login_branding.manag.text: The unique identifier assigned by Amazon Cognito to this managed login branding configuration.

aws_cognito_managed_login_branding.retur.text: Indicates whether the API should return the merged branding resources (combination of user pool and client branding settings) after applying managed login branding, rather than only the explicitly provided values.

aws_cognito_managed_login_branding.setti.text: The JSON object containing the customizable branding settings (such as colors, logo, and layout) that are applied to the managed login pages of the associated user pool app client.

aws_cognito_managed_login_branding.use_c.text: Indicates whether to use the preset branding provided by Amazon Cognito for the managed login experience, rather than the custom values you supply for the branding configuration.

aws_cognito_managed_login_branding.user_.text: The ID of the user pool for which managed login branding is configured.

aws_cognito_terms.user_pool_id.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Cognito user pool to which these terms are associated.

aws_cognito_user_pool.account_recovery_s.text: Configures the account recovery methods (such as email verification, SMS, or admin-only) that users can use to regain access to their accounts in the Cognito user pool.
Specifies the ordered list of account recovery mechanisms (like verified email or phone number) with priorities that determine how a user can recover their account in this user pool.
The name of the recovery mechanism, which must be one of `verified_email`, `verified_phone_number`, or `admin_only` and identifies the method (email, phone, or admin) used for user account recovery.
This number determines the order in which the recovery mechanism is attempted for user account recovery, with lower values having higher precedence and being tried first.

aws_cognito_user_pool.admin_create_user_.text: Configuration for the admin create user flow, controlling whether only administrators can create users and customizing the invitation message sent to new users.
When true, only administrators are allowed to create user accounts in the user pool, disabling self-registration by end users.
Configures the email subject, email body, and SMS body used in the invitation message sent to a new user when an administrator creates that user's account.

Specifies the body of the email message that is sent as an invitation to a new user when an administrator creates the user in the user pool, allowing placeholders such as {username} and {####} for the temporary password/verification code.
The subject line for the email invitation message sent to a newly created user when an administrator creates the user account in the user pool.
The SMS message body that is sent to a user when an admin creates their account, containing placeholders for the username and the temporary password.
Sets the number of days that a user account created by an administrator remains valid without any sign-in activity, after which it expires and the user must reset their password.

aws_cognito_user_pool.alias_attributes.text: Specifies the list of user attributes (such as email, phone_number, or preferred_username) that can be used as alternate sign-in aliases for the user pool.

aws_cognito_user_pool.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Cognito user pool, typically in the form arn:aws:cognito-idp:region:account-id:userpool/user-pool-id.

aws_cognito_user_pool.auto_verified_attr.text: Specifies the list of user attributes (such as email or phone_number) that Cognito automatically attempts to verify during user sign-up, marking them as verified when the verification process succeeds.

aws_cognito_user_pool.deletion_protectio.text: Indicates whether deletion protection is enabled for the user pool, with allowed values of ACTIVE or INACTIVE to prevent accidental deletion.

aws_cognito_user_pool.device_configurati.text: Specifies device configuration settings for the user pool, determining whether a new device must pass a challenge and whether devices are remembered only when the user explicitly chooses to keep them signed in.
If true, a challenge is required when a user attempts to sign in from a device that has not been previously recognized, as part of the user pool's device tracking and remembered device settings.
When true, a user's device is remembered only if the user explicitly chooses to remember it during sign-in; when false, devices are automatically remembered regardless of user prompt.

aws_cognito_user_pool.email_authenticati.text: Specifies the email message body that Amazon Cognito sends to users when they need to authenticate using a one-time passcode (OTP) delivered to their email address, supporting the {####} placeholder for the actual code.
Specifies the subject line of the email message that Amazon Cognito sends when users use email as an authentication factor (email MFA).

aws_cognito_user_pool.email_configuratio.text: Configures the email delivery settings for the user pool, specifying the source ARN, reply-to address, and delivery method used for messages such as verification codes and account notifications.
The name of the Amazon SES configuration set to use when sending emails from the user pool.
Specifies which email account Amazon Cognito uses to send emails, either Cognito's default account ('COGNITO_DEFAULT') or a developer-configured Amazon SES account ('DEVELOPER').
The sender email address that Amazon Cognito uses in the 'From' field of emails it sends to users, which must be verified in Amazon Simple Email Service (SES).
The email address that recipients of Cognito notification emails can reply to, configured in the email configuration of the user pool.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a verified email address in Amazon SES that Cognito uses as the sender for user pool emails.

aws_cognito_user_pool.email_verification.text: The custom email message that AWS Cognito sends to users to verify their email address, where you can include the verification code placeholder {####}.
The subject line of the email that is sent to users when they need to verify their email address.

aws_cognito_user_pool.enabled_mfas.text: A list of the multi-factor authentication (MFA) methods enabled for the Cognito user pool, where each item is either 'SMS_MFA' or 'SOFTWARE_TOKEN_MFA'.

aws_cognito_user_pool.issuer_configurati.text: Specifies the issuer configuration for the user pool, which defines the custom issuer ID and issuer URL that Cognito uses for tokens.

The type field in issuer_configuration selects whether the user pool issues tokens with a custom issuer URL (provided via the associated issuer field) or uses the default Cognito issuer, thereby controlling the issuer claim.

aws_cognito_user_pool.key_configuration.text: Defines the AWS KMS key configurations used for encrypting custom email and SMS sender messages in the Cognito user pool, specifying the KMS key ID and provider for each custom sender.

aws_cognito_user_pool.key_configuration..text: Defines the cryptographic key type (RSA or ECC) used for signing the user pool's JSON Web Tokens (JWTs).
The ARN of an AWS KMS customer-managed key that Amazon Cognito uses to encrypt user pool data at rest instead of the default AWS-owned encryption key.

aws_cognito_user_pool.lambda_config.text: Configures AWS Lambda triggers for user pool workflows, allowing you to specify Lambda function ARNs for events such as pre-signup, post-confirmation, and custom message, among others.

aws_cognito_user_pool.lambda_config.crea.text: The ARN of the Lambda function invoked when Cognito needs to create a custom authentication challenge as part of the user pool's custom authentication flow.

aws_cognito_user_pool.lambda_config.cust.text: Configuration for a custom email sender Lambda trigger, specifying the ARN and version of the Lambda function that handles sending email notifications for the user pool.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function that Cognito invokes to send custom email messages for the user pool.
The version of the AWS Lambda function to invoke for custom email sending, which must be set to 'V1_0'.
ARN of the Lambda function Amazon Cognito invokes to customize email and SMS messages for user verification, invitation, and account confirmation.
The configuration for a custom SMS sender Lambda trigger, specifying the Lambda function ARN and version used to send SMS messages for user verification and account recovery.
The ARN of the Lambda function invoked by Amazon Cognito for custom SMS sender triggers to send SMS messages.
Specifies the version of the AWS Lambda function to invoke for the custom SMS sender trigger, where 'V1_0' is the only currently supported value.

aws_cognito_user_pool.lambda_config.defi.text: The ARN of the Lambda function invoked for the Define Auth Challenge trigger, which determines whether a custom authentication challenge is required and defines the challenge presented to the user.

aws_cognito_user_pool.lambda_config.kmsk.text: The KMS key ID to use for encrypting the Lambda environment variables of the user pool's Lambda trigger functions.

aws_cognito_user_pool.lambda_config.post.text: The ARN of a Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes after a user is authenticated, enabling custom post-authentication logic such as logging or modifying the authentication response.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function that Amazon Cognito triggers after a user confirms their account, enabling custom post-confirmation workflows.

aws_cognito_user_pool.lambda_config.pre_.text: The ARN of the Lambda function invoked by the pre-authentication trigger for the user pool.
The ARN of an AWS Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes as a pre sign-up trigger, allowing you to customize or validate the sign-up flow before the user is created.
The ARN of an AWS Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes before generating identity and access tokens, allowing you to customize token claims.
Specifies the ARN and version of the Lambda function to invoke on the pre token generation trigger, enabling customization of access token and ID token claims.

Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes for the pre token generation trigger, allowing customization of identity and access token claims before issuance.
Specifies the version of the pre token generation Lambda trigger to use, with 'V2_0' enabling the newer behavior that supports adding or modifying claims in the token.

aws_cognito_user_pool.lambda_config.user.text: The ARN of an AWS Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes to migrate a user from an external user directory into the user pool when the user attempts to sign in for the first time.

aws_cognito_user_pool.lambda_config.veri.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a Lambda function that AWS Cognito invokes to verify a user's response to a custom auth challenge, enabling custom verification logic during authentication.

aws_cognito_user_pool.mfa_configuration.text: Specifies whether multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled for the user pool, with valid values 'OFF', 'ON', or 'OPTIONAL'.

aws_cognito_user_pool.policies.text: Configures the password policy for the user pool, specifying rules for password length, required character types, and temporary password validity duration.

aws_cognito_user_pool.policies.password_.text: Specifies the password policy for the user pool, including rules for minimum length, required character types (uppercase, lowercase, numbers, symbols), and temporary password validity, which must be satisfied by users when they set or change their passwords.
Specifies the minimum number of characters a user password must contain in the Cognito user pool, enforcing a length requirement with a default of 8 characters.
Specifies the number of previous passwords that Amazon Cognito remembers for each user, preventing the reuse of those passwords when a user changes their password.
Specifies whether user passwords must contain at least one lowercase letter, with true enforcing the requirement and false making it optional.
A Boolean that specifies whether passwords in the user pool must include at least one numeric character (0-9) when users set or change their password.
Specifies whether passwords in the user pool must contain at least one symbol (non-alphanumeric character).
Specifies whether passwords in the user pool must contain at least one uppercase letter (A-Z).
The number of days a temporary password generated for a user (e.g., by an admin or during a password reset) remains valid before the user must change it.

aws_cognito_user_pool.policies.sign_in_p.text: Defines the sign-in policy for the Cognito user pool, which dictates the allowed sign-in methods (such as username, email, or phone number) and whether sign-in aliases are enabled.
Specifies the list of authentication factors (such as PASSWORD, EMAIL_OTP, SMS_OTP, or WEB_AUTHN) that are allowed as the first step in the sign-in flow for the user pool.

aws_cognito_user_pool.provider_name.text: ProviderName is a read-only attribute that returns the name of the Amazon Cognito user pool, which identifies the user pool as the provider.

aws_cognito_user_pool.provider_url.text: The AWS-created URL for the user pool, typically formatted as https://cognito-idp.<region>.amazonaws.com/<pool_id>, which clients use to make authentication requests to this user pool.

aws_cognito_user_pool.schema.text: Specifies the list of schema attributes (standard and custom) for the user pool, including each attribute's data type, whether it is required or mutable, and any validation constraints.

aws_cognito_user_pool.schema.attribute_d.text: Specifies the data type of the user pool schema attribute, which must be one of String, Number, DateTime, or Boolean and determines how the attribute's value is stored and validated.

aws_cognito_user_pool.schema.developer_o.text: Indicates whether the schema attribute is a developer-only custom attribute that cannot be modified by end users and is only settable through the Cognito admin/developer APIs.

aws_cognito_user_pool.schema.mutable.text: This boolean property specifies whether the user pool schema attribute can be changed after the user profile is created.

aws_cognito_user_pool.schema.name.text: Specifies the name of the user pool schema attribute, such as a built-in or custom attribute like 'email' or 'my_custom_attr'.

aws_cognito_user_pool.schema.number_attr.text: Specifies the minimum and maximum numeric values allowed for a schema attribute of type Number in the user pool schema.
Sets the inclusive maximum numeric value allowed for a custom Number-type schema attribute in the user pool, so that submitted values above this limit are rejected.
Defines the lower bound for the numeric value of a number-type custom attribute in the user pool's schema.

aws_cognito_user_pool.schema.required.text: Specifies whether this user pool schema attribute is required for users signing up.

aws_cognito_user_pool.schema.string_attr.text: Configures the minimum and maximum character length limits for a string attribute in the user pool's schema definition.
Maximum number of characters allowed in a string attribute value, used to define the upper bound for string schema attributes in the user pool.
The minimum number of characters that a string attribute value must contain, enforced for the Cognito user pool schema attribute.

aws_cognito_user_pool.sms_authentication.text: The customizable SMS message text that Amazon Cognito sends to users for authentication (such as MFA code delivery), which must include the {####} placeholder for the verification code.

aws_cognito_user_pool.sms_configuration.text: Configures the Amazon SNS settings used by the user pool to send SMS messages for user verification and authentication, including the SNS caller ARN and external ID required for Cognito to publish SMS messages.

aws_cognito_user_pool.sms_configuration..text: The external ID that AWS Cognito includes when it assumes the IAM role for sending SMS messages, preventing confused-deputy attacks and must match the external ID on the role's trust policy.

An arbitrary string that must match the `sts:ExternalId` condition in the IAM role's trust policy that Cognito assumes to send SMS messages via Amazon SNS, providing a security control against the confused deputy problem.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon Cognito assumes to send SMS messages via Amazon SNS for the user pool.
Specifies the AWS Region in which Amazon SNS is used for sending SMS messages from the user pool.

aws_cognito_user_pool.sms_verification_m.text: The SMS message template sent to users when they verify their phone number, which can include the verification code placeholder {####}.

aws_cognito_user_pool.user_attribute_upd.text: Defines the user pool's attribute update settings, specifically the list of user attributes that require verification before a user can update them.

Specifies which user attributes (such as email or phone_number) require verification before a user can update them in the Cognito user pool, and if any attribute is listed, that attribute's change is blocked until the new value is verified via a verification code or token.

aws_cognito_user_pool.user_pool_add_ons.text: Configures the advanced security features for the user pool, specifically the advanced security mode (e.g., ENFORCED, AUDIT, or OFF) for threat protection.

aws_cognito_user_pool.user_pool_add_ons..text: Specifies additional authentication flows, such as custom auth, to be included in the advanced security threat protection settings for the user pool.
Determines the AWS Cognito Advanced Security mode (AUDIT or ENFORCED) for custom authentication flows, overriding the pool-level advanced security mode.
Specifies the advanced security mode for the user pool, which can be OFF, AUDIT, or ENFORCED, enabling features like compromised credential detection and account takeover protection.

aws_cognito_user_pool.user_pool_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the user pool.

aws_cognito_user_pool.user_pool_name.text: Specifies a unique name for the user pool within the AWS region, which may contain letters, numbers, and underscores.

aws_cognito_user_pool.user_pool_tags.text: The user_pool_tags field specifies a map of key-value tags to attach to the Cognito user pool for metadata, cost allocation, and resource management.

aws_cognito_user_pool.user_pool_tier.text: Specifies the feature tier of the Cognito user pool (Lite, Standard, or Enterprise), which determines the available features and pricing for the pool.

aws_cognito_user_pool.username_attribute.text: Defines the list of user attributes (such as email or phone number) that can be used as the username for signing in to the user pool.

aws_cognito_user_pool.username_configura.text: A configuration object that controls whether usernames are case-sensitive (via the CaseSensitive property) for the user pool.
Determines whether usernames in the user pool are case-sensitive, meaning 'User' and 'user' would be considered distinct when true, and the same when false.

aws_cognito_user_pool.verification_messa.text: Configures the templates for verification messages (email/SMS) sent to users, such as account verification or password reset, including subject, body, and the default email delivery method.
Specifies whether the default email verification message uses a confirmation link or a confirmation code, with valid values CONFIRM_WITH_LINK or CONFIRM_WITH_CODE.
Specifies the body of the email message sent to users for verification purposes (such as account or email/phone verification), which can include the verification code placeholder {####}.
The custom email message body, including a placeholder for the verification link, that Amazon Cognito sends to users when email verification uses a link instead of a code.
The subject line used in the email verification message sent to users when their email address is being verified.
The subject line for the verification email sent to users when they verify their email address or phone number using a link (as opposed to a verification code).
The SMS message content sent to users for verification, which can include the {####} placeholder that is replaced with the actual verification code.

aws_cognito_user_pool.web_authn_factor_c.text: Configures WebAuthn as a second factor for the user pool, specifying the relying party ID, relying party name, user verification preference, and timeout for passwordless sign-in with security keys.

aws_cognito_user_pool.web_authn_relying_.text: The Relying Party ID for WebAuthn passkey authentication, which specifies the domain (e.g., 'example.com') that the user pool associates with registered passkeys.

aws_cognito_user_pool.web_authn_user_ver.text: Specifies the user verification requirement for WebAuthn passkeys in the user pool, determining whether a user must complete an additional verification step (such as biometric or PIN) when using a passkey, with allowed values 'required', 'preferred', or 'discouraged'.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.access_toke.text: The validity duration, in minutes, for access tokens issued by this Cognito user pool client, after which they expire.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.allowed_oau.text: The list of allowed OAuth flows (such as code, implicit, or client_credentials) for the user pool client, which determines how tokens can be obtained via the hosted UI or API.

This boolean enables the OAuth 2.0 authorization flows (such as authorization code, implicit, and client credentials) for this user pool client, allowing it to be used with the hosted UI and OAuth tokens.

Defines the list of OAuth 2.0 scopes that the user pool client is allowed to request (e.g., email, phone, openid, profile, or custom scopes), controlling the access scope granted during the authorization code or implicit OAuth flows.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.analytics_c.text: Configures the Amazon Pinpoint analytics settings for the user pool client, including the Pinpoint application ID, IAM role ARN, external ID, and whether user data is shared, to enable tracking of user events.
The ARN of the Amazon Pinpoint project or Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream used by the user pool client's analytics configuration to send user activity data.
The Amazon Pinpoint application ID that receives user pool client analytics data.
Specifies the external ID that Amazon Cognito uses when it assumes the IAM role defined in the analytics configuration to send user activity data to the analytics application.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon Cognito assumes to publish analytics events to Amazon Pinpoint for this user pool client.
Indicates whether user data from the user pool client is shared with the configured Amazon Pinpoint analytics provider.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.auth_sessio.text: The number of minutes (1-15) that an authentication session remains valid before expiring, controlling how long a user can complete the interactive sign-in flow without restarting.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.callback_ur.text: List of allowed callback URLs for the Cognito user pool client's OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoints, which Cognito redirects to after authentication.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.client_id.text: The unique identifier (ID) of the user pool client, assigned by Amazon Cognito when the client is created.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.client_name.text: The name of the user pool client, used to identify the client application in the AWS Management Console and in API responses.
