aws_cognito_user_pool_client.client_secr.text: The client secret that this app client uses to authenticate with the Cognito User Pool service, generated by Cognito and exposed as a read-only attribute after creation.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.default_red.text: The URI that the user is redirected to after sign-in or sign-out if no redirect_uri parameter is supplied in the authorization request.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.enable_prop.text: Indicates whether the user pool client propagates additional user context data (such as device fingerprints) to the user pool for advanced security risk evaluation.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.enable_toke.text: Enable token revocation for the user pool client, allowing Cognito to revoke refresh tokens (e.g., after a password change or user disablement) so they can no longer be used.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.explicit_au.text: Lists the authentication flows explicitly enabled for this user pool client (e.g., ALLOW_USER_SRP_AUTH, ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH, ALLOW_CUSTOM_AUTH, ALLOW_ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH), overriding the default set of allowed flows for the app client.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.generate_se.text: Indicates whether the app client will have a generated client secret, used for confidential clients to authenticate to the token endpoint.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.id_token_va.text: The number of minutes that an ID token issued by the user pool client remains valid before it expires.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.logout_urls.text: Specifies the list of allowed logout redirect URIs to which Cognito may redirect users after signing out from the user pool client.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.name.text: This attribute returns the name of the Cognito user pool application client, as originally specified in the ClientName parameter during client creation.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.prevent_use.text: Indicates whether the user pool client prevents user enumeration by returning a generic error when a user does not exist, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'LEGACY'.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.read_attrib.text: Specifies the user pool attributes that the app client can read from the user's profile.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.refresh_tok.text: Determines whether refresh token rotation is enabled for the user pool client, with valid values being 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.

Sets the retry grace period, in seconds, during which an old refresh token remains valid after it has been rotated for a new one, allowing clients that still present the previous token to successfully obtain new tokens before the old token is revoked.
The number of days that a refresh token remains valid before the user must re-authenticate.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.supported_i.text: A list of identity provider names (e.g., COGNITO, Facebook, Google, LoginWithAmazon, or custom SAML/OIDC providers) that are enabled for this app client, controlling which IdPs can be used for sign-in.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.token_valid.text: Specifies the time units (such as seconds, minutes, hours, or days) for the expiration of access, ID, and refresh tokens issued by the user pool client, enabling separate validity durations for each token type.
Specifies the time unit (e.g., seconds, minutes, hours, or days) used to interpret the numeric value of the access token validity period for the Cognito user pool client.
Specifies the unit of time (e.g., seconds, minutes, hours, days) used for the ID token's validity period in the user pool client.
Specifies the time unit (e.g., seconds, minutes, hours, or days) used for the refresh token's validity period in the user pool client.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.user_pool_i.text: The unique ID of the Amazon Cognito user pool to which this app client belongs, used to link the client configuration to its parent pool.

aws_cognito_user_pool_client.write_attri.text: Specifies the list of user pool attributes that the app client is allowed to update (write) for users, controlling which profile fields can be modified through the client.

aws_cognito_user_pool_domain.cloud_front.text: The Amazon CloudFront distribution associated with the user pool domain, used to serve traffic for the custom domain.

aws_cognito_user_pool_domain.custom_doma.text: Specifies the configuration for a custom domain, including the ARN of the ACM certificate to use for HTTPS.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate used for the custom domain of the Cognito user pool domain.

Sets the TLS security policy for the CloudFront distribution backing the custom domain, determining the minimum TLS version (e.g., TLS_1_0, TLS_1_2) required for HTTPS connections to the user pool domain.

aws_cognito_user_pool_domain.domain.text: The domain (either a custom domain or a prefix) that will be assigned to the user pool to serve the hosted UI, API, and authentication endpoints.

aws_cognito_user_pool_domain.managed_log.text: Specify the version of the managed login experience for the user pool domain, with 1 representing the original hosted UI and 2 representing the new managed login experience.

aws_cognito_user_pool_domain.routing.fai.text: Specifies the secondary AWS region to which the user pool domain routes traffic during failover, ensuring availability if the primary region fails.

aws_cognito_user_pool_domain.user_pool_i.text: The ID of the Amazon Cognito user pool to associate with the custom domain or Amazon Cognito-hosted domain.

aws_cognito_user_pool_group.description.text: A description of the user pool group.

aws_cognito_user_pool_group.group_name.text: The name of the Cognito user pool group, which serves as the group's unique identifier within the user pool and is referenced in IAM policies and app client authentication flows.

aws_cognito_user_pool_group.precedence.text: Defines the numerical precedence of the group, which determines the IAM role that Cognito applies when a user belongs to multiple groups, with lower numbers having higher priority.

aws_cognito_user_pool_group.role_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that is associated with the user pool group and applied to its users.

aws_cognito_user_pool_group.user_pool_id.text: The ID of the Cognito user pool that this group belongs to.

aws_cognito_user_pool_identity_provider..text: Maps user pool attribute names to the corresponding attribute names from the external identity provider (IdP) for this user pool identity provider.
Specifies a list of custom identifiers for the identity provider that are included in the user's identities claim, enabling your application to distinguish which IdP a user used to sign in.

A map of provider-specific configuration settings (e.g., client_id, client_secret, and authorize_scopes for OIDC, or MetadataURL for SAML) that define how the identity provider integrates with the user pool.
The name of the identity provider (e.g., Google, Facebook, LoginWithAmazon, or a custom OIDC/SAML provider name) that uniquely identifies this provider within the user pool.
The identity provider type, such as 'Facebook', 'Google', 'LoginWithAmazon', 'SignInWithApple', 'OIDC', or 'SAML'.
The unique identifier of the Amazon Cognito user pool to which this identity provider configuration is attached.

aws_cognito_user_pool_regional_configura.text: Configures the email delivery settings for the Cognito user pool, including the sender address, reply-to address, and the Amazon SES configuration set or source ARN used to send emails.
Specifies the name of the Amazon SES configuration set that Amazon Cognito uses when sending email messages for the user pool's email configuration.
Specifies whether Cognito uses its default email account (COGNITO_DEFAULT) or a developer-provided Amazon SES account (DEVELOPER) to send emails for this regional user pool configuration.
The sender email address that Amazon Cognito uses to send email notifications from the user pool, as part of the attached email configuration.
The email address that Amazon Cognito uses as the reply-to address for emails sent to users from the user pool.
The ARN of a verified email address or domain in Amazon SES that Amazon Cognito uses as the sender for emails sent from the user pool's email configuration.
Specifies the ARN of the Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes to create an authentication challenge during custom authentication flows.
Configures a custom email sender Lambda function for the Cognito user pool, using the specified Lambda ARN and version to handle outgoing email messages instead of Cognito's default email service.
The ARN of the Lambda function that Cognito invokes as the custom email sender to send email messages for the user pool.
Specifies the version (V1_0 or V2_0) of the AWS Lambda function used as the custom email sender in the user pool's email configuration.
The ARN of the Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes for the CustomMessage trigger, which customizes verification codes and welcome messages sent to users.
Configures a custom AWS Lambda function to be used as the SMS sender for this Cognito User Pool regional configuration, specifying the Lambda function's ARN and version.
The ARN of the Lambda function that Cognito invokes to send custom SMS messages when using the CustomSMSSender Lambda trigger for the user pool's Lambda configuration.
The version qualifier (e.g., V1_0) of the Lambda function used as the custom SMS sender for the user pool's SMS configuration.
The ARN of an AWS Lambda function that serves as the DefineAuthChallenge trigger, enabling custom authentication challenge definition for the user pool.

The ARN of the Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes for the inbound federation trigger in the regional configuration, used to process or customize claims for federated identity provider sign-ins.
Specifies the KMS key ID or ARN that Amazon Cognito uses to encrypt the code delivery messages to users, within the lambda_config block of this regional configuration attachment.
The ARN of a Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes after a user is successfully authenticated, enabling custom logic like auditing or post-login workflows.
The ARN of a Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes after a user confirms their account, used to run custom post-confirmation logic such as creating a user profile or sending a welcome message.
The ARN of an AWS Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes before user authentication, allowing you to customize the authentication flow.
The ARN of an AWS Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes before sign-up registration, used to customize the pre-sign-up trigger behavior.
The ARN of the Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes for the pre-token generation trigger, allowing customization of the token before it is issued during authentication.
Configuration for the pre token generation Lambda trigger, specifying the ARN and version of the Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes before generating tokens for authentication.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes before generating the ID token or access token, allowing you to customize claims or add/remove attributes.
Specifies the version (e.g., V1_0 or V2_0) of the Lambda function used for the pre-token generation trigger, which determines the event payload format and expected behavior.
The ARN of the Lambda function that is invoked for the Cognito user migration trigger, which allows existing users to be migrated into the user pool when they sign in.
The ARN of the Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes to verify a user's answer to a custom authentication challenge for the user pool region configuration.
Specifies the SMS message configuration (e.g., SNS caller ARN and external ID) used by the user pool to send SMS verification codes and MFA messages.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon Cognito assumes to send SMS messages through Amazon SNS for this regional user pool configuration.
Name of the Amazon SNS configuration set used to track and manage SMS messages sent by the user pool for this regional configuration, enabling message delivery status and event logging.

The `in_entity_id` field specifies the India-specific DLT entity ID that is passed as the `AWS.SNS.SMS.EntityId` SMS attribute when Cognito sends SMS messages for this user pool's regional configuration, satisfying TRAI compliance for Indian phone numbers.
Specifies the SMS origination identity (e.g., a sender ID or origination number) used by this regional SMS configuration when Cognito sends SMS messages for the associated user pool.
The external ID to include in the IAM role trust policy that authorizes Amazon Cognito to send SMS messages through Amazon SNS, preventing the confused deputy problem.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon Cognito assumes to send SMS messages through Amazon SNS for this user pool's regional SMS configuration.
The AWS region where Amazon SNS is configured to send SMS messages for the user pool's SMS configuration.
A map of key-value tags to assign to the Amazon Cognito user pool associated with this regional configuration attachment.

aws_cognito_user_pool_replica.region_nam.text: Specifies the AWS region where the Cognito user pool replica is created, which must be different from the primary pool's region.

aws_cognito_user_pool_replica.user_pool_.text: The ID of the original user pool in the primary region that this replica is created from, which is required to set up the cross-region replica.
Sets the initial tags on the user pool replica at creation, which are key-value pairs that help manage, identify, and categorize the resource.

aws_cognito_user_pool_resource_server.id.text: The unique identifier for the resource server, typically a URI (e.g., https://my-api.example.com), used by clients to reference the resource server and its scopes in OAuth flows.

aws_cognito_user_pool_resource_server.na.text: A friendly name for the resource server, used to identify it within the user pool.

aws_cognito_user_pool_resource_server.sc.text: Defines the OAuth 2.0 scopes that this resource server exposes to client apps, each scope specifying a name and a description.
A human-readable description that explains the purpose or permissions of the OAuth 2.0 scope defined for the user pool resource server.
The scope_name defines the unique name of the OAuth 2.0 scope that clients can request for authorization from this resource server.

aws_cognito_user_pool_resource_server.us.text: The unique ID of the user pool that this resource server is associated with.

aws_cognito_user_pool_risk_configuration.text: Configures the account takeover risk configuration for a user pool, including the actions (e.g., block, MFA) to take for low, medium, and high risk events and the notification settings.
Defines the response actions (notify and event action) to take for high, medium, and low risk sign-in attempts in the account takeover risk configuration.
Defines the action to take for high-risk sign-in attempts, including whether to send notifications and whether to block the sign-in for the user pool.
Specifies whether to block or allow the authentication attempt when the risk level for account takeover is high, accepting values such as 'BLOCK' or 'NO_ACTION'.
Whether Amazon Cognito sends a notification to the user when the high-risk account takeover action is triggered.
Configures how Amazon Cognito responds to low-risk account takeover events, specifying the event action (such as allowing or blocking) and whether to send notification alerts.
When a sign-in attempt is classified as low-risk, this required string specifies which action the user pool should take, with valid values being BLOCK, MFA_IF_CONFIGURED, MFA_REQUIRED, and NO_ACTION.
Whether to send a notification to the user when the low-risk account takeover action is triggered.
Determines the AWS Cognito action (block, require MFA, or no action) and whether to notify users when the account takeover risk level is medium.

Specifies the action that Amazon Cognito takes when a sign-in attempt is assessed as a medium-risk event, such as blocking the sign-in, requiring multi-factor authentication if it is configured, requiring MFA, or taking no action.
Whether to send a notification to the user when a medium-risk account takeover event is detected.

This object specifies the notification settings for account takeover risk responses, including the source email address, reply-to address, and the email templates (NoActionEmail, MfaEmail, BlockEmail) sent to users when those risk actions are triggered.
Configuration for the email notification sent when account takeover risk triggers a block action, defining the email subject and body for that notification.
The HTML body of the email notification sent to users when their account is blocked due to account takeover risk.
The subject line of the email notification sent to the user when their account is blocked due to a suspected account takeover.
The body text of the email notification sent to users when an account takeover attempt is blocked, as part of the account takeover risk configuration's notify settings.
Sets the sender email address ('From' header) for the account-takeover risk notification emails, which must be an Amazon SES verified address or belong to your Amazon Cognito domain.

Configures the email notification sent to the user when adaptive authentication requires multi-factor authentication, specifying the email subject and HTML/plain-text body via the NotifyEmailType structure.
The HTML body of the email notification sent to the user when an MFA challenge is triggered as part of the account takeover risk configuration.
The subject line of the email sent to users when multi-factor authentication is required as part of the account takeover risk notification.
The plain-text body of the email message sent to the user when multi-factor authentication (MFA) is triggered by the account takeover risk configuration.
Configures the email message that is sent to users when no action is taken on an account takeover risk assessment.

Specifies the HTML body of the email that Amazon Cognito sends to the user when the account takeover risk assessment determines no action is required, as part of the no-action email notification configuration.
In the account takeover risk configuration's notification settings, this field specifies the subject line of the email sent to the user when no action is taken on a detected risk.
The plain-text body of the email notification sent to the user when a risk assessment results in no action being taken.
Specifies the email address that Cognito uses as the reply-to address in the account takeover risk notification emails.
The ARN of the Amazon SES identity or Amazon SNS topic used as the sender source for account takeover notifications in the Cognito user pool risk configuration.
The app client ID of the Amazon Cognito user pool client to which this risk configuration is attached.

This object configures AWS Cognito's compromised credentials risk detection settings, specifying the event types to monitor (e.g., sign-in, sign-up) and the automatic action (block or no action) to take when a compromised credential event is detected.
Specifies the action to take when compromised credentials are detected, such as blocking the sign-in or allowing it with no action.
Specifies the action to take when a compromised credentials risk is detected, with allowed values such as BLOCK or NO_ACTION.
Specifies the event types (such as SIGN_IN, PASSWORD_CHANGE, or SIGN_UP) to which the compromised credentials risk configuration applies.
Configures risk exceptions by providing lists of IP address ranges that are either always blocked or always allowed to bypass risk-based authentication checks for the user pool client.
Specifies a list of IP address ranges in CIDR notation that are always blocked for authentication in AWS Cognito, regardless of the assessed risk level.
Specifies the list of IP address ranges for which Amazon Cognito will skip (exempt from) the risk-based authentication rules for this user pool client.
The unique ID of the Amazon Cognito user pool to which this risk configuration is attached.

aws_cognito_user_pool_uicustomization_at.text: The unique ID of the user pool app client to which this UI customization is attached.
The CSS string that defines the custom styling for the user pool's hosted UI pages.
The user_pool_id specifies the unique identifier of the Amazon Cognito User Pool where the UI customization will be applied.

aws_cognito_user_pool_user.client_metada.text: A map of custom key-value pairs that are passed to AWS Lambda triggers (such as PreSignUp, PostConfirmation, etc.) when a user is created in the Cognito user pool.

aws_cognito_user_pool_user.desired_deliv.text: Specifies the delivery channels (email, SMS, or both) through which the newly created Cognito user receives the temporary password and invitation to set their password.

aws_cognito_user_pool_user.force_alias_c.text: If set to true, this property allows the user to be created even when the specified username or an alias (such as email or phone number) already exists in the user pool, suppressing the error that would otherwise occur.

aws_cognito_user_pool_user.message_actio.text: When creating a user in the Cognito user pool, this optional value controls the invitation message behavior: 'RESEND' resends the invitation message, while 'SUPPRESS' suppresses it.

aws_cognito_user_pool_user.user_attribut.text: Specifies the custom attributes for the user, where each attribute provides a name and value, used to set user information during user creation in the Cognito user pool.
Specifies the name of a user attribute (e.g., 'email', 'phone_number', or a custom attribute prefixed with 'custom:') for a user in an Amazon Cognito user pool.
The actual value for a user pool user attribute (e.g., an email address or phone number), paired with the attribute's Name in the same UserAttributes entry.

aws_cognito_user_pool_user.user_pool_id.text: The ID of the Cognito User Pool in which the user is created.

aws_cognito_user_pool_user.username.text: Specifies the username for the user in the Cognito user pool, which can be an email address, phone number, or custom string used for sign-in.

aws_cognito_user_pool_user.validation_da.text: Validation data (key-value pairs) provided by the caller to validate the user's attributes during user creation, which is passed to pre-sign-up Lambda triggers for custom validation and is not stored as persistent user attributes.
The name of a temporary custom attribute included in the validation data for the user pool user, which is passed to the pre sign-up Lambda trigger for validation and then discarded.
The value of a name-value pair in the validation data for the user, such as an email address or phone number, used to temporarily verify ownership during user creation.

aws_cognito_user_pool_user_to_group_atta.text: The name of the Cognito user pool group to which the user is attached.
The unique ID of the Cognito user pool that contains the group and user to be attached.
The username of the Cognito user to attach to the specified group.

aws_comprehend_document_classifier.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the document classifier in Amazon Comprehend.

aws_comprehend_document_classifier.data_.text: The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon Comprehend assumes to access the training documents in the S3 bucket specified as the input data source for the document classifier.

aws_comprehend_document_classifier.docum.text: The unique name of the document classifier, which identifies it within your AWS account and region.

aws_comprehend_document_classifier.input.text: Specifies the S3 location and format of the training data (documents and labels) used to train the document classifier, including the S3 URI, data format, and optional test data location.
Specifies the augmented manifest files from Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth that provide labeled training data for the document classifier.
Lists the attribute names (JSON keys) in each augmented manifest line that contain the document text and, optionally, the class label used as training data for the document classifier.
Specifies the S3 URI of the augmented manifest file that contains the labeled documents used to train the document classifier.
The split of the augmented manifest data set, which determines whether the documents are used for training or testing the document classifier.
Specifies the format of the training data for the document classifier, either COMPREHEND_CSV (default) for a CSV file or AUGMENTED_MANIFEST for an augmented manifest file.
Specifies the Amazon Textract document reader settings (document read action, read mode, and feature types) used to extract text from input PDF or Word documents for the document classifier.

Specifies the Amazon Textract document reading action to apply to input documents, either TEXTRACT_DETECT_DOCUMENT_TEXT for text extraction or TEXTRACT_ANALYZE_DOCUMENT for extraction including forms and tables.

Specifies whether the document reader uses the service default text extraction behavior (SERVICE_DEFAULT) or forces the Textract action defined in the document reader configuration (FORCE_DOCUMENT_READ_ACTION).

Specifies a list of feature types (such as TABLES or FORMS) that Amazon Textract should extract from input documents when the document reader processes them, allowing the document classifier to leverage those additional extracted elements.
Specifies the format of the training data (either COMPREHEND_CSV or AUGMENTED_MANIFEST) for the document classifier.
Provides the S3 URIs for the training documents (and optionally test documents) used to train the document classifier.
The S3 URI of the training documents (e.g., a CSV or augmented manifest file) used to train the Amazon Comprehend document classifier.
The S3 URI of the test documents used to evaluate the trained document classifier model.
The single character that separates the label from the text in each line of the training data files for the document classifier (e.g., a pipe '|').
The S3 URI of the bucket or folder that contains the training documents used to train the document classifier.
The S3 URI of the test dataset used to evaluate the trained document classifier.

aws_comprehend_document_classifier.langu.text: Specifies the language code of the training documents, such as 'en' for English or 'es' for Spanish, which the document classifier is trained on.

aws_comprehend_document_classifier.mode.text: Specifies the classification mode for the document classifier: MULTI_CLASS for assigning a single class per document, or MULTI_LABEL for assigning multiple labels per document.

aws_comprehend_document_classifier.model.text: Specifies the AWS KMS key ID used to encrypt the trained document classifier model.
The model_policy field specifies a JSON-based resource policy that grants other AWS services or IAM principals permission to use the trained document classifier for inference.

aws_comprehend_document_classifier.outpu.text: Specifies the Amazon S3 location (and optionally the AWS KMS key for encryption) where the document classifier training output, such as model artifacts and evaluation metrics, is stored.
The KMS key ID used to encrypt the output data stored in S3 for the document classifier.
The S3 URI where the document classifier's output data, such as training metrics and evaluation results, is stored.

aws_comprehend_document_classifier.tags.text: Specifies a list of key-value tags to attach to the document classifier resource.

aws_comprehend_document_classifier.tags..text: The tag key (e.g., 'project') for a user-defined tag attached to the Amazon Comprehend document classifier, used for metadata, cost tracking, and access control.
The value part of a tag attached to the Amazon Comprehend document classifier, used for cost allocation or organizational categorization.

aws_comprehend_document_classifier.versi.text: Specifies a user-defined version name for the document classifier, allowing you to manage and reference distinct versions of the same classifier within Amazon Comprehend.

aws_comprehend_document_classifier.volum.text: The identifier of the AWS KMS key that Amazon Comprehend uses to encrypt the storage volume attached to the compute instance during training of the document classifier.

aws_comprehend_document_classifier.vpc_c.text: Configures the VPC settings (security group IDs and subnet IDs) used by the document classifier to access training data or other resources in a private VPC.

Specifies the list of security group IDs that the Amazon Comprehend document classifier uses when it accesses resources in your VPC, controlling inbound and outbound network traffic for training and inference operations.
The list of subnet IDs in the Amazon VPC where the document classifier runs, enabling private network access to resources such as training data in S3.

aws_comprehend_flywheel.active_model_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the model that is currently active for the flywheel, used for performing inference and can be updated to switch to a different trained model version.

aws_comprehend_flywheel.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the dedicated flywheel, automatically assigned by AWS when the flywheel is created and used to reference this flywheel in IAM policies, resource relationships, and Amazon Comprehend API operations.

aws_comprehend_flywheel.data_access_role.text: The ARN of the IAM role that allows Amazon Comprehend to access the data (e.g., S3 buckets) used for training and evaluating models in the flywheel.

aws_comprehend_flywheel.data_lake_s3_uri.text: The S3 URI of the data lake that the flywheel uses as its central repository for training data and documents during model training and continuous learning.

aws_comprehend_flywheel.data_security_co.text: Configures encryption and network isolation for the flywheel by specifying optional KMS key ARNs for the model, volume, and data lake, along with an optional VPC configuration for private VPC access.
The AWS KMS key ID used to encrypt the data lake S3 bucket that stores flywheel training data and model artifacts.
Specifies the AWS KMS key ARN or ID used to encrypt the model artifacts (trained models) associated with the flywheel.
The AWS KMS key ID used to encrypt the storage volume attached to the compute resources for the flywheel's training and evaluation jobs.
Specifies the VPC configuration (subnets and security group IDs) for the flywheel, enabling it to access resources within a private network for secure data processing and storage.
A list of security group IDs to associate with the VPC configuration for the AWS Comprehend Flywheel, controlling network access to the resources used by the flywheel.
The list of subnet IDs within the specified VPC where the Amazon Comprehend flywheel launches its resources to enable private, secure communication with other AWS services.

aws_comprehend_flywheel.flywheel_name.text: The unique name that identifies the Amazon Comprehend flywheel.

aws_comprehend_flywheel.model_type.text: Specifies the type of custom model the flywheel is configured for, either DOCUMENT_CLASSIFIER for document classification or ENTITY_RECOGNIZER for entity recognition.

aws_comprehend_flywheel.tags.text: A list of tags (key-value pairs) to assign to the flywheel for metadata and cost tracking, as supported by AWS Comprehend.

aws_comprehend_flywheel.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the Amazon Comprehend flywheel, used to identify and organize the resource, optionally for cost allocation and access control.

aws_comprehend_flywheel.task_config.text: Specifies the configuration for the natural language processing task that the flywheel will support, including the language code and task-specific settings such as document classification or entity recognition configurations.

aws_comprehend_flywheel.task_config.docu.text: This object configures the document classification task of the flywheel, specifying the classification mode (MULTI_CLASS or MULTI_LABEL) and, for multi-label mode, the delimiter used to separate labels in the training data.
Defines the list of labels (classes) that the flywheel's document classification task uses to categorize input documents, such as in a custom classifier.
Specifies the document classification mode, either MULTI_CLASS to assign exactly one class per document or MULTI_LABEL to assign one or more labels per document.

aws_comprehend_flywheel.task_config.enti.text: This object configures the entity recognition task for the flywheel, specifying the custom entity types that the model is trained to detect.
For this flywheel's entity recognition task, defines the list of custom entity types (e.g., PRODUCT, PERSON) that the model will recognize or be trained to extract from text.

aws_comprehend_flywheel.task_config.lang.text: The language code (e.g., 'en') that specifies the language of the input data for the flywheel's configured task, such as document classification or entity recognition.

aws_compute_optimizer_automation_rule.cr.text: Defines the filter conditions that match recommendations for the automation rule, including criteria such as resource type, finding status, and savings opportunity threshold.
Defines a list of EBS volume size (in GiB) conditions used to filter which EBS volume recommendations are targeted by the Compute Optimizer automation rule.
Defines the comparison operator (e.g., GREATER_THAN, LESS_THAN) used to evaluate the EBS volume size in GiB against the target value in this automation rule's criteria.
The list of EBS volume size values (in GiB) that the automation rule's criteria matches against when selecting eligible EBS volumes for the rule.
A list of objects that specify the EBS volume types used to match against EBS volume recommendations in the automation rule's criteria.

The estimated_monthly_savings criterion defines a lower and upper bound, in US dollars, for the estimated monthly cost savings of a recommendation, so only recommendations whose projected savings fall within this range match the automation rule.
The comparison operator (for example, GREATER_THAN or LESS_THAN) used to evaluate the resource's estimated monthly savings against a threshold in the Compute Optimizer automation rule's criteria.
The numeric threshold values that the automation rule compares against a resource's estimated monthly savings to determine if the resource matches the criterion.
Specifies the look-back period in days that AWS Compute Optimizer uses to evaluate historical resource utilization when determining whether a recommendation matches the automation rule's criteria.

Specifies the comparison operator (such as GREATER_THAN or LESS_THAN) that determines whether a recommendation's lookback period in days matches the threshold defined in the automation rule's criteria.
The list of look-back periods in days (for example, 7, 14, or 30) used by the automation rule's criteria to filter AWS Compute Optimizer recommendations based on historical utilization data.
The comparison operation (for example, EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) applied to the region criterion of the Compute Optimizer automation rule to filter resources by their AWS region.
In the automation rule's criteria, `values` specifies the list of AWS Region names (e.g., `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`) that the rule uses to match resources for the `region` condition.

Within the criteria block, resource_arn is a list of objects that specify the Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the AWS resources the Compute Optimizer automation rule matches to determine which resources the rule applies to.
The comparison operator used to evaluate whether a resource's ARN matches the target value in this automation rule criterion.
Specifies the list of AWS resource ARNs that the Compute Optimizer automation rule uses as a matching criterion to select which resources the rule applies to.
A list of tag key-value pairs used as selection criteria, so that the Compute Optimizer automation rule only matches resources carrying the specified tag(s).

Specifies the comparison operator applied to the resource tag's key/value pair in the automation rule's criteria (e.g., equal, starts with, contains) to determine whether the rule matches a given resource.
The key of a resource tag that the automation rule's criteria uses to match target resources for automated actions.
The list of tag values that the resource_tag criterion uses to match resources, where a resource is considered a match if the value of the specified tag key equals any of these values.
Specifies the list of filter values (e.g., 'true' or 'false') for the restart-needed condition, matching Compute Optimizer recommendations that require or do not require an instance restart.

Specifies the comparison operator (such as Equals or NotEquals) used to evaluate the `restart_needed` criterion in the Compute Optimizer automation rule, determining whether a recommendation's restart requirement matches the configured value.
Specifies the list of acceptable 'restartNeeded' values (such as 'true' or 'false') that an EC2 recommendation must have for the automation rule's criteria to match and trigger the rule's action.

aws_compute_optimizer_automation_rule.sc.text: Defines the schedule for when the Compute Optimizer automation rule runs, including the frequency and timing at which the rule's recommended actions are applied to the targeted resources.

aws_config_config_rule.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Config rule, automatically assigned by AWS when the rule is created and used to uniquely identify the rule.

aws_config_config_rule.config_rule_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the Config rule when it is created.

aws_config_config_rule.evaluation_modes..text: Specifies the evaluation mode of the AWS Config rule, which is either 'DETECTIVE' (evaluates resources after changes are made) or 'PROACTIVE' (evaluates resources before deployment to prevent noncompliant resources).

aws_config_config_rule.source.source_det.text: For a custom AWS Config rule, this field indicates the AWS service that emits the events that trigger the rule, and the only valid value is `aws.config`.
Specifies how often AWS Config runs the rule's evaluations (e.g., One_Hour, TwentyFour_Hours) when the rule's source details define a periodic trigger.
The type of event that triggers the AWS Config rule's Lambda function, such as ConfigurationItemChangeNotification or ScheduledNotification.

aws_config_configuration_aggregator.acco.text: Specifies the list of AWS accounts from which to aggregate AWS Config configuration data, optionally restricting the regions that are aggregated for each account.
Specifies the AWS account IDs from which AWS Config will aggregate configuration data into the configuration aggregator.
Determines whether this account aggregation source includes all AWS regions (true) or only the specific regions listed in the 'regions' property (false).
The list of AWS regions from which AWS Config aggregates data for the specified source accounts.

aws_config_configuration_aggregator.orga.text: Specifies the AWS organization (by IAM role ARN and list of regions, with an option to enable all regions) that acts as the source of configuration data for this AWS Config configuration aggregator.
Indicates whether to aggregate Config data from all AWS regions in the organization (true) or only from the regions specified in the AwsRegions list (false).

Specifies the list of specific AWS regions from which the organization aggregator collects configuration data; if omitted, all regions are included (as long as the parent's allAwsRegions setting is true).
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Config assumes to access organization data for the organization aggregation source.

aws_config_configuration_aggregator.tags.text: The user-defined key of a tag applied to the AWS Config configuration aggregator, used to identify and organize the aggregator resource within your AWS environment.
The value portion of a key-value tag assigned to the AWS Config configuration aggregator.

aws_config_configuration_recorder.id.text: The physical resource ID of the configuration recorder, which is the same as its user-defined Name.

aws_config_configuration_recorder.name.text: The name of the configuration recorder, which must be unique within the region and defaults to 'default' if not specified.

aws_config_configuration_recorder.record.text: Specifies which AWS resource types are recorded by the configuration recorder, including whether to record all supported resource types and global resource types like IAM resources.
When set to true, AWS Config records configuration changes for all supported AWS resource types in the region.
Specifies the resource types to exclude from being recorded by AWS Config, allowing you to record all supported types except those listed when allSupported is enabled.
Specifies the list of AWS resource types that will be excluded from recording by the configuration recorder.
Indicates whether AWS Config records configuration changes to global resource types (such as IAM users, groups, roles, and customer managed policies) across all regions.
Defines the recording strategy for AWS Config, specifying whether to record all supported resource types, only included resource types, or all except excluded resource types.

Defines the recording strategy for the configuration recorder, with values such as ALL_SUPPORTED_RESOURCE_TYPES to record all supported resource types, INCLUDE_SPECIFIED_RESOURCE_TYPES to record only those listed in the recording group's resourceTypes, or EXCLUDE_SPECIFIED_RESOURCE_TYPES to record all except those listed.
Specifies the list of AWS resource types to be recorded by AWS Config; if omitted or empty, AWS Config records all supported resource types.
Specifies the recording frequency (continuous or periodic) that controls how often AWS Config records configuration changes for supported resources.
Specifies how often AWS Config records configuration changes for the resources in scope, either continuously or on a daily basis.

Specifies a list of overrides that set the recording mode (either CONTINUOUS or RECORD_ONLY) for specific AWS resource types, allowing you to customize recording behavior on a per-resource-type basis within the configuration recorder's recording mode.
A description that you provide for this recording mode override, explaining its purpose or distinguishing it from other overrides for specific resource types.
Specifies how often AWS Config records configuration changes for the resource types in this override, either CONTINUOUS for real-time recording or DAILY for a single daily snapshot.
Lists the AWS resource types (e.g., 'AWS::EC2::Instance') for which this recording mode override applies, allowing a different recording frequency to be set for those specific resources.

aws_config_configuration_recorder.role_a.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that AWS Config uses to record resource changes and deliver them to the delivery channel.

aws_config_conformance_pack.conformance_.text: The name of an input parameter declared in the conformance pack template, used to provide a value when creating or updating the pack.
The value assigned to a specific input parameter defined by the conformance pack template, used to customize the pack's configuration when deployed.

aws_config_conformance_pack.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS Config Conformance Pack, used to categorize, organize, or identify the conformance pack resource in AWS.

aws_config_conformance_pack.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag key-value pair assigned to the Conformance Pack, used for identifying, organizing, and managing the pack in AWS Config.

aws_config_conformance_pack.template_ssm.text: The name of the AWS Systems Manager (SSM) document that contains the conformance pack template.
The version of the AWS Systems Manager (SSM) document that provides the conformance pack template; when omitted, the default version of the document is used.

aws_config_delivery_channel.config_snaps.text: Specifies how often AWS Config delivers configuration snapshot updates (e.g., every hour, six hours, or twenty-four hours) to the delivery channel's destination.
Specifies the frequency with which AWS Config delivers configuration snapshots to the S3 bucket, accepting values like One_Hour, Three_Hours, Six_Hours, Twelve_Hours, and TwentyFour_Hours.

aws_config_delivery_channel.id.text: This field is the name of the AWS Config delivery channel, which serves as its unique identifier and is typically set to 'default' unless otherwise specified.

aws_config_delivery_channel.name.text: The name of the AWS Config delivery channel, which must be unique in the account and defaults to 'default' if not specified.

aws_config_delivery_channel.s3_bucket_na.text: Specifies the name of the Amazon S3 bucket to which AWS Config delivers configuration snapshots and configuration history files for the account.

aws_config_delivery_channel.s3_key_prefi.text: The prefix for the Amazon S3 keys that AWS Config uses to store configuration snapshots and delivery logs in the bucket.

aws_config_delivery_channel.s3_kms_key_a.text: The ARN of the AWS KMS key that AWS Config uses to encrypt the configuration snapshots and configuration history delivered to the Amazon S3 bucket.

aws_config_delivery_channel.sns_topic_ar.text: The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic to which AWS Config delivers configuration snapshots and configuration change notifications.

aws_config_organization_config_rule.excl.text: Specifies the AWS account IDs to exclude from the evaluation of this organization config rule, ensuring the rule does not apply to those accounts.

aws_config_organization_config_rule.id.text: The unique identifier that AWS Config assigns to this organization config rule upon creation.

aws_config_organization_config_rule.orga.text: The name assigned to the organization config rule, which must be unique within the organization.

Defines the configuration for a custom policy rule in AWS Config, including the PolicyText and other attributes like trigger types and resource scope, used when creating an organization-level config rule.
The list of AWS account IDs that can access the debug logs generated by this organization custom policy rule for troubleshooting rule evaluation.
An optional description that you provide for the organization custom policy rule, which is displayed in AWS Config to help identify its purpose.
Specifies the input parameters, as a JSON string, that are supplied to the organization's custom policy rule for evaluation.
For an AWS Config Organization Custom Policy Rule, this sets the maximum execution frequency (e.g., One_Hour, TwentyFour_Hours) at which the rule is evaluated.

Specifies the list of event types that trigger evaluation of the organization custom policy rule, such as ConfigurationItemChangeNotification, OversizedConfigurationItemChangeNotification, or Periodic.
The policy text that defines the compliance rule logic for the custom policy rule, written in the AWS Config policy language.
Limits the evaluation of this AWS Config organization custom policy rule to a specific AWS resource ID, so only that resource's configuration is checked against the policy.
The list of AWS resource types (e.g., 'AWS::EC2::Instance') that the custom policy rule will evaluate, limiting the rule's scope to only those resource types.
Specifies the runtime system for the custom policy rule, which must be 'guard' for AWS Config organization custom policy rules.
The tag key that limits the rule to evaluate only AWS resources that have this tag key.

Specifies the tag value that, when used with the tag key scope, limits the AWS Config organization custom policy rule to only those resources that have that exact tag key-value pair, excluding resources without it from evaluation.

Defines the metadata for an AWS Config custom rule powered by Lambda at the organization level, including the Lambda function ARN, trigger types, input parameters, maximum execution frequency, and the resource and tag scopes that limit which resources are evaluated.
Provides a human-readable description of the AWS Config organization custom rule, displayed in the AWS Config console to indicate the rule's purpose.
A JSON-formatted string of input parameters that are passed to the custom Lambda function when AWS Config evaluates resources for this organization custom rule.
The ARN of the Lambda function that AWS Config invokes to evaluate whether the resources in the organization comply with this custom rule.
The maximum frequency at which AWS Config runs evaluations for the custom rule, such as 'One_Hour' or 'Three_Hours', specified in the organization custom rule metadata.
Specifies the types of events that trigger the AWS Config organization custom rule, such as ConfigurationItemChangeNotification or ScheduledNotification.
The ID of a single AWS resource that this custom rule evaluates, limiting the rule's scope to that specific resource.
A list of AWS resource types (e.g., AWS::EC2::Instance) that limits the organization custom rule's evaluation to only the specified resource types, leaving all other resources out of scope.
Limits the AWS Config rule evaluation to resources that have the specified tag key in their tags, restricting the rule's scope to only those resources.
The tag value that, together with the tag key scope, limits the rule to evaluate only AWS resources carrying that specific tag value.

This block provides the configuration for an AWS managed Config rule that applies to the entire organization, specifying the managed rule identifier and optional settings such as input parameters and resource type scoping.
A human-readable description of the AWS Config managed rule that explains its purpose and what it evaluates.
A JSON-encoded string of input parameters to pass to the AWS Config managed rule, overriding default rule parameters.
Sets the maximum frequency at which the organization managed rule is evaluated by AWS Config, accepting values like One_Hour, Three_Hours, Six_Hours, Twelve_Hours, or TwentyFour_Hours.
The ID of a specific AWS resource to which the organization managed config rule applies, restricting evaluation to only that resource.
A list of AWS resource types that scopes the organization config rule's evaluation to only those resource types, such as AWS::EC2::Instance or AWS::S3::Bucket.
The identifier of the AWS Config managed rule to deploy across all accounts in the organization, such as 'S3_BUCKET_VERSIONING_ENABLED' or 'IAM_PASSWORD_POLICY'.
Specifies the tag key (and optionally the tag value via related field) that restricts this organization managed AWS Config rule to evaluate only resources bearing that tag key.

The value of the tag key that defines the resource scope for this organization managed Config rule, combined with tag_key_scope to limit the rule's evaluation to resources with that specific tag key and value.

aws_config_organization_conformance_pack.text: The name of an input parameter for the conformance pack, used to pass a value into the conformance pack template.

The value portion of a key-value input parameter pair (with the associated parameter_key) that is supplied to the AWS Config organization conformance pack template when the conformance pack is deployed or updated.
The value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Config organization conformance pack, used for metadata and resource identification.

aws_config_remediation_configuration.aut.text: When set to true, AWS Config automatically executes the remediation action on noncompliant resources associated with the rule; when false, remediation must be invoked manually.

aws_config_remediation_configuration.con.text: The name of the AWS Config rule for which this remediation configuration is defined, associating the remediation actions with that rule.

aws_config_remediation_configuration.exe.text: Configures the SSM execution controls for the remediation, including the concurrent execution rate percentage and error percentage that limit how many concurrent remediation executions are allowed and the acceptable error rate.
Configures the Systems Manager automation controls for the remediation, specifically the concurrent execution rate and error rate percentages that determine how SSM documents are run.
Specifies the maximum percentage of remediation actions that can run in parallel for the rule's SSM document, throttling concurrent executions (default is 100).
The maximum percentage of remediation actions that are allowed to fail before the remediation action is stopped.

aws_config_remediation_configuration.max.text: Determines the maximum number of times AWS Config automatically retries the remediation action on a non-compliant resource, with a valid value between 1 and 5.

aws_config_remediation_configuration.par.text: Specifies the set of parameters passed to the AWS Systems Manager automation document that performs the remediation, mapping each parameter name to a static value or a dynamic value derived from the evaluated resource.

aws_config_remediation_configuration.res.text: The type of AWS resource (e.g., 'AWS::EC2::Instance') that this Config remediation configuration applies to for automatic remediation actions.

aws_config_remediation_configuration.ret.text: The maximum time, in seconds, during which AWS Config will make automatic remediation attempts for a noncompliant resource before giving up.

aws_config_remediation_configuration.tar.text: The identifier of the remediation target, which is the name of the SSM document or the ARN of the custom action that remediates the noncompliant resource.
The type of target for the remediation action, which must be set to SSM_DOCUMENT because AWS Config currently supports only SSM Automation documents as remediation targets.
Specifies the version of the AWS Systems Manager automation document to use for the remediation action; if not provided, the default version of the document is used.

aws_config_stored_query.query_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the stored AWS Config query.

aws_config_stored_query.query_descriptio.text: The query_description field provides an optional, human-readable description for the AWS Config stored query, used to document the query's purpose or details.

aws_config_stored_query.query_expression.text: The SQL query expression (in AWS Config query language) that defines the resource configurations to retrieve when this stored query is executed.

aws_config_stored_query.query_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the stored query when it is created.

aws_config_stored_query.query_name.text: The name of the AWS Config stored query, which must be unique within the AWS account and is used to identify the query resource.

aws_config_stored_query.tags.value.text: For an AWS Config stored query, this field provides the value portion of a user-defined tag (key-value pair) used to organize and identify the query resource.

aws_connect_campaigns_campaign.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Amazon Connect Campaigns campaign, used to categorize the resource for cost allocation, ownership, and access control.

aws_connect_campaigns_campaign.tags.valu.text: The string value paired with each tag key on the Amazon Connect campaigns campaign, used for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource.

aws_connect_campaigns_v2_campaign.commun.text: The number of time units (such as days, weeks, months, or years) that defines the period over which the maximum number of contacts per recipient is enforced for a given channel subtype in the communication limit list.
Specifies the maximum number of communications that can be sent to a single recipient for the associated channel subtype, overriding the default communication limits for that subtype.
Specifies the time unit (e.g., DAY, WEEK, or MONTH) used to interpret the communication frequency limit for a given channel subtype in the campaign's communication limits override.
Specifies the day of the week (e.g., MONDAY, TUESDAY) for which the daily open hours are defined in the email communication time config of the campaign.
In the email channel's open hours configuration, the daily_hours.value list holds the daily recurring time windows (including day and start/end times) when the campaign is permitted to send emails.
Specifies the end time (in 24-hour HH:MM format) of the daily time window during which the campaign is allowed to send email communications to contacts.
The start time (in HH:MM format) for the daily email communication hours on the specified day of the week in the campaign's communication time configuration.
The inclusive end date (in YYYY-MM-DD format) of a restricted period during which email communications are suppressed for the campaign's communication time configuration.
The name of a restricted period during which email communication is disallowed, used to identify the period within the campaign's email communication time configuration.
The date (YYYY-MM-DD) on which a restricted email period begins, marking the start of a window when outbound email communications are suppressed within the campaign's communication time config.
Defines the day-of-week key (such as MONDAY) that identifies which day the corresponding SMS open hour time ranges apply to in the daily hours list of the SMS communication time configuration.
Specifies the list of time range objects (each with start and end times) for a given weekday, defining the SMS open hours within the campaign's communication time configuration.

Specifies the end time (in 24-hour HH:MM format) of an allowed daily time window for sending SMS communications, used within the open hours configuration for SMS in the campaign's communication time config.
The start time (HH:MM) of the allowed time window for sending SMS messages on a particular day of the week, as part of the campaign's SMS communication time configuration.
The end date (in YYYY-MM-DD format) of a restricted period during which SMS communications are not allowed to be sent to contacts for the campaign.
Specifies a descriptive name for the restricted period within the SMS communication time configuration, which identifies a time window during which outbound SMS messages are suppressed.
Defines the inclusive start date (YYYY-MM-DD) of a restricted period during which SMS communications are suppressed for this campaign.
The day of the week (e.g., MONDAY) for which these open hours apply.

Specifies the list of time-range objects (each with start and end times) that define the permitted daily calling hours for outbound telephony contacts on a given weekday in the campaign's communication time configuration.
The time of day (in HH:MM format, within the campaign's timezone) when the daily allowed telephony contact window ends.
The start time, in 24-hour format (e.g., '14:00'), of the daily open-hours window during which outbound telephony calls are permitted for the campaign.
The end date (in YYYY-MM-DD format) of a restricted period during which outbound calls are suppressed for the campaign's telephony communication time configuration.
A user-defined name for a restricted period, identifying a time window during which outbound telephony calls are prohibited for this campaign.
The start date of a restricted period, specified in YYYY-MM-DD format, during which outbound telephony calls are disallowed for the campaign.
The day of the week (e.g., MONDAY) for which the WhatsApp communication open hours are configured within the campaign's communication time settings.

The `value` field contains a list of time-range objects (each specifying a start and end time) that define the allowed daily operating hours for sending WhatsApp messages on a particular day of the week.
Defines the end time (in 24-hour HH:MM format) of a daily open hours window for WhatsApp communications in the campaign's communication time configuration.
Specifies the start time (in 24-hour HH:MM format) of the daily window during which WhatsApp communications are allowed for this campaign.
The date on which the restricted period ends, during which WhatsApp messages are suppressed in the campaign's communication time configuration.
The user-defined name that identifies a restricted period within the WhatsApp communication time configuration, which defines a time window during which outbound WhatsApp messages are not sent.
The start date (in ISO 8601 format) of a restricted period during which WhatsApp outbound communications are not allowed, used in the campaign's communication time configuration.

aws_connect_campaigns_v2_campaign.tags.k.text: The key of a tag assigned to the AWS::ConnectCampaignsV2::Campaign resource, used to categorize and manage the campaign in AWS.

aws_connect_campaigns_v2_campaign.tags.v.text: The value component of a tag attached to an AWS Connect Campaigns v2 campaign, used to store custom metadata such as environment, owner, or cost center for the campaign.

aws_connect_contact_flow.tags.key.text: The key portion of a tag applied to an Amazon Connect contact flow, used to categorize the resource and enforce tag-based access control in IAM policies.

aws_connect_contact_flow.tags.value.text: The value of an individual tag assigned to the Amazon Connect contact flow.

aws_connect_contact_flow_module.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to an Amazon Connect contact flow module for resource metadata and management.

aws_connect_contact_flow_module.tags.val.text: The value of a tag applied to the Amazon Connect contact flow module, used for organizing, managing, and identifying the resource within AWS.

aws_connect_data_table.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to attach to the Amazon Connect data table, used for organizing and identifying the resource within AWS.

aws_connect_data_table_attribute.data_ta.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the data table to which this attribute is attached.

aws_connect_data_table_attribute.instanc.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Connect instance that contains the data table to which this attribute belongs.

aws_connect_data_table_attribute.last_mo.text: The AWS Region where the data table attribute was last updated or modified.

aws_connect_data_table_attribute.primary.text: Boolean flag indicating whether this attribute serves as the primary key for the Amazon Connect data table, uniquely identifying each row.

aws_connect_data_table_attribute.validat.text: The allowed string values for this enum validation, which restricts the attribute to one of the specified values.
Sets the exclusive upper bound for a numeric data table attribute's value, requiring any stored value to be strictly less than this number to pass validation.
Defines an exclusive minimum validation constraint on a numeric attribute in an Amazon Connect data table, requiring that the attribute's value must be strictly greater than the specified number.
Specifies the maximum number of characters allowed for a string-type attribute value in an AWS Connect data table, used to validate that input does not exceed this length.
Specifies the maximum numeric value allowed for a data table attribute when the attribute's validation rule is of numeric type.
Specifies the minimum number of characters that a string-type data table attribute value must have to be considered valid in Amazon Connect.
Specifies the minimum numeric value allowed for this data table attribute, used to validate that input is not less than this threshold when the attribute is of a numeric type.
The numeric value that an attribute value must be a multiple of, used as a validation constraint for number-type attributes in an Amazon Connect data table.

aws_connect_data_table_attribute.value_t.text: Specifies the data type of the attribute value (e.g., string, number, boolean) in an Amazon Connect data table, controlling how the value is stored and used in contact flows.

aws_connect_data_table_record.data_table.text: The 'data_table_record' object holds the key-value pairs (column names to values) that constitute the record to be inserted into the specified Amazon Connect data table.
Specifies the values of the record's primary key fields, which uniquely identify the record within the Amazon Connect data table.
The identifier of the attribute (column) within the Amazon Connect data table's schema that this primary key value is associated with.
The value for a primary key attribute of the data table record, which combined with other primary values uniquely identifies a record in the specified Amazon Connect data table.
The list of key-value pairs that constitute the record's data, where each object maps a field name to its value as defined by the Amazon Connect data table's schema.
Specifies the value for a single attribute (key) in a record's values map for an Amazon Connect data table record.

aws_connect_data_table_record.instance_a.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Connect instance that contains the data table record.

aws_connect_data_table_record.record_id.text: The unique system-generated identifier of the data table record, returned by Amazon Connect after the record is created.

aws_connect_email_address.alias_configur.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an email address that is configured as an alias for the primary Connect email address.

aws_connect_email_address.tags.key.text: The user-defined key for a tag attached to the AWS Connect email address, used to organize and manage the resource.

aws_connect_email_address.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the Amazon Connect email address resource.

aws_connect_evaluation_form.auto_evaluat.text: Indicates whether Amazon Connect automatically triggers this evaluation form after a completed contact, as part of the auto-evaluation configuration.

aws_connect_evaluation_form.evaluation_f.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Connect evaluation form, uniquely identifying it within AWS.

aws_connect_evaluation_form.items.sectio.text: The section definition for an item in the evaluation form, specifying the section's title, instructions, and any nested items or questions within that section.
The instructions text displayed to the agent for this section of the Connect evaluation form.
Specifies whether this section is excluded from the overall evaluation form scoring, so that its items do not contribute to the calculated total score.
A list of evaluation form items (such as questions or subsections) nested within a section of the AWS Connect evaluation form.
Defines a question item within a section of the Amazon Connect evaluation form, specifying the question text, optional instructions, and answer options for the evaluator.
Controls whether the question is always enabled, always disabled, or conditionally enabled based on an automated rule (type MANUAL) that references prior answers in the evaluation form.
In an AWS Connect evaluation form, the 'enablement' block's 'action' string specifies whether the question is enabled or disabled (e.g., 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED') when the associated condition is met.
Specifies the enabling condition for the question, such as comparing a previous answer to a given value, which must match for the question to be active in the evaluation form.

The list of operands (each a literal value or an automation ID) that the condition compares against the answer of the referenced question using the specified operator, to determine whether the current question should be enabled.
The comparator is the comparison operator (such as equals, not_equals, greater_than, less_than) used to evaluate the answer value against the operand in a condition's expression.
Identifies the source of the operand's value (for example, agent attribute, customer attribute, or item answer) that the condition evaluates to determine if the question is enabled.
Specifies the unique identifier of the question whose answer is used as the source operand in a condition expression for enabling a subsequent question in the evaluation form.
Indicates the type of source referenced by the expression in an enablement condition operand, typically `Question` to reference another question's response within the evaluation form.
The values to match against the referenced answer or attribute in the operand's expression, determining when the question is enabled.
The RefId of an answer option that serves as the value in an enablement condition expression, identifying the previous question response that triggers the condition for the current question.
Specifies the data type of each value in the operand expression of a question's enablement condition, such as STRING, NUMBER, or BOOLEAN.

Specifies the comparison operator (such as equals, not equals, or contains) used by the enablement condition to evaluate the answer of a referenced question and determine whether the current question is enabled.

This field specifies the default action for a question that is not enabled in the evaluation form, with allowed values 'ANSWER' and 'NO_ANSWER' determining whether the question is treated as answered or not answered for scoring purposes.
Provides the instructional guidance text displayed alongside the question to help the evaluator or agent understand how to complete it.
Indicates whether the evaluator can select a 'Not applicable' answer option for the question, allowing the question to be skipped without affecting the score.
The type of the question in an Amazon Connect evaluation form, which determines the answer format and available properties, with supported values including NUMERIC, SINGLE_SELECT, and TEXT.

Holds the configuration properties specific to the question type, such as the answer options and display settings for a single-select question or the minimum and maximum values for a numeric question.
Specifies the configuration for a multi-select evaluation question, including the list of answer options and the maximum number of choices an evaluator can select.
Defines the automated scoring configuration for a multi-select question, specifying which answer options are correct and how they contribute to the overall evaluation score.

Defines the external source (such as a contact attribute or AWS Lambda function) from which the answer choices for a multi-select question are automatically populated in an Amazon Connect evaluation form.
Specifies the type of the answer source (such as 'Agent' or 'Customer') that provides automated answer choices for the multi-select evaluation question.
Specifies the list of option reference IDs that are automatically chosen as default answers for the multi-select question when this automation value is applied in the evaluation form.
Specifies the list of automated scoring options, where each option references a candidate answer of the multi-select question and assigns a numeric score if that answer is selected by the evaluator.

The rule category name that associates this multi-select answer option with a predefined scoring category in the evaluation form's automation rules, so selecting it contributes to that category's score automatically.
Specifies the category name assigned to this multi-select answer option's automation rule, used for grouping and reporting evaluation results in Amazon Connect.

Specifies the option reference IDs of the answer choices in this multi-select question that are grouped under this rule category, which are used by the automation rule to apply scoring or branching based on which of these options are selected.
Controls how the answer choices for a multi-select evaluation question are presented to the evaluator, such as a checkbox list or a multi-select dropdown.
Defines the list of selectable answer choices for a multi-select evaluation form question, where each option specifies its reference identifier and the text shown to the evaluator.
When true, selecting this multi-select option will automatically fail the evaluation.
Specifies whether selecting this multi-select answer option automatically fails the evaluation, along with any related settings for that automatic failure.
Specifies the identifier of the section that will be displayed to the evaluator after this multi-select option is selected and the evaluation is automatically failed.
Specifies the point value awarded to the respondent when this answer option is selected in a multi-select evaluation form question.
If set to true, the points assigned to this multi-select option are treated as bonus points, which are added to the evaluation score without counting toward the maximum possible score.
Defines the score that this particular answer option contributes to the overall evaluation form score when chosen by the evaluator.
A unique identifier for an answer option within a multi-select question in the evaluation form, used to reference the selected option when storing or reporting evaluation results.
The numeric score assigned to each answer option in a multi-select question, used to calculate the total evaluation score.
The display label shown for each selectable option in a multi-select question, used as the option's text in the Connect evaluation form.
For an Amazon Connect evaluation form question, this object configures the numeric answer type, including the allowed minimum and maximum values and optional automatic scoring behavior.
Defines the automation settings that determine which Amazon Connect property (e.g., overall customer sentiment score) automatically supplies the numeric answer for this evaluation-form question.
The answer_source object within the numeric automation of an AWS Connect evaluation form question specifies where the automated numeric value is pulled from, such as a contact attribute.
Specifies whether the automated numeric answer is sourced from agent interaction data or customer interaction data, determining which entity's attributes populate the field's pre-filled response.
The contact attribute property name (key) that automatically supplies the numeric response for this Amazon Connect evaluation form question.
The label of an automated answer option for a numeric question in an AWS Connect evaluation form, which is the human-readable text displayed for that predefined numeric response.
The maximum numeric value that a respondent can enter for a numeric evaluation form question, used to define the upper bound of the allowed answer range.
Specifies the minimum numeric value allowed as an answer for this numeric question type in the Amazon Connect evaluation form.

Specifies the list of numeric answer options for a numeric question in an Amazon Connect evaluation form, where each option pairs a numeric value with a display label that agents can select as a score.
When set to true, an answer falling within the range defined by this numeric option automatically causes the evaluation form to be marked as failed.
Specifies the automatic failure criteria for a numeric answer option, which when met causes the overall evaluation form to be immediately marked as failed.
Specifies the unique identifier of the section to which the evaluation form should navigate when an evaluator's numeric answer falls within this option's range and triggers an automatic fail.
Specifies the maximum numeric value within which an agent's response must fall for this option's score to be applied in a numeric evaluation form question.
The lower bound of the numeric range for this option, defining the minimum value that can be assigned when answering this numeric question.
Specifies the point value and related scoring behavior (such as automatic failure) assigned to a specific numeric answer option in an Amazon Connect evaluation form.
Indicates whether the points assigned to this numeric answer option are bonus points, allowing them to be awarded as extra credit outside the standard scoring total.
The number of points awarded to the evaluated response when the numeric answer falls within the range defined by this option's points configuration.
The numeric score assigned to a range of values for a numeric evaluation question in an Amazon Connect evaluation form.
Defines the configuration for a single-select question in an evaluation form, specifying the answer options (with scores or weights) that the agent can choose from.
Specifies the automation to execute when a particular answer option is selected for a single-select question, including the target ARN and the option reference that triggers it.
Specifies the automatic source (such as a contact attribute) used to pre-populate the answer for this single-select question in an AWS Connect evaluation form.
Specifies the type of the source (such as agent, customer, contact, queue, or system) from which the answer to the single-select question is automatically populated when automation is enabled.
The reference identifier of the answer option that is automatically preselected when the single-select question is answered by the evaluation form's automation rule.
A list of automation options that map answer choices (by reference ID) to automated actions (such as creating a task) for a single-select question in an Amazon Connect evaluation form.

In an Amazon Connect evaluation form's single-select question automation option, this field specifies the rule category that identifies the outcome or action to be taken when the option's conditions are satisfied.

Specifies the name of an Amazon Connect category to be automatically assigned to the contact when the selected answer option is chosen in the single-select question's automation rule, enabling contact classification.
In an automation rule for a single-select evaluation question, this field references the unique ID of an answer option so that selecting that option triggers the associated rule category.
Determines whether the single-select question's answer choices are displayed to the agent as a dropdown list or as radio buttons.
The list of answer choices for a single-select question in an Amazon Connect evaluation form, where each option specifies the displayed text and the score assigned if selected.
If set to true, selecting this option automatically fails the evaluation form, regardless of other answers.
Defines the configuration that, when set, causes the evaluation to be automatically marked as failed if the agent selects this single-select question option.
The identifier of the section where the evaluation form should redirect after this option triggers an automatic failure.

The points_configuration object defines the scoring parameters (points and weight) for a given answer option in a single-select evaluation question, determining how that choice contributes to the overall evaluation score.
Indicates whether the points assigned to this answer option are bonus points, which are added to the evaluation score without increasing the total possible score.
The numeric score assigned to this single-select answer option, which contributes to the total evaluation score when the option is selected.
This field stores an optional unique reference identifier for each single-select option in an Amazon Connect evaluation form, used to programmatically reference the option.
The numeric score assigned to an individual answer option in a single-select question, used to compute the evaluation form's overall result.
The display text of an answer option for a single-select question in an AWS Connect evaluation form.
