aws_dax_cluster.ssespecification.sseenab.text: Enables or disables server-side encryption (SSE) for the DAX cluster, using AWS KMS to protect data at rest when enabled.

aws_dax_cluster.subnet_group_name.text: The name of the subnet group that defines the VPC subnets in which the DAX cluster nodes are launched.

aws_dax_parameter_group.description.text: A user-specified description that identifies the purpose or contents of this DAX parameter group.

aws_dax_parameter_group.id.text: The computed unique identifier for the DAX parameter group, which is its parameter group name.

aws_dax_parameter_group.parameter_group_.text: The name of this DAX parameter group, which is used when associating the group with a DAX cluster and must be unique in the account and region.

aws_dax_parameter_group.parameter_name_v.text: Specifies the name-value pairs of DAX parameters to apply to the parameter group, where each key is a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) parameter name and its value is the parameter's configured value.

aws_dax_subnet_group.description.text: An optional user-provided description that identifies the purpose or context of this DAX subnet group.

aws_dax_subnet_group.id.text: The name of the DAX subnet group, which uniquely identifies the resource within AWS.

aws_dax_subnet_group.subnet_group_name.text: The name of this DAX subnet group; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name based on the logical resource ID.

aws_dax_subnet_group.subnet_ids.text: The list of subnet IDs in the VPC where the DAX cluster will be deployed, defining the network locations for the cluster's nodes.

aws_deadline_budget.actions.description.text: A human-readable description of a budget action, explaining the action taken when the budget threshold is reached.

aws_deadline_budget.actions.threshold_pe.text: The percentage of the budget's usage threshold that, when reached, triggers the corresponding budget action (such as stopping or limiting the farm).

aws_deadline_budget.actions.type.text: Defines the type of budget action to take when the threshold is reached, such as STOP_SESSION_WORKER or STOP_QUEUE.

aws_deadline_budget.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS Deadline budget, used for organizing and managing the budget resource.

aws_deadline_farm.arn.text: The unique Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the farm, used to reference the farm across AWS services and in IAM policies.

aws_deadline_farm.description.text: A human-readable description of the Deadline Cloud farm, used to identify the farm's purpose or details.

aws_deadline_farm.display_name.text: Specifies the human-readable name for the farm, which is used to identify it in the AWS Deadline Cloud console and API operations.

aws_deadline_farm.farm_id.text: The unique identifier assigned to the farm by AWS Deadline when the farm is created.

aws_deadline_farm.kms_key_arn.text: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt data for the AWS Deadline Cloud farm; if not provided, AWS uses an AWS-managed key.

aws_deadline_farm.tags.key.text: The user-defined key for a tag attached to the AWS Deadline Cloud farm, used to identify and organize the resource.

aws_deadline_farm.tags.value.text: Specifies the value of a tag applied to the AWS Deadline Farm, allowing you to categorize and manage the farm with custom metadata such as cost allocation or team identification.

aws_deadline_fleet.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Deadline fleet.

aws_deadline_fleet.capabilities.text: This read-only object describes the effective resource capabilities of the fleet, such as CPU architecture, CPU count, memory size, and GPU resources, as reported by AWS Deadline Cloud after fleet creation.

aws_deadline_fleet.capabilities.amounts.text: Specifies the list of amount capabilities for the fleet, where each object defines a named resource (e.g. memory or CPU) along with its minimum and maximum amount that a worker can provide.

aws_deadline_fleet.capabilities.amounts..text: Specifies the upper bound of a numeric amount capability (e.g., memory or CPU count) that a fleet worker in AWS Deadline Cloud can provide, used to define a valid range alongside the min value.
The minimum numeric amount of a specific capability (e.g., vCPUs or memory) that the Deadline fleet can offer, used to match jobs requiring at least that amount.
The name of the amount capability, which is a string key identifying the resource quantity (e.g., 'gpu' or 'memory') that the fleet advertises in its capabilities.

aws_deadline_fleet.capabilities.attribut.text: Specifies the list of attribute capabilities for the fleet, where each entry defines a custom attribute name and its set of allowed values that workers in the fleet must support.
The name of a single fleet capability attribute (for example, 'GPU' or 'OS') within the attributes list of the fleet's capabilities.

Specifies the list of values for a specific attribute within the fleet's capabilities, enabling job definitions to match fleets based on these attribute values when scheduling jobs in AWS Deadline Cloud.

aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.text: Defines the compute environment for the fleet, selecting either a service-managed Amazon EC2 configuration (specifying instance types, allocation strategy, and capacity) or a customer-managed configuration (specifying worker capabilities such as operating system, CPU, and memory).

aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.custome.text: Specifies the customer-managed configuration for the fleet, including the required worker capabilities (such as CPU architecture, memory, and OS) and the usage mode indicating whether those capabilities are mandatory.
Configures the minimum and maximum worker count that the customer-managed fleet's auto-scaling uses to scale worker instances in response to job demand.
Specifies the maximum number of worker instances that can be added to the customer-managed fleet per minute during a scale-out event.
Specifies the number of idle workers to maintain as standby capacity, reducing the time jobs wait for worker availability in the auto-scaling fleet.
The number of seconds a worker can remain idle before it is considered idle by the auto-scaling policy and potentially scaled down.
The operating mode of the customer-managed fleet, set to either RESUME (active and accepting jobs) or PAUSE (suspended and not accepting jobs).
The unique identifier of the storage profile that defines the file system locations available to this customer-managed fleet.

Determines whether tags applied to the fleet are propagated to the underlying EC2 worker instances in a customer-managed fleet, with supported values like NONE (no propagation) or TO_EC2 (propagate tags to EC2 instances).
Defines the hardware and OS capabilities (CPU architecture, OS type, memory, vCPU count, and accelerator types) that worker instances in a customer-managed AWS Deadline Cloud fleet must have.
Defines the minimum and maximum number of accelerator devices (e.g., GPUs) that must be available on a worker in a customer-managed AWS Deadline fleet.
The maximum number of accelerators (e.g., GPUs) a single worker in the customer-managed fleet can have, serving as the upper bound for the accelerator count range in worker capabilities.
The minimum number of accelerators (such as GPUs) that each worker in the customer-managed fleet must have available.
Specifies the minimum and maximum total accelerator memory in MiB for workers in this customer-managed fleet, used by Deadline Cloud to match tasks requiring a certain amount of accelerator memory.
The maximum total accelerator memory in mebibytes (MiB) allowed on a worker for this customer-managed fleet, used to match workers to job requirements.
The minimum total accelerator memory in MiB that a worker must have for the customer-managed fleet to be eligible.
Specifies the GPU accelerator types (e.g., specific GPU model names) available on the worker, which Deadline Cloud uses to match jobs requiring those accelerator types.
Specifies the CPU architecture (x86_64 or arm64) of the worker instances in a customer managed Deadline fleet, used to match jobs that require a specific architecture.

Defines user-defined numeric capability amounts (each with a name and value) that worker instances in a customer-managed fleet advertise, allowing job requirements to match against these custom worker capacity metrics.
The maximum value for a custom worker capability amount in a customer-managed Deadline fleet, capping the upper end of the numeric range that can be reported for that capability.
The minimum value for this custom worker capability amount, used as the lower bound when matching jobs to fleet worker capabilities.
The name of a custom worker capability amount, serving as the identifier or key for the user-defined capability metric on the fleet's worker nodes.
Specifies custom worker attributes as key-value pairs that define the worker's capabilities, allowing Deadline Cloud to match jobs to appropriate customer-managed fleet workers.
Specifies the name (key) of a custom worker capability attribute used to match worker capacity requirements for a customer-managed fleet.
The list of values for a custom attribute that defines a worker's capability, used to match jobs to appropriate workers in a Deadline fleet.
The maximum memory capacity in MiB that a worker in this customer-managed fleet is expected to have, used by Deadline Cloud to match jobs to fleets based on resource requirements.
The minimum amount of memory in MiB that a worker must have to be considered eligible when using customer-managed fleets in AWS Deadline Cloud.
Specifies the operating system family (e.g., Linux or Windows) that workers in a customer-managed fleet must match for task scheduling.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of vCPUs that each worker instance can have in the customer-managed fleet.
The maximum number of vCPUs that a worker in the customer-managed fleet can use.
The minimum number of vCPUs that a worker in the customer-managed fleet must have for the fleet to consider it usable when matching jobs.

aws_deadline_fleet.configuration.service.text: The service-managed EC2 configuration specifies the EC2 instances that AWS Deadline Cloud automatically launches and manages for this fleet, including instance capabilities and instance count limits.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of worker instances for the service-managed EC2 fleet, enabling automatic scaling within these bounds.
Determines the number of worker instances that are added to the fleet per minute when the service-managed EC2 auto scaling configuration scales out.
Specifies the number of worker instances to keep provisioned and idle as standby capacity, so that the fleet can scale up quickly when new tasks arrive rather than waiting for instances to launch.
The amount of time in seconds that a worker can remain idle before the AWS Deadline Cloud auto scaling configuration scales it down to reduce fleet capacity.

Defines the service-managed EC2 instance requirements for the fleet, including min/max CPU cores, min/max memory in MiB, CPU architecture type, OS name, and optionally allowed instance types and root volume size.
Defines the required GPU accelerator specifications (including accelerator type and count) for the Amazon EC2 instances provisioned for this Deadline fleet.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of GPU accelerators for the fleet's instances, represented as an object with `Min` and `Max` integer properties, used to filter eligible instance types.
The maximum number of accelerators (such as GPUs) that each worker instance in the service-managed EC2 fleet should have.
The minimum number of accelerator cards (e.g., GPUs) that an instance must have in order to be considered for the fleet's instance selection.
Specifies the list of accelerator (GPU) selections available to the fleet's service-managed EC2 instances, including each accelerator's name and runtime (e.g., 'gpu' or 'opt-in').
The name of the accelerator selection (e.g., 'nvidia_a10g') that identifies the specific GPU or accelerator type to be used by the service-managed EC2 instances in the Deadline fleet.
Specifies the runtime (e.g., CUDA) required for the selected GPU accelerator type in a Deadline fleet's service-managed EC2 instances.
Specifies the list of EC2 instance types that the fleet is allowed to use for worker instances.
Specifies the CPU architecture (x86_64 or arm64) for the Amazon EC2 instances that the service-managed fleet will launch.

Specifies a list of custom amount capabilities (each with a name, min, and max) that the Service Managed EC2 fleet advertises, enabling jobs with matching resource amount requirements to be scheduled on the fleet.
The maximum numeric value for a custom instance capability amount, defining the upper bound of the range that Deadline Cloud uses when selecting EC2 instances for the fleet.

For a custom amount in an AWS Deadline Cloud service-managed EC2 fleet's instance capabilities, this min property sets the lower bound (numeric minimum) for the named custom attribute, such as vCPU, memory, or GPU, used when selecting matching EC2 instances.
The name of the custom amount, which must match a custom amount defined on the worker to associate that amount with the fleet's instance capability requirements.

Defines custom key-value pairs (attribute name and value) that worker instances in the fleet advertise as additional capabilities, allowing job requirements to target instances with these specific attributes.
The key of a custom attribute assigned to service-managed EC2 worker instances in the fleet, used for categorizing or matching instances to workload requirements in AWS Deadline Cloud.
Provides the list of string values for a custom attribute that this fleet advertises as a worker capability, used by Deadline Cloud to match jobs that require those attribute values.
Specifies the EC2 instance types that are excluded from the fleet's capacity, preventing these instance types from being used when provisioning worker instances.
Specifies the minimum and maximum memory (in MiB) allowed for instances in the service-managed EC2 fleet, used to constrain eligible instance types.
Specifies the maximum memory in MiB for the service-managed EC2 instances in the fleet, used by AWS Deadline Cloud to determine eligible instance types.
The minimum amount of memory in MiB that a worker instance must have to be eligible for the fleet's service-managed EC2 instances.
Specifies the operating system family (LINUX or WINDOWS) for the service-managed EC2 worker instances in the AWS Deadline Cloud fleet.
Specifies the configuration for the root Amazon EBS volume attached to each service-managed EC2 instance in the Deadline fleet, including settings like volume size, IOPS, throughput, and encryption.
Specifies the provisioned IOPS (I/O operations per second) for the root EBS volume attached to each instance in the AWS Deadline fleet's service-managed EC2 instances.
Specifies the size in GiB of the root EBS volume for the service-managed EC2 instances in the Deadline fleet.
Specifies the throughput in MiB/s for the root EBS volume attached to worker instances in a service-managed EC2 fleet configuration for AWS Deadline Cloud.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of vCPUs allowed for Amazon EC2 instances in this service-managed fleet.
Specifies the maximum number of vCPUs for the service-managed EC2 instances in the AWS Deadline Cloud fleet.
The minimum number of vCPUs an EC2 instance type must provide to be eligible for this Deadline Cloud service-managed fleet's instance capabilities.
Configures the Spot or On-Demand purchase option for the fleet's EC2 instances, including Spot-specific settings like maximum price and allocation strategy.
Specifies the market type for the fleet's EC2 instances, either 'on-demand' or 'spot', determining how the instances are purchased for the Deadline Cloud fleet.
Specifies the configuration for the persistent EBS volume attached to each worker instance in the service-managed EC2 fleet, including volume size, type, I/O characteristics, and encryption settings.
The provisioned IOPS (input/output operations per second) for the persistent EBS volume attached to instances in the service-managed EC2 fleet, determining storage performance.
Specifies the absolute file path within the fleet's service-managed EC2 worker instances where the configured persistent volume will be mounted, enabling shared storage access.
The size of the persistent volume attached to the fleet's worker instances, specified in gibibytes (GiB).
Specifies the throughput (in MiB/s) to provision for the persistent EBS volume attached to the fleet's worker instances.
The ID of the storage profile that defines the file system mounts (e.g., Amazon EFS or FSx) available to the fleet's worker instances.
Specifies the VPC subnets and security groups that the service-managed EC2 instances of the Deadline fleet will use.
Specifies the list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of Deadline Cloud resource configurations to apply to the worker instances launched in the VPC for a service-managed EC2 fleet.

aws_deadline_fleet.description.text: A human-readable description of the fleet, used to identify the fleet's purpose or configuration in the Deadline Cloud console and APIs.

aws_deadline_fleet.display_name.text: The human-readable name assigned to the fleet, used for identification within the Deadline Cloud farm.

aws_deadline_fleet.farm_id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS Deadline Cloud farm that this fleet is associated with.

aws_deadline_fleet.fleet_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by Deadline Cloud to the fleet when it is created, returned as a read-only value.

aws_deadline_fleet.host_configuration.text: Specifies the network configuration for the worker hosts in the fleet, including the VPC subnet IDs and security group IDs that the EC2 instances for service-managed fleets will launch into.

aws_deadline_fleet.host_configuration.sc.text: Specifies the body of a script that runs on each fleet host at startup, enabling custom configuration of the worker environment in AWS Deadline Cloud.
Specifies the maximum time in seconds that a worker's startup or lifecycle script may run on a host in the Deadline Cloud fleet before the script is considered failed or terminated.

aws_deadline_fleet.max_worker_count.text: The maximum number of worker instances the fleet can scale up to, setting an upper capacity limit for the fleet's auto-scaling behavior.

aws_deadline_fleet.min_worker_count.text: Specifies the minimum number of worker instances that must be maintained in the fleet, ensuring baseline capacity for render workloads.

aws_deadline_fleet.role_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the fleet's workers assume to interact with AWS services and perform job tasks.

aws_deadline_fleet.status.text: The current lifecycle state of the fleet, such as CREATING, ACTIVE, UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS, or DELETING, as reported by the Deadline Cloud service.

aws_deadline_fleet.status_message.text: The status_message attribute is a read-only string that provides a detailed explanation or reason for the fleet's current status, as reported by AWS Deadline Cloud.

aws_deadline_fleet.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the AWS Deadline Cloud fleet, providing a user-defined label for organizing and managing the fleet through standard AWS tagging practices.

aws_deadline_fleet.tags.value.text: The value part of a user-defined tag attached to an AWS Deadline Fleet, used to categorize and manage the fleet for cost allocation or operational purposes.

aws_deadline_fleet.worker_count.text: The current number of active workers in the fleet, as computed and maintained by AWS Deadline Cloud.

aws_deadline_license_endpoint.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS Deadline Cloud license endpoint.

aws_deadline_license_endpoint.dns_name.text: The DNS name assigned to the license endpoint, used to connect to the endpoint for license management.

aws_deadline_license_endpoint.license_en.text: The unique identifier assigned by Deadline Cloud when the license endpoint is created.

aws_deadline_license_endpoint.security_g.text: Specifies the list of VPC security group IDs to associate with the license endpoint's elastic network interface, defining the firewall rules that permit traffic to and from the license endpoint.

aws_deadline_license_endpoint.status.text: Represents the current lifecycle state of the license endpoint, such as CREATING, READY, or DELETING, as tracked by AWS Deadline Cloud.

aws_deadline_license_endpoint.status_mes.text: A computed string that provides additional context or error details about the current lifecycle state of the AWS Deadline Cloud license endpoint, such as why it might be in a transitional or failed status.

aws_deadline_license_endpoint.subnet_ids.text: The list of subnet IDs in the VPC where the license endpoint's elastic network interfaces are provisioned to connect to license servers.

aws_deadline_license_endpoint.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS Deadline license endpoint, enabling you to categorize and manage the endpoint for cost allocation and access control.

aws_deadline_license_endpoint.tags.value.text: Specifies the value for a user-defined tag on the Deadline license endpoint, used to categorize, track costs, or apply IAM-based access control through resource tags.

aws_deadline_license_endpoint.vpc_id.text: The ID of the VPC in which the license endpoint is created.

aws_deadline_limit.current_count.text: The current number of resources that are using this limit, as tracked by AWS Deadline Cloud and updated automatically as usage changes.

aws_deadline_limit.description.text: Provides an optional human-readable description for the AWS Deadline Cloud limit, clarifying the limit's purpose or scope.

aws_deadline_limit.display_name.text: A human-readable name for the limit, used to identify and display the limit in the AWS Deadline Cloud console and API.

aws_deadline_limit.farm_id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS Deadline Cloud farm to which this limit belongs.

aws_deadline_limit.limit_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS Deadline Cloud to this limit resource when it is created, used to refer to the limit in other resources.

aws_deadline_limit.max_count.text: The maximum number of resources that the limit permits to be used simultaneously, enforcing a cap on concurrent usage in the Deadline Cloud farm.

aws_deadline_metered_product.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Deadline Cloud metered product.

aws_deadline_metered_product.family.text: The product family (e.g., 'Arnold' or 'V-Ray') that Deadline Cloud assigns to the metered product, automatically determined and read-only.

aws_deadline_metered_product.license_end.text: The unique identifier of the license endpoint with which the metered product is associated in AWS Deadline Cloud.

aws_deadline_metered_product.port.text: The network port number on which the metered product's licensing service listens, returned by Deadline Cloud after the product is created.

aws_deadline_metered_product.product_id.text: The product_id specifies the unique AWS Marketplace product identifier for the software product that is metered and associated with the Deadline farm.

aws_deadline_metered_product.vendor.text: The vendor of the metered product, representing the company or provider that offers the software, as assigned by AWS Deadline Cloud.

aws_deadline_monitor.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Deadline Cloud monitor.

aws_deadline_monitor.display_name.text: A human-readable name for the Deadline Cloud monitor, used to identify it in the AWS console and APIs.

aws_deadline_monitor.identity_center_app.text: The ARN of the AWS IAM Identity Center application that AWS Deadline Cloud creates and associates with this monitor.

aws_deadline_monitor.identity_center_ins.text: The ARN of the IAM Identity Center instance used to manage user access and single sign-on for the AWS Deadline Cloud monitor.

aws_deadline_monitor.monitor_id.text: The unique identifier assigned to the monitor.

aws_deadline_monitor.role_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the Deadline Cloud monitor uses to access the storage resources (such as the S3 bucket and file system) associated with the Deadline Cloud environment.

aws_deadline_monitor.subdomain.text: Specifies the subdomain that forms part of the monitor's unique web address, used to access the Deadline Cloud monitor endpoint.

aws_deadline_monitor.tags.key.text: A key for a tag assigned to the AWS Deadline Cloud monitor, used to categorize and identify the resource.

aws_deadline_monitor.url.text: The URL of the AWS Deadline monitor, used to access the monitor's web-based user interface.

aws_deadline_queue.allowed_storage_profi.text: Specifies the list of storage profile IDs that are allowed to be used by this Deadline Cloud queue for job attachments.

aws_deadline_queue.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Deadline queue, used for IAM policies and API operations.

aws_deadline_queue.default_budget_action.text: Specifies the action Deadline takes when the queue's budget limit is exceeded, with valid values NONE and STOP_SCHEDULING_AND_CANCEL_JOBS.

aws_deadline_queue.description.text: A human-readable description of the queue, used to provide context about the queue's purpose or contents in AWS Deadline Cloud.

aws_deadline_queue.display_name.text: The user-friendly display name of the Deadline Cloud queue, used to identify it in the AWS console and API.

aws_deadline_queue.farm_id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS Deadline Cloud farm to which this queue belongs and is associated.

aws_deadline_queue.job_attachment_settin.text: Configures the S3 bucket and root prefix where job attachments for the queue are stored.
Specifies the S3 key prefix (within the job attachment S3 bucket) that serves as the root location for storing all job attachments for this queue.
The name of the S3 bucket that AWS Deadline Cloud uses to store job attachments for this queue.

aws_deadline_queue.job_run_as_user.text: Specifies the operating system user (and group for POSIX, or Windows user) that jobs submitted to this Deadline queue will run as, along with the run-as mode (USER or WORKER) that determines whether jobs use the queue-defined user or the worker's user.

aws_deadline_queue.job_run_as_user.posix.text: Configures the POSIX user and group under which jobs in this Deadline queue run.
The POSIX group name or ID used to run jobs in the queue.
The POSIX user name that jobs in this AWS Deadline queue will run as.

aws_deadline_queue.job_run_as_user.run_a.text: Specifies whether jobs run as the AWS-managed user or the queue-configured user, with valid values 'AWS_MANAGED_USER' and 'QUEUE_CONFIGURED_USER'.

aws_deadline_queue.job_run_as_user.windo.text: Specifies the Windows user account settings, including the user name and the ARN of the password stored in AWS Secrets Manager, that Deadline Cloud uses to run jobs on Windows worker nodes in this queue.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the password for the Windows user that jobs will run as on this queue.
The Windows user account name that jobs submitted to this AWS Deadline queue will run as on Windows worker nodes.

aws_deadline_queue.queue_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS Deadline Cloud to the queue when it is created, used to reference the queue in other operations and resources.

aws_deadline_queue.required_file_system_.text: Specifies the names of file system locations that must be available and mounted for jobs in this Deadline Cloud queue to run.

aws_deadline_queue.role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that the queue assumes to access AWS resources such as S3 buckets.

aws_deadline_queue.scheduling_configurat.text: Specifies the priority-balanced scheduling settings for the queue, which allocate worker capacity based on job priority while preventing starvation of lower-priority jobs.
Specifies the number of rendering tasks to buffer in the queue scheduler for workers, helping to minimize idle time and improve rendering throughput.
Determines whether the queue schedules jobs using priority-based ordering (true) or first-in, first-out (FIFO) ordering (false).
Specifies the weighted-balanced scheduling mode for the queue, which distributes jobs to workers proportionally based on assigned weights to maintain balanced resource utilization.
Defines the relative weight given to the error rate metric when the weighted balanced scheduling type scores and orders jobs in the queue's scheduling policy.
Specifies the maximum priority value a job can be assigned in the queue's weighted balanced scheduling, overriding any higher priority requested by the job to cap job precedence.
When set to true, ensures that the highest-priority job in the queue is always scheduled first, even under weighted balanced scheduling.
Specifies the relative priority weight that the weighted balanced scheduling configuration uses to determine how jobs in this queue are allocated workers compared to other queues.
For weighted balanced scheduling, the rendering task buffer sets the number of rendering tasks prefetched for each worker to reduce idle time and latency.
Sets the relative scheduling weight for rendering tasks within a weighted-balanced queue scheduling configuration, influencing the proportion of rendering tasks the service assigns.

The submission_time_weight field sets the relative weight applied to a job's submission time when the queue uses weighted balanced scheduling, so a higher value makes older submissions more strongly prioritized.

aws_deadline_queue.tags.key.text: The key portion of a tag assigned to the AWS Deadline queue, used to categorize, identify, and manage the queue resource.

aws_deadline_queue.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag key attached to the AWS Deadline queue resource.

aws_deadline_queue_environment.farm_id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS Deadline Cloud farm that this queue environment is associated with.

aws_deadline_queue_environment.name.text: The name of the queue environment, which is derived from the `name` field defined in the environment's template content (YAML or JSON).

aws_deadline_queue_environment.priority.text: Controls the order in which this queue environment is applied relative to other queue environments associated with the same queue, with the priority value used to rank the environments.

aws_deadline_queue_environment.queue_env.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS Deadline to this queue environment resource.

aws_deadline_queue_environment.queue_id.text: The unique identifier of the Deadline queue that this environment is associated with, used to scope the environment to a specific queue.

aws_deadline_queue_environment.template.text: Defines the queue environment's setup as a structured string (typically JSON), specifying environment variables and script actions that run for jobs using this queue environment.

aws_deadline_queue_environment.template_.text: Specifies the template format for the queue environment, either JSON or YAML.

aws_deadline_queue_fleet_association.far.text: The unique identifier of the AWS Deadline Cloud farm that contains the queue and fleet being associated.

aws_deadline_queue_fleet_association.fle.text: The unique identifier of the fleet that is associated with the queue in AWS Deadline Cloud.

aws_deadline_queue_fleet_association.que.text: The unique identifier of the Deadline queue to associate with the fleet, linking the queue to the specified fleet.

aws_deadline_queue_limit_association.far.text: The unique identifier of the farm that contains the queue and limit to be associated.

aws_deadline_queue_limit_association.lim.text: The unique identifier of the Deadline Cloud limit to associate with the queue.

aws_deadline_queue_limit_association.que.text: The unique identifier of the Deadline Cloud queue that is associated with the specified limit.

aws_deadline_storage_profile.display_nam.text: The human-readable name of the storage profile, used to identify it in the Deadline Cloud console and API.

aws_deadline_storage_profile.farm_id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS Deadline Cloud farm to which this storage profile belongs.

aws_deadline_storage_profile.file_system.text: Defines the list of file system locations (each consisting of a name and a mount path) that this storage profile makes available to worker instances for accessing job data.
The user-defined name for a file system location in the AWS Deadline Cloud storage profile, used to identify the shared or local storage path.
The absolute filesystem path (e.g., a mount point or drive letter) on the worker where the file system location referenced by this storage profile entry is accessible.

In an AWS Deadline Cloud storage profile, each file system location's `type` indicates whether the location represents a shared file system (accessible to all workers) or a local file system (strictly for a single worker).

aws_deadline_storage_profile.os_family.text: Specifies the operating system family (such as WINDOWS or LINUX) that this AWS Deadline Cloud storage profile is configured for.

aws_deadline_storage_profile.storage_pro.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS Deadline Cloud to this storage profile.

aws_deadline_worker.tags.key.text: The key for a tag to assign to the AWS Deadline Worker resource, allowing you to categorize and manage workers in AWS Deadline Cloud.

aws_deadline_worker.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag applied to an AWS Deadline Worker, used to attach custom metadata such as environment or project labels to the worker resource.

aws_detective_graph.tags.text: The list of tags to attach to the Detective graph, where each tag consists of a key and a value to help organize, identify, and manage the resource.

aws_detective_graph.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Detective graph, used to organize, identify, and manage access to the graph through resource-level permissions and cost allocation.

aws_detective_graph.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS Detective graph, used to categorize, manage, and control access to the graph alongside other AWS resources.

aws_dev_ops_agent_agent_space.operator_a.text: In an AWS::DevOpsAgent::AgentSpace, the `operator_app.iam` field defines the IAM role and permission settings the operator application uses to securely access AWS resources on behalf of the agent space.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM Identity Center (IdC) instance used by the operator application in the agent space for its identity configuration.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the operator application assumes within the AWS IAM Identity Center (IDC) configuration for the agent space.

aws_dev_ops_guru_notification_channel.co.text: The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic that DevOps Guru publishes notification messages to for this channel.

aws_dev_ops_guru_resource_collection.res.text: The tag key (AppBoundaryKey) that DevOps Guru uses to define the application boundary for selecting which tagged AWS resources are included in the resource collection.
Specifies the list of tag values for the tag key in the parent `tags` filter, used to match which AWS resources are included in the DevOps Guru resource collection.

aws_direct_connect_connection.tags.value.text: Specifies the value for a tag assigned to the Direct Connect connection, used to store arbitrary metadata or cost-allocation information.

aws_direct_connect_direct_connect_gatewa.text: The key of a tag assigned to the Direct Connect gateway, used to categorize and identify the resource.
Specifies the value of a tag key attached to the Direct Connect gateway, used for identifying and categorizing the gateway resource.

aws_direct_connect_lag.tags.key.text: Specifies the key of a tag attached to the AWS Direct Connect LAG, used for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization.

aws_direct_connect_lag.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to the Direct Connect LAG, used for metadata and resource management.

aws_direct_connect_private_virtual_inter.text: The IP address family (ipv4 or ipv6) used for the BGP session on this Direct Connect private virtual interface.
Specifies the IP address on the Amazon side of the BGP peering session for this BGP peer.
The autonomous system number (ASN) for the customer's BGP peer on the private virtual interface.
The MD5 authentication key (BGP password) used for BGP peering on this Direct Connect private virtual interface.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the BGP peer configured on this Direct Connect private virtual interface.
The customer_address specifies the IP address on the customer's side of the BGP peering session for a private virtual interface in AWS Direct Connect.
The key of a tag attached to the Direct Connect private virtual interface, used to identify the tag in a key-value pair.

aws_direct_connect_public_virtual_interf.text: The IP address family (IPv4 or IPv6) to use for the BGP peer on this Direct Connect public virtual interface.
The public IP address assigned to the Amazon side of the BGP session for this peer on the Direct Connect public virtual interface.
The autonomous system number (ASN) of the BGP peer for this Direct Connect public virtual interface.
Specifies the BGP MD5 authentication key (BGP password) required for establishing the BGP session with this Direct Connect peer.
The BGP peer ID is a unique identifier assigned by AWS Direct Connect to this BGP peer when it is created on the public virtual interface.
The customer-side IP address for this BGP peer, used as the BGP endpoint on the customer's router for the public virtual interface.
Specifies the key of a tag to apply to the AWS Direct Connect public virtual interface for managing and categorizing the resource.
The value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to the AWS Direct Connect public virtual interface, used to organize or identify the resource.

aws_direct_connect_transit_virtual_inter.text: The address family (IPv4 or IPv6) used for the BGP session on the transit virtual interface.
The IPv4 address on the Amazon side of the BGP peering session for a Direct Connect transit virtual interface, used to establish BGP connectivity with the customer's router.
The autonomous system number (ASN) of the BGP peer used to establish the BGP session for the transit virtual interface.
The MD5 authentication key used for BGP peering on this transit virtual interface, enabling authenticated BGP sessions with the on-premises router.
The AWS-assigned unique identifier for the BGP peer configured on the transit virtual interface, used to reference the peer in Direct Connect API operations.
The IP address assigned to the customer's side of the BGP session for this transit virtual interface.
The key of a tag (e.g., 'Name') applied to the Direct Connect Transit Virtual Interface, used to filter, organize, and control access to the resource.
The value component of a tag applied to this AWS Direct Connect transit virtual interface, used for arbitrary metadata such as cost allocation or ownership.

aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.alias.text: The DNS alias automatically generated by AWS for the Microsoft Active Directory, used to uniquely identify the directory when connecting to it.

aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.creat.text: If set to true, AWS Directory Service creates a public alias for the Microsoft AD directory (used in the directory's access URL), and when omitted the default is true.

aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.dns_i.text: The automatically assigned IP addresses of the DNS servers for the Microsoft Active Directory directory, returned by AWS.

aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.editi.text: Specifies the edition of the Microsoft Active Directory, either Standard (default) or Enterprise, which determines the directory's feature set and scaling capabilities.

aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.enabl.text: Enables single sign-on (SSO) for the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory, allowing users to access supported applications using their existing Active Directory credentials.

aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory, assigned by AWS upon creation.

aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.name.text: The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) for the Microsoft Active Directory, such as corp.example.com.

aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.passw.text: The password for the directory administrator account, which must meet the complexity and length requirements for AWS Managed Microsoft AD.

aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.short.text: Specifies the short name (NetBIOS name) of the Active Directory domain, which is a single-label name that can be used in place of the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) when referring to the domain.

aws_directory_service_microsoft_ad.vpc_s.text: Specifies the VPC and subnets (two in different Availability Zones) where the Microsoft AD directory is deployed.
The identifiers of two subnets in different Availability Zones where the directory's domain controllers will be deployed.
The ID of the VPC in which the Microsoft Active Directory is created.

aws_directory_service_simple_ad.tags.text: A list of tag objects (each with a Key and Value) to associate with the AWS Directory Service Simple AD directory, enabling cost allocation, access control, and resource identification.

aws_directory_service_simple_ad.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the Simple AD directory resource.

aws_directory_service_simple_ad.vpc_sett.text: Specifies the VPC configuration for the Simple AD directory, including the VPC ID and the subnets where the directory's domain controllers are deployed.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this DLM lifecycle policy.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.copy_tags.text: Indicates whether to copy tags from the source EBS volume to the snapshots created by this lifecycle policy.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.create_interval.text: The interval (in hours or days) between automatic EBS snapshot creations for a schedule in the DLM lifecycle policy, controlled by the associated interval unit.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.cross_region_co.text: Defines the destination regions and their encryption configurations (including optional KMS key ARN) to which snapshots or AMIs created by this DLM lifecycle policy are copied.
The destination AWS region to which the policy copies snapshots or AMIs as part of its cross-region copy action.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.description.text: A user-provided descriptive text that identifies the purpose and details of the DLM lifecycle policy, helping to distinguish it from other policies in the AWS account.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.exclusions.text: Specifies the tags and resource types that exclude matching resources from the lifecycle policy, preventing automatic snapshots or AMI creation for those resources.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.exclusions.excl.text: When true, the lifecycle policy excludes boot volumes from its snapshot schedules, preventing snapshots from being created for EC2 instance boot volumes.
The list of key-value tag pairs that, when matched on a resource, cause that resource to be excluded from the lifecycle policy.
The tag key that, when present on a resource, excludes that resource from the DLM lifecycle policy's actions.
The tag value that, when paired with the corresponding tag key in an exclusion filter, causes matching resources to be excluded from the lifecycle policy's actions.
Specifies the EBS volume types (for example, gp2 or io1) that should be excluded from the lifecycle policy's snapshot or AMI creation actions.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.execution_role_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that AWS Data Lifecycle Manager assumes to create snapshots and manage the lifecycle of the target resources.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the DLM lifecycle policy.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details.text: This object defines the core configuration of the DLM lifecycle policy, specifying the resource type (e.g., EBS snapshots or AMIs), target resource tags, state, and the schedules with their associated actions, such as creating, retaining, and deleting snapshots or AMIs.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.policy_details..text: Specifies the list of actions, each containing a name and cross-Region copy settings, that an event-based DLM lifecycle policy executes when its configured event is triggered.
Specifies the cross-Region copy action parameters that define how snapshots or AMIs are copied from the source Region to one or more target Regions as part of the lifecycle policy's action.

Specifies the encryption settings for snapshot copies created by the cross-region copy action, including whether the copied snapshots are encrypted and the ARN of the AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) to use for encryption.
The ARN of the AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) used to encrypt snapshots copied to the destination region, defaulting to the region's default EBS encryption key if not specified.
Whether the cross-Region snapshot copies are encrypted, which when true uses the specified KMS key or an AWS managed key.

Specifies the retention rule for snapshots copied to the target region, defining either a retention interval (value and unit such as days, weeks, months, or years) or a maximum count of snapshots to retain.
Specifies the retention period value for cross-region copied snapshots or AMIs, which combined with interval_unit determines how long they are kept in the destination region.
Specifies the unit of time (DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, or YEARS) for the retention interval of the cross-region copy action in the lifecycle policy.
The AWS Region to which the resource is copied by this cross-region copy action in the DLM lifecycle policy.
Identifies the type of action to be performed by the DLM lifecycle policy, such as 'cross-region-copy', which determines the operation executed on the target resources.
Indicates whether to copy all user-defined tags from the source snapshot to the target snapshots created by the lifecycle policy.

The create_interval determines how often the Data Lifecycle Manager policy creates snapshots or AMIs, specified in hours for EBS snapshot policies (1–24) and in days for EBS-backed AMI policies (1–7).
Defines the list of destination Regions to which snapshots or AMIs are copied, along with per-target encryption and retention settings.
The AWS region code to which the lifecycle policy copies snapshots as part of a cross-region copy target configuration.

Defines the event source that triggers an event-based lifecycle policy, such as a CloudWatch Events rule, including its type (e.g., MANAGED_CWS_EVENT) and parameters like event type and snapshot owner.

The parameters object of an event source in a DLM lifecycle policy, used when the event source type is MANAGED_CWE, contains a description that identifies the CloudWatch Events rule that triggers the event-based policy.
A regular expression used to match the description of snapshots to trigger this event-based DLM lifecycle policy.
Specifies the type of event that triggers this event-based lifecycle policy, with `shareSnapshot` being the only supported value, meaning the policy runs when a snapshot is shared with your account.
Specifies the AWS account IDs of the snapshot owners that can trigger the lifecycle policy when an event occurs (e.g., shared snapshot event) for an event-driven DLM policy.
Specifies the type of event source for an event-based DLM lifecycle policy, where the only valid value is MANAGED_CWL to use Amazon CloudWatch Events.

Defines the exclusions for the lifecycle policy, which identify specific resources or resource types (such as volumes with certain tags or specific volume types) that should not be affected by the policy.
Indicates whether the Data Lifecycle Manager policy excludes boot volumes from all snapshot and AMI creation actions, so that boot volumes are not affected by the policy's lifecycle rules.
Defines tag key-value pairs that identify resources to exclude from the lifecycle policy's actions, such as snapshot or AMI creation.
The key of a tag that identifies resources to be excluded from the lifecycle policy's actions.
Specifies the tag value for a tag-based exclusion rule, which excludes resources that have this tag value from the lifecycle policy.
Specifies the list of EBS volume types (e.g., 'gp2', 'io1', 'gp3') to exclude from the lifecycle policy, so the policy does not apply to or create snapshots for volumes of those types.
Specifies optional parameters, such as ExcludeBootVolume or NoReboot, that modify the behavior of the lifecycle policy's snapshot creation operations.
Indicates whether the boot volume of the instance is excluded from the EBS snapshots created by this lifecycle policy when the policy targets instances.
A list of tag filters (key-value pairs) that identifies data volumes to exclude from the lifecycle policy's snapshot or AMI creation actions.
The tag key used to identify data volumes to exclude from the lifecycle policy's snapshot management.

The value portion of a key-value pair in the exclude data volume tags list, used to match an Amazon EBS volume tag and exclude that volume from the lifecycle policy's snapshot or AMI creation actions.
Indicates whether to skip rebooting the instance when creating snapshots, so a value of true prevents the typical reboot that occurs during snapshot creation.
Specifies the policy language format, either SIMPLIFIED or STANDARD, which determines how resource types and actions are expressed in the policy.

Specifies the type of lifecycle policy, which can be EBS_SNAPSHOT_MANAGEMENT to manage EBS snapshots, IMAGE_MANAGEMENT to manage EBS-backed AMIs, or EVENT_BASED to trigger on Amazon CloudWatch events.
Specifies the target resource locations for the lifecycle policy, allowing values like 'CLOUD' for resources in the AWS cloud and 'OUTPOST' for resources on an AWS Outpost.
Specifies the type of AWS resource (either 'VOLUME' or 'INSTANCE') that a DLM lifecycle policy targets, determining whether the policy creates EBS snapshots or AMIs.
The types of resources (such as VOLUME or INSTANCE) that this lifecycle policy will manage and snapshot.
Defines the schedule(s) that specify when to create Amazon EBS snapshots (or AMIs) and how long to retain them under this lifecycle policy.
Defines the archive rule for this schedule, specifying how long snapshots are retained in the Amazon EBS Archive tier (e.g., the number of days to keep them archived) before deletion.
Specifies the retention duration for archived snapshots created by the containing archive rule, defining how long they are kept before being expired.
Specifies the retention period for snapshots stored in the archive tier, either as a count of snapshots or as an interval with a unit (e.g., days), after which they expire.
The number of snapshots to retain in the archive storage tier.
Specifies the numeric value for how long snapshots are retained in the archive tier before deletion, paired with the interval_unit property to define the unit of time (e.g., days, weeks).
Specifies the unit of time (e.g., DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, YEARS) for the retention period of snapshots in the archive tier, used with the retention_archive_tier.interval value.
Copies all user-defined tags from the source snapshot to the snapshots created by this schedule.
Defines when the schedule triggers resource creation (e.g., EBS snapshots or AMIs), typically via a recurring interval or a cron expression.
The cron expression that specifies when this create rule triggers snapshot or AMI creation in the DLM lifecycle policy.

Specifies how often the lifecycle policy creates snapshots; for example, a value of 12 with an interval_unit of 'hours' creates snapshots every 12 hours, and it must be paired with the interval_unit property to define the schedule frequency.
For the create rule of a schedule, this field sets the time unit (HOURS or DAYS) that the interval value uses to control how often AWS Data Lifecycle Manager creates snapshots or AMIs.
Specifies whether the lifecycle policy creates snapshots of resources in the AWS Cloud (CLOUD) or on AWS Outposts (OUTPOST).
Determines whether the DLM lifecycle policy should proceed with the snapshot creation operation even if this script fails to execute successfully.

Specifies the ARN of the AWS Lambda function or the name of an AWS Systems Manager document that acts as the execution handler for the script configured in this DLM lifecycle policy schedule, enabling custom pre-snapshot or post-snapshot actions.
Specifies the AWS service that executes the script (for example, AWS Systems Manager) when the create rule triggers snapshot creation in a DLM lifecycle policy.

Sets the maximum time in seconds that AWS Data Lifecycle Manager waits for the script (a Systems Manager automation document) to finish executing before declaring the pre/post snapshot action a failure, applied per script in the create rule of the lifecycle policy schedule.
Specifies the maximum number of times AWS DLM will retry a script (defined in the schedule's create rule) after it fails before marking the script execution as failed.
Specifies the stage(s) during the EBS snapshot creation process at which the script should run, with allowed values 'pre' and 'post'.
Specifies the times in UTC (formatted as HH:00) at which the lifecycle policy creates snapshots according to this schedule.
Configures the rules for copying snapshots to other AWS Regions as part of this schedule, including destination region, encryption, and retention settings.
The ARN of the AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) used to encrypt the EBS snapshots or AMIs copied to the target region under this cross-region copy rule in the DLM lifecycle policy.
Indicates whether to copy all user-defined tags from the source EBS snapshot (or AMI) to the cross-region copied snapshot (or AMI).
Specifies the interval and interval unit after which the cross-region copied AMIs are deprecated in the target Region.

The numeric length of the time period (with units set in the sibling `interval_unit` field) after which copied AMIs in the target Region are deprecated according to this cross-region copy deprecate rule.
The unit of time (e.g., days, weeks, months, or years) that, together with the interval value, determines how long the copied AMI is retained in the target region before it is deprecated.
Specifies whether snapshots copied to the target region by this cross-region copy rule are encrypted.

Defines the retention behavior for snapshots copied to the destination region, specifying either a time-based interval (with unit such as days, weeks, months, or years) or a maximum count of snapshots to retain.
The number of interval units (as specified by the associated interval_unit) to retain cross-Region copied snapshots in the target Region before they are deleted.
The unit of time used with the retention interval to specify how long cross-region snapshot copies are retained in the target region, such as days, weeks, months, or years.
The destination AWS Region to which the snapshot or AMI is copied, specified as a Region name (e.g., us-east-1) in the cross-Region copy rule.
The destination AWS Region to which snapshots or AMIs are copied by this cross-Region copy rule.
Defines when AMIs created by this schedule are automatically deprecated, either by specifying a maximum retained count or a time-based interval (e.g., days) after which the AMI is deprecated.
The maximum number of AMIs to retain; when this count is exceeded, the oldest AMIs are deprecated by the lifecycle policy.
The number of time units (as specified by the associated interval_unit field) after which the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) is deprecated in this lifecycle policy's deprecation rule.
The unit of time (DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, or YEARS) used with the interval to determine how long to wait before deprecating the AMI in this schedule's deprecate rule.

Configures the fast snapshot restore rule for this schedule, specifying the Availability Zones in which to enable fast snapshot restore and the number of snapshots (or time interval) for which fast restore is retained, allowing EBS snapshots to be restored quickly in those zones.
Specifies the list of Availability Zones in which to enable fast snapshot restore for snapshots created by this schedule.
Specifies the Availability Zones in which fast snapshot restore is enabled for snapshots created by this schedule.
The number of snapshots to enable Fast Snapshot Restore on for this schedule's fast restore rule in the DLM lifecycle policy.

Specifies the interval number, paired with the interval unit, that determines how frequently the lifecycle policy enables fast snapshot restore for snapshots taken under this schedule, used as an alternative to the count parameter.
The unit of time (DAYS or WEEKS) for the interval during which snapshots created by this schedule will have fast snapshot restore enabled.
The name of the DLM lifecycle policy schedule, which must be unique among all schedules in the policy and is used to reference the schedule in associated tags and rules.
Specifies the retention rule for snapshots or AMIs created by this schedule, controlling whether to keep a maximum count or retain for a specific interval (in days or years) before deletion.
Specifies the maximum number of snapshots to retain for the policy schedule when the retain rule is based on a count, after which the oldest snapshots are deleted.
The number of intervals (measured in the unit specified by the sibling field interval_unit) that snapshots or AMIs are retained by this lifecycle policy schedule before they are deleted.
Specifies the unit of time (DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, or YEARS) used with the retain rule's interval value to determine how long snapshots created by this schedule are retained.
Specifies the rules for sharing snapshots created by this schedule with other AWS accounts, including target account IDs and the interval for unsharing them.
Specifies the AWS account IDs to which snapshots created by this schedule are shared, as defined in the share rules of the lifecycle policy.
Specifies the numeric interval, paired with the associated unit, after which DLM automatically unshares snapshots or AMIs that were shared with the target accounts in this share rule.
The unit of time (DAYS or WEEKS) used with the unshare interval to determine how frequently snapshots are unshared from other accounts in the lifecycle policy's share rule.
Specifies the tags to apply to the snapshots or AMIs created by this schedule, allowing you to organize and identify the resources created by the lifecycle policy.
The key of a tag to be added to resources created by this lifecycle policy schedule, such as snapshots or AMIs, where the corresponding value is specified in the adjacent value field.
The value for a custom tag that AWS Data Lifecycle Manager applies to the snapshots or AMIs created by this schedule.

Specifies a list of tags with variable placeholders that are applied to the snapshots or AMIs created when the schedule triggers, where tag values can use DLM-supported variables such as $(instance-id), $(timestamp), or $(uuid) and are replaced with actual resource information at execution time.

The tag key for a variable tag entry that DLM attaches to snapshots or AMIs created by this schedule, where the corresponding value can contain dynamic variables such as $(instance-id) or $(timestamp).

This string defines the value of a variable tag applied to snapshots or AMIs created by the schedule, and may contain DLM-supported placeholders such as ${instance-id} or ${timestamp} to dynamically populate the tag value from the source resource or event time.
Tags that identify the resources the lifecycle policy will manage; the policy applies to resources that have all these tags.
The tag key used to identify resources that the lifecycle policy should target.
The tag value used together with the corresponding key in policy_details.target_tags to identify the resources that the lifecycle policy will manage for snapshot or AMI creation.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.retain_interval.text: The numeric interval for retaining snapshots in a DLM lifecycle policy schedule, working with `retain_interval_unit` to define the duration (e.g., number of days, weeks, months, or years).

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.state.text: Specifies whether the lifecycle policy is set to ENABLED or DISABLED, controlling whether the policy is active and can create snapshots.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.tags.text: This field defines the user-defined tags to attach to the lifecycle policy, which can be used to organize, identify, and manage the policy through cost allocation and resource tagging.

aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy.tags.value.text: The value for a tag key assigned to the Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager lifecycle policy, used to categorize, identify, or manage access to the policy.

aws_dms_data_migration.data_migration_se.text: Specifies the execution settings for the data migration, including the number of parallel jobs to run (NumberOfJobs) and the JSON selection rules that determine which database objects are included in the migration.

aws_dms_data_migration.source_data_setti.text: Specifies the position in the source database's transaction log (such as binary log) from which AWS DMS starts reading changes when using change data capture (CDC) for the data migration.
The timestamp (in the source database's timezone) from which change data capture (CDC) begins for ongoing replication in the data migration.
Specifies the UTC timestamp at which Change Data Capture (CDC) stops collecting incremental changes from the source database for this data migration.
Specifies the name of the PostgreSQL replication slot that DMS uses to capture change data for ongoing replication (change data capture) from the source database.

aws_dms_data_migration.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS DMS data migration resource, used for categorizing, cost tracking, and access control.

aws_dms_data_migration.tags.value.text: Specifies the value of a tag attached to the DMS data migration resource, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_dms_data_provider.settings.doc_db_se.text: The ARN of the certificate used for secure TLS/SSL connection to the Amazon DocumentDB database when the data provider connects.
The name of the DocumentDB database to which the DMS data provider connects for data migration.
The port number used to connect to the DocumentDB instance.
The hostname or cluster endpoint of the Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) database that this DMS data provider uses to connect for migration.
Specifies the SSL/TLS mode used when connecting to the DocumentDB cluster, with allowed values including none, require, verify-ca, and verify-full.

aws_dms_data_provider.settings.ibm_db2_l.text: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the certificate used to secure connections to the IBM Db2 LUW database for this AWS DMS data provider.
The name of the IBM Db2 LUW database that the data provider connects to.
TCP port number on which the IBM Db2 LUW database listens for connections, required when configuring an IBM Db2 LUW data provider for AWS DMS.
The hostname or IP address of the IBM Db2 LUW database server that the data provider connects to.
Defines the SSL encryption and certificate verification mode used when connecting to the IBM Db2 LUW database.

aws_dms_data_provider.settings.ibm_db2z_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an SSL/TLS certificate that is used to encrypt and verify connections to the IBM Db2 for z/OS database associated with this DMS data provider.
Specifies the database name to use when connecting to the IBM Db2 for z/OS instance for this DMS data provider.
The TCP port number used to connect to the IBM Db2 for z/OS database.
The host name or IP address of the IBM Db2 for z/OS server that this DMS data provider connects to.
Specifies the SSL/TLS connection mode used when connecting to the IBM Db2 for z/OS database, such as requiring encryption or verifying the server certificate.

aws_dms_data_provider.settings.maria_db_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the certificate used for SSL/TLS encryption when connecting to the MariaDB database as a DMS data provider.
The TCP port number on which the MariaDB server listens for incoming connections.
The hostname or IP address of the MariaDB database server that the data provider connects to.
Specifies the SSL mode used for connections to the MariaDB database, with values such as none, require, verify-ca, or verify-full.

aws_dms_data_provider.settings.microsoft.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SSL/TLS certificate used to encrypt connections to the Microsoft SQL Server database.
Specifies the name of the Microsoft SQL Server database to be used by the data provider.
Specifies the TCP port number on which the Microsoft SQL Server database is listening for connections.
The hostname or IP address of the Microsoft SQL Server database that serves as the data provider source.
Specifies the SSL mode used when connecting to the Microsoft SQL Server database, controlling whether the connection is encrypted and whether the server certificate is verified.

aws_dms_data_provider.settings.mongo_db_.text: Specifies the MongoDB authentication mechanism used when connecting to the database, with valid values including 'default', 'mongodb_cr', and 'scram_sha_1'.
The name of the MongoDB authentication database (authSource) that contains the user credentials used when connecting to the source database.
Specifies the authentication type used when connecting to the MongoDB data source, such as NONE or PASSWORD.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the certificate used for SSL/TLS encryption when connecting to the MongoDB database.
The name of the MongoDB database that the DMS data provider uses for connections and migrations.
The TCP port number on which the MongoDB source database is listening for connections.
The hostname or IP address of the MongoDB server to connect to for this data provider.
Specifies the SSL mode used when connecting to the MongoDB data provider, such as 'none', 'require', 'verify-ca', or 'verify-full'.

aws_dms_data_provider.settings.my_sql_se.text: The ARN of a certificate authority (CA) or SSL/TLS certificate used to verify or encrypt the connection to the MySQL database when a secure connection is configured.
The TCP port number the MySQL data provider uses to connect to the MySQL database.
The hostname or IP address of the MySQL server that the data provider connects to.
Defines the SSL/TLS enforcement level for connections to the MySQL data provider, with valid values such as none, require, verify-ca, and verify-full to control encryption and certificate validation.

aws_dms_data_provider.settings.oracle_se.text: Specifies the hostname or IP address of the Oracle Automatic Storage Management (ASM) server that the DMS data provider connects to for Oracle database settings.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the certificate used to encrypt connections to the Oracle database when SSL/TLS is enabled.
Specifies the Oracle database name (SID or service name) that the AWS DMS data provider uses to connect to the Oracle source database.
The TCP port number used to connect to the Oracle database.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS DMS uses to access Oracle Automatic Storage Management (ASM) credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager for the Oracle data provider.
The identifier of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the Oracle ASM credentials used for this data provider's Oracle settings.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS DMS uses to access the AWS Secrets Manager secret storing the Oracle database encryption key, enabling DMS to decrypt the Oracle database data.

Specifies the AWS Secrets Manager secret identifier (ARN or name) that stores the Oracle database security encryption password, used by the DMS data provider to authenticate and access the encrypted Oracle data source.
The host name or IP address of the Oracle database server that this data provider connects to.
Specifies the SSL mode (e.g., none, require, verify-ca, verify-full) for connections to the Oracle data provider, controlling whether and how TLS encryption and certificate verification are applied.

aws_dms_data_provider.settings.postgre_s.text: The ARN of the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate used to securely connect to the PostgreSQL database when SSL/TLS is enabled for the data provider.
The name of the PostgreSQL database that this DMS data provider connects to and manages metadata for.
The TCP port number on which the PostgreSQL database server accepts connections.
Specifies the host name or IP address of the PostgreSQL server that the data provider connects to.
Specifies the SSL mode to use when connecting to the PostgreSQL database, such as 'none', 'require', 'verify-ca', or 'verify-full'.

aws_dms_data_provider.settings.redshift_.text: The name of the Redshift database that the AWS DMS data provider connects to.
The TCP port number used to connect to the Amazon Redshift data provider (default is 5439).
The hostname or IP address of the Amazon Redshift server that the DMS data provider connects to.

aws_dms_data_provider.settings.sybase_as.text: The ARN of the certificate used to encrypt connections between the DMS data provider and the Sybase ASE database via SSL/TLS.
The name of the Sybase ASE database to which the data provider connects.
Indicates whether the password for the Sybase ASE database is encrypted in the data provider settings.
The TCP port number used to connect to the Sybase Adaptive Server Enterprise database.
The hostname or IP address of the Sybase Adaptive Server Enterprise (ASE) database server to which the data provider connects.
Determines the SSL mode for the Sybase ASE data provider connection, specifying whether SSL is enforced and how the server certificate is verified.

aws_dms_data_provider.tags.key.text: The tag key for a tag attached to the AWS DMS data provider, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_dms_data_provider.tags.value.text: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the DMS Data Provider, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_dms_endpoint.tags.key.text: The key portion of a user-defined tag attached to the DMS endpoint, used for identifying and organizing the resource within AWS.

aws_dms_endpoint.tags.value.text: Specifies the value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS DMS endpoint.

aws_dms_event_subscription.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS DMS event subscription, used to categorize and identify the resource.

aws_dms_event_subscription.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS DMS event subscription.

aws_dms_migration_project.schema_convers.text: The S3 bucket path (prefix) where the AWS DMS Schema Conversion application stores schema conversion artifacts (such as converted schemas and mapping rules) for the migration project.

The ARN of the IAM role that AWS DMS assumes to access the S3 bucket used by the schema conversion application, enabling it to read and write schema conversion artifacts to the bucket specified by the sibling `s3_bucket_path` attribute.

aws_dms_migration_project.source_data_pr.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the source data provider used to configure the migration project in AWS Database Migration Service.
Specifies the unique identifier or ARN of the AWS DMS source data provider associated with this migration project.
The name of an existing AWS DMS data provider that acts as the source for this migration project, used within a source data provider descriptor.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS DMS assumes to access the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the source data provider's credentials.
Specifies the ARN or name of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the credentials for the source database in the migration project.

aws_dms_migration_project.tags.key.text: The key of a tag that can be assigned to an AWS DMS migration project, used for categorizing, identifying, and managing the project resource within the service.

aws_dms_migration_project.tags.value.text: The user-defined string value of a tag applied to an AWS DMS migration project, used to store metadata such as project purpose, owner, or environment for resource management and cost tracking.

aws_dms_migration_project.target_data_pr.text: The ARN of the AWS DMS data provider that acts as the target endpoint for the migration project.
In the list of target data provider descriptors for the migration project, specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the target data provider.
The name of the target data provider that the DMS migration project uses as its destination, referencing an existing AWS DMS data provider resource.
ARN of the IAM role that AWS DMS assumes to read the target data provider's connection credentials from AWS Secrets Manager.

The secrets_manager_secret_id within a target data provider descriptor specifies the AWS Secrets Manager secret (by name or ARN) that stores the connection details for the target database endpoint used by the DMS migration project.

aws_dms_replication_config.compute_confi.text: Specifies the Availability Zone (AZ) in which the AWS DMS replication instance associated with this replication config will be provisioned.
Specifies the custom DNS name servers (as a comma-separated list of IP addresses) that the AWS DMS replication instance uses for name resolution.
The ARN or ID of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt data on the storage attached to the AWS DMS replication instance.
The maximum number of DMS capacity units that the replication can scale to, defining the upper limit of compute capacity for the AWS DMS replication config.
Sets the minimum number of DMS capacity units to provision for a serverless replication, defining the lower bound for automatic scaling of compute resources.

Specifies whether to enable Multi-AZ deployment for the AWS DMS replication config's compute environment, providing high availability by provisioning a standby replica in a different Availability Zone.

Specifies the preferred weekly maintenance window (in UTC, format ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi) during which AWS Database Migration Service can perform maintenance on the replication services associated with this replication config.
The identifier of the AWS DMS replication subnet group in which the replication instance for this replication config is deployed.
Specifies the VPC security group IDs to associate with the compute configuration for the AWS DMS replication, controlling network access to the replication environment.

aws_dms_replication_config.tags.key.text: The key of a key-value tag that can be attached to the DMS replication configuration for resource management and cost allocation.

aws_dms_replication_config.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag assigned to the AWS DMS replication configuration, used for metadata, identification, and cost allocation.

aws_dms_replication_instance.allocated_s.text: Specifies the amount of storage (in gigabytes) to allocate for the AWS DMS replication instance.

aws_dms_replication_instance.allow_major.text: Indicates whether major version upgrades are allowed for the replication instance, and must be set to true to permit such upgrades when the engine version is changed.

aws_dms_replication_instance.auto_minor_.text: Indicates whether minor engine version upgrades are applied automatically to the replication instance during the maintenance window.

aws_dms_replication_instance.availabilit.text: Specifies the Availability Zone (AZ) in which the AWS DMS replication instance is created, influencing placement and failover behavior for Multi-AZ deployments.

aws_dms_replication_instance.dns_name_se.text: Specifies a comma-separated list of DNS name servers that the AWS DMS replication instance uses to resolve domain names for source and target endpoints.

aws_dms_replication_instance.engine_vers.text: Specifies the DMS engine version number to use for the replication instance, such as '3.4.4'.

aws_dms_replication_instance.id.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the DMS replication instance, generated by AWS and used as the unique Terraform resource identifier.

aws_dms_replication_instance.kms_key_id.text: This field specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or ID of an AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) used to encrypt the storage and data on the DMS replication instance, instead of the default AWS-managed key.

aws_dms_replication_instance.multi_az.text: Specifies whether the replication instance is deployed across multiple Availability Zones for high availability.

aws_dms_replication_instance.network_typ.text: Specifies whether the replication instance uses IPv4 only (ipv4) or dual-stack IPv4 and IPv6 (dual) for network connectivity.

aws_dms_replication_instance.preferred_m.text: Specifies the preferred time window (in the format ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi, e.g., 'sun:01:00-sun:02:00') during which AWS may perform maintenance on the replication instance.

aws_dms_replication_instance.publicly_ac.text: Whether the DMS replication instance is publicly accessible, meaning it receives a public IP address and can be reached from the internet, as opposed to being private within the VPC.

aws_dms_replication_instance.replication.text: The compute and memory capacity class for the replication instance, such as dms.t2.small or dms.c4.large, which determines the performance and cost of the instance.
Specifies a user-defined name for the replication instance, which must be unique within the AWS account and region and can include letters, numbers, and hyphens.
The list of private IP addresses assigned to the AWS Database Migration Service replication instance.
The public IP addresses assigned to the DMS replication instance when it is configured for public accessibility.
The identifier of an existing DMS replication subnet group that determines the VPC and subnets where the replication instance's network interfaces are placed.

aws_dms_replication_instance.tags.text: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) to associate with the DMS replication instance, which are used for cost allocation, access control, and identifying the resource in AWS.

aws_dms_replication_instance.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the AWS DMS replication instance, used to associate arbitrary metadata (e.g., environment, owner, or cost center) with the resource for management and cost allocation purposes.

aws_dms_replication_instance.vpc_securit.text: Specifies the VPC security group IDs to be associated with the DMS replication instance.

aws_dms_replication_subnet_group.tags.va.text: The value portion of a tag (key-value pair) assigned to the DMS replication subnet group, used to categorize and manage the resource for cost allocation and operational purposes.

aws_dms_replication_task.cdc_start_posit.text: Specifies the native source database position (such as a log file number or LSN) from which AWS DMS begins reading change data capture (CDC) changes when starting the replication task.
