aws_dms_replication_task.cdc_start_time.text: The Unix timestamp in seconds that specifies when Change Data Capture (CDC) should begin for the replication task, defining the starting point for capturing ongoing data changes.

aws_dms_replication_task.cdc_stop_positi.text: Specifies the point in time (as a Unix timestamp) or LSN (log sequence number) up to which the change data capture (CDC) portion of the replication task should process changes, after which the task stops.

aws_dms_replication_task.id.text: The ARN of the DMS replication task, which uniquely identifies it within AWS.

aws_dms_replication_task.migration_type.text: Specifies the migration type for the replication task, which can be one of 'full-load', 'cdc', or 'full-load-and-cdc'.

aws_dms_replication_task.replication_ins.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS DMS replication instance that will run the replication task.

aws_dms_replication_task.replication_tas.text: A user-supplied unique identifier for the DMS replication task within an AWS account, used to reference and manage the task in AWS DMS.
A JSON-format string that configures the AWS DMS replication task's operational settings, such as target table preparation mode, full load behavior, and error handling options.

aws_dms_replication_task.source_endpoint.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the source database endpoint that the DMS replication task reads data from during migration.

aws_dms_replication_task.table_mappings.text: JSON string that specifies table mapping rules, including selection and transformation rules, for a DMS replication task.

aws_dms_replication_task.tags.text: Assigns metadata key-value pairs to the DMS replication task for resource categorization and cost tracking.

aws_dms_replication_task.tags.key.text: Specifies the key of a tag attached to the AWS DMS replication task, used for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource.

aws_dms_replication_task.target_endpoint.text: The ARN of the target database endpoint that the replication task connects to for writing migrated data.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.availability_zones.text: The list of Availability Zones where the cluster's instances are distributed, enabling multi-AZ deployment for high availability.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.backup_retention_pe.text: The number of days for which automated backups of the DocumentDB cluster are retained.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.cluster_resource_id.text: The unique cluster resource identifier assigned by AWS when the DocDB cluster is created, used to construct the cluster ARN.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.copy_tags_to_snapsh.text: Indicates whether to copy all tags from the DB cluster to snapshots of the cluster, so that the snapshots inherit the cluster's tags.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.dbcluster_identifie.text: Specifies a unique identifier for the DB cluster, which is stored as a lowercase string and used as the cluster's name.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.dbcluster_parameter.text: The name of the DocumentDB cluster parameter group to associate with this DB cluster, which contains engine configuration values applied to all instances in the cluster.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.dbsubnet_group_name.text: The name of the DB subnet group the DocumentDB cluster uses, which must contain subnets in at least two Availability Zones.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.deletion_protection.text: When set to true, deletion protection is enabled for this DocumentDB cluster, preventing the cluster from being deleted via the AWS Management Console or API until deletion protection is explicitly disabled.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.enable_cloudwatch_l.text: Specifies the log types (for example, 'audit' or 'profiler') that the DocumentDB cluster exports to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.endpoint.text: The endpoint is the read-only primary connection hostname for the DocumentDB cluster, used to connect applications to the cluster's primary instance.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.engine_version.text: Specifies the version number of the database engine (e.g., '4.0', '5.0') to use for the DocumentDB cluster.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.global_cluster_iden.text: The identifier of the Amazon DocumentDB global cluster to which this DB cluster belongs, used to join a cluster to a global cluster that spans multiple regions.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.id.text: The cluster's unique identifier, which corresponds to the DB cluster's name as specified at creation time.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.kms_key_id.text: The AWS KMS key ID or ARN used to encrypt the storage for this DocumentDB cluster.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.manage_master_user_.text: Indicates whether the master user password is managed by AWS Secrets Manager, enabling automatic rotation and secure retrieval.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.master_user_passwor.text: The password for the master database user used to authenticate and manage the Amazon DocumentDB cluster, required when creating a new cluster unless you are restoring from a snapshot.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.master_user_secret_.text: The AWS KMS key identifier used to encrypt the master user password stored as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager, where omitting it defaults to the aws/secretsmanager key.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.master_username.text: The master username for the DocumentDB cluster, used to authenticate as the administrative user.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.network_type.text: Specifies the network type for the cluster, either IPV4 for IPv4 only or DUAL to support both IPv4 and IPv6 addressing.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.port.text: The port number on which the DocumentDB DB cluster accepts connections, defaulting to 27017.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.preferred_backup_wi.text: The daily time range, in UTC and 24-hour format (HH24:MI-HH24:MI), during which automated backups are created for the DocumentDB cluster.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.preferred_maintenan.text: The weekly time range (in UTC) during which system maintenance, such as patching, may occur on the Amazon DocumentDB cluster, specified in the format ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi (e.g., Mon:00:00-Mon:03:00).

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.read_endpoint.text: The reader endpoint for the DocumentDB cluster, which routes read connections to available replica instances.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.restore_to_time.text: Specifies the UTC time (in ISO 8601 format) to restore the DB cluster to, when performing a point-in-time restore.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.restore_type.text: Specifies the type of restore to perform when creating the DB cluster from a snapshot or point-in-time backup, with allowed values typically being 'full' or 'copy-on-write'.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.rotate_master_user_.text: Indicates whether to rotate the master user password for the DocumentDB cluster; enabling this triggers generation of a new password stored as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.serverless_v2_scali.text: Configures the minimum and maximum Amazon DocumentDB capacity units (ACUs) for a DocumentDB cluster running in Serverless v2 mode.
The maximum number of DocumentDB capacity units (DCUs) that the serverless v2 cluster can scale up to, setting the upper bound for compute and memory capacity.
The minimum capacity in Amazon Capacity Units (ACUs) that the DocumentDB Serverless v2 cluster can scale down to.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.snapshot_identifier.text: The identifier of an existing DB cluster snapshot to restore the cluster from when creating it.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.storage_encrypted.text: Indicates whether the DB cluster's storage is encrypted at rest, using AWS Key Management Service (KMS) keys.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.storage_type.text: Selects the storage configuration for the DocumentDB cluster, where 'standard' uses general-purpose SSD storage and 'iopt1' uses I/O-Optimized storage with dedicated IOPS pricing.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.tags.text: A list of key-value tags to attach to the DocumentDB cluster for identification and resource management.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.use_latest_restorab.text: When performing a point-in-time restore, this boolean determines whether to restore the DB cluster to the latest restorable time; if true, `restore_to_time` must be omitted, and a source cluster identifier is required.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster.vpc_security_group_.text: The list of VPC security group IDs to associate with the DocumentDB cluster, controlling which network security groups can access the cluster.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.des.text: A user-supplied description of the DB cluster parameter group, which is required when creating the group and helps identify its purpose.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.fam.text: The database engine family that this DocDB cluster parameter group applies to (e.g., 'docdb3.6' or 'docdb4.0'), which determines the set of parameters available for the cluster.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.id.text: The name of the DocumentDB cluster parameter group, which serves as its unique identifier.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.nam.text: The name of the DB cluster parameter group; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name for the group.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.par.text: The parameters block defines the individual parameters (name, value, and apply method) to associate with the DocumentDB cluster parameter group.

aws_doc_db_dbcluster_parameter_group.tag.text: A list of key-value pairs (tags) to assign to the DocumentDB DB cluster parameter group for resource categorization and management.
The key of a key-value tag attached to the DocumentDB cluster parameter group, used to identify and categorize the resource within AWS.
The value portion of a tag attached to the DocumentDB cluster parameter group, which together with the tag key forms a key-value label used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.auto_minor_version.text: Indicates whether minor engine version upgrades are applied automatically to the DB instance during its maintenance window.

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.availability_zone.text: Specifies the Availability Zone (AZ) where the Amazon DocumentDB DB instance is provisioned, for example, us-east-1a.

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.cacertificate_iden.text: Specifies the identifier of the CA certificate used for the DocumentDB DB instance's server certificate, allowing you to rotate the certificate used for TLS connections.

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.certificate_rotati.text: Whether the DocumentDB instance is restarted automatically when the CA certificate for the instance is rotated, allowing the new certificate to take effect without manual action.

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.dbcluster_identifi.text: The identifier of the DocumentDB cluster this instance will belong to, defining the cluster in which the instance is created and replicated.

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.dbinstance_class.text: The compute and memory capacity class of the Amazon DocumentDB instance (e.g., db.r5.large), which determines its performance characteristics and pricing.

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.dbinstance_identif.text: The user-supplied unique identifier for the DocumentDB DB instance, which must be unique within an AWS account and Region; if not provided, CloudFormation generates one automatically.

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.enable_performance.text: A boolean flag that when true enables Performance Insights, a database performance monitoring and tuning feature, for the Amazon DocumentDB DB instance.

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.endpoint.text: The endpoint address of the DocumentDB instance, providing the hostname used to connect to the database.

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.id.text: The unique identifier of the DocumentDB DB instance, matching the DB instance identifier.

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.port.text: The TCP port number, assigned by AWS, on which the DocumentDB instance accepts connections (for example, 27017).

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.preferred_maintena.text: Specifies the weekly time range (in UTC) during which Amazon DocumentDB performs system maintenance on this DB instance, using the format ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi (e.g., sun:05:00-sun:06:00).

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.tags.text: Specifies a list of tags (key-value pairs) to associate with the DocumentDB DB instance for categorization and access control.

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to assign to the DocumentDB DB instance, used for identifying and organizing the resource (for example, 'Name' or 'Environment').

aws_doc_db_dbinstance.tags.value.text: The user-defined value of a tag applied to the DocumentDB DB instance, used to store arbitrary metadata such as environment, cost center, or project for resource organization and management.

aws_doc_db_dbsubnet_group.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the Amazon DocumentDB DB subnet group, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the resource (e.g., via cost allocation or access control).

aws_doc_db_dbsubnet_group.tags.value.text: Specifies the value of a tag attached to the DocumentDB DB subnet group, used for metadata and cost allocation.

aws_doc_db_global_cluster.tags.key.text: The key portion of a user-defined tag attached to the Amazon DocumentDB global cluster, used for metadata, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_doc_db_global_cluster.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the DocumentDB global cluster.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.admin_user_nam.text: The administrative (master) username for the DocumentDB elastic cluster, used as the initial admin user for authentication.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.admin_user_pas.text: Password for the admin user account that is created to access the elastic cluster's database.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.auth_type.text: Specifies the authentication type for the cluster, indicating whether the admin password is supplied as plain text (PLAIN_TEXT) or via a Secrets Manager secret ARN (SECRET_ARN).

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.backup_retenti.text: Specifies the number of days that automatic backups of the Amazon DocumentDB elastic cluster are retained.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.cluster_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the DocumentDB elastic cluster.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.cluster_endpoi.text: The connection endpoint for the Amazon DocumentDB elastic cluster, used by applications to connect to the cluster.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.cluster_name.text: Specifies the name of the Amazon DocumentDB elastic cluster, which is used as a unique identifier for the cluster within your AWS account and region.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.kms_key_id.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt data at rest in the DocumentDB elastic cluster.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.preferred_back.text: Specifies the preferred daily time range, in UTC (format HH24:MI-HH24:MI), during which AWS automatically creates backups for the Amazon DocumentDB Elastic Cluster.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.preferred_main.text: The weekly time range (in UTC) during which system maintenance may occur for the DocumentDB elastic cluster, specified in the format ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi (e.g., Mon:01:00-Mon:02:00).

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.shard_capacity.text: The number of vCPUs allocated to each shard in the Amazon DocumentDB elastic cluster, defining the compute capacity per shard.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.shard_count.text: The desired number of shards for the Amazon DocumentDB elastic cluster, where each shard is an independent partition of the cluster's data and this value directly determines the cluster's storage and compute capacity.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.shard_instance.text: Specifies the number of instance nodes to provision for each shard in the DocumentDB elastic cluster, affecting shard high availability and failover behavior.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.subnet_ids.text: Specifies the VPC subnet IDs in which the Amazon DocumentDB Elastic Cluster's instances are deployed, determining the cluster's network placement within a VPC.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.tags.text: Specifies the key-value tags to associate with the DocumentDB Elastic Cluster for resource identification and management within AWS.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Amazon DocumentDB Elastic Cluster, enabling the resource to be categorized, identified, and filtered by user-defined metadata.

aws_doc_dbelastic_cluster.vpc_security_g.text: A list of VPC security group IDs to associate with the cluster, controlling inbound and outbound network access.

aws_drs_source_network.tags.key.text: A user-defined key for a tag on the AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) Source Network, used to categorize and identify the resource.

aws_dsql_cluster.multi_region_properties.text: Specifies the Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the linked regional DSQL clusters that form the multi-region cluster.

aws_dsql_cluster.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the DSQL cluster, used to organize and identify the cluster for management and cost allocation.

aws_dsql_cluster.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the DSQL cluster, used for metadata and cost allocation.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the DynamoDB global table, assigned by AWS upon creation.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.attribute_def.text: Defines the name and type of each attribute used in the key schema (partition key and optional sort key) for the DynamoDB global table, where each item specifies an AttributeName and AttributeType.
The name of the attribute to be used in the global table's key schema or secondary indexes, matching the attribute names in the table's item definitions.
The data type of the attribute in the DynamoDB Global Table's attribute definition, which must be one of 'S' (string), 'N' (number), or 'B' (binary).

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.billing_mode.text: Specifies how read and write throughput is billed for the global table, either PROVISIONED (with provisioned capacity) or PAY_PER_REQUEST (on-demand).

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_second.text: Specifies the global secondary indexes (GSIs) for the DynamoDB global table, defining each index's name, key schema, projection, and provisioned throughput settings that are replicated across all regional replicas.
The name of the global secondary index for the DynamoDB global table, which must be unique within the table and is used to query the indexed data.
Key schema for the global secondary index, defining the partition (HASH) and optional sort (RANGE) key attributes that determine the index's data organization.
The name of the attribute that serves as the partition key or sort key in the global secondary index's key schema, which must match an attribute defined in the table's attribute definitions.
Specifies whether the key attribute is a HASH (partition) key or RANGE (sort) key for the global secondary index's key schema in a DynamoDB global table.

Specifies the set of attributes that are projected into the global secondary index, including the projection type (e.g., ALL, KEYS_ONLY, or INCLUDE) and any non-key attributes to include when the type is INCLUDE.
Specifies the list of non-key attribute names to include in the global secondary index's projection, used only when the projection type is set to INCLUDE.
Specifies the set of attributes that are projected into the global secondary index, allowing values such as KEYS_ONLY, INCLUDE, or ALL to control which table attributes are copied to the index.
Configures the on-demand read throughput settings for this global secondary index, setting the maximum read request units so the index scales automatically with DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode.
Sets the maximum number of read request units that the global secondary index can consume in on-demand capacity mode, capping its read throughput within the read on-demand throughput settings.
Configures the read capacity units or auto scaling settings for read throughput of the specified global secondary index in this DynamoDB global table.
For each global secondary index on the DynamoDB global table, this specifies the maximum number of strongly consistent reads consumed per second before DynamoDB returns a ThrottlingException.
Specifies the warm throughput settings (read and write units per second) for the global secondary index of the DynamoDB global table.
The number of warm read units per second for the global secondary index, used to pre-provision read capacity for on-demand DynamoDB tables to prevent throttling during sudden traffic spikes.
Specifies the number of warm write throughput capacity units to allocate for this global secondary index of the DynamoDB global table.
Specifies the maximum write request units that this global secondary index can consume when the table is set to on-demand capacity mode.
Specifies the maximum number of write request units that the global secondary index can consume per second when the DynamoDB global table is set to on-demand capacity mode.
Specifies the write capacity settings (either fixed write capacity units or auto-scaling configuration) for the global secondary index of the DynamoDB global table.
Configures auto scaling settings (minimum/maximum write capacity units and target utilization) for the write capacity of the global secondary index in a DynamoDB global table.

The maximum number of write capacity units that Application Auto Scaling can scale the global secondary index's write capacity up to under the associated scaling policy, as defined in the write capacity auto scaling settings of a DynamoDB global table.
The minimum number of write capacity units that the auto scaling policy can scale down to for the global secondary index.
The initial number of write capacity units to allocate for the global secondary index before DynamoDB auto scaling adjusts capacity based on actual utilization.

Configuration for the target-tracking scaling policy that DynamoDB Auto Scaling uses to manage the write capacity of this global secondary index, including the target utilization percentage (TargetValue) and whether scale-in is disabled.
When set to true, prevents the target tracking scaling policy from scaling in (decreasing) the write capacity of the global secondary index.
The scale-in cooldown period, in seconds, for the write capacity auto scaling of this global secondary index, during which DynamoDB suppresses scaling-in actions.

Scale-out cooldown, in seconds, for the write capacity auto scaling target tracking policy of the global secondary index, controlling how long to wait after a scale-out activity before another can start.

Specifies the target utilization percentage (e.g., 70 for 70%) that the target tracking scaling policy for write capacity of this global secondary index will maintain, triggering scaling when actual utilization deviates.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.global_table_.text: The ARN of an existing DynamoDB table whose data is used to populate the global table when it is created.
Configures the witness regions for the DynamoDB global table, which participate in quorum for multi-Region strong consistency without storing a full replica of the table data.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.key_schema.text: Determines the primary key for the global table by listing the attributes that form the partition key and optional sort key, each with a KeyType of HASH or RANGE.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.key_schema.at.text: Specifies the name of an attribute that is part of the primary key (partition key or sort key) of the DynamoDB global table's key schema.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.key_schema.ke.text: Specifies whether the attribute named in this key schema element serves as the hash (partition) key or range (sort) key of the DynamoDB table's primary key.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.local_seconda.text: A list of local secondary indexes (LSIs) for the global table, each specifying an alternate sort key to enable querying by a non-key attribute within a partition.
The unique name of the local secondary index, which is required to define the index and is used to reference it in DynamoDB queries and operations.

Defines the partition key and optional sort key for the local secondary index, using AttributeName and KeyType pairs that must reference attributes declared in the parent table's AttributeDefinitions.
Specifies the name of a key attribute in the key schema of a local secondary index, which must match an attribute defined in the global table's attribute definitions.
Specifies whether the key is a partition key (HASH) or a sort key (RANGE) in the key schema of a local secondary index for the DynamoDB global table.
Specifies which table attributes are copied into the local secondary index, defined by a ProjectionType (ALL, KEYS_ONLY, or INCLUDE) and optional NonKeyAttributes for the INCLUDE type.
Specifies the non-key attribute names to include in the projection of the local secondary index when ProjectionType is set to INCLUDE.

Determines which attributes are projected into the local secondary index, valid values are KEYS_ONLY, INCLUDE, or ALL, controlling whether only the key attributes, a specified set of non-key attributes, or all attributes are copied into the index.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.multi_region_.text: Specifies the multi-region consistency mode for the DynamoDB global table, with allowed values of 'EVENTUAL' or 'STRONG', controlling whether strongly consistent reads are available across all replica regions.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.read_on_deman.text: Specifies the read on-demand throughput settings for a replica in the global table, including the maximum read request units allowed when the table uses on-demand capacity mode.
Sets the maximum read capacity, in read request units, that the global DynamoDB table can scale up to when using on-demand capacity mode.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.read_provisio.text: Specifies the read capacity provisioning settings for a replica of the DynamoDB global table, including a fixed read capacity unit count or auto-scaling configuration.

Sets the maximum number of strongly consistent read operations per second consumed per replica for a DynamoDB global table, used to configure the provisioned capacity for the replica's read throughput.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.text: Defines the AWS Regions in which replicas of the DynamoDB global table are created, along with per-replica settings such as point-in-time recovery and contributor insights.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.cont.text: Specifies the Contributor Insights configuration for this replica, including whether Contributor Insights is enabled on the replica table.
Specifies whether CloudWatch Contributor Insights is enabled for this replica of the DynamoDB global table.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.dele.text: When true, deletion protection is enabled for this replica table in the DynamoDB global table, preventing the replica from being successfully deleted via a DeleteTable operation.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.glob.text: Specifies the global secondary indexes to be configured on a specific replica of the DynamoDB global table, allowing per-replica provisioning overrides (such as read/write capacity) for those indexes in that region.
Configures whether CloudWatch Contributor Insights is enabled for a specific global secondary index on a replica table of a DynamoDB global table.
Determines whether CloudWatch Contributor Insights is enabled for the global secondary index on this replica of the DynamoDB global table.
This field sets the CloudWatch Contributor Insights mode for the specified global secondary index within a replica of the DynamoDB global table, with allowed values ENABLED and DISABLED.
The name of the global secondary index in the replica's configuration that the GSI override settings apply to, matching an index defined on the DynamoDB global table.
Specifies the on-demand (pay-per-request) read throughput settings for the global secondary index replica, including the maximum read request units that can be consumed per second.
Specifies the maximum number of read request units for the global secondary index in a replica of a DynamoDB global table when it uses on-demand capacity mode.
Specifies the read capacity settings for a global secondary index in a specific replica of a DynamoDB global table.

Configures the application auto-scaling settings for the read capacity of the global secondary index in the replica, including minimum and maximum read capacity and the target tracking scaling policy.
The maximum number of read capacity units that auto scaling can scale the global secondary index to for this replica in a DynamoDB global table.
The minimum number of read capacity units that Application Auto Scaling can scale down to for this global secondary index replica's read capacity.
Seed capacity for the global secondary index's read auto scaling in this replica, representing the initial read capacity units DynamoDB provisions before scaling adjusts.

This object configures the target tracking scaling policy for Application Auto Scaling on the read capacity of a global secondary index in a DynamoDB global table replica, specifying the target utilization value that triggers scaling adjustments.

When set to true, prevents the DynamoDB read capacity auto scaling target tracking policy from scaling in (reducing) the provisioned read capacity for the global secondary index, while still allowing scale-out to increase capacity.
The scale-in cooldown period (in seconds) that DynamoDB waits after a scale-in activity before it can trigger another scale-in for read capacity of a global secondary index replica.
The amount of time, in seconds, after a scale-out activity completes before another scale-out activity can start for the global secondary index read capacity of this replica.

The target utilization percentage for the read capacity auto scaling policy, representing the desired ratio of consumed read capacity to provisioned read capacity for the global secondary index in the replica's read capacity autoscaling configuration.
The number of read capacity units to provision for the global secondary index in the specified replica, controlling the read throughput for that index in that region.
Sets the replication mode for the global table, within a replica's global table settings, to either STANDARD (no cross-region replication) or REMOTE (cross-region global table).

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.kine.text: Specifies the Kinesis Data Streams configuration for a replica of the DynamoDB global table, controlling whether a stream is enabled and optionally referencing an existing stream ARN.
Specifies the precision of the ApproximateCreationDateTime value in the Kinesis stream for a replica, either MILLISECOND or MICROSECOND.
Specifies the ARN of the Amazon Kinesis Data Stream that receives item-level updates for this replica in the DynamoDB global table.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.poin.text: Configuration for point-in-time recovery (PITR) settings on a specific replica of the DynamoDB global table, containing a boolean flag that enables or disables PITR for that replica.
Enables or disables point-in-time recovery for the corresponding replica of the DynamoDB global table, allowing the replica to be restored to any point in time within the backup window.
Specifies the number of days for which point-in-time recovery data is retained for the given replica of the DynamoDB global table.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.read.text: Configures the read on-demand throughput settings for a replica in a DynamoDB global table, including the maximum read request units for on-demand capacity mode.
Specifies the maximum number of read request units that a replica of the DynamoDB global table can consume on-demand, setting an upper bound on its read throughput.
Defines the provisioned read capacity settings for a specific replica of the DynamoDB global table, including either a fixed read capacity unit count or auto scaling read settings.

Specifies the read capacity auto scaling settings for a replica, including the minimum and maximum provisioned capacity, optional seed capacity, and the target tracking scaling policy configuration that DynamoDB uses to adjust read capacity.
The maximum provisioned read capacity units that the auto scaling policy is allowed to scale up to for this replica.
The minimum number of read capacity units that DynamoDB auto scaling can scale down to for the replica's read capacity.
Specifies the initial read capacity units for the replica that are provisioned before auto scaling begins, serving as the starting point for the auto scaling group.

Specifies the target tracking scaling policy configuration for read capacity auto scaling on a DynamoDB Global Table replica, controlling target utilization, scale-in/scale-out cooldowns, and whether scale-in is disabled.
DisableScaleIn determines whether the target tracking scaling policy for read capacity auto scaling on this replica is prevented from scaling in (reducing provisioned read capacity).

The number of seconds for the scale-in cooldown period, during which App Auto Scaling suppresses additional scale-in activities for the read capacity of this replica after a scale-in activity completes.
The amount of time, in seconds, to wait after a scale-out activity before another scale-out activity can occur, controlling how quickly read capacity increases for this replica.
The target utilization percentage for the read capacity auto scaling policy on this global table replica, representing the desired fraction of provisioned read capacity to consume.
Specifies the maximum number of strongly consistent reads per second for the replica table in a DynamoDB global table.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.regi.text: The AWS Region in which a replica of the DynamoDB global table is created.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.repl.text: Configures DynamoDB Streams for a specific replica in the global table, including whether streaming is enabled and the stream view type (e.g., NEW_IMAGE, OLD_IMAGE) that determines which data changes are written.
Specifies a resource-based policy that controls access to the DynamoDB stream associated with the replica, enabling cross-account stream sharing and read access.
Specifies the JSON policy document that defines the resource-based permissions for the DynamoDB stream attached to this replica, controlling cross-account or cross-region access to the stream data.
The key of a tag to be applied to the stream specification of a replica in a DynamoDB global table.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.reso.text: Defines the IAM resource-based policy (JSON) applied to the DynamoDB replica table in the corresponding region, allowing replica-specific access control separate from the global table's default policy.

The IAM policy document (in JSON format) that defines the resource-based permissions policy for the replica table, allowing you to grant cross-account or cross-service access to that specific replica in the DynamoDB global table.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.sses.text: Configures the server-side encryption (SSE) for a specific replica of a DynamoDB global table, allowing you to specify an AWS KMS key (via KMSMasterKeyId) for encrypting data in that replica.
The KMS key ID or ARN used for server-side encryption in the SSE specification of a specific replica of the DynamoDB global table.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.tabl.text: Specifies the table class for a replica, either STANDARD or STANDARD_INFREQUENT_ACCESS, which determines the storage and throughput cost tier for that regional table copy.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.replicas.tags.text: Specifies the list of tags to associate with each replica table in the DynamoDB global table, allowing you to apply different tags per replica region.
The value of a tag attached to a specific replica (Region) of the global DynamoDB table.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.ssespecificat.text: Specifies the server-side encryption (SSE) configuration for the DynamoDB global table, including whether encryption is enabled and the encryption key type (such as AWS owned or customer-managed KMS) to use.
Specifies whether server-side encryption (SSE) is enabled for the DynamoDB global table, with true enabling encryption using AWS Key Management Service (KMS).
Specifies the server-side encryption type for the global table, either AES256 (DynamoDB-managed key) or KMS (AWS KMS customer-managed key).

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.stream_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the DynamoDB stream for the global table, automatically generated when stream specification is configured.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.stream_specif.text: The stream specification object configures Amazon DynamoDB Streams for the global table, including the stream enabling flag and stream view type that determines which item changes (keys only, new image, old image, or both) are written to the stream.
Specifies which item changes (keys only, new image, old image, or both) are captured in the DynamoDB stream for the global table.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.table_id.text: The read-only DynamoDB table ID that uniquely identifies this global table, assigned by AWS when the table is created.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.table_name.text: The name to assign to the DynamoDB global table; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.time_to_live_.text: Configures Time to Live (TTL) settings for the global table, including whether TTL is enabled and the attribute name that stores the expiration timestamp.
Specifies the name of the item attribute that stores the expiration timestamp, enabling DynamoDB to automatically delete expired items from the global table.
Whether time-to-live (TTL) is enabled for the global table, allowing DynamoDB to automatically delete items after a specified expiry timestamp.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.warm_throughp.text: Specifies the warm throughput (pre-allocated read/write capacity units per second) for the global table to sustain high traffic without throttling.
Sets the number of warm read capacity units per second for the DynamoDB global table.
Specifies the number of write capacity units per second to provision for warm throughput on the DynamoDB global table.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.write_on_dema.text: Specifies the optional on-demand write capacity cap (MaxWriteRequestUnits) for the DynamoDB global table, applying this write throughput limit uniformly across all replicas.
Sets the maximum number of write request units for on-demand capacity mode of a replica in a DynamoDB global table.

aws_dynamo_db_global_table.write_provisi.text: Configures the write capacity (provisioned throughput) for the AWS::DynamoDB::GlobalTable, specifying either a fixed number of write capacity units or auto-scaling settings for each replica in the global table.
Defines the application auto scaling settings for write capacity on each replica of the DynamoDB global table, including scaling limits and target utilization.
Specifies the maximum number of write capacity units that the write auto scaling policy can scale the global table's write throughput up to.
The minimum number of write capacity units that DynamoDB can scale down to for a replica's write capacity auto scaling in a global table.
The initial number of write capacity units to provision for a new replica table in a DynamoDB global table, applied only when the replica is created before auto scaling adjusts it.
Configuration for the target tracking policy that DynamoDB uses to automatically adjust write capacity, including the target utilization percentage and whether scale-in is disabled.
Indicates whether scale-in by the target tracking policy is disabled for the write capacity auto scaling of this replica in the DynamoDB global table.
The amount of time, in seconds, after a scale-in activity completes before another scale-in activity can begin for the DynamoDB write capacity auto scaling target tracking policy.
The amount of time, in seconds, to wait after a scale-out activity completes before another scale-out activity can begin, allowing DynamoDB write capacity to stabilize for the global table.
The target utilization percentage (0-100) for the write capacity auto scaling target tracking policy on the DynamoDB global table.

aws_dynamo_db_table.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the DynamoDB table, automatically assigned by AWS when the table is created.

aws_dynamo_db_table.attribute_definition.text: The name of an attribute in the DynamoDB table's attribute definitions, which must correspond to a key schema attribute (partition key, sort key, or index key) for the table or its secondary indexes.
Specifies the data type for the attribute, which must be one of S (string), N (number), or B (binary).

aws_dynamo_db_table.global_secondary_ind.text: Configures CloudWatch Contributor Insights for the global secondary index, with an `Enabled` setting to enable or disable Contributor Insights on that index.
Whether CloudWatch Contributor Insights are enabled for this global secondary index.
Enables or disables CloudWatch Contributor Insights for this global secondary index, with valid values ENABLED or DISABLED.
The name of the global secondary index, which must be unique within the DynamoDB table and is used to query data through that index.
Specifies the attribute names and key types (HASH or RANGE) that form the partition key and optional sort key for each global secondary index, determining how items are indexed in that GSI.
The name of the table attribute that serves as the partition or sort key for this global secondary index, which must match an attribute declared in the table's AttributeDefinitions.
Specifies whether the key element is a HASH (partition) key or a RANGE (sort) key in the key schema of the global secondary index.

Specifies the maximum read and write request units for a global secondary index when the table is configured for on-demand capacity mode, allowing fine-grained control over the index's throughput limits.
The maximum number of read request units that can be consumed per second by this global secondary index when the table is in on-demand capacity mode.
Sets the maximum number of write request units that this global secondary index can use when it operates in on-demand (pay-per-request) capacity mode, capping its write throughput.
Configures which table attributes are copied to the global secondary index, including the projection type (ALL, KEYS_ONLY, or INCLUDE) and optional non-key attributes.
Lists the additional (non-key) table attributes that are copied into the global secondary index when its projection type is INCLUDE.

Determines which table attributes are copied to the global secondary index: ALL copies every attribute, KEYS_ONLY copies only the table and index keys, and INCLUDE copies only the attributes listed in the projection's NonKeyAttributes.
Configures the read and write capacity units for a global secondary index when the DynamoDB table uses provisioned billing mode.
The number of read capacity units to provision for the global secondary index, controlling the index's throughput for strongly consistent reads when using provisioned billing mode.
The maximum number of write capacity units consumed per second for the global secondary index's provisioned throughput.

Specifies the warm throughput capacity (read and write units per second) for the global secondary index when the table uses the Standard-IA (Infrequent Access) storage class, allowing throughput to be set separately for data in the warm storage tier.
The number of read capacity units per second for warm throughput of the global secondary index.
The maximum number of write operations per second for the global secondary index's warm throughput, setting a capacity limit for writes to data in the warm storage tier of the DynamoDB table.

aws_dynamo_db_table.local_secondary_inde.text: The name of the local secondary index, which must be unique within the table and is used to query the table using an alternate sort key.

Defines the key schema for the local secondary index, specifying the partition key (which must be the same as the table's partition key) and a distinct sort key, each with an attribute name and key type (HASH or RANGE).

The name of the attribute that serves as either the required partition key (matching the table's primary key) or the optional sort key in the local secondary index's key schema, and must correspond to an attribute defined in the table's attribute definitions.

Specifies whether the corresponding attribute in the local secondary index's key schema is the partition key (HASH) or the sort key (RANGE), which for a local secondary index must be the table's partition key plus an additional attribute for the sort key.
Specifies which table attributes are copied into the local secondary index, using ALL, KEYS_ONLY, or INCLUDE modes, with INCLUDE requiring an explicit list of non-key attributes to project.
A list of non-key attributes that are projected into the local secondary index, in addition to the table's primary key attributes.

Specifies which attributes are copied from the table to the local secondary index: KEYS_ONLY (only index and table keys), INCLUDE (only the specified non-key attributes), or ALL (all table attributes).

aws_dynamo_db_table.stream_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the DynamoDB stream associated with the table, available when a stream specification is enabled on the table.

aws_dynamo_db_table.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key-value pair assigned to the DynamoDB table, used for resource categorization and identification.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.availabilit.text: The Availability Zone where the capacity reservation is created, used to reserve compute capacity in that specific zone for EC2 instances.
Specifies the ID of the Availability Zone (such as use1-az1) in which to create the Capacity Reservation, serving as an alternative to specifying the Availability Zone by name.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.available_i.text: The number of instances that remain available for use in the Capacity Reservation, reflecting unused capacity that can still be used to launch instances.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.capacity_al.text: A computed list of objects that describes how the total instance capacity of the reservation is allocated among different allocation types (e.g., 'used' or 'future'), as reported by the EC2 DescribeCapacityReservations API.
Indicates whether the allocated capacity is for 'used' (currently running instances) or 'future' (reserved but not yet running) usage, with allowed values of 'used' or 'future'.
The number of EC2 instances of the specified instance type to reserve in this capacity reservation allocation.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.capacity_re.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the EC2 Capacity Reservation, used to uniquely identify the reservation across AWS services.
The ID of the Capacity Reservation Fleet that this capacity reservation belongs to, if it was created as part of a fleet; this value is only set when the reservation is managed by a fleet.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.commitment_.text: commitment_info is a computed object that exposes the commitment duration and commitment end date for this EC2 Capacity Reservation, reflecting the reserved capacity's committed term details.
The timestamp indicating when the committed term of the EC2 Capacity Reservation ends, marking the expiration of a reserved capacity commitment.

The number of EC2 instances you are committed to running as part of this Capacity Reservation's commitment, which underpins the capacity reservation's usage commitment and corresponding billing discount.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.create_date.text: The date and time at which the Capacity Reservation was created.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.ebs_optimiz.text: Indicates whether the capacity reservation is EBS-optimized, which provides dedicated throughput for Amazon EBS I/O.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.end_date.text: The date and time (in ISO 8601 format) when the Capacity Reservation expires, after which the reserved capacity is released and any instances running in the reservation are automatically stopped or terminated.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.end_date_ty.text: Determines whether the Capacity Reservation has a specific end date/time (limited) or persists indefinitely (unlimited).

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.ephemeral_s.text: A Boolean value indicating whether the Capacity Reservation supports instances that use ephemeral (instance store) storage.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.id.text: The unique capacity reservation identifier (e.g., cr-1234567890abcdef0) assigned by AWS when the reservation is created, used to reference this reservation in API calls and other resources.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.instance_co.text: The number of instances for which to reserve capacity in the Capacity Reservation.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.instance_ma.text: Determines how the capacity reservation matches instances: 'open' allows any matching instance to use the reservation automatically, while 'targeted' requires instances to explicitly specify the reservation ID to use it.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.instance_pl.text: Specifies the operating system platform (e.g., Linux/UNIX, Windows, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, SUSE Linux) that the capacity reservation will support, matching the platform of the AMI used to launch instances.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.instance_ty.text: The EC2 instance type for which to reserve capacity, such as m5.large or c5.xlarge.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.out_post_ar.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Outpost on which to create the Capacity Reservation.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.owner_id.text: The ID of the AWS account that owns the Capacity Reservation.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.placement_g.text: The ARN of the cluster placement group in which to create the capacity reservation.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.reservation.text: The type of the Capacity Reservation, either 'default' for on-demand reservations or 'capacity-block' for future-dated reservations.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.start_date.text: The date and time at which the capacity reservation was started, as reported by the AWS EC2 API.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.state.text: The current lifecycle state of the capacity reservation, such as 'active', 'pending', 'failed', 'expired', or 'cancelled', as reported by AWS.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.tag_specifi.text: Specifies one or more tag specifications, each defining a resource type (such as 'capacity-reservation') and a set of tags to apply to the capacity reservation.
Specifies the type of resource to tag, which for an EC2 Capacity Reservation must be set to `capacity-reservation` to apply the associated tags to that reservation.
The list of tags to associate with the EC2 Capacity Reservation, as part of the tag specifications for the resource.
The key of a tag to apply to the EC2 Capacity Reservation.
The value of a tag to assign to the EC2 Capacity Reservation, used to categorize or identify the reservation.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.tenancy.text: The tenancy of the Capacity Reservation, either 'default' for shared hardware or 'dedicated' for a single physical server.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.total_insta.text: The total number of instances for which this Capacity Reservation reserves capacity, reported by EC2 as a read-only attribute that cannot be modified.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.unused_rese.text: Specifies the AWS account ID that will be billed for unused capacity in this EC2 Capacity Reservation.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.alloc.text: Determines how the Capacity Reservation Fleet allocates capacity across the specified instance types, either by spreading evenly across them (diversified) or by honoring the priority order you set (prioritized).

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.capac.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the EC2 Capacity Reservation Fleet.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.end_d.text: Specifies the date and time at which the Capacity Reservation Fleet expires.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.insta.text: Determines how instances are matched to the capacity reservation fleet: 'open' (default) allows any matching instance to use the reserved capacity, while 'targeted' requires instances to explicitly target the fleet.

Defines the list of instance type specifications for the capacity reservation fleet, each indicating an instance type, the number of instances to reserve, and the weight used to calculate total capacity.
The Availability Zone in which the capacity reservation for this instance type specification is allocated, enabling the fleet to target capacity across specific zones.
Specifies the unique identifier of the Availability Zone where capacity for the given instance type is reserved, allowing the fleet to target an AZ by its ID rather than its name.
Specifies whether instances launched in this capacity reservation are EBS-optimized for enhanced performance.
The operating system platform (e.g., Linux/UNIX, Windows, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, SUSE Linux) for the instance type specification within the EC2 Capacity Reservation Fleet.
Specifies the EC2 instance type (e.g., `m5.large`, `c5.xlarge`) for which this individual capacity reservation specification within the fleet will reserve capacity.
The priority of this instance type in the capacity reservation fleet, where lower values indicate higher priority for fulfilling the reservation.

The weight value for an instance type in a Capacity Reservation Fleet determines how much of the fleet's total target capacity each instance of that type consumes when calculating the number of instances needed.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.no_re.text: Setting this to true indicates the Capacity Reservation Fleet has no end date, so it does not expire and automatically release its capacity reservations, remaining active until explicitly deleted.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.remov.text: When set to true, this removes the configured end date for the capacity reservation fleet, causing it to remain active indefinitely.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.tag_s.text: Specifies the tags to apply to the Capacity Reservation Fleet during creation, enabling resource management and cost allocation through key-value pairs.
Specifies the type of resource to tag; for a Capacity Reservation Fleet the only valid value is `capacity-reservation-fleet` (the fleet itself).
The list of tags to apply to the resources identified by the parent tag specification, such as the capacity reservation fleet itself, when creating or managing the fleet.
The key of a user-defined tag applied to an EC2 Capacity Reservation Fleet for identification and management.
The tag value to associate with the Capacity Reservation Fleet, used for identifying, organizing, and managing the fleet through resource grouping and cost allocation.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.tenan.text: The tenancy of the Capacity Reservation Fleet, which indicates whether instances launched in the fleet run on shared (default) or dedicated hardware.

aws_ec2_capacity_reservation_fleet.total.text: The total amount of capacity, in units (each instance counts as one unit unless you apply instance type weights), that the Capacity Reservation Fleet aims to reserve across all instance types and Availability Zones.

aws_ec2_carrier_gateway.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag associated with this EC2 Carrier Gateway, used for identifying, organizing, and cost allocation of the resource.

aws_ec2_carrier_gateway.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS EC2 Carrier Gateway, used for metadata, organization, and cost tracking alongside its corresponding tag key.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_authorization_rule.ac.text: The ID of the Active Directory group that is allowed access to the network; if omitted, all users in the directory are permitted.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_authorization_rule.au.text: Indicates whether to authorize access to all groups, so when set to true, the rule applies to every Active Directory group, and when false, you must specify target groups via the GroupId field.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_authorization_rule.cl.text: The ID of the Client VPN endpoint to which this authorization rule applies.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_authorization_rule.de.text: A brief, optional description that identifies the purpose of the Client VPN authorization rule.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_authorization_rule.ta.text: The CIDR block of the target network that this authorization rule grants access to for the specified clients or groups.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.authenticati.text: Specifies the authentication methods (certificate-based, directory service, or federated/SAML) that clients must use to authenticate to the Client VPN endpoint.
Defines the Active Directory (AWS Directory Service) authentication settings for the Client VPN endpoint, including the directory ID used to authenticate clients.
The ID of the AWS Managed Microsoft Active Directory used for client authentication.
Specifies the SAML-based federated authentication configuration for the Client VPN endpoint, including the IAM SAML provider ARN(s) used to authenticate users.
The ARN of the IAM SAML identity provider that the Client VPN endpoint uses to authenticate users via federated SAML-based authentication.
The ARN of the IAM SAML identity provider used to authenticate users accessing the self-service portal (where clients can manage their own certificates) for this AWS Client VPN endpoint.
Configures mutual authentication (client certificate) for the Client VPN endpoint, requiring the ARN of the client root certificate chain to verify client certificates.
The ARN of the client root certificate chain that is used for mutual authentication with the AWS Client VPN endpoint.
Specifies the authentication method to use for the Client VPN endpoint, which can be one of certificate-authentication, directory-service-authentication, or federated-authentication.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.client_cidr_.text: The IPv4 CIDR range from which client IP addresses are allocated when they connect to the VPN.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.client_conne.text: Specifies the client connect options for the Client VPN endpoint, including the Lambda function used for connection authorization and post-connection feedback.
Specifies whether to enable Client Connect for the Client VPN endpoint, which allows an AWS Lambda function to handle custom authentication and authorization of client connections.
The ARN of the Lambda function that handles client connection authorization for the Client VPN endpoint, used when client connect options are enabled.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.client_login.text: Configures the optional client login banner for the VPN endpoint, specifying whether a banner is enabled and the banner text that clients see during authentication.
The customizable text displayed in the banner on the AWS-provided client VPN client during a connection session, with a maximum length of 1400 characters.
Specifies whether the Client VPN endpoint shows a customizable login banner to clients before they authenticate.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.client_route.text: Configures the automatic addition of a default route (0.0.0.0/0) for client VPN connections, controlling whether egress-only internet traffic is routed through the VPN tunnel (when set to true) or excluded (when set to false).

When set to true, this enforces that client traffic only uses routes advertised through the Client VPN endpoint, preventing clients from using other local network routes; when false, clients may also use their own local routes.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.connection_l.text: Configures whether client connection logs are enabled and, if so, the CloudWatch Logs log group and log stream to which they are published.
The name of the CloudWatch log group where AWS Client VPN publishes connection logs when connection logging is enabled.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs stream to which the Client VPN endpoint publishes connection logs; if not specified, a default stream under the configured log group is used.
Specifies whether connection logging is enabled for the Client VPN endpoint, which determines if detailed logs of client connections are sent to the specified CloudWatch Logs group.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.description.text: A user-specified description for the Client VPN endpoint, used to identify it.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.disconnect_o.text: Specifies whether to disconnect a client after the session timeout period expires for the Client VPN endpoint.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.dns_servers.text: Specifies the IPv4 addresses of DNS servers that are used by clients for DNS resolution when connected to the AWS Client VPN endpoint.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.endpoint_ip_.text: Specifies whether the Client VPN endpoint uses IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, which must match the IP version of the client CIDR block.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.id.text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for the Client VPN endpoint, such as cvpn-endpoint-1234567890abcdef0.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.security_gro.text: Specifies the IDs of the security groups to be associated with the Client VPN endpoint to control inbound and outbound traffic to the VPC.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.self_service.text: Specifies whether the self-service portal is enabled for the Client VPN endpoint, allowing clients to request and manage their own client certificates.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.server_certi.text: The ARN of the server certificate that the Client VPN endpoint uses for TLS authentication with clients.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.session_time.text: The maximum duration in hours that a client connection can remain active before being terminated, valid values are from 1 to 24.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.split_tunnel.text: Controls whether the Client VPN endpoint routes only traffic destined for the VPC through the tunnel (split-tunnel, true) or all traffic from the client (full-tunnel, false).

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.tag_specific.text: Specifies the tags to apply to the Client VPN endpoint at creation, by providing a list of tag specifications that each include a resource type (client-vpn-endpoint) and tag key-value pairs.
Specifies the type of AWS resource the tags apply to, which must be the string `client-vpn-endpoint` for a Client VPN endpoint.
Specifies the key-value tags to attach to the resource identified by the parent tag_specifications resource_type during Client VPN endpoint creation.
The value portion of a key-value tag assigned to the AWS Client VPN endpoint, used to organize and identify the resource for management and billing purposes.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.traffic_ip_a.text: Specifies whether the Client VPN endpoint routes IPv4 or IPv6 traffic, with valid values 'ipv4' or 'ipv6'.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.transit_gate.text: Specifies the IDs of the Availability Zones where the VPC attachment for the Client VPN endpoint is created when using a transit gateway.

For Client VPN endpoints that use a transit gateway, this list specifies the Availability Zones (e.g., us-east-1a) where the VPC attached to the transit gateway must have subnets, so the transit gateway attachment can route traffic.
The unique identifier of the transit gateway to which the Client VPN endpoint attaches for routing client traffic through a transit gateway.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.transport_pr.text: Specifies the transport protocol (TCP or UDP) used by the Client VPN endpoint for the VPN session.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.vpc_id.text: The ID of the VPC to associate with the Client VPN endpoint, which determines the VPC in which the endpoint's network interfaces are created and is needed to attach subnets via association resources.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.vpn_port.text: Specifies the port number (either 443 or 1194) that the Client VPN endpoint will use for the VPN tunnel, controlling whether the tunnel uses TCP (443) or UDP (1194).

aws_ec2_client_vpn_route.client_vpn_endp.text: The ID of the Client VPN endpoint to which this route is associated.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_route.description.text: A user-defined description for the route, often used to identify its purpose or destination in the Client VPN endpoint.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_route.destination_cid.text: The IPv4 CIDR block (e.g., 10.0.0.0/16) of the destination network that this Client VPN route forwards traffic through the VPN tunnel.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_route.id.text: The computed unique identifier for the Client VPN route, formatted as the client VPN endpoint ID, destination CIDR block, and target subnet ID separated by colons.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_route.target_vpc_subn.text: The ID of the VPC subnet to which the Client VPN endpoint routes traffic for the destination CIDR block.

aws_ec2_client_vpn_target_network_associ.text: The availability zone of the subnet that the Client VPN endpoint is associated with, automatically derived from the specified subnet.
This field contains the unique identifier of the Availability Zone where the target network's subnet resides; it is automatically populated from the associated subnet and cannot be independently set.
The ID of the Client VPN endpoint to which the target network is associated.
The unique association ID assigned by AWS to the target network (subnet) when it is associated with the Client VPN endpoint.
The ID of the subnet to associate with the Client VPN endpoint, enabling the endpoint to route traffic to and from that subnet's network.

aws_ec2_dhcpoptions.dhcp_options_id.text: The unique identifier (DHCP options ID) that AWS assigns to the DHCP options set when it is created, and which is used to associate the set with a VPC or subnet.

aws_ec2_dhcpoptions.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a tag assigned to the DHCP options set, used to identify and organize the resource within AWS.

aws_ec2_dhcpoptions.tags.value.text: The value portion of a user-defined tag attached to the DHCP options set, used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_ec2_eipassociation.eip.text: The Elastic IP address (IPv4) to associate with the specified instance or network interface; this can be an IP string or a reference to an EIP resource.

aws_ec2_eipassociation.id.text: The unique identifier of the Elastic IP association, which is the association ID (e.g., eipassoc-...) returned by AWS.

aws_ec2_fleet.context.text: The `context` field specifies a string that AWS reserves for future use in the EC2 Fleet, and it does not currently alter fleet behavior.

aws_ec2_fleet.excess_capacity_terminatio.text: Controls whether excess instances are terminated when the EC2 Fleet's target capacity is reduced below its current running capacity, accepting values 'termination' (default) or 'no-termination'.

aws_ec2_fleet.fleet_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the EC2 Fleet, used to reference the fleet in API calls and other resources.

aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.text: Specifies the launch template configurations (including launch template ID/name and overrides for instance type, subnet, etc.) that the EC2 Fleet uses to launch instances.

aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.la.text: Specifies the launch template ID or name and its version, which the EC2 Fleet uses as the base configuration for launching instances in this fleet.

Specifies the ID of the EC2 launch template that defines the instance configuration (such as AMI, instance type, and network settings) for the instances launched by the EC2 Fleet from this launch template config.
The name of the EC2 launch template to use for instances launched in this fleet's launch template configuration.
The version of the launch template (e.g., a specific version number, $Latest, or $Default) that the EC2 Fleet uses when launching instances for this launch template configuration.

aws_ec2_fleet.launch_template_configs.ov.text: Specifies the instance types, subnets, and other parameters that override the associated launch template when EC2 Fleet selects them for launching instances.
Specifies the Availability Zone in which to launch the instances for this fleet, overriding the placement specified in the launch template.
Specifies the ID of the Availability Zone (e.g., use1-az1) in which the EC2 Fleet launches instances for this override, replacing any Availability Zone from the launch template.
Defines the block device mapping overrides applied to instances launched using this launch template override, such as attaching additional EBS volumes or modifying root volume settings.

The device name (e.g., /dev/xvda or /dev/sdh) exposed to the instance for a block device mapping override applied to a launch template configuration in the EC2 Fleet, determining where the attached volume or instance store volume appears within the guest OS.
Specifies the EBS volume settings (e.g., volume size, type, IOPS, encryption, and delete-on-termination behavior) for a block device in an EC2 Fleet launch template override.
Indicates whether the EBS volume created by this block device mapping is automatically deleted when the EC2 instance terminates.
Specifies whether the EBS volume for this block device mapping in the EC2 Fleet launch template override should be encrypted, allowing enforcement of encryption on launched instances.

Specifies the provisioned IOPS (I/O operations per second) for the EBS volume in a launch template override's block device mapping, used when configuring an EC2 Fleet with volume types that support custom IOPS (io1, io2, or gp3).
The ID or ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the EBS volume created by this block device mapping override in the EC2 Fleet launch template configuration.
The ID of the snapshot from which to create the EBS volume, used to initialize the volume with the data from that snapshot.
Specifies the size of the EBS volume in GiB for the block device mapping override in the EC2 Fleet launch template configuration.
Specifies the EBS volume type (e.g., gp2, gp3, io1) to use for the block device in the launch template override when the EC2 Fleet launches instances.
Indicates that the specified device name should not be mapped to a block device on the launched instance, effectively suppressing that device from the instance's block device mapping.
Specifies the virtual device name (e.g., ephemeral0) for an ephemeral instance store volume in the block device mapping of a launch template override used by the EC2 Fleet.
Specifies the IAM instance profile to associate with instances launched according to this launch template override, which overrides any IAM instance profile set in the launch template.
The ARN of the IAM instance profile to associate with the instances launched from this EC2 Fleet override.
Specifies the name of the IAM instance profile assigned to instances launched from this fleet override, providing them with the permissions of the associated IAM role.
Defines the hardware requirements (such as vCPU count and memory) that an instance type must meet for EC2 Fleet to select it for this launch template override.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of accelerators (such as GPUs) that an instance must have to be considered for the fleet.
The maximum number of accelerators (such as GPUs or FPGAs) that an instance type can have in order to match the instance requirements for the EC2 Fleet override.
The minimum number of accelerators (such as GPUs) that an instance type must have to satisfy the instance requirements for the EC2 Fleet.
Defines which accelerator (GPU) manufacturers are acceptable for instance types that match this launch template override, filtering by vendors such as NVIDIA or AMD.
Lists the accelerator names (e.g., 'a100', 'v100') that instance types must have, so the EC2 Fleet only selects instances with those accelerators when using this launch template override.
Defines the minimum and maximum total memory (in MiB) required for accelerators (such as GPUs) on instance types that the EC2 Fleet can launch.
The maximum total accelerator memory, in MiB, that an instance type must have to match the instance requirements.
The minimum total accelerator (GPU) memory, in MiB, that an instance type must have to be considered for the EC2 Fleet.

Specifies the types of hardware accelerators (such as GPU, FPGA, or inference) that instances must have to meet the instance requirements, filtering which instance types are eligible for the EC2 Fleet.
Specifies a list of instance types that are allowed for the fleet to use, ensuring that the fleet launches instances only on these permitted types.
Specifies whether the instance type must be a bare metal instance, with allowed values included, excluded, or required.
Specifies the minimum and maximum baseline EBS bandwidth (in Mbps) that an instance type must meet to be eligible for the EC2 Fleet.
Specifies the maximum baseline EBS bandwidth in Mbps that an instance type must have to be considered for the EC2 Fleet, used as a filter in the instance requirements overrides.
Specifies the minimum baseline EBS bandwidth (in Mbps) that an instance must meet to be considered for the EC2 Fleet's instance requirements.
Specifies the baseline performance requirements for CPU and memory of instance types that the EC2 Fleet can launch, enabling filtering based on a minimum performance threshold.

Specifies the CPU baseline performance factor, which uses a set of reference instance families to define the minimum expected CPU performance that instance types must meet for the fleet's launch configuration overrides.
A list of CPU performance factor references, each defining an instance family (e.g., m5, c5) that serves as the baseline for CPU performance when selecting instance types for the EC2 Fleet.
The instance family name (e.g., c5, m5) used as a baseline CPU performance reference when specifying instance requirements for the EC2 Fleet.

Specifies whether to include, require, or exclude burstable performance instance types (such as T3, T4g) in the EC2 Fleet's instance requirements, with valid values 'included', 'required', or 'excluded'.
A list of CPU manufacturers (such as Intel, AMD, and Amazon Web Services) that the instance requirements will accept when selecting instance types for the EC2 Fleet to launch.
List of EC2 instance types that are explicitly excluded from consideration when the fleet launches instances under these instance requirements.
Specifies the list of instance generations (for example, 'current' or 'previous') that the instance types must belong to in order to be used for this fleet's launch template override.
Specifies whether the instance types selected for the fleet must have local storage (such as NVMe) or not, with values like `required`, `preferred`, or `excluded`.
Filters candidate instances for the fleet to those whose local storage type matches the specified values (hdd and/or ssd), so only instances with that kind of local storage are considered.

Specifies the maximum Spot Instance price you are willing to pay as a percentage of the optimal On-Demand price for that instance type, used as a price protection threshold to filter candidate instance types in the fleet's instance requirements.
Specifies the minimum and maximum memory in GiB per vCPU for an instance type to be considered when fulfilling the fleet's launch template overrides.
The maximum memory per vCPU (in GiB) that an instance must have to match the specified instance requirements in the EC2 Fleet launch template override.
The minimum amount of memory (in GiB) per vCPU that an instance type must have to match the instance requirements when launching an EC2 Fleet.
Defines the range of memory (in MiB) for instance types that the EC2 Fleet can select, with minimum and maximum values.
The maximum amount of memory, in MiB, that an instance type must have to be eligible for the fleet.
The minimum amount of memory, in MiB, that an instance type must have to be included in the fleet's selection.
Defines the minimum and maximum network bandwidth in gigabits per second (Gbps) that an instance type must offer to be considered a match for the EC2 Fleet's overrides.
Sets the maximum network bandwidth (in Gbps) that an instance type must offer to be selected by the EC2 Fleet when using this launch template override's instance requirements.
The minimum network bandwidth in gigabits per second that instances must meet to be considered by the EC2 Fleet's launch template override instance requirements.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of network interfaces that an instance must have to satisfy the instance requirements for an EC2 Fleet launch template override.
The maximum number of network interfaces that an instance type must support for it to be considered by the EC2 Fleet.
The minimum number of network interfaces that an instance must have to satisfy the instance requirements in an EC2 Fleet launch template override.

Sets the maximum price for On-Demand instances as a percentage above the lowest-priced instance type that meets the specified requirements, used to control costs when EC2 Fleet selects instance types.
When set to true, only instance types that support encryption in transit are considered when fulfilling the fleet's launch template overrides.
Indicates whether the instance types must support hibernation; when set to true, only instance types that can hibernate are considered for the fleet.

Specifies the maximum price you are willing to pay for a Spot Instance as a percentage above the lowest Spot price among the eligible instance types, used within a launch template override's instance requirements to control Spot selection in the fleet.
Defines the minimum and maximum amount of local storage (in GB) that an instance type must provide for the fleet to consider it, filtering candidate instance types.
The maximum amount of local storage (in GB) that an instance must have to satisfy the instance requirements for this launch template override in the EC2 fleet.
The minimum total amount of local storage (in GB) that an instance type must have to be considered for the EC2 Fleet.
Defines the minimum and maximum number of vCPUs that an instance type must have to be eligible for the EC2 Fleet.
The maximum number of vCPUs an instance type can have to be eligible for the launch template override.
The minimum number of vCPUs that an instance type must offer to be eligible for the EC2 Fleet's capacity.
The EC2 instance type to launch in this override of the launch template configuration for the EC2 Fleet.
Specifies the EC2 key pair name to associate with instances launched by this launch template override.
The maximum price per unit hour that you are willing to pay for a Spot Instance in this EC2 Fleet, which overrides the max price set in the associated launch template.

Sets the instance metadata service (IMDS) options—such as requiring token usage with HttpTokens and controlling the HTTP endpoint with HttpEndpoint—for EC2 instances launched by this specific fleet override.
Indicates whether the IPv4 instance metadata endpoint (enabled or disabled) is enabled for instances launched from this launch template override in the EC2 Fleet.
Determines whether HTTP tokens are required for accessing the instance metadata service for instances launched with this override, enforcing the use of IMDSv2 when set to 'required'.
Indicates whether to automatically assign a public IPv4 address to the primary network interface of an instance launched using this launch template override.
Indicates whether this network interface is deleted when the EC2 instance is terminated.
