Provides a text description for the network interface created for the fleet's instances, overriding the description in the launch template if provided.

The zero-based position of the network interface on the instance (e.g., 0 for the primary interface) for this launch template override, which determines the attachment order when multiple interfaces are specified.
The list of security group IDs to attach to the network interface defined by this override in the EC2 Fleet launch template configuration.

Specifies the type of network interface for the override, with valid values being 'interface' for a standard VPC network interface, 'efa' for an Elastic Fabric Adapter, or 'trunk' for a trunk network interface.
Specifies the number of IPv6 addresses to assign to the network interface for instances launched using this EC2 Fleet launch template override.
The IPv6 addresses to assign to the network interface when overridden for a launch template configuration in the EC2 Fleet.
The specific IPv6 address to assign to the network interface for the EC2 Fleet instance override, enabling a static address from the subnet's IPv6 range.
The index of the network card on the instance, which associates the network interface with a specific network card for instance types that support multiple network cards.
The ID of an existing Elastic Network Interface (ENI) that overrides the network interface configuration from the launch template for instances launched by this fleet override.
Specifies the primary private IPv4 address to assign to the network interface; if omitted, AWS automatically selects an available address from the subnet's range.
Defines private IPv4 addresses to assign to the network interface for instances launched by the EC2 Fleet, where each entry specifies the IP address and whether it is the primary private IP.
Indicates whether the specified private IP address is the primary private IP address for the network interface.
The private IPv4 address to assign to a network interface in the EC2 Fleet launch template override, where each entry in the private_ip_addresses list specifies one such address.
Sets the number of secondary private IPv4 addresses to automatically assign to the network interface when an EC2 Fleet instance is launched with this launch template override.
The ID of the subnet in which the instances will be launched when applying this network interface override.
Overrides the EC2 placement settings (e.g., Availability Zone, Affinity, Tenancy) for instances launched with this launch template override in the EC2 Fleet.

The affinity setting (such as 'host' or 'default') that determines whether instances launched with this placement override are associated with a dedicated host in the EC2 Fleet's launch template configuration.
Specifies the Availability Zone in which to launch the instances for this fleet override, overriding the placement setting from the launch template.
The name of the placement group in which to launch the instances for this fleet launch template override.
The ID of the Dedicated Host on which to launch the instances in this fleet override.
The ARN of the host resource group in which to launch the instances, used to place instances on a group of dedicated hosts for the EC2 Fleet.
Specifies the partition number within a partition placement group where the instances launched from this launch template override should be placed.
Specifies a specific spread domain within a spread placement group for the instance overrides, controlling which fault-isolated partition the fleet-launched instances are placed into.
Specifies the tenancy (default, dedicated, or host) for instances launched using this placement override in the EC2 Fleet.
Defines the order in which EC2 Fleet prioritizes this instance type override when fulfilling capacity, where lower numbers indicate higher priority.
The ID of the subnet in which to launch the instances, overriding any subnet specified in the associated launch template.
The number of capacity units that each instance of this instance type contributes to the fleet's target capacity, enabling instance weighting for mixed instance types in the EC2 Fleet.

aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options.text: Specifies the allocation strategy and other options for On-Demand Instances in the EC2 Fleet, such as how capacity is prioritized and whether to use capacity reservations.

aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options.allocati.text: Determines the order in which On-Demand Instances are launched across instance types in the fleet, with 'lowest-price' selecting the lowest-priced type first (default) and 'prioritized' following the priority order defined in the launch template.

aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options.capacity.text: Specifies whether to use unused Capacity Reservations to fulfill On-Demand Instance capacity in the EC2 Fleet, including the usage strategy (e.g., use-capacity-reservations-first).

Determines whether the EC2 Fleet uses unused Capacity Reservations first to fulfill On-Demand capacity before launching new On-Demand Instances, with the only valid value being 'use-capacity-reservations-first'.

aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options.max_tota.text: Specifies the maximum amount per hour (in USD) you are willing to pay for all On-Demand Instances launched by the EC2 Fleet.

aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options.min_targ.text: The minimum number of On-Demand Instances that the EC2 Fleet must maintain, ensuring a baseline of On-Demand capacity within the fleet's total target capacity.

aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options.single_a.text: Indicates whether the fleet launches all On-Demand Instances into a single Availability Zone.

aws_ec2_fleet.on_demand_options.single_i.text: When enabled, this makes the On-Demand portion of the EC2 Fleet launch only a single instance type (as specified in the launch template or its overrides) rather than multiple types chosen by the allocation strategy.

aws_ec2_fleet.replace_unhealthy_instance.text: Indicates whether EC2 Fleet automatically replaces instances that become unhealthy, launching new instances to maintain the fleet's target capacity.

aws_ec2_fleet.reserved_capacity_options..text: Specifies the types of reserved capacity (e.g., capacity-reservation or capacity-block) that the EC2 Fleet can use to fulfill On-Demand capacity.

aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.text: Configures the Spot Instance purchasing behavior for the fleet, including allocation strategy, instance interruption behavior, and maximum price per hour.

aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.allocation_st.text: Determines how the EC2 Fleet allocates Spot Instance capacity across Spot pools, using strategies such as lowest-price, diversified, or capacity-optimized.

aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.instance_inte.text: Controls the behavior of Spot Instances in the fleet when they are interrupted by EC2, allowing values such as 'terminate', 'stop', or 'hibernate' to specify whether instances are terminated, stopped, or hibernated.

aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.instance_pool.text: Specifies the number of Spot capacity pools across which the EC2 Fleet distributes its target Spot capacity, and is only used when the Spot allocation strategy is set to 'lowestPrice'.

aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.maintenance_s.text: Specifies the maintenance strategies for the Spot Instances in the fleet, such as enabling capacity rebalancing to automatically replace instances that are at risk of interruption.

Configures the capacity rebalance behavior for the fleet's Spot Instances, allowing EC2 Fleet to attempt to launch a replacement instance before an existing Spot Instance is interrupted, with a configurable replacement strategy.

Determines whether EC2 Fleet launches a replacement Spot Instance when the current instance is at risk of interruption (launch) or launches a replacement before terminating the current instance (launch-before-terminate).
The number of minutes to wait after receiving a Spot Instance rebalance notification before terminating the instance, allowing proactive replacement during capacity rebalancing.

aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.max_total_pri.text: The maximum hourly price you are willing to pay for Spot Instances in the EC2 Fleet, specified as a string representing a dollar amount (e.g., '0.50').

aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.min_target_ca.text: Specifies the minimum target capacity for Spot Instances in the fleet; if the fleet cannot reach this capacity, it launches no instances.

aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.single_availa.text: When set to true, the Spot Fleet launches all instances in the same single Availability Zone, instead of potentially spreading across multiple, to keep them co-located for low latency.

aws_ec2_fleet.spot_options.single_instan.text: Indicates whether the Spot Fleet will launch a single instance type to fulfill the entire target capacity, rather than diversifying across multiple instance types.

aws_ec2_fleet.tag_specifications.text: The list of tag specifications that define the tags to apply to the EC2 Fleet resource itself, typically using the resource type 'fleet'.

aws_ec2_fleet.tag_specifications.resourc.text: Specifies the type of resource to tag, such as an instance or the fleet itself, within a tag specification for the EC2 Fleet.

aws_ec2_fleet.tag_specifications.tags.text: Specifies the list of tags (key-value pairs) to apply to the fleet's launched resources, such as instances or volumes, as part of the parent tag specification.

aws_ec2_fleet.tag_specifications.tags.ke.text: The tag key (e.g., 'Name') of a tag to apply to EC2 instances that the fleet launches, as defined in this tag specification.

aws_ec2_fleet.tag_specifications.tags.va.text: Specifies the value of a tag assigned to the EC2 Fleet, used to categorize and identify the fleet among your AWS resources.

aws_ec2_fleet.target_capacity_specificat.text: Configures the overall target capacity for the EC2 Fleet, including total, On-Demand, and Spot capacity values, the default capacity type for provisioning, and the unit type (instances or vCPU) used for measurement.
Sets the default purchase type (on-demand or spot) for the EC2 Fleet's target capacity when individual capacity types are not otherwise specified.
The number of On-Demand units to request as the target capacity for the EC2 Fleet.
Specifies the number of units to request for Spot Instance capacity in the EC2 Fleet's overall target capacity.
The unit of measure for the target capacity of the EC2 Fleet, either 'vcpu' or 'memory-mib'.
The total number of capacity units (instances or other units) that the EC2 Fleet aims to launch and maintain across all specified capacity reservation and instance type options.

aws_ec2_fleet.terminate_instances_with_e.text: Indicates whether running instances should be terminated when the EC2 Fleet reaches its expiration time (validUntil); if false, instances continue to run beyond expiration.

aws_ec2_fleet.type.text: Specifies the type of EC2 Fleet (maintain, request, or instant), which controls whether the fleet maintains a target capacity over time, fulfills a one-time request, or launches the capacity immediately.

aws_ec2_fleet.valid_from.text: The timestamp (in UTC) at which the EC2 Fleet request becomes valid, after which the fleet can begin launching instances.

aws_ec2_fleet.valid_until.text: The date and time when the EC2 Fleet request expires, and after which AWS will not launch any new instances for the fleet.

aws_ec2_host.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag assigned to the EC2 Dedicated Host.

aws_ec2_host.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag attached to the EC2 Dedicated Host.

aws_ec2_instance_connect_endpoint.tags.k.text: The key of a tag attached to the EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint, used to identify, categorize, and filter the resource within AWS.

aws_ec2_ipam.default_resource_discovery_.text: Sets the AWS Organizations entity path (the OU path, e.g., 'ou-1234-abcdefgh') for an organizational unit to exclude from the IPAM default resource discovery, preventing resources in that OU from being automatically discovered.

aws_ec2_ipam.description.text: A user-specified, free-form text description of the IP address manager (IPAM) used to identify it in the AWS console and APIs.

aws_ec2_ipam.operating_regions.region_na.text: The name of the AWS Region in which the IPAM operates, defining one of the operating regions for the IPAM.

aws_ec2_ipam.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the EC2 IPAM resource, used to categorize or identify the IPAM with custom metadata (e.g., 'Name' or 'Environment').

aws_ec2_ipam.tags.value.text: Specifies the value of a user-defined tag key assigned to the EC2 IPAM resource for organizational or management purposes.

aws_ec2_ipamallocation.description.text: A user-defined free-form text description that annotates the IPAM allocation, typically used to record the purpose, owner, or other identifying information for the allocated CIDR block.

aws_ec2_ipampool.allocation_resource_tag.text: The key of a tag that is automatically applied to resources allocated from this IPAM pool, as part of the allocation_resource_tags map.
The value of a tag that will be applied to resources that receive CIDR allocations from this IPAM pool.

aws_ec2_ipampool.description.text: Sets a user-defined descriptive text for the EC2 IPAM pool, used to identify the pool's purpose and displayed in IPAM management views and API responses.

aws_ec2_ipampool.provisioned_cidrs.cidr.text: The CIDR block (in CIDR notation) that is provisioned to the IPAM pool, defining a specific address range added to the pool's managed address space.

aws_ec2_ipampool.source_resource.resourc.text: The resource ID of the source resource (such as a VPC) that provides CIDRs to be allocated to the IPAM pool.
The AWS account ID of the source resource (such as a VPC or another IPAM pool) that this IPAM pool uses as the origin for its CIDR provisioning, required when defining a source resource for the pool.
Specifies the AWS region in which the source resource (such as a VPC or subnet) that provides the CIDR block for this IPAM pool resides.
The type of the source resource being admitted into the IPAM pool, such as 'vpc' or 'subnet', which is paired with the source resource ID to identify the originating VPC or subnet.

aws_ec2_ipampool.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag to associate with the IPAM pool, used for identifying and organizing the pool.

aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver.rules.c.text: Limits the rule to prefix list entries that are associated with the given AWS resource ID, such as a VPC or subnet.

aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver.rules.i.text: The ID of the IPAM scope that this resolver rule is associated with, used to determine which IPAM-managed prefix list the rule selects during resolution.

aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver.rules.r.text: Specifies the type of AWS resource (e.g., VPC, subnet) that a rule matches when resolving resources into the prefix list.

aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver.rules.s.text: Specifies the static CIDR block included in a rule entry for the prefix list resolver, defining the IP address range used to match traffic.

aws_ec2_ipamprefix_list_resolver_target..text: The value of a user-defined tag assigned to the IPAM prefix list resolver target, used for organizing and managing the resource in AWS.

aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery.descripti.text: Specifies a custom description for the IPAM resource discovery, which is used to provide human-readable context or identification for the discovery resource within the AWS EC2 IPAM service.

aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery.operating.text: Specifies the AWS Region (e.g., us-east-1) in which the IPAM resource discovery operates.

aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery.organizat.text: Defines the AWS Organizations entity path (e.g., 'o-1234567890abcdef0') of an organizational unit to exclude from IPAM resource discovery, preventing resources in that OU from being discovered.

aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery.tags.valu.text: The value for a tag key attached to the IPAM resource discovery, which is a user-defined string for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_ec2_ipamresource_discovery_associati.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the IPAM resource discovery association, used to organize and identify the resource within AWS.
Specifies the value of a tag key attached to the IPAM resource discovery association, used to organize and identify the association for purposes like cost allocation and access management.

aws_ec2_ipamscope.description.text: A user-defined description for the IPAM scope.

aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs to associate with the local gateway route table for identification and categorization, where each object consists of a Key and a Value string.

aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table.tags.k.text: The key of a user-defined tag that can be attached to an EC2 Local Gateway Route Table for resource identification and management.

aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table_virtua.text: A user-defined key for a tag on this AWS Local Gateway Route Table Virtual Interface Group Association, used to categorize, organize, or filter the resource in AWS.
The value of a tag key attached to the Local Gateway Route Table Virtual Interface Group Association, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_ec2_local_gateway_route_table_vpcass.text: Tags are user-defined key-value pairs that label and identify the VPC association with the local gateway route table, enabling cost allocation and resource management.
The key of a tag attached to the Local Gateway Route Table VPC Association, serving as the name portion of a user-defined metadata label for the association.
The value of a tag attached to the association between a local gateway route table and a VPC.

aws_ec2_local_gateway_virtual_interface..text: The user-defined key for a tag attached to the EC2 Local Gateway Virtual Interface, used to organize and identify the resource.
The value of a tag attached to the Local Gateway Virtual Interface, used to categorize or identify the resource.

aws_ec2_local_gateway_virtual_interface_.text: The value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to the Local Gateway Virtual Interface Group, enabling you to assign custom metadata for identification and management.

aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.icmp.text: Specifies the ICMP type and code for the network ACL rule when the protocol is ICMP or ICMPv6, used to match specific ICMP traffic patterns.

aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.icmp.code.text: The ICMP code number, used to filter ICMP traffic in a network ACL entry, where it must be specified when the ICMP type is set to a specific value (e.g., 0 for echo request) rather than -1.

aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.icmp.type.text: The ICMP type number for the ICMP protocol, used when the protocol is set to ICMP (e.g., 8 for echo request).

aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.id.text: A computed identifier that combines the network ACL ID and rule number to uniquely represent this network ACL entry.

aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.port_range.text: Specifies the inclusive lower and upper bounds of the port range to match for the network ACL rule, typically used when the protocol is TCP or UDP.

aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.port_range.fro.text: The starting (lower) port number of the TCP or UDP port range that this network ACL entry rule applies to, used together with the 'to' value to define the range of allowed or denied destination ports.

aws_ec2_network_acl_entry.port_range.to.text: Specifies the highest port number in the inclusive range of ports that this network ACL entry applies to, paired with the port_range.from value to define the upper boundary of allowed or denied traffic.

aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope.cr.text: The ISO 8601 formatted timestamp when the network insights access scope was created.

aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope.ex.text: Specifies a list of network path statements to exclude from the access scope, so that traffic matching any of these paths is not analyzed.
Specifies the destination endpoint (such as an IP address, resource ID, or ARN) of a network path that is excluded from the access scope.
Specifies the packet header fields (such as source/destination IP addresses, ports, and protocols) that the destination of an excluded path must match in the Network Insights Access Scope.
Specifies the destination IP addresses or CIDR ranges that a packet must match to be considered part of the excluded path's destination traffic, used as filters in the packet header statement.
Specifies the destination ports or port ranges (e.g., '80' or '1000-1024') that a packet must match for its path to be considered for exclusion in the network access scope.

For the excluded path's destination component, this list specifies the destination prefix list IDs (e.g., pl-0123456789abcdef0) that the packet header statement matches, causing traffic destined to any of these prefix lists to be excluded from the access scope.
Specifies the list of network protocols (e.g., tcp, udp, icmp) that the destination packet header statement matches for traffic to be excluded from the access scope.
The list of source IP address CIDR ranges that the packet header statement matches for the destination of an exclusion path in the Network Insights access scope.
Specifies the source port or port ranges (e.g., '80' or '1-1024') that the packet header statement matches on to define excluded traffic in the Network Insights Access Scope.
The source prefix list IDs used to match traffic in the packet header statement for the destination of an exclude path in a Network Insights access scope.
Specifies the destination resources to exclude from the network insights access scope, identified by ARN, resource type, or tags.
Specifies the AWS resource types (e.g., AWS::EC2::Instance) that the destination resource statement matches in an exclusion path for the Network Insights Access Scope.
Specifies the list of destination resources (by resource ID or ARN) that define the excluded path's destination in the network insights access scope.
Defines the source of a path to exclude from the access scope, using a path statement that can specify resources like VPCs, subnets, or security groups, as well as packet header conditions.
Defines the packet header criteria (such as IP addresses, ports, and protocols) that identify the source of a network path to exclude from the access scope analysis.
The list of destination IP addresses or CIDR blocks used in the packet header statement to match traffic for the source of this exclude path.
The list of destination ports to match in the packet header statement for the source of an excluded path, used to define traffic to omit from the network insights access scope.
Specifies the IDs of managed prefix lists that the packet's destination address must match for the packet header statement to apply within an exclude path in the Network Insights Access Scope.

Specifies the list of IP protocols (such as TCP, UDP, or ICMP) to match for packets originating from the source when defining the packet header statement for the excluded path in the Network Insights access scope.
The list of source IP addresses (IPv4 or IPv6, in CIDR or IP format) that the packet header statement uses to match traffic to be excluded from the Network Insights access scope.

Specifies the source port ranges (e.g., '80', '443', '80-90') that the packet header statement matches on the path's source, used within an exclude path to filter out traffic from the Network Insights Access Scope analysis.

Specifies the AWS-managed prefix list IDs or names whose IP address ranges are used as the source match criteria in the packet header statement, so that packets originating from any of these prefix lists are considered for the exclude path in the Network Insights Access Scope.
Specifies the resource statement that defines the source resources for this excluded path, matching traffic based on the listed resource ARNs (Resources) and resource types (ResourceTypes).

Specifies the AWS resource types (such as AWS::EC2::Instance or AWS::EC2::VPC) that the source resource statement in an exclude path must match to exclude the source resource from the network access scope.
A list of resource ARNs or IDs that specify the source resources to exclude from the Network Insights Access Scope's traffic analysis, as part of an exclusion path's source resource statement.
Specifies the intermediate resources through which traffic must pass for each excluded path, as a list of resource statements that match by ARN or resource type.

The resource_statement object specifies which AWS resources (by ARN or resource type) are matched for this hop in the exclude path, determining the network paths that are excluded from the access scope analysis.
Specifies the AWS resource types (e.g., 'AWS::EC2::VPC') that the resource statement matches when selecting through-resources for this exclusion path in the Network Insights Access Scope.
Specifies the exact resource ARNs (such as VPC, subnet, or ENI ARNs) that the resource statement matches when determining which traffic paths to exclude from the network insights access scope.

aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope.ma.text: Specifies the list of network paths to match, where each path defines a source, destination, and optional intermediate resources that the access scope applies to.
Specifies the destination endpoint of a path in the Network Insights Access Scope, defining where the matched traffic is directed (such as a resource ARN, CIDR block, or port range).

The packet header statement for the destination in a match path specifies the packet header criteria (such as destination addresses, ports, and protocol) that traffic must match to be included in the Network Insights access scope.
A list of destination IP addresses or CIDR blocks that the packet header statement matches for traffic reaching the destination in the network insights access scope path.

The list of destination port numbers or ranges (e.g., '80' or '80-90') that the packet header statement matches on the destination side of the path, used to filter traffic in the Network Insights Access Scope.
The list of managed prefix list IDs used to match the destination IP address of traffic in the packet header statement.
The protocols list specifies the IP protocols (such as tcp, udp, or icmp) that the packet header statement matches for the destination path in the network insights access scope.
The list of source IP addresses or CIDR ranges to match in the packet header criteria for the destination access scope path, which filters traffic originating from those addresses.
The list of source ports or port ranges that the packet header statement matches on for the destination endpoint of the network insights access scope path.
The IDs of the prefix lists whose CIDR blocks define the allowed source IP addresses for this packet header statement in the destination match path of the access scope.
Specifies the resource statement that defines the destination resources (by ARN or resource type) for this match path in a Network Insights Access Scope.

Defines the list of AWS resource types (e.g., AWS::EC2::Instance, AWS::EC2::VPC) that the destination resource statement matches when specifying the destination endpoint for a network access scope path in Network Insights Access Analyzer.

Specifies the list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) for the destination resources that this match path's destination resource statement applies to, defining which destination resources are eligible for network path analysis.
Identifies the source endpoint of a network path to match in the access scope analysis, such as a VPC, subnet, or resource ARN.

Specifies the packet header statement that defines the source and destination IP addresses, ports, and protocols used to match traffic for the source endpoint in this path of the Network Insights access scope.

The list of destination IP addresses or CIDR blocks (e.g., 10.0.0.0/8) that the packet's destination address must match for the source packet header statement to apply in the Network Insights Access Scope match path.
The destination ports or port ranges (e.g., '80' or '80-90') that the source path's packet header statement must match for traffic to be included in the Network Insights access scope.

Lists the prefix lists whose CIDR blocks are used as the destination address match criteria in this packet header statement, so traffic is considered a match if its destination IP falls within any of the specified prefix lists.
Specifies the list of network protocols (such as tcp, udp, or icmp) to match in the packet header for the source path statement in the access scope.
Specifies the list of source IP addresses (in CIDR notation) that the packet header statement uses to match traffic originating from those addresses within the access scope's match path source.
Specifies the source port numbers or ranges to match in the packet header statement, used to filter traffic based on the source TCP/UDP port for the network insights access scope path.
Specifies the managed prefix list IDs whose CIDRs define the source addresses for this packet header statement in the source match path.
Specifies the AWS resources (by ARN or resource type) that the source of a path must match to be included in the network insights access scope.

Specifies the AWS resource types (e.g., 'AWS::EC2::Instance') that the resource statement filters on, limiting the network insights access scope to paths involving those resource types in the source match paths.
Specifies the ARNs of the resources to match as the source of traffic in the network insights access scope path statement.
List of resources through which traffic must pass (each specified by ARN and resource type, such as subnet, internet gateway, or VPC) for a path to match this access scope path.
Specifies the resources and/or resource types (such as subnets or VPCs) that a path must pass through in order to match the access scope, identified by resource IDs in a list.

Specifies the list of AWS resource types (e.g., AWS::EC2::Instance, AWS::EC2::VPC) that define which resources the resource statement matches when identifying traffic passing through a resource in the network insights access scope.

A list of ARNs of the specific AWS resources (such as VPCs, subnets, or EC2 instances) that the resource statement applies to, used to include or exclude paths that traverse any of these resources in the access scope analysis.

aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope.ne.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Network Insights Access Scope, which uniquely identifies it in AWS.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS when the Network Insights Access Scope is created.

aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope.ta.text: A list of key-value tags to associate with this EC2 Network Insights Access Scope, used to categorize and manage the resource in AWS.
The key of a tag applied to the EC2 Network Insights Access Scope, used to assign custom metadata for identifying, organizing, and managing the access scope.
The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the AWS EC2 Network Insights Access Scope resource, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope.up.text: The date and time when the network insights access scope was last updated.

aws_ec2_network_insights_access_scope_an.text: The number of network interfaces analyzed by the access scope analysis.
The date and time when the network insights access scope analysis completed.
Indicates whether the analysis detected any network paths matching the access scope, returning 'true' if findings were found and 'false' otherwise.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Network Insights Access Scope Analysis.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the Network Insights Access Scope Analysis when it is created.
The ID of the Network Access Scope that this analysis will use to identify and analyze network paths.
The date and time when the access scope analysis started.
The status of the access scope analysis, indicating whether it is running, succeeded, or failed.
A computed human-readable message that provides additional detail about the status of the network insights access scope analysis, typically indicating the reason when the analysis fails.
Specifies the tags to assign to the Network Insights Access Scope Analysis resource, which are key-value pairs used for identifying and managing the analysis.
The key of a user-defined tag that can be attached to the Network Insights Access Scope Analysis resource to label or categorize it for management and identification.
The value of a tag key attached to the Network Insights Access Scope Analysis resource, used for custom metadata and resource organization.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.additi.text: The list of additional AWS account IDs to include in the network insights analysis, enabling cross-account reachability analysis by including resources from those accounts.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.altern.text: Lists the potential intermediate components (by ID and ARN) that could form an alternate valid path between the analyzed source and destination.
The ARN of the component referenced by the alternate path hint, identifying the network resource on the alternate path in the network insights analysis.
The component_id of an alternate path hint identifies the ID of the network component (such as a subnet or network interface) on the alternate path discovered during the network insights analysis.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.explan.text: Returns a list of explanation objects that describe the network path analysis results, including the source, destination, and intermediate components along the path.
Specifies the network ACL component evaluated during the Network Insights path analysis, including its rules and whether it allowed or denied the traffic.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the network ACL associated with this explanation component in the network insights analysis.
The ID of the network ACL (network access control list) that this explanation entry refers to in the network insights analysis result.
The network ACL rule that explains the traffic path, including details such as CIDR, port range, protocol, rule action, and rule number.
The CIDR block (IPv4 or IPv6 range) matched by the network ACL rule referenced in this explanation of the network insights analysis path.
Indicates whether this network ACL rule applies to outbound (egress) traffic, as opposed to inbound (ingress) traffic.
Specifies the inclusive range of ports (from and to port numbers) that the network ACL rule applies to in the reachability explanation.
The inclusive lower bound of the port range that this network ACL rule matches for the analyzed path.
The inclusive upper bound of the port range for the network ACL rule described in this explanation.
The IP protocol (e.g., tcp, udp, icmp, or a protocol number) that the network ACL rule applies to, identifying which traffic matches this rule in the analysis explanation.
The action taken by the network ACL rule, either 'allow' or 'deny', indicating whether the rule permits or drops the traffic.
The rule number of the network ACL entry that was matched during the path analysis, as part of the ACL rule explanation.
The IP address or CIDR block that this explanatory component in the network path analysis refers to, identifying the specific address involved in the reachability explanation.
The list of IP addresses associated with the component or step described by this explanation in the network insights analysis.
The 'attached_to' object identifies the network resource (such as an EC2 instance, network interface, or internet gateway) to which the explained network path component is attached.
The ARN of the network resource that the component in this analysis explanation is attached to, as identified by the Network Insights analysis.
The unique identifier of the AWS network resource (such as a subnet, network interface, or route table) to which this explanation segment is attached.
The list of Availability Zones for the component or network path analyzed in this explanation, indicating which AZs are involved in the path's reachability or analysis.
The list of CIDR address ranges associated with this explanation in the network insights analysis, indicating the relevant IP blocks for the analysis step.
Configuration details of the Classic Load Balancer listener (such as its load balancer port and instance port) that is associated with this step of the network insights analysis explanation.
The port on the EC2 instance to which the Classic Load Balancer listener forwards traffic, as recorded in the network insights analysis explanation.
The port number on which the Classic Load Balancer listener accepts traffic, as identified by the network insights analysis.

This object represents the network component (such as an EC2 instance, subnet, security group, or VPC) that an explanation step in the network insights path analysis refers to, providing identifying metadata like ARN and name.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the component referenced by this explanation in the network insights analysis result.
The ID of the network component (e.g., a security group, subnet, or EC2 instance) that this explanation refers to in the network insights analysis.
For each explanation in a network insights analysis, this field contains the AWS account ID that owns the component being described by that explanation.
The AWS Region where the component referenced by this explanation is located.
The customer gateway object referenced in this network path explanation, identifying the customer gateway (e.g., its ID and ARN) involved in a VPN connection segment of the analyzed path.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the customer gateway component involved in the network path explanation.

The state of the transit gateway route table route, such as 'active' or 'blackhole', indicating whether the route is currently usable or drops traffic.
The VPC object in this return-path explanation step, containing identifying details such as the VPC ARN and ID for the virtual private cloud involved in the analyzed path.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the VPC referenced in this explanation entry for the analyzed network path component.
The ID of the VPC referenced by this explanation segment in the analyzed return path.
The VPC endpoint involved in this explanation step, capturing endpoint details (such as its ID and type) that contributed to the analyzed network path.
The ARN of the VPC endpoint associated with this explanation for a return path component in the network insights analysis.
The unique identifier of the VPC endpoint that is associated with this explanation component in the network path analysis.
The VPC peering connection that this explanation component refers to, providing details about the peering connection used in the analyzed network path.
The ARN (Amazon Resource Name) of the VPC peering connection identified in this explanation, uniquely designating the specific peering connection involved in the analyzed network path.
The unique identifier of the VPC peering connection referenced in this explanation component of the return path.
This field contains the VPN connection object that is part of an explanation for a path component in the EC2 Network Insights analysis, describing the VPN connection involved in the network path.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the VPN connection associated with this explanation component in the return path analysis.
The unique identifier of the VPN connection referenced within an explanation of a network path component in the return path analysis.
Details of the VPN gateway that is part of an explanation for a return path component in the network insights analysis.
The ARN of the VPN gateway that is associated with this explanation step in the return path of the network insights analysis.
The ID of the VPN gateway that explains this step in the network path.
Describes the packet header information for traffic entering this path component, including source and destination addresses, protocol, and source/destination port ranges.
The destination IP addresses carried in the inbound header of the component on the return path.
The destination port ranges in the inbound packet header of a return path component, indicating the range of destination ports covered by the analyzed network path's return traffic.
The inclusive lower bound of the destination port range in the inbound header of a return path component for an EC2 Network Insights Analysis, indicating the starting port of the range.
The upper bound of a destination port range for the inbound header of a return path component in a Network Insights Analysis.

The IP protocol carried in the inbound header of this return path component, indicating which network protocol (e.g., TCP, UDP, or ICMP) is used for the return traffic on that segment of the analyzed path.
The list of source IP addresses from the inbound packet header for this component of the analyzed return path.

For each return path component in the network insights analysis, this field lists the source port ranges (from-to pairs) contained in the inbound header of the analyzed traffic, representing the source ports from which the flow originates at that network segment.
The inclusive starting port number of a source port range in the inbound header of a return path component for the network insights analysis.
The inclusive end value of a source port range in the inbound header of a return path component for a network insights analysis.
Contains the outbound packet header properties (such as source and destination addresses, port ranges, and protocol) at this hop of the return path in the network insights analysis.
The list of destination IP addresses in the outbound header of this return path component, indicating where the analyzed traffic is headed on the return path.
Defines the destination port ranges (each with a start and end port) in the outbound header of a component on the return path of the network insights analysis.
The starting port of a destination port range in an outbound header for a return path component of a network insights analysis, specifying the lower bound of the range.
The inclusive end of the destination port range for the outbound header of this return path component in the network insights analysis.
The IP protocol (for example, tcp, udp, or icmp) used in the outbound header of this return path component in the network insights analysis.
The source IP addresses in the outbound packet header of the corresponding return path component in the network insights analysis.

The list of source port ranges (each containing `from_port` and `to_port`) for the outbound packet header of this return-path component, representing the source ports used by the flow in that direction of the analyzed network path.
The inclusive lower bound of the source port range in the outbound header of this return path component.
The inclusive upper bound of a source port range in the outbound header of a return path component for a network insights analysis.
Details of the route table entry traversed in the return path, including destination CIDR block, route target (gateway, instance, etc.), and route origin.
The destination CIDR block of the route table entry used in the return path of the network insights analysis.
The destination prefix list ID for the route table route in the return path component, identifying the managed prefix list that defines the destination CIDR block for routing decisions.
The ID of the egress-only internet gateway associated with this route table route in the analyzed return path.
The ID of the gateway (such as an internet gateway or virtual private gateway) that the route table route in the analyzed return path targets for traffic forwarding.
The ID of the EC2 instance that is the target of the route table route traversed in the return path of the analyzed network path.
The ID of the NAT gateway that serves as the destination for this route table route in the return path component of the network insights analysis.
The ID of the network interface that serves as the target for this route table route in the analyzed return path.
The origin of the route table route, indicating how the route was created (for example, CreateRoute, CreateRouteTable, EnableVgwRoutePropagation, or VpcPeeringConnection).
The state of the route table entry traversed on the return path, indicating whether the route is active or a blackhole route.
The ID of the transit gateway that the route in the route table uses as its target for the return path.
The ID of the VPC peering connection that this route table route uses as its target, if the route directs traffic to a VPC peering connection.
The security group rule that was evaluated for this component in the network path, identifying the rule ID, direction, and referenced security group that determined the traffic outcome.
The CIDR range specified in the security group rule that governs the return path segment of the network analysis.
Indicates whether the security group rule is an inbound (ingress) or outbound (egress) rule.
Represents the port range (with lower and upper bounds) that the security group rule matched on the corresponding component along the return path of the network insights analysis.
The starting port number of the port range for the security group rule that matched on the return path of the network insights analysis.
The `to` field specifies the inclusive upper bound of the port range allowed by the security group rule in the analyzed return path.
The ID of the prefix list referenced by the security group rule that was evaluated along the return path of the network insights analysis.
The IP protocol (such as tcp, udp, icmp, or a protocol number) associated with the security group rule that matched in the return path component of the network insights analysis.
The ID of the security group that contains the security group rule matched along the analyzed return path, identifying the security group responsible for allowing or denying the return traffic.
The sequence number of this component in the return path of the network insights analysis.
The name of the AWS service (e.g., 'com.amazonaws.s3') that this return path component represents, typically identifying a VPC endpoint service in the analyzed network path.
The VPC from which traffic originates for this hop in the return path of the network insights analysis.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the source VPC for this component in the return path.
The ID of the VPC that serves as the source for this return path component in the network insights analysis result.
The subnet object in a return path component identifies the specific VPC subnet through which the analyzed return path passes, providing details such as the subnet ID, ARN, and CIDR block.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the subnet that appears as a component in the return path of the analyzed network path for the EC2 Network Insights Analysis.
The unique identifier of the subnet that appears in this hop of the return path analyzed by the EC2 Network Insights Analysis.
Details about the transit gateway that appears as a component in the return path of the network insights analysis, including its resource identifier and ARN.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the transit gateway encountered along the analyzed return path, uniquely identifying that gateway within the network path component.
The unique identifier of the transit gateway that appears in a return path component of a network insights analysis, indicating the gateway the traffic traversed on the reverse path.
Details about the transit gateway route table route traversed by the return path, including attributes such as the route origin and route state.
The ID of the transit gateway attachment (such as a VPC or VPN attachment) that serves as the target for this route in the transit gateway route table.
The destination CIDR block that the transit gateway route table route matches for the analyzed return path.
The ID of the prefix list referenced by the transit gateway route table route in the return path component.

The resource_id of the transit gateway route table route in the return path identifies the specific AWS resource (such as a transit gateway attachment) that the route resolves to or targets during network insights analysis.
The type of the AWS resource that the transit gateway route table route points to (e.g., VPC, VPN connection), as recorded in a return path component of a network insights analysis.
Indicates whether the transit gateway route table route used in the network insights analysis was created as a static route or learned through route propagation.
The state of the transit gateway route table route encountered in the return path analysis, indicating whether the route is active or blackholed.
The VPC details (including its ARN and VPC ID) for a given component in the return path of the network insights analysis.
The ARN of the VPC traversed by this return path component in the network insights analysis.
The ID of the VPC through which the return path of the analyzed network traffic traverses, as part of a path component.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.start_.text: The timestamp indicating when the network insights analysis was started.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.status.text: The current status of the network insights analysis, such as 'running', 'succeeded', or 'failed'.
Provides additional context about the current status of the network insights analysis, such as the reason the analysis failed or could not be completed.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.sugges.text: A list of AWS account IDs that the analysis suggests might contain resources (such as security groups or network ACLs) relevant to the network path, even though they are not directly on the path.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.tags.text: Assigns metadata tags to the network insights analysis resource for identification and organization.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.tags.k.text: The key of a tag assigned to the Network Insights Analysis, used to identify and organize the resource.

aws_ec2_network_insights_analysis.tags.v.text: The value of a user-defined tag key attached to the EC2 Network Insights Analysis resource, used for identifying and organizing the analysis.

aws_ec2_network_insights_path.created_da.text: The date and time when the network insights path was created, returned as a string timestamp.

aws_ec2_network_insights_path.destinatio.text: The ID of the AWS resource that serves as the destination for the network insights path, such as an EC2 instance or network interface, used when specifying the destination by resource ID instead of an IP address.
The ARN of the destination resource for the network insights path, computed by AWS after creation.
The IP address of the destination resource used for the network insights path analysis.
The destination port to use for the path analysis when the protocol is TCP or UDP.

aws_ec2_network_insights_path.filter_at_.text: Specifies the path filter applied to the destination endpoint, defining the source and destination addresses and port ranges that determine which traffic is analyzed.
The destination IP address to match when filtering network insights path analysis at the destination.
Defines the destination port range (from and to) used to filter the network path analysis at the destination, so only traffic sent to that port range is considered for the path.
The inclusive lower bound of the destination port range used to filter network path analysis at the destination endpoint.
The end (inclusive) of the destination port range used to filter the path analysis at the destination.
Specifies the source IPv4 address to match when filtering traffic at the destination endpoint of the network insights path.
The source port range to filter network paths at the destination, specifying which source ports are included in the path analysis when the filter is applied at the destination.
The starting port of the source port range used to filter traffic at the destination of the Network Insights Path.
The upper bound (inclusive) of the source port range used to filter traffic at the destination when running an EC2 Network Insights path analysis.
Specifies the filter conditions (such as source/destination IP addresses and port ranges) to apply to the source endpoint when analyzing the network path.
The destination IP address used to filter the network path analysis from the source component, matching traffic to that address.
Specifies the destination port range to filter the path analysis at the source, using From and To integer values to define an inclusive port range.
The lower bound of the destination port range used to filter traffic at the source in the network insights path analysis.
The upper bound of the destination port range for the filter applied at the source of the Network Insights Path.
Specifies the source IPv4 address used to filter the network insights path analysis, so that the path considered is limited to traffic originating from that address.
The inclusive From and To source port numbers used to filter the network path analysis at the source, matching only packets whose source port falls within this range.
The inclusive lower bound of the source port range used to filter traffic at the source endpoint when running the network insights path analysis.
The inclusive upper bound of the source port range used to filter traffic at the path's source.

aws_ec2_network_insights_path.network_in.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Network Insights Path.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS for this network insights path.

aws_ec2_network_insights_path.protocol.text: Specifies the protocol (e.g., TCP or UDP) that the network insights path will analyze between the source and destination.

aws_ec2_network_insights_path.source.text: Specifies the ID of the source resource (such as an EC2 instance, network interface, or subnet) from which the network insights path originates.

aws_ec2_network_insights_path.source_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the source resource in this Network Insights Path, which is automatically resolved from the specified Source property and returned as a read-only attribute.

aws_ec2_network_insights_path.source_ip.text: Specifies the source IP address for the network insights path, used to set the origin of the path when the source resource has multiple IPs or when directly specifying an IP source.

aws_ec2_network_insights_path.tags.text: The tags to attach to the EC2 Network Insights Path, allowing you to organize and identify the path for cost allocation and resource management.

aws_ec2_network_insights_path.tags.key.text: The key portion of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS EC2 Network Insights Path, used for resource categorization and access control.

aws_ec2_network_insights_path.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the EC2 Network Insights Path.

aws_ec2_prefix_list.entries.cidr.text: The CIDR block for the prefix list entry, defining the IP address range that this entry permits.

aws_ec2_prefix_list.entries.description.text: Provides an optional human-readable description for the CIDR entry in an EC2 prefix list.

aws_ec2_prefix_list.tags.key.text: The key of a tag (e.g., 'Name') to be assigned to the EC2 prefix list, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_ec2_prefix_list.tags.value.text: The value of a tag applied to the EC2 prefix list, allowing users to attach arbitrary metadata for identification, management, and cost allocation.

aws_ec2_route_server_endpoint.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the EC2 Route Server Endpoint, used to organize and identify the resource in AWS.

aws_ec2_security_group_egress.id.text: The unique AWS-assigned ID of the security group egress rule (e.g., 'sgr-...'), used to identify the rule after creation.

aws_ec2_security_group_vpc_association.s.text: The current state of the security group's association with the VPC, which can be one of 'associating', 'associated', 'association-failed', 'disassociating', or 'disassociated'.

aws_ec2_spot_fleet.spot_fleet_request_co.text: This object defines the configuration for the Spot Fleet request, including the IAM fleet role, target capacity, launch specifications for instances, and allocation strategy.

Determines how Spot Fleet selects and launches Spot Instances to meet the target capacity, such as lowestPrice for the cheapest pools, diversified across many pools, or capacityOptimized for the pools with optimal capacity.
A user-specified context string for the Spot Fleet request, reserved for future use and currently has no effect on the service.
Determines the policy for terminating instances when the Spot Fleet has excess capacity beyond its target, where 'Default' terminates the excess instances and 'NoTermination' leaves them running.
The ARN of an IAM role that grants Amazon EC2 Spot Fleet permission to launch, manage, and terminate instances on your behalf.
Specifies whether interrupted Spot Instances in the fleet are terminated, stopped, or hibernated when capacity is no longer available at the requested price.

The number of Spot capacity pools (each defined by instance type and Availability Zone) across which the Spot Fleet distributes its target capacity, allowing the fleet to diversify and reduce the risk of losing all capacity if one pool is interrupted.

A list of launch specifications that define the EC2 instances to be launched in the Spot Fleet, including instance type, AMI ID, security groups, IAM instance profile, and other instance configuration settings.
Specifies the block device mappings, such as EBS volumes and instance store volumes, to be attached to the instances created from this launch specification in the Spot Fleet request.

The device name (e.g., /dev/sdh) exposed to the operating system for the block device, as defined in the Spot Fleet launch specification's block device mapping to attach an EBS volume or instance store volume.

Specifies the Amazon EBS volume configuration (including volume size, type, snapshot, encryption, and delete-on-termination settings) for the corresponding block device in the Spot Fleet launch specification.
Specifies whether the attached EBS volume should be automatically deleted when the Spot Instance launched from this launch specification terminates.
Indicates whether the EBS volume created by this block device mapping should be encrypted.
Specifies the number of provisioned I/O operations per second (IOPS) for the EBS volume, used when the volume type is io1 or io2.
The ID of the snapshot to use when creating the Amazon EBS volume for the block device mapping in the Spot Fleet launch specification.
Specifies the size of the EBS volume, in GiB, for the block device attached to each instance launched from this launch specification within the Spot Fleet request.
Specifies the EBS volume type (e.g., gp2, gp3, io1, io2, sc1, st1, or standard) for the block device attached to the spot fleet instances.

Indicates whether to suppress (omit) the specified device from the block device mapping for the Spot Fleet launch specification, overriding any device that would otherwise be inherited from the AMI's block device mapping.
Specifies the virtual device name (e.g., 'ephemeral0') for an instance store volume in the block device mapping of a Spot Fleet launch specification.
Specifies whether instances launched from this launch specification are EBS-optimized, providing dedicated network and storage throughput to Amazon EBS.
The IAM instance profile to associate with the instances launched from this launch specification, specified by its Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or name.
The ARN of the IAM instance profile that is associated with the instances launched for this Spot Fleet launch specification, granting them permissions to access AWS services and resources.
The ID of the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) used to launch instances for this spot fleet launch specification.
Defines the minimum and maximum CPU, memory, and other instance attribute requirements that Spot Fleet uses to select compatible instance types for the launch specification.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of accelerators (for example, GPUs) that an instance must have to match the instance requirements for the Spot Fleet launch specification.
The maximum number of accelerators (e.g., GPUs) that an instance must have, used as an upper bound when filtering instance types for the Spot Fleet's launch specifications.
Specifies the minimum number of accelerators (for example, GPUs) that an instance type must have to be considered for the Spot Fleet, as part of the instance requirements in the launch specification.
Restricts eligible Spot Fleet instance types to those whose accelerators (GPUs) are produced by the specified manufacturers, such as amazon-web-services, amd, nvidia, or xilinx.

Specifies the names of GPU accelerators (e.g., 'a100', 'v100', 't4') that instance types must have, filtering the eligible instance types for the Spot Fleet launch specifications to only those with matching accelerator names.
Specifies the minimum and maximum total accelerator (for example, GPU) memory, in MiB, that the instance types in the Spot Fleet must satisfy.
The maximum total memory, in MiB, that the accelerator(s) must have, used to filter which instance types are eligible for the Spot Fleet.
The minimum total accelerator memory in MiB required for the instance type, used to filter eligible EC2 instance types for the Spot Fleet launch specification.

Specifies the required types of hardware accelerators (e.g., gpu, fpga, inference) that each instance launched as part of the Spot Fleet must include, if any are configured in the instance requirements.
Lists the specific EC2 instance types that are permitted for the Spot Fleet's launch specifications, so EC2 only selects from these types when fulfilling the fleet's capacity.
Specifies whether the instance type must be a bare metal instance, with valid values of included, excluded, or required.
Specifies the minimum and maximum baseline EBS bandwidth (in Mbps) that an instance type must satisfy to be considered for the Spot Fleet.
The maximum baseline EBS bandwidth (in Mbps) that an instance type must meet to be considered for the Spot Fleet launch specification.
The minimum baseline EBS bandwidth (in Mbps) that an instance type must offer to be eligible for the Spot Fleet's instance requirements.
Defines the baseline CPU and memory performance factors (e.g., CPU architecture, manufacturer, memory clock speed) used to filter eligible instance types for the Spot Fleet's instance requirements.
Specifies the CPU baseline performance requirements (e.g., baseline vCPU count and supported instance types) that an instance type must meet to be selected by the Spot Fleet's instance requirements.

Defines the list of CPU baseline performance references, each specifying an instance family and a minimum CPU speed (in GHz) that instance types must meet or exceed for the Spot Fleet's instance requirements.

Specifies the EC2 instance family name (e.g., c6i) that serves as the CPU performance baseline against which other instance types are compared when the Spot Fleet launch specification's instance requirements include baseline performance factors.
Specifies whether the Spot Fleet's instance requirements include or exclude instance types with burstable performance (such as T2 and T3 instances), with valid values of 'include' or 'exclude'.
The list of CPU manufacturers (such as amazon-web-services, amd, or intel) that the instance types must have in order to be considered for the Spot Fleet.
Specifies the list of EC2 instance types that the Spot Fleet will not consider when fulfilling the capacity from the launch specification's instance requirements.

Specifies the acceptable instance generations (e.g., 'current' or 'previous') that the Spot Fleet can use when selecting instance types for the launch specification, filtering out unsupported generations.

Defines the local storage (instance store) requirement for instances in the Spot Fleet launch specification, using one of 'included' (instances may have local storage), 'required' (instances must have local storage), or 'excluded' (instances must not have local storage).
The local storage type (hdd or ssd) that instances must support for their instance store volumes.
Maximum spot price as a percentage of the optimal On-Demand price that you are willing to pay for a Spot Instance, used to filter candidate instance types in the Spot Fleet launch specification.
Defines the minimum and maximum amount of memory (in GiB) per vCPU that an instance type must have to be eligible for the Spot Fleet, specified as an object with Min and Max numeric properties.
The maximum amount of memory (in GiB) per virtual CPU (vCPU) that an instance type must have to be eligible for the Spot Fleet.
The minimum amount of memory (in GiB) per vCPU that an instance type must provide to be considered for the Spot Fleet launch specification.
Defines the minimum and maximum memory (in MiB) an instance must have to be eligible for the Spot Fleet launch specification.
The maximum amount of memory, in MiB, that an instance type must have to meet the Spot Fleet's instance requirements.
The minimum amount of memory, in MiB, that an instance type must have to be considered for the Spot Fleet's launch specification.
Defines the minimum and maximum network bandwidth (in Gbps) that an instance type must support for the launch specification's instance requirements in a Spot Fleet request.
The maximum network bandwidth in Gbps that an instance type must meet for the Spot Fleet to consider it, as specified in the instance requirements of the launch specification.
The minimum network bandwidth in Gigabits per second that an instance type must provide to be considered for the Spot Fleet.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of network interfaces that instance types must support to be considered for the Spot Fleet, used to filter candidate instances by network interface count.
The maximum number of network interfaces that a candidate instance type must have to satisfy the instance requirements of a Spot Fleet launch specification.
The minimum number of network interfaces that an instance type must have to be considered for the Spot Fleet's launch specification, filtering out instances with fewer interfaces.

Specifies the maximum on-demand price per hour that you are willing to pay, expressed as a percentage of the lowest-priced on-demand instance type, to filter which instance types are used for the Spot Fleet's launch specifications.
When enabled, restricts the Spot Fleet to instance types that support encryption of data in transit, such as those offering ENA Express or similar network encryption features.
Determines whether Spot Fleet only launches instances that support hibernation, requiring the instance type to be capable of hibernation.

Specifies the maximum price you are willing to pay for a Spot Instance, expressed as a percentage over the lowest Spot price for the instance types that match the requirements, allowing you to bid above the lowest price to increase your chances of obtaining capacity.
Configures the minimum and maximum total local storage (in GB) required for the instance types, as part of the instance requirements for the Spot Fleet launch specification.

Specifies the maximum total local storage (in GB) that an instance type must have, used as a filter in the instance requirements for selecting eligible instance types in the Spot Fleet launch specification.
The minimum amount of local storage, in GB, that an instance must have to match the Spot Fleet's instance requirements.
Defines the minimum and maximum number of vCPUs an instance type must offer to be considered eligible for the Spot Fleet, filtering instance types based on their vCPU count.
The maximum number of vCPUs that an instance type must have to be eligible for the Spot Fleet.
The minimum number of vCPUs that an instance type must have to satisfy the instance requirements for the Spot Fleet's launch specifications.
The EC2 instance type (e.g., t2.micro, m5.large) that the Spot Fleet uses when launching instances from this launch specification.
The ID of the kernel to select for instances launched with this launch specification, overriding the default kernel from the AMI.
The name of the EC2 key pair used for SSH access to the instances launched by the Spot Fleet.
Configures whether detailed monitoring (1-minute CloudWatch metrics) is enabled for instances launched from this spot fleet launch specification, via an 'Enabled' subfield.
Indicates whether detailed monitoring is enabled for the instances launched by the Spot Fleet.
Specifies one or more network interfaces to attach to the Spot Fleet instances launched from this launch specification, including settings such as device index, subnet, and public IP assignment.
When true, automatically assigns a public IPv4 address to the network interface for instances launched from this Spot Fleet launch specification.
Controls whether the network interface is deleted when the Spot Instance terminates, as part of each network interface definition in the Spot Fleet launch specification.
The description of the network interface, providing a human-readable label for the ENI in the EC2 console and APIs.
The device index for the network interface, where 0 denotes the primary network interface (eth0) and higher values attach additional interfaces to the spot instance.
Specifies the security group IDs to attach to the network interface when the Spot Fleet launches instances.
Specifies the number of IPv6 addresses to assign to the network interface in the launch specification for instances in the Spot Fleet.
The list of IPv6 addresses to assign to the network interface of the Spot Fleet instance launched from this launch specification.
Specifies an IPv6 address to assign to the network interface of the Spot Fleet instance.
The ID of an existing EC2 network interface to attach to instances launched from this launch specification, instead of creating a new one.
Defines the private IP addresses (with a Primary flag for each) to assign to the network interface in the Spot Fleet launch specification.
Specifies whether the private IP address is the primary private IP address of the network interface in the Spot Fleet launch specification.
Specifies the private IPv4 address to assign to a network interface on a Spot Fleet instance, used when configuring multiple private IP addresses for an interface in a launch specification.
Specifies the number of secondary private IP addresses to assign to the network interface in the Spot Fleet launch specification, in addition to the primary private IP address.
The ID of the subnet in which to place the network interface for instances launched from this launch specification.

Specifies the placement preferences for instances launched from this launch specification, including the Availability Zone, placement group name, and tenancy that determine where the Spot Fleet places its instances.
The Availability Zone in which the Spot Fleet launches instances for this launch specification.
The stable, provider-specific identifier of the Availability Zone (such as use1-az1) in which the Spot Fleet launches the instances for this launch specification, independent of the zone's name.
The name of the placement group in which to launch the instances for this Spot Fleet launch specification.
Specifies the tenancy model (e.g., default, dedicated, or host) for instances launched from this Spot Fleet launch specification, determining whether they run on shared or single-tenant hardware.
The ID of the RAM disk to select for the instance, typically used with instance store-backed AMIs to specify a particular kernel RAM disk image.
Specifies the security groups to associate with the instances launched from this launch specification.
The ID of the security group to associate with each instance launched from this Spot Fleet launch specification, controlling network access to the instances.
The maximum Spot price per instance hour for instances launched using this launch specification, which overrides the Spot Fleet's default spot price if specified.
The ID of the subnet in which the Spot Fleet launches instances for this launch specification.
Defines the tags to apply to the EC2 instances and volumes created from the associated launch specification in the Spot Fleet request.
The AWS resource type (e.g., 'instance' or 'volume') to which the tags in this tag specification apply for the EC2 instances launched by the Spot Fleet.
The key-value pairs that define the tags to apply to the resource type (such as instance or volume) specified in the parent tag specification for the Spot Fleet launch specifications.
The key of a tag to apply to the resources (e.g., instances or volumes) launched by the Spot Fleet via this launch specification.
Specifies the value for a tag key applied to a resource type (e.g., instance or volume) created by this Spot Fleet launch specification.

The base64-encoded user data script or configuration that is injected into instances launched from this launch specification, enabling initialization tasks like bootstrapping or cloud-init directives.

Defines the relative weight (capacity units) for this launch specification when the Spot Fleet calculates its total capacity against the target capacity, letting a mix of instance types of differing sizes contribute to fleet capacity.

Specifies one or more launch template configurations that the Spot Fleet uses to launch spot instances, including the launch template to use and any overrides for instance types, Availability Zones, subnet IDs, and weighted capacity.
Identifies the EC2 launch template to use for the Spot Fleet's launch configuration, including the launch template ID or name, and optionally the version.
Specifies the unique ID of the Amazon EC2 launch template that the Spot Fleet uses to launch instances for this launch template configuration.
The name of the EC2 launch template that the Spot Fleet uses to launch instances for this launch template configuration, as specified in the launch template specification.
Specifies the version of the launch template to use when launching instances for the Spot Fleet (for example, a specific version number or '$Latest').
Specifies a list of overrides that define instance types and subnets (with optional capacity and priority) to apply to the launch template when the Spot Fleet places instances.
Overrides the Availability Zone in which Spot Instances are launched for this launch template configuration, allowing the Spot Fleet to distribute instances across specific AZs.

Defines the Availability Zone ID (e.g., use1-az1) for the Spot Fleet's launch template override, directing the fleet to launch instances in that specific Availability Zone instead of using the zone name.

Specifies the instance attribute requirements (e.g., minimum and maximum vCPUs, memory, and storage) that the Spot Fleet uses to filter and select eligible instance types for this launch template override.
Specifies the minimum and maximum number of GPU accelerators (e.g., GPUs) required for instance types to match the Spot Fleet's launch template overrides.
The maximum number of accelerators (e.g., GPUs) that an instance must have to be considered matching the Spot Fleet's instance requirements.
The minimum number of accelerators (e.g., GPUs) that an instance type must have to satisfy the instance requirements for the Spot Fleet launch template override.

Specifies the acceptable manufacturers of accelerators (such as NVIDIA, AMD, or Xilinx) for instances that meet the stated requirements, filtering to instances with accelerators from the listed manufacturers in the Spot Fleet's instance requirements.
Specifies a list of accelerator names (e.g., 'a100', 'v100', 't4') that instance types in the Spot Fleet launch template overrides must have, acting as a filter within the instance requirements.
Specifies the minimum and maximum total accelerator memory in MiB that an instance must have to match the instance requirements for the Spot Fleet's launch template overrides.

Maximum total accelerator memory (in MiB) that an instance type must have to be considered for the Spot Fleet, used to filter instance types based on the total memory of all accelerators (e.g., GPUs, FPGAs) on the instance.
The minimum total accelerator memory in MiB that an instance type must have to be considered for the Spot Fleet's launch template overrides.
Specifies the accelerator hardware types (e.g., 'gpu', 'fpga', 'inference') that the instance must include to match the spot fleet's instance requirements.

Defines the list of EC2 instance types that the Spot Fleet may select from when launching instances, filtering the available instance types based on the other instance requirements such as vCPU and memory.
Determines whether the instance must be a bare metal instance (e.g., i3.metal), with allowed values of 'included', 'excluded', or 'required'.
Specifies the minimum and maximum baseline EBS bandwidth (in Mbps) that an instance type must meet for the Spot Fleet to consider it.
The maximum baseline EBS bandwidth, in Mbps, that an instance must have to be selected for the Spot Fleet.
Specifies the minimum baseline EBS bandwidth in Mbps that an instance type must provide to match the Spot Fleet's instance requirements.
Specifies the baseline CPU and memory performance requirements (low, medium, or high) that EC2 instance types must satisfy to be considered for the Spot Fleet's launch template override.
Provides the CPU baseline performance requirements (such as baseline cores and baseline speed) that an instance type must meet to be considered for the Spot Fleet.
References to CPU performance baselines (e.g., specific CPU names or manufacturers) that filter instances according to their baseline CPU performance for the Spot Fleet's instance requirements.
The name of an EC2 instance family (e.g., c6i or m5) used as a reference to define the CPU baseline performance factor in the instance requirements for the Spot Fleet's launch template overrides.

Specifies whether the Spot Fleet should include, exclude, or require burstable performance instance types (such as T3, T3a, T2) when matching instance requirements, with allowed values 'included', 'excluded', or 'required'.
Specifies the allowed CPU manufacturers (e.g., amazon-web-services, intel, amd) for instance requirements, filtering eligible instance types by CPU vendor.
Specifies instance types that should not be used when fulfilling the Spot Fleet request, excluding them from consideration based on your instance requirements.

Specifies the instance generations (e.g., current or previous) that the Spot Fleet can consider when selecting instance types from the launch template overrides, filtering out instance families that are not from the chosen generation(s).
Specifies whether instance types that have local (instance store) storage are included, required, or excluded from the Spot Fleet's instance type selection.
Specifies the type of local storage (hdd or ssd) that instances must have, restricting launch to instance types with the specified local storage types.
