Specifies the Amazon EBS volume type (e.g., gp3, io2) for the managed EBS volume attached to tasks in this ECS service.

aws_ecs_service.volume_configurations.na.text: The name of the EBS volume attached at the ECS service level, which must match the volume name referenced by container mount points as sourceVolume in the task definition.

aws_ecs_service.vpc_lattice_configuratio.text: Specifies the name of the port mapping in the task definition that VPC Lattice uses to route traffic to the service.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon ECS assumes to register and deregister the service with the associated VPC Lattice target group.
The ARN of the VPC Lattice target group that this ECS service registers with as a target.

aws_ecs_task_definition.container_defini.text: The command to run in the container, which overrides the default command specified in the container image.
The number of CPU units reserved for this container, which determines the relative CPU share allocated to it within the task.

A list of ARNs for Windows credential specification files (used for gMSA or domain-joined containers) that are applied to this container definition, either stored in an S3 bucket or in the ECS service-linked role.

Specifies dependencies on other containers in the same task, controlling startup and shutdown order by requiring a container to reach a certain condition (e.g., START, COMPLETE, SUCCESS, HEALTHY) before this container starts.
Specifies the state that the container named in depends_on must reach for this container to start, such as START, COMPLETE, SUCCESS, or HEALTHY.
Specifies the name of the container that this container depends on, as part of the container's dependency conditions within the same task definition.
When set to true, disables networking for the container, meaning it does not receive a network interface and has no network access within the task.
A list of DNS search domain names that are passed to the container's resolver configuration, allowing the container to search these domains when resolving hostnames.
Specifies the DNS servers for the container, which are written to the container's /etc/resolv.conf file as nameserver entries.
Specifies the custom Docker labels to add to the container as key-value pairs, which can be used for organizing or identifying the container.
Specifies the Docker security options (a list of strings) that are passed to the container runtime, such as 'no-new-privileges', to enforce additional security constraints on the container.

Specifies the entry point for the container as a list of strings, overriding the default ENTRYPOINT defined in the container image, where the first string is the executable and the rest are arguments.
The environment variables to pass to the container, as a list of objects each containing a name and a value.
The name of the environment variable to configure in the container as part of the task definition's container environment list.
The value of the environment variable defined for the container in the ECS task definition, paired with the corresponding name in the environment key-value list.
A list of environment files (S3 objects) whose contents define environment variables that are injected into the container at task launch.
Specifies the type of the environment file, where the only supported value is 's3', indicating the file is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket.
The Amazon S3 object ARN (e.g., arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/key-name) of the environment variables file that ECS loads into the container environment.
Specifies whether this container is essential to the task; if an essential container stops or fails, all other containers in the task are stopped and the task is considered failed.
Specifies additional hostname-to-IP address mappings to add to the container's /etc/hosts file, allowing the container to resolve those hostnames.
The hostname to add to the container's /etc/hosts file, paired with its IP address in the same extra_hosts entry.
The IP address to which the corresponding hostname in the extra_hosts entry is resolved inside the container's network configuration (e.g., appended to /etc/hosts).

Specifies the FireLens configuration for a container in the ECS task definition, enabling log routing to destinations like Fluentd or Fluent Bit via a configurable type and options such as log metadata and config file delivery.
Configures FireLens log routing by providing settings such as config-file-type, config-file-value, and enable-ecs-log-metadata.
Specifies the log router to use for Firelens, either 'fluentd' or 'fluentbit' (required).
Defines the container health check configuration, including the command to run and parameters such as interval, timeout, retries, and start period, which ECS uses to determine container health.

The command (as a list of strings, e.g., ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost/"]) that the container runs to perform its health check, corresponding directly to the Docker HEALTHCHECK instruction's command portion.
The time period in seconds between each container health check execution, as part of the ECS task definition container health check configuration.
Specifies the number of times to retry a failed health check before the container is considered unhealthy, with a default of 3.

Specifies the duration in seconds that Amazon ECS waits after the container starts before it begins counting failed health check results, providing a grace period for containers that need time to initialize before being marked unhealthy.
The number of seconds to wait for a health check to succeed before considering the container unhealthy.
Sets the hostname of the container, which other containers in the same task definition can use for DNS resolution.
The Docker image (e.g., a repository URL or image name:tag) to run for this container in the ECS task definition.
When set to true, this enables the container's interactive mode, keeping STDIN open and allowing a shell or other process to interact with the container, equivalent to Docker's `--interactive` flag.
Specifies a list of container names to link, enabling network connectivity and injecting environment variables for inter-container communication.

Specifies Linux-specific container configuration options such as kernel capabilities, device mappings, init process enablement, shared memory size, tmpfs mounts, and swap settings for a container in an ECS task definition.
Specifies the Linux capabilities to add or remove from the container's default set, with 'add' and 'drop' lists of capability names.
Specifies additional Linux capabilities to grant the container, such as SYS_ADMIN or NET_ADMIN, in the task definition's Linux parameters.
Specifies the Linux capabilities to remove from the container's default set, such as SYS_ADMIN or NET_RAW, to restrict its privileges at runtime.
A list of host devices to expose to the container, each specifying the host path, optional container path, and access permissions (read, write, mknod).
The path inside the container at which the host device is mounted and exposed.
The absolute path on the host of the device to expose to the container, used in a Linux container's devices configuration to grant access to host devices.

Specifies the device permissions (e.g., read, write, mknod) that grant the container access to each host device listed in the devices block, controlling what operations the container can perform on those devices.
When true, runs an init process as PID 1 inside the container to reap zombie processes and properly forward signals, such as SIGTERM, to the main application.
The maximum amount of swap memory (in MiB) the container can use, overriding the host's default swap settings for this container.
Specifies the size in MiB of the shared memory (/dev/shm) volume to allocate for the container, overriding the default 64 MiB.
The swappiness parameter controls the relative weight of swapping out anonymous pages versus page cache in the container, accepting an integer from 0 to 100 that is passed as a kernel tuning option.

Configures temporary file system (tmpfs) mounts for the container, listing each mount's container path, size in MiB, and optional mount options as defined under LinuxParameters in the ECS task definition.
The absolute file path inside the container where the tmpfs volume is mounted.
Specifies the mount options (e.g., size, mode, ro) passed to the tmpfs mount for the container.
The size of the tmpfs mount in MiB, specifying the maximum capacity of the temporary filesystem mounted at the container's path.

This object configures the logging driver for the container (e.g., awslogs, json-file, syslog) and its options, such as awslogs-group and awslogs-region, controlling how container logs are captured and delivered to the specified destination.
Specifies the logging driver used by the container, such as awslogs for CloudWatch Logs, fluentd, syslog, json-file, or splunk, which determines how and where container logs are delivered.
The options map provides the key-value configuration parameters for the container's chosen log driver (for example, awslogs-group and awslogs-region for the awslogs driver).
Specifies the secrets to pass to the log driver configuration, allowing you to reference sensitive information from AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store.
The name (key) of the log driver option for which the referenced secret's value is used, such as 'splunk-token' or 'project' in the log configuration.
The ARN of the secret (from AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store) that provides the value for the corresponding log driver option in the ECS task definition's log configuration.
Specifies the hard limit (in MiB) of memory available to the container; when the container's memory usage reaches this limit, the container is killed.
The soft memory limit in MiB for the container, which ECS uses for placement and scheduling, allowing the container to burst above this value when the host has spare memory.
Specifies the mount points for data volumes in the container, including the source volume name and the container path where the volume is mounted.
The container_path specifies the absolute path inside the container where the volume is mounted.
Determines whether the container has read-only access to the mounted volume; when set to true, writes to the volume are rejected, and when false, read/write access is permitted.
Name of the volume to mount, which must match the name of a volume defined in the task definition's volumes block.

The name of the container definition, which must be unique among all container definitions in the task definition and is used to reference the container from other definitions (e.g., links, dependsOn, and volume mounts).
Defines the port mappings for a container, specifying container port, host port, and protocol (tcp/udp), which controls how traffic is routed to the container in the ECS task.
Specifies the application protocol (e.g., http, http2, grpc) for this port mapping, which is used by AWS App Mesh and Amazon ECS Service Connect to route traffic to the container.
The port number on the container that receives inbound traffic, paired with a host port to map a container port to a port on the host for ECS task definition port mappings.
Specifies the inclusive range of container ports to map to the host, using the format 'startPort-endPort' (for example, '8000-8080'), enabling the task to expose multiple ports in one definition.

The port number on the container instance (host) that receives inbound traffic and forwards it to the container's `containerPort`, used with bridge and host network modes; it can be left empty to map directly to the container port.
The name that identifies this port mapping, used when configuring Service Connect for the ECS service.
The transport protocol (tcp, udp, or tcpudp) that this port mapping uses for communication in the container definition.
When set to true, the container runs in privileged mode, granting it elevated permissions on the host container instance (similar to Docker's --privileged flag).
Indicates whether to allocate a pseudo-TTY (teletypewriter) for the container, enabling an interactive terminal session, similar to the Docker `--tty` flag.
Specifies whether the container's root filesystem is mounted in read-only mode, preventing the container from writing to its root filesystem while still permitting writes to attached volumes.
Specifies the AWS Secrets Manager secret or SSM parameter ARN that holds the credentials needed to pull the container image from a private registry.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret or Systems Manager parameter that stores the authentication credentials for the private container repository used by this container definition.
Specifies the type and amount of a resource (such as GPU or InferenceAccelerator) that the container requires, used to request hardware accelerators like NVIDIA GPUs or AWS Inferentia chips.
Specifies the type of resource to reserve for the container, such as GPU or InferenceAccelerator, in the ECS task definition's container definition resource requirements.
The value of the resource requirement, which specifies the number of GPUs for the 'GPU' type or the device name for the 'InferenceAccelerator' type.

Specifies the restart policy for the container, including whether it is enabled and the attempt period, allowing the container to automatically restart after a failure or exit; it is only supported for tasks using the Fargate launch type.
Whether the container's restart policy is enabled, allowing ECS to automatically restart the container if it exits or fails.
Specifies a list of container exit codes that are ignored by the ECS restart policy, so the container is not restarted when it exits with any of these codes.
The number of seconds to wait after a container exits before attempting to restart it, as part of the ECS restart policy to control the frequency of restart attempts.

Specifies the secrets to pass to the container, referencing either AWS Secrets Manager secrets or SSM Parameter Store parameters, each containing a name and a valueFrom ARN or full SSM parameter name.
The name of the environment variable that will be set on the container, with its value securely supplied from the secret specified in the corresponding valueFrom field.
Specifies the ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret or the name/ARN of the SSM parameter that supplies the secret value to be injected into the container.
Specifies the time duration in seconds to wait for the container to become healthy after it starts, after which the container is considered failed if it has not reached a healthy state.
The time in seconds to wait for the container to stop after sending SIGTERM before the system sends SIGKILL, overriding the Docker daemon's default stop timeout.

Specifies a list of system control (sysctl) settings to apply to the container, allowing you to modify kernel parameters such as network stack settings (e.g., net.ipv4.ip_forward) as defined in the container definition.
The sysctl namespace (kernel parameter name) to configure for the container, such as `kernel.msgmax` or `net.ipv4.ip_forward`.
The value assigned to the Linux kernel system control (sysctl) specified by the `namespace` field, such as `1` to enable IP forwarding in the container's network namespace.
Defines a list of ulimit settings for the container that override Docker defaults, each specifying a resource type (such as 'nofile' or 'cpu') along with soft and hard limits.
The hard limit (maximum value) for the ulimit setting on the container, which the container cannot exceed.
Specifies the type of ulimit to apply to the container, such as 'cpu', 'nofile', 'nproc', or other valid Linux resource limit names.
The lower boundary (soft limit) for the container's ulimit value, specifying the resource limit that can be raised by the process up to the hard limit.
The user name or numeric UID (and optionally group) to run the container process as, overriding the image's default user.

Specifies whether ECS version consistency is enabled for this container definition, accepting values 'enabled' or 'disabled' to control whether the container image is pinned to an exact digest for immutable deployments.
Specifies the volumes to mount from other containers in the same task definition, including the source container name and whether the mount is read-only.
If true, the container mounts the volume from the source container as read-only.
The name of the source container from which this container mounts volumes, as defined in the containerDefinitions.
The working directory inside the container where the container's entrypoint command is run.

aws_ecs_task_definition.inference_accele.text: Configures the Amazon Elastic Inference accelerators to attach to the task, where each accelerator is specified by a device name and device type.
The name of the inference accelerator device, which the container uses to access the accelerator (e.g., 'device1').
Specifies the Elastic Inference accelerator type (e.g., eia2.medium or eia1.large) to attach to the task.

aws_ecs_task_definition.placement_constr.text: The cluster query language expression that defines the placement constraint when the type is 'memberOf', specifying which container instances the task can be placed on.

The placement constraint type, which must be either 'distinctInstance' (place each task on a distinct container instance) or 'memberOf' (use a cluster query language expression defined in the expression field).

aws_ecs_task_definition.proxy_configurat.text: This is the name (key) of a key-value pair in the ECS task definition's proxy configuration properties, identifying which proxy setting (e.g., ProxyIngressPort, ProxyEgressPort, IgnoredUID, or AppPorts) the corresponding value applies to.
The string value of a key in the proxy configuration properties map, defining parameters such as AppPorts, EgressIgnoredPorts, or IgnoredUIDs for the AWS App Mesh proxy in the ECS task definition.

aws_ecs_task_definition.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a key-value tag attached to the ECS task definition, used for resource identification and cost allocation.

aws_ecs_task_definition.task_definition_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this task definition.

aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.configur.text: When set to true, indicates that the volume is configured on the container instance at launch time rather than being fully specified in the task definition, enabling dynamic volume configuration (such as for Docker volumes) at runtime.

aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.docker_v.text: Specifies the Docker volume configuration for a volume in the task definition, including the volume scope, autoprovision setting, driver, driver options, and labels when the volume type is 'docker'.
When true, ECS automatically creates the named Docker volume if it does not already exist when the task is launched.
Specifies the Docker volume driver to use, such as 'local' or a third-party driver (e.g., 'rexray'), for the volume configured in the task definition.
Specifies a map of Docker driver-specific options passed to the volume driver when configuring a Docker volume in an ECS task definition.
Specifies key-value pairs that are assigned as Docker volume labels, which serve as metadata for organizing and identifying the volume and are passed to the Docker volume driver.
Determines the lifecycle of the Docker volume, where 'task' auto-provisions and deletes the volume when the task stops, and 'shared' allows the volume to exist independently of any single task.

aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.efsvolum.text: Configures an Amazon EFS volume for the task definition, specifying the EFS filesystem ID, root directory path, transit encryption and port, and optional IAM authorization via an access point.
The authorization configuration for an Amazon EFS volume, specifying the EFS access point ID and IAM role to use for the volume's file system access.
The access point ID of the EFS file system that Amazon ECS uses to mount the volume, applying the access point's root directory and POSIX user/group permissions to the task's container.
Specifies whether to use IAM authorization for the EFS volume's access point, with a value of 'ENABLED' to enable IAM authentication or 'DISABLED' to use the default EFS security settings.
The ID of the Amazon EFS file system that this volume mounts, identifying the target file system for the container's persistent storage.
The path on the Amazon EFS file system to mount as the root directory for the container, defaulting to '/' if not specified.
Indicates whether Amazon EFS uses encryption for data in transit when the volume is mounted in the task, accepting 'ENABLED' to enable encryption or 'DISABLED' to disable it.
Specifies the port on the EFS file system to use for transit encryption, required when transit encryption is enabled.

aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.fsx_wind.text: Specifies the configuration for using an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server volume as a data volume in the ECS task definition, including the file system ID, root directory, and authorization configuration.
Specifies the domain and the AWS Secrets Manager credential secret that the container uses to mount the FSx for Windows File Server volume.
Specifies the ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret or Systems Manager parameter that stores the Microsoft Active Directory domain credentials for mounting the FSx Windows file server volume.
The domain field specifies the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of the Active Directory domain to use for authentication when accessing the FSx Windows File Server volume.
The ID of the Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system to mount for this volume in the ECS task definition.
The root directory on the FSx Windows File Server file system to mount as the root for the container's volume.

aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.host.text: The host object defines the source path on the container instance for a bind mount volume, with its `sourcePath` property specifying the exact host directory to mount.

aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.host.sou.text: Specifies the path on the host container instance (EC2) that is mounted into the container when the volume type is 'host'.

aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.name.text: The name of the volume, which is referenced by container definitions in the mountPoints.sourceVolume property.

aws_ecs_task_definition.volumes.s3_files.text: Configuration for an Amazon S3 file volume within an ECS task definition, specifying the S3 bucket, key (object path), and optional object version used to mount a single S3 object as a file into the container.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 access point that ECS uses to access the S3 bucket for this volume configuration.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 bucket that ECS mounts as a file system volume to tasks using the S3 file volume configuration.
Specifies the subdirectory within the S3 bucket that is mounted as the root of the ECS volume, determining the base path for files exposed via this volume configuration.
Specifies the custom port used for encrypted (TLS) communication with Amazon S3 when the S3 volume's transit encryption is enabled.

aws_ecs_task_set.capacity_provider_strat.text: Specifies the capacity provider strategy for the task set, defining which capacity providers to use and the weights and base values that govern how tasks are distributed among them.
The minimum number of tasks to run on this capacity provider before the task set's weight-based scaling applies.
The name of the capacity provider, as registered in the ECS cluster, that this task set should use for running tasks.
The relative weight assigned to a capacity provider in the strategy, determining what proportion of tasks from the task set are placed on that provider.

aws_ecs_task_set.load_balancers.text: Configures the load balancer or target groups that route traffic to the tasks in this ECS task set, specifying the container and port to receive traffic.

aws_ecs_task_set.load_balancers.containe.text: The name of the container, as defined in the task definition, to which the load balancer routes traffic for this task set.
The container port on which the task set's containers receive traffic from the associated load balancer or target group, used to route incoming requests to the correct container port.

aws_ecs_task_set.load_balancers.target_g.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the target group to which the ECS task set's tasks are registered for load balancing.

aws_ecs_task_set.scale.text: Specifies the scaling configuration for the task set, including the unit (e.g., PERCENT) and value that determine the target number of tasks for the task set.

aws_ecs_task_set.service_registries.cont.text: Specifies the container name from the task definition to use for the service discovery (Cloud Map) registry, and if not provided, the default container in the task definition is used.
Specifies the container port that the Amazon ECS task set's service registry uses for service discovery with AWS Cloud Map.

aws_ecs_task_set.service_registries.port.text: The port number that the service discovery service uses for the task's registry entry, which overrides the container's port mapping if specified.

aws_ecs_task_set.service_registries.regi.text: The ARN of the AWS Cloud Map service registry in which the task set's tasks are registered for service discovery.

aws_ecs_task_set.tags.key.text: The key of a tag that can be assigned to the ECS task set for organizational or identification purposes.

aws_ecs_task_set.tags.value.text: Specifies the value of a user-defined tag attached to the ECS task set, which can be used for resource categorization, cost allocation, and operational management.

aws_efs_access_point.access_point_id.text: The AWS-assigned unique identifier for the EFS access point, used to reference the access point in other resources or APIs.

aws_efs_access_point.access_point_tags.k.text: The key of a tag in the access_point_tags list on the EFS access point, corresponding to the Key property of the CloudFormation AccessPointTags tag objects.

aws_efs_access_point.access_point_tags.v.text: The value of a tag applied to the EFS access point, used for metadata and resource categorization.

aws_efs_access_point.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the EFS access point, which uniquely identifies the access point within AWS.

aws_efs_file_system.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this EFS file system, used to reference it in IAM policies and other AWS services.

aws_efs_file_system.file_system_id.text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier (e.g., fs-12345678) for the EFS file system, returned by AWS and used to reference the file system in other resources.

aws_efs_file_system.file_system_tags.key.text: The key of a tag applied to the EFS file system, used to organize and identify the resource within AWS.

aws_efs_file_system.file_system_tags.val.text: The value portion of a tag assigned to the EFS file system, used for metadata, cost allocation, or access control.

aws_efs_file_system.lifecycle_policies.t.text: Specifies when EFS moves files to the Archive storage class (e.g., AFTER_30_DAYS) based on the number of days since last access, as part of the file system's lifecycle policy.
Specifies the number of days (as a string such as 'AFTER_7_DAYS') after which files are transitioned to the Amazon EFS Infrequent Access (IA) storage class within this lifecycle policy.

Specifies when EFS transitions files from the Infrequent Access storage class back to the Standard storage class, with the only valid value being AFTER_1_ACCESS, meaning a file is moved after it is accessed once.

aws_efs_file_system.replication_configur.text: Designates the Availability Zone in which the destination file system of the EFS replication configuration is created, allowing a one-zone replicated file system target; if omitted, AWS chooses an AZ for the destination.
The ID of the destination EFS file system that receives replicated data from the source file system in an EFS replication configuration.
The ID of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the replicated file system data in the destination Region.
Specifies the AWS Region of the destination EFS file system to which the source EFS file system replicates data.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon EFS assumes when replicating the source file system to the destination file system.
The computed status of the replication destination, indicating whether replication to this file system is enabled, enabling, deleting, or in an error state.
For an Amazon EFS file system's replication destination, this string contains the descriptive message about the current replication status, such as an error reason when replication is failing.

aws_efs_mount_target.id.text: The unique identifier of the EFS mount target, typically the mount target ID (e.g., fsmt-12345678), used to reference the mount target in other resources.

aws_egress_only_internet_gateway.tags.ke.text: The key portion of a tag attached to the egress-only internet gateway, used for identifying, organizing, and managing this VPC component in AWS.

aws_egress_only_internet_gateway.tags.va.text: The tag value (string) for a tag applied to the egress-only internet gateway, allowing you to categorize and manage this IPv6 outbound-only VPC component.

aws_eip.allocation_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this Elastic IP address when it was allocated for use in a VPC.

aws_eip.public_ip.text: The public IPv4 address that AWS allocates to the Elastic IP (EIP) resource, which you can associate with an EC2 instance or network interface.

aws_eip.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the Elastic IP address.

aws_eks_access_entry.access_policies.acc.text: Defines the scope of the access policy, either for the entire cluster when the type is 'cluster' or for the specified namespaces when the type is 'namespace'.
The namespaces that the access policy applies to when the access scope type is set to 'namespace', restricting the policy's permissions to those specific Kubernetes namespaces.
Specifies whether the access policy applies to the entire EKS cluster or only to specific Kubernetes namespaces, with allowed values of 'cluster' or 'namespace'.

aws_eks_access_entry.access_policies.pol.text: The ARN of the IAM access policy that is associated with the access entry for the EKS cluster.

aws_eks_access_entry.tags.key.text: A user-defined key for a tag attached to the EKS access entry, used to label and categorize the entry for management and cost tracking in AWS.

aws_eks_access_entry.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the EKS access entry, used to categorize or identify the resource for management and access control purposes.

aws_eks_addon.pod_identity_associations..text: The ARN of the IAM role to associate with the Kubernetes service account for the EKS pod identity association, which grants pods that use that service account permissions to call AWS APIs.
The name of the Kubernetes service account that the addon's pod identity association will map to the specified IAM role, granting the addon permissions via that role.

aws_eks_addon.tags.value.text: The string value assigned to a tag key on the EKS addon, used to store arbitrary metadata such as environment or owner identifiers for the addon.

aws_eks_capability.configuration.argo_cd.text: Specifies a list of IAM principal ARNs (users or roles) that are mapped to the corresponding Argo CD RBAC role, granting those identities the permissions defined for that role in the Kubernetes cluster.
Defines the identity type (user or group) for an Argo CD RBAC role mapping in the EKS capability configuration.

aws_eks_cluster.encryption_config.text: Specifies the AWS KMS key ARN and the Kubernetes resources (like secrets) to enable envelope encryption for the EKS cluster.

aws_eks_cluster.encryption_config.provid.text: Specifies the AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) ARN used to encrypt Kubernetes secrets for the EKS cluster.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt Kubernetes secrets in the EKS cluster.

aws_eks_cluster.encryption_config.resour.text: Specifies the Kubernetes resource types (such as 'secrets') that are encrypted with the KMS key configured in this encryption configuration for the EKS cluster.

aws_eks_cluster.logging.cluster_logging..text: Specifies one Kubernetes control plane log type (such as api, audit, authenticator, controllerManager, or scheduler) to enable for the EKS cluster.

aws_eks_cluster.remote_network_config.re.text: Defines the list of CIDR blocks for the remote node networks, specifying the IP address ranges used by remote (hybrid) nodes in the EKS cluster.
The list of IPv4 CIDR blocks that define the remote pod network address space for this EKS cluster's hybrid node remote network configuration.

aws_eks_cluster.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS EKS cluster, which must be unique within the cluster's tag set and is used to categorize or filter the cluster.

aws_eks_cluster.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag assigned to the EKS cluster, used for metadata such as cost centers or environment identification.

aws_eks_fargate_profile.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Fargate profile.

aws_eks_fargate_profile.selectors.text: Specifies the Kubernetes namespaces and label selectors that determine which pods are scheduled to run on Fargate using this profile.

aws_eks_fargate_profile.selectors.labels.text: Specifies Kubernetes labels (key-value pairs) that the selector uses to match pods in the specified namespace for scheduling on Fargate.
The key of a Kubernetes label pair used in the selector to match pods that will be scheduled on the Fargate profile.
The value of a Kubernetes label, paired with its key in the selector’s labels map, that a pod must have to be eligible for scheduling on this Fargate profile.

aws_eks_fargate_profile.selectors.namesp.text: The Kubernetes namespace that this selector matches; only pods running in this namespace are eligible to be scheduled onto Fargate.

aws_eks_fargate_profile.subnets.text: Specifies the list of subnet IDs where Amazon EKS launches Fargate pods for this profile; if omitted, the subnets selected for the EKS cluster are used.

aws_eks_fargate_profile.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the EKS Fargate profile, used to organize and identify the profile for purposes such as cost allocation, access control, and resource filtering within AWS.

aws_eks_fargate_profile.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag assigned to the EKS Fargate profile, used for cost allocation, organization, and identification of the profile.

aws_eks_identity_provider_config.oidc.re.text: Specifies the list of required claims (each a key-value pair) that must be present in the OIDC identity token with matching values for authentication to succeed.
Specifies the name of an OIDC claim that must be present in the token issued by the identity provider for authentication to be considered valid.

The expected value for a required claim in the OIDC identity provider's token, where the map key is the claim name and this value must match the claim's value in the token for authentication to succeed.

aws_eks_identity_provider_config.tags.ke.text: The key of a tag assigned to the Amazon EKS identity provider configuration resource.

aws_eks_identity_provider_config.tags.va.text: The value of a tag key-value pair applied to the Amazon EKS identity provider configuration, used for metadata management such as cost allocation and resource identification.

aws_eks_nodegroup.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the EKS node group, which uniquely identifies it within AWS and is used for permissions and resource referencing.

aws_eks_nodegroup.launch_template.id.text: The ID of the EC2 launch template that specifies the configuration (e.g., instance type, AMI, user data) for the worker nodes in the EKS node group.

aws_eks_nodegroup.launch_template.name.text: The name of the EC2 launch template to use for configuring the node group's instances.

aws_eks_nodegroup.launch_template.versio.text: The version of the AWS EC2 launch template that the node group will use to launch instances.

aws_eks_nodegroup.node_repair_config.nod.text: Sets the minimum wait time (in minutes) that an unhealthy node in the EKS managed node group must remain in a failed state before the node repair process automatically replaces it.
Specifies the Kubernetes node condition name (e.g., Ready, NetworkUnavailable) that the EKS node auto-repair feature monitors to determine that a node is unhealthy and should be replaced.

The EKS node health detection reason code (such as DiskPressure, KernelDeadlock, or ReadonlyFilesystem) that identifies which unhealthy node condition this node repair configuration override applies to, allowing you to customize the automated repair behavior for that specific failure reason.

aws_eks_nodegroup.remote_access.ec2_ssh_.text: The ec2_ssh_key field specifies the name of an existing EC2 key pair that is used to enable SSH access to the worker nodes in the EKS nodegroup.

aws_eks_nodegroup.remote_access.source_s.text: The list of EC2 security group IDs that are allowed SSH (port 22) access to the worker nodes when remote access is enabled for the EKS node group.

aws_eks_nodegroup.scaling_config.desired.text: The desired number of worker nodes that the EKS node group should maintain, as part of its scaling configuration.

aws_eks_nodegroup.scaling_config.max_siz.text: The maximum number of nodes that the node group's Auto Scaling group can scale out to.

aws_eks_nodegroup.scaling_config.min_siz.text: The minimum number of worker nodes that the EKS managed node group will scale down to, setting the lower limit for the Auto Scaling group's instance count.

aws_eks_nodegroup.taints.effect.text: The Kubernetes taint effect (e.g., NO_SCHEDULE, NO_EXECUTE, or PREFER_NO_SCHEDULE) that determines how pods are scheduled on nodes in the EKS node group.

aws_eks_nodegroup.taints.key.text: The key of a Kubernetes taint applied to the node group, which together with the effect defines how pods are restricted from scheduling onto the nodes.

aws_eks_nodegroup.taints.value.text: The value component of a Kubernetes taint applied to the node group's nodes, paired with the taint key and effect.

aws_eks_pod_identity_association.tags.ke.text: The tag key used to label the Pod Identity Association, enabling cost allocation, access control, and resource identification.

aws_eks_pod_identity_association.tags.va.text: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the EKS Pod Identity Association, used for labeling, organizing, and managing the association with custom metadata.

aws_elasti_cache_cache_cluster.configura.text: The configuration endpoint of the ElastiCache cache cluster, returned as an object containing the DNS address and port that client applications use to connect to the cluster.
The DNS hostname of the configuration endpoint for a Memcached cache cluster, which clients use to discover all cache nodes.
The TCP port of the ElastiCache cluster's configuration endpoint, used by Redis clients to connect and discover shard endpoints when cluster mode is enabled.

aws_elasti_cache_cache_cluster.log_deliv.text: Specifies the destination for log delivery, which must contain either a CloudWatch Logs log group or a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream, matching the selected DestinationType.
Specifies the CloudWatch Logs destination details for the log delivery configuration, including the log group name where ElastiCache logs are delivered.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group where ElastiCache publishes the selected log type (e.g., slow-log or engine-log) when log delivery is configured with CloudWatch Logs as the destination.

The Kinesis Data Firehose destination details object, which contains the delivery stream name where ElastiCache delivers the cache cluster's log records (e.g., slow or engine logs) when log delivery is configured for Firehose.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to which ElastiCache cache engine logs are delivered.

Specifies the type of destination for the logs, either 'cloudwatch-logs' or 'kinesis-firehose', determining whether the log delivery sends logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs or to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
Specifies the format (text or json) in which ElastiCache engine logs or slow logs are delivered to the configured destination.
Specifies the type of cache log being delivered, either 'slow-log' for slow query logs or 'engine-log' for engine logs, for the ElastiCache cluster.

aws_elasti_cache_cache_cluster.redis_end.text: The DNS address and port of the Redis cache cluster's primary node, provided as an object with address and port attributes.
The DNS address of the ElastiCache Redis cluster's endpoint, used by applications to connect to the Redis cache.
The port number of the Redis endpoint for this ElastiCache cache cluster, representing the network port on which the Redis engine accepts client connections.

aws_elasti_cache_cache_cluster.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the ElastiCache cache cluster, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_elasti_cache_cache_cluster.tags.valu.text: The value of a tag associated with the ElastiCache cache cluster, used to categorize and manage the cluster within AWS.

aws_elasti_cache_global_replication_grou.text: The identifier of the ElastiCache replication group that is included as a member of the global replication group.
Specifies the AWS Region where the member replication group of this global replication group is located.

Indicates whether this member's replication group is the primary (write) or secondary (read) cluster in the global replication group, controlling which cluster accepts writes and acts as the source for replication.
Specifies the ID of the ElastiCache replication group that is associated with this regional configuration within the global replication group.
The AWS Region where the specified ElastiCache replication group resides, identifying one regional member of the global replication group.
Defines the list of node-group-level resharding settings, including preferred availability zones, for a regional replication group when the ElastiCache global replication group is resharded.

The identifier of the node group (shard) within the regional replication group that this resharding configuration applies to, used to specify which shard's availability zones or slot mapping are adjusted during a resharding operation.
A list of preferred Availability Zones for the nodes in a node group (shard) during a resharding operation on a regional replication group associated with the ElastiCache Global Datastore.

aws_elasti_cache_parameter_group.tags.va.text: Specifies the value of a user-defined tag attached to the ElastiCache parameter group, enabling metadata-based organization, cost tracking, and IAM access control on the resource.

aws_elasti_cache_replication_group.confi.text: The configuration endpoint of the replication group, providing the DNS address and port for client connections.

aws_elasti_cache_replication_group.log_d.text: Specifies the concrete destination (CloudWatch Logs log group ARN or Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream ARN) for a log delivery configuration of the ElastiCache replication group, selected based on the destination type.
Specifies the Amazon CloudWatch Logs destination for delivering replication group logs, including the CloudWatch Logs log group name to which logs are sent.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group where ElastiCache delivers the replication group's engine or slow logs when log delivery is configured to CloudWatch Logs.
Specifies the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that receives the detailed logs of the ElastiCache replication group, identified by its delivery stream name.
The name of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to which the replication group's logs are delivered for this log delivery configuration.
The type of destination for ElastiCache replication group logs, which must be either 'cloudwatch-logs' or 'kinesis-firehose'.
For each log delivery configuration on the ElastiCache replication group, this specifies whether the delivered log (for Redis slow logs or engine logs) is in 'text' or 'json' format.
Determines which type of ElastiCache log (engine-log or slow-log) is delivered to the configured destination for the replication group.

aws_elasti_cache_replication_group.node_.text: Assigns a unique zero-padded numeric identifier (e.g., '0001') to each node group in a cluster-mode replication group so that multiple node groups can be individually configured.
Specifies the Availability Zone for the primary node of a specific node group (shard) in a cluster-mode-enabled ElastiCache replication group, allowing per-shard placement control.

Specifies the list of Availability Zones (AZs) for the replica nodes in this node group (shard), one per replica, so you can control the physical placement of read replicas across AZs for high availability.
Specifies the number of replica nodes that should be created in each node group (shard) of the replication group.
Assigns a contiguous range of hash slots (e.g., '0-4999') to the node group, determining which part of the keyspace the shard manages in a cluster-mode replication group.

aws_elasti_cache_replication_group.prima.text: The endpoint (hostname and port) of the primary node in the replication group, computed after creation and used by applications to connect for read/write operations.

aws_elasti_cache_replication_group.read_.text: The read endpoint of the replication group, a DNS address and port used for read-only connections that are distributed across the replica nodes in the cluster.

aws_elasti_cache_replication_group.reade.text: The read-only endpoint (DNS address and port) automatically assigned by ElastiCache that points to the replication group's read replicas, used for distributing read traffic.

aws_elasti_cache_replication_group.tags..text: The value of a tag applied to the ElastiCache replication group, which can be used to organize, track, or control access to the resource through IAM policies and cost allocation.

aws_elasti_cache_security_group_ingress..text: The name of the existing ElastiCache cache security group to which the ingress rule is applied, allowing access from the specified EC2 security group.
The name of the EC2 security group that is permitted to access the associated ElastiCache security group.
The AWS account ID of the owner of the EC2 security group specified in the ingress rule, used when authorizing cross-account access.

The computed unique identifier for this ElastiCache security group ingress rule, composed from the cache security group name, the EC2 security group name, and the EC2 security group owner ID to uniquely represent the authorization.

aws_elasti_cache_serverless_cache.tags.k.text: Specifies the key of a user-defined tag to attach to the ElastiCache Serverless Cache.

aws_elasti_cache_serverless_cache.tags.v.text: The user-defined string value for a tag attached to the ElastiCache Serverless Cache, which pairs with a tag key to provide custom metadata for resource organization and management.

aws_elasti_cache_serverless_cache_snapsh.text: This read-only object describes the configuration of the serverless cache from which the snapshot was taken, capturing settings such as the cache engine and related parameters at snapshot time.
A user-defined key for a tag attached to this ElastiCache serverless cache snapshot, used for organizing and identifying the resource (e.g., by environment or project).

aws_elasti_cache_subnet_group.tags.text: A list of key-value tag objects to associate with the ElastiCache subnet group, used for organizing, identifying, and allocating costs for the resource.

aws_elasti_cache_subnet_group.tags.key.text: The tag key assigned to the ElastiCache subnet group, used to categorize and manage the resource through AWS tagging features.

aws_elasti_cache_subnet_group.tags.value.text: Defines the value of a user-defined tag assigned to the ElastiCache subnet group, used for metadata and resource organization.

aws_elasti_cache_user.authentication_mod.text: Specifies the authentication mode for the ElastiCache user, including the type (password or IAM) and, for password mode, the list of passwords used to authenticate.

aws_elasti_cache_user.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the ElastiCache user, used to assign metadata for identification and cost allocation.

aws_elasti_cache_user.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag key-value pair attached to this ElastiCache user, used to categorize or manage the resource.

aws_elasti_cache_user_group.tags.key.text: The tag key that, paired with its value, labels this ElastiCache user group for cost allocation, access control, and operational management.

aws_elasti_cache_user_group.tags.value.text: The value of a metadata tag attached to the ElastiCache User Group, used to assign arbitrary identifiers like environment or owner for resource organization and cost tracking.

aws_elastic_beanstalk_application.resour.text: Defines how Elastic Beanstalk manages the lifecycle of application versions, including whether to delete expired versions, how long to retain them, and the service role used for cleanup.
Defines the lifecycle policy for application versions, including optional max count and max age rules that control how many versions are retained and how old they may become before deletion.

This object defines the rule that automatically deletes application versions older than a specified number of days, optionally deleting their source bundles from S3, for the Elastic Beanstalk application version lifecycle configuration.

Specifies the max-count-based lifecycle rule for Elastic Beanstalk application versions, including whether the rule is enabled, the maximum number of versions to keep (MaxCount), and whether to delete the source bundle from S3.

aws_elastic_beanstalk_application_versio.text: The source_bundle specifies the Amazon S3 bucket and key where the application version source bundle is located.

aws_elastic_beanstalk_configuration_temp.text: The namespace that identifies the AWS service and configuration section (e.g., 'aws:autoscaling:asg') to which the option setting applies in the Elastic Beanstalk configuration template.
The name of the configuration option being set within its namespace, identifying the specific Elastic Beanstalk setting (e.g., 'InstanceType' in the 'aws:autoscaling:launchconfiguration' namespace).
A unique name identifying the specific AWS resource (such as an Auto Scaling group or load balancer) within the Elastic Beanstalk environment that the configuration option applies to.
The value assigned to the Elastic Beanstalk configuration option identified by the sibling OptionName within the specified Namespace.
Specifies an existing Elastic Beanstalk configuration template (identified by application name and template name) whose settings are copied to create the new configuration template.

aws_elastic_beanstalk_environment.endpoi.text: The endpoint URL for the environment, which is the CNAME of the load balancer for load-balanced environments or the public DNS address for single-instance environments, used to access the running application.

aws_elastic_beanstalk_environment.option.text: Specifies the AWS Elastic Beanstalk configuration namespace (e.g., 'aws:autoscaling:asg', 'aws:ec2:instances') that groups related option settings for the environment.
The name of the Elastic Beanstalk configuration option (e.g., 'IamInstanceProfile' or 'InstanceType') that this option setting defines within the specified namespace.

Specifies the name of a specific resource (such as an Amazon RDS DB instance or an Auto Scaling group) in the Elastic Beanstalk environment that this option setting applies to, used when the option namespace supports multiple resources of the same type.
Specifies the actual value to apply for the given Elastic Beanstalk configuration option, controlling environment settings such as instance type, load balancing, or health checks.

aws_elastic_beanstalk_environment.tags.k.text: The key (name) of a tag assigned to the Elastic Beanstalk environment, used to categorize and filter the resource for cost allocation, access control, and operational management.

aws_elastic_beanstalk_environment.tags.v.text: The value of a tag applied to the Elastic Beanstalk environment, used to categorize and manage the environment as an AWS resource.

aws_elastic_beanstalk_environment.tier.text: Specifies the environment tier (such as WebServer or Worker) including its name, type, and version, determining whether the Elastic Beanstalk environment runs a web server or a background worker.

aws_elastic_load_balancing_load_balancer.text: The name of the application cookie that the classic load balancer uses to route a user's subsequent requests to the same registered instance for session stickiness.

The name to assign to this application-controlled cookie stickiness policy, which is created for the Classic Load Balancer and can be referenced in a listener's policy list to enable session affinity based on a custom application cookie.
Specifies the time period in seconds after which the load balancer's sticky cookie expires, where omitting it makes the cookie last only for the duration of the browser session.
The name assigned to the LBCookieStickinessPolicy for a Classic Load Balancer, used to identify and reference this policy when configuring listener stickiness.
The TCP port on the registered EC2 instances to which the Classic Load Balancer forwards traffic, as defined for each listener.
Specifies the protocol (e.g., HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, SSL) that the Classic Load Balancer uses to communicate with backend instances, which defaults to the listener's protocol if not set.
The external port on which the load balancer listens for incoming client traffic, such as 80 for HTTP or 443 for HTTPS.
Specifies the list of load balancer policy names to apply to this listener, enabling features like SSL negotiation or backend authentication for traffic on the listener's port.
Specifies the client-facing protocol for a classic load balancer listener (e.g., HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, or SSL), which must match the port and determines how incoming traffic is handled.
The ARN of the IAM server certificate (or ACM certificate) used for SSL/TLS termination on this listener, required when the listener protocol is HTTPS or SSL.

Specifies the list of key-value attribute pairs (each with a Key and Value) that define the configuration settings for the associated Elastic Load Balancing policy, such as stickiness expiration periods or other policy-specific parameters.
The name of a policy attribute within a classic load balancer policy, paired with its value to define settings such as session stickiness or cookie behavior.
The value string for a load balancer policy attribute, paired with its Key, such as a cookie expiration period or stickiness setting.
Specifies the list of instance ports to which the classic load balancer policy is applied, commonly used with proxy protocol or other policy types that target specific ports.
Specifies the load balancer (front-end) ports to which this classic Elastic Load Balancing policy (e.g., a stickiness or SSL negotiation policy) is applied.
The name of the load balancer policy, which must be unique within the load balancer and is used to reference the policy in listener configurations.
The type of the classic load balancer policy, such as SSLNegotiationPolicyType or ProxyProtocolPolicyType, which determines the policy's behavior and the set of attributes it supports.

Computed read-only object holding the group name and owner alias of the automatically created source security group for the classic load balancer, used to authorize inbound traffic to backend instances in security group rules.
The key of a tag assigned to the Classic Load Balancer, used to identify and categorize the resource.
The value of a tag attached to a Classic Load Balancer, which together with the tag key forms a key-value pair used for organizing and identifying AWS resources.

aws_elastic_load_balancing_v2_listener.c.text: The ARN of the certificate to associate with the Application Load Balancer listener, used for TLS/SSL termination.

aws_elastic_load_balancing_v2_listener.d.text: This object specifies the Amazon Cognito user pool authentication parameters for a listener default action of type `authenticate-cognito`, including settings such as the user pool ARN, client ID, domain, session timeout, and session cookie name.
Specifies additional query parameters (key-value pairs) to include in the authentication request sent to the Cognito user pool, such as 'redirect_url' or 'response_type'.

Specifies how the ALB handles requests that fail Cognito authentication: 'deny' (default) rejects them with HTTP 401, 'allow' forwards them without authentication, and 'authenticate' redirects to the IdP for authentication.
The OAuth 2.0 scopes (space-separated) requested from the Cognito user pool during authentication, controlling which user claims are returned by the IdP.
The name of the cookie that the load balancer uses to maintain session affinity for users authenticated via the Cognito authentication action.
The maximum duration in seconds that the user's authentication session remains valid before expiring, after which they must re-authenticate.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Cognito user pool that the authenticate-cognito action uses to verify users for this Application Load Balancer listener's default action.
Specifies the client ID of the Cognito user pool client that the load balancer uses to authenticate users for this listener action.
The domain name of the Amazon Cognito user pool used for authentication, such as 'example.auth.us-east-1.amazoncognito.com'.

Specifies the OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider configuration for an authenticate action, including the issuer, authorization endpoint, token endpoint, user info endpoint, client ID, and client secret, enabling the load balancer to validate user identity for requests routed to the target group.

A map of additional query parameters (key-value pairs) that are appended to the authentication request URI sent to the OIDC identity provider when the listener's default action invokes authenticate-oidc.
The authorization endpoint of the OIDC identity provider; the load balancer redirects users to this URL to authenticate and obtain an authorization code.
The OAuth 2.0 client identifier that the load balancer uses when communicating with the OIDC identity provider during the authentication action.

For an authenticate-oidc listener action, this is the client secret issued by the OIDC identity provider (IdP), which the load balancer uses together with the client ID to exchange authorization codes for tokens.
The issuer is the HTTPS URL of the OpenID Connect provider's issuer, used to validate the issuer claim in the identity token.

Determines the behavior for requests that fail OIDC authentication, accepting one of the values 'authenticate' (redirect to IdP), 'allow' (forward the request unauthenticated), or 'deny' (reject with 401).
The OAuth 2.0 scope to request from the OIDC identity provider during authentication.
Defines the name of the session cookie that the load balancer uses to maintain the authenticated session for the OIDC identity provider, preserving state across requests.
The maximum duration, in seconds, that an OIDC-authenticated session remains valid before the user is required to re-authenticate with the identity provider (default 604800).
The URL of the OIDC token endpoint used by the load balancer to exchange the authorization code for access, ID, and refresh tokens during the authentication flow.
Determines whether the OIDC client secret is sourced from an existing AWS Secrets Manager secret (true) instead of being provided directly in the ClientSecret field (false).
The user info endpoint URI provided by the OIDC identity provider, from which the load balancer obtains user claims (e.g., email, name) to forward to the target after successful authentication.

This object configures the fixed-response action for the listener's default rule, specifying the HTTP status code, optional content type, and optional message body that the load balancer returns directly to the client without forwarding to a target group.
The MIME content type (e.g., text/plain or application/json) of the fixed-response body returned to the client when a request matches this default action.
The message body of the fixed response that the Application Load Balancer returns to clients when a listener rule doesn't match, limited to 1024 characters.
Specifies the HTTP status code (e.g., '200', '404') that the load balancer returns in the fixed-response action for this listener default action.
Defines the weighted target groups and target group stickiness settings used when this listener action forwards traffic to target groups.
Configures the stickiness settings (enabled flag and duration in seconds) for traffic forwarded to the target group in a listener's forward action.
The length of time (in seconds) for which the load balancer will consistently route requests to a single target in the target group when sticky sessions are enabled for this forward action.
When true, enables target group stickiness for the forward action, ensuring that consecutive requests from the same client are routed to the same target group.
Specifies the list of target groups (with their weights) to which the listener forwards traffic when this forward action is executed.
The ARN of the target group in a forward action's target group list, specifying the target group where the listener routes incoming traffic.
The weight assigned to the target group for weighted load balancing when the listener forwards requests to multiple target groups.
Defines the JWT validation settings, including the trusted issuer and audience, used by the listener's authentication action to verify tokens presented by clients.

Specifies a list of additional claim requirements (claim name and expected value) that must be validated on the JWT token, in addition to the issuer and audience, for the OIDC authentication action on the ALB listener.

For a given additional claim entry in the JWT validation configuration, this is the claim name that the Application Load Balancer will inspect in the token, and it must match the associated expected value.

A list of allowed values for a specific JWT claim (the claim name is the key in the additional_claims map) that the listener's OIDC authentication action requires in the presented JWT token; the token is accepted only if its claim value matches one of these entries.
The issuer URL (iss) of the JSON Web Token (JWT) that the Application Load Balancer uses to validate the token's signature and claims in a `validate-jwt` action.

The URI of the JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint from which the Application Load Balancer fetches the public keys used to verify the JSON Web Token signature for requests routed by this listener's default action.
The integer order in which the listener's default actions are evaluated, with lower values processed first and the action having the lowest order acting as the default action.
Specifies the redirect configuration for a listener rule action, including the target host, path, port, protocol, query, and HTTP redirect status code (301, 302, 303, 307, or 308).
Specifies the hostname to use in the redirect target's Location header, which can be a fixed value or contain the #{host} token to preserve the original request's host.
The exact HTTP path to use in the redirect target URL of this listener action, overriding the original request's path if specified.

The port to which traffic is redirected, specified either as a literal port number (e.g., '8080') or the placeholder '#{port}' to preserve the incoming listener port, defaulting to the original port if not set.
Specifies the protocol for the redirect target, which can be HTTP, HTTPS, or #{protocol} to preserve the original listener protocol.
The query string to include in the redirect target URL; if omitted, the original request's query string is preserved.
Specifies the HTTP redirect status code (one of HTTP_301, HTTP_302, HTTP_303, HTTP_307, or HTTP_308) that the load balancer returns when a listener default action of type redirect is executed.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the target group that the load balancer forwards traffic to when this default action is of type 'forward'.

Specifies the type of action for the listener's default action, determining whether traffic is forwarded to a target group, redirected, returned as a fixed response, or authenticated via Cognito or OIDC.

aws_elastic_load_balancing_v2_listener.l.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Application or Network Load Balancer listener, automatically assigned by AWS when the listener is created.

Identifies the specific Elastic Load Balancing v2 listener attribute being configured, such as routing.http2.enabled or deletion_protection.enabled, whose value is supplied in the corresponding 'value' field.
The value of a listener attribute, such as routing.http2.enabled or idle_timeout.timeout_seconds, which configures the behavior of the Application or Network Load Balancer listener.

aws_elastic_load_balancing_v2_listener.t.text: A list of key-value tag pairs to attach to the Application Load Balancer or Network Load Balancer listener for resource identification and cost allocation.
The value portion of a tag assigned to the load balancer listener.

aws_elastic_load_balancing_v2_listener_c.text: Specifies the list of ACM certificate ARNs to attach to the listener, allowing the load balancer to present these certificates during TLS handshakes.
The ARN of the certificate (from AWS Certificate Manager or IAM) to associate with the listener for TLS/SSL termination.
The unique identifier for the listener certificate, composed of the listener ARN and certificate ARN.
Specifies the ARN of the Application Load Balancer or Network Load Balancer listener to which the certificate is associated.

aws_elastic_load_balancing_v2_listener_r.text: Configures the Amazon Cognito user pool attributes (like user pool ARN, client ID, and domain) used for authenticating users when this listener rule action is set to authenticate-cognito.
Specifies a map of additional query parameters (key-value pairs) to be appended to the authentication request URI when redirecting users to the specified Cognito user pool for authentication.
Determines how the load balancer handles unauthenticated requests when using Cognito authentication, with valid values being 'authenticate', 'allow', or 'deny'.

The OAuth 2.0 scope to request from the Cognito user pool during authentication, such as 'openid' or 'aws.cognito.signin.user.admin', which controls the user attributes and access permissions granted to the application.
Specifies the name of the cookie used to maintain session affinity for the authenticate-cognito action, defaulting to AWSELBAuthSessionCookie if not set.
Specifies the maximum duration of the authentication session, in seconds, for the Amazon Cognito authentication action on this listener rule.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Cognito user pool that the Application Load Balancer uses to authenticate users for this listener rule action.
The client ID of the Cognito user pool client that the load balancer uses when redirecting users for authentication in an authenticate-cognito action.

Defines the user pool domain prefix (e.g., 'my-user-pool') that the Application Load Balancer uses when constructing the Cognito authentication endpoint for this listener rule's authenticate-cognito action.

Specifies the OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider parameters—including issuer, authorization/token/user-info endpoints, client ID, and client secret—that the Application Load Balancer uses to authenticate users when the listener rule action type is `authenticate-oidc`.
Specifies additional query parameters (key-value pairs) to be appended to the authentication request sent to the OIDC identity provider's authorization endpoint.
The absolute URL of the OIDC authorization endpoint to which the load balancer redirects clients for user authentication as part of the authenticate-oidc action.
The client identifier (client ID) that the Application Load Balancer uses when communicating with the OIDC identity provider in the authenticate-oidc action.
The client secret for the OIDC identity provider, used together with the client ID to authenticate when exchanging the authorization code for tokens.
Specifies the OIDC identity provider's issuer identifier (the URL, such as https://example.com) that the ALB uses to validate the issuer claim of the ID token during authentication.

Specifies the behavior when a user is not authenticated, with valid values `deny`, `allow`, or `authenticate`, where `deny` rejects the request, `allow` permits it unauthenticated, and `authenticate` redirects to the IdP for authentication.
Specifies the OAuth 2.0 scope for the OIDC authentication request, controlling which user claims are returned and defaulting to `openid`.
Specifies the name of the session cookie that the Application Load Balancer uses to store the OIDC authentication session state for the listener rule's authenticate-OIDC action.
The maximum duration in seconds that a user remains authenticated via the OIDC identity provider before being forced to re-authenticate; defaults to 604800 seconds (7 days).
The token endpoint URL of the OIDC identity provider, used by the load balancer to exchange the authorization code for access and ID tokens.

When set to true, this boolean indicates that the rule should reuse the OIDC client secret already configured for the same client ID in a previous listener rule, rather than specifying a new ClientSecret in this rule's authenticate_oidc_config.
The user info endpoint URL of the OIDC identity provider, used to retrieve user claims after authentication in the authenticate-oidc action.

Specifies the fixed response action settings for the listener rule, including the HTTP response status code, content type, and message body that the load balancer returns when the rule action is invoked.
Specifies the Content-Type header value for the fixed-response action (e.g., 'text/plain' or 'application/json') that the load balancer returns to the client.
The response body that the load balancer returns for a fixed-response action when the listener rule condition is met.
Specifies the HTTP status code to return in the fixed-response action, for example '200' or '404'.
Specifies the target groups and target group stickiness settings for the forward action, enabling weighted routing and session stickiness for the listener rule.

Specifies the target group stickiness configuration for the forward action, which controls whether client requests are consistently routed to the same target group for the duration set by DurationSeconds.
Specifies the duration in seconds for which the load balancer should keep requests routed to the same target when target group stickiness is enabled on this forward action.
Indicates whether the client's requests are routed to the same target group for the specified duration, enabling target group stickiness for this forward action.
Specifies the list of target groups and their weights for forwarding traffic when the listener rule action type is forward.

The ARN of a target group that receives traffic in a weighted forward action; used with the corresponding weight to distribute requests among multiple target groups configured in the listener rule's forward config.
The relative weight assigned to a target group in a weighted forward action, determining the proportion of traffic routed to it compared to other target groups in the same forward config.
Configures JWT validation parameters (issuer and audience) for an OIDC authentication action in an Application Load Balancer listener rule.
Defines additional JWT claims (key-value pairs) that must be present in the token payload with the exact specified values for the ALB's JWT validation to succeed.
The data type (such as string, number, or boolean) of the additional claim's expected value, used to enforce claim format during JWT validation in the ALB listener rule.
Specifies the name of an additional claim that must be present in the JWT, used by the ALB 'authenticate-oidc' action's JWT validation configuration for the listener rule.

This list defines the allowed string values for the corresponding additional JWT claim (keyed by the parent claim key) that must be matched by the token for the ALB listener rule action's authentication to succeed.

The expected issuer (iss claim) URL of the JWT tokens that the load balancer's authenticate-oidc action will accept for the listener rule, matching the issuer configured in the OIDC identity provider.
The URL of the JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint from which the load balancer fetches the public keys used to validate the JWT signature for the authenticated action.
Specifies the order in which this action is evaluated relative to other actions in the listener rule, with lower numbers evaluated first and required when the rule has multiple actions.
The redirect configuration for a redirect action, specifying the protocol, host, port, path, query, and HTTP status code (e.g., HTTP_301) for redirecting client requests from one URL to another.
The hostname to which the redirect action sends traffic, where you can specify a literal host or use the #{host} variable to preserve the original request's host.
The path of the redirect target, which can be a literal path (e.g., /new/index.html) or a pattern using #{...} variables (e.g., /new/#{path}) that is substituted from the original request.
Specifies the target port for the redirect, either a fixed port number (1-65535) or the `#{port}` placeholder to preserve the original incoming port.
The protocol to use in the redirect action (HTTP, HTTPS, or #{protocol} to preserve the original listener protocol), applied to the URI when the target group redirects requests.

Specifies the query string to include in the redirect target URL; when omitted, the original request's query string is preserved, and the value can contain literal text or #{...} placeholders to substitute original components.
Specifies the HTTP redirect status code (e.g., HTTP_301) to return in the response for a redirect action.
For a forward action, this attribute specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the target group that receives traffic matching the listener rule; it is required when the action type is 'forward'.
The type of action to perform when the listener rule matches, such as forward to a target group, redirect, return a fixed response, or authenticate with OIDC or Cognito.
Specifies the type of condition to match, such as host-header, path-pattern, or http-header, which determines which request attribute the listener rule evaluates.
Specifies the host header configuration for a listener rule condition, containing the list of host header values (such as domain names) that the rule uses to match incoming requests.
A list of regular expression patterns that the host header of an incoming request must match for the listener rule condition to be satisfied.
Specifies the host header patterns (for example, 'example.com' or '*.example.com') that the listener rule matches against the Host header of incoming requests.
Configures an HTTP header match condition for the listener rule, specifying the header name and the list of values that the incoming request's HTTP header must match for the rule to apply.
The name of the HTTP header to match in a listener rule condition of the 'http-header' type.

In an HTTP header condition of an AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::ListenerRule, this field is the list of value patterns (supporting wildcard characters such as * and ?) that the HTTP header value must match for the rule to apply.

Specifies one or more strings to compare against the value of the HTTP header named in the parent http-header condition, and the listener rule condition is satisfied when the request header value matches any of these values, with support for wildcard characters like * and ?.
Specifies the HTTP request method values (such as GET, POST, or DELETE) that a rule condition matches against for forwarding traffic in the Application Load Balancer listener rule.
Defines the list of HTTP request methods (e.g., GET, POST) that must match the incoming request method for this listener rule condition to apply.

Defines the path pattern configuration for a path-based routing condition, containing a list of path patterns (e.g., /img/*) that determine whether the listener rule action is taken based on the URL path of the request.
The regular expression patterns used to match the path of incoming requests for this listener rule, enabling path-based routing with regex matching.
The list of path patterns (such as '/img/*') that the listener rule matches against the request URL path.
Defines the query string key-value pair patterns that an incoming request's query string must match for the corresponding application load balancer listener rule condition to be satisfied.
Specifies the list of query string key/value pairs that the listener rule condition matches against, where each object contains the key and value to match in the request query string.
Specifies the query string key (parameter name) to match in the listener rule's query string condition.
The value of a query string key-value pair that the listener rule inspects in the request's query string to determine whether the condition matches.
Specifies a list of regular expression patterns used by the listener rule condition to match the request's host header or path pattern, enabling regex-based routing instead of exact values.
Defines the source IP matching criteria for a listener rule condition, specifying one or more CIDR ranges that the originating client IP address must fall within for the rule to apply.
For a source IP-based listener rule condition, this field specifies whether the allowed source IP addresses are IPv4 or IPv6 addresses.
The list of source IP address CIDR ranges that the rule condition matches for incoming traffic.

For a given listener rule condition (such as host-header, path-pattern, or http-header), this is the list of strings to evaluate the request against, where at least one value must match for the condition to be met.
Indicates whether this listener rule is the default rule of the listener, which handles traffic that does not match any other rule.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the listener rule, which uniquely identifies the rule within the load balancer after it has been created.
Specifies the list of tags to attach to this listener rule, where each tag object contains a Key and optionally a Value.
The tag key assigned to the listener rule, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the resource in AWS.
The value component of an AWS tag attached to the Elastic Load Balancing v2 listener rule, used for metadata and cost allocation.
