The numeric UID or GID that identifies the user or group for which this OpenZFS volume quota is set.
Defines the storage capacity quota in GiB for a user or group on the FSx for OpenZFS volume, limiting how much space that user or group can consume.
The type of quota, either USER or GROUP, determines whether the quota applies to a specific user or group by ID.

aws_fsx_volume.resource_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the FSx volume.

aws_fsx_volume.tags.key.text: The tag key portion of a tag attached to the FSx volume, used to organize and identify the volume, support cost allocation, and enable IAM-based access control, with uniqueness required among tags on the volume.

aws_fsx_volume.tags.value.text: The value portion of a user-defined tag associated with the FSx volume, enabling customization of metadata for resource tracking, cost allocation, and access control policies.

aws_fsx_volume.uuid.text: The system-assigned UUID for an FSx for OpenZFS volume, which serves as the unique mount name that clients use to access the volume and is distinct from the volume's resource ID.

aws_fsx_volume.volume_id.text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for the FSx volume, formatted as `fsvol-` followed by a 17-character hexadecimal string, which is populated after the volume is created.

aws_fsx_volume.volume_type.text: Specifies the type of FSx volume being created, either ONTAP or OPENZFS, which determines the applicable file system and volume configuration.

aws_game_lift_alias.routing_strategy.text: The routing strategy defines how a GameLift alias directs game session requests to fleets, either by specifying a fleet ID for simple routing or by providing a terminal message to stop routing.

aws_game_lift_build.storage_location.text: The S3 bucket and object key where the build's game build files are stored, along with the IAM role ARN that GameLift assumes to access the files.

aws_game_lift_container_fleet.instance_i.text: Specifies the starting port number of the range of inbound ports that are allowed on the container fleet's instances.
Specifies the CIDR IP address range allowed to connect to the container fleet's game server ports.
Specifies the IP protocol (TCP or UDP) for the inbound traffic that is allowed to reach the container fleet's instances.
The upper bound of the port range that is allowed for inbound traffic to the container fleet's instances, used together with the from_port value to define a contiguous range.

aws_game_lift_container_fleet.locations.text: A list of objects, each representing a GameLift location (AWS Region) where the container fleet has active instances, including the location name and its operational status and capacity, as computed and returned by the service.

aws_game_lift_container_fleet.locations..text: The name of an AWS Region or Local Zone location to add to the container fleet's set of enabled locations.
Specifies the scaling limits for the number of EC2 instances hosting container groups in the corresponding location, including desired, minimum, and maximum counts.
Sets the desired number of EC2 instances to run in this location for the container fleet, used by GameLift to scale capacity toward that target.
Specifies the managed capacity configuration for the container fleet at this location, defining settings like the desired number of instances for that location.
Determines the number of minutes of idle time (no active game sessions) that must elapse before Amazon GameLift scales in (removes) an instance in the container fleet.
Controls whether the managed container fleet maintains a warm pool of instances or scales to zero when there are no active game sessions in that location.
The `max_size` property under a location's `location_capacity` specifies the upper bound of container instances that can run in that location for this GameLift container fleet.
The minimum number of container instances that GameLift maintains in the corresponding fleet location, defining the lower bound for auto scaling capacity for that location.
Indicates the current operational status of the player gateway in the fleet's location, such as ACTIVE or ERROR.

Specifies the fleet actions to stop in a particular location (e.g., AUTO_SCALING, CUSTOM_GAME_SERVER_ACTIONS, or CUSTOM_GAME_SERVER_SHUTDOWN) to prevent them from running there for the container fleet.

aws_game_lift_container_fleet.scaling_po.text: The comparison operator used to evaluate the scaling metric against the threshold in the container fleet scaling policy, such as GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold or LessThanThreshold.
The number of consecutive 1-minute evaluation periods that the fleet's metric must breach the policy's threshold before the target tracking scaling policy triggers an adjustment.
The name of the CloudWatch metric (e.g., CPUUtilization, PlayerCount) that this scaling policy watches to determine when to trigger scaling actions for the container fleet.
The name string that uniquely identifies this scaling policy within the container fleet, used to reference the policy in metrics and API calls.
The type of scaling policy for the container fleet, either 'TargetTracking' to adjust capacity based on a target metric value or 'RuleBased' to scale based on custom conditions.
The number of instances by which the GameLift Container Fleet's desired capacity is increased or decreased when a CHANGE_IN_CAPACITY scaling policy is triggered.
Specifies whether the scaling adjustment is an absolute change in capacity, an exact capacity value, or a percentage change in capacity (ChangeInCapacity, ExactCapacity, or PercentChangeInCapacity).

The target tracking configuration for a scaling policy, specifying the metric and target value (e.g., a target fleet utilization or instance count) that the GameLift container fleet automatically adjusts capacity to maintain.
The target value for the metric used by the target-based scaling policy; GameLift adjusts the fleet's desired capacity to keep the metric near this value.
The target value of the specified metric that, when crossed, triggers the scaling adjustment for the container fleet's autoscaling policy.

aws_game_lift_container_fleet.tags.key.text: The case-sensitive key of a tag attached to the Amazon GameLift container fleet, which serves as the tag's identifier for categorization and cost tracking.

aws_game_lift_container_fleet.tags.value.text: The value part of a key-value tag attached to the GameLift container fleet, used for resource organization, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_game_lift_container_group_definition.text: Determines the condition (such as START, COMPLETE, SUCCESS, or HEALTHY) that the referenced dependency container must satisfy before the game server container is allowed to start.
The name of the container that the game server container depends on, used to define the startup order between containers in the container group.
The name of the environment variable whose value is being overridden for the game server container defined in this GameLift container group.
Specifies the value for an environment variable override applied to the game server container at runtime, replacing any default value defined in the container image.
Specifies whether the mounted volume is read-only or read-write, using values like READ_ONLY or READ_WRITE.
The file path inside the game server container where the mounted volume is accessible, as specified in the mount point configuration for the container group definition.
Specifies the file path on the underlying EC2 instance that the container mount point references, allowing the container to access data stored on the instance's filesystem.
Specifies the starting port in a contiguous range of ports that the game server container uses for incoming game traffic, as part of a container port range for the container group definition.
The network protocol (TCP or UDP) for the container port range, used for routing traffic to the game server container.

The ending port number in the inclusive range of ports that the game server container uses for inbound game traffic, as part of the container port configuration for the GameLift container group definition.
The name assigned to the support container, which serves as a unique identifier within the container group definition.
Defines which other containers in the same container group must reach a specified condition (e.g., START, COMPLETE, SUCCESS, HEALTHY) before this support container is started.

Defines the required condition (e.g., START, COMPLETE, SUCCESS, HEALTHY) on the referenced container that must be met before the support container in the GameLift container group definition is started.
The name of a container in the same container group that this support container depends on, used to define startup order.

A list of environment variable overrides applied to the support container when it runs, each specifying the variable name and value to replace any value defined in the container image, for a GameLift container group definition.
Specifies the name of the environment variable to override in the support container's runtime configuration.
The value portion of an environment variable override applied to a support container in the GameLift container group definition, replacing the container image's default environment variable value.
Indicates whether the support container is essential, meaning that if an essential support container stops or fails, the entire container group is stopped.

Specifies the container health check configuration, including the command to run, interval, timeout, retries, and start period, used by Amazon GameLift to determine whether the support container is healthy.
The command to run inside the support container to perform a health check, specified as a list of strings representing the executable and its arguments.
Specifies the time interval (in seconds) between successive health check runs for this support container in the GameLift container group definition.
The retries field specifies the number of consecutive failed health checks after which the container is considered unhealthy in the GameLift container group definition.
The number of seconds that the health check waits after the support container starts before beginning its health checks in a GameLift container group definition.
The amount of time (in seconds) that GameLift waits for the container health check command to return before considering the health check failed and marking the container unhealthy.
The URI of the container image that this support container in the GameLift container group definition will pull and run.
Configures the Linux kernel capabilities (additional or dropped) for the support container, controlling which privileged operations the container is allowed to perform.
Specifies the list of Linux capabilities to add (include) for the support container, granting the container these additional Linux privileges on top of its default capabilities.
Sets the maximum memory (in mebibytes) that the support container is allowed to use, enforcing a hard limit on its memory consumption.
Defines the mount points for the support container, specifying the container path and the source volume to attach for shared storage within the GameLift container group.
Specifies whether the mounted container path is accessible as read-only (READ_ONLY) or read-write (READ_WRITE) to the support container.
Specifies the path inside the support container where a mounted volume is accessible, used to define the container's mount point for persistent storage.

Specifies the absolute file system path on the host EC2 instance that serves as the source volume for a mount point in a support container definition within an AWS GameLift container group definition.
Defines the port range and protocol (e.g., TCP or UDP) that the support container exposes for inbound traffic in the GameLift container group definition.

Specifies an inclusive range of container ports (from a starting port to an ending port) that a support container in an Amazon GameLift container group definition exposes for game traffic or other networking purposes.
Specifies the starting (lower) port number in a contiguous range of ports that this support container is configured to use within its port configuration.
The network protocol (TCP or UDP) used by the container port range in the GameLift container group.
Specifies the upper (inclusive) bound of the port range that this support container can use for its network traffic.
The resolved image digest for the support container, computed from the image URI to uniquely identify the exact container image version used by the container group definition.
The number of vCPU units allocated to this support container in the GameLift container group definition, which sets the CPU resource limit for that container.
The key of a tag applied to an Amazon GameLift container group definition, enabling resource organization and cost allocation.

aws_game_lift_fleet.certificate_configur.text: Determines whether an AWS GameLift fleet uses a generated TLS certificate, with valid values DISABLED (no certificate) or CERTIFICATE_GENERATED (automatically generated by GameLift).

aws_game_lift_fleet.ec2_inbound_permissi.text: The lower bound of the port range for inbound traffic allowed to the fleet's EC2 instances from the specified IP range.
The IP address range, in CIDR notation, that is allowed to connect to the fleet's EC2 instances for the specified protocol and port.
The IP protocol (TCP or UDP) allowed for inbound traffic on the specified port range for the fleet's EC2 instances.
The upper bound of the port range that is allowed for inbound traffic to the fleet's EC2 instances, used with `from_port` to define the permitted range.

aws_game_lift_fleet.locations.text: The locations attribute lists the AWS Regions (locations) where the GameLift fleet has deployed instances, returned as a computed list of location objects.

aws_game_lift_fleet.locations.location.text: The AWS Region code (e.g., 'us-east-1') that identifies where this GameLift fleet location is deployed for hosting game servers.

aws_game_lift_fleet.locations.location_c.text: Defines the desired, minimum, and maximum instance counts for the fleet in a specific location (region).
Sets the desired number of EC2 instances for a given fleet location, which GameLift uses as the scaling target for that location's capacity within its configured minimum and maximum limits.
Specifies how many minutes an instance in a managed GameLift fleet location can remain idle before it is targeted for scale-in (termination) as part of the location's managed capacity configuration.
Determines the managed capacity strategy for a GameLift fleet location when there is no demand, specifying whether the fleet can scale down to zero instances or must maintain a minimum capacity.
The maximum number of EC2 instances that can be active for this fleet location, setting the upper bound for auto-scaling capacity.
Specifies the minimum number of EC2 instances that must be maintained for the fleet in the associated location as part of its capacity configuration.

aws_game_lift_fleet.locations.player_gat.text: The player gateway status for each fleet location, representing the operational state of the gateway that routes player connections to game sessions in that location.

aws_game_lift_fleet.runtime_configuratio.text: The number of game server processes to launch concurrently on each instance for this server process configuration.
Specifies the file path to the server executable within the game build that GameLift launches to host game sessions for this fleet.

The parameters string supplies command-line arguments that Amazon GameLift passes to the server executable when launching the server process, as defined within the runtime configuration's server process definition.

aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.com.text: Specifies the comparison operator used to evaluate the scaling metric against the threshold in a GameLift fleet scaling policy, such as GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold, GreaterThanThreshold, LessThanThreshold, or LessThanOrEqualToThreshold.

aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.eva.text: Determines how many recent metric evaluation periods are considered when deciding whether to trigger a scaling adjustment for the fleet based on the associated CloudWatch metric.

aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.loc.text: Specifies the name of the location (such as an AWS Region or custom location) where this scaling policy is applied, enabling per-location autoscaling in a multi-location GameLift fleet.

aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.met.text: The name of the GameLift metric (such as ActivatingGameSessions, ActiveInstances, or IdleInstances) that this scaling policy uses to trigger scaling actions.

aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.nam.text: The unique, descriptive name that identifies this scaling policy within the fleet.

aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.pol.text: Determines the type of scaling policy for the GameLift fleet, either 'TargetTracking' for dynamic scaling based on a target metric value or 'RuleBased' for policies defined by custom scaling rules.

aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.sca.text: The numeric value applied to the fleet's desired instance count when the scaling policy's conditions are met, interpreted as a change, exact capacity, or percentage according to the ScalingAdjustmentType property.

Specifies how the scaling adjustment value in the policy is applied, with valid values including ChangeInCapacity (adjust by a set number of instances), ExactCapacity (set capacity to an exact number), and PercentChangeInCapacity (adjust by a percentage of current capacity).

aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.sta.text: The current lifecycle state of the scaling policy, such as ACTIVE, UPDATE_REQUESTED, UPDATING, DELETE_REQUESTED, DELETING, DELETED, or ERROR.

aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.tar.text: Provides the target value for the metric used in a target-based scaling policy, determining the desired instance capacity for the GameLift fleet.
Specifies the target value of the metric used by a target-based scaling policy to decide when to adjust fleet capacity for an Amazon GameLift fleet.

aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.thr.text: The numeric value that the scaling policy's specified metric is compared against using the comparison operator to trigger a fleet capacity adjustment.

aws_game_lift_fleet.scaling_policies.upd.text: The update status of the scaling policy, indicating whether the latest requested update has been successfully applied (e.g., PENDING, SUCCESS, FAILED).

aws_game_lift_game_server_group.instance.text: The EC2 instance type (e.g., c5.large, m5.large) that GameLift uses to launch instances in this game server group's underlying fleet.

Sets the relative weighting that this instance type contributes to the game server group's total capacity, used by Amazon GameLift to determine how many instances of each type are needed to meet the group's target capacity.

aws_game_lift_game_server_group.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to this GameLift game server group.

aws_game_lift_game_server_group.tags.val.text: The value of an arbitrary tag key assigned to the GameLift GameServerGroup, used for resource organization, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_game_lift_game_session_queue.destina.text: The ARN of a GameLift fleet or alias that this game session queue uses as a destination for game session placement requests.

aws_game_lift_game_session_queue.filter_.text: Filters the locations where the queue can place new game sessions by specifying a list of allowed AWS region codes.

aws_game_lift_game_session_queue.player_.text: Sets the maximum acceptable latency in milliseconds for an individual player to a game location; if the player's latency exceeds this threshold, that location is excluded from consideration for the player's game session placement.
The length of time in seconds that this player latency policy remains in effect for the game session placement.

aws_game_lift_game_session_queue.priorit.text: Specifies the priority settings for the GameLift session queue, including the order in which locations are used and the order in which placement criteria like latency and cost are prioritized.

aws_game_lift_game_session_queue.tags.ke.text: The key of a tag attached to this GameLift game session queue, used to organize and identify the queue for cost and access management.

aws_game_lift_game_session_queue.tags.va.text: The value component of a tag key-value pair applied to the GameLift game session queue for resource organization and management.

aws_game_lift_location.location_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the GameLift location, returned after the location is created and used for referencing it in IAM policies and other resources.

aws_game_lift_location.location_name.text: Specifies the name of the GameLift location, which is typically an AWS Region code (e.g., 'us-east-1') or a custom location name used to identify the location for game hosting.

aws_game_lift_location.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the GameLift location, used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_game_lift_matchmaking_configuration..text: The identifying key of a custom game property (a key-value pair) that is passed to a matchmade game session to provide custom configuration data.
The string value of a game property key-value pair that is passed to GameLift matchmaking to filter or customize game sessions.
The key of a tag attached to a GameLift matchmaking configuration, used to identify, organize, and manage the resource.

aws_game_lift_matchmaking_rule_set.tags..text: The key of a tag attached to the GameLift matchmaking rule set, used to identify and categorize the rule set for resource management and cost allocation.
The value portion of a tag attached to the GameLift matchmaking rule set, used to organize and identify the rule set within AWS.

aws_game_lift_script.storage_location.text: The Amazon S3 bucket and key that store the zipped script file, along with the IAM role that allows GameLift to access that location.

aws_game_lift_script.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the GameLift script, used to identify and categorize the resource.

aws_game_lift_script.tags.value.text: The string value paired with a tag key on the GameLift script, used to label and categorize the resource for cost allocation and identity-based policies.

aws_global_accelerator_accelerator.tags.text: Specifies custom tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the AWS Global Accelerator accelerator for resource categorization and management.

aws_global_accelerator_accelerator.tags..text: The value of a tag attached to the accelerator, used to categorize and manage the resource as a user-defined string.

aws_global_accelerator_cross_account_att.text: Specifies the IP address range in CIDR notation (e.g., '10.0.0.0/8') for a resource being attached, used when the resource is an IP range rather than an endpoint ID in this cross-account attachment.
The ARN or resource identifier of the AWS resource (such as a Network Load Balancer, Application Load Balancer, or Elastic IP) that is attached to the accelerator from a different AWS account.
The AWS Region where the resource being added to the cross-account attachment is located, such as when the resource is a regional endpoint group.
Specifies a list of key-value tags to attach to the cross-account attachment, which can be used for resource identification, cost allocation, and tag-based access control in AWS Global Accelerator.

The key of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS Global Accelerator cross-account attachment, allowing you to attach custom metadata such as cost center or environment for identification and management.
The value component of a tag key-value pair that you attach to an AWS Global Accelerator cross-account attachment for metadata and resource categorization.

aws_global_accelerator_endpoint_group.en.text: The ARN of the AWS resource (such as an Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer, or EC2 instance) that is attached as an endpoint in this endpoint group.
Indicates whether client IP address preservation is enabled for this endpoint, which keeps the original client IP address in the packet headers forwarded by Global Accelerator to the endpoint.

The ARN of the endpoint resource (such as an Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer, EC2 instance, or Elastic IP address) that Global Accelerator routes traffic to for this endpoint configuration.
The weight assigned to the endpoint, controlling the proportion of traffic routed to it relative to other endpoints in the group (values 0-255, higher means more traffic).

aws_global_accelerator_endpoint_group.he.text: The URI path that AWS Global Accelerator uses to perform health checks against endpoints in the endpoint group, such as '/health' or '/'.

aws_global_accelerator_endpoint_group.po.text: A list of port overrides that map a listener port to a different endpoint port for the endpoint group, allowing traffic to be redirected to a custom port on the endpoint.
The actual port on the endpoint that receives traffic when this port override is applied, replacing the listener port for the mapped endpoint.
Specifies the original port on the accelerator listener that this port override maps to the endpoint port, redirecting traffic received on that listener port to the endpoint's configured port.

aws_global_accelerator_listener.port_ran.text: Defines the list of port ranges (each with a `from` and `to` port) that the listener forwards traffic on.
The first port in the inclusive range of ports (from_port to to_port) that the AWS Global Accelerator listener accepts and forwards traffic on.
The inclusive ending port number of the range for the listener.

aws_glue_blueprint.tags.key.text: A user-defined tag key attached to the AWS Glue Blueprint resource within the tags map, used for organizing and managing the blueprint.

aws_glue_blueprint.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag (key-value pair) attached to the AWS Glue Blueprint, used for organizing, tracking, and allocating costs for the blueprint.

aws_glue_catalog.create_database_default.text: The list of AWS Glue permissions (e.g., 'ALL' or 'CREATE_TABLE') granted by default to the specified principal on newly created databases in the Data Catalog.
Defines the principal (IAM user, role, or all users) that the Glue database's default permissions are granted to, via its Data Lake principal identifier.
The unique identifier (such as an IAM role ARN, IAM user ARN, or AWS account ID) of the Data Lake principal that receives the default permissions for databases created in the Glue catalog.

aws_glue_catalog.create_table_default_pe.text: The list of permissions (e.g., ALL, SELECT, INSERT) to be granted to the principal in the default permissions for tables created in this Glue catalog database.
Specifies the principal (such as an IAM role, user, or AWS account) that receives the configured default permissions on newly created tables in the Glue data catalog.
The ARN or identifier of the IAM role, user, or group that is granted default permissions on the Glue catalog table.

aws_glue_catalog.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key in the Tags property of the AWS Glue Catalog, used to attach custom metadata to the Glue Data Catalog for identification and resource management.

aws_glue_classifier.csv_classifier.text: Defines the configuration for an AWS Glue classifier that parses CSV files, including the delimiter, quote symbol, header detection, and whether to treat a single column as a valid CSV format.

aws_glue_classifier.grok_classifier.text: Configures a Grok classifier in AWS Glue, specifying the grok pattern used to parse log or unstructured data, custom pattern definitions, and the classification name applied to matched data.

aws_glue_classifier.json_classifier.text: Specifies a JSON classifier for AWS Glue that uses a JSON path to identify the JSON data structure within input records.

aws_glue_classifier.xmlclassifier.text: Defines the row tag and optional classification for an XML classifier, used by AWS Glue to parse XML data and infer its schema.

aws_glue_connection.catalog_id.text: The identifier of the AWS Data Catalog (typically the AWS account ID) in which the Glue connection is stored or referenced.

aws_glue_connection.connection_input.text: Configuration object that defines the properties of an AWS Glue connection, including connection type, connection properties, and physical connection requirements for the target data store.

aws_glue_connection.connection_input.ath.text: A map of key-value pairs that define the Athena connection properties (e.g., workgroup and catalog) used when the connection type is ATHENA.

aws_glue_connection.connection_input.aut.text: Configures OAuth-based authentication details (such as client credentials and token endpoint) for Glue connection types that require OAuth, like Salesforce or ServiceNow.
Specifies whether the connection authenticates using basic inline credentials (username and password) or by referencing a secret in AWS Secrets Manager.
Specifies the username and password used for basic authentication when connecting to the data source for this AWS Glue connection.
The password component of the basic authentication credentials used to authenticate to the data source for this AWS Glue connection.
Specifies the username for basic authentication when connecting to the data source using this AWS Glue connection.
Specifies a JSON object of custom authentication key-value pairs for the Glue connection, used when the authentication type is CUSTOM to pass connector-specific credential parameters.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the credentials or secret associated with this Glue connection's authentication configuration.
Specifies the OAuth2 authentication parameters (such as client ID, client secret, token URL, and grant type) for the Glue connection.
Defines the OAuth2 authorization code grant parameters (such as authorization code and redirect URI) used in the authentication configuration of an AWS Glue connection.

In an AWS Glue connection's OAuth2 authentication configuration for the authorization code grant flow, this field supplies the authorization code returned by the identity provider, which Glue exchanges for access and refresh tokens.
The redirect URI to which the OAuth2 authorization server sends the user after authorization, used in the authorization code flow for the Glue connection's authentication configuration.

Specifies the OAuth2 client application for the Glue connection's authentication configuration, either referencing an AWS-managed client application or supplying the client ID for a user-managed application.
Specifies the reference to an AWS managed OAuth2 client application (e.g., an AWS-supported SaaS application) used for OAuth2 authentication in the Glue connection.
The client ID of the user-managed OAuth2 client application used in the OAuth2 authentication configuration for the Glue connection.
Configures the OAuth2 client credentials (such as authorization code and refresh token) required to authenticate the Glue connection to the data source via OAuth2.
The OAuth2 access token used by the Glue connection to authenticate with the external data source as part of its OAuth2 authentication flow.
The JSON Web Token (JWT) used as the OAuth2 credential for authenticating to the data source in this AWS Glue connection.
The refresh token that is used to obtain a new OAuth2 access token when the current access token expires.
The OAuth2 client secret associated with the user-managed client application used for authentication in this AWS Glue connection.
Specifies the OAuth 2.0 grant type (e.g., AUTHORIZATION_CODE, CLIENT_CREDENTIALS) that determines the authorization flow Glue uses to obtain access tokens for this connection.
The OAuth2 token endpoint URL where the connection requests access tokens for authentication.
Defines a map of additional query parameters (key-value pairs) to be appended to the OAuth2 token endpoint URL when retrieving an access token for the Glue connection.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the credentials for the Glue connection's authentication configuration.

aws_glue_connection.connection_input.con.text: A dynamic map of connection type-specific key-value pairs, such as JDBC_CONNECTION_URL, USERNAME, and PASSWORD for JDBC connections, or KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS and security settings for Kafka connections.
The type of the connection, such as JDBC, SFTP, MONGODB, KAFKA, or NETWORK, which determines the connector and connection parameters used by AWS Glue.

aws_glue_connection.connection_input.des.text: Specifies the user-defined description for the Glue connection, providing additional context about the connection's purpose or configuration.

aws_glue_connection.connection_input.mat.text: Specifies a list of match criteria that AWS Glue uses to decide whether this connection should be selected for a given resource, often matching network identifiers such as subnet IDs or security group names.

aws_glue_connection.connection_input.nam.text: Specifies the name of the Glue connection, which must be unique in the AWS account and Region and is used to identify the connection when referencing it in Glue jobs.

aws_glue_connection.connection_input.phy.text: Specifies the VPC network configuration (subnet ID, security group IDs, and availability zone) needed to establish a physical connection to a data source such as a JDBC database.
The Availability Zone (AZ) of the subnet to use when the Glue connection is attached to a VPC, typically required for JDBC and other physical connections.
The list of VPC security group IDs that AWS Glue uses when establishing a connection to resources in a private network, controlling inbound and outbound traffic for the connection.
The ID of the subnet within the VPC where the Glue connection's network interface will be placed.

aws_glue_connection.connection_input.spa.text: Specifies a map of key-value pairs for Spark-specific connection properties, such as Spark options like 'spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold', used when the Glue connection is consumed by an Apache Spark job.

aws_glue_connection.connection_input.val.text: Indicates whether AWS Glue should validate the connection's credentials by attempting to connect to the data store during creation, defaulting to false.
Specifies the list of compute environments (for example, SPARK or ATHENA) against which the connection is validated when the connection is created or updated.

aws_glue_connection.id.text: The name of the Glue connection, serving as its unique resource identifier.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.catalog_targets.text: The name of an existing AWS Glue connection that the crawler uses to access the catalog target database when the target requires network access through a connection (for example, for a Redshift or JDBC target catalog).
The name of the AWS Glue Data Catalog database whose tables the crawler targets when processing this catalog target.

Specifies the ARN of the Amazon SQS dead-letter queue to use as a destination for events that fail to be processed from the event queue for this catalog target, enabling change tracking in the crawler.
The ARN of an Amazon SQS queue that the crawler subscribes to so it can receive data catalog event notifications for the specified catalog target tables, enabling event-driven re-crawling.
The list of table names in the specified AWS Glue Data Catalog database that the crawler will target to update their metadata definitions.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.delta_targets.c.text: The connection_name field specifies the name of the AWS Glue connection used to access the Delta Lake table during crawling.
Specifies whether the crawler creates a native Delta Lake table instead of a symlink table for the discovered Delta targets.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.delta_targets.d.text: A list of Amazon S3 paths to Delta Lake tables that the crawler will crawl.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.delta_targets.w.text: Specifies whether the crawler writes a manifest file for each Delta Lake table it crawls, enabling query engines like Amazon Athena and Presto to read the Delta table via the manifest.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.dynamo_dbtarget.text: Specifies the DynamoDB table name that this DynamoDB target points to, which the AWS Glue crawler scans.
When set to true, the Glue crawler scans all items in the DynamoDB table, whereas false limits it to a sample of approximately 1,000 items.
The percentage of the DynamoDB table's provisioned read throughput that the crawler will consume while scanning, controlling scan speed and impact on the source table.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.hudi_targets.co.text: The name of the AWS Glue connection used by the crawler to access and catalog Hudi table metadata from the specified Hudi data store.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.hudi_targets.ex.text: Specifies a list of glob patterns that the crawler will ignore when scanning the Hudi data store, allowing specific files or directories to be excluded from the crawl.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.hudi_targets.ma.text: Specifies the maximum directory depth to traverse when crawling Hudi target paths, limiting how deep the crawler will explore the data store.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.hudi_targets.pa.text: List of Amazon S3 paths that define the root locations of Hudi datasets to be crawled by the Glue crawler.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.iceberg_targets.text: Name of the AWS Glue connection that the crawler uses to access the Iceberg table's metadata (such as a connection to a custom metastore or the Glue Data Catalog) during the crawl.
Specifies a list of glob patterns (e.g., '*.tmp') that the crawler excludes from the Iceberg data store when crawling, preventing certain files or folders from being included in the table metadata.
Specifies the maximum number of directory levels deep that the crawler will traverse under each Iceberg target path to discover table definitions and partition layouts.
Specifies the S3 paths to Iceberg tables (or directories containing Iceberg metadata) that the crawler will scan and catalog.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.jdbc_targets.co.text: The name of the JDBC connection to use for this JDBC target.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.jdbc_targets.en.text: Specifies additional metadata (currently only 'COMMENTS') to be captured from JDBC data sources during the crawl, enabling table and column comments to be stored in the Data Catalog.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.jdbc_targets.ex.text: List of glob-style path patterns (e.g., 'table_[0-9]*') that the crawler excludes from the JDBC target's scan, preventing specified tables or partitions from being cataloged.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.jdbc_targets.pa.text: The path of the JDBC target, identifying the database table (or tables) to crawl, typically in the form `database.table` or `schema.table` relative to the configured JDBC connection.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.mongo_dbtargets.text: The name of an AWS Glue connection that stores connection details for the MongoDB data store to crawl.
The database and collection path (for example, database.collection) for the MongoDB target in the AWS Glue crawler.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.s3_targets.conn.text: The name of a Glue connection used to access this S3 target, enabling the crawler to reach S3 data inside an Amazon VPC via a VPC endpoint or similar network configuration.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.s3_targets.dlq_.text: The ARN of the SQS dead-letter queue that receives failed events from the S3 event queue configured for this Glue crawler's S3 target.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.s3_targets.even.text: The ARN of an Amazon SQS queue that receives S3 object-created events, enabling event-based incremental crawling of the S3 target.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.s3_targets.excl.text: A list of glob patterns (such as '*.log') used to exclude specific S3 objects from being crawled by this crawler.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.s3_targets.path.text: The path to the Amazon S3 location (bucket or bucket/prefix) that the Glue crawler will crawl to populate the data catalog.

aws_glue_crawler.targets.s3_targets.samp.text: Sets the number of records sampled from the S3 target by the crawler to infer the schema.

aws_glue_database.database_input.create_.text: For each entry in create_table_default_permissions, the list of permissions (e.g., ALL, ALTER, CREATE_TABLE) granted to the specified principal for tables created in the database.

Specifies the IAM principal (such as a user, role, or federated user) to which the default permissions on tables created in this database apply, identified by its data lake principal identifier (for example, an IAM ARN).
The unique identifier of the data lake principal (such as an IAM role ARN or an AWS account ID) that is granted the default permissions on tables created in this Glue database.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.arguments.text: A map of key-value pairs that specify configuration arguments passed to the Apache Spark environment of the development endpoint.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.endpoint_name.text: Specifies a user-defined name for this AWS Glue development endpoint, which AWS Glue uses to identify it; if omitted, CloudFormation automatically generates a unique name.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.extra_jars_s3_path.text: The S3 path to one or more Java JAR files that provide custom jars to be used by the Glue development endpoint.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.extra_python_libs_.text: The S3 path to a Python library (or set of libraries) that AWS Glue installs on the development endpoint for use by your ETL scripts.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.glue_version.text: Specifies the AWS Glue version (such as '1.0' or '2.0') that defines the Apache Spark and Python runtime environment for this development endpoint.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.id.text: The unique identifier for the Glue development endpoint, which is the same as the endpoint's name and is used as the Terraform resource ID for import and state tracking.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.number_of_nodes.text: Specifies the number of compute nodes for the development endpoint, which determines its processing capacity and parallelism.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.number_of_workers.text: The number of worker nodes allocated to this AWS Glue development endpoint.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.public_key.text: The SSH public key that AWS Glue uses to authenticate connections to the development endpoint.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.public_keys.text: A list of SSH public keys used to authenticate to the dev endpoint for secure access.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that the development endpoint assumes to access resources such as data stores and scripts.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.security_configura.text: The name of an AWS Glue security configuration to attach to this development endpoint, which defines encryption and other security settings.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.security_group_ids.text: List of security group IDs to attach to the Glue dev endpoint for VPC networking.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.subnet_id.text: The subnet ID within a VPC where the AWS Glue development endpoint is provisioned, used when the endpoint needs access to resources in a Virtual Private Cloud.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.tags.text: Specifies a set of key-value tags to attach to the AWS Glue development endpoint, used for resource organization, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_glue_dev_endpoint.worker_type.text: The worker type for the development endpoint, such as Standard, G.1X, or G.2X, which determines the compute capacity of each worker.

aws_glue_integration.data_filter.text: Specifies a SQL query string that filters the source data to be included in the Glue integration, such as selecting specific columns or rows from a source table.

aws_glue_integration.tags.value.text: The value of the tag assigned to the Glue integration, used with the tag key to attach metadata for cost allocation, access control, and resource identification.

aws_glue_integration_resource_property.t.text: The key of a tag assigned to the AWS Glue integration resource, enabling you to categorize and manage the integration according to your organizational conventions.

aws_glue_job.command.text: Specifies the job's run command, including the script language (e.g., Python or Scala), the S3 path to the script, and optionally the Python version.

aws_glue_job.connections.text: Specifies the names of the AWS Glue connections to be used by the job, enabling it to access external data stores.

aws_glue_job.execution_property.text: Specifies the execution property for the job, specifically the maximum number of concurrent runs allowed (MaxConcurrentRuns).

aws_glue_job.notification_property.text: Specifies the notification property for the job, which contains the number of minutes to wait after a job run starts before AWS Glue sends a notification if the run is still in progress.

aws_glue_mltransform.input_record_tables.text: The identifier of the AWS Glue Data Catalog in which the specified input table resides; if omitted, the current AWS account's catalog ID is used.
The name of an AWS Glue connection used to access the source table, required when the table resides in an external data store such as JDBC rather than being purely stored in the Glue Data Catalog.
The name of the AWS Glue Data Catalog database that contains the table used as an input record source for the machine learning transform.
The name of the Glue Data Catalog table that supplies the input records for the ML transform.

aws_glue_partition.catalog_id.text: The identifier of the AWS Glue Data Catalog (typically the AWS account ID) that contains the database and table where this partition is created.

aws_glue_partition.database_name.text: The name of the Glue Data Catalog database that contains the table for which this partition is defined.

aws_glue_partition.id.text: The unique identifier of the Glue partition, typically a composite of the database name, table name, and partition values (e.g., 'database:table:value1/value2').

aws_glue_partition.partition_input.text: The partition_input field defines the metadata and storage configuration for a single partition in a Glue table, including its values, storage descriptor, and parameters.

aws_glue_partition.partition_input.param.text: Specifies key-value pairs that store custom metadata for the partition (e.g., compression type or other table properties), as a dynamic map of strings.

aws_glue_partition.partition_input.stora.text: Defines the physical storage details for the partition, including its location (such as an S3 path), input and output formats, column schema, SerDe configuration, and bucket or sort key settings.
The list of column names by which the partition data is bucketed (hash-partitioned) within the Glue table.
Defines the columns (name, data type, and optional comment) that make up the schema of the partition's storage descriptor.
Sets the optional comment or description for a column within the partition's storage descriptor, providing human-readable context for that column in the AWS Glue Data Catalog.
The name of a column in the storage descriptor for the partition, defining the schema of the data stored in the partition.
The data type (e.g., string, int, boolean) of the column in the partition's schema, as used by Glue when reading or writing the underlying data format.
Indicates whether the data in the partition is compressed, as defined in the AWS Glue StorageDescriptor for the partition's table format.
The fully qualified class name of the input format used for reading files in this partition, such as org.apache.hadoop.mapred.TextInputFormat.
The URI of the storage location (typically an S3 prefix) where the data files for this partition reside, as defined in the partition's StorageDescriptor.
Specifies the number of buckets in the storage descriptor for the partition, which defines the bucketing layout of the underlying data in AWS Glue.

Specifies the fully qualified class name of the Hadoop OutputFormat used for writing data files in the partition, such as org.apache.hadoop.hive.ql.io.parquet.MapredParquetOutputFormat or org.apache.hadoop.hive.ql.io.HiveIgnoreKeyTextOutputFormat.
Specifies custom key-value pairs (parameters) for the storage descriptor, such as SerDe or compression properties, for the Glue partition.
Specifies a reference to a schema in the AWS Glue Schema Registry, including the schema identifier and version, that defines the column structure for this partition.
Identifies the schema in the AWS Glue Schema Registry (by schema ARN or registry name and schema name) that this partition's storage descriptor references via its schema reference.
The name of the AWS Glue Schema Registry that contains the schema referenced by the partition's storage descriptor.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the schema in the AWS Glue Schema Registry that this partition's storage descriptor references.
The name of the AWS Glue Schema Registry schema that this partition's storage descriptor references.

The unique identifier (UUID) of a specific version of a schema in the AWS Glue Schema Registry, used to reference that schema version for this partition's storage descriptor when schema reference is configured.
The version number of the referenced Glue schema, used to pin the partition's storage descriptor to a specific schema version for schema evolution compatibility.
Specifies the serialization/deserialization (SerDe) configuration, including the SerDe library name and parameters, used to interpret the data in the partition's storage descriptor.
The name of the serializer/deserializer (SerDe) library used to read and write data for the partition's storage descriptor.
Specifies the key-value configuration parameters for the SerDe (serializer/deserializer), such as format-specific options like delimiters, applied to the partition's storage descriptor.
Specifies the fully qualified class name of the SerDe library (e.g., org.openx.data.jsonserde.JsonSerDe) used to serialize and deserialize data in the table partition.
Specifies skewed column names, skewed column values, and their location mappings for the partition's storage descriptor, used to optimize storage and query handling for skewed data in the table.

A list of column names in the partition's storage descriptor that are identified as having skewed data values, used together with skewed column value maps for optimizing storage and query performance in AWS Glue.
Specifies a mapping from skewed column values to their physical file or directory locations within the storage descriptor, allowing query engines to locate data for unbalanced values efficiently.

Specifies the list of skewed values (in the same order and count as the skewed column names) that should be mapped to separate physical locations for asymmetric or skewed data in the Glue table's storage descriptor.
Sorts the data stored in the partition by the specified columns, each entry providing a column name and an integer sort order (0 for descending, 1 for ascending).
The name of the column that serves as the sort key for this partition, determining the order of data within the partition's storage descriptor.
Specifies whether the column is sorted in ascending (0) or descending (1) order.
Specifies whether the partition's data is stored in subdirectories rather than in a single directory, as part of the storage descriptor.

aws_glue_partition.partition_input.value.text: The list of partition key values that uniquely identify this partition within the Glue table, matching the order of the table's partition key columns.

aws_glue_partition.table_name.text: The name of the Glue table to which this partition belongs.

aws_glue_registry.tags.key.text: The tag key part of a key-value pair used to tag an AWS Glue registry, enabling you to categorize and filter the resource.

aws_glue_registry.tags.value.text: The value portion of a user-defined tag attached to this AWS Glue registry, used to categorize, identify, or manage the registry.

aws_glue_schema.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to an AWS Glue schema, which allows you to assign custom metadata to the schema for cost tracking, access control, and operational organization.

aws_glue_security_configuration.encrypti.text: Specifies whether CloudWatch Logs encryption is disabled or uses SSE-KMS for the Glue security configuration, with allowed values 'DISABLED' and 'SSE-KMS'.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt CloudWatch log data for the Glue security configuration.
Sets the encryption mode for job bookmark data to either DISABLED (no encryption) or CSE-KMS (client-side encryption via an AWS KMS key specified in the same job_bookmarks_encryption block).
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt job bookmark data when job bookmark encryption is enabled for the Glue security configuration.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt data in Amazon S3 when the encryption mode is set to SSE-KMS, as part of a Glue security configuration's S3 encryption settings.
Specifies the S3 encryption mode for the Glue security configuration, which can be 'DISABLED', 'SSE-S3', or 'SSE-KMS' to control how data in S3 is encrypted.

aws_glue_table.catalog_id.text: The ID of the AWS Glue Data Catalog (typically the AWS account ID) in which the table and its parent database reside.

aws_glue_table.database_name.text: The name of the Glue Data Catalog database in which the table is stored.

aws_glue_table.id.text: The id is the provider-assigned unique identifier for the Glue table, formatted as the database name and table name joined by a colon (e.g., my_db:my_table).

aws_glue_table.name.text: The name of the table stored in the AWS Glue Data Catalog, uniquely identifying it within the Glue database.

aws_glue_table.open_table_format_input.text: Specifies the open table format configuration for the Glue table, including Iceberg input (metadata operation) and table identifier, allowing the table to be used with open data formats like Apache Iceberg.

aws_glue_table.open_table_format_input.i.text: Provides Iceberg-specific input settings for the glue table's open table format, including the metadata operation (e.g., CREATE) that AWS Glue should perform on the table's Iceberg metadata.

Configures the Iceberg-specific table metadata, including the metadata operation (such as CREATE or UPDATE) and version, used when the Glue table is registered as an Iceberg table in the Data Catalog.
The S3 URI where the Iceberg table's data and metadata are stored, required when registering the table in the Glue Data Catalog.

Specifies the partitioning for an Iceberg table by defining a list of partition fields, where each field names a source column and a transform (such as identity, bucket, or truncate) used to compute partition values.

Defines the partition fields for the Iceberg table, where each field specifies the source column name and the transform (such as identity, bucket, truncate, year, month, day, or hour) that determines how the table data is partitioned.

The unique integer identifier assigned to this partition field within the Iceberg partition spec, used to distinguish it from other partition fields when the table's partition layout is referenced by Iceberg metadata and query engines.
Specifies the name of a partition field in the Iceberg partition spec, which is the source column name or a derived name when a partition transform (such as bucket, truncate, or year) is applied.
The numeric identifier of the source column in the Iceberg table's schema that this partition field is based on.
The Iceberg partition transform (e.g., identity, year, month, day, hour, bucket, truncate) applied to the source column in the partition spec field.
Defines the unique identifier for the Iceberg partition spec, used to reference the specific partition spec when creating or updating the table.

A map of key-value pairs specifying Iceberg table properties (e.g., `format-version`, `write.format.default`) to be applied to the Iceberg table when the Glue table uses the Iceberg open table format.
Defines the Iceberg table's schema, including its columns, data types, and structure, as required when using the Iceberg open table format for the Glue table.
Specifies the required list of column definitions (fields) for the schema of the Iceberg table, where each field defines a column's name and data type in the Glue Data Catalog.
Provides a human-readable documentation string (doc) that describes this field/column in the Iceberg table schema within AWS Glue.
Unique numeric identifier for each column field within the Iceberg table schema, used by Iceberg to reference the field positionally in metadata and partition specs.
The name of a column (field) in the Iceberg table schema, used as the column identifier within the Iceberg table input for the Glue table.
Indicates whether this field in the Iceberg table schema is required (non-nullable); when false, the field is optional and can contain null values.

Defines the data type of a specific field in the Iceberg table's schema, using Iceberg type strings such as 'int', 'string', 'boolean', 'array<...>', or 'struct<...>' to represent primitive or nested types.
Specifies which field IDs from the Iceberg table schema collectively form the table's identifier (primary key).
The integer identifier for the Iceberg schema within the table, used to uniquely reference this schema version in the table's Iceberg metadata.
The `type` field of the Iceberg table schema, which identifies the top-level Iceberg schema type (usually `struct`) for the Glue table's open table format input.
Specifies the list of sort fields that define the write order (sort order) for data written to the underlying Iceberg table, with each field indicating a source column, transform, and sort direction.
The sort direction (either 'asc' or 'desc') for this field within the Iceberg table's write order sort spec.
Specifies whether null values are sorted first or last for this field within the Iceberg table's write order sort field, typically set to 'NULLS_FIRST' or 'NULLS_LAST'.
The numeric ID of the source column in the Iceberg table schema that this write-order/sort field references, used to define which column the sort order applies to.
Specifies the Iceberg sort transform (e.g., identity, bucket, truncate, year) applied to the source column for this write-order field in the Iceberg table.
The numeric identifier that uniquely identifies this write sort order within the Iceberg table metadata, used to reference and apply the write order when writing data.
Specifies the metadata operation (e.g., CREATE or UPDATE) to perform when registering the Apache Iceberg table in the Glue Data Catalog.
The version identifier of the Iceberg table metadata to update, used when the metadata operation is set to UPDATE.

aws_glue_table.table_input.text: The table_input object specifies the full metadata definition of the Glue Data Catalog table, including its name, storage descriptor, partition keys, table type, parameters, and other table properties used when creating or updating the table.

aws_glue_table.table_input.description.text: The user-provided description of the table, stored in the AWS Glue Data Catalog to document the table's contents or purpose.

aws_glue_table.table_input.name.text: The name of the Glue table to be created or updated.

aws_glue_table.table_input.owner.text: Specifies the owner of the table, typically the AWS account ID or IAM role that owns it in the AWS Glue Data Catalog.

aws_glue_table.table_input.parameters.text: Specifies a map of key-value pairs that define the table's metadata and format-specific options, such as 'classification' (e.g., csv, parquet), 'separatorChar', and 'compressionType', which AWS Glue uses when reading or writing the underlying data.

aws_glue_table.table_input.partition_key.text: Defines the list of partition columns for the Glue table, with each object specifying the column name, data type, and optional comment for a partition key.
The comment associated with a partition key (column) in the Glue table's schema.
The name of a partition key column in the Glue table's partition keys list.
The data type of the partition key column (e.g., STRING, INT, or DATE), defining how the partition values are interpreted in the Glue table's schema.

aws_glue_table.table_input.retention.text: Specifies the number of days that the table should be retained in the AWS Glue Data Catalog, as represented by the Retention field of the TableInput property.

aws_glue_table.table_input.storage_descr.text: Specifies the physical storage information for the table, including its column list, file location, data format (input/output), and SerDe configuration, used by AWS Glue for reading and writing data.
The list of column names that determine bucketing for the table data, defining how records are distributed into buckets in the storage descriptor.
A list of Column objects defining the table's schema, where each column specifies its name, data type, and optional comment within the storage descriptor.
The comment for a column in the Glue table's storage descriptor, providing a human-readable description of the column's meaning or purpose.
The name of a column in the Glue table's storage descriptor, which serves as the column's identifier within the table schema.
The data type of the column, specified as a Glue/Athena data type string (e.g., 'string', 'int', 'map<string,string>', 'struct<...>').
A boolean flag indicating whether the underlying table data is compressed, as defined in the Glue table's StorageDescriptor.
The fully qualified Java class name of the input format used to read the table's data, such as 'org.apache.hadoop.mapred.TextInputFormat'.
The physical location of the table data, typically an S3 URI (e.g., 's3://bucket/path') that the Glue table points to in its storage descriptor.
The number of buckets in the table, which is used by partition pruning and query optimization for bucketed data.
The fully qualified class name of the output format (e.g., org.apache.hadoop.hive.ql.io.HiveIgnoreKeyTextOutputFormat) that the table uses to write data, as part of the storage descriptor.
Specifies user-defined key-value parameters for the storage descriptor, allowing custom metadata to be associated with the underlying table storage.
Specifies a reference to an AWS Glue Schema Registry schema (via schema ID and version) that defines the table's schema instead of providing inline column definitions.
Identifies the AWS Glue schema registry schema referenced by this table's storage descriptor, specified via schema ARN or registry name plus schema name.
The name of the AWS Glue Schema Registry that contains the referenced schema.
The ARN of the schema in the AWS Glue Schema Registry that this table references, used to uniquely identify the schema when creating or updating the table's storage descriptor.
The name of the schema in the AWS Glue Schema Registry that this table references via its schema_id, used together with the registry name to identify the schema.
The unique identifier of the specific schema version in the AWS Glue Schema Registry that this table's storage descriptor references, determining the column definition and format used.
The version number of the referenced schema in the Glue Schema Registry that this table is based on, used to pin the table to a specific schema version.
Defines the serialization/deserialization (SerDe) configuration for the table, including the SerDe library name and associated parameters.
The user-supplied name of the serializer/deserializer (SerDe) referenced by this storage descriptor, typically matching the SerDe class name used in the table.

A map of key-value configuration parameters passed to the SerDe (serializer/deserializer) specified in serde_info, controlling how data is serialized and deserialized (e.g., 'field.delim' for delimiter-separated formats or 'serialization.format' for Parquet).

The fully qualified class name of the SerDe (serializer/deserializer) used by AWS Glue to read and write data in the table, such as org.apache.hadoop.hive.serde2.lazy.LazySimpleSerDe or org.openx.data.jsonserde.JsonSerDe.
Defines skew information for the table's storage descriptor, including skewed column names, their values, and mapping of those values to file locations to optimize querying of skewed data.
A list of column names that contain skewed values, enabling AWS Glue to optimize storage and querying for skewed data.
Maps each skewed column value to a distinct file location where rows with that value are stored, enabling optimized handling of data skew in the Glue table's storage descriptor.
The list of values that appear frequently in the skewed columns defined in the parent `skewed_info`, used by Glue to optimize storage and query performance for skewed data.
Specifies the columns (with optional ascending/descending order) by which the table's data is sorted, as part of the Glue table's storage descriptor.
Specifies the name of a column to be used for sorting the table data in the Glue table's storage descriptor, where each entry in the sort columns list defines a sort key column.
The sort order for the sort column, where 0 indicates ascending order and 1 indicates descending order.

This Boolean flag indicates that the table's data is stored in subdirectories, which is typically used for partitioned tables so that AWS Glue treats each partition key value as a directory in the underlying storage.

aws_glue_table.table_input.table_type.text: Specifies the table type, such as EXTERNAL_TABLE for a table backed by external data or VIRTUAL_VIEW for a view, in the AWS Glue TableInput.

aws_glue_table.table_input.target_table.text: For a table defined as a resource link, this field provides the catalog, database, and name of the destination table that the link resolves to, enabling cross-catalog or cross-database table references in the Glue Data Catalog.

aws_glue_table.table_input.target_table..text: Identifies the AWS Glue Data Catalog (account ID) that contains the target table, used when creating a table link that points to an existing table in another catalog.
The name of the database that contains the target table when this Glue table is a resource link pointing to another table.
The name of the target Glue table that this table references when using the TargetTable configuration to point to an existing table.
The AWS region in which the target table is located, enabling cross-region references for Glue tables.

aws_glue_table.table_input.view_definiti.text: This object represents the view definition, including the SQL query (DefinedBy) and sub-objects, that marks the table as a view in the AWS Glue Data Catalog rather than a physical table.
Specifies the security definer (the principal whose permissions are used) for the view, used when the Glue table's ViewDefinition is set.
A Boolean value that indicates whether the view can be used in a query.
Specifies a list of view representations, each providing a dialect-specific SQL query definition (like for Athena or Spark SQL) that defines the view for different query engines.
Specifies the query engine dialect (such as SPARK or ATHENA) used by this representation of the view definition for the AWS Glue table.
The version of the SQL dialect used by this view representation, enabling AWS Glue to interpret the view text correctly for that dialect.
This field specifies the name of the AWS Glue connection used to validate the SQL representation of the view against the underlying data source.
The expanded SQL query text for the view representation in the specified dialect, used by AWS Glue to resolve the view's logical table.
The original SQL text of the view, as initially defined, for this representation of the AWS Glue table's view definition.
Specifies the list of source tables (identified by ARN or table identifier) that a Glue view definition is built upon, defining which base tables the view queries.

aws_glue_table.table_input.view_expanded.text: The expanded SQL text that defines the view when the table is a view, stored in the Glue Data Catalog as part of the TableInput.

aws_glue_table.table_input.view_original.text: Specifies the original SQL text used to define a view when the table represents a view rather than a physical table.

aws_glue_table_optimizer.table_optimizer.text: Defines the table optimizer's settings, such as whether automatic optimization is enabled and the IAM role ARN that runs the optimizer jobs.
Defines the settings for the compaction operation in the Glue table optimizer, including whether compaction is enabled (Enabled flag) for the table.
Specifies the Iceberg-specific settings for the compaction configuration of the AWS Glue table optimizer, controlling how compaction is performed on Apache Iceberg table data.
Configuration for the orphan file deletion optimizer, specifying the retention period (in days) for orphan files before they are deleted from the S3 table.
Specifies the Iceberg-specific settings for the orphan file deletion optimizer, including the retention period in days that determines when orphan files are eligible for deletion.
Configures the retention settings for the Glue table optimizer, specifying the snapshot retention period and the number of snapshots to retain for Apache Iceberg tables.
Specifies Iceberg-specific snapshot retention settings, such as the number of snapshots to retain and the retention period in days, for the Glue table optimizer's retention configuration.

When enabled, this flag instructs the Glue table optimizer to physically delete expired Iceberg data files that are no longer referenced by any retained snapshot as part of the table's retention policy.
The maximum number of Iceberg snapshots to retain when expiring old snapshots for the table, as part of the table optimizer's retention configuration.
The number of days to retain Iceberg snapshots before they are automatically expired by the Glue table optimizer.
Configures the VPC settings, including subnet and security group IDs, that the AWS Glue job running the table optimization uses to access resources within a virtual private cloud.

aws_glue_trigger.actions.arguments.text: The set of key-value pairs that are passed as arguments to the referenced Glue job when this trigger action runs.

aws_glue_trigger.actions.crawler_name.text: The name of the AWS Glue crawler to start when this trigger action is invoked, used for crawler-based trigger actions.

aws_glue_trigger.actions.job_name.text: The name of the AWS Glue job that will be started when the trigger fires, as defined in the Actions property of the Glue trigger.

aws_glue_trigger.actions.notification_pr.text: Defines the notification settings for a Glue trigger action, specifically the number of minutes after a job run starts before a job run delay notification is sent (NotifyDelayAfter).
Specifies the number of minutes to wait after a job run completes before sending a notification for this Glue trigger action.

aws_glue_trigger.actions.security_config.text: The name of the AWS Glue security configuration that encrypts the job run's data and connections when this trigger action starts a job.

aws_glue_trigger.actions.timeout.text: The job run timeout in minutes for the action, overriding the timeout value of the associated job.

aws_glue_trigger.predicate.conditions.cr.text: The crawl state (e.g., SUCCEEDED, FAILED, RUNNING) that the crawler referenced in this condition must reach for the trigger predicate to evaluate as true.
The name of the AWS Glue crawler that must reach the specified crawl state (e.g., COMPLETED) to satisfy the trigger condition.

aws_glue_trigger.predicate.conditions.jo.text: The name of the AWS Glue job whose run state (e.g., SUCCEEDED, FAILED, TIMEOUT) this predicate condition evaluates to determine whether the trigger fires.

aws_glue_trigger.predicate.conditions.lo.text: Specifies the logical operator (AND or OR) that combines this condition with the previous condition in the trigger's predicate, defaulting to AND when not specified.

aws_glue_trigger.predicate.conditions.st.text: The state (e.g., SUCCEEDED, FAILED) that the referenced job or crawler must be in for this condition to be met within the trigger's predicate.

aws_glue_usage_profile.configuration.text: The configuration for the Glue usage profile, defining the profile's data access permissions, usage limits, and other settings as a JSON object.

aws_glue_user_defined_function.resource_.text: Specifies the type of resource stored at the URI, such as 'JAR', 'FILE', or 'ARCHIVE', for the user-defined function's resource URIs.
The URI (typically an S3 path or similar location) of the resource (e.g., jar, archive, or file) associated with the user-defined function.

aws_grafana_workspace.tags.value.text: The value assigned to a tag key for the Grafana workspace, used to categorize, organize, and track the resource for cost and management purposes.

aws_greengrass_connector_definition.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Greengrass connector definition.

aws_greengrass_connector_definition.id.text: The AWS-assigned unique identifier for this Greengrass connector definition.

aws_greengrass_connector_definition.init.text: Specifies the initial connector definition version that contains the list of connectors and their parameter configurations to be deployed with this Greengrass connector definition.
Specifies the connectors that compose the initial version of the AWS Greengrass connector definition, each providing a connector ARN, a unique ID, and optional parameters for the connector.
The ARN of the AWS Greengrass connector to include in the connector definition version.
A user-defined identifier for each connector in the Greengrass connector definition version, used to uniquely reference that connector within the group.
Specifies the configuration parameters for the connector as a map of key-value pairs.

aws_greengrass_connector_definition.late.text: Returns the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the most recently created version of this AWS Greengrass connector definition.

aws_greengrass_connector_definition.name.text: The descriptive name of the AWS IoT Greengrass connector definition, required to create and reference the definition in your AWS account.

aws_greengrass_connector_definition.tags.text: Metadata tags to attach to the Greengrass connector definition resource for organization, identification, or cost allocation.

aws_greengrass_connector_definition_vers.text: Specifies the ID of the Greengrass connector definition to which this version belongs, linking the version to its parent ConnectorDefinition resource.
Defines the list of connectors that make up this Greengrass connector definition version, where each connector specifies its connector ARN and configuration parameters.
The ARN of the AWS IoT Greengrass connector that this connector definition version includes.
The user-defined unique identifier for each connector within the Greengrass connector definition version, used to reference the connector in the group configuration.
Specifies the configuration parameters for the Greengrass connector, passed as key-value pairs to the connector's Lambda function.
The unique version UUID that AWS IoT Greengrass assigns to this connector definition version, returned by the CreateConnectorDefinitionVersion API.

aws_greengrass_core_definition.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Greengrass core definition, uniquely identifying it across AWS.

aws_greengrass_core_definition.id.text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier of the Greengrass core definition resource.

aws_greengrass_core_definition.initial_v.text: Defines the initial version of the core definition by specifying a list of Greengrass core devices, each identified by its AWS IoT thing ARN and associated certificate ARN, that are used when the definition is first created.
Specifies the list of core devices (each with a thing ARN and certificate ARN) that make up the initial version of this AWS Greengrass core definition.
The ARN of the AWS IoT certificate that authenticates the core device in the Greengrass group.
The user-defined identifier for this core within the Greengrass core definition version, used to reference the core in the group configuration.
Indicates whether the Greengrass core device's shadow sync is enabled with the AWS IoT cloud, allowing the local shadow to be synchronized with the cloud-shadow service.
The ARN of the AWS IoT thing that this Greengrass core represents.

aws_greengrass_core_definition.latest_ve.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the most recent version of the Greengrass core definition, automatically updated whenever the definition is revised.

aws_greengrass_core_definition.name.text: The name of the AWS IoT Greengrass core definition, a required user-defined identifier used to distinguish this resource.

aws_greengrass_core_definition.tags.text: Attaches key-value metadata tags to the AWS Greengrass core definition, useful for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_greengrass_core_definition_version.c.text: The unique ID of the AWS Greengrass core definition that this core definition version is associated with.

The cores list specifies the Greengrass core devices for this core definition version, where each object includes the core device's Thing ARN, its associated certificate ARN, and an optional flag to enable shadow synchronization.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS IoT certificate that identifies the Greengrass core device when it connects to AWS IoT.
The logical ID assigned to this core within the Greengrass core definition version, used to uniquely identify the core among the list of cores.
Indicates whether the Greengrass core device's shadow is synchronized with the cloud.
The ARN of the AWS IoT Thing that acts as the Greengrass core device in this core definition version.

aws_greengrass_core_definition_version.i.text: The unique AWS-assigned version ID (typically a UUID) for the Greengrass core definition version, returned after creation.

aws_greengrass_device_definition.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Greengrass device definition, used to reference it in IAM policies and other AWS services.

aws_greengrass_device_definition.id.text: The service-assigned unique identifier for this AWS IoT Greengrass device definition, used to reference the definition in other resources.

aws_greengrass_device_definition.initial.text: Specifies the initial version of the device definition, containing a list of devices (each with an ID, certificate ARN, and optional sync shadow setting) that is created when the device definition is first created.
A list of devices (each with a device ID, Thing ARN, Certificate ARN, and optional SyncShadow flag) that comprise the initial version of the AWS Greengrass device definition.
The ARN of the AWS IoT certificate that identifies and authenticates the Greengrass device within the device definition version.
The user-defined identifier that uniquely identifies each device within the Greengrass device definition version.
Indicates whether the device's shadow is synchronized with AWS IoT for this device in the Greengrass device definition.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS IoT thing representing the Greengrass device to include in the initial version of this device definition.
