aws_greengrass_device_definition.latest_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the latest version of this AWS IoT Greengrass device definition.

aws_greengrass_device_definition.name.text: Specifies a user-friendly name for the AWS IoT Greengrass device definition, required to identify the definition in the console and API.

aws_greengrass_device_definition.tags.text: Tags are user-defined key-value pairs that can be attached to the AWS IoT Greengrass device definition resource for organizing, identifying, and managing it within AWS.

aws_greengrass_device_definition_version.text: The ID of the Greengrass device definition to which this version belongs, required to scope the version resource within a specific device definition.

Defines the list of AWS IoT devices (things) included in this Greengrass device definition version, each specifying the device's ID, thing ARN, certificate ARN, and whether local shadow synchronization is enabled.
The ARN of the AWS IoT certificate used to authenticate the Greengrass device when it connects to the AWS Greengrass core.
The device ID, which must be unique within the device definition version and is used to identify the device in this version.
Indicates whether the device's shadow is synchronized with the AWS IoT shadow.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS IoT thing that this device represents in the Greengrass device definition version.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this Greengrass device definition version, used as a computed resource identifier.

aws_greengrass_function_definition.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the function definition.

aws_greengrass_function_definition.id.text: The unique ID that AWS IoT Greengrass assigns to this function definition, returned as a read-only attribute after the resource is created.

aws_greengrass_function_definition.initi.text: Provides the initial version of the function definition, specifying the default configuration and the Lambda functions to be deployed.

Specifies the default execution configuration (such as container isolation mode, memory limit, and timeout) applied to all Lambda functions in this function definition version unless overridden by an individual function's settings.

Defines the default execution settings for all functions in the definition version, specifying the container isolation mode (e.g., GreengrassContainer or NoContainer) and the system user/group (runAs) that Lambda functions use when running on the Greengrass core.
Specifies the container isolation mode for the Lambda function, either 'GreengrassContainer' or 'NoContainer', determining whether the function runs inside a Greengrass-managed container.
Specifies the user and group identifiers (UID and GID) that Lambda functions in the Greengrass group run as, controlling operating system permissions for execution.
The Linux group ID (GID) that the Lambda function runs as when executed on the Greengrass core, used to override the default system group for the function's process.
The numeric user ID (UID) under which the Lambda function runs when Greengrass executes it, as specified in the default execution run-as configuration for the function definition version.

Defines the list of functions included in the initial version of this AWS Greengrass function definition, where each function entry provides the function ARN and its configuration such as memory limit, timeout, and environment variables.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function that this Greengrass function invokes on the core.
Specifies the runtime configuration for the Lambda function in a Greengrass function definition version, including memory size, timeout, environment variables, and execution parameters.
Specifies the encoding type (binary or json) of the input payload for the Lambda function in the Greengrass function definition.
Defines the Lambda function's runtime environment, including environment variables (Variables) and access to local Greengrass resources (ResourceAccessPolicies).
Indicates whether the Lambda function can access the host's /sys filesystem.
Specifies the execution settings for the Lambda function, such as the container isolation mode (GreengrassContainer or NoContainer) and the run-as user/group that the function uses.
Determines whether the Lambda function runs in a Greengrass container (GreengrassContainer) or directly on the host (NoContainer), controlling the isolation level of the execution environment.
Specifies the Unix user ID (Uid) and group ID (Gid) that the Lambda function uses to run in the Greengrass container.
The numeric group ID (GID) of the system group that the Lambda function runs as in the Greengrass execution environment.
The numeric user ID (UID) that the Lambda function runs as in the Greengrass group.
The list of resource access policies that grant the Lambda function permissions (read or write) on specific Greengrass local resources, each referencing a resource ID.
Specifies the access level for the function to the local resource, either 'ro' for read-only or 'rw' for read/write.
The ID of the Greengrass group resource (for example, a local volume or device) that the function is granted access to via this resource access policy.
A map of environment variable names to values that are made available to the Lambda function when it runs on the Greengrass core.
In a Greengrass function definition's function configuration, this specifies the command-line arguments to pass to the executable when the Lambda function runs.
The path to the executable file (e.g., a script or binary) that the Lambda function runs on the Greengrass core.
The amount of memory, in megabytes, to allocate to the Lambda function on the Greengrass core for this function configuration.
Indicates whether the Lambda function is pinned to the Greengrass core, which causes it to be deployed and kept running in memory rather than invoked on demand.
The maximum time in seconds that the Lambda function is allowed to execute before it is terminated, as part of the function configuration for this AWS Greengrass function definition.
A user-defined, unique identifier for this function within the Greengrass function definition version.

aws_greengrass_function_definition.lates.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the latest version of the Greengrass function definition, automatically assigned by AWS and updated whenever a new version is created.

aws_greengrass_function_definition.name.text: The name of the Greengrass function definition, serving as a user-friendly identifier for the resource.

aws_greengrass_function_definition.tags.text: A map of key-value pairs that you can attach to the function definition resource to identify and organize it.

aws_greengrass_function_definition_versi.text: Default configuration settings (execution and environment) that apply to all Lambda functions in this Greengrass function definition version unless overridden per-function.
Specifies the default execution behavior for Lambda functions in the Greengrass group, including the isolation mode and the system user and group that the functions run as.
Specifies the isolation mode (GreengrassContainer or NoContainer) used when Lambda functions in this version run on the Greengrass core.
Specifies the default UID and GID (operating system user and group) that Lambda functions in this Greengrass function definition version run as when invoked on the Greengrass core.
Specifies the numeric group ID (GID) used by the Greengrass container to run Lambda functions when applying this default execution configuration for the function definition version.
Specifies the numeric user ID (UID) under which the Lambda function process runs when the execution run-as mode is set to a specific user.
The ID of the AWS Greengrass function definition that this version belongs to.

The list of Lambda functions that are defined in this function definition version, where each object specifies the function's unique ID, its ARN, and its configuration (including memory, timeout, encoding, and environment variables).
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function that this Greengrass function definition version will deploy to the Greengrass core.
Specifies the runtime configuration for the Lambda function in the Greengrass group, including its executable, arguments, memory size, timeout, environment variables, and pinned state.
Specifies whether the function's input and output payloads are encoded as JSON or binary, with allowed values 'json' and 'binary' (default is 'json').
Configures the Lambda execution environment for the Greengrass function, including environment variables, resource access policies, and whether sysfs access is allowed.
If true, this grants the Greengrass Lambda function access to the host's /sys filesystem (sysfs) on the core device, with the default being false.
Determines whether the Lambda function runs in a Greengrass container (`GreengrassContainer`) or without containerization (`NoContainer`), controlling the execution isolation mode.
Specifies the numeric system user ID (UID) and group ID (GID) that the Greengrass Lambda function runs as, enabling the function to execute under a specific OS user context.
Specifies the POSIX group ID (gid) that the Greengrass Lambda function runs under in the core environment, determining the operating system group permissions for its execution.

The numeric user ID (UID) that the Lambda function runs under inside the Greengrass container, paired with the group ID (gid) to define the OS-level execution permissions for the function's containerized process.

Specifies the list of resource access policies that grant the Lambda function permissions to access Greengrass local resources (such as devices or volumes) on the core, where each policy includes a resource identifier and a read-only or read-write permission.
Specifies the access level granted to the Lambda function for the associated local resource, with valid values 'ro' for read-only or 'rw' for read/write.
The ID (ARN) of the local Greengrass resource (e.g., a volume or device) that this policy grants the Lambda function access to.
A map of key-value pairs that define environment variables passed to the Lambda function when it runs in the Greengrass group.
In an AWS Greengrass function definition version, this field sets the command-line arguments passed to the Lambda function when it executes on the Greengrass core.
Specifies the name or path of the executable that the Lambda function runs, used by the Greengrass function configuration to invoke the function.
The amount of memory, in megabytes, allocated to the Lambda function in the Greengrass function configuration.

Indicates whether the function is pinned to the Greengrass core, meaning it is pre-loaded and stays resident in memory so it can start quickly and run continuously rather than being invoked on demand.
Specifies the maximum execution time in seconds for the Lambda function; when exceeded, the function is stopped (default is 3 seconds).
The unique identifier for this function within the Greengrass function definition version.
The unique Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to this Greengrass function definition version, used as the resource identifier in Terraform.

aws_greengrass_group.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Greengrass group, automatically assigned by AWS when the group is created.

aws_greengrass_group.id.text: The AWS-assigned unique identifier for the Greengrass group.

aws_greengrass_group.initial_version.text: Specifies the initial version of the Greengrass group, which includes references to the core, devices, functions, loggers, subscriptions, and resource definitions that define the group's initial configuration.

aws_greengrass_group.initial_version.con.text: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a connector definition version to associate with the group's initial version, defining which connectors are available in the group.

aws_greengrass_group.initial_version.cor.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the core definition version to associate with the initial Greengrass group version.

aws_greengrass_group.initial_version.dev.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the device definition version to include in the initial group version when the group is created.

aws_greengrass_group.initial_version.fun.text: The ARN of the function definition version that defines the Lambda functions for the Greengrass group, included in the initial group version configuration.

aws_greengrass_group.initial_version.log.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a Greengrass logger definition version to associate with the group's initial version, enabling the group to use the specified logging configuration.

aws_greengrass_group.initial_version.res.text: This field specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the resource definition version that defines the local resources available to the Greengrass group's initial group version, which is used when the group is first created.

aws_greengrass_group.initial_version.sub.text: The ARN of the subscription definition version to associate with the group's initial version.

aws_greengrass_group.latest_version_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the latest version of the Greengrass group.

aws_greengrass_group.name.text: The name of the Greengrass group, which is a user-defined identifier for the group in AWS IoT Greengrass.

aws_greengrass_group.role_arn.text: The ARN of an IAM role that AWS Greengrass assumes on behalf of the group to access other AWS services (e.g., for Lambda function execution or connector interactions).

aws_greengrass_group.role_attached_at.text: The timestamp (in milliseconds) when the IAM role was attached to the Greengrass group.

aws_greengrass_group.tags.text: Tags to assign to the Greengrass group, providing key-value metadata for organizing, identifying, and managing the resource in AWS.

aws_greengrass_group_version.connector_d.text: The ARN of the connector definition version to associate with this Greengrass group version.

aws_greengrass_group_version.core_defini.text: The ARN of the core definition version to associate with this Greengrass group version, which defines the core device for the group.

aws_greengrass_group_version.device_defi.text: The ARN of the device definition version to include in this Greengrass group version.

aws_greengrass_group_version.function_de.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the function definition version that this group version references, which determines the Lambda functions included in the group.

aws_greengrass_group_version.group_id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS Greengrass group that this group version belongs to and whose configuration this version specifies.

aws_greengrass_group_version.id.text: The unique identifier of the Greengrass group version, assigned by AWS upon creation.

aws_greengrass_group_version.logger_defi.text: The ARN of the logger definition version to associate with this Greengrass group version.

aws_greengrass_group_version.resource_de.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the resource definition version to associate with this Greengrass group version.

aws_greengrass_group_version.subscriptio.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the subscription definition version that this Greengrass group version references for its MQTT subscription routing configuration.

aws_greengrass_logger_definition.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Greengrass logger definition, which uniquely identifies this resource in AWS and can be used to reference it in IAM policies and other AWS services.

aws_greengrass_logger_definition.initial.text: Specifies the initial version of the logger definition, which consists of a set of loggers that define how Greengrass components write logs to CloudWatch or the local file system.

Specifies the list of logger configuration objects for the initial version of the AWS Greengrass logger definition, each defining the component to log (e.g., GreengrassSystem or Lambda), the log output type (e.g., FileSystem or AWSCloudWatch), log level, and (for file-based logging) the disk space limit.
Specifies the component type the logger applies to (e.g., GreengrassSystem or Lambda) in an AWS Greengrass logger definition version.
A unique identifier for this logger within the Greengrass logger definition version, used to reference the logger when configuring logging for a Greengrass group.
Specifies the log severity threshold for the logger, with allowed values such as DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, and FATAL, determining which messages are recorded.
Specifies the maximum amount of log data (in kilobytes) that the logger can store for the associated Greengrass component.
Specifies whether this logger applies to Greengrass system components or user-defined Lambda/component loggers, with allowed values 'GreengrassSystem' and 'Component'.

aws_greengrass_logger_definition.latest_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the most recent version of the logger definition, automatically assigned by AWS.

aws_greengrass_logger_definition.name.text: The name that identifies this Greengrass logger definition in the AWS IoT Greengrass console and API.

aws_greengrass_logger_definition_version.text: The id is the unique ARN assigned by AWS to this Greengrass logger definition version, used to reference the version in other resources and API calls.
The ID of the Greengrass logger definition that this version belongs to, required when creating a logger definition version.
Specifies a list of logger configuration objects, each for an AWS Greengrass component, that determine where logs are sent (CloudWatch Logs or local file system) and the minimum log level to record.
Specifies the component that writes the logs captured by this logger, typically the literal value `GreengrassSystem` for system components or the ARN of a Lambda function for lambda components.
The unique identifier used to reference this logger component within the logger definition version.
The log level for this Greengrass logger, determining the minimum severity (e.g., DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, FATAL) of log messages that will be recorded.
The maximum amount of file space (in kilobytes) that the logger can use for storing log files, applicable to file-system based loggers in a Greengrass logger definition.
The logger destination type: AWSCloudWatch for logs published to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, or FileSystem for logs written to the local file system.

aws_greengrass_resource_definition.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this AWS Greengrass resource definition, assigned by AWS upon creation and used to reference the definition in other services.

aws_greengrass_resource_definition.id.text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier of the Greengrass resource definition, used to reference this definition in other Greengrass resources and API calls.

aws_greengrass_resource_definition.initi.text: Defines the initial version of the Greengrass resource definition, which contains an array of resource instances (such as local volumes or secrets) to be associated with the core when first deployed.
The `resources` list under `initial_version` defines the set of Greengrass resource instances (such as local device or volume resources) that comprise the initial version of the resource definition.
A unique identifier for this resource within the Greengrass resource definition version.
The user-defined name that identifies this resource instance within the Greengrass resource definition version.

An object that encapsulates a single Greengrass resource definition, containing a type field that selects exactly one of the five concrete data structures—local device, local volume, S3 machine learning model, SageMaker machine learning model, or Secrets Manager secret—and holds the corresponding configuration data for that resource type.
Specifies the source path of the local device resource on the Greengrass core device, such as a physical device like /dev/ttyAMA0.
Specifies the Linux group owner settings for the local device resource, including whether to automatically add the group owner and which group name to use.
Indicates whether the Greengrass core (group owner) automatically gains read/write access to the local device, or whether access is manually specified with the GroupOwner property.
The name of the Linux group that owns the local device resource, used to control file permissions on the device.
The absolute path of the local device on the Greengrass core that this resource references, for example /dev/ttyUSB0 or /dev/video0.
Specifies the configuration for a local volume resource, including the source path on the host file system, the destination path in the container, and optional group owner and permission settings.
The absolute path on the Greengrass core device where the local volume is mounted and made available to Lambda functions.
Configures the OS group owner and its read/write permissions that are applied to a Greengrass local volume resource, controlling how Lambda functions access the volume's file system.
Automatically sets the Greengrass group owner as the OS group owner of the local volume, granting the group owner access to the volume without requiring explicit permission settings.
The name of the operating system group that will be set as the owner of the local volume resource, used when auto-inheriting group ownership is disabled.
The absolute path to the local volume on the Greengrass core device that this resource data represents.
Configures a machine learning model resource hosted in Amazon S3, specifying the model's S3 URI and the local destination path where the Greengrass core will store it.
The absolute path on the Greengrass core device where the S3 machine learning model artifact is downloaded and stored.
Sets the Linux group owner and group read/write permissions applied to the S3 machine learning model artifact when it is deployed to a Greengrass core device.
The group name or group ID that will be set as the owner of the downloaded S3 machine learning model resource on the Greengrass core device.
Specifies the permission level (either 'ro' or 'rw') that the Greengrass group has for the S3 machine learning model resource data in the owner setting.
The S3 URI of the machine learning model artifact that this Greengrass resource points to.
This object configures an Amazon SageMaker machine learning model as a resource in the Greengrass group, specifying the model ARN and the local destination path on the core device.
The absolute local path on the Greengrass core device where the SageMaker machine learning model artifact is stored or downloaded to.
Specifies the Linux group owner and permissions for the SageMaker model resource, controlling access to the model on the Greengrass core device.
The operating system group that owns the SageMaker machine learning model resource within the Greengrass group.
Specifies whether the group owner has read-write ('rw') or read-only ('ro') permission to the SageMaker machine learning model resource in an AWS Greengrass resource definition.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SageMaker training job that produced the machine learning model to be deployed to the Greengrass core.
Specifies an AWS Secrets Manager secret to be available to the Greengrass group, by providing the secret's ARN and optionally additional staging labels to append for staged secret versions.

Specifies additional AWS Secrets Manager staging labels, beyond the default current version, for the referenced secret in the Greengrass resource definition, so that the core device downloads and exposes those labeled secret versions locally.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that provides the secret value for this Greengrass secret resource.

aws_greengrass_resource_definition.lates.text: The ARN of the latest version of the AWS IoT Greengrass resource definition.

aws_greengrass_resource_definition.name.text: The name of the resource definition, which provides a user-friendly identifier for this set of local resources in AWS Greengrass.

aws_greengrass_resource_definition.tags.text: Assigns metadata (key-value pairs) to this AWS Greengrass resource definition for identification and cost allocation.

aws_greengrass_resource_definition_versi.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this Greengrass resource definition version.
The ID of the AWS Greengrass resource definition that this version belongs to, required to associate the version with an existing resource definition.
Specifies the list of resources (such as local volumes, devices, or secrets) that are included in this AWS Greengrass resource definition version.
The user-defined ID that uniquely identifies this resource within the Greengrass resource definition version.
A user-defined name for the resource (such as a local device, local volume, or S3 object) in an AWS Greengrass resource definition version.
Defines the resource data container for each Greengrass resource, specifying either a local device or local volume resource (e.g., source path, permissions).
Configures a local device resource by specifying its source path on the host file system and optional group owner settings, used when the resource is a physical device such as /dev/ttyAMA0.

Configures the Linux group owner, group ID, and read/write/execute permissions for a local device resource in a Greengrass group, enabling the Greengrass core to access the device with specific ownership and access rights.
Indicates whether the Greengrass group owner is automatically added as the owner of the local device resource.
The name of the Linux group that owns the local device resource and has read/write access to it.
The source_path specifies the local device path on the Greengrass core device that this local device resource maps to, such as /dev/ttyUSB0 or /dev/video0.
Configures a local volume resource definition for a Greengrass group, specifying the device's source path and the destination path inside the Lambda runtime environment.
The absolute path on the Greengrass core where the source directory is mounted and available to the Lambda function.
Determines whether the Greengrass group owner is automatically granted ownership of the local volume, and optionally specifies a custom group owner for the volume.
If true, automatically adds the group owner (the core device's OS group) to the Linux permissions of the local volume resource, allowing the group to access the volume.
Specifies the Linux group name that will own the local volume resource when group ownership is configured for a Greengrass group.
The source path of the local volume resource, specifying the directory on the Greengrass core device that is used as the source for the volume.
Specifies the S3 machine learning model resource data, containing the S3 URI of the model and the destination path on the core device.
The absolute filesystem path on the Greengrass core device where the S3 machine learning model is downloaded and stored.
Specifies the Linux group owner and group read/write permission for the S3 machine learning model artifact, controlling its file ownership and access on the AWS IoT Greengrass core.

The name of the operating system group that owns the machine learning model artifact downloaded from S3 on the Greengrass core device, used in the owner setting for the S3 machine learning model resource.
The permission level (either 'ro' for read-only or 'rw' for read-write) that the specified group owner has on the referenced S3 machine learning model resource.
The S3 URI of the machine learning model object that this resource references.
Specifies the resource data container for a SageMaker machine learning model resource, defining the S3 URI of the model artifact and the local destination path on the Greengrass core.
Specifies the absolute local path on the Greengrass core where the SageMaker machine learning model artifact is downloaded or mounted for use by the Lambda function.
Specifies the owner setting for the SageMaker machine learning model resource, including the Linux group owner and its permissions on the model artifact used by the Greengrass core.
Defines the operating system group owner for the SageMaker machine learning model resource when it is deployed to the Greengrass core.
The permission level, either 'rw' (read/write) or 'ro' (read-only), that the group owner is granted on the SageMaker machine learning model resource.
ARN of the SageMaker training job whose model artifact is used to create the local machine learning model resource in Greengrass.
Defines the configuration for referencing a secret from AWS Secrets Manager in the Greengrass resource, specifying the secret ARN and any additional properties needed for access.
Specifies additional AWS Secrets Manager staging labels (beyond the default AWSCURRENT) whose secret versions are downloaded to the Greengrass core for this secret resource.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that this Greengrass resource references, used to retrieve the secret's value on the Greengrass core.

aws_greengrass_subscription_definition.a.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely assigned to this Greengrass subscription definition, which is used to reference the definition in IAM policies and other AWS services.

aws_greengrass_subscription_definition.i.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS IoT Greengrass to this subscription definition.

The initial subscription definition version, which contains a list of subscription objects (each specifying a source, target, and subject) that define how MQTT messages are routed between devices, functions, and connectors in the Greengrass group.
Defines the list of subscriptions to include in the initial version of the Greengrass subscription definition, where each subscription specifies a source, target, and topic.
A user-defined alphanumeric identifier for the subscription, used to uniquely reference it within the Greengrass subscription definition version.
The ARN of the device, Lambda function, or connector that publishes messages to the MQTT topic in this Greengrass subscription.
Specifies the MQTT topic filter (subject) for a Greengrass subscription, which defines the topic, normally with wildcards, that messages are routed on from the source to the target.
The ARN of the target destination (a Greengrass core, device, or Lambda function) that receives messages published to the subscription's subject topic.

aws_greengrass_subscription_definition.l.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the latest version of the AWS Greengrass subscription definition, which is computed and returned after the resource is created.

aws_greengrass_subscription_definition.n.text: The required name for this AWS IoT Greengrass subscription definition, serving as a human-readable identifier used in the console and API.

aws_greengrass_subscription_definition.t.text: A map of key-value pairs that tag the Greengrass subscription definition, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_greengrass_subscription_definition_v.text: The ID of the Greengrass subscription definition that this subscription definition version belongs to.

The subscriptions field defines the list of MQTT message routing rules for this subscription definition version, each specifying a source, target, and topic filter that controls how messages are passed between Greengrass devices, functions, and connectors.

The subscriptions.id is a required, user-defined unique identifier for each subscription within the AWS Greengrass subscription definition version, used to distinguish and reference individual subscription entries.
Specifies the ARN of the source device or Lambda function that publishes messages to the target on the given topic.
The MQTT topic filter that determines which messages are routed from the source to the target in this subscription.

Specifies the target of the subscription as an ARN (for example, a Greengrass device, Lambda function, or connector ARN) that receives messages published to the subscription's subject from the source.

aws_greengrass_v2_component_version.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS IoT Greengrass V2 component version, used to reference it in other AWS operations.

aws_greengrass_v2_component_version.comp.text: The name of the Greengrass component (e.g., 'com.example.HelloWorld') as specified in the component recipe, returned as a read-only attribute of the created component version.
The version string (e.g., 1.0.0) that AWS IoT Greengrass assigns to the created component version.

aws_greengrass_v2_component_version.inli.text: The inline recipe for the component, specified as a string in YAML or JSON format, which defines the component's metadata, artifacts, lifecycle, and configuration.

aws_greengrass_v2_component_version.lamb.text: Provides the Lambda function configuration that Greengrass uses to create the component version, including the Lambda function ARN and optional component name, version, input parameters, and publish/subscribe settings.
Maps each dependent component name to its version requirement and dependency type (HARD or SOFT), defining the component dependencies declared for this Lambda function's Greengrass component recipe.
Specifies the runtime parameters for the Lambda function component, including environment variables, execution arguments, timeout, and pinning behavior.
A map of environment variable names to values that are passed to the Lambda function when it runs as part of the Greengrass component.
Specifies the list of event sources (each with a topic and type such as IOT_CORE or PUB_SUB) that the Lambda function component subscribes to for triggering invocations.
The MQTT topic on AWS IoT Core that the Lambda function subscribes to for this event source.
Specifies the type of event source for a Lambda function in a Greengrass V2 component, such as `PUB_SUB` for MQTT Pub/Sub messages or `IOT_CORE` for AWS IoT Core topic messages.
The list of command-line arguments to pass to the Lambda function when it executes as a Greengrass component.
Specifies whether the input payload to the Lambda function is decoded as JSON or binary, with allowed values 'BINARY' and 'JSON'.
Specifies the runtime parameters for the Lambda function process on Linux systems, including the isolation mode (GreengrassContainer or NoContainer) and optional container resource limits.
Provides container configuration for the Lambda function when it runs as a containerized Linux process in AWS IoT Greengrass v2, including memory limit, mount points, devices, and volumes.
Specifies the list of host devices to mount into the container for the Lambda function, where each device object includes the host device path and its permissions (e.g. ro, rw).

For each device mounted into the Lambda container, this boolean controls whether the device's group owner is added to the container's supplementary groups, enabling the container process to access the device.
The absolute filesystem path to a host device that is made available inside the Lambda container, as specified in the container devices list for a Greengrass V2 component version.
The permission value ('ro' or 'rw') for a device mount within the Greengrass v2 Lambda container parameters determines whether the mounted device is read-only or read-write inside the container.
The memory size in kilobytes allocated to the container when the Lambda function runs in a container on the Greengrass core device.
Specifies whether to mount the host's /sys filesystem as read-only inside the container for the Greengrass Lambda component.
Defines the volumes to mount into the container running the Lambda function, with each volume specifying a source path and a destination path.

Determines whether the host system's group owner for a container volume is added to the container's group, allowing the Lambda container process to read and write the volume with matching group permissions.
The absolute path in the container's filesystem where the host volume (specified by the corresponding source path) is mounted.

For each volume mounted in the Greengrass Lambda container, the permission property sets the mount access mode to either 'ro' (read-only) or 'rw' (read-write), determining whether the containerized function can modify files on the underlying host volume.
The source_path is the host filesystem path on the Greengrass core device that gets mounted as a volume inside the Lambda container.
Specifies whether the Lambda function runs in a Greengrass-managed container (GreengrassContainer) or directly on the host system (NoContainer).

The maximum time, in seconds, that the Lambda function can remain idle (without receiving an invocation) before AWS IoT Greengrass V2 stops the running process, after which it will be restarted on the next event if the component is not pinned.
The maximum number of concurrent instances of the Lambda function that AWS IoT Greengrass V2 will run on a core device for this component version.
The maximum number of messages that can be queued for the Lambda function before AWS IoT Greengrass drops incoming messages.
When true, the Lambda function is pinned to the Greengrass core and runs continuously until the core stops; when false, it starts on demand in response to events and stops after a timeout.
The timeout in seconds that AWS IoT Greengrass waits for the Lambda function component to report its lifecycle status before the deployment is marked as failed.
Specifies the maximum time in seconds that the deployed Lambda function is allowed to run before it is forcibly stopped.
The name of the Greengrass component that this Lambda function version is packaged into; when not provided, the component name defaults to the Lambda function's name.
Specifies the list of supported platform configurations for the Lambda function component, where each object defines a platform name and optional platform-specific attributes.
The attributes map contains key-value pairs that define the platform's properties (such as operating system and architecture) used to match a Greengrass core device to this component platform.
The name of the operating system platform (e.g., 'Linux' or 'Windows') that this Lambda function component targets, used to define the component's platform-specific recipe.
The version of the Greengrass component to create from the specified Lambda function, e.g., '1.0.0'.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function that this component version runs.

aws_greengrass_v2_component_version.tags.text: A map of key-value pairs that you assign to the component version to add metadata and manage it by category, cost center, or environment.

aws_greengrass_v2_deployment.components.text: Specifies the components to deploy and their deployment configuration, including component version, configuration updates, and system resource limits for each component within the AWS IoT Greengrass V2 deployment.

aws_greengrass_v2_deployment.deployment_.text: The unique identifier assigned to the deployment by AWS IoT Greengrass V2.
Specifies a friendly name for the deployment, which is used to identify the deployment in the AWS IoT Greengrass V2 console and API; if not provided, AWS IoT Greengrass generates a unique name.
Specifies the policies that govern component update behavior and failure handling during a Greengrass V2 deployment, including the component update policy and failure handling policy.

Specifies the policy for updating components that are already deployed on the device, including the action to take (NOTIFY_COMPONENTS or SKIP_NOTIFY_COMPONENTS) and the timeout in seconds for the component update.
Specifies whether the AWS IoT Greengrass V2 deployment sends a notification to components that they need to update (NOTIFY) or skips the notification entirely (SKIP_NOTIFY).
The timeout in seconds for the component update policy, which sets how long the deployment waits for components to update before stopping.
Defines the configuration validation policy, which specifies the timeout (in seconds) for validating component configurations before applying a Greengrass V2 deployment.
The maximum time in seconds that a Greengrass core device will wait for component configuration validation to complete before the deployment is considered failed.
Determines the deployment behavior when a component fails: ROLLBACK rolls back the deployment to the previous version, while DO_NOTHING leaves the deployment in a failed state.

aws_greengrass_v2_deployment.iot_job_con.text: Specifies the AWS IoT job configuration for the deployment, including rollout, abort, and timeout behaviors for the job that deploys the components to target devices.

Specifies the abort criteria for the AWS IoT job that executes the Greengrass V2 deployment, allowing the job to be canceled if a set number or percentage of devices fail or exceed a threshold based on failure type.

Specifies a list of abort criteria for the AWS IoT job that performs the deployment, each defining a failure type, minimum number of executed things, and threshold percentage that must be met before the job is aborted.
Determines whether AWS IoT Jobs cancels or continues the deployment job when the abort criteria's failure threshold is reached, with allowed values CANCEL or CONTINUE.
Specifies the type of AWS IoT job execution failure (e.g., FAILED, REJECTED, TIMED_OUT, or ALL) that triggers the abort condition for the deployment's IoT job.

The minimum number of IoT job executions that must have occurred before the abort criteria can trigger, ensuring that the abort condition is only evaluated after at least this many things have executed the job.

The percentage of devices in the job execution that must fail the associated failure type (e.g., FAILED or TIMED_OUT) to trigger the abort action, when the abort criteria list is used in an AWS IoT job for a Greengrass V2 deployment.
Specifies the rollout configuration for the AWS IoT job that deploys the Greengrass V2 deployment to devices, controlling the rate at which the job is initiated across the device fleet.

Configures the exponential rollout rate for the AWS IoT job that performs the deployment, specifying the base rate per minute, the increment factor, and the criteria (number of notified or succeeded things) that trigger the rate increase.
Specifies the base number of IoT things per minute that the deployment is initially rolled out to, before the exponential rate increment increases the rollout speed.
The multiplier applied to the base job execution rollout rate for each increment, controlling how the number of Greengrass v2 deployment IoT job executions started per minute grows exponentially.
Defines the threshold (number of notified or succeeded IoT things) that, when reached, triggers an increase in the exponential rollout rate of the AWS IoT job for this Greengrass deployment.
Specifies the number of notified things at which the IoT job rollout rate increases exponentially for the Greengrass V2 deployment.

Specifies the number of succeeded thing executions that must be reached before the exponential rollout rate increases the job execution rate for an AWS IoT Greengrass V2 deployment's IoT job configuration.
The maximum number of IoT job executions that can be started per minute for the deployment.
The timeout configuration for the AWS IoT deployment job, specifying the maximum number of minutes a device has to complete the job execution before it times out.
Sets the in-progress timeout in minutes for the AWS IoT job that performs the Greengrass deployment, after which a device-level deployment still in progress is marked as timed out.

aws_greengrass_v2_deployment.parent_targ.text: ARN of the AWS IoT thing or thing group that is the target of the parent deployment, used to create this deployment as a subdeployment under that parent.

aws_greengrass_v2_deployment.tags.text: A map of key-value pairs used to tag the AWS IoT Greengrass V2 deployment, enabling you to categorize, identify, and manage deployments by cost, environment, or other criteria.

aws_greengrass_v2_deployment.target_arn.text: The ARN of the target AWS IoT thing or thing group to which the deployment is applied.

aws_ground_station_config.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Ground Station config.

aws_ground_station_config.config_data.text: The required config data that defines this Ground Station config, containing one of the supported configuration types (such as antenna downlink, antenna uplink, antenna downlink demod decode, tracking, dataflow endpoint, or uplink echo) along with its specific parameters.

aws_ground_station_config.config_data.an.text: Defines the receive (downlink) configuration for the Ground Station antenna, specifying parameters such as frequency, bandwidth, and polarization to capture satellite data.
Defines the spectral characteristics of the downlink signal, including center frequency, bandwidth, and polarization, used by the Ground Station to receive data from a satellite.
The bandwidth of the downlink signal spectrum, specified as an object with a numeric value and a unit (GHz, MHz, or kHz), defining the width of the frequency range to receive.
The unit of measurement for the downlink bandwidth (e.g., MHz or GHz) in the spectrum configuration of the antenna downlink for the Ground Station config.

The numeric magnitude of the downlink spectrum bandwidth, which is interpreted along with the separate units field to determine the actual bandwidth in hertz (e.g., if units is 'MHz', the bandwidth in Hz equals this value times 1e6).
Specifies the center frequency of the downlink signal for the antenna's receive spectrum, used to tune the Ground Station receiver.
Specifies the unit of measurement for the center frequency, either 'GHz' or 'MHz'.
The center frequency value in hertz for the downlink spectrum, used within the antenna downlink config's spectrum config.
The polarization mode (RIGHT_HAND or LEFT_HAND) for the downlink spectrum in the antenna downlink config, specifying the electromagnetic wave orientation used for receiving the signal.

Defines the demodulation and decode configuration for an antenna downlink, including the demodulation settings and decode configuration (typically specified as JSON) used to process the received satellite signal.

Specifies how the downlink signal is decoded, providing a decode configuration consisting of an unvalidated JSON payload that defines the decoding parameters for the Ground Station antenna downlink demodulation and decode processing.
Provides the unvalidated JSON that defines the decode configuration for the antenna downlink, specifying how the received signal is demodulated and decoded.
Configures the demodulation scheme (e.g., BPSK or QPSK) and processing options used by the antenna downlink demodulation and decode chain.
Specifies the demodulation configuration as a raw JSON string, containing the parameters for demodulating the received signal in the Ground Station antenna downlink.
Configures the center frequency and bandwidth of the downlink spectrum to be processed for this demodulation and decoding step.
Defines the bandwidth of the downlink spectrum signal, specifying the numeric value and its units (e.g., MHz or kHz) used in the antenna downlink demodulate/decode configuration.
The unit of measure for the bandwidth value (such as MHz or GHz) in the spectrum configuration for the antenna downlink demodulation and decoding.

The value is the numeric magnitude of the frequency bandwidth (in the unit given by the sibling `units` field) for the downlink demodulation decode spectrum config, used to set the demodulator's bandwidth for the received signal.
Specifies the center frequency of the downlink signal spectrum for antenna demodulation and decoding, represented as a frequency object with a numeric value and a unit (e.g., Hz, MHz, GHz).
Specifies the unit of measurement for the center frequency value, such as GHz, MHz, or kHz.
The numeric value of the center frequency, expressed in the units set by the parent center_frequency object, used for the downlink demodulation and decoding of the antenna signal.
Specifies the polarization of the downlink signal, which can be 'RIGHT_HAND' or 'LEFT_HAND'.
Defines the uplink spectrum settings and target satellite ARN for an antenna uplink configuration in AWS Ground Station.
Specifies the frequency and polarization (e.g., RIGHT_HAND or LEFT_HAND) for the uplink radio signal transmitted from the ground station antenna.
Specifies the center frequency of the uplink signal, containing a numeric value and a unit (GHz or MHz), used for the antenna uplink spectrum configuration.
The unit of measurement for the uplink center frequency value, such as GHz or MHz.
The numeric value of the center frequency for the antenna uplink spectrum, interpreted in the units defined by the sibling `units` field (e.g., GHz or MHz).
Specifies the polarization of the uplink signal, which can be either RIGHT_HAND or LEFT_HAND.
Specifies the target effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) for the uplink transmission, defined as an object containing the numeric value and its units (e.g., dBW).
The unit of measurement for the target effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) of the uplink, typically dBW.
The target effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) in decibel-watts (dBW) for the ground station's uplink antenna beam.
Determines whether the antenna's uplink transmission is disabled; when set to true, the uplink transmitter is turned off so no signal is sent.

aws_ground_station_config.config_data.da.text: Provides the dataflow endpoint configuration for the Ground Station config, identifying the named endpoint (with its socket address and port) to use for data exchange.
The name of the dataflow endpoint that this Ground Station configuration references, identifying where data is sent or received for the dataflow endpoint config.
Specifies the AWS region in which the dataflow endpoint is located.

aws_ground_station_config.config_data.s3.text: Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket and prefix where the Ground Station service stores recorded antenna data when this config is used for S3 recording.
The ARN of the S3 bucket where AWS Ground Station stores the recorded data for the S3 recording config.
The S3 key prefix under which recorded data files are stored in the bucket, allowing you to organize output files.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Ground Station assumes to write antenna downlink data to the associated S3 bucket.

aws_ground_station_config.config_data.te.text: The telemetry_sink_data object specifies the dataflow endpoint ARN to which the Ground Station telemetry sink forwards satellite telemetry data.
Specifies the Kinesis Data Stream that serves as the telemetry sink destination, defining where Ground Station telemetry data is delivered for the telemetry sink configuration.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Kinesis data stream that receives telemetry data from the ground station config.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Ground Station assumes to write telemetry data to the specified Kinesis Data Stream.
Specifies the type of telemetry sink used to deliver ground station telemetry data, distinguishing between sink types such as S3 bucket storage and agent-based streaming.

aws_ground_station_config.config_data.tr.text: Defines the tracking behavior for the ground station antenna, including the autotrack setting that controls whether automatic satellite tracking is required, preferred, or removed.
Sets the autotrack mode for the ground station antenna, determining whether automatic satellite tracking is disabled (NO_CONTACT), preferred (PREFERRED), or required (REQUIRED) during a contact.

aws_ground_station_config.config_data.up.text: Configures the uplink echo feature for the ground station config, which echoes the uplink signal back for testing and includes the antenna uplink config ARN and an enabled flag.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the antenna uplink config whose transmitted signal is echoed back for the uplink echo function in this Ground Station config.
When true, enables the Ground Station antenna to receive and downlink echoes of the uplink signal for testing or observation purposes.

aws_ground_station_config.name.text: The user-defined name assigned to this AWS Ground Station config, used to identify it within the service.

aws_ground_station_config.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Ground Station Config resource, used to label and categorize the configuration with custom metadata such as environment or purpose.

aws_ground_station_config.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the AWS Ground Station Config resource, used to categorize or identify the configuration.

aws_ground_station_config.type.text: The type of the Ground Station config, such as 'antenna-downlink' or 'tracking', which is automatically derived from the configuration data provided in the resource.

aws_ground_station_dataflow_endpoint_gro.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the Ground Station dataflow endpoint group, assigned by AWS when the group is created.
Specifies the list of endpoint details, each containing a name, security group, and subnet, that define the endpoints for this Ground Station Dataflow Endpoint Group.
Specifies the agent-based endpoint configuration for an AWS Ground Station dataflow endpoint group, including the endpoint name, ingress and egress addresses, and agent status.
The current status of the Ground Station agent associated with this endpoint, indicating whether the agent has successfully connected and validated (e.g., SUCCESS or FAILED).
The result of AWS Ground Station's validation audit of the agent endpoint, returned as a computed string value such as AUDIT_SUCCESSFUL.
Defines the socket address (name and port) that the AWS Ground Station agent uses for egress (outbound) data flow in the dataflow endpoint group.
The maximum transmission unit (MTU) size in bytes for the egress network connection of the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint.
Defines the IP address (or hostname) and port for the egress socket of the agent endpoint, which AWS Ground Station uses to send data from this dataflow endpoint group.
The hostname or IP address of the egress socket that the Ground Station agent endpoint uses to send data.
The TCP/UDP port number on the egress socket address that the AWS Ground Station agent uses to send outbound data to the dataflow endpoint group.
The ingress address specifies the IP address and port on which the Ground Station agent listens for incoming data from AWS Ground Station.
Specifies the maximum transmission unit (MTU) in bytes for the ingress address of the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint, defining the largest packet size allowed on the incoming network connection.
The socket address (hostname and port) for the ingress endpoint of an AWS Ground Station agent, defining where the agent listens for incoming data.
The hostname or IP address of the ingress socket for the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint, as part of its socket address configuration.
Configures the inclusive minimum and maximum port numbers in the range that the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint will accept incoming dataflow traffic on at this ingress address.
The maximum port number in the inclusive range of ports that the Ground Station agent endpoint will listen on for incoming data.
The minimum port number in the range of ports on which the Ground Station agent accepts incoming data at the ingress address.
Specifies the name of the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint, which should match the agent name configured on the AWS Ground Station Agent to connect to that agent.
The endpoint property defines the dataflow endpoint's name, socket address (host and port), and MTU for communication within the Ground Station dataflow endpoint group.
Provides the socket address (IP address and port) for this dataflow endpoint, defining the network location where Ground Station sends and receives data.
The IP address or DNS hostname of the dataflow endpoint's socket address, used with the port to connect to the endpoint.
The TCP or UDP port number used by the Ground Station dataflow endpoint to send and receive data over the socket address specified in the parent 'address' object.
The maximum transmission unit (MTU) size in bytes for the dataflow endpoint, controlling the maximum packet size sent over the connection.
The name of the dataflow endpoint, providing a human-readable identifier for the endpoint within the AWS Ground Station dataflow endpoint group.
The security_details object specifies the IAM role, security group IDs, and subnet IDs used to grant AWS Ground Station access to the dataflow endpoint in your VPC.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Ground Station assumes to access the security groups associated with this endpoint.
The list of VPC security group IDs that AWS Ground Station attaches to the elastic network interface of the dataflow endpoint, controlling which inbound and outbound traffic the endpoint accepts.
The subnet IDs in the VPC where the Ground Station dataflow endpoint is deployed.
The unique identifier (UUID) assigned by AWS to the dataflow endpoint group.
Defines a list of key-value tag objects to apply to the Ground Station dataflow endpoint group for identifying and organizing AWS resources.
The value of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS Ground Station dataflow endpoint group, used to store arbitrary metadata such as cost centers or project identifiers.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Ground Station dataflow endpoint group, assigned by AWS and used to reference the group in other Ground Station operations.

The endpoint_details field is the computed list of endpoint configurations (each specifying the socket address, port, and security settings) for the dataflow endpoints in the AWS Ground Station dataflow endpoint group.

Configuration for the AWS Ground Station Agent endpoint used for downlink dataflows, specifying the agent's ingress/egress socket addresses (IP and port) and agent status to receive data from a satellite.
Indicates whether the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint passed validation, with 'SUCCESS' meaning it is ready for use and 'FAILED' meaning configuration or connectivity checks did not pass.
Specifies the audit results for the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint, indicating the outcome of agent health and configuration audits.

This object defines the dataflow-specific configuration for the downlink AWS Ground Station agent endpoint, such as the dataflow ID and optional MTP (Message Transfer Protocol) settings used to map the endpoint to a particular dataflow in the mission profile.
Specifies the socket address (IP address and port) for the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint, which is used to establish the downlink dataflow connection.
Specifies the IP address and port (socket address) used by the AWS Ground Station agent for its downlink data flow, as part of the agent connection details in the endpoint group.
Specifies the maximum transmission unit (MTU) size, in bytes, for the network connection between the agent and the AWS Ground Station dataflow endpoint.
The IP address and port of the Ground Station agent's socket, specifying where downlink dataflow packets are sent.
The DNS name or IP address of the agent endpoint's socket, used as part of the address for the downlink dataflow connection.
Specifies the lower and upper bounds (min/max) of the network port range that the AWS Ground Station agent uses for the downlink dataflow connection.
The maximum port value in the inclusive range that the AWS Ground Station agent will listen on for downlink dataflow connections to the endpoint.
The lowest port number in the inclusive range of ports used for the agent endpoint's socket address when communicating over the downlink dataflow.
Specifies the egress IP address and port used by the AWS Ground Station agent to send downlink data to your VPC resources.
The maximum transmission unit (MTU) in bytes for the egress network connection, limiting the maximum packet size sent from the agent to Ground Station.
Specifies the hostname (name) and port that compose the socket address for egress traffic from the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint in the dataflow endpoint group.
The hostname or IP address (the name component of the socket address) that the Ground Station agent uses as the destination for egress data in this downlink endpoint connection.
The destination port number for the egress socket connection from the AWS Ground Station agent, used for downlink data flow.
The user-defined name for the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint that receives downlink data in this dataflow endpoint group.
Defines the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint configuration for uplink data flows, including ingress/egress socket addresses, protocol, and agent status details.
The status of the AWS Ground Station agent for this uplink endpoint, indicating whether the agent is operational and ready to handle satellite data flows.
This field contains the audit findings for the Ground Station agent endpoint, describing any issues detected during agent validation.
Specifies the source and destination addresses (IP and port) for the dataflow through the uplink AWS Ground Station agent endpoint.
Specifies the IP address and port of the agent that AWS Ground Station uses to connect for transmitting uplink data through the dataflow endpoint group.
Defines the IP address and port of the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint used for the uplink dataflow connection, specifying the destination network address for the data flow.
Specifies the maximum transmission unit (MTU) size in bytes for the agent connection's IP and port address, determining the largest network packet size allowed for data flow.
Specifies the IP address and port of the AWS Ground Station agent's socket used for this uplink dataflow endpoint.
Specifies the hostname or IP address portion of the socket address used to connect to the Ground Station agent endpoint, with the port specified separately.
Defines the inclusive range of source ports (start and end) that the agent connection uses for uplink data flow over the specified socket address.
The maximum port number in the range of ports that the agent can use for the connection.
The lower bound of the port range that the agent socket address can use for the uplink connection.
Defines the IP address and port that the Ground Station agent listens on for incoming uplink data traffic, used as the ingress endpoint for the agent connection.
The Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) size in bytes for the ingress network path from the Ground Station agent to the dataflow endpoint.
Defines the socket address (hostname or IP address and port) for the ingress connection of the uplink AWS Ground Station agent endpoint, specifying where the agent receives incoming data.

A friendly name for the socket address that defines the ingress address and port for the AWS Ground Station agent's dataflow connection, used as a user-provided identifier within the uplink endpoint details.
The port number of the ingress socket address for the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint, specifying the TCP port on which the agent receives uplink data from the ground station.
The name of the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint for the uplink path, which uniquely identifies the agent endpoint within the dataflow endpoint group configuration.
Defines the list of endpoints (including their address, port, and security configuration) that make up the AWS Ground Station dataflow endpoint group.
This object defines the downlink endpoint for an AWS Ground Station agent, specifying the network address and socket settings (such as IP, port, and MTU) used to receive data from a satellite.
Specifies the dataflow destination and AWS Region for the downlink AWS Ground Station agent endpoint, determining where downlinked data is sent.
Specifies the IP address and port number for the agent endpoint, used to establish the network connection for downlink dataflow from the AWS Ground Station agent.
The maximum transmission unit (MTU) size in bytes for the network connection to the agent's IP address.
Defines the IP address and port of the socket used by the AWS Ground Station agent for downlink communication in this dataflow endpoint.
The name of the socket address, identifying this agent endpoint within the AWS Ground Station dataflow endpoint group.
This object defines the minimum and maximum port numbers that constitute the allowed port range for the agent's socket address, used for downlink dataflow in the Ground Station endpoint group.
The maximum port number in the range of ports that the Ground Station agent can use for the dataflow connection to the endpoint.
The inclusive lower bound of the port range that the Ground Station agent will use for the socket connection.
For a downlink AWS Ground Station agent endpoint, this object specifies the egress IP address and port that the agent uses for outbound data transmission.
The Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) size for the egress network socket used by the Ground Station agent endpoint.
Specifies the network socket address, including the hostname or IP address and port number, used for egress traffic from the Ground Station agent endpoint's dataflow details.
The hostname or IP address portion of the socket address used as the destination for egress traffic from the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint.
The TCP port component of the egress socket address used by the AWS Ground Station agent when sending downlink data to the customer's endpoint.
Specifies the name used to identify this downlink AWS Ground Station agent endpoint within the dataflow endpoint group.
Specifies the network connection parameters (such as the IP address and port) for the Ground Station agent used by this uplink dataflow endpoint.
Specifies the IP address and port of the Ground Station agent endpoint for uplink data, which is used to establish the connection for the dataflow endpoint group.
Specifies the maximum transmission unit (MTU) size in bytes for the network connection between the Ground Station agent and the dataflow endpoint.
Defines the socket address, consisting of an IP address and port number, used for the agent connection in the uplink Ground Station agent endpoint.

The user-defined name for the socket address used by the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint in the uplink dataflow, which together with the port identifies the network endpoint for the agent connection.
Specifies the inclusive start and end TCP ports on the agent's IP address that the Ground Station dataflow endpoint uses for uplink communication.

The upper bound of the port range used for the socket address of the agent's IP and port endpoint for uplink dataflow, defining the highest port number that Ground Station can use for communication with the agent.
The lower bound of the port range that the Ground Station agent will use for the socket connection to the dataflow endpoint.
This object defines the ingress IP address and port that the Ground Station service uses to send uplink data to the agent.
The maximum transmission unit (MTU), in bytes, for the ingress socket of the agent connection, specifying the largest network packet size the endpoint can handle.
Specifies the hostname or IP address and port number for the ingress socket connection used by the Ground Station agent's uplink dataflow.
The hostname or IP address that forms the ingress socket address for the AWS Ground Station agent endpoint's dataflow connection.
The TCP port number for the ingress socket address used by the agent connection in this uplink dataflow endpoint.
The name of the uplink AWS Ground Station agent endpoint, used to identify this endpoint within the dataflow endpoint group.
The unique identifier for the dataflow endpoint group, assigned by AWS Ground Station when the group is created.
Defines a list of key-value tag objects to attach to the Ground Station dataflow endpoint group, supporting cost allocation and resource management.
The key of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS Ground Station dataflow endpoint group, used to categorize and manage the resource.
The value of a tag key applied to the AWS Ground Station dataflow endpoint group, used for resource identification and cost allocation.

aws_ground_station_mission_profile.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Ground Station mission profile.

aws_ground_station_mission_profile.dataf.text: Specifies the list of dataflow edges that define how data moves between satellite and ground station endpoints, with each edge containing source and destination configuration references.
The destination is the ARN or ID of the Ground Station config that receives data from the source in this dataflow edge, defining the next step in the mission profile's dataflow path.
Specifies the source config for a dataflow edge in the mission profile, identifying where the data stream originates before flowing to the destination config.

aws_ground_station_mission_profile.id.text: The AWS-assigned unique identifier for this Ground Station mission profile, which is exposed as the 'Id' attribute and used to reference the mission profile in Ground Station APIs.

aws_ground_station_mission_profile.strea.text: The AWS KMS key (specified as an ARN or alias) used to encrypt data streams produced by this mission profile, enabling customer-controlled encryption of downlinked satellite data.
The alias ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the mission profile's data streams, as an alternative to specifying the KMS key ARN directly.
Specifies the alias name of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the data streams (uplink and downlink) associated with this Ground Station mission profile.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the satellite data streams processed by the mission profile.

aws_ground_station_mission_profile.tags.text: Assigns a list of tag objects (key-value pairs) to the AWS Ground Station mission profile, which can be used for cost allocation and resource management.

aws_ground_station_mission_profile.tags..text: Specifies the key (name) of a tag attached to the AWS Ground Station mission profile, used for resource identification and organization.
The value of a tag attached to the AWS Ground Station mission profile, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_ground_station_mission_profile.track.text: ARN of the tracking config resource that defines how the ground station antenna tracks the satellite during the mission profile.

aws_guard_duty_custom_detection_rule_ass.text: The key of a tag attached to the GuardDuty custom detection rule association, used as the name of the key-value metadata pair for organizing or identifying the resource.
The value component of a tag attached to the GuardDuty custom detection rule association, allowing you to associate arbitrary metadata such as ownership or environment with the association.

aws_guard_duty_detector.data_sources.text: Specifies which GuardDuty data sources (e.g., S3 logs, Kubernetes audit logs, Malware Protection) are enabled for the detector.

aws_guard_duty_detector.data_sources.kub.text: Configures Kubernetes audit logs as a GuardDuty data source for this detector.
Configures whether AWS GuardDuty uses Kubernetes audit logs as a data source, typically containing an 'Enable' boolean to turn this feature on or off.
Whether to enable Kubernetes audit logs as a data source for the GuardDuty detector.

aws_guard_duty_detector.data_sources.mal.text: Configuration for GuardDuty Malware Protection, which controls whether EC2 instances with active Amazon GuardDuty findings are scanned for malware.
This object configures Malware Protection for EC2 instances with active GuardDuty findings, with the nested `ebs_volumes` property controlling whether attached EBS volumes are scanned for malware.

When enabled, GuardDuty malware protection scans the EBS volumes attached to EC2 instances associated with GuardDuty findings, under the scan_ec2_instance_with_findings malware protection configuration.

aws_guard_duty_detector.data_sources.s3_.text: Configures whether GuardDuty monitors S3 data events by enabling the S3 logs data source for the detector.
Whether to enable S3 logs as a data source for the GuardDuty detector.

aws_guard_duty_detector.enable.text: Enables or disables the GuardDuty detector, determining whether GuardDuty is active and can generate findings for the account in the specified region.

aws_guard_duty_detector.features.text: Specifies which optional GuardDuty features (such as S3 Protection, EBS Protection, or EKS Audit Logs) are enabled for the detector, with each entry containing a feature name and an enabled/disabled status.

aws_guard_duty_detector.features.additio.text: Specifies the list of additional configuration settings for a GuardDuty feature, where each object defines a Name (e.g., EKS_ADDON_MANAGEMENT) and a Status (ENABLED or DISABLED) to enable or disable that supplementary setting.

The name of a specific additional configuration setting for a GuardDuty detector feature, such as 'EBS_SNAPSHOT' for the malware protection feature, identifying which optional sub-setting is being configured.
Indicates whether a specific additional configuration (sub-feature) of a GuardDuty detector feature is enabled or disabled, with values such as 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.

aws_guard_duty_detector.features.name.text: Specifies the name of an additional GuardDuty feature to enable or configure, such as S3_DATA_EVENTS or EKS_AUDIT_LOGS.

aws_guard_duty_detector.features.status.text: Specifies whether the corresponding GuardDuty feature (e.g., S3_DATA_EVENTS) is currently enabled or disabled, accepting values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.

aws_guard_duty_detector.finding_publishi.text: Specifies how often GuardDuty publishes new findings to CloudWatch Events and S3, with valid values of FIFTEEN_MINUTES, ONE_HOUR, or SIX_HOURS.

aws_guard_duty_detector.id.text: The unique identifier for the GuardDuty detector, generated by the service when the detector is created.

aws_guard_duty_detector.tags.text: Specifies a list of key-value tags to attach to the GuardDuty detector, which can be used for identifying and organizing the detector resource.

aws_guard_duty_detector.tags.value.text: The value of a single tag assigned to the GuardDuty detector, a user-defined string used for metadata, access control, and cost allocation.

aws_guard_duty_filter.action.text: Specifies the action taken by the GuardDuty filter when a finding matches the filter criteria, either 'NOOP' to leave the finding's state unchanged or 'ARCHIVE' to archive the finding.

aws_guard_duty_filter.description.text: A user-supplied description of the GuardDuty filter, used to explain the purpose or criteria of the filter.

aws_guard_duty_filter.detector_id.text: The unique identifier of the GuardDuty detector that this filter is associated with.

aws_guard_duty_filter.finding_criteria.text: Defines the criteria used to filter GuardDuty findings, consisting of conditions on fields such as severity, type, or resource.

aws_guard_duty_filter.finding_criteria.c.text: Specifies the conditions used to filter findings, where each key is a finding field name (e.g., severity, type) and the value defines the comparison operators (Eq, Lt, Gt, etc.) and values to match.

aws_guard_duty_filter.name.text: The name of the GuardDuty filter, which uniquely identifies the filter within the detector and is required when creating or updating the filter.

aws_guard_duty_filter.rank.text: Rank sets the filter's priority among other GuardDuty filters, where a lower value places it higher in the saved-filters list.

aws_guard_duty_filter.tags.text: Defines the list of key-value tags to attach to the GuardDuty filter for resource categorization and cost allocation.

aws_guard_duty_filter.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the GuardDuty filter, corresponding to the Key attribute of a Tag object in the AWS CloudFormation AWS::GuardDuty::Filter resource.

aws_guard_duty_filter.tags.value.text: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the GuardDuty filter resource, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the filter in AWS.

aws_guard_duty_ipset.activate.text: Indicates whether the GuardDuty IP set is activated (enabled) for use in threat detection, where true activates the set and false deactivates it.

aws_guard_duty_ipset.detector_id.text: The detector_id specifies the unique ID of the Amazon GuardDuty detector to which this IPSet is associated, identifying the GuardDuty account and region context for the IP set.

aws_guard_duty_ipset.expected_bucket_own.text: The AWS account ID of the owner of the S3 bucket where the GuardDuty IPSet file is stored, used to validate that the bucket is owned by the expected account.

aws_guard_duty_ipset.format.text: Specifies the format of the file that contains the IP set, such as TXT, STIX, OTX_CSV, ALIEN_VAULT, or PROOF_POINT.

aws_guard_duty_ipset.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by GuardDuty to this IPSet.

aws_guard_duty_ipset.location.text: The URI (typically an S3 object URL) of the file that contains the IP addresses used by this GuardDuty IPSet.

aws_guard_duty_ipset.name.text: The friendly name of the GuardDuty IP set, used to identify it in the GuardDuty console and API.

aws_guard_duty_ipset.tags.text: The tags to apply to the GuardDuty IPSet, which can be used for organizing, identifying, and controlling access to the resource via IAM policies.

aws_guard_duty_ipset.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to this GuardDuty IP set, used to organize and manage the resource within AWS.

aws_guard_duty_ipset.tags.value.text: Specifies the value for a tag key used to manage and categorize the GuardDuty IP set.

aws_guard_duty_malware_protection_plan.a.text: Defines the actions to take when malware is detected on the protected resource, including the IAM role for EC2 instance isolation and whether to tag S3 buckets with scan status.
Configures the automatic tagging of scanned S3 objects with the GuardDuty malware scan status, controlled by setting the nested status property to ENABLED or DISABLED.

aws_guard_duty_malware_protection_plan.p.text: Specifies the S3 bucket (and optional object prefixes) that the malware protection plan is set to protect.

aws_guard_duty_malware_protection_plan.s.text: A string code that identifies the reason for the current status of the GuardDuty malware protection plan, such as an error or warning condition.
The human-readable message that explains the reason for the current status of the GuardDuty malware protection plan, such as a description of why the plan is disabled or encountered an error.

aws_guard_duty_malware_protection_plan.t.text: The tag key for a tag associated with the AWS GuardDuty Malware Protection Plan, used to label and organize the plan for management and cost allocation.

aws_guard_duty_member.detector_id.text: The ID of the GuardDuty detector in the administrator account that the member account is associated with.

aws_guard_duty_member.disable_email_noti.text: Whether to disable the email notification sent to the member account when it is invited to GuardDuty.

aws_guard_duty_member.email.text: The email address of the AWS account that is being added as a GuardDuty member, used to identify the account when creating the association.
