aws_guard_duty_member.member_id.text: The AWS account ID of the member account being added to the GuardDuty administrator account.

aws_guard_duty_member.message.text: The custom message included in the invitation sent to the member account when inviting them to join Amazon GuardDuty.

aws_guard_duty_member.status.text: The status of the GuardDuty member account, which can be one of Created, Invited, Disabled, or Enabled, and is used to manage the member's association with the GuardDuty administrator account.

aws_guard_duty_publishing_destination.de.text: Configures the GuardDuty publishing destination by specifying the ARN of the Amazon S3 bucket to receive findings and the ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt those findings.

aws_guard_duty_publishing_destination.ta.text: A list of key-value tags to attach to the GuardDuty publishing destination for organizing and identifying the resource.
The key of a tag assigned to the GuardDuty publishing destination, used to organize and identify the resource.
The value portion of a user-defined tag that is associated with the GuardDuty publishing destination, used for resource organization, cost tracking, and management.

aws_guard_duty_threat_entity_set.activat.text: Specifies whether to activate the threat intel set after it is created, so that GuardDuty begins using it to generate findings.

aws_guard_duty_threat_entity_set.created.text: The date and time when the GuardDuty threat entity set was created, provided as a computed read-only attribute.

aws_guard_duty_threat_entity_set.detecto.text: The ID of the GuardDuty detector to which this threat entity set belongs, used to associate the set with a specific detector.

aws_guard_duty_threat_entity_set.error_d.text: If the threat intelligence set is in an error state, this attribute provides the detailed error message describing why the set could not be created, activated, or updated.

aws_guard_duty_threat_entity_set.expecte.text: The AWS account ID of the owner of the S3 bucket that stores the threat entity set file, used by GuardDuty to verify bucket ownership and prevent accessing objects from an unintended bucket.

aws_guard_duty_threat_entity_set.format.text: Specifies the format of the uploaded threat intelligence set file, which for AWS GuardDuty must be one of TXT, STIX, OTX_CSV, or ALIEN_VAULT.

aws_guard_duty_threat_entity_set.locatio.text: The S3 URI (for example, s3://bucket/prefix/object) of the file that contains the threat intelligence set, which GuardDuty retrieves and imports as the indicators for this set.

aws_guard_duty_threat_entity_set.name.text: A user-friendly name for the GuardDuty threat intel set, used to identify it in the GuardDuty console; if omitted, GuardDuty automatically generates a name.

aws_guard_duty_threat_entity_set.status.text: The current activation or processing status of the threat intel set (for example, ACTIVE, INACTIVE, or ERROR) as determined by GuardDuty.

aws_guard_duty_threat_entity_set.tags.text: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the GuardDuty threat intel set, which can be used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_guard_duty_threat_entity_set.updated.text: The timestamp of the most recent update to the GuardDuty threat intelligence set, returned by AWS after the set is created or modified.

aws_guard_duty_threat_intel_set.activate.text: Whether the threat intel set is activated (enabled) for use by GuardDuty, as opposed to being created but inactive.

aws_guard_duty_threat_intel_set.detector.text: The ID of the GuardDuty detector to which this threat intel set belongs, or the default detector if not specified.

aws_guard_duty_threat_intel_set.expected.text: Specifies the AWS account ID expected to own the S3 bucket that holds the threat intel set file, allowing GuardDuty to verify the bucket owner before accessing it.

aws_guard_duty_threat_intel_set.format.text: The format of the threat intelligence set file (e.g., TXT, STIX, OTX_CSV, or ALIEN_VAULT) that GuardDuty uses to parse the uploaded list.

aws_guard_duty_threat_intel_set.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the GuardDuty threat intel set, which is the ThreatIntelSetId.

aws_guard_duty_threat_intel_set.location.text: The URI (typically an S3 object URL) of the file that contains the threat intelligence set content.

aws_guard_duty_threat_intel_set.name.text: A friendly name for the threat intel set, used for identification and display in GuardDuty.

aws_guard_duty_threat_intel_set.tags.text: Specifies the key-value tags to attach to the GuardDuty threat intel set for managing and identifying the resource.

aws_guard_duty_threat_intel_set.tags.key.text: The user-defined key of a tag applied to the GuardDuty threat intel set, used to categorize, identify, and manage the resource through AWS tagging conventions.

aws_guard_duty_threat_intel_set.tags.val.text: The value portion of a tag assigned to the GuardDuty threat intel set, used for resource-level permissions, cost allocation, and organization.

aws_guard_duty_trusted_entity_set.expect.text: The AWS account ID of the S3 bucket owner that GuardDuty expects when accessing the bucket for this trusted entity set, used to verify bucket ownership and prevent cross-account misconfiguration.

aws_guard_duty_trusted_entity_set.locati.text: The S3 URI of the file containing the trusted entities (such as IP addresses or domain names) that GuardDuty uses for this set.

aws_health_imaging_datastore.datastore_i.text: The unique identifier assigned to the datastore by AWS HealthImaging when it is created.

aws_health_lake_data_transformation_prof.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS HealthLake data transformation profile, used to identify, organize, and manage the profile among AWS resources.
The value part of a key-value tag attached to the AWS HealthLake data transformation profile, used to assign arbitrary string metadata for resource identification, organization, and management.

aws_health_lake_fhirdatastore.tags.text: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the FHIR datastore, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the resource, such as for cost allocation or access control.

aws_health_lake_fhirdatastore.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the AWS HealthLake FHIR Data Store, used to organize and identify the datastore for cost allocation and resource management.

aws_health_lake_fhirdatastore.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to an AWS HealthLake FHIR DataStore, used to organize, categorize, and track the datastore for cost allocation and access control.

aws_iam_access_key.id.text: The AWS access key ID (e.g., AKIA...) that uniquely identifies the IAM access key.

aws_iam_access_key.secret_access_key.text: The secret access key that is paired with the access key ID and is returned only when the IAM access key is first created, after which it cannot be retrieved again.

aws_iam_access_key.serial.text: The serial number for the access key, which must be unique among all access keys belonging to the same IAM user; it allows CloudFormation to create and manage multiple access keys for that user.

aws_iam_access_key.status.text: Specifies the status of the IAM access key, either Active or Inactive, controlling whether the key can be used for programmatic calls.

aws_iam_access_key.user_name.text: The name of the IAM user to which this access key belongs.

aws_iam_group.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the IAM group, such as arn:aws:iam::123456789012:group/group-name.

aws_iam_group.policies.policy_document.text: A JSON-formatted IAM policy document that defines the permissions for an inline policy attached to the IAM group.

aws_iam_group.policies.policy_name.text: Specifies the name of an inline policy attached to the IAM group, used to identify the policy within the group's Policies list.

aws_iam_instance_profile.arn.text: The ARN of the IAM instance profile, which uniquely identifies the profile across AWS and is used when attaching the profile to an EC2 instance or referencing it in IAM policies.

aws_iam_managed_policy.attachment_count.text: The number of IAM users, groups, and roles to which this managed policy is currently attached, as reported by the AWS API.

aws_iam_managed_policy.create_date.text: The creation date and time of the IAM managed policy, in ISO 8601 format, as set by AWS when the policy is created.

aws_iam_managed_policy.default_version_i.text: The identifier of the default version of the managed policy, such as v1.

aws_iam_managed_policy.is_attachable.text: Indicates whether the managed policy can be attached to IAM users, groups, or roles.

aws_iam_managed_policy.permissions_bound.text: The number of IAM users or roles that use this managed policy as a permissions boundary.

aws_iam_managed_policy.policy_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the managed IAM policy.

aws_iam_managed_policy.policy_id.text: The unique, service-assigned identifier (e.g., ANPA...) for the IAM managed policy, which differs from the policy ARN and is automatically generated when the policy is created.

aws_iam_managed_policy.update_date.text: The date and time when the policy was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

aws_iam_oidcprovider.client_id_list.text: The list of client IDs (also known as audiences) that are allowed to use the OIDC provider to authenticate to AWS.

aws_iam_oidcprovider.tags.text: Defines one or more custom tag key-value pairs to attach to the IAM OIDC provider, which can be used for cost allocation, access control, and metadata management.

aws_iam_oidcprovider.tags.key.text: Specifies the key (name) of a tag assigned to the AWS IAM OIDC provider, allowing you to filter, control access, and track costs for the resource.

aws_iam_oidcprovider.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the IAM OIDC provider, used to manage, identify, and categorize the resource.

aws_iam_oidcprovider.thumbprint_list.text: The list of server certificate thumbprints used to identify the OIDC identity provider's server certificate.

aws_iam_oidcprovider.url.text: Specifies the URL of the OIDC identity provider (IdP), which must be a valid HTTPS URL that matches the issuer in the OIDC tokens issued by the provider.

aws_iam_policy.arn.text: The policy's real ARN, computed, known only after ship.

aws_iam_policy.name.text: The policy's own name. Conflicts with `name_prefix`.

aws_iam_policy.name_prefix.text: A prefix, with a generated suffix appended. Conflicts with `name`.

aws_iam_policy.policy_id.text: AWS's own stable unique identifier for the policy.

aws_iam_role.arn.text: The role's real ARN, computed, known only after ship.

aws_iam_role.assume_role_policy.text: The trust policy naming who may assume this role.

aws_iam_role.create_date.text: When the role was actually created, in ISO 8601.

aws_iam_role.force_detach_policies.text: Detach every attached policy before destroying the role.

aws_iam_role.max_session_duration.text: Longest a session assuming this role may last, in seconds. `3600` to `43200`.

aws_iam_role.name.text: The role's own name. Conflicts with `name_prefix`.

aws_iam_role.name_prefix.text: A prefix, with a generated suffix appended. Conflicts with `name`.

aws_iam_role.permissions_boundary.text: ARN of a policy used as this role's permissions boundary.

aws_iam_role.policies.policy_document.text: The JSON or YAML policy document that defines the permissions for an inline IAM role policy, specifying allowed or denied actions and resources.

aws_iam_role.policies.policy_name.text: Specifies the name of an inline IAM policy attached to the role as part of the policies list.

aws_iam_role.role_id.text: The stable, unique identifier (RoleId) that AWS assigns to the IAM role, such as AROA...

aws_iam_role.tags.key.text: The key portion of a tag attached to the IAM role, used to organize and identify the role within AWS.

aws_iam_role.tags.value.text: Specifies a user-generated value for an arbitrary tag attached to the IAM role, which can be used for role identification and attribute-based access control (ABAC).

aws_iam_role.unique_id.text: AWS's own stable unique identifier for the role.

aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.id.text: A computed identifier combining the role name and policy ARN.

aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.policy_ar.text: The ARN of the policy to attach.

aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.role.text: The name of the role to attach the policy to.

aws_iam_samlprovider.name.text: The name of the SAML provider, which serves as the unique identifier in IAM and is appended to the provider ARN; if omitted, CloudFormation derives it from the resource's logical ID.

aws_iam_samlprovider.saml_metadata_docum.text: The SAML 2.0 metadata document (XML) that contains the identity provider's entity ID, signing certificate, and other configuration needed for IAM to trust the external SAML identity provider.

aws_iam_samlprovider.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs that can be attached to the SAML provider to help identify, categorize, and manage the provider, and can be used in IAM policies for attribute-based access control.

aws_iam_samlprovider.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the IAM SAML provider, which can be used in IAM policies via the aws:ResourceTag condition key to enforce tag-based access control on the provider.

aws_iam_samlprovider.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag attached to the AWS IAM SAML provider, allowing you to label or categorize the provider for organizational and management purposes.

aws_iam_server_certificate.certificate_b.text: The PEM-encoded certificate body (the public key certificate) for the IAM server certificate, used to enable TLS/SSL connections for AWS services.

aws_iam_server_certificate.certificate_c.text: Specifies the PEM-encoded certificate chain of intermediate certificates that must be included when the server certificate is presented to clients, establishing trust back to a root CA.

aws_iam_server_certificate.path.text: Specifies the IAM path under which the server certificate is stored, used to organize and identify the certificate within the AWS account.

aws_iam_server_certificate.private_key.text: The PEM-encoded private key that pairs with the uploaded server certificate, allowing AWS services such as Elastic Load Balancing to terminate SSL/TLS traffic.

aws_iam_server_certificate.server_certif.text: Specifies the name of the server certificate, which must be unique within the AWS account; if omitted, AWS CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_iam_server_certificate.tags.text: Specifies a list of tag key-value pairs to attach to the IAM server certificate for identification, organization, and cost allocation.

aws_iam_server_certificate.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the IAM server certificate, used to identify and categorize the certificate.

aws_iam_server_certificate.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key attached to the IAM server certificate, used to store custom metadata that helps identify, organize, or manage the certificate within AWS.

aws_iam_user.arn.text: The ARN is a unique identifier for the IAM user in the format arn:aws:iam::account-id:user/username, used for referencing the user in IAM policies.

aws_iam_user.policies.policy_document.text: The JSON-encoded IAM policy document that defines the permissions for this inline policy attached to the IAM user.

aws_iam_user.policies.policy_name.text: The name of an inline policy attached to the IAM user, uniquely identifying the policy within the user's set of inline policies.

aws_iam_user.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to an IAM user, which can be used in IAM policies to enforce tag-based access control.

aws_iam_user.tags.value.text: The value of a key-value tag attached to the IAM user, used for metadata management such as cost allocation or attribute-based access control.

aws_iam_user_to_group_addition.group_nam.text: The name of the IAM group that the user is added to.

aws_iam_user_to_group_addition.users.text: Specifies the list of existing IAM user names to add to the group specified in the GroupName property.

aws_iam_virtual_mfadevice.path.text: The IAM path under which the virtual MFA device is stored, which controls the device's location in the IAM hierarchy and must follow IAM path syntax (e.g., '/division/') to organize and identify the device.

aws_iam_virtual_mfadevice.serial_number.text: The ARN (Amazon Resource Name) of the virtual MFA device, which serves as its unique serial number.

aws_iam_virtual_mfadevice.tags.text: Adds metadata tags to the virtual MFA device, which can be used to organize and identify the device in IAM.

aws_iam_virtual_mfadevice.tags.key.text: The tag key for a virtual MFA device in IAM, which identifies a tag applied to the device for organizational or access-control purposes.

aws_iam_virtual_mfadevice.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the IAM virtual MFA device, used as an arbitrary metadata label for organizing, identifying, or managing the device.

aws_iam_virtual_mfadevice.users.text: Specifies the list of IAM users that are associated with this virtual MFA device.

aws_iam_virtual_mfadevice.virtual_mfa_de.text: Assigns a name to the virtual MFA device, which is used to identify the device within AWS IAM.

aws_image_builder_container_recipe.compo.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Image Builder component to apply as part of this container recipe's build configuration.

Defines the list of parameter name/value pairs to supply to an Image Builder component (referenced by the containing components list entry) when the container recipe is used to build a container image, overriding default values defined in the component document.
The name (key) of a parameter that is passed to the Image Builder component when building the container image, matching a parameter defined in that component.
Specifies a list of values to assign to the named build component parameter when this container recipe is used to build an image.

aws_image_builder_container_recipe.insta.text: The device name (e.g., /dev/sda1) for a block device attached to the EC2 instance used by Image Builder to build the container image.
Specifies the Amazon EBS volume settings for a block device mapping in the instance configuration, including volume size, volume type, IOPS, encrypted flag, and snapshot identifier.
Whether the EBS volume should be deleted when the associated EC2 instance is terminated, as part of the block device mapping for the build instance in the Image Builder container recipe.
Determines whether the EBS volume in this block device mapping is encrypted on the build instance used by the container recipe, matching the standard EC2 block device mapping encryption setting.
Specifies the IOPS (input/output operations per second) rate for the EBS volume, used only when the volume type is io1, io2, or gp3 in the block device mapping.
The KMS key ID used to encrypt the EBS volume defined in this block device mapping, enabling a customer-managed encryption key for the volume created during the image build.
Specifies the ID of an existing EBS snapshot to use as the source for the EBS volume defined in this block device mapping.

The throughput in MB/s to provision for the EBS gp3 volume defined in a block device mapping for the instance configuration of the Image Builder container recipe, used to set the performance characteristics of the attached volume during build and test.
For a block device in the container recipe's build instance configuration, the size in GiB of the EBS volume to attach.
Defines the Amazon EBS volume type for the block device mapped to the build instance, where valid values include gp2, gp3, io1, io2, sc1, st1, and standard.
Indicates whether to suppress this block device mapping so that no device is exposed to the instance, overriding any device mapping from the base image.

Specifies the virtual device name (e.g., ephemeral0) for an ephemeral instance store volume in the block device mapping of the instance used to build the container, matching EC2 ephemeral device naming conventions.

aws_image_builder_distribution_configura.text: Defines the configuration for distributing the built image as an Amazon Machine Image (AMI), including AMI tags, launch permissions (e.g., user groups or organization ARNs), and an optional AMI name prefix.
The tags to apply to the AMI when it is distributed to the target region.
The description of the AMI distribution configuration, providing a human-readable explanation of the distribution settings for the AMI.
The customer-managed AWS KMS key ID used to encrypt the AMI volumes created from this distribution configuration.
Specifies the AWS accounts and user groups that are granted launch permissions for the distributed AMI, effectively controlling who can launch the AMI created by this distribution configuration.
The list of ARNs of AWS Organizations organizational units (OUs) that this AMI distribution will be shared with via launch permissions.
Specifies the ARNs of the AWS Organizations organizational units (OUs) to which launch permissions for the distributed AMI are granted, so that all accounts within those OUs can launch the image.
Specifies the AWS user groups that will be granted launch permissions for the distributed AMI.
Lists the AWS account IDs that are granted permission to launch the AMI created by the distribution configuration.
The name assigned to the AMI produced by this distribution configuration.
Specifies the AWS account IDs to which the built AMI is shared after distribution.
Configures how a container image is distributed, specifying the target container repository and optional container tags for each distribution in an Image Builder distribution configuration.
The tags to apply to the container image (e.g., an ECR image) when it is distributed to the target AWS account and region.
A user-defined description for the container distribution configuration, used to provide additional context or identify the purpose of these distribution settings.

Specifies the destination container repository (e.g., an Amazon ECR repository) to which Image Builder delivers container images built by this distribution configuration, including the repository name and service type.
The name of the container repository (e.g., within Amazon ECR) where the built container image is distributed by this distribution configuration.
The service that the target repository belongs to, which must be 'ECR' (Amazon Elastic Container Registry) for container images distributed by Image Builder.
Configures fast launch settings for Windows AMIs in this distribution, including enabling fast launch, snapshot configuration, and target accounts.
Specifies the AWS account ID for which the distribution's fast launch configuration is enabled, allowing that account to use the AMI with faster launch times.
This boolean enables or disables fast launch for the distribution, which pre-provisions snapshots to speed up instance launches.
The launch template configuration that specifies the EC2 launch template (by ID or name) used when launching instances from the fast-launch enabled Windows AMI in this distribution.
The ID of the EC2 launch template that Image Builder uses to configure pre-provisioned snapshots for fast launch of the distributed AMI.
The name of the EC2 launch template that defines the configuration for fast launching Windows AMIs in this distribution configuration.
Specifies the version of the EC2 launch template to use for the fast launch configuration, allowing you to pin to a specific version or use the default/latest version.
Specifies the maximum number of parallel EC2 instances that can be launched for testing the AMI as part of the fast launch configuration.
Configures the pre-provisioned snapshots for a Windows fast launch setup, defining the target number of snapshots to retain for faster instance launching.
Specifies the target number of pre-provisioned snapshots to retain for fast launching Windows instances in this distribution configuration.

The launch template configurations specify the EC2 launch templates that Image Builder uses when distributing the AMI to specific AWS accounts, including the launch template ID and whether to set it as the default version.
The AWS account ID to which this launch template configuration applies, so that the specified launch template is used for image builds in that account.
The ID of the EC2 launch template used by Image Builder when distributing the image to a target region, as defined in the launch template configuration.
Indicates whether to set the specified EC2 launch template as the default launch template for the target AWS account when this launch template configuration is used by the Image Builder distribution.
Specifies the AWS License Manager license configuration ARNs to apply to the AMI when it is distributed to the target region, enabling licensing compliance and usage tracking for that distribution.
The AWS Region to which this distribution configuration applies, enabling per-region settings for the output AMIs.
Lists the Systems Manager (SSM) parameter name-value pairs used to configure the EC2 instances launched from the image within this distribution, each object defining a parameter name and its value.
The ID of the AWS account that owns the AMI to be distributed to the specified Systems Manager parameter.
Data type (String or StringList) of the SSM parameter that Image Builder creates in the target account when the AMI is distributed.
The name of the AWS Systems Manager parameter that Image Builder updates with the AMI ID when the distribution configuration is applied.

aws_image_builder_image.workflows.on_fai.text: Specifies the action to take when this Image Builder workflow fails, with allowed values such as 'Continue' or 'Abort' controlling whether the image build proceeds or stops.

aws_image_builder_image.workflows.parall.text: Specifies the name of a parallel group in which to run this workflow, allowing workflows in the same group to execute concurrently during the image build process.

aws_image_builder_image.workflows.parame.text: Specifies a list of key-value pairs that Image Builder passes as input parameters to the corresponding workflow when it runs during the image build.
The name of the workflow parameter, identifying which input parameter of the Image Builder workflow this value corresponds to.
Provides a list of values for a workflow parameter, which is passed to an Image Builder workflow during image creation.

aws_image_builder_image.workflows.workfl.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Image Builder workflow to execute as part of the image creation process.

aws_image_builder_image_pipeline.workflo.text: Specifies the action to take when this workflow fails; valid values are CONTINUE or ABORT.
The parallel group name for this workflow; multiple workflows with the same parallel group are executed concurrently during the image build process.
Specifies the list of parameter name/value pairs to pass to a workflow attached to this image pipeline, controlling how that workflow runs during the image build and test process.

The name of an individual input parameter passed to an Image Builder workflow configured for this image pipeline, serving as the key that the workflow definition uses to reference the parameter value.
Defines the list of string values for a given workflow parameter key in the Image Builder image pipeline's workflow configuration.
The ARN of an Image Builder workflow to associate with the image pipeline, defining a custom build/test step sequence.

aws_image_builder_image_recipe.block_dev.text: The device name (e.g., /dev/xvda) that identifies the block device mapping to the instance in the Image Builder image recipe.

Specifies the Amazon EBS-specific block device mapping settings, including encryption, volume size, volume type, IOPS, throughput, snapshot ID, KMS key ID, and delete-on-termination behavior, for the corresponding block device in the image recipe.
Indicates whether the EBS volume should be deleted when the associated EC2 instance is terminated, as part of the block device mapping configuration for the image recipe.

Specifies whether the EBS volume created from this block device mapping should be encrypted; when set to true, AWS encrypts the volume at rest using the default EBS encryption key or the KMS key specified in the same EBS configuration.
The number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) to provision for the EBS volume, applied when the volume type is io1, io2, or gp3, to control the volume's performance level.
The identifier of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the EBS volume for this block device mapping in the image recipe.
The ID of the snapshot to use as the source for the EBS volume in the block device mapping.
The throughput in MiB/s to provision for the EBS volume, applicable when the volume type is gp3.
Specifies the size, in GiB, of the EBS volume used by the block device mapping in the EC2 Image Builder image recipe.
Specifies the EBS volume type (e.g., gp2, gp3, io1) for the block device in the image recipe's block device mapping.
When set, this field removes the corresponding device from the image's block device mapping, overriding a device that was present in the base image.
The virtual device name (e.g., 'ephemeral0') for an ephemeral (instance store) block device mapped to the image recipe, used when the mapping specifies a non-EBS virtual storage device.

aws_image_builder_image_recipe.component.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a component (a software configuration) that is included as a step in the image recipe's build process.
Specifies the list of parameter name-value pairs to pass to the component when the image recipe runs, overriding any default parameter values defined in the component document.
The name (key) of a parameter to pass to the component, which must match a parameter name defined in the component's recipe.
The value (or list of values) to assign to a named build component parameter, which is passed to that component when AWS Image Builder uses the recipe to build an image.

aws_image_builder_lifecycle_policy.polic.text: Defines the lifecycle action (such as deleting the resource or creating a snapshot) that Image Builder performs on the resources selected by the policy's rule.
Specifies the resource types (e.g., AMIs, container images, and snapshots) that the lifecycle policy action applies to.
Determines whether the lifecycle policy action applies to Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) in the resource set.
Specifies whether container images are included as a resource type for this lifecycle policy action.
Specifies whether snapshots are included as a resource type that the lifecycle policy action (such as deletion) applies to.
Specifies the lifecycle action to apply to matching images when the policy conditions are met, with allowed values of 'DELETE' to remove the image or 'DEPRECATE' to mark it as deprecated.

Defines exclusion criteria for the lifecycle policy, allowing resources to be omitted from policy actions based on attributes such as whether they are shared or public, the AWS Regions they reside in, or matching tags.
Defines AMI-specific exclusion rules that identify AMIs to exempt from lifecycle actions based on shared AWS accounts and tag conditions.
When set to true, the lifecycle policy excludes AMIs that are public (publicly shared) from the lifecycle action, preventing them from being expired or deregistered.

Defines an exclusion criterion based on how recently an AMI was last used to launch an EC2 instance, where a value and unit (e.g., DAYS) set a window such that AMIs launched within that recent period are excluded from the lifecycle policy's actions.
Specifies the time unit (DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, or YEARS) used with the numeric value to define the last-launched age threshold for excluding an AMI from the lifecycle policy.
The numeric threshold (e.g., number of days) since an AMI was last launched, used by the last_launched exclusion rule to determine which AMIs are excluded from the lifecycle policy action.

Specifies a list of AWS Regions in which an AMI must also be present to be excluded from the lifecycle policy's delete or deprecate actions; if the AMI exists in any of the listed regions, it will not be affected by the policy.
The list of AWS account IDs that an AMI must be shared with for the AMI to be excluded from the lifecycle policy's action (for example, deregistration).

Specifies a map of tag keys and values used to identify AMIs that should be excluded from the lifecycle policy's actions, meaning any image with exactly matching tags is not affected by the defined lifecycle rules.
Defines a map of tag keys and values used to identify matching Image Builder resources that should be excluded from the lifecycle policy's actions.
Defines the selection criteria (such as age, count, tag values, or retain-at-least threshold) that determine which resources the lifecycle policy actions apply to.
Sets the minimum number of resources (e.g., images) that must be retained, ensuring that at least this many resources are kept even when a count-based lifecycle filter would otherwise expire more.
Indicates the filter type used to select resources for the lifecycle policy action, such as `age`, `tag`, or `schedule`.
The unit of time (such as days or months) used with the filter's value to define the retention period for the lifecycle policy.
Specifies the numeric threshold (e.g., the number of days for an AGE filter, or the number of resources for a COUNT filter) at which the lifecycle policy triggers its configured action.

aws_image_builder_lifecycle_policy.resou.text: Specifies the name of an Image Builder recipe (image or container recipe) that the lifecycle policy's resource selection targets, so the policy applies to images built from that recipe.
The semantic version of the Image Builder recipe to match in the lifecycle policy's resource selection, identifying the specific recipe version (e.g., 1.0.0) that the policy applies to.

aws_inspector_assessment_target.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of this Inspector assessment target, used as a reference when creating Inspector assessment templates.

aws_inspector_assessment_target.assessme.text: The user-defined name for the Amazon Inspector assessment target, used to identify the collection of EC2 instances being assessed.

aws_inspector_assessment_target.resource.text: The ARN of an AWS Resource Groups group that defines the set of EC2 instances to include in this Inspector assessment target.

aws_inspector_assessment_template.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the assessment template.

aws_inspector_assessment_template.assess.text: The ARN of the AWS Inspector assessment target that this template will run assessments against.

A user-defined name for the assessment template, which must be unique within the AWS Region and is used to identify the template in the Inspector console and API; if omitted, AWS generates a default name.

aws_inspector_assessment_template.durati.text: Specifies the duration (in seconds) for which the Inspector assessment run will be executed.

aws_inspector_assessment_template.rules_.text: The list of Amazon Inspector rules package ARNs that define the security checks run against the assessment targets.

aws_inspector_assessment_template.user_a.text: Specifies user-defined key-value pairs (tags) that are assigned to every finding generated by the assessment template, enabling you to filter or categorize findings by these attributes.
The key of a user-defined key-value pair that is assigned to findings generated by this assessment template.
The value of a user-defined attribute (key-value pair) attached to findings generated by this assessment template, used to categorize or filter findings in Amazon Inspector.

aws_inspector_resource_group.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Inspector resource group.

aws_inspector_resource_group.resource_gr.text: Defines the tag key-value pairs that identify the EC2 instances to include in this Inspector resource group, used as the basis for an assessment target.
The key of a tag that, along with its value, defines an Amazon Inspector resource group, which is used to select EC2 instances for assessment.
The value of a tag that, combined with its key, defines an Amazon Inspector resource group used to scope which EC2 instances the Inspector service targets.

aws_inspector_v2_cis_scan_configuration..text: The CIS benchmark security level (e.g., LEVEL_1 or LEVEL_2) that this scan configuration is applied against.
The tags to assign to the CIS scan configuration resource, used for organizing and identifying it in AWS.
Specifies the AWS accounts and resource tags that the CIS scan targets, determining which resources are included in the scan.

aws_inspector_v2_code_security_integrati.text: Specifies the event type and API call used to create the Inspector v2 code security integration, defining when and how the integration is established for a repository.
Provides the configuration details for integrating AWS Inspector code security with a self-managed GitLab instance, including the necessary connection and authentication information.
The personal access token for the self-managed GitLab instance that AWS Inspector uses to authenticate and access repositories for code security scanning.
The base URL of the self-managed GitLab instance that AWS Inspector connects to for code security integration.
The read-only integration status, automatically set to 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED' to indicate whether Amazon Inspector code security scanning is active for the account.
Specifies the type of code security integration to configure, such as GITHUB or GITLAB, indicating which source code repository service to connect to Inspector for vulnerability scanning.
The GitHub-specific configuration object within the update integration details, which defines repository-level scan and encryption settings for the AWS Inspector V2 code security integration.
The unique identifier of the GitHub App installation within the GitHub organization or account that AWS Inspector V2 uses to access and scan repositories.
This object holds the settings needed to update the integration with a self-managed GitLab repository, including the instance URL and authentication credentials.
The personal access token (auth code) required for AWS Inspector v2 to authenticate to the self-managed GitLab instance when updating the code security integration.

aws_inspector_v2_code_security_scan_conf.text: Configuration is an object that specifies how Inspector v2 performs code security scans, including the scan mode (continuous or on a schedule) and any associated scheduling details such as daily start time.

Configures continuous integration scan behavior for Inspector code security scans, including whether auto-scan is enabled and which scan type (full or diff) to apply when scanning code from CI systems.
Specifies the continuous integration events (such as push or pull_request) that trigger an Inspector v2 code security scan for the associated repository.
Defines the schedule for recurring code security scans, specifying the interval (e.g., daily or weekly) at which AWS Inspector automatically rescans the configured repository.
Specifies the recurrence interval (e.g., daily, weekly, or monthly) at which AWS Inspector periodically runs code security scans for the configured resources.
The cron expression that determines when periodic code security scans are triggered by AWS Inspector V2.

The list of rule set categories (valid values: `SECURITY` and `CODE_QUALITY`) that the code security scan configuration uses to select which security and code-quality rule groups are applied during scans.
Determines the set of programming languages and their associated severity scan modes (e.g., HIGH or CRITICAL) that limit which code security findings are generated by the scan configuration.

For the AWS Inspector v2 code security scan configuration, this field specifies the project selection scope, which determines whether the scan applies to all available projects or only to a chosen subset of projects.
Assigns customizable tags to the CodeSecurityScanConfiguration resource to help identify, organize, and manage it within AWS Inspector V2.

aws_inspector_v2_connector.health.text: Specifies the current health status of the connector (such as HEALTHY or UNHEALTHY) along with the timestamp of the last health status change, as returned by Amazon Inspector V2.

aws_inspector_v2_connector.health.connec.text: The `connector_status` field under `health` reports the current health state of the AWS Inspector v2 connector, indicating whether it is operational and able to receive vulnerability findings.

aws_inspector_v2_connector.health.last_c.text: For the AWS Inspector V2 connector, this field records the timestamp of when the connector's health status was last checked by the service.

aws_inspector_v2_connector.health.messag.text: The message providing additional details about the health status of the Inspector v2 connector, such as why it is unhealthy or in an error state.

aws_inspector_v2_connector.provider_conf.text: Configuration for the Azure connector, containing the client ID, client secret, and tenant ID used by AWS Inspector to authenticate with and scan Azure resources.

Specifies the scope type for container image scanning in the Azure connector, with valid values 'ALL' indicating all images in the subscribed Azure container registries are scanned, and 'SPECIFIC' indicating only images matching the specified scope objects are scanned.
Determines whether container image scanning is enabled or disabled for the Azure scope configuration in the Amazon Inspector v2 connector.

In the AWS Inspector V2 connector's Azure provider configuration, this required field determines the scope of serverless scanning for Azure Functions, where `ALL` scans all functions in the configured Azure scope and `NONE` disables serverless scanning.
Specifies whether serverless scanning is enabled for the Azure connector, with valid values being `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`.

Determines the scope of Azure VM scanning: a value of ALL applies scanning to all virtual machines in the connected Azure subscription, while a value of SUBSET restricts scanning to a specific subset defined in the scope configuration.
Sets whether scanning is enabled or disabled for Azure virtual machines in this provider configuration's scope.

aws_inspector_v2_connector.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag (key-value pair) that you can assign to the AWS Inspector v2 connector for organizational or billing purposes.

aws_inspector_v2_filter.filter_action.text: The action taken on findings that match the filter criteria, either 'NONE' to do nothing or 'SUPPRESS' to suppress the findings.

aws_inspector_v2_filter.filter_criteria.text: The filter criteria object, which specifies the conditions (e.g., on finding fields like severity, resource tags, or EC2 instance properties) that determine which Inspector findings match the filter.

aws_inspector_v2_filter.filter_criteria..text: This filter criterion matches findings based on the AWS account ID that owns the resource, using a list of string filter objects that compare the account ID against specified values (e.g., EQUALS).
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to evaluate the AWS account ID against the filter's value.
The 12-digit AWS account ID that the filter criterion compares against, using the specified comparison operator, to include or exclude findings originating from that account.
Filter criterion that matches findings based on the name of the security detector (for example, Amazon CodeGuru Security) that identified the code vulnerability.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the code vulnerability detector name against the filter value.
The detector name string that this Inspector V2 filter condition compares against the code vulnerability detector name when evaluating findings.

This filter criterion matches Inspector V2 findings based on the detector tags of a code vulnerability (such as CWE tags), using the specified string comparison operators (for example, EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) and values.
Specifies the operator (such as EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, or PREFIX) that determines how the code vulnerability detector tag value is compared to the filter's expected value.
The tag value to match against the code vulnerability detector's tags when filtering Inspector V2 findings.

Filters Inspector v2 findings based on the file path where a code vulnerability was detected, allowing multiple string comparison conditions (e.g., equals, contains) to include or exclude matching findings.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to compare the code vulnerability file path against the value in this filter criterion.
The file path of the code vulnerability (e.g., a source file path) used as the value for the filter criterion, matched according to the associated comparison operator.

The filter_criteria.component_id field is a list of string filter conditions (comparison and value) that match Inspector v2 findings based on the identifier of the vulnerable software component (e.g., package name or library) associated with the finding.
The comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS) used to match the filter against the component ID value.
Specifies the component ID value to match when filtering findings, used to identify findings associated with a particular software component.

In an AWS Inspector v2 filter, this list of string filters selects findings based on the type of vulnerable component (such as an operating system package or an application dependency) using the configured comparator and value.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the component type of findings in the Inspector V2 filter criteria.
This value specifies the type of component to match when filtering Amazon Inspector findings, such as 'OS' (operating system) or 'PACKAGE' (software package).
Filters findings by the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) ID of the associated EC2 instance, using a list of comparison objects with operators and values.
The comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the EC2 instance image ID against the filter value.
Specifies the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) ID of an EC2 instance that findings must match when this ec2_instance_image_id filter criterion is applied.
Defines a list of string comparison filters on the EC2 instance's subnet ID, used to include or exclude Inspector V2 findings from the filter based on the subnet where the instance resides.
The comparison operator used to match the EC2 instance's subnet ID against the filter value, such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS.
The subnet ID (e.g., subnet-12345678) that an EC2 instance must be associated with to match the Inspector v2 filter criterion, compared against the instance's subnet ID.
Filters findings by the VPC ID of the EC2 instance, where each object in the list defines a comparison operator and a VPC ID value that must match for the finding to be included.
Specifies the comparison operator (EQUALS, PREFIX, NOT_EQUALS, or NOT_PREFIX) used to match findings against the EC2 instance VPC ID value in this Inspector v2 filter criterion.
Specifies the VPC ID that an EC2 instance must be associated with for the AWS Inspector v2 filter to match it.
Filters findings by the CPU architecture of the ECR container image (e.g., amd64 or arm64) using a comparison operator and value to include or exclude matches.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used when matching the ECR image architecture of a finding against the configured filter value.
Specifies the CPU architecture value (such as X86_64 or ARM64) of the ECR image to match when filtering findings.

Defines a list of filter conditions that match findings based on the SHA256 digest (hash) of the associated Amazon ECR container image, where each condition includes an image hash value and a comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) to evaluate against the finding's image hash.
Defines the comparison operator (such as EQUALS) used to match the ECR image hash against the specified value in the filter criteria.
Specifies the exact ECR image hash (SHA256 digest) value that an image must have for the filter to match.
Filters findings to include only ECR images whose push date falls within one of the specified date ranges, with each object in the list containing a start and end timestamp.
Sets the inclusive upper bound timestamp for an ECR image push date range, so only images pushed at or before this time match the filter.
The inclusive start timestamp (in Unix epoch seconds) for filtering findings by when the associated ECR image was pushed.
Filters Inspector2 findings based on the ECR image registry (typically the AWS account ID of the registry) using the specified comparison and value.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS) used to match the ECR image registry against the configured value for the filter criteria.
Sets the ECR image registry (such as an AWS account ID or registry hostname) that the filter criteria matches against when filtering Inspector v2 findings by ECR image source.

When creating or updating an AWS Inspector V2 filter, this field defines the ECR image repository name condition as a list of criterion objects (each with a comparison operator and value) to include or exclude findings based on the source ECR repository name.
Defines the operator used to compare the ECR image repository name field against the specified value, such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS.
Specifies the exact ECR image repository name value that the Inspector v2 filter compares against when evaluating findings based on the ecrImageRepositoryName criterion.
Filters findings by matching the provided comparison (e.g., EQUALS) and string against the Amazon ECR image tag associated with the container image.
The comparison operator used to evaluate the ECR image tag against the filter's value, such as EQUALS or PREFIX.
Specifies the ECR image tag value to match when filtering findings, combined with the comparator to include or exclude images with that tag.

Specifies a list of numeric ranges used to filter findings by their Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) score, matching findings whose EPSS value falls within at least one defined lower and upper boundary.
The lower inclusive bound of the EPSS score range used to match findings against the filter.
Defines the inclusive upper bound of the EPSS score range used to filter Inspector v2 findings, retaining only those with an EPSS score at or below this value.
Specifies the exploit availability condition for the filter, using a list of string filter objects with comparison and value to match whether a known exploit exists (e.g., YES or NO) for a finding.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match findings based on whether an exploit is available for a vulnerability.
The value to match against the exploit availability status of an Inspector v2 finding, used to filter for findings where a public exploit is or is not available (e.g., 'YES' or 'NO').
Filters findings by their Amazon Resource Name (ARN), using string filter conditions to include or exclude findings with specific ARNs.
The operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to compare the finding ARN against the specified value(s) to determine if a finding matches the filter criteria.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a finding that this Inspector v2 filter criterion matches to include or exclude findings with that exact ARN.
Filters findings based on their current status (for example, ACTIVE, CLOSED, or SUPPRESSED) using the specified comparison operator and status value.
Defines the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the finding status value in this filter criterion.
The finding status value (e.g., ACTIVE, SUPPRESSED, CLOSED) that the filter criteria matches against for this Inspector v2 filter.
Specifies the finding type values (such as PACKAGE_VULNERABILITY or CODE_VULNERABILITY) to match when filtering findings, using a comparison operator like EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS) used to match the finding type against the values you provide in the filter criteria for AWS Inspector v2.
This value specifies the Inspector finding type that the filter matches, with allowed values including 'PACKAGE_VULNERABILITY' and 'NETWORK_REACHABILITY'.
Filters findings by the date and time they were first observed, defined as a list of DateFilter objects each specifying an inclusive start and end timestamp.
The inclusive end timestamp (in Unix epoch seconds) that limits the filter to findings first observed at or before this time.
The inclusive start timestamp (Unix epoch seconds) of the window used to match findings whose first observed time falls on or after this value.
A list of BooleanFilter conditions that match findings based on whether a fix is available for the vulnerability, using a comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS) against a boolean value.

Sets the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) for the fix_available filter condition, controlling how a finding's fix availability status is matched against the specified value (e.g., TRUE or FALSE).
The value to match for the fix_available criterion, such as 'YES' or 'NO', to filter findings based on whether a fix is available for the vulnerability.
This list of number filter objects defines the criteria for matching findings by their Amazon Inspector risk score, allowing numeric comparisons like EQUALS or GREATER_THAN against a specified score.
Sets the lower inclusive threshold (0-100) for the Inspector score that a finding must meet to match the filter.
The inclusive upper bound for the Inspector score range, so resources with an Inspector score less than or equal to this value are included in the filter criteria.

Defines a list of StringFilter objects that match Inspector findings by the execution role ARN of the associated Lambda function, using comparison operators like EQUALS or PREFIX to include or exclude findings based on that ARN.
The comparison operator used to match the Lambda function's execution role ARN against the specified value(s) in the Inspector v2 filter criteria, such as EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, PREFIX, or NOT_PREFIX.
Specifies the ARN of the Lambda function's execution role, so that only findings associated with Lambda functions using this role match the filter.
Specifies a list of date-range conditions that match findings for Lambda functions whose last modified timestamp falls within the given start and end times.
The inclusive upper bound, as a Unix timestamp in seconds, for filtering AWS Lambda functions by their last modification time.
Defines the inclusive lower bound (as an epoch timestamp) of the range used by the Inspector v2 filter to match findings based on when the associated Lambda function was last modified.
Specifies a list of string filter conditions that match findings based on the layers associated with the affected Lambda function.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS) used to match a Lambda function layer against the filter value, determining whether the resource meets this filter condition.
The string value that specifies the ARN of an AWS Lambda layer, used to match findings from Lambda functions that use that layer.
Specifies a list of string filter conditions that match findings based on the name of the associated Lambda function in an Amazon Inspector filter criteria.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the Lambda function name against the filter value in this Inspector v2 filter criteria.
The value used with the comparison operator to match a Lambda function name when filtering Amazon Inspector v2 findings.

Filters findings based on the runtime identifier of the associated Lambda function (e.g., 'nodejs14.x', 'python3.9') using a comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS) and a value specified in each list item.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the Lambda function runtime against the filter's value(s) in the Inspector v2 filter criteria.
The Lambda runtime identifier (such as python3.9 or nodejs18.x) that the AWS Inspector v2 filter compares against the runtime of a Lambda function to determine inclusion.

Within the filter_criteria block of an AWS Inspector v2 filter, last_observed_at is a list of objects that lets you specify a start and end timestamp to match findings by when the finding was last observed.
Specifies the inclusive end of the date range (as a Unix timestamp) for when a finding was last observed, used to filter Inspector v2 findings by their last observed time.
Filters findings to include only those last observed at or after this inclusive epoch timestamp (in Unix seconds) within the last_observed_at date/time range.
Filters findings based on the network protocol (e.g., TCP, UDP) involved in network reachability findings, using comparison operators such as EQUALS to match the specified protocol values.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS) used to match the network protocol of a finding against the filter's configured value.
The network protocol (such as TCP, UDP, or ICMP) to match when filtering findings, used in the Inspector v2 filter criteria.
Matches findings based on the open network port range (begin_port to end_port) observed on the resource.
The inclusive lower bound of the port range used to match network connections in the Inspector v2 filter criteria.
The inclusive upper bound of the port range used to match findings where the network port associated with the finding falls within the specified range.
Filters findings by the identifiers of related vulnerabilities, using string comparison operators to include or exclude findings whose related Vulnerabilities list matches the specified value.
The comparison operator used to match related vulnerability IDs in the Inspector v2 filter criteria, such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS.
Specifies the vulnerability identifier (such as a CVE) to match when filtering Inspector v2 findings by related vulnerability.

The `resource_id` filter criterion matches findings whose affected resource identifier (such as an EC2 instance ID or ECR repository ARN) equals the specified value according to the chosen comparison operator.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the resource ID against the filter's expected value in an Amazon Inspector v2 filter.
The value to match for the resource ID condition in the Inspector filter criteria, used to filter findings based on the resource's identifier.
Defines the resource tag conditions used to filter Inspector findings, specifying tag keys, values, and comparison operators that resources must match to be included or excluded.
Defines the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used when matching a resource's tag value against the specified key in the resource_tags filter criteria.
The key of the resource tag that the Inspector V2 filter uses to match against resource tags when determining which resources are included in or excluded from the filter's findings.
The tag value to match for the resource tag filter, used to include or exclude resources based on their tags.
Defines one or more string comparison conditions that filter findings by the resource type (such as EC2, ECR, or Lambda) associated with the finding.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the resource type against the value in this filter criterion.
The resource type value to match in an Inspector V2 filter, such as AWS_EC2_INSTANCE or AWS_ECR_CONTAINER_IMAGE, used with the StringFilter comparison when filtering findings.
Specifies the severity levels (e.g., Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational) to include or exclude in the Inspector v2 findings filter, using comparison and value objects.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS) used to match the severity of findings against the filter's severity value.
The severity value to match in the filter criterion, provided as an uppercase string such as 'HIGH' or 'CRITICAL'.
The title criterion in the filter criteria, which matches findings by their title using a comparison operator and one or more string values.
Specifies the string comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, PREFIX, NOT_PREFIX) used to match the finding title against the configured value in the filter criteria.
The value to match against the title of an Inspector V2 finding when the filter's title criterion is applied.
The updated_at filter criteria item specifies a date range (with start and end times) used to match findings based on when their findings record was last updated.
The inclusive end (as a Unix epoch timestamp) of the time range used to filter Inspector v2 findings by their last updated time.
Specifies the inclusive start of the Unix epoch timestamp range used to filter resources by their last update time, so only resources updated at or after this time match.
Filters findings by the severity level assigned by the vendor, using a list of string comparison filters to include or exclude findings with specific vendor severity values.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the vendor-severity value against the filter criterion.
This value specifies a vendor-reported severity level (such as CRITICAL, HIGH, or MEDIUM) that the Inspector v2 filter matches against findings to include or exclude them.
Specifies the vulnerability identifier (such as a CVE ID) to include or exclude in the filter results, using comparison operators and a value for matching.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS) used to match a vulnerability's CVE identifier against the filter value.
The vulnerability ID (for example, a CVE identifier) that the filter matches against findings.
The vulnerabilitySource criteria filters Inspector v2 findings to those whose vulnerability data originates from a specified source (such as NVD) using one or more string comparison filters.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS) used to match the vulnerability source in the filter criteria.
The vulnerability source identifier, such as 'NVD' or 'CNVD', that the Inspector v2 filter will match against when evaluating findings.
Filters findings based on the properties of the vulnerable package, such as its name, version, architecture, epoch, release, or source layer hash, using a list of package filter objects.
Filters findings by the CPU architecture of the vulnerable package, using a comparison operator and value such as 'x86_64' or 'arm64'.
Defines the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the vulnerable package's architecture against the specified value.
Specifies the exact CPU architecture string (e.g., 'x86_64','arm64') used to match vulnerable package findings in the Inspector v2 filter criteria.
Specifies the numeric filter condition (comparison and value) for the epoch component of a vulnerable package's version, used to match AWS Inspector V2 findings.
The lower inclusive bound for the epoch value of a vulnerable package version to match in an Inspector v2 filter.
The upper inclusive bound for the package epoch value used to filter Inspector findings on vulnerable packages.
Specifies the file-path matching condition for filtering findings by vulnerable package location, using a string comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS) and the path value to include or exclude.
The comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, PREFIX) used to match the vulnerable package's file path against the specified value.
The exact file path string used as the comparison value when filtering findings based on the vulnerable package's file path.

Specifies a filter condition on the name of the vulnerable software package in an Amazon Inspector finding, allowing you to match findings where the package name equals or does not equal a specified string value using a comparison operator.
The comparison operator that determines how the vulnerable package name is matched (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS) in the AWS Inspector v2 filter criteria.

This field specifies the exact or pattern-matching value for the vulnerable package name (e.g., 'openssl') used in the Inspector v2 filter criteria to include or exclude findings based on the package name.
Specifies the release string (such as the distro-specific package release suffix) of the vulnerable package to match when defining the filter criteria.

When building an Amazon Inspector V2 filter, this field sets the string comparison operator (such as EQUALS, PREFIX, or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the vulnerable package's release value against the value you specify, thereby controlling which findings are included or excluded.
Specifies the release version of a vulnerable package that findings must match for the filter to apply.
The source_lambda_layer_arn criterion filters findings to include only those vulnerable packages that originate from a specified AWS Lambda layer, matched by its ARN.
Specifies the comparison operator used to match the source Lambda layer ARN of a vulnerable package when filtering Inspector v2 findings (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS).
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda layer that the vulnerable package originates from, used to filter Inspector v2 findings to only those associated with that layer.
Specifies the source layer hash of a vulnerable container image layer to match when filtering Inspector findings, part of the vulnerable packages filter criteria.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the source layer hash of a vulnerable package when filtering Inspector v2 findings.

The source_layer_hash.value field sets the string value for the source layer hash of a vulnerable package, used to match findings against the specific container image layer SHA that contains the vulnerable package.
Configures the version filter for vulnerable packages, using a comparison operator (such as EQUALS) and a value to match the package version in Inspector v2 findings.
Defines the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, GREATER_THAN) used to match the vulnerable package version against a specified value in the filter criteria.
The value of the version condition for the vulnerable package filter, specifying the exact package version (e.g., '1.2.3') to match in Inspector V2 findings.

aws_inspector_v2_filter.tags.text: Tags assigned to the Inspector V2 filter, used for organizing and identifying the filter resource in AWS cost allocation and management.

aws_instance.block_device_mappings.devic.text: The device name (e.g., /dev/sda1) under which the block device is exposed inside the EC2 instance, identifying the attached EBS volume or instance-store device in the block device mapping.

aws_instance.block_device_mappings.ebs.text: Configures the Amazon EBS volume to attach at the specified device name for this block device mapping, including settings such as volume size, volume type, IOPS, throughput, encryption, and delete-on-termination behavior.

aws_instance.block_device_mappings.ebs.d.text: Specifies whether the EBS volume should be deleted automatically when the EC2 instance is terminated.

aws_instance.block_device_mappings.ebs.e.text: Specifies whether the EBS volume created from this block device mapping should be encrypted at rest, applying AWS-managed or customer-managed KMS encryption when enabled.

aws_instance.block_device_mappings.ebs.i.text: The number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) to provision for the EBS volume, used with io1, io2, and gp3 volume types to control performance.

aws_instance.block_device_mappings.ebs.k.text: The KMS key ID used to encrypt the EBS volume specified in the block device mapping for the EC2 instance.

aws_instance.block_device_mappings.ebs.s.text: Specifies the ID of the EBS snapshot to use as the source for creating the EBS volume attached to the instance via this block device mapping.

aws_instance.block_device_mappings.ebs.v.text: The size of the EBS volume, in GiB, to attach to the EC2 instance via this block device mapping.
Specifies the Amazon EBS volume type for the block device, such as gp2, gp3, io1, io2, st1, sc1, or standard, which determines the volume's performance and cost characteristics.

aws_instance.block_device_mappings.no_de.text: When set to true, suppresses the specified device, ensuring that the device named in the block device mapping is not exposed to the EC2 instance, effectively removing it from the mapping.

aws_instance.block_device_mappings.virtu.text: Specifies the virtual device name (e.g., ephemeral0) used to map an instance store volume in the block device mapping.

aws_instance.cpu_options.core_count.text: The number of CPU cores to allocate for the EC2 instance, enabling a custom core count in the instance's CPU options.

aws_instance.cpu_options.threads_per_cor.text: Sets the number of threads per CPU core for the EC2 instance; specify 1 to disable Intel Hyper-Threading Technology or 2 to enable it.

aws_instance.credit_specification.cpucre.text: Specifies the CPU credit option for the instance (either 'standard' or 'unlimited'), which controls whether a T2/T3/T3a instance can burst above its baseline CPU performance and how it accrues or spends CPU credits.

aws_instance.elastic_gpu_specifications..text: Specifies the type of Elastic GPU to attach to the instance, such as eg1.medium.

aws_instance.elastic_inference_accelerat.text: Specifies the number of Elastic Inference accelerators of the selected type to attach to the EC2 instance.
The type of the Elastic Inference accelerator (e.g., eia2.medium, eia2.large) to attach to the EC2 instance.

aws_instance.ipv6_addresses.ipv6_address.text: Specifies an individual IPv6 address to associate with the EC2 instance's network interface, as one entry in the ipv6_addresses list.

aws_instance.launch_template.text: Specifies the launch template and its version to use for configuring the instance at launch, referencing the template by ID or name.

aws_instance.license_specifications.lice.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS License Manager license configuration to associate with this EC2 instance.

aws_instance.metadata_options.text: Configures the EC2 instance metadata service (IMDS), including whether the metadata endpoint is enabled, whether IMDSv2 tokens are required, the hop limit, and whether instance metadata tags are allowed.

aws_instance.network_interfaces.associat.text: Indicates whether to associate a carrier IP address with the network interface, enabling the instance to communicate over a carrier network in AWS Wavelength zones.

Indicates whether to automatically assign a public IP address to this network interface during instance launch, applicable only when the network interface is created as part of the instance's network configuration.

aws_instance.network_interfaces.delete_o.text: Controls whether the network interface attached to this EC2 instance is automatically deleted when the instance is terminated.

aws_instance.network_interfaces.descript.text: Specifies a human-readable description for the elastic network interface (ENI).

aws_instance.network_interfaces.device_i.text: The device index for the network interface, starting at 0 for the primary interface; higher values assign additional interfaces in the instance's network attachment order.

aws_instance.network_interfaces.ena_srd_.text: Configures Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD) settings for this network interface, which can improve network performance for supported instance types.
Specifies whether to enable Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD) for the network interface, which can improve network performance and reduce latency.
Configuration block for the ENA Express UDP specification on the network interface, controlling whether UDP traffic uses ENA Express to reduce latency and increase throughput.
Enables or disables ENA Express (SRD) for UDP traffic on this network interface.

aws_instance.network_interfaces.group_se.text: The list of security group IDs to attach to the network interface of the EC2 instance.

aws_instance.network_interfaces.ipv6_add.text: The number of IPv6 addresses to assign to the network interface, which EC2 automatically selects from the subnet's IPv6 range.
Specifies the list of IPv6 addresses to associate with the EC2 instance's network interface.
When you specify a custom network interface for an EC2 instance, this field provides one specific IPv6 address from the subnet's IPv6 CIDR block to assign to that interface.

aws_instance.network_interfaces.network_.text: The ID of an existing Elastic Network Interface (ENI) to attach to the EC2 instance when launched, as specified in the network_interfaces block.

aws_instance.network_interfaces.private_.text: The private IP address to assign to the network interface, which becomes the primary private IP address of the instance.
Defines a list of private IP address specifications for an EC2 instance's network interface, each specifying a private IPv4 address and whether it is the primary private IP.
Specifies whether this private IP address is the primary private IP address for the network interface on the EC2 instance.

Defines the private IPv4 address to assign to the network interface at launch, as part of the instance's network interface private IP specification, where the Primary flag determines whether it is the primary IP.

aws_instance.network_interfaces.secondar.text: Specifies the number of secondary private IP addresses that AWS automatically assigns to this network interface when the instance launches.

aws_instance.network_interfaces.subnet_i.text: Specifies the ID of the subnet in which the network interface is launched, determining the subnet placement for the EC2 instance when using custom network interface configuration.

aws_instance.private_dns_name_options.text: Configures the instance's private DNS hostname behavior, such as the hostname type (resource-name or ip-name) and whether to enable DNS A and AAAA records for the resource name.

aws_instance.ssm_associations.associatio.text: Specifies the key-value input parameters (each value a list of strings) passed to the SSM document when the association is executed on the instance.
The name of a parameter to pass to the SSM document when the association runs on the instance, such as a command or configuration parameter expected by the document.
The list of values assigned to a specific parameter key within an SSM association parameter set, which are passed to the associated SSM document when the association is applied to the EC2 instance.

aws_instance.ssm_associations.document_n.text: The name of the SSM document that the association runs on the EC2 instance.

aws_instance.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to assign to the EC2 instance, used to categorize or identify the instance.

aws_instance.tags.value.text: The value of a tag applied to the EC2 instance, forming a key-value pair used for organizing, identifying, and managing the instance.

aws_instance.volumes.device.text: The device name (e.g., /dev/sdf) where the volume is exposed inside the instance.

aws_instance.volumes.volume_id.text: The ID of the Amazon EBS volume to attach to the EC2 instance at launch, corresponding to the VolumeId property in the AWS::EC2::Instance Volumes list.

aws_interconnect_connection.tags.value.text: The value part of a key-value tag applied to the AWS Direct Connect connection (interconnect) resource, used to store arbitrary metadata for organizing and managing the connection.

aws_internet_gateway.internet_gateway_id.text: The unique identifier (e.g., `igw-...`) assigned by AWS to the internet gateway.

aws_internet_gateway.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag entry in the tags map for this AWS internet gateway, used to label the gateway with custom metadata such as environment or owner.

aws_internet_gateway.tags.value.text: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the Internet Gateway, used to store metadata for identification, organization, or cost allocation.

aws_internet_monitor_monitor.health_even.text: Configures the thresholds and conditions that determine when Internet Monitor generates health events based on measured availability and performance degradation.

Configures the thresholds and enablement for availability-based local health events, determining when Internet Monitor generates a health event for a specific client location based on local availability score and traffic impact.
Sets the availability health score threshold (0-100) below which CloudWatch Internet Monitor triggers a local health event for the impacted city or metro location.
The minimum percentage of client traffic that must be impacted to trigger a local availability health event, expressed as a number between 0 and 100.
Specifies whether health events for local availability are enabled or disabled for the monitor, with valid values 'ENABLED' and 'DISABLED'.
Defines the availability score threshold (0-100) for the monitor; when the observed availability score drops below this value, CloudWatch Internet Monitor triggers a health event.

Configures local health events triggered by performance degradation, including whether the events are enabled, the performance health score threshold that triggers an event, and the minimum traffic impact required for the event to be raised.
Determines the performance health score threshold (0–100) for local networks at or below which AWS Internet Monitor triggers a health event for performance issues.
The minimum percentage of client traffic impact that must be met for a performance-related local health event to be triggered by the monitor.
Specifies whether performance-related local health events are enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for the monitor.
A value from 0 to 100 that sets the performance score threshold; when a monitored location's performance score falls below this value, AWS Internet Monitor generates a health event.

aws_internet_monitor_monitor.include_lin.text: Indicates whether the monitor includes internet health data from linked accounts (member accounts of your AWS Organization).

aws_internet_monitor_monitor.internet_me.text: Defines the configuration for publishing internet measurement data to an Amazon S3 bucket or a CloudWatch Logs log group.
Specifies the Amazon S3 destination for internet measurements logs, including the bucket name and an optional object key prefix under which logs are stored.
The name of the S3 bucket where internet measurements logs are delivered when internet measurements log delivery to Amazon S3 is enabled for the monitor.
The S3 key prefix (folder path) under which the published internet measurements logs are stored, within the specified S3 bucket.
Indicates whether internet measurements logs are delivered to the configured S3 bucket, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED' controlling the delivery.

aws_internet_monitor_monitor.linked_acco.text: The AWS account ID of a linked account in your organization whose internet health events the monitor reports, enabling you to filter monitoring to a specific linked account.
