aws_internet_monitor_monitor.max_city_ne.text: Limits the maximum number of city networks (client locations) that AWS Internet Monitor will monitor for this monitor, overriding the default of 100 to help control monitoring costs.

aws_internet_monitor_monitor.monitor_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Internet Monitor monitor.

aws_internet_monitor_monitor.monitor_nam.text: The name of the Internet Monitor monitor, a required unique identifier for the monitor within your AWS account.

aws_internet_monitor_monitor.processing_.text: Indicates the processing status of the monitor, such as 'OK' when it is functioning normally or 'PROCESSING' when it is being initialized or updated.
Provides additional diagnostic details about the monitor's processing status, including the reason when the monitor is not in an OK state.

aws_internet_monitor_monitor.resources.text: A list of ARNs (for example, VPCs, Network Load Balancers, or CloudFront distributions) whose internet traffic the monitor will measure and report on.

aws_internet_monitor_monitor.resources_t.text: The list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the resources (such as VPCs) to add to the Internet Monitor for monitoring traffic.
A list of resource ARNs to remove from the monitor's set of monitored resources when updating the monitor.

aws_internet_monitor_monitor.status.text: Specifies the desired operational state of the Internet Monitor monitor, either ACTIVE to enable monitoring and metric collection or INACTIVE to disable it.

aws_internet_monitor_monitor.tags.text: Tags to assign to the Internet Monitor monitor, where each tag is a key-value pair used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_internet_monitor_monitor.tags.value.text: The user-defined value for a tag key attached to the AWS Internet Monitor monitor, used for metadata and resource categorization.

aws_internet_monitor_monitor.traffic_per.text: Configures the percentage of overall internet traffic that AWS Internet Monitor samples and analyzes, allowing you to trade off monitoring coverage for reduced cost.

aws_invoicing_invoice_unit.description.text: The description field provides an optional, user-defined textual description for the invoice unit, allowing you to record the purpose or context of this billing grouping.

aws_invoicing_invoice_unit.invoice_recei.text: The AWS account ID of the account that receives the consolidated invoice for this invoice unit.

aws_invoicing_invoice_unit.invoice_unit_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the invoice unit created by this resource.

aws_invoicing_invoice_unit.last_modified.text: The numeric timestamp indicating when the invoice unit was most recently modified, computed and read-only by the service.

aws_invoicing_invoice_unit.name.text: Sets the unique name of this invoice unit, a logical group of accounts used to consolidate and customize AWS billing invoices.

aws_invoicing_invoice_unit.resource_tags.text: The resource_tags field defines a list of tag objects (each containing a key and value) to associate with the invoice unit, enabling you to categorize and manage the invoice unit resource within AWS Invoicing.
The key part of a resource tag attached to the AWS Invoicing invoice unit, used to define custom metadata for organizing, filtering, and managing the invoice unit.
The value component of a resource tag (key-value pair) that can be attached to this invoice unit for cost allocation and organizational purposes.

aws_invoicing_invoice_unit.rule.text: Defines which AWS accounts are included in the invoice unit for consolidated invoicing and which account is designated as the invoice receiver.

aws_invoicing_invoice_unit.rule.linked_a.text: Specifies the list of linked account IDs (as strings) that are included under this invoice unit's rule when grouping accounts for invoicing.

aws_invoicing_invoice_unit.tax_inheritan.text: When set to true, this disables the invoice unit's inheritance of tax configuration from the payer account, forcing the invoice unit to use its own tax settings.

aws_io_t_account_audit_configuration.aud.text: Configures the Amazon SNS topic and IAM role used by AWS IoT Device Defender to deliver account audit notifications, representing the SNS target within the audit notification target configuration map.

aws_io_t_authorizer.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS IoT authorizer.

aws_io_t_authorizer.authorizer_function_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function that AWS IoT invokes to authorize device connections for this authorizer.

aws_io_t_authorizer.authorizer_name.text: The name of the custom IoT authorizer, serving as a unique identifier within the AWS account; if not provided, CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_io_t_authorizer.enable_caching_for_h.text: Determines whether AWS IoT caches the authorization results for HTTP requests made to this custom authorizer.

aws_io_t_authorizer.signing_disabled.text: Determines whether token signing is disabled for this custom authorizer; when set to true, AWS IoT Core will not require or verify the signature of the authorization token.

aws_io_t_authorizer.status.text: The status of the IoT authorizer, indicating whether it is ACTIVE or INACTIVE, which determines if the authorizer is used for authorization.

aws_io_t_authorizer.tags.text: A list of key-value tags to associate with the AWS IoT Authorizer for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_io_t_authorizer.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to attach to the AWS IoT authorizer, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_io_t_authorizer.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS IoT authorizer, used to store arbitrary metadata for the resource.

aws_io_t_authorizer.token_key_name.text: The name of the HTTP header in the incoming request that contains the authentication token used by this custom authorizer.

aws_io_t_authorizer.token_signing_public.text: Specifies a map of public keys, each identified by a logical name, that AWS IoT uses to verify the digital signature of the authorization token.

aws_io_t_billing_group.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IoT billing group, uniquely identifying it across AWS.

aws_io_t_billing_group.billing_group_nam.text: The name that uniquely identifies the IoT billing group, used to group devices for consolidated billing and usage tracking.

aws_io_t_billing_group.billing_group_pro.text: Contains properties of the billing group, such as a description field (BillingGroupDescription) for identifying the group's purpose.
A user-defined, free-form description of the AWS IoT billing group, used to provide additional context about the group's purpose.

aws_io_t_billing_group.id.text: The unique name of the AWS IoT billing group, which serves as the resource's identifier in AWS IoT.

aws_io_t_billing_group.tags.value.text: The string value of a tag assigned to the AWS IoT Billing Group, used to store arbitrary metadata about the billing group.

aws_io_t_cacertificate.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that AWS assigns to the CA certificate when it is registered in AWS IoT.

aws_io_t_cacertificate.auto_registration.text: Controls whether certificates signed by this CA certificate are automatically registered with AWS IoT upon first use, with allowed values such as 'ENABLE' and 'DISABLE'.

aws_io_t_cacertificate.cacertificate_pem.text: The PEM-encoded CA certificate content that AWS IoT uses to register device certificates and verify their authenticity.

aws_io_t_cacertificate.certificate_mode.text: Specifies whether the CA certificate is used for device authentication (DEFAULT) or TLS client authentication (SNI_ONLY) in AWS IoT.

aws_io_t_cacertificate.id.text: The unique identifier of the CA certificate, assigned by AWS IoT when the CA certificate is registered.

aws_io_t_cacertificate.registration_conf.text: Specifies the registration configuration for this CA certificate, including the registration template body and the IAM role that AWS IoT uses to provision device certificates.
The ARN of the AWS IoT role that grants permission to register the CA certificate during device certificate registration.
The body of the AWS IoT provisioning template used to automatically register device certificates signed by this CA certificate.

The name of the AWS IoT provisioning template used during certificate registration to define the resources and policies automatically created when a device certificate is registered under this CA certificate.

aws_io_t_cacertificate.remove_auto_regis.text: When set to true, this boolean removes the auto-registration for device certificates signed by this CA certificate when the CA certificate is deleted from AWS IoT.

aws_io_t_cacertificate.status.text: Specifies the operational status of the CA certificate, which must be either 'ACTIVE' or 'INACTIVE', controlling whether the certificate is enabled for device authentication in AWS IoT.

aws_io_t_cacertificate.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a tag attached to the AWS IoT CA certificate, used to identify and categorize the certificate within AWS resource tagging systems.

aws_io_t_cacertificate.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS IoT CA certificate, used to categorize or identify the resource.

aws_io_t_certificate.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to the IoT certificate, used to uniquely identify it within AWS IoT and IAM policies.

aws_io_t_certificate.cacertificate_pem.text: The PEM-encoded CA certificate that signed the device certificate, used when registering the certificate with a certificate authority.

aws_io_t_certificate.certificate_mode.text: Specifies the certificate mode (DEFAULT or SNI_ONLY) for the AWS IoT certificate, determining whether it is used with the standard IoT endpoint or only with SNI-based custom domains.

aws_io_t_certificate.certificate_pem.text: The PEM-encoded certificate data that AWS IoT registers when you import an existing certificate rather than creating one from a certificate signing request.

aws_io_t_certificate.certificate_signing.text: The PEM-encoded certificate signing request (CSR) used to create the certificate, allowing the certificate to be issued from an existing key pair rather than generating a new one.

aws_io_t_certificate.id.text: The unique certificate ID (a UUID-like string) generated by AWS IoT for the certificate, serving as the resource's primary identifier.

aws_io_t_certificate.status.text: Specifies the operational status of the AWS IoT certificate, such as ACTIVE, INACTIVE, REVOKED, PENDING_TRANSFER, or PENDING_ACTIVATION, which determines whether the certificate can be used for authentication.

aws_io_t_certificate_provider.account_de.text: The AWS::IoT::CertificateProvider account default for operations property specifies the list of certificate provider operations (RegisterCertificate or RegisterCertificateWithoutCA) for which this certificate provider is the default provider in the AWS account.

aws_io_t_certificate_provider.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS IoT certificate provider.

aws_io_t_certificate_provider.certificat.text: Specifies the unique name of the AWS IoT certificate provider, which identifies it within the AWS account and region and is referenced when associating CA certificates with this provider.

aws_io_t_certificate_provider.lambda_fun.text: The ARN of the Lambda function that AWS IoT invokes to perform custom certificate signing or validation for this certificate provider.

aws_io_t_certificate_provider.tags.key.text: The key portion of a tag assigned to the AWS IoT certificate provider resource, used to label and manage the certificate provider with custom metadata.

aws_io_t_certificate_provider.tags.value.text: The value string of a tag key-value pair attached to the AWS IoT certificate provider, used to store arbitrary metadata for identification and management.

aws_io_t_command.mandatory_parameters.de.text: The boolean default value used for this mandatory command parameter when a device executing the command does not supply a value for it.
This number specifies the default value for a mandatory parameter in an AWS IoT Command.
The string form of the default value (the 'S' attribute) for a mandatory parameter in an AWS IoT command, used to initialize the parameter when not provided at runtime.
In the AWS IoT Command resource, the 'ul' property holds the string representation of the unsigned long default value for a mandatory command parameter.
Provides a human-readable description of a mandatory parameter that must be supplied when invoking this AWS IoT command.

aws_io_t_command.mandatory_parameters.ty.text: Defines the data type of a mandatory parameter in an AWS IoT command, restricting the parameter value to a supported primitive type such as STRING, INTEGER, BOOLEAN, FLOAT, or BINARY.

aws_io_t_command.mandatory_parameters.va.text: The string value of a mandatory parameter in the AWS IoT Command definition, which must be supplied when invoking the command on a device.
Specifies the value for a mandatory parameter of type unsigned long in an AWS IoT command, expressed as a string.
Defines the validation conditions (such as equality or range constraints) that the value of each mandatory command parameter must satisfy when the command is invoked in AWS IoT.

The number field specifies the numeric constant that forms the operand in a value condition applied to a mandatory parameter of an AWS IoT Command, defining the comparison target for validating that parameter's value.
Defines the lower and upper bounds of the numeric range that a mandatory parameter's value must fall within for the value condition to be satisfied.
For the AWS IoT command resource, this string specifies the maximum numeric value allowed by a number-range constraint on a mandatory parameter's operand.
Specifies the minimum allowed value for a mandatory command parameter when its value condition is defined as a number range.

Defines the numeric values (represented as strings) that serve as the operand for a value condition on a mandatory parameter of the IoT command, such as the range or allowed numbers for numeric comparisons.

Specifies the string value of the operand in a value condition applied to a mandatory parameter of an AWS IoT command, defining the expected string match (e.g., equality or pattern) that the parameter's value must satisfy.
For a value condition on a mandatory parameter of an AWS IoT command, this list specifies the allowed string values that the operand can take.

aws_io_t_command.payload.text: Specifies the JSON payload object that is delivered to the target IoT device via MQTT when the command is executed.

aws_io_t_command.payload.content.text: The payload content of the AWS IoT command, which is the message body sent to the target device when the command is invoked.

aws_io_t_command.payload.content_type.text: Specifies the MIME content type (such as application/json or text/plain) of the command payload sent to an AWS IoT device.

aws_io_t_command.preprocessor.text: An optional object that specifies the ARN of an AWS Lambda function (via its 'lambdaArn' subfield) used to preprocess the command payload before it is delivered to the target device.

aws_io_t_custom_metric.tags.key.text: Represents the key of a tag attached to an AWS IoT Custom Metric, enabling metadata-based identification and management of the metric.

aws_io_t_dimension.tags.value.text: The tag value, paired with its key, assigns arbitrary metadata to the AWS IoT Dimension resource for categorization, filtering, and cost allocation.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.applicatio.text: Specifies the application protocol (SECURE_MQTT or HTTPS) that the domain configuration is used for, determining which protocol traffic it serves.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IoT domain configuration.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.authentica.text: Specifies the authentication type (e.g., AWS_X509, AWS_SIGV4, CUSTOM_AUTH, or AWS_IOT_CORE) used by the AWS IoT domain configuration for TLS client authentication.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.authorizer.text: Configures the AWS IoT authorizer used by this domain configuration, including the authorizer name and whether authorizer override is allowed.
When true, allows a client's specific authorizer to override the domain configuration's default authorizer for authentication.
Specifies the name of the default AWS IoT authorizer used to authenticate requests sent to this domain configuration, overriding the account-level default authorizer.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.client_cer.text: Configures client certificate authentication for the domain by specifying the ARN of the Lambda function that AWS IoT calls to validate client certificates.
The ARN of the Lambda function that AWS IoT invokes when a client certificate is presented for authentication, enabling custom certificate validation for this domain configuration.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.domain_con.text: The name of the AWS IoT domain configuration, which uniquely identifies the domain configuration within your AWS account.
The desired status (ENABLED or DISABLED) for the domain configuration, which determines whether the domain configuration is active for IoT connections.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.domain_nam.text: The domain name (e.g., 'example.com') to associate with this AWS IoT domain configuration, required when setting up a custom domain for AWS IoT and omitted for AWS-managed endpoint configurations.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.domain_typ.text: The type of the domain configuration, indicating whether the domain is AWS-managed (AWS_MANAGED) or customer-managed (CUSTOMER_MANAGED).

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.server_cer.text: Specifies the ARNs of the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificates used as the server certificates for the IoT domain configuration.

Configures the server certificate behavior for the IoT domain, specifically enabling Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) stapling checks and optionally specifying a Lambda function ARN for OCSP response handling.
Enables or disables the Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) check for the server certificate used by the domain configuration.
The ARN of an OCSP (Online Certificate Status Protocol) authorized responder used by AWS IoT to perform certificate revocation checks for the domain's server certificate.
The ARN of the Lambda function that acts as a custom OCSP responder for validating the server certificate in this AWS IoT domain configuration.
The computed list of server certificates attached to the IoT domain configuration, each containing the certificate ARN and its status.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) server certificate that AWS IoT uses to secure TLS connections on this custom domain configuration.

Indicates the current status of a server certificate associated with the AWS IoT domain configuration, such as ACTIVE or INACTIVE, reflecting whether the certificate is actively used for TLS termination.
The server certificate status detail, providing a human-readable reason or additional information about the status of the server certificate used by the AWS IoT domain configuration.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.service_ty.text: Specifies the type of AWS IoT service (DATA, CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER, or JOBS) that the domain configuration's endpoint is for, determining which service's traffic the domain applies to.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.tags.text: A list of tag objects (key-value pairs) to associate with the IoT domain configuration, which AWS IoT uses for labeling, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.tags.key.text: The tag key used to identify a custom metadata label assigned to this AWS IoT domain configuration, enabling resource categorization and filtering.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key applied to the AWS IoT domain configuration, allowing you to attach arbitrary metadata for cost allocation and management.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.tls_config.text: The tls_config object specifies the TLS security policy for the domain configuration, controlling the minimum TLS version and allowed cipher suites for client connections.
Specifies the TLS security policy (e.g., TLS_1_2_2021) for the domain configuration, which controls the allowed TLS versions and cipher suites for secure communication.

aws_io_t_domain_configuration.validation.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate used to validate ownership of the domain for this AWS IoT domain configuration.

aws_io_t_encryption_configuration.accoun.text: This field contains the AWS account ID of the account that owns the IoT encryption configuration, which is populated automatically by the AWS IoT service.

aws_io_t_encryption_configuration.encryp.text: Specifies the type of encryption key used for AWS IoT data encryption, either AWS-owned (AWS_OWNED) or customer-managed (CUSTOMER_MANAGED), determining whether you use an AWS-managed key or your own KMS key.

aws_io_t_encryption_configuration.kms_ac.text: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to access the customer-managed KMS key used for encrypting device data, required when the encryption type is CUSTOMER_MANAGED_KMS_KEY.

aws_io_t_encryption_configuration.kms_ke.text: The ARN of a customer-managed AWS KMS key used to encrypt IoT data; when omitted, AWS IoT uses an AWS-managed key.

aws_io_t_encryption_configuration.last_m.text: The computed timestamp indicating when the AWS IoT default encryption configuration was last modified, as returned by the DescribeDefaultEncryptionConfiguration API operation.

aws_io_t_fleet_metric.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to attach to the AWS IoT fleet metric, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the resource with custom metadata.

aws_io_t_fleet_metric.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to the AWS IoT Fleet Metric, used for metadata management, resource identification, and cost allocation.

aws_io_t_job.abort_config.criteria_list..text: Specifies the abort action (CANCEL or CONTINUE) to perform when the job's abort criteria are met.
The type of job execution failure that triggers the abort criteria for an AWS IoT job, such as FAILED, TIMED_OUT, or ALL.

The minimum number of things that must have completed the job execution before the abort criteria can be evaluated, allowing the abort action to trigger only after a certain number of executions have occurred.

The percentage of the total number of things in the job that must experience the specified failure type before the abort criteria triggers the abort action, when combined with the minimum number of executed things.

aws_io_t_job.job_executions_retry_config.text: Specifies the type of job execution failure (e.g., FAILED, TIMED_OUT, or ALL) that this retry criterion applies to, determining which failures trigger the configured retry count.
The maximum number of retry attempts for a job execution that fails with the associated failure type before the execution is marked as failed.

aws_io_t_job.scheduling_config.maintenan.text: Specifies the length of each maintenance window, in minutes, during which the AWS IoT job is allowed to run before the window closes and job executions are paused.
The start time of the maintenance window, in ISO 8601 format, during which the AWS IoT job execution can be started.

aws_io_t_job.tags.key.text: Specifies the key of a tag to attach to the AWS IoT job, allowing you to categorize, organize, and manage the job resource in AWS.

aws_io_t_job.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS IoT Job, used to categorize the job and enable resource-level access control via IAM condition keys such as aws:ResourceTag.

aws_io_t_job_template.abort_config.crite.text: Specifies a list of criteria that define when a running IoT job is aborted, including the action (CANCEL or CONTINUE), failure type (FAILED or TIMED_OUT), minimum number of executed things, and threshold percentage.
The action to take when the abort criteria threshold is reached, which for AWS IoT Job templates is always 'CANCEL'.
Specifies the type of job execution failure (e.g., FAILED or TIMED_OUT) that triggers this abort criterion in the IoT job template's abort configuration.
Specifies the minimum number of things that must have executed the job before the thresholdPercentage in this abort criterion can trigger an abort action.
The threshold percentage of total job executions that must fail with the specified failure type in order to trigger the job abort, expressed as a number between 0 and 100.

aws_io_t_job_template.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS IoT job template.

aws_io_t_job_template.destination_packag.text: Specifies the package version identifiers that are the deployment targets for the job, used to define the destination software versions in an AWS IoT OTA update job template.

aws_io_t_job_template.job_executions_ret.text: Specifies the retry configuration for failed job executions, including the retry criteria that define which failure types can be retried and the maximum number of retry attempts.

A list of retry criteria, each specifying a failure type (FAILED, TIMED_OUT, or ALL) and the maximum number of retry attempts for job executions that match that failure type, used to configure automatic retries for the job template.
The type of job execution failure that triggers a retry, such as FAILED, TIMED_OUT, or ALL, used in the retry criteria for an AWS IoT job template.
Specifies the maximum number of retry attempts for a job execution when it fails with the associated failure type, after which the execution is considered failed.

aws_io_t_job_template.job_executions_rol.text: The number of IoT things that are notified of the job per minute at the start of the rollout, before any rate increases are applied.
The multiplier applied to the base job execution rollout rate at each interval defined by the rate increase criteria, causing the rate of job executions to grow exponentially over time.
Specifies the threshold of notified or succeeded job executions that triggers an increase in the job rollout rate during exponential rollout.
The number of notified things at which the job rollout rate will be increased as part of the exponential rollout configuration.
The number of succeeded job executions (things) that must be reached before the rollout rate is increased exponentially for the remaining things in the job.
Specifies the maximum number of job executions that AWS IoT starts per minute for this job template's rollout, throttling the rate at which the job is deployed to devices.

aws_io_t_job_template.job_template_id.text: The unique identifier for the job template, which is required to create and reference the template in AWS IoT.

aws_io_t_job_template.maintenance_window.text: A list of maintenance windows, each specifying a start time and duration in minutes, that restrict when the AWS IoT job is allowed to be executed.
Specifies the duration in minutes that the maintenance window remains open for job execution, starting from the window's start time, in an AWS IoT job template.
The start time of the maintenance window for the AWS IoT job, specified as a 24-hour time in HH:MM format in UTC.

aws_io_t_job_template.tags.key.text: Specifies the key part of a key-value pair used to tag the IoT job template, which helps in identifying, organizing, and managing the resource.

aws_io_t_job_template.tags.value.text: The user-defined string that serves as the value for a tag associated with the AWS IoT job template, allowing you to categorize it for cost tracking, access control, and operational management.

aws_io_t_logging.event_configurations.ev.text: The AWS IoT event type (such as MqttActivity, Connections, or DeviceShadowOperations) that this logging configuration applies to within the event configurations map.

aws_io_t_logging.event_configurations.lo.text: The destination ARN (e.g., an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group or Amazon S3 bucket) to which AWS IoT delivers logs for the corresponding event configuration.

For each event type in the AWS IoT logging event configurations, this property sets the log level (e.g., DEBUG, INFO, ERROR, WARN, or DISABLED) that controls how detailed the IoT logs are for that event type.

aws_io_t_mitigation_action.action_params.text: The template_name specifies the name of the AWS IoT policy template that is used to generate the new policy version, which then replaces the existing default policy version for the target principal.
Specifies whether to activate or deactivate the CA certificate, with allowed values 'ACTIVATE' and 'DEACTIVATE'.
The action to perform on the device certificate, either 'DEACTIVATE' or 'ACTIVATE'.

aws_io_t_mitigation_action.mitigation_ac.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the AWS IoT mitigation action, assigned by AWS upon creation.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS IoT to the mitigation action.

aws_io_t_mitigation_action.role_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT permission to perform the mitigation action.

aws_io_t_mitigation_action.tags.key.text: The key of a tag that you can attach to an AWS IoT mitigation action, used to categorize and identify the action by metadata such as environment or purpose.

aws_io_t_mitigation_action.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the AWS IoT mitigation action, used for metadata such as owner, purpose, or environment.

aws_io_t_policy.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to the AWS IoT policy.

aws_io_t_policy.id.text: The unique identifier (policy name) of this AWS IoT policy, which is set to the policy name at creation time.

aws_io_t_policy.policy_document.text: A JSON-formatted policy document that defines the permissions for the AWS IoT policy, specifying allowed or denied actions and resources for IoT principals.

aws_io_t_policy.policy_name.text: The name of the AWS IoT policy; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_io_t_policy.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs to attach to the IoT policy, used for labeling and organizing the policy in AWS.

aws_io_t_policy.tags.key.text: The key of a key-value tag attached to an AWS IoT policy, used to categorize and identify the policy resource for management and access control.

aws_io_t_policy.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS IoT policy, used to organize and categorize the policy for management and cost tracking.

aws_io_t_policy_principal_attachment.id.text: This computed identifier uniquely represents the attachment between the IoT policy and the principal (certificate ARN or Cognito identity), typically composed of the policy name and the target principal ARN.

aws_io_t_policy_principal_attachment.pol.text: The name of the AWS IoT policy that will be attached to the specified principal (such as a certificate or Amazon Cognito identity) in the AWS::IoT::PolicyPrincipalAttachment resource.

aws_io_t_policy_principal_attachment.pri.text: The ARN of the IoT principal (e.g., a certificate ARN or Cognito identity) to which the policy is attached.

aws_io_t_provisioning_template.descripti.text: The Description property provides an optional, user-defined text description for the AWS IoT provisioning template, aiding in identifying the template's purpose and intended use case.

aws_io_t_provisioning_template.enabled.text: Determines whether the provisioning template is enabled, allowing or denying device provisioning operations through this template.

aws_io_t_provisioning_template.pre_provi.text: The pre-provisioning hook, an object that defines an AWS Lambda function to be invoked before device provisioning to validate or modify the provisioning request, including the Lambda function's ARN and payload version.
Specifies the payload version for the AWS IoT pre-provisioning hook, controlling the data format that the Lambda function receives (for example, '2020-10-22' or '2021-03-08').
The ARN of the Lambda function that AWS IoT invokes as the pre-provisioning hook to validate or customize device provisioning.

aws_io_t_provisioning_template.provision.text: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to perform the provisioning actions defined in the template, such as creating certificates, policies, and thing resources.

aws_io_t_provisioning_template.tags.text: Specifies an optional array of key-value tags to attach to the IoT provisioning template, which can help organize, identify, and manage the template alongside other AWS resources.

aws_io_t_provisioning_template.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the AWS IoT provisioning template, used to categorize, organize, and identify the resource for management purposes.

aws_io_t_provisioning_template.tags.valu.text: Specifies the value of a tag attached to the AWS IoT provisioning template, used to label and categorize the resource.

aws_io_t_provisioning_template.template_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to the AWS IoT provisioning template, used to uniquely identify the template.
The `template_body` is the JSON-formatted contents of the AWS IoT provisioning template that defines the parameters and resources (such as certificates and policies) to be provisioned for devices.
The unique, user-defined name that identifies this AWS IoT provisioning template.

Specifies the provisioning template type, which is either FLEET_PROVISIONING for fleet provisioning or JITP for just-in-time provisioning, determining how devices are provisioned with certificates and policies.

aws_io_t_role_alias.credential_duration_.text: Specifies the duration, in seconds, for which the temporary credentials returned by the AWS IoT role alias remain valid when the role is assumed via the alias.

aws_io_t_role_alias.role_alias.text: The unique name for the role alias, used in IoT policies and API calls to refer to the IAM role associated with this alias.

aws_io_t_role_alias.role_alias_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IoT role alias, automatically assigned by AWS when the alias is created.

aws_io_t_role_alias.role_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the role alias points to, which devices assume when authenticating through the AWS IoT credentials provider.

aws_io_t_role_alias.tags.text: Defines the list of tag objects to attach to the AWS IoT role alias, which can be used to organize, identify, and control access to the alias resource.

aws_io_t_role_alias.tags.key.text: The user-defined key of a tag attached to the AWS IoT Role Alias, used for metadata, cost tracking, and access management.

aws_io_t_role_alias.tags.value.text: Specifies the value portion of a tag attached to an AWS IoT Role Alias, used for organizing and identifying the alias with custom metadata.

aws_io_t_scheduled_audit.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to attach to the AWS IoT scheduled audit resource.

aws_io_t_scheduled_audit.tags.value.text: The value component of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS IoT scheduled audit, used to attach metadata like environment or owner to the audit resource.

aws_io_t_security_profile.additional_met.text: The name of the AWS IoT device metric to retain for the security profile, as part of the MetricToRetain object in AdditionalMetricsToRetainV2.
Specifies the named dimension (e.g., a thing group or device attribute) and operator (IN or NOT_IN) that scopes the additional metric to be retained by the AWS IoT security profile.
The name of the AWS IoT Device Defender metric dimension (such as a device or topic filter) that defines the scope for the metric to retain in the security profile.
The operator (IN or NOT_IN) that determines whether the metric applies to values that are in or not in the specified dimension.

aws_io_t_security_profile.behaviors.crit.text: Defines the conditions (such as comparison operator, value, and duration) that trigger an alert when a device's behavior deviates from the expected threshold in an AWS IoT Security Profile.

Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., less-than, greater-than-equals, in-set) used by the AWS IoT Security Profile behavior to evaluate whether a device's reported metric value deviates from the configured threshold during a detection window.
The number of consecutive datapoints that must violate the behavior's criteria before an alarm is triggered.
The number of consecutive datapoints that must fall within the clear threshold for the alarm to be cleared (resolving a detected violation).
Specifies the time period (in seconds) over which the behavior metric is measured and compared against the configured value to detect a violation.
Specifies the machine learning detection configuration for a Device Defender security profile behavior, including the confidence level (LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH) at which the behavior is triggered.
Determines the sensitivity (LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH) of the machine learning anomaly detection model used to evaluate behavior in this AWS IoT Device Defender security profile behavior.
Defines the statistical threshold (statistic and confidence level) that AWS IoT Device Defender evaluates the behavior's metric against to trigger an alarm in the security profile.
The statistical calculation (e.g., Average, Count, Sum, Variance) that AWS IoT Device Defender applies to the monitored metric to compare against the threshold.
The metric value to compare against, such as a count, number, set of CIDRs, or set of ports, as defined by the behavior's metric type.

Specifies the list of IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR blocks (e.g., '192.168.1.0/24') that define the allowed network address range for the security profile behavior's metric value, used in AWS IoT Device Defender to monitor device network connection locations.
The numeric threshold (specified as a string) for the number of times the metric can occur within the evaluation window before the security profile behavior triggers an alert.
Specifies the numeric threshold value that the AWS IoT behavior's criteria uses to evaluate the selected metric and trigger an alert if the metric crosses it according to the comparison operator.
The list of allowed destination port numbers for the behavior's criteria, used when the metric is `aws:message-by-ports`.
Defines a list of expected string values for string-based metrics in the behavior criteria, used as the benchmark against which device behavior is compared.

aws_io_t_security_profile.behaviors.expo.text: Specifies whether the device behavior metric is exported to CloudWatch.

aws_io_t_security_profile.behaviors.metr.text: The name of the AWS IoT Device Defender metric (such as 'aws:message-byte-size' or 'aws:all') that this behavior monitors, where the behavior's criteria will be evaluated against metric values reported by devices.

For a security profile behavior, this object specifies the metric's dimension—the name of an AWS IoT dimension (such as a thing group or topic) and an optional IN/NOT_IN operator that defines whether the metric is included or excluded for that dimension.
Specifies the name of the AWS IoT Device Defender metric dimension that scopes the security profile behavior's metric to a particular device set, such as a thing group or a specific dimension type.

The operator of the metric dimension, set to either 'IN' to apply the behavior's metric only to resources within the specified dimension or 'NOT_IN' to apply it to all resources outside that dimension.

aws_io_t_security_profile.behaviors.name.text: The unique, required name for a behavior within the AWS IoT Device Defender security profile, used to identify the behavior and its associated metrics.

aws_io_t_security_profile.behaviors.supp.text: Whether to suppress alerts for this behavior, preventing violation alerts from being generated for this specific behavior in the security profile.

aws_io_t_security_profile.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a tag attached to the AWS IoT Security Profile, used to identify and categorize the profile.

aws_io_t_software_package.description.text: A free-form text description of the software package (up to 1024 characters) that provides details about its purpose or contents.

aws_io_t_software_package.package_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS IoT software package in this account and Region.

aws_io_t_software_package.package_name.text: The user-defined name for the AWS IoT software package, which must be unique within your AWS account and can be omitted for AWS IoT to auto-generate a name.

aws_io_t_software_package.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS IoT software package.

aws_io_t_software_package.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key-value pair assigned to the AWS IoT Software Package, used as metadata to identify, organize, and search for the package.

aws_io_t_software_package_version.attrib.text: Specifies metadata attributes as key-value pairs that are attached to the software package version in AWS IoT, allowing you to add custom searchable or informational data to the version's registry entry.

aws_io_t_software_package_version.descri.text: Provides a user-defined description of this AWS IoT software package version.

aws_io_t_software_package_version.error_.text: The error reason reported by AWS IoT when the software package version enters a FAILED state, providing details about why version creation or update failed.

aws_io_t_software_package_version.packag.text: The name of the AWS IoT software package that this software package version belongs to.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS IoT software package version.

aws_io_t_software_package_version.status.text: The current status of the software package version, such as DRAFT, PUBLISHED, or DEPRECATED, as tracked by AWS IoT Software Package Catalog.

aws_io_t_software_package_version.tags.k.text: Specifies the key of a tag attached to the AWS IoT software package version, used to identify and manage the resource.

aws_io_t_software_package_version.tags.v.text: The value of a tag attached to this AWS IoT Software Package Version resource, providing arbitrary metadata for the package version.

aws_io_t_software_package_version.versio.text: The user-specified name for this version of the AWS IoT software package, which must be unique within the package; if omitted, AWS IoT/CloudFormation will generate a unique version name.

aws_io_t_stream.files.file_id.text: The unique numeric identifier for this file within the AWS IoT Stream, used by devices to reference and load the specific file from the stream.

aws_io_t_stream.files.s3_location.text: Specifies the Amazon S3 location (bucket, key, and optional version) of a file to be added to the AWS IoT stream, used to retrieve the file content for the stream.

aws_io_t_stream.files.s3_location.bucket.text: The name of the S3 bucket that contains the file referenced by this IoT stream file entry.

aws_io_t_stream.files.s3_location.key.text: Specifies the S3 object key (path) of the file to be added to the AWS IoT stream, locating the object within the bucket defined by the same s3_location block.

aws_io_t_stream.files.s3_location.versio.text: The version ID of the S3 object that contains the file to be streamed.

aws_io_t_thing.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the IoT thing within AWS IoT, used for referencing the thing in IAM policies and other AWS services.

aws_io_t_thing.attribute_payload.text: Specifies the thing's attribute payload, including a map of attribute names to values and whether to merge with existing attributes on update.

aws_io_t_thing.attribute_payload.attribu.text: A map of key-value pairs defining the AWS IoT thing's attribute payload, which is used to store and manage the device's metadata attributes.

aws_io_t_thing.id.text: For an AWS IoT Thing, the computed id is the thing's name, which is the resource's unique identifier within the AWS IoT registry and its CloudFormation physical ID.

aws_io_t_thing.thing_name.text: The unique name to assign to this AWS IoT thing; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a name.

aws_io_t_thing_group.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the IoT thing group.

aws_io_t_thing_group.id.text: The unique identifier of the IoT Thing Group, which is the thing group name as assigned by AWS.

aws_io_t_thing_group.parent_group_name.text: The name of the parent thing group to which this thing group belongs, establishing a hierarchical relationship in AWS IoT.

aws_io_t_thing_group.query_string.text: The query string that defines the dynamic thing group membership criteria, selecting which AWS IoT things are included in the group.

aws_io_t_thing_group.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a tag assigned to the AWS IoT Thing Group, used to organize and identify the group in AWS.

aws_io_t_thing_group.tags.value.text: The value for a tag attached to the AWS IoT Thing Group resource.

aws_io_t_thing_group.thing_group_name.text: The user-provided name for this IoT Thing Group, which must be unique within the AWS account; if omitted, CloudFormation or AWS IoT generates a unique name.

aws_io_t_thing_group.thing_group_propert.text: The thing group properties object, which specifies the thing group's description and attribute payload (key-value pairs) for the AWS IoT Thing Group.
The attribute payload defining the thing group's attributes, containing a map of attribute names to values and a boolean merge flag to determine whether to append or replace existing attributes.
Specifies a map of key-value pairs that define the attributes of the IoT thing group, used for describing and grouping things in AWS IoT.
The thing group description provides a user-defined text string that describes the purpose or contents of the IoT thing group in the AWS IoT registry.

aws_io_t_thing_principal_attachment.prin.text: The ARN of the AWS IoT certificate or Amazon Cognito identity that is attached as a principal to the IoT thing.

aws_io_t_thing_principal_attachment.thin.text: The name of the AWS IoT thing to which the principal (certificate or Cognito identity) is attached.

aws_io_t_thing_type.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS IoT thing type, assigned by AWS when the type is created.

aws_io_t_thing_type.deprecate_thing_type.text: Indicates whether the thing type should be deprecated, which prevents new things from being associated with it after the type is created.

aws_io_t_thing_type.id.text: The id is the unique name of the IoT thing type, which serves as the resource's primary identifier and is used to reference the thing type in other AWS IoT operations.

aws_io_t_thing_type.tags.value.text: Specifies the value part of a tag key-value pair used to label the AWS IoT Thing Type.

aws_io_t_thing_type.thing_type_name.text: Specifies a user-defined name for the AWS IoT thing type, which must be unique within the AWS account and is used to identify the thing type in IoT Core operations; if omitted, AWS IoT automatically generates a name.

aws_io_t_thing_type.thing_type_propertie.text: Configures the properties of the AWS IoT thing type, including a human-readable description and a list of searchable attributes used to search for things of this type.
Specifies the list of thing attributes (each defined by a key and optional static value) that AWS IoT propagates into MQTT5 messages published by things associated with this thing type.
Specifies the MQTT5 connection attribute (e.g., SourceIp, ThingName, or ThingTypeName) whose value is propagated into the CONNECT message's user properties for devices of this thing type.
The name of the thing attribute that will be propagated to MQTT5 messages for the AWS IoT Thing Type.
Specifies the key of the MQTT5 user property that carries the value of the associated thing attribute when messages are published.
Specifies a list of thing attribute names that can be used to search for things of this thing type in AWS IoT.
An optional human-readable description that provides additional context about the purpose or characteristics of the AWS IoT thing type.

aws_io_t_topic_rule.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the IoT topic rule, assigned by AWS upon creation.

aws_io_t_topic_rule.rule_name.text: The name to assign to the AWS IoT topic rule, which must be unique within an AWS account and Region.

aws_io_t_topic_rule.tags.key.text: The user-defined tag key portion of a tag attached to the AWS IoT topic rule, used to organize, identify, and manage the rule according to your AWS tagging strategy.

aws_io_t_topic_rule.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag attached to the AWS IoT Topic Rule, used to assign metadata that can be used for identification, organization, and IAM access control based on tags.

aws_io_t_topic_rule.topic_rule_payload.text: Defines the body of the AWS IoT rule, including the SQL query (sql), actions to invoke when the query matches, and optional settings such as rule disabled flag, error action, and AWS IoT SQL version.

aws_io_t_topic_rule.topic_rule_payload.a.text: The list of actions to execute when the AWS IoT rule is triggered, such as republishing to another MQTT topic, invoking a Lambda function, or writing to a DynamoDB table.
Configures a CloudWatch alarm action for the IoT rule, specifying the alarm name, state reason, state value, and IAM role ARN needed to change the alarm state when the rule is triggered.
The name of the CloudWatch alarm that the AWS IoT rule triggers when the rule’s action executes.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to access the CloudWatch alarm for this action.
The reason for the CloudWatch alarm state change that is sent when the IoT rule triggers a CloudWatch alarm action.
The state value to assign to the CloudWatch alarm, which must be one of OK, ALARM, or INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
The CloudWatch Logs action that sends the IoT message payload to the specified CloudWatch Logs log group using the configured IAM role.
Determines whether multiple IoT messages are delivered to CloudWatch Logs in a single batch (true) or as individual log events (false, default).
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group to which the IoT rule sends message data.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to write to the specified CloudWatch Logs log group when the rule triggers a CloudWatch Logs action.
Specifies a CloudWatch metric action that publishes a data point to a specified CloudWatch metric, including the metric name, namespace, unit, value, timestamp, and the IAM role used for the publish.
The name of the CloudWatch metric to which the IoT rule action publishes data.
Specifies the CloudWatch namespace under which the IoT rule's metric data point is published for the cloudwatch_metric action.
The timestamp for the CloudWatch metric data point, expressed in ISO 8601 format, which is used as the metric's time.
Specifies the unit of measure for the CloudWatch metric (e.g., Count, Bytes, Seconds) that the AWS IoT rule action publishes.
The value published to the CloudWatch metric by this AWS IoT rule action.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to gain permission to publish the metric data to Amazon CloudWatch.
Defines a DynamoDB action in the AWS IoT rule that writes message payload data into an Amazon DynamoDB table using a hash key, range key, and optional payload field mappings.
The name of the DynamoDB table's hash key (partition key) attribute that the IoT rule action populates from the message payload to identify the item being written.
Specifies the data type (STRING or NUMBER) for the hash key value used in the DynamoDB action, defaulting to STRING when not provided.
The value (or substitution template) to use for the hash key (partition key) when writing an item to the DynamoDB table in this IoT rule action.
Determines the value that AWS IoT writes to the DynamoDB table, allowing a static string or a dynamic reference to a property in the incoming payload (e.g., ${payload.someField}).
The name of the range key field in the DynamoDB table that the IoT rule writes to.
Specifies the data type (STRING, NUMBER, or BINARY) for the range key field when the DynamoDB action writes to an Amazon DynamoDB table.
The value of the range key column in the DynamoDB table row that the IoT rule writes, which can contain substitution templates to reference data from the MQTT message payload.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT permission to write to the DynamoDB table for this action.
The name of the target DynamoDB table to which the AWS IoT rule writes message data.
Configures an AWS IoT rule action that writes message payload data into a DynamoDB table using the DynamoDBv2 API, which requires a role ARN and a PutItem specification naming the target table.
The name of the Amazon DynamoDB table that the AWS IoT rule writes the message payload to.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to write data to the DynamoDB table when the rule is triggered.
The elasticsearch action sends the message payload to an Amazon Elasticsearch (OpenSearch) domain, with fields specifying the endpoint, index, type, document ID, and IAM role for the action.
The Amazon Elasticsearch Service domain endpoint (e.g., https://my-domain.es.amazonaws.com) to which the IoT message is written by the Elasticsearch action.
The unique identifier (document ID) used when writing the message payload to the Amazon Elasticsearch service, which can be a static string or a substitution template.
The name of the Elasticsearch index that AWS IoT writes the message data to when the rule triggers the Elasticsearch action.
The IAM role ARN that AWS IoT assumes to write data to the Amazon Elasticsearch Service domain in the Elasticsearch action of the topic rule.
The Elasticsearch document type (the _type) that the AWS IoT rule's Elasticsearch action uses when indexing the message data into the specified index.

Configuration for a Kinesis Data Firehose action within an AWS IoT rule, specifying the delivery stream, IAM role, and optional separator or batch mode used when writing message payloads to the stream.
Determines whether AWS IoT sends the rule's messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose as a single batch (true) or as individual records (false).
The name of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that the AWS IoT rule's firehose action sends message data to.
The IAM role ARN that AWS IoT assumes to write to the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream in the Firehose action of the topic rule.
Specifies the separator (such as a newline or comma) that AWS IoT inserts between records when sending message payloads to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream via this rule action.
The HTTP action configuration that forwards the IoT message to an HTTPS endpoint, defining the URL, optional headers, and authentication details.
Configures authentication for the HTTP action, allowing the use of SigV4 request signing or static credentials to invoke the endpoint.
Specifies the SigV4 signing configuration, including the IAM role ARN, service name, and signing region, used to authenticate the HTTP action's outbound requests.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to sign the HTTP request with SigV4 authentication in the HTTP action of the topic rule.
Specifies the AWS service name (e.g., 'execute-api' for API Gateway) used when signing the HTTP action request with SigV4 authentication.
The AWS Region (e.g., 'us-east-1') used by SigV4 to sign the HTTP request to the target endpoint for this IoT rule's HTTP action.
Configures the batching of messages sent by an AWS IoT rule's HTTP action, including the batch mode and the AWS IoT thing ID to associate with the batch.
When batch mode is enabled, controls whether messages from different MQTT topics are included together in a single HTTP request payload (true) or kept in separate batches per topic (false).
Specifies the maximum time in milliseconds that a batch of messages is kept open before the AWS IoT rule forces the HTTP action to send the accumulated messages in a single request.
The maximum number of messages to include in a single HTTP request batch for this IoT Topic Rule's HTTP action.
The maximum total payload size, in bytes, for a single HTTP batch sent by the AWS IoT rule action when batching is enabled, valid up to 1,048,576 bytes.
The URL to which AWS IoT sends a confirmation message when the HTTP action is configured, in order to verify that the endpoint is active and can receive data.
When set to true, AWS IoT Core groups and sends multiple messages to the HTTP endpoint in a single request instead of sending each message separately.
Specifies a list of HTTP header key-value pairs (each with key and value) to include in the HTTP request sent by this IoT rule action.
Defines the name of an HTTP header to be sent with the HTTP action's request to the endpoint specified in the AWS IoT rule.

Specifies the value of the HTTP header key-value pair that AWS IoT includes in the HTTP request to the endpoint when this topic rule action triggers, and can contain substitution templates for dynamic values.
The URL of the HTTP endpoint that the AWS IoT rule invokes to send the message payload when this HTTP action is triggered.
Defines an AWS IoT Analytics action that routes IoT rule messages to a specified IoT Analytics channel, requiring a channelName and roleArn to authorize the write.
When true, the IoT Analytics action batches multiple MQTT messages into a single IoT Analytics message; when false, each incoming message is processed separately.
The name of the AWS IoT Analytics channel to which the message data is forwarded.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to send data to the AWS IoT Analytics channel.
Specifies the AWS IoT Events action, which sends the message payload to an AWS IoT Events input for processing by a detector model.
When true, the IoT Events action sends the message data as a batch to AWS IoT Events; when false, it processes each MQTT message individually (default).
The name of the AWS IoT Events input that receives the message from this action.
A custom message identifier that AWS IoT includes when it sends event data to AWS IoT Events, allowing the event to be recognized or deduplicated by that ID.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT permission to send message data to the AWS IoT Events input.
Configures an action that sends IoT message data to AWS IoT SiteWise for asset property updates or time series ingestion.
A list of asset property value entries that define the IoT SiteWise asset property updates (identified by alias or asset/property IDs) and their time-series values written by this topic rule action.
The ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset containing the property to which the value is written.

The entry ID is an optional, client-specified identifier used to correlate a particular PutAssetPropertyValue entry with its corresponding result when AWS IoT SiteWise processes a batch of entries in a single action.
The property alias that identifies the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property to which this entry's value will be written, for example '/company/windfarm/3/turbine/7/temperature'.
Specifies the ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property to which the time-series values are written, within a put-asset-property-value entry of an IoT SiteWise action triggered by the IoT rule.
Defines the list of asset property values (each containing a timestamp, value, and optional quality) that are written to the specified AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when the IoT rule is triggered.
Sets the quality of the IoT SiteWise asset property value (e.g., GOOD, BAD, UNCERTAIN) when this AWS IoT rule action writes data to AWS IoT SiteWise.
Specifies the time (Unix epoch seconds and optional nanosecond offset) at which the asset property value was recorded, used by AWS IoT SiteWise when the topic rule action writes property values.

The nanosecond offset (as a string) relative to the epoch second provided in `time_in_seconds`, used to define the exact timestamp when putting an asset property value to AWS IoT SiteWise from an IoT rule action.
The Unix epoch time in seconds, as a string, when the asset property value was measured for the IoT SiteWise action in the AWS IoT Topic Rule.
Defines the variant data value (a union of booleanValue, doubleValue, integerValue, or stringValue) that is written as an asset property value to AWS IoT SiteWise by the IoT rule action.
Specifies the boolean value of the asset property that the AWS IoT rule sends to AWS IoT SiteWise, represented as a string (e.g., 'true' or 'false') in this CloudFormation property.
The double value (as a string) to assign to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when the rule action writes to a SiteWise asset property entry.
Specifies the integer value (as a string) to associate with the asset property when the property's data type is INTEGER, in an IoT SiteWise PutAssetPropertyValue action.
The string value to write to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when the property value entry's variant has type STRING, used in the put-asset-property-value action of an AWS IoT rule.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to access the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property.
Configures a Kafka action for the AWS IoT rule, specifying the destination Kafka cluster ARN, the target Kafka topic, and optionally the message key, partition, and headers.
Specifies a map of Kafka client property keys and values (such as security protocol and SASL configuration) used when connecting to the Kafka destination.
The ARN of the Amazon MSK cluster that the AWS IoT rule action sends messages to.
Defines the list of key-value pairs that are attached as Kafka message headers when this action sends the MQTT payload to the target Kafka topic.
The name of a Kafka message header key to include when this IoT rule action writes the message to the Kafka topic.
The value for a Kafka message header that the AWS IoT rule Kafka action attaches to the outbound Kafka message.
The Kafka message key used by the AWS IoT rule when it writes the message to the configured Kafka topic.
The Kafka partition number (as a string) to which the message is sent by this AWS IoT rule Kafka action.
The name of the Kafka topic to which the AWS IoT rule action sends the message payload.
The 'kinesis' action configuration for an AWS IoT rule that sends message data to an Amazon Kinesis stream, specifying the target stream name, partition key, and IAM role ARN.
The partition key that the AWS IoT rule uses to determine which shard in the Kinesis stream the message data is sent to; if omitted, a random partition key is used.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to send data from the rule to the specified Kinesis stream.
The name of the Amazon Kinesis stream to which the IoT rule sends data.
Invokes an AWS Lambda function when the IoT rule matches, using the specified Lambda function ARN.
The ARN of the Lambda function that AWS IoT invokes when this topic rule action is triggered.
Defines the parameters for the AWS IoT rule action that sends device location data to an Amazon Location Service tracker, including the tracker name, device ID, timestamp, and IAM role.

The device identifier that the AWS IoT rule uses when sending a location update to Amazon Location Service, supporting a substitution template that resolves to the actual device ID for the tracker event.
The latitude coordinate, expressed as a string, that the IoT rule's location action sends to Amazon Location Service for the device's position.

The longitude coordinate (as a string, typically a substitution template) that this AWS IoT rule's Location action includes in the device location update it sends to the Amazon Location Service tracker.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT permission to perform the Location action, such as sending device coordinates to Amazon Location Service.

Specifies the timestamp for the location update sent to Amazon Location Service, with a value (string) and a unit (e.g., 'seconds' or 'milliseconds') that define how the time value should be interpreted.
Specifies the time unit of the timestamp value for the AWS IoT Location action, such as Unix_epoch_seconds, Unix_epoch_milliseconds, or Unix_epoch_microseconds.
The value (a time expression) used as the timestamp for the location data sent to Amazon Location Service, typically an AWS IoT SQL time function such as `timestamp()`.
The name of the Amazon Location Service tracker resource that the location action sends device location data to.
Specifies an action that writes the IoT message payload to an Amazon OpenSearch Service domain, using the configured endpoint, index, type, and IAM role for the destination.
The HTTPS endpoint of the Amazon OpenSearch Service domain to which the IoT rule sends data.
The document ID used when writing data to the Amazon OpenSearch Service (or Elasticsearch) index; it can be a substitution template.
The name of the OpenSearch index to which the IoT rule action writes the message data.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to write data to the Amazon OpenSearch Service domain.
The document type under which the data is written to the Amazon OpenSearch Service index in the AWS IoT rule OpenSearch action.
Configures a republish action that forwards the incoming message payload to a specified MQTT topic via the AWS IoT message broker, with an IAM role for authorization and an optional QoS level.
Specifies the MQTT headers (such as content type, message expiry, response topic, and user properties) to include when the republish action publishes the message to the new MQTT topic.
Specifies the MQTT5 Content Type header to include in messages republished by this IoT rule action.
Sets the MQTT 5 correlation data header on the republished message, allowing receivers to correlate a response with its original request.
This field sets the MQTT message expiry interval (in seconds) for the message republished by the republish action, as part of its MQTT v5 headers.
Sets the MQTT 5 payload format indicator in the republished message header, either UTF8_DATA for UTF-8 encoded payload or UNSPECIFIED_BYTES for uninterpreted bytes.
Specifies the MQTT response topic to include in the MQTT v5 headers when the republish action publishes the message, enabling request/response patterns.
Specifies the MQTT 5.0 user properties to set on the republished message's headers, where each entry consists of a key and a value.
The key for a user property pair included in the MQTT headers of the message republished by the AWS IoT rule's republish action.
The value of a user-defined MQTT 5 user property that AWS IoT includes in the headers of the republished message.
The Quality of Service (QoS) level (0 or 1) used when the republish action sends the message to the destination MQTT topic.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to republish messages to the specified topic.
The MQTT topic to which the republish action publishes the message payload.
Configures an AWS IoT rule action that publishes the MQTT message payload to an Amazon S3 bucket using a templated object key and an IAM role that grants the necessary write permissions.
The name of the S3 bucket where the AWS IoT rule's S3 action writes the message payload.
Sets the Amazon S3 canned ACL that AWS IoT applies to the object when the rule action writes data to the specified S3 bucket, controlling its access permissions.
The S3 object key for the uploaded message, which can include template substitutions (e.g., ${topic()}) to dynamically generate the key per MQTT message.
The IAM role ARN that AWS IoT assumes to write the message payload to the specified S3 bucket.
Specifies an SNS action that publishes the IoT rule payload as a message to the specified SNS topic.
For the SNS action in an AWS IoT rule, this sets the message format to either RAW (publishing the message as-is) or JSON (publishing it as a JSON object).
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to publish messages to the SNS topic specified in this action.
The ARN of the SNS topic to which the IoT rule publishes messages.
Defines the SQS action for the AWS IoT rule, specifying the target queue URL, the IAM role ARN that grants IoT permission to send messages, and an optional flag to base64-encode the message payload.
The URL of the SQS queue to which AWS IoT sends the message payload when this rule action is triggered.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT permission to send messages to the specified SQS queue.
If set to true, AWS IoT base64-encodes the message payload before sending it to the SQS queue in this action.
Specifies the configuration for invoking an AWS Step Functions state machine when the IoT rule action is triggered.
Specifies a prefix that, combined with a UUID, forms the name of the Step Functions state machine execution started by this IoT rule action.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to execute the Step Functions state machine when the topic rule action triggers.
The name of the AWS Step Functions state machine to start when the IoT rule is triggered, as defined in the stepFunctions action.

Configuration for an AWS IoT Topic Rule action that writes message data to an Amazon Timestream database, specifying the IAM role, target database and table, and dimensions used to partition the data.
This field specifies the name of the Amazon Timestream database that the AWS IoT rule action writes the message payload to.
Defines name-value pairs that are attached as metadata dimensions to each Timestream record written by this AWS IoT rule action, enriching the stored time-series data.
Defines the Timestream dimension name that the AWS IoT rule's Timestream action writes the corresponding value to.
The value of the Timestream dimension entry, used as the value associated with the dimension name in the time-series record written by the IoT rule action.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT permission to write to the Amazon Timestream database and table specified in this action.
The name of the Amazon Timestream table to which the AWS IoT rule action writes the incoming message data.
Defines the timestamp (time value and unit) for the time-series data that this AWS IoT rule action writes to Amazon Timestream.
The unit of the timestamp value (e.g., SECONDS, MILLISECONDS, MICROSECONDS, or NANOSECONDS) that the AWS IoT Timestream action uses when writing the time dimension to Amazon Timestream.
Specifies the time value (a string, optionally using IoT substitution templates like ${timestamp()}) that is written to the Timestream record's timestamp column for this action.
Specifies the version of the AWS IoT SQL rules engine to use for the topic rule (for example, '2016-03-23' or '2015-10-08').

aws_io_t_topic_rule.topic_rule_payload.d.text: A user-defined description of the AWS IoT rule that documents its purpose or intent.

aws_io_t_topic_rule.topic_rule_payload.e.text: Specifies the action to execute when an error occurs during the evaluation or execution of this IoT rule.
Defines the CloudWatch alarm action to run as the error action when the IoT rule's primary action fails, triggering the specified alarm with a state change.
Specifies the name of the CloudWatch alarm that AWS IoT triggers when the rule's primary action fails, as part of the error action configuration.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to perform the CloudWatch alarm action.
The reason string that AWS IoT includes as the 'State Reason' in the CloudWatch alarm state-change event when this error action triggers the alarm.
The state value to send to the CloudWatch alarm when the rule triggers an error action, such as OK, ALARM, or INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
Configures the CloudWatch Logs action for the rule's error action, specifying the target log group and IAM role used to send messages when the primary action fails.
Determines whether log events are sent to CloudWatch Logs in batch mode, with true enabling batched delivery and false sending each event individually.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group to which the IoT rule error action sends log events.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT permission to write to the CloudWatch Logs log group specified in this error action.

Specifies the CloudWatch metric action to execute as the error action when the IoT rule's primary action fails, defining the metric name, namespace, unit, value, timestamp, and IAM role for publishing the metric.
The name of the CloudWatch metric to which the IoT rule publishes when the primary action fails, as part of the error action's CloudWatch metric target.
The CloudWatch metric namespace to which the IoT rule's CloudWatch metric action publishes the metric value.
The timestamp for the CloudWatch metric data point (in ISO 8601 format) used when the IoT rule's error action publishes the metric to CloudWatch.
The unit of measure for the CloudWatch metric (e.g., Count, Bytes, Seconds) that the IoT rule's error action emits when the rule action fails.
Specifies the numeric value, expressed as a string, that AWS IoT publishes to the CloudWatch metric when this error action is invoked.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to publish the CloudWatch metric data point for this error action.
The DynamoDB action to run as the error action when the rule's primary action fails, writing the message payload to a DynamoDB table.
The name of the hash key (partition key) attribute in the DynamoDB table that the IoT rule's error action writes to.
Specifies the data type of the DynamoDB hash key (STRING or NUMBER) for the DynamoDB action used as the error action of the IoT topic rule.
For the DynamoDB error action in an AWS IoT rule, this field specifies the value to use for the table's hash key when writing the item.

In an AWS IoT rule's DynamoDB error action, this parameter specifies the name of the DynamoDB attribute (column) that receives the message payload; if omitted, the entire payload is stored as a string.
Specifies the name of the range (sort) key column in the target DynamoDB table that the IoT rule writes to via its error action, required only when the table has a composite primary key.
Specifies the data type (STRING or NUMBER) for the range key in the DynamoDB action used as the error action for the AWS IoT rule.
Specifies the value for the range key attribute of a DynamoDB table entry that the IoT rule's error action writes, which may include substitution templates from the original message payload.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to write the error action's payload to the DynamoDB table.
The name of the DynamoDB table where the error action writes data when the IoT rule's main action fails.
Specifies the DynamoDBv2 action to execute when the rule's main action fails, writing the message payload to a DynamoDB table.
Specifies the DynamoDB PutItem operation configuration, including the target table name and the hash/range key field-value pairs used to write the message payload from the IoT rule action.
The name of the target DynamoDB table in which the IoT rule's put_item action writes the message payload data.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to write to the DynamoDB table when this DynamoDBv2 action is invoked as the error action.
Specifies an Elasticsearch error action that AWS IoT executes when the rule's normal action fails, sending the failed message payload to an Amazon Elasticsearch Service domain.
The endpoint URL of the Amazon Elasticsearch Service (or OpenSearch) domain to which the error action sends the message.
The document ID for the Elasticsearch document that the rule writes, which can include substitution templates to evaluate device state.
The name of the Elasticsearch index to which the AWS IoT rule writes message data when this error action is triggered.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to write to the Amazon Elasticsearch Service domain.
Specifies the Elasticsearch document type (e.g., 'product') under which the IoT rule error action writes data to the Elasticsearch index.

This object defines the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose action to execute when the main action of the IoT rule fails, specifying the Firehose delivery stream and IAM role used to forward the error payload.
Enables delivery of IoT messages to Kinesis Data Firehose in batches rather than one message per request, improving throughput when processing high-volume message streams.
The name of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to which the IoT rule error action sends data.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to write to the specified Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose stream when this error action is triggered.

The delimiter (such as a newline or comma) that the AWS IoT rule uses to separate individual records written to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream when this Firehose action is invoked as the error action.
Defines the HTTP action that AWS IoT executes as the error action when the main rule action fails, specifying the endpoint URL and optional headers for the fallback request.
Specifies the authentication mechanism, including SigV4 signing credentials via the nested 'sigv4' property, used when the IoT error action makes an HTTP request to the configured endpoint.
Specifies the AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4) authorization configuration for the HTTP error action, including the signing region, service name, and IAM role ARN used to sign the outgoing request.
The ARN of an IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to generate SigV4-signed HTTP requests for this error action's HTTP endpoint.
The AWS service name (e.g., 'execute-api') that the SigV4 signature is generated for, used to authenticate the HTTP error action request to an AWS service endpoint.
Specifies the AWS region to use when SigV4 signs requests to the HTTP endpoint in the IoT rule's error action, matching the region of the target AWS service.
Specifies whether messages from multiple MQTT topics are batched together into a single HTTP request when this error action's HTTP action uses batching, enabling batch processing across topics.

For the HTTP action used as the error action in an AWS IoT Topic Rule, this specifies the maximum time in milliseconds that a batch may remain open before it is sent, even if it has not reached the maximum batch size.
The maximum number of IoT messages to include in a single batch when the HTTP error action sends messages in batches, as part of the batch configuration for an AWS IoT topic rule.
Specifies the maximum size, in bytes, of a batch that the HTTP error action sends when batching messages to the configured HTTPS endpoint.
The URL to which AWS IoT sends a confirmation message when the topic rule is created or updated, used to verify ownership of the HTTP endpoint for the error action.
When set to true, AWS IoT batches multiple messages into a single HTTP request for the error action's HTTP endpoint, rather than sending each message separately.
Specifies the HTTP headers to include in the request sent by the error action's HTTP target to the endpoint.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the outgoing request when this rule's error action invokes the configured HTTP endpoint.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the error action's HTTP request.
The URL of the HTTP endpoint to which AWS IoT sends the message when the rule's primary action fails, as specified in the error action's HTTP action.
