Specifies the AWS IoT Analytics action to execute as the error action, forwarding the message payload to an IoT Analytics channel when the primary action of the rule fails.
Determines whether the IoT Analytics error action delivers messages as a batch (true) or individually (false).
Specifies the name of the AWS IoT Analytics channel to which the error message data is sent when the IoT rule action fails.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT permission to send message data to the AWS IoT Analytics channel.
Configures the error action that sends the rule payload to an AWS IoT Events input, specifying the target input name and the IAM role that grants AWS IoT permission to write to that input.
If true, the IoT Events error action sends the batch of messages as a single input to the AWS IoT Events detector; if false, each message is sent individually.
The name of the AWS IoT Events input where the error message data is sent when the rule's main action fails.
The message ID to assign to the AWS IoT Events message sent by this error action, enabling correlation with the corresponding IoT Events input.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to call AWS IoT Events when the rule's error action is triggered.
Specifies an error action that forwards the message data to AWS IoT SiteWise, allowing device data to be ingested into SiteWise asset properties.
A list of asset property value entries that specify the data to write to AWS IoT SiteWise asset properties when this error action is triggered.
The ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset to which the property value entry is associated.
A unique entry identifier required for each asset property value entry in the IoT SiteWise batch put operation, used to map the entry to the corresponding response and error results.
The alias of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property that the IoT rule writes the message payload data to, used instead of the property ID when writing values.
The ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property to which this entry writes the value.
Specifies the list of asset property values to write to AWS IoT SiteWise for the associated property, including each value's timestamp, quality, and numeric value.
The quality string specifies the quality of the asset property value ('GOOD', 'BAD', or 'UNCERTAIN') when writing to AWS IoT SiteWise from an IoT rule error action.
Specifies the timestamp for an asset property value, including the Unix epoch time in seconds (TimeInSeconds) and an optional offset in nanoseconds (OffsetInNanos).
The nanosecond offset component of the timestamp, which is added to the timeInSeconds value to provide sub-second precision for the asset property value entry.
Specifies the Unix epoch time in seconds for the timestamp of the asset property value entry, provided as a string, to record when the value was captured.
Defines the asset property value variant to write in the AWS IoT SiteWise action, containing exactly one of a boolean, double, integer, or string value to publish to the asset property.
The Boolean value to send to AWS IoT SiteWise as the asset property value when the property data type is BOOLEAN, within the put asset property value entry of the IoT SiteWise error action.

The `double_value` field specifies the double-precision floating-point numeric value to be written to the IoT SiteWise asset property when the corresponding value type is set to double, as part of the put asset property value entries in the error action of an AWS IoT topic rule.
The integer value to write to the IoT SiteWise asset property, specified as a string (e.g., "42") in the put asset property value entry.
The string value to write to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when using the string variant of an asset property value in an error action of an AWS IoT rule.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to send data to AWS IoT SiteWise when the primary action fails and this error action is invoked.
Defines the Kafka action configuration used as the error action for an AWS IoT TopicRule, specifying the destination broker and topic to which messages are sent when the rule's primary action fails.
The map of Kafka client configuration properties (key-value pairs) applied to the Kafka producer connection when this error action sends message data to the configured Kafka topic.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK) cluster that the error action delivers messages to.
Specifies a list of Kafka message headers (each with a key and value) to include when the IoT rule sends a message to Kafka as part of an error action.
The key for a Kafka message header attached to the message sent to the Kafka topic when this IoT rule error action is triggered.
The value of a Kafka message header to include when the IoT rule's Kafka action is used as an error action, which can contain substitution templates such as ${topic()} or ${payload().field}.
Specifies the Kafka message key to be included in the Kafka record when the AWS IoT rule's error action sends data to the configured Kafka topic.
The Kafka partition (or a substitution template resolving to it) to which the message is sent when this IoT Topic Rule error action writes to Kafka.
Specifies the Kafka topic to which the error action publishes message data when the IoT rule's main action fails.
Specifies the configuration for sending data to an Amazon Kinesis stream as the error action when the primary rule action fails.
For the Kinesis action used as an error action in this IoT rule, this sets the partition key that determines the Kinesis shard to which the message data is written.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT permission to put data to the associated Kinesis stream when this error action is triggered instead of the main action.
The name of the Amazon Kinesis data stream to which the IoT rule sends error output when the main action fails.
The Lambda action to invoke when the rule's primary action fails, specifying the function ARN and optional parameters for the error action.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function that AWS IoT invokes as the error action when the rule's primary action fails.
The Amazon Location Service action to use as the error action for this AWS IoT rule, which sends device location data to a tracker when the primary rule action fails.
The unique device identifier that AWS IoT includes in the location update sent to Amazon Location Service when this rule's error action invokes the location action.
The latitude coordinate to be reported by the AWS IoT Location action when it is used as the error action for this AWS IoT Topic Rule, specified as a string that can contain substitution templates.
The longitude (in decimal degrees) for the Amazon Location Service action used as the error action of this IoT topic rule, sent when the rule's primary action fails.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to access the Amazon Location Service resource when an error action of type location is triggered.
Specifies the timestamp value and unit that AWS IoT uses when the error action sends a location update to Amazon Location Service, identifying when the device location was captured.
The unit of time in which the timestamp's value is expressed (e.g., seconds or milliseconds) for the AWS IoT Location action within the error action of a topic rule.

The timestamp value to send with the device location update to Amazon Location Service when this AWSS IoT rule error action triggers, typically an epoch time in milliseconds or an expression that evaluates to a time.
The name of the Amazon Location Service tracker that receives the device position data when this IoT rule's error action executes.
Specifies the OpenSearch Service action configuration used as the error action, which sends device data to an Amazon OpenSearch domain when the rule's primary action fails.
The endpoint URL of the Amazon OpenSearch Service domain to which the IoT rule's error action writes data.
The unique document ID used when writing the message payload to the OpenSearch index in this IoT Topic Rule error action.
Specifies the OpenSearch index to which the IoT rule's error action writes message data, matching the `index` field of the AWS IoT OpenSearch action.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to write error data to the Amazon OpenSearch Service domain when the main topic rule action fails.
The document type to be indexed in the OpenSearch domain when this IoT rule error action fires, specifying the item type within the designated index.
Defines the AWS IoT Republish action that publishes the triggering message to a different MQTT topic when the rule's primary action fails.
Configures MQTT headers (including content type, correlation data, message expiry, response topic, and user properties) attached to the message republished by this error action.
The MQTT Content Type header to set on the republished message, describing the payload format (e.g., 'application/json').
Sets the MQTT 5 correlation data header value for the republished message in the AWS IoT republish action.

Specifies the message expiry interval in seconds for the MQTT message when republished through the AWS IoT republish action, controlling how long the message remains valid before it expires if not delivered.
Sets the MQTT 5 payload format indicator in the republished message's headers, where 1 indicates a UTF-8 encoded JSON payload and 0 indicates an unspecified binary payload.
The MQTT 5 response topic included in the republished message headers from the error action, allowing the receiving client to send a response to that topic.
Specifies a list of MQTT 5.0 user property key-value pairs to include in the republished message headers when the rule's republish error action executes.
Specifies the key (name) of an MQTT user property to include in the republished message headers when the error action's republish step sends the message to the configured MQTT topic.
The value of a user property key-value pair included in the MQTT header when the republish action is used as the error action of the IoT rule.
The Quality of Service (QoS) level (0 or 1) used when this republish action, as an error action, publishes the message to the destination MQTT topic.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to republish the message to the designated MQTT topic when the primary action fails and this republish error action is triggered.
The MQTT topic to which the republish action sends the message when the rule's primary action fails and this error action is triggered.
The S3 error action writes the IoT message to an Amazon S3 bucket (using the given bucket, key, and IAM role) when the rule's primary action fails to execute.
The name of the S3 bucket to which the AWS IoT rule error action sends the message payload when the rule's primary action fails.
The canned ACL (e.g., 'private', 'public-read') to apply to the object stored in Amazon S3 when this error action writes the message payload.
The object key (path) in the S3 bucket where the IoT rule error action writes the message payload.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to write to the specified S3 bucket.
Configuration for the SNS error action, which publishes a message to an Amazon SNS topic when the rule's main action fails.
Specifies the format of the message sent to the Amazon SNS topic, with valid values RAW or JSON (defaulting to RAW).
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to publish to the Amazon SNS topic when the rule action fails, used in the error action's SNS configuration.
The ARN of the SNS topic that receives the error message when the rule's main action fails.
Specifies the Amazon SQS action that AWS IoT executes as the error action when the rule's main action fails, sending the message to a configured SQS queue.
The URL of the Amazon SQS queue to which the IoT message is sent when this error action is triggered.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT permission to send messages to the Amazon SQS queue in the error action.
Specifies whether the message payload is Base64-encoded before the SQS action sends it to the queue.

Specifies a Step Functions error action for an AWS IoT rule, so that when the rule's primary action fails, AWS IoT starts an execution of the referenced Step Functions state machine using the configured IAM role.
Specifies a prefix prepended to the Step Functions execution name when this IoT rule error action invokes the state machine, helping identify the related executions.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to invoke the Step Functions state machine when an error occurs in the topic rule's action.
The name of the Step Functions state machine to invoke as the error action for the IoT rule.
Configures an Amazon Timestream action for error handling, so that when the IoT rule fails, the error payload is written to a Timestream table using the specified database, role, and dimensions.
The name of the Amazon Timestream database to which the IoT rule writes error-action data when the configured action fails.
A list of Dimension objects that specify the metadata key-value pairs to be written with each Timestream record in the error action of an AWS IoT rule.
Specifies the name of the dimension that will be added to the Timestream record when the IoT rule error action writes to Timestream.
The value of the dimension to include in each Timestream record, which can be a static string or a substitution template such as ${topic} populated from the MQTT message payload.
The ARN of an IAM role that grants AWS IoT permission to write to the Amazon Timestream database and table when used as an error action in the topic rule.
Specifies the name of the Amazon Timestream table that the IoT rule's Timestream error action writes to when a rule action fails.
Configures the timestamp value and unit (e.g., milliseconds or seconds) used when writing the IoT rule payload to Amazon Timestream, overriding the default Timestream timestamp.
The unit of time for the timestamp value in the Timestream error action of an AWS IoT rule, such as MILLISECONDS, SECONDS, MICROSECONDS, or NANOSECONDS.

Specifies the timestamp value to be written to the Timestream table's timestamp column when the IoT rule's error action writes to Timestream, typically expressed as a substitution template or SQL expression.

aws_io_t_topic_rule.topic_rule_payload.r.text: Indicates whether the AWS IoT topic rule is disabled, preventing it from triggering actions on incoming messages.

aws_io_t_topic_rule.topic_rule_payload.s.text: The SQL SELECT query that the AWS IoT rule uses to transform and filter messages from the MQTT topic before the rule's actions are triggered.

aws_io_t_topic_rule_destination.http_url.text: Specifies the HTTP destination's confirmation URL, which AWS IoT uses to verify ownership of the endpoint before activating the topic rule destination.
The URL of the HTTP endpoint where AWS IoT sends a confirmation message to verify the destination's ownership.

aws_io_t_topic_rule_destination.status.text: Sets the desired status (ENABLED or DISABLED) of the AWS IoT topic rule destination, controlling whether it can be used by IoT rule actions.

aws_io_t_topic_rule_destination.vpc_prop.text: Defines the VPC configuration for the IoT topic rule destination, including the subnets and security groups that the destination uses to deliver messages to resources inside a VPC.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT assumes to access the VPC for the topic rule destination's VPC configuration.
Specifies the list of security group IDs to attach to the VPC endpoint used by the AWS IoT TopicRuleDestination, controlling network access to the destination.
The IDs of the subnets in the VPC that the IoT topic rule destination is associated with, used to define the network location for the destination.
The ID of the VPC in which the topic rule destination's network resources are provisioned, used with subnet and security-group settings to route AWS IoT rule actions to VPC targets.

aws_io_tanalytics_channel.channel_name.text: The name of the AWS IoT Analytics channel; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name for the channel.

aws_io_tanalytics_channel.channel_storag.text: Configures the storage destination for the channel's message data, choosing between an AWS IoT Analytics service-managed S3 bucket or a customer-managed S3 bucket.
Specifies the customer-managed S3 bucket configuration where the IoT Analytics channel stores its data, including the bucket name and optional key prefix.
The name of the S3 bucket in which the channel's data is stored when using customer-managed S3 storage.
Specifies the key prefix for objects stored in the customer-managed S3 bucket in the IoT Analytics channel's storage, used to organize or filter the channel data.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT Analytics assumes to access the customer-managed S3 bucket for storing channel data.
Specifies that AWS IoT Analytics uses a service-managed S3 bucket for channel storage, indicated by the presence of this empty object.

aws_io_tanalytics_channel.retention_peri.text: Specifies how long message data is kept in the channel, either as a finite number of days or indefinitely.
Specifies the number of days that message data in the channel is retained, after which it is automatically deleted.

When set to true, the channel retains its data indefinitely with no automatic expiration, and when false you must supply a finite retention period in days using the `numberOfDays` field of the same `retentionPeriod` object.

aws_io_tanalytics_channel.tags.text: Tags are key-value pairs that you can attach to an AWS IoT Analytics channel to help identify and organize the channel, and they can be used for resource-level access control and cost tracking.

aws_io_tanalytics_channel.tags.value.text: The value of a tag associated with an AWS IoT Analytics channel, used to assign metadata for resource tracking and management.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.actions.text: The actions define the orders of operations that create the dataset content, either by running a SQL query on the IoT Analytics data store or by invoking a containerized application to transform the data.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.actions.action.text: A user-defined string that names this IoT Analytics dataset action, distinguishing it from other actions in the dataset's actions list.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.actions.contai.text: Defines the container action that runs a Docker container to execute custom code for generating the dataset content, including the Docker image, execution role, and resource configuration.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants the container action access to the AWS resources it needs to execute, such as data in the datastore or output to other services.
The Docker image used to run the container action for the IoT Analytics dataset.
Defines the compute resources (CPU and memory) allocated to the container that runs the container action for the IoT Analytics dataset.
Specifies the compute type (e.g., ACU_1 or ACU_2) allocated for the container action's resource configuration in the AWS IoT Analytics dataset.
Specifies the size, in gigabytes, of the volume to allocate to the container's storage for this IoT Analytics dataset container action.
Provides the set of variables (name-value pairs) that are passed as environment parameters to the container when the dataset's container action runs.
Configures this container action variable to take its value from the content of the specified dataset (via its DatasetName), effectively supplying the latest dataset content version to the container.
The name of the source AWS IoT Analytics dataset whose latest content version is used to populate this variable in the container action.
Specifies the double-precision numeric value for this container action variable, which will be passed as a parameter to the containerized application when the dataset content is produced.
This object holds the Amazon S3 file name (URI) of an output file produced by the container action, which is used as the value for this variable.
Sets the string value of a variable in the container action's variable list, used to pass a fixed string parameter to the container that generates the dataset content.
The name of the variable to pass to the container action, which is used to identify the value in the container's environment.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.actions.query_.text: This object defines a query action that executes an SQL query against the IoT Analytics data source to generate the dataset's content.

A list of filter objects, each containing an 'Include' time-window expression that restricts the rows returned by the query action to a specific time range (e.g., '1hour'), thereby controlling the dataset content.
Defines the time-based filter for the IoT Analytics dataset query, using an offset in seconds and a time expression (e.g., cron) to limit data to a specific sliding time window.
The number of seconds before the current time from which to include data in the dataset query, used to define a rolling time window.
Provides the time expression (e.g., 'timestamp') that names the message timestamp field used by the delta-time filter to select records within the query's relative time window.
The SQL query that is executed against the IoT Analytics data store to populate this dataset when the query action runs.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.content_delive.text: Defines the content delivery rules for the dataset, which automate delivery of dataset contents to a destination (such as an Amazon S3 bucket) according to each rule's schedule or trigger configuration.

Specifies the destination configuration for delivering dataset content, which can be either an S3 bucket (via S3DestinationConfiguration) or an AWS IoT Events input (via IotEventsDestinationConfiguration), as part of a content delivery rule for the AWS IoT Analytics dataset.
Configuration for delivering dataset content to an AWS IoT Events input, specifying the input name and the IAM role used to write the content.
The name of the AWS IoT Events input that receives the dataset contents when this content delivery rule is triggered.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT Analytics permission to deliver dataset contents to the specified AWS IoT Events input.
Specifies the configuration for delivering dataset content to an Amazon S3 bucket, including the target bucket, key prefix, and output format.
The name of the S3 bucket where the dataset content is delivered when the content delivery rule triggers.
Specifies the AWS Glue configuration for the S3 destination, including the database and table names under which the dataset content is registered in the Glue Data Catalog.
The name of the AWS Glue database in which the dataset's table is registered when content delivery exports the dataset to Amazon S3 via AWS Glue.
The name of the AWS Glue table that the IoT Analytics dataset content is delivered to when using the S3 destination with Glue configuration.

The S3 object key template (for example, `dataset/{version}/data.json`) under the destination bucket where IoT Analytics dataset contents are delivered, with the `{version}` placeholder replaced by the dataset content version.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT Analytics permission to write the dataset content to the S3 bucket defined in this destination configuration.

For each content delivery rule in an AWS IoT Analytics dataset's content_delivery_rules list, this string provides the rule's entry name, which is used to identify the delivery rule when the dataset content is delivered to its configured destination (e.g., an Amazon S3 bucket).

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.dataset_name.text: The name to assign to the AWS IoT Analytics dataset; if not provided, CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.late_data_rule.text: Defines the late data rules for the AWS IoT Analytics dataset, each specifying a delta-time configuration that determines when late-arriving data should trigger a dataset content update.
Contains the delta time session window configuration for the late data rule, specifying the timeout in minutes during which late data can still be included in the dataset.

Configures the delta time session window for a late data rule, defining the maximum delay in minutes between when a data point was emitted and when it arrives, during which the IoT Analytics dataset will still include it in its content.
The timeout in minutes for the delta time session window, which specifies how long the dataset waits for late data before considering it missing.
The name of the late data rule, which identifies the rule that configures a delayed data session window for handling late-arriving data in the IoT Analytics dataset.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.retention_peri.text: Specifies how long the dataset's data is retained, either for a finite number of days or indefinitely.
Specifies the number of days that dataset contents are retained before they are automatically deleted.
When true, the dataset content is retained indefinitely, and any specified number of days is ignored; when false, content is retained for the specified number of days.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs used to tag the AWS IoT Analytics dataset for identification and categorization.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.tags.key.text: The Key of a tag attached to the AWS IoT Analytics dataset, used to identify the tag within the resource's set of tags.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the IoT Analytics dataset, used for user-defined metadata and resource management.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.triggers.text: Specifies the list of triggers that determine when the dataset content is generated, each trigger containing either a schedule cron expression or a reference to another dataset whose content creation triggers this dataset.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.triggers.sched.text: Specifies the schedule (cron expression) that determines when this trigger initiates dataset content creation.
The cron-based schedule expression that defines when this trigger runs to refresh the IoT Analytics dataset.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.triggers.trigg.text: This object names another IoT Analytics dataset whose content generation, when completed, automatically triggers an update of this dataset's content.
The name of the dataset whose successful completion triggers the creation of this dataset.

aws_io_tanalytics_dataset.versioning_con.text: Configures how dataset content versions are retained, specifying either unlimited versioning or a maximum number of versions to keep.
Maximum number of dataset content versions to retain when dataset versioning is enabled.
When true, the dataset keeps all versions of its content without a limit, overriding the maxVersions setting; when false, the number of versions is limited by maxVersions.

aws_io_tanalytics_datastore.datastore_na.text: The unique name of the AWS IoT Analytics datastore, which is optional; if omitted, AWS CloudFormation generates a unique physical ID for the datastore.

aws_io_tanalytics_datastore.datastore_pa.text: This object defines the time-based partitioning configuration for the IoT Analytics datastore, allowing data to be partitioned by a specified time period such as month or week.

Defines the list of partition configurations for the AWS IoT Analytics datastore, where each partition is specified as either a timestamp-based partition (with an attribute name and interval like DAY or HOUR) or an attribute-based partition (with an attribute name).
Defines a partition for the IoT Analytics data store by specifying the message attribute name that acts as the partition key.

The name of the attribute (column) in the AWS IoT Analytics datastore that is used to partition the data when the partition is defined by a simple attribute (as opposed to a timestamp-based partition).
Defines a timestamp-based partition dimension for the data store, using a specified attribute name and timestamp format to group data by time intervals.
The name of the timestamp attribute in the message payload that AWS IoT Analytics uses to create time-based partitions within the datastore.
Specifies the timestamp format (e.g., a Java SimpleDateFormat pattern) used by the timestamp partition to determine time-based partitioning of data in the AWS IoT Analytics data store.

aws_io_tanalytics_datastore.datastore_st.text: Configure the storage type for the IoT Analytics datastore, choosing between AWS-managed S3 or a customer-managed S3 bucket with an optional prefix for data storage.

Specifies the customer-managed S3 bucket and optional key prefix where the AWS IoT Analytics datastore stores its data, used when you choose to provide your own S3 storage instead of using the service-managed storage.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket in which the datastore stores its data when using customer-managed S3 storage.
The key prefix under which IoT Analytics stores datastore data in the customer-managed S3 bucket.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT Analytics permission to access the customer-managed S3 bucket used for datastore storage.
Specifies the AWS IoT SiteWise multi-layer storage configuration for the datastore, which stores data in a customer-managed Amazon S3 bucket via the nested `customerManagedS3` setting.
This object defines the customer-managed S3 bucket (with an optional key prefix) where the AWS IoT Analytics datastore stores its data when using IoT SiteWise multi-layer storage.
The name of the S3 bucket where the IoT Analytics datastore data is stored when using customer-managed S3 storage.
Specifies the key prefix in the customer-managed S3 bucket under which AWS IoT Analytics stores the multi-layer storage data for the datastore.
When defined, this object indicates that the datastore uses AWS IoT Analytics-managed S3 storage, meaning the service provisions and manages the S3 bucket on your behalf.

aws_io_tanalytics_datastore.file_format_.text: Defines the file format (JSON or Parquet) used for data stored in the IoT Analytics datastore, including the Parquet schema when that format is selected.
Specifies that the datastore uses the JSON file format, an empty structure that selects JSON as the storage format for message data.
Defines the Parquet file format settings for the datastore, including the schema definition that specifies the columns and data types for the data stored.
Specifies the schema definition (column names and data types) that AWS IoT Analytics uses to interpret the data in the datastore when the file format is configured for Parquet.
Defines the list of columns that make up the schema of the Parquet file format in the datastore, with each column specifying its name and data type for the stored data.
Specifies the name of a column in the Parquet schema definition for the datastore, which is used to interpret incoming message data when stored in Parquet format.
Specifies the data type (e.g., STRING, INTEGER, DOUBLE) for a column in the Parquet schema definition of an AWS IoT Analytics datastore's file format configuration.

aws_io_tanalytics_datastore.id.text: The computed unique identifier of the AWS IoT Analytics datastore, which is the datastore name assigned by the provider.

aws_io_tanalytics_datastore.retention_pe.text: The retention period object specifies how long AWS IoT Analytics retains the data in this datastore, either as a finite number of days via `number_of_days` or as unlimited storage via the `unlimited` flag.
The number of days for which IoT Analytics retains data in the data store before it is automatically deleted.
When true, the datastore retains its data indefinitely, and the number of days specified in the retention period is ignored.

aws_io_tanalytics_datastore.tags.text: A list of objects that define key-value metadata tags to associate with the IoT Analytics data store for identification and management.

aws_io_tanalytics_datastore.tags.value.text: The value of a tag associated with an AWS IoT Analytics datastore, used as user-defined metadata to organize or identify the resource.

aws_io_tanalytics_pipeline.id.text: The unique identifier of the IoT Analytics pipeline, which is set to the pipeline name specified in the configuration.

aws_io_tanalytics_pipeline.pipeline_acti.text: Specifies the ordered list of pipeline activities (such as filter, select attributes, math, device registry, and channel or datastore writes) that process messages as they flow through the IoT Analytics pipeline.
Defines an AddAttributes activity, which adds the specified attributes to the message payload within an AWS IoT Analytics pipeline.
Defines the key-value pairs of attributes to add to the message in the AddAttributes pipeline activity, where each key is the attribute name and the value is the attribute value (both strings).
Specifies the name of the addAttributes pipeline activity, which uniquely identifies this activity within the AWS IoT Analytics pipeline.
The name of the next activity in the pipeline to execute after this AddAttributes activity, chaining the processing steps in sequence.

Defines a channel activity that specifies the AWS IoT Analytics channel from which the pipeline reads messages as its source, including the activity's name, the channel name, and the next activity in the pipeline.
The name of the AWS IoTAnalytics channel from which this pipeline activity reads messages.
The name of the channel activity within the IoT Analytics pipeline, which uniquely identifies this activity in the pipeline's activity list.
Specifies the name of the next activity in the pipeline to execute after this channel activity, enabling the chaining of processing steps.
Defines a datastore activity that writes the incoming messages to a specified AWS IoTAnalytics datastore, identified by its datastore name.
The name of the IoT Analytics datastore to which this pipeline activity writes data.
The name of this datastore activity inside an AWS IoT Analytics pipeline, serving as a unique identifier for the activity within the pipeline's ordered activity list.

This object configures a DeviceRegistryEnrich pipeline activity that uses the AWS IoT device registry to look up device attributes by the device ID in each message and add them to the message payload.
The name of the message attribute that AWS IoT Analytics populates with the device registry information for the IoT thing specified in the thingName property.
The name of the device registry enrichment activity, which serves as the unique reference identifier used by the `next` property of other pipeline activities to chain execution.
The name of the next activity in the pipeline to execute after this device registry enrich activity.
ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS IoT Analytics permission to read from the AWS IoT device registry to enrich messages with device metadata.
Specifies the name of the AWS IoT thing whose registry data is retrieved and added to the message by the DeviceRegistryEnrich activity.
This object configures a device shadow enrichment activity, which retrieves the latest device shadow state for a specified IoT thing and adds it to the message payload.
The name of the device shadow attribute whose value is read and added to the message payload by the DeviceShadowEnrich activity.
Specifies a unique name for the device shadow enrich activity within the pipeline, used to reference this activity in the pipeline's activity list.
The name of the next pipeline activity to run after this device shadow enrichment step.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT Analytics assumes to access the device shadow data for the enrich activity.
The name of the AWS IoT thing whose shadow is used to enrich the message data in the device shadow enrich activity.
The filter block defines an IoT Analytics pipeline filter activity, which passes only messages that satisfy the specified filter expression on to the next pipeline activity.
The expression used by the filter activity to select which messages in the pipeline are passed to the next activity, retaining only those that satisfy the condition.
The name that uniquely identifies the filter activity within the IoT Analytics pipeline, used to refer to this activity in the pipeline's data processing flow.
Specifies the name of the next pipeline activity to execute after this Filter activity completes.

The lambda activity configuration in an AWS IoT Analytics pipeline, specifying the Lambda function name (lambdaName), the batch size for processing messages, and the name of the next activity to execute.
The maximum number of messages that the Lambda activity passes to its configured Lambda function in a single invocation (batch size).
The name of the AWS Lambda function that this activity invokes to process message data in the AWS IoTAnalytics pipeline.
The name of the Lambda activity, which must be unique within the AWS IoT Analytics pipeline.
The name of the next activity in the pipeline to execute after this Lambda activity completes.
Specifies the math activity in the pipeline, which performs arithmetic operations on message attributes and assigns the computed value to a specified attribute for further processing.
The name of the IoT Analytics message attribute that will store the result of the math expression evaluated by this pipeline activity.
The mathematical expression to evaluate for the Math activity, written using IoT Analytics expression syntax.
The name of the math activity, which identifies it within the IoT Analytics pipeline for reference by other activities.
Specifies the name of the next pipeline activity to run after this math activity in the AWS IoT Analytics pipeline.
The remove_attributes block configures a RemoveAttributes pipeline activity, which removes the specified attributes from each message processed by the AWS IoT Analytics pipeline.
Specifies the list of attribute names to remove from the message payload in the RemoveAttributes pipeline activity.

The name of the removeAttributes activity within the pipeline, which must be unique across all activities in the pipeline and is used by the IoT Analytics service to identify this activity when processing messages.
Specifies the name of the next pipeline activity to execute after the 'removeAttributes' activity removes the listed attributes from the message.

Configuration for a selectAttributes pipeline activity that creates a new message containing only the specified attributes from the original message, discarding all others before passing it to the next activity.
Specifies the list of message attribute names to keep in the output message when the SelectAttributes pipeline activity creates a new message from the input.
The name of the select_attributes activity, which must be unique within the pipeline and is used to identify the activity in the pipeline's activity list.
Specifies the name of the next pipeline activity to execute after this select attributes activity in the AWS IoT Analytics pipeline.

aws_io_tanalytics_pipeline.pipeline_name.text: The name of the AWS IoT Analytics pipeline, which serves as the pipeline identifier and must be unique within the AWS account and region.

aws_io_tanalytics_pipeline.tags.text: Attaches a list of key-value tags to the IoT Analytics pipeline, which can be used for cost allocation, resource categorization, and access control via IAM policies.

aws_io_tanalytics_pipeline.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS IoT Analytics pipeline, which is a custom string used to categorize and identify the pipeline for management and cost allocation purposes.

aws_io_tcore_device_advisor_suite_defini.text: Defines the core configuration for the Device Advisor suite definition, including the device permission role ARN, devices under test, root group, and suite definition name.
The ARN of the X.509 certificate that identifies the device under test in the Device Advisor suite definition's device configuration.
The ARN of the AWS IoT thing that the Device Advisor suite definition will test, identifying the device under test.
The key of a tag assigned to the AWS IoT Core Device Advisor suite definition, used for resource categorization and management.
The value of a tag (identified by its key) attached to the AWS IoT Device Advisor suite definition, used to add custom metadata for identifying, organizing, and managing this resource.

aws_io_tevents_alarm_model.alarm_event_a.text: Configuration for writing the alarm state to an Amazon DynamoDB table when the alarm changes state.
The name of the hash key (partition key) column in the Amazon DynamoDB table where AWS IoT Events writes the alarm event data.
Specifies the data type of the hash key value (e.g., 'STRING' or 'NUMBER') that is written to the DynamoDB table when the alarm action triggers.

The value to use for the partition (hash) key when this alarm event's DynamoDB action writes a record to the configured table, which can be a literal string or an expression evaluated from the alarm input payload.
Specifies the DynamoDB operation (such as INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE) that the alarm action performs on the table.
Defines the content and format of the payload sent to the DynamoDB table, specifying the expression and payload type (JSON or STRING) for the DynamoDB action in the alarm's event actions.

Defines the content of the DynamoDB payload in the alarm action by evaluating a string expression that can include variables such as alarm state, input variables, and other contextual data at the time the alarm action executes.
The type of payload for the DynamoDB alarm action, specifying whether the content expression is formatted as JSON or as a string.
Specifies the name of the DynamoDB table column that receives the action payload for this DynamoDB alarm action.
Specifies the name of the range key column in the target Amazon DynamoDB table where the IoT Events alarm action writes the alarm data.
Specifies the data type of the range key for the DynamoDB table entry written by this alarm action, with allowed values 'STRING' or 'NUMBER'.
Specifies the value to write to the range (sort) key attribute of the DynamoDB table when this alarm event triggers the DynamoDB action.
The name of the Amazon DynamoDB table to which the alarm action writes data when triggered.
Specifies a DynamoDB v2 action that writes alarm state data to an Amazon DynamoDB table.
Defines the payload (content expression and type) sent to the DynamoDB table via the DynamoDBv2 action when the alarm event is triggered.
The expression that defines the JSON content (the DynamoDB item) written by the DynamoDBv2 action when an alarm event triggers the action.
This field defines the payload encoding type for the DynamoDBv2 alarm action, with allowed values 'STRING' or 'JSON' to determine how the payload content is structured.
The name of the DynamoDB table to which the alarm data is written by this DynamoDBv2 action.
Configuration for sending an alarm message to a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream, including the delivery stream name and an optional payload.
Specifies the name of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that receives the alarm event data when this Firehose action is triggered from the alarm model's alarm event actions.
Defines the body of the message that is sent to the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream when an alarm triggers the Firehose action, using a content expression and payload type.
Specifies the expression that defines the content of the data payload sent to the Firehose delivery stream when this alarm action is triggered.
Determines whether the payload sent to the Firehose delivery stream is formatted as JSON or as a raw string, with allowed values 'JSON' or 'STRING'.
The separator string (such as a newline or comma) that is inserted between the payloads of multiple alarm events when they are delivered to the Kinesis Data Firehose stream.
Specifies the AWS IoT Events action that sends the alarm data to a target IoT Events input, including the required input name and optional payload configuration.
The name of the AWS IoT Events input that the alarm action sends the alarm event data to.
The payload specifies the content of the input message sent to the AWS IoT Events detector model when the alarm action triggers, typically containing an expression that defines the message body.
Specifies the expression that defines the payload content sent to AWS IoT Events when this alarm action fires, allowing interpolation of input variables and static text.
Specifies the format of the payload sent to AWS IoT Events, either as a JSON object (JSON) or as a plain string (STRING).

The IotSiteWise action configuration for alarm actions, which specifies the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property (by asset ID, property ID, or alias) to which the alarm state is written, optionally including an entry ID.
The ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset to which alarm data is written when an alarm event occurs.
The unique identifier for the property value entry sent to AWS IoT SiteWise, which is used to deduplicate request entries and prevent duplicate data writes when the alarm action is triggered.
Specifies the alias of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property to which the alarm action sends data (alarm state or value) when the alarm event occurs.
The ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property that the alarm action writes alarm event data to.

Specifies the value to write to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when the alarm action executes, defined as an AssetPropertyValue structure that includes a Variant (such as integer, double, string, or boolean) and an optional timestamp.
Sets the quality (GOOD, BAD, or UNCERTAIN) for the asset property value that the alarm action writes to AWS IoT SiteWise.
The timestamp object specifies the Unix epoch time (in seconds and optional nanosecond offset) associated with the asset property value sent to AWS IoT SiteWise from the alarm model's alarm actions.
The offset in nanoseconds past the associated second (time_in_seconds) that together form the full timestamp for the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property value written by the alarm action.
Specifies the epoch time in seconds for the timestamp of the AWS IoT SiteWise property value written when the alarm action executes.
The value object defines the actual data variant (string, integer, double, or boolean) to write to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when the alarm action is invoked.
The string representation of a boolean value ('true' or 'false') for the asset property that AWS IoT Events writes when an alarm action triggers an Iot SiteWise property value update.
The double_value field specifies the double-precision floating-point value that gets sent to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property as part of the alarm action's property value update.
Sets the integer value to write to the specified AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when the alarm action is triggered, as a string representation of the integer.
The string value to assign to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when the alarm action writes the property value, used when the property data type is STRING.
Specifies the IoT Topic Publish action parameters, including the MQTT topic to publish to and the payload message to send when the alarm is triggered.
The MQTT topic to which AWS IoT Events publishes the alarm state change payload when this IotTopicPublish action is triggered.

Defines the content and format of the message payload sent to the AWS IoT Core MQTT topic by this alarm action, using an expression (e.g., a string or JSON object) that is evaluated to generate the published payload.

Specifies an expression or static string that evaluates to the payload content published to the AWS IoT Core topic when the alarm action sends an IoT Topic Publish message, and which can reference input variables and alarm data.
Specifies the payload format type (either 'STRING' or 'JSON') for the MQTT message content that AWS IoT Events publishes to the IoT topic in this alarm action.
Specifies the AWS Lambda function (by ARN) and the input payload that AWS IoT Events invokes when the alarm is triggered.
The ARN of the Lambda function that AWS IoT Events invokes when the alarm action is triggered.

Defines the payload sent to the AWS Lambda function when the alarm action triggers, including a content expression and a format type (JSON or STRING) that controls how alarm data is serialized in the invocation.
The expression that is evaluated to produce the JSON or string content of the payload sent to the Lambda function when this alarm action is triggered.
Specifies whether the Lambda action payload is a literal string (STRING) or a JSON expression (JSON).
Specifies the SNS action details, including the target ARN and optional payload, used to send a notification when the alarm event occurs.
Configuration for the message payload sent to the SNS topic, including the content expression and payload type (STRING or JSON).
The expression that generates the payload content sent to the SNS topic when the alarm event action is triggered.
Specifies the format of the SNS actionable payload in an alarm event action, where JSON sends the payload as a structured JSON object and STRING sends it as plain text.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic to which the alarm action sends a notification when the alarm is triggered.

Defines an SQS (Simple Queue Service) action for the alarm event, specifying the target queue URL and optionally whether the message payload is base64-encoded, to which the alarm notification is sent.
Defines the message body sent to the SQS queue, using a contentExpression that can reference alarm data and a type indicating whether the payload is a JSON or string.
The expression that defines the content of the SQS message payload when the alarm action is triggered.
For an SQS action in an IoT Events alarm model, this field defines the payload type (either STRING or JSON) that controls how the payload content is structured in the message sent to the SQS queue.
The URL of the SQS queue to which the alarm action sends a message.
Indicates whether to Base64-encode the message payload before sending it to the SQS queue in the alarm action.

aws_io_tevents_alarm_model.tags.key.text: Defines the key portion of a tag attached to the AWS IoT Events alarm model, allowing you to categorize and identify the alarm model with custom metadata.

aws_io_tevents_detector_model.detector_m.text: Defines the events and actions that execute when a detector transitions into this state in the AWS IoT Events detector model.
Defines the list of events that are evaluated when the detector instance enters this state, where each event specifies its name, condition, and actions to execute.
Specifies the list of actions to execute when this 'on enter' event is triggered, such as setting a variable, resetting a timer, or sending a message to an AWS IoT topic or other AWS service.
Defines a ClearTimer action that stops a previously started timer by its name, preventing the timer's timeout event from firing.
The name of the timer to clear when this action is executed, matching the timer set by a set_timer action.
Configures a DynamoDB write action that is executed when the detector enters this state, specifying the target table name and key fields used to store the event payload.
Specifies the partition (hash) key column name in the target DynamoDB table for the write action, matched with the value expression from hash_key_value to form the item's primary key.
Specifies the data type (STRING or NUMBER) of the hash key attribute in the DynamoDB table entry that the action writes, used when the hash key value is a variable or expression.
The hash key value for the DynamoDB table entry that AWS IoT Events writes when this action is triggered from an 'on_enter' event of a detector state.
Specifies the DynamoDB write operation to perform when this action is triggered, with valid values of INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE.
Configures the payload object (defining the content expression and its type) that determines the JSON data written to the DynamoDB item for this detector model action.
The expression that computes the payload content sent to DynamoDB when this action is triggered, evaluated at event execution time using detector variables and input attributes.
Specifies the payload format for the DynamoDB action in an AWS IoT Events detector model, either STRING for a plain text payload or JSON for a structured JSON payload.
Specifies the DynamoDB attribute name that serves as the range (sort) key for the table entry written by this IoT Events DynamoDB action.
The data type (STRING or NUMBER) of the range key value used when writing to the Amazon DynamoDB table from this detector model action.
Sets the range key value for the DynamoDB entry written by this action, which can be a static string or an expression referencing input payload or detector state (e.g., '${payload.rangeKey}').
The name of the DynamoDB table that the action writes data to when the detector model enters this state, as part of an on-enter event.
Configuration for a DynamoDB v2 action that writes an item to a DynamoDB table, including the table name, key fields, and the payload to store.
Specifies the payload content expression and type (e.g., JSON) used to write data to the DynamoDB table in this DynamoDBv2 action.
Specifies the content expression for the payload of the DynamoDBv2 action executed when the detector state is entered, defining the data to write to the DynamoDB table.
The type of the payload (STRING or JSON) that determines how the content expression is interpreted when the DynamoDBv2 action writes data to the table.
Specifies the name of the DynamoDB table that the IoT Events DynamoDBv2 action writes the detector's payload to when the associated event is triggered.
Defines the Firehose action, which delivers the message payload to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream.
The name of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to which the detector model sends data when this action is triggered.

The payload configuration for the Firehose action, which specifies the content expression (a string expression) and payload type (such as JSON or STRING) that defines the data sent to the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream.

Specifies the expression that determines the content of the payload sent to the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream when this action is triggered, typically composed of input variables, static strings, and IoT Events expressions.
The payload type for the Firehose action, either JSON or STRING, which determines how the contentExpression is formatted in the data sent to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
Specifies the delimiter string inserted between each JSON message payload when the Firehose action writes to the delivery stream, defaulting to a newline if not provided.
Configures an IoT Events action that publishes an event to a specified AWS IoT Events input, including the target input name and an optional payload.
The name of the AWS IoT Events input to which this action publishes the detector model's data when the state's on-enter event is executed.
This object defines the payload content and format (JSON or string) sent to an AWS IoT Events input when the associated IoT Events action is triggered from a state's on-enter event.
Specifies the content of the payload to send to AWS IoT Events in this action, expressed as a string that can include references to detector variables using `${}` syntax.
The payload type, either STRING or JSON, which determines how the action's payload content is interpreted by AWS IoT Events when the action is triggered.

Defines an IoT SiteWise action that, when the state is entered, writes the detector's computed value to a specified AWS IoT SiteWise asset property using the configured asset ID, property ID, and property value.
The ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset to which the detector model writes the property value when the action is triggered.
Defines the unique entry identifier used to correlate the property value written to AWS IoT SiteWise when this action is triggered.
The alias of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property that receives the data from this onEnter event action.
The ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property (not its name) to which this detector model action writes output data when the on-enter event triggers.
Defines the value, timestamp, and quality of the data that AWS IoT Events writes to the specified AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when this action is triggered.
Specifies the quality (e.g., GOOD, BAD, or UNCERTAIN) assigned to the asset property value when publishing data to AWS IoT SiteWise.
Specifies the timestamp (in seconds and nanosecond offset) to associate with the property value when writing to an AWS IoT SiteWise asset property from the detector model's on-enter event action.
Specifies the nanosecond offset to add to the time in seconds when sending the property value timestamp to AWS IoT SiteWise.

The time in seconds (Unix epoch) for the property value sent to AWS IoT SiteWise, specified as a string literal or an expression (e.g., ${...}) that evaluates to the timestamp when the data was measured.
The asset property value to write to AWS IoT SiteWise, specified as a variant object containing one of a boolean, double, integer, or string value.
Sets the boolean value for the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property, as a string (e.g., 'true' or 'false'), when the property data type is BOOLEAN.
The double-precision floating-point value (represented as a string) to write to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when this action is triggered during the on-enter event of a detector state.

The integer value to write to the referenced AWS IoT SiteWise asset property, specified as a string so it can also contain IoT Events variable expressions (e.g., `${myVariable}`) that resolve to an integer.
The string representation of the value to send to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when the detector model's on-enter event action is executed.

This object configures the IoT Topic Publish action for an on-enter event, causing an MQTT message to be published to the specified AWS IoT Core topic each time the detector model enters this state, with optional payload content.
The MQTT topic to which AWS IoT Events publishes the message when this action is executed.
Defines the message payload (content expression and payload type) that AWS IoT Events publishes to the specified IoT topic when this action is triggered.

Specifies the expression that defines the payload content of the MQTT message published to an AWS IoT topic by the iotTopicPublish action, allowing dynamic values based on detector model variables and input data.
The payload type (e.g., STRING or JSON) that determines how the content expression is formatted in the message published to the IoT topic.
Specifies the lookup of an AWS Lambda function to invoke as part of the actions executed when the detector model enters the state, including the Lambda function ARN and an optional payload to pass.
The ARN of the AWS Lambda function that AWS IoT Events invokes when a detector model enters the specified state, as part of an on-enter event action.
Specifies the payload content and type (JSON or STRING) sent to the Lambda function when this on-enter event action is invoked in a detector model state.
Specifies the expression that is evaluated to generate the payload content sent to the AWS Lambda function when the action is triggered, used when the payload type is set to EXPRESSION.
The payload format (STRING or JSON) for the input data sent to the Lambda action when the detector state is entered.
The reset_timer action resets an existing timer in the detector model, specifying the timer to reset via its timerName property.
The name of the timer that the ResetTimer action targets, causing the timer to be reset to its original expiry schedule as configured in the detector model.

Defines a setTimer action that starts a named timer with a specified duration (in seconds, or via a duration expression) for the detector instance, enabling time-based state transitions or event triggering.
Specifies the duration of the timer in seconds, as a literal numeric string or an expression (e.g., a variable reference) that evaluates to a numeric duration.
The number of seconds to wait before the timer expires and triggers subsequent actions in the detector model.
The unique name assigned to the timer that this SetTimer action creates or resets, which later detector model events can reference to trigger on its expiry.
Defines a setVariable action that assigns a value (expression) to a named variable in the detector model when this event is triggered.
The value to assign to the variable in a setVariable action, which can be a string literal or an expression using input properties, variables, and functions.
The name of the variable, defined in the detector model's variable list, to which the setVariable action's value is assigned.
Defines the target SNS topic and message payload for sending notifications from an IoT Events detector model when this on-enter event is triggered.
Specifies the message content (payload) sent to the SNS topic when this action is triggered, allowing you to define a static or dynamic content expression and the payload format (JSON or string).
The expression evaluated when the action runs to generate the payload content sent to the SNS topic, allowing dynamic references to detector model state variables and input data.
Determines the format of the message sent to the SNS topic, where 'STRING' sends a raw string and 'JSON' sends a JSON object.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic to which the IoT Events detector model sends a message when this action is triggered, such as upon entering a state in the on_enter event.
Specifies the SQS queue URL and optional payload settings for sending messages to an Amazon SQS queue when the event action is triggered.
Specifies the content and format (JSON or STRING) of the message body sent to the SQS queue when this IoT Events detector model action is triggered.

Defines the expression that is evaluated to produce the body content of the message sent to the Amazon SQS queue when this event action executes, enabling dynamic values from the detector model and inputs to be included.
Specifies whether the SQS message payload is formatted as JSON or as a plain string, controlling how the content expression is encoded in the message body sent to the queue.
The URL of the Amazon SQS queue to which the action sends a message when the detector state is entered.
Enables Base64 encoding of the message body sent to the SQS queue by the detector model's IoT Events action.

For an on-enter lifecycle event of a detector-model state, this condition is a logical expression (using AWS IoT Events expression syntax) that determines whether the event's actions are executed when the state is entered.
The required unique name for this event within the state's on-enter events list, used to identify and distinguish it from other events in the detector model definition.
A list of events that run when the detector model leaves this state, allowing cleanup or final actions before transitioning.
Defines the list of events (each with an event name, optional condition, and actions) that are evaluated and executed when the detector instance exits this state.
Specifies the actions to perform when an onExit event is triggered upon leaving the state, such as setting variables, publishing to AWS IoT topics, or invoking SNS, SQS, or Lambda targets.
Clears a named timer in the detector instance, canceling the timeout action that would otherwise fire when the timer expires.
The name of the timer to clear when this ClearTimer action is executed.

Configures a DynamoDB action that writes an item to a specified Amazon DynamoDB table when the parent on-exit event fires, using fields like the hash key and optional range key to determine the table entry.
The name of the hash/partition key attribute in the target DynamoDB table that the detector model writes to in this action.
Sets the data type (STRING or NUMBER) for the hash key field of the DynamoDB action executed when the state exits.
The value of the DynamoDB hash key (partition key) used by this DynamoDB action, which can be a literal string or a computed expression (e.g., an input payload or detector state variable).
Specifies the DynamoDB operation type (INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE) that this action performs on the target table, defaulting to INSERT.
Defines the payload (content expression and type) that determines the data written to the DynamoDB table when this action executes.
The expression that generates the payload content delivered to the DynamoDB table, typically using input variables and string functions.

The payload `type` field within a DynamoDB action of an AWS IoT Events detector model's state event defines whether the `contentExpression` is evaluated as a JSON object or a plain string, determining how the DynamoDB item is constructed.
The name of the DynamoDB attribute that the input payload is written to when this `dynamodb` action runs during an `on_exit` event.
The name of the DynamoDB table column that serves as the range key for the entry written by this action.
Specifies the data type (STRING or NUMBER) for the range key in the target DynamoDB table, used when writing detector state data as an AWS IoT Events action.

Specifies the value for the range (sort) key of the DynamoDB table item, which can be a static string or a payload expression (e.g., ${payload.field}) that resolves to a string, used to identify the exact item to write or update.
The name of the DynamoDB table that the IoT Events action writes the detector's input payload to when this on-exit event action is triggered.
Configures a DynamoDBv2 action that writes the event's payload to the specified DynamoDB table, used for an on-exit event from a detector model state.
Defines the payload structure (content expression and type) that AWS IoT Events uses as the item data for the DynamoDBv2 PutItem action, executed when the detector exits the state.

Specifies the expression that evaluates to the JSON object to be written as the payload to the DynamoDBv2 table by this action when the detector model exits the state, using detector variables and input data.
Defines whether the payload sent to DynamoDB in the DynamoDBv2 action is formatted as JSON or as a plain STRING when the on-exit event fires.
The name of the DynamoDB table that the DynamoDBv2 action targets when the detector model exits this state, writing the associated payload entry to that table.
Specifies a Firehose action that sends the detector model's event data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream when the state is exited.
The name of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to which the detector model action sends the message payload.
Configures the payload content and format (JSON or string expression) sent to the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream when the exit event triggers the action.
This field defines the IoT Events content expression that is evaluated to produce the data payload sent to the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream when the on-exit event action fires.
Specifies the payload format (STRING or JSON) for the data sent to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose in this IoT Events detector model exit action.
The separator string (e.g., a newline or comma) that AWS IoT Events inserts between each data record when delivering payloads to the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream.
Specifies the AWS IoT Events input (and optional message ID and payload) to which the event is sent, enabling the detector model to trigger other IoT Events workflows.
The name of the AWS IoT Events input that receives the event data when this action is triggered.
Specifies the payload (content expression and its type) for the AWS IoT Events action sent when the detector state's on-exit event fires.

The expression that defines the content of the payload sent to another AWS IoT Events detector model when the action is triggered, allowing dynamic interpolation of detector state, variables, and input values.
Specifies whether the payload for the IoT Events action is a JSON or string literal, determining how the content expression is evaluated.
Defines an action that writes a value to an AWS IoT SiteWise asset property, including the asset and property IDs and the value to report, when the state exits in a detector model.
The ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset that this action writes data to when the detector model state exits.

The optional unique identifier for the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property entry used in an on-exit event action, allowing you to track or differentiate multiple SiteWise writes within the same event; if omitted, AWS IoT Events generates one automatically.
The property alias of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property to which the detector model action writes data, enabling the action to target a property by its alias rather than by asset and property IDs.
The ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property to which the detector model writes data in this action.

Specifies the value to write to the associated AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when this action is triggered, including the optional quality, timestamp, and the actual value (string, integer, double, or boolean).
Sets the quality indicator (e.g., GOOD, BAD, or UNCERTAIN) for the property value sent to AWS IoT SiteWise in the detector model's SiteWise action.
Specifies the timestamp (with time in seconds since Unix epoch and optional offset in nanoseconds) assigned to the asset property value when the IoT Events action writes data to AWS IoT SiteWise.
The nanosecond offset to add to the `time_in_seconds` value to specify the asset property value timestamp with sub-second precision.

Specifies a string expression (evaluated at runtime) that provides the Unix epoch time in seconds for the timestamp of the asset property value sent to AWS IoT SiteWise, overriding the default event timestamp.
The value object that specifies the actual data to write to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property, containing type-specific subfields such as stringValue, integerValue, doubleValue, or booleanValue.
The boolean value, specified as a string or dynamic expression, that AWS IoT Events writes to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when the associated on-exit action is executed.
Sets the double-precision floating-point value to be written to the AWS IoT SiteWise property when the detector model action triggers on state exit.
The integer value, represented as a string, to write to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when the on-exit event action triggers.
Sets the string value of the AWS IoT SiteWise property value to be written by this action when the detector model exits the state.
This object configures an AWS IoT Events action that publishes a message to a specified AWS IoT Core MQTT topic, containing properties for the MQTT topic name and an optional payload structure.
The MQTT topic to which the IoT Events detector model publishes a message when this action is triggered.

Specifies the payload object for the IoT topic publish action, containing a contentExpression and type (STRING or JSON) that define the message content sent to the AWS IoT topic when this on_exit action triggers.

The string expression that defines the message payload (body) to publish to the AWS IoT Core topic when the iot_topic_publish action is triggered from an event (e.g., on_exit) in an AWS IoT Events detector model.
Specifies the payload type (JSON or STRING) for the IoT Topic Publish action, which determines how the message content is formatted when published to the AWS IoT Core topic.
Specifies the AWS Lambda function invocation configuration (Lambda action) that runs when the state exit event is triggered, including the Lambda function ARN and optional input payload.
The ARN of the Lambda function that AWS IoT Events invokes when this exit action is triggered.
Specifies the payload object that defines the content expression and type (JSON or STRING) of the message sent to the AWS Lambda function when this on_exit event action is triggered.
Specifies the textual content of the payload delivered to the AWS Lambda function, supporting IoT Events substitution templates (such as $variable and $input) to embed detector state and event data.
Specifies how the payload content is formatted when invoking the Lambda function, either as a plain string (STRING) or as structured JSON (JSON).
Defines a 'reset timer' action that resets a named timer to a specified duration in seconds (or restores its original duration if the new duration is omitted) when the detector state is exited.
The name of the timer to reset, which restarts the timer's countdown; this must match the name of a timer that was previously created by a set_timer action in the detector model.

Defines a timer to be armed when an exit event fires for this state, including the timer name and its duration specified either as a fixed number of seconds or an expression that evaluates to a duration in seconds.
The expression that specifies the duration of the timer (in seconds) set by this action, which can be a literal number or an expression that evaluates to an integer duration.
The duration, in seconds, after which the timer expires and triggers the next state.
The unique name of the timer that this set_timer action creates or updates, used to reference the timer in later events or conditions.

Configures the set_variable action for an on_exit event, assigning a specified value (literal, expression, or another variable) to a named variable within the detector model instance when the state is exited.
The value to assign to the specified variable in the SetVariable action; this can be a literal string, a reference to another variable, or an expression using AWS IoT Events expression syntax.
The name of the variable defined in the detector model that this setVariable action assigns a value to.
Specifies the configuration for an SNS action that sends a notification to an SNS topic when the state is exited, including the target topic ARN and the payload to publish.

Configures the payload content and format for the SNS action, specifying a content expression (like '$$' to send the entire input) and the payload type (JSON or STRING) that defines how the message is delivered to the SNS topic.
Specifies the content expression that defines the SNS message payload for an action in an onExit event, enabling dynamic content based on detector variables and input fields.
The type of the payload published to the SNS topic, which must be either 'STRING' for a plain text message or 'JSON' for a Java Script Object Notation structured message.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic to which a message is published when the detector model exits this state, as part of the SNS action in the on_exit event.
Defines the Amazon SQS queue action that sends a message to a specified queue when this on-exit event is triggered for a detector state.
Defines the content and format of the message payload sent to the SQS queue when the action is triggered, using a content expression and a payload type (e.g., JSON or string).
Specifies the expression evaluated at runtime to generate the message payload content sent to the SQS queue when the detector model triggers an action in an on-exit event of a state.
The payload type for the SQS action, which determines whether the content expression is sent as a plain string or as JSON (valid values: STRING, JSON).
The URL of the Amazon SQS queue to which AWS IoT Events sends a message as part of this SQS action in the detector model's state transition.
Determines whether the message payload sent to the Amazon SQS queue is base64-encoded before transmission.
The Boolean expression evaluated when the detector state is exited; if it resolves to true, the actions defined for this on-exit event are executed.
The name of the event that defines the actions to execute when the detector model state is exited, within the on_exit event list.
Defines the actions and events to execute when the detector instance receives an input event while in this state.

Defines the list of events processed when the detector instance receives an input message while in this state, where each event can specify a condition and a set of actions such as variable assignment or state transitions.

The actions to be executed when the event's condition is satisfied for an input to the detector, which can include setting variables, manipulating timers, and publishing to SNS, SQS, IoT topics, or Lambda.
Defines a clear timer action that removes the specified timer from the detector instance, preventing its timeout from triggering, used within an event's action list in the state's on-input logic.
The name of the timer to clear within the detector model's state, matching a timer previously started by a setTimer action.
Defines a DynamoDB action that writes the incoming event payload as a record to a specified Amazon DynamoDB table using the configured hash and range key fields.
Specifies the name of the hash key (partition key) attribute in the target DynamoDB table, where the evaluated value from the input is used as the primary key for the item being written.
Specifies the data type (e.g., STRING or NUMBER) of the DynamoDB hash key in the DynamoDB action, controlling how the hash key value is stored when writing detector model output.
The value of the DynamoDB hash key (partition key) used to locate the item to write, which can be a literal string or a dynamic expression referencing input payloads, detector states, and variables.
Specifies the DynamoDB operation type (e.g., INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE) to execute when the detector state action triggers.

Defines the payload for a DynamoDB action in an AWS IoT Events detector model, specifying the content expression and payload type (JSON or STRING) that determines how the resulting DynamoDB item is populated.
Specifies the content expression that defines the payload data written to the DynamoDB table by this IoT Events detector model action.
Specifies whether the payload for the DynamoDB action is a plain string (STRING) or a JSON object (JSON), controlling how the input payload is interpreted when writing to the table.
Specifies the name of the range key column in the Amazon DynamoDB table to which the action writes data.
Specifies the data type (STRING, INTEGER, or BOOLEAN) for the range key of the DynamoDB table that the IoT Events detector model action writes to, used when the table has a composite primary key.
Specifies the value that will be written to the range key (sort key) of the DynamoDB table when the IoT Events detector model triggers this DynamoDB action.
The name of the DynamoDB table to which the IoT Events detector model writes the payload when this action is executed.
Configures a DynamoDB v2 action that writes an item to a DynamoDB table, using the table name and payload expression specified in this object.
Configures the DynamoDB item to write by specifying a payload object whose content expression (typically a JSON string) and type (JSON or STRING) define the item attributes for the DynamoDBv2 action.

In the DynamoDBv2 action of an AWS IoT Events detector model, this field provides the expression that evaluates to the payload content (e.g., a JSON string representing the item) that is written to the DynamoDB table.
Specifies whether the payload content for the DynamoDBv2 action is interpreted as a JSON object (JSON) or as a string literal (STRING), per the AWS IoT Events payload type enum.
