The name of the DynamoDB table where the detector model writes the payload when this action is triggered.

Configures an AWS IoT Events detector model event action that sends the message payload to a specified Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream, including the delivery stream name and an optional separator.
The name of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to which the detector model sends data when this action is triggered.
Defines the content and format of the data sent to the Firehose delivery stream, including the content expression and payload type (JSON or STRING).

The expression that is evaluated to produce the payload content sent to the Amazon Data Firehose (Kinesis Firehose) delivery stream in an IoT Events detector model action, allowing interpolation of variables and JSON literals.
Specifies the format of the payload for the Firehose action, either 'STRING' for a raw string payload or 'JSON' for a structured JSON payload.
The separator string used to delimit the payload records when writing to the Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream.
Specifies an IoT Events action that sends event data to a named IoT Events input, which can trigger processing by another detector model.
The name of the AWS IoT Events input to which the action sends data, triggering a new detector model execution.
Specifies the content of the message (payload) sent to the target IoT Events input when this action fires, defined by a content expression string that can reference detector model variables.

The expression that defines the payload content sent to the AWS IoT Events input for this action, which can reference input variables and is evaluated at runtime according to the payload type (STRING or JSON).

The payload type for the IoT Events action, either STRING or JSON, determines how the payload content is encoded when sent to an AWS IoT Events input, with STRING indicating a literal string with substitution templates and JSON indicating a serialized JSON object.
Configures the action that sends the detector model's event data to an AWS IoT SiteWise asset property, specifying the asset ID, property ID, or property alias to update.
The ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset to which this action writes data.

For an AWS IoT SiteWise action within an IoT Events on-input event, this entry_id uniquely identifies the asset property value entry when the detector model calls the AWS IoT SiteWise PutAssetPropertyValue API.
The alias of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property that this action writes the input data to.
The ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property that this action writes data to.
The property value to write to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property, containing the value variant (integer, double, string, or boolean) and optional timestamp and quality fields.
Specifies the quality of the asset property value (e.g., GOOD, BAD, UNCERTAIN) that this IoT Events detector model action writes to AWS IoT SiteWise.
The timestamp object for the asset property value, containing timeInSeconds and optionally offsetInNanos, which defines the time at which the data was measured when writing to AWS IoT SiteWise.
Specifies the nanosecond offset (0–999999999) to add to the timestamp's seconds value for the IoT SiteWise asset property value write from the IoT Events detector model.

Specifies the time in seconds since the Unix epoch for the property value's timestamp, as a string expression (e.g., using detector model variables), used when sending data from the IoT Events detector model to AWS IoT SiteWise.

This object specifies the actual value to send to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property, choosing exactly one of the variant fields (stringValue, integerValue, doubleValue, or booleanValue) to represent the property's new value.
Sets the boolean value to publish to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when this action executes, which must be the string 'true' or 'false' (only one of the value type options should be supplied).
The double_value field specifies the property value as a double (floating-point) number expressed as a string, which is written to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when the event action executes.

This field specifies the integer value to be written to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property, expressed as a string that can be a literal integer or a dynamic expression (e.g., ${myVariable}) within the IoT Events detector model action.
The string value to assign to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when the action is executed.
Defines an action that publishes an MQTT message to an AWS IoT Core topic, with configurable topic and payload, executed when the associated event (e.g., on-input) is triggered.
The MQTT topic string on AWS IoT Core to which the detector model publishes the message when this action is triggered.
The payload to publish to the IoT topic, defined by a content expression and a payload type (JSON or STRING).
The expression that determines the message payload content published to the AWS IoT topic in this IoT Topic Publish action.
Specifies the payload type (STRING or JSON) for the message content published to the AWS IoT topic in this IoT Events action.
Configures an AWS Lambda function invocation when the event is triggered, specifying the function's ARN and an optional payload to pass to it.
The ARN of the AWS Lambda function that AWS IoT Events invokes when this action is triggered.
Defines the content and format of the payload sent to the Lambda function when the action is triggered, including the expression and whether it is JSON or STRING.
Specifies the expression that defines the payload content sent to the AWS Lambda function, allowing dynamic values from the detector model's input and state to be inserted into the payload.
Determines whether the payload for the Lambda action is formatted as a JSON payload or as a plain string, with valid values 'JSON' and 'STRING'.
Resets the specified timer to its original configured duration, causing it to restart counting down from that duration.
The name of the timer to reset when this resetTimer action is executed.
Starts a named timer with a specified duration in seconds when the event is triggered, initiating a timer that can later transition the detector state.
The expression that defines the duration of the timer, which can be a fixed number of seconds or a dynamic expression using variables and asset property values.
The number of seconds for the timer to elapse before it triggers the associated event in the AWS IoT Events detector model.
The unique name of the timer to set, which is used later in the detector model's states and transitions to evaluate when the timer expires.
Defines a setVariable action that assigns a computed value to a named variable within the detector model's state machine.
Specifies the literal string or dynamic expression to assign to the variable when the SetVariable action is executed in the IoT Events detector model's state event.
The name of the IoT Events variable to which the evaluated value is assigned in this SetVariable action, referenced elsewhere in the detector model by this identifier.
Defines an SNS action that publishes a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) topic when the event triggers, including the target topic ARN and optional message payload.

This object configures the message payload for the SNS action, specifying the content expression (e.g., a string or JSON expression) and the payload type (STRING or JSON) sent to the SNS topic when the detector model triggers.
The expression (using AWS IoT Events' built-in syntax) that is evaluated to produce the message body content sent to the Amazon SNS topic when this action is triggered.

Specifies the payload format for the SNS action in an AWS IoT Events detector model, with values either STRING (raw text) or JSON (structured object), controlling how the content expression is interpreted.
The ARN of the SNS topic to which the detector model sends a notification message when the event is triggered.
Defines the SQS action parameters for sending a message to an Amazon SQS queue when the detector model state's input event occurs.
Configures the message payload to send to the SQS queue, including the content expression and payload type (e.g., JSON).
The expression that defines the content of the SQS message payload, supporting dynamic interpolation of detector model variables and input values using the ${...} syntax.
The payload type for the SQS action, which determines whether the input data is sent as a JSON object or as a string.
The URL of the SQS queue to which the IoT Events detector model action sends the message payload.
Determines whether the message payload sent to the Amazon SQS queue is base64-encoded (true) or sent as a raw string (false).
Boolean expression evaluated against detector variables and inputs; when it evaluates to true, the actions defined in this event are triggered.
A friendly name that identifies this input-triggered event within the state, used to reference the event's condition and actions in AWS IoT Events.

Specifies the list of transition events evaluated when the detector receives input; each event defines an optional condition, actions to run, and a next state to transition to if the condition is true.

Specifies the list of actions to execute when the transition event's condition evaluates to true, such as setting variables, managing timers, publishing to AWS IoT Core topics, or sending data to services like Lambda, SNS, Firehose, and DynamoDB.
Configures a ClearTimer action that clears (stops and resets) the specified timer within the detector model instance for a state transition.
The name of the timer to clear, which must match the timer name set by a previous set_timer action in the detector model.
Specifies a DynamoDB action that writes data to an Amazon DynamoDB table when this transition event fires, configuring the table name and key fields for the item.
The name of the hash key (partition key) attribute in the target DynamoDB table that the IoT Events detector model's DynamoDB action writes to when triggered by a transition event.
Specifies the data type (e.g., STRING or NUMBER) of the hash key value in the DynamoDB action that writes data from the detector model.
The value to assign to the hash key of the DynamoDB table when this action executes, which can be an expression using input payload variables or a static string.
Specifies the type of DynamoDB operation to perform (INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE) when the corresponding transition event is fired.

Determines the payload (with a JSON or string type) that the DynamoDB action writes to the 'payload' attribute of the target table, using a contentExpression that can reference the detector model's input and state variables.

Specifies the content expression that is evaluated at runtime to produce the payload sent to DynamoDB when the transition event triggers, allowing dynamic use of input values and detector state variables.
The type of the payload for the DynamoDB action, either 'JSON' or 'STRING'.
The name of the column in the target DynamoDB table where the evaluated result of the action's payload expression is written when a transition event fires this DynamoDB action.
The name of the DynamoDB table's range key (sort key) attribute that this action accesses, used together with the hash key field to identify the item.
Specifies the data type (for example, STRING or NUMBER) for the range key value used when the detector model writes to the DynamoDB table in this action.

Defines the value assigned to the range key attribute of the DynamoDB table when this action writes a record from the IoT Events detector model, which can be a literal string or an expression such as a payload field.
The name of the Amazon DynamoDB table that the IoT Events action writes to when a transition event is triggered.
This object configures a DynamoDBv2 action for the transition event, specifying the target DynamoDB table name and an optional payload to write as an item when the event triggers.

Specifies the content expression and payload type (JSON or STRING) for the DynamoDBv2 action, determining the data that is written to the DynamoDB table in an AWS IoT Events detector model transition.

Specifies the string expression that is evaluated to produce the JSON content of the item written to the DynamoDB table by this DynamoDBv2 action, as part of the IoT Events detector model's transition event action payload.
Specifies the payload format for the DynamoDBv2 action, with allowed values JSON or STRING, determining how the content expression is evaluated for the DynamoDB item.
Specifies the name of the Amazon DynamoDB table where the detector model action stores the input payload via the DynamoDBv2 action.
Specifies an action that sends detector input or computed state-variable data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream when the transition event is triggered.
The name of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to which the IoT Events detector model action sends the message payload.

Defines the custom payload sent to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose from an IoT Events detector model's transition action, allowing you to specify the content expression and payload type (JSON or STRING) for the data delivered to the Firehose stream.

For an AWS IoT Events detector model, this field defines the content expression for the payload delivered to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose when a transition event action fires, enabling dynamic values from detector model variables, inputs, and other context to be included in the message.
Sets the payload format for the Firehose action, either JSON for a structured object or STRING for a raw content expression, controlling how data is delivered to Kinesis Data Firehose.

The separator string defines the delimiter, such as a newline, that AWS IoT Events inserts between each payload when writing the detector model's Firehose action output to the Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream.
Configures the AWS IoT Events action for this transition event, specifying the target input name and payload to send, which triggers the associated detector model.
The name of the AWS IoT Events input to which the detector model sends data when this transition event's action is executed.

The payload object that specifies the content expression and data type (JSON or STRING) for the message sent to the AWS IoT Events input when the iot_events action is executed as part of a transition event.
The expression or static string that defines the content of the payload sent by the IoT Events action, evaluated at runtime to produce the message delivered to the target.
Determines the payload format for the AWS IoT Events action, specifying whether the content expression is sent as a JSON object (JSON) or as a literal string (STRING).
Specifies the AWS IoT SiteWise action that sends asset property values to AWS IoT SiteWise when this transition event is triggered, including the asset ID, property ID, and optional property alias.
The ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset to which the detector model writes data when this transition event action is triggered.
The entry ID assigned to this IoT SiteWise asset property value entry, used to uniquely identify and correlate the result of the BatchPutAssetPropertyValue operation.
Specifies the alias (e.g., '/company/windfarm/3/turbine/7/temperature') of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property that this IoT Events detector model action writes data to.
The ID of the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property that the IoT Events action writes the detector model output to.
Defines the asset property value sent to AWS IoT SiteWise, including its value, quality, and timestamp, which can be static or derived from expressions in the detector model.
Sets the quality of the property value written to AWS IoT SiteWise, which must be one of `GOOD`, `BAD`, or `UNCERTAIN`.
Specifies the timestamp for the IoT SiteWise asset property value, overriding the default event time with Unix epoch seconds and a nanosecond offset.
Specifies the offset in nanoseconds from the Unix epoch time (given in the parent timestamp's `time_in_seconds` field) for the asset property value sent to AWS IoT SiteWise.
Specifies the time, in Unix epoch seconds, at which the property value was captured and should be associated with the data sent to AWS IoT SiteWise.
An object that specifies the typed value (booleanValue, doubleValue, integerValue, or stringValue) to write to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property, where each field can be a literal or an expression.
The boolean value to write to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property, represented as a string ('true' or 'false'), when this transition event action is invoked.
The double-precision value to write to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property when its data type is DOUBLE, expressed as a string.
Specifies the integer value for the AWS IoT SiteWise property, as a string that can be either a literal integer or a dynamic expression, such as a variable reference.
Specifies the string-valued data to write to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset property as part of this IoT Events detector model transition action.
Publishes an MQTT message to a specified AWS IoT Core topic as one of the actions executed when the transition event fires.
The MQTT topic to which the IoT Events message is published when this action is triggered.
Specifies the payload of the MQTT message to publish to the AWS IoT Core topic, configured via an object containing a content expression and a payload type (STRING or JSON).
The content expression that defines the body of the MQTT message published by the IoT Topic Publish action, evaluated at runtime to produce the payload content.
Specifies whether the payload sent to the AWS IoT topic is a JSON object (type JSON) or a raw string (type STRING) when the transition event action triggers.
Defines an action that invokes an AWS Lambda function, specifying the function ARN and optional payload, when the associated transition event is triggered in the detector model.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Lambda function that AWS IoT Events invokes when this transition event is triggered.
Defines the payload sent to the Lambda function, using a contentExpression and a type (e.g., 'JSON') to specify how the detector's input data is formatted and delivered to the Lambda action.
Defines the payload content expression sent to the Lambda target when the transition event fires, using AWS IoT Events expression syntax to dynamically incorporate variables, inputs, and other data.
For an AWS IoT Events detector model, this field specifies the payload format (either `JSON` or `STRING`) for the Lambda action's input payload.
This object specifies a reset timer action, which resets the referenced IoT Events timer to its originally configured duration when the transition event is triggered.
The name of the timer to reset, which must match the name of a timer previously set by a SetTimer action within the detector model definition.
Configures a set_timer action, which creates or restarts a timer by name and sets its duration in seconds, so that when the timer expires the detector model can trigger a transition or other event.
Specifies the duration of the timer in seconds, expressed as a string that can be a literal number or a dynamic expression involving variables and input values.
Specifies the duration, in seconds, for the timer set by this setTimer action in an AWS IoT Events detector model; when the timer expires, it can trigger an event.
The unique name of the timer being set, used later to reference or clear the timer within the detector model.
Configuration for a set-variable action that assigns a value to an AWS IoT Events variable, executed as part of this transition event's actions when the transition condition is met.
Sets the value of the variable specified by the setVariable action, which can be a literal string or a dynamic expression using the input payload and other variables.
The name of the IoT Events variable that this SetVariable action assigns a new value to, used to store state information that can be referenced in later detector expressions.
Defines the parameters for publishing a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) topic as the action to execute when the parent transition event fires.
Specifies the payload (message content) sent to the SNS topic, including a content expression and a type (STRING or JSON), for the SNS action on an input transition event in the detector model.

Defines the dynamic expression that AWS IoT Events evaluates to generate the message content sent to the SNS topic for this transition event action, allowing interpolation of detector state and input variables.
The payload type (either 'STRING' or 'JSON') for the SNS action's message payload in a transition event, determining how the contentExpression is encoded.
The ARN of the SNS topic to which the IoT Events action publishes a message when the transition event's action is triggered.
The SQS action that publishes a message to an Amazon SQS queue when the transition event is triggered, allowing configuration of the destination queue URL, message payload, and base64 encoding.
Specifies the payload content and its type (e.g., JSON) that is sent to the SQS queue when the transition event triggers.
The expression that defines the message payload sent to the SQS queue, evaluated using AWS IoT Events expression syntax (e.g., a static string or a dynamic expression referencing state variables).
Specifies whether the SQS action payload is sent as a plain string (STRING) or as a JSON object (JSON), determining the message body format delivered to the Amazon SQS queue.
The URL of the Amazon SQS queue to which the action sends a message when the transition event is triggered.
If true, the SQS action base64-encodes the message payload before sending it to the queue.
The Boolean expression that, when evaluated to true, triggers this transition event from one state to another in an AWS IoT Events detector model.
The name of this transition event, which uniquely identifies it among the transition events defined for the state's on_input logic.
The name of the next detector state to transition to when the transition event's condition evaluates to true.

Specifies a name for the state that is unique within the detector model, used to identify the state in the detector's logic and referenced by transition events and onInput, onEnter, and onExit event actions.

aws_io_tevents_input.input_definition.at.text: Specifies the JSON path (e.g., 'payload.temperature') within the incoming message payload that this input attribute maps to, used by AWS IoT Events to extract attribute data from the input message.

aws_io_tevents_input.tags.value.text: The value for a tag key attached to an AWS IoT Events input, used to add arbitrary metadata for resource identification and management.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS IoT FleetWise campaign.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.collection_s.text: Defines the data collection scheme for the campaign, specifying either a time-based interval or a condition-based trigger (based on signal values) that determines when vehicle data is captured and sent to AWS IoT FleetWise.
Configures the campaign to collect vehicle data based on a condition expression, such as a signal value threshold, rather than on a fixed time interval.
The version of the condition language used to interpret the condition expression in this condition-based collection scheme.

The logical expression, written in AWS IoT FleetWise condition language, that determines when the campaign collects vehicle data, for example by comparing signal values like `$variable.MySignal > 10`.
Specifies the minimum interval in milliseconds between two consecutive data collection events triggered by the condition, preventing overly frequent data collection.
Determines whether the campaign collects data continuously (`ALWAYS`) or only when the conditional expression transitions from false to true (`RISING_EDGE`) or from true to false (`FALLING_EDGE`).
Defines a time-based collection scheme for the campaign, which collects vehicle data at a fixed interval specified by the PeriodMs property.
The time interval in milliseconds between consecutive data collection operations for the time-based collection scheme.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.compression.text: Specifies the compression algorithm (OFF or SNAPPY) used for the data collected by this AWS IoT FleetWise campaign.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.creation_tim.text: CreationTime returns the timestamp, in Unix epoch seconds, indicating when the AWS IoT FleetWise campaign was created.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.data_destina.text: Specifies the destinations (such as Amazon S3 buckets or Amazon Timestream tables) where the campaign's collected vehicle data is delivered.
Specifies the MQTT topic configuration, including the topic name and execution role ARN, used to publish the campaign's decoded data to AWS IoT Core.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT FleetWise assumes to publish collected vehicle data to the configured MQTT topic.
The ARN of the AWS IoT Core MQTT topic to which the FleetWise campaign publishes collected vehicle data when the destination type is MQTT.
Defines the S3 destination for campaign data, specifying the bucket ARN, object key prefix, and optional storage compression format.
The ARN of the S3 bucket to which the campaign's collected vehicle data is delivered.
Defines the file format (JSON or PARQUET) used to store vehicle signal data in the S3 destination for the FleetWise campaign.
The key prefix (folder path) within the S3 bucket where the campaign's collected data objects are written.
Specifies the compression format (e.g., NONE or GZIP) applied to the data files delivered to the S3 bucket configured as the campaign's data destination.
Specifies the Amazon Timestream configuration, including the target table ARN and execution role ARN, used to deliver and store the processed vehicle data from the AWS IoT FleetWise campaign.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS IoT FleetWise assumes to write campaign data to the specified Amazon Timestream database and table.
The ARN of the Amazon Timestream table where the campaign's collected vehicle data is delivered.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.data_extra_d.text: Defines a list of vehicle attribute names (such as make, model, or VIN) to be included as extra metadata dimensions in the data collected by the campaign.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.data_partiti.text: Configures the data partitions for the campaign, where each partition defines an expression and storage conditions that route collected vehicle data to distinct storage destinations.
The unique identifier assigned to a data partition within the IoT FleetWise campaign, used to distinguish and reference this partition among others in the data_partitions list.
Defines the Amazon S3 storage destination (bucket and prefix) for the partition's collected vehicle data.
Specifies the unit of measurement (e.g., GB or TB) for the maximum size of a data partition's storage in an AWS IoT FleetWise campaign.
The numeric value of the maximum storage size (combined with the unit) that limits how much data a data partition can store in the IoT FleetWise campaign.
Defines the minimum time-to-live duration (value and unit) for collected campaign data stored in this partition, after which the data becomes eligible for automatic deletion from storage.
The unit of time (such as DAYS or HOURS) that applies to the minimumTimeToLive value, controlling the retention duration of vehicle data in this time-based data partition of the campaign.

The numeric value for the minimum time-to-live period, which determines how long data is retained in the partition before it can be expired, with the time unit defined by the associated storage option's unit field.
Specifies the S3 bucket name or object prefix where IoT FleetWise stores the data collected for this campaign data partition.
Sets the partition expression and optional upload priority for a FleetWise campaign data partition, governing how signal data is grouped and ordered during cloud upload.

Specifies the version of the AWS IoT FleetWise condition expression language used to parse and evaluate the partition upload condition expression, ensuring the expression syntax is interpreted according to the intended language capabilities.
Specifies the condition expression (e.g., a vehicle attribute name or logical condition) that determines which fleet data is assigned to this data partition when uploading campaign data to Amazon S3.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.description.text: A human-readable description of the campaign to help identify its purpose.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.diagnostics_.text: Specifies the diagnostics mode for the IoT FleetWise campaign, controlling whether active diagnostic trouble codes are collected; valid values are OFF (default) and SEND_ACTIVE_DTCS.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.expiry_time.text: Specifies the ISO 8601 timestamp when the AWS IoT FleetWise campaign stops collecting data from vehicles; after this time, the campaign is no longer active.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.last_modific.text: The date and time when the AWS IoT FleetWise campaign was last updated, as set by the service and returned as a read-only value.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.name.text: The name of the AWS IoT FleetWise campaign, which is required, must be unique within the account and region, and is used as the primary identifier for the campaign resource.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.post_trigger.text: The duration in seconds after a trigger event to continue collecting data from the vehicle, applicable when the campaign uses a condition-based collection scheme.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.priority.text: The priority of the campaign in the collection system, where a higher value (from 0 to 100) causes data to be collected more quickly when multiple campaigns overlap.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.signal_catal.text: The ARN of the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog that defines the signals to be collected by this campaign.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.signals_to_c.text: Specifies the list of signals (by name) from the vehicle that the campaign will collect, with optional per-signal sampling parameters such as maximum sample count and minimum sampling interval in milliseconds.
The identifier of the data partition that the signal is assigned to, allowing collected signal data to be stored and transmitted in separate partitioned streams within the FleetWise campaign.
The maximum number of signal samples to collect for the associated signal during the campaign.
Specifies the minimum sampling interval in milliseconds for the signal, controlling how frequently the vehicle's signal is sampled for data collection in the campaign.
The fully qualified name of the signal, as defined in the signal catalog or vehicle model, that this campaign collects data from.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.signals_to_f.text: Defines the list of vehicle signals (such as sensors, actuators, or attributes) whose data the campaign will collect from the fleet vehicles.
Specifies the fully qualified name of a vehicle signal (e.g., Vehicle.Transmission.Gear) that the campaign will collect and report from the vehicles.
Specifies the fetch strategy for the signal, choosing between condition-based triggering and a fixed time-based interval.

Specifies a condition-based signal fetch configuration that includes the condition expression which must be true to trigger signal collection, the trigger mode (e.g., always or rising edge), and the duration to collect signals after the condition is met.
Specifies the condition expression in the AWS IoT FleetWise condition language that determines when data from the selected signals is collected and transmitted for this campaign.

Specifies when the condition expression triggers a data collection: 'ALWAYS' collects data whenever the condition is true, while 'RISING_EDGE' collects data only when the condition transitions from false to true.
Defines the time-based settings (such as execution start time and frequency in seconds) that control when and how often the signal is fetched from the vehicle for this campaign.
Specifies how often, in milliseconds, the vehicle fetches and transmits the signal data for this signal during the campaign.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.spooling_mod.text: Controls whether vehicle data collected during offline periods is spooled to Amazon S3 for later forwarding, with allowed values of S3 (spooling enabled) or OFF (no spooling).

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.start_time.text: The ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g., '2023-11-30T12:00:00Z') at which the IoT FleetWise campaign begins collecting data from vehicles; if omitted, the campaign starts immediately upon activation.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.status.text: The current lifecycle state of the campaign, such as CREATING, WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL, RUNNING, SUSPENDED, or ERROR, as reported by AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.tags.text: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) that are attached to the AWS IoT FleetWise campaign to aid in resource identification and organization.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS IoT FleetWise campaign, used to organize and identify the resource in AWS.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS IoT FleetWise campaign, providing arbitrary metadata for resource management and cost allocation.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign.target_arn.text: Target ARN of the destination (such as an Amazon S3 bucket or Amazon Timestream table) that the campaign sends collected vehicle data to.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_decoder_manifest.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the decoder manifest in AWS IoT FleetWise, assigned by AWS when the resource is created.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_decoder_manifest.crea.text: The creation timestamp of the decoder manifest, indicating when it was created in AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_decoder_manifest.defa.text: This string field (typically 'true' or 'false') indicates whether the decoder manifest should assign a default decoder to signals that are not explicitly mapped in any signal decoder, allowing unmapped signals to be decoded; when set to false (the default), unmapped signals are not decoded.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_decoder_manifest.desc.text: A user-defined text description that provides human-readable context for the decoder manifest, such as its purpose or the vehicle models it applies to.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_decoder_manifest.last.text: The timestamp indicating when the decoder manifest was last modified.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_decoder_manifest.mode.text: The ARN of the AWS IoT FleetWise model manifest that defines the vehicle model and signals referenced by this decoder manifest.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_decoder_manifest.name.text: Specifies a unique, friendly name that identifies the decoder manifest within the AWS account, used to reference the manifest when associating it with a vehicle model or fleet.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_decoder_manifest.netw.text: Defines the list of network interfaces (CAN and/or OBD) that the decoder manifest uses to decode signals from the vehicle's onboard networks.

This object specifies the CAN bus interface for a network interface, containing the required name and optional protocol name (e.g., 'CAN' or 'CAN FD') that the decoder manifest uses to identify and decode CAN messages.
The name that uniquely identifies the CAN interface within the vehicle network, used to associate signals in the decoder manifest.
Specifies the CAN protocol name (such as CAN or J1939) that the network interface uses, determining how messages are decoded.
Specifies the version of the CAN protocol (e.g., '2.0') used by the CAN interface, which determines the frame format for decoding messages on that interface.
Defines the custom decoding interface configuration for a network interface, used to decode messages from a custom vehicle network protocol when the interface type is set to CUSTOM_DECODING.
A user-defined name that uniquely identifies this custom decoding network interface within the decoder manifest, used to reference the interface when configuring signal decoders.
Specifies a unique identifier (name) for the network interface within the decoder manifest, used to reference it in signal decoders and other manifest components.
Defines the OBD-II interface settings for the network interface, including the diagnostic request message ID, OBD standard, and PID request interval used by the decoder manifest.
Specifies the interval in seconds between successive requests for Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) from the vehicle's OBD interface.
Specifies whether the vehicle has a transmission ECU that communicates over the same OBD-II port, enabling the decoder manifest to include transmission data from that interface.
The unique name identifying this OBD network interface in the decoder manifest.
Identifies the OBD-II emission standard (e.g., OBD2 or OBD1) this network interface conforms to, so the decoder manifest can correctly interpret OBD requests and PID responses from the vehicle.
Specifies the time interval in seconds between OBD-II PID requests sent over the OBD interface to retrieve vehicle diagnostic data.
The CAN message ID used to send OBD-II diagnostic requests on the vehicle network.
Specifies whether the OBD interface uses extended 29-bit CAN identifiers (true) or standard 11-bit identifiers (false).
Specifies the type of the vehicle network interface, such as CAN or OBD.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_decoder_manifest.sign.text: A list of signal decoder definitions that specify how to decode CAN or OBD bus signals into vehicle signals for the decoder manifest.

The can_signal object specifies the CAN (Controller Area Network) signal decoding parameters, such as message ID, start bit, length, scale, offset, bit-endianness, and signedness, used by the decoder to extract the signal value from a CAN frame.
Multiplicative scaling factor (e.g., 0.1) used to convert a raw CAN signal's integer value into the corresponding physical value during message decoding in AWS IoT FleetWise.
Specifies whether the CAN signal uses big-endian byte ordering (true) or little-endian byte ordering (false).
Indicates whether the CAN signal's raw integer value should be interpreted as a signed (two's complement) number, allowing negative values, or as an unsigned number.
The length of the CAN signal in bits, defining how many bits the signal occupies within the CAN message frame.
The CAN message identifier (ID) of the CAN frame that carries the signal being decoded.
The offset value added to the scaled signal (after applying the factor) to compute the physical value of a CAN signal in the decoder manifest.
Specifies the data type of the decoded CAN signal value, such as integer, float, or boolean, which FleetWise uses to interpret the raw signal bytes.
The bit position in the CAN message frame where the signal's data starts, used to locate and decode the signal value from the raw vehicle network message.

Configures a custom decoding signal by providing its name, used when the signal decoder type is CUSTOM_DECODING_SIGNAL so the decoder manifest can map a non-CAN/OBd custom signal to a vehicle's fully qualified signal.
The identifier of the custom decoding signal, which uniquely identifies the signal within the decoder manifest for custom network interface decoding.

Specifies the fully qualified name of the vehicle signal that this decoder is responsible for decoding, which must match the signal name defined in the vehicle model (e.g., `VehicleEngineRPM`) and is used to link decoded network data to that signal.
The ID of the network interface (e.g., a CAN or ethernet interface) that this signal decoder is associated with, determining which interface's decoded messages are used.
Defines the OBD-II signal decoder settings, including the PID, service mode, message type, and scaling/offset, that the decoder manifest uses to interpret diagnostic data from a vehicle's OBD port.
The length in bits of the bit mask applied to raw OBD-II data to extract the signal value in an OBD signal decoder.
The number of bits to right-shift the raw OBD data after applying the bit mask, used to extract the signal value for a decoder.
For an OBD signal decoder in an AWS IoT FleetWise decoder manifest, specifies the number of bytes that the signal's data occupies in the CAN message payload, used to decode the raw value.
Determines whether the OBD signal's raw data is interpreted as a signed integer (two's complement) or unsigned, affecting how the decoded value is computed.

Specifies the constant offset added to the product of the raw OBD signal byte value and the scaling factor when converting the signal to its physical measurement (e.g., physical = raw * factor + offset).
The OBD-II parameter ID (PID) that identifies the specific vehicle diagnostic signal to decode from the on-board diagnostic (OBD) interface, such as 0x0D for vehicle speed.
The expected length (in bytes) of the OBD PID response message that the decoder uses to parse the signal value from raw vehicle data.
The multiplicative scaling factor that converts the raw OBD signal value into the physical value, as configured in the FleetWise decoder manifest's OBD signal decoder.
The OBD service mode (e.g., 0x01 for current data) that determines the diagnostic service used to retrieve the PID's data.
Defines how the decoded OBD signal value is interpreted, allowing values of INTEGER or FLOATING_POINT to represent the numeric type of the signal.
Specifies the byte offset within the CAN message frame at which the OBD signal's data begins, used to parse the signal from the payload.
Specifies the protocol type of the signal decoder (CAN_SIGNAL, OBD_SIGNAL, or MESSAGE_SIGNAL), which determines how the decoder interprets the raw signal data in the IoT FleetWise decoder manifest.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_decoder_manifest.stat.text: The status of the decoder manifest, which is set to either 'DRAFT' or 'ACTIVE' to indicate whether the manifest is in a draft state or ready for use.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_fleet.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the fleet in AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_fleet.creation_time.text: The timestamp of when the fleet was created in AWS IoT FleetWise, returned as an ISO 8601 formatted string.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_fleet.description.text: Provides an optional human-readable description of the fleet, such as its purpose or operational context, with a maximum length of 2048 characters.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_fleet.id.text: The user-defined unique fleet ID that identifies the fleet in AWS IoT FleetWise, which is required when creating the fleet.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_fleet.last_modificati.text: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) of the last modification to the fleet.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_fleet.signal_catalog_.text: The ARN of the signal catalog that this fleet is associated with.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_fleet.tags.text: Defines a list of tags, each containing a key and value, applied to the AWS IoT FleetWise fleet to support cost allocation, access control, and resource identification.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_fleet.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS IoT FleetWise fleet, used to label and categorize the fleet resource.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_fleet.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key assigned to the AWS IoT FleetWise fleet, used for identifying or organizing the resource.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the IoT FleetWise model manifest.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest.creati.text: The creation_time field provides the timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) of when the AWS IoT FleetWise model manifest was created.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest.descri.text: An optional textual description that helps identify the purpose or contents of the vehicle model manifest in AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest.last_m.text: The timestamp when the model manifest was last modified, set automatically by AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest.name.text: The name of the model manifest, which is a unique, user-defined identifier used to reference the manifest within the AWS IoT FleetWise service.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest.nodes.text: A list of node names (signals and attributes) from the associated signal catalog that define the signals and attributes included in this model manifest.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest.signal.text: The ARN of the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog that this model manifest is associated with.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest.status.text: This field sets the lifecycle status of the IoT FleetWise model manifest between DRAFT (editable) and ACTIVE (production-ready), allowing you to control when the manifest becomes usable.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest.tags.text: Specifies the list of tag key-value pairs to attach to the AWS IoT FleetWise model manifest for organizing and managing the resource.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest.tags.k.text: Specifies the key for a tag attached to the AWS IoT FleetWise model manifest, enabling metadata-based identification and organization of the resource.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest.tags.v.text: The value part of a tag (key-value pair) that can be assigned to the AWS IoT FleetWise model manifest, used to organize, identify, or manage the resource.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog.creati.text: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog was created.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog.descri.text: A brief, user-defined description of the signal catalog, used to identify the catalog's purpose and contents.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog.last_m.text: The ISO 8601 timestamp when the signal catalog was last updated, returned by AWS IoT FleetWise as a read-only attribute.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog.name.text: The unique, human-readable name of the signal catalog; if not provided, AWS IoT FleetWise generates one automatically.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog.node_c.text: The total number of nodes in the signal catalog, automatically computed by AWS IoT FleetWise and broken down by node type (branches, sensors, actuators, attributes).
The total number of actuator nodes in the signal catalog, as reported in the node counts summary.
The total number of attribute nodes (attributes) defined in the signal catalog.
The total number of branch nodes in the signal catalog, which are used to organize other nodes hierarchically.
The total number of nodes (including branches, sensors, actuators, and attributes) in the signal catalog.
The total number of sensor nodes in the signal catalog, representing the count of sensor-type nodes that define data streams from vehicle devices.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog.nodes.text: Specifies the list of nodes (branches, sensors, actuators, and attributes) that define the signal catalog's hierarchy and signal definitions.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog.nodes..text: Defines an actuator node in the signal catalog, representing a controllable vehicle component such as a switch or valve, and specifying its fully qualified name, data type, unit, and optional allowed/min/max value constraints.

The allowed_values field defines the list of permissible string values for an actuator node in the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog, restricting the actuator's signal data to only these enumerated values.
The value that is assigned to the actuator when it is triggered, representing the default or commanded state for the actuator node in the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog.
Specifies the data type of the actuator signal (e.g., BOOLEAN, INT32, FLOAT, or DOUBLE), which defines the format of the value that the actuator produces or consumes.
The description of the actuator node, providing a human-readable explanation of the actuator's purpose in the signal catalog.
Defines the unique, dot-separated fully qualified name of the actuator node, which identifies its position in the signal catalog's hierarchical structure.
The maximum numeric value allowed for the actuator, defining the upper bound of its valid data range.
Minimum value that the actuator's numeric signal can report, defining the lower bound of its valid measurement range in the signal catalog.
Defines the unit of measurement (e.g., 'Celsius' or 'RPM') applied to the actuator's value in the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog.
Defines an attribute node in the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog, representing a static vehicle attribute such as make, model, or color, with a specified data type and optional unit.
Defines the list of permissible values that the attribute node can accept, restricting the attribute's value set to an enumerated list in the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog.
The string value assigned to this attribute node in the signal catalog, representing a fixed vehicle property such as a model, make, or color.
Specifies the data type (e.g., STRING, INTEGER, FLOAT, BOOLEAN) of the value held by this attribute node in the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog.
Sets the default value for this attribute node in the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog, used when no vehicle-provided value is available.
Specifies a short description of the attribute node, used to document the purpose or meaning of the attribute within the signal catalog.
The fully qualified name of the attribute node, which uniquely identifies it within the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog hierarchy (e.g., 'Vehicle.Window.Rear'), using dot-separated levels.
The maximum allowed value for the attribute node, defining the upper bound of the valid numeric range for the attribute in the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog.
Specifies the minimum value permitted for an attribute node with a numeric data type, enforcing a lower bound on the attribute's allowed range.

The branch attribute of a node defines a branch in the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog, which is a non-leaf node that groups other nodes (sensors, actuators, attributes, or nested branches) under a fully qualified name and description.
A brief, human-readable description of a branch node in the signal catalog, used to document the purpose or grouping of signals under that branch.
The fully qualified, dot-delimited name of a branch node in the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog (for example, Vehicle.Body.Engine), which defines the branch's hierarchical position in the node tree.

Defines a sensor node in the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog, specifying a fully-qualified name (e.g., 'Vehicle.Engine.Speed'), a data type such as DOUBLE or INT32, optional unit, description, and a list of allowed values for the measured signal.
The allowed values for the sensor node in the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog, defining the set of valid string values that the sensor can report for data validation.

For a sensor node in the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog, this field specifies the sensor's data type, which must be one of the supported primitive types (e.g., BOOLEAN, INT8, UINT8, INT16, UINT16, INT32, UINT32, INT64, UINT64, FLOAT, DOUBLE, STRING).
The description of the sensor node, providing human-readable context about the measurement, such as its purpose or data source.

Specifies the unique fully qualified name of the sensor node, using dot-separated hierarchical identifiers (e.g., Vehicle.Engine.Speed) that define the sensor's location and measurement within the signal catalog.
The maximum value that this sensor signal can report, defining the upper bound of the sensor's valid measurement range.
Sets the lower bound of the valid measurement range for the sensor, used to validate or constrain sensor readings in the signal catalog.
The physical unit of measurement for the sensor signal (e.g., 'Celsius' or 'm/s'), which defines how the numeric sensor value is interpreted in the signal catalog.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog.tags.text: A list of key-value tags that can be attached to the IoT FleetWise signal catalog to help organize, track, and manage the resource within your AWS environment.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog.tags.k.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog.tags.v.text: The user-defined value paired with a tag key to label and manage the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog resource.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the state template, which uniquely identifies it within AWS.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template.creati.text: The date and time the state template was created in AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template.data_e.text: Specifies a list of extra dimension signals (e.g., Vehicle.Make, Vehicle.Class) to be collected alongside the signals defined in the state template, enriching the vehicle data with additional metadata.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template.descri.text: A brief, user-provided description of the AWS IoT FleetWise state template, which defines a set of vehicle state signals to collect.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template.id.text: The read-only unique identifier (a UUID) that AWS IoT FleetWise assigns to this state template upon creation.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template.last_m.text: The timestamp of the most recent modification to the state template, automatically set by AWS IoT FleetWise when the resource is created or updated.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template.metada.text: Specifies a list of additional vehicle attribute names (e.g., make, model) to be included as metadata dimensions in the state template's collected data.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template.name.text: The required, user-defined name that identifies the state template within AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template.signal.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS IoT FleetWise signal catalog that this state template is associated with.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template.state_.text: The `state_template_properties` field specifies the list of signal or property names (as strings) that define the set of vehicle data points to collect when using this state template in AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template.tags.text: A list of Tag objects (each with a Key and Value) that are applied to the AWS IoT FleetWise state template for resource organization and cost allocation.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template.tags.k.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS IoT FleetWise state template, used for resource categorization, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template.tags.v.text: Defines the tag value for a tag attached to the AWS IoT FleetWise state template, which can be used to categorize or identify the template.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the vehicle in AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle.association_b.text: Specifies whether to create or update the association between the vehicle and its associated fleet, with valid values being CREATE or UPDATE.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle.attributes.text: A map of custom string key-value pairs that define metadata attributes for the vehicle, such as make, model, year, or fleet-specific identifiers, used by AWS IoT FleetWise to describe and manage the vehicle.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle.creation_time.text: The timestamp (ISO 8601 format) indicating when this vehicle was created in AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle.decoder_manif.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the decoder manifest that defines the signal decoding rules for this vehicle.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle.last_modifica.text: The timestamp of the most recent update to the vehicle's configuration or metadata in AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle.model_manifes.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the model manifest that defines the vehicle's attributes and signals.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle.name.text: The unique name of the vehicle, which is used to identify it in AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle.state_templat.text: Specifies a list of state templates that each define a named set of vehicle signals (e.g., speed, gear) to represent and report the vehicle's current state in AWS IoT FleetWise.
The unique identifier that associates a state template with the vehicle, used to reference the state template within the vehicle's state template associations.
Specifies how the state template is updated, either by a periodic schedule (with a cron/rate expression and an action to take on update) or immediately when a change occurs.
Enables the on-change update strategy for this state template, meaning the state template is refreshed whenever the vehicle's signal values change rather than on a periodic schedule.
The periodic update strategy for a state template, indicating that the vehicle should send state updates at a fixed interval configured by its subfields.
The state_template_update_rate field defines the interval (e.g., a duration such as '1d' or '1h') at which the periodic state template update strategy triggers an update for the FleetWise vehicle.
The unit of time (e.g., MILLISECONDS, SECONDS, MINUTES, HOURS) for the periodic state template update rate, which determines how often the state template is updated for the vehicle.
The periodic state template update rate in seconds, which determines how often the vehicle sends state template data to AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle.tags.text: Associates a list of key-value tags with the vehicle for metadata, categorization, and access control in AWS IoT FleetWise.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS IoT FleetWise vehicle, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle.tags.value.text: The value of a single tag attached to the AWS IoT FleetWise vehicle, allowing you to assign arbitrary metadata to the vehicle resource.

aws_io_tsite_wise_asset.asset_hierarchie.text: The list of asset hierarchies that define parent-child relationships from this asset to other assets, each including the hierarchy's logical ID and the target child asset's ID.
The child_asset_id specifies the ID of the child asset that this asset's hierarchy references, linking the two assets in the IoT SiteWise asset hierarchy.
Defines an optional external identifier for this asset hierarchy, allowing it to be referenced or matched with external systems in AWS IoT SiteWise.
The logical ID of the asset hierarchy, which must match a hierarchy logical ID defined in the asset model and uniquely identifies the parent–child relationship between the asset and its child asset.

aws_io_tsite_wise_asset.asset_properties.text: The computed list of property definitions for the IoT SiteWise asset, each including the logical ID, alias, notification state, and resolved value from the asset model.
The alias provides an external, human-readable identifier for the asset property that can be used to map the property to data from an external data source.
The external_id of an asset property specifies a unique, customer-supplied identifier for that property, which can be used to map or reference the property across systems.
The unique identifier of the asset property, assigned by AWS IoT SiteWise when the asset is created, used to reference the property in API operations.
The logical ID of the asset property, which uniquely identifies the property within the asset and must match a property definition's logical ID in the asset model.
Indicates the current notification state (ENABLED or DISABLED) for the asset property, which controls whether value updates trigger AWS IoT SiteWise notifications.
The physical unit of measurement (e.g., 'Celsius', 'kPa') for a property of the asset, defining the standard in which the property's value is expressed.

aws_io_tsite_wise_asset.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset, used to identify and categorize the asset.

aws_io_tsite_wise_asset.tags.value.text: The value string of a tag (key-value pair) attached to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset, used for metadata and resource categorization.

aws_io_tsite_wise_asset_model.asset_mode.text: The unique ID of the child asset model that this hierarchy composite model references, establishing a parent-child relationship between asset models in AWS IoT SiteWise.
Specifies the list of property definitions for a composite model, including each property's name, data type, unit, and data type configuration.
Specifies the data type of the property within a composite model, determining whether the property's values are strings, integers, doubles, booleans, or structured data.

An optional customer-defined external ID for a composite model property in an AWS IoT SiteWise asset model, used to map the property to an external system or business object without relying on AWS-generated identifiers.
The unique AWS-assigned identifier for this composite model property, used to reference the property within the asset model.
A unique, customer-defined logical identifier for a property in an IoT SiteWise asset model composite model, used as a stable reference for the property across the asset model and associated assets.
The name of the composite model property, which is a required string that uniquely identifies the property within the composite model in AWS IoT SiteWise.
Specifies the property type (Attribute, Measurement, Transform, or Metric) and its configuration for a property within a composite model of an AWS IoT SiteWise asset model.
Defines the attribute property type configuration for this composite model property, including an optional default value used when no time-series data is provided.
The default value string for an attribute property in an IoT SiteWise asset model, used as the initial attribute value when a new asset derived from the model is created.
Configures the composite model property as a metric by specifying an expression and variables that compute a time-series value from other asset properties.
The mathematical expression (e.g., 'Temperature * 9/5 + 32') that defines how the metric property's value is calculated from other asset properties referenced in the composite model.

Defines the list of named variable mappings used within the metric expression, where each variable references a source asset property (by ID or alias) that provides the measurement data for the calculation.
The name of the variable referenced in the metric expression, which maps to an asset property or attribute whose value is used in the computed metric.
This object specifies the asset property that a metric expression variable refers to, using a property ID and an optional hierarchy ID to reference properties from other asset models.
Specifies the external ID of an asset hierarchy that the metric variable's value refers to, so the metric can operate on assets from that hierarchy in AWS IoT SiteWise.
The ID of the asset hierarchy that defines the related assets whose property values are referenced by this metric variable, used to evaluate the metric expression.
The logical ID of an asset model hierarchy that scopes the property referenced by this metric variable, used when computing the metric from an asset related through that hierarchy.
The external ID of the asset property that this metric variable references, used to identify the property in the metric expression.
The physical ID of the asset model property to use as the value for this variable in the metric expression.
Specifies the logical ID of an asset model property that provides the value for this metric variable.
Specifies a property path (a list of path segments) that identifies a specific property in a related asset model, used as the value source for this metric variable.

For a metric variable in an AWS IoT SiteWise asset model, this name identifies one segment in the property path that references the source property (through a hierarchy) whose value is used in the metric expression.
Defines the time window for the metric calculation, specifying the tumbling interval and an optional delay for data lag in AWS IoT SiteWise asset models.
Configures the tumbling window for this metric property, using a fixed interval to divide time into consecutive, non-overlapping windows over which IoT SiteWise computes the metric.
The interval duration (for example, '1h' or '5m') for the tumbling window that defines the frequency at which the metric aggregation is computed.
Specifies the time offset that shifts the start of each tumbling window relative to the interval's scheduled start, expressed as a duration string such as '5m' or '1h'.
Defines the expression and input variables for a transform property, which computes asset property values from other properties using an IoT SiteWise expression.
The mathematical expression that defines how this transform property computes its value from other asset properties in the IoT SiteWise asset model.
The list of variables used in the transform expression, where each variable maps a name to a property value that the expression references.
The name of the variable that serves as a placeholder for a referenced asset property within the transform expression, used to compute the composite model's metric.
The value of this transform variable is an expression variable value object that references an asset property by its property ID, which serves as the input to the transform expression.
The external ID of the asset model hierarchy that a property value is referenced from, used in a transform variable to retrieve a property from a child asset associated via that hierarchy.

This field specifies the ID of an asset hierarchy within the IoT SiteWise asset model that provides the source asset for a transform variable, allowing the variable to reference a property from an asset linked through that hierarchy.

The logical ID of an asset model hierarchy that defines the variable's value within a transform expression for a composite model property, allowing the transform to reference properties from related assets.
Specifies the external ID of the property that this transform variable references, providing an alternative to using a property ID within the transform expression.
The ID of the asset property whose value is used as the input for this variable within the transform expression of the composite model property.
Specifies the logical ID of a property within the same asset model (or referenced alias) whose value is used as the input variable in the transform expression.

Represents the hierarchical path to a property in the asset model, as a list of objects where each object contains the property name (and optional ID) of a segment, used to bind a variable in a transform expression to that property's value.
Specifies the name of a property in the asset model's property path that a transform variable references as its source.
Defines the property type within a composite model of the asset model, such as 'Measurement', 'Attribute', 'Metric', or 'Transformation', determining how the property value is handled or calculated.
The unit (for example, 'Celsius' or 'm/s') that applies to a property within a composite model of an AWS IoT SiteWise asset model, used to describe the measurement's physical dimension.
Provides a textual description of the composite model, clarifying its role or purpose within the IoT SiteWise asset model.
Specifies a customer-supplied external ID for the composite model, which can be used to reference it in other AWS services or to align with existing external systems.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS IoT SiteWise to the composite model, returned after the asset model is created.

The unique, user-defined name for this composite model within the AWS IoT SiteWise asset model, which distinguishes it from other composite models and is used as its identifier when referencing the composite model in API calls.
Specifies the external ID of the parent composite model in the same asset model that this composite model is a child of.

The path of composite model names (starting from the asset model root) that specifies the parent composite model for this composite model; it is used to define nested composite models in AWS IoT SiteWise.
The type of this composite model, either 'AWS/ALARM' for alarm composite models or a custom component type name defined in the asset model's component type definitions.
Specifies the ID of the child asset model that this hierarchy references, establishing a parent-child relationship between asset models in AWS IoT SiteWise.
The customer-assigned external ID for this asset model hierarchy, which you can use to reference the hierarchy in AWS IoT SiteWise API operations instead of the system-generated ID.
The customer-defined logical identifier for the asset model hierarchy, uniquely identifying it within the asset model.
Uniquely identifies this hierarchy within the asset model, used as a reference in asset model properties and composite models.
The unique name of the hierarchy, used as its logical ID to identify it within the asset model.
Specifies the data type of the asset model property, valid values are BOOLEAN, DOUBLE, INTEGER, STRING, or STRUCT.
Specifies the data type specification for the asset model property, required only when the property's data_type is STRUCT to reference the structure definition that defines its fields.
Enables you to assign a custom external identifier to this asset model property so that it can be referenced from external systems, without using the AWS-generated property ID.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS IoT SiteWise to this asset model property.
The unique logical ID for the property within the asset model, which is used to reference the property in asset model expressions and AWS IoT SiteWise API operations.
The name of the asset model property, which uniquely identifies the property within the asset model and is used when referencing the property in asset model definitions and measurements.

Defines the specific type of asset model property (Attribute, Measurement, Transform, or Metric) and includes the corresponding configuration such as default value for an attribute, expression and variables for a transform or metric, and window for a metric.

The `attribute` configuration block defines an attribute-type property for the asset model, which represents a static value stored on the asset and can optionally include a `default_value` to initialize the property.
Sets the initial (default) value for an attribute-type property, used as the attribute's value when an asset is created from this asset model.
Configures a metric property type for the asset model, specifying the expression and variables that the AWS IoT SiteWise service evaluates to compute the property's value.
The mathematical expression that defines the metric, using variables that reference other asset properties and supporting operators and functions to compute the metric value.

Defines the variables used in the metric's mathematical expression, each mapping a variable name to a referenced asset property (by property ID or alias) that provides input data for the metric calculation.
The name of the variable as used in the metric expression, which references a property or time series in the asset model.

This object specifies the source property that a metric expression variable refers to, using PropertyId or PropertyLogicalId (and optionally HierarchyId for properties on assets in a hierarchy) to bind the variable name to a property's value.

Specifies the external ID of the hierarchy that acts as the source for the variable's value within a metric property of an AWS IoT SiteWise asset model, allowing the metric expression to reference data from a hierarchy by its external identifier.
The ID of the asset model hierarchy that defines the relationship from the parent asset to the related asset whose property is used as the value for this metric variable.

For a metric variable in an IoT SiteWise asset model, this is the logical ID of a hierarchy defined in the same model, used to reference properties from assets belonging to that hierarchy in the metric expression.
The external ID of the asset model property that supplies the value for this metric variable, enabling the variable to reference the property by its external ID instead of its internal property ID.
The ID of the property (from the same or a referenced asset model) that supplies the value for this metric variable, used when the variable is not defined by a property alias.
The logical ID of the asset model property whose value is used as the input variable in the metric expression.

This list defines a hierarchical path to a property used as a metric variable's value, where each object segment provides a property name and optionally a hierarchy name to traverse through asset relationships.
Specifies the name of the asset property referenced by the metric variable's property path in an AWS IoT SiteWise asset model.
Specifies the time interval window used by the metric property to aggregate data, including the tumbling interval and optional offset.
Defines the fixed interval (such as 5 minutes) for the tumbling window used in the IoT SiteWise metric aggregation, controlling how frequently the metric is calculated over a rolling time period.
Specifies the duration of each tumbling window (for example, '5m' or '1h') used to aggregate the metric data for the asset model property.

Specifies the offset duration (as an ISO 8601 string such as '1h' or '15m') that shifts the start time of each tumbling window in a SiteWise asset model metric, enabling alignment of aggregation intervals with external time boundaries.
Defines the transform formula (expression) and the input property variables used to compute this property's value for a transform-type asset model property.
The mathematical expression that defines how the transform property value is calculated from other asset properties.
Specifies the list of variables referenced in the transform expression, each binding a variable name to an asset property or another variable.
The name of a variable in the transform expression, which acts as a placeholder that is resolved to the referenced property value when the transform is evaluated.

The value object of a transform variable references the source asset model property (by property ID or logical ID, optionally scoped by a hierarchy ID) whose data is used as the input for the variable in the transform expression.

Specifies the external ID of an asset hierarchy referenced by this transform variable, allowing the transform expression to use data from a hierarchy identified by its external ID instead of its internal ID.

The ID of the hierarchy in the asset model whose associated asset property is referenced by this transform variable, required when the variable's value comes from an asset associated through that hierarchy.
The logical ID of an asset model hierarchy from which the transform variable reads its value when the variable value is a hierarchy reference.

In an AWS IoT SiteWise asset model transform property, this field specifies the external ID of the other asset model property that this transform variable refers to, allowing the transform expression to use that property's value.
The ID of the asset model property that serves as the input for this transform variable, used in the transform expression.
The logical ID of an asset model property that serves as the input value for a variable used in a transform expression.
The list of property path segments (each an object with a 'name') that defines the hierarchy path to the asset property used as the variable's value in a transform expression.

The `name` field specifies one segment of a property path used in an AWS IoT SiteWise asset model transform variable, where each segment is a property name that traces a hierarchy from an asset to the referenced property for evaluating the transform expression.
Specifies the data type of the asset model property, with valid values being BOOLEAN, DOUBLE, INT, or STRING.
The unit of measurement for the asset property, such as 'Celsius' or 'kPa', which defines the physical quantity being measured in AWS IoT SiteWise.

aws_io_tsite_wise_asset_model.enforced_a.text: The unique ID of the IoT SiteWise asset model that defines an interface, which this enforced relationship requires another asset model to implement.

Defines the mapping of asset model properties between the interfaces of an enforced asset model interface relationship in AWS IoT SiteWise, specifying which property from one interface corresponds to which property on the other.
The external ID of the asset model property that is mapped in the property mapping of an enforced asset model interface relationship.

Identifies the logical ID of the asset model's own property that an interface relationship property mapping binds to, establishing the correspondence between the interface's external property and the asset model's internal property.

The external identifier assigned to a property in the referenced interface asset model, used to match that property to a corresponding property in the current asset model as part of the property mapping configuration for an enforced asset model interface relationship.

aws_io_tsite_wise_asset_model.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the AWS IoT SiteWise asset model for metadata and resource management.

aws_io_tsite_wise_computation_model.comp.text: Specifies the anomaly detection configuration for the IoTSiteWise computation model, including the associated ML model and a threshold that determines when asset data points are flagged as anomalous.

aws_io_tsite_wise_dashboard.tags.key.text: The tag key that identifies a tag applied to the AWS IoT SiteWise dashboard, used for metadata and resource categorization.

aws_io_tsite_wise_dashboard.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag (a key-value pair) attached to the AWS IoT SiteWise dashboard, allowing you to categorize and manage the dashboard resource.

aws_io_tsite_wise_dataset.dataset_source.text: Specifies the source configuration for the IoT SiteWise dataset, including the Amazon S3 location (bucket and prefix) of the data files and the file format for importing data into the dataset.

Provides source-specific configuration details (such as an Amazon Kendra index or AWS IoT SiteWise source) for the dataset source, as defined by the DatasetSource property of an AWS::IoTSiteWise::Dataset resource.
The Kendra source detail that specifies the Amazon Kendra index ARN and an IAM role ARN used by the IoT SiteWise dataset to retrieve and ingest data from that index.

aws_io_tsite_wise_dataset.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key-value pair applied to the AWS IoT SiteWise dataset.

aws_io_tsite_wise_gateway.gateway_capabi.text: The configuration JSON string for the gateway capability, which defines how the capability is configured (e.g., OPC-UA server endpoint settings) and is validated by the capability's schema.
The namespace that uniquely identifies this IoT SiteWise gateway capability, for example 'iotsitewise:gateway:opcua'.
