aws_io_tsite_wise_gateway.tags.key.text: The user-defined key portion of a key-value tag applied to an AWS IoT SiteWise gateway, allowing categorization and filtering of gateway resources.

aws_io_tsite_wise_gateway.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag key-value pair assigned to the AWS IoT SiteWise Gateway, used for metadata such as cost allocation, access control, and resource organization.

aws_io_tsite_wise_portal.tags.value.text: The value part of a key-value tag that you assign to the AWS IoT SiteWise portal to help organize and identify the resource.

aws_io_tsite_wise_project.tags.key.text: Specifies the key of a tag, a user-defined label used to identify, organize, and manage AWS IoT SiteWise projects in AWS.

aws_io_tsite_wise_project.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag key-value pair applied to the AWS IoT SiteWise project, used for resource organization, cost allocation, and IAM access control.

aws_io_tthings_graph_flow_template.compa.text: The version of the user's namespace that the flow template is compatible with, used to ensure the flow definition aligns with a specific published namespace version.

aws_io_tthings_graph_flow_template.defin.text: The definition object specifies the flow template's workflow via a definition document containing the GraphQL language and text that describes the nodes and connections.
Specifies the language of the flow template definition; the only supported value is `GRAPHML`, the GraphML XML format used to describe the flow.
The GraphQL text that defines the flow template, using AWS IoT Things Graph's data model language.

aws_io_tthings_graph_flow_template.id.text: The unique identifier of the flow template, as assigned by AWS IoT Things Graph upon creation.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_component_type.creati.text: The date and time when the component type was created.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_component_type.status.text: The status object indicates the current lifecycle state of the component type (e.g., CREATING, UPDATING, ACTIVE, ERROR) and includes error details if an operation failed.
The error object (containing code and message) reported for this AWS IoT TwinMaker component type when its status is in an error state (e.g., after a failed create or update).
The error code that identifies the type of failure encountered when AWS IoT TwinMaker processed this component type.
The message of the error that caused the component type to fail, providing details about what went wrong.
Represents the lifecycle state of the component type (e.g., CREATING, UPDATING, ACTIVE, DELETING, or ERROR) as reported in the status object returned by AWS IoT TwinMaker.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_component_type.update.text: The date and time when the component type was last updated.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_entity.creation_date_.text: The date and time when the IoT TwinMaker entity was created, in ISO 8601 format.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_entity.status.text: The current status of the entity, including its state (e.g., CREATING, UPDATING, ACTIVE, DELETING, DELETED) and any error details if an operation failed.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_entity.status.error.text: Contains the error code and message returned by AWS IoT TwinMaker when the entity is in an ERROR state, providing details about why an entity operation such as creation or update failed.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_entity.status.error.c.text: The machine-readable error code returned in the entity's status when AWS IoT TwinMaker fails to create or update the entity, providing a programmatic identifier for the failure type.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_entity.status.error.m.text: The error message from AWS IoT TwinMaker explaining why the entity is in the failed or error state.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_entity.status.state.text: The current lifecycle state of the IoT TwinMaker entity, such as CREATING, ACTIVE, UPDATING, DELETING, or ERROR, as reported by AWS IoT TwinMaker.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_entity.update_date_ti.text: The date and time when the entity was last updated, returned as a string in ISO 8601 format.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_scene.creation_date_t.text: The date and time when the scene was created, returned as a string in date-time format.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_scene.update_date_tim.text: The date and time when the scene was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_sync_job.creation_dat.text: The date and time at which the AWS IoT TwinMaker sync job was created, expressed in ISO 8601 format.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_sync_job.update_date_.text: The date and time when the sync job was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_workspace.creation_da.text: The date and time when the workspace was created, in ISO 8601 format.

aws_io_ttwin_maker_workspace.update_date.text: The date and time when the workspace was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

aws_io_twireless_destination.tags.key.text: Represents the key of a tag attached to an AWS IoT Wireless destination, enabling you to organize, identify, and filter the resource by custom metadata.

aws_io_twireless_destination.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS IoT Wireless destination, used to add metadata for organizing, identifying, or controlling access to the destination resource.

aws_io_twireless_device_profile.lo_ra_wa.text: The lo_ra_wan field configures LoRaWAN-specific parameters for the device profile, including whether the device supports Class B and Class C modes.
Specifies the Class B timeout in seconds for the LoRaWAN device profile.
The Class C timeout in seconds for the LoRaWAN device profile, used to configure the receive window timeout for Class C devices.
Specifies a list of factory preset frequencies for the LoRaWAN device profile, which the device uses during radio configuration.
The LoRaWAN MAC version of the device profile, such as 1.0.3 or 1.1, which determines the LoRaWAN specification compliance for the device.
Sets the maximum duty cycle, as a percentage of time the LoRaWAN device may transmit, to limit channel occupancy.
The maximum Effective Isotropic Radiated Power (EIRP) in dBm that the LoRaWAN device is permitted to transmit with, as configured in the LoRaWAN device profile.
Ping slot data rate for the LoRaWAN Class B mode, determining the transmission data rate used in the device's periodic ping slots.
Sets the frequency (in MHz) used by the LoRaWAN Class B mode for the periodic ping slot on the device profile.
Sets the periodicity of LoRaWAN Class B ping slots in the device profile, controlling how frequently the device opens receive windows for downlink messages.

The revision of the regional parameters document used by the LoRaWAN device profile (e.g., '2017-01-01' or '2020-04-15'), which determines the applicable regional LoRaWAN specification version for the device.
Specifies the RF region (e.g., US915, EU868) for the LoRaWAN radio, defining the frequency band used for device communication in the device profile.
Configures the data rate index for the second receive window (RX2) in LoRaWAN, which the device uses for downlink traffic when it does not receive a response in the first receive window.
Sets the RX1 delay (in seconds) for the LoRaWAN device profile, which determines how long after an uplink transmission the device opens its first receive window for downlink messages.
Sets the data rate offset for the first receive window (RX1) in LoRaWAN, used to compute the RX1 downlink data rate from the uplink data rate in adaptive data rate mode.
The frequency (in Hz) for the second receive window (RX2) in LoRaWAN, used for downlink transmissions when the device uses this receive window.
Indicates whether the LoRaWAN device profile supports 32-bit frame counters, allowing devices to use a larger frame counter value for reliable over-the-air activation and message integrity.
Indicates whether the LoRaWAN device profile supports Class B, enabling scheduled downlink communication using beacon synchronization.

Specifies whether the LoRaWAN device profile supports Class C mode, allowing the device to continuously listen for downlink communications rather than opening receive windows only after uplink transmissions.
Specifies whether the LoRaWAN device supports joining a network via Over-the-Air Activation (OTAA), enabling the Join procedure to obtain network credentials.

aws_io_twireless_device_profile.tags.key.text: Key of a user-defined tag attached to the IoT Wireless device profile, used to identify, organize, and filter the resource in AWS IoT Wireless.

aws_io_twireless_device_profile.tags.val.text: The value portion of a key-value tag that can be assigned to the AWS IoT Wireless device profile for metadata and resource organization.

aws_io_twireless_fuota_task.lo_ra_wan.text: The LoRaWAN-specific configuration for this FUOTA task, containing the multicast frequency and data rate parameters as computed by AWS.

aws_io_twireless_multicast_group.lo_ra_w.text: The LoRaWAN radio configuration (downlink class and frequency band) that AWS IoT Wireless applies to this multicast group, returned as a read-only attribute after group creation.

aws_io_twireless_multicast_group.tags.ke.text: Defines the key of a tag applied to the IoT Wireless Multicast Group, allowing you to attach custom metadata for resource grouping and management.

aws_io_twireless_network_analyzer_config.text: The value part of a key-value tag on the AWS IoT Wireless Network Analyzer Configuration, used to store custom metadata associated with the resource.
The verbosity level for logs collected by the network analyzer for wireless devices, such as 'OFF', 'INFO', or 'DEBUG'.
Specifies whether frame-level information for wireless devices is captured in the network analyzer trace, enabling or disabling wireless device frame tracing.

aws_io_twireless_partner_account.sidewal.text: This optional object configures the Sidewalk partner account credentials, including the application server private key used for authenticating with the Sidewalk network.

The sidewalk block's app_server_private_key specifies the Sidewalk application server private key that AWS IoT Wireless uses to encrypt and authenticate messages exchanged with your backend application server for the partner account.
The Sidewalk account response information returned by AWS IoT Wireless, including the assigned Amazon client ID and the cryptographic fingerprint used to authenticate the partner account.
The Amazon ID assigned by AWS to the Sidewalk partner account, returned in the sidewalk response.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Sidewalk partner account, which uniquely identifies the partner account within AWS.
The fingerprint returned by AWS IoT Wireless in the Sidewalk response after creating a partner account, which you provide to Sidewalk to validate and link the device.
The sidewalk_update property specifies updated Sidewalk credentials, including the application server private key and device certificates, to associate with the partner account.
Specifies the private key of the Sidewalk application server, used to authenticate and encrypt communication between the application server and AWS IoT Wireless for the partner account.

aws_io_twireless_partner_account.tags.ke.text: The key (name) of a tag assigned to the IoT Wireless Partner Account, used to organize and identify the tag for cost allocation and resource management.

aws_io_twireless_partner_account.tags.va.text: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the AWS IoT Wireless Partner Account, allowing you to manage and categorize the resource with custom metadata.

aws_io_twireless_service_profile.lo_ra_w.text: The LoRaWAN configuration block of the service profile, which contains the maximum EIRP, maximum duty cycle, and flags for join, class B, and class C support as returned by AWS.
When true, this boolean enables the LoRaWAN service profile to include gateway metadata such as RSSI and SNR in the uplink messages forwarded to AWS IoT Core.
Specifies the LoRaWAN channel mask used by the service profile to indicate which channels are enabled for the device.
The frequency (in seconds) at which the LoRaWAN network server sends Device Status Request messages to the device, as configured in the service profile's LoRaWAN settings.

This field specifies the downlink bucket size for the LoRaWAN service profile, which controls the maximum burst of downlink traffic by setting the size of the token bucket used for downlink rate limiting.
The downlink data rate (in kbps) for the LoRaWAN service profile, controlling the speed at which devices receive messages from the network server.
The maximum LoRaWAN data rate (DR) index allowed for wireless transmissions under this service profile.
Specifies the minimum data rate (DR_min) for LoRaWAN transmissions, setting the lower bound of the allowed data rate range in this service profile.
When enabled, this LoRaWAN service profile allows a device to perform handover between gateways, as represented by the HrAllowed parameter in the AWS IoT Wireless service profile.
The minimum number of gateways that must successfully receive a LoRaWAN uplink for the transmission to be considered valid, enabling uplink diversity in the IoT Wireless service profile.
Indicates whether the LoRaWAN service profile supports network geolocation for devices.
Indicates whether the LoRaWAN service profile allows private network operation for wireless devices.
When true, this enables roaming aggregation (RA) for the LoRaWAN service profile, allowing devices using the profile to participate in RA-based LoRaWAN roaming.
Indicates whether the battery level of the LoRaWAN device is reported to AWS IoT Core for LoRaWAN; when true, the service profile requests that device status reports include battery level.
Controls whether the LoRaWAN service profile reports the device status link margin to the application server.
Specifies the target packet error rate (PER) for the LoRaWAN service profile, representing the maximum acceptable percentage of lost or errored packets in wireless transmissions.
The uplink bucket size, which sets the maximum number of uplink messages that can be sent per second for devices using this LoRaWAN service profile.
Sets the uplink data rate for the LoRaWAN service profile, used together with the uplink bucket size and rate policy to govern how uplink messages from wireless devices are rate-limited.
Determines the billing rate policy for uplink LoRaWAN messages, typically set to 'Billed' or 'Unbilled' to indicate whether uplink transmissions are billed to the customer.

aws_io_twireless_service_profile.tags.ke.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS IoT Wireless Service Profile, used to identify the tag within the resource's tag set.

aws_io_twireless_service_profile.tags.va.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS IoT Wireless Service Profile, used for management and identification.

aws_io_twireless_task_definition.lo_ra_w.text: Provides the LoRaWAN update gateway task entry, including the current and update version details for the wireless gateway firmware update.
Specifies the current LoRaWAN gateway firmware and software version, represented as a LoRaWANGatewayVersion object, that serves as the baseline for the gateway update task entry.
Specifies the model name or identifier of the LoRaWAN gateway that this task definition version is intended for.
The package version of the LoRaWAN gateway's current firmware, used to identify the existing firmware state before an update task is applied.
The station version of the LoRaWAN gateway, used as part of the gateway's current version information in the update task.
Specifies the target LoRaWAN gateway version (model, package, station, and firmware version) that defines the firmware to which the gateway should be updated for this task entry.
The model identifier of the LoRaWAN gateway that the update version in this LoRaWAN update gateway task entry is intended for.
The version of the LoRaWAN update package to be applied to the wireless gateway as part of the update gateway task entry.
The station version component of the LoRaWAN gateway firmware version used in the update version of a LoRaWAN update gateway task entry.

aws_io_twireless_task_definition.tags.ke.text: The key of a tag assigned to the IoT Wireless task definition, used to label and categorize the resource for management and identification.

aws_io_twireless_task_definition.update.text: The Update object defines the over-the-air firmware update parameters for the task definition, specifying the S3 URL of the firmware update image and the IAM role that AWS IoT Wireless assumes to perform the update.

aws_io_twireless_task_definition.update..text: Specifies the LoRaWAN update configuration for the task definition, including the update signature, signature key CRC, and current and target gateway versions used to create a gateway update task.
Specifies the current LoRaWAN gateway firmware version that the update task expects the device to have before applying the update, used to match gateways eligible for the task definition.
Specifies the device model identifier (e.g., a product model number) for the current firmware version of a LoRaWAN device in a wireless task definition update.
Specifies the version string of the firmware package for the current LoRaWAN device update in the task definition.
The LoRaWAN base station version of the device's current firmware update version in the task definition.
The cyclic redundancy check (CRC) of the LoRaWAN session signature key, used to validate the integrity of the security key during Over-the-Air (FUOTA) firmware updates.

The update signature is a base64-encoded cryptographic signature, generated with the update signing key, that LoRaWAN devices use to verify the authenticity of the multicast session key during a FUOTA (firmware update over the air) for the multicast group defined by this task definition.
Specifies the LoRaWAN update version metadata, including the firmware update image and the IAM role used to perform the over-the-air firmware update for this wireless task definition.
The LoRaWAN device model identifier that the firmware update version is associated with, used to target compatible devices in the task definition's LoRaWAN update configuration.
The package version of the LoRaWAN gateway software to be set during the firmware update, used to identify the target firmware package for the update task.
Specifies the IAM role that the wireless task definition assumes to update data for the LoRaWAN network server.
The S3 URL pointing to the update data (such as a firmware image) that is deployed to target wireless devices during the execution of this task.

aws_io_twireless_wireless_device.lo_ra_w.text: Specifies the LoRaWAN configuration for the wireless device, including the device profile ID, service profile ID, and over-the-air activation parameters for connecting to AWS IoT Wireless.

Defines the Activation by Personalization (ABP) configuration for LoRaWAN 1.0.x devices, including the device address (DevAddr) and the network and application session keys (NwkSKey, AppSKey) used for encrypted downlink/uplink communication.
The 32-bit device address (DevAddr) for LoRaWAN ABP v1.0.x activation, specified as an 8-character hexadecimal string.
Defines the ABP v1.0.x session keys (AppSKey and NwkSKey) for the LoRaWAN device, which are used to encrypt and authenticate uplink and downlink communications.
The Application Session Key (AppSKey) used for encryption and decryption of application-layer payloads in the LoRaWAN ABP v1.0.x activation mode for this wireless device.
The LoRaWAN network session key (NwkSKey) used to secure communication between the device and network server in ABP v1.0.x activation mode.
Configures the LoRaWAN 1.1 Activation by Personalization (ABP) parameters for the wireless device, including the end-device address and session keys.
The LoRaWAN device address (DevAddr) used in ABP v1.1 activation, a 32-bit identifier that uniquely identifies the device on the network.
Specifies the required LoRaWAN ABP v1.1 session keys (FNwkSIntKey, SNwkSIntKey, NwkSEncKey, and AppSKey) used to encrypt and authenticate the device's network and application traffic.
The Application Session Key (AppSKey) used by AWS IoT Wireless to encrypt and decrypt application-layer payloads in the LoRaWAN ABP v1.1 session keys of the wireless device.

The Forward Network Session Integrity Key (FNwkSIntKey) used to verify and protect the integrity of downlink frames for a LoRaWAN 1.1 device activated via ABP (Activation by Personalization) in AWS IoT Wireless.
The network session encryption key (NwkSEncKey) used to encrypt MAC commands for a LoRaWAN 1.1 device activated by personalization (ABP).
The serving network session integrity key (SNwkSIntKey) used for LoRaWAN ABP v1.1 activation, which authenticates and validates downlink frames from the network server.
The DevEUI, a 16-character hex string that uniquely identifies the LoRaWAN device on the network.
The unique identifier of the LoRaWAN device profile that defines the device's MAC-layer parameters, such as supported device class (A, B, or C) and other connection settings for this wireless device.
The fports object defines the LoRaWAN FPort numbers to use for Firmware Update Over The Air (FUOTA), multicast, and clock synchronization operations on the wireless device.
The name of the AWS IoT Wireless destination that defines where uplink data sent on this LoRaWAN FPort (frame port) for this application is routed.
The LoRaWAN frame port (FPort) number that routes messages to the associated application for this wireless device.
The type of the LoRaWAN application (for example, SemtechGeoLocation) associated with the FPort, which tells AWS IoT Wireless how to interpret the uplink messages on that port.
Over-the-air activation (OTAA) configuration for LoRaWAN 1.0.x devices, containing the DevEui, AppEui, and AppKey used to authenticate and join the device to the network.
The AppEUI (Application EUI), a 64-bit identifier required for LoRaWAN OTAA v1.0.x activation, used to identify the application during the join procedure.
The AppKey is the 128-bit application key used for authentication and session establishment during OTAA v1.0.x activation of the LoRaWAN wireless device.

Specifies the LoRaWAN Over-the-Air Activation (OTAA) parameters for version 1.1, including the NwkKey, AppKey, JoinEui, and DevEui settings that define how the wireless device authenticates and joins a LoRaWAN network.
The AppKey for OTAA v1.1 activation of the LoRaWAN device, a base64-encoded 128-bit key used to derive the application session key (AppSKey) for encrypting application-layer payloads.
The JoinEUI (formerly AppEUI) of the LoRaWAN device's OTAA v1.1 activation, which identifies the join server or application server the device uses during the join procedure.
Specifies the LoRaWAN network key (NwkKey) used for OTAA v1.1 activation to secure communication between the wireless device and the network server.
The ID of the service profile assigned to the LoRaWAN wireless device, which defines the device's communication parameters and permissions.

aws_io_twireless_wireless_device.tags.ke.text: The key component of a key-value tag applied to the AWS IoT Wireless wireless device, used for identifying and managing the device.

aws_io_twireless_wireless_device.tags.va.text: The value portion of a key-value tag that can be attached to the AWS IoT Wireless device for resource identification, management, and cost allocation.

aws_io_twireless_wireless_device_import_.text: The S3 URL of the CSV file that lists the Sidewalk devices to import as part of this import task.
The Sidewalk manufacturing serial number (SMSN) that uniquely identifies the Sidewalk device to be imported in this import task.
The key of a tag applied to the AWS IoT Wireless device import task, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the import task via AWS tagging.

aws_io_twireless_wireless_gateway.lo_ra_.text: The LoRaWAN configuration for the wireless gateway, specifying the gateway EUI and service profile ID.
The LoRaWAN gateway EUI is the unique 16-character hexadecimal identifier for the gateway, required to register it with AWS IoT Wireless.
The LoRaWAN RF region for the gateway, which specifies the frequency band (e.g., US915, EU868) used for communication.

aws_io_twireless_wireless_gateway.tags.k.text: The key of a tag attached to an AWS IoT wireless gateway, used to organize, identify, and filter the gateway resource for management and cost tracking.

aws_io_twireless_wireless_gateway.tags.v.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS IoT Wireless Gateway, used for arbitrary metadata, identification, and cost allocation.

aws_ivs_channel.multitrack_input_configu.text: Configures multitrack input for the IVS channel, including whether multitrack input is enabled and the maximum resolution allowed for the input.

aws_ivs_channel.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the IVS channel, enabling you to categorize and manage the resource by custom metadata.

aws_ivs_channel.tags.value.text: The string value of a tag attached to the AWS IVS channel, used to store arbitrary metadata such as environment, project, or owner information.

aws_ivs_encoder_configuration.tags.key.text: A user-defined tag key to associate with the IVS encoder configuration, used for resource management and cost allocation.

aws_ivs_ingest_configuration.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the IVS ingest configuration, enabling you to categorize and filter the resource.

aws_ivs_playback_key_pair.tags.key.text: The key portion of a tag attached to the IVS playback key pair, used to label and organize the resource within AWS.

aws_ivs_playback_key_pair.tags.value.text: The value of a tag applied to the Amazon IVS playback key pair, used for metadata management.

aws_ivs_playback_restriction_policy.tags.text: Specifies a tag key for the IVS playback restriction policy, used to assign metadata that helps manage, categorize, and filter the policy resource.
Specifies the value for a tag key attached to the AWS IVS playback restriction policy, used to categorize and manage the policy resource.

aws_ivs_public_key.tags.value.text: The value associated with a tag key attached to the AWS IVS public key, used for organizing or identifying the resource.

aws_ivs_recording_configuration.destinat.text: The name of the Amazon S3 bucket where AWS IVS stores the recorded video segments for this recording configuration.

aws_ivs_recording_configuration.tags.val.text: The value of a tag attached to an AWS IVS recording configuration, used to organize, categorize, and manage the resource.

aws_ivs_stage.tags.key.text: A key for a metadata tag that you assign to an Amazon IVS Stage resource, enabling you to organize, filter, and control access to the stage for purposes such as cost allocation and resource management.

aws_ivs_stage.tags.value.text: The value portion of a user-defined tag applied to the Amazon IVS stage resource, used for metadata, identification, and cost tracking.

aws_ivs_storage_configuration.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag to associate with the IVS storage configuration, used for resource categorization and access control.

aws_ivs_storage_configuration.tags.value.text: A user-defined tag value (the 'value' part of a key-value tag) applied to this IVS storage configuration for resource identification and management.

aws_ivs_stream_key.tags.value.text: Specifies the value of a tag assigned to the AWS IVS stream key, used for identifying and categorizing the resource.

aws_ivschat_logging_configuration.tags.k.text: Specifies the key of a tag to attach to the IVS Chat Logging Configuration, enabling you to organize, identify, and manage the resource for purposes such as cost allocation or access control.

aws_ivschat_logging_configuration.tags.v.text: The value of a tag attached to the IVS Chat logging configuration, used to assign arbitrary metadata for resource organization, cost allocation, or access control.

aws_ivschat_room.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the IVS Chat Room, used to organize and identify the resource (e.g., 'Environment' or 'Owner').

aws_kafka_connect_connector.plugins.cust.text: For each plugin in the connector's plugin list, this object specifies the custom plugin's ARN and revision, which the connector uses to run the plugin's worker code.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Kafka Connect custom plugin to associate with this connector's plugin configuration.
The revision of the custom plugin, which combined with the plugin ARN identifies a specific version of the plugin to use for the connector.

aws_kafka_connect_connector.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the MSK Connect connector, used to identify, organize, and manage the resource.

aws_kafka_connect_connector.tags.value.text: The value for a tag key attached to the AWS Kafka Connect connector, used to manage, identify, and organize the connector resource.

aws_kafka_connect_custom_plugin.tags.key.text: The key of a tag applied to the AWS Kafka Connect custom plugin, used to organize and manage the resource.

aws_kafka_connect_custom_plugin.tags.val.text: The value of a tag key-value pair applied to the Kafka Connect custom plugin, used for AWS resource tagging to support cost allocation, access control, and resource management.

aws_kafka_connect_worker_configuration.t.text: Specifies the key of a tag to attach to this AWS Managed Kafka Connect worker configuration, enabling cost allocation, resource organization, and access control in AWS.
The value component of a key-value tag applied to the AWS Kafka Connect worker configuration, used for custom metadata, resource organization, and cost tracking.

aws_kendra_data_source.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Kendra data source in AWS.

aws_kendra_data_source.custom_document_e.text: Configures custom document enrichment for the data source, allowing you to apply inline transformations or invoke Lambda-based pre- and post-extraction hooks to modify document metadata and content before indexing.
Defines the document attribute condition that must evaluate to true for the inline custom document enrichment action to be applied during data source ingestion.
The name (key) of the document metadata attribute whose value is evaluated in this condition for a custom document enrichment inline configuration.

Specifies the value that the document attribute (identified by condition_document_attribute_key) is compared against when evaluating the enrichment condition, allowing you to define the match criteria for the data source's custom document enrichment.
Specifies the date, as an ISO 8601 string, that is used as the value to compare against the document attribute in the enrichment condition.
The numeric value used as the expected value when evaluating a document metadata attribute as part of a condition that determines whether inline custom document enrichment actions are applied.

Specifies the list of string values that serves as the condition's comparison value when the condition_on_value type is set to StringList, determining whether a Kendra custom document enrichment inline configuration applies based on a match against this list.
The string value that a document attribute is compared against in the condition, used when condition_on_value is of string type during custom document enrichment.

Defines the comparison operator (e.g., Equals, Contains, GreaterThan) used to evaluate the configured document attribute against a value in the condition, controlling when the inline custom document enrichment action is applied.
When set to true, this inline configuration deletes the document content (body text) for documents that match the associated condition, making the content unsearchable.
Configures the document attribute to be modified by the inline enrichment rule, including the attribute key, the value to set, or whether to delete the attribute.
The name (key) of the document attribute that the inline custom document enrichment configuration will set, modify, or delete in the Amazon Kendra data source's index.

Specifies the value to assign to the target document attribute key in an inline custom document enrichment configuration, where the value object can hold a string, string list, long, or date as defined by the Kendra DocumentAttributeValue type.
The date value (in ISO 8601 format) to assign to the target document attribute when this inline custom document enrichment configuration's condition is met.
Specifies the long integer value to set as the target document attribute when applying this inline custom document enrichment configuration.
Defines a list of string values to assign to the target document attribute as part of the inline custom enrichment configuration in an AWS Kendra data source.
When the target document attribute value is a string, this holds the literal string value that will be assigned to that attribute during Kendra document enrichment.
When set to true, deletes the target document attribute's value during inline custom document enrichment, instead of setting or updating it.
Specifies the AWS Lambda function, IAM role, and optional S3 bucket that Kendra invokes after extracting documents from the data source, enabling custom enrichment before indexing.
A condition on document attributes that must be met for the post-extraction hook to be invoked, such as checking that a specific attribute matches a value.
The name of the document attribute (such as a metadata field) whose value is compared with the condition's value to determine whether the post-extraction hook should be invoked.

The value to compare against the document attribute (specified by condition_document_attribute_key) using the condition operator, to decide whether the post-extraction Lambda hook is invoked; it can be a string, string list, long, or date value.
The date value used as the condition in the invocation condition, specifying the date to compare the document field against.
Provides the numeric (Long) value that Kendra compares against a document attribute in the invocation condition for the post-extraction hook, when the condition_on_value type is Long.

Specifies the list of string values used as the condition value in a custom document enrichment post-extraction hook invocation condition, enabling comparisons of a document attribute against a set of strings when the condition evaluates on a string list.

Specifies the exact string value that the document attribute (referenced in the condition's condition_on_document_attribute) must equal for the post-extraction hook invocation condition to be satisfied.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as Equals, Contains, or Exists) used in the document attribute condition that determines whether the post-extraction hook is invoked.
ARN of the Lambda function that AWS Kendra invokes to process documents after the extraction step in the custom document enrichment workflow.
The name of the S3 bucket that stores the document to be processed by the post-extraction Lambda hook for custom document enrichment in this Kendra data source.

Specifies the AWS Lambda function and associated settings (such as the function ARN, S3 bucket, and IAM role) that Kendra invokes before extracting text from documents during a data source sync, enabling custom pre-processing for document enrichment.
Specifies a condition on a document attribute (key, operator, value) that must be satisfied for the pre-extraction Lambda hook to be invoked during custom document enrichment.
The document attribute key used by the condition to determine whether the pre-extraction hook is invoked, matching against the document's metadata attributes.
The value that the document attribute is compared against when evaluating the pre-extraction hook's invocation condition, allowing the hook to trigger only when the attribute matches this value.
The date value (in ISO 8601 format) that the invocation condition compares against when deciding whether to run the pre-extraction hook.
Specifies the numeric long value used as the operand in the comparison condition for triggering the pre-extraction hook in the custom document enrichment configuration.

The list of string values to use as the condition's value when the condition requires a list, used to determine if a document's metadata field matches the invocation condition for the pre-extraction hook.
The string value used as the condition's comparison value when evaluating the document attribute in the invocation condition for the pre-extraction hook.
The operator (e.g., Equals, NotEquals, GreaterThan) used in the invocation condition to determine whether the pre-extraction hook is triggered for a document.
The ARN of the AWS Lambda function that AWS Kendra invokes to process documents before text extraction, as part of the pre-extraction hook in custom document enrichment.
The name of the S3 bucket that stores the source document to be processed by the pre-extraction Lambda hook in Kendra's custom document enrichment.

aws_kendra_data_source.data_source_confi.text: Defines the type-specific configuration for the data source, such as connection details, document extraction settings, and metadata mapping for repositories like Amazon S3, databases, or web crawlers.

Defines the connection settings and crawl scope for indexing content from a Confluence server, including authentication, URL, and which Confluence entities (spaces, blogs, attachments, etc.) to include.
Specifies whether to extract Confluence attachments and how to map attachment fields to Kendra index fields.
Specifies mappings between Confluence attachment fields and Amazon Kendra index fields, enabling you to control how attachment metadata such as attachment title, author, and file type is indexed.
The name of the Confluence attachment field (e.g., title, author) to map from the Confluence data source to an Amazon Kendra index field.
The date_field_format specifies the date format (e.g., yyyy/MM/dd) that Kendra uses to parse the Confluence attachment's date field when mapping it to an index field.
Specifies the name of the Amazon Kendra index field that the Confluence attachment field (defined in the mapping's data source field name) is mapped to.
Whether to crawl and index attachments from Confluence pages in addition to the page content.
Specifies how AWS Kendra indexes Confluence blog posts, including field mappings that define which blog attributes are captured and mapped to Kendra index fields.
Maps Confluence blog fields to Amazon Kendra index fields, enabling customized indexing of blog content from Confluence.
The name of the Confluence blog field (such as _title, _author, or _url) that this mapping associates with an Amazon Kendra index field.
Defines the expected format of date values in the mapped Confluence blog field, so Amazon Kendra can correctly parse and index them.
The name of the Amazon Kendra index field into which the value of the mapped Confluence blog field is indexed.
Specifies the list of regular expression patterns that exclude matching Confluence content from being indexed by the data source.
A list of regular expression patterns that define which Confluence content items (e.g., pages, attachments) are included in the Amazon Kendra index for this data source.
This object defines how Confluence pages are crawled by specifying field mappings from Confluence page fields to Amazon Kendra index fields, enabling those page attributes to be searchable.
Maps Confluence page fields to Amazon Kendra index fields, defining which page attributes are crawled and how they are stored in the index.
The name of the Confluence page field (e.g., title, url, author) that is mapped to a Kendra index field in the page field mappings.
Specifies the format of the date string in the Confluence page field being mapped, allowing Amazon Kendra to correctly parse and index the date value into the target index field.
The name of the Amazon Kendra index field that a Confluence page field is mapped to for indexing.
The ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the credentials used to authenticate with the Confluence instance for the Kendra data source.
The base URL of the Confluence instance that Amazon Kendra connects to for indexing documents.
Specifies which Confluence spaces to crawl, with options to crawl all spaces, only a specified list, or exclude a specified list from the data source.
Determines whether AWS Kendra indexes content from archived Confluence spaces when crawling the configured Confluence data source.
Specifies whether to crawl personal spaces in the Confluence environment when indexing content for Amazon Kendra.
Specifies the keys of Confluence spaces that are excluded from the data source, preventing their content from being indexed.
Specifies the list of Confluence space keys to include in the crawl, so only content from these spaces is indexed by Amazon Kendra.
Defines mappings from Confluence space attributes (like SPACE_KEY, URL, DISPLAY_URL) to custom Amazon Kendra index fields, letting space metadata be included in search results.
The name of the Confluence space field (such as 'name', 'url', or 'description') to map to an Amazon Kendra index field.
For each Confluence space field mapping, this specifies the date format (such as 'yyyy-MM-dd') that Amazon Kendra uses to parse and index date values from Confluence spaces.
Specifies the name of the target field in the Amazon Kendra index to which the Confluence space field is mapped.
The version of the Confluence instance, either CLOUD or SERVER, which determines the endpoint and authentication method used when connecting to the data source.
Specifies the VPC configuration, including subnets and security group IDs, that the Kendra Confluence data source uses to connect to a Confluence instance inside a VPC.
A list of security group IDs that the AWS Kendra Confluence data source uses in its VPC configuration to control network access to Confluence resources within the VPC.
The subnet IDs (list of strings) that specify the subnets in the Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) where the Confluence data source will run, allowing it to access resources in a private VPC.

Specifies the connection and indexing settings for a database data source, including the database engine type, connection credentials, VPC configuration, column mappings, and SQL query used to extract documents into Amazon Kendra.
Defines the column in the database table that stores the access control lists (ACL) for documents, used to enforce user permissions in Amazon Kendra indexes.
Specifies the column name in the database table that contains the group names allowed to access the documents indexed by this Kendra data source.
Maps columns from the database table to Kendra document fields, specifying which column holds the document ID, document data, document title, and defining additional field mappings to the index.
The list of column names in the database table that Amazon Kendra uses to detect when a row has been added or updated, enabling incremental indexing of the data source.
The name of the database column that contains the actual document content to be indexed by Amazon Kendra.
The name of the column in the database table that contains the unique identifier for each document, which Amazon Kendra uses as the document ID for indexing.
The name of the column in the database table that contains the document's title, which Amazon Kendra uses as the title when indexing the document.
Maps database columns from the data source's column configuration to Amazon Kendra index fields by specifying the column name and the corresponding index field name and data type.
The name of the database column that is mapped to the corresponding Kendra index field in this field mapping.
Specifies the format of a date value in the data source column so that Kendra can parse and index it as a date field.
The name of the Amazon Kendra index field that the source database column is mapped to, as part of the field mapping in the database data source column configuration.
Defines the connection settings for the database, including the host, port, credentials, and SSL configuration, used by the Kendra data source to access the database.
The host name or IP address of the database server that Amazon Kendra connects to.
The name of the database that contains the data to be indexed by Amazon Kendra for this database data source, used in the connection configuration.
The TCP port number on which the database server listens for connections.
The ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the database credentials used by the Kendra data source to connect to the database.
The name of the database table that Amazon Kendra reads from as its data source when using the database connector.
The type of database engine for the Kendra database data source, such as RDS_AURORA_MYSQL, RDS_AURORA_POSTGRESQL, RDS_MYSQL, or RDS_POSTGRESQL.
Defines SQL query execution settings for the Kendra database data source, specifically using the QueryIdentifier property to indicate that extraction runs as a direct query (DIRECT_QUERY).
Specifies whether SQL identifiers (e.g., table and column names) are enclosed in double quotes when querying the database, with accepted values 'DOUBLE_QUOTES' or 'NO_ENCLOSING'.
This optional object specifies the VPC subnets and security group IDs that AWS Kendra uses to connect to the database (e.g., RDS or Aurora) within your virtual private cloud.

The list of security group IDs that define the inbound and outbound rules for the VPC configuration of the database data source, allowing Amazon Kendra to connect to the database instance within the VPC.
Provides the list of VPC subnet IDs where AWS Kendra will deploy resources to connect to the database data source, enabling private access to the database within the VPC.
Configures the connector to a Google Drive repository, specifying the AWS Secrets Manager secret for OAuth authentication and the drive path to be indexed.
Specifies a list of MIME types (e.g., application/pdf) to exclude from indexing when syncing documents from Google Drive.
A list of Google Drive shared drive identifiers that Amazon Kendra excludes from the data source so documents in those shared drives are not indexed.
Specifies a list of Google Drive user accounts whose files or documents should be excluded from indexing by Amazon Kendra.
A list of regular expression patterns that define which Google Drive files or folders to exclude from the indexed content.

Configures the mapping of Google Drive source fields to Amazon Kendra index fields, allowing you to define which Google Drive attributes (such as title, author, content) are indexed and how they are stored in the corresponding index field names.
The name of the Google Drive field (e.g., a standard metadata property or custom property) to map to a corresponding Amazon Kendra index field.
Specifies the format (e.g., 'yyyy-MM-dd') of the date values in the Google Drive source field so they can be correctly parsed and mapped to the Kendra index field.
Specifies the name of the custom field in the Amazon Kendra index that the Google Drive source field maps to.
Specifies regular expression patterns to include only files in Google Drive that match the patterns in the Amazon Kendra data source, with exclusion patterns taking precedence over inclusions.

The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the Google Drive OAuth credentials (client ID and client secret) used to authenticate and authorize the Kendra data source to access the configured Google Drive account.

This object defines the settings required to connect Amazon Kendra to a Microsoft OneDrive for Business account, including the tenant domain, the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing OAuth credentials, and optional inclusion/exclusion patterns to control which documents are indexed.

When set to true, this flag disables the synchronization and use of local groups (groups defined directly in OneDrive) for document access control, so only groups from the connected directory (e.g., Microsoft 365) are considered.
A list of regular expression patterns that define which file paths or folder paths within OneDrive should be excluded from being crawled and indexed by the Kendra data source.
Specifies the mapping of OneDrive data source fields to Amazon Kendra index fields, allowing you to customize which fields are indexed and how they are named in the index.
The name of the field in the OneDrive data source that is mapped to a field in the Amazon Kendra index.
Specifies the format of a date field value in the OneDrive data source when mapping it to a Kendra index field of type DATE.
The name of the target field in the Amazon Kendra index that the OneDrive data source field is mapped to.
Specifies a list of regular expression patterns for including files and folders from OneDrive in the Amazon Kendra index.
Defines the set of OneDrive users (by user principal or email) whose files and documents are included in the Kendra data source index.
The list of OneDrive user accounts (email addresses or user principal names) whose drive content is indexed by this Kendra data source when users are specified directly in the configuration.
The S3 bucket and object key prefix under which the documents belonging to the associated OneDrive user are stored for Kendra to index.
The name of the S3 bucket that stores the OneDrive user's documents, used to map that user to the S3 content specified in the one_drive_user_s3_path.
Specifies the S3 object key prefix within the given S3 bucket where the OneDrive user's crawled documents are stored during the Kendra data source indexing process.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the application credentials (client ID and client secret) used to authenticate with Microsoft OneDrive for this Kendra data source.
The domain of the Office 365 tenant hosting the OneDrive for Business site (e.g., `tenant.onmicrosoft.com`), which Kendra uses to connect to the data source.
Specifies the S3 object that contains the access control list (ACL) data for documents in the S3 data source, including the bucket and key path to that object.
The S3 path to the access control list (ACL) file that defines user and group access permissions for the indexed documents in the S3 data source.
The name of the S3 bucket that contains the documents to be indexed by the Kendra data source.
Specifies the configuration for document metadata files in the S3 data source, including the S3 prefix where AWS Kendra looks for metadata files to enrich document attributes.
Sets the S3 object key prefix that Kendra uses to locate and filter the document metadata files within the S3 bucket when processing documents for the data source.
A list of regular-expression patterns for S3 file paths to exclude from being indexed by Amazon Kendra.
Regular expression patterns that define which object keys in the S3 bucket are included in the data source, with only files matching at least one pattern being indexed.
Specifies the S3 object key prefixes that should be included in the Amazon Kendra index, filtering out objects that do not start with these prefixes.

Defines the connection settings for a Salesforce data source, including the AWS Secrets Manager secret with OAuth credentials, standard object configurations to index, and optional knowledge article sync settings.
Configures how Amazon Kendra indexes Salesforce Chatter feeds, allowing you to specify the data field to use as the document content and map additional Salesforce fields to Kendra attributes.
The name of the Salesforce field that contains the content of the chatter feed item to be indexed by Kendra.
The name of the field in the Salesforce Chatter feed that contains the document title, used to map that field to the document title for indexing by Amazon Kendra.
Maps Salesforce Chatter feed source fields to Amazon Kendra index fields for the Chatter feed data source.
The name of the Salesforce field to map to a Kendra index field for Chatter feed data, used in the field_mappings of the Salesforce chatter feed configuration.
Specifies the format of a date field from the Salesforce chatter feed when mapping it to an Amazon Kendra index field, for example 'yyyy-MM-dd'.
The name of the Amazon Kendra index field to which the Salesforce Chatter feed field is mapped.
Filters the type of Salesforce chatter feed items (such as ACTIVE or RESOLVED) that are included when indexing, so only matching items are crawled.
Specifies whether to crawl and index attachments (files) associated with Salesforce objects in addition to the standard objects during a data source sync.
A list of regular expression patterns that match Salesforce attachment file names to exclude from being indexed by Kendra.
A list of regular expression patterns that determine which Salesforce attachment file names are included in the index; matching attachments are indexed.
Configures how Salesforce knowledge articles are ingested, including which article states (e.g., DRAFT or PUBLISHED) are indexed and how article fields map to Kendra index fields.
Defines the list of custom Salesforce knowledge article types to crawl, each with a name, document status field, and field mappings that map source fields to Kendra index fields.
Specifies the name of the Salesforce field that holds the body/content for custom knowledge article types indexed by Kendra.
Specifies the name of the field in the custom knowledge article type that maps to the document title for indexing in Amazon Kendra.
Specifies how fields from a custom Salesforce knowledge article type are mapped to Amazon Kendra index fields.
The name of the field in the Salesforce custom knowledge article type that is mapped to an Amazon Kendra index field.

Specifies the date format used to parse the value of the Salesforce field being mapped to a Kendra index field, allowing Kendra to correctly interpret dates when synchronizing custom knowledge article type data.

The name of the field in the Amazon Kendra index to which a Salesforce custom knowledge article source field is mapped, as specified in a field mapping within the custom knowledge article type configuration for a Salesforce data source.
The name of the custom Salesforce knowledge article type in Salesforce that this configuration defines mappings and title field for.
Specifies which Salesforce knowledge article states (e.g., DRAFT, PUBLISHED, ARCHIVED) Kendra includes when indexing articles from the connected Salesforce instance.
Specifies the indexing configuration for standard Salesforce knowledge articles, including field mappings to Kendra document attributes and the article field used as the document title.
Specifies the name of the Salesforce field that contains the knowledge article's content (body) to be indexed by Amazon Kendra.
The name of the Salesforce field whose value is used as the document title when indexing standard knowledge articles in Amazon Kendra.
Maps Salesforce knowledge article fields to Amazon Kendra index fields, allowing specific article attributes to be indexed.
The name of a field in the Salesforce standard knowledge article object that is mapped to a corresponding Amazon Kendra index field.

In the field mapping for mapping a date field from Salesforce to an Amazon Kendra index field, this string specifies the format (e.g., ISO 8601) of the source date value so Kendra can parse and convert it correctly.

The name of the field in the Amazon Kendra index that the specified Salesforce knowledge article field (from the source) is mapped to, used in the field mapping for the standard knowledge article type configuration.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the authentication credentials (e.g., username, password, or OAuth token) for connecting to Salesforce.
The URL of the Salesforce instance that contains the data to index.
This object specifies how attachments to standard Salesforce objects are indexed in Amazon Kendra, including the document title field name and optional field mappings for metadata extraction.
Specifies the name of the field within the Salesforce standard object attachment that contains the document title, used by Kendra as the title for the indexed attachment.

Defines the list of mappings that map fields from Salesforce standard object attachments (such as case or account attachments) to Amazon Kendra index fields, controlling how attachment metadata is indexed.
The name of the field in the Salesforce standard object attachment that is mapped to an Amazon Kendra index field.
Specifies the format (e.g., ISO 8601) used to parse date values from Salesforce standard object attachments when mapping them to Kendra index fields.
Specifies the name of the Amazon Kendra index field to which the Salesforce attachment source field is mapped in the standard object attachment configuration.

Specifies the list of standard Salesforce objects (for example, Account, Contact, or Opportunity) that Amazon Kendra crawls from your Salesforce instance, with each object optionally defining field mappings to index its data.
Specifies the Salesforce object field that contains the document content (data) to be indexed by Amazon Kendra.
Specifies the name of the Salesforce field in the standard object whose value is used as the document title for the indexed documents.
Maps Salesforce fields to Amazon Kendra index fields for each standard object, determining which object data is indexed and how it appears in search results.
The name of the field in the Salesforce object that maps to an Amazon Kendra index field.
Specifies the date/time format string used to parse the Salesforce standard object field's values so that Kendra can correctly convert them into the target index field of type date.
Specifies the name of the target field in the Amazon Kendra index to which the Salesforce standard object's source field is mapped.
The name of the Salesforce standard object (e.g., Account, Contact, Opportunity) to sync into the Amazon Kendra index.
Configuration for connecting Amazon Kendra to a ServiceNow instance, including authentication details, host URL, and options for indexing knowledge articles and service catalogs.
Specifies the authentication type used to connect to the ServiceNow instance, such as HTTP_BASIC or OAUTH2.
The base URL of the ServiceNow instance to index, such as https://yourinstance.service-now.com.

Configures how Amazon Kendra indexes ServiceNow knowledge articles for the data source, including the document title field to use, the source template for article URLs, and optional attachment file pattern filters.
Indicates whether to crawl attachments to ServiceNow knowledge articles when indexing them from the ServiceNow data source.
Specifies the name of the field in the ServiceNow knowledge article table (such as 'text' or 'html') that contains the article body, which Kendra uses as the document data for indexing.
The name of the ServiceNow field that contains the title of a knowledge article, which Amazon Kendra uses as the document title when indexing the article.
Specifies file patterns (such as file extensions or regex patterns) used to exclude attachment files from being indexed when crawling ServiceNow knowledge articles.
Specifies the mapping of ServiceNow knowledge article attributes (such as title, body, or custom fields) to Amazon Kendra index fields, allowing those attributes to be indexed and searched.
The name of a field in the ServiceNow knowledge article data source that is mapped to a target Kendra index field.
Specifies the format of date values in ServiceNow knowledge article fields so Amazon Kendra can correctly parse and map them to index fields.
The name of the Amazon Kendra index field that receives the value from the corresponding ServiceNow knowledge article source field in this field mapping.
Specifies a query used to filter which ServiceNow knowledge articles are ingested into the index.
Specifies the file name patterns that determine which attachment files of ServiceNow knowledge articles are included for indexing.
The ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the credentials (user name and password) used to authenticate with the ServiceNow instance.
Configures the crawling and indexing behavior for ServiceNow service catalog items within the Kendra data source, including attachment processing and document field mappings.
Determines whether Amazon Kendra crawls attachments associated with ServiceNow service catalog items.
The name of the ServiceNow field that holds the body or content of the service catalog item, which Kendra uses as the document text to index.
Specifies the name of the field in ServiceNow service catalog items that Amazon Kendra uses as the document title when indexing those items.
A list of regular expression patterns used to exclude attachment file names from an indexed ServiceNow service catalog item's attachments in the Kendra data source.
Maps ServiceNow Service Catalog source fields to Amazon Kendra index fields for the Kendra data source's ServiceNow connector, allowing customization of how catalog data is indexed.
Specifies the name of the ServiceNow service catalog field whose value is mapped to an Amazon Kendra index field.
The format of the date string in the ServiceNow service catalog source field, used to parse it into Kendra's index date format.
The name of the field in the Amazon Kendra index that the ServiceNow service catalog field maps to.
A list of file name patterns that determine which attachment files in ServiceNow service catalog items are included for indexing by Amazon Kendra.
Specifies the ServiceNow build version (such as LONDON or OTHERS) that Amazon Kendra uses to determine the correct data extraction and indexing behavior for the connected ServiceNow instance.
When true, AWS Kendra includes file attachments associated with SharePoint items during the crawl; when false, it only indexes the SharePoint items themselves.
When set to true, prevents AWS Kendra from indexing local SharePoint groups, which reduces the number of access control entries synchronized into the index.
The name of the SharePoint column that holds the document title, which Amazon Kendra uses to populate the title attribute for indexed documents and search results.
Defines a list of regular expression patterns that identify SharePoint document URLs or paths to exclude from being indexed by Amazon Kendra.
Defines how SharePoint columns or metadata attributes are mapped to Amazon Kendra index fields, including the source field name and the target index field name and type for ingestion.
The name of the field in the SharePoint data source that is mapped to an Amazon Kendra index field as part of the field mapping configuration.
Specifies the expected format of the date value in the SharePoint field so Amazon Kendra can correctly parse and index it when mapping a date-type field to an index field.
The name of the field in the Amazon Kendra index where the value from the mapped SharePoint data source field is stored.

Specifies regular expression patterns that define which SharePoint document URLs are included in the Amazon Kendra index, so only documents whose URL matches any of these patterns are crawled and indexed.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the SharePoint authentication credentials used by Kendra to connect to the SharePoint site.
Specifies the SharePoint deployment version (e.g., SHAREPOINT_ONLINE or SHAREPOINT_2019) that the Kendra data source connects to, determining the valid connection URL and authentication requirements.
Specifies the S3 location (bucket and key) of the SSL certificate used to securely connect to the SharePoint server when it uses a self-signed certificate.
The name of the S3 bucket that contains the SSL certificate file used to establish a secure connection to the SharePoint server for this Kendra data source.
The S3 object key of the SSL certificate that Kendra uses to securely connect to the SharePoint data source.
The list of SharePoint site URLs (paths to SharePoint sites) that this Amazon Kendra data source will crawl to index documents and content.
Indicates whether to use the SharePoint change log to identify documents that need updating, enabling incremental synchronization instead of a full crawl of the site.
Specifies the VPC configuration (subnets and security group IDs) that Amazon Kendra uses to connect to your SharePoint data source when the SharePoint site is inside a VPC.
Specifies the list of security group IDs that define the security groups for the VPC used to connect to your SharePoint data source.
The list of subnet IDs in the Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) that the SharePoint data source uses to communicate with the Microsoft SharePoint environment.
Provides a JSON template that defines the configuration for a Kendra data source when the data source type is TEMPLATE, enabling custom data source parameters to be specified with the template.
The JSON or YAML template that defines the connection, authentication, and schema configuration for a custom Kendra data source using the TEMPLATE type.
Defines the configuration for crawling web pages, such as seed URLs, crawl depth, and link-following behavior, for the Kendra data source when it is of type `WEBCRAWLER`.
Specifies the authentication configuration used to access websites when crawling with the web crawler, including basic authentication and custom authentication using a secret in AWS Secrets Manager.
Specifies the list of basic authentication credentials (host and secret ARN) that the Amazon Kendra web crawler uses to authenticate with websites requiring HTTP basic authentication.
The ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the basic authentication credentials (username and password) used by the Kendra web crawler to access the specified host.
The hostname of the website that requires this basic authentication, used by the Kendra web crawler to apply the associated credentials when accessing that site.
The port number of the web server to authenticate with when the web crawler accesses the host for basic authentication.
Specifies the maximum number of link levels from the seed URLs that the web crawler will traverse, controlling how deep into the site's hierarchy the crawler goes.
Sets the maximum size in megabytes of a web page that the Kendra web crawler will process; pages larger than this limit are skipped.
Limits the number of outbound links that the Amazon Kendra web crawler follows from each webpage, preventing excessive crawling of large link-heavy pages.
The maximum number of URLs the web crawler can crawl per minute, used to rate-limit the crawl and avoid overloading the target site.
Specifies the proxy configuration, including host, port, and optional credentials, that the web crawler uses to connect to the internet when indexing web pages.
The ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the proxy authentication credentials (user name and password) used to connect through the proxy.
The hostname or IP address of the proxy server that AWS Kendra's web crawler uses to access the internet and crawl the target website.
The TCP port number of the proxy server used by the web crawler when accessing the target web site.
A list of regular expression patterns that exclude matching URLs from being crawled by the Amazon Kendra web crawler data source.
Specifies the regular expression patterns that determine which URLs the web crawler includes for indexing, so only pages matching at least one inclusion pattern are crawled.
The URLs configuration for the web crawler, specifying the seed URLs (starting points) and site maps used to discover and crawl pages.
Defines the seed URLs that the Amazon Kendra web crawler uses as starting points, along with optional crawl depth and URL processing limits.
A list of seed URLs that the web crawler uses as starting points to crawl and index web pages.
Specifies whether the web crawler crawls only the seed URL's host or also its subdomains, with allowed values HOST_ONLY and SUBDOMAINS.
Defines the sitemap configuration for the web crawler, specifying a list of sitemap URLs that Amazon Kendra uses to discover web pages to index.
Specifies the list of sitemap URLs that the web crawler uses to discover pages to index for the Kendra data source.
Configuration for an Amazon WorkDocs data source, specifying the WorkDocs organization ID, whether to crawl comments and shared documents, and which files to include or exclude via patterns.
Determines whether comments from Amazon WorkDocs documents are crawled and included in the index.
A list of regular expression patterns to exclude documents or folders from being indexed by the WorkDocs data source.
Maps WorkDocs document source fields to Amazon Kendra index fields, defining how document metadata is indexed and stored in the Kendra index.
The name of a metadata field in the WorkDocs data source that is mapped to a target Kendra index field.
Specifies the date format string that Amazon Kendra uses to interpret a date value from a WorkDocs field when mapping it to an Amazon Kendra index field.
The name of the field in the Amazon Kendra index that the WorkDocs data source field is mapped to.
A list of regular expression patterns that match WorkDocs document names to include in the Kendra index; only documents matching at least one pattern are indexed.
Specifies the identifier of the AWS WorkDocs organization (directory) that contains the documents to be indexed by this Kendra data source.
Specifies whether to use the WorkDocs change log to identify and update only documents that have changed since the last crawl, rather than scanning the entire repository.

aws_kendra_data_source.tags.key.text: The key of a key-value tag attached to the Kendra data source.

aws_kendra_faq.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Kendra FAQ resource.

aws_kendra_faq.name.text: The name of the FAQ, a required human-readable identifier used to distinguish this FAQ within Amazon Kendra.

aws_kendra_faq.role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon Kendra assumes to read the FAQ file from your S3 bucket.

aws_kendra_faq.s3_path.text: The S3 location (bucket and object key) of the FAQ file stored in Amazon S3.

aws_kendra_faq.s3_path.bucket.text: The name of the S3 bucket that contains the FAQ data file specified for the Kendra FAQ.

aws_kendra_faq.s3_path.key.text: The S3 object key (file name/path) within the bucket that points to the FAQ file used by the Kendra index.

aws_kendra_faq.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Kendra FAQ, used to identify and categorize the resource for management and cost allocation.

aws_kendra_faq.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag (a key-value pair) attached to the Amazon Kendra FAQ resource, used for metadata, categorization, and cost allocation.

aws_kendra_index.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Kendra index within AWS.

aws_kendra_index.capacity_units.text: Specifies the query and storage capacity units that configure the throughput and storage capacity of the Amazon Kendra index.

aws_kendra_index.capacity_units.query_ca.text: The number of query capacity units allocated to the index, which determines the query throughput in queries per second that the index can support.

aws_kendra_index.capacity_units.storage_.text: Specifies the storage capacity (in gigabytes) provisioned for the Amazon Kendra index, determining how much document content and metadata can be stored.

aws_kendra_index.description.text: Provides a description of the Amazon Kendra index, e.g., to indicate its intended use or contents.

aws_kendra_index.document_metadata_confi.text: Configures the list of metadata fields that can be attached to documents in the Kendra index, defining each field's name, data type, and search properties such as faceting, display, and sorting.
The name of a custom metadata field for documents in the index, as defined in the DocumentMetadataConfiguration property.
Specifies relevance settings, such as importance and freshness, that control how this metadata field influences search result ranking in the Kendra index.
Sets the ISO 8601 duration (e.g., 'P30D') during which a document is considered recent for freshness-based relevance scoring within this metadata field's relevance configuration.
Determines whether the last-updated timestamp of this metadata field is used as a freshness signal to boost recently updated documents in Kendra search ranking.
Determines the weighting of this custom metadata field in Kendra's relevance scoring, where higher values increase the impact of matches on this field on search result rankings.
Determines whether the values of this metadata field are ranked in ascending or descending order when contributing to a document's relevance score.
Specifies a list of importance weights for specific values of this metadata field, used to adjust the relevance ranking of documents based on the presence of those field values.
The specific metadata field value (e.g., a string like 'Premium') for which the associated importance score adjusts relevance for documents containing that exact value.

The numeric importance weight (from 1 to 10) assigned to a specific value of a metadata field, which determines how much that value influences search relevance for the Kendra index, with 5 as the neutral baseline.
Specifies search-related settings for the metadata field, including whether it is facetable, searchable, displayable, and sortable in Amazon Kendra search results.
Indicates whether the metadata field's values can be displayed in the search results returned by Amazon Kendra.
Indicates whether the metadata field can be used to create facets in Kendra search results, allowing users to filter and narrow down search results by that field.
Indicates whether this document metadata field can be searched (i.e., used in query text) within the Amazon Kendra index.
Indicates whether this metadata field can be used to sort search results in the Kendra index.
Specifies the data type of the document metadata field (e.g., STRING, STRING_LIST, LONG_VALUE, DATE_VALUE), which determines how the field's values are indexed and used for filtering and search.

aws_kendra_index.server_side_encryption_.text: Specifies the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the index for server-side encryption.
Specifies the AWS KMS key ID (ARN) used to encrypt the index data, enabling customer-managed key encryption for the Amazon Kendra index.

aws_kendra_index.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the Amazon Kendra index, used to categorize and manage the index for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization.

aws_kendra_index.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag attached to the Amazon Kendra index, used for metadata, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_kendra_index.user_context_policy.text: Determines whether user context filtering is applied to search results, using either attribute-based filtering or user token-based access control.

aws_kendra_index.user_token_configuratio.text: Configures token-based user context filtering for the index by specifying either a JSON token or JWT token type and its associated parameters.
Specifies the JSON token type configuration for user token authentication, defining which attributes in the JSON token map to the user name and group fields for access control in Amazon Kendra.
The name of the group attribute field in the JSON token that identifies the user's group memberships for access control.
Specifies the name of the JSON field that contains the user name, used by the index's JSON token configuration for access control.

Defines the JWT token type configuration for Kendra index user access control, including how to retrieve the JWT token from a secret or URL, and which user and group attributes to use for access control.
Specifies a regular expression pattern used to extract the user name from the JWT token's claim for mapping to a Kendra user identity in access control.
The name of the JWT token attribute that contains the list of group names for the user, used by Amazon Kendra to filter search results based on group membership.
The issuer claim (iss) from the JWT token that identifies the principal that issued the token, used by Kendra to validate the token's origin.
Specifies where the JWT signing key is stored, either in a URL or in AWS Secrets Manager.
The ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the JWT signing keys used to validate user tokens for Kendra index access control.
The URL of the identity provider (IdP) that issues the JWT tokens used for user access control in the Kendra index.
The name of the attribute in the JWT token that contains the user name for access control.

aws_kendra_query_suggestions_block_list..text: The tag key for a tag assigned to the query suggestions block list, used to organize, categorize, and identify the resource within your AWS environment.

tags.value represents the value component of a user-defined tag attached to the Amazon Kendra query suggestions block list, enabling you to assign metadata such as environment, project, or cost center for resource organization and management.

aws_kendra_ranking_execution_plan.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Kendra Ranking execution plan.

aws_kendra_ranking_execution_plan.capaci.text: Specifies the capacity configuration for the execution plan, including the number of rescore capacity units allocated to handle query processing for Amazon Kendra Intelligent Ranking.
Specifies the number of rescore capacity units for the execution plan, which determines the rescoring query capacity (throughput) of the plan.

aws_kendra_ranking_execution_plan.descri.text: An optional description of the Amazon Kendra ranking execution plan, used to provide additional context or identification for the plan.

aws_kendra_ranking_execution_plan.tags.k.text: The key (name) of an arbitrary tag attached to the AWS Kendra Ranking execution plan, used for organizing, identifying, and filtering the resource.

aws_kendra_ranking_execution_plan.tags.v.text: The value of a tag key-value pair assigned to the Amazon Kendra Intelligent Ranking execution plan, used to organize, identify, and manage access to the resource.

aws_kendra_thesaurus.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to an AWS Kendra thesaurus, used to organize and identify the resource for management and billing.

aws_kendra_thesaurus.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag entry associated with the AWS Kendra thesaurus, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_key_pair.key_fingerprint.text: The SHA-1 digest of the DER-encoded public key for the EC2 key pair, used to verify the key's identity.

aws_key_pair.key_pair_id.text: The unique identifier that AWS assigns to the key pair upon creation, for example 'key-1234567890abcdef0'.

aws_key_pair.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the EC2 key pair, used to organize and identify the resource within AWS.

aws_kinesis_analytics_application.applic.text: Specifies the SQL statements that define the data processing logic of the Kinesis Analytics application, including how input streams are transformed and output to destinations.
A user-supplied, optional description string that provides human-readable context for the Kinesis Analytics application.
The name of the Kinesis Analytics application, used to identify and reference the application within AWS.
