The `duration_in_seconds` field in `iceberg_destination_configuration.retry_options` specifies the maximum number of seconds that Kinesis Data Firehose retries delivery of data to the Iceberg destination after a write failure before treating the data as undeliverable.
The ARN of the IAM role that Firehose assumes to write to the Iceberg table, granting permissions for the Glue catalog and underlying S3 data.
Sets whether Amazon S3 receives backup copies of only failed events or all events when delivering to the Iceberg destination.

Specifies the S3 staging configuration, including bucket ARN, prefix, buffering hints, compression, encryption, and CloudWatch logging options, that Kinesis Data Firehose uses to temporarily store data before delivering it to the Iceberg destination.
The ARN of the S3 bucket that Kinesis Data Firehose uses as a staging location for incoming data before delivering it to the specified Iceberg table.
Configures the buffering size (in MBs) and interval (in seconds) that determine how much incoming data is accumulated before Firehose writes a new object to the S3 destination.
Specifies the number of seconds Kinesis Data Firehose buffers incoming data for the Iceberg destination before delivering it to the intermediate S3 bucket, controlling the frequency of S3 writes.
The maximum size in megabytes that Firehose buffers for the S3 configuration of the Iceberg destination before delivering data to the Iceberg table.

Specifies whether CloudWatch logging is enabled for the S3 configuration of the Iceberg destination, and if enabled, identifies the CloudWatch log group and log stream names that Firehose will deliver S3 operation logs to.
Enables or disables CloudWatch logging for the S3 staging bucket used by the Iceberg destination.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group where the S3 configuration for this Firehose Iceberg destination sends operational logs, such as delivery errors for backup S3 objects.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log stream where Firehose publishes log entries for the S3 configuration associated with the Iceberg destination.
Specifies the compression format (such as GZIP or Snappy) applied to objects written to the S3 bucket that backs the Iceberg destination configuration.
The encryption settings for the S3 staging/backup location used by the Iceberg destination, which lets you specify a KMS key ARN to encrypt the objects written to S3.
Specifies the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the staging Amazon S3 objects when writing to an Iceberg destination, enabling server-side encryption with a customer-managed key.
Specifies the ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the S3 configuration of the Iceberg destination for the Firehose delivery stream.
Specifies that no encryption is applied to the S3 destination by setting the value to 'NoEncryption', effectively opting out of server-side encryption for the Iceberg destination's S3 configuration.

The S3 object key prefix for error output (records that failed delivery to the Iceberg destination) within the S3 bucket configured in this s3_configuration, used to segregate failed records from successfully processed ones.
Specifies the prefix for Amazon S3 object keys when Firehose writes data to the S3 bucket configured for the Iceberg destination's S3 configuration (used for staging or error records).

The ARN of the IAM role that Kinesis Data Firehose assumes to write to the S3 bucket specified in this S3 configuration, which serves as the staging and error-handling storage for the Iceberg destination.
Specifies whether Firehose automatically updates the Iceberg table schema as new fields arrive, including the catalog type used for schema tracking.
Whether Firehose automatically evolves the Iceberg table schema to accommodate new fields in incoming records.
Specifies the configuration for automatically creating an Iceberg table in the Glue Data Catalog when delivering data via this Firehose stream, including the table schema and partitioning.
Indicates whether Kinesis Data Firehose automatically creates the destination Iceberg table if it does not already exist when delivering to the Iceberg destination.

aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream.kin.text: Specifies the configuration for using a Kinesis data stream as the source of the delivery stream, including the Kinesis stream ARN and the IAM role that Firehose assumes to read from it.
The ARN of the Kinesis data stream that serves as the source for the Firehose delivery stream, from which records are read and delivered.
The ARN of the IAM role that grants Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose permission to read records from the source Kinesis stream.

aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream.msk.text: Defines the Amazon MSK source parameters for the delivery stream, including the Kafka topic name, MSK cluster endpoint, and authentication configuration used to ingest streaming data from an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka cluster.
The authentication configuration for the MSK source, specifying the connectivity type (public or private) and the IAM role ARN that Firehose assumes to access the cluster.
The connectivity setting determines whether the Delivery Stream connects to the MSK cluster over the public internet or through a VPC (private connectivity), with valid values PUBLIC and PRIVATE.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon Data Firehose assumes to access the Amazon MSK cluster.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the MSK cluster that the delivery stream reads data from.
Specifies the ISO 8601 timestamp from which the Firehose delivery stream begins consuming records from the MSK topic, allowing replay of historical data from that point onward.
The name of the Apache Kafka topic on the MSK cluster that this Firehose delivery stream reads from as its source.

aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream.red.text: Specifies the destination settings for delivering Firehose stream data to an Amazon Redshift cluster, including the JDBC connection URL, copy command, S3 staging configuration, and IAM role.
Configures CloudWatch Logs for the Redshift destination of the delivery stream, specifying whether logging is enabled and the log group and log stream where delivery stream logs are written.
Specifies whether CloudWatch logging is enabled for the Redshift destination, allowing Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver delivery stream logs to CloudWatch Logs.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group where Kinesis Data Firehose delivers logs for the Redshift destination.
Specifies the name of the CloudWatch Logs log stream where Kinesis Data Firehose delivers the log events for the Redshift destination (such as authentication or delivery failure logs).
The JDBC connection URL for the Amazon Redshift cluster that Firehose uses to connect when delivering data.
Defines the Amazon Redshift COPY command settings (target table name, column list, and copy options) that Kinesis Data Firehose uses to load staged S3 data into the Redshift destination table.
Specifies the options string (e.g., 'CSV', 'GZIP') that is appended to the Redshift COPY command to control the format and behavior of data loading from the Firehose S3 source.
Comma-separated list of column names in the target Redshift table that the COPY command should load data into, controlling which columns receive the incoming Firehose records.
The name of the target Redshift table (which must already exist) into which the Firehose delivery stream loads data via the COPY command.
The password for the Redshift user account that Firehose uses to authenticate and execute the COPY command when loading data into the Redshift cluster.
Specifies the processing configuration for the Redshift destination, enabling data transformation (such as via Lambda) to run on incoming records before they are loaded.
Indicates whether data processing (e.g., Lambda transformation) is enabled for the delivery stream before delivering data to Redshift.
A list of data processors (such as AWS Lambda functions) that are applied to incoming records before they are delivered to Redshift, allowing for transformation and format conversion.
Specifies the name-value pairs that configure a processing processor in the Redshift destination, such as the Lambda function ARN and buffering settings for the AWS Lambda processor.
The name of the processing parameter (e.g., LambdaArn, NumberOfRetries, BufferSizeInMBs, or BufferIntervalInSeconds) passed to the processor in the Redshift destination's processing configuration.
The value to assign to the processor parameter (as identified by its parameter_name) for the data processing transform applied to records before they are delivered to the Redshift destination.
Specifies the kind of transformation applied to source records before they are delivered to Redshift, such as AppendDelimiterToRecord, RecordDeAggregation, MetadataExtraction, or Lambda.
Configures the retry behavior for the Redshift destination, defining the duration in seconds during which Kinesis Data Firehose retries a failed delivery before giving up.
Specifies the duration of time (in seconds) for which Kinesis Data Firehose retries delivering data to Amazon Redshift after a delivery failure.
The ARN of the IAM role that Kinesis Data Firehose assumes to access the Redshift cluster and perform the load operation.
The S3 destination configuration used to back up data delivered to the Redshift destination when S3 backup mode is enabled.
The ARN of the S3 bucket that Firehose uses to back up data before delivering to Redshift.
The buffering hints that define the size (in MBs) and interval (in seconds) for buffering incoming data before it is written to the S3 backup destination of the Redshift destination.

The number of seconds (0-900) for which Kinesis Data Firehose buffers incoming data to the backup S3 bucket before delivering it to Redshift, controlling the buffering interval for the s3_backup_configuration.
Specifies the buffer size in MBs that Firehose accumulates in memory before flushing data to the S3 backup destination, triggering a write once the buffered data reaches this threshold.
Specifies the CloudWatch logging options (enabled flag, log group name, and log stream name) for the S3 backup configuration used when delivering data to Redshift.
Whether CloudWatch logging is enabled for the S3 backup destination of the Redshift destination configuration.
The name of the CloudWatch log group where logs for the S3 backup configuration of the Redshift destination are delivered.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log stream that receives log events for the S3 backup delivery of the Redshift destination.
Specifies the compression format (e.g., GZIP, ZIP, SNAPPY, or UNCOMPRESSED) applied to objects stored in the S3 backup bucket for the Redshift destination.
Configures the server-side encryption settings (e.g., AWS KMS key) for the S3 backup bucket used by the Redshift destination when data delivery fails or is backed up.
The KMS encryption configuration object for the S3 backup bucket of the Redshift destination, containing the ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt backup data at rest.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the S3 backup bucket for the Redshift destination of the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream.
Indicates that no server-side encryption is applied to the S3 backup of the Redshift destination, and when set to 'NoEncryption', disables encryption for that backup bucket.
The path prefix under the S3 backup bucket where Firehose writes files containing records that failed to be processed or delivered when backing up to S3 from the Redshift destination.

This prefix determines the directory structure within the S3 backup bucket that Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose uses when writing backup data from the Redshift destination, allowing you to organize backup files under a specific key prefix.
The ARN of the IAM role that Kinesis Data Firehose assumes to write backup data to the S3 bucket.
Specifies whether backups of all data delivered to Amazon Redshift are also sent to Amazon S3; valid values are 'Disabled' (default) and 'Enabled'.
Defines the S3 bucket and prefix (with optional buffering, compression, and encryption settings) where Firehose temporarily stores incoming data before loading it into the Redshift destination.
The ARN of the S3 bucket that Kinesis Data Firehose uses as a staging location to store intermediate data before delivering it to the Redshift destination.
Configures the buffering size (in MBs) and interval (in seconds) for the intermediate S3 bucket that receives data before it is copied to Redshift.

Specifies the length of time, in seconds, that Kinesis Data Firehose buffers incoming data for the Amazon S3 staging location before delivering it to S3, where this S3 configuration serves as the intermediate destination for the Redshift COPY operation.

The size in MB of the data buffer that, when filled, triggers Firehose to deliver the buffered data to the S3 staging bucket before copying it to Redshift for the Redshift destination's S3 configuration.
Configures CloudWatch logging for the S3 backup used by the Redshift destination, including whether logging is enabled and the log group and stream where Firehose delivers logs.
Whether CloudWatch logging is enabled for the S3 backup configuration associated with the Redshift destination of this Kinesis Firehose delivery stream.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group to which the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream sends S3 backup or error logs for the Redshift destination's S3 configuration.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log stream where Kinesis Data Firehose delivers log entries for the S3 configuration associated with the Redshift destination.
The compression format (e.g., GZIP, ZIP, SNAPPY) used for objects written to the S3 bucket configured for the Redshift destination of the Firehose delivery stream.
Configures the encryption settings for the S3 staging/backup bucket used by the Redshift destination, including the AWS KMS key ARN when KMS encryption is enabled.
Specifies the AWS KMS key (via its ARN) used to encrypt the S3 staging bucket data for the Redshift destination in the Firehose delivery stream.

The ARN of the AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) used to encrypt the data in the S3 bucket that Kinesis Data Firehose delivers to before loading into Redshift, as configured under the S3 encryption settings for the Redshift destination.
Indicates that no server-side encryption should be used for the S3 destination, with the only valid value being 'NoEncryption'.
Specifies the Amazon S3 key prefix under which Kinesis Data Firehose writes records that fail to be delivered to Redshift, allowing you to organize error output files separately in the S3 bucket.

The prefix to prepend to S3 object keys in the staging bucket used by the Redshift destination, enabling organization and dynamic partitioning (e.g., with !{timestamp:yyyy}) before data is loaded into Redshift.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Kinesis Firehose assumes to write to the S3 bucket used as the staging location for loading data into Redshift.

Configures the AWS Secrets Manager integration for the Redshift destination, allowing Firehose to retrieve the Redshift database credentials from a Secrets Manager secret instead of supplying them inline.
Indicates whether the Firehose delivery stream uses AWS Secrets Manager to retrieve the Redshift destination's credentials.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Kinesis Firehose assumes to access the AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the Redshift cluster credentials.

The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the Redshift cluster credentials (such as username and password) used by Firehose to connect to the Amazon Redshift cluster for this destination configuration.

The username of the Amazon Redshift database user that Kinesis Data Firehose authenticates with to load data into the Redshift cluster, requiring privileges for the COPY, INSERT, and CREATE TEMP TABLE operations.

aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream.s3_.text: Configures an Amazon S3 bucket as the delivery destination for a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream, specifying the bucket ARN, IAM role, and optional prefix/buffering settings.
The ARN of the S3 bucket that the Firehose delivery stream delivers data to when S3 is configured as the destination.
Specifies the buffering size (in MBs) and buffering interval (in seconds) that determine when data is flushed from the Firehose delivery stream to the S3 destination.
The number of seconds (60–900) to buffer incoming data before delivering a batch to Amazon S3, after which the Firehose delivers the accumulated records even if the size hint hasn't been reached.
Specifies the approximate size, in mebibytes (MiBs), of the data buffer before Kinesis Data Firehose delivers the data to the S3 destination.
Configures CloudWatch Logs delivery for the S3 destination, specifying whether logging is enabled and the target log group and log stream names.
Whether CloudWatch logging is enabled for the S3 destination of the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group where the Firehose delivery stream sends its S3 destination delivery logs.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log stream to which Kinesis Data Firehose delivers logs for the S3 destination.
This field specifies the compression format for objects stored in the S3 destination, such as UNCOMPRESSED, GZIP, ZIP, or SNAPPY.
Configures encryption for the destination S3 bucket, with an optional KMSEncryptionConfig property to specify an AWS KMS key for server-side encryption.
Specifies the AWS KMS key ARN used to encrypt data delivered to the S3 bucket.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt data written to the S3 destination of the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream.
This optional string field, when set to 'NoEncryption', explicitly disables encryption for the S3 destination; it must not be specified alongside the KMS encryption configuration.
Specifies the prefix for S3 objects that store records that failed to be processed or delivered by the Kinesis Firehose stream, written to the configured S3 bucket.
The S3 object key prefix that Firehose prepends to each delivered object's name, which can include date/time format variables like YYYY/MM/dd/HH to organize data by time.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose assumes to write data to the S3 bucket in this destination configuration.

aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream.sno.text: This field specifies the configuration for delivering Kinesis Data Firehose stream data to a Snowflake destination, including the Snowflake account URL, database, schema, table, and authentication credentials.
The URL of the Snowflake account (e.g., https://account-name.snowflakecomputing.com) to which the Firehose delivery stream writes data.

Buffering hints configure the in-flight data buffering size (in MB) and buffering interval (in seconds) before the Kinesis Data Firehose delivers the accumulated data to Snowflake, allowing you to trade off between lower latency and lower delivery frequency.
The number of seconds that Kinesis Data Firehose buffers incoming data before delivering it to the Snowflake destination, with a maximum of 900 seconds.
Specifies the buffer size in MBs for the Snowflake destination, defining how much data Kinesis Data Firehose accumulates before writing to Snowflake.
CloudWatch logging options for the Snowflake destination, including whether logging is enabled and the CloudWatch log group and stream names to send Firehose delivery errors to.
Whether CloudWatch logging is enabled for the Snowflake destination of the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group to which Firehose delivers log events for the Snowflake destination configuration, used to monitor delivery status and errors.
Specifies the name of the CloudWatch Logs log stream where the Firehose delivery stream sends its log events when CloudWatch logging is enabled for the Snowflake destination.
Specifies the name of the column in the Snowflake table where the Firehose-delivered data (the actual content payload) is stored, separate from any metadata columns.
Specifies how Firehose loads data into Snowflake: 'JSON_MAPPING' (default) maps JSON fields to individual columns, whereas 'VARIANT_CONTENT' stores each entire record as a single VARIANT column.
The name of the Snowflake database to which the delivery stream writes data.
The passphrase that protects the encrypted private key used for Snowflake authentication, required only when the private key is encrypted.
Specifies the name of the metadata column that Firehose creates in the Snowflake destination table to store metadata about each delivered record.
The private key used for Snowflake key-pair authentication, required when AuthenticationMode is set to KeyPair.
Configures data transformation (such as an AWS Lambda function) to process records before they are delivered to the Snowflake destination.
Indicates whether data transformation processing (such as an AWS Lambda processor) is enabled for the Snowflake destination configuration.
Defines the ordered list of data transformation processors (such as AWS Lambda or built-in record formatting) applied to incoming records before they are delivered to the Snowflake destination.
Defines the list of key-value parameter objects (e.g., LambdaArn, NumberOfRetries) that configure each processor in the data processing pipeline for the Snowflake destination.
The name of the processor parameter, such as 'LambdaArn' or 'NumberOfRetries', that defines the specific setting for the firehose processing step.

Holds the value for a processor configuration parameter (such as the Lambda function ARN or buffer size) associated with the corresponding parameter name in the processors parameters list of the Firehose processing configuration.
Specifies the type of data processor to apply to records before they are delivered to the Snowflake destination, such as Lambda, RecordDeAggregation, MetadataExtraction, or AppendDelimiterToRecord.
Specifies the retry behavior for delivery to Snowflake, including the maximum retry duration in seconds when a delivery attempt fails.
Specifies the duration in seconds during which Kinesis Data Firehose retries delivering data to the Snowflake destination in the event of a delivery failure.
The ARN of the IAM role that Kinesis Data Firehose assumes to access Snowflake, granting the necessary permissions for the Snowflake destination.
Controls whether Firehose backs up the original source records to the Amazon S3 bucket specified in the Snowflake destination's S3Configuration, with valid values 'Enabled' and 'Disabled'.

Configures the S3 bucket where Kinesis Data Firehose buffers or backs up data before delivering it to the Snowflake destination, including bucket name, prefix, buffering hints, compression, and encryption settings.
The ARN of the S3 bucket that Kinesis Data Firehose uses to stage data before delivering it to Snowflake.
Specifies how much data (in MB) and how long (in seconds) Firehose should buffer incoming records in the intermediate S3 bucket before delivering them to Snowflake.

Specifies the maximum time, in seconds, that Kinesis Data Firehose buffers incoming data in the S3 bucket used for staging before delivering it to Snowflake, as part of the buffering hints for the S3 configuration.
Specifies the buffer size in MBs that Firehose accumulates before delivering data to the S3 staging bucket used for the Snowflake destination.
Configures CloudWatch Logs for the S3 staging bucket used by the Snowflake destination, controlling whether to enable logging and specifying the log group and stream for the S3 operations.
Indicates whether CloudWatch logging is enabled for the S3 backup configuration used by the Snowflake destination, controlling whether Firehose delivers S3-related delivery logs to CloudWatch Logs.
Specifies the name of the CloudWatch Logs log group to which Kinesis Data Firehose delivers log events for the S3 staging bucket associated with the Snowflake destination.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log stream that records log entries for the S3 backup configuration of the Snowflake destination in the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream.
Specifies the compression format (e.g., UNCOMPRESSED, GZIP, ZIP, SNAPPY) for S3 backup objects written by the Snowflake destination configuration in this Firehose delivery stream.
Specifies the encryption settings (including the KMS key ARN) for the S3 backup bucket used by the Snowflake destination in the Firehose delivery stream.
Specifies the AWS KMS key used to encrypt data in the S3 bucket for the Snowflake destination of the Firehose delivery stream.
Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the S3 staging bucket content for the Snowflake destination.
Specifies that no server-side encryption is applied to the S3 bucket; the only valid value is 'NoEncryption'.
The S3 object key prefix used for records that fail to be delivered to the Snowflake destination, written to the specified S3 bucket in the S3 configuration.
The S3 object key prefix under which data files are stored in the staging S3 bucket for the Snowflake destination.
The ARN of the IAM role that Kinesis Data Firehose assumes to write the Snowflake destination's backup or intermediate data to the configured S3 bucket.
The name of the Snowflake database schema where Firehose writes the ingested data.
Configuration for retrieving Snowflake credentials from AWS Secrets Manager instead of specifying them directly in the destination configuration.

Indicates whether the Snowflake destination is configured to fetch credentials from AWS Secrets Manager, allowing the delivery stream to reference a secret instead of embedding the password in the configuration.
The ARN of the IAM role that Kinesis Data Firehose assumes to retrieve the Snowflake connection credentials from AWS Secrets Manager.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the Snowflake credentials (such as username and password) used by the delivery stream to authenticate with Snowflake.
Contains settings to enable and specify a Snowflake role that the Firehose delivery stream uses when writing data to the Snowflake destination.
Indicates whether the IAM role configuration is enabled for the Snowflake destination, allowing Firehose to assume the specified role when delivering data.
Specifies the Snowflake role that Kinesis Data Firehose uses for the Snowflake session when delivering data to the configured Snowflake destination.
Defines the VPC configuration for the Snowflake destination, specifying the PrivateLink VPC endpoint ID that Firehose uses to connect to Snowflake over a private network.
The ID of the VPC endpoint (VPCE) that Firehose uses to connect to Snowflake via AWS PrivateLink.
The name of the Snowflake table that the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream writes records to.
The Snowflake user name used to authenticate the delivery stream when writing data to the configured Snowflake database and schema.

aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream.spl.text: Defines the destination configuration for sending data to Splunk, including the Splunk endpoint, access credentials, buffering and retry settings, and optional S3 backup for failed records.
Settings that control when data is buffered and sent to Splunk, such as the buffer size in MB and the buffer interval in seconds, to optimize delivery batching.
The number of seconds that Kinesis Data Firehose buffers incoming data before delivering it to the Splunk destination, with a minimum of 60 seconds and a maximum of 900 seconds.
The buffer size in MB that Kinesis Data Firehose accumulates for a Splunk destination before delivering the data, controlling the trade-off between delivery frequency and throughput efficiency.
CloudWatch logging options for the Splunk destination, specifying whether logging is enabled and the log group and log stream names where Firehose delivery logs are published.
Whether CloudWatch logging is enabled for the Splunk destination of the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group where Kinesis Data Firehose delivers logs related to the Splunk destination configuration when CloudWatch logging is enabled.
The name of the CloudWatch log stream where Kinesis Data Firehose sends the logs for this Splunk destination when CloudWatch logging is enabled.
The number of seconds Kinesis Data Firehose waits for an acknowledgment from Splunk after sending data before treating the delivery as failed and retrying.
The URL of the Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) endpoint that Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose uses to deliver data to your Splunk cluster.
Specifies whether the Splunk HEC endpoint type is for event data or raw data, accepting the values 'Event' or 'Raw'.
The HTTP Event Collector (HEC) token that authenticates the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to the configured Splunk HEC endpoint.

Configure data transformation for the Splunk destination by specifying whether processing is enabled and the list of processors (such as a Lambda function) that act on incoming records before they are delivered to Splunk.
Whether data processing (e.g., Lambda transformation) is enabled for the delivery stream before delivering to Splunk.
Specifies the list of data processors (such as Lambda or record format conversion) applied to records in the processing configuration before they are delivered to the Splunk destination.

A list of ProcessorParameter objects (name-value pairs) that configure the processing processor, e.g., for the Lambda processor specifying the LambdaArn, NumberOfRetries, and other settings, applied to records before they are sent to Splunk.

Identifies the specific configuration parameter to set for a processor in the Splunk destination's data processing configuration (for example, 'LambdaArn' or 'NumberOfRetries' for a Lambda processor, or 'Delimiter' for an append-delimiter processor).
Specifies the value for a processing parameter, such as the Lambda function ARN when parameter_name is 'LambdaArn', or the JSONPath expression when parameter_name is 'MetadataExtractionQuery'.
Specifies the type of data transformation processor to apply to records before delivering them to Splunk, such as AppendDelimiterToRecord, Lambda, or MetadataExtractor.

Configures the retry behavior for the Splunk destination, specifically the length of time (in seconds) during which Firehose retries data delivery to the Splunk HTTP Event Collector after a failed attempt.
The maximum length of time, in seconds, during which Kinesis Data Firehose retries sending data to Splunk after a delivery failure.
Determines whether all data or only events that failed to deliver to Splunk are backed up to the configured S3 bucket, accepting values 'FailedEventsOnly' or 'AllEvents'.

This object specifies the S3 backup location where Kinesis Data Firehose buffers and stores data before delivering it to the Splunk destination, including the bucket name, prefix, and optional encryption settings.
The ARN of the S3 bucket to which Kinesis Data Firehose delivers backup data for the Splunk destination.
Configures the buffering size (in MB) and buffering interval (in seconds) that determine when data is written to the S3 bucket for the Splunk destination.

Specifies the number of seconds that Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose buffers incoming data to the S3 bucket before delivering it, as part of the buffering hints for the S3 configuration used with the Splunk destination.
The size_in_mbs property sets the buffer size in MiB for incoming data before it is delivered to Amazon S3 as part of the Splunk destination's S3 backup configuration.

Specifies whether CloudWatch logging is enabled for the S3 backup used by the Splunk destination, and optionally names the CloudWatch log group and log stream that receives Firehose's S3 delivery error logs.
Enables Amazon CloudWatch logging for the S3 backup or intermediate destination associated with the Splunk delivery stream, so Firehose can report S3 delivery errors to a CloudWatch log group.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group to which Kinesis Data Firehose delivers logs for the S3 backup destination used by the Splunk destination configuration.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log stream where Firehose delivers logs for the S3 backup configuration when CloudWatch logging is enabled.
Specifies the compression format (e.g., UNCOMPRESSED, GZIP, ZIP, SNAPPY) applied to records delivered to the S3 backup bucket for the Splunk destination in a Firehose delivery stream.
Configures optional server-side encryption for the S3 bucket where Firehose delivers Splunk-backed data, specifying an AWS KMS key via its ARN to encrypt the stored objects.
Specifies the AWS KMS key (via its ARN, under the `AWSKMSKeyARN` property) used to encrypt data in the S3 bucket for the Splunk destination's S3 configuration, when server-side encryption is enabled.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt data in the S3 backup configuration for the Splunk destination.
Determines that the S3 backup bucket for the Splunk destination has no server-side encryption enabled, typically set to 'NoEncryption' as an alternative to KMS-based encryption.
Defines the Amazon S3 key prefix under which Firehose writes error logs for records that failed to deliver to Splunk, within the destination's backup S3 bucket.
The prefix for the S3 object keys, which can include dynamic variables like timestamp and random strings, used to organize and partition the delivered data within the S3 bucket.
The IAM role ARN that grants Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose permission to write to the S3 bucket used for backup or error output when delivering records to Splunk.
Configuration for referencing an AWS Secrets Manager secret that supplies the Splunk HEC token or other credentials used by the Firehose delivery stream to authenticate with Splunk.
Enables the use of AWS Secrets Manager to store and retrieve the Splunk HEC token, instead of providing it directly in the Splunk destination configuration.
The ARN of the IAM role that Kinesis Data Firehose assumes to retrieve the Splunk HTTP endpoint and token from AWS Secrets Manager for the Splunk destination.

The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the Splunk authentication credentials (such as the Splunk access token) used by Firehose when delivering data to the specified Splunk destination.

aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream.tag.text: Assigns a list of key-value tags to the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream, enabling resource categorization for cost allocation and access management.
The key of a user-defined tag assigned to the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_kinesis_stream.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Kinesis stream, used to organize, identify, and manage access to the stream.

aws_kinesis_stream.tags.value.text: Specifies the value of a user-defined tag applied to the Kinesis data stream, allowing you to associate arbitrary metadata with the resource.

aws_kinesis_stream_consumer.tags.key.text: The key of a tag applied to the Kinesis stream consumer, enabling resource identification and attribute-based access control for the consumer.

aws_kinesis_stream_consumer.tags.value.text: Specifies the value for a tag assigned to the Kinesis stream consumer, used for cost allocation, access control, and metadata organization.

aws_kinesis_video_signaling_channel.tags.text: The key of a tag that you can attach to the Kinesis Video Signaling Channel, enabling you to categorize and filter the channel by user-defined metadata.
The value portion of a user-defined tag attached to the signaling channel, allowing you to store arbitrary metadata (e.g., names, owners, or environments) for resource management and cost allocation.

aws_kinesis_video_stream.tags.key.text: The key (name) portion of a tag attached to the Kinesis Video Stream, used as a unique identifier within the stream's tag set for organizing, managing, and tracking the resource.

aws_kinesis_video_stream.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the Kinesis video stream, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_kms_key.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the KMS key, which uniquely identifies the key in AWS and can be used to reference the key in IAM policies and other AWS services.

aws_kms_key.key_id.text: The globally unique identifier (key ID) of the KMS key, such as a UUID, automatically generated by AWS KMS.

aws_kms_key.tags.key.text: The tag key of a metadata tag attached to the AWS KMS key, used for organizing, identifying, and controlling access to the key through tag-based policies.

aws_kms_key.tags.value.text: The arbitrary value portion of a tag attached to the AWS KMS key, enabling metadata for cost allocation, access control, and resource identification.

aws_kms_replica_key.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the replica key.

aws_kms_replica_key.key_id.text: The unique identifier of the replica KMS key, returned as a 32-character UUID string, which can be used to reference the key in IAM policies, aliases, and encryption operations.

aws_kms_replica_key.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS KMS replica key, used as part of a key-value pair to identify, categorize, and manage the resource.

aws_kms_replica_key.tags.value.text: The value component of a key-value tag that can be assigned to the AWS KMS replica key for resource identification and management.

aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings.ad.text: Specifies the list of data lake administrator principals (e.g., IAM users, roles, or AWS accounts) who are granted administrative permissions on the Lake Formation data catalog and resources.
Specifies the identifier (such as an IAM user ARN, role ARN, or account ID) of a principal that is granted administrative rights to the data lake settings.

aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings.al.text: Indicates whether third-party query engines are allowed to access the metadata location for external data filtering in Lake Formation.

Determines whether external data access is allowed to read full Lake Formation tables without applying row- or column-level security filters, enabling unfiltered table data to be accessed by external engines.

aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings.au.text: Specifies the list of session tag values that are authorized for the 'lakeFormation:principal' session tag, controlling which principals can use Lake Formation with those session tags.

aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings.cr.text: Specifies the default permissions that Lake Formation automatically grants to principals on newly created databases in the data lake.
The list of Lake Formation permissions (such as ALL, ALTER, CREATE_TABLE, DESCRIBE, and DROP) that are granted by default to the specified principal when a new database is created in the data lake.
Specifies the principal (such as an IAM role, IAM user, or account) that receives the default permissions for newly created databases in the data lake.
The ARN or identifier of the Lake Formation principal (such as an IAM role or account) to whom the default database creation permissions are granted.
The default permissions granted to principals when new tables are created in the data lake.
Specifies the list of Lake Formation table permission strings (such as SELECT, INSERT, ALTER, or DROP) that are granted by default to the principal on newly created tables in the data lake.
Identifies the principal (such as an IAM user, IAM role, or AWS account) that is granted the default table permissions specified in the Lake Formation data lake settings.
Identifies the Lake Formation principal (such as an IAM role, IAM user, or AWS account) to which the default table permissions apply.

aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings.ex.text: Specifies the list of data lake principals (AWS accounts or IAM roles) that are allowed to filter data externally in Lake Formation settings, enabling those principals to use external data filtering capabilities.
The ARN of an IAM principal permitted to use external data filtering, as an entry in the ExternalDataFilteringAllowList of the Lake Formation data lake settings.

aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings.id.text: The catalog ID (typically the AWS account ID) that identifies the data lake settings for this resource.

aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings.mu.text: Specifies the type of mutation to apply to the data lake settings, with allowed values APPEND, REPLACE, ALLOW, or DROP.

aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings.pa.text: Specifies the Parameters map of the Lake Formation DataLakeSettings object, which carries administrative settings like CROSS_ACCOUNT_VERSION to control the cross-account permission model version.

aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings.re.text: A list of Lake Formation principals (such as IAM users or roles) that are granted read-only administrative access to the Data Catalog, allowing them to view data but not modify settings or permissions.

The Data Lake principal identifier (typically an IAM role or user ARN) for a principal included in the read-only admins list, granting that principal read-only administrator permissions on the Lake Formation data lake settings.

aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings.tr.text: A list of AWS account IDs that are trusted to register resources into the data lake, allowing these accounts to create and manage data lake resources even though they are not the data lake owner.

aws_lake_formation_permissions.data_lake.text: The AWS Lake Formation principal (such as an IAM user, role, or account) that receives the granted permissions, identified by its data lake principal identifier.
The data lake principal identifier specifies the unique AWS identity (such as an IAM role ARN, IAM user ARN, or AWS account ID) that the Lake Formation permissions are granted to.

aws_lake_formation_permissions.id.text: A computed composite identifier that uniquely represents the Lake Formation permissions grant, encoding the principal, resource, and permissions to allow Terraform to manage and import the resource.

aws_lake_formation_permissions.permissio.text: The list of Lake Formation permissions to grant on the target resource, such as SELECT, ALTER, DROP, or CREATE_TABLE, defining the actions the principal is allowed to perform.
The list of Lake Formation permissions (e.g., SELECT, INSERT) that are granted to the principal on the resource along with the ability to grant these same permissions to other principals.

aws_lake_formation_permissions.resource.text: The resource object identifies the data lake resource (such as a catalog, database, table, or table with columns) on which the Lake Formation permissions are granted.

aws_lake_formation_permissions.resource..text: This object specifies the Amazon S3 data location (a bucket or prefix) in the Lake Formation catalog to which the permissions are granted, identified by its resource ARN and optional catalog ID.
The ID of the Data Catalog where the data location is registered, defaulting to the caller's account ID if omitted.

The Amazon S3 resource ARN (e.g., arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name) that specifies the data location for which the Lake Formation permissions are granted, under the DataLocationResource of the AWS::LakeFormation::Permissions resource.
Identifies the specific database in the Lake Formation catalog to which the permissions apply, using the database's name (and optionally its catalog ID).
The identifier of the Data Catalog (typically the AWS account ID) where the target database resides, used to scope the permission grant to the database in that specific catalog.
The name of the Lake Formation database to which the permissions apply.
Specifies the table (by database and table name or wildcard) in the Lake Formation catalog for which permissions are granted or revoked.
The identifier of the AWS Glue Data Catalog (typically the AWS account ID) that contains the table to which Lake Formation permissions are being granted.
The name of the Lake Formation database that contains the table for which permissions are being granted.
The name of the Lake Formation table, matching a table in the specified database, to which the permissions are granted.

When set, this object indicates that the table resource refers to all tables in the underlying database via a wildcard, rather than a specific named table, for the Lake Formation permissions resource.

When set, this object identifies the target data resource for the Lake Formation permissions as a specific Data Catalog table (in a database) with a defined list of columns or a column wildcard, scoping the granted permissions to those columns.
The identifier of the Data Catalog (Glue catalog) in which the table is located; if omitted, defaults to the current AWS account ID.
The list of column names in the specified table for which Lake Formation permissions are granted, enabling column-level access control.
Specifies a column wildcard for the table, allowing permissions to apply to all columns except those listed in its excluded column names.
The list of column names to exclude from the column wildcard when granting Lake Formation permissions on a table, effectively granting access to all columns except those listed.
The name of the database in the AWS Glue Data Catalog that contains the table for which Lake Formation permissions are being granted or revoked.
The name of the table within the Lake Formation table-with-columns resource that these permissions apply to.

aws_lake_formation_principal_permissions.text: The list of Lake Formation permissions to grant to the principal, with allowed values such as ALL, ALTER, CREATE_DATABASE, CREATE_TABLE, DATA_LOCATION_ACCESS, DELETE, DESCRIBE, DROP, INSERT, and SELECT.
The list of Lake Formation permissions to grant to the principal, where the principal also receives the ability to grant these permissions to other principals.
Unique identifier for the principal receiving the Lake Formation permissions, such as an AWS account ID, IAM role ARN, or IAM user ARN.
The identifier of the Lake Formation principal (such as an IAM user or role ARN, or an AWS account ID) to which the permissions are granted or revoked.
When set, this field identifies the Data Catalog itself as the resource to which the granted principal permissions apply, meaning the permissions cover all metadata objects in the catalog.
The name of the Lake Formation database that contains the data cells filter to which the principal permissions are being granted.
The name of the AWS Lake Formation Data Cells Filter to which the principal permissions are being granted.
The AWS Glue Data Catalog ID (usually the account ID) of the catalog that contains the database and table for which this data cells filter is defined.
The name of the table in the AWS Glue Data Catalog on which the referenced data cells filter is defined, identifying the specific table resource for this Lake Formation principal permission.
The ID of the AWS Glue Data Catalog (typically the AWS account ID) where the S3 data location is registered and for which permissions are being granted.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 data location that this principal permission applies to, identifying the exact AWS Lake Formation data location resource for the permission grant.
The identifier of the Data Catalog (typically the AWS account ID) that contains the database, used to specify which database resource the principal permissions apply to.
The name of the AWS Glue Data Catalog database to which the principal permissions apply.
The ID of the Data Catalog (typically the AWS account ID) that contains the LF-tag on which the principal permissions are granted.
The key of the Lake Formation LF-tag that defines the resource to which the principal permissions apply.
The LF-tag values that, combined with the tag key, identify the tag resource to which the principal permissions are granted.
The ID of the Glue Data Catalog (typically the AWS account ID) where the LF-Tag policy is defined.

The expression is a list of LF-tag key-value pairs that define the set of Lake Formation resources (e.g., databases or tables) to which the granted principal permissions apply, requiring the resource to match all specified tag keys and at least one value from each key's allowed list.
The key of the LF-Tag in an LF-Tag policy expression that specifies the set of LF-Tags to which the principal permissions apply.
Specifies the allowable values for the LF-tag key in a tag condition of the LF-tag policy expression that determines resource access.
Specifies the resource type for the LF-tag policy, which must be either DATABASE or TABLE, determining the type of Lake Formation resource to which the tag-based permissions apply.
The Data Catalog ID (typically the AWS account ID) that contains the table for which the principal permissions are being granted, used to uniquely identify the table resource.
The name of the AWS Glue Data Catalog database that contains the table for which these Lake Formation principal permissions are being granted.
The name of the table within the database to which the principal permissions are granted.
When set, this field represents a table wildcard, meaning the permission applies to every table under the specified database instead of a single named table.
The identifier of the Data Catalog, typically the AWS account ID, for the table with columns resource.
Specifies the list of column names within the table that the principal's permissions are scoped to, when the resource is set to a TableWithColumns resource.
A list of column names to exclude from the column wildcard, meaning all other columns in the table are matched by the wildcard for the Lake Formation permission grant.
The name of the database in which the table resides for the table-with-columns resource to which permissions apply.
The name of the table (within the specified database) to which the principal permissions apply for selected columns.
The unique AWS-generated identifier for this Lake Formation principal permission grant, which encapsulates the principal and resource that the permission applies to.

aws_lake_formation_resource.hybrid_acces.text: When true, enables hybrid access for the registered resource, allowing it to be accessed through both Lake Formation permissions and IAM/S3 permissions.

aws_lake_formation_resource.id.text: This field is the unique identifier of the Lake Formation resource, typically the ARN of the underlying AWS resource (such as an S3 bucket or DynamoDB table) that has been registered.

aws_lake_formation_resource.resource_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 bucket, database, or table to be registered with AWS Lake Formation.

aws_lake_formation_resource.role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Lake Formation assumes to access and manage the registered S3 data lake location.

aws_lake_formation_resource.use_service_.text: Indicates whether to use the Lake Formation service-linked role when registering the S3 resource; if false, a custom IAM role must be provided in the RoleArn field.

aws_lake_formation_resource.with_federat.text: When set to true, this flag registers the S3 location as a federated resource in AWS Lake Formation, enabling integration with a federated data catalog for access management.

aws_lake_formation_tag.catalog_id.text: The identifier of the Data Catalog (usually the AWS account ID) where the LF-tag is defined, defaulting to the current account if not specified.

aws_lake_formation_tag.tag_key.text: The key (name) of the Lake Formation LF-tag, which together with TagValues forms a tag pair used to classify resources.

aws_lake_formation_tag.tag_values.text: The tag_values field specifies the list of possible values for this Lake Formation tag (LF-tag), which can be assigned to data lake resources for attribute-based access control.

aws_lake_formation_tag_association.lftag.text: The list of LF-Tags (key-value pairs) to associate with the specified resource, where each LF-Tag consists of a tag key and a list of tag values.
The AWS account ID of the Data Catalog where the LF-tag to associate is defined; if omitted, the current account's Data Catalog is used.
The key of an LF-Tag (Lake Formation tag) that is associated with the resource, which must match an existing tag key in AWS Lake Formation.
The list of tag values for a given LF-Tag key in the tag association, specifying which value(s) of that key are applied to the associated Lake Formation resource.

aws_lake_formation_tag_association.resou.text: Specifies the Lake Formation resource (database, table, or table with columns) to which the LF-tags are attached, including optional catalog ID and resource identifiers.
The unique identifier of the AWS Glue Data Catalog (typically the AWS account ID) in which the target database or table exists, used to locate the resource for the LF-Tag association.
The `database` object defines a database resource in the AWS Lake Formation catalog, specifying the catalog ID and database name, to which the referenced LF-tags are associated.
The catalog_id property specifies the AWS account ID of the Data Catalog that contains the database to which the tag is being associated.
The name of the Data Catalog database to which the LF-tag association applies.
The table property of the resource object defines the specific table in the AWS Glue Data Catalog to associate the LF-tags with, supplied via its catalog ID, database name, and table name.
The catalog ID (typically the AWS account ID) of the Data Catalog where the table resides, used to identify the table for which the LF-tag association is being defined.
The name of the Glue database that contains the table to which the LF-tag association is applied.
The name of the table identified in the resource's table property, specifying which table in the referenced database receives the LF-tag association.
When set, this indicates the LF-tag association applies to all tables in the database (a table wildcard), rather than a single named table.
Specifies the Data Catalog table columns to associate the LF-Tag with, including the catalog ID, database name, table name, and a list of column names.
Specifies the AWS Glue Data Catalog ID (typically the AWS account ID) that contains the table whose columns are being associated with an LF-tag, required when targeting a specific table's columns.
The names of the columns within the specified table to which the LF-tags will be associated.
The name of the database in which the table (and optionally its columns) being associated with LF-tags is located.
The name of the table in the Data Catalog to which this tag association applies, as part of the table_with_columns resource identifier.

aws_lambda_alias.routing_config.addition.text: The Lambda function version (e.g., '1' or '$LATEST') that receives a portion of the alias's traffic when weight is assigned, serving as the map key in the additional version weights routing configuration.
Specifies the traffic weight (a number between 0 and 1) that this Lambda function version receives when the alias uses routing configuration to shift traffic between two versions.

aws_lambda_code_signing_config.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the AWS Lambda code signing configuration, used to identify and organize the resource.

aws_lambda_code_signing_config.tags.valu.text: The value of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS Lambda code signing configuration.

aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.amazon_m.text: Specifies the authentication method (e.g., AWS_IAM or BASIC_AUTH) used to access the Glue Schema Registry when the Lambda event source mapping uses Amazon Managed Kafka.
The URI of the schema registry endpoint that Lambda uses to access and resolve message schemas for the Amazon Managed Kafka (MSK) event source mapping.
The name of the Kafka message header attribute that Lambda uses to locate the schema in the MSK Schema Registry for validating records consumed from the topic.

aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.event_so.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Lambda event source mapping.

aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.filter_c.text: The pattern is a JSON string in the event pattern format (for example, an EventBridge pattern or a filter pattern for self-managed sources like Kafka) that determines which events are delivered to the Lambda function from the event source mapping, with each filter in the list defining a single pattern to match against the event payload.

aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.id.text: The unique UUID assigned by AWS to this event source mapping, used to reference it in API calls and other resources.

aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.self_man.text: Specifies the authentication method (e.g., BASIC_AUTH or SASL_SCRAM_256_AUTH) that Lambda uses to access the self-managed Apache Kafka schema registry in the event source mapping's access configuration.
The URI of the schema registry that AWS Lambda connects to for accessing schemas when processing messages from the self-managed Kafka event source.

aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.source_a.text: Specifies the type of source access configuration used by the Lambda event source mapping when connecting to a self-managed Kafka or Amazon MQ broker, such as BASIC_AUTH, VPC_SUBNET, VPC_SECURITY_GROUP, SASL_SCRAM_512_AUTH, SASL_SCRAM_256_AUTH, CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_TLS_AUTH, or SERVER_ROOT_CA_CERTIFICATE.

Specifies the URI whose meaning depends on the SourceAccessConfiguration Type, such as a Kafka bootstrap server URL, a VPC security group ID, or an Amazon MQ basic-auth secret ARN, used when the Lambda event source mapping points to a self-managed Kafka or Amazon MQ source.

aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.tags.key.text: Specifies the key portion of a tag attached to the AWS Lambda event source mapping, which is used to categorize the resource for cost tracking, operational management, and access control via resource-level policies.

aws_lambda_function.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function, which uniquely identifies it within AWS and follows the format arn:aws:lambda:<region>:<account-id>:function:<function-name>.

aws_lambda_function.file_system_configs..text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon EFS access point that provides access to the file system mounted to the Lambda function.
Specifies the directory path (starting with '/mnt/') in the Lambda function's file system where the Amazon EFS file system is mounted, such as '/mnt/efs-data'.

aws_lambda_function.publish_to_latest_pu.text: When set to true, this field triggers publishing a new version of the Lambda function on each deployment, making it the latest published version.

aws_lambda_function.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Lambda function, used to categorize and organize the resource.

aws_lambda_function.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag associated with the Lambda function, used to define metadata such as environment, cost center, or ownership for resource management and cost allocation.

aws_lambda_layer_version.content.text: The `content` field specifies the Amazon S3 bucket, key, and optional object version that store the Lambda layer version's deployment package.

aws_lambda_layer_version.layer_version_a.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Lambda layer version.

aws_lambda_microvm_image.code_artifact.u.text: The Amazon S3 URI of the code artifact that contains the MicroVM image to be registered as a Lambda MicroVM image.

aws_lambda_microvm_image.hooks.microvm_h.text: Specifies the command to execute when the microVM resumes from a paused state, enabling custom lifecycle actions.

aws_lambda_permission.id.text: The unique identifier for the Lambda permission, typically a combination of the function name and the statement ID.

aws_lambda_url.cors.text: Configures cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) settings for the Lambda function URL, specifying allowed origins, methods, headers, and other CORS options.

aws_lambda_url.cors.allow_headers.text: Specifies the list of HTTP headers that are allowed in cross-origin requests to the Lambda function URL when CORS is enabled.

aws_lambda_url.cors.allow_methods.text: Specifies the list of HTTP methods (e.g., GET, POST) that are allowed for cross-origin requests to the Lambda function URL.

aws_lambda_url.cors.allow_origins.text: Specifies the list of origins that are allowed to make cross-origin requests to the Lambda function URL.

aws_lambda_url.cors.expose_headers.text: Specifies the list of response headers that browsers and clients are allowed to access from the cross-origin response in the CORS configuration of an AWS Lambda function URL.

aws_lambda_url.cors.max_age.text: The maximum time in seconds that the browser caches the preflight response for CORS requests to the Lambda function URL.

aws_launch_configuration.block_device_ma.text: The device name (e.g., /dev/xvda, /dev/sdb) exposed to the EC2 instance for this block device mapping in the launch configuration.
The EBS-specific settings (e.g., volume size, type, IOPS, snapshot, encryption, delete-on-termination) for the volume attached via this block device mapping in the Auto Scaling launch configuration.
Controls whether the EBS volume defined in this block device mapping is automatically deleted when the EC2 instance terminates.
Whether the EBS volume in this block device mapping is encrypted, using the default AWS KMS key or the one specified by kms_key_id.

The number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) to provision for the EBS volume, which is required when the volume type is `io1` (provisioned IOPS SSD) in the launch configuration's block device mapping.
The ID of the snapshot to use as the source for the EBS volume in this block device mapping.
The throughput (in MiB/s) to provision for the EBS volume, which is applicable only when the volume type is gp3.
The size of the Amazon EBS volume, in GiB, for the block device mapping in the Auto Scaling launch configuration.
Specifies the Amazon EBS volume type (e.g., gp2, gp3, io1, st1, sc1, standard) for the block device mapped in the launch configuration, affecting performance and cost.
When set to true, suppresses the block device mapping for the specified device name, so the launch configuration does not attach that device to instances launched from it.
Specifies the virtual device name (such as ephemeral0 or ephemeral1) for an ephemeral (instance store) block device in the launch configuration's block device mapping.

aws_launch_template.default_version_numb.text: The version number of the launch template that is currently designated as the default, used when no specific version is requested.

aws_launch_template.latest_version_numbe.text: The current latest version number of the launch template, automatically assigned and incremented by AWS when the template is created or modified.

aws_launch_template.launch_template_data.text: Specifies the device name (for example, /dev/xvda) for the block device as exposed to the EC2 instance, used to identify the volume within the launch template's block device mapping.

Specifies the Amazon EBS volume configuration for the block device mapping, including volume size, type, IOPS, throughput, encryption, delete-on-termination, and snapshot-based settings for the attached EBS volume.
Indicates whether the EBS volume is deleted when the associated EC2 instance is terminated, controlling the lifecycle persistence of the volume.
The index of the EBS card on the Nitro System instance to which this EBS volume is attached, used to specify the EBS card for instances with multiple EBS cards.
Indicates whether the EBS volume is encrypted.

The number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) to provision for the EBS volume, used for Provisioned IOPS volumes (io1/io2) or configurable for gp3 volumes in the launch template's block device mapping.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the EBS volume in this block device mapping; if omitted, the default EBS encryption key is used.
The ID of the Amazon EBS snapshot to use as the source for the EBS volume created by this block device mapping in the launch template.
Specifies the throughput (in MiB/s) to provision for a gp3 EBS volume in the launch template's block device mapping.
Specifies the initialization rate for an EBS volume created from a snapshot, controlling the speed at which the volume is populated and made ready for use.
The size of the EBS volume in GiB to attach to the instance when the block device mapping is applied.
Specifies the Amazon EBS volume type (e.g., gp2, gp3, io1, io2, sc1, st1, standard) for the block device mapping defined in the EC2 launch template's LaunchTemplateData.
Indicates whether to suppress the device mapping for the device specified by the corresponding `device_name`, effectively preventing that device from being attached to the instance.
The virtual device name (e.g., ephemeral0) for an instance store volume in the block device mapping, used when the mapping is for an ephemeral device rather than an EBS volume.
The instance family (e.g., 'c5', 'm5') that serves as a CPU baseline reference when defining baseline performance factors for the launch template's instance requirements.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS License Manager license configuration to associate with instances launched from this launch template.
Indicates whether to associate a Carrier IP address with the network interface (eth0) for instances launched in AWS Wavelength zones using this launch template.
Indicates whether to associate a public IPv4 address with the network interface for instances launched from this launch template.

Specifies the connection tracking idle timeout values (in seconds) for TCP established connections and UDP flows on the network interface, allowing you to tune how long connection states are retained after no activity.
The timeout in seconds for established TCP connections tracked on the network interface, as part of the connection tracking specification in the AWS EC2 launch template.

Specifies the timeout in seconds for an established UDP stream (a bidirectional flow) tracked on the network interface, after which the flow is considered inactive and removed from the connection tracking table.
Specifies the timeout (in seconds) for UDP flows tracked by connection tracking on the network interface.
Indicates whether the network interface is deleted when the associated EC2 instance terminates.
The human-readable description assigned to the network interface, used to identify the purpose or context of the interface within the launch template.
The index of the network interface within the launch template, starting at 0, which determines the order in which interfaces are attached to the instance.
The number of Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) queues to enable for the network interface, which influences the network throughput and packet processing performance of the attached EC2 instance.
Configures Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD) settings for the network interface, including whether SRD is enabled and optional UDP-specific SRD configuration.
Indicates whether Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) Scale Reliable Datagrams (SRD) is enabled for this network interface in the launch template.
Specifies whether UDP traffic over the network interface can use ENA SRD, containing a boolean EnaSrdUdpEnabled setting.
Indicates whether ENA SRD (Scalable Reliable Datagram) is enabled for UDP traffic on this network interface.
The IDs of the security groups to attach to this network interface when instances are launched using the launch template.
Determines the type of network interface to create, where "interface" denotes a standard Elastic Network Interface (ENI) and "efa" enables an Elastic Fabric Adapter for high-throughput HPC workloads.
Specifies the number of IPv4 prefixes to automatically assign to the network interface, enabling the allocation of multiple private IPv4 addresses via CIDR prefixes.
Specifies the IPv4 prefixes to assign to the network interface, where each entry provides a CIDR prefix (and optional description) for an IPv4 prefix to be associated with the interface.
The specific IPv4 CIDR prefix (e.g., 10.0.0.0/28) assigned to the network interface, enabling it to use a block of IPv4 addresses from that prefix.
The number of IPv6 addresses to assign to the network interface in the launch template.
Specifies one or more specific IPv6 addresses to assign to the network interface of the EC2 instance when launched using this launch template.
Specifies an IPv6 address to assign to the network interface when the instance launches.
The number of IPv6 prefixes to assign to the network interface, enabling automatic allocation of /56 IPv6 address blocks for the instance's network configuration.
Specifies one or more IPv6 prefix CIDR blocks to assign to the network interface, where each entry is an object that defines an IPv6 prefix for the interface.
Specifies an IPv6 prefix (CIDR) to be assigned to the network interface when the instance is launched using this launch template.
Specifies the index of the network card for this network interface, used on instance types that support multiple network cards (default is 0, and the primary interface must use card index 0).
The ID of an existing elastic network interface (ENI) to attach to the instance when launched using this launch template.
When set to true, EC2 automatically assigns a primary IPv6 address to the network interface; you cannot specify an explicit IPv6 address in the same network interface when this flag is enabled.
The primary private IPv4 address to assign to the network interface; if omitted, AWS automatically selects an available address from the subnet.
Defines the private IP addresses to assign to the network interface, where each item can specify the IP address and whether it is the primary private IP address.
Indicates whether the specified private IP address is the primary private IP address for the network interface.
Defines the specific private IPv4 address to assign to the network interface, used in the list of private IP address specifications for the EC2 launch template's network interface configuration.
Specifies the number of secondary private IP addresses to assign to the network interface for an EC2 instance launched from this launch template.
Specifies the ID of the subnet in which the network interface is launched, allowing the instance to be placed into a specific VPC subnet.
The type of resource to apply the tags to, such as 'instance' or 'volume'.
A list of key-value pairs that define the tags to apply to the resource type specified by the containing tag specification, such as EC2 instances or volumes launched from this launch template.
The key of the tag to apply to the resource type specified in the tag specification, used to identify and categorize AWS resources launched from the template.
The tag value string to associate with the corresponding tag key for the specified resource type in the launch template's tag specifications.

aws_launch_template.launch_template_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the EC2 launch template.

aws_launch_template.tag_specifications.r.text: The type of AWS resource (such as an EC2 instance or EBS volume) that the tags in this tag specification block apply to, determining which resources created from the launch template receive the defined tags.

aws_launch_template.tag_specifications.t.text: The list of tag objects (key-value pairs) to apply to the AWS resources of the type specified in the enclosing tag_specifications resource_type field when instances are launched from this launch template.
The key of a tag to apply to the resource type defined in the parent tag specification when that resource is created from the launch template.
The value assigned to a tag key in the `tags` map of a tag specification, used to tag the resources (such as EC2 instances or volumes) created by the launch template.

aws_launch_wizard_deployment.specificati.text: The map of key-value pairs that define the application and infrastructure parameters (for example, instance types, subnet IDs, and security group names) used to configure the deployment for the chosen Launch Wizard pattern.

aws_launch_wizard_deployment.status.text: The status of the Launch Wizard deployment, indicating its current lifecycle state such as 'COMPLETED', 'IN_PROGRESS', or 'FAILED'.

aws_launch_wizard_deployment.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Launch Wizard deployment, allowing you to assign arbitrary metadata to the deployment for organizational or cost-tracking purposes.

aws_launch_wizard_deployment.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the AWS Launch Wizard deployment, which lets you attach arbitrary metadata to the deployment for categorization, access control, and cost tracking.

aws_lex_bot.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Amazon Lex bot in AWS.

aws_lex_bot.bot_file_s3_location.text: Configuration for the Amazon S3 location of the bot definition file, specifying the S3 bucket and object key used to import the bot.

aws_lex_bot.bot_file_s3_location.s3_buck.text: The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that contains the bot definition file referenced by this location.

aws_lex_bot.bot_file_s3_location.s3_obje.text: The S3 object key (path) of the JSON file that defines the bot, used when the bot's definition is stored in an S3 bucket.
Specifies the version ID of the S3 object that contains the bot definition file, allowing retrieval of a specific version when S3 versioning is enabled on the bucket.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.text: Defines the list of locale-specific configurations for the bot, each with its own language and country, intents, slot types, and localized prompt/voice settings.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.audio_filler_set.text: Configures the bot locale's audio filler settings, including the maximum duration a filler audio can play while the bot waits for user input.
Specifies the type of audio filler (SILENCE or NOISE) that Amazon Lex uses to manage gaps in speech within a bot locale.
Whether the bot locale uses audio filler, which plays brief audio during pauses to make conversations feel more natural.

Specifies the minimum length of time, in milliseconds, that audio filler (e.g., a beep or spoken filler like 'um') is played during a conversation pause, so that the filler is not interrupted too abruptly when the user resumes speaking.

The delay in milliseconds that Amazon Lex waits before delivering the audio filler response to the user in the specified bot locale, used to prevent premature audio interruption during silence or barge-in.
The number of milliseconds that Amazon Lex waits before playing audio filler in a bot locale when a user pauses during a conversation.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.custom_vocabular.text: Configures the custom vocabulary for the bot locale, containing a list of domain-specific phrases with optional weights that Amazon Lex uses to improve speech recognition accuracy.

Defines the list of custom vocabulary entries (each with a phrase and optional weight/display-as) for the bot locale's custom vocabulary, controlling how Amazon Lex V2 recognizes and renders specific words.
Specifies the alternate display text used in conversation transcripts for this custom vocabulary item, replacing the raw phrase for readability.
The word or phrase to add to the custom vocabulary for a Lex V2 bot locale, enabling the service to recognize and handle this expression in speech recognition.
Sets the relative preference (1-3) that Amazon Lex gives to this custom vocabulary item when matching speech input against the phrase.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.description.text: Provides a descriptive note for a bot locale, identifying the language or regional variant (e.g., English (US)) for the bot's conversational experience.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.generative_aiset.text: Defines the generative AI settings for the bot locale, including configuration for integrating an Amazon Bedrock agent and enabling runtime features such as slot resolution improvement.
Configures the generative AI assistant's behavior during the bot building process, including whether it can retrieve knowledge base answers and the prompt specification used.

Configures the descriptive bot builder feature for the locale's build-time settings, enabling you to control whether the feature is active and specify the Amazon Bedrock model ARN used to generate human-readable descriptions for the bot and its components.
Specifies the Amazon Bedrock foundation model and its inference parameters that the descriptive bot builder uses to generate or improve bot descriptions.

This object configures the Amazon Bedrock guardrail (e.g., its ID and version) that is applied to the Bedrock model used by the descriptive bot builder within the bot locale's generative AI buildtime settings.
Specifies the Amazon Bedrock guardrail identifier (such as its ARN) that is applied to the model's responses during Lex bot build time.
Specifies the version (e.g., '1' or 'DRAFT') of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail that the descriptive bot builder should use to filter the model's responses.
Specifies a custom prompt to use with the Bedrock model for the descriptive bot builder during build time, overriding the default prompt.
Determines whether trace reporting (enabled or disabled) is activated for the Amazon Bedrock model used by the descriptive bot builder within the Lex bot's generative AI settings.
The ARN of the Amazon Bedrock foundation model used to generate descriptive bot builder responses during build-time settings in the Lex bot's generative AI configuration.
Enables or disables the descriptive bot builder, which uses generative AI to automatically generate or refine the bot's description and conversation flow during build time for this locale.

Configures automatic generation of sample utterances during bot build time, including toggling generation on/off and setting the maximum number of sample utterances to generate per intent or slot type.
Specifies the Amazon Bedrock model used to generate sample utterances for the bot locale during build time.
Defines the Amazon Bedrock guardrail (identifier and version) to apply when the specified Bedrock model generates sample utterances.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail to apply to the Bedrock model used for generating sample utterances in the Lex bot's build-time generative AI settings.
Specifies the version of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail to use when the Lex bot's generative AI sample utterance generation feature invokes the Bedrock model.
Specifies a custom prompt template to guide the Bedrock model when generating sample utterances for the bot locale during build-time.
bedrock_trace_status indicates whether trace logging is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for the Amazon Bedrock model calls used during sample utterance generation in the bot locale.
Specifies the Amazon Bedrock model ARN used to generate sample utterances during bot build time for the given locale.
When enabled, Amazon Lex automatically generates additional sample utterances for the bot locale during the build process to improve model understanding.
Specifies the runtime configuration for the Lex bot locale's generative AI feature, including the Amazon Bedrock model and inference settings used at runtime.
