Defines the configuration for the locale's natural language understanding improvement feature, which uses generative AI to enhance the bot's comprehension and classification of user input.
Determines whether the bot locale uses generative AI assistance through Amazon Bedrock to improve intent classification, with values typically 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Whether to enable the NLU improvement specification, which uses generative AI to improve natural language understanding for the bot locale.

Configures intent disambiguation for the bot locale, enabling or disabling Amazon Lex's ability to select the most likely intent when user input could match multiple intents as part of its NLU improvement settings.
Specifies a custom message that Amazon Lex displays to the user to clarify which intent they want to fulfill when the bot cannot confidently determine the user's intent.
Enables or disables intent disambiguation for the bot locale, which lets the bot ask clarifying questions when user input could match multiple intents.
Sets the maximum number of intents Amazon Lex can consider as candidates when performing intent disambiguation for the bot locale's NLU improvement configuration.

Configures whether Amazon Lex uses generative AI to improve slot resolution in the bot locale, and optionally defines the elicitation prompt (via ElicitationSpecification) used when the improved resolution cannot determine a slot value.
Specifies the Amazon Bedrock model configuration, including the model ARN and related settings, used by the slot resolution improvement feature for this Lex bot locale.
Configures the Amazon Bedrock guardrail applied when the Bedrock model performs slot resolution improvement, specifying the guardrail identifier and version to use.
The ARN of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail to use with the Bedrock model for slot resolution improvement.
The version of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail to apply when using the Bedrock model for slot resolution improvement, controlling the guardrail behavior for that model.
Custom prompt text passed to the Bedrock model when it is used to improve slot resolution in Lex bot conversations.
Specifies whether trace logging is enabled for the Amazon Bedrock model used in slot resolution improvement, with allowed values ENABLED and DISABLED.
This is the ARN of the Amazon Bedrock model used by the slot resolution improvement specification to enhance slot filling in a bot locale's generative AI runtime settings for Amazon Lex.

Enables the slot resolution improvement specification within the bot locale's generative AI runtime settings, which directs Amazon Lex to use advanced machine learning to enhance the accuracy of resolving slot values from user input.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.text: Specifies the list of intents defined for a user locale in the Lex bot, where each intent includes its name, sample utterances, and slot configuration.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.bedrock_.text: Defines the Bedrock agent intent configuration for the intent, specifying the Bedrock agent and agent intent IDs that this Lex intent uses to delegate handling to a Bedrock agent.
Defines the configuration for the Amazon Bedrock agent that Lex should invoke for this intent, such as the Bedrock agent alias ARN.
The identifier of the Amazon Bedrock agent alias that this intent uses to invoke the agent for handling conversation.
The unique identifier of the Amazon Bedrock agent that the Lex bot intent is configured to use for agent-based conversation handling.
Configures the Amazon Bedrock knowledge base (identified by its ARN) that this Lex Bedrock agent intent will use to retrieve and ground its responses.
The ARN of the Amazon Bedrock knowledge base that the Bedrock agent for this intent uses to retrieve information for generating responses.
This object configures the Amazon Bedrock model used by the Bedrock agent intent's knowledge base, including the model ARN and related model parameters.
Specifies the Amazon Bedrock guardrail configuration (including the guardrail identifier and version) to apply to the Bedrock model used by the knowledge base configuration for the Lex bot intent.
The identifier (such as an ARN or name) of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail attached to the model configuration for the knowledge base, used to filter or control the model's responses for this intent.
Specifies the version of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail used by the intent's model configuration, such as 'DRAFT' or a specific numeric version like '1'.
Specifies a custom prompt string used to guide the Bedrock model's behavior when it generates responses based on the knowledge base for this intent.
Controls whether detailed trace logs are generated for Bedrock model invocations used by the knowledge base in this Bedrock agent intent, with allowed values like ENABLED or DISABLED.
The ARN of the Amazon Bedrock foundation model used by the knowledge base associated with the Bedrock agent intent configuration in the Lex bot.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.descript.text: A human-readable description of the intent that clarifies its purpose within the bot locale.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.dialog_c.text: Configures the dialog code hook for this intent, including whether it is enabled and the ARN of the Lambda function to invoke for dialog initialization and validation.
When enabled, the dialog code hook (a Lambda function) is invoked for each user input in the intent's conversation to handle fulfillment and validation.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.fulfillm.text: Configures the fulfillment code hook, including the Lambda function and optional post-fulfillment updates, that is invoked to complete the user's request once the intent is fully elicited.
Indicates whether the fulfillment code hook is enabled for the intent, allowing an AWS Lambda function to be invoked to generate a response and fulfill the user's request.
Configures the timeout and provides responses to the user while the fulfillment code hook is running, including start, update, and final messages, to keep the session active during async fulfillment.
Indicates whether fulfillment updates are enabled for the intent, controlling whether Lambda can send progress updates to the user during the fulfillment process.
Defines the initial message and its configuration that Lex sends to the user when the fulfillment update starts, including the message groups and whether the response can be interrupted.
Whether the user can interrupt the start response message while it is being played.
Number of seconds to wait after the fulfillment code hook starts before sending the start response message to the user.

Defines the message groups for the start response, which determine the initial message(s) sent to the user when the Lambda fulfillment code hook begins, where each message group can contain a message and its variations.
Defines a message variant (with contentType and content) that appears as part of a message group in the start response sent to the user when the fulfillment code hook begins executing its updates.
Specifies the custom payload, a free-form string, for the message that is sent to the user when the fulfillment code hook starts providing an update.
Specifies the JSON-formatted custom payload string that is sent to the messaging platform for this start response message in the fulfillment code hook.
Defines the image response card message for the start response of the fulfillment update, specifying the card's title, subtitle, image URL, and optional buttons to present to the user.
Defines the list of buttons displayed on the image response card, where each button has a text label and a value sent back to the bot when selected.
Defines the label text displayed on a button in the image response card for the start response message group of the fulfillment code hook, which users can click to trigger an action in the Lex bot.
The value sent to the Amazon Lex bot when the user clicks this button on the image response card.
The URL of the image displayed in the image response card included in the start response message for the fulfillment updates specification of a code hook.
The subtitle text displayed beneath the title in the image response card shown during the Lex bot's fulfillment update message.
The title of the image response card shown to the user in the start response message group for the intent's fulfillment code hook update in Amazon Lex.

This object provides the literal text for a plain-text message sent to the user at the beginning of intent fulfillment, as part of a message group within the start response of the fulfillment code hook.
The plain text message content sent to the user when the fulfillment update starts, as defined in the start response of the fulfillment code hook for a Lex bot locale intent.
The SSML message object that provides the SSML-formatted text to be spoken to the user in the start response message group when the fulfillment code hook begins.
The SSML text that will be spoken to the user when the fulfillment update starts, allowing the use of SSML tags for speech synthesis.

Defines a list of alternative message variations for a message group within the bot's fulfillment start response, where each variation is a Message object specifying content and formatting for potentially different user experiences.
Defines the custom payload message variation, a JSON string used by the bot to send structured data to the user during the start of a fulfillment update response.

The value that is sent to the Amazon Lex bot as the user's response when this button in the image response card is clicked.
The URL of the image to display in the image response card used in a variation of the declination response message group for the intent confirmation setting.
The subtitle text displayed within an image response card, used in a message variation for the intent confirmation declination response in an Amazon Lex bot.
Sets the title displayed on the image response card for a message variation that Amazon Lex sends when the user declines the intent confirmation prompt.
Configures the plain-text variant of the message sent to the user when they decline the intent confirmation, containing the exact text to be displayed or spoken.
The actual text of the plain-text message shown to the user when they decline to confirm the intent, within the intent confirmation declination response's message group variation.
The SSML-formatted text used as one variation of a message in the message group that Amazon Lex sends when the user declines to confirm an intent.
The SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) text for this variation of the declination response message, which Amazon Lex speaks when the user declines to confirm the intent.
The Lambda function configuration that is invoked when the bot is eliciting confirmation from the user for this intent, allowing the confirmation prompt or acceptance logic to be customized.

If true, the bot invokes the configured code hook (Lambda function) when eliciting confirmation from the user for the intent; if false, no code hook is invoked during the confirmation elicitation step.

Specifies an optional label that is passed to the Lambda function of the elicitation code hook, allowing the Lambda to identify which specific code hook invocation triggered it during intent confirmation.

Defines the conditional branches (including a default branch) that the Lex bot evaluates when the user's response to the intent confirmation prompt fails (i.e., the confirmation is declined or invalid), determining the next dialog action.

The list of conditional branches for the failure conditional of an intent's confirmation setting, each branch containing a condition expression, a response specification, and a next step that are evaluated when the user's confirmation fails.
Defines the condition expression that is evaluated to determine whether the associated conditional branch is executed in the intent confirmation failure flow.

In the context of an intent confirmation failure conditional, this expression string is evaluated at runtime to decide whether the corresponding conditional branch should be executed, supporting variables and comparison/logical operators as defined by Lex.
Specifies the name of the conditional branch, which is used to identify and reference it when evaluating conditions in the failure conditional of the intent's confirmation setting.

Defines the next dialog state (such as eliciting a slot, invoking another intent, or ending the conversation) that the bot transitions to when the failure conditional branch's condition is met during intent confirmation.

Defines the specific Lex action (e.g., elicit a slot, start an intent, or close the conversation) that the bot performs as the next step when the failure conditional branch of the intent confirmation setting is triggered.
Specifies the name of the slot that the bot should elicit from the user when executing this dialog action in the failure conditional branch of the intent confirmation setting.
Indicates whether Amazon Lex should suppress the next message after executing this dialog action in the conditional failure branch, preventing the followed-up message from being sent to the user.
Defines the type of dialog action (e.g., ConfirmIntent, ElicitSlot, Delegate, CloseIntent, ElicitIntent) to be executed in the next step of the conditional branch when intent confirmation fails.
Configures the intent that Lex switches to when this conditional branch's next step is executed, setting the target intent name and optional slot overrides for the new intent.
The name of the target intent for the next step defined in a conditional branch of the failure conditional of an intent's confirmation setting.
Specifies the slot values to set on the target intent when this conditional branch invokes an intent as the next step, mapping each slot name to its overridden value.
The name of the slot in the target intent to set when the failure conditional branch's next step is executed.

Specifies the shape and value used to override a slot in the subsequent intent when executing a conditional branch's next step, enabling the bot to control that slot's value during the conversation flow.
Specifies the shape of the slot value override, either Scalar for a single value or List for multiple values, which determines how the override value is applied to the slot.
Specifies the slot value override's value object that holds the interpreted value (or list of values) to set for the referenced slot in the next step of the conversation.
The string value that Lex uses as the interpreted value for the slot override when setting the slot value in the next step of the conditional branch.
In an AWS Lex bot, this list holds the slot values to use when overriding a list-shaped slot as part of the next step in a conditional branch of an intent's confirmation-setting failure response.

Holds a list of key-value objects that define session attributes to be set in the Amazon Lex session when the bot executes the next step after a conditional branch of an intent's failure confirmation is taken.
The key that names the session attribute to be set in the next step of the conditional branch when the intent confirmation fails.
Value of a session attribute that is set on the next step when the failure conditional branch is taken for an intent's confirmation setting in an Amazon Lex V2 bot.
Defines the message groups and interruption policy that Amazon Lex uses to respond to the user when this conditional branch is taken.
Determines whether the user can interrupt the bot's dynamic response delivered on the failure conditional branch of intent confirmation in the Lex bot.

Lists the message groups (each containing a primary message and optional variations) that Lex uses as the response for the conditional branch within the failure condition of the intent confirmation setting.
Specifies the message content and type (e.g., PlainText, SSML, or CustomPayload) within a message group for the response triggered when a conditional branch's failure condition is met.
Specifies a custom payload (a JSON string) for the message, enabling structured or channel-specific content to be sent in place of plain text or SSML for this response message.
The JSON-formatted string that defines the custom payload of the message, allowing the bot to send arbitrary structured data to the client instead of a plain text or SSML message.
Defines the image response card displayed in the Lex message, allowing configuration of a title, subtitle, image URL, and optional buttons for the card.
List of buttons to display on the image response card, where each button defines a text label and a value sent to the bot when clicked by the user.
The text label displayed on the button of the image response card used in the failure conditional branch of the intent confirmation setting within a Lex bot locale intent.

The value returned to the Amazon Lex bot when a user clicks a button on an image response card that is included in the response of a conditional branch for the failure condition of an intent's confirmation setting.
The URL of the image displayed in the image response card for this message group within the conditional branch response.
Sets the subtitle text of the image response card (ImageResponseCard) used in the failure conditional branch's message when the user fails to confirm the intent.
Specifies the title text displayed at the top of the image response card in the conditional failure branch of the intent confirmation setting for the Lex bot intent.
Specifies the plain-text message that Amazon Lex sends to the user when the failure conditional branch is triggered during the intent confirmation flow.
The text content of a plain text message that Amazon Lex sends when the failure condition for confirming the intent is met.
The SSML message configuration object that specifies the Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) text to be spoken by the Lex bot when this conditional branch is taken.
The SSML-formatted text that Amazon Lex speaks to the user when the conditional branch defined for the failure of the intent's confirmation is triggered.
A list of alternative message variations (e.g., plain text, SSML, or custom payload) for a message group, which the bot selects among when presenting the conditional response.
Custom payload for a message variation, which defines a channel-specific JSON payload sent when the intent confirmation fails and the failure conditional branch is triggered.
The stringified custom payload (e.g., JSON) returned as the message variation when the intent confirmation failure conditional branch is triggered.

Defines an image response card variation that presents an image, title, subtitle, and optional buttons in the Lex chat response when the intent confirmation failure conditional branch response is delivered.
Defines the list of buttons on an image response card, where each button specifies text and a value that is sent back to the bot when selected by the user.
The text label displayed on a button of the image response card used in a message variation for the conditional failure response of the intent confirmation setting.
The value sent back to the bot when the user clicks this button on the image response card.
For an Amazon Lex bot, this is the URL of the image shown in the image response card for a message variation within the failure conditional branch of the intent's confirmation setting.
The subtitle text displayed beneath the title in the image response card used in a Lex bot conditional branch message.
The title text displayed at the top of the image response card in the message variation for the conditional branch when intent confirmation fails.

Defines a plain-text message variation within a message group for the response of a conditional branch in the intent confirmation failure flow, specifying the literal text to present to the user when that branch is triggered.
Specifies the plain-text message that Amazon Lex sends to the user when the intent-confirmation failure condition is met and this conditional branch's response is selected.

Defines the SSML message variant for a message group variation in the response of a failure conditional branch for the intent confirmation setting, holding SSML-formatted text in its value to control how the bot speaks the message.
The SSML-formatted text (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) used to speak the bot's message, allowing control over pronunciation, pauses, and emphasis.
Specifies the default dialog state that Amazon Lex transitions to when none of the conditional branches defined in the failure conditional are fulfilled.

Specifies the next dialog step that Amazon Lex executes when the default branch of the intent's failure conditional is triggered, defining whether to close, delegate, elicit an intent, or elicit a slot.

Specifies the dialog action to perform in the next step of the default branch under an intent confirmation failure conditional, such as eliciting a slot, starting an intent, closing the conversation, or fulfilling the intent.
When the dialog action is set to elicit a slot, this field specifies the name of the slot that the bot should ask the user for in the next step of the conversation.
Specifies whether Lex suppresses the next message after executing the dialog action, preventing that message from being sent to the user.

For a given intent in a bot locale, this field sets the type of dialog action the bot performs as the next step in the default branch of the failure conditional of the intent confirmation setting, defining how to proceed when confirmation fails (such as by closing the intent, eliciting a slot, or starting another intent).
Specifies the intent to invoke as the next step in the default branch of the failure conditional of the intent confirmation setting, including the intent name and its slot values.
The name of the Amazon Lex intent to transition to when the bot's confirmation prompt fails and the default branch of the failure conditional is executed.
Specifies the slot value overrides to apply to the target intent when the failure conditional's default branch transitions to a dialog state that invokes that intent.
In the next-step intent's slot map, this specifies the name of the slot whose value is being set when the intent is invoked.
Specifies the slot value that overrides the current slot value in the intent invoked as the next step of the default branch under the failure conditional of the intent confirmation setting.
Specifies the shape of the slot value override, which is either Scalar or List, determining whether the override provides a single value or a list of values for the slot.

The slot value override's value, a SlotValue object that specifies the interpreted value to assign to the slot when taking the next step in the default branch of the intent confirmation failure conditional.
Specifies the interpreted value to assign to a slot when overriding its value for the next intent invoked in the default branch of a failed intent confirmation condition.
Specifies the list of slot values to assign when overriding the slot's value in the next step of the failure conditional's default branch for the intent confirmation setting.
Defines the list of session attribute key-value pairs to set on the session when the next step in the failure conditional branch is executed after intent confirmation fails.
Defines the name (key) of a session attribute to set in the Lex bot's session when the intent confirmation fails and the default branch of the failure conditional is executed.
Specifies the value to assign to a session attribute when the default branch of the failure conditional is executed during intent confirmation, affecting subsequent dialog steps.
Defines the response (message groups) that Amazon Lex sends to the user when intent confirmation fails and the default branch of the failure conditional is executed.
Determines whether the user can interrupt this response message (barge in) or whether the bot must finish delivering it before accepting input.
Specifies the message groups that define the bot's response to the user when the intent confirmation fails and the default branch of the failure conditional is executed.

This object defines the message content (plain text or SSML) sent to the user in the default branch of the failure conditional for the intent's confirmation setting, within a message group of the response.

Defines the custom payload (a structured JSON object) used as the message content in the default branch of the intent confirmation failure conditional, enabling the bot to send a non-text/non-SSML response to the user.
Specifies the string content of the custom payload message delivered in the default branch of the failure conditional response to intent confirmation.

Defines an image response card (with image URL, title, subtitle, and optional buttons) to display as part of the message in the default branch of the failure conditional for an intent's confirmation setting in Amazon Lex.
A list of buttons to display on the image response card, where each button defines a text label and a value that is sent back to the bot when selected.
The text displayed on a button in the image response card used in the default branch of the failure conditional response for the intent confirmation setting.
The value sent to the Amazon Lex bot when the user clicks this button on the image response card.
The URL of the image displayed in the image response card for the failure conditional branch of the intent confirmation setting's message in an Amazon Lex bot.

The subtitle text displayed below the title on the image response card within the default branch response of the intent confirmation failure conditional, providing supplementary descriptive information to the user in the Amazon Lex bot.
The title text displayed on the image response card within the message of the default branch of a failed intent confirmation.

This PlainTextMessage object supplies the plain-text string (via its Value property) that Lex returns in the default branch response when the intent confirmation setting's failure conditional is triggered.
The text content of the plain text message used in the failure conditional response when an intent's confirmation is not successful.

Contains the SSML-formatted message that Amazon Lex speaks to the user in the failure conditional branch of the intent confirmation setting, defining the speech synthesis markup for the bot's voice response.
The SSML markup string that defines the spoken message for this message in the default branch of the failure conditional response for intent confirmation, within a message group in a bot locale.

Provides the list of message variations for a message group in the default branch response of the failure conditional under the intent confirmation setting, enabling multiple alternative texts (plain text/SSML) to be defined for a single message position.

Defines a custom payload object containing a value string that is passed as-is to an integration (such as a Lambda function) for the response message variation in the failure conditional branch of the intent confirmation setting.

The string content of the custom payload message to deliver when intent confirmation fails and the default branch of the failure conditional is executed, allowing a raw JSON-formatted message to be sent.

Defines the image response card variation for a message in the intent confirmation failure response, specifying the image URL and optional title, subtitle, and buttons to display in the Lex chat interface.
The list of buttons on the image response card, where each button has a text label and a value returned to the bot when selected.
The label text displayed on a button within the image response card, which is part of a message variation for the default branch of the failure conditional in the intent confirmation setting.
The value (a string) that is sent to the Amazon Lex bot when the user clicks this button on the image response card, often used to populate a slot value or trigger a specific intent.
The URL of the image to display in the image response card that is part of the default branch message variation for the failure conditional of the intent confirmation setting.
Specifies the subtitle text displayed on the image response card in the message variation for the failure conditional's default branch response.
The title text displayed on the image response card used in the default branch of the failure conditional for the intent confirmation setting, within a message group variation of the response.

Holds the plain text content for a message variation in the message groups list of the default branch response under the intent confirmation setting's failure conditional in the Lex bot locale intent.
The plain text content of the message variation that Amazon Lex uses as the response when the failure conditional default branch is triggered.
The SSML message object that provides an SSML-formatted speech variant in the message variations for the default branch of the failure conditional response within the intent confirmation setting.
The SSML-formatted text content of this message variation, which Amazon Lex speaks when the failure condition's default branch is selected in the intent confirmation setting.
Indicates whether the failure conditional branch is active for the intent confirmation setting, enabling the evaluation of the failure response when the user does not confirm the intent.
Defines the next dialog step (such as eliciting a slot or closing the intent) that the bot takes when an intent confirmation fails.
Specifies the dialog action to take when the user fails to confirm the intent, defining the next step action type (such as ElicitSlot, StartIntent, or Close) and optionally the slot to elicit.
Specifies the slot that Amazon Lex should elicit from the user when this dialog action (type ElicitSlot) is executed as the failure next step in the intent's confirmation setting.
When true, suppresses the next message that would otherwise be shown to the user after the dialog action completes.
Specifies the type of dialog action to take when the user fails to confirm the intent, such as ElicitIntent, StartIntent, CloseIntent, ConfirmIntent, Delegate, or ElicitSlot.

This object specifies the target intent (by name) and any slot overrides that Amazon Lex should transition to after the user fails or declines to confirm the current intent, used in the failure next step of the intent confirmation setting.
The name of the intent to which the bot will route the conversation when the user does not confirm the current intent (i.e., when the confirmation fails).
The list of slot overrides for the target intent when the confirmation prompt fails, each defining a slot name and its value to apply in the next step.
The name of the slot to set in the target intent when the user does not confirm the current intent, within the failure next step of the intent confirmation setting for a Lex bot.
Defines the value override to apply to one slot of the intent invoked as the next step when intent confirmation fails, allowing control over the slot's runtime value before that intent is executed.
Specifies whether the slot value override is for a scalar value or a list of values, with allowed values Scalar or List, for the slot override in the next step after intent confirmation failure.
In an intent confirmation failure flow, this object provides the actual value that will be assigned to the slot referenced by the slot_value_override when the failure next step is executed.
Sets the normalized, interpreted value for the slot when overriding its value, which is used in place of the raw user input for the intent's failure next step.

This field contains the list of nested slot value override objects (used when the slot has a List shape) to apply when overriding a slot value in the intent specified in the failure next step of an intent's confirmation setting.
Specifies the session attributes to be set in the session state when the bot executes the failure next step after the user fails to confirm the intent.
The key (name) of a session attribute that Amazon Lex will set in the session when the user does not confirm the intent, as specified by the failure next step of the intent confirmation setting.
The value assigned to the session attribute key when the bot transitions to the failure next step after intent confirmation is unsuccessful.

This object defines the response the bot sends to the user when the user does not confirm the intent (i.e., after the user fails to accept the confirmation prompt), including the message groups and any allow-interrupt behavior.
This boolean determines whether the user can interrupt the failure response message when an intent confirmation fails in a Lex bot.
Defines the list of message groups for the bot's failure response when a user does not confirm an intent, with each group containing a primary message and optional variations to present to the user.
Defines the content (text, SSML, or custom payload) of a failure response message shown to the user when they decline an intent confirmation prompt in an Amazon Lex bot.

Specifies a custom payload string (the value within this object) that is passed as the message content when the intent confirmation failure response is triggered, allowing the message to be handled by a Lambda function or other custom processing.

Specifies the raw string value of the custom payload (commonly a JSON-encoded object) that Lex delivers as the failure response message when intent confirmation fails for the specified locale and intent.
The image response card configuration (with optional title, subtitle, image URL, and buttons) used in a message within the failure response for the intent confirmation setting of a Lex bot locale.
Specifies a list of buttons for the image response card, where each button includes a display text and a value sent to the bot when selected.
The text displayed on the button of the image response card used in the failure response for intent confirmation, which is part of the message group in the bot locale's intent.
The value sent to the Amazon Lex bot as the user's reply when the corresponding button on the image response card is clicked.
The URL of the image displayed in the image response card for the failure response message when intent confirmation fails.
Specifies the subtitle text shown on the image response card in the failure response message for intent confirmation, providing additional context beneath the card's title.
Specifies the title text shown at the top of the image response card in the message Amazon Lex sends when the user fails to confirm the intent, within the failure response message group.
Specifies the plain-text message content shown to the user when the intent confirmation fails, within the failure response's message group.
The actual plain-text string content sent to the user as the failure response when intent confirmation fails.
Represents the SSML message variant within the failure response of the intent confirmation setting, specifying the SSML text that Amazon Lex speaks when the user does not confirm the intent.
The SSML-formatted text that Amazon Lex speaks to the user as the failure response message when the user does not confirm the intent during the confirmation prompt.
This list defines the different message variations (Message objects) that Amazon Lex randomly selects from when delivering the failure response to an intent confirmation prompt.

Defines the custom payload object (containing a value) for a message variation in the failure response of the intent confirmation setting, which Lex sends to the client or Lambda as a structured message.

The string content of the custom payload message variation that is used in the failure response for the intent confirmation setting, allowing arbitrary text or structured data to be sent as the message.
The image response card to display as part of this message variation in the failure response of the intent confirmation setting, specifying the card's image URL, title, subtitle, and any buttons.

Specifies the buttons displayed on the image response card for this message variation in the failure response of the intent's confirmation setting, where each button has a text label and a value returned to Amazon Lex when selected.
The text label displayed on a button in the image response card used in the failure response of the intent confirmation setting.
The value sent to the Amazon Lex bot when the user clicks this button on the image response card displayed in the failure response for the intent's confirmation prompt.

The URL of the image to display in the image response card that serves as a variation in a message group of the failure response for the intent's confirmation setting within a locale of the Amazon Lex bot.
The subtitle text displayed below the image in an image response card, used as part of a variation within a message group for the failure response of an intent confirmation setting.
The title text displayed as the heading of the image response card in the failure response message for the intent's confirmation setting.

Defines a plain-text message variation within a message group for the failure response of the intent's confirmation prompt, encapsulating the text content (value) shown to the user when confirmation fails.
The actual text content of a plain-text message variation used in the failure response for the intent confirmation setting within a Lex bot locale.
Specifies the SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) content for a message variation used in the failure response when a user does not confirm an intent in the Lex bot.

Provides the SSML text for a message variation in the failure response of the intent confirmation setting, which is the spoken response sent when the user's reply to the confirmation prompt cannot be interpreted as either confirmation or denial.
When set to true, enables the intent confirmation prompt so that Amazon Lex asks the user to confirm the intent before proceeding; when false, the confirmation step is skipped.
Configures the prompt shown to the user to confirm the intent, including the message groups, maximum retries, and interruption behavior.
Determines whether the user can interrupt the prompt (for example, by speaking) while the bot is delivering it, with a default of false when not specified.
The maximum number of times the bot will repeat the confirmation prompt to elicit a valid response from the user before giving up or taking fallback action.

Defines the list of message groups that provide the prompt's message content for the intent confirmation prompt, where each group contains a primary message and an optional list of variation messages.

The `message` object defines a single message variant (plain text, SSML, or custom payload) within a message group used for the intent confirmation prompt, allowing the bot to confirm the user's intent with the specified content.

The custom payload object whose 'value' field supplies a raw JSON string that Amazon Lex delivers as the message content for this intent confirmation prompt, enabling direct integration with external services.
The string content of the custom payload message that is delivered to the user as part of the intent confirmation prompt in an Amazon Lex bot.
Defines an image response card that accompanies the message in the intent confirmation prompt, containing an optional image URL, title, subtitle, and a list of buttons for user interaction.
Specifies the list of buttons that appear on the image response card, each button carrying text and a value that is sent to the bot when selected.
The text label displayed on the button within the image response card.
Specifies the value that is sent to the Amazon Lex bot when the user selects this button on the image response card.
Specifies the HTTPS URL of the image that is displayed in the image response card for the prompt message used in the intent confirmation setting.
The subtitle text displayed beneath the title on the image response card used in the intent confirmation prompt.
The title text displayed at the top of the image response card within the intent confirmation prompt's message group, providing a header for the card presented to the user.
Specifies the plain text variant of the message shown in the intent confirmation prompt to the user.
The text content of the plain text message displayed in the intent confirmation prompt for the specified Lex bot locale.
The SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) message used in the confirmation prompt, allowing voice output with custom pronunciation, pauses, and emphasis in the Lex bot's intent confirmation.
The SSML text of the confirmation prompt message spoken to the user to confirm the intent before fulfillment, allowing markup like pauses or emphasis.

A list of alternative message variations for this message group, where each variation is a Message object (e.g., PlainText, SSML, or CustomPayload) that Amazon Lex can use as alternate renditions of the primary prompt message.
Specifies the custom payload (a user-defined string, such as JSON) for a message variation in the intent confirmation prompt, allowing the bot to send structured data to the client.
The custom payload value that holds the JSON-encoded message content for an intent confirmation prompt variation within a message group of an Amazon Lex bot.

Configures an image response card (including image URL, title, subtitle, and optional buttons) that Amazon Lex can display as one variation of a message group in the prompt used to confirm the user's intent.
Defines the list of buttons to be displayed on the image response card, each containing a text label and a value sent to the bot when the button is clicked.
Specifies the label text displayed on a button within an image response card, which appears as part of the intent confirmation prompt for the user to select.
The value sent to the Amazon Lex bot when the user clicks this button on the image response card.
The URL of the image displayed on an image response card used in a message variation of the intent confirmation prompt.
Specifies the subtitle text displayed below the title on the image response card used in the intent confirmation prompt message.
The title text displayed on the image response card when that message variation is used in the intent confirmation prompt's prompt specification.

Provides a plain text message variation for the prompt that Amazon Lex sends to the user when confirming the intent, as part of a message group within the intent confirmation setting's prompt specification.
The plain-text message string that is sent to the user as part of the prompt variation for the intent confirmation step.
Defines the SSML message variation for this confirmation prompt, providing the value containing SSML-formatted speech that Amazon Lex speaks to the user when asking for intent confirmation.
The SSML text content of the audio message variation used in the intent confirmation prompt.
Specifies whether the confirmation prompt selects messages from the message group in sequential order or at random; choose Random to rotate messages randomly or Sequential to use them in order.
Specifies per-attempt configuration (e.g., for initial, retry1, retry2) for the confirmation prompt, including allowed input types and audio/DTMF/text input settings.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.kendra_c.text: Configuration that connects the intent to an Amazon Kendra index, enabling the bot to query the index and use its results as responses when the intent is invoked.
The ARN of the Amazon Kendra index that the intent queries to provide search-based answers when the intent is triggered.
A filter string, expressed in Amazon Kendra query syntax, that is applied to the Kendra search request for this intent to narrow the search results returned from the configured Kendra index.
Indicates whether the Amazon Kendra query filter string, specified in queryFilterString, is applied to filter the results returned from the Amazon Kendra index for the intent.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.name.text: The unique name of the intent within a bot locale, which must be composed of letters, numbers, and underscores (starting with a letter) and is used to identify the intent in the Lex bot definition.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.output_c.text: Defines the output contexts that are activated when the intent is fulfilled, controlling which other intents can be invoked in the subsequent conversation turns.
Sets the name of an output context that becomes active after the intent is fulfilled, used to manage conversation flow and pass state to subsequent intents.
The number of seconds that the output context remains active after the associated intent is fulfilled, after which it expires and can no longer be used by subsequent intents.
The number of conversation turns that the output context remains active after being set, after which it expires.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.parent_i.text: Specifies the signature of an Amazon Lex built-in intent that this custom intent is based on, allowing the intent to inherit the built-in intent's behavior and configuration.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.qin_conn.text: Configures the Amazon Q in Connect assistant linked to this intent, allowing the bot to leverage Q in Connect's real-time AI and generative assistance during the intent's execution.
The ARN of the Amazon Q in Connect assistant used by the Lex intent to provide AI-generated answers and recommendations.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.qn_ainte.text: Configuration for the built-in AMAZON.QnAIntent, defining data sources (e.g., Amazon Kendra indexes) and fallback intent behavior for answering user questions in a Lex bot locale.
Specifies the Amazon Bedrock model configuration used by the QnA intent to generate responses to user queries.
Configuration for the Amazon Bedrock guardrail applied to the Bedrock model used by this QnA intent, specifying the guardrail identifier and version.
The ARN or unique identifier of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail that is applied to filter and moderate the responses generated by the QnA intent's Bedrock model configuration.
The version of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail that is applied to the QnA intent when using a Bedrock model, as part of the guardrail configuration.
The custom prompt that overrides the default prompt sent to the Amazon Bedrock model when the QnA intent uses a Bedrock model to generate answers.
Controls whether trace logging is enabled for the Amazon Bedrock model calls made by this QnA intent, accepting either 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Bedrock model that this Lex QnA intent configuration uses to generate answers.
Configures the data source (such as an Amazon S3 bucket or an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base) that supplies the question-and-answer pairs used by the QnA intent.

This object configures the Amazon Bedrock knowledge store that Lex uses as the data source for answering user queries in this QnA intent, including the knowledge store's ARN and an optional flag for exact response matching.
The ARN of the Amazon Bedrock knowledge base that the Lex QnA intent uses as its knowledge store for retrieving answers.

Specifies the list of field names from the Amazon Bedrock knowledge store response that should be returned exactly as-is (exact response) for the QnA intent, rather than being paraphrased by the model.
The name of the field in the Amazon Bedrock knowledge store that contains the exact answer to be returned for the QnA intent.
Determines whether the bot returns the exact response text from the Bedrock knowledge store or a paraphrased version when answering QnA intents.
Specifies the Amazon Kendra index (and optional query filter string) that the QnA intent uses to retrieve answers from a Kendra data source.
When true, the QnA intent returns only the exact answer supplied by the connected Amazon Kendra index instead of a synthesized or fallback response.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Kendra index that the QnA intent uses to search for answers for user queries.
Specifies the query filter string that Amazon Lex uses to filter the Amazon Kendra index results when the QnA intent retrieves answers from the configured data source.
Indicates whether the configured query filter string is enabled to filter Amazon Kendra search results for this QnA intent.
Specifies the Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection and index used by the QnA intent's data source to retrieve answers, including the collection ARN and index name.
The endpoint URL of the Amazon OpenSearch Service domain that the QnA intent's data source configuration uses to query for answers.
When true, Amazon Lex returns the exact text of the top OpenSearch result as the bot's answer, rather than generating a natural language response from that result.
Specifies the Amazon OpenSearch Service index fields (answerField and sourceField) that store the exact answer text and its source for high-confidence matches returned by the QnA intent.
Specifies the OpenSearch index field name that contains the exact answer text returned to the user when the QnA intent matches a query using exact response matching.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.sample_u.text: Defines the list of sample utterances (phrases) that are used to train the bot's language model and determine when the intent should be triggered.
The user's natural language phrase that triggers this intent, used as training data for the bot's language model.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.slot_pri.text: Defines the order in which slots are filled for the intent, where each item specifies a slot name and its priority level.
Sets the order in which Amazon Lex elicits slot values for the intent, with lower numbers indicating higher priority (e.g., priority 1 is elicited before priority 2).
The name of the slot whose elicitation order is being set in the intent's slot priority list, matching a slot defined in the intent's slots collection.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.slots.text: Defines the list of slots for the intent, each specifying a unique name, a slot type, whether the slot is required, and the prompts used to elicit and confirm the slot value from the user.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.slots.de.text: Provides a short text description of the slot's purpose within the intent, used for clarity and documentation.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.slots.mu.text: Configures whether a slot in an intent can capture and store multiple values for its assigned slot type, typically controlled by an allowMultipleValues boolean flag.
When true, this setting allows the slot to capture multiple values in a single user utterance; when false, the slot captures only a single value.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.slots.na.text: The unique name of the slot within the intent, used as a reference in slot resolution and Lambda function events.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.slots.ob.text: Specifies the obfuscation setting for the slot value to protect sensitive data in transcripts, with the type either 'None' or 'DefaultObfuscation'.
Determines whether the slot value is obfuscated in conversation logs, accepting `NONE` (no obfuscation) or `DEFAULT_OBFUSCATION` (masks the value).

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.slots.sl.text: Specifies the name of the slot type that defines the allowed values and data format for this slot, which is used to interpret and validate user input during a conversation.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.slots.su.text: Defines the settings for a composite slot, where the slot is made up of multiple sub-slots, including an expression and the sub-slot specifications that determine how the slot value is assembled.
Defines a template expression that composes a composite slot's value from sub-slot values, using curly-brace placeholders that reference the sub-slot names.
Specifies the configuration for each sub-slot within a composite slot, defining the slot type and value elicitation settings for each named sub-slot.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.intents.slots.va.text: Configures how Amazon Lex prompts the user for the slot value, including prompt messages and wait-and-continue behavior during the conversation.
Defines the default value specification for a slot, listing default values that are used when the user does not supply a value during elicitation.
Defines the list of default values Amazon Lex uses for a slot when the user does not provide a response during elicitation.
Defines a specific default value that Amazon Lex uses for the slot when the user does not supply a value during the conversation.
Defines the prompt messages, maximum retries, and other settings used to elicit the slot value from the user when the slot is empty or invalid.
Determines whether the user can interrupt the prompt while it is being spoken, allowing them to provide input before the prompt finishes.
The maximum number of times the bot repeats the prompt when trying to elicit a valid value for the slot from the user.

Specifies the ordered sequence of message groups for the slot's value elicitation prompt, where each group contains one or more message variants (e.g., plain text, SSML, custom payload) that Amazon Lex cycles through to prompt the user for a value.
Defines the primary message object (containing content and content type) that Amazon Lex uses to prompt the user when eliciting a slot value.

This object defines the custom payload (a JSON-formatted message containing a `value` string) that is sent to the user as part of a message group in the prompt specification for eliciting a slot value, enabling integration with Lambda functions or other custom processing.
The custom payload string that Lex sends to the user when eliciting the slot, as defined in the prompt message group.
Specifies the image response card message shown to the user during slot value elicitation, including its title, subtitle, image URL, and optional buttons.

Defines a plain-text message to present to the user, containing the actual message text in its 'value' property.
The plain text message that Amazon Lex sends to the user to elicit a slot value during conversation.
Specifies the SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) content for the message, enabling fine-grained control over how Amazon Lex pronounces and delivers the prompt to the user through voice.
The SSML text that defines the message content spoken to the user during slot value elicitation.

The variations list inside a message group defines alternative versions of the prompt message (e.g., plain text, SSML, or custom payload) from which Amazon Lex can select to vary the prompt presented to the user.
The custom payload message variation, which lets you specify a user-defined string payload for the prompt when the variation type is CustomPayload.

The actual content of the custom payload message variation, which is sent as the prompt's message to the user (or to a Lambda function), allowing structured data such as JSON to be delivered for advanced message handling.

Configures an image response card (specifying an image URL, title, subtitle, and optional buttons) that can be shown as a visual variation in the prompt message group used to elicit the slot value in an Amazon Lex bot.
Defines the list of buttons on the image response card, where each button includes a display text and the value sent to the bot when selected.
The text label displayed on a button inside an image response card, which appears as a user-selectable option in the Lex chat prompt.

The subtitle of the image response card, displayed beneath the title to give additional context or instructions for the user during slot value elicitation.

Defines the plain-text message variant for this message group variation, specifying the exact text content that Amazon Lex will present to the user in the prompt.

The SSML-based message variation that the bot uses in the prompt, allowing you to specify the exact speech synthesis markup for audio output.

Determines whether the bot selects prompt messages in the order they are defined (Ordered) or randomly (Random) when multiple messages are configured in the slot's value elicitation prompt specification.
Configures the retry attempts for the prompt used to elicit slot values, specifying per-attempt settings such as the allowed number of retries and the message groups to display.
List of sample utterances that Amazon Lex uses to recognize when a user is providing a value for the slot during elicitation.
The literal text of an example phrase that Lex uses to recognize and capture a user's response when eliciting a value for this slot.
Defines the response, next step, and code hook behavior that is invoked after the slot's value is successfully captured in Amazon Lex V2.

Defines the condition that must be satisfied for the slot value to be captured, and if the condition is not met, the bot skips the capture and proceeds to the appropriate failure handling defined in the slot capture setting.

Defines the list of conditional branches evaluated in order for the slot capture conditional, where each branch specifies a condition expression and a response specification to be executed when the condition is met.
Defines the condition (a Lex condition object with an expression string) that must evaluate to true for this branch to be followed when determining whether to capture the slot value.
An Amazon Lex condition expression string that must evaluate to true for this conditional branch to be taken when capturing the slot value.
A descriptive name for this conditional branch, used to identify it among the branches defined in the slot capture conditional.
Defines the dialog state that the bot should transition to when the capture conditional branch's condition is met, used in the slot's value elicitation setting for an Amazon Lex bot.
Specifies the dialog action to perform in the next step, such as ElicitSlot, ElicitIntent, ConfirmIntent, Delegate, or Close, optionally naming the slot to elicit.

When set to true, this field suppresses the next message that would normally be sent to the user after this dialog action executes, such as a slot prompt or follow-up message, as part of the conditional branch's next step in slot capture.
Specifies the type of dialog action to execute in the next step of the conditional branch, such as ElicitSlot, ConfirmIntent, Delegate, or Close, controlling the bot's conversational behavior.
Specifies the target intent (name and optional slot overrides) that Amazon Lex invokes as the next step when this conditional branch's condition is evaluated as true.
The name of the Amazon Lex intent that the conversation transitions to when the conditional branch condition is met during slot capture.
Specifies a list of slot name/value pairs to assign to the target intent of the conditional branch's next step, overriding any default slot values for that intent within the slot capture setting.
Specifies the name of the slot within the intent that is the target of the next step, used by the conditional branch to indicate which slot value to set when the capture condition is met.
Describes the slot value override to apply when a conditional branch's next step targets another intent, specifying the slot shape (scalar/list) and the interpreted value or values to assign.
Specifies the shape of the slot value override, either 'Scalar' for a single value or 'List' for multiple values.

Specifies the response message(s) and allow-interrupt setting sent to the user when this conditional branch's condition is met during slot capture.
Controls whether the user can interrupt the response message that is delivered as part of this conditional branch during slot capture.
A list of message groups, each containing one or more messages, that defines the response Lex delivers when the slot capture conditional branch's condition is met.

Defines the message object (with content type such as PlainText or SSML, content text, and optional image response card) that is delivered to the user when the slot capture conditional branch's condition is met.

Specifies a custom payload object (containing a string Value) that is sent to the channel as an alternative message type, allowing the Lex bot to deliver channel-specific or arbitrary data in this message.

Defines the image response card (including image URL, title, subtitle, and optional buttons) that is displayed to the user as part of a message in a conditional response branch for slot capture.

The SSML-formatted text content of the message used in the conditional response when the slot value is captured.
Defines a list of alternative message variations that can be chosen for a message group within a conditional branch's response.
Represents a custom payload variation for a response message, containing a UTF-8 encoded value that is sent to a custom conversation runtime for this Lex bot slot.
The literal string content of the CustomPayload message variation, which Lex delivers to the client or passes to a Lambda function when the capture conditional branch's response is selected.

Specifies the image response card used in a message variation, including its title, subtitle, image URL, and buttons, for the response triggered by the capture conditional branch of the slot's value elicitation setting.
Defines the buttons displayed on the image response card, each containing text and a value that is returned to the bot when the user clicks it.

Specifies the value returned to the bot when a user clicks this button on the image response card.
Specifies the URL of the image displayed in the image response card for this conditional branch's message variation in the Lex bot slot capture setting.
Specifies the subtitle text displayed below the title on an image response card used in a conditional slot-capture response message within an Amazon Lex bot locale.

Defines a plain-text message variation whose `value` property specifies the exact text Amazon Lex sends to the user in a conditional branch response message group.

Specifies the SSML markup text used to synthesize the bot's spoken response to the user for this variation in the conditional branch's message group.
The SSML-markup text spoken by the bot when the slot capture condition is met for this conditional branch.

Specifies the next step (dialog state) to transition to after the slot value is captured, when the capture conditions fail and the default branch of the conditional is taken.
Defines the action (such as eliciting a slot or starting an intent) the bot takes after following the default branch of the capture conditional in the slot's value elicitation setting.
The name of the slot that the bot elicits from the user when executing this dialog action, typically used in an ElicitSlot action within the bot's conversation flow.

When set to true, this flag instructs Amazon Lex to suppress the next message that would otherwise be sent to the user after the dialog action is performed, effectively skipping the subsequent message in the conversation.
Determines the kind of dialog action Lex performs (such as ElicitSlot, Close, or ConfirmIntent) when following the default branch of the capture conditional in the slot's value elicitation setting.
Specifies the intent to invoke as the next step after the default branch of the capture conditional in the slot's value elicitation setting.
The name of the intent that the Lex bot transitions to in the default branch of the slot capture conditional after the slot value is successfully elicited and captured.
A list of slot values to set for the specified intent when the next step is executed, with each entry identifying a slot name and its associated value expression.
The name of a slot that is overridden or elicited when the default branch of a capture conditional proceeds to the next intent step in the Lex bot's slot value elicitation setting.

In a Lex bot's conditional branch default next-step intent, this object specifies the structured override value (scalar or list) for a targeted slot, controlling the slot's value when the conversation transitions to that intent.

List of message groups, each with one or more message variations, that defines the response sent to the user in the default branch when the slot capture condition is evaluated.

Defines the SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) message content that Amazon Lex speaks to the user when the slot capture conditional's default branch response is triggered, contained within the message object of a message group.

Defines the list of conditional branches to evaluate when the slot capture condition fails, each specifying a condition and the associated response to return.

The condition object defines the logical expression (with operator and operands) that must evaluate to true for this failure conditional branch to be selected, determining the response when slot capture fails.
The condition expression string that determines whether this conditional branch is taken when slot value elicitation fails, evaluated using Lex's condition expression syntax.
The user-defined name that uniquely identifies this conditional branch within the slot capture failure conditional of the Lex slot value elicitation setting.
The dialog state (next step) to transition to when the condition on this conditional branch is met, determining the subsequent conversation flow after a slot-capture failure.
Specifies the dialog action (such as ElicitSlot, StartIntent, or Close) that the Lex V2 bot should execute as the next step when the failure conditional branch is selected.
The name of the slot that the bot elicits from the user when this dialog action is of type ElicitSlot, used in the next step after a conditional branch failure.
When set to true, suppresses the bot's next message after this dialog action executes in the failure conditional branch of the slot capture setting.

Specifies the type of dialog action (e.g., ElicitSlot, ConfirmIntent, Close, StartIntent) that the bot performs as the next step in the failure conditional branch of a slot capture setting, determining how the conversation proceeds when slot capture fails.
The IntentOverride object that defines the name and slot overrides of the intent to which Amazon Lex redirects the conversation when this failure conditional branch is selected during slot capture.
The name of the Amazon Lex intent to switch to when a slot capture failure triggers this conditional branch and its next step is defined as an intent.

Defines slot value overrides for the target intent specified in the next step of a conditional branch, used when the failure conditional is triggered during slot capture in a Lex bot's value elicitation setting.
The name of a slot in the destination intent, used as the key for the slot value override map in the next step's intent override when the slot capture failure conditional branch is taken.
Specifies a value override for a slot in the target intent when a failed slot capture triggers a conditional transition, allowing the bot to set the slot to a specific value during the next step.
Specifies the shape (Scalar or List) of the slot value override, indicating whether the provided value is a single value or a list of values for the slot.
The SlotValue object holding the literal text value to assign to the slot when the conditional branch's next step is executed after slot capture fails.
The concrete string value that Amazon Lex should use as the slot's interpreted value when this slot override is applied in the next step of the conditional branch.
Defines the list of values to assign to the slot when the conditional branch's next step overrides the slot value, which occurs after slot capture fails.

Defines the session attributes to be set on the dialog state when this conditional branch (used when slot capture fails) transitions to its next step, enabling the bot to carry custom key-value data forward in the conversation.
The name/key of the session attribute that is set on the next step when a failure conditional branch is taken during slot capture in a Lex bot.
The value of a session attribute to set or overwrite when the next step of a slot-capture failure conditional branch is executed during value elicitation.
Specifies the response (message groups and interruption settings) to deliver to the user when this conditional branch's condition is true during slot capture failure.
Indicates whether the user can interrupt the response delivered when this conditional branch's failure condition is met, during slot capture.

Defines a list of message groups for the response to use when the slot capture failure conditional branch is triggered, where each group can contain a primary message and multiple variation messages from which Lex can choose.
Defines the message content delivered to the user for this conditional response, which can be a plain-text, SSML, or custom payload message within a message group.
Specifies a custom JSON-formatted payload to be returned from this message to the client or Lambda function, allowing structured data to be sent instead of plain text or SSML.

The JSON-formatted value of the custom payload for a message in the slot capture failure conditional branch, sent to the client when slot capture fails, allowing integration with external systems or services.
Defines an image response card (with title, subtitle, image URL, and optional buttons) that is displayed to the user as part of the conditional branch response message in the slot capture setting.
Defines the list of buttons to display on the image response card, where each button contains a text label and a value returned to the bot when clicked.
The text label displayed on a button in an image response card for a Lex slot capture failure conditional branch response message.
Defines the value that is sent to the Amazon Lex bot when the user selects this button on the image response card.
Specifies the URL of the image displayed in the image response card that is part of the message sent in the conditional branch when slot capture fails for a slot in a Lex bot.
The subtitle text displayed below the title on the image response card, shown in the message that is sent when the slot capture failure condition is triggered.
The title text displayed on the image response card in the message sent to the user when the slot capture fails and the associated failure conditional branch is triggered in Amazon Lex.
Defines the plain-text message object containing the literal text displayed to the user when slot capture fails, within the chosen failure conditional branch's response message group.
The text content of a plain text message that Amazon Lex sends as part of the response for a conditional branch when slot capture fails during value elicitation.
Defines the SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) message that Amazon Lex speaks to the user when this failure conditional branch is triggered during slot capture.
The value of the SSML message, which is the actual speech-synthesis markup (SSML) text that Amazon Lex speaks when this conditional branch is triggered.
A list of alternative message objects that Amazon Lex can choose from when delivering the failure conditional response for slot capture, allowing variation in how the prompt is presented to the user.

custom_payload defines a custom structured message payload (an object containing a 'value' string, typically JSON) for a message variation in a conditional response, enabling non-plain-text responses for advanced integrations.
The string payload delivered as the custom message variation in the conditional response branch for slot capture failure in the Lex bot's slot value elicitation setting.
Specifies the image response card (with image URL, title, subtitle, and optional buttons) to display as a message variation in the conditional failure response when slot capture fails.
Defines the list of buttons displayed on an image response card in a Lex bot's message, where each button specifies a label and the value sent to the bot when clicked.
The text displayed on the button in an image response card for the conditional branch's message.
The value sent back to the Lex bot when a user clicks this button on the image response card.
The URL of the image displayed in the image response card for this message variation within the slot capture failure conditional branch's response.
Specifies the subtitle text that appears on the image response card used in the message variation for the slot capture failure conditional branch.
The title text displayed on the image response card in a message variation used when the conditional branch for slot capture failure is selected.
Defines a plain-text message variation within a message group, which Lex displays to the user when the conditional branch's failure condition is met.
The text content of the plain text message variation used in a message group for the failure conditional response when slot capture fails during value elicitation in an AWS Lex bot locale.
Defines an SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) message variation used in the response for the slot capture failure conditional branch, allowing the bot to speak synthesized speech with markup.

The SSML-formatted text content of an SSML message variation that Amazon Lex speaks when the slot-capture failure conditional branch is triggered, allowing custom speech synthesis markup like <speak> tags.

Defines the default dialog state (including the next step Lex should take) that is executed when the failure conditional is evaluated after a slot capture failure and none of its explicit condition branches match.
Specifies the next step in the conversation (such as a dialog action or a follow-up intent) to execute when slot capture fails and the default branch of the failure conditional is taken.

Specifies the next action the bot takes when slot capture fails and the failure conditional's default branch is chosen, such as eliciting the slot again, starting a different intent, or closing the conversation.
The name of the slot that the dialog action attempts to elicit from the user when the action type is set to ElicitSlot in the Lex bot's failure handling flow.
Indicates whether the next message from the bot should be suppressed after executing this dialog action within the slot capture failure conditional's default branch next step.
Specifies the type of dialog action to execute in the next step, such as ElicitSlot, StartIntent, or Close.
The intent that the bot should switch to when the slot capture failure conditional's default branch is executed, defining the next step in the conversation flow.
Specifies the name of the Amazon Lex intent to transition to when slot capture fails and the failure conditional's default branch executes a next step that invokes another intent.

Defines the list of slot value overrides for the target intent that is the destination of the default branch in the failure conditional of the slot capture setting, allowing you to supply values for that intent's slots when the original slot elicitation fails.
The name of the slot in the intent to set in the next step when the slot capture failure conditional's default branch is executed.
Specifies the value to use for overriding a slot on the target intent when a slot capture failure triggers the default branch of the conditional in the value elicitation setting.
Specifies whether the overridden slot value is a scalar (Scalar) or a list of values (List), matching the Lex slot value override's shape.

The slot value override object that sets the value of the referenced slot when the dialog moves to the next intent after a slot capture failure, supporting either a scalar string or a list of strings based on the slot's value shape.
The interpreted (resolved) value to assign to the slot when overriding its value in the next step of the conversation flow.
Specifies a list of string values that override the slot's value in the next intent, used when slot capture fails and the failure conditional routes to the default branch.
Specifies the key-value session attributes to be set when the failure conditional's default branch is executed and the next step is taken in the Lex bot conversation flow.

This key is the name of a session attribute that Lex sets when the conversation follows the default branch of the failure conditional after slot capture fails, as part of the next step's session attributes.
The value of the session attribute to set when the bot executes the next step in the default branch of the failure conditional for slot capture during value elicitation.

The response specification (message groups and allow-interrupt settings) that Amazon Lex uses to reply to the user when the slot capture fails and the default branch of the failure conditional is selected.
Indicates whether the user is allowed to interrupt this response (e.g., to provide a new utterance) while it is being delivered by the bot.

Specifies a list of message groups, each containing a message (plain text, SSML, or custom payload), that Lex uses to respond to the user when a slot capture failure triggers the default branch of the failure conditional.

Defines the content and format (plain text, SSML, or custom payload) of the response sent to the user when slot capture fails and the failure conditional's default branch is selected, within a message group.
Specifies the custom payload (a JSON string) used as the message content in the response when the slot capture failure condition's default branch is selected.

The string payload of the custom message that Lex sends to the user in the default branch of the failure conditional for slot capture, enabling arbitrary structured content beyond the standard message types.

Defines the image response card (with title, subtitle, image URL, and optional buttons) that is shown to the user as part of the response message in the failure conditional default branch for slot capture within the Lex bot locale's intent slot.
Defines the list of buttons on the image response card, where each button pairs a display text with a value sent to the bot when clicked.
The text displayed on the button of an image response card in an Amazon Lex bot, which users click to trigger the associated value.
The value that is sent to the Amazon Lex bot when the user selects this button on the image response card.
The URL of the image to display in the image response card for the message in the default branch of the failure conditional for slot capture.
Defines the supplementary text shown beneath the title of an image response card in a Lex bot message.

Specifies the title (heading) text for the image response card that is shown to the user in the Amazon Lex conversation when the slot capture fails and the default branch of the conditional response is taken.
Defines the plain-text message that Amazon Lex sends to the user when the failure condition's default branch is triggered during slot capture.
The plain text string that Amazon Lex delivers to the user in the response of the default branch of the failure conditional for the slot capture setting when slot capture fails.
The SSML message object, containing the Speech Synthesis Markup Language content that the bot speaks when slot capture fails and the failure conditional's default branch is taken.
The SSML-formatted text that Alexa speaks as the message, using Speech Synthesis Markup Language to control pronunciation, intonation, pauses, and other speech attributes.
