Defines the list of alternative message variations (e.g., plain text, SSML, or custom payload) within each message group of the response for the default branch of the failure conditional in the slot capture setting, allowing Lex to select among them when a slot capture attempt fails.
Defines the custom JSON payload for a message variation in the message group, which is sent to the client or integration when this variation is selected.

The value string of a CustomPayload message variation, which carries the raw payload data that Lex returns to the client or Lambda as part of the bot's response message, used within the failure conditional's default branch for slot capture.
This object defines an image response card variation for a message in the Lex bot, including the image URL, title, and optional buttons that appear in the chat interface.
Defines the list of buttons shown on the image response card, where each button consists of a text label and a value that is sent back to the bot when selected.

Specifies the text to display on a button in the image response card used in the default branch of the slot capture failure conditional response within a Lex bot intent slot's value elicitation setting.
The value that is sent back to the Lex bot when a user clicks this button on the image response card.
The HTTPS URL of the image to display in the image response card for this message variation in the slot capture failure conditional response of the Lex bot slot.
The subtitle text displayed on the image response card presented to the user when slot capture fails and the default branch of the failure conditional is executed.
The title text displayed on the image response card in the default branch of the failure conditional response for slot capture.

Defines a plain-text message object (with a 'value' property) used as a variation in the response message group for the default branch when a slot-capture failure condition is triggered in the Amazon Lex bot.
Specifies the text content of the plain text message shown in the default branch response when slot capture fails for this slot.
Defines the SSML message content for this response variation in the default branch of the slot capture failure conditional.
The SSML-formatted text that Amazon Lex speaks as a variation of the response message when the slot's failure conditional default branch is triggered during value elicitation.
Indicates whether the failure conditional, which defines the conditions under which slot capture is considered failed, is enabled.
Specifies the next step in the conversation that the bot takes when it fails to capture a slot value (e.g., the user's input cannot be interpreted or the slot is not validated).
Defines the dialog action Amazon Lex V2 performs when slot capture fails, such as eliciting a different slot, closing the conversation, or invoking an intent.
The name of the slot that Amazon Lex elicits from the user when the dialog action is ElicitSlot, used here to define which slot to reprompt for after a previous slot capture attempt failed.

When handling a slot capture failure, this boolean controls whether Amazon Lex suppresses the next message (such as a slot prompt or follow-up) for the specified dialog action, allowing a previously shown message to remain without an additional bot message.
Defines the type of dialog action (e.g., ElicitSlot, Close) that Amazon Lex executes when slot capture fails during value elicitation.
The specific intent to which the conversation should be routed when the slot capture attempt fails, as defined in the failure next step of the slot capture setting.
The name of the Lex intent to invoke when slot capture fails, as specified in the failure next step of the slot capture setting for this slot.
A list of slot value overrides to apply to the target intent when the dialog transitions to that intent after a slot capture failure.

In the failure next step dialog state, this field specifies the name of a slot that the Lex bot should set or override on the target intent when the current slot capture fails and control transitions to that next intent.

Specifies an individual slot value override within the intent override for the failure next step, providing the slot's shape and value to use when the bot continues in the specified intent after a slot capture failure.
Specifies the shape of the slot override value, determining whether the override is a single scalar value (Scalar) or a list of values (List).
The slot value object that specifies the replacement value to assign to this slot when the slot capture failure next step executes the intent override, overriding the originally captured value.
When slot capture fails and the bot proceeds to the failure next step's intent, this string provides the interpreted value used for the slot value override, replacing the slot's value in that intent.

Provides a list of dynamic slot-value-override entries (each capable of carrying its own shape, value, and nested values) used to recursively define the overridden slot values for the follow-up intent when the slot capture fails.
A list of key-value pairs that define session attributes to set when the failure next step for slot capture is executed in the Lex bot, persisting session state across turns.
The name of the session attribute to set in the Amazon Lex session when slot capture fails and the bot moves to the specified failure next step.
The value of a session attribute to set in the slot capture failure next step, where the attribute key is the parent map key, used to pass context to the next step in the Amazon Lex bot conversation.

The `failure_response` object defines the response specification (including message groups and allow-interrupt behavior) that Amazon Lex uses to prompt the user again when it fails to capture a valid slot value during value elicitation.
Indicates whether the user can interrupt the failure response message while it is being spoken or displayed during slot capture.

Specifies the list of message groups for the failure response of the slot capture setting, where each group contains a message and an optional set of variations to use when the bot is unable to capture the slot value.
Defines the message object (with content and content type) that Amazon Lex includes in this message group of the failure response when it cannot capture the slot value.
Defines a custom payload object containing a value string that Lex uses as the message content when slot capture fails, within the failure response message group.
Specifies the content of the custom payload message returned to the user when Lex fails to capture the slot value, allowing the response to be in a client-defined format such as JSON.
Configures the image response card, with image URL, title, subtitle, and optional buttons, displayed as part of the failure message when slot capture fails.
Defines the list of buttons displayed on the image response card used in the failure response for slot capture, where each button has a text label and a value sent to the bot when selected.
The text displayed on the button of the image response card used in the failure response when the slot capture setting fails, within the Lex bot's message groups list.
The value sent to the bot when the user clicks this button on the image response card in the failed slot capture message.
The URL of the image displayed in the image response card within the failure response message group for slot capture.
The subtitle text shown beneath the title of the image response card in the failure message returned when slot capture fails, used to provide additional context to the user.
The title text displayed on the image response card shown to the user in the failure response when Lex cannot capture the slot value.
Defines the plain text message that Amazon Lex uses in the failure response when a user fails to provide a valid value for the slot during value elicitation, as part of the slot capture setting.
The text content of a plain-text message sent to the user when slot capture fails in the failure response of the slot capture setting during value elicitation in an Amazon Lex bot.

Defines the SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) version of the message that Amazon Lex speaks when slot capture fails, enabling control over pronunciation, intonation, and other speech aspects in the failure response.
The SSML-formatted text of the message that Amazon Lex sends as the failure response when slot capture fails, using SSML to control speech synthesis.
Specifies a list of alternative message variations for a message group in the slot-capture failure response, allowing the bot to randomly select one to present to the user.

Defines a custom JSON payload (with a 'value' string) as an alternative message variation in the failure response for slot capture, allowing a structured, non-text response to be delivered to the user.
The value of a CustomPayload is the raw string (often JSON) that is sent to the user in the failure response message when slot capture fails, as defined within a message group variation.
Defines the image response card shown to the user in the failure message variation, including properties such as title, subtitle, image URL, and buttons for interactive choices.
Defines the list of buttons shown on the image response card of the failure response when slot capture fails, where each button includes its display text and associated value.
The text displayed on a button within an image response card used in the failure response message for slot capture.
The value sent to the bot when a user clicks this button on the image response card shown as part of the failure response for a slot capture.
The URL of the image displayed on the image response card used in the failure message when the slot capture setting fails to capture a value.
Specifies the subtitle text displayed on the image response card used in the failure response when slot capture fails.
The title text displayed on the image response card included in the failure response when the slot capture fails.
The plain text message object defines the text variant used within the failure response's message group when slot capture fails for the slot's value elicitation setting in an Amazon Lex bot intent.
The text content of the plain text message variation used in the failure response when slot capture fails.
Defines the SSML-formatted text for this variation of the failure response message that is shown when the slot is not captured successfully in the Lex bot's intent.
The SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) text of the message variation to be spoken to the user as the failure response when slot capture fails.
Specifies whether the slot must be filled (Required) or may be left empty (Optional) when eliciting values for the intent.

Defines the prompts and behavior for a slot's value elicitation when the bot is waiting for user input (still-waiting response) and after the user provides input (continue response), including whether those prompts are active and their response specifications.
Defines the message (via message groups and an allow-interrupt flag) that Amazon Lex sends to the user when they choose to continue after the waiting prompt during slot value elicitation.
Indicates whether the bot's continue response message in the wait-and-continue specification can be interrupted by user input.
A list of message groups that comprise the bot's continue-response messages, sent when the bot resumes slot value elicitation after a waiting period.
Defines the content and content type of a single message within a message group in the continue response of the wait-and-continue slot value elicitation prompt.
The custom payload object that defines a custom message format (e.g., JSON or YAML) sent to the client for the continue response, rather than using plain text or SSML.
Specifies the string content of the custom payload (e.g., a JSON-encoded payload) that Amazon Lex uses as the message to deliver to the user in the continue-after-wait response.
Defines the image response card displayed to the user, containing a title, subtitle, image URL, and optionally one or more buttons.
Defines the interactive buttons displayed on the image response card in the continue response message, where each button carries a text label and a value sent back to the bot when selected.
The text label displayed on a button in the image response card within the continue response message of a slot's wait-and-continue specification.
Specifies the value that is sent to Amazon Lex as the user's response when this button is clicked on the image response card.
Specifies the URL of the image displayed in the image response card that is included in the continue message sent to the user when the bot proceeds after waiting during slot value elicitation.
The subtitle is the secondary text displayed below the title on the image response card in the Lex bot's message.
The title text displayed on the image response card within the continue-response message used during slot value elicitation in an Amazon Lex bot.

Specifies the plain-text message that the bot sends to the user as part of the continue response in a wait-and-continue slot value elicitation, which typically prompts the user to provide the required slot value.

The text of the plain-text message that Amazon Lex sends to the user as the 'continue' response after a wait-and-continue slot elicitation step, typically prompting the user to proceed or providing follow-up information.

Defines the SSML-formatted message text that the Lex bot speaks to the user in the continue response of a wait-and-continue prompt, allowing control over pronunciation, pauses, and prosody via Speech Synthesis Markup Language.
Specifies the SSML-formatted text of the message sent to the user as the continue response during wait-and-continue elicitation.
Specifies a list of message variations for the continue response within this message group, enabling Amazon Lex to randomly choose among the variants when delivering the prompt.

Specifies the custom payload (a user-defined string, typically JSON) to deliver to the client for this variation of a message in the continue-response group, as part of the wait-and-continue value elicitation setting.
The string content of the custom payload message sent to the user in this continue-response variation.

Specifies an image response card for a message variation, including its title, optional subtitle, image URL, and optional buttons, as part of the continuation message in the slot's value elicitation wait-and-continue prompt.
A list of buttons for the image response card, where each button specifies its displayed text and the value sent to the bot when clicked.

The text label displayed on the button in the image response card used in the continue-response message, which is part of the wait-and-continue specification for value elicitation on a slot in a Lex bot intent.
The value sent to the Amazon Lex bot when a user clicks this button on the image response card.
The HTTPS URL of the image displayed in the image response card for the continue response message in the Lex bot slot's value elicitation setting.
Subtitle text displayed on the image response card, providing additional context below the title in a message variation.
The title text displayed on the image response card that appears in the continue response during wait-and-continue slot elicitation in the Lex bot.
Defines the plain-text message variation for a continuation response within a slot's wait-and-continue elicitation setting, providing the literal text the Lex bot can deliver to the user.
The actual plain-text string content of this message variation, which Lex displays to the user as part of the continue response prompt during slot value elicitation.
This object defines an SSML-based message variation for the continue message in a wait-and-continue specification, providing the SSML markup that Amazon Lex uses for speech synthesis.
The SSML string content of an alternative message that Amazon Lex speaks to the user as part of the continue-response message group during the wait-and-continue value elicitation for a slot.
Indicates whether the wait-and-continue prompt behavior for the slot's value elicitation is enabled in the Amazon Lex bot.

Defines the response that Amazon Lex sends to the user repeatedly while the user is still waiting to provide a slot value, including the message groups, the frequency (in seconds) at which the message repeats, and whether the user can interrupt the still-waiting prompt.
Indicates whether the user can interrupt the still-waiting response while the bot is waiting for the slot value.
Specifies how often (in seconds) the bot sends the still-waiting response message to the user while waiting for a slot value during elicitation.

Defines the ordered list of message groups, each containing a primary message and optional variations, that Amazon Lex sends to the user while they are still waiting during a slot's value elicitation wait-and-continue response.

Specifies the primary message (plain text, SSML, custom payload, or image response card) that the Lex bot sends to the user within a message group while it is still waiting for the required slot value.

Defines the custom payload object for a still-waiting response message, where the object's value is a JSON string containing the payload sent to the user when the bot is waiting for slot value elicitation.

The value of the custom payload, a string containing the actual content of the custom message that Amazon Lex sends to the user while still waiting for a slot value, within a still-waiting response message group of a wait-and-continue specification.
Defines the image response card (with image URL, title, subtitle, and optional buttons) used in the still-waiting response message for the slot's value elicitation setting in an Amazon Lex bot.
Defines the list of buttons that appear on an image response card used in a still-waiting response message for a Lex bot's slot value elicitation setting.
The text displayed on a button within an image response card sent as a still-waiting message during slot elicitation in an Amazon Lex bot.
The value sent to the Amazon Lex bot when the user clicks this button on the image response card.
The URL of the image displayed in the image response card for the still-waiting response message, which the Lex bot shows to the user while waiting for slot value elicitation.
The subtitle text displayed in the image response card, providing additional detail below the title in the Lex bot conversation.
The title displayed on the image response card shown when the bot is still waiting for user input.
Defines the plain text message that Amazon Lex presents in a message group within the still-waiting response, used to prompt the user again while slot value elicitation is still waiting for input.
The text content of the plain text message shown to the user while the bot is still waiting for a slot value during elicitation, as part of the wait-and-continue specification.
Specifies the SSML-formatted message content to be spoken to the user during the still-waiting response, provided as an object containing the SSML text in its value field.
The SSML markup text that Amazon Lex uses as the spoken message when the user does not respond during the slot's wait-and-continue prompt, defined within the message group's SSML message.

Represents a list of alternative message variations (e.g., different text, SSML, or custom payloads) for the still-waiting response, allowing the bot to present varied prompts while waiting for user input.

Specifies a custom JSON payload message to be sent to the user as one of the message variations when the bot is still waiting for a slot value, enabling channel-specific or structured data interactions.
The string content of the custom payload sent to the Lambda function as part of a message variation in the still-waiting response for a slot's wait-and-continue specification in an Amazon Lex bot.
Specifies an image response card variation, which displays an image, title, subtitle, and optional buttons to the user during a slot's wait-and-continue prompt.
Defines the list of buttons shown on the image response card within the still-waiting message, where each button specifies its display text and the value sent to the bot when selected.
The text displayed on the button in the image response card of the still waiting response for the slot's value elicitation.
The value sent to Amazon Lex as the user's response when the corresponding button on the image response card is clicked.
The HTTPS URL of the image displayed in the image response card that accompanies the still-waiting message during slot value elicitation in Amazon Lex.
The subtitle displayed below the title on the image response card used in the still-waiting response message variation for a slot's wait-and-continue prompt in an Amazon Lex bot.
The title text displayed on the image response card, which serves as the main heading for the card presented to the user in the still-waiting message.

Defines a plain-text message object (containing the actual message string) used as a variation within a message group in the still-waiting response of an Amazon Lex bot's slot value-elicitation wait-and-continue configuration.
The plain text content of the message that Amazon Lex displays to the user in the still-waiting response while waiting for a slot value, within the wait-and-continue specification.
Defines the Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) content for one variation of the message group in the still-waiting response.
The SSML-formatted text content of a message variation used in the still-waiting response within a slot's wait-and-continue specification for an Amazon Lex bot.
Specifies the number of seconds to wait before sending a 'still waiting' message to the user during a slot's wait-and-continue prompt in the still waiting response configuration.

For an Amazon Lex V2 bot, defines the response specification (messages and interruption settings) that the bot uses to prompt the user while waiting for them to provide the value for the slot, as part of the wait-and-continue configuration in value elicitation.
Determines whether the user can interrupt the waiting response message while it is being played.

Specifies the list of message groups, each containing a message and optional response variations, that the bot uses to send messages to the user while waiting for a response during slot value elicitation.
Defines the primary message (plain text, SSML, or custom payload) that the bot presents to the user while waiting for the response during slot value elicitation.

The custom payload object for the message, containing a raw value string (JSON) that is passed to a Lambda function or integration for advanced, non-text response handling during the slot elicitation wait-and-continue flow in an Amazon Lex bot.
The JSON-encoded string that contains the custom payload to send to the user when Amazon Lex waits for a response, as defined in the waiting response message for a slot's value elicitation setting.

Configures an image response card sent as a waiting message in the wait-and-continue specification, allowing an image with optional title, subtitle, and buttons to be displayed to the user during slot elicitation.
Defines the list of buttons shown on the image response card in the waiting message, where each button has a text label and a value that is sent back to the bot when selected.
Specifies the text displayed on the button of the image response card in the waiting response message used during slot value elicitation.
The value sent to the Amazon Lex bot when the user clicks this button on the image response card.
The URL of the image to display on the image response card for the waiting response message in the slot's value elicitation setting.
The subtitle text shown below the title on the image response card, providing supplementary context to the user.

The title displayed on the image response card within a waiting response message group, used in a slot's wait-and-continue specification to show a card to the user while the bot pauses during value elicitation.
The plain text message displayed to the user while the bot is waiting for a response during slot value elicitation.
The actual text content of the plain text message that Amazon Lex sends to the user as a waiting response during slot value elicitation when the wait-and-continue specification is active.
Specifies the SSML-formatted message content that the bot uses for the waiting response when it pauses for user input in the slot's value elicitation setting.
The SSML markup that defines the spoken waiting message used by Amazon Lex while it waits for the user's response in a slot value elicitation wait-and-continue configuration.

Specifies a list of alternative message variations for the waiting response message group in the slot's value elicitation wait-and-continue behavior, allowing Lex to present different message content (e.g., plain text, SSML, custom payload, or image response card) to the user.
Defines the custom payload message variation, specifying the raw JSON string that is sent to the user as part of the waiting response message group.
The string content of the custom payload sent to the user during the waiting response for a wait-and-continue specification while eliciting a slot value.

Defines an image response card (with title, subtitle, image URL, and optional buttons) displayed to the user within the waiting response's message group variation during slot value elicitation in an Amazon Lex bot.
The buttons to display on the image response card, each with text and a value sent to the bot when clicked, used to prompt user interaction during the wait-and-continue flow.
The text label displayed on a button in an image response card that appears as a variation within a waiting response message for a slot's value elicitation wait-and-continue specification.
The value sent to Amazon Lex when the user clicks the corresponding button on the image response card.
Specifies the URL of the image displayed on the image response card within the waiting message shown while the bot waits for the user to provide a slot value.
The subtitle text displayed on the image response card that accompanies the waiting response message for a slot during value elicitation in an Amazon Lex bot.
Specifies the title text displayed on the image response card within a waiting response message variation for a slot's wait-and-continue value elicitation setting in an Amazon Lex bot.
Defines the plain-text message variation used in the waiting response during slot elicitation, where the actual message text is provided in the 'value' property of this PlainTextMessage object.
The actual text content of this plain-text message variation, which the bot plays as part of the waiting response shown to the user while it elicits a slot value.
Defines the SSML-formatted text for this message variation, used when the bot is waiting for the user to provide a slot value in the wait-and-continue prompt.
The SSML-formatted text that Amazon Lex speaks as one variation of the waiting response when prompting the user to continue during slot value elicitation.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.locale_id.text: Specifies the unique language and regional variant identifier (e.g., 'en_US' or 'de_DE') for this bot locale, enabling the bot to support multiple locales within the same bot.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.nlu_confidence_t.text: Sets the minimum confidence score (0.0 to 1.0) that Amazon Lex requires for a user's utterance to be considered a match for an intent in this bot locale.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.slot_types.text: Defines the custom slot types available within this locale, specifying how slot values are captured and validated in the bot's interactions.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.slot_types.compo.text: Specifies the component slot types and their names that together form a composite slot type in an Amazon Lex bot locale.
Specifies the list of sub-slots that compose this composite slot type, where each sub-slot defines its name and the slot type it references.
Specifies the name of an individual sub-slot within a composite slot type, which is used to identify and reference that sub-slot when the composite slot is captured in a conversation.
The unique identifier of the slot type assigned to this sub-slot within the composite slot type, which determines the data format and validation for values captured in that sub-slot.
The name of an existing slot type (custom or built-in) that this sub-slot references within a composite slot type, enabling the definition of structured multi-slot values in Amazon Lex V2.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.slot_types.descr.text: A free-form description of the slot type, used to document its intended purpose and assist in maintenance and identification within the Amazon Lex bot.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.slot_types.exter.text: Configures an external grammar source (such as a file in Amazon S3) that defines the valid values for a slot type in a Lex bot locale.
Specifies the grammar slot type settings for a slot type that uses an external source, including the S3 bucket and object key of the grammar definition file.
Specifies the Amazon S3 location of the grammar file used as the source for the grammar slot type.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to decrypt the S3 object containing the grammar definition file for this external grammar slot type source.
The name of the S3 bucket that contains the grammar definition file for the grammar slot type.
The S3 object key (file path) of the grammar file inside the specified S3 bucket, used as the source for defining this grammar slot type in Amazon Lex.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.slot_types.name.text: The name of the custom slot type within the bot locale, used as a unique identifier for the slot type in that locale.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.slot_types.paren.text: The signature (name) of the parent slot type that this slot type inherits from, allowing the slot type to reuse and extend the parent's configuration within the Lex bot's locale.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.slot_types.slot_.text: Specifies the acceptable values for a custom slot type, where each entry can include a primary `value` and optional `synonyms` that map alternative phrases to that value.
Defines the sample utterance (a string stored under the nested 'value' property) that represents a slot type value for a Lex bot locale.
The actual text string that Amazon Lex uses to match user input to this slot type value within the bot's locale.
Provides a list of alternative words or phrases (synonyms) that map to this slot type value, enabling the bot to recognize multiple expressions for the same value.
Specifies an alternative string that can be used to refer to the canonical slot type value, which is matched during user input and mapped to that value.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.slot_types.value.text: This object configures how slot values for the slot type are selected, specifying the resolution strategy (OriginalValue or TopResolution) and optionally a regex pattern for matching values when the strategy is Regex.
Specifies advanced recognition options for the slot type's value selection, including whether fuzzy matching is enabled to recognize user input that approximates defined slot values.

Specifies the audio recognition strategy for the slot type, where the only supported value is 'UseSlotTypeAsCustomVocabulary', which uses the slot type's values as a custom vocabulary for audio recognition.
The regex_filter object specifies a regular expression pattern that constrains which user utterances are valid values for slots using this slot type in the Lex bot.
The regular expression pattern used by Lex to validate or filter slot values, defining which user inputs match for the slot type when the value selection setting includes a regex filter.
Specifies how Amazon Lex resolves a slot value when multiple slot type entries match the user's utterance, with options such as returning the original value or the top resolution.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.speech_detection.text: Determines the sensitivity of speech detection in the bot locale, with valid values of AUTO, HIGH, or LOW, which controls how aggressively Amazon Lex recognizes spoken input in the audio stream.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.speech_recogniti.text: For each locale of the bot, the speech recognition settings configure how speech is recognized, including whether speech recognition is enabled and the engine type used (standard or cross-talk).
Configures the custom language model used by Amazon Lex for speech recognition in this bot locale, via a SpeechModelConfig object that specifies the model name.
Configuration for Deepgram as the third-party speech recognition provider, including API key and model settings, used when the speech model type is set to Deepgram.

For the Deepgram speech model configuration in the bot locale's speech recognition settings, this field specifies the ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the Deepgram API token used to authenticate requests.
The identifier of the Deepgram speech recognition model to use in this bot locale, such as a specific model version name.
Specifies the preferred speech recognition model type (e.g., 'Standard' or 'Generative') used by Amazon Lex when converting audio input to text for this bot locale.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.unified_speech_s.text: Specifies speech recognition settings for the locale, including phrase lists and custom vocabulary that improve transcription accuracy.
Specifies the foundation model (e.g., Amazon Nova) and its version used for automatic speech recognition in the bot locale, enabling enhanced ASR under unified speech settings.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the speech foundation model used to perform speech recognition and natural language understanding for the bot's locale.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.voice_settings.text: Configures the voice used by the bot for this locale, including the Amazon Polly voice ID and engine type.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.voice_settings.e.text: The text-to-speech voice engine used for the bot locale, which can be either 'standard' or 'neural'.

aws_lex_bot.bot_locales.voice_settings.v.text: Specifies the Amazon Polly voice ID that Amazon Lex uses for text-to-speech in this bot locale.

aws_lex_bot.bot_members.bot_member_alias.text: The unique identifier of the alias of the member Lex V2 bot that is associated with this bot via its bot_members list.
The alias name of the child bot that is included as a member of this composite (parent) Lex bot.

aws_lex_bot.bot_members.bot_member_id.text: The Amazon Lex bot ID (unique identifier) of a member bot that is associated with this bot in its network of related bots.

aws_lex_bot.bot_members.bot_member_name.text: The unique name given to a member bot within the parent bot's multi-bot configuration, used to identify and reference that bot in the overall bot routing and orchestration logic.

aws_lex_bot.bot_members.bot_member_versi.text: The version of the bot member (e.g., '1' or '$LATEST') that is being associated with the parent bot in an Amazon Lex multi-region bot network.

aws_lex_bot.bot_tags.text: A list of key-value tag pairs (each containing 'key' and 'value') that are attached to the Amazon Lex bot for metadata, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_lex_bot.bot_tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Amazon Lex bot, serving as the map key in the bot_tags collection to identify the tag.

aws_lex_bot.bot_tags.value.text: Stores the value portion of a key-value tag assigned to the Amazon Lex bot for resource metadata and management.

aws_lex_bot.data_privacy.text: Specifies data privacy settings for the bot, including the ChildDirected flag that indicates whether the bot is intended for children under 13, affecting how Amazon Lex stores and processes speech and user data.

aws_lex_bot.data_privacy.child_directed.text: Indicates whether the Amazon Lex bot collects information from children under age 13, requiring compliance with the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA).

aws_lex_bot.error_log_settings.text: Configures the CloudWatch log group and IAM role used to store error logs generated by the Amazon Lex bot.

aws_lex_bot.error_log_settings.enabled.text: Toggles whether the Amazon Lex bot captures and forwards error-level conversation logs to the configured log destination.

aws_lex_bot.id.text: The unique identifier of the Lex bot, which is the bot's name.

aws_lex_bot.idle_session_ttlin_seconds.text: Sets the number of seconds an Amazon Lex bot session remains active after the user's last interaction before the session is closed.

aws_lex_bot.name.text: The unique name assigned to the Amazon Lex bot, which is required and must be unique within the AWS account.

aws_lex_bot.replication.text: The 'replication' property defines the cross-region replication configuration for the Lex bot, specifying the IAM replication role and the list of destination AWS regions to which the bot is replicated.

aws_lex_bot.replication.replica_regions.text: Specifies the list of AWS Regions to replicate the Lex bot to, enabling the bot to operate in multiple regions for high availability and reduced latency.

aws_lex_bot.role_arn.text: The ARN of an IAM role that Amazon Lex assumes to access other AWS services (such as Lambda functions) on behalf of the bot.

aws_lex_bot.test_bot_alias_settings.text: Configures the test bot alias used for validating the bot, including locale-specific alias settings, conversation log settings, and a description.

aws_lex_bot.test_bot_alias_settings.bot_.text: Defines the per-locale settings (including Lambda code hook and enabled status) for the test bot alias associated with this Lex bot.
Specifies the per-locale configuration for the test bot alias, including whether the alias is enabled for that locale and the Lambda code hook specification used to handle slot and intent requests.
Specifies the AWS Lambda function and optional interface version that Amazon Lex V2 invokes to handle the bot's dialog for each locale configured on this bot alias.
The lambda_code_hook object defines the AWS Lambda function used as the code hook for the bot alias locale, specifying the Lambda function ARN and the code hook interface version.
Specifies the version of the Lambda code hook interface used by the bot, with the only valid value being 1.0.
ARN of the Lambda function invoked as the code hook for this bot alias locale, used to handle conversation flow or fulfillment logic.
Determines whether the locale is enabled for the bot alias in the test bot alias settings; when false, the locale is not available for use.
Specifies the locale identifier (such as 'en_US' or 'es_ES') for which the corresponding bot alias locale settings apply, enabling language-specific alias configuration.

aws_lex_bot.test_bot_alias_settings.conv.text: Configures the conversation log settings, including text and audio log destinations, for the test bot alias of the Lex bot.
Specifies the list of audio log settings for the test bot alias's conversation logs, defining the S3 bucket destination and whether each audio log is enabled.
Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket that receives audio conversation logs for the bot alias.
The S3 bucket destination for audio conversation logs, specifying the bucket name, ARN, and optional KMS key ARN used for encrypting the log files.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt audio conversation logs delivered to the S3 bucket.
For Amazon Lex conversation logs, this sets the S3 object prefix under which the audio logs are stored in the destination S3 bucket.
The ARN of the S3 bucket where audio conversation logs are delivered for this bot alias.
Whether audio conversation logs are enabled for the bot alias, allowing capture of audio streams to the configured S3 destination.
Specifies a list of settings for text conversation logs on the bot alias, each containing an enabled flag and the ARN of the CloudWatch Logs log group where Lex delivers text transcripts.
Defines the Amazon S3 bucket (including optional KMS encryption key) where text conversation logs are delivered when text logging is enabled for the test bot alias's conversation log settings.
This object defines the destination for text conversation logs as a CloudWatch Logs log group, specifying the log group ARN to which Amazon Lex delivers the logs.
The ARN of the CloudWatch log group where Amazon Lex delivers text conversation logs for this bot alias.
The prefix that is prepended to the log stream names in CloudWatch Logs where Amazon Lex writes text conversation logs for the bot alias.
Whether text conversation logs are enabled for the bot alias.

aws_lex_bot.test_bot_alias_settings.sent.text: Specifies sentiment analysis settings for the test bot alias, including the detectSentiment flag that enables or disables Amazon Lex sentiment detection on user utterances.
Indicates whether Amazon Lex detects the sentiment of user utterances for the test bot alias, enabling sentiment-based responses when set to true.

aws_lex_bot.test_bot_alias_tags.text: Defines the list of key-value tags applied to the test bot alias that AWS Lex creates for testing the bot.

aws_lex_bot.test_bot_alias_tags.key.text: The tag key component of a key-value pair in the test_bot_alias_tags map, which assigns tags to the test alias of the Amazon Lex bot.

aws_lex_bot.test_bot_alias_tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the test bot alias of the Amazon Lex bot, as part of the test_bot_alias_tags map.

aws_lex_bot_alias.bot_alias_locale_setti.text: This object defines the alias behavior for a single locale, specifying whether the alias is enabled for that locale and optionally the Lambda code hook invoked for user interactions in that locale.
Defines the Lambda code hook specification for a particular locale in the bot alias, including the Lambda ARN and code hook interface version that Lex invokes during conversation.
The `lambda_code_hook` object specifies the Amazon Lex Lambda function and its version that is invoked as the code hook for the bot alias locale, enabling custom logic in the conversation flow.
Specifies the version of the code hook interface that the Lambda function uses, with '1.0' being the supported value for Lex V2 bots.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function that is invoked as the code hook for the bot alias locale.
Whether the bot alias is enabled for the specified locale; when false, the alias is disabled and unavailable for that locale.
The locale identifier (such as en_US or en_GB) that identifies which set of bot alias locale settings this entry applies to.

aws_lex_bot_alias.bot_alias_status.text: The current status of the bot alias, such as CREATING, READY, or FAILED, indicating whether the alias is prepared for use.

aws_lex_bot_alias.bot_alias_tags.key.text: The tag key to assign to the Amazon Lex bot alias, used to categorize or identify the alias in AWS tagging systems.

aws_lex_bot_alias.bot_alias_tags.value.text: The value of a tag (a key-value pair) assigned to the Amazon Lex bot alias, used to categorize or manage the alias resource.

aws_lex_bot_alias.conversation_log_setti.text: Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket configuration where audio conversation logs for this Lex bot alias are delivered.
The Amazon S3 bucket ARN where audio conversation logs are delivered for this bot alias.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt audio conversation logs delivered to the S3 bucket destination.
The prefix prepended to the S3 object keys for audio conversation logs, enabling logs to be stored under a specific folder path in the bucket.
The ARN of the S3 bucket where Amazon Lex delivers audio conversation logs.
Indicates whether audio conversation logs are enabled for the bot alias.
Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket where text logs are delivered, including the bucket name and ARN.
Specifies the CloudWatch Logs destination for text conversation logs, including the log group ARN and the IAM role that authorizes Lex to write logs to that group.
The ARN of the CloudWatch Logs log group to which text conversation logs are delivered for this Lex bot alias.
The log prefix to prepend to the names of CloudWatch Logs log streams that store text conversation logs for the Lex bot alias.
Determines whether text conversation logs are recorded to the specified CloudWatch Logs log group for the Lex bot alias.

aws_lex_bot_version.bot_version_locale_s.text: Specifies the details of a locale in the bot version, including the source bot version from which the locale's version is derived.
The version number of the source bot to use as the basis for the locale version in this bot version.
Identifies the locale (such as 'en_US' or 'en_GB') that this bot version locale specification entry applies to, and must match a locale configured on the bot.

aws_license_manager_grant.allowed_operat.text: Specifies the list of license operations, such as checking out, checking in, creating a grant, or extending consumption, that the grant recipient is permitted to perform on the licensed resource.

aws_license_manager_grant.grant_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the license grant in AWS License Manager.

aws_license_manager_grant.license_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the license whose entitlements are being granted to a recipient.

aws_license_manager_grant.principals.text: Specifies the ARNs of the AWS principals (users, roles, or accounts) that receive the license grant.

aws_license_manager_grant.status.text: Specifies the intended lifecycle state of the license grant, such as ACTIVE for immediate activation or PENDING_ACCEPT to require grantee acceptance, and can be updated to REJECTED or DELETED to terminate the grant.

aws_license_manager_grant.tags.key.text: The tag key that you assign to an AWS License Manager grant to categorize and manage the grant.

aws_license_manager_license.consumption_.text: Defines the license consumption model, specifying the renewal type (e.g., none, weekly, monthly) and any optional borrow or provisional configurations that govern how the license is used.
Configures the borrowing parameters for the license, including whether early check-in is allowed and the maximum duration in minutes that the license can be borrowed for offline use.
Determines whether licensees can return a borrowed license before the maximum borrow time expires.
The maximum time, in minutes, that a license can be borrowed when the license's consumption configuration uses a borrow configuration.
Specifies the provisional configuration for the license, which defines the maximum time in minutes that the license remains valid in its provisional state before expiring.
Specifies the maximum time in minutes that a license can be provisionally consumed before it expires, requiring renewal or a different consumption configuration.
Specifies how often the license renews automatically, with valid values being 'None', 'Weekly', or 'Monthly'.

aws_license_manager_license.entitlements.text: Defines the list of entitlements granted by the license, each specifying a name, unit, and value (such as a maximum count of a resource like vCPUs or instances).
Indicates whether the entitlement can be checked in (returned) after use, releasing the license capacity back to the available pool.
The maximum number of units (such as vCPUs, instances, or other license-allowable resources) that can be consumed under this entitlement.
The name of the entitlement, which defines the specific resource or capability (e.g., vCPU, instance type) that the license grants usage rights for.
Indicates whether this license entitlement allows overage, meaning usage beyond the allowed maximum count is permitted.
The unit of measurement for the entitlement (for example, 'Count' or 'None'), indicating how the entitlement value is quantified.
For each entitlement in the license, this is the entitlement's value (for example, a quantity or usage amount) expressed as a string.

aws_license_manager_license.issuer.text: Defines the entity that issues the license, including the issuer's name (and optionally a signing key) used to identify and verify the license source.

aws_license_manager_license.issuer.name.text: The name of the issuer that grants the license, identifying the entity (such as 'AWS' or a custom vendor) that created the license record.

aws_license_manager_license.issuer.sign_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS KMS symmetric customer managed key used by the issuer to sign the license.

aws_license_manager_license.license_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the license.

aws_license_manager_license.license_meta.text: Specifies a list of key-value pairs (metadata) that AWS License Manager attaches to the license and exposes for tracking and management.
Specifies the name (key) of a metadata entry in a license's custom metadata list, used to store key-value information for the license.

Specifies the value portion of a key-value metadata pair attached to an AWS License Manager license, used to store custom information such as cost center or department alongside the corresponding `key` field.

aws_license_manager_license.status.text: Specifies the desired status of the license, such as AVAILABLE to activate it immediately or PENDING_AVAILABLE to keep it inactive until a later time.

aws_license_manager_license.validity.text: Defines the start and end dates of the license's validity period, during which the license can be used.

aws_license_manager_license_asset_rule_s.text: Defines a conjunctive (AND) grouping of instance rule statements, such that every condition inside must evaluate to true for the overall license rule to match an EC2 instance.
A list of sub-rule statements that must all match (logical AND) for the containing AND rule statement to be satisfied.

The `or_rule_statement` within an `instance_rule_statement` specifies an array of instance rule statements that are combined with logical OR, meaning the rule matches if any one of the included statements (such as `ec2InstanceType` conditions) is true for the instance.

Defines the list of alternative rule statements that are evaluated under an OR condition within an instance rule statement, where the overall statement matches if any of the listed sub-statements matches.

For a License Manager asset rule set, this constraint string on the instance matching rule specifies the value or pattern (such as an instance type or family) that the resource attribute must satisfy for the OR rule statement's matching rule to be true.

A list of sub-rule statements that must all evaluate to true to satisfy the AND rule statement inside a license configuration rule statement, defining the combined conditions for the license asset rule set.

Provides the list of individual rule statements that are evaluated with OR logic within the parent 'or_rule_statement', so the overall rule is satisfied when at least one of these matching statements matches the license configuration.

Defines the list of string values used as matching criteria within each rule statement, which are combined under an AND condition to determine whether a license asset meets the rule set's requirements in AWS License Manager.
The key (such as a tag key or resource attribute) that the license rule statement's matching condition uses to identify which asset resources match the rule.
Defines the list of rule statements that are combined with OR logic, so the parent OR rule statement is satisfied if any of these matching rule statements evaluates to true.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as equals, contains, or startsWith) used by a matching rule statement within an OR rule statement to evaluate a resource attribute against a value.
Specifies the attribute key (such as a tag key or resource property) that the license rule statement evaluates against the match value to determine if a resource qualifies.
The list of string values that a license rule statement compares against a resource attribute, where the statement is satisfied when the attribute equals any one of these values.

aws_lightsail_alarm.alarm_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lightsail alarm, uniquely identifying it in AWS.

aws_lightsail_bucket.bucket_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the Lightsail bucket, such as arn:aws:lightsail:region:account-id:bucket/bucket-name.

aws_lightsail_bucket.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to assign to the Lightsail bucket.

aws_lightsail_bucket.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the Lightsail bucket, used for metadata, identification, and cost allocation.

aws_lightsail_certificate.certificate_ar.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lightsail certificate, assigned by AWS when the certificate is created.

aws_lightsail_certificate.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the Lightsail certificate, used to categorize and identify the certificate in the Lightsail console and API.

aws_lightsail_certificate.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag assigned to the AWS Lightsail certificate, used to label, organize, and support cost allocation for the certificate.

aws_lightsail_container.container_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lightsail container service.

aws_lightsail_container.container_servic.text: Specifies the command to run inside the container, overriding the default entrypoint or command from the container image, as an array of strings.

The unique name of the container within the Lightsail container service deployment, used to identify the container in the deployment configuration and when routing traffic from the service's public endpoint.
Defines the environment variables (as key-value pairs) to pass into the container within a Lightsail container service deployment.
Sets the value for an environment variable key in the container, which is passed to the container at runtime in the Lightsail container service deployment.
The name of an environment variable for the container, paired with its value in the container's environment map.
Specifies the container image (e.g., a Docker Hub image or Amazon ECR repository URI) to use for this container in the Lightsail container service deployment.
Defines the ports on which the container listens, including the port number and the protocol (HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, or UDP) that the container service routes requests to for each exposed port.
The port number that the container listens on, used by the Lightsail container service to expose the container's application to incoming traffic.
The protocol assigned to a container's open port, such as HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, or UDP, defining how traffic reaches the container within an AWS Lightsail container service deployment.

aws_lightsail_container.public_domain_na.text: The name of the SSL/TLS certificate associated with the corresponding public domain name in the Lightsail container service configuration.

The list of fully qualified domain names (such as subdomains or alternate names) attached to a main domain entry for the Lightsail container service, used to route custom domain traffic to the service.

aws_lightsail_container.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key attached to the Lightsail container service, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_lightsail_database.database_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the Lightsail database, assigned by AWS upon creation.

aws_lightsail_database.relational_databa.text: Specifies the allowed values for the relational database parameter, such as a range or list of valid options, as defined by the Lightsail database engine.
Specifies whether the parameter change is applied immediately or after the database reboots (pending-reboot).
Indicates whether the parameter is dynamic (applied immediately without a reboot) or static (requires a database reboot to take effect).
The data type of the relational database parameter, such as 'string', 'integer', or 'boolean'.
Provides a descriptive text explaining the purpose or meaning of the relational database parameter in the AWS Lightsail database.
Indicates whether the specified relational database parameter can be modified from its default value.

The name of the database parameter (e.g., `max_connections`) that this entry in the relational database parameter list refers to, used to identify which parameter's value is being specified or modified.

The value to assign to the specified relational database parameter (identified by its parameter_name) in the Lightsail database, used for configuring engine-level settings such as MySQL or PostgreSQL parameters.

aws_lightsail_database.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Lightsail database, which identifies the tag for organizing and managing the database resource in AWS.

aws_lightsail_database.tags.value.text: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the Lightsail database, which holds the metadata string that accompanies the tag key.

aws_lightsail_database_snapshot.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to attach to the Lightsail database snapshot.

aws_lightsail_database_snapshot.tags.val.text: The value of a tag attached to the Lightsail database snapshot, used to categorize or identify the resource.

aws_lightsail_disk.add_ons.add_on_type.text: Specifies the type of add-on to enable for the Lightsail disk, such as AutoSnapshot for automatic snapshots.

aws_lightsail_disk.add_ons.auto_snapshot.text: Configures the automatic snapshot add-on for the Lightsail disk, including the daily time (in HH:00 format) at which the snapshot is created.
Specifies the time of day (in 24-hour HH:00 format, e.g., '02:00') when the automatic snapshot of the disk is created for the auto snapshot add-on.

aws_lightsail_disk.add_ons.status.text: The status of the disk add-on, typically 'Enabled' or 'Disabled', indicating whether the add-on is active on the Lightsail disk.

aws_lightsail_disk.disk_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Lightsail disk.

aws_lightsail_disk.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to attach to the Lightsail disk, used to organize and identify the disk resource.

aws_lightsail_disk.tags.value.text: Specifies the tag value in a key-value pair that you attach to the Lightsail disk for metadata and resource management purposes.

aws_lightsail_disk_snapshot.tags.key.text: The key of a tag, such as 'Name' or 'Environment', that you can attach to the Lightsail disk snapshot for identification and management.

aws_lightsail_disk_snapshot.tags.value.text: The value of a tag (key-value pair) applied to the AWS Lightsail disk snapshot.

aws_lightsail_distribution.cache_behavio.text: Specifies the cache behavior for the associated path pattern, with supported values of 'cache' or 'no-cache' indicating whether matching requests are cached.
The path pattern (such as `/images/*`) that determines which requests this cache behavior applies to in the Lightsail distribution.

aws_lightsail_distribution.distribution_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the Lightsail distribution.

aws_lightsail_distribution.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to attach to the Lightsail distribution, used to identify and categorize the resource.

aws_lightsail_distribution.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag attached to the Lightsail distribution, used to store arbitrary metadata (e.g., environment, owner) for resource organization, cost allocation, or access control.

aws_lightsail_domain.domain_entries.is_a.text: Indicates whether the domain entry is an alias record that routes traffic to an AWS resource such as a load balancer or distribution, rather than a standard DNS record with a literal target.

aws_lightsail_domain.domain_entries.name.text: The subdomain or hostname for the DNS record, such as 'www' or '@' for the root domain, that this domain entry defines.

aws_lightsail_domain.domain_entries.targ.text: The destination value that this Lightsail domain DNS record resolves to, such as an IPv4 address for an A record or a hostname for a CNAME record.

aws_lightsail_domain.domain_entries.type.text: The DNS record type for this domain entry, such as A, CNAME, MX, or TXT.

aws_lightsail_domain.tags.key.text: The key of a tag that can be assigned to a Lightsail domain, enabling you to categorize, manage, and control access to the domain.

aws_lightsail_instance.add_ons.add_on_ty.text: Specifies the type of add-on to attach to the Lightsail instance, with the only supported value being `AutoSnapshot` to enable automatic daily snapshots of the instance.

aws_lightsail_instance.add_ons.auto_snap.text: Configures the automatic snapshot add-on for the Lightsail instance, specifying the daily time of day for the snapshot to be created.
Specifies the time of day (in 24-hour HH:00 format) at which the automatic snapshot is taken for the Lightsail instance when the Auto Snapshot add-on is enabled.

aws_lightsail_instance.add_ons.status.text: Indicates whether the add-on is enabled or disabled, with values such as 'Enabled' or 'Disabled' for a Lightsail instance add-on.

aws_lightsail_instance.hardware.disks.at.text: The name of the Lightsail instance to which the disk is attached, which for a disk in an instance's hardware list is typically the instance itself.
Indicates whether the disk is currently attached to the instance, typically with values such as 'attached' or 'detached'.

aws_lightsail_instance.hardware.disks.di.text: The unique name of the disk attached to the Lightsail instance, used to identify the disk within the instance's hardware configuration.

aws_lightsail_instance.hardware.disks.io.text: The provisioned input/output operations per second (IOPS) for the block storage disk attached to the Lightsail instance, defining its performance level.

aws_lightsail_instance.hardware.disks.is.text: Indicates whether this disk is the system (boot) disk for the AWS Lightsail instance.

aws_lightsail_instance.hardware.disks.pa.text: The device path (e.g., /dev/sda1) for the attached block storage disk on the Lightsail instance, used to identify the disk within the operating system.

aws_lightsail_instance.hardware.disks.si.text: The size of the disk in gigabytes for a block storage disk attached to the Lightsail instance, as specified in the hardware.disks list.

aws_lightsail_instance.instance_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the Lightsail instance across AWS.

aws_lightsail_instance.networking.ports..text: Specifies whether the port rule applies to inbound or outbound traffic, with values 'inbound' or 'outbound'.
The source IP address or CIDR range that is allowed to access the specified port on the Lightsail instance.
Specifies whether the port is open to the public internet (Public) or restricted to private access within the Lightsail network (Private).
Lists named CIDR aliases (e.g., 'myIp', 'amazon') whose defined IP ranges are used as the allowed source addresses for this port rule in the instance's networking firewall.
The list of IPv4 CIDR blocks that are allowed to access the instance via the associated port.
Specifies the common name (e.g., SSH, RDP, HTTP) associated with the port, providing a human-readable label for the port's purpose.
The starting port number of a range to open in the Lightsail instance's firewall rules.
The list of IPv6 CIDR blocks that are allowed to access the port in the Lightsail instance networking configuration.
Specifies the network protocol (such as TCP, UDP, or ICMP) that the firewall rule applies to for the Lightsail instance's networking port mapping.
The inclusive end of the port range for this Lightsail instance networking rule, paired with the port set in fromPort to define which ports are opened.

aws_lightsail_instance.tags.key.text: The key of the tag to associate with the Lightsail instance.

aws_lightsail_instance.tags.value.text: The user-defined value paired with a tag key on the Lightsail instance, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_lightsail_instance_snapshot.tags.key.text: Specifies the key of a tag applied to the AWS Lightsail instance snapshot, used for organizing and identifying the snapshot.

aws_lightsail_load_balancer.load_balance.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Lightsail load balancer.

aws_lightsail_load_balancer.tags.key.text: The unique key of a tag attached to the Lightsail load balancer, used to identify, organize, and manage the resource for purposes such as cost tracking, access control, and operational grouping.

aws_lightsail_load_balancer.tags.value.text: The value of a tag associated with the Lightsail load balancer, allowing you to attach arbitrary metadata to the resource for management and identification.

aws_lightsail_load_balancer_tls_certific.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lightsail load balancer TLS certificate, assigned by AWS when the certificate is created.

aws_lightsail_static_ip.static_ip_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the Lightsail static IP within AWS.

aws_location_apikey.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Location Service API key.

aws_location_apikey.description.text: An optional user-provided description that annotates or identifies the API key in AWS Location Service.

aws_location_apikey.force_delete.text: Controls whether the API key can be deleted even when it is still referenced by AWS Location Service resources such as trackers or geofences.

aws_location_apikey.force_update.text: When true, forces the update of the API key so that you can modify its attributes (such as description) without providing the existing restrictions in the update request.

aws_location_apikey.key_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the API key, which uniquely identifies it across AWS.

aws_location_apikey.key_name.text: The name of the API key, which is used to identify and refer to the key in AWS Location Service resources and operations.

aws_location_apikey.no_expiry.text: Controls whether the Amazon Location API key is exempt from expiration, where true disables expiration so the key never expires, and false (or omitted) allows the key to expire according to its expiration time.

aws_location_apikey.restrictions.text: Defines the access control rules for the API key, specifying which actions and resources are allowed or denied via the AllowActions, AllowResources, DenyActions, and DenyResources properties.

aws_location_apikey.restrictions.allow_a.text: Specifies the list of action strings (such as geo:GetMap* or geo:SearchPlaceIndexForText) that the API key is permitted to invoke, defining the allowed Amazon Location Service operations for the API key.
List of Android application package names (application IDs) that are allowed to use the API key, defining the set of Android apps permitted to call AWS Location services with this key.
The SHA-1 certificate fingerprint of an Android app that is allowed to use this AWS Location API key, as part of the restriction rules for Android applications.
The Android application package name (e.g., com.example.myapp) that is allowed to use the API key when this restriction applies.
This restriction specifies the list of Apple app bundle identifiers (for example, com.example.app) that are allowed to use the AWS Location API key when making requests.
The bundle identifier (bundle ID) of an Apple iOS app, such as com.example.myapp, that is explicitly allowed to use the API key when the allow_apple_apps restriction is applied.

aws_location_apikey.restrictions.allow_r.text: List of allowed HTTP referer strings that can use this API key, restricting requests based on the originating website.
Specifies the list of AWS Location Service resource ARNs (or wildcard patterns) that this API key is allowed to access.

aws_location_apikey.tags.value.text: The value of a tag applied to the AWS Location Service API key, used to categorize, filter, and control access to the key via IAM policies and cost allocation.

aws_location_geofence_collection.arn.text: The unique Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to the geofence collection.

aws_location_geofence_collection.collect.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the geofence collection, which uniquely identifies it within AWS and is assigned by the service when the collection is created.
The name of the geofence collection, which must be unique within the AWS account and region and serves as the collection's identifier.

aws_location_geofence_collection.descrip.text: An optional descriptive text that provides a human-readable overview or purpose of the geofence collection in Amazon Location Service.

aws_location_geofence_collection.kms_key.text: The identifier (key ID or ARN) of the customer-managed AWS KMS key used to encrypt the geofence collection's data.

aws_location_geofence_collection.pricing.text: The pricing plan for the geofence collection, which determines the billing model (such as request-based usage) for geofencing operations performed on that collection.

aws_location_geofence_collection.tags.ke.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Location geofence collection, used to label the resource with custom metadata for identification, organization, and access control.

aws_location_map.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS Location Service map resource.

aws_location_map.configuration.text: Specifies the map style (e.g., VectorEsriStreets or RasterEsriImagery) used by the map resource.

aws_location_map.configuration.custom_la.text: Specifies the list of custom layers to include in the map configuration, allowing additional data layers to be displayed on top of the base map style.

aws_location_map.configuration.political.text: Sets the ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code that determines the political view of the map, controlling which country's rendering of borders, labels, and contested territories is used.

aws_location_map.configuration.style.text: Specifies the map style (e.g., 'VectorEsriStreets' or 'VectorHereExplore') that determines the visual appearance and data provider for the AWS Location map resource.

aws_location_map.map_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Location Service map, assigned by AWS when the map is created.

aws_location_map.map_name.text: A user-defined name for the Amazon Location Service map resource, used to identify it within the AWS account and in API calls.

aws_location_map.pricing_plan.text: Specifies the pricing plan for the map, such as RequestBasedUsage, which determines how the map's usage is billed.

aws_location_map.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Location Service map, used to identify and categorize the resource.

aws_location_map.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to an AWS Location Service map, used for cost allocation and resource identification.

aws_location_place_index.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the place index resource.

aws_location_place_index.data_source.text: The data provider (such as Esri, Here, or Grab) that supplies the location data for the place index and is required when creating the resource.

aws_location_place_index.data_source_con.text: Specifies the data storage options for the place index, including the intended use, such as single-use queries versus persistent storage of location data.
Sets the intended use of the place index to either SingleUse (geocode without storing results) or Storage (store results for later use), affecting how AWS Location Service handles query data.

aws_location_place_index.description.text: An optional user-supplied description of the place index, used to identify or note its purpose.

aws_location_place_index.index_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the place index resource.

aws_location_place_index.index_name.text: The custom name assigned to the place index, which must be unique within an AWS account and region and is used as the resource identifier in its ARN.

aws_location_place_index.pricing_plan.text: The pricing plan (RequestBasedUsage or MobileAssetTracking) for the place index, which determines the billing model for geocoding and reverse geocoding requests.

aws_location_place_index.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Amazon Location Service place index resource, used to identify and organize the resource.

aws_location_place_index.tags.value.text: The value for a tag assigned to the Amazon Location Service place index, used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_location_route_calculator.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the route calculator.

aws_location_route_calculator.calculator.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the route calculator in AWS.
The name of the route calculator, which is required, must be unique within your AWS account, and can only contain alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores, up to 100 characters.

aws_location_route_calculator.data_sourc.text: The data source for the route calculator, specifying the geospatial data provider (such as 'Esri' or 'Here') used to calculate routes.

aws_location_route_calculator.descriptio.text: An optional user-supplied description for the route calculator resource, used to identify or annotate it.

aws_location_route_calculator.pricing_pl.text: Defines the pricing plan for the route calculator, which determines the billing method (e.g., RequestBasedUsage, MobileAssetTracking, or MobileAssetManagement) for its usage.

aws_location_route_calculator.tags.key.text: The key of a tag (a user-defined label) applied to the AWS Location route calculator resource, used to categorize the resource for cost allocation and access control.

aws_location_route_calculator.tags.value.text: The value portion of a user-defined tag key-value pair attached to the Route Calculator, used for metadata management such as cost tracking and access control.

aws_location_tracker.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Location Service tracker, assigned by AWS when the tracker is created.

aws_location_tracker.description.text: The optional description string for the AWS Location Service tracker, allowing users to attach a human-readable note to the resource.

aws_location_tracker.event_bridge_enable.text: Specifies whether the tracker publishes geofence and location events to Amazon EventBridge for downstream processing.

aws_location_tracker.kms_key_enable_geos.text: When set to true, enables the tracker to encrypt and perform geospatial queries (e.g., search by polygon) using the specified AWS KMS key, rather than only simple positional updates.

aws_location_tracker.kms_key_id.text: The ID of an AWS KMS customer-managed key used to encrypt the tracker's location data; if not specified, an AWS-owned key encrypts the data.

aws_location_tracker.position_filtering.text: Specifies how incoming device position updates are filtered for storage, with valid values being TimeBased, DistanceBased, or AccuracyBased.

aws_location_tracker.pricing_plan.text: Specifies the pricing plan for the tracker, which determines the billing rate and feature set, with valid values such as 'RequestBasedUsage', 'MobileAssetTracking', and 'MobileAssetManagement'.

aws_location_tracker.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the Amazon Location Service tracker, used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_location_tracker.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag assigned to the AWS Location Service tracker, used to identify and organize tracker resources.

aws_location_tracker.tracker_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Location Service tracker, which uniquely identifies the tracker resource.

aws_location_tracker.tracker_name.text: A unique name for the tracker resource, used as its identifier and required when creating the tracker in Amazon Location Service.

aws_location_tracker_consumer.consumer_a.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the consumer resource (such as an EventBridge rule) that will receive location updates from the tracker.

aws_location_tracker_consumer.tracker_na.text: The name of the Amazon Location Service tracker that the consumer (such as a geofence collection) is associated with, linking the consumer to receive position updates from that tracker.

aws_logs_delivery.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to this CloudWatch Logs delivery, used to assign metadata for identifying, organizing, and managing the delivery resource, including cost allocation and access control.

aws_logs_delivery_destination.delivery_d.text: The IAM resource policy attached to the delivery destination, specifying which AWS accounts or services are granted permission to deliver log events to this destination.

aws_logs_delivery_destination.tags.key.text: This field specifies the key of a tag applied to the CloudWatch Logs delivery destination, allowing you to categorize and filter the resource for cost tracking and access management.

aws_logs_delivery_destination.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the CloudWatch Logs delivery destination, used for organizing, categorizing, and controlling access to the destination via IAM policies.

aws_logs_delivery_source.tags.value.text: Specifies the value of a tag attached to the CloudWatch Logs delivery source, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the resource via metadata such as cost allocation and access control.

aws_logs_destination.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this CloudWatch Logs destination, returned after creation and used to reference the destination in other AWS resources.

aws_logs_destination.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a tag to associate with the CloudWatch Logs destination, used to identify and organize the destination resource.

aws_logs_destination.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the CloudWatch Logs destination resource.

aws_logs_integration.resource_config.ope.text: This object defines the Amazon OpenSearch Service resource configuration for the CloudWatch Logs integration, including the target OpenSearch collection, application, index prefix, and time-to-live (TTL) for the imported log data.
The ARN of the OpenSearch Serverless application that this CloudWatch Logs integration delivers logs to.
Specifies the IAM principals (e.g., user ARNs, role ARNs) that are granted permission to view the OpenSearch dashboards provisioned for this logs integration.
The ARN of the IAM role that CloudWatch Logs assumes to access the configured OpenSearch data source for the integration.

The ARN of an AWS KMS customer managed key used to encrypt the Amazon OpenSearch Service domain or data source associated with this CloudWatch Logs integration, enabling customer-controlled encryption at rest.
Specifies the number of days that log data is retained in the associated OpenSearch index for this CloudWatch Logs integration.

aws_logs_log_anomaly_detector.anomaly_vi.text: Sets the number of days of historical log data that the anomaly detector uses as a baseline to establish normal behavior and detect deviations, effectively controlling how far back the detector looks for anomalies.

aws_logs_log_anomaly_detector.filter_pat.text: The CloudWatch Logs filter pattern that selects which log events in the associated log groups the anomaly detector analyzes, using standard filter pattern syntax.
