aws_logs_log_group.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this CloudWatch Logs log group.

aws_logs_log_group.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the CloudWatch log group, used for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization via AWS tagging best practices.

aws_logs_log_group.tags.value.text: Specifies the value portion of a tag assigned to the CloudWatch Logs log group, which can be used to categorize the log group for cost tracking and access control.

aws_logs_metric_filter.metric_transforma.text: Specifies the default value to assign to the CloudWatch metric when a log event matches the filter pattern but no metric value can be extracted from the log data.
Specifies the dimensions for the metric filter, where each dimension object contains a Key and Value that define a dimension on which to group the metric data.
The name/key of a dimension that is attached to the metric emitted by this CloudWatch Logs metric filter, used to segment the metric data.
The value of the dimension, which can be a literal string or a JSON path expression (e.g., $.eventType) used to extract a value from the log event and attach it as a dimension to the metric.
The name of the CloudWatch metric that the metric filter publishes matching log events to.
The CloudWatch namespace under which the extracted metric is published by this metric filter transformation.
The value to publish for the metric, which can be a literal number or a JSON expression (like '$.field') evaluated from the matched log event and sent to CloudWatch Metrics.
The unit of measure for the metric value (e.g., Seconds, Bytes, Count) that CloudWatch uses to interpret and display the metric's data, aligning with standard AWS unit enums.

aws_logs_query_definition.parameters.des.text: An optional human-readable description of the query definition, used to identify its purpose or contents.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.creation_time.text: The creation_time attribute is a read-only number representing the Unix epoch timestamp, in seconds, at which the scheduled query was created.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.description.text: An optional, user-defined text string that describes the purpose or details of the scheduled query, stored as metadata on the query definition in CloudWatch Logs Insights.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.destination_con.text: Specifies the destination configuration for delivering the results of the scheduled query, including the S3 bucket where the query results are written.
Defines the target S3 bucket (and optional prefix) where the results of the scheduled query will be delivered when the destination type is S3.
The destination name that CloudWatch Logs uses to construct the S3 path prefix for the scheduled query's result files, enabling distinct storage locations within the specified bucket.
The ARN of the IAM role that allows CloudWatch Logs to write the scheduled query's results to the specified S3 bucket.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.execution_role_.text: The ARN of the IAM role that CloudWatch Logs assumes to execute the scheduled query on your behalf.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.last_execution_.text: Contains the status of the most recent execution of the scheduled query (such as RUNNING, COMPLETE, or FAILED), as a computed read-only value maintained by CloudWatch Logs.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.last_triggered_.text: The Unix timestamp of the most recent automatic execution of the scheduled query by CloudWatch Logs.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.last_updated_ti.text: The timestamp, in Unix time milliseconds, when the scheduled query was last updated.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.log_group_ident.text: Specifies the list of log group names or ARNs that the scheduled query will run against.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.query_language.text: The query language used to parse and execute the scheduled query string, where `CWLI` denotes CloudWatch Logs Insights and `PPL` denotes OpenSearch Piped Processing Language.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.query_string.text: The CloudWatch Logs Insights query string that the scheduled query executes against the specified log groups to generate its results.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.schedule_end_ti.text: The optional Unix timestamp (in milliseconds) that defines when the scheduled query's recurrence should end, after which the query will no longer be automatically executed.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.schedule_expres.text: The rate or cron expression that defines how often the CloudWatch Logs scheduled query runs, e.g., 'rate(5 minutes)' or a cron expression.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.schedule_start_.text: The epoch time (in milliseconds) when the scheduled query's recurring execution schedule starts.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.scheduled_query.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the scheduled query, assigned by AWS when the query is created.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.start_time_offs.text: The number of seconds before a scheduled query execution that determines the start of the time window from which logs are queried, enabling retrieval of logs from a recent period relative to each run.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.state.text: Specifies whether the scheduled query is enabled or disabled (valid values are ENABLED and DISABLED), allowing you to pause or resume automatic execution of the query on its defined schedule.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.tags.key.text: For the AWS::Logs::ScheduledQuery resource, this field is the key of a user-defined tag attached to the scheduled query, which can be used for cost allocation and access control.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.tags.value.text: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the CloudWatch Logs scheduled query, used for organizing, identifying, and tracking costs of the resource.

aws_logs_scheduled_query.timezone.text: The IANA timezone (such as 'UTC' or 'America/New_York') used to evaluate the schedule's cron expression for the scheduled query; if omitted, UTC is assumed.

aws_logs_transformer.transformer_config..text: Defines a set of key-value pairs to append to each log event processed by the transformer, where each entry specifies a key and a value to add to the log record.
The entries list defines the key-value pairs to add to log events, where each entry specifies a key and its value.
The name of the new field that CloudWatch Logs Transformer adds to the log event, serving as the key in the key-value pair inserted by the add_keys operation.

For the add_keys processor of a CloudWatch Logs transformer, this boolean specifies whether to overwrite the value of a key if it already exists in a log event (true) or leave the original value unchanged (false).
The value to assign to the new key when the add_keys transformation is applied to a log event in the AWS::Logs::Transformer resource.

Defines the copyValue transformation for a CloudWatch Logs Transformer, which copies the value from a specified source field to a target field in each log event via a list of entries containing source and target field names.
Defines copy operations that duplicate a value from a source field to a target field within each log event, with each entry specifying the source and target keys.
Specifies whether to overwrite the destination field with the copied value if that destination field already exists in the log event.
The name of the source field in the log event whose value is copied to the target field by the copy_value transformation.
Specifies the destination field name in the log event where the value from the source key is copied by the copyValue transformation processor.

The 'csv' property within the transformer configuration defines a processor that parses comma-separated values from a log event field, with options for the source field, delimiter, quote character, column names, and handling of missing or trailing fields.
Provides the ordered list of column names that the CSV transformation processor uses to map comma-separated values extracted from each log event.
The delimiter character used by the CSV transformer to separate fields in the log message for parsing.
Specifies the character used to enclose quoted fields in the CSV input, so that delimiters within quoted fields are treated as literal characters rather than separators.
The name of the source field in the log event that contains the CSV-formatted data to be parsed into separate fields by the CSV transformer.
Configures the date-time converter processor, which transforms a datetime field in a log event by specifying a source field, a destination field, and the target output format.
Specifies the locale (e.g., en-US) used by the date-time converter when parsing or formatting date/time values, affecting language-specific month/day names and date format conventions.
The list of date/time patterns that the DateTimeConverter processor attempts to match against the source field's value in order to parse it before converting to the specified target format.
The source field specifies the name of the log event field that contains the datetime value to be converted by the date-time converter processor.

Specifies the time zone (e.g., 'UTC', 'America/New_York') of the source timestamp, which the DateTimeConverter processor uses to interpret and convert the log record's time before applying the target format.
Specifies the log event field name where the date/time converter writes the converted date/time value, using the configured target format.
Defines the target strftime-compatible format (e.g., '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') that the dateTimeConverter processor uses to rewrite the value of the source datetime field in transformed log events.
Specifies the IANA time zone (e.g., 'America/New_York') to which the source date/time value is converted when setting the target field.
Specifies the log event keys to be removed by the deleteKeys processor within the AWS Logs transformer configuration.
The list of log event field names to delete when the transformer's deleteKeys operation is applied.
Defines a Grok-based transformation processor that uses user-supplied Grok patterns to parse and extract structured fields from a log event's source field.
The grok pattern string used to match and extract named fields from the log event, e.g. '%{TIMESTAMP_ISO8601:timestamp} %{LOGLEVEL:level} %{GREEDYDATA:message}'.
Specifies the source log event field (e.g., @message or a custom field name) that the grok pattern is applied to for extracting structured data.
Configures the list-to-map processor, which converts a source list field into a map by extracting key-value pairs from each element.
When true, the list_to_map processor flattens the resulting map so that each key maps directly to the value field of the source object, rather than to the entire object.

Specifies how the list-to-map transformation handles multiple list elements that share the same key, with valid values 'first' (use the first value), 'last' (use the last value), or 'all' (collect all values into an array).
The name of the attribute in each source list element that is used as the map key when transforming a list of objects into a map.
The name of the log event field that contains the list of strings to be converted into a map by the ListToMap processor.
The name of the destination field where the map created from the source list is written.
Specifies the field in each list item whose value is used as the value in the map produced by the list-to-map transformation.
Configures the lowerCaseString processor, which lowercases the values of specified keys in log events.
Specifies which fields (keys) in the log event should have their string values converted to lowercase by the lower_case_string transformation.

In the AWS::Logs::Transformer resource, this field defines the key-rename mappings for the moveKeys processor, where each mapping specifies a source key and a target key to rename fields in incoming log events.
Specifies the list of move-key entries, where each entry defines a source and target key to rename fields in a log event as part of the moveKeys processor.
Whether to overwrite the target key in the log event if it already exists when moving the source key to the target key.
The source key path in the log event whose value is moved to the target key by the MoveKeys processor.
The destination key path to which the value of the source key is moved within the log event.
This field configures the CloudFront access log parser, where you specify the source log field to parse (and optionally a destination field for the extracted structured data).
The source field specifies the name of the log event attribute that contains the raw CloudFront access log line to be parsed by the parse_cloudfront processor.
Configures the parse JSON processor to parse a specified log message field as JSON and add the resulting key-value pairs to the log event.

In the `parseJson` processor, `destination` is the output field path where the JSON-decoded content of the source field is placed; if omitted, the parsed fields are merged directly into the root of the log event.
Specifies the name of the source field within the log event whose JSON string value is parsed by the ParseJSON processor.

This field configures the `parse_key_value` processor within the CloudFormation `AWS::Logs::Transformer` resource, defining how key-value pairs are extracted from log messages by specifying parameters such as `source`, `destination`, `delimiter`, `key_value_delimiter`, and `key_prefix`.
Specifies the destination field in the log event where the parsed key-value pairs are written, such as a top-level key or a nested path.
Specifies the delimiter used to separate key-value pairs (fields) in the source log event when applying the parse_key_value transformation, for example a space or comma.
When set, prepends this string to every key parsed from the log message by the parse_key_value processor, so that the generated CloudWatch Logs fields are namespaced under the specified prefix.
Sets the specific character (such as '=' or ':') that separates a key from its value when the parse-key-value processor splits a log entry into key-value pairs.
Sets the string value to substitute for a key when the input text does not contain a matching value delimiter, so the key is still present with this fallback value.
When parsing key-value pairs from the log message, if this flag is true the parser replaces the value of any existing target key with the newly parsed value, otherwise it keeps the existing value.
Specifies the name of the source field in a log event that contains a key-value pair string, which the transformer parses into individual fields according to the configured delimiters.

This object configures the Postgres log parser within the CloudWatch Logs Transformer, specifying the source field that contains the raw PostgreSQL log message so that structured data is extracted from it.
The name of the log event field containing the PostgreSQL query text that the parse_postgres transformer will parse.
Configures the transformation that parses Route 53 DNS query log events, extracting structured fields such as domain name, query type, and response code from the raw log line.
Specifies the key (field) in each incoming log event that contains the Route 53 DNS query log text to be parsed by this transformer processor.
Specifies the configuration for the parse-to-OCSF processor within the transformer, which converts incoming log events to the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) format.
Specifies the OCSF event source (such as 'cloudtrail' or 'vpcflow') that the ParseToOCSF transformer uses to interpret and map the log record into the OCSF schema.
Specifies the version of the OCSF (Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework) mapping to use when converting the log event to OCSF format.
Specifies the version of the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) to use when converting log records to OCSF format.
Specifies the name of the source field in the incoming log event that contains the data to be parsed and converted into OCSF format.
Defines the ParseVpc processor settings for the transformer, including the source field to parse VPC flow log data from and the target field to write the parsed structured fields to.
The name of the source field in the log event containing the VPC flow log record to parse; if omitted, defaults to the `message` field.
Configures a processor that parses AWS WAF log entries into a structured format, extracting fields such as the rule, action, and request details from the raw JSON logs.
Specifies the name of the log event key that contains the raw AWS WAF log string to be parsed by the parse_waf processor.
Specifies a mapping of original log field names to their replacement names, used to rename fields during log transformation.
Defines a list of key rename mappings, where each mapping specifies an existing log event key and the new key name to replace it with during transformation.
The original key name in the log event that will be renamed to the value of this entry in the renameKeys transformation.

If true, the transformer overwrites the target key's value when renaming a source key to a key name that already exists; if false, the rename does not overwrite the existing key and leaves the original key unchanged.
Specifies the new name to assign to a log event key in a renameKeys entry of the CloudWatch Logs transformer, replacing the original key name.
Configures a split-string processor that divides a specified string field into an array of substrings using a delimiter.
The list of split operations, where each entry defines the source field to split, the delimiter to use, and the target field names to receive the resulting substrings.
The delimiter string used by the splitString processor to divide the source log field's value into separate parts.
Specifies the field in the log event whose string value is segmented into multiple substrings using the configured delimiter for the splitString processor.

The substitute_string object configures a string substitution processor that replaces occurrences of a specified source pattern (regular expression) in the log event message with the provided replacement string.

The list of source-target string pairs, where each entry specifies a source pattern to find in the log message and the replacement target string to substitute in its place when this SubstituteString transformation runs.
Specifies the literal substring within the log event that the substituteString processor will replace with the corresponding 'to' string.
The literal string to find within the log event that will be replaced by the corresponding target string in this substitute_string entry.
The replacement string that is substituted for every occurrence of the entry's source string in the log event during this transformer's substitute_string processing.
This object configures the TrimString processor, which trims leading and trailing whitespace from the values of the specified fields in the log event.
The with_keys property under trim_string specifies the list of log event keys whose string values should have leading and trailing whitespace trimmed.

Specifies the type converter processor that changes the data type of selected fields in CloudWatch Logs events to a target type (such as integer, double, boolean, or string) for normalization and downstream processing.
Specifies the list of type conversion entries for the typeConverter processor, where each entry defines a log field name and the target data type to convert that field to.
The key is the name of the log event field that the type converter processes, telling the transformer which field's value should be converted to the target type.
The target data type to which the field value is converted, such as integer, double, boolean, or string.
The upper_case_string processor in the transformer config converts the string values of the specified log event fields to uppercase.
Specifies the list of log event keys whose values are converted to uppercase in the upper-case-string transformer processor.

aws_lookout_equipment_inference_schedule.text: The name of the S3 bucket that contains the sensor or equipment data used as input for the inference scheduler.
The S3 key prefix under the input bucket that identifies the sensor data files used by the inference scheduler for running model inferences.
The name of the S3 bucket where the inference scheduler outputs its inference results and monitoring data.
The S3 key prefix (folder path) under the specified S3 bucket where the inference scheduler stores its inference output files (results).
The key portion of a tag attached to the inference scheduler.
The value portion of a tag key-value pair that can be attached to the Lookout for Equipment inference scheduler, used for custom metadata, resource grouping, and cost allocation.

aws_lookout_vision_project.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lookout for Vision project, which uniquely identifies the project in AWS.

aws_m2_application.application_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the AWS Mainframe Modernization (M2) application, assigned by AWS and used to reference the application in other services, IAM policies, and monitoring tools.

aws_m2_application.application_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the Mainframe Modernization application when it is created.

aws_m2_application.definition.text: Contains the application definition for the AWS M2 mainframe modernization application, supplying the code or configuration either inline or via an S3 location.

aws_m2_application.definition.content.text: The inline application definition content, specified as a string, that contains the application's definition in a format like JSON or YAML to be used for the M2 application.

aws_m2_application.definition.s3_locatio.text: The S3 URI (e.g., s3://bucket/key) that points to the application definition file stored in Amazon S3, used to specify the application definition when it is not provided inline.

aws_m2_application.description.text: This optional string supplies a customer-defined description for the AWS Mainframe Modernization application, used to identify the application's purpose.

aws_m2_application.engine_type.text: The engine type for the application, which determines the runtime environment (either Micro Focus or Blu Age).

aws_m2_application.name.text: Specifies the required name for the AWS Mainframe Modernization application, which must be unique across all applications in your AWS account and Region and serves as the human-readable identifier in the M2 console and API.

aws_m2_application.role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that the application assumes to access other AWS services and resources needed for its operation.

aws_m2_application.tags.text: Specifies a map of key-value tags to attach to the AWS Mainframe Modernization application for management and categorization.

aws_m2_environment.high_availability_con.text: The desired number of instances to run in the high availability configuration of the AWS Mainframe Modernization (M2) environment.

aws_m2_environment.network_type.text: Specifies the network type for the environment, either 'VPC' for a customer-managed virtual private cloud or 'EDGE' to use the AWS Mainframe Modernization managed network without a VPC.

aws_macie_allow_list.tags.key.text: The key of a tag that can be applied to this Amazon Macie allow list resource for organizing and identifying it.

aws_macie_findings_filter.action.text: Specifies the action to take on findings that match the filter's criteria, with allowed values ARCHIVE to archive (suppress) the findings or NOOP to not change them, in AWS Macie.

aws_macie_findings_filter.finding_criter.text: Defines the matching conditions, evaluated against finding attributes such as severity, type, or other properties, that determine which findings are included in the filter.

aws_macie_findings_filter.tags.key.text: Specifies the key of a tag that you can attach to the findings filter to help identify and organize it in AWS Macie.

aws_managed_blockchain_accessor.accessor.text: Specifies the accessor type (BILLING_TOKEN, ETHEREUM_GOERLI, or ETHEREUM_MAINNET), which determines whether the accessor is a billing token or grants access to a specific Ethereum network.

aws_managed_blockchain_accessor.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Managed Blockchain accessor.

aws_managed_blockchain_accessor.billing_.text: The unique billing token assigned by AWS to the accessor, used to identify the accessor for metering and billing when interacting with Amazon Managed Blockchain.

aws_managed_blockchain_accessor.creation.text: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) at which the AWS Managed Blockchain accessor was created, automatically set by the service and returned as a computed value.

aws_managed_blockchain_accessor.id.text: The unique identifier assigned to the Managed Blockchain accessor by AWS.

aws_managed_blockchain_accessor.network_.text: Specifies the Ethereum network type that the Managed Blockchain accessor connects to, such as ETHEREUM_MAINNET for the public mainnet or ETHEREUM_TESTNET for a public test network.

aws_managed_blockchain_accessor.status.text: The current lifecycle status of the Managed Blockchain accessor, indicating whether it is available for use (AVAILABLE) or in a deletion state (PENDING_DELETION, DELETED).

aws_managed_blockchain_accessor.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the Managed Blockchain Accessor, used to organize, identify, and manage accessor resources.

aws_managed_blockchain_member.invitation.text: The unique identifier of the invitation that was sent to this AWS account to join the Managed Blockchain network, required when adding a member to an existing network via an invitation.

aws_managed_blockchain_member.member_con.text: Specifies the member's configuration, including its name, description, and framework-specific settings such as admin credentials for Hyperledger Fabric.
An optional description of the Managed Blockchain member, which is attached to the member's configuration for identification purposes.
Specifies the Hyperledger Fabric-specific configuration for this Managed Blockchain member, including the administrator credentials (username and password) for the peer node.
This object configures Hyperledger Fabric settings for the member, including the admin username and password used to access the member's Fabric CA.
The password for the Hyperledger Fabric admin user associated with this member, used to authenticate to the Managed Blockchain network's Fabric client.
The admin username for the Hyperledger Fabric certificate authority (CA) of the member, used to authenticate as the Fabric CA admin.
The user-defined name of the member, required in the member configuration, used to identify and distinguish the member within the Managed Blockchain network.

aws_managed_blockchain_member.member_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the Managed Blockchain member when it is created.

aws_managed_blockchain_member.network_co.text: Defines the configuration for creating a new Hyperledger Fabric network when this member is the first member of a new network, including the network name, framework version, and voting policy.
Provides an optional description for the Managed Blockchain network that is created when this member creates a new network as part of its network configuration.
The blockchain framework (e.g., HYPERLEDGER_FABRIC or ETHEREUM) that defines the network protocol when creating a new network via the first member.
Specifies the version of the blockchain framework (e.g., Hyperledger Fabric 1.4) that the network configuration uses for the member's network.
The name of the Hyperledger Fabric network to be created when the member creates a new network, as specified in the network configuration.
Specifies the framework-specific settings for the blockchain network that the member joins, such as the Hyperledger Fabric edition (STARTER or STANDARD) within the network configuration.

Specifies the Hyperledger Fabric configuration for the blockchain network, including the Edition property that determines whether the network runs on the STARTER or STANDARD edition for the member's network.
The Hyperledger Fabric network edition (STARTER or STANDARD) that determines the allowed number of peer nodes and ordering service nodes for the member's network.
Defines the voting rules for the network, including the approval threshold and proposal duration, which govern decisions on membership proposals.
Defines the approval threshold rules (such as proposal duration, threshold comparator, and threshold percentage) that govern how Hyperledger Fabric proposals are approved in the member's network.
The maximum duration in hours that a proposal remains open for voting before it expires in the Managed Blockchain network's voting policy.
Specifies the comparator used to compare the voting threshold against the number of approvals, such as GREATER_THAN or GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO.
Specifies the percentage of all voting outcomes that must be 'yes' for a proposal to be approved, used by the approval threshold policy in the Managed Blockchain network's voting policy.

aws_managed_blockchain_member.network_id.text: The unique identifier of the Managed Blockchain network to which this member belongs.

aws_managed_blockchain_node.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Managed Blockchain node.

aws_managed_blockchain_node.member_id.text: The unique identifier of the Managed Blockchain member to which this node belongs.

aws_managed_blockchain_node.network_id.text: The unique identifier of the Managed Blockchain network to which the node belongs.

aws_managed_blockchain_node.node_configu.text: Defines the operational parameters of the Managed Blockchain node, including the required EC2 instance type and optional Availability Zone and log publishing configuration.
Specifies the Availability Zone in which the Amazon Managed Blockchain node is created.
The EC2 instance type (e.g., bc.t3.large) that determines the compute, memory, and storage capacity allocated to the Managed Blockchain node.

aws_managed_blockchain_node.node_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this Managed Blockchain node.

aws_media_connect_bridge.bridge_state.text: The current lifecycle state of the MediaConnect bridge (e.g., ACTIVE, STANDBY, or DELETING), as reported by AWS after the bridge is created or updated.

aws_media_connect_bridge.egress_gateway_.text: Defines the egress gateway bridge settings for an AWS Elemental MediaConnect bridge, including the gateway instance ID and optional maximum bitrate for transmitting media flows to a remote network.

aws_media_connect_bridge.ingress_gateway.text: The 'ingress_gateway_bridge' object configures the ingress gateway bridge settings for the MediaConnect bridge, including the maximum number of outputs it can support.

aws_media_connect_bridge.outputs.network.text: Configures the destination IP address, port, protocol, TTL, and other network parameters for sending the bridge's media output over the network.
The destination IP address to which this bridge's network output sends media.
The name assigned to a network output of the AWS Elemental MediaConnect bridge, used to identify that output within the bridge.
Specifies the name of the network that this bridge network output uses, identifying the destination network for the output.
The destination port number on which the MediaConnect bridge network output sends media to the remote device.
Specifies the transport protocol used by the bridge's network output, such as RTP, RTP-FEC, or UDP, for sending media over IP.
The Time-to-Live (TTL) value for multicast packets sent from the network output, limiting the number of network hops the traffic can traverse.

aws_media_connect_bridge.source_failover.text: Specifies the failover mode of the bridge source, using FAILOVER to enable automatic failover to a redundant source or DEFAULT for standard behavior.
Indicates whether automatic failover is enabled or disabled for the bridge's source, with valid values ENABLED or DISABLED.

aws_media_connect_bridge.sources.flow_so.text: FlowSource is an object that configures the bridge source to use an existing MediaConnect flow as its source, specifying the flow ARN and the VPC interface attachment for the flow.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the MediaConnect flow that serves as the source of the bridge source.
Specifies the VPC interface attachment settings, including the name of the VPC interface, for this flow source of the AWS Elemental MediaConnect bridge.
The name of the VPC interface on the source MediaConnect flow that the bridge flow source attaches to for network connectivity.
Specifies the name assigned to the flow source of the AWS MediaConnect bridge, used to identify the source within the bridge's source configuration.

aws_media_connect_bridge.sources.network.text: Configures the network source for a source in a MediaConnect bridge, defining the multicast IP address, port, and protocol that the bridge listens on to ingest video from the network.
The multicast IP address of the network source that the MediaConnect bridge subscribes to.
Configures the multicast source settings for the network source on the bridge, specifying the multicast IP address and port from which the bridge receives media.
The IP address of the multicast source from which the MediaConnect bridge receives content, used in the multicast source settings of a network source.
A user-defined name that identifies this network source within the bridge's sources configuration in AWS Elemental MediaConnect.
The name of the network where the bridge source is located, used to identify the network that provides the content for this MediaConnect bridge source.
The network port on the bridge's source that receives the incoming media stream from an on-premises sender.
Specifies the transport protocol used for the network source, which can be either RTP or RTP-FEC, indicating how the incoming media stream is delivered.

aws_media_connect_bridge_source.network_.text: Specifies the transport protocol (RTP or RTP-FEC) used by the network source to ingest the media stream into the bridge.

aws_media_connect_flow.encoding_config.text: Configures the video encoding algorithm (such as H.264) and its specific parameters (resolution, bitrate, frame rate) applied to the MediaConnect flow's video stream for output.

aws_media_connect_flow.media_streams.att.text: The attributes object within a media stream specifies its encoding parameters, such as video resolution, frame rate, and bitrate, which control how the stream is encoded and transmitted.
The FMTP (Format Parameters) for this media stream, containing codec- or transport-specific parameters (as defined in SDP) that describe the stream's encoding characteristics.
The channel_order FMTP parameter defines the ordering of audio channels in the media stream, such as 'L,R' for stereo or 'L,R,C,LFE' for 5.1 surround.
The colorimetry FMTP parameter of the media stream, which specifies the color space standard (e.g., BT.601, BT.709) for the video content.

Sets the exact video frame rate (in frames per second) for this media stream, which is included in the FMTP (Format-Specific Parameters) configuration that MediaConnect uses to define the stream's format.
The pixel aspect ratio (PAR) for the media stream, expressed as a string ratio such as '16:9'.
Specifies the horizontal and vertical RTP video range (such as 'full' or 'narrow') for the FMTP attributes of this media stream.
Specifies the scan mode (for example, progressive or interlaced) of the video in the media stream's FMTP parameters for an AWS MediaConnect flow.
Specifies the language code of the media stream (e.g., 'en-US') in RFC 5646 format, used to identify the language of the audio content.

aws_media_connect_flow.media_streams.clo.text: The RTP clock rate (in Hz) for the media stream, which MediaConnect uses to timestamp and synchronize packets for that stream (e.g., 48000 for audio, 90000 for video).

aws_media_connect_flow.media_streams.des.text: A user-defined description for the media stream, used to identify it within an AWS Elemental MediaConnect flow.

aws_media_connect_flow.media_streams.fmt.text: The RTP payload type number (0-127) that identifies the format of the media stream, such as the codec and sampling rate for audio or video.

aws_media_connect_flow.media_streams.med.text: The unique numeric identifier for the media stream within the MediaConnect flow, used to reference the media stream when configuring sources and outputs.
A unique name for the media stream within the MediaConnect flow, used to identify the stream when associating it with outputs or entitlements.
The type of the media stream, such as video, audio, ancillary-data, or combination, which determines how the stream is handled in the flow.

aws_media_connect_flow.media_streams.vid.text: The video format of the media stream, specifying the video resolution and frame rate (e.g., '1080p') for the flow's video transport.

aws_media_connect_flow.ndi_config.ndi_di.text: The IP address or hostname of the NDI Discovery Server used by the flow to discover NDI sources on the network.
The TCP port on which the NDI discovery server listens, used to discover NDI sources for the MediaConnect flow.

Specifies the VPC interface adapter name that the NDI discovery server uses to communicate within a virtual private cloud, enabling the MediaConnect flow to connect to NDI sources on that private network.

aws_media_connect_flow.ndi_config.ndi_st.text: Specifies whether the NDI (Network Device Interface) output configuration is enabled or disabled for the flow, using values ENABLED or DISABLED.

aws_media_connect_flow.source.media_stre.text: The encoding name (e.g., 'raw', 'aac', or 'nal') assigned to the media stream within the flow source's media stream source configuration.
Specifies the input port and network interface for each media stream in the flow's source, enabling the flow to receive each media stream on a dedicated port and interface.
The port number on the referenced interface where this input configuration receives the media stream from the upstream source.
This object identifies the VPC interface used for this input configuration by the flow's VPC interface name, which must correspond to a VPC interface attached to the flow's source.
The name of the network interface on the source device that receives the media stream for this input configuration.
Specifies the friendly name of the media stream that this source configuration applies to, matching the media stream name that the upstream source encodes.

aws_media_connect_flow.source.ndi_source.text: This object configures the NDI (Network Device Interface) source for the flow, specifying the listening port and NDI tier (e.g., NDI or NDI|HX) that MediaConnect uses to receive the stream from an NDI device.
Specifies the NDI source name that identifies the incoming NDI stream to be used as the source for the MediaConnect flow.

aws_media_connect_flow.source.router_int.text: Indicates the current integration state of the source with an AWS Elemental MediaConnect router, such as ENABLED or DISABLED.
Specifies the AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the encryption key used for decrypting the incoming media source's transit integration.
The ARN of an IAM role that AWS Elemental MediaConnect assumes to access the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the transit encryption key for decryption of the source flow.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the decryption key for decrypting transit traffic on this MediaConnect flow source.
The type of encryption key (for example, 'static_key') used by the MediaConnect flow to decrypt the transit stream arriving from the router integration source.

aws_media_connect_flow.source.tags.value.text: This field specifies the value portion of a tag applied to a source of an AWS Elemental MediaConnect flow, used to attach metadata such as environment or project names to the source for identification and cost allocation.

aws_media_connect_flow.source_failover_c.text: Determines whether automatic source failover is enabled for the MediaConnect flow; set to 'ENABLED' to allow failover to the secondary source, or 'DISABLED' to turn it off.

aws_media_connect_flow.source_monitoring.text: Configures silent audio monitoring for the MediaConnect flow's source, including the duration threshold that triggers a silence alert and whether detection is enabled.
Controls whether the flow's source detects silent audio; set to ENABLED to activate monitoring or DISABLED to turn it off.
The duration (in seconds) that incoming audio must remain silent before MediaConnect triggers a silent audio monitoring alarm.
Indicates whether black frame detection is enabled for the MediaConnect source's video monitoring, with allowed values ENABLED or DISABLED.
The threshold_seconds value determines the minimum continuous duration of black frames in the video stream that must be detected before the source monitoring alert is triggered.

Specifies the detection settings for frozen frames in the video stream, including whether the detection is enabled and the maximum duration (in milliseconds) that a frame can remain unchanged before it is considered frozen.
The state of frozen frame detection in the source's video monitoring settings, specifying whether the detection of frozen video frames is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED).
Specifies the number of seconds a video frame must remain frozen before MediaConnect considers the source frozen and raises an alarm.

aws_media_connect_flow.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to associate with the MediaConnect flow, used to organize and identify the flow resource for cost allocation and access management.

aws_media_connect_flow.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the MediaConnect flow, used for identifying, organizing, and managing the flow via AWS cost allocation and resource-level access controls.

aws_media_connect_flow.vpc_interfaces.na.text: The name of the VPC interface, which identifies it within the flow.

aws_media_connect_flow.vpc_interfaces.ne.text: Specifies the network interface type for the VPC interface, either 'EIP' to allocate an Elastic IP address or 'ANY' for a standard network interface without a public IP.

aws_media_connect_flow.vpc_interfaces.ro.text: ARN of the IAM role that MediaConnect assumes to create and manage the elastic network interface in the VPC for this flow's VPC interface.

aws_media_connect_flow.vpc_interfaces.se.text: The list of security group IDs that are associated with the VPC interface used by the MediaConnect flow.

aws_media_connect_flow.vpc_interfaces.su.text: The ID of the subnet in which the VPC interface is created.

aws_media_connect_flow.vpc_interfaces.ta.text: The key of a tag applied to a VPC interface within an AWS MediaConnect flow, used to attach identifying or organizational metadata to that interface.

aws_media_connect_flow_entitlement.tags..text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Elemental MediaConnect flow entitlement, used to organize, identify, and optionally drive cost allocation for this entitlement resource.
The value part of a tag key-value pair associated with this AWS Elemental MediaConnect flow entitlement, used for metadata, cost allocation, and resource management.

aws_media_connect_flow_output.media_stre.text: A list of destination configurations that specify the IP address and port for sending a media stream, along with protocol-specific settings such as RTP or UDP parameters.
The IP address to which the MediaConnect flow delivers the media stream output for this destination configuration.
Specifies the destination port number to which the media stream output sends data for this destination configuration.
Specifies the VPC interface configuration, including the interface name and type, that AWS Elemental MediaConnect uses to route the output media stream to its destination.
The name of the VPC interface on the MediaConnect flow used as the egress interface for this destination configuration, which must match a VPC interface already defined on the flow.
Specifies the encoding name for the media stream output, such as 'jxsv' or 'raw', which identifies the compression scheme used for the stream.
Configures the encoding parameters for a media stream output, such as the compression factor and encoder profile applied to the stream.

Controls the amount of compression applied to the video stream for this media stream output configuration's encoding parameters, with lower values generally yielding higher quality and higher values increasing compression.
Specifies the encoder profile (such as high, medium, or quality) that MediaConnect uses to encode the media stream for this flow output.
The name of the media stream that this output configuration sends to, matching the media stream name defined in the flow's media stream settings.

aws_media_connect_flow_output.router_int.text: When set to true, AWS Elemental MediaConnect automatically generates and manages an encryption key for the router integration's transit encryption, and you do not need to specify a key ARN; when false, you must provide an explicit key ARN in the surrounding encryption key configuration.

Defines the configuration for referencing an encryption key stored in AWS Secrets Manager, typically including the secret's ARN or name and the IAM role that grants MediaConnect permission to retrieve it.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Elemental MediaConnect assumes to access the encryption key stored in AWS Secrets Manager for transit encryption of this router integration.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that holds the static encryption key configured for transit encryption on this MediaConnect flow output when routed through a router integration.
Defines the type of encryption key used for the router integration transit encryption, with valid values such as `static-key` and `srt-password`.

aws_media_connect_flow_output.tags.value.text: The value portion of a user-defined tag associated with this AWS Elemental MediaConnect flow output, used for cost allocation, access control, or organizational metadata.

aws_media_connect_flow_source.tags.value.text: Specifies the value portion of a user-defined tag attached to the MediaConnect flow source for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_media_connect_flow_vpc_interface.tag.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Elemental MediaConnect flow VPC interface, used to organize and identify the resource.
The value of a tag assigned to the MediaConnect flow VPC interface, used for resource metadata and categorization.

aws_media_connect_gateway.networks.cidr_.text: CIDR block of the subnet where the gateway's network interface resides, used to define the network's IP address range.

aws_media_connect_gateway.networks.name.text: The name of the network interface, used to identify it within the gateway.

aws_media_connect_router_input.arn.text: This computed, read-only field contains the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that AWS assigns to uniquely identify the MediaConnect router input, used for cross-service references and IAM authorization.

aws_media_connect_router_input.configura.text: The failover configuration for the MediaConnect router input, defining whether the input participates in automatic failover and its priority relative to other router inputs.

Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the elastic network interface (ENI) that the MediaConnect router input uses for failover, allowing the input to switch to this interface if the primary network interface becomes unavailable.

The zero-based index of the source input that serves as the primary source in the failover configuration, ensuring that traffic is routed to this source first and to the secondary source if the primary becomes unavailable.
The port number used for RIST protocol communication in the failover protocol configuration of the MediaConnect router input.
The recovery latency in milliseconds for the RIST protocol in the failover configuration of the router input.
The network port number that the router input uses to receive RTP media traffic when failover is triggered under the rtp protocol configuration.
Specifies the algorithm and AWS KMS key or Secrets Manager secret ARN used to decrypt the SRT stream when the router input acts as an SRT caller under this failover protocol configuration.
Defines the encryption key used to decrypt incoming SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) traffic for an SRT caller protocol within the router input's failover decryption configuration.

The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Elemental MediaConnect assumes to access the AWS KMS key used for decrypting the SRT caller stream, paired with the secret ARN in the same encryption key configuration.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that holds the encryption key used to decrypt the incoming SRT caller stream when decryption is enabled.
Sets the minimum acceptable latency in milliseconds for the SRT caller protocol used in the failover configuration of the AWS MediaConnect router input.
The source IP address used by the SRT caller in the failover protocol configuration for a MediaConnect router input.
The source_port specifies the network port on the SRT source endpoint that the SRT caller in the router input's failover configuration connects to.
The SRT stream ID used by the SRT caller in this failover configuration to identify the media stream input to the router.

The decryption configuration for the SRT listener under failover, defining how encrypted SRT traffic is decrypted by specifying the encryption algorithm and the source of the decryption key (such as a static key or AWS Secrets Manager secret).
The ARN of the IAM role that MediaConnect assumes to access the AWS KMS key used for decrypting the incoming SRT listener stream.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that holds the encryption key used to decrypt the SRT listener's incoming traffic in this failover configuration.

Specifies the minimum latency in milliseconds for the SRT listener used in the router input's failover protocol configuration, which sets the lower bound for the playback buffer to smooth network jitter and packet retransmission.
The UDP port number on which the SRT listener accepts incoming SRT connections for this failover configuration.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Elemental MediaConnect flow output that serves as the media source for this router input.
Defines the encryption key parameters, such as the key ARN, role, and algorithm, used to decrypt the source media arriving over the transit-encrypted MediaConnect flow.
The ARN of the IAM role that MediaConnect assumes to access the AWS Secrets Manager secret used to decrypt the source's transit encryption.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the encryption key used to decrypt the source transit stream in the MediaConnect flow configuration.
Specifies the type of encryption key used to decrypt the source transit content in the MediaConnect flow, such as 'static-key' or 'speke'.
The ARN of the AWS Elemental MediaLive channel referenced by the media_live_channel configuration block of this MediaConnect router input.
Specifies the name of the MediaLive channel output that this router input is configured to receive media from.
This object configures the encryption key settings (such as the key ARN and algorithm) used to decrypt the transit stream coming from the AWS MediaLive channel for this router input.
Specifies the AWS Secrets Manager secret that holds the decryption key used to decrypt source transit encryption on the attached MediaLive channel.
The ARN of the IAM role that MediaConnect assumes to access the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the decryption key for source transit.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the encryption key used to decrypt the media source when using source transit decryption for the MediaLive channel input.
Specifies the type of encryption key used to decrypt the transit-encrypted source from the linked MediaLive channel, with typical values being a static key or an SRT key.

Specifies the number of milliseconds that the MediaConnect router input waits for a merged input stream to recover after a loss before it switches to the secondary/failover stream, controlling the smoothness of the transition.
Specifies the list of protocol configurations that are merged together to allow the router input to accept and combine multiple media streams from different protocols into a single logical input.
Configuration object that sets the RIST (Reliable Internet Stream Transport) parameters for a protocol configuration within the merge settings of the MediaConnect router input.
The network port number on which the RIST protocol listens to receive incoming media streams for this MediaConnect router input within the merge configuration.
Defines the recovery latency in milliseconds for the RIST protocol when this input is merged, which determines how long the receiver buffers data to recover from packet loss.
Configuration object for the RTP transport protocol settings used by a MediaConnect router input when merging multiple incoming media streams, defining how RTP packets are received and processed.
The UDP port on which the router input accepts incoming RTP media when configured with the RTP protocol under the merge input configuration.
The ARN of the network interface used by the standard configuration of this MediaConnect router input to receive media traffic.
Specifies the protocol-specific settings (such as transport protocol and network parameters) for the standard input of a MediaConnect router.
Specifies the RIST (Reliable Internet Stream Transport) protocol settings for this standard router input, including transport parameters such as the listening port and RIST profile.
The UDP port number on which the RIST protocol endpoint of the MediaConnect router input listens for incoming media traffic.
Specifies the recovery latency in milliseconds for the RIST protocol configuration of the MediaConnect router input.
The destination UDP port number that this MediaConnect router input uses to receive RTP packets.

This object specifies how incoming SRT traffic to the MediaConnect router input is decrypted, including the decryption algorithm and the ARN of the KMS key or Secrets Manager secret used to derive the decryption key.
Specifies the encryption key used to decrypt the SRT caller stream within the decryption configuration of a MediaConnect router input's standard protocol settings.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Elemental MediaConnect assumes to access the decryption key used to decrypt the SRT stream from the caller.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the encryption key used to decrypt incoming SRT traffic for this MediaConnect router input.
Specifies the minimum latency in milliseconds for the SRT caller input, setting the lower bound of the receive buffer to maintain stream stability under network jitter.
Specifies the IP address or hostname of the remote SRT endpoint that the MediaConnect router input, acting as an SRT caller, initiates a connection to.
Defines the remote UDP port on the destination host to which the SRT caller connection is made, so the router input can receive the media stream from the upstream source.
Specifies the SRT stream ID that the caller uses to request a specific media stream from the remote SRT listener in this router input's protocol configuration.
The SRT listener settings for the router input's standard protocol configuration, defining how the input accepts and binds incoming SRT media streams.

Specifies the decryption settings for the SRT listener, including the encryption algorithm, key material or secret ARN, and the IAM role used to access that key for decrypting the incoming SRT stream.
Defines the encryption key material used by the SRT listener's decryption configuration to decrypt incoming media streams on this router input.
The ARN of the IAM role that MediaConnect assumes to access the AWS KMS key used for decrypting the SRT stream.

The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the encryption key used to decrypt incoming SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) listener traffic in the MediaConnect router input's standard protocol configuration.
The minimum acceptable latency in milliseconds for the SRT listener input, which controls the required buffer size for handling network jitter and ensuring reliable packet delivery.
The port number on which the SRT listener accepts incoming media streams.

aws_media_connect_router_input.content_q.text: Configures content-level detection settings for black frames in the incoming video stream, allowing you to define when a frame is considered black and how to respond.
Specifies whether black frame detection is enabled or disabled in the content level of the content quality analysis configuration for this MediaConnect router input.
Specifies the detection parameters for silent audio within the content level of the media input, allowing adjustment of silence thresholds and durations for quality analysis.
Specifies the threshold duration in seconds for detecting silent audio in the content, where a period of silence longer than this value triggers a quality analysis alert.

aws_media_connect_router_input.maintenan.text: Specifies the preferred day and time within the week for scheduling maintenance on this MediaConnect router input.

aws_media_connect_router_input.routing_s.text: Determines the geographic routing boundary (such as a specific Availability Zone or an entire AWS Region) for this MediaConnect router input, controlling where the input can route traffic.

aws_media_connect_router_input.state.text: The read-only state of the MediaConnect router input, returned by AWS to indicate whether the input is currently active, inactive, or in an error/transitional state at the router.

aws_media_connect_router_input.transit_e.text: Provides the AWS Secrets Manager secret ARN and IAM role ARN used to retrieve the encryption key for the transit encryption of this MediaConnect router input.
The ARN of the IAM role that MediaConnect assumes to access the transit encryption key stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the encryption key used for transit encryption on this MediaConnect router input.
Specifies the type of encryption key used for transit encryption on this MediaConnect router input, such as SPEKE or static-key.

aws_media_connect_router_network_interfa.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the MediaConnect router network interface.
The list of security group IDs to associate with the VPC network interface for this MediaConnect router, which determines the firewall rules for traffic to and from the interface.
The ID of the subnet within the customer's VPC where the MediaConnect router network interface is created, as specified in the router's configuration VPC settings.
The key of a user-defined tag attached to this MediaConnect router network interface, used to categorize and manage the resource.
The value portion of a key-value tag pair applied to the AWS MediaConnect router network interface, used for categorizing, identifying, and managing the resource within AWS.

aws_media_connect_router_output.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the MediaConnect router output, automatically assigned by AWS upon creation.

aws_media_connect_router_output.configur.text: Specifies the encryption settings for the transport of media between the router and the MediaConnect flow destination, such as the encryption algorithm and key reference used to protect the stream in transit.
Defines the encryption key setup (key type and key material reference) for transit encryption of the media stream sent from this output to the destination MediaConnect flow.
Specifies the AWS Secrets Manager configuration, including the secret ARN and IAM role, used to access the encryption key for destination transit encryption.
The ARN of the IAM role that MediaConnect assumes to retrieve the encryption key from AWS Secrets Manager for the destination transit encryption.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the encryption key used to decrypt the destination transit content for this MediaConnect flow output.

Specifies the type of encryption key (e.g., 'static-key' or 'speke') used for the destination transit encryption of the MediaConnect flow output, determining how the media stream is encrypted during transmission to the destination.
The ARN of the AWS Elemental MediaConnect flow to which this router output delivers media, specified within the media_connect_flow destination configuration.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the MediaConnect flow that serves as the source for this router output.
This object configures the router output to deliver its media stream to an AWS Elemental MediaLive input, specifying the destination input's ARN and connection parameters.
When set, this field enables automatic management of the encryption key for destination transit encryption to the MediaLive input, so you do not need to provide a secret ARN.
Configuration for referencing an AWS Secrets Manager secret that supplies the encryption key for transit encryption of the MediaLive input destination in the router output.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Elemental MediaConnect assumes to access the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the encryption key used for transit encryption to the MediaLive input destination.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the encryption key used to encrypt the transit of the MediaLive input destination.
Specifies the type of encryption key used to secure the media stream during transit from the MediaLive input to the router output's destination, determining how the destination decrypts the video.
The ARN of the AWS Elemental MediaLive input that this router output sends the stream to.
The ID of the AWS Elemental MediaLive input pipeline (0 or 1) that the MediaConnect router output targets when its configuration is set to a MediaLive input.
Configures a standard router output in AWS MediaConnect, specifying the destination IP address, port, protocol, and related encoding parameters for delivering a flow to a single remote endpoint.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Elastic Network Interface (ENI) that the MediaConnect router output uses in its standard configuration to send video traffic.

Defines the protocol-specific settings for a standard MediaConnect router output, such as the transport protocol (e.g., Zixi, SRT, RTP) and its associated parameters like stream ID or listener/caller mode.

The `rist` object contains the RIST (Reliable Internet Stream Transport) protocol-specific configuration for the router output, including parameters such as the RIST profile and stream identifier, within the standard protocol configuration.
The destination IP address to which the RIST output transmits media packets.
The UDP destination port number used by the RIST protocol configuration for this MediaConnect router output.
Configures the RTP protocol-specific options for this router output, including the destination IP address and port for media delivery.
The destination IP address to which the MediaConnect router output sends RTP protocol packets.
The destination UDP port number to which the output's RTP media packets are sent when the protocol configuration is set to RTP.
This object specifies the SRT caller settings, including the remote destination address and port that the router output will use to initiate an SRT connection.
The destination IP address or hostname to which the SRT caller protocol connects for sending the media stream.
The destination port number that the SRT caller uses to establish the output connection in the standard protocol configuration.

Defines the encryption settings, including the encryption algorithm and key material, used to encrypt the SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) caller output stream in the MediaConnect router's standard configuration.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS MediaConnect assumes to retrieve the encryption key from AWS Secrets Manager for the SRT caller output's encryption configuration.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the encryption key used for SRT caller encryption in this MediaConnect router output.
Specifies the minimum latency in milliseconds for the SRT caller output, which sets the lower bound for the SRT stream latency before the connection is considered unstable.
The stream ID to include in the SRT caller connection, identifying the media stream to the receiving endpoint.

Defines the SRT listener settings for the MediaConnect router output when using the SRT protocol in listener mode, including the port to listen on and optional encryption parameters for incoming streams.
Configures the encryption properties for the SRT listener, including the encryption algorithm and the reference to the secret key used to encrypt the video stream.
This object specifies the cryptographic key (such as a static key or reference to a secret) used to encrypt the SRT listener's output stream in the MediaConnect router output configuration.
The ARN of the IAM role that MediaConnect assumes to access the customer-managed KMS key used to encrypt the SRT listener traffic.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the encryption key used for the SRT listener output.
Sets the minimum latency in milliseconds for the SRT listener, defining the receive buffer delay used to absorb network jitter.
The network port number on which the SRT listener listens for incoming SRT media streams.

aws_media_connect_router_output.maintena.text: The day of the week, specified as an uppercase string such as 'MONDAY' or 'SATURDAY', on which maintenance is preferred for this router output.
Specifies the preferred time of day (in 24-hour HH:MM format) for the maintenance window on the MediaConnect router output.

aws_media_connect_router_output.routed_s.text: The current routing status of the router output, reported by the AWS API as either 'ACTIVE' (actively routing media) or 'STANDBY' (not actively routing media).

aws_media_connect_router_output.tags.val.text: The value portion of a tag associated with an AWS Elemental MediaConnect router output, used for metadata and resource organization.

aws_media_connect_router_output.tier.text: Specifies the service tier for the router output, with valid values 'BASIC' and 'STANDARD', controlling the throughput and performance characteristics of the output.

aws_media_convert_job_template.accelerat.text: Configures accelerated transcoding behavior for jobs using this template, with the Mode property set to DISABLED, ENABLED, or PREFERRED to control whether faster GPU-based transcoding is used.
Indicates whether AWS Elemental MediaConvert job acceleration is enabled for jobs that use this template, with allowed values DISABLED, ENABLED, or PREFERRED.

aws_media_convert_job_template.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Elemental MediaConvert job template.

aws_media_convert_job_template.category.text: Assigns a category to the job template for organizational grouping and management.

aws_media_convert_job_template.descripti.text: A user-defined description that helps identify the purpose or contents of the AWS Elemental MediaConvert job template.

aws_media_convert_job_template.hop_desti.text: Specifies the list of alternate MediaConvert queues (as hop destinations with associated priorities) to which a job is re-routed when it cannot be processed in the current queue, as defined in the job template.
This number sets the priority of this hop destination, controlling the order in which the job attempts to hop to the associated queue when higher-priority queues are unavailable.
The name of the MediaConvert queue to which the job will be sent when this hop destination is triggered as part of the job template's queue-hopping configuration.
Specifies the number of minutes to wait before transitioning the job to the next queue in the hop destination list.

aws_media_convert_job_template.id.text: The name of the MediaConvert job template, which is the resource's unique identifier within the AWS account.

aws_media_convert_job_template.name.text: Specifies a user-defined name for the MediaConvert job template; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_media_convert_job_template.priority.text: Specifies the default priority (0-50) for jobs created from this template, where higher values indicate a higher priority in the MediaConvert job queue.

aws_media_convert_job_template.queue.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the MediaConvert queue that jobs created from this template are submitted to, falling back to the account's default queue when not specified.

aws_media_convert_job_template.settings_.text: The JSON-formatted job settings that define the inputs, outputs, and encoding configurations for the MediaConvert job template.

aws_media_convert_job_template.status_up.text: Specifies how often (in seconds) MediaConvert sends job status updates to CloudWatch Events and your SNS topic, with valid values of 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360, 420, 480, 540, or 600, defaulting to 600 if not set.

aws_media_convert_preset.tags.text: Defines the key-value tags applied to the MediaConvert preset, which can be used for categorizing, organizing, and tracking costs associated with the resource.

aws_media_convert_queue.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS Elemental MediaConvert queue, assigned by AWS upon creation.

aws_media_convert_queue.concurrent_jobs.text: The maximum number of concurrent transcoding jobs that this MediaConvert queue can process at the same time.

aws_media_convert_queue.description.text: An optional user-defined description of the MediaConvert queue, used to identify its purpose in the AWS Elemental MediaConvert console.

aws_media_convert_queue.name.text: The name of the MediaConvert queue; if omitted, AWS Elemental MediaConvert automatically generates a unique queue name.

aws_media_convert_queue.pricing_plan.text: The pricing plan for the queue, either ON_DEMAND or RESERVED, which determines how you are billed for MediaConvert jobs.

aws_media_convert_queue.status.text: The status of the MediaConvert queue, either ACTIVE or PAUSED, which controls whether it can accept and process new jobs.

aws_media_convert_queue.tags.text: Assigns key-value tags to the MediaConvert queue, enabling cost allocation, access control, and resource categorization.

aws_media_live_channel.anywhere_settings.text: Configures the channel for MediaLive Anywhere, specifying the control plane endpoint and channel placement group to run on-premises MediaLive infrastructure.
Specifies the ID of the channel placement group to use for this MediaLive channel when running in an Anywhere environment, identifying the set of on-premises nodes that will process the channel.
Specifies the ID of the MediaLive Anywhere cluster on which this channel runs.

aws_media_live_channel.arn.text: The ARN is the unique Amazon Resource Name assigned to the MediaLive channel, used to reference the channel across AWS services.

aws_media_live_channel.cdi_input_specifi.text: Defines the Cloud Digital Interface (CDI) input configuration for the channel, including the resolution (e.g., HD or FHD) that the CDI inputs must conform to.
Specifies the resolution of the CDI (Cloud Digital Interface) input signal for the MediaLive channel, with supported values HD, FHD, or UHD.

aws_media_live_channel.channel_class.text: Specifies whether the MediaLive channel uses the SINGLE_PIPELINE (one pipeline) or STANDARD (two pipelines for high availability) class.

aws_media_live_channel.channel_engine_ve.text: Specifies the version of the MediaLive engine to run the channel, as an object containing a `version` string (the CloudFormation property `ChannelEngineVersion`).
Defines the version identifier of the MediaLive engine to use for the channel; when not specified, MediaLive automatically uses the default engine version.

aws_media_live_channel.channel_security_.text: This is a list of AWS security group IDs that are attached to the MediaLive channel's elastic network interfaces when the channel is deployed in a VPC, controlling inbound and outbound network traffic to the channel's endpoints.

aws_media_live_channel.destinations.text: Specifies the output destinations for the MediaLive channel, where each destination includes an ID and settings for delivering encoded media to targets like MediaPackage, a multiplex, or other endpoints.

aws_media_live_channel.destinations.id.text: The unique identifier for this MediaLive channel destination, which is referenced by output and output group settings to route media to this specific destination.

aws_media_live_channel.destinations.logi.text: Specifies the logical interface names that the MediaLive channel uses to send output to this destination, applicable when the channel runs in a MediaLive Anywhere environment.

aws_media_live_channel.destinations.medi.text: Specifies a list of MediaConnect router settings for the destination, where each setting includes the router ARN and priority used for routing the channel's output to one or more MediaConnect routers.
Specifies the encryption protocol (e.g., AES128 or SRTP) used on the transport flow when MediaLive sends output to the AWS Elemental MediaConnect router.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the credentials used to authenticate to the MediaConnect router for this MediaLive destination.
Specifies the AWS Elemental MediaPackage channel ID and origin endpoint name that this output destination uses for packaging and delivering the media stream.
The identifier of the MediaPackage channel endpoint that MediaLive uses as the target for this output destination.
Specifies the MediaPackage channel group name to which MediaLive sends this output destination.
The ID of the AWS Elemental MediaPackage channel to which this MediaLive output destination sends the stream.
The name of the AWS Elemental MediaPackage channel to which the MediaLive output is sent, used to target the specific MediaPackage channel for the destination.

Specifies the AWS region of the MediaPackage channel that this MediaLive destination sends output to, allowing the output to target a MediaPackage endpoint in a different region than the MediaLive channel.

aws_media_live_channel.destinations.mult.text: Specifies the settings for sending this destination's output to an AWS Elemental MediaLive Multiplex, including the target multiplex ID and program number.
Specifies the ID of the AWS Elemental MediaConnect multiplex that this MediaLive channel destination sends its output to.
Specifies the name of the program within the multiplex that this destination output is assigned to, used when the channel's destination type is a multiplex (MediaLive Multiplex output).

aws_media_live_channel.destinations.sett.text: The list of output destination settings that define the delivery parameters (such as URL, stream name, or port) for each destination in the MediaLive channel.

The name of an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter that holds the password for authenticating with the destination (such as an RTMP endpoint), so the actual password is never placed directly in the configuration.
The name of the stream to which the MediaLive channel pushes content at this destination, typically appended to the destination URL for RTMP or other streaming protocols.

The URL of the MediaLive channel destination, which specifies the network endpoint or storage location where the encoded output will be sent (for example, an RTMP push URL, a MediaPackage endpoint, or an S3 bucket path).
The username used for authentication when pushing content to the destination endpoint (e.g., an RTMP server) in these MediaLive channel destination settings.

aws_media_live_channel.destinations.srt_.text: The srt_settings block configures SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) output settings for this destination, including encryption type and latency parameters.
Specifies the SRT connection mode as either `CALLER` or `LISTENER`, controlling whether the MediaLive channel initiates or accepts the SRT connection to the destination.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that holds the encryption passphrase used to encrypt the SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) output stream for the MediaLive channel destination.
The TCP port on which the SRT listener receives incoming content for this destination.
The SRT stream identifier sent in the SRT handshake when MediaLive transmits this output to the remote SRT listener, allowing the receiver to identify or route the incoming stream.
Specifies the SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) destination URL to which the MediaLive channel pushes its output stream.

aws_media_live_channel.dry_run.text: When set to true, this field triggers a dry run of the MediaLive channel create/update operation, validating the configuration without actually provisioning or modifying the channel.

aws_media_live_channel.encoder_settings.text: Defines the encoding configuration for the MediaLive channel, including video, audio, captions, and output group settings that control how input sources are transcoded and delivered.

aws_media_live_channel.encoder_settings..text: Specifies the list of audio outputs to be encoded, where each item describes the audio source selector, codec settings, and language information for that audio output.
Assigns one or more DASH role values (e.g., 'main', 'alternate', 'commentary') to this audio description so that it can be properly labeled in DASH manifest outputs.
Audio normalization settings for the audio description, which adjust the loudness to a target level using a specified algorithm (e.g., ITU-R BS.1770) to produce consistent audio output levels.
Specifies the audio normalization algorithm used by the MediaLive channel, such as ITU_BS_1770_1 or ITU_BS_1770_2.
Determines whether the audio normalization algorithm actively corrects the audio (CORRECT_AUDIO) or only measures loudness levels (MEASURE_ONLY) when applied to the audio description.
Specifies the method used to calculate the peak level for audio normalization, either TRUE_PEAK for true peak calculation or ITU_R_1770 for the ITU-R BS.1770 standard.
Sets the peak limiter threshold in dBFS, enforcing an upper bound on the audio sample peak level after normalization to avoid clipping.
Specifies the target loudness level in LKFS (Loudness Units Full Scale) that the audio normalization algorithm will attempt to achieve for the associated audio track.

Specifies the name of the audio selector from the input that this audio description uses as its source, and it must match the Name of an AudioSelector defined in the channel's input attachments or global audio selectors.
Specifies the type of audio content (e.g., HEARING_IMPAIRED, VISUAL_IMPAIRED_COMMENTARY) to embed in the output for this audio description, following ATSC standards.

Controls whether the audio type for this audio description is set to follow the input's detected audio type (FOLLOW_INPUT) or to use the separately configured AudioType value (USE_CONFIGURED) in AWS MediaLive.
