Configures audio watermarking for the audio description, including Nielsen watermark settings such as provider and distribution identifier.
Defines the Nielsen watermarking configuration for this audio description, including distribution type and source, to enable audience measurement.

Configures the Nielsen CBET (Content Bandwidth Efficient Transport) watermarking settings, which embed Nielsen audio watermarks according to the CBET standard within the audio description's watermarking configuration.
The Nielsen CBET check digit string specifies the two-digit check digit used with Nielsen's Content Bandwidth Efficient Transport (CBET) watermarking to authenticate the audio watermark.
Specifies whether the Nielsen CBET step-aside feature is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED), which determines if the CBET watermark is inserted in a separate audio track.
Specifies the Nielsen Content Source ID (CSID) used to identify the content source for Nielsen audience measurement in CBET watermarking.
Specifies whether the Nielsen audio watermark is applied for final distribution (FINAL_DISTRIBUTOR) or programmed distribution (PROGRAMMED), affecting how MediaLive embeds the watermark in the audio.

Specifies the Nielsen NAES II NW watermarking settings, which configure how Nielsen network watermarks are inserted into the audio via the NAES II NW protocol, including the destination endpoint for the watermark payload.
Specifies the Nielsen check digit string used by the NAES II NW watermarking system for audio audience measurement, embedded by MediaLive in the audio stream for validation.
The Nielsen source ID (SID) that identifies the content source for Nielsen NAES II watermarking in MediaLive audio descriptions.
Sets the IANA timezone (e.g., 'UTC' or 'America/New_York') that MediaLive uses to interpret and embed the timecode associated with Nielsen NAES II NW watermarking in the audio output.
Configures the audio codec and its encoding parameters for the audio description, such as AAC, AC3, or other supported codecs in MediaLive.
Settings that configure Advanced Audio Coding (AAC) for the audio encode, including bitrate, sample rate, coding mode, and profile.
The average output bitrate in bits per second for the AAC audio codec, which controls the audio quality of the encoded stream.
Specifies the MPEG-4 AAC audio coding mode (transport format) for the audio encoding, with valid values including ADTS, LATM, and LOAS.
Determines how the AAC encoder interprets the incoming audio stream by specifying whether the input format is ADTS or MP4A.
The AAC audio coding profile (HEV1, HEV2, or LC) that determines compression efficiency and compatibility for the audio output in the MediaLive channel's encoder settings.
Determines whether the AAC encoder uses constant bitrate (CBR) or variable bitrate (VBR) mode.
Specifies the raw audio framing format (ADTS or LATM_LOAS) used by the AAC encoder in the MediaLive channel's audio description codec settings.
The sample rate, in Hz, of the AAC audio output; valid values include 48000, 44100, 32000, 22050, and 16000.
Sets the AAC specification (MPEG-2 or MPEG-4), which determines the transport framing used for the AAC audio output.
Specifies the VBR quality level (1-10) used only when the AAC rate control mode is set to VBR, representing a trade-off between audio quality and bitrate.
Configures the AC-3 audio codec settings for the audio description, including bitrate, coding mode, and other AC-3-specific parameters.
Sets whether the AC3 audio is attenuated by 3 dB to avoid clipping, with valid values 'ATTENUATE_3_DB' and 'NONE'.

The bitrate (in bits per second) for the AC3 audio codec, with valid values ranging from 32000 to 640000 bits per second, as defined by the AC3 settings in the MediaLive channel encoder's audio description.
Specifies the bitstream mode (such as complete main, commentary, dialogue, or emergency) applied to the AC3 audio encoding in the MediaLive channel.
Sets the AC3 audio coding mode, which determines the output channel configuration (e.g., 1/0 mono, 2/0 stereo, or 3/2 5.1 surround).
Sets the dialogue normalization (dialnorm) level in dB, a value from -31 to -1, that adjusts the program's loudness for AC3 audio encoding in MediaLive.
Determines the Dolby Digital dynamic range control profile applied to the AC3 audio, specifying how much dynamic range compression is used (e.g., FILM_STANDARD, MUSIC_LIGHT, or NONE).
Enables or disables the low-frequency effects (LFE) filter for the AC3 audio codec, which high-pass filters the LFE (subwoofer) channel to remove unwanted low-frequency content.

Controls whether the AC3 audio metadata (e.g., dialnorm and other parameters) is derived from the input signal (FOLLOW_INPUT) or from the values explicitly configured in this AC3 settings object (USE_CONFIGURED).
Specifies the encoding parameters for the EAC3 (Dolby Digital Plus) Atmos audio codec used by this audio description, such as bitrate, coding mode, and dynamic range control.
Specifies the bitrate in bits per second used to encode the Dolby Digital Plus (EAC3) audio stream with Atmos (Dolby Atmos) coding in MediaLive.
Specifies the channel coding mode for the EAC3-Atmos audio, determining the number and layout of audio channels (e.g., 5.1 or 7.1) transmitted in the Atmos stream.

Sets the dialogue normalization (dialnorm) value in dB for the EAC3 Atmos audio output, which tells the decoder the average loudness of the dialogue so it can maintain a consistent loudness level during playback.

Sets the Dynamic Range Control (DRC) profile for the line (standard consumer playback) listening mode, controlling the amount of dynamic range compression applied to the EAC3 ATMOS audio (e.g., FILM_STANDARD, NONE).
Specifies the RF (radio frequency) dynamic range control (DRC) mode for the EAC3 Atmos audio, determining the amount of dynamic range compression applied to the RF encoded signal.
Specifies the amount of height gain trim in decibels applied to the Atmos height channels for this audio description.
Specifies the amount (in dB) by which to trim (attenuate or boost) the surround channels in the EAC3 Atmos audio encoding, adjusting their level relative to the other channels.
Configures the Dolby Digital Plus (E-AC3) audio codec parameters for this audio description, including options such as bitrate, coding mode, and filter settings.
Determines whether the EAC3 audio decoder applies a 3 dB attenuation when the dialnorm value is set to -31, with allowed values ATTENUATE_3_DB and NONE.
The average bitrate in bits per second for the EAC3 (Dolby Digital Plus) audio encoding; valid values depend on the coding mode.
Specifies the bitstream mode (service type) for E-AC-3 audio, such as COMPLETE_MAIN, COMMENTARY, or DIALOGUE, which defines how the audio stream is intended to be used by the decoder.
Specifies the EAC3 (Dolby Digital Plus) audio coding mode, such as CODING_MODE_1_0, CODING_MODE_2_0, or CODING_MODE_3_2, which determines the number and configuration of audio channels.
Specifies whether to apply a DC filter to the EAC3 audio signal to remove DC offset, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Sets the EAC3 dialogue normalization (dialnorm) level in dB, which controls the perceived loudness of dialogue in the encoded audio.
Determines the dynamic range control profile applied to the line mode output (intended for TV speakers) within the EAC3 audio codec settings.
Sets the Dynamic Range Compression profile for RF (radio frequency) mode, controlling how much the EAC3 audio's dynamic range is compressed for playback on RF devices.
Configures whether the low-frequency effects (LFE) subwoofer channel is encoded in the EAC3 audio output, using values like LFE or NO_LFE to enable or disable that channel.
Enables or disables the Low Frequency Effects (LFE) filter in the EAC3 audio codec settings of the MediaLive channel.
The level in decibels (dB) of the center channel when downmixing to the Lo/Ro (left-only/right-only) stereo output in the EAC3 audio codec settings.
Specifies the level (in decibels) at which the surround channels (Ls/Rs) are mixed into the Lo/Ro stereo downmix for the EAC3 audio codec in AWS MediaLive.
Sets the attenuation level in dB applied to the center channel when downmixing to Lt/Rt stereo, with valid values from -3 to 3 in 1.5 dB increments.
Sets the level of the surround channel mix when producing the Lt/Rt (left total/right total) downmix, controlling the amount of surround audio in the matrixed stereo output.
Determines whether the EAC3 audio metadata (such as dialnorm and surround mode) is passed through from the input or set from the configured values, using FOLLOW_INPUT or USE_CONFIGURED.
Controls whether the input's EAC3 (Dolby Digital Plus) bitstream information is passed through to the output (WHEN_POSSIBLE) or whether the encoder generates its own EAC3 metadata (NO_PASSTHROUGH).

Specifies the phase control setting for EAC3 audio encoding, which adjusts the phase of the audio signal (one of NO_PHASE_CONTROL, PHASE_90, or PHASE_180) to avoid phase cancellation during downmixing.
Specifies how MediaLive performs the stereo downmix for EAC3 (Dolby Digital Plus) audio, using an enum value such as DPL2, NOT_INDICATED, STEREO, or SURROUND to define the downmix type.

Controls the Dolby Surround EX mode flag in the E-AC-3 audio bitstream, indicating whether the audio is encoded for an EX (surround EX) playback environment, with values such as NOT_INDICATED, ENABLED, or DISABLED.
Specifies the EAC3 surround mode encoding setting, determining whether the audio is encoded for surround sound or not, with allowed values like NOT_INDICATED, ENABLED, or DISABLED.
Configures the MP2 audio codec parameters, including bitrate and sample rate, used when encoding this audio description in MediaLive.
Specifies the average bitrate in bits per second for the MP2 audio codec output.
Specifies the MP2 audio coding mode, which determines whether the audio is mono or stereo (e.g., CODING_MODE_1_0 for mono, CODING_MODE_2_0 for stereo).
The audio sample rate for the MP2 codec, specified in Hz (e.g., 32000, 44100, or 48000).
Configures the audio codec to pass the audio through unchanged, so MediaLive does not transcode or modify the audio stream.
Defines the WAV audio codec configuration for this audio description, specifying uncompressed WAV format parameters such as bit depth and sample rate used by the MediaLive channel.
The number of bits per sample used to encode the WAV audio output, commonly 8, 16, 24, or 32.
Determines the number of audio channels (e.g., 'CODING_MODE_1_0' for mono, 'CODING_MODE_2_0' for stereo) used when encoding the WAV audio output.
Specifies the sample rate of the WAV audio output in hertz, which must be one of 8000, 16000, 22050, 32000, 44100, 48000, or 96000 to control audio fidelity and encoding rate.
Specifies whether this audio description is marked as accessible for DVB Dash (DASH) outputs, with valid values NONE or ENABLED.
The ISO 639-2 three-letter language code identifying the language of the audio in this audio description, used for signaling to downstream outputs and enabling features like language-based switching.
Controls whether the language code in the output follows the input (FOLLOW_INPUT) or uses the configured LanguageCode value (USE_CONFIGURED).
Sets the unique name for this audio description, which is referenced by output settings (such as AudioDescriptionName) to route audio to specific outputs.
Configures how the input audio channels are mapped and mixed to produce the output audio channels for this audio description.

Defines the list of channel mappings that specify how input audio channels are mixed and assigned to each output channel in the audio remix setup, with each mapping containing input channel level configurations and the target output channel index.
Specifies the gain level (in dB) and source input channel number for each input channel mixed into the output channel of this audio remix mapping.
The gain, in decibels (dB), applied to the corresponding input channel when audio remixing is enabled, controlling the channel's relative level in the resulting mix.
The zero-based index of the input audio channel to include in the remix mapping.
Specifies the destination output channel number (0-based index) to which the corresponding source audio channel is remixed in the MediaLive audio remix settings.

For the AWS::MediaLive::Channel resource, this specifies the number of input audio channels to be used in the remix configuration for this audio description, defining how many source channels are available for mapping.
Specifies the number of output channels for the remixed audio, with a range from 1 to 16.
Specifies the stream name assigned to the audio output, which output groups such as HLS use to identify the audio rendition in the output manifest.
Determines whether MediaLive inserts black video during ad avails (avail blanking) and optionally specifies an image to display during those periods, controlled by an enabled/disabled state.
Defines the image used to blank the video during avail periods, including its URI and optional password parameter.
The name of the AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter that stores the password used to access the secured avail blanking image URL.
The URI of the image file (e.g., an S3 or HTTP URL) that AWS Elemental MediaLive uses as the static image to display during avail blanking, replacing the underlying video signal.
The username used for HTTP Basic authentication when MediaLive fetches the avail blanking image from the specified URI.
Specifies whether avail blanking is enabled or disabled for the channel, accepting values ENABLED or DISABLED.
Specifies the ad avail configuration for the encoder, including SCTE-35 message handling such as splice insert or time signal settings.
Configures the ad avail signaling for the channel's encoder, specifying the SCTE-35 splice insert or time signal APOS method and associated parameters.

Configures the ESAM (Event Signaling and Management) server for the channel, defining how ad avail signals are exchanged with the ESAM server, including settings like the acquisition point ID and signal behavior.
The identifier that MediaLive passes to the ESAM server to specify the acquisition point from which to retrieve ad avail signaling information.
Specifies the offset in milliseconds from the normal start of the ad avail to the actual start of the ad, allowing timing adjustments between the upstream signaling system and MediaLive.
References an AWS Systems Manager (SSM) parameter store key that contains the password for authenticating to the ESAM server used for ad avail signaling.
The URL of the ESAM (Event Signaling and Management) POIS (Program Out-of-band Information System) endpoint to which MediaLive sends ad avail signaling messages for the channel's encoder settings.
The username used to authenticate with the ESAM (Event Signaling and Management) server for signaling ad avail events.
Specifies the zone identity of the ESAM server, which MediaLive uses to identify the active zone for ad avail signaling.
Determines how MediaLive inserts a SCTE-35 splice insert message into the stream at ad avail boundaries, including the ad avail offset and whether regional blackout and web delivery are allowed.
Specifies the offset, in milliseconds, from the SCTE-35 splice_insert message to the start of the ad avail, allowing you to adjust the timing of ad insertion.
Specifies whether to set the no regional blackout flag (bit) in the SCTE-35 splice insert message, which controls whether regional blackout constraints are applied by downstream devices.
Specifies whether AWS Elemental MediaLive follows or ignores the web delivery allowed flag in the SCTE-35 splice insert, with valid values 'FOLLOW' or 'IGNORE'.

Specifies the SCTE-35 Time Signal APOS (Avail Placement Opportunity Start) settings for the MediaLive channel, controlling how ad avail opportunities are signaled with time signal messages, including ad avail offset and regional blackout/web delivery flags.
Specifies the offset, in milliseconds, between the SCTE-35 time signal and the ad avail, which MediaLive uses to align ad insertion with the signal in the channel output.

Determines the value of the 'No Regional Blackout' flag in the SCTE-35 time signal APOS message, where '1' indicates the content is exempt from regional blackout rules and '0' indicates it is subject to them.
This field sets the web delivery allowed flag on SCTE-35 time signal Apos messages, controlling whether the ad avail is permitted for web delivery.
Specifies the SCTE-35 segmentation scope for the output, where ALL applies SCTE-35 messages to every segment and NONE disables them.

Specifies the blackout slate settings used by the MediaLive encoder to display a slate image (or other content) during blackout periods, such as when the input signal is lost or at the end of a network blackout.

The blackout_slate_image object specifies the InputLocation (e.g., an S3 URI) of the image to display as the blackout slate during blackout periods defined in the MediaLive channel's encoder settings.
The reference to an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter that holds the password required to access the blackout slate image when its URI (e.g., HTTP/S3) is password-protected.
The URI (typically an Amazon S3 URI) of the image file used as the blackout slate, shown by the channel encoder when the blackout slate is enabled.
The username part of the credentials used to authenticate when fetching the blackout slate image from the location specified by its URI.
Specifies whether MediaLive displays the blackout slate when the network ends, with a value of 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
In MediaLive's blackout slate configuration, this property provides the InputLocation of the image to be displayed when the network ends, overriding the default slate for that condition.
The name of the AWS Systems Manager (SSM) parameter that stores the password required to access the network end blackout image, used by AWS Elemental MediaLive to fetch the image from its source URI.
The URI (S3 bucket or HTTP path) of the image displayed as the blackout slate when network programming ends.
The username (used with the sibling password) to authenticate when the MediaLive channel fetches the network end blackout image from a protected source such as a private S3 bucket.
Defines an optional network identifier that narrows the blackout slate to only be applied when the lost input belongs to that network; if omitted, the slate applies regardless of network.
The state of the blackout slate, indicating whether the blackout slate is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED).
Configures the caption outputs for the MediaLive channel by defining how captions are selected, encoded, and delivered in the encoder settings.
Indicates whether the caption track is accessible to viewers with hearing impairments, with allowed values of ACCESSIBLE or UNKNOWN.
Assigns DASH roles (such as CAPTION or DESCRIPTION) to this caption description, controlling how the caption track is labeled in DASH/CMAF output manifests.
Specifies the name of the caption selector that supplies the source captions for this caption description in the MediaLive channel encoder settings.
Defines the destination-specific configuration (such as burn-in or embedded caption settings) for a single caption description in the MediaLive channel's encoder settings.

The `arib_destination_settings` block is an empty (argument-less) configuration object used to select ARIB (Association of Radio Industries and Businesses) as the caption output format for this caption description in the MediaLive channel.
Configures burn-in captions that are overlaid directly onto the video frame, controlling appearance such as font, color, and positioning.
Determines the horizontal alignment of the burn-in captions text within the video frame, such as left, center, or right.
Specifies the background color of the burn-in captions, with allowed values such as BLACK or WHITE.
Sets the opacity of the background color behind burned-in captions as a percentage from 0 (transparent) to 100 (opaque).
Specifies the InputLocation object that provides the font file used for rendering burn-in captions in the MediaLive channel.

The password_param field specifies the AWS Systems Manager parameter that stores the password used to access a burn-in caption font file from a remote location (such as HTTPS or S3) that requires authentication.
The URI (e.g., an S3 URI) of the TrueType or OpenType font file that MediaLive uses to render the burn-in caption text.
The username for HTTP basic authentication when the burn-in caption destination retrieves its custom font file from the URL in the font settings.
Sets the color of the burn-in caption text displayed over the video, with allowed values such as black, blue, green, red, white, and yellow.
Determines the opacity (0 to 100, integer) of the burned-in captions text, where 0 is fully transparent and 100 is fully opaque.
Specifies the font resolution in DPI (dots per inch) for burned-in captions, typically 96 or 192, which controls the sharpness of the rendered caption text.
Sets the font size for the burned-in captions text, with valid values small, medium, or large.
Specifies the color of the outline surrounding the burned-in caption text, with valid values including BLACK, BLUE, GREEN, RED, WHITE, and YELLOW.
Specifies the width of the outline around the burn-in caption text; valid values are 1 (thin), 2 (medium), or 3 (thick), controlling the thickness of the text outline in MediaLive burn-in captions.
Specifies the color of the drop shadow behind the burn-in caption text, with valid values such as BLACK, NONE, or WHITE.
Sets the opacity of the shadow behind the burned-in captions text, where 0 is fully transparent and 100 is fully opaque.
Specifies the horizontal offset in pixels of the shadow relative to the burn-in caption text.
Specifies the vertical offset of the burn-in caption drop shadow, in pixels, relative to the caption text baseline.
Specifies the maximum number of rows (lines) of captions to display in the burn-in output, controlling the vertical space reserved for rendered subtitles.
Determines whether the burn-in teletext character grid is fixed to a set size or scales with the video resolution, with valid values FIXED and SCALED.
Specifies the horizontal position, in pixels, of the burn-in captions relative to the left edge of the video.
Sets the vertical position (y-coordinate) of the burned-in caption text relative to the top of the video frame, in pixels, within the MediaLive channel's burn-in destination settings.
Specifies the destination settings for DVB-Sub captions, controlling how the subtitle text is rendered (e.g., font, color, background, and positioning) in the MediaLive output.
Sets the horizontal alignment of the DVB Sub captions text, controlling whether the subtitle text is left-aligned, center-aligned, or right-aligned within its box.
Specifies the background color (e.g., BLACK, WHITE) for the DVB-Sub captions, which is drawn behind the subtitle text in the video output.
Sets the opacity of the background box behind DVB-Sub captions, using a numeric value from 0 (fully transparent) to 255 (fully opaque).
Specifies the Amazon S3 location of a font file (e.g., .ttf or .otf) used to render DVB Sub captions in the output, allowing a custom font instead of the default.
The reference to an AWS Systems Manager parameter that stores the password required to access the DVB Sub caption font file when that font file is password-protected.
The S3 URI of the TrueType font file that MediaLive uses to render DVB Sub captions within the channel output.
The username used to authenticate to the location that hosts the DVB Sub font file for this caption destination.

Specifies the color of the DVB-Sub subtitle text (e.g., WHITE, YELLOW, BLACK, RED, BLUE, GREEN) applied within the destination settings of a caption description in the MediaLive channel's encoder configuration.
For DVB Sub captions, sets the transparency of the caption text font, using an integer from 0 (fully transparent) to 255 (fully opaque).
Sets the font resolution in dots per inch (DPI) for DVB-Sub subtitle rendering, with valid values of 96 or 120, affecting the size and sharpness of the subtitles.
Specifies the font size in pixels (valid range 1–96) for the DVB Sub caption output.
Specifies the color of the outline drawn around DVB-Sub subtitle text in the MediaLive channel's caption output.
Sets the width (in pixels) of the outline drawn around DVB-Sub caption text.
Sets the color of the drop shadow rendered behind DVB-Sub subtitle text in the MediaLive channel's encoded output.
Sets the opacity of the drop shadow behind DVB-Sub captions, from 0 (fully transparent) to 255 (fully opaque) as a numeric value.
Sets the horizontal offset, in pixels, from the DVB-Sub subtitle text at which the shadow is rendered, controlling the left/right placement of the shadow.
Specifies the vertical offset, in pixels, of the text shadow relative to the character position for DVB-Sub captions in the MediaLive channel's DVB Sub destination settings.
Specifies the number of subtitle rows (lines of text) to display for DVB-Sub captions, controlling the vertical capacity of the subtitle area.
Controls whether the DVB Sub captions use a fixed or scaled teletext grid for positioning and scaling.
Specifies the horizontal position of the DVB Sub captions in pixels, measured from the left edge of the video frame.
Specifies the vertical position of the DVB-Sub captions in pixels, relative to the top or bottom of the video frame as set by the origin property in the same DvbSubDestinationSettings.
Specifies the EBU-TT-D subtitle output settings (such as font family, fill line gap, and style control) used by the caption destination for a MediaLive channel encoder.
Specifies the copyright holder string that is embedded in the EBU-TT-D captions output, identifying the copyright information in the caption metadata.
Specifies the default font size in pixels for EBU-TT-D caption text, used when the caption itself does not define a font size.
Specifies the default line height in pixels to use for EBU-TT captions when the source caption track does not define an explicit line height.
Specifies whether the Ebu-TT-D destination fills the gap between subtitle lines with the background color, an option that applies only when the caption style control is passthrough.
Specifies the font family to be used for rendering EBU-TT-D captions in the output, controlling the typeface of the displayed subtitles.
Controls whether EBU-TT-D caption style information (such as font, color, and positioning) is included in the output, with valid values of INCLUDE_STYLE or NO_INCLUDE_STYLE.
Enables this caption destination to embed CEA-608/708 (Line 21) captions directly into the video stream, with no additional output configuration required.
Specifies the destination settings for embedded plus SCTE-20 captions, which embed CEA-608/708 captions and SCTE-20 data into the output video stream.
Configures RTMP caption info as the destination type for a caption description, embedding captions in an RTMP output as caption info with no additional parameters.
Specifies the SCTE-20 plus embedded caption destination type, an empty configuration object indicating that captions are delivered in the SCTE-20 plus embedded format with no extra parameters.
Specifies the SCTE-27 caption destination settings, an empty structure that enables embedding SCTE-27 captions in the channel's transport stream output without requiring further configuration.

Configures the output appearance of SMPTE-TT (Timed Text) captions within the MediaLive channel, including settings like font color, opacity, size, outline, shadow and positioning for the caption destination.
Specifies the destination settings for Teletext captions; in the current AWS MediaLive API, this object is an empty placeholder with no configurable properties.
Specifies the settings for TTML caption output in a MediaLive channel, including the destination where the captions are delivered and how style information from the source captions is handled.
Specifies whether the TTML destination should preserve the style information from the source captions (PASSTHROUGH) or apply locally configured style settings (USE_CONFIGURED).
Configures how WebVTT subtitle captions are formatted for the output, including accessibility and style control settings.
Controls whether WebVTT caption style information from the input is passed through to the output (PASSTHROUGH) or stripped out (NO_STYLE_DATA).
Specifies whether DVB-Sub captions are marked as accessibility captions in DASH outputs, with values like 'ACCESSIBLE' and 'NO_ACCESSIBILITY'.
Specifies the language code (e.g., 'eng' for English) for the caption track, identifying the language of the captions in the MediaLive channel output.
Specifies a human-readable description (such as 'English') for the language of the captions, complementing the machine-readable languageCode in the caption description.
The name of this caption description, which must be unique within the MediaLive channel and is used to reference this caption description in output settings.
Configures color space conversion and color correction adjustments applied to the video in the channel's encoder pipeline.
Defines a list of global color space corrections applied to all video in the channel, each specifying an input color space, output color space, and optional gamma and saturation adjustments.

Specifies the color space of the input video (for example, HDR10 or HLG) that this global color correction entry applies to, mapping from that source color space to the corresponding output color space.
Specifies the target output color space (such as HDR10 or HLG_2020) that MediaLive applies to the video after performing the global color correction.
The URI of the color correction lookup table (LUT) file, such as an S3 path, that defines the color transformation for the global color correction.
Specifies which MediaLive encoding features, such as input prepare and static image fade in/out, are enabled for this channel's encoder settings.
Controls whether MediaLive automatically prepares inputs before scheduled input switches, with allowed values ENABLED or DISABLED (defaulting to DISABLED).
Configures whether output static image overlay schedule actions are enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for this MediaLive channel.
Configures global encoder settings that apply across all outputs in the MediaLive channel, including input loss behavior, output timing source, and initial frame rate.
Sets the initial audio gain level, in dB, applied to all audio outputs of the channel at the start of processing.
Controls whether MediaLive automatically switches to the next configured input when the current input ends, where NONE takes no action and SWITCH_INPUT switches to the next input.
Defines how the channel reacts to a loss of input signal, specifying whether to show a black frame, a custom image, or other fallback behavior during input loss.
The duration (in milliseconds) to wait after the input signal is lost before MediaLive inserts a black frame to replace the missing video in the output.
Specifies the hexadecimal color value (e.g., #000000 for black) that MediaLive displays when an input is lost and the input loss behavior is set to use a solid color.
Specifies the image or color that MediaLive displays as the slate when the input signal is lost.
Sets the identifier of the AWS Systems Manager (SSM) parameter or AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the password used to authenticate when fetching the input loss image from its location.
Specifies the URI (e.g., S3 or HTTP URL) of the image that is displayed as the slate on the output when the input signal is lost.
The username for the S3 bucket that hosts the input loss image slate, used to authenticate access when the bucket is private.
Specifies whether the input loss image is a solid color or a slate image, determining what viewers see when the input signal is lost.
Specifies the number of milliseconds MediaLive repeats the last good frame of the input after signal loss before switching to a black frame or the configured input loss image.
Determines whether the channel synchronizes its outputs using epoch locking or pipeline locking mode for global configuration.
Configures output locking for the MediaLive channel, specifying how output frames are locked to a reference clock (e.g., EPOCH_LOCKING or PIPELINE_LOCKING) to maintain synchronization across outputs.
The disabled_locking_settings object is an empty placeholder used when the output locking mode is set to DISABLED, containing no configurable sub-properties.
Specifies the epoch and mode for epoch-based output locking, which sets a common UTC reference time to synchronize the start of the channel's encoded outputs.
Specifies a custom epoch value in milliseconds that MediaLive uses as the reference timing point for output locking when epoch locking is enabled, overriding the system default epoch.
Specifies the epoch timestamp (in milliseconds) used as the jam sync reference time for locking the MediaLive channel output to an absolute time in the epoch-locking configuration.
This object enables pipeline locking for the channel's output, synchronizing the output of the redundant pipelines to keep them aligned.

Sets a custom epoch timestamp (in seconds) used as the reference point for MediaLive pipeline locking, enabling multiple pipelines to align their output timing to a specified time instead of the current epoch.

Specifies the pipeline locking method for MediaLive channel outputs, which is either EPOCH_LOCKING to align pipelines to a specific epoch time or PIPELINE_LOCKING to align the two pipelines to each other.
Determines whether the channel output timing is based on the input clock (INPUT_CLOCK) or the system clock (SYSTEM_CLOCK).
Indicates whether MediaLive supports inputs with a frame rate lower than 1 fps by duplicating frames, with valid values ENABLED or DISABLED.
Configures the motion graphics overlay feature for the channel, specifying whether motion graphics insertion is enabled and the URL of the HTML5 asset to be overlaid on the video output.
Specifies whether motion graphics insertion is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for the channel's motion graphics configuration.
Defines the type and configuration for motion graphics overlays, allowing selection between HTML5-based and SCTE-35-based motion graphics settings in the MediaLive channel output.

Settings that specify an HTML document for motion graphics overlays and optionally how long it should be displayed, used when the channel's motion graphics configuration employs HTML-based motion graphics.
Defines the Nielsen audience measurement settings for the channel, including watermark and distribution configuration used to enable Nielsen tracking in the encoded output.
Specifies the unique distributor ID that MediaLive passes to Nielsen for watermarking, identifying the content distributor in the audio stream.
Determines whether MediaLive inserts Nielsen ID3 metadata tags into the PCM audio stream, with allowed values NONE (no tagging) and TAG_PCM (enable tagging).
Specifies the output groups for the channel, which define how encoded outputs are packaged and delivered to destinations such as MediaStore, MediaPackage, or S3.
A user-defined name for this output group, used to identify and manage it within the MediaLive channel.
Defines the protocol-specific settings for the output group, such as HLS, UDP, or RTMP group settings, that control how the output group formats and delivers its outputs.
Specifies the destination (e.g., an S3 bucket) and rollover interval for an archive output group, controlling where and how archived media segments are written.
Configures the CDN settings for the archive output group, including S3-specific options like access control and distribution.
Configures the Amazon S3 destination (bucket and prefix) and optional access-control settings used by the archive output group to store MediaLive channel output files.

Specifies the canned ACL (such as PRIVATE, PUBLIC_READ, or BUCKET_OWNER_FULL_CONTROL) that AWS Elemental MediaLive applies to the archive files it writes to the S3 bucket for this archive output group.
Specifies the destination URL (such as an S3 bucket path) where archived media outputs from this archive group are stored.

The reference ID that maps this archive output group to a destination defined in the channel's Destinations collection, determining the S3 bucket or MediaStore container where archived outputs are stored.
Specifies the number of seconds between rollovers of an archive output file, causing MediaLive to close the current file and begin a new one at each interval.
Defines the settings for a CMAF Ingest output group, specifying the destination location (base URL) to which MediaLive outputs CMAF media segments and manifest files.

Defines extra destination endpoints (each an object containing a URL) for the CMAF Ingest output group, allowing the encoded stream to be sent to multiple target locations in addition to the primary destination.
Identifies the alternative MediaPackage ingest endpoint for this additional CMAF ingest destination, using a destination reference ID that corresponds to a destination configured in the output group.
The destination_ref_id field references the ID of a destination configured in the channel's Destinations list, directing this additional CMAF ingest output to that destination.

Configures the list of caption language mappings for the CMAF Ingest output group, where each mapping pairs a caption language code with a human-readable language description, enabling proper language metadata for the captions.
The zero-based index of the caption channel in the input to map to a specific language code, used to select which caption track is included in the CMAF Ingest output group.

The three-letter ISO 639-2 language code that specifies the language of the captions for the CMAF ingest caption language mapping, which is used to populate the language attribute in the output manifest.
The destination URL, typically an AWS Elemental MediaStore container endpoint, to which the CMAF ingest output group delivers its streaming segments.
It specifies the ID of a channel-level destination (defined in the channel's Destinations list) that identifies where the CMAF Ingest output group should send its media.
Controls whether ID3 metadata from the input is passed through to the CMAF output (PASSTHROUGH) or discarded (NO_PASSTHROUGH).
Appends the specified string to the end of the ID3 timestamp in the CMAF Ingest output, allowing you to customize the ID3 metadata timestamp value.
Specifies whether KLV (Key-Length-Value) metadata in the CMAF ingest stream is passed through to the output (PASSTHROUGH) or discarded (NO_PASSTHROUGH).
Sets a name modifier for the KLV (Key-Length-Value) metadata track in the CMAF Ingest output, which MediaLive uses as part of the track name in the output.
Determines whether Nielsen ID3 metadata in the incoming source is passed through to the output or ignored, as part of the CMAF ingest output group settings.

Specifies a string that modifies the name of the Nielsen ID3 metadata inserted by MediaLive in the CMAF ingest output group, allowing you to customize the metadata identifier for Nielsen audience measurement.

Specifies a custom text string that MediaLive appends to SCTE-35 message names in the CMAF Ingest output group, which can be used to differentiate these events from SCTE-35 messages in other output groups.

Specifies how SCTE-35 ad signaling markers are handled in the CMAF Ingest output group, such as passing them through (PASSTHROUGH), ignoring them (NONE), or allowing the caller to insert them (CALLER_INSERT).
Specifies the duration, in seconds, of each CMAF segment that MediaLive writes for this output group.
Determines whether the segment length value is interpreted in seconds or milliseconds.
Specifies the delay in milliseconds before the CMAF Ingest output group sends its content to the destination.
For the CMAF Ingest output group in AWS MediaLive, this field specifies the ID3 frame identifier (e.g., PRIV, TDRL, or a custom value) used to embed timed metadata into the output segments.
Determines the interval in seconds between insertions of ID3 timed metadata into the CMAF Ingest output group.
Indicates whether timed metadata (such as ID3) from the input is passed through to the CMAF Ingest output; set to PASSTHROUGH to pass through or NO_PASSTHROUGH to discard it.
Configures the destination S3 location (and optional CDN settings) for a MediaLive frame capture output group, which periodically captures video frames as still JPEG images.
References an output destination defined in the channel's Destinations list, specifying where frame capture outputs are sent.
Specifies the ID of a channel-level destination (defined in the channel's Destinations list) that this frame capture output group uses to deliver its output files.
Specifies the CDN settings (S3 or WebDAV) that MediaLive uses to deliver frame capture output files for this output group.
Specifies the Amazon S3 CDN settings for a frame-capture output group, including the S3 bucket base URL and optional key prefix used to store captured frames.
Specifies the canned ACL (e.g., private, public-read) that is applied to each frame capture object written to the S3 bucket.
Configures the HLS output group settings in MediaLive, including segment length, destination, and encryption options for HTTP Live Streaming outputs.
Specifies which ad marker types (e.g., ADOBE, ELEMENTAL, SCTE35_ENHANCED) to include in the HLS output for signaling ad insertion events.
Base URL for the HLS content segments, prepended to the media segment URLs in the HLS playlist (e.g., an S3 bucket or CDN path).

Specifies the secondary base URL for content (video/audio segments) in the HLS output group, which MediaLive uses as an alternative URL for the media segments to provide redundancy or load distribution.
Sets the base URL that is prepended to the HLS manifest file path in the generated URLs for this output group, allowing the manifest to be served from a custom domain or CDN.
The base URL used to generate the first HLS manifest (manifest1) in this HLS output group.
Specifies a list of caption language mappings, each associating a caption channel number with a language code, so that HLS outputs carry correct language metadata for captions.
Specifies the numeric caption channel (e.g., 1-4) that is mapped to a language code in the HLS output, identifying which embedded caption stream to use for that language.
Specifies the language code (e.g., an ISO 639-2 three-letter code) for the caption language mapping, which is inserted into the HLS manifest to associate captions with a particular language.

The language_description specifies the human-readable description of the caption language (for example, "English") that MediaLive includes in the HLS manifest's LANGUAGE attribute for the corresponding caption channel.
Specifies whether the caption language code is inserted into the HLS manifest's EXT-X-MEDIA tags, with valid values INSERT or NONE, in the HLS output group settings of a MediaLive channel.
Determines whether the HLS output includes a Cache-Control HTTP header that enables or disables client-side caching of video segments, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Specifies the codec specification used in the HLS output, either RFC_4281 or RFC_6381, which determines the format of the codec string in the HLS manifest.
Specifies a fixed, user-defined initialization vector (IV) used when encrypting HLS segments, overriding the default auto-generated IV for the output.
Defines the destination output reference for the HLS output group, pointing to a preconfigured output location ID that determines where HLS segments and playlists are stored.
References, by ID, a destination in the channel's encoder_settings.destinations list, specifying where HLS output files (segments and playlists) are stored.
Determines whether HLS output files are placed in a single directory or in separate subdirectories per stream, with allowed values SINGLE_DIRECTORY and SUBDIRECTORY_PER_STREAM.
Determines whether MediaLive inserts EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY tags into the HLS output, with allowed values 'INSERT' or 'NEVER_INSERT'.
Sets the encryption type for the HLS output group, controlling whether and how the stream is encrypted (e.g., AES128, SAMPLE_AES, or NONE).
Specifies the CDN settings for delivering HLS output, including provider-specific configuration for destinations such as AWS Elemental MediaStore, Amazon S3, or HTTP/PUT-based CDNs.

Configures Akamai CDN-specific parameters for HLS output groups, such as connection retry interval, file cache duration, HTTP transfer mode, restart delay, and authentication salt/token, enabling delivery to Akamai's network.
Specifies the number of seconds to wait between retry attempts when establishing a connection to the Akamai CDN for HLS output groups.
Sets the number of seconds that HLS file segments are cached for the Akamai CDN before being discarded.
Determines whether the HLS output uses chunked or non-chunked HTTP transfer when sending media to Akamai's CDN, with valid values being 'CHUNKED_TRANSFER' and 'NON_CHUNKED_TRANSFER'.
The number of times MediaLive retries a failed HTTP request to the Akamai CDN before considering the transfer failed.
Number of seconds to wait before retrying a failed connection to the Akamai CDN in HLS output groups.
The salt string used to generate the Akamai token for authenticating HLS output requests when delivering content to Akamai CDN.
The token specifies the authentication token used by MediaLive to authenticate requests to the Akamai CDN when delivering HLS content.
Configuration for using basic HTTP PUT as the HLS CDN delivery method, specifying retry and cache settings for pushing segments to an origin server.

The number of seconds to wait between retry attempts when a connection to the HLS basic PUT destination fails, affecting how frequently MediaLive attempts to re-establish the connection for segment uploads.
Specifies the number of seconds that MediaLive caches HLS segment files in the CDN when using basic PUT (e.g., S3) delivery.
Number of retry attempts for HLS basic put operations (uploading segments to the destination) when they fail, allowing the channel to recover from transient errors before giving up.
The number of seconds that MediaLive waits before restarting a failed HLS file transfer to the CDN when using basic PUT settings.

Specifies connection, retry, and cache settings for delivering HLS output group content to an AWS Elemental MediaStore CDN, including retry interval, number of retries, file cache duration, and storage class.
Number of seconds MediaLive waits before attempting to reconnect to AWS Elemental MediaStore after a connection is lost, used in HLS output group CDN settings.
Specifies the number of seconds that MediaLive caches HLS media files in AWS Elemental MediaStore before they are made available for HTTP requests, controlling the output delay for the HLS stream.
Specifies the AWS Elemental MediaStore storage class (STANDARD or REDUCED_REDUNDANCY) used for the HLS output destination, controlling the storage tier for the media segments.
Specifies the number of times MediaLive will retry a request to AWS Elemental MediaStore before considering the delivery failed.
Specifies the number of seconds to wait before restarting the HLS output to AWS Elemental MediaStore after an interruption occurs.
Configures Amazon S3 as the content delivery network (CDN) destination for the HLS output group, specifying the S3 bucket and related settings for storing HLS segments.
Specifies the canned ACL (access control list) to apply to the HLS output files written to the S3 bucket.
Configures the HLS WebDAV output destination settings for an HLS output group in MediaLive, including HTTP transfer mode, retry behavior, and authentication.
The number of seconds MediaLive waits between attempts to re-establish a failed connection to the WebDAV server when delivering HLS output.
Specifies the number of seconds MediaLive caches HLS segment files locally before uploading them to the WebDAV server, controlling the cache duration for WebDAV delivery.
Specifies whether to use HTTP chunked transfer encoding (CHUNKED) or a standard non-chunked transfer (NON_CHUNKED) when delivering HLS segments to the WebDAV destination.
The number of retries to perform when writing HLS output to the WebDAV server.
The number of seconds to wait before restarting a failed HTTP transfer to the WebDAV server in the HLS output group.
Specifies the ID3 segment tagging method for the HLS output group, with values such as NO_TAGGING, PRIV, or TDRL to control whether and how ID3 metadata is inserted into each segment.
Specifies whether to include an I-frame-only playlist in the HLS output group, which enables trick-play in HLS players (INCLUDE) or omit it (EXCLUDE).
Determines whether a partially filled HLS segment is emitted or suppressed when the output halts before the segment completes, with accepted values typically 'USE' or 'SUPPRESS'.
The number of HLS media segments to retain in the playlist before older segments are removed.
Defines the action taken when the input signal is lost for this HLS output group, with valid values including PAUSE_OUTPUT (stop output) and EMIT_OUTPUT (continue emitting output).
Determines whether the encryption initialization vector (IV) is written into the HLS manifest, with 'INCLUDE' or 'EXCLUDE' as valid values.
Determines the source of the initialization vector (IV) for encrypted HLS segments, either following the segment number or the key ID.
Specifies the number of completed HLS segments to retain in the output destination before older segments are deleted.
Specifies the format of the encryption key used in the HLS output group, which is passed to the key provider to control how the key is referenced in the manifest.
Specifies the version of the encryption key format (v1 or v2) used in the HLS output group's media playlists and segments.
Configures the DRM key provider for HLS outputs, defining whether to use a static key or a SPEKE-compliant key server for content encryption.
Defines the settings for using a static key to encrypt HLS output groups, including the static key value and optional key provider server configuration.
The URL of the HTTP server that MediaLive uses to retrieve the static encryption key for securing HLS output group segments.
Specifies the name of an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter that contains the password for authenticating to the HLS static key provider server.
The URI of the static key provider server that MediaLive contacts to retrieve the encryption key for HLS output groups.
The username used to authenticate with the key provider server when retrieving the static encryption key for HLS output groups in AWS MediaLive.
The static key value used to encrypt HLS output segments for content protection.
Specifies whether the HLS manifest is compressed with gzip or sent uncompressed (none) in the MediaLive HLS output group.
Specifies the format of the segment duration value that MediaLive writes in the HLS manifest's EXTINF tags, either FLOATING_POINT or INTEGER.
Specifies the minimum duration, in seconds, for the media segments generated in the HLS output group, preventing segment durations from falling below this threshold.

Determines whether the HLS output group provides a live streaming output (LIVE) or a video-on-demand file-based output (VOD), where VOD writes the manifest and media segments to a destination for later playback.

Controls whether the HLS output group generates both manifest files and media segments (MANIFESTS_AND_SEGMENTS) or only media segments (SEGMENTS_ONLY), affecting the output files written to the destination.
Specifies whether the HLS output group includes the EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME tag in the media playlists, which sets the program date and time on segments, typically with values ENABLE or DISABLE.
Determines the source of the program date/time (UTC) that MediaLive writes into the HLS playlist, either deriving it from the output timecode or using the system clock.
The period in seconds between insertions of the EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME tag in the HLS output, used to synchronize player clock timing.
Specifies whether to generate redundant manifests and segments for HLS outputs, with possible values like MANIFESTS_AND_SEGMENTS or MANIFESTS_ONLY.
Specifies the length (in seconds) of each MPEG-2 transport stream segment for the HLS output group.

Specifies whether the HLS output group segments are defined by the input's own segmentation boundaries (USE_INPUT_SEGMENTATION) or packaged as byte-range references into a single output file (SEGMENT_IN_SINGLE_FILE).

Specifies the number of HLS segment files to write into each subdirectory of the output destination before MediaLive starts a new subdirectory, enabling folder-based organization of generated segments.
Configures whether the video resolution (widthxheight) is included in the EXT-X-STREAM-INF tag of HLS playlists, with allowed values 'INCLUDE' and 'EXCLUDE'.
Specifies the ID3 frame to use for timed metadata in HLS output segments (for example, PRIV or TDRL).
Specifies the interval in seconds at which MediaLive inserts timed metadata ID3 frames into the HLS output.
Sets the amount of time in milliseconds to shift the HLS output's timestamps, where a positive value delays the output and a negative value advances it.
Controls whether HLS output segments are written as separate .ts files (SEGMENTED_FILES) or appended into a single .ts file (SINGLE_FILE) for the MediaLive channel's HLS output group.
Sets the list of Availability Zones in which the MediaConnect flow for this output group is created, allowing you to specify one or two AZs for high availability and redundancy.
Configures the destination MediaPackage channel for the output group, specifying the MediaPackage channel ID where the encoded video and audio are delivered.
Defines the destination for a MediaPackage output group, specifying the MediaPackage channel ID where the encoded output is delivered.
Specifies the ID of a channel-level destination (from the channel's `destinations` list) that this MediaPackage output group will use for delivering output.
Configures the AWS Elemental MediaPackage v2 output group settings, specifying the MediaPackage v2 channel group, channel, and stream names to which the MediaLive output group delivers content.

Adds additional MediaPackage v2 destinations (each with an ID and URL) to this output group, so the encoded stream is delivered to multiple MediaPackage v2 packaging groups in addition to the primary destination.
Defines the MediaPackage v2 channel group and channel name for this additional destination, which is where the output group's stream is delivered.
Specifies the unique reference ID of a destination defined elsewhere in the encoder settings, allowing this MediaPackage v2 output group to send additional output to that destination.

Configures a list of language mappings for embedded captions, assigning a DASH language code and description to each caption channel so MediaPackage v2 can identify and present the appropriate caption language.
The channel number in the input that contains the caption to map to a specific language code in MediaPackage v2 group settings.
Specifies the ISO 639 language code (e.g., 'eng' or 'spa') for a caption track mapped to a language in the MediaPackage v2 output group.
Specifies a human-readable description of the caption language (e.g., 'English') for a caption-language mapping in a MediaPackage v2 output group of the MediaLive channel.
Controls whether ID3 metadata (e.g., timed metadata from the input) is passed through to the MediaPackage v2 output group, typically set to PASSTHROUGH or NO_PASSTHROUGH.
Determines whether Key-Length-Value (KLV) metadata from the input is passed through to the MediaPackage v2 output, with allowed values 'NO_PASSTHROUGH' and 'PASSTHROUGH'.
Determines whether Nielsen ID3 metadata is passed through from the input to the MediaPackage v2 output group, with values typically 'PASSTHROUGH' or 'NO_PASSTHROUGH'.
Determines how SCTE-35 ad signaling markers are handled in the MediaPackage v2 output group, such as passing them through (PASSTHROUGH) or removing them (NONE).
The segment length (in seconds) of each media segment that AWS MediaLive generates for the MediaPackage v2 output group, controlling the duration of packaged segments.
Specifies the unit of measure (SECONDS or MILLISECONDS) for the segment length setting of the MediaPackage v2 output group in AWS Elemental MediaLive.
Specifies the ID3 frame type (such as PRIV) that MediaLive uses to identify and pass through timed metadata from the input to the MediaPackage v2 output group.
Specifies the interval, in seconds, at which ID3 timed metadata is inserted into the output for the MediaPackage v2 output group.

Determines whether timed metadata (e.g., ID3 tags) is passed through to the MediaPackage v2 output, enabling or disabling the preservation of timing and metadata information in the streaming pipeline.
Configures the output group for Microsoft Smooth Streaming delivery, including settings for packaging and streaming your encoded output to an IIS Smooth Streaming endpoint.
Specifies the value of the `c:isLive` attribute in the Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest, which identifies the acquisition point for the stream.
Specifies whether MediaLive uses the configured clock or the input timecode for timecodes in audio-only outputs within the Microsoft Smooth Streaming output group.
Specifies whether to use a self-signed certificate or a certificate from a certificate authority (such as AWS Certificate Manager) for encrypting the Microsoft Smooth Streaming output.
Specifies the number of seconds MediaLive waits between retry attempts to re-establish a connection to the Microsoft Smooth Streaming destination after a connection failure.
Specifies the destination location, as a reference to one of the channel's configured destinations, where the Microsoft Smooth Streaming output group writes its output files.
DestinationRefId specifies the reference ID of the destination (from the channel's top-level Destinations list) that this Microsoft Smooth Streaming output group should publish to.
When the event ID mode is set to 'USE_EVENT_ID', this string serves as the event identifier that MediaLive inserts into the Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest for the output group.
Controls how the Microsoft Smooth Streaming event ID is assigned in the output group, either using the configured event ID or deriving it from the timestamp.
Determines whether MediaLive sends an end-of-stream (EOS) signal when the Microsoft Smooth event stops, with allowed values NONE or SEND_EOS.

Specifies the duration, in seconds, that MediaLive buffers file segments in the cache before writing them to the Microsoft Smooth Streaming output destination, controlling the trade-off between output latency and resilience to network interruptions.
Specifies the length in seconds of each media fragment in the Microsoft Smooth Streaming output group, controlling the fragment duration for the Smooth Streaming format.
Determines the MediaLive behavior when input loss occurs for the Microsoft Smooth Streaming output group, with options to emit output as-is or pause output entirely.
The number of times the encoder retries sending a chunk to the Microsoft Smooth Streaming endpoint before giving up.
Specifies the number of seconds to wait before restarting the encoder after a failure or error in the Microsoft Smooth Streaming output group.

Determines whether the Smooth Streaming output group uses the input source's existing segmentation (USE_INPUT_SEGMENTATION) or creates its own fixed-size segments (FIXED_SEGMENTATION), controlling how the output is chunked for Microsoft Smooth Streaming playback.
The number of milliseconds to delay the output to the Microsoft Smooth Streaming endpoint, allowing for buffering or time-shifting of the stream.
Specifies the type of sparse track to include in the Microsoft Smooth output, enabling insertion of SCTE-35 timed metadata when set to 'SCTE_35', or no sparse track when set to 'NONE'.

Determines whether MediaLive writes a separate manifest file for each stream in the Smooth Streaming output group (with 'PUT_MANIFEST') or only a single combined manifest (with 'DO_NOT_PUT_MANIFEST').

Specifies a millisecond value that MediaLive adds to the input timestamps for the Microsoft Smooth Streaming group, letting you offset the output timeline to compensate for time differences or synchronize with other outputs.
Specifies whether the Smooth Streaming output's timestamp offset is derived from the input ('FOLLOW_INPUT') or uses a fixed value from the 'timestamp_offset' field ('USE_CONFIGURED_OFFSET').
Settings for an AWS Elemental MediaLive Multiplex output group, configuring how the channel's outputs are delivered to a multiplex destination.

Settings for the RTMP output group, controlling authentication scheme, cache duration and length, caption data handling, input loss behavior, and restart delay when sending the stream to an RTMP destination.
Specifies the SCTE-35 ad markers (e.g., 'ON_CUE_POINT_SCTE35') that MediaLive inserts into the RTMP output group to signal ad insertion points.
Specifies the authentication scheme (AKAMAI or COMMON) used for RTMP output connections in this output group.
Determines how MediaLive reacts when the RTMP output buffer becomes full, either disconnecting immediately or waiting for the server to catch up.
Sets the duration in seconds that MediaLive buffers RTMP output data before transmitting it to the destination, smoothing network jitter.
Specifies how the RTMP output group handles caption data, with allowed values such as PASSTHROUGH to include captions and OMIT to exclude them.
Enables the insertion of filler NAL units into the RTMP output stream to maintain a consistent group of pictures (GOP) structure and bitrate.
Specifies whether to emit the last frame or drop the video when input loss is detected for this RTMP output group, with allowed values 'EMIT_OUTPUT' and 'DROP'.
Specifies the number of seconds MediaLive waits before attempting to reconnect to the RTMP destination after a connection loss or failure.
Specifies settings for an SRT output group in an AWS MediaLive channel, including the list of destination endpoints to which the stream is sent.
Specifies the action the SRT output group takes when the upstream input is lost, either dropping the producer (DROP_PRODUCER) or continuing to emit output (EMIT_OUTPUT).
Configure how the output is transmitted over UDP, including the action to take on input loss and the timing parameters for embedded ID3 timed metadata.

Specifies how the UDP output group handles input signal loss, where the value is either 'DROP_PACKETS' to discard data during loss or 'EMIT_PACKETS' to continue emitting packets, as defined in the AWS MediaLive UDP group settings.
Specifies the ID3 frame type used to embed timed metadata in the UDP output group's transport stream.
Specifies the interval in seconds at which ID3 timed metadata is inserted into the UDP output stream.

The outputs in an output group define each individual stream output, specifying its destination, encoding settings for video, audio, and captions, and other output-specific configuration in a MediaLive channel.
Specifies the list of audio description names (from the channel's audio_description definitions) to include in this output, determining which audio tracks are carried in the output's encoding.
Lists the names of the caption descriptions (defined at the encoder settings level) that should be attached to this output, controlling which captions are included in the output's media.
The name assigned to this output within the output group, used to identify and reference the output in the channel's configuration and downstream systems.

Defines the output-specific settings for a MediaLive channel output, which can be one of several types (e.g., archive, frame capture, HLS, MediaPackage, MS Smooth, RTMP, or UDP) and contains the corresponding nested configuration for that output type.

Archive output settings configure the container format (e.g., MP4) and the destination (such as an S3 bucket or MediaStore container) for delivering an archive (file-based) output from a MediaLive channel.
Configures the container format (e.g., MP4, M2TS, or RAW) for the archived output, including any container-specific parameters such as M2TS settings.
Specifies the M2TS container settings (such as PIDs, bitrate, and rate control) used when archiving the output to an MPEG-2 transport stream.
When set to DROP, the M2TS output omits audio packets entirely if no input audio is present; when set to ENCODE_SILENCE, it generates silent audio frames to maintain a continuous audio stream.
Whether to enable ARIB (Association of Radio Industries and Businesses) caption data in the M2TS output, used for Japanese digital broadcasting.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) to use for ARIB caption data in the M2TS container of this archive output.
Controls how the PID for ARIB captions is assigned in the M2TS container, either automatically by MediaLive or using the configured ARIB captions PID value.
Determines the audio buffer model (ATSC or DVB) for the M2TS output, controlling how audio data is buffered and timestamped within the transport stream.
Specifies the number of audio frames to include in each Packetized Elementary Stream (PES) packet for the M2TS output.
Specifies the packet identifiers (PIDs) for audio in the MPEG-2 transport stream output, as a single PID or a comma-separated list, overriding the default auto-assignment.
Sets the audio stream type in the M2TS container settings, with valid values ATSC or DVB, determining whether the audio stream is formatted for ATSC or DVB transport standards.

Specifies the target average bitrate in bits per second for the M2TS (MPEG-2 transport stream) container of this archive output, controlling the compressed size and quality of the stored video stream.
Determines the buffering model for the M2TS output, either MULTIPLEX for a multi-program transport stream or SINGLE_PLEX for a single-program transport stream.
Controls whether the M2TS output includes a closed caption descriptor in the PMT (Program Map Table), with 'ENABLED' inserting the descriptor and 'DISABLED' omitting it.

Configuration for the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) that MediaLive inserts into the M2TS container of this archive output, specifying parameters such as the network ID, network name, and repeat interval.
Sets the 16-bit network identifier broadcast in the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) for the M2TS container output.
Specifies the network name to be carried in the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) for the MPEG-2 transport stream.
Specifies the repetition interval, in seconds, for inserting the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) into the M2TS output within the archive output settings.
Configures the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) for the M2TS container, defining the service provider name, service name, and whether to embed the SDT in the output.
Determines the presence and initialization of the Service Description Table (SDT) in the M2TS output, with valid values including SDT_PRESENT, SDT_ABSENT, and SDT_PRESENT_AND_INIT_PACKETS.
Specifies the repetition interval (in milliseconds) between consecutive transmissions of the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) in the M2TS output.
The service name to be inserted into the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) in the MPEG-2 transport stream.
Specifies the service provider name inserted into the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) within the M2TS container, identifying the broadcaster or content provider.
Specifies one or more comma-separated DVB subtitle packet identifiers (PIDs) to embed in the M2TS container of the output.
Configures the DVB Time and Date Table (TDT) for the M2TS container, including an optional repetition interval for inserting time and date information into the transport stream.
Determines how often the DVB Time and Date Table (TDT) is repeated within the M2TS output, expressed in seconds or frames based on the associated 'rep_interval_unit' setting.
Sets the packet identifier (PID) for DVB Teletext in the M2TS container of an archive output, specified as a string value.
Specifies whether EBIF (Enhanced Binary Interchange Format) data is inserted into the M2TS output, with valid values of NONE to omit EBIF or PASSTHROUGH to pass through EBIF data from the input.

Specifies how often EBP (Encryption Boundary Point) packets are inserted into the audio stream when using M2TS container settings, either at both video PTS boundaries and fixed intervals (VIDEO_AND_FIXED_INTERVALS) or only at video PTS boundaries (VIDEO_INTERVAL).
The number of milliseconds to look ahead for placement of Elementary Buffer Period (EBP) metadata in the MPEG-TS output.

Determines where EBP (Extended Broadcasting Profile) markers are inserted in the M2TS transport stream, with values 'video_and_audio_pids' placing them in both video and audio PIDs or 'video_pid' placing them only in the video PID, affecting SCTE-35 message signaling.
Specifies the PID (Packet Identifier) used for Entitlement Control Messages (ECMs) in the MPEG-2 transport stream, which carry conditional access scrambling information.
Controls whether the elementary stream rate is written into the PES (Packetized Elementary Stream) packets of the MPEG-2 transport stream output, set to either 'INCLUDE' or 'EXCLUDE'.
Sets the PID (packet identifier) for the Enhanced TV (ETV) platform data within the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
The PID (packet identifier) for the Enhanced TV (ETV) signal in the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
The duration, in seconds, of each MPEG-2 TS fragment emitted by the M2TS container, used for archive or output segmentation.

For the M2TS container settings in an archive output group, this field controls whether KLV (Key-Length-Value) metadata is passed through to the transport stream output, accepting values such as 'PASSTHROUGH' or 'NONE'.
Specifies one or more PIDs (packet identifiers) used for KLV (Key-Length-Value) metadata in the MPEG-TS output, enabling embedding of SMPTE KLV data in the stream.
Determines whether Nielsen ID3 metadata is passed through in the M2TS container, with PASSTHROUGH to preserve the tags or NO_PASSTHROUGH to strip them from the archived output.
Specifies the bitrate (in bits per second) of null packets to insert into the MPEG-2 transport stream to maintain the output bitrate when the input bitrate is lower.
Specifies the interval, in seconds, between Program Association Table (PAT) packets in the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
Determines whether Program Clock Reference (PCR) packets are inserted at a configured period or in every packet, with valid values 'CONFIGURED_PCR_PERIOD' or 'PCR_EVERY_PACKET'.
Specifies the interval in milliseconds between Program Clock Reference (PCR) packets inserted into the M2TS transport stream.
The PID (packet identifier) for the Program Clock Reference (PCR) in the output MPEG-2 transport stream, used to synchronize decoder timing.
Sets the interval in seconds between Program Map Table (PMT) packets in the MPEG-TS multiplex, controlling how frequently the receiver can acquire program tuning information.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) used for the Program Map Table (PMT) in the MPEG-2 transport stream output of the M2TS container.
Specifies the program number for the MPEG-2 transport stream, identifying this output's program within a multiplexed stream.
Specifies whether the M2TS output uses constant bitrate (CBR) or variable bitrate (VBR) encoding.
Specifies the SCTE-27 packet identifiers (PIDs) for ad cue messages in the MPEG-2 transport stream, provided as a comma-separated list of PID numbers.
Controls whether SCTE-35 ad signaling messages are passed through (PASSTHROUGH) or discarded (NONE) in the MPEG-2 Transport Stream output for this M2TS container.
Sets the Packet Identifier (PID) for SCTE-35 messages in the MPEG-TS stream, used to carry ad signaling cues.
Adjusts the timing of SCTE-35 splice events in the M2TS output by the specified number of milliseconds, where a positive value shifts the event earlier (preroll) and a negative value shifts it later.
Controls whether SCTE-35 segmentation markers are passed through from the input or disabled in the M2TS output for this archive output group.

Controls how timestamps are handled across MPEG-2 TS segments in the archive output, either maintaining correlation between segments (MAINTAIN_CORRELATION) or resetting the timestamps at the start of each segment (RESET_CORRELATION).
Specifies the duration in seconds of each MPEG-2 transport stream segment within the M2TS container, controlling how the archive output is segmented into timed chunks.
Controls whether timed metadata (such as ID3) is passed through from the input to this M2TS output, with allowed values PASSTHROUGH or NO_PASSTHROUGH.
Specifies the PID (packet identifier) used for the timed metadata stream (for example, SCTE-35 messages) within the MPEG-2 transport stream (M2TS) container for this archive output.
Sets the transport stream identifier (TSID) carried in the MPEG-TS header of the M2TS output, distinguishing this stream from other multiplexed streams.
The packet identifier (PID) assigned to the video stream in the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
Configures the archive output container to use raw storage, meaning the encoded video/audio is written without any container wrapper or multiplexing, preserving the elementary streams as-is.
The file extension (e.g., .ts, .mp4) applied to the archive output file generated for this output group in MediaLive.
Appends a custom string to the base file name of the archived media output, enabling multiple outputs in the same archive group to have unique file names.
Specifies the destination endpoint (URL) and optional authentication credentials used by the MediaLive channel to push CMAF-chunked output to a remote CMAF ingest receiver.
Appends the specified text as a suffix to the output file names of the CMAF Ingest output, allowing you to customize or differentiate the generated segments and manifests.
Specifies the capture interval and its units (milliseconds or seconds) for a frame capture output in a MediaLive channel output group.
Adds a custom string that is incorporated into the file names of frame capture outputs, letting you label or differentiate the generated image files.

Specifies the HLS-specific packaging settings for this output, including the choice of standard or audio-only HLS variant via nested HlsSettings and optional name/segment modifiers that affect the generated HTTP Live Streaming segment file naming.
Specifies whether H.265/HEVC outputs are packaged as HEV1 or HVC1 in the HLS output.
Specifies which HLS output variant (standard, audio-only, fragmented MP4, or frame-capture) applies to this output and configures the associated settings for that variant.
Configures an audio-only rendition for an HLS output group, specifying the audio group ID, segment control method, and optional audio stream selection or cover image.
Assigns an identifier to the audio-only rendition group in the HLS manifest, enabling the player to group related audio tracks together.

Configures the image shown as the placeholder video track for the audio-only HLS rendition, specified as an InputLocation identifying a JPEG file (typically in Amazon S3) that MediaLive uses for the video representation of the audio-only variant.
The Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter that holds the password required to access the audio-only image file specified in the URI, used for the audio-only HLS rendition.
The URI (e.g., an Amazon S3 or HTTP URL) of the JPEG or PNG image that MediaLive displays in place of video frames when producing an audio-only HLS output.
The username used for basic HTTP authentication when MediaLive retrieves the audio-only image from the specified URI (the audio_only_image input location).

Determines whether the HLS audio-only output uses the alternate audio auto-select track type (ALTERNATE_AUDIO_AUTO_SELECT) or the default track type (ALTERNATE_AUDIO_AUTO_SELECT_DEFAULT), controlling how the audio rendition is signaled in the HLS master playlist.
Specifies the segment type for the audio-only HLS output, selecting either 'AAC' or 'TS' as the format of the media segments.
Configures the fragmented MP4 (fMP4) container settings for an HLS output group, including options for audio rendition sets and timed metadata handling.

Specifies the audio rendition sets (a comma-separated list of audio group identifiers) to include in the FMP4 HLS output, determining which audio tracks from the channel input are carried in this output group.
Specifies how AWS Elemental MediaLive handles Nielsen ID3 tags in the FMP4 HLS output, where INSERT adds tags at specified times and NO_TAG suppresses them.
Determines whether timed metadata (e.g., ID3 tags) is passed through to the fragmented MP4 HLS output, with allowed values PASSTHROUGH and NO_PASSTHROUGH.
This configuration block indicates that the HLS output is a frame-capture HLS output; it has no child arguments and its presence selects the FrameCaptureHlsSettings variant for the HLS settings.
Contains the configuration for standard HLS output mode, including the M3U8 container settings and optional audio rendition sets used when the HLS output group is not using MediaStore.
Specifies the comma-separated list of audio rendition set IDs (for example, program_audio) that MediaLive includes as audio-only renditions in the HLS output group.
Defines the M3U8 manifest and playlist settings, such as timing metadata, PID controls, and segment handling, for the HLS output in MediaLive.
The number of audio frames to include in each PES (Packetized Elementary Stream) packet for the HLS output; set to 0 to have AWS MediaLive automatically determine the appropriate value.
Specifies the audio PIDs (packet identifiers) to include in the M3U8 manifest, as a comma-separated string of PID values.
The PID (Packet Identifier) for Entitlement Control Messages (ECM) in the MPEG-2 transport stream, used for conditional access/encryption in the HLS output.
Specifies whether KLV (Key-Length-Value) metadata is passed through to the output (PASSTHROUGH) or ignored (NO_PASSTHROUGH) when generating the HLS M3U8 manifest.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) for the Key-Length-Value (KLV) data stream in the MPEG-TS multiplex of the HLS output, used to carry ancillary metadata such as subtitles or timing data.
Determines whether Nielsen ID3 metadata from the source is passed through or removed in the HLS M3U8 output, with allowed values PASSTHROUGH and NO_PASSTHROUGH.
The number of seconds between insertions of the Program Association Table (PAT) in the MPEG-TS output of the HLS stream.
Determines how often the Program Clock Reference (PCR) is inserted in the HLS output, either in every PES packet (PCR_EVERY_PES) or at a configured period (CONFIGURED_PCR_PERIOD).
