Specifies the interval, in milliseconds, between Program Clock Reference (PCR) packets inserted in the HLS output m3u8 stream.
Specifies the PID (Packet ID) for the Program Clock Reference (PCR) in the MPEG-2 transport stream output of the HLS m3u8 settings.
Specifies the interval in seconds between Program Map Table (PMT) packets in the MPEG-TS output, controlling how frequently the PMT is repeated to aid channel tuning.
Specifies the PID (Packet Identifier) value for the Program Map Table (PMT) in the MPEG-TS segments of the HLS output.
Sets the program number for the MPEG-2 transport stream in the HLS output, used in the m3u8 playlist to identify the program.
Specifies how SCTE-35 messages are handled in the HLS M3U8 manifest, with values NO_PASSTHROUGH, PASSTHROUGH, or AD_MARKERS (where AD_MARKERS converts cues to ad markers).
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) for SCTE-35 ad signaling messages in the MPEG-TS segments of the HLS output, enabling downstream players to recognize and act on ad cues.
Specifies whether ID3 timed metadata is passed through (PASSTHROUGH) or ignored (NO_PASSTHROUGH) in the HLS M3U8 output.
Sets the packet identifier (PID) in the MPEG-TS segments for timed metadata (such as ID3) in the HLS output's m3u8 settings.
Specifies the Transport Stream ID used in MPEG-TS packet headers for the M3U8 output in this HLS output group.
Sets the packet identifier (PID) for the video stream in the MPEG-2 transport stream segments generated by the HLS output.

The name modifier string is prepended to the filenames of HLS output segments and playlists generated by this output group, allowing you to customize or disambiguate object names in the destination bucket.
Specifies a string that is appended to the segment duration in the HLS media playlist to fine-tune the reported duration of each segment, commonly used to adjust for rounding or discontinuities.

The connected_router_inputs field lists the MediaConnect input ARNs that are attached to the MediaConnect router used for this output, enabling MediaLive to route the encoded channel output through that router to those connected inputs.
The ARN of the AWS Elemental MediaConnect router input to connect to pipeline 0 for this output.
Specifies the MediaConnect router input ARN (or identifier) to connect to for pipeline 1 (the first redundant pipeline) in this MediaLive output.
Defines the container format settings for the MediaLive output that is routed to an AWS Elemental MediaConnect flow.
The M2TS container settings for this MediaConnect output, defining MPEG-2 transport stream encapsulation parameters such as packetization, PIDs, and buffer model.
Controls how the M2TS encoder handles input audio that is absent, either dropping the audio from the output or encoding silence (valid values: DROP or ENCODE_SILENCE).
Controls whether ARIB (Association of Radio Industries and Businesses) captions are enabled or disabled in the MPEG-2 transport stream output from AWS MediaLive.
Sets the packet identifier (PID) for ARIB caption data carried in the MPEG-2 transport stream.

Controls how the PID for ARIB (Japanese broadcast) captions is assigned in the M2TS container, either automatically by MediaLive or using the configured PID value (valid values: AUTO, USE_CONFIGURED).
Specifies the audio buffer model (ATSC or DVB) used for the M2TS container, which controls the buffer size for audio payloads in the transport stream.
Number of audio frames to include in each Packetized Elementary Stream (PES) packet for the M2TS container output.
Specifies the comma-separated list of program IDs (PIDs) for the audio streams to include in the MPEG-TS container output.
Configures the audio stream type (ATSC, DVB, or MPEG) for the MPEG-2 transport stream (M2TS) output within the MediaConnect router output settings.
The target output bitrate in bits per second for the MPEG-2 transport stream generated by the M2TS container settings in a MediaConnect output group.
Determines the buffering model for the MPEG-2 transport stream output, with allowed values 'MULTIPLEX' or 'TRANSPORT_STREAM'.
Specifies the closed caption descriptor value (such as CC1, CC2, or SERVICE1) to insert into the M2TS container's PMT for the output, identifying the caption service carried in the stream.
Configures the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) that MediaLive inserts into the M2TS transport stream, specifying network ID, network name, and repetition interval.
Specifies the network ID (network_id) used in the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) for the M2TS output, identifying the broadcast network to which the service belongs.
Specifies the network name string included in the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) for the M2TS output, used to identify the broadcast network.
Defines the repetition interval, in seconds, for emitting the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) in the M2TS output.
Configures the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) for the M2TS output, controlling whether the SDT is included, its repetition interval, and the service provider and service name identifiers.

Determines whether the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) is emitted in the M2TS stream, and if so, whether it follows the current program or is absent entirely, using the allowed values SDT_PRESENT, SDT_ABSENT, or SDT_FOLLOWING.
Specifies the repetition interval in seconds between consecutive DVB Service Description Table (SDT) messages in the M2TS container for this MediaLive channel output group.
Specifies the service name to include in the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) for the M2TS output, used to identify the service to receivers.
Specifies the service provider name that is inserted into the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) of the M2TS container output.
The dvb_sub_pids field specifies a comma-separated list of packet identifiers (PIDs) for DVB subtitle streams to be included in the M2TS output container.
Configures the DVB Time and Date Table (TDT) insertion into the M2TS output, including the repetition interval between TDT packets.
The repetition interval in seconds at which the DVB Time and Date Table (TDT) is inserted into the M2TS output.
The packet ID (PID) used for DVB Teletext data in the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
Specifies the EBIF (Enhanced TV Binary Interchange Format) data to embed in the M2TS output, enabling interactive television services.
Specifies whether audio EBP markers are inserted only at video intervals (VIDEO_INTERVAL) or at both video and fixed intervals (VIDEO_AND_FIXED_INTERVALS) in the M2TS output.

Specifies the number of milliseconds to look ahead for Elementary Buffer Period (EBP) placement in the M2TS output, controlling how much buffer time is allowed before the EBP packet is inserted relative to the video frames.

Determines where Elementary Bitstream Priority (EBP) markers are placed within the M2TS transport stream, controlling whether they appear only on packets containing video and audio PSI or additionally on every ancillary packet.
PID for the Entitlement Control Message (ECM), which carries conditional access control data in the MPEG-TS output.
Determines whether the elementary stream (ES) rate is written into the Packetized Elementary Stream (PES) header, with allowed values 'NO' and 'YES'.
Sets the packet identifier (PID) for the ETV (Enhanced TV) platform signal in the M2TS container output.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) for the Enhanced TV (ETV) signal in the MPEG-2 transport stream output configured by these M2TS settings.
Specifies the length, in seconds, of each MPEG-2 transport stream fragment generated by the M2TS container, controlling the segmentation interval for the output.
Controls whether KLV (SMPTE 2038) metadata is passed through from the input to the output, with valid values PASSTHROUGH and NO_PASSTHROUGH.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) for the KLV (Key-Length-Value) data stream in the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
Controls how Nielsen ID3 metadata is handled in the M2TS container output, with valid values like PASSTHROUGH, NO_PASSTHROUGH, CALLER_APP, or FINAL_PASSTHROUGH.
Sets the bitrate, in bits per second, at which null packets are inserted into the M2TS transport stream to maintain a constant output bitrate.
The interval in milliseconds between program association table (PAT) insertions in the M2TS output, which is used by decoders to locate the program map table (PMT) for a transport stream.
Sets how PCR (Program Clock Reference) packets are inserted in the M2TS output, either at a configured interval or on every PES packet.
Number of milliseconds between insertions of Program Clock Reference (PCR) packets into the MPEG-2 transport stream, used by the decoder to recover the encoder's timing.
Sets the PID for Program Clock Reference (PCR) packets, which carry timing information for the MPEG-2 transport stream and enable the receiver to synchronize its clock with the encoder.
pmt_interval specifies the interval, in milliseconds, between successive Program Map Table (PMT) packets in the MPEG-2 transport stream for this M2TS container output.
Sets the PID (Packet Identifier) for the Program Map Table (PMT) in the M2TS container, determining which packet carries the PMT in the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
Defines the MPEG-TS program number for the M2TS output, identifying which program in the transport stream is selected by the receiver (e.g., MediaConnect) when multiple programs are multiplexed.
Sets the bitrate control mode for the M2TS output, either constant bitrate (CBR) or variable bitrate (VBR).
Sets the packet identifier (PID) used for SCTE-27 messages within the M2TS output container.
Determines whether SCTE-35 messages from the input are passed through (PASSTHROUGH) or discarded (NONE) in the M2TS container for this MediaConnect router output.
Sets the PID (packet identifier) used for SCTE-35 messages in the M2TS output.

This field specifies the number of milliseconds by which the SCTE-35 preroll time is pulled up (moved earlier) in the M2TS container output, which adjusts the timing of SCTE-35 event insertion relative to the splice point.
Specifies which segmentation markers (such as NONE, TIMESTAMP, PCR, TIME, EBP, or EBP_LEGACY) are inserted into the MPEG-2 transport stream to control packetization for ad insertion or recording.

The segmentation_style field controls how segmentation messages are inserted into the MPEG-2 transport stream for MediaLive M2TS outputs, with valid values such as 'maintains-cadence' for regular interval insertion or 'separated-segmentation' for segment-boundary insertion.
Specifies the duration (in milliseconds) of each MPEG-TS segment in the M2TS container, controlling segment boundaries for downstream packaging (such as HLS).
Determines whether timed metadata (such as ID3) is passed through or stripped from the M2TS output, with valid values of PASSTHROUGH or NO_PASSTHROUGH.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) for the timed metadata stream (such as ID3) carried in the M2TS output, overriding the default value when set.
Sets the 16-bit transport stream identifier (TSID) carried in the MPEG-2 transport stream headers of the M2TS output.
The packet identifier (PID) used for the video stream in the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
The ARN of the MediaConnect flow that serves as the destination for this MediaConnect router output.
Specifies the settings for an output that is sent to AWS Elemental MediaPackage; this object is empty and serves only to indicate MediaPackage as the output destination.
Configures the destination for MediaPackage v2 outputs by specifying the channel group and channel name to which the encoder sends the packaged stream.
Specifies the audio group ID that MediaLive assigns to the audio tracks of this output, grouping them under a shared identifier in the MediaPackage v2 asset.
Specifies the audio rendition sets to include in the MediaPackage v2 output, as a comma-separated string of rendition set names.
Sets whether MediaLive automatically selects the HLS output stream for the MediaPackage v2 destination, with typical values like 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
The default HLS manifest URL for the MediaPackage v2 destination, which specifies the endpoint to which MediaLive publishes the packaged HLS stream.
Settings for a Microsoft Smooth Streaming output, controlling parameters such as bitrate, buffer duration, and stream naming.
Specifies the H.265 packaging type (HEV1 or HVC1) used for the Microsoft Smooth Streaming output, controlling how H.265 video is encapsulated for compatibility with Smooth Streaming players.
Specifies a string appended to the end of the output file name for Microsoft Smooth Streaming outputs, helping to create unique file names or apply custom naming conventions.
Configures the destination and program reference for sending this output to an AWS Elemental MediaLive Multiplex, enabling the output to be combined into an MPTS stream.
Specifies the container format and its configuration for the multiplex output, namely the M2TS multiplex container settings that control how the MPEG-2 transport stream is packaged for broadcast.

Configures the M2TS (MPEG-2 Transport Stream) container settings for the multiplex output, controlling packetization details such as PID mappings and buffer model when delivering to an AWS MediaLive Multiplex.
Specifies whether to drop the audio or encode silence when input audio is absent in the multiplex M2TS output.
Controls the audio buffer model used for smoothing audio bitrate fluctuations in the multiplex M2TS output (e.g., ATSC or DVB).
Specifies the number of audio frames to include in each Packetized Elementary Stream (PES) packet for the multiplex M2TS output.
Determines whether the multiplex M2TS output uses the default audio stream or an alternate audio stream.
Specifies whether to include the closed caption descriptor in the MPEG-2 transport stream multiplex output, with allowed values 'DISABLED' or 'ENABLED'.
Specifies whether EBIF (Enhanced Binary Interchange Format) data is included in the M2TS multiplex output, with values NONE to omit it or PASSTHROUGH to pass through EBIF data from the input.
Specifies whether the elementary stream rate is included in the PES (Packetized Elementary Stream) header for the M2TS multiplex output, with value ENABLED or DISABLED.
Specifies how Key-Length-Value (KLV) metadata is handled in the multiplexed M2TS container, where 'PASSTHROUGH' passes KLV data through from the input and 'NONE' discards it.
Determines whether Nielsen ID3 metadata is passed through from the input to the multiplex M2TS output, with valid values including PASSTHROUGH and NO_PASSTHROUGH.
Controls the timing for sending Program Clock Reference (PCR) packets in the M2TS multiplex output, either at a configured period or on every packet.
Specifies the Program Clock Reference (PCR) period in milliseconds between PCR packets in the multiplexed MPEG-2 transport stream.
Specifies whether SCTE-35 messages are passed through (PASSTHROUGH) or ignored (NONE) in the multiplex M2TS output.
Specifies the number of milliseconds by which SCTE-35 preroll events are pulled up (advanced) in the multiplex M2TS output, adjusting the timing of these events relative to the program timeline.
Configures the destination of the multiplex output, specifying the MediaConnect flow ARN where the multiplexed video is delivered.
Specifies the destination reference ID for a multiplex output, identifying the multiplex program destination to which this output is routed.
Specifies the RTMP-specific output parameters, such as the destination URL/stream key and connection retry behavior, for a MediaLive output group.

Determines whether the RTMP output verifies the authenticity of the server's SSL certificate (VERIFY_AUTHENTICITY) or accepts any self-signed certificate (SELF_SIGNED) when connecting to a secure RTMP endpoint.
Number of seconds to wait before retrying an RTMP output connection after a connection failure.
Specifies the destination URL and stream key for the RTMP output, defining where the media stream is published.
Identifies a named destination from the output group's destinations list, allowing this RTMP output to share that destination configuration (e.g., the same URL) with other outputs.
Specifies the number of times MediaLive retries sending data to the RTMP destination before treating the output as failed.

Specifies the SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) protocol-specific output settings for this output, including the SRT destination address and transport configuration, within the MediaLive channel's encoder settings.
Specifies the size of the SRT output buffer in milliseconds, which controls the amount of data buffered before transmission and thus influences the target latency of the SRT stream.
The container settings for the SRT output, which define how the encoded audio and video are encapsulated (e.g., MPEG-TS configuration) before transmission over SRT.
Configures the MPEG-2 Transport Stream (M2TS) container settings for the SRT output, controlling parameters like packet timing, PID mapping, and buffering behavior.
Controls whether missing input audio is dropped or replaced with a silent audio track when encoding the MPEG-TS output, with allowed values 'DROP' and 'ENCODE_SILENCE'.
Controls whether ARIB (Japanese broadcasting standard) caption data is included in the MPEG-2 Transport Stream output, with 'ENABLED' including the captions and 'DISABLED' excluding them.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) used for ARIB caption data within the MPEG-2 transport stream.
Controls whether the ARIB caption PID is automatically selected (AUTO) or uses the configured PID value (USE_CONFIGURED).
Determines the model used for audio buffering in the M2TS container, with allowed values such as 'ATSC' or 'DVB' that adjust the audio buffer size and timing for the output.
Specifies the number of audio frames to include in each PES (Packetized Elementary Stream) packet within the MPEG-2 transport stream output for the SRT output group.
Specifies the packet identifiers (PIDs) for the audio elementary streams in the MPEG-2 transport stream, as a comma-separated string.
Specifies the MPEG-2 audio stream type (ATSC or DVB) used for the M2TS container in this SRT output.
Sets the target bitrate (in bits per second) for the MPEG-2 transport stream (M2TS) container used in this SRT output group.
Determines the buffering model for the M2TS container in the SRT output, accepting 'MULTIPLEX' to apply a multiplex buffer or 'NONE' to disable buffering.
Determines whether the MPEG-2 transport stream output includes a closed caption descriptor (set to 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED') for the SRT output's M2TS container settings.
Configures the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) parameters for the MPEG-2 transport stream, including network name, network ID, and repacketing interval.
Sets the network identifier (network_id) that is inserted into the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) of the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
The network name that MediaLive inserts into the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) for the transport stream.
Specifies the repetition interval in seconds for inserting the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) into the M2TS output stream.
This field configures the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) for the MPEG-2 transport stream output, controlling parameters such as the SDT emission interval and the inclusion of the network name.
Determines whether the output carries the DVB Service Description Table (SDT), with values such as SDT_PRESENT, SDT_ABSENT, or SDT_FOLLOW_INPUT.
Specifies the repetition interval (in seconds) between successive transmissions of the DVB SDT (Service Description Table) in the M2TS container output.
Specifies the service name that MediaLive inserts into the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) for the M2TS output.
Sets the service provider name (as defined in DVB standards) that is inserted into the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) for the M2TS output.
Specifies the DVB Subtitle PIDs (as a comma-separated string) to be included in the MPEG-2 transport stream output for the M2TS container settings.
Specifies the DVB Time and Date Table (TDT) settings for the MPEG-2 transport stream, such as the repetition interval for how often the TDT packets are inserted.
Specifies the repetition interval in seconds between successive DVB Time and Date Table (TDT) packets inserted into the M2TS output.
Sets the packet identifier (PID) for DVB teletext in the M2TS container settings applied to the SRT output, enabling inclusion of teletext subtitles.
Determines whether EBIF (Enhanced Broadcast Interconnect Format) data from the input is passed through to the M2TS output, with valid values of NONE or PASSTHROUGH.
Specifies the interval at which audio EBP markers are inserted, with choices for video intervals only or video plus fixed intervals.
Adjusts the lookahead time in milliseconds used for aligning Elementary Buffer Period (EBP) markers in the MPEG-2 Transport Stream output.
Specifies whether the Extended Broadcast Profile (EBP) is placed on both the video and audio PIDs or only on the video PID of the M2TS transport stream.
Sets the PID (packet identifier) used for the Entitlement Control Message (ECM) in the MPEG-TS output.
In the MPEG-TS container settings, this value controls whether the elementary stream rate is written into the Packetized Elementary Stream (PES) header.
The PID (packet identifier) for the Enhanced TV (ETV) platform, identifying the interactive TV data stream within the MPEG-2 transport stream of the M2TS output.
Sets the packet identifier (PID) for the Enhanced TV (ETV) signal within the MPEG-2 transport stream (M2TS) output.
Sets the duration, in seconds, of each MPEG-2 TS fragment emitted in the M2TS container for this SRT output, controlling the segmentation granularity for delivery.
Specifies the KLV (Key-Length-Value) data handling in the M2TS container, with valid values NONE (ignore KLV) or PASSTHROUGH (pass KLV data through).
Specifies the packet IDs (PIDs) on which KLV (Key-Length-Value) metadata is carried in the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
Specifies whether Nielsen ID3 metadata from the input is passed through to the output (PASSTHROUGH) or ignored (NO_PASSTHROUGH) in the M2TS container of this SRT output.
Sets the rate (in bits per second) at which null packets are inserted into the M2TS container of the SRT output to maintain a constant bitrate.

The `pat_interval` field specifies the number of seconds between insertions of the Program Association Table (PAT) in the M2TS transport stream, controlling how frequently the decoder receives this table for program mapping.

Specifies whether the M2TS encoder inserts a Program Clock Reference (PCR) in every transport stream packet (pcr_every_packet) or at the interval set by the PCR period (configured_pcr_period) to help synchronize the decoder's clock.

The `pcr_period` field specifies the interval in milliseconds between Program Clock Reference (PCR) packets inserted into the MPEG transport stream, which synchronizes decoder timing in the M2TS output.
Sets the Packet ID (PID) for the Program Clock Reference (PCR) packets in the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
The number of milliseconds between instances of the Program Map Table (PMT) in the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
Sets the Packet Identifier (PID) used for the Program Map Table (PMT) in the M2TS output stream.
Assigns the MPEG-2 transport stream program number to the M2TS container used for the SRT output.
Sets the rate control mode for the M2TS output to either constant bitrate (CBR) or variable bitrate (VBR).
Specifies the Packet Identifier (PID) used for SCTE-27 messages within the M2TS container settings for this SRT output group.
Controls whether SCTE-35 ad signaling messages are passed through (PASSTHROUGH) or omitted (NONE) from the output MPEG-2 transport stream in this M2TS container.
Specifies the PID (Packet Identifier) used for SCTE-35 messages in the MPEG-2 transport stream output of the MediaLive channel.
Specifies the number of milliseconds to pull up (shift earlier) the SCTE-35 preroll timing in the M2TS container, enabling alignment of ad insertion cues for downstream processing.
Specifies how MPEG-TS segmentation markers (e.g., SCTE-35 ad cues) are inserted into the M2TS output, typically as NONE, PAS_THROUGH, or SCTE35_ESAM.
Determines the segmentation cadence behavior for the M2TS output, allowing either 'maintain-cadence' to keep a fixed interval or 'reset-cadence' to reset at each new segment.
Specifies the duration, in seconds, of each MPEG2-TS segment for segmented outputs, controlling how frequently the M2TS container is split into segments for SRT delivery.
Specifies how MediaLive handles timed metadata in the M2TS container for the SRT output, either passing it through ('PASSTHROUGH') or suppressing it ('NO_PASSTHROUGH').
Assigns the packet identifier (PID) for timed ID3 metadata packets in the MPEG-2 transport stream output, controlling where timed metadata is embedded in the M2TS container.
Sets the MPEG-2 transport stream ID (TSID) for the MPEG-TS output, used in the transport stream header.
Specifies the MPEG-2 Transport Stream Packet Identifier (PID) used for the video elementary stream within the M2TS container of the SRT output.

For this SRT output, the destination object references an output destination (an SRT endpoint URL) defined in the enclosing output group's Destinations list, directing where MediaLive sends the stream.
The reference ID of a pre-defined SRT destination in the channel's destination configuration, used to route the output packets instead of specifying a direct URL.
Specifies whether the SRT output uses AES-128 encryption or is unencrypted, with values 'AES128' or 'UNENCRYPTED'.
The latency (in milliseconds) for the SRT output, setting the target delay to compensate for network jitter and ensure reliable stream delivery.
Configures the UDP output destination (address and port) along with container settings (such as M2TS), FEC, and buffer timing for the MediaLive output group.
Specifies the size of the buffer in milliseconds that the UDP output uses to absorb network jitter before sending packets to the destination.
Specifies the container settings (such as M2TS parameters) for the UDP output stream, controlling how the output is packetized.
Configures the MPEG-2 transport stream (M2TS) container settings for the UDP output, controlling PID assignments, buffer model, and other multiplexing parameters.
Specifies how MediaLive handles moments when input audio is absent: DROP removes the audio, while ENCODE_SILENCE inserts silence to keep the output continuous.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) for ARIB (Association of Radio Industries and Businesses) data in the MPEG-2 transport stream, typically used for Japanese broadcast captions.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) used for ARIB caption data in the MPEG-2 transport stream of this UDP output container settings.
Controls whether MediaLive automatically assigns the PID for ARIB captions (AUTO) or uses the explicitly configured PID from the arib_captions_pid field (USE_CONFIGURED) when encoding to M2TS.

Sets the audio buffer model for the MPEG-2 transport stream (M2TS) output, with valid values ATSC (default) or DVB, which affects how the audio buffer is sized and managed in the MediaLive UDP output.
Sets the number of audio frames to include in each Packetized Elementary Stream (PES) packet for M2TS output, controlling the packetization of audio data in the container.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) for audio in the MPEG-2 transport stream output, provided as a decimal value or a comma-separated list of decimal values.
Specifies the audio stream type (ATSC or DVB) to be used in the M2TS container for the UDP output group.
Specifies the bitrate of the M2TS transport stream (in bits per second) for the UDP output.
Specifies the buffer model for the M2TS multiplex, determining whether multiplex buffering is used (valid values are MULTIPLEX or NONE).
Configures the closed caption descriptor (such as CC1 or CC2) to be inserted into the M2TS output, specifying which line 21 caption service the captions are associated with.
Configures the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) insertion in the MPEG-2 transport stream, allowing you to set the network ID, network name, and repetition interval.
Sets the network ID (network_id) in the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) for the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
The network name that MediaLive inserts into the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) in the M2TS output.
The repetition interval in seconds for the DVB Network Information Table (NIT) inserted into the M2TS output.
Controls insertion of the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) in the MPEG-2 transport stream, allowing configuration of SDT presence, repetition interval, service provider name, and service name.
Specifies how the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) is output in the M2TS container, with valid values such as SDT_TABLE_AND_PACKETS, SDT_TABLE_ONLY, or NONE.
The interval in seconds between Service Description Table (SDT) messages in the DVB transport stream.
Specifies the service name to be included in the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) within the M2TS container output for the UDP output group.
Specifies the service provider name to insert into the DVB Service Description Table (SDT) carried in the M2TS output.
Specifies the DVB Subtitle packet identifiers (PIDs) from the input to include in the MPEG-2 transport stream output, provided as a string of one or more comma-separated PIDs.
Configures the DVB Time and Date Table (TDT) insertion for the M2TS output, specifying how often the table is repeated.
Repetition interval in seconds for the DVB Time and Date Table (TDT) carried in the M2TS output.
Sets the packet identifier (PID) used for DVB Teletext in the M2TS output.
Enables or disables the Elementary Buffer Input Filter (EBIF), which smooths the output bitrate of the M2TS stream; valid values are ENABLED or DISABLED.

Specifies the interval at which EBP (Extended Broadcast Profile) audio access units are inserted in the M2TS output, with valid values 'VIDEO_AND_FIXED_INTERVALS' or 'VIDEO_INTERVAL' to control whether EBP audio packets align with video frames only or also with fixed time intervals.
Specifies the number of milliseconds of lookahead to use for Extended Base Packet (EBP) insertion in the M2TS output, where 0 disables lookahead.
Determines whether the EBP (Extended Broadcast Profile) marker is placed in the video or audio stream of the M2TS output.
Sets the Packet Identifier (PID) for the Entitlement Control Message (ECM) in the M2TS container output, used for conditional access systems.
Controls whether the elementary stream (ES) rate is included in the Packetized Elementary Stream (PES) header for the M2TS container output, typically set to 'NO' or 'YES'.
Sets the packet identifier (PID) for Enhanced TV (ETV) platform data in the M2TS output.
Sets the packet identifier (PID) for the Enhanced TV (ETV) data stream in the MPEG-2 transport stream, allowing you to override the default PID that MediaLive uses.
Sets the duration in seconds of each MPEG-TS fragment when fragmented MPEG-TS output is enabled, typically used for HLS or CloudFront delivery.
Specifies whether to pass through Key Length Value (KLV) metadata in the M2TS container of the UDP output, with valid values of 'NONE' (discard) or 'PASSTHROUGH' (pass through).
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) used for multiplexing KLV (Key-Length-Value) metadata, such as STANAG 4609, into the M2TS container in the UDP output.
Specifies how Nielsen ID3 metadata is handled in the M2TS transport stream output, typically controlling whether the metadata is passed through from the input or ignored.
Specifies the bitrate (in bits per second) at which null packets are inserted into the MPEG-2 transport stream, used to maintain a constant output bitrate.
Specifies the interval, in seconds, between insertions of the Program Association Table (PAT) in the MPEG-2 transport stream output for this M2TS container settings.

Determines whether the MPEG-2 transport stream inserts a Program Clock Reference (PCR) in every packet (PCR_EVERY_PACKET) or only at the configured PCR interval (CONFIGURED_PCR_PERIOD) for MediaLive's M2TS output.
Sets the interval in milliseconds between Program Clock Reference (PCR) packets in the MPEG-2 transport stream, used by receivers to synchronize and recover the system clock.
The PID (packet identifier) for the Program Clock Reference (PCR) in the MPEG-2 transport stream, which can be set to a specific value or left as 'AUTO' for MediaLive to assign automatically.
Specifies the interval in seconds between Program Map Table (PMT) insertions in the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
Sets the PID (Packet Identifier) for the Program Map Table (PMT) in the M2TS container, controlling where PMT packets are placed in the UDP output stream.
The MPEG-2 transport stream program number assigned to this M2TS output, identifying the program within the transport stream.
Specifies whether the M2TS output uses constant bitrate (CBR) or variable bitrate (VBR) rate control.
Sets the packet identifier (PID) or comma-separated list of PIDs used for SCTE-27 messages carried in the MPEG-2 transport stream output.
Specifies how SCTE-35 ad markers are handled in the M2TS output, with PASSTHROUGH carrying them from the input and NONE stripping them.
Specifies the PID (packet identifier) used for SCTE-35 messages in the MPEG-2 transport stream output, allowing the decoder to identify and extract SCTE-35 data packets.
Specifies the number of milliseconds by which to pull up the SCTE-35 preroll in the M2TS output, enabling the SCTE-35 preroll pullup feature when set to a non-zero value.

Specifies the segmentation markers to insert in the M2TS output (allowed values include NONE, RAI_ADAPT, PSI_SEGSTART, EBP, and EBP_LEGACY), which control how the encoder signals segment boundaries to downstream devices.
Controls whether segmentation markers in the M2TS output are inserted at a fixed cadence or redistributed to align with other output streams.
Specifies the duration in seconds of each MPEG-TS segment within the UDP output, controlling how the transport stream is split into timed chunks for downstream packaging.
Controls whether timed metadata (such as ID3) is passed through from the input to the M2TS output, accepting values like PASSTHROUGH or NO_PASSTHROUGH.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) used for the timed metadata stream (e.g., ID3) within the MPEG-TS container of this UDP output's M2TS settings.
The 16-bit Transport Stream ID (TSID) placed in the MPEG-2 transport stream header (per ISO 13818-1) to identify this output's transport stream from others.
The video_pid field sets the packet identifier (PID) for the video elementary stream within the MPEG-2 transport stream generated by the M2TS container settings.
Specifies the destination IP address and port to which the UDP output stream is sent.

Specifies the logical ID of a predefined destination in the output group's destinations list, allowing the UDP output to use the URL associated with that destination instead of providing a direct URL.
Configures forward error correction (FEC) settings for the UDP output, including parameters like column depth and row length that define the FEC matrix for data protection.
Sets the number of packets per column in the forward error correction (FEC) matrix for a MediaLive UDP output, determining the degree of parity data added for packet loss recovery.
Specifies whether the UDP output includes column-only or column-and-row forward error correction (FEC), with allowed values 'COLUMN' and 'COLUMN_AND_ROW'.
Number of packets per row in the Pro-MPEG FEC matrix used for forward error correction of the UDP output.

The name of the video description that defines the encoding parameters (codec, resolution, bitrate) for the video in this output, which must match a video description defined in the channel's encoder settings.
Configures whether the MediaLive channel generates thumbnails, and if enabled, the interval (in seconds) at which thumbnails are captured.
Indicates whether thumbnail generation is enabled or disabled for the channel, with valid values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Configures the channel's timecode source and synchronization, such as using an embedded timecode from the input or generating one from the system clock, for outputs.

Specifies the source of the timecode for the channel, which can be set to EMBEDDED (from the input), SYSTEMCLOCK, or ZEROBASED, controlling how timecode is generated or passed through in the encoder output.

When the timecode source is EMBEDDED, this number sets the maximum frame difference between the input timecode and the channel's output timecode that triggers MediaLive to resync the output to the input, controlling how sensitively the channel follows source timecode drift.
Specifies the video encoding parameters for the MediaLive channel, including codec settings, resolution, frame rate, bitrate, and other output stream properties for each video description.
Specifies the video codec and its codec-specific settings (such as H.264 or H.265 parameters) for this video description within the MediaLive channel encoder configuration.
Configures the AV1 video codec settings for the video description, including frame rate, GOP size, bitrate, and rate control options.

Controls how Active Format Description (AFD) metadata is signaled in the AV1 video encode, accepting values such as NONE, FIXED, FOLLOW_INPUT, or FOLLOW_GET_AFD to manage insertion or passthrough of AFD information.
Specifies the number of bits per color sample (either '8' or '10') used for AV1 video encoding in the MediaLive channel.
Specifies the target video bitrate in bits per second for the AV1 video encoding.
Specifies the size of the video buffer used by the AV1 encoder for rate control, interpreted according to the sibling buf_size_unit setting (e.g., bits or kilobits).
Configures the color space and high dynamic range (HDR) metadata (e.g., HDR10 or Rec.709) for the AV1 video encoder output.
When set, this empty settings block instructs MediaLive to pass the input's color space information through unchanged to the AV1-encoded output, rather than converting it to a specified color space.
Specifies the HDR10 high dynamic range metadata settings for the AV1 video encode, including luminance and content light level values that MediaLive signals to HDR-compatible displays.
The maximum content light level (in nits) for the HDR10 metadata, representing the brightest pixel value used in the video content.
The maximum frame average light level (MaxFALL) in nits, used for HDR10 color space metadata when encoding AV1 video.
Configures HLG2020 color space settings for AV1 video encoding, specifying the constant IP gain and hue adjustment applied to the high dynamic range signal.
Specifies the Rec.601 color space settings (contrast and gamma) applied within the AV1 codec configuration for video encoding in MediaLive.

The rec709_settings block is an empty object that specifies the output video should use the Rec.709 color space standard for high-definition content, overriding the input color space when this setting is present.
Specifies the fixed Active Format Description (AFD) value to encode when AFD signaling is set to FIXED for the AV1 codec, used to convey aspect ratio and picture format information.

In the AV1 codec settings, framerate_denominator is the denominator of the frame rate fraction (e.g., 1001 for 29.97 fps) that, together with framerate_numerator, defines the output video's frames per second.
Sets the numerator of the frame rate (fps) for the AV1 video codec, used together with framerate_denominator to define the output video frame rate.
The size of the group of pictures (GOP) for the AV1 video encoder, expressed as either frames or seconds depending on the value of the associated gop_size_units setting.
Specifies whether the GOP size is measured in frames or seconds, with allowed values FRAMES or SECONDS.
Sets the AV1 encoder level, which constrains the maximum resolution, frame rate, and bitrate for the video encode, with allowed values such as auto, 1, 2.1, 4, 6.2, etc.
Specifies the amount of look-ahead used by the AV1 encoder's rate control, accepting LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH to trade compression efficiency against latency.
The maximum bitrate in bits per second for the AV1 video codec, limiting the output bandwidth of the encoded video.
For this AV1 video encoder, min_bitrate defines the lowest bitrate (in bits per second) the encoder will output, preventing the stream from dropping below a guaranteed quality threshold.
Sets the minimum interval between I-frames in frames, controlling how often full-frame encoding occurs in AV1 video output.
Specifies the denominator of the pixel aspect ratio (PAR) for the AV1 video output, used together with par_numerator to define the aspect ratio of individual pixels.
Defines the numerator of the pixel aspect ratio (PAR) for the AV1 video encode, which combined with par_denominator determines the display aspect ratio of the output.
The quality level (1-10) used when the AV1 encoder's rate control mode is set to QVBR, with higher values producing higher quality video output.
Specifies the rate control mode for AV1 encoding, determining whether the codec uses constant bitrate (CBR) or quality-defined variable bitrate (QVBR) to manage output bitrate.
Controls whether the AV1 encoder performs scene change detection and how it adjusts the encoded output (such as inserting keyframes) when scene changes occur.
Enables or disables spatial adaptive quantization, which adjusts compression levels across different spatial regions of the video frame to improve perceptual quality at a given bitrate.
Enables or disables temporal adaptive quantization, which adjusts the quantization strength across time to improve AV1 encoding efficiency and perceived quality.
Configures the burn-in of the timecode into the AV1-encoded video output, including enabling it, setting its on-screen position, and defining the prefix text shown before the timecode.
Specifies the font size (SMALL, MEDIUM, or LARGE) for the timecode text burned into the video when AV1 encoding is used.
Determines where the burned-in timecode appears on the video frame, such as TOP_LEFT or BOTTOM_RIGHT.
Specifies a text prefix that appears before the burned-in timecode in the output, such as 'TC:' to display 'TC:01:00:00:00'.
Specifies whether to insert timecode information into the AV1 video stream, using either DISABLED (no insertion) or PIC_TIMING_SEI (inserting picture timing SEI messages).
Specifies the frame capture codec settings (e.g., capture interval and interval units) used when the video codec is set to FRAME_CAPTURE, configuring how video is captured as JPEG frames.
Specifies the interval, in seconds, between frame captures for the frame capture video codec, supporting fractional values for sub-second capture rates.
Specifies the units (SECONDS or MILLISECONDS) for the capture interval used by the frame capture codec settings in an AWS Elemental MediaLive channel encoder.
Configures the burned-in timecode display on the frame capture output, including the timecode font size, position, and prefix characters that appear on the captured video frames.
Specifies the size (SMALL, MEDIUM, or LARGE) of the timecode text that is burnt into the frame-captured video.
Specifies the corner of the frame where the burned-in timecode is displayed, such as TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, or BOTTOM_RIGHT.
Specifies an optional text string that is prepended to the timecode displayed in the frame capture video output.

This object configures H.264 video encoding parameters, such as bitrate, frame rate, resolution, profile, and GOP structure, for the associated video description in the MediaLive channel's encoder settings.
Controls the intensity of adaptive quantization used by the H.264 encoder to improve subjective visual quality by adjusting quantization levels per macroblock (e.g., HIGH, MEDIUM, OFF, AUTO).

Specifies how Active Format Description (AFD) metadata is signaled in H.264 output, with values such as NONE, FIXED, FOLLOW_AFD, or FOLLOW_INPUT controlling whether and how AFD is inserted into the video stream.
The average bitrate in bits per second for the H.264 video output, which controls the quality and size of the encoded video stream.
Specifies the initial decoder buffer fill percentage for H.264 encoded video, controlling how much the buffer is pre-filled at the start of playback.
Sets the buffer size (in bits) used by the H.264 rate control algorithm, controlling how much bitrate variation is permitted.
Controls whether color metadata (such as color space information) is inserted into the H.264 video stream, with allowed values INSERT or IGNORE.
Configures color space conversion settings for the H.264 encoder, specifying the input color space and how it is converted to the output color space.

Configures the H.264 color space passthrough settings, an empty block that tells AWS Elemental MediaLive to preserve the input video's color space without conversion when the H.264 colorSpace is set to PASSTHROUGH.
Specifies the Rec. 601 color-space correction settings (including contrast, gamma, offset, and saturation) applied to the H.264 encoder video description.
This block enables Rec.709 color space settings for the H.264 encoder, controlling the color space conversion for the video output.
Specifies the entropy encoding mode (CABAC or CAVLC) used for H.264 video compression, balancing compression efficiency against decoder compatibility.
Configures the video filter settings for the H.264 encoder, including temporal filter settings that reduce noise and improve compression efficiency.
Defines the strength of the bandwidth reduction filter applied to H.264 video, which smooths picture detail to lower the output bitrate, with a configurable level such as LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH.
Determines the strength of the sharpening filter applied after the bandwidth reduction filter in the H.264 encoder, with values such as DISABLED, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or AUTO.
Determines how strongly the bandwidth reduction filter is applied to the H.264 video stream, adjusting the trade-off between bitrate reduction and video quality.
Configures temporal filtering for H.264 encoding, which reduces noise by analyzing frames over time, with settings for filter strength and optional post-filter sharpening.
Specifies whether sharpening is applied to the video after the temporal filter, with allowed values of ENABLED, DISABLED, or AUTO to control the sharpening behavior.
The strength of the temporal filter, specified as an integer string from -4 to 5 (default 0), where negative values reduce filtering and positive values increase filtering to suppress temporal noise.
When afd_signaling is set to FIXED, this specifies the Active Format Description (AFD) value (a number from 0 to 15 represented as a string) that MediaLive will encode into the H.264 video output.
Enables or disables adaptive quantization to reduce flicker in H.264 video encoding, with accepted values ENABLED or DISABLED.
Controls whether the H.264 encoder forces field (interlaced) pictures instead of progressive frame pictures, with values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Determines whether the H.264 output uses the input's frame rate (INITIALIZE_FROM_SOURCE) or a fixed frame rate you specify (SPECIFIED) via framerate_numerator and framerate_denominator.
Specifies the denominator of the frame rate fraction (together with framerate_numerator) that defines the output video frame rate for H.264 encodes, e.g., 1001 for 30000/1001 ≈ 29.97 fps.
Defines the integer numerator of the fractional frame rate used for the H.264 video output (e.g., 30000 with a denominator of 1001 yields 29.97 fps) when the frame rate is specified manually.
Determines whether B-frames are used as reference frames in the H.264 GOP (Group of Pictures) structure, with valid values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Specifies the number of closed GOPs that occur between open GOPs in the H.264 video encode, controlling the cadence of closed GOPs for better error resilience and random access.
Specifies the number of B-frames (bidirectional prediction frames) placed between reference frames in the H.264 Group of Pictures (GOP), which affects compression efficiency and encoding latency.
Specifies the number of frames (or seconds, depending on the associated gop_size_units value) between keyframes (GOP length) for the H.264 encoder settings.
Specifies the units for the Group of Pictures (GOP) size in the H.264 encoder settings, either 'FRAMES' or 'SECONDS', which determines how the gop_size value is interpreted.

Defines the H.264 encoding level for the video output, which limits the maximum decoded picture size, bit rate, and frame rate per the H.264 standard; it can be set to a specific level (e.g., H264_LEVEL_3_1) or AUTO for automatic selection.

Specifies the rate control mode for H.264 encoding, where HIGH or MEDIUM enables a look-ahead rate control algorithm that can improve video quality but may increase latency, while LOW disables look-ahead.
Sets the maximum output bitrate in bits per second for this H.264 video encoder, used to cap the encoding rate when variable bitrate (VBR or QVBR) rate control is selected.

Sets the minimum bitrate in bits per second for the H.264 video encoding, which is used when the rate control mode is variable (VBR) to prevent the bitrate from falling too low and help ensure stable video quality.
Sets the minimum interval between I-frames in the H.264 video output, expressed in seconds or frames depending on the GOP size units, controlling keyframe frequency.
Determines the lowest quantization parameter (QP) value that the H.264 encoder can use, which sets an upper bound on video quality and helps control bitrate for the video stream.
Sets the number of reference frames used for H.264 encoding, balancing compression efficiency against decoder complexity and memory usage.
Controls whether the pixel aspect ratio (PAR) is set to the source's PAR or manually specified via par_numerator and par_denominator values.
Specifies the denominator of the pixel aspect ratio (PAR) for the H.264 encoded video, used together with par_numerator to define the shape of non-square pixels in the output.
The numerator of the pixel aspect ratio (PAR) for the H.264 video output, paired with par_denominator to define the pixel shape.
Sets the H.264 profile used for encoding the video, with allowed values like BASELINE, MAIN, HIGH, HIGH_10BIT, and HIGH_422.
Specifies the quality level for the H.264 video encode, applicable only when the rate control mode is QVBR, with valid values including MEDIUM, HIGH, HIGHER, HIGHEST, and LOW.
For QVBR rate control mode, specifies the target video quality level from 1 (lowest) to 10 (highest), to balance bitrate and visual quality.
Controls whether the H.264 encoder uses constant bitrate (CBR), variable bitrate (VBR), or quality-defined variable bitrate (QVBR) for the video output.
Sets the scanning system for the H.264 video output, either INTERLACED or PROGRESSIVE.
This field controls whether the H.264 encoder enables or disables scene change detection, which forces a keyframe when a scene change is detected, with allowed values 'ENABLED' and 'DISABLED'.
Specifies the number of slices per frame for H.264 encoding, accepting an integer from 1 to 4, where a higher number improves error resilience at the cost of compression efficiency.
The amount of softening applied to the video output, where values from 0 to 100 control how soft the image appears, with higher values producing a more softened picture.
Specifies whether to enable spatial adaptive quantization, which redistributes encoding bits within a frame to preserve detail in areas of high spatial complexity.

Specifies the number of frames in a sub-group of pictures (sub-GOP) for H.264 encoding, controlling the frequency of intra frames within the main GOP to support seeking and segment alignment in streaming outputs.
Specifies the H.264 output syntax for the video encode, with values such as DEFAULT or RP2027 (the latter used for broadcast-compliant RP 2027 syntax).
Determines whether H.264 temporal adaptive quantization is enabled or disabled to improve visual quality by adjusting quantizer parameters based on temporal complexity.
Configures the timecode burn-in overlay for the H.264 video, including font size, position, and optional prefix.
Specifies the font size of the timecode burn-in text overlaid on the H264 video output in the MediaLive channel encoder settings.
Determines where in the video frame the burned-in timecode appears, with allowed values such as TOP_LEFT, TOP_CENTER, TOP_RIGHT, MIDDLE_LEFT, etc.
The custom string that is prepended to the timecode when timecode burn-in is enabled for the H.264 video, appearing before the timecode value in the output.
Determines the method of timecode insertion for the H.264 output, using SEI messages (such as PIC_TIMING_SEI or SCTE_35_SEI) or disabling insertion altogether.
Specifies the H.265/HEVC codec configuration, including bitrate, frame rate, GOP structure, and rate-control settings, used by MediaLive to encode this video description.
Specifies the level of adaptive quantization applied during H.265 encoding (auto, high, low, medium, or off) to improve subjective quality by allocating bits based on local scene complexity.
Controls how Active Format Description (AFD) signaling is emitted in the H.265 video encode, with values such as NONE, AUTO, or FIXED determining the handling of AFD metadata.
Sets an alternative transfer function (such as BT709, HLG, or PQ) for the H.265 video to use when the source lacks an embedded transfer function, controlling HDR color interpretation.
Specifies the target average bitrate in bits per second for the H.265 (HEVC) encoder, controlling the output video quality and file size for this video description in the MediaLive channel.
Sets the size of the encoder's HRD buffer in bits, controlling how much coded H.265 video data can be buffered before output, which affects bitrate constancy and latency.
Specifies whether MediaLive inserts color metadata (such as color space and range information) into the H.265 encoded video output, with valid values INSERT or IGNORE.
Configures the color space settings (including color space type and conversion parameters such as HDR10, Rec. 709, or Rec. 601) for the H.265 video output in the MediaLive channel's encoder settings.
Indicates that the H.265 encoder should pass through the video's color space information without converting it, preserving the original color metadata.
Specifies the Dolby Vision 8.1 color space settings for the H.265 encoder, including the base64-encoded luma and chroma data used to carry Dolby Vision metadata.
Defines the HDR10 settings (MaxCll and MaxFall) applied to the H.265 video codec within the MediaLive channel's color space settings.
Sets the maximum content light level (MaxCLL), in nits, that is written into the HDR10 metadata for the H.265 video encode in the MediaLive channel's encoder settings.
The maximum frame average light level (MaxFALL) in units of 0.0001 nits, used as part of the HDR10 mastering display color volume metadata in the H.265 color space settings.
The hlg2020_settings block, when present, enables the HLG2020 color space for the H.265 video description; it is an empty configuration block that requires no sub-parameters.
Defines the color space conversion settings for Rec.601 in the H.265 encoder, including adjustments for contrast, gamma, and gamma correction.
Specifies that the H.265 video encoder should use the Rec.709 color space for output; this settings block is an empty structure that selects Rec.709 conversion.
Specifies the filter settings for H.265 video encoding, including temporal filter settings that reduce noise and improve compression efficiency.
Configures the bandwidth reduction filter for the H.265 encoder, which lowers the encoded bitrate by selectively reducing high-frequency detail through adjustable filter strength settings.
Controls whether post-filter sharpening is enabled or disabled in the H.265 bandwidth reduction filter settings, applying a sharpening filter to enhance the perceived quality of the video output.

Specifies the strength of the bandwidth reduction filter applied to the H.265 video encode, with values such as AUTO or STRENGTH_1 through STRENGTH_5 controlling how aggressively the filter reduces bitrate.
Settings that control the temporal filter for H.265 video encoding, which reduces temporal noise and flicker across frames to improve compression efficiency.
Specifies the post-filter sharpening mode applied after temporal filtering in H.265 encodes, with allowed values AUTO, DISABLED, or ENABLED.
Sets the temporal filter strength for the H.265 encoder, controlling how aggressively temporal noise reduction is applied (e.g., AUTO, STRENGTH_1, STRENGTH_2, etc.).
Specifies the Active Format Description (AFD) value that MediaLive embeds in the H.265 output when the AFD signaling mode is set to FIXED, overriding any AFD value from the input source.
Controls whether MediaLive applies adaptive quantization to reduce visual flicker in the H.265 video encode, with values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Specifies the denominator of the frame rate fraction (together with framerateNumerator) that defines the output video frame rate in H.265 encoding, e.g., 1001 for a 29.97 fps rate.
Specifies the numerator of the frame rate fraction for H.265 encoded video, used with framerate_denominator to determine the output frame rate (e.g., 30000/1001 for 29.97 fps).
Specifies whether the H.265 encoder uses a B-frame as a reference for subsequent frames (ENABLED) or disables this behavior (DISABLED), affecting compression efficiency and picture structure.
Sets the number of B-frames between reference frames to control the GOP closed cadence for the H.265 encoder in a MediaLive channel.
Specifies the number of B-frames between reference frames (I/P frames) in the H.265 encoded output, controlling the GOP structure and compression efficiency.
Specifies the maximum interval between keyframes (in frames or seconds, depending on the gop_size_units setting) for the H.265 video encoder.
Specifies the units for the gop_size field, either SECONDS or FRAMES, in the H.265 encoder settings for a video description in an AWS MediaLive channel.
Specifies the H.265/HEVC level for this video encode, which controls the maximum supported resolution, frame rate, and bitrate for the encoder output (e.g., H265_LEVEL_4_1).
Determines the look-ahead rate control mode for H.265 encoding in MediaLive, where HIGH improves quality but reduces speed, MEDIUM balances quality and speed, and LOW maximizes encoding speed.
The maximum bitrate in bits per second for the H.265 video encoder, limiting the output bitrate for this video description.
The minimum bitrate in bits per second that the H.265 encoder should target, ensuring the output stays above this lower bound even in low-complexity scenes.

Sets the minimum interval between I-frames for the H.265 encoder, measured in frames or seconds depending on the gop_size_units setting, to prevent I-frames from occurring more frequently than this value.
Sets the minimum quantization parameter (QP) value for H.265 video encoding in AWS MediaLive, preventing the encoder from using lower QPs that would produce higher quality and larger bitrate.

Controls whether the H.265 encoder permits motion vectors to cross picture boundaries, with ENABLED allowing them to extend beyond the picture edge and DISABLED restricting them within the picture frame.
Specifies whether temporal motion vector prediction is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for H.265 video encoding, affecting inter-frame prediction efficiency and compression.
Specifies the denominator of the pixel aspect ratio (PAR) for the H.265 video encode, which together with par_numerator controls the display aspect ratio, with 1 commonly denoting square pixels.
The numerator of the pixel aspect ratio (PAR) for the H.265 video output, used together with par_denominator to define non-square pixel dimensions.
Specifies the H.265 profile for the video encoder, which determines features such as bit depth and chroma subsampling (e.g., MAIN, MAIN_10BIT, HIGH).

The `qvbr_quality_level` specifies the target quality level (1–10) for QVBR (Quality-defined Variable Bitrate) rate control in H.265 encodes, where higher values produce better quality and higher bitrates.
Determines whether the H.265 encoder uses constant bitrate (CBR), variable bitrate (VBR), or quality-defined variable bitrate (QVBR) rate control.
Specifies the scanning mode for the H.265 video output, either progressive or interlaced, controlling whether each frame is encoded as a single progressive frame or split into two interlaced fields.
Determines whether H.265 scene change detection is enabled or disabled (ENABLED/DISABLED), allowing the encoder to insert IDR frames at scene changes for more efficient compression.
Specifies the number of slices per picture for H.265 encoding, an integer between 1 and 16.
Specifies the number of frames in each sub-group of pictures (sub-GOP) within the H.265 video output, subdividing the GOP to control compression efficiency and error resilience.
Specifies the H.265 encoding tier (MAIN or HIGH), which determines the codec's maximum bit rate and quality profile.
Specifies the height, in pixels, of each tile used in the H.265 encoding when tiling is enabled, and must be a multiple of 32.
Specifies the width of each H.265 tile in units of 128x128-pixel blocks, controlling how the frame is divided into tiles for parallel encoding.
Configures how MediaLive overlays (burns in) the timecode onto the H.265 video output, including settings such as the timecode prefix, source, and font size.
Sets the font size of the burned-in timecode (SMALL, MEDIUM, or LARGE) when timecode burn-in is enabled for the H.265 video encode.
Controls the corner of the video frame where the burned-in timecode overlay appears (e.g., top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right).
Specifies a custom text prefix that MediaLive prepends to the timecode display when burning timecodes into the H.265 video output.
Specifies whether timecode information is embedded in the H.265 video output, typically via the picture timing SEI message (e.g., DISABLED or PIC_TIMING_SEI).

Specifies the treeblock size for H.265 encoding in MediaLive, where 'LARGE' and 'SMALL' control the coding tree unit dimensions (e.g., 64x64 for large, 16x16 for small) to trade compression efficiency against quality.

The mpeg2_settings object holds the MPEG-2 codec configuration for the video description, specifying parameters such as frame rate, GOP size and structure, scan type, color metadata, and timecode insertion.
Controls the MPEG-2 encoder's adaptive quantization mode (OFF, LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH), which dynamically adjusts quantization levels based on scene complexity to optimize perceptual video quality.
Controls the insertion of Active Format Description (AFD) signaling into MPEG-2 video output, with valid values including NONE, AUTO, and FIXED.
Specifies whether to include color metadata (such as color space, color primaries, and transfer characteristics) in the MPEG-2 video output, with allowed values INSERT or IGNORE.
Sets whether the MPEG-2 encoder uses the input's color space automatically (AUTO) or forces the color space specified in ColorSpaceRec (FORCE).
Specifies the display aspect ratio (e.g., 4:3 or 16:9) used for the MPEG-2 video encode output.
Configures temporal filtering for MPEG-2 video encoding, controlling the strength of noise reduction applied across frames before compression.

Configures the temporal noise-reduction filter for MPEG-2 encoding, including the filter strength and optional post-filter sharpening, which smooths visual noise across frames to improve compression efficiency.
Controls the amount of sharpening applied to the video after temporal filtering, with allowed values AUTO, DISABLED, LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH.
Sets the intensity of the temporal noise reduction filter applied to MPEG-2 video, where higher values (typically 1-5 or 'AUTO') produce stronger filtering.
Specifies the Active Format Description (AFD) value to be inserted into the MPEG-2 video stream when the associated AFD mode is set to 'fixed'.
The denominator of the fractional frame rate (numerator/denominator) that sets the output frame rate for MPEG-2 encoding, such as 1001 for 29.97 or 59.94 fps or 1 for integer frame rates.
The numerator of the MPEG-2 output frame rate fraction, paired with framerate_denominator to define values such as 30000/1001 for 29.97 fps.
Specifies the number of GOPs between each closed GOP, where 0 disables closed GOPs, 1 makes every GOP closed, 2 makes every second GOP closed, and so on.
The number of B-frames (bi-directional predictive frames) to include in each Group of Pictures (GOP) for MPEG2 video encoding.

Defines the numeric size of the Group of Pictures (GOP) for MPEG2 encoding, determining how frequently full keyframes are inserted, where the unit (frames or seconds) is specified by the accompanying `gop_size_units` property.
Specifies whether the gop_size value is measured in frames or seconds for the MPEG2 codec settings.
Specifies whether the MPEG-2 encoded video output uses progressive or interlaced scanning (valid values: PROGRESSIVE or INTERLACED).
Specifies the number of pictures (frames) in each sub-group of pictures (sub-GOP) used for MPEG-2 video encoding in the MediaLive channel.
Specifies how the MPEG2 encoder burns in timecode onto the video output, including settings such as the timecode source and an optional prefix.
Specifies the font size (SMALL, MEDIUM, or LARGE) used for the burned-in timecode on MPEG2 video output.
Determines the placement of the burned-in timecode on the video frame within the MPEG2 encoder settings (e.g., TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT).
Specifies the prefix string that is prepended to the timecode displayed in the burned-in timecode overlay on the MPEG2 video output.
Determines how timecode is inserted into the MPEG2 video output, with allowed values such as DISABLED, GOP_TIMESTAMP, and PIC_TIMING_SEI.
The height of the video output in pixels, which combined with `width` defines the encoding resolution of the channel's output video.
Specifies a unique name for this video description, used to reference it from output settings in the channel via the video_description_name property.
Determines the encoder's response to AFD (Active Format Description) codes in the input video when applying scaling or aspect ratio adjustments, using values such as NONE, PASSTHROUGH, or RESPOND.

Specifies how the video is scaled to match the output resolution: DEFAULT preserves the original aspect ratio by adding letterboxing/pillarboxing as needed, while STRETCH_TO_OUTPUT stretches the video to fill the entire output frame, disregarding the original aspect ratio.
The amount of sharpening to apply to the video output, where a higher value increases sharpness and can improve perceived image quality for the encoded video.
The width of the video in pixels for this video description, which must be an even number and defaults to the source width if omitted.

aws_media_live_channel.id.text: The unique channel identifier assigned by AWS when the MediaLive channel is created.

aws_media_live_channel.inference_setting.text: Defines the list of audio feed inputs that supply audio to the MediaLive inference engine, mapping each named audio feed to a source from the channel's input for use in inference operations.
Defines the name of an audio selector within the MediaLive channel that supplies the audio to this inference feed, so the inference settings can process that specific audio input.

aws_media_live_channel.input_attachments.text: Defines the list of input attachments for the MediaLive channel, each specifying the input to use, its attached settings, and optional automatic input failover configuration.

Defines the automatic input failover configuration for this input attachment, including the input preference (primary or not) and failover conditions such as video black that trigger switching to a secondary input.
The time, in milliseconds, that MediaLive waits after an input error clears before marking the input as available again for automatic failover, preventing rapid re-failover.

Specifies the list of conditions (such as audio loss or video loss) that, when met, trigger an automatic failover from the primary input to the secondary input in an input attachment with automatic failover enabled.
Specifies the condition settings that determine when automatic failover to the backup input is triggered, such as input loss thresholds.
Defines the audio silence threshold (in milliseconds) that MediaLive monitors to trigger automatic input failover when audio is absent for that duration.
The name of the audio selector that MediaLive monitors for silence to trigger an automatic input failover.
The duration of audio silence in milliseconds that must be exceeded before the automatic input failover condition is considered met, triggering a failover to the alternate input.
Configures the input loss failover condition, specifying the threshold in milliseconds to wait before declaring an input loss and triggering a failover to the backup input.
Specifies the threshold in milliseconds that an input must be lost before the automatic input failover condition is considered triggered.
Configures failover detection based on black video, including thresholds for black detection and minimum black video duration before triggering an automatic input switch.

The black detection threshold, expressed as a percentage of the video frame (0 means the entire frame must be black, 100 means any black pixels are sufficient), used in the video black failover condition to trigger automatic input failover.
The threshold in milliseconds for detecting a black video signal, used as a failover condition trigger in MediaLive channel input failover settings.
Determines whether the primary or secondary input is used as the active input when both are healthy, with valid values being PRIMARY_INPUT (default) or SECONDARY_INPUT.
The unique ID of the secondary input used as the failover target in an automatic input failover pair.
Specifies a user-defined name for this input attachment, used to identify it within the MediaLive channel.
Identifies the MediaLive input that this attachment connects to the channel, referencing an existing AWS::MediaLive::Input resource.
Specifies the processing and filtering settings for this input attachment, including audio/caption selectors and what happens when the source input ends.
Configures the audio selectors for the input attachment, which determine the audio tracks to be extracted from the input source and made available for encoding in the MediaLive channel.
Specifies a name for this audio selector, which is used to reference it in audio descriptions and other channel settings.
Specifies the exact audio stream to select from the source input, using criteria such as PID, language, or track selection.
Selects a specific HLS rendition for the audio selector by specifying the rendition's group ID and name, enabling the channel to use that variant from an HLS input as the audio source.
Specifies the HLS rendition group ID (GROUP-ID) from which to select an audio rendition for this audio selector.
The name of the HLS audio rendition to select for this audio selector, matching the NAME attribute of the rendition in the HLS media playlist.
Configures the audio selector to automatically choose the audio track matching a designated language code (e.g., 'eng') from the input source.
The ISO 639-2 language code (e.g., 'eng' for English) used by MediaLive to match and select the appropriate audio track when the audio selector's selection mode is set to LANGUAGE.

Controls whether the audio language selection uses a loose match (selecting the first audio track that matches the specified language) or a strict match (only selecting an audio track whose language exactly matches), with allowed values LOOSE and STRICT.
Specifies the audio PID (program identifier) to select from the input source for this audio selector.
The packet identifier (PID) of the specific audio stream to select from the input when using PID-based audio selection.
Specifies the list of program identifiers (PIDs) that the audio selector uses to extract audio from the transport stream input.
Specifies the Dolby E program number (0-7) to select from the Dolby E audio stream identified by the PID.
The specific program identifier (PID) of the audio track to extract from the input when using PID-based audio selection in this audio selector.
Specifies the settings for a secondary audio PID to be mixed with the primary audio PID selected by the parent, enabling premixing of two audio streams from the same input.
Configures audio normalization for the selected PID, specifying the loudness normalization algorithm (e.g., ITU-R BS.1770-2) and the target loudness level in LUFS to be applied to the audio.
Specifies the loudness normalization algorithm (e.g., ITU-R BS.1770-1 or ITU-R BS.1770-2) applied to the audio PID within the premix settings of the audio selector.
Specifies whether MediaLive's audio normalization algorithm corrects the audio (CORRECT_AUDIO) or only measures loudness without applying correction (MEASURE_ONLY).
Specifies the method for calculating the peak level in audio normalization, either TRUE_PEAK or SAMPLE_PEAK.
Sets the maximum output level (in dBFS) that the peak limiter allows after audio normalization, attenuating audio peaks that exceed this threshold to prevent clipping.
Specifies the target loudness level in LKFS units for the audio normalization process, controlling the perceived loudness of the output audio.
Configures the audio remix settings for the selected PID, defining how input channels are combined and mapped to output channels through channel mappings and input channel levels.
Specifies the channel mappings for audio remixing, where each mapping item defines how a set of input audio channels (by index) are mixed and routed to a single output channel.
Defines the gain level for each input channel that is mixed into the corresponding output channel in the MediaLive remix settings.
Sets the gain (in dB) for this input channel within the audio remix, determining the volume level at which it is mixed into the output.
The zero-based index of the input audio channel that is mixed into this output channel level as part of the remix channel mapping.
The output_channel field specifies the destination channel number in the remixed audio output to which the selected input channel is mapped.
Defines the number of input audio channels involved in the remix, which the remix settings use to map source channels to output channels in the MediaLive channel's audio remix configuration.
The total number of output audio channels that result from the remix operation configured in this audio selector's remix settings.
Specifies audio selection by track number for the input, including a list of tracks and optional Dolby E decode settings.
Contains the Dolby E decoding settings for the selected audio track, including which Dolby E program to extract and decode.
Selects the specific Dolby E audio program (or 'ALL' to decode all programs) from the incoming Dolby E stream.

The `tracks` list specifies the individual audio tracks to select from the input, where each track object identifies the track by its track ID and optionally a byte-rate range to be used for the audio selector.
Specifies the premix gain (in dB) to apply to the selected audio track in the MediaLive channel input.
Specifies the loudness normalization settings applied to the selected audio track before premixing, controlling parameters such as the normalization algorithm and target loudness level.
Determines which loudness normalization standard MediaLive applies to the track, selecting among ITU-R BS.1770-1 through BS.1770-4 or the Leq(A) weighting curve.
Specifies whether the loudness normalization algorithm (ITU-R BS.1770) corrects the audio gain to a target level (CORRECT_AUDIO) or merely measures loudness without changing the audio (MEASURE_ONLY).
Specifies whether the peak level used for audio normalization is calculated as true peak (accounting for inter-sample peaks) or sample peak.
Sets the peak limiter threshold for audio normalization, controlling the maximum peak amplitude that will be allowed before the limiter attenuates louder peaks.
Sets the target loudness level in LKFS (Loudness K-weighted Full Scale) for the audio normalization process, with a default of -24 LKFS.
The gain in decibels (dB) applied to the audio track in the premix settings, controlling its volume level relative to other tracks in the audio selector.
Defines the remix settings for the audio track, specifying channel mappings and channel counts to control how the input audio channels are mixed.

Specifies the channel mappings that define how the selected audio track's input channels are mixed into output channels, including gain levels and destination output channel numbers, for the remix settings in the MediaLive channel audio track premix configuration.
Defines the list of input channel levels (each specifying an input channel and gain) that are mixed together to produce a single output channel within a remix channel mapping.
Specifies the gain in decibels applied to the input channel when remixing audio in AWS Elemental MediaLive.

The input_channel field specifies which audio channel number from the source input is used in a remix mapping, determining the source channel that is mixed with a defined gain level into a MediaLive audio output track.
The index of the output audio channel to which the remixed input track is mapped in the channel mapping for MediaLive remix settings.
The number of input channels to include in the remix, determining how many source audio channels are mapped to the output mix.
Specifies the number of output channels to be produced after the audio remix operation.
The zero-based index of the audio track within the input to select for this audio selector.
Defines the caption selectors for the input, allowing extraction and processing of caption tracks such as embedded or SCTE-27 captions from the input source.
Specifies the language code of the caption track to select from the input, such as 'eng' or 'spa'.
The name of the caption selector, which links the extracted captions to a specific caption output in the channel.
Configures the specific caption source format and decoding parameters for this caption selector, such as embedded, ancillary, SCTE-20, SCTE-27, ARIB, DVB-Sub, or teletext settings.
Specifies configuration for extracting ancillary captions (such as EIA-608) from the input video, including which ancillary data channel number to use when selecting the captions.
Specifies which of the ancillary data channels (1-4) in the input source to extract captions from.
Selects ARIB (Japanese broadcast) captions for the caption selector, and because this settings object is empty in MediaLive, its presence alone enables ARIB caption extraction from the source.
Defines the DVB-Sub caption source parameters, including the PID and language of the subtitle stream to extract from the input.
