Sets the language code (e.g., 'eng') that MediaLive uses for OCR processing of DVB Sub bitmap subtitles so they can be converted to text captions.
The PID (packet identifier) in the transport stream from which to extract DVB Subtitle captions.
Specifies the detailed settings for extracting embedded (EIA-608/708) captions from the video input, such as whether to convert 608 captions to 708 and which 608 channel number to capture.
Specifies whether to convert CEA-608 captions to CEA-708 captions for the embedded captions source, accepting values such as 'DISABLED' or 'UPCONVERT'.
Determines whether SCTE-20 captions embedded in the input are detected, with valid values 'AUTO' to enable detection and 'OFF' to disable it.
Specifies the EIA-608 channel number (1-4) from which to extract embedded captions when the input contains multiple caption channels.
Specifies the CEA-608 caption track number (1-4) from the embedded source to select for caption extraction.
Defines the parameters for extracting captions from an SCTE-20 source, such as whether to convert the embedded 608 captions to 708 and which 608 channel number to select.
Specifies whether to upconvert 608 captions to 708 format in the SCTE-20 source settings of a MediaLive caption selector, with valid values like DISABLED or UPCONVERT.
The number of the 608 caption channel to extract from the SCTE-20 source, which can be either 1 or 2.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) and related settings used to extract SCTE-27 captions from the input for this caption selector.
Specifies the language for the OCR engine used to extract captions from the SCTE-27 source.
Specifies the Packet Identifier (PID) for the SCTE-27 captions within the MPEG-TS stream, used by the MediaLive channel to select the correct elementary stream for caption extraction.
Defines the Smart Subtitles caption selector source settings, which specify how MediaLive extracts the subtitle track from the input when that source type is selected.
Sets whether the smart subtitle captions are synchronized with the video timing, using the enum values 'DISABLED' (default) or 'ENABLED' to control time alignment with the source content.
Specifies the ARN of an AWS Elemental MediaLive channel output that supplies the inference feed used by the smart subtitle source for generating captions in this caption selector.
Settings that define how to extract Teletext captions from the input, including the Teletext page number (and optional output rectangle) to use when decoding the captions.
Specifies the rectangular region within the video frame from which teletext caption data is decoded, defined by left, top, width, and height in pixels.
The height, in pixels, of the output rectangle that defines the region of the teletext page from which captions are extracted.
The left offset in pixels of the output rectangle within the teletext source image, specifying the horizontal start position of the region from which teletext captions are extracted.
The top offset, in pixels, of the output rectangle that defines the teletext caption region within the video frame, measured from the top edge of the frame.
Specifies the width, in pixels, of the rectangular region of the video frame from which teletext captions are extracted.
Specifies the teletext page number to extract captions from in the teletext source for this caption selector.
Specifies whether MediaLive applies a deblocking filter to the input video to reduce blocking compression artifacts, with valid values ENABLED or DISABLED.
Enables or disables the noise reduction filter applied to the incoming video signal, with valid values 'DISABLED' or 'ENABLED'.
Specifies the strength of the video filter applied to the input, which is used when the input filter is set to AUTO to adjust the level of filtering.
Determines whether MediaLive applies a filter to the input signal, using AUTO (service decides based on input type), DISABLED (no filter), or FORCE (always apply the filter).
Specifies the network input settings, including HLS input configuration and server validation, that MediaLive applies to this input attachment.
Provides HLS-specific configuration for this network input, such as bandwidth, buffer segments, retry and retry interval, and SCTE-35 handling.
The maximum bandwidth (in bits per second) that MediaLive uses to select the HLS video variant from the input playlist.
Specifies the number of HLS segments that MediaLive buffers before starting playback from the source.
The number of times MediaLive retries fetching a failed HLS segment before reporting an input error.
The number of seconds to wait between retry attempts when fetching HLS segments or playlists for this input fails.
Determines whether SCTE-35 ad markers are read from the HLS manifest (MANIFEST) or from the elementary stream (ELEMENTAL) of the input.
Contains settings for receiving a multicast UDP input stream, such as the multicast source IP address and port.
Specifies the source IP address from which the multicast input will receive packets, filtering only traffic originating from that sender.
Specifies the level of server certificate validation for a network input (RTMP) source, with allowed values CHECK_CRYPTOGRAPHY_AND_VALIDATE (default) and CHECK_CRYPTOGRAPHY_ONLY.
The Packet Identifier (PID) of the SCTE-35 stream in the transport stream input, which MediaLive uses to extract ad-insertion signaling cues.
Controls whether MediaLive prefers or ignores SMPTE 2038 ancillary data embedded in the input, with valid values PREFER or IGNORE.
Specifies whether MediaLive continues to the next input or loops the current input when the source stream ends (for VOD-type inputs), accepting values like CONTINUE or LOOP.
Determines which video stream from the attached input is used for the channel, allowing selection by PID or program ID.
Specifies the color space of the input video for this video selector (e.g., REC_601, REC_709, HDR10, or FOLLOW), which MediaLive uses to interpret and process the video's color information.

Defines the color space settings for the video selector, including the color space (e.g., HDR10, HLG) and color space usage (e.g., FALLBACK, FORCE), to control how MediaLive processes the video's color information.
Configures the HDR10 color space metadata for the video selector, including MaxCLL and MaxFALL values used for tone mapping.
Specifies the maximum content light level (MaxCLL) in nits for HDR10 video content, used in the HDR10 color space settings of the input attachment's video selector.
Specifies the maximum frame average light level (MaxFALL) in nits for HDR10 content in MediaLive.

Determines how MediaLive handles color space metadata for the selected video input, with FALLBACK using the input's native color space when present and otherwise the configured color space, and FORCE always using the configured color space.
Specifies the specific video stream selection settings (such as PID, program number, or SCTE-27) used by the video selector to choose the video from the input.
Defines the PID-based video selector settings, which specify the packet identifier (PID) of the video stream to extract from the input when the video selector is configured to use a PID.
The packet identifier (PID) of the video stream to select from an MPEG-TS transport stream.
Specifies the program number (ID) within a multiplexed input that this video selector should use to pick the video stream.
The numeric program number within the multiplex or transport stream that this video selector will select for processing.

Defines a list of logical interface names on the attached input that the channel should use, enabling the input attachment to target specific interfaces (e.g., per-pipeline) rather than all available ones.

aws_media_live_channel.input_specificati.text: Specifies the input codec, maximum bitrate, and resolution for the channel's inputs, which MediaLive uses to determine the appropriate input settings.
Specifies the codec (e.g., MPEG2, AVC, or HEVC) of the input, which is part of the channel's input specification that defines the expected input format.
Specifies the maximum input bitrate (in megabits per second) that the channel can accept for its input, with supported values such as MAX_10_MBPS, MAX_20_MBPS, and MAX_50_MBPS.
Specifies the video resolution of the input source (e.g., SD, HD, UHD) so that MediaLive can properly process and encode the input.

aws_media_live_channel.inputs.text: The list of input IDs attached to the MediaLive channel.

aws_media_live_channel.linked_channel_se.text: The ARN of the primary MediaLive channel that this follower channel is linked to for channel-level failover (channel follow) configuration.

Specifies whether this linked channel is designated as the primary or secondary channel in the linked-channel relationship, with accepted values `PRIMARY` and `SECONDARY`, within the primary channel settings of the MediaLive channel's linked channel configuration.

aws_media_live_channel.log_level.text: Specifies the verbosity of the channel's logging, accepting values such as ERROR, WARNING, INFO, and DEBUG to control which log messages are emitted.

aws_media_live_channel.maintenance.text: Specifies the day and start time for the weekly maintenance window of the MediaLive channel.

aws_media_live_channel.maintenance.maint.text: Specifies the day of the week on which the AWS Elemental MediaLive channel's maintenance window is scheduled (for example, MONDAY or TUESDAY).
Specifies the start time (in 24-hour HH:MM format, UTC) for the weekly maintenance window of the MediaLive channel.

aws_media_live_channel.name.text: The name of the MediaLive channel, a user-friendly identifier for the channel within the AWS account.

aws_media_live_channel.role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Elemental MediaLive assumes to access input sources and output destinations for the channel.

aws_media_live_channel.tags.text: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the AWS Elemental MediaLive channel, which can be used for cost allocation, access control, and identifying the channel in the AWS console.

aws_media_live_channel.vpc.text: Specifies the VPC settings, including subnet IDs and security group IDs, that determine which VPC the MediaLive channel runs in.

aws_media_live_channel.vpc.public_addres.text: The list of Elastic IP allocation IDs to assign to the channel's network interfaces in the VPC, giving the channel public IP addresses for internet connectivity.

aws_media_live_channel.vpc.security_grou.text: The list of security group IDs attached to the elastic network interfaces that MediaLive creates in the VPC for the channel, controlling inbound and outbound traffic for the channel.

aws_media_live_channel.vpc.subnet_ids.text: Specifies the subnets within your VPC where MediaLive places the channel's resources, such as inputs and outputs, to enable access to private resources.

aws_media_live_channel_placement_group.t.text: The value of a user-defined tag key attached to the AWS MediaLive channel placement group, used for resource identification, organization, and cost allocation.

aws_media_live_cloud_watch_alarm_templat.text: The date and time when the CloudWatch alarm template was created, returned as a string.
The unique identifier (ID) automatically assigned by MediaLive to this CloudWatch alarm template, used to reference the template in AWS APIs and other resources.
The timestamp indicating when the CloudWatch alarm template was last modified.
The timestamp (ISO 8601) indicating when this CloudWatch alarm template group was created.
The computed unique group identifier that AWS MediaLive assigns to the CloudWatch alarm template group, matching the value returned by the CloudFormation Ref intrinsic function for this resource.
Indicates the most recent modification time of the CloudWatch alarm template group, returned as a string in RFC3339 timestamp format.

aws_media_live_cluster.network_settings..text: Specifies the logical name you assign to a physical network interface in a MediaLive cluster's interface mapping, which is used to reference that interface within the cluster's network configuration.

In an AWS::MediaLive::Cluster's network settings, the network_id field of each interface mapping specifies the network identifier (such as a VPC or subnet ID) that the associated IP addresses belong to.

aws_media_live_cluster.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS MediaLive cluster, used to add custom metadata for identifying, organizing, or managing the cluster in AWS.

aws_media_live_event_bridge_rule_templat.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the target resource that the EventBridge rule invokes for this MediaLive event bridge rule template.
The timestamp indicating when the EventBridge rule template group was created (computed by AWS).
The unique identifier assigned by AWS MediaLive to this event bridge rule template group, used to reference the group after creation.
The date and time when the EventBridge rule template group was last modified.

aws_media_live_input.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Elemental MediaLive input.

aws_media_live_input.destinations.text: Specifies the destination endpoints (e.g., RTMP URLs or RTP IP/port pairs) for a push input, defining the network locations where AWS MediaLive will listen for the incoming media stream.

aws_media_live_input.destinations.networ.text: For a MediaLive input using a UDP or RTP push type, specifies the network IP address of the destination where the input stream is sent.

The `network_routes` list within each destination defines static routes (CIDR and gateway) that MediaLive uses to route push input traffic to the specified destination IP addresses, enabling delivery through a VPC or AWS Direct Connect.
The CIDR block (e.g., '10.0.0.0/24') for a network route associated with the MediaLive input's destination, specifying the IP address range that the route applies to.

aws_media_live_input.destinations.stream.text: The stream name of the input destination, which represents the push endpoint (for example, the RTMP stream key or URL) that an upstream encoder uses to send content to this AWS Elemental MediaLive input.

aws_media_live_input.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the MediaLive input, used for referencing the input in other resources.

aws_media_live_input.input_devices.text: Specifies the MediaLive hardware input devices (such as Elemental Live or Link devices) that are attached to this input to deliver video/audio content to a MediaLive channel.

aws_media_live_input.input_devices.id.text: The unique ID of the AWS Elemental MediaLive input device associated with this input.

aws_media_live_input.input_network_locat.text: Specifies whether the input is located on AWS ('ON_AWS') or on-premises ('ON_PREMISES'), determining how AWS Elemental MediaLive accesses the input source.

aws_media_live_input.input_security_grou.text: Specifies the input security groups (by ARN) to attach to this MediaLive input, which control the permitted IP addresses and CIDRs that can push content to it.

aws_media_live_input.media_connect_flows.text: Specifies the AWS Elemental MediaConnect flows that this MediaLive input is linked to, where each flow is identified by its ARN.
The ARN of an AWS Elemental MediaConnect flow to attach to this MediaLive input as a source.

aws_media_live_input.multicast_settings.text: Configures the source IP address and port for a MediaLive input that receives content over multicast, enabling the input to join a specific multicast group.

aws_media_live_input.multicast_settings..text: Configures the list of multicast source endpoints (IP addresses and ports) that MediaLive will use to receive the input stream.
Specifies the source IP address of the multicast input stream, used by MediaLive to bind to and receive the multicast traffic.
The URL of the multicast source, typically in the form of udp:// or rtp://, specifying the multicast group IP address and port from which the MediaLive input receives the stream.

aws_media_live_input.name.text: The user-defined name you assign to this AWS Elemental MediaLive input, used for identification and management in the AWS console and API operations.

aws_media_live_input.role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Elemental MediaLive assumes to access the input source, such as an S3 bucket for media files or an external pull endpoint.

aws_media_live_input.router_settings.enc.text: For an SRT MediaLive input, this field sets the encryption type (AES128 or AES256) used for the incoming stream.

aws_media_live_input.sdi_sources.text: Associates the MediaLive input with the specified SDI sources (physical serial digital interface video inputs) by their identifiers, used when the input type is set to SDI.

aws_media_live_input.smpte2110_receiver_.text: Configures the SMPTE 2110 receiver group settings for the MediaLive input, specifying the number of receiver groups to provision for redundant IP-based media transport.
Defines a list of SMPTE 2110 receiver groups, each specifying the multicast IP address and audio channel configuration used to receive the SMPTE 2110 stream for the input.

Contains the Session Description Protocol (SDP) settings, including the SDP body that describes the video and audio streams and network parameters, for the associated SMPTE 2110 receiver group in an AWS MediaLive input.

Specifies the SDP content for each ancillary data stream (such as captions or timecode) in the SMPTE 2110 receiver group, with each item in the list providing the session description for one ancillary stream.
The index of the media stream in the main SDP that this ancillary SDP applies to, allowing multiple ancillary SDPs to target different media streams within the SMPTE-2110 receiver group.
The URL of the ancillary SDP (Session Description Protocol) file that provides additional media streams (such as audio or ancillary data) for the SMPTE 2110 receiver group.
Specifies the list of SDP (Session Description Protocol) URIs for the audio streams in the SMPTE 2110 receiver group.
The index of the audio media section within the SDP file, used to identify which audio stream to associate with the SMPTE 2110 receiver group.
Specifies the URL of the Session Description Protocol (SDP) file for an audio stream used by an SMPTE 2110 receiver group in the AWS Elemental MediaLive input.
The Session Description Protocol (SDP) for the video stream in an SMPTE 2110 receiver group, defining the video's codec, resolution, and IP transport parameters.
The zero-based index of the video media description within the SDP, identifying which media line corresponds to the video stream for SMPTE 2110 receiver group input.
The URL of the SDP (Session Description Protocol) file that defines the video stream configuration within the SMPTE 2110 receiver group, which MediaLive uses to receive and parse the video input.

aws_media_live_input.sources.text: Specifies the source URLs (and optional credentials) from which AWS Elemental MediaLive pulls the input stream, typically used for pull-based input types such as RTMP_PULL or RTP_PULL.

aws_media_live_input.sources.password_pa.text: Specifies the name of the AWS Systems Manager (SSM) parameter that stores the password used for authenticating to the source server when the input source requires credentials.

aws_media_live_input.sources.url.text: Specifies the URL of the media stream to pull into the MediaLive input, such as an RTMP or RTP endpoint from which the input is retrieved.

aws_media_live_input.sources.username.text: The username used for basic authentication when an AWS Elemental MediaLive pull input connects to an upstream source server (such as an RTMP or RTP source) that requires credentials.

aws_media_live_input.srt_settings.text: Configures the SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) input settings for a MediaLive input, including the source IP address and listener port used to receive SRT media streams.

aws_media_live_input.srt_settings.srt_ca.text: Specifies a list of SRT caller sources, each defined by a hostname and port, that connect to MediaLive to deliver SRT content for this input.
Specifies the decryption settings, including the encryption algorithm (AES-128 or AES-256) and the associated decryption key, used to decrypt the incoming SRT stream from this caller source.
The decryption algorithm for the SRT caller source, which must be either AES-128 or AES-256.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the passphrase used to decrypt the SRT caller source stream.
The minimum latency in milliseconds for the SRT caller source, which acts as the lower bound for the SRT connection's target latency and directly influences the size of the receive buffer.
The hostname or IP address of the SRT listener that this SRT caller source will connect to.
The TCP port on which the MediaLive input listens for incoming SRT connections from each caller source in the SRT caller sources list.
The SRT stream ID (stream identifier) for this caller source, which MediaLive uses to identify and receive the SRT stream from that source.

aws_media_live_input.srt_settings.srt_li.text: Configures the SRT listener for the input, specifying the allowed source IP address and port that MediaLive accepts incoming SRT connections from.
Configures the decryption of the incoming SRT stream for this listener, typically by specifying the ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the decryption key.
The AES decryption algorithm (e.g., AES-128 or AES-256) used to decrypt the incoming SRT stream for this MediaLive input.
ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the passphrase required to decrypt the SRT input stream.
Defines the minimum latency in milliseconds for the SRT listener, setting the lower bound of the configured latency window for the input.
Specifies the SRT stream ID used by the listener to identify and associate the incoming SRT stream with the MediaLive input.

aws_media_live_input.tags.text: Assigns metadata tags (key-value pairs) to the MediaLive input, which can be used for cost allocation, resource grouping, and IAM-based access control.

aws_media_live_input.type.text: Defines the type of MediaLive input, such as UDP_PUSH, RTP_PUSH, RTMP_PUSH, RTMP_PULL, or URL_PULL, which determines the transfer protocol or method used to provide the source content.

aws_media_live_input.vpc.text: Configures the input to be provisioned inside a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), including the subnets and security groups that define the input's network placement and access rules.

aws_media_live_input.vpc.security_group_.text: The list of security group IDs associated with the VPC that the MediaLive input is attached to, controlling network access to the input.

aws_media_live_input.vpc.subnet_ids.text: Specifies the list of subnet IDs in the VPC where the incoming video streams for the MediaLive input will be provisioned, enabling the input's elastic network interfaces to be placed in those subnets.

aws_media_live_input_security_group.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the MediaLive input security group.

aws_media_live_input_security_group.id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS Elemental MediaLive input security group, returned as a string when the resource is created.

aws_media_live_input_security_group.whit.text: Specifies the list of IPv4 CIDR blocks (with optional descriptions) that are allowed to access the input security group, controlling which source IPs can send media content.
The CIDR block that is allowed to send input requests to the MediaLive input security group.

aws_media_live_multiplex.destinations.mu.text: Specifies the MediaConnect output destination settings for a multiplex destination, including the ARN of the MediaConnect output.

aws_media_live_multiplex.state.text: The current lifecycle state of the MediaLive multiplex, such as IDLE, STARTING, RUNNING, or STOPPING, as reported by AWS.

aws_media_live_multiplex.tags.key.text: The key of a tag applied to the AWS Elemental MediaLive Multiplex, used to attach metadata for organizing, cost allocation, and access management of this media transmission resource.

aws_media_live_multiplex.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag pair applied to the MediaLive multiplex for metadata and resource organization.

aws_media_live_multiplexprogram.multiple.text: The constant bitrate in bits per second for the video output of the MediaLive multiplex program, defining the fixed bitrate when the program's video settings use constant-bitrate encoding.

Specifies statistical multiplexing (statmux) settings for the program's video, including priority and minimum/maximum bitrate limits that control how bandwidth is dynamically allocated among programs within the MediaLive multiplex.

Specifies the maximum bitrate in bits per second that the video may use for this program when statistical multiplexing (statmux) is enabled, capping the bandwidth allocated to this program within the multiplex.

The minimum bitrate in bits per second that the video encoder will target for this multiplex program when statistical multiplexing is enabled, ensuring the program does not fall below this rate during allocation of multiplex bandwidth.

Sets the relative priority of this program's video within the statistical multiplex (statmux) group, where higher numbers cause the multiplexer to allocate bandwidth to this program before lower-priority programs when the total multiplex bandwidth is constrained.

aws_media_live_multiplexprogram.packet_i.text: Specifies the packet identifiers (PIDs) for the audio elementary streams in the MediaLive multiplex program.
Specifies the DVB Subtitle packet identifiers (PIDs) to associate with the multiplex program, used for delivering DVB subtitle streams through the multiplex.
Sets the DVB Teletext packet identifier (PID) used by the multiplex program's packet identifiers map.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) for the Enhanced TV (ETV) platform service within the MPEG-2 transport stream of the MediaLive multiplex program.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) for the Enhanced TV (ETV) signal within the multiplex program's packet identifiers map, used to carry ETV metadata in the MPEG-2 transport stream.
Configures the KLV (Key-Length-Value) data packet identifiers (PIDs) in the multiplex program's packet identifier map, specifying which PIDs carry KLV metadata in the output transport stream.
The Packet Identifier (PID) for the Program Clock Reference (PCR) stream, which carries timing information for the program in the MediaLive multiplex.
Specifies the packet identifier (PID) for the Program Map Table (PMT) in the multiplex program's MPEG-TS packet identifiers map.
Sets the packet identifier (PID) for the private metadata stream within the MPEG-2 transport stream of this MediaLive multiplex program.
Specifies the packet identifiers (PIDs) used for SCTE-27 cue messages in the multiplex output.
The packet identifier (PID) for SCTE-35 messages in the multiplex program, used to carry ad insertion signaling.
The packet identifier (PID) assigned for timed metadata (e.g., ID3 timed metadata) in the MPEG-TS output of the MediaLive multiplex program.
The PID (packet identifier) assigned to the video elementary stream in the MPEG-2 transport stream output of the MediaLive multiplex program.

aws_media_live_multiplexprogram.pipeline.text: Identifies which MediaLive channel pipeline (PIPELINE_0 or PIPELINE_1) is currently active for the multiplex program pipeline.
Identifies the MediaLive pipeline (0 or 1) for which the settings in this pipeline detail object apply.

aws_media_live_network.associated_cluste.text: The list of unique identifiers for the AWS Elemental MediaLive clusters that are associated with this network.

aws_media_live_network.ip_pools.cidr.text: Specifies the CIDR block address range for an IP pool in the MediaLive network, defining the subnet of IP addresses that can be used.

aws_media_live_network.routes.cidr.text: The destination CIDR block (e.g., '10.0.0.0/16') for a static route in the MediaLive network, used to direct matching traffic to the associated gateway.

aws_media_live_network.routes.gateway.text: The IPv4 gateway address (next hop) used by the MediaLive network route to reach the destination CIDR for network traffic.

aws_media_live_network.state.text: The current lifecycle state of the MediaLive network, as reported by the AWS MediaLive API (for example, CREATING, CREATE_COMPLETE, UPDATE_COMPLETE, DELETE_COMPLETE).

aws_media_live_network.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS MediaLive network, allowing you to attach arbitrary metadata such as environment, team, or cost center for resource organization and identification.

aws_media_live_node.node_interface_mappi.text: Specifies the logical name (e.g., 'eth0') assigned to a network interface on a MediaLive Anywhere node, used to map that interface to a specific Elastic Network Interface (ENI).
Specifies whether the node's network interface uses DHCP or static IP addressing for its interface mapping in an AWS Elemental MediaLive cluster.
Specifies the name of the physical network interface (such as eth0) on the on-premises MediaLive node that is mapped to a logical interface name for MediaLive Anywhere connectivity.

aws_media_live_node.sdi_source_mappings..text: The physical SDI input card number on the MediaLive node to which the corresponding SDI source is mapped.
The logical channel number within the MediaLive multiplex to which the corresponding SDI source (specified in the same mapping) is assigned, identifying which channel the SDI input feeds.

The SDI source identifier (e.g., the ARN of an AWS::MediaLive::SdiSource resource) that this mapping associates with a logical source name on the node, enabling MediaLive channels to use that physical SDI input.

aws_media_live_node.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Elemental MediaLive node, used for metadata organization and resource categorization.

aws_media_live_node.tags.value.text: The value assigned to a tag on the AWS MediaLive node, used to attach metadata such as environment or cost center for resource management and cost allocation.

aws_media_live_sdi_source.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the SDI source.

aws_media_live_signal_map.cloud_watch_al.text: Specifies the list of CloudWatch alarm template group identifiers (typically ARNs) that this MediaLive signal map references, so that the alarms defined in those template groups are applied to the signal map for monitoring.
A read-only list of CloudWatch alarm template group IDs attached to this MediaLive signal map, defining which alarm templates are included as signal sources for the map.

aws_media_live_signal_map.created_at.text: The date and time when the signal map was created, in ISO 8601 format.

aws_media_live_signal_map.event_bridge_r.text: Specifies the list of EventBridge rule template group identifiers to associate with this AWS Elemental MediaLive signal map, enabling the signal map to use the event rules from those groups for monitoring and alerting.
The list of Amazon EventBridge rule template group identifiers associated with the MediaLive signal map, as resolved and maintained by the service.

aws_media_live_signal_map.identifier.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Elemental MediaLive signal map.

aws_media_live_signal_map.last_discovere.text: The `last_discovered_at` field is a read-only timestamp string representing the date and time when AWS MediaLive last ran its automatic discovery of the signal map's resources.

aws_media_live_signal_map.modified_at.text: The timestamp (ISO 8601 format) indicating when the signal map was last modified, automatically set by AWS Elemental MediaLive.

aws_media_package_asset.egress_endpoints.text: The identifier of the AWS Elemental MediaPackage packaging configuration that defines how the asset is packaged (e.g., HLS or DASH) for delivery through this egress endpoint.
The URL for this egress endpoint, which AWS Elemental MediaPackage generates to provide a streaming or download URL for the asset via the associated packaging configuration.

aws_media_package_channel.egress_access_.text: This property specifies the CloudWatch Logs log group where egress access logs for the MediaPackage channel are delivered.

aws_media_package_channel.hls_ingest.ing.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS MediaPackage to this HLS ingest endpoint.
The password used to authenticate HTTP requests to the HLS ingest endpoint when pushing media content from an upstream encoder.
The URL of the HLS ingest endpoint that receives live content from an upstream encoder for the MediaPackage channel.
The username used to authenticate to the ingest endpoint when pushing content into the MediaPackage channel.

aws_media_package_channel.ingress_access.text: Specifies the CloudWatch Logs log group that captures access logs for incoming requests to the MediaPackage channel's ingress endpoints.

aws_media_package_channel.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Elemental MediaPackage channel, enabling you to assign metadata such as environment or project for resource filtering and cost tracking.

aws_media_package_channel.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag key-value pair applied to an AWS Elemental MediaPackage channel, used for resource identification and management.

aws_media_package_origin_endpoint.cmaf_p.text: Determines how SCTE-35 ad markers are handled in the HLS manifests for this CMAF endpoint, with supported values including PASSTHROUGH, SCTE35_ENHANCED, DATERANGE, and NONE.
Specifies which SCTE-35 ad marker types (e.g., SPLICE_INSERT, BREAK) in the source content trigger ad insertion in this HLS manifest.
Specifies the ad marker restrictions for this HLS manifest in the CMAF packaging configuration, limiting which ad markers are permitted (NONE, RESTRICTED, UNRESTRICTED, or BOTH).
Unique identifier for this HLS manifest within the CMAF package, which is used to construct the manifest's URL and must be unique among all HLS manifests for the endpoint.
Whether to include an I-frame only stream (a video stream containing only key frames) in this HLS manifest.
Sets the short string that MediaPackage appends to the end of the base URL to create the unique path for the generated HLS manifest file in the CMAF package.
Determines whether the HLS manifest for the CMAF package uses an EVENT or VOD playlist type, controlling whether the playlist grows as new content is published or remains a fixed VOD playlist.
Specifies the duration in seconds of the sliding window for the HLS manifest, controlling how much of the live stream's media segments are listed in the playlist.

For each HLS manifest under the CMAF package, this interval (in seconds) controls how often EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME tags are inserted into the manifest, enabling downstream players to align content with absolute time.
The complete URL that clients use to request this HLS manifest from the MediaPackage origin endpoint.

aws_media_package_origin_endpoint.tags.k.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the MediaPackage origin endpoint, which can be used to categorize and manage the resource, such as for cost allocation or access control.

aws_media_package_origin_endpoint.tags.v.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS Elemental MediaPackage origin endpoint, used to categorize the resource for cost allocation and IAM resource-level permissions.

aws_media_package_packaging_configuratio.text: Specifies how SCTE-35 ad markers are signaled in this HLS manifest, with valid values NONE, SCTE35_ENHANCED, or PASSTHROUGH.
When enabled, this HLS manifest generated by the CMAF packaging configuration includes an I-frame-only stream (a variant containing only keyframes), which players can use for fast seek or scrubbing.
Specifies the name of the HLS manifest that is generated as part of the CMAF packaging configuration.
Specifies the interval in seconds between EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME tags in the HLS manifest, used for timestamp alignment.
When true, MediaPackage repeats the EXT-X-KEY tag for each media segment in the HLS manifests generated by this CMAF packaging configuration, rather than including it only once in the playlist.

The stream_selection object defines criteria such as minimum and maximum video bitrate and stream ordering that determine which video and audio tracks are included in the HLS manifest for the CMAF packaging configuration.
This sets the maximum video bitrate threshold for selecting which video streams to include in the HLS manifest for the CMAF packaging configuration.
Specifies the minimum video bitrate (in bits per second) for video streams to be included in the HLS manifest of the CMAF package, so only streams with at least this bitrate are selected for output.
Determines the order in which video streams appear in the HLS manifest, with allowed values such as ORIGINAL, VIDEO_BITRATE_ASCENDING, and VIDEO_BITRATE_DESCENDING.
Determines the DASH manifest layout: FULL outputs a single manifest for all periods, while COMPACT outputs one manifest per period.
Specifies the name of the DASH manifest that AWS Elemental MediaPackage generates for this packaging configuration, which is used in the output URL.
For each DASH manifest, this specifies the minimum buffer time in seconds that a media player must buffer before it can start playing the stream.
Specifies the DASH profile for the manifest, such as NONE, HBBTV_1_5, or DVB_DASH_2014, which determines the DASH compliance and features used in the packaging configuration.
Specifies whether SCTE-35 markers for the DASH manifest are sourced from the input manifest (MANIFEST) or from the encoded segments (SEGMENTS).
Defines the criteria (such as minimum and maximum video bitrates and stream ordering) used to select the video, audio, and subtitle tracks to include in the DASH manifest.
Sets the maximum video bitrate (in bits per second) used to select which video streams are included in the DASH manifest, filtering out higher-bitrate tracks.
The minimum video bitrate in bits per second that a video stream must meet to be included in the DASH manifest's stream selection.
Specifies the order in which streams are listed in the DASH manifest, with valid values ORIGINAL, VIDEO_BITRATE_ASCENDING, or VIDEO_BITRATE_DESCENDING.
Determines the ad marker type to include in the HLS manifest, with valid values of none, scte35-enhanced, and passthrough, controlling how SCTE-35 ad signaling is represented in the manifest.
When enabled, the HLS manifest includes an additional I-frame-only media playlist, enabling trick-play (fast-forward and rewind) for video content.
Specifies the name of the HLS manifest file (e.g., 'index') that MediaPackage generates for the packaging configuration, which is used in the playback URL to request the manifest playlist.
Specifies the interval in seconds between EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME tags in the HLS manifest.
When true, MediaPackage repeats the EXT-X-KEY tag for every media segment in the HLS manifest; when false, the tag appears only once.
Specifies which input video/audio streams are included in this HLS manifest, based on bitrate range and stream ordering criteria.
Defines the maximum video bitrate (in bits per second) for streams selected into the HLS manifest, so streams with a higher bitrate are excluded.
The minimum video bitrate (in bits per second) that a video stream must have to be included in the HLS manifest's stream selection.

Specifies the order in which video streams are listed in the HLS manifest, with valid values typically 'ORIGINAL' (preserving source order), 'VIDEO_BITRATE_ASCENDING', or 'VIDEO_BITRATE_DESCENDING' (sorting by video bitrate).
Specifies the name of the Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest, which is used to generate the URL for requesting that manifest.

Configures which source video and audio streams are selected for the Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest, supporting bitrate-based selection (MinVideoBitsPerSecond, MaxVideoBitsPerSecond) and stream ordering (StreamOrder).
The maximum video bitrate (in bits per second) to include in the Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest, filtering out video streams above this threshold.
Specifies the minimum video bitrate (in bits per second) a video stream must have to be included in this Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest, filtering out lower-bitrate streams.
Determines the order in which video streams are listed in the Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest, with options for original order or sorting by video bitrate ascending or descending.
The key of a user-defined tag applied to the MediaPackage packaging configuration, used for organizing, identifying, and managing access to the resource.
The value of a user-defined tag attached to the MediaPackage packaging configuration, used for metadata, cost allocation, and resource management.

aws_media_package_packaging_group.author.text: Defines the CDN authorization configuration for the packaging group, specifying the identifier secret and the IAM role that MediaPackage uses to access AWS Secrets Manager for rotating credentials.

aws_media_package_packaging_group.egress.text: Specifies the CloudWatch Logs log group where egress access logs for this packaging group are sent.

aws_media_package_packaging_group.tags.v.text: The value portion of a key-value tag assigned to the MediaPackage packaging group, used for resource metadata, organization, and cost allocation.

aws_media_package_v2_channel.channel_gro.text: The name of the MediaPackage v2 channel group that this channel belongs to, used as part of the channel's identifier and required when creating or referencing the channel.

aws_media_package_v2_channel.channel_nam.text: The human-readable name of the AWS MediaPackage v2 channel, which must be unique within an AWS account and is incorporated into the channel's Amazon Resource Name (ARN).

aws_media_package_v2_channel.ingest_endp.text: The list of ingest URLs that the encoder sends content to for this MediaPackage v2 channel, assigned by AWS when the channel is created.
The unique identifier assigned to this ingest endpoint by MediaPackage v2, distinguishing it from other endpoints in the same channel.
The URL of a MediaPackage v2 channel ingest endpoint, which serves as the input destination where upstream streaming content is received.

aws_media_package_v2_channel.input_type.text: Specifies the input type of the channel, which determines whether incoming content is in HLS or CMAF format, with allowed values 'HLS' and 'CMAF'.

aws_media_package_v2_channel.output_lock.text: Specifies the output locking mode of the MediaPackage v2 channel, which enforces consistent segment timing and alignment across all of the channel's packaging endpoints to enable synchronized downstream playback and failover.

aws_media_package_v2_channel.tags.text: A list of Tag objects (each with Key and Value) that you can attach to a MediaPackage v2 channel to add metadata for organization, access control, and cost tracking.

aws_media_package_v2_channel.tags.value.text: Specifies the value part of a tag assigned to the MediaPackage v2 channel, allowing custom metadata to be associated with the channel.

aws_media_package_v2_channel_group.chann.text: The unique name for the channel group within the AWS Region, used to identify and reference this group of channels in AWS Elemental MediaPackage v2.

aws_media_package_v2_channel_group.tags.text: A list of tag objects (each containing a key and value) to attach to the channel group for organizing and identifying AWS resources.

aws_media_package_v2_channel_group.tags..text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the MediaPackage v2 channel group for metadata and resource management.
The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the MediaPackage v2 channel group, used for metadata and resource categorization.

aws_media_package_v2_channel_policy.chan.text: The name of the MediaPackage v2 channel group that contains the channel to which this policy is attached.
The name of the AWS MediaPackage v2 channel that this channel policy applies to.

aws_media_package_v2_channel_policy.poli.text: The JSON resource policy document that defines the permissions for accessing the MediaPackage v2 channel, typically specifying allowed principals and actions.

aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint.cha.text: The name of the channel group that contains the channel this origin endpoint is associated with.
The name of the MediaPackage v2 channel to which this origin endpoint belongs.

aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint.con.text: ContainerType specifies the container format of the packaged content for the origin endpoint, which must be either "ts" (MPEG-TS) or "cmaf" (Common Media Application Format).

aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint.das.text: The URLs of the DASH manifests generated by this origin endpoint, which clients use to access the DASH streaming content.
Configures the availability start time for the DASH manifest, allowing you to set a specific wall-clock time from which the manifest's content begins playback.
Sets a fixed absolute UTC timestamp (ISO 8601) that anchors the start of the DASH manifest's availability window, instead of letting it roll with the live edge.

For a DASH manifest in an AWS MediaPackage v2 origin endpoint, this field specifies the base URLs that MediaPackage inserts into the manifest's BaseURL elements, enabling clients to resolve segment and submanifest paths relative to these URLs.

Specifies the service location (such as an AWS region or 'global') that identifies where the base URL for the DASH manifest is hosted, used by MediaPackage v2 to route manifest requests to the appropriate endpoint.
The base URL used by the DASH manifest in the origin endpoint, which serves as the origin path for client requests to fetch the manifest and associated media segments.
Specifies the compactness of the DASH manifest, where 'COMPACT' includes only the minimum required information to reduce manifest size and 'FULL' includes all available metadata for the manifest.
Determines whether the DASH manifest includes DRM signaling (such as ContentProtection elements) for encrypted outputs, with allowed values 'SIGNAL' and 'NO_SIGNAL'.
Settings for DVB subtitles in the DASH manifest, specifying the PIDs and language codes of the DVB subtitle tracks to include.
This field sets the probability (between 0 and 1) that DVB error metrics are emitted for the DASH manifest, controlling the sampling rate of error metric reporting in MediaPackage v2.
Specifies the URL to which DVB error metrics are reported for the DASH manifest's DVB settings.

In AWS Elemental MediaPackage v2 origin endpoints for DASH, this property sets the font family name advertised in the DASH manifest's FontDownload descriptor, which clients use to associate a downloadable font with DVB subtitle rendering.
The MIME type (e.g., font/ttf) of the font file that MediaPackage downloads for DVB subtitle rendering in the DASH manifest.
Specifies the URL of the font file that MediaPackage downloads to render DVB subtitles in the DASH manifest.
Defines time-based filtering parameters (start, end, and time delta) that restrict the content window included in the DASH manifest.
Specifies the ISO 8601 timestamp from which the DASH manifest's content window begins, so that playback starts at a particular point in the source stream rather than from the original start.
Specifies the DRM system and encryption settings applied to the DASH manifest when manifest filtering is active, controlling the digital rights management protection for the filtered output.
The end timestamp (ISO 8601 in UTC) that defines the upper boundary of the content time window to include in the DASH manifest for this origin endpoint.
A regular expression applied to DASH manifest references to include only matching manifests in the origin endpoint's filter configuration.
Defines the start timestamp of the DASH manifest's filter window, causing media segments earlier than this time to be excluded from the manifest output.
Delays the DASH manifest by the specified number of seconds so that segments are not listed until that time after they are ingested, effectively shifting the manifest's availability window.
The manifest name that uniquely identifies this DASH manifest and is used as part of the endpoint URL to request it.
Specifies the duration (in seconds) of the manifest window, which controls how much live content is available for playback in the DASH manifest.
Specifies the minimum number of seconds that a media player should buffer before starting playback for each DASH manifest generated by this origin endpoint.
Specifies the minimum update period in seconds for the DASH manifest, indicating to players how often they should check for manifest updates.
Specifies the events (such as ad avail markers, DRM key rotation, source content changes, or slate insertion) that trigger the start of a new DASH period in the generated manifest.
Defines the DASH profiles (e.g., urn:mpeg:dash:profile:isoff-on-demand:2011 or urn:mpeg:dash:profile:isoff-live:2011) that determine the manifest's compliance and feature set for this DASH manifest.
Defines the program information metadata (such as title, copyright, and parental rating) that is included in the DASH manifest generated by this MediaPackage v2 origin endpoint.
Specifies the copyright string to include in the DASH manifest's ProgramInformation element.
The language code to place in the program information of the DASH manifest, identifying the primary language of the content (for example, 'en' or 'fr').
Specifies the URL that is included in the ProgramInformation element of DASH manifests to provide viewers with a link to additional details about the program.
Specifies the source attribute of the DASH ProgramInformation element, which is included in the manifest as the source of the program information.
Specifies the title of the program information element in the DASH manifest, which appears as the <ProgramInformation> title in the MPD output.
Configures SCTE-DASH ad marker signaling for this DASH manifest by specifying the ad marker format (binary or XML) used to indicate splice points in the stream.
Specifies the ad marker style for DASH manifests, indicating whether SCTE-35 markers appear as binary (BINARY) or XML (XML).
Controls whether SCTE-35 ad markers are included in the DASH manifest, and which SCTE-35 signals to insert.
Determines whether the DASH manifest's SegmentTemplate uses a number-based timeline (NUMBER_WITH_TIMELINE) or a time-based timeline (TIME_WITH_TIMELINE) for referencing media segments.
Configures how subtitles are included in the DASH manifest, using subtitle manifest settings and subtitle extensions to map subtitle resources (e.g., WebVTT or TTML) to the output manifest.
Defines TTML subtitle configuration for DASH manifests, specifying period trigger commands and whether to splice subtitles at period boundaries.
Specifies the TTML profile for subtitles in this DASH manifest's subtitle configuration, which determines whether subtitles are passed through as-is or converted to DVB-subtitle format.
The duration (in seconds) that the DASH manifest advertises as the suggested presentation delay, indicating to the player how long to buffer before starting playback to ensure smooth rendering.
Specifies the URI path type for the DASH manifest, which controls the URL path format (such as V1 or V2) used to access the manifest on the origin endpoint.
Specifies the UTC timing method (such as HTTP, HTTP-HEAD, HTTP-XSDATE, or DIRECT) and an optional UTC timing offset used in the DASH manifest's UTCTiming element.
Specifies how the DASH manifest communicates UTC timing to downstream players, with supported values including HTTP_HEAD, HTTP_ISO, HTTP_XSDATE, and DIRECT.

Specifies the source URL or identifier from which the DASH manifest's UTC timing element retrieves the current wall-clock time, enabling synchronized playback when the timing mode is set to HTTP or HTTP-ISO.

aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint.hls.text: The list of HTTPS URLs for the HLS manifests served by this origin endpoint, used to play back content in HLS-compatible players.
The name that, when appended to the endpoint URL, creates a child manifest used to serve a low-latency HLS (LL-HLS) variant of the main manifest for this origin endpoint.
Specifies the start and end timestamps and an optional manifest filter expression that control which content is included in the HLS manifest.
Filters the HLS manifest to include only content starting from the specified clip start time, determining the earliest media segment included in the output.
The end timestamp (ISO 8601) of the time window used to filter the HLS manifest, restricting the manifest to content up to that point.

The manifest_filter identifies a pre-defined MediaPackage v2 filter (via name or ARN) that is applied to this HLS manifest to include only the content (e.g., specific renditions or ad-marker-tagged segments) that satisfy the filter's rules.
Specifies the start timestamp (ISO 8601 format) of the time window used by the HLS manifest filter, including only segments whose timestamps fall at or after this time.
Specifies the amount of time (in seconds) by which the HLS manifest is delayed relative to the live edge, controlling how far behind real time the manifest starts.
A short string appended to the endpoint URL that uniquely identifies this HLS manifest, creating a distinct path for accessing the manifest.
Specifies the duration of the sliding window for the HLS manifest, in seconds, determining how far back from the live edge the manifest lists available segments.
Specifies the interval in seconds between EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME tags inserted in the HLS manifest, used for client synchronization and seeking.
Configures SCTE-35 ad signaling for the HLS manifest, defining how ad markers are inserted (e.g., using EXT-X-CUE-OUT/EXT-X-CUE-IN cue formats).
Specifies the ad marker type for HLS manifests when using SCTE-35 signaling, with supported values such as DATERANGE and SCTE35_ENHANCED.
Specifies the SCTE-35 ad marker mode for the HLS manifest, with values like 'NONE' (no markers) or 'SCTE35_ENHANCED' (include enhanced SCTE-35 markers).
Specifies the EXT-X-START tag configuration for the HLS manifest, including whether the tag is enabled and the time offset (in seconds) from which playback should start.
Enables precise placement of the EXT-X-START tag's time offset in the HLS manifest, ensuring the playback start time is exact rather than approximated.
Determines the time offset (in seconds) from the beginning of the media playlist that the EXT-X-START tag in the HLS manifest specifies as the preferred playback start point.

Determines whether the HLS manifest URI path uses a simple format (e.g., `/manifest`) or a normal format that includes segment duration and start number (e.g., `/1234/5678/manifest`), with allowed values `SIMPLE` and `NORMAL`.}
The complete URL that serves the HLS manifest for this origin endpoint, computed and returned by AWS MediaPackage v2.
Specifies whether the child manifest URL is URL-encoded in the HLS manifest, which affects how special characters in the child manifest path are represented in the parent manifest.

aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint.low.text: The list of URLs for the low-latency HLS manifests served by this origin endpoint.
Sets the name used for the child manifest within the low-latency HLS manifest group, which is appended to the endpoint's URL to request that specific media rendition.
Configures which variant streams and time range are included in a low-latency HLS manifest by specifying an optional manifest filter expression and start/end timestamp boundaries.
Sets the timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) of the earliest clip to include in the low-latency HLS manifest, defining the start boundary of the playback window.
The end time (in ISO 8601 format) defining the exclusive upper bound of the time window for which the low-latency HLS manifest includes media segments.
Specifies a manifest filter expression that determines which segments are included in the low-latency HLS manifest output.
Sets the start boundary (ISO 8601 timestamp) for the low-latency HLS manifest's filter window, causing content before this time to be excluded from the manifest output.
For each low-latency HLS manifest, sets the manifest's time delay in seconds, which determines how far behind the live edge content is served to viewers.

The manifest name is the unique identifier for this low-latency HLS manifest, which gets appended to the origin endpoint's base URL to form the manifest's playback URL (e.g., .../<manifest_name>.m3u8).
Specifies the total duration (in seconds) of the low-latency HLS manifest's sliding window, controlling how much previously available content is listed in the manifest.
Specifies the interval in seconds between EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME tags inserted into the low-latency HLS manifest generated by this origin endpoint.
Configures SCTE-35 ad insertion for the low-latency HLS manifest, specifying ad marker types and optional SCTE-35 filtering.
Specifies whether SCTE-35 ad markers are passed through or enhanced (PASSTHROUGH or SCTE35_ENHANCED) for the low-latency HLS manifest.
For each low-latency HLS manifest, the scte_in_manifests field in its scte_hls configuration specifies which SCTE-35 event IDs are included in the manifest, controlling which ad markers are emitted.
Configures the EXT-X-START tag on the low-latency HLS manifest to control the playback start offset and precision for the media player.
Controls whether the EXT-X-START tag in the low-latency HLS manifest includes the PRECISE attribute, signaling that the start time offset is exact rather than approximate.
Specifies the time offset (in seconds) from the beginning of the content at which playback should start, as advertised by the EXT-X-START tag in the low-latency HLS manifest.
The URL of the low-latency HLS manifest, which is the endpoint that media players use to request the streaming content from this origin endpoint.
Determines whether the low-latency HLS parent manifest URL-encodes the query string of the child manifest URLs, which is necessary when those strings contain reserved characters.

aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint.mss.text: The list of URLs for the Microsoft Smooth Streaming (MSS) manifests generated by this MediaPackage v2 origin endpoint, which clients use to access the packaged stream.
Defines filtering options for the Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest, such as a start/end time window and a delay, to control which content is available to players.

Sets the beginning of the timestamp range (in ISO 8601 format) used to filter which segments appear in the Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest for this origin endpoint, so that content before this time is excluded from the delivered manifest.
Defines the end timecode of the manifest window, causing the Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest to include only segments up to that specified time.

For a Microsoft Smooth Streaming (MSS) manifest, this string defines a manifest filter expression that determines which tracks (e.g., video or audio) are included in the delivered manifest, enabling content selection based on filter criteria.
Specifies the beginning of the time window for the Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest, limiting the manifest to content at or after this timestamp.
Specifies the delay (in seconds) before content appears in the Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest, which is used to control the availability window for live streams.
Determines the format of the Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest, using COMPACT for a condensed layout or FULL for a detailed layout.
The name of the Microsoft Smooth Streaming (MSS) manifest associated with this manifest configuration.
Sets the time window, in seconds, of the Microsoft Smooth Streaming manifest, determining how far back the manifest lists segments for playback.

aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint.ori.text: The name of the origin endpoint, which uniquely identifies it within its parent channel and channel group in AWS MediaPackage v2.

aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint.seg.text: Specifies the encryption method applied to CMAF (fMP4) segments, with allowed values 'SAMPLE_AES' for sample-based AES and 'AES_CTR' for AES counter mode.
Specifies the encryption method for Microsoft Smooth Streaming (ISM) segments in the endpoint's encryption configuration.
Specifies the MPEG-TS encryption method (e.g., AES-128 or SAMPLE_AES) used for HLS and low-latency HLS outputs when the encryption method is TS-based.

Specifies the SPEKE v2.0 encryption contract preset for audio content, selecting the predefined audio encryption scheme and key provider configuration (e.g., PRESET-AUDIO-1) applied to all audio tracks in the origin endpoint's segments.
Specifies the SPEKE v2 encryption contract preset for video content, defining the encryption algorithm and key parameters applied to video segments in the origin endpoint.
Specifies whether SCTE-35 messages are inserted into the media segments for the origin endpoint, with 'INSERT' enabling insertion and 'NONE' disabling it.

aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint.tag.text: Defines a list of key-value tags to attach to the MediaPackage v2 origin endpoint, enabling resource identification, cost allocation, and access management.
The key of a user-defined tag applied to this MediaPackage v2 origin endpoint, which must be unique among the endpoint's tags and is used for cost allocation and resource filtering.

For the MediaPackage v2 origin endpoint resource, this field specifies the value part of a tag, which is a user-defined string used to organize, identify, and categorize the resource for management and cost tracking.

aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint.uri.text: For the DASH manifest of an AWS Elemental MediaPackage v2 origin endpoint, this property sets the URI separator character (either '/' or '_') used in the segment template URL to delimit segment numbers from the preceding path.

aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint_pol.text: Specifies the name of the MediaPackage v2 channel group that contains the origin endpoint to which this policy is attached.
The name of the AWS MediaPackage v2 channel that contains the origin endpoint for which this policy is defined.
The name of the MediaPackage v2 origin endpoint that this resource attaches the IAM resource policy to.

The IAM resource policy document (in JSON) that authorizes specific principals or accounts to access this MediaPackage v2 origin endpoint, controlling allowed API actions such as playback or content retrieval.

aws_media_store_container.access_logging.text: Enables or disables access logging for the MediaStore container, which generates detailed logs of requests made to the container.

aws_media_store_container.container_name.text: The name of the container, which must be unique within the region and can contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens.

aws_media_store_container.cors_policy.text: Configures the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policy for the container, allowing you to specify which origins, methods, and headers are permitted for cross-origin requests to the container's endpoints.

aws_media_store_container.cors_policy.al.text: Specifies the list of HTTP headers that are allowed in cross-origin requests to the MediaStore container, defining which headers can be included in the actual request as part of a CORS policy.
Specifies the list of HTTP methods (such as GET, PUT, POST, DELETE, HEAD) that are allowed for cross-origin requests to this MediaStore container.
Specifies the list of origin domains that are allowed to make cross-origin requests to the MediaStore container.

aws_media_store_container.cors_policy.ex.text: Specifies the list of response headers that browsers are allowed to access when making cross-origin requests to the MediaStore container, as part of the CORS rule.

aws_media_store_container.cors_policy.ma.text: The number of seconds that the browser is allowed to cache the CORS preflight response for this MediaStore container.

aws_media_store_container.endpoint.text: The fully qualified HTTPS endpoint assigned to the MediaStore container, used to access its content.

aws_media_store_container.id.text: The unique container name that identifies this MediaStore container and serves as the resource's primary identifier.

aws_media_store_container.lifecycle_poli.text: Specifies the JSON lifecycle policy for the container, defining rules that automate the deletion of objects after a specified number of days.

aws_media_store_container.metric_policy.text: The metric policy object that configures which CloudWatch metrics MediaStore publishes for the container, including container-level and per-object-group metrics.

aws_media_store_container.metric_policy..text: Specifies whether CloudWatch container-level metrics are enabled for this AWS Elemental MediaStore container, with valid values ENABLED or DISABLED.
Defines the list of metric policy rules that specify object group patterns and their names for enabling CloudWatch metrics on those object groups within the MediaStore container.
Specifies the object group name pattern (e.g., '/content/$(folder)') that this metric policy rule applies to, determining which objects' metrics are emitted.

Provides the friendly name for the object group in an AWS Elemental MediaStore container metric policy rule, identifying a set of object paths that the rule applies to for CloudWatch metric collection.

aws_media_store_container.policy.text: Specifies the resource-based policy, as a JSON string, that defines access permissions for the MediaStore container.

aws_media_store_container.tags.text: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the AWS Elemental MediaStore container for organizing, identifying, and managing the resource, such as for cost allocation and access control.

aws_media_store_container.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Elemental MediaStore container, used to identify and categorize the resource within AWS.

aws_media_store_container.tags.value.text: The value portion of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Elemental MediaStore container, used to organize and identify the container.

aws_media_tailor_channel.channel_name.text: The name of the MediaTailor channel, which must be unique within an AWS account and region and is used as a logical identifier when creating outputs, configuring playback, or referencing the channel in IAM policies.

aws_media_tailor_channel.outputs.dash_pl.text: Specifies the DASH manifest settings for the output, including the manifest window duration, minimum buffer time, and suggested presentation delay that MediaTailor uses when generating DASH content.
Specifies the total duration in seconds of each DASH manifest window for this MediaTailor channel output.
Specifies the minimum buffer time in seconds for DASH playlists generated by this MediaTailor channel.

In an AWS MediaTailor channel's DASH output settings, this field sets the minimum update period in seconds for the DASH manifest, determining the lowest frequency at which MediaTailor can refresh the manifest.
Sets the suggested presentation delay duration (in seconds) for the DASH manifest of this MediaTailor channel output.

aws_media_tailor_channel.outputs.hls_pla.text: The HLS playlist settings for this output, which define the ad marker formatting (such as DATERANGE or EXT-X-CUE-OUT) utilized in the generated HLS playlists.
Specifies the ad markup types for the HLS playlist output, with valid values of DATERANGE or SCTE35_ENHANCED, which determine how ad markers are represented in the channel's HLS playlists.
The duration in seconds of the HLS manifest window for this output, controlling how much playback history is available in the playlist.

aws_media_tailor_channel.outputs.manifes.text: The manifest name for this output, which appears as the filename in the playback manifest URL (e.g., index.m3u8 or index.mpd) that MediaTailor generates for the channel's output.

aws_media_tailor_channel.outputs.source_.text: The name of the source group that this output uses, matching one of the source groups defined in the channel's sources list.

aws_media_tailor_channel.playback_mode.text: Specifies whether the MediaTailor channel plays content in a continuous loop (LOOP) or according to a linear schedule (LINEAR).

aws_media_tailor_channel.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to this MediaTailor channel, used to organize and identify the channel for cost allocation and access control.

aws_media_tailor_channel.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the MediaTailor channel, used to categorize and identify the channel for cost allocation and management.

aws_media_tailor_channel.tier.text: The pricing tier for the channel, which determines the feature set and cost, with allowed values `basic` and `standard`.

aws_media_tailor_channel_policy.channel_.text: The name of the MediaTailor channel to which this channel policy is attached.

aws_media_tailor_function.http_request_c.text: A map of custom HTTP headers that the MediaTailor function includes in outgoing requests to its configured endpoint, enabling authentication or environment-specific header values.

aws_media_tailor_function.sequential_exe.text: In the AWS::MediaTailor::Function resource, the run_condition property within the function_list of a sequential executor configuration defines a logical expression that controls when that specific function is executed in the sequence.
The runtime environment in which the MediaTailor function's code executes when using the sequential executor configuration, specifying the programming language and version.

aws_media_tailor_live_source.http_packag.text: Specifies the relative path to the HTTP media package, which MediaTailor appends to the source location's base URL to fetch the live content.

Specifies the name of the source group to which this HTTP package configuration belongs, allowing MediaTailor to route playback requests to the correct source for a given package type (e.g., DASH or HLS).
Specifies the streaming format (e.g., DASH or HLS) for this HTTP package configuration.

aws_media_tailor_live_source.live_source.text: The name that uniquely identifies this live source within its MediaTailor source location.

aws_media_tailor_live_source.source_loca.text: The name of the source location that contains this live source.

aws_media_tailor_live_source.tags.key.text: Specifies the key for a tag associated with the AWS MediaTailor live source, enabling metadata-based resource management.

aws_media_tailor_live_source.tags.value.text: The user-defined value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to the MediaTailor LiveSource, used for resource metadata, identification, and cost allocation.

aws_media_tailor_playback_configuration..text: Specifies whether to condition the streaming media file for ad stitching, with allowed values 'NONE' (no conditioning) or 'AUDIO_ONLY' (condition the audio track only).
The hls_configuration object is a read-only block that exposes the generated manifest endpoint prefix assigned by MediaTailor for delivering the HLS playlist for this playback configuration.
The mode for ad insertion in the playback configuration, where PLAYER_SERVER directs MediaTailor to handle server-side ad insertion and CUSTOM allows the use of a custom ad insertion server.
Configures CloudWatch Logs logging for the playback configuration, including the percentage of session logs to send to CloudWatch Logs.
Configures whether MediaTailor logs ad interaction events, such as clicks and impressions, to CloudWatch Logs for this playback configuration, typically via an Enabled flag within the object.
This object configures whether MediaTailor logs manifest service interaction events to Amazon CloudWatch, with an `Enabled` subfield to turn this logging on or off.
The value of a tag keyed on the AWS MediaTailor playback configuration, providing an arbitrary string for categorizing, filtering, or cost-allocating the resource.

aws_media_tailor_source_location.access_.text: Determines the access method for the source location, with valid values `S3_SIGV4` for authenticated Amazon S3 access and `STREAMING` for streaming-based access.

aws_media_tailor_source_location.segment.text: Specifies the base URL from which MediaTailor retrieves content segments for the source location, serving as the origin for segment delivery.
The name of the segment delivery configuration, which uniquely identifies this configuration within the source location.

aws_media_tailor_source_location.source_.text: The unique name that identifies this AWS Elemental MediaTailor source location, required when creating the resource and used to reference it in other MediaTailor APIs and resources.

aws_media_tailor_source_location.tags.ke.text: A user-defined tag key assigned to this AWS MediaTailor source location for resource organization and identification.

aws_media_tailor_source_location.tags.va.text: The value portion of a key-value user-defined tag applied to the MediaTailor source location, used for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource.

aws_media_tailor_vod_source.http_package.text: The relative path to the manifest file (e.g., /path/to/index.m3u8) for the HTTP package configuration of the VOD source.
The source group name that groups this HTTP package configuration with others in the same VOD source, used by MediaTailor to select the appropriate manifest during playback.
Specifies the type of media packaging for this HTTP package configuration, which must be either HLS or DASH.

aws_media_tailor_vod_source.source_locat.text: The name of the MediaTailor source location that this VOD source is associated with; the source location defines the origin server and delivery settings for the media content.

aws_media_tailor_vod_source.tags.key.text: A key in the user-defined tag map applied to the MediaTailor VOD source resource, used for metadata and resource organization.

aws_media_tailor_vod_source.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag assigned to the MediaTailor VOD source, serving as the value portion of a key-value metadata pair.

aws_media_tailor_vod_source.vod_source_n.text: A unique identifier for the VOD source within its MediaTailor location, used when referencing the source in playback configurations and other resources.

aws_memory_db_acl.tags.key.text: The key name of a tag to associate with the MemoryDB ACL.

aws_memory_db_acl.tags.value.text: The string value of a key-value pair in the tags map for the MemoryDB ACL, allowing users to attach custom metadata to the resource.

aws_memory_db_cluster.cluster_endpoint.text: The DNS hostname and port of the MemoryDB cluster's endpoint, which clients use to connect to the cluster.

aws_memory_db_cluster.data_tiering.text: Specifies whether data tiering is enabled for the cluster, a feature that stores infrequently accessed data in Amazon S3 to reduce memory cost and is supported only on r6gd node types, using values 'true' or 'false'.

aws_memory_db_cluster.ip_discovery.text: Specifies the IP discovery protocol for the MemoryDB cluster, determining whether client connections use IPv4 or IPv6; valid values are 'ipv4' and 'ipv6'.

aws_memory_db_cluster.network_type.text: The network type of the MemoryDB cluster, either 'ipv4' or 'dualstack', which determines whether the cluster uses only IPv4 or both IPv4 and IPv6 addressing.

aws_memory_db_cluster.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag applied to the MemoryDB cluster, used for organizing and identifying cluster resources.

aws_memory_db_multi_region_cluster.tags..text: The value of a tag attached to the MemoryDB Multi-Region Cluster, used for labeling and cost allocation.

aws_memory_db_parameter_group.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a tag to attach to the MemoryDB parameter group, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_memory_db_parameter_group.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag assigned to the MemoryDB parameter group, used to organize, identify, and manage the resource in AWS.

aws_memory_db_subnet_group.tags.key.text: The key portion of a tag applied to this MemoryDB subnet group, used to organize, identify, and apply IAM-based access controls to the resource.

aws_memory_db_user.authentication_mode.text: Specifies the authentication method for the MemoryDB user, including the authentication type and the list of passwords that can be used to access the user's cluster.

aws_memory_db_user.tags.value.text: The value of the tag key-value pair applied to the MemoryDB user.

aws_mgn_network_migration_definition.sou.text: Specifies the environment of the source network (typically 'ON_PREMISES' or 'AWS') for each source configuration in the network migration definition.
The name of the S3 bucket that contains the source network configuration data used by the MGN network migration definition when the source type is S3.
Specifies the AWS account ID of the owner of the S3 bucket referenced in the source configuration, enabling MGN to access buckets across accounts for network migration data.

aws_mgn_network_migration_definition.tag.text: The key portion of a tag attached to the network migration definition, used to label the resource for filtering, cost tracking, and operational management.

aws_mpa_approval_team.approval_strategy..text: In the M-of-N approval scheme (indicated by the path element 'mof_n'), specifies the minimum number of approvals (the 'm' value) that must be granted by the approval team for the strategy to be satisfied.

aws_mpa_approval_team.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the approval team, used as a durable reference in IAM policies and AWS Marketplace APIs.

aws_mpa_approval_team.last_update_time.text: A read-only string field that records the time when the approval team was last updated, managed automatically by AWS.

aws_mpa_identity_source.identity_source_.text: The URL of the approval portal associated with the IAM Identity Center identity source, where users can review and approve or deny access requests.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS Single Sign-On) instance that this identity source is associated with.
The AWS region where the IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO) instance used as the identity source is deployed.

aws_msk_batch_scram_secret.cluster_arn.text: The ARN of the Amazon MSK cluster to which the batch of SASL/SCRAM secrets will be associated.

aws_msk_batch_scram_secret.secret_arn_li.text: The list of AWS Secrets Manager secret ARNs to associate with the MSK cluster for SCRAM authentication.

aws_msk_channel.iceberg_destination_conf.text: The name of the destination database in the target Apache Iceberg catalog where the replicated table is stored, as specified in the Iceberg destination table list.
The name of the Apache Iceberg destination table that the channel's delivery stream writes records to.
Specifies the partitioning scheme for the destination Iceberg table, defining how records are grouped into table partitions using transforms such as bucket, truncate, or time-based functions.
