In the MSK channel's Iceberg destination configuration, this list defines the source columns (with their partition transforms) from each incoming Kafka record that determine how data is partitioned in the corresponding destination Iceberg table.
The name of a source field in the Kafka record (key or value) that is used as a partition column in the destination Iceberg table.

aws_msk_channel.topic_configuration_list.text: The ARN of the AWS Glue Schema Registry schema used to define the record format for the Kafka topic, enabling serialization and validation of messages.

aws_msk_cluster.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the MSK cluster.

aws_msk_cluster.broker_node_group_info.text: Configures the compute and networking resources for the Apache Kafka broker nodes, including instance type, number of brokers, subnets, and EBS storage settings.

aws_msk_cluster.broker_node_group_info.b.text: Defines how broker nodes are distributed across Availability Zones for the MSK cluster, with `DEFAULT` distributing them evenly and `USE_DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY_ZONES` using the cluster's default AZ configuration.

aws_msk_cluster.broker_node_group_info.c.text: The list of subnets in the VPC where the Apache Kafka broker nodes are deployed, determining their Availability Zone placement and network reachability for clients.
Configures VPC connectivity and public access settings for the broker nodes in the MSK cluster.
Specifies the network type for the broker nodes, either 'VPC' for private VPC-only access or 'PUBLIC' for public internet access.
Defines public accessibility for the cluster brokers by setting a type, such as DISABLED (no public access) or SERVICE_PROVIDED_EIPS (public access via Elastic IP addresses).
Specifies the public access mode for the MSK cluster brokers, with allowed values DISABLED (no public access) or SERVICE_PROVIDED_EIPS (brokers are assigned public Elastic IP addresses).
Configures VPC connectivity for the cluster's broker nodes, specifying client authentication methods (TLS and SASL) for clients accessing the cluster over VPC.
Specifies the client authentication methods (SASL/SCRAM, SASL/IAM, and TLS) that clients must use when connecting to the MSK cluster brokers through VPC connectivity.
Configures SASL authentication (enabling IAM, SCRAM, or both) for clients connecting to the cluster via VPC connectivity.
Specifies whether AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) is enabled for SASL authentication for clients connecting via VPC connectivity.
When set to true, enables IAM-based SASL authentication for clients connecting to the cluster through VPC connectivity.
Specifies the SCRAM authentication settings for MSK cluster VPC connectivity, including an Enabled flag to turn on SASL/SCRAM username-password authentication for clients.
Indicates whether SCRAM (Salted Challenge Response Authentication Mechanism) authentication is enabled for SASL client authentication over VPC connectivity in the MSK cluster.
Specifies the TLS client authentication settings for clients using VPC connectivity, allowing you to enable or disable mutual TLS authentication for the cluster.
When set to true, enables TLS client authentication for clients connecting to the MSK cluster through VPC connectivity, requiring them to present valid certificates.

aws_msk_cluster.broker_node_group_info.i.text: The EC2 instance type for the broker nodes, such as kafka.m5.large, which determines the compute and memory capacity of each broker.

aws_msk_cluster.broker_node_group_info.s.text: One or more security group IDs to attach to the cluster's broker nodes, controlling inbound and outbound network traffic to the Apache Kafka brokers.
Specifies the EBS storage configuration for the broker nodes, including the volume size and optional provisioned throughput settings.
Configures the size and optional provisioned throughput of the Amazon EBS storage volumes attached to each broker node of the MSK cluster.

This object configures provisioned I/O throughput for the EBS storage volumes attached to the MSK broker nodes, allowing you to specify a higher throughput than the baseline for performance-critical workloads.
Indicates whether to enable provisioned throughput on the EBS storage attached to the broker nodes.
Sets the target provisioned throughput in MiB/s for the EBS volumes attached to the Kafka broker nodes.
Specifies the size in GiB of the EBS storage volume for each broker node in the MSK cluster, determining the total storage capacity available for Kafka data.

aws_msk_cluster.client_authentication.text: Defines client authentication methods for the MSK cluster, such as TLS, SASL/SCRAM, IAM, or unauthenticated access, via the nested `sasl`, `tls`, and `unauthenticated` properties.

aws_msk_cluster.client_authentication.sa.text: Configures the SASL authentication mechanisms (e.g., SCRAM or IAM) enabled for clients connecting to this MSK cluster.
Enable IAM-based access control for SASL authentication, allowing Kafka clients to authenticate using AWS IAM credentials.
Enables AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) as the SASL authentication mechanism for the cluster, allowing clients to authenticate using IAM credentials.
Configures SASL/SCRAM authentication for the MSK cluster, including whether it is enabled and how credentials are stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
Enables SASL/SCRAM authentication for the MSK cluster, allowing clients to authenticate with usernames and passwords stored in AWS Secrets Manager.

aws_msk_cluster.client_authentication.tl.text: Enables TLS mutual authentication for clients connecting to the MSK cluster by specifying the Certificate Authority (CA) ARNs used to issue and verify client certificates.
A list of AWS Private Certificate Authority (ACM PCA) ARNs used to validate client certificates for mutual TLS authentication in the MSK cluster.
Controls whether TLS-based client authentication (mutual TLS) is enabled for the MSK cluster, requiring clients to present valid certificates when connecting.

aws_msk_cluster.client_authentication.un.text: This is a boolean flag that enables or disables unauthenticated (anonymous) access to the Apache Kafka brokers in the MSK cluster, allowing clients to connect without SASL/SCRAM or IAM authentication when set to true.
Enables or disables unauthenticated access to the Apache Kafka cluster, allowing clients to connect without providing credentials when set to true.

aws_msk_cluster.cluster_name.text: A unique, user-friendly name for the MSK cluster, which must be unique within the AWS account and Region and is used as the cluster's identifier in the AWS Management Console and API calls.

aws_msk_cluster.configuration_info.text: Specifies the Amazon MSK configuration (ARN and revision) to use for the cluster.

aws_msk_cluster.configuration_info.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the MSK cluster configuration that the cluster is associated with.

aws_msk_cluster.configuration_info.revis.text: The revision number of the Amazon MSK configuration to apply to the cluster.

aws_msk_cluster.encryption_info.text: Specifies the encryption configuration for the MSK cluster, including encryption at rest using a KMS key and encryption in transit for client and broker communication.

aws_msk_cluster.encryption_info.encrypti.text: Configures encryption of data at rest for the MSK cluster's broker volumes, including the AWS KMS key used for encryption.
The ARN or ID of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt data at rest on the broker volume(s) of the MSK cluster.

Specifies in-transit encryption settings for the MSK cluster, including the client broker encryption mode (TLS, TLS_PLAINTEXT, or PLAINTEXT) and whether communication between brokers within the cluster is encrypted.
Specifies the encryption setting for client-to-broker communication, with valid values TLS, TLS_PLAINTEXT, or PLAINTEXT.
Indicates whether data encryption among broker nodes in the Amazon MSK cluster is enabled (default true).

aws_msk_cluster.enhanced_monitoring.text: Determines the granularity of Amazon CloudWatch metrics for the MSK cluster, with valid values including DEFAULT, PER_BROKER, PER_TOPIC_PER_BROKER, and PER_TOPIC_PER_PARTITION.

aws_msk_cluster.kafka_version.text: The version of Apache Kafka to use for the cluster, such as '2.8.1'.

aws_msk_cluster.logging_info.text: Specifies the broker log delivery configuration for the MSK cluster, including destinations such as CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3, and Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.

aws_msk_cluster.logging_info.authorizer_.text: Defines the destinations and settings for delivering Amazon MSK authorizer logs, which contain details about authentication and authorization requests for the cluster's IAM access control.
Configures the destination and enablement for streaming the cluster's authorizer logs (from the AWS IAM access control) to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, specifying the log group to which MSK delivers them.
When true, enables delivery of Amazon MSK authorizer logs to the configured CloudWatch Logs log group.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group where MSK delivers authorizer logs (records of client authentication and authorization attempts).

Configures the delivery of Amazon MSK authorizer logs (Kafka authentication and authorization events) to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream, including whether delivery is enabled and the name of the destination delivery stream.
The name of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that the MSK cluster's authorizer logs are sent to when Firehose logging is enabled.
Whether to enable delivering Amazon MSK authorizer logs to the specified Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream.
Configures delivery of MSK authorizer logs to an Amazon S3 bucket, including whether delivery is enabled, the destination bucket name, and an optional key prefix.
The name of the S3 bucket where Amazon MSK sends authorizer logs for the cluster.
Whether to enable delivery of Amazon MSK authorizer logs to the specified Amazon S3 bucket.
Specifies the S3 key prefix under which authorizer logs are stored in the destination bucket.

aws_msk_cluster.logging_info.broker_logs.text: Configures delivery of the cluster's Apache Kafka broker logs to one or more supported destinations (CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3, or Kinesis Data Firehose), including whether each destination is enabled.
Specifies the settings for delivering Apache Kafka broker logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, including an Enabled flag and an optional LogGroup name.
Whether Amazon MSK delivers Kafka broker logs to the specified Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group where Amazon MSK broker logs are delivered when CloudWatch Logs logging is enabled.

Specifies the configuration for delivering Amazon MSK broker logs to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream, including whether delivery is enabled and the ARN of the destination delivery stream.
The name of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that receives the MSK broker logs when Firehose is chosen as the logging destination.
Indicates whether broker logs are delivered to the specified Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream for this MSK cluster.
Specifies the Amazon S3 destination for Apache Kafka broker logs, including whether delivery is enabled, the bucket name, and an optional key prefix.
The name of the S3 bucket where Amazon MSK delivers broker logs when S3 logging is enabled.
Whether to enable the delivery of Apache Kafka broker logs to an Amazon S3 bucket.
The S3 object key prefix that is prepended to the names of the broker log files uploaded to the S3 bucket for MSK broker logs.

aws_msk_cluster.number_of_broker_nodes.text: The number of broker nodes to be provisioned in the Amazon MSK cluster.

aws_msk_cluster.open_monitoring.text: Configures open monitoring settings for the MSK cluster, including Prometheus exporter settings for JMX and node metrics.

aws_msk_cluster.open_monitoring.promethe.text: Specifies the Prometheus exporter configuration for the MSK cluster's open monitoring, with nested settings for the JMX and node exporters.
Configures the JMX Exporter settings for the cluster's Prometheus open monitoring, including whether the exporter is enabled on the brokers.
Indicates whether to enable the JMX Exporter on the Apache Kafka broker nodes to expose JMX metrics to Prometheus for open monitoring.
Specifies the Node Exporter configuration for the cluster's Prometheus monitoring, including the flag that enables or disables the Node Exporter on the broker nodes.
Enables the Prometheus NodeExporter on each MSK broker node to expose node-level metrics (CPU, memory, disk, network) for open monitoring.

aws_msk_cluster.rebalancing.text: Specifies the rebalancing settings for the MSK cluster, which control how the cluster automatically reassigns partition leaders and replicas among brokers during topology changes.

aws_msk_cluster.rebalancing.status.text: Determines whether automatic partition rebalancing is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for the MSK cluster.

aws_msk_cluster.storage_mode.text: Specifies the storage mode for the MSK cluster, either LOCAL for local EBS storage only or TIERED to enable tiered storage that automatically moves older data to Amazon S3.

aws_msk_configuration.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this MSK configuration.

aws_msk_configuration.description.text: A user-friendly description of the MSK configuration.

aws_msk_configuration.kafka_versions_lis.text: Defines the list of Apache Kafka versions that this MSK configuration supports, restricting its use to clusters running one of the specified versions.

aws_msk_configuration.latest_revision.text: Provides details about the latest revision of the MSK configuration, including its revision number, creation time, and description.

aws_msk_configuration.latest_revision.cr.text: Creation time of the latest revision of the MSK configuration, returned as an RFC3339 timestamp string.

aws_msk_configuration.latest_revision.de.text: The description of the latest revision of this Amazon MSK configuration, which is an optional user-defined string.

aws_msk_configuration.latest_revision.re.text: The revision number of the latest version of the MSK configuration, incremented each time the configuration is updated.

aws_msk_configuration.name.text: The name of the MSK configuration, which must be unique within an AWS account and Region.

aws_msk_configuration.server_properties.text: Specifies the Apache Kafka server properties for this MSK configuration, supplied as a string of newline-separated `key=value` pairs that define broker settings such as `auto.create.topics.enable`.

aws_msk_replicator.kafka_clusters.amazon.text: Defines the Amazon MSK cluster details (containing the MSK cluster ARN) for a source or destination Kafka cluster in the replicator.
The ARN of an Amazon MSK cluster that is included in the replicator's set of Kafka clusters, serving as a source or target for replication.

aws_msk_replicator.kafka_clusters.apache.text: Configuration for a self-managed Apache Kafka cluster used as a source or target in the MSK replicator, specifying the bootstrap broker string and VPC settings for network connectivity.
A unique user-supplied string that identifies the self-managed Apache Kafka cluster so the MSK replicator can reference it in the replication info.
The bootstrap broker string (comma-separated list of host:port pairs) of the self-managed Apache Kafka cluster used as a source or target for replication.

aws_msk_replicator.kafka_clusters.client.text: The client_authentication property specifies the authentication mechanism (such as IAM, TLS, or SASL/SCRAM) used by the replicator to securely connect to this Kafka cluster during replication.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the client certificate and private key used for mutual TLS authentication when connecting to this Kafka cluster.

Specifies SASL/SCRAM authentication settings for the associated Kafka cluster, including an 'Enabled' flag that determines whether the replicator uses SASL/SCRAM authentication when connecting to the cluster.
Specifies the SASL/SCRAM authentication mechanism (e.g., SCRAM-SHA-512) used by the replicator to connect to the Kafka cluster.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the SASL/SCRAM credentials used to authenticate to the Kafka cluster.

aws_msk_replicator.kafka_clusters.encryp.text: Configures encryption-in-transit settings for the connection to this Kafka cluster, specifying whether TLS is used (e.g., TLS or PLAINTEXT).
Sets the encryption-in-transit type (either 'TLS' or 'PLAINTEXT') that the MSK replicator uses when communicating with this Kafka cluster.
The root CA certificate (in PEM format) used to validate the Kafka broker's certificate when establishing an encrypted TLS connection to the source or target Kafka cluster.

aws_msk_replicator.kafka_clusters.vpc_co.text: Specifies the VPC configuration for the Kafka cluster, including the subnets and security groups used for network access to the cluster.
Specifies the security groups that the MSK replicator uses to access the Kafka cluster in its VPC.
Specifies the list of subnet IDs in the VPC where the Kafka cluster's network interfaces are deployed for the replicator to communicate with the cluster.

aws_msk_replicator.replication_info_list.text: Defines the configuration for replicating consumer groups between the source and target Kafka clusters, including the list of consumer group names to replicate and whether to synchronize their offsets.
Determines how consumer group offsets are synchronized from the source Kafka cluster to the target Kafka cluster during replication.
The list of consumer group names to exclude from being replicated by the MSK Replicator for this replication pair, meaning their offsets will not be copied between clusters.
A list of consumer group names whose offsets will be replicated from the source Kafka cluster to the target cluster as part of the MSK Replicator's consumer group replication.
Indicates whether to automatically detect and replicate newly created consumer groups to the target cluster during ongoing replication.

Specifies whether to periodically synchronize consumer group offsets from the source Kafka cluster to the target cluster, ensuring that consumer group positions are kept in sync for failover or migration scenarios.
The ARN of the source Kafka cluster from which the replicator replicates data, specified within each replication info entry.
The identifier of the source Apache Kafka cluster from which data is replicated within a replication configuration.
Defines the compression type (e.g., NONE, GZIP, SNAPPY, LZ4, ZSTD) applied to the topic data as it is replicated from the source cluster to the target cluster in the MSK Replicator.
In each replication info entry, the ARN of the target Kafka cluster to which the replicator replicates data.
The identifier (typically the ARN) of the target Kafka cluster that this replication entry replicates topics and consumer group data to.
Specifies the topic replication configuration for a given replication pair, including which topics to replicate, the starting position for reading records, and how topic names are handled.
Whether to copy access control lists (ACLs) for topics from the source cluster to the target cluster in the MSK replicator.
Indicates whether topic configurations (such as topic-level settings) are copied from the source cluster to the target cluster during replication.
When enabled, the replicator automatically detects newly created topics in the source cluster and begins replicating them to the target cluster.
Specifies where the replicator starts reading topics from in the source cluster, using either the latest or earliest offset to determine the initial synchronization point.
Determines whether topic replication starts from the latest offset (LATEST) or the earliest available offset (EARLIEST) in the source cluster.
Specifies the configuration for how replicated topic names are derived, such as using the same name or prefixing with the source alias.
Specifies whether replicated topic names are kept identical to the source topics (SAME_AS_SOURCE) or prefixed with the replication prefix (PREFIXED_WITH_SOURCE).
Specifies the list of Kafka topic names that are excluded from replication, meaning these topics will not be replicated to the destination cluster.
A list of Kafka topic names to replicate from the source cluster to the target cluster.

aws_msk_serverless_cluster.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the serverless cluster.

aws_msk_serverless_cluster.client_authen.text: Configures client authentication for the MSK Serverless cluster, specifically enabling or disabling AWS IAM access control via the nested Sasl.Iam property.

Defines the SASL authentication configuration for the MSK Serverless cluster, which must include the Iam property to enable IAM-based client authentication, as serverless clusters support only IAM as the SASL mechanism.
Enables IAM access control for SASL authentication, allowing clients to authenticate to the cluster using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) credentials.
Enables IAM-based access control for SASL authentication on the MSK Serverless cluster.

aws_msk_serverless_cluster.cluster_name.text: The name to assign to the serverless Apache Kafka cluster.

aws_msk_serverless_cluster.vpc_configs.text: Specifies the VPC subnets and security groups that define the network configuration for the serverless cluster, allowing client applications to connect to the Kafka endpoints.

aws_msk_serverless_cluster.vpc_configs.s.text: A list of security group IDs to associate with the MSK Serverless cluster's elastic network interfaces in the VPC.
The list of subnet IDs in the customer VPC where the MSK Serverless cluster's network interfaces and broker endpoints are provisioned.

aws_msk_vpc_connection.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to the MSK VPC connection.

aws_msk_vpc_connection.client_subnets.text: Specifies the subnets in the client VPC where the MSK VPC connection is created, enabling network access from those subnets to the cluster.

aws_msk_vpc_connection.security_groups.text: Specifies the security group IDs to attach to the elastic network interface created for the MSK VPC connection, controlling traffic to and from client resources.

aws_msk_vpc_connection.vpc_id.text: The ID of the client VPC that will be connected to the MSK cluster using this VPC connection.

aws_mwaa_environment.logging_configurati.text: The ARN of the CloudWatch log group where Apache Airflow DAG processing logs are delivered in the MWAA environment.
Indicates whether DAG processing logs are enabled for the Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA) environment.
Sets the log level (e.g., CRITICAL, ERROR, WARNING, INFO, or DEBUG) for the DAG processing logs in the Amazon MWAA environment.
The ARN of the CloudWatch Logs log group that receives the scheduler logs for the MWAA environment, enabling access and monitoring of those logs in CloudWatch.
Whether to enable the publishing of scheduler logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs for the MWAA environment.
Sets the CloudWatch Logs log level (e.g., INFO, DEBUG) for the scheduler component of the Amazon MWAA environment, controlling the verbosity of scheduler logs.
The ARN of the CloudWatch Logs log group to which the MWAA environment delivers its Airflow task logs.
Whether to enable task-level logging for the Amazon MWAA environment, which captures logs from Airflow task instances.
The log level for Amazon MWAA task logs, controlling which task-level Airflow log messages are recorded in CloudWatch Logs.
The ARN of the CloudWatch Logs log group that receives the Apache Airflow web server logs for the MWAA environment.
Whether to enable the collection of Apache Airflow web server logs into CloudWatch Logs for this MWAA environment.
The severity threshold for the Amazon MWAA web server logs, which determines the verbosity of log output and accepts values like CRITICAL, ERROR, WARNING, INFO, and DEBUG.
The ARN of a pre-existing CloudWatch Logs log group where Amazon MWAA sends worker environment logs, allowing you to use a custom log group instead of the automatically created one.
Whether to enable logging for the worker instances in the MWAA environment.
Specifies the verbosity level (CRITICAL, ERROR, WARNING, INFO, or DEBUG) for Airflow worker logs in the MWAA environment's CloudWatch log group.

aws_mwaaserverless_workflow.created_at.text: The timestamp, in ISO 8601 format, that indicates when the serverless workflow was created.

aws_mwaaserverless_workflow.definition_s.text: The name of the S3 bucket where the workflow definition file (DAG) for this MWAA Serverless workflow is stored.
The S3 object key (key) identifying the workflow definition file within the bucket specified by the parent definition_s3_location, which is required to load the workflow's DAG from S3.
The specific version identifier of the S3 object that contains the workflow definition, used to reference a particular version of the file in the S3 bucket.

aws_mwaaserverless_workflow.encryption_c.text: Specifies the AWS KMS key configuration for encrypting the MWAA environment's data, with the key ARN provided in the nested 'KmsKey' property.
Specifies the customer-managed AWS KMS key ID (or ARN/alias) that Amazon MWAA uses to encrypt the serverless workflow's definition and related data at rest.

aws_mwaaserverless_workflow.logging_conf.text: Configures the logging settings for the AWS MWAA serverless workflow, specifying whether to enable logging and the log level (e.g., INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL) for each component such as DAG processing, scheduler, task, web server, and worker logs.

aws_mwaaserverless_workflow.modified_at.text: The read-only timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the MWAA serverless workflow was last modified, as provided by the AWS API.

aws_mwaaserverless_workflow.network_conf.text: Defines the VPC network configuration, including the subnet IDs and security group IDs, that the serverless workflow uses to run and access resources within your VPC.
A list of security group IDs that AWS MWAA attaches to the VPC network interfaces of the serverless workflow environment, controlling inbound and outbound traffic.
Provides the private subnet IDs within your VPC that the serverless workflow's underlying AWS resources are placed in, allowing the workflow to run in your own isolated network.

aws_mwaaserverless_workflow.role_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that Amazon MWAA (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow) assumes to access resources in your account, such as S3 buckets and CloudWatch Logs, on behalf of the serverless workflow.

aws_mwaaserverless_workflow.schedule_con.text: The cron expression that defines the schedule on which the serverless workflow runs, using standard Unix cron syntax.

aws_mwaaserverless_workflow.trigger_mode.text: Specifies how the workflow is triggered, with allowed values such as SCHEDULE (for cron-based scheduling) or EVENT (for event-driven execution).

aws_nat_gateway.availability_zone_addres.text: The allocation IDs of the Elastic IPs to associate with the NAT Gateway for each usable Availability Zone, so that a specific public IP is assigned per AZ.

aws_nat_gateway.eni_id.text: The identifier of the Elastic Network Interface (ENI) automatically created for the NAT gateway to provide network connectivity, as returned by AWS.

aws_nat_gateway.nat_gateway_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the NAT gateway.

aws_nat_gateway.tags.key.text: The key of a tag in the tag set for the NAT gateway, used to categorize and identify the resource.

aws_nat_gateway.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag attached to the NAT gateway, used for resource metadata, organization, and cost allocation.

aws_neptune_dbcluster.associated_roles.f.text: The name of the Neptune feature (for example, `FullTextSearch`) that the associated IAM role enables for the DB cluster.

aws_neptune_dbcluster.associated_roles.r.text: The ARN of an IAM role to associate with the Neptune DB cluster, granting the cluster permissions to access other AWS services such as S3 for data loading or SageMaker for machine learning.

aws_neptune_dbcluster.tags.key.text: The tag key for a tag assigned to the Neptune DB cluster, enabling custom categorization and cost tracking.

aws_neptune_dbcluster.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag applied to the Neptune DB cluster, used for resource identification and organization.

aws_neptune_dbcluster_parameter_group.ta.text: Specifies the value portion of a tag applied to this Neptune DB cluster parameter group, where each tag is a user-defined key-value pair.

aws_neptune_dbinstance.tags.key.text: The key of an arbitrary tag attached to the Neptune DB instance, used to identify the tag for resource organization, cost tracking, and access control.

aws_neptune_dbinstance.tags.value.text: Value of the tag key assigned to the Neptune DB instance, used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_neptune_dbparameter_group.tags.key.text: The customer-defined key portion of a tag attached to the Neptune DB parameter group, used to label and organize the resource according to your own metadata scheme.

aws_neptune_dbparameter_group.tags.value.text: The value part of a key-value tag that can be attached to the AWS Neptune DB parameter group, used for identifying and categorizing the resource for cost allocation and operational management.

aws_neptune_dbsubnet_group.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to associate with the Neptune DB subnet group.

aws_neptune_dbsubnet_group.tags.value.text: The value of a tag associated with the Neptune DB subnet group, used to categorize and manage the resource within AWS.

aws_neptune_event_subscription.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Neptune event subscription, used to organize, categorize, and identify the subscription for cost allocation and resource management.

aws_neptune_event_subscription.tags.valu.text: The value of a tag attached to the Neptune event subscription, used for metadata such as environment, owner, or cost tracking.

aws_neptune_global_cluster.tags.key.text: The user-defined key of a key-value pair tag applied to the AWS::Neptune::GlobalCluster resource.

aws_neptune_global_cluster.tags.value.text: The user-defined value associated with a tag key on the Neptune global cluster, used for metadata and resource categorization.

aws_neptune_graph_graph.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Neptune Analytics graph, used to identify the tag within the resource's tag set.

aws_neptune_graph_graph_snapshot.tags.ke.text: The key of a tag (a key-value pair) attached to the Neptune Graph snapshot, used for identifying, organizing, or managing the resource.

aws_neptune_graph_graph_snapshot.tags.va.text: The value string paired with a tag key in the tags list for the Neptune graph snapshot, used for resource organization and cost tracking.

aws_network_acl.id.text: The AWS-assigned identifier for the network ACL, which uses the format acl-xxxxxxxx.

aws_network_acl.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the network ACL, used to label and organize the resource for identification and management within AWS.

aws_network_acl.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag applied to the network ACL, used to assign metadata such as purpose or ownership to the ACL.

aws_network_firewall_firewall.availabili.text: Controls whether the firewall's assigned Availability Zones can be changed, with true preventing any modifications to the Availability Zones associated with the firewall.
Specifies the Availability Zones and subnet IDs where the firewall endpoints are created, enabling network traffic filtering in those zones.
The Availability Zone (e.g., us-east-1a) where the Network Firewall endpoint is deployed, matching the zone of the associated subnet in the mapping.

aws_network_firewall_firewall.delete_pro.text: Whether the firewall is protected from deletion, so you cannot delete it without first disabling this setting.

aws_network_firewall_firewall.descriptio.text: A description of the firewall, as provided by the user, which helps identify the firewall's purpose or context.

aws_network_firewall_firewall.endpoint_i.text: The list of VPC endpoint IDs created for the firewall in each of its associated subnets, used to route traffic to the firewall.

aws_network_firewall_firewall.firewall_i.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this Network Firewall firewall.

aws_network_firewall_firewall.firewall_n.text: A descriptive name for the Network Firewall firewall, used as an identifier for the resource.

aws_network_firewall_firewall.firewall_p.text: When set to true, prevents the firewall policy associated with this firewall from being changed, allowing updates only after this protection is disabled.

aws_network_firewall_firewall.subnet_cha.text: Indicates whether the firewall's subnet mappings are protected from changes, requiring the protection to be disabled before you can modify the subnets associated with the firewall.

aws_network_firewall_firewall.subnet_map.text: Specifies the subnets within the VPC where the Network Firewall endpoint is attached, enabling the firewall to filter traffic for each associated subnet.
Specifies whether the firewall endpoint in the associated subnet uses an IPv4 or IPv6 address, with valid values 'IPV4' or 'IPV6'.
The ID of the subnet in the VPC where the firewall endpoint is deployed.

aws_network_firewall_firewall.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the Network Firewall firewall, used to categorize and identify the resource for management and cost allocation.

aws_network_firewall_firewall.tags.value.text: The tag value pairs with a corresponding tag key to label the Network Firewall firewall for resource organization, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_network_firewall_firewall.transit_ga.text: The unique identifier of the Transit Gateway attachment that connects the firewall to its VPC, populated after the firewall is created.

aws_network_firewall_firewall.vpc_id.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) where the AWS Network Firewall firewall is deployed.

aws_network_firewall_firewall_policy.des.text: A user-provided description of the firewall policy, used to identify its purpose or contents.

aws_network_firewall_firewall_policy.fir.text: Defines the core AWS Network Firewall policy configuration, including references to stateless and stateful rule groups and the default actions for unmatched traffic.
Enables the Network Firewall to hold the TLS session and buffer handshake packets during TLS inspection, ensuring the certificate is evaluated before the connection continues.

Defines named policy variables (such as IP set and port set values) that are substituted into Suricata rules within stateful rule groups associated with this firewall policy, allowing reuse of common values across rules.
Defines the rule variables (IP sets and port sets) for the firewall policy, which are used by the Suricata rule engine to enable dynamic matching of source and destination IPs or ports.
Specifies the default actions to apply to traffic that does not match any stateful rule group in the firewall policy (e.g., 'aws:drop' or 'aws:pass').

Specifies the stateful engine behavior for the firewall policy, including the rule group evaluation order (STRICT_ORDER or DEFAULT_ACTION_ORDER) and the action to take for stream exceptions (DROP or CONTINUE).
Specifies the idle timeout durations for TCP and UDP flows processed by the stateful inspection engine.
Specifies the idle timeout in seconds for TCP flows, after which the firewall considers the connection idle and may terminate it.

Determines the order in which stateful rules are evaluated, with valid values such as DEFAULT_ACTION_ORDER, STRICT_ORDER, and LAST_ACTION_ORDER, affecting how traffic is matched and actions are applied.

Controls whether packets that do not match any stateful rule are dropped (DROP) or passed to the stateless engine for further inspection (CONTINUE) within the firewall policy's stateful engine options.

Specifies the stateful rule groups, identified by their ARNs, that are used in the firewall policy's stateful rule engine, with an optional priority controlling the order in which their rules are evaluated.
Enables deep threat inspection for the referenced stateful rule group, allowing the firewall to perform deeper packet analysis on traffic matching that rule group.
This object configures an override action (DROP_TO_FIRST or PASS_TO_FIRST) that alters the default evaluation behavior of the associated stateful rule group reference within the firewall policy.
Specifies the override action (DROP, PASS, or CONTINUE) for a stateful rule group reference in the firewall policy, determining how traffic matching the rule group's rules is handled.
Determines the order in which the referenced stateful rule group is evaluated relative to other stateful rule groups in the policy, with lower numbers evaluated first.
The ARN of the stateful rule group to associate with the firewall policy, used to apply stateful inspection to matching traffic.

Defines the list of custom actions you can reference in stateless rules within this firewall policy, where each action specifies a name and an action definition such as publishing metrics to CloudWatch.
Defines the action taken by a stateless custom action in an AWS Network Firewall policy, which currently supports a publish_metric_action that publishes metrics to Amazon CloudWatch.
Configures CloudWatch metric publishing for this stateless custom action, including the metric dimensions to include when metrics are emitted.
Specifies the list of key-value dimensions that are attached to the CloudWatch metric published by this stateless custom action's publish-metric action.
The value for a CloudWatch dimension that is attached to the metric published when a stateless custom action is invoked, as part of the firewall policy's publish metric action.
The action_name is a user-defined, policy-unique friendly name for a custom stateless action, which is referenced by stateless rules in the firewall policy to invoke the defined action.
Specifies the default actions (e.g., 'aws:pass' or 'aws:drop') to apply to packets that do not match any stateless rule in the firewall policy.
A required list of default actions applied to fragmented packets that do not match any stateless rule in the firewall policy, such as 'aws:drop' or 'aws:forward_to_sfe'.
Defines the stateless rule groups to associate with the firewall policy, each with a priority and rule group ARN, controlling the order in which stateless rules are evaluated.
The priority of a stateless rule group reference, where lower numbers are evaluated first, determining the order in which stateless rule groups are processed within the firewall policy.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the stateless rule group that this reference points to, which the firewall policy uses to apply stateless packet inspection in the specified priority order.
The unique identifier assigned to the firewall policy by AWS Network Firewall, used to reference this policy in other resources.
The descriptive name of the firewall policy, used to identify it within AWS Network Firewall.

aws_network_firewall_firewall_policy.tag.text: A key of a tag that is assigned to the Network Firewall firewall policy to help organize and identify it.

aws_network_firewall_logging_configurati.text: The name of the Network Firewall firewall resource that this logging configuration applies to, used as an alternative to the firewall ARN.

Specifies the logging destinations and configuration for the network firewall, including the list of log destination configs that define where firewall logs are sent (e.g., to CloudWatch Logs, S3, or Kinesis Data Firehose).
Specifies the destinations and log types (alert or flow) to which Network Firewall sends its logs, such as Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3, or Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.

Specifies the actual destination details as key-value pairs, such as the S3 bucket name, CloudWatch Logs log group, or Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream, that correspond to the chosen LogDestinationType in the Network Firewall logging configuration.
Defines the kind of service that receives the firewall logs, such as Amazon S3, CloudWatch Logs, or Kinesis Data Firehose.
The type of Network Firewall log to send to this destination, either ALERT for firewall alert logs or FLOW for firewall flow logs.

aws_network_firewall_rule_group.capacity.text: The maximum number of capacity units the rule group can consume, limiting the total number of rules and rule actions that can be defined in the group.

aws_network_firewall_rule_group.descript.text: A user-provided description for the rule group, used to identify its purpose or contents within AWS Network Firewall.

aws_network_firewall_rule_group.rule_gro.text: Configuration object for the rule group, specifying the stateful or stateless rules source, rule variables, and reference sets that define the network traffic inspection behavior.
Specifies named sets of IP addresses or domain names that can be referenced by the rule group's stateful rules (e.g., using the REF keyword in Suricata rules).
Specifies the named IP set references for the rule group, mapping each reference name to the ARN of an AWS Network Firewall IP set that rules in this rule group can use.
Defines the IP sets and port sets that can be referenced by the rule group's rules for matching traffic attributes.
Defines named IP set variables, each mapping a key to an object containing a list of CIDR ranges, which can be referenced in the rule group's rules to match source or destination addresses.
Defines named port sets, each mapping a name to a list of port ranges, which are referenced in the rule group's rules to match source or destination port numbers.
Defines the rules for the rule group, specifying either stateless rules and custom actions or stateful rule configuration using a rules string, rules source list, or individual stateful rules.

Specifies the list of IP addresses or domain names that the rule group inspects, the target types (such as HTTP_HOST, TLS_SNI, SOURCE, or DESTINATION) that determine how the targets are matched, and whether matching traffic is allowed or dropped via the GeneratedRulesType.
Specifies whether the rule group generates allow or deny rules for the referenced domain list, with values 'ALLOWLIST' or 'DENYLIST'.
Specifies the target types to inspect (such as TLS_SNI for TLS server name indication or HTTP_HOST for HTTP host header) when using the domain list rules source in the rule group.
The list of IP addresses or CIDR blocks that the stateful rule group inspects traffic to or from, as defined in the rules source list.
Specifies the Suricata-compatible rules string that defines the stateful inspection rules for the rule group, used when the rule group is configured as a stateful rule group.

Defines a list of ordered stateful rules, each combining a header (protocol, source, destination, action) with Suricata rule options, used by AWS Network Firewall to perform stateful inspection of traffic.
Defines the action taken when traffic matches the stateful rule, such as PASS, DROP, ALERT, or REJECT.
Defines the match criteria for a stateful rule's traffic header, specifying the protocol, source and destination IP addresses and ports, and the direction of traffic to match.
The destination IP address or CIDR range that the stateful rule matches in the traffic header.
Defines the destination port (or port range) to match in the stateful rule's header, expressed as a number, a range separated by a colon (e.g., 20:80), or the keyword ANY.
Specifies the traffic direction to match, either FORWARD or ANY, for stateful rules in the rule group.
The IP protocol (e.g., TCP, UDP, ICMP, IP) that the stateful rule header matches, determining which network protocol the rule applies to.
Specifies the source IP address or CIDR range that the stateful rule matches on.
The source port (or port range) to match in the stateful rule's header, representing the originating port of the traffic.
Configures the keyword options applied to each stateful rule in the Network Firewall rule group, such as the rule's sid, rev, msg, or protocol-specific keywords.

This field specifies the keyword (name) of a key-value rule option for a stateful rule, such as 'sid', 'rev', 'content', or 'flow', which is used by the Suricata-compatible rule engine to set matching conditions or metadata for the rule.

Specifies the values for a Suricata rule option in a stateful rule, such as the rule ID for a `sid` keyword or the message text for a `msg` keyword, used to customize matching and inspection in AWS Network Firewall.
Defines the stateless rules and custom actions to use in a stateless rule group.
Specifies custom actions that can be referenced by stateless rules to perform additional behaviors such as publishing metrics to Amazon CloudWatch.

Defines the action definition for a custom stateless action, which contains the PublishMetricAction configuration that specifies the CloudWatch metric dimensions to report when the action matches traffic.
Configures the CloudWatch metric publication for this custom action by specifying the dimension(s) that the published metrics are tagged with.
Specifies the list of key-value dimension pairs attached to the CloudWatch metric published when this custom action is invoked, enabling you to filter or group the metric by these dimensions.
The value of a dimension to include in the CloudWatch metric published by the custom action's publish_metric_action.
A unique name that identifies a custom action within the rule group, which stateless rules reference to invoke the action's defined behavior.
Defines the list of stateless rules that specify match criteria and actions for packets processed without stateful inspection in the Network Firewall rule group.
The priority value for the stateless rule, which determines the order in which rules are evaluated (lower numbers take precedence).
Defines the actions to take and the matching criteria (such as source and destination addresses, ports, and protocols) for a stateless rule in the rule group.
Specifies the actions to take on packets that match the stateless rule, such as 'aws:pass', 'aws:drop', or custom action names defined in the rule group.
Defines the traffic match criteria (such as source/destination addresses, ports, protocols, and TCP flags) against which the stateless rule evaluates packets.
Defines the destination port ranges (from and to) that a stateless packet must match for the rule to apply.
The lower bound of the destination port range that a stateless rule uses to match traffic.
The upper bound (inclusive) of a destination port range to match in stateless rule evaluation, with valid values 0-65535 and defaulting to the lower bound if omitted.
Specifies the destination IP address or CIDR range that the stateless rule matches against traffic to evaluate the rule.
The destination IP address or CIDR block to match in the stateless rule's traffic attributes, such as '192.0.2.0/24'.
Specifies the IP protocol numbers (for example, 6 for TCP, 17 for UDP) that the stateless rule matches, or if omitted, matches all protocols.
Defines the source port ranges (with FromPort and ToPort) that the stateless rule matches on for incoming traffic.
The lower bound (inclusive) of the source port range to match in the stateless rule's source ports.
The upper bound (inclusive) of the source port range that a stateless rule uses to match traffic.
Specifies the source IP addresses (as CIDR blocks or individual IPs) that this stateless rule matches; if empty, matches any source address.
The IP address or CIDR range that defines a source address to match in a stateless rule's match attributes, used by AWS Network Firewall to filter traffic based on packet source.
Defines the TCP flags (e.g., SYN, FIN, ACK) that this stateless rule matches on, including optional masks to limit which flag bits are inspected.
Specifies the TCP flags (e.g., FIN, SYN, RST, PSH, ACK, URG, ECE, CWR) to match in the packet's TCP header for the stateless rule.
The list of TCP flag names (for example, 'SYN', 'ACK', 'FIN', 'RST') that define which flags in the packet's TCP header are examined (masked) when evaluating this stateless rule's match conditions.
This object specifies the rule order and stream exception policy for a stateful rule group in AWS Network Firewall.

Specifies how the stateful rule group evaluates rules: either in the default action order (DEFAULT_ACTION_ORDER) based on action type and priority, or in the strict order in which rules are defined (STRICT_ORDER).
The unique identifier (UUID) assigned by AWS to the rule group when it is created.
Specifies the name of the rule group, which must be unique within the AWS account and Region.

aws_network_firewall_rule_group.summary_.text: Configures the optional rule group summary feature, which enables generation of per-rule match counts for stateful rules in the group, with an enabled flag and a subject (such as `rulegroupsummary`) that specifies the type of summary.

aws_network_firewall_rule_group.tags.text: Specifies the AWS resource tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the Network Firewall rule group, used for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization.

aws_network_firewall_rule_group.type.text: Specifies whether the rule group is a stateful rule group (STATEFUL) or a stateless rule group (STATELESS), which determines the kind of rules and matching behavior it supports.

aws_network_firewall_tlsinspection_confi.text: An optional user-defined description for the TLS inspection configuration, helping to identify the resource within AWS Network Firewall.
A list of key-value tag objects to attach to the TLS inspection configuration for resource identification, organization, and cost allocation.
The key of a tag attached to the AWS Network Firewall TLS inspection configuration, used for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource.
The user-defined string value associated with a tag key on the AWS Network Firewall TLS inspection configuration, used for identifying or categorizing this resource.
Defines the TLS inspection configuration for the Network Firewall, including the server certificate configurations that specify how encrypted traffic is decrypted and inspected.

Defines the list of server certificate configurations, where each configuration specifies an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate ARN and optional scopes (such as destination IP addresses and protocols) that determine which TLS traffic is decrypted and re-encrypted using that certificate in the Network Firewall TLS inspection configuration.
The ARN of the certificate authority (CA) used to issue the certificates for this TLS inspection configuration.
Defines the actions (pass, drop, or reject) to apply when a client certificate's revocation status check returns 'revoked' or 'unknown' during TLS inspection.
Defines the action (REJECT or PASS) that AWS Network Firewall takes when the revocation status check for the presented server certificate indicates that the certificate is revoked.
Specifies how AWS Network Firewall handles traffic when the revocation status of a certificate is unknown during TLS inspection, such as by passing or dropping the traffic.

Defines the list of network traffic scope objects (matching source/destination CIDRs, ports, and protocols) that determine which server certificate is used for TLS inspection in the AWS Network Firewall configuration.

Defines the list of destination port ranges to match for the TLS inspection scope, controlling which inbound traffic to the specified ports is inspected by the Network Firewall TLS inspection configuration.
The inclusive lower bound of the destination port range that defines which traffic the TLS inspection scope matches.
The upper bound (inclusive) of the destination port range that this TLS inspection scope uses to match network traffic.
Specifies the destination IP addresses or CIDR ranges that define which traffic this TLS inspection scope applies to.
Specifies an IP address or CIDR block used as a destination address in the TLS inspection scope.
The list of IP protocol numbers (e.g., 6 for TCP, 17 for UDP) that define which protocols the TLS inspection scope applies to.
Defines a list of source port ranges (with from_port and to_port) that the TLS inspection scope uses to match incoming traffic, controlling which connections are inspected.
The lower bound (inclusive) of a source port range in a scope that determines which traffic's source port the TLS inspection configuration applies to.
Defines the inclusive upper end of a range of source ports that are matched when determining whether TLS inspection applies to traffic in this server certificate configuration scope.
Specifies the source IP addresses for the TLS inspection scope, as a list of address definitions (such as CIDR blocks) that traffic must match to be inspected.
The source IP address or CIDR range that defines which traffic this scope applies to for TLS inspection, using a string in IP/CIDR format or the 'ANY' wildcard.
Specifies the server certificates that AWS Network Firewall uses to decrypt and inspect TLS traffic for this server certificate configuration, identified by their Amazon Resource Names (ARNs).
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the server certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that AWS Network Firewall uses for TLS inspection.
The unique identifier (UUID) assigned by AWS to this Network Firewall TLS inspection configuration.
A unique, user-friendly name for the TLS inspection configuration, used to identify it within the AWS account and Region.

aws_network_firewall_vpc_endpoint_associ.text: Defines the subnet mappings (each with subnet ID and optional IP address type) to associate with the Network Firewall VPC endpoint.
The unique identifier of the association between the Network Firewall firewall and the VPC endpoint, which is generated by AWS and used to track the association.
The ID of the VPC in which the VPC endpoint is being associated with the Network Firewall firewall.

aws_network_flow_monitor_monitor.local_r.text: The identifier of a local resource (such as a subnet or instance) that the monitor targets, typically the resource's ARN or AWS resource ID.
The AWS resource type of a local resource to monitor, such as AWS::EC2::VPC, AWS::EC2::Subnet, or AWS::EC2::Instance.

aws_network_flow_monitor_monitor.remote_.text: Specifies the AWS resource type of the remote resource (e.g., AWS::EC2::VPC or AWS::EC2::Subnet) that this monitor configuration applies to.

aws_network_interface.connection_trackin.text: Specifies the connection tracking configuration for the network interface, including idle timeout values for established TCP connections and UDP flows to control stateful traffic tracking.
Specifies the timeout (in seconds) for TCP established connections for the network interface's connection tracking configuration.
The timeout in seconds for UDP streams in the established state on this network interface, after which connection tracking removes the flow if no packets are seen.
Specifies the idle timeout in seconds for UDP traffic on the network interface, determining how long a UDP flow remains active in connection tracking before it expires.

aws_network_interface.ipv4_prefixes.ipv4.text: The IPv4 prefix (CIDR block) assigned to the network interface.

aws_network_interface.ipv6_addresses.ipv.text: Specifies an IPv6 address from the subnet's IPv6 CIDR block to assign to the network interface.

aws_network_interface.ipv6_prefixes.ipv6.text: The IPv6 prefix (CIDR block) assigned to the network interface, such as 2001:db8::/64.

aws_network_interface.private_ip_address.text: Indicates whether this private IP address is the primary private IP address of the network interface.
Specifies the private IPv4 address for a secondary IP address assignment on the network interface.

aws_network_interface.public_ip_dns_name.text: Specifies the type of DNS hostname to assign to the public IP address of the network interface, either 'ip-name' (default) or 'resource-name'.

The public_dual_stack_dns_name is the fully qualified public DNS hostname that AWS assigns to the network interface, resolving to both its public IPv4 and public IPv6 addresses when dual-stack DNS naming is enabled in the containing public IP DNS name options.

The DNS name automatically assigned to the network interface's public IPv4 address (e.g., ec2-203-0-113-10.compute-1.amazonaws.com), determined by the HostnameType and DNS A record settings configured in the public_ip_dns_name_options block.

aws_network_interface.tags.value.text: The value of a tag applied to the network interface, used for resource categorization, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_network_interface_attachment.attachm.text: The unique identifier for the attachment between the network interface and the instance.

aws_network_interface_attachment.ena_srd.text: Enable ENA Express (Scalable Reliable Datagram) for UDP traffic on the network interface attachment, which can improve throughput and reduce latency for UDP workloads.

aws_network_interface_permission.aws_acc.text: The AWS account ID that is granted permission to attach the network interface to an instance or associate it with an Elastic IP.

aws_network_interface_permission.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this network interface permission, used to reference the permission in other API calls.

aws_network_interface_permission.network.text: The ID of the Elastic Network Interface (ENI) to which this permission grants cross-account attachment access.

aws_network_interface_permission.permiss.text: The type of permission to grant on the network interface, either INSTANCE-ATTACH (allows an instance to attach to the interface) or EIP-ASSOCIATE (allows an Elastic IP to be associated with the interface).

aws_network_manager_connect_attachment.p.text: The key of a tag applied to the proposed network function group change for the AWS Network Manager connect attachment.

The value of a tag key-value pair in the list of tags to attach to the network function group when the proposed network function group change, defined on the AWS Network Manager Connect Attachment, is applied.
The key of a tag in the list of tags associated with the proposed segment change for the Network Manager connect attachment, used to specify metadata for the segment association.
The value of a key-value tag that will be applied to the Connect Attachment when the proposed segment change is executed.

aws_network_manager_connect_attachment.t.text: The value component of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Network Manager Connect Attachment, used for organizing and identifying the attachment through metadata.

aws_network_manager_connect_peer.bgp_opt.text: The autonomous system number (ASN) of the BGP peer used by the Connect Peer to establish a BGP session.

aws_network_manager_connect_peer.configu.text: The computed configuration of the Connect Peer, including the inside CIDR blocks, the protocol (GRE or IPSec), and the BGP configuration details such as peer and core network ASNs, IP addresses, and the Core Network edge endpoint address.
The BGP configurations of the connect peer, where each object contains the core network address and peer address that define the BGP peering for the connection.
The IPv4 address on the core network (Transit Gateway) side used for BGP peering in this Connect peer BGP configuration.
The autonomous system number (ASN) of the core network used for the BGP session of the connect peer.
The IP address of the BGP peer used to establish and identify the BGP session for the Connect Peer's BGP configuration.
The autonomous system number (ASN) of the BGP peer for the Connect peer.

aws_network_manager_connect_peer.tags.ke.text: The key part of a tag applied to the Network Manager Connect Peer, used to assign metadata for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_network_manager_connect_peer.tags.va.text: The value of a tag key attached to the Network Manager Connect Peer, used for resource metadata and cost tracking.

aws_network_manager_core_network.edges.a.text: The Autonomous System Number (ASN) assigned to the edge location for BGP peering within the core network.

aws_network_manager_core_network.edges.e.text: The AWS Region code (e.g., us-east-1) of the core network edge, returned as part of the edges list for the core network.

aws_network_manager_core_network.edges.i.text: The list of CIDR blocks assigned to a core network edge, indicating the IP address ranges that are routed within that edge's network segment.

aws_network_manager_core_network.network.text: Specifies the AWS Regions (edge locations) where the network functions in this network function group are deployed and operate within the core network.
The name of the network function group, which uniquely identifies this group within the core network's policy and is referenced when attaching network functions to segments.
Defines the list of core network segment names to which this network function group is associated, controlling the segments where the group's network functions can be deployed.
Specifies the list of segment names to which this segment can forward traffic, defining inter-segment reachability in the core network.
Specifies the list of network function groups through which traffic from the segment is routed, enabling service insertion in the core network.

aws_network_manager_core_network.segment.text: Specifies the list of AWS Regions (edge locations) where resources in this segment can be attached, controlling segment availability across the core network's global network.
The name of the network segment, which uniquely identifies it within the core network and is referenced by other configuration elements such as segment actions and route policies.
Specifies the list of other segment names within the same core network that this segment is allowed to share attachments with.

aws_network_manager_core_network.tags.ke.text: The key (name) of a user-defined tag assigned to the AWS Network Manager core network.

aws_network_manager_core_network.tags.va.text: The value portion of a tag key-value pair applied to the core network, used to store arbitrary metadata for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_network_manager_device.tags.value.text: For each tag attached to an AWS Network Manager device, this field specifies the tag's value, enabling you to associate arbitrary metadata (such as device location or environment) with the device for identification, resource organization, and cost allocation.

aws_network_manager_direct_connect_gatew.text: The key of a tag applied to the proposed network function group change for an AWS Network Manager Direct Connect Gateway attachment, used to add custom metadata to the change proposal.
The value of a tag associated with the proposed network function group change for this Direct Connect gateway attachment, used to label or categorize the change.
The key of a tag to apply to the proposed segment change for the Direct Connect Gateway attachment.
The value portion of a tag attached to the proposed segment change, used to tag the segment update for this Direct Connect Gateway attachment in Network Manager.
The key of a tag attached to the Direct Connect Gateway attachment, used to categorize the attachment for cost allocation and management within AWS Network Manager.
The value of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS Network Manager Direct Connect Gateway Attachment, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the attachment within AWS.

aws_network_manager_global_network.tags..text: The key part of a tag attached to the AWS Network Manager global network, used to label and organize the resource.

The value component of a tag associated with this AWS Network Manager global network, used to store an arbitrary string that helps identify or categorize the network for management and cost allocation purposes.

aws_network_manager_link.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the Network Manager link, used to organize and identify the resource for management and cost allocation purposes.

aws_network_manager_link.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the Network Manager link, used for organizing, identifying, or managing cost allocation for the link.

aws_network_manager_site.tags.key.text: The tag key is a metadata label that can be applied to an AWS Network Manager Site, allowing you to categorize and filter the site within your global network for management and cost tracking.

aws_network_manager_site.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS Network Manager site.

aws_network_manager_site_to_site_vpn_att.text: The key of a tag associated with the proposed network function group change for the Site-to-Site VPN attachment, used to label the network function group change for tracking and management.
The key (name) of a tag to apply to the proposed segment change for the AWS Network Manager site-to-site VPN attachment, used to identify or organize the change metadata.
The value of a tag attached to the proposed segment change for the site-to-site VPN attachment.
The key (name) of a tag to assign to the Site-to-Site VPN attachment, used to organize and identify the attachment within AWS Network Manager.
The value component of a tag (key-value pair) applied to the AWS Network Manager site-to-site VPN attachment, used for organization, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_network_manager_transit_gateway_peer.text: The key portion of a user-defined tag applied to the transit gateway peering, used to categorize and identify the resource for cost tracking, access control, and organizational purposes.
The value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Network Manager transit gateway peering, used for metadata and resource categorization.

aws_network_manager_transit_gateway_rout.text: Specifies the key (name) of a tag to apply to the proposed network function group change for the transit gateway route table attachment.
The value of a tag defined in the proposed network function group change for the AWS Network Manager transit gateway route table attachment.
The key of a tag object within the proposed segment change's tags list for the transit gateway route table attachment, serving as the identifier in the key-value metadata pair.

In the proposed segment change for an AWS Network Manager transit gateway route table attachment, this value is the tag value for the associated tag key that will be applied to the attachment when the change takes effect.
Defines the key portion of a user-defined tag applied to this Network Manager Transit Gateway Route Table Attachment, enabling identification, cost allocation, and access control for the resource.
The value of a user-defined tag applied to the transit gateway route table attachment, used for metadata, organization, and cost allocation.

aws_network_manager_vpc_attachment.propo.text: The key of a tag applied to the proposed network function group change for this VPC attachment.

The value part of a tag attached to the proposed network function group change for the VPC attachment, used to label or categorize the network function group proposal with metadata such as environment or purpose.
The key of a tag to be applied to the VPC attachment as part of the proposed segment change.
The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the proposed segment change for the VPC attachment, used to provide metadata about the change.

aws_network_manager_vpc_attachment.tags..text: The value of a tag (key-value pair) attached to the AWS Network Manager VPC attachment, used to organize and identify the attachment within AWS.

aws_notifications_contacts_email_contact.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this email contact resource in AWS User Notifications.
The email address of the contact that will be used to receive notifications from AWS services.
The email_contact field is a computed object that returns the details of the created email contact, including its ARN and current status, from the AWS Notifications Contacts service.
The email address of the contact that will receive AWS notifications.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the email contact that this resource associates with the notifications service.
The creation time of the email contact, stored as an ISO 8601 string, indicating when the contact was added to AWS User Notifications.
The friendly name assigned to the email contact, used to identify the contact in the AWS console and notifications.
The timestamp indicating when this email contact was last updated.
The friendly name for the email contact, used as a human-readable identifier for the contact within AWS User Notifications.
Provides the string value for a tag key attached to an email contact resource in AWS Notifications Contacts, enabling custom metadata for categorization and management.

aws_notifications_event_rule.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Notifications event rule, used to reference the rule in IAM policies, cross-service resource sharing, and API operations.

aws_notifications_event_rule.creation_ti.text: The timestamp indicating when the event rule was created, formatted as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

aws_notifications_event_rule.event_patte.text: Specifies a JSON string containing the event pattern that determines which events trigger this rule, such as matching AWS service, event type, or resource attributes.

aws_notifications_event_rule.event_type.text: Specifies the event type from the source AWS service that this notification rule matches (for example, a named event such as an EC2 instance state-change notification).

aws_notifications_event_rule.managed_rul.text: The list of Amazon EventBridge managed rule ARNs that AWS automatically creates and manages for this notification event rule.

aws_notifications_event_rule.notificatio.text: The ARN of the notification configuration to which this event rule belongs, determining the channel and settings used for delivering notifications from matched events.

aws_notifications_event_rule.regions.text: Specifies the AWS Regions in which the event rule is active and should apply.

aws_notifications_event_rule.source.text: Specifies the AWS service or event source (such as aws.ec2) that the notification rule monitors for events, acting as the source of the triggering events.

aws_notifications_event_rule.status_summ.text: This computed field provides a region-by-region summary of the event rule's status, indicating for each region whether the rule is active or has an error condition.

aws_notifications_notification_configura.text: Controls how long the notification configuration collects related events before delivering them as one aggregated notification, balancing timeliness against notification volume.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this notification configuration.
The timestamp when the notification configuration was created.

The Description property is a required string that provides a human-readable description of the notification configuration, enabling users to identify and distinguish configurations within AWS User Notifications.
The user-defined name for the notification configuration, used to identify and display the configuration in the AWS Management Console and APIs.
The read-only status of the notification configuration, indicating whether it is active (enabled) or inactive (disabled) for delivering notifications.
The key part of a tag applied to the notification configuration, used to label and categorize the AWS resource.

aws_notifications_notification_hub.creat.text: The date and time when the notification hub was created, typically returned as a string in ISO 8601 format.

aws_notifications_notification_hub.notif.text: Returns a summary of the current status of the notification hub in each region where it is enabled, with each entry specifying the region and its operational status (such as ACTIVE).
A human-readable explanation accompanying the hub's status that provides additional context when the notification hub is not fully active, such as a reason for an inactive or pending state.

aws_oam_link.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Observability Access Manager link.

aws_oam_link.label.text: The unique label generated by AWS for the link, which is used to identify this source account when configuring cross-account observability in the monitoring (sink) account.

aws_oam_link.label_template.text: Defines a template that generates the label for the link, which is used to identify the linked observability data within the monitoring account.

aws_oam_link.link_configuration.text: Specifies the configuration for the link, including filter settings for the log groups and metrics that will be shared from the source to the monitoring account.

aws_oam_link.link_configuration.log_grou.text: Specifies the configuration for sharing log groups through the link, including a filter pattern that determines which log groups are included.

Specifies a filter expression (such as a regex or a 'LogGroupName = ...' condition) that determines which CloudWatch Logs log groups in the source account are shared with the monitoring account through the OAM link.

aws_oam_link.link_configuration.metric_c.text: Specifies the configuration for sharing metric data from the source account, including a filter that defines which metric namespaces to include.
Specifies the comma-separated list of CloudWatch metric namespaces (e.g., AWS/EC2,AWS/S3) that the source account shares with the monitoring account via this OAM link for metric sharing.

aws_oam_link.resource_types.text: Specifies the AWS resource types to share with the monitoring account via this link, such as AWS::CloudWatch::Metric, AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm, or AWS::CloudWatch::LogGroup.

aws_oam_link.sink_identifier.text: The ARN of the sink in the monitoring account that this link sends observability data to.

aws_observability_admin_organization_cen.text: The rule configuration that defines how observability data is centralized across the organization, including the type of data to centralize and the target accounts or organizational units.
Configures the destination AWS account (and region) that serves as the central monitoring account for receiving observability data from member accounts according to this rule.
The AWS account ID of the destination account that receives centralized observability data (logs, metrics, and traces) when the rule's destination type is set to 'ACCOUNT'.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the backup data for the centralized logging destination, enabling customer-managed encryption of backup copies.
The AWS Region code (e.g., 'us-east-1') where the backup destination for the centralized logs is provisioned, providing a redundant copy for high availability.

Specifies an optional prefix and suffix that are added to the original CloudWatch log group names when logs are centralized to the destination account, controlling how the centralized log groups are named.
Specifies the pattern (e.g., a wildcard or regex) used to match CloudWatch log group names from member accounts that are selected for centralization to the destination defined by this rule.

Configures the encryption settings (such as the AWS KMS key ARN) used to encrypt the logs that are delivered to the centralized destination, ensuring the destination logs are encrypted with the specified key.

Specifies the strategy to resolve encryption key conflicts when centralizing logs, determining whether the organization's central encryption configuration overrides member accounts' existing log encryption settings or preserves them.
Defines the encryption strategy for logs delivered to the centralized destination, using 'SSE_S3' for AWS-managed encryption or 'SSE_KMS' for customer-managed KMS key encryption.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt logs delivered to the centralization rule's destination, enabling customer-managed key encryption for centralized log data.
Specifies the AWS Region of the backup destination for metrics when the primary destination is unavailable.
The AWS region of the destination where the organization's observability data is centralized by this rule.
Defines the source accounts or organizational units whose observability data (such as CloudWatch logs) is aggregated into the delegated administrator account by this organization centralization rule.
Specifies the AWS regions (e.g., us-east-1) whose telemetry from the source accounts is included in the centralized observability rule, limiting the rule's scope to those regions.
Specifies the strategy to apply to CloudWatch log groups that are encrypted with AWS KMS keys when collecting source logs for the organization's centralization rule.

The log_group_selection_criteria field specifies the selection mechanism used to choose which log groups from the source logs configuration are centralized by the rule, such as indicating whether all log groups or only those matching a defined pattern should be included.

Determines the metrics to centralize for the given source, enabling the administrator to specify whether to centralize all or a selected set of metrics as part of the observability centralization rule.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this centralization rule in AWS Observability Admin.
A user-defined name for the organization centralization rule, required to uniquely identify and manage the rule within AWS Observability Admin.

aws_observability_admin_organization_tel.text: The AWS region code (e.g., us-east-1) identifying the region whose telemetry rule status is reported in this region_statuses entry.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the telemetry rule created for a specific region, as reported in the region status map of the organization telemetry rule.
The current status of the organization telemetry rule in the associated AWS region, indicating whether the rule is active for that region.
Specifies the list of field selectors (e.g., eventCategory, eventName, or resource type) used to filter which CloudTrail events are matched by each advanced event selector in the telemetry rule.

Defines the list of strings that the value of the referenced field (e.g., event name, resource type) must end with for the event to match the advanced event selector in a CloudTrail telemetry destination configuration.

In the CloudTrail advanced event selectors of the destination configuration for this organization telemetry rule, the 'equals' field on a field selector defines the list of exact string values that the corresponding CloudTrail event attribute (e.g., eventName, readOnly) must match for the event to be delivered.

Specifies the CloudTrail event field name (such as 'eventCategory', 'eventName', or 'resources.type') used by the advanced event selector to filter which events are included for delivery to the configured destination in this organization telemetry rule.
