Specifies the list of values that the event field must not end with for the advanced event selector to match, filtering CloudTrail events in the destination configuration of the organization telemetry rule.

In the CloudTrail parameters of the telemetry rule, this list defines the values that the selected event field must not equal for the advanced event selector to match the event for telemetry collection.

Specifies a list of string prefixes that, when matched at the beginning of the selected event field's value, cause the event to be excluded from delivery, so only events whose field value does not start with any of these strings are delivered.

Within a CloudTrail advanced event selector's field selector, this list defines the prefixes that the selected event field's value must start with for the telemetry rule to forward matching events to CloudTrail.
The name of the advanced event selector, an optional user-defined label used to identify the selector within CloudTrail configuration.
The output format for the load balancer access logs delivered to the configured destination, specifying whether the logs are written as text (gzip compressed) or in Parquet format.
Determines whether log records that match the filter's condition are kept (KEEP) or dropped (DROP) from the WAF logging output.
Specifies the match conditions (such as AWS WAF action, label, or country) applied to each log record to determine whether it is kept or dropped by this logging filter for WAF log delivery.
Defines a condition that matches the WAF action (such as ALLOW, BLOCK, or COUNT) of a web request, used to determine whether the logging filter keeps or drops the log entry.
The action (such as ALLOW, BLOCK, or COUNT) taken by AWS WAF on the matched request, used as the condition for filtering WAF log entries.
Represents the label name matching condition used to filter WAF logs, with properties for the label name and comparison operator.

Specifies the exact WAF label name (e.g., a label added by a rule or rule group) that a web request must carry for this label-name condition in the logging filter to match and be included in the telemetry destination.
This field indicates that the HTTP method (such as GET or POST) is redacted (omitted) from AWS WAF logs in the telemetry rule's WAF logging destination configuration.
Configures a single HTTP header to redact from AWS WAF logging output, using a field-match type that identifies the header by its name.
The name of the HTTP header whose value will be redacted from the WAF logging data for this organization telemetry rule's destination configuration.

aws_observability_admin_s3_table_integra.text: The key of a tag that you can assign to the AWS Observability Admin S3 table integration to help identify, categorize, or manage the integration resource.

aws_observability_admin_telemetry_pipeli.text: The ARN (Amazon Resource Name) of a telemetry pipeline, which uniquely identifies the pipeline within the AWS Observability Admin service.
The Unix epoch timestamp (in seconds) indicating when the telemetry pipeline was created.
The timestamp (epoch time) indicating when the telemetry pipeline was last updated.
The user-defined name that uniquely identifies a telemetry pipeline within the AWS Observability Admin TelemetryPipelines resource.
Provides the reason text for the telemetry pipeline's current status, including error details when the pipeline is in a failed or non-active state.
Provides a human-readable message that explains why the telemetry pipeline is in its current state, as part of the status reason object.
Specifies the key of a tag attached to the telemetry pipeline, used to organize and identify the pipeline within AWS Observability Admin.
The value half of a key-value tag attached to the telemetry pipeline, used to store arbitrary metadata (such as an environment or owner name) for identifying and managing the pipeline.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the telemetry pipeline, used to reference the pipeline when managing or querying telemetry configurations.
The current lifecycle status of the telemetry pipeline (e.g., CREATING, ACTIVE, or FAILED), as determined by AWS.
The status_reason object contains detailed information, such as an error code and message, explaining why the telemetry pipeline is in its current state (e.g., ready, failed, or updating).
Provides a human-readable message that explains why the telemetry pipeline is in its current status, offering context beyond the status code.
The key portion of a tag applied to an AWS Observability Admin telemetry pipeline, used to attach custom metadata for organizing, identifying, and managing the pipeline resource.

aws_observability_admin_telemetry_rule.r.text: The AWS Region code (e.g., us-east-1) where the telemetry rule is applied or reported, as part of the RegionStatuses list.
For the corresponding region in the region status list, this attribute contains the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the telemetry rule deployed in that region.
Indicates whether the telemetry rule is active or inactive in the corresponding region, reflecting the rule's operational state for that region.

Specifies the list of field selectors that define which CloudTrail events match each advanced event selector, by comparing event fields such as eventName, readOnly, or resources against configured values for the telemetry rule.
Specifies the list of substrings that the selected event field's value must end with for the CloudTrail advanced event selector to match and the telemetry rule to forward the event.
Specifies the list of values that the selected CloudTrail event field must match exactly for an event to be included in the advanced event selector.
Specifies the name of a CloudTrail event field (e.g., eventCategory, eventName, resources.type) used by an advanced event selector to filter which telemetry events are delivered to CloudTrail.

Specifies a list of string suffixes that the field value must not end with, excluding events where the corresponding CloudTrail field matches any of these suffixes from being forwarded by the telemetry rule.
In a CloudTrail advanced event selector, not_equals specifies a list of values that the evaluated field must not equal for an event to be included in the telemetry rule's CloudTrail destination.
Defines a list of prefix strings such that if the value of the selected event field begins with any of these prefixes, that event is excluded from the telemetry rule's CloudTrail-based selection.

In the telemetry rule's CloudTrail destination configuration, this list sets the prefix values for the field selector so that only events whose field value starts with one of these strings are included by the advanced event selector.
A user-defined name for an advanced event selector, used to identify the selector within the CloudTrail configuration for the Observability Admin telemetry rule.
Specifies the output format for the load balancer access logs delivered to the telemetry sink, with valid values 'plain_text' or 'parquet'.
Specifies whether to keep or drop WAF logs that match this filter, with allowed values 'KEEP' or 'DROP'.

Defines the list of conditions for a WAF logging filter, where each condition matches on either a web ACL action (such as ALLOW or BLOCK) or a label name to determine which traffic is included in or excluded from the telemetry destination.

A condition that matches web requests based on the action taken by AWS WAF (such as ALLOW, BLOCK, or COUNT), used within a logging filter in the WAF logging parameters to determine which requests are logged.
Specifies the action value (e.g., ALLOW, BLOCK, COUNT) that the condition matches to filter WAF log entries.
Defines the exact WAF label name a request must contain for the logging filter to include the log, evaluated as one of the conditions in the filter's list for the WAF logging parameters.
The name of the AWS WAF label that must be present on a request for the logging filter condition to match.
Specifies whether the WAF logging filter condition is satisfied as a match (IS) or not match (IS_NOT) when applying the filter's keep/drop behavior to logs.
This field is the single header redaction specification, which contains the header name to be redacted from AWS WAF logs, ensuring that header's values are excluded from telemetry log output.
The name of the HTTP header that AWS WAF should redact from logs for this single-header redaction field.

aws_observability_admin_telemetry_rule.t.text: The key of a user-defined tag used to label an AWS::ObservabilityAdmin::TelemetryRule resource, enabling resource organization and cost tracking.

aws_odb_cloud_exadata_infrastructure.cus.text: The email address of a customer contact that Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) will send notifications to regarding this Exadata infrastructure.

aws_odb_cloud_vm_cluster.db_nodes.backup.text: The Oracle Cloud Identifier (OCID) of the second backup virtual network interface card (VNIC) assigned to the database node in the cloud VM cluster.

aws_odb_cloud_vm_cluster.db_nodes.cpu_co.text: Specifies the number of CPU cores allocated to each database node in the cloud VM cluster.

aws_odb_cloud_vm_cluster.db_nodes.memory.text: Specifies the memory size in gigabytes to allocate to each database node in the cloud VM cluster.

aws_odb_cloud_vm_cluster.db_nodes.ocid.text: For each database node in the Cloud VM Cluster, this field contains the node's Oracle Cloud Identifier (OCID), which uniquely identifies the node within Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.

aws_odb_cloud_vm_cluster.db_nodes.vnic2_.text: The `vnic2_id` field stores the OCID (unique identifier) of the secondary virtual network interface (VNIC) attached to the database node, providing an additional network connection for that node.

aws_odb_network.managed_services.cross_r.text: Specifies the AWS region where the S3 bucket serving as a cross-region restore source is located.

aws_odb_network.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the network resource, used as the tag's unique identifier within the resource.

aws_omics_annotation_store.creation_time.text: The timestamp indicating when the annotation store was created in AWS Omics.

aws_omics_annotation_store.description.text: A user-supplied description of the annotation store, providing optional additional context about the store's purpose or contents.

aws_omics_annotation_store.name.text: The name of the annotation store, which must be unique within the AWS account and region and serves as the primary identifier for the store.

aws_omics_annotation_store.reference.text: The reference property specifies the reference genome (such as GRCh38) that the annotation store is associated with, by providing either the ARN or the ID of an existing AWS Omics reference.

aws_omics_annotation_store.reference.ref.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Omics reference that defines the coordinate system against which the annotations in the store are interpreted.

aws_omics_annotation_store.sse_config.text: Specifies the server-side encryption (SSE) configuration for the annotation store, including the encryption type (such as KMS) and the AWS KMS key ARN to use for encrypting data at rest.

aws_omics_annotation_store.sse_config.ke.text: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the annotation store with server-side encryption.

aws_omics_annotation_store.sse_config.ty.text: The server-side encryption type for the annotation store, specifying whether to use Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) or AWS KMS managed keys (SSE-KMS).

aws_omics_annotation_store.status.text: The current lifecycle status of the annotation store, which can be one of CREATING, ACTIVE, UPDATING, DELETING, or FAILED.

aws_omics_annotation_store.status_messag.text: Provides a human-readable message about the current operational status of the annotation store, such as the reason a requested operation is pending or failed.

aws_omics_annotation_store.store_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the annotation store.

aws_omics_annotation_store.store_format.text: Specifies the file format of the annotation data stored in the annotation store, which is either TSV or VCF and determines the required store options.

aws_omics_annotation_store.store_options.text: StoreOptions specifies the format and schema for the annotation store, allowing you to choose either TSV options (which require a schema for each column) or VCF options (which configure how variant call files are interpreted).

Configures the TSV-format-specific options for the annotation store, including the annotation type (generic or chromosome-position) and the schema that defines the tab-separated column headers and data types.

Specifies whether the TSV annotation store contains chromosome-position-aware data (CHR_POS) or generic annotations (GENERIC), which determines how the store parses the schema and interprets genomic coordinates.
Indicates whether the first line of the TSV file is treated as a header row containing column names.
Specifies the schema of the TSV annotation store, listing each column's name and data type (such as STRING or LONG) to validate and parse the annotation files.

aws_omics_annotation_store.store_size_by.text: The total storage size of the annotation store in bytes, as reported by the AWS Omics service.

aws_omics_annotation_store.update_time.text: The timestamp of the last update to the annotation store, reported as an ISO 8601 string.

aws_omics_configuration.run_configuratio.text: The run_configurations object specifies the JSON run configuration settings (such as parameters and output locations) that are used when starting workflow runs for this Omics configuration.
Specifies the VPC settings (subnet IDs and security group IDs) for the compute environment used by Omics runs, enabling workflows to access resources within a Virtual Private Cloud.
Specifies the list of subnet IDs to use in the VPC configuration for an AWS Omics workflow run configuration.

aws_omics_reference_store.reference_stor.text: The unique identifier assigned to the reference store by AWS when it is created.

aws_omics_reference_store.sse_config.typ.text: The type of server-side encryption applied to the reference store, which must be either 'KMS' for a customer-managed AWS KMS key or 'S3' for Amazon S3-managed encryption.

aws_omics_reference_store.tags.text: A map of key-value tags to assign to the reference store for organizing, identifying, and managing it within AWS Omics.

aws_omics_run_cache.tags.value.text: The value of a tag (key-value pair) applied to the AWS Omics run cache.

aws_omics_run_group.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Omics run group.

aws_omics_run_group.creation_time.text: The time (in ISO 8601 format) when the run group was created.

aws_omics_run_group.id.text: The unique identifier automatically assigned by AWS Omics to the run group.

aws_omics_run_group.max_cpus.text: The maximum number of CPUs that can be used by all runs within this run group.

aws_omics_run_group.max_duration.text: Specifies the maximum duration in seconds that a run can run in this group, after which the run is automatically terminated.

aws_omics_run_group.max_gpus.text: Sets the maximum number of GPUs that a single workflow run within this run group can use.

aws_omics_run_group.max_runs.text: The maximum number of concurrently running workflows that this run group is allowed to have.

aws_omics_run_group.name.text: The user-specified name for the run group, used to identify the run group within the AWS account.

aws_omics_sequence_store.etag_algorithm_.text: Specifies the ETag algorithm family (e.g., MD5 or SHA256) used to compute ETags for sequence files in this AWS Omics sequence store.

aws_omics_sequence_store.sequence_store_.text: The unique AWS-generated identifier for the sequence store, used to reference the store in other Omics operations.

aws_omics_sequence_store.sse_config.type.text: Specifies the server-side encryption type for the sequence store; when set to 'KMS', data is encrypted using an AWS KMS key.

aws_omics_sequence_store.status.text: The current lifecycle status of the Omics sequence store, such as CREATING, ACTIVE, DELETING, or FAILED.

aws_omics_variant_store.creation_time.text: The timestamp when the variant store was created, in ISO 8601 format.

aws_omics_variant_store.description.text: A user-supplied description of the variant store, providing human-readable context for the resource.

aws_omics_variant_store.id.text: The unique ID of the variant store, which is the same as the store's name and is the identifier used by the AWS Omics API to reference the store.

aws_omics_variant_store.name.text: The name of the variant store, which is required, must be unique within the AWS account and region, and serves as the primary identifier for the resource.

aws_omics_variant_store.reference.text: Configures the reference genome for the variant store, specifying either the ARN or the alias of the reference sequence used for variant annotation.

aws_omics_variant_store.reference.refere.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the reference genome that the variants in this variant store are aligned to, typically from an AWS HealthOmics reference store.

aws_omics_variant_store.sse_config.text: Specifies the server-side encryption configuration for the variant store, including the encryption type (KMS or S3) and the KMS key ARN when using KMS.

aws_omics_variant_store.sse_config.key_a.text: The ARN of the AWS KMS customer-managed key used to encrypt the variant store data at rest.

aws_omics_variant_store.sse_config.type.text: Specifies the server-side encryption type for the variant store, which must be either 'KMS' (use a customer-managed key specified in KeyArn) or 'S3' (use S3-managed encryption).

aws_omics_variant_store.status.text: The current lifecycle status of the variant store, such as CREATING, ACTIVE, UPDATING, DELETING, or FAILED.

aws_omics_variant_store.status_message.text: The status message provides additional details about the current state of the variant store, such as the reason for a failure during creation or updates.

aws_omics_variant_store.store_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Omics variant store, assigned by AWS when the store is created.

aws_omics_variant_store.store_size_bytes.text: The total size of the variant store in bytes, computed and reported by AWS after the store is created.

aws_omics_variant_store.tags.text: Tags to assign to the variant store for cost allocation, access control, and resource management in AWS Omics.

aws_omics_variant_store.update_time.text: The timestamp indicating when the variant store was last updated, typically in ISO 8601 format.

aws_omics_workflow.accelerators.text: The accelerators property specifies the type of compute accelerator (such as GPU) to use for the workflow run.

aws_omics_workflow.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Omics workflow.

aws_omics_workflow.container_registry_ma.text: A map of container image names to their fully-qualified registry image URIs, used to override the default container registries from which the workflow's container images are pulled.
Specifies a list of container image mappings that map original image URIs in the workflow definition to replacement URIs (e.g., private registry copies) for the corresponding container registry key.
The destination container image URI that replaces the source image when the Omics workflow pulls its containers, redirecting to an alternate registry or repository.
The original container image URI as referenced in the workflow definition, which is mapped to an alternative image URI for execution via the container registry map.
Specifies a list of container registry mappings, each mapping a registry name to an image URI, so that the workflow can use custom or private container images for its tasks.
The AWS account ID of a private Amazon ECR registry mapped to the Omics workflow, allowing the workflow to pull container images from that account's ECR repositories.

Specifies the Amazon ECR repository prefix used for a given container registry mapping, allowing the Omics workflow to substitute a custom ECR repository for the default registry when building and running workflow container images.
Specifies the URL of the upstream container registry that the workflow uses to pull container images, allowing registry mappings to redirect image pulls to a private or alternate registry.

Specifies the upstream repository prefix that AWS HealthOmics prepends to container image paths when pulling images from the corresponding registry mapping, allowing the workflow to use an alternate repository for container images.

aws_omics_workflow.creation_time.text: The read-only timestamp indicating when the workflow was created.

aws_omics_workflow.definition_repository.text: Specifies the source control repository (type, URI, and version) from which AWS HealthOmics retrieves the workflow definition file when it is not provided inline or via an S3 URI.
The ARN of the AWS CodeStar Connections connection used to access the Git repository that provides the workflow definition.
A list of glob-style file patterns that specify which files in the workflow definition repository should be excluded when the workflow source is fetched and packaged.
The full repository ID (e.g., 'owner/repository' for GitHub) of the Git repository that contains the workflow definition, used when the workflow source is a repository rather than an S3 URI or ZIP.
Specifies the S3 URI or GitHub repository path from which the workflow definition is retrieved.
Specifies the type of the source repository (S3 or GIT) that stores the workflow definition for this AWS Omics workflow.

The `value` field of `source_reference` within `definition_repository` is the actual repository reference (for example, a Git branch, tag, commit hash, or S3 URI) that points to the workflow definition to be used.

aws_omics_workflow.definition_uri.text: The S3 URI of the workflow definition file (WDL or Nextflow) that defines this AWS Omics workflow.

aws_omics_workflow.description.text: A user-provided description that is stored with the workflow and displayed in the AWS Omics console to help identify the workflow.

aws_omics_workflow.engine.text: The engine used to run the workflow, such as WDL, NEXTFLOW, or CWL.

aws_omics_workflow.id.text: The unique identifier (workflow ID) assigned to the Omics workflow by AWS upon creation.

aws_omics_workflow.main.text: Specifies the relative path to the main workflow definition file (the entry point) within the provided workflow package, used when the workflow is defined as a collection of files.

aws_omics_workflow.name.text: A user-provided name that identifies the workflow within AWS Omics, used for display in the console and for filtering and looking up the workflow.

aws_omics_workflow.parameter_template.text: Defines the workflow's input parameters as a map, where each key is a parameter name and the value contains properties such as whether the parameter is optional and its description, used to customize workflow runs.

aws_omics_workflow.status.text: The current lifecycle status of the Omics workflow, indicating whether it is being created, active, being updated, being deleted, or has failed.

aws_omics_workflow.storage_capacity.text: Specifies the storage capacity (in gigabytes) to allocate for the workflow's run environment, controlling the disk space available to tasks during execution.

aws_omics_workflow.storage_type.text: The type of storage used for the workflow run, either 'STATIC' for a fixed storage capacity or 'DYNAMIC' for storage that scales with input data.

aws_omics_workflow.type.text: The read-only workflow type, which is set to either 'WDL' or 'NEXTFLOW' by the service based on the workflow's engine.

aws_omics_workflow.uuid.text: The read-only UUID assigned by AWS to uniquely identify this Omics workflow.

aws_omics_workflow_version.accelerators.text: Specifies a comma-separated list of accelerator types (such as GPU) that are available to tasks in this workflow version, controlling whether GPU-accelerated compute resources can be used.

aws_omics_workflow_version.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Omics workflow version.

aws_omics_workflow_version.container_reg.text: Maps container names to the registry URIs from which the workflow's container images are pulled, enabling customization of image sources (e.g., private or custom registries) for the workflow version.

The image_mappings field defines a list of container image mappings that link container names used in the workflow definition to their corresponding image URIs in the container registry map of the AWS Omics workflow version.
Specifies the destination container image URI that a source image from the container registry map is overridden with for this workflow version's runtime.
Defines the original container image reference (e.g., `myorg/myapp:latest`) that appears in the workflow definition and is mapped to a destination image for the container registry.
The AWS account ID associated with the Amazon ECR container registry entry in the container registry map of the workflow version.
Specifies the ECR repository prefix (including AWS account ID and region) that maps to a container registry name, allowing the workflow version to resolve and pull container images from Amazon ECR.

For an AWS Omics workflow version, this optional string is the URI (such as an S3 URI) to a file containing the container registry map that overrides the default container image registry locations for the workflow steps.

aws_omics_workflow_version.creation_time.text: The timestamp (string in ISO 8601 format) when this workflow version was created, as returned by AWS HealthOmics.

aws_omics_workflow_version.definition_re.text: Specifies the repository (e.g., an S3 URI or Git location) from which the workflow definition for this Omics workflow version is retrieved.
The ARN of the AWS CodeStar Connections connection used to access the git repository that contains the workflow definition.

A list of file patterns (e.g., glob patterns) that should be excluded from consideration when loading workflow definition files from the configured source repository in the definition_repository block.
The full identifier of the repository that contains the workflow definition, used to locate the source file when the definition is fetched from a repository.
Identifies the specific revision (such as a Git branch, tag, or commit SHA) within the definition repository that this workflow version points to, determining the exact workflow definition source.
The type of source repository (either 'GIT' or 'S3') that contains the workflow definition, used with the source reference to specify which version of the definition to use.

aws_omics_workflow_version.definition_ur.text: The S3 URI (or other supported location) where the workflow definition file (e.g., a WDL or Nextflow script) is stored, used to specify the execution logic for this workflow version when the definition is not provided inline.

aws_omics_workflow_version.description.text: The description of the workflow version, used to provide a human-readable summary or note about the specific version of the AWS Omics workflow.

aws_omics_workflow_version.engine.text: Specifies the workflow engine used by this version, such as WDL or Nextflow.

aws_omics_workflow_version.main.text: Specifies the main workflow script file (e.g., a WDL file or Nextflow main.nf) within the workflow source that serves as the entry point for the workflow version.

aws_omics_workflow_version.parameter_tem.text: Specifies the template of input parameters for the workflow, mapping each parameter name to its configuration (e.g., data type, required flag) as defined by the workflow version.

aws_omics_workflow_version.status.text: The current lifecycle status of the workflow version (e.g., CREATING, ACTIVE, UPDATING, DELETING, or FAILED), as determined by AWS HealthOmics.

aws_omics_workflow_version.storage_capac.text: Specifies the storage capacity in gigabytes for the workflow, controlling the amount of data storage available during workflow runs.

aws_omics_workflow_version.storage_type.text: Determines whether the workflow version uses static or dynamic task-storage allocation (STATIC or DYNAMIC, with DYNAMIC as the default) for AWS Omics run tasks.

aws_omics_workflow_version.type.text: The workflow engine type (such as WDL or Nextflow) for this Omics workflow version, automatically assigned by the service when the version is created.

aws_omics_workflow_version.version_name.text: The version_name field assigns a user-defined name to this version of the Omics workflow, which must be unique among all versions of the same workflow.

aws_omics_workflow_version.workflow_buck.text: Specifies the AWS account ID that owns the S3 bucket containing the workflow definition files, which is required to grant cross-account access when the bucket is owned by a different account.

aws_omics_workflow_version.workflow_id.text: The unique identifier of the parent Omics workflow to which this workflow version belongs.

aws_open_search_serverless_collection.fi.text: A computed object that contains the FIPS-compliant endpoint URLs for the OpenSearch Serverless collection, which are read-only and provided by AWS for accessing the collection over a FIPS-validated connection.
The FIPS-compliant collection endpoint URL for the OpenSearch Serverless collection, which is used when the collection is accessed via FIPS-compliant settings.
The FIPS-compliant URL endpoint for accessing the OpenSearch Dashboards (formerly Kibana) interface for the OpenSearch Serverless collection.

aws_open_search_serverless_collection.ta.text: A tag key is a case-sensitive string up to 128 characters (and cannot start with 'aws:') that, when paired with a tag value, attaches metadata to the OpenSearch Serverless collection for management and identification purposes.
The value component of a key-value tag attached to the OpenSearch Serverless collection, allowing you to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_open_search_serverless_collection_gr.text: Defines the maximum indexing and search capacity in OpenSearch Compute Units (OCUs) that the collection group is allowed to use, effectively limiting the total capacity available to all collections within the group.

aws_open_search_serverless_index.setting.text: The settings object configures index-level settings such as the number of primary shards and replica shards for the OpenSearch Serverless index.
The 'settings.index' object specifies index-level configuration for the OpenSearch Serverless index, including settings like the number of primary shards and replica shards.

aws_open_search_service_application.app_.text: The key name that identifies a specific configuration parameter within the app_configs list of an AWS OpenSearch Service application.
The value of a single key-value pair within the AppConfigs list, which supplies custom settings for the OpenSearch Service application when it is provisioned.

aws_open_search_service_application.data.text: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an underlying AWS data source (for example, an S3 bucket or CloudWatch Logs log group) that this OpenSearch Service application uses for direct querying.
Specifies a descriptive text for a data source that is associated with the Amazon OpenSearch Service application.

aws_open_search_service_application.iam_.text: The ARN of the AWS IAM Identity Center instance used to authenticate users for this OpenSearch Service application.

aws_open_search_service_application.tags.text: The value of a user-defined tag key assigned to the OpenSearch Service application, used for metadata management, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_open_search_service_domain.access_po.text: IAM policy document (JSON) that defines the resource-based access policy for the OpenSearch domain, specifying which IAM principals and actions are allowed on the domain's APIs and endpoints.

aws_open_search_service_domain.advanced_.text: Configures advanced OpenSearch cluster options as key-value pairs, such as allowing explicit index names (rest.action.multi.allow_explicit_index) or setting the maximum number of query clauses (indices.query.bool.max_clause_count).

The advanced security options applied to the OpenSearch Service domain, including whether fine-grained access control is enabled, the internal user database setting, and the master user or SAML authentication configuration.
The date and time (in ISO 8601 format) after which anonymous access to the OpenSearch Service domain is automatically disabled, used when temporary anonymous authentication has been enabled.
Enables or disables anonymous authentication, allowing unauthenticated users to access the OpenSearch domain without credentials.
Enables fine-grained access control (advanced security) for the Amazon OpenSearch Service domain, requiring authentication and authorization for access.

Specifies the IAM federation configuration for the OpenSearch Service domain, allowing IAM identities to authenticate to OpenSearch Dashboards through an external identity provider instead of using the internal user database.
Indicates whether IAM federation is enabled for the OpenSearch domain's advanced security options, allowing the domain to use IAM roles for authentication instead of internal users.
The SAML response attribute that contains the IAM role mappings used to grant federated users access to the OpenSearch Service domain.
Specifies the source attribute in the IAM Identity Center (or IdP assertion) that is used to derive the OpenSearch username for federated users.
Indicates whether the internal user database is enabled for fine-grained access control in the Amazon OpenSearch Service domain.

Configures JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication and authorization for the OpenSearch domain's advanced security, including enabling JWT and specifying the subject and roles claim keys for token validation.
Whether JWT-based authentication is enabled for the OpenSearch domain's advanced security options.
The public key used to verify JWT tokens for JWT authentication within the OpenSearch domain's advanced security settings.
Specifies the JWT payload key whose value contains the user's roles, which OpenSearch Service uses to assign backend roles to the authenticated user.
The JWT claim key (e.g., 'sub') that contains the user's subject identifier, used to authenticate and map the token to an OpenSearch user for access control.

Specifies the master user (the administrative user) for the OpenSearch Service domain when fine-grained access control is enabled, allowing you to provide either an IAM role ARN (MasterUserARN) or a username and password (MasterUserName/MasterUserPassword).
Specifies the ARN of the IAM user or role that acts as the master user for the OpenSearch domain's fine-grained access control.
The master user name for the OpenSearch domain's internal user database, used when configuring fine-grained access control with the internal user database as the master user.
The master user password for the OpenSearch Service domain's fine-grained access control, used in combination with the master user name to authenticate the primary administrative user.

Specifies the SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) options for the domain's advanced security, enabling SAML-based single sign-on for OpenSearch Dashboards with settings such as identity provider metadata, subject key, and roles key.
Whether SAML authentication is enabled for the OpenSearch domain.
Configuration for the SAML identity provider, including the entity ID and the IdP metadata XML document, used to enable SAML authentication for the OpenSearch domain.
The unique identifier (entity ID) of the SAML identity provider (IdP) that OpenSearch Service uses for SAML-based authentication, typically the issuer URL from the IdP's SAML metadata.
The metadata content (XML) of the SAML identity provider used for configuring SAML authentication on the OpenSearch Service domain.
Specifies the IAM role ARN to use as the master backend role (the master user) for the OpenSearch Service domain when SAML authentication is enabled, granting that role full access to the cluster.
The SAML username of the master user who receives full access to the OpenSearch domain when SAML authentication is enabled.
Specifies the SAML attribute name that contains the user's roles, which are mapped to OpenSearch backend roles in the advanced security options.
Specifies the SAML session timeout in minutes, after which an authenticated user's OpenSearch Dashboards session expires.
Specifies the SAML assertion attribute (such as NameID) that maps to the user's subject identifier for authentication when SAML is enabled for the OpenSearch domain.

aws_open_search_service_domain.aimloptio.text: Configures AI/ML features for the Amazon OpenSearch Service domain, such as natural language query generation and integration with IAM Identity Center.
Configures the S3 vector engine for the OpenSearch Service domain, which specifies the S3 bucket and IAM role used to store and query vector embeddings for vector search.
Configuration for serverless vector acceleration on the OpenSearch Service domain, used to enable or disable accelerated vector search for serverless engine workloads.

aws_open_search_service_domain.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the OpenSearch domain, uniquely identifying the domain across AWS.

aws_open_search_service_domain.automated.text: Configures a recurring time window during which automated snapshots are paused for the OpenSearch Service domain, preventing snapshot creation during periods of high activity or maintenance.

Enables or disables the automated snapshot pause feature, allowing Amazon OpenSearch Service to temporarily pause automated snapshots during high traffic or maintenance windows to reduce impact on cluster performance.
The UTC time of day at which the automated snapshot pause window ends, after which Amazon OpenSearch Service resumes automated snapshot creation for the domain.
Specifies the start time (in UTC, in HH:mm format) of the daily window during which automated snapshots are paused for the OpenSearch Service domain.

aws_open_search_service_domain.cluster_c.text: The cluster_config object configures the OpenSearch cluster's compute and sizing settings, including instance type, instance count, dedicated master nodes, and zone awareness for the domain.
Options for managing cold storage in the OpenSearch cluster, where the `Enabled` flag determines whether cold storage is turned on for the domain.
Enables or disables cold storage for the OpenSearch Service domain, allowing infrequently accessed data to be stored on lower-cost storage while remaining searchable via the cluster.
Number of dedicated master nodes to deploy for the OpenSearch Service domain cluster, used when dedicated_master_enabled is true.
Specifies whether the OpenSearch Service domain is configured to use dedicated master nodes, which provide more stable cluster management for production workloads.
Specifies the instance type for the dedicated master nodes of the OpenSearch cluster, typically a value like m5.large.search, and is required when dedicated_master_enabled is set to true.
The number of data nodes (instances) that form the OpenSearch Service domain's cluster.
Defines the Amazon OpenSearch Service instance type for the data nodes in the cluster, such as 'm5.large.search' or 'c5.large.search'.

Enables or disables Multi-AZ with standby for the OpenSearch Service domain, which deploys the cluster across three Availability Zones (two active data nodes and one standby) to provide higher availability.
Configures the list of node options for the OpenSearch domain cluster, allowing you to specify dedicated coordinator nodes and their counts to optimize cluster performance and stability.
Configuration for a node option in the OpenSearch domain cluster, specifying the node count and whether the option is enabled for the selected node type.
Specifies the number of nodes of the configured node type (such as coordinator nodes) to provision for the OpenSearch domain's cluster, as defined within the node option's node configuration.
This boolean determines whether the specified node configuration (for example, dedicated coordinator nodes) is enabled for the OpenSearch Service domain cluster.
Specifies the type of node (e.g., 'data', 'master', 'ultrawarm', or 'cold') for which the node option is configured within the OpenSearch domain's cluster configuration.
Specifies the number of UltraWarm nodes for the OpenSearch domain, used to enable warm storage tiers in the cluster.
Indicates whether UltraWarm, a low-cost storage tier for large amounts of read-only data in Amazon OpenSearch Service, is enabled for the domain.
Specifies the instance type for UltraWarm nodes in the OpenSearch domain's cluster configuration, enabling the UltraWarm storage tier for warmer, cheaper storage of read-only indices.
Specifies the number of Availability Zones for the domain when zone awareness is enabled, used to configure multi-AZ deployment.

Specifies the number of Availability Zones (typically 2 or 3) that the OpenSearch Service domain's cluster spans when zone awareness is enabled, controlling distribution of data nodes across zones for high availability.
Indicates whether to enable zone awareness for the OpenSearch domain cluster, which distributes nodes across multiple Availability Zones to improve availability and fault tolerance.

aws_open_search_service_domain.cognito_o.text: Cognito options for OpenSearch Dashboards authentication, specifying whether Cognito authentication is enabled and the associated Cognito user pool, identity pool, and IAM role used for Dashboards login.
Indicates whether authentication through Amazon Cognito is enabled for OpenSearch Dashboards (formerly Kibana) on the OpenSearch Service domain.
The ID of the Cognito identity pool used to authenticate users to OpenSearch Dashboards.
The ARN of the IAM role that OpenSearch Service assumes to access Amazon Cognito for authentication, which is required when Cognito options are enabled on the domain.
The ID of the Amazon Cognito user pool used for authentication to OpenSearch Dashboards when CognitoOptions is enabled.

aws_open_search_service_domain.deploymen.text: Specifies the deployment strategy for the OpenSearch domain, including the deployment mode (e.g., BLUE_GREEN) that controls how updates and changes are applied to the domain during configuration changes.

Defines whether the OpenSearch Service domain uses a blue/green deployment (creating a new environment and swapping traffic) or an in-place deployment (applying changes directly to the existing cluster) when configuration changes are made.

aws_open_search_service_domain.domain_ar.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the OpenSearch Service domain, uniquely identifying it across AWS.

aws_open_search_service_domain.domain_en.text: The fully qualified domain endpoint URL (e.g., https://search-<domain-name>-<random-string>.<region>.es.amazonaws.com) that is automatically assigned to the OpenSearch domain and can be used to access the search service.
Configures endpoint access for the domain, including whether HTTPS is enforced, the TLS security policy version, and optional custom endpoint settings such as a custom hostname and certificate.
Specifies the fully qualified custom domain name (e.g., search.example.com) used as the domain's endpoint when custom endpoint is enabled.
The ARN of the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate that secures the custom endpoint of the OpenSearch Service domain when a custom domain endpoint is enabled.
Indicates whether a custom endpoint is enabled for the OpenSearch Service domain, allowing you to use a custom domain name instead of the default endpoint.
Indicates whether the OpenSearch Service domain requires all traffic to use HTTPS, disabling HTTP access.

Sets the minimum TLS version for the domain's HTTPS endpoint, with valid values of 'Policy-Min-TLS-1-0-2019-07' (default, allowing TLS 1.0 and above) or 'Policy-Min-TLS-1-2-2019-07' (enforcing TLS 1.2 or higher).
This computed field contains the V2 domain endpoint (a URL) for the OpenSearch Service domain, which clients use to access the domain's search and indexing APIs.
A computed map of the OpenSearch Service domain's endpoint URLs, with keys such as 'vpc' for the VPC endpoint (when deployed in a VPC) and 'public' for the public endpoint.

aws_open_search_service_domain.domain_na.text: A unique, user-friendly name for the OpenSearch domain, which appears in the domain's endpoint URL (e.g., https://<domain-name>.region.es.amazonaws.com) and must be unique within the AWS account and region.

aws_open_search_service_domain.ebsoption.text: Configures the EBS volumes attached to the data nodes of the OpenSearch domain, including volume type, size, and IOPS settings.
Whether EBS (Elastic Block Store) storage is enabled for the data nodes of the OpenSearch Service domain.
The provisioned IOPS (I/O operations per second) for the EBS volumes attached to the OpenSearch domain, used when the volume type is set to io1, io2, or gp3.
Sets the provisioned throughput (in MiB/s) for the EBS volumes attached to the OpenSearch Service domain, used when the volume type supports specifying throughput such as gp3.
The size in GiB of the EBS volume attached to each data node for the OpenSearch Service domain.
Specifies the EBS volume type (e.g., gp2, gp3, io1) used for the OpenSearch Service domain's EBS storage volumes.

aws_open_search_service_domain.encryptio.text: Configures encryption at rest for the OpenSearch Service domain, specifying whether it is enabled and the AWS KMS key ID used to encrypt the domain's data.
Whether encryption of data at rest is enabled for the OpenSearch Service domain, with a custom KMS key configurable via the KmsKeyId property in the same EncryptionAtRestOptions object.
The KMS key ID used for encryption-at-rest of the OpenSearch Service domain, which must be a symmetric customer master key in the same region as the domain.

aws_open_search_service_domain.engine_ve.text: The version of the OpenSearch or Elasticsearch engine that the domain runs, such as 'OpenSearch_1.0' or 'Elasticsearch_7.10'.

aws_open_search_service_domain.id.text: The name of the OpenSearch domain, which serves as the unique identifier for the domain resource.

aws_open_search_service_domain.ipaddress.text: Specifies whether the OpenSearch Service domain uses IPv4 only or dual-stack networking (IPv4 and IPv6), controlling the IP address type assigned to the domain endpoints.

aws_open_search_service_domain.log_publi.text: Configures the publishing of OpenSearch Service domain logs (such as index slow logs, search slow logs, and audit logs) to a CloudWatch Logs group.

aws_open_search_service_domain.node_to_n.text: Specifies settings for encrypting traffic between nodes in the Amazon OpenSearch Service domain, with an Enabled boolean that must be true to activate node-to-node encryption.
Whether node-to-node encryption is enabled for all communications between nodes in the OpenSearch Service domain.

aws_open_search_service_domain.off_peak_.text: Configures a daily off-peak window during which the OpenSearch Service domain can perform maintenance activities such as software updates, helping minimize impact on active traffic.
Indicates whether the off-peak maintenance window is enabled for the OpenSearch Service domain, allowing software updates to occur during a scheduled low-traffic period.
Specifies the daily off-peak maintenance window for the OpenSearch Service domain by defining the start time (hours and minutes) for when maintenance tasks can be performed.
Defines the starting hour and minute (UTC) of the daily off-peak maintenance window for the OpenSearch Service domain.
The hour of the day (0-23) at which the off-peak maintenance window starts for the OpenSearch Service domain.
The minute (0-59) of the hour at which the daily off-peak window starts for maintenance activities on the OpenSearch Service domain.

aws_open_search_service_domain.service_s.text: Provides the current service software version for the OpenSearch domain, including whether an update is available, the update status, and the scheduled automated update date.
The timestamp (ISO 8601 string) at which an available service software update will be automatically applied to the OpenSearch Service domain, as scheduled by AWS.
A boolean that indicates whether the currently running service software update on the OpenSearch Service domain can be cancelled.
The current_version field indicates the version of the OpenSearch service software currently installed on the domain, which is populated by the AWS API and cannot be set by the user.
Contains a human-readable description of the current or latest service software update for the OpenSearch domain, as reported by the AWS service.
The version of the OpenSearch service software that the domain can be updated to, when an update is available.
A boolean that indicates whether the deployment of the pending service software update is optional, allowing you to defer or manually schedule the update instead of having it automatically applied.
Indicates whether a new service software update is available for the OpenSearch domain, as reported by the AWS OpenSearch Service.
Indicates the status of a service software update for the OpenSearch Service domain, including states such as PENDING_UPDATE, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, or NOT_AVAILABLE.

aws_open_search_service_domain.skip_shar.text: Set this to true to make Terraform skip waiting for shard migration to complete when reducing the number of data nodes in the OpenSearch domain, allowing the cluster configuration update to finish faster.

aws_open_search_service_domain.snapshot_.text: Configures the automated snapshot start hour (0-23) for the OpenSearch Service domain, controlling when daily snapshots are taken.
The hour in UTC at which the OpenSearch Service domain's automated daily snapshots are taken, specified as an integer from 0 to 23.

aws_open_search_service_domain.software_.text: Controls whether Amazon OpenSearch Service can automatically apply software updates to the domain, including the option to enable or disable automatic updates.
Enables or disables automated software updates (patching) for the OpenSearch Service domain.
This boolean field enables or disables automatic blue/green deployment to update the OpenSearch Service domain to the latest service software.

aws_open_search_service_domain.tags.valu.text: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the Amazon OpenSearch Service domain, used for metadata organization, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_open_search_service_domain.vpcoption.text: Configures the Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) options for the OpenSearch Service domain, specifying the subnets and security groups in which the domain's endpoints will be placed.
The list of security group IDs to associate with the VPC endpoint for the OpenSearch Service domain, controlling network access to the domain within the VPC.
Specifies the subnet IDs within a VPC where the OpenSearch domain's VPC endpoints (for the data nodes) are placed, used when the domain is deployed inside a virtual private cloud.

aws_organizations_account.tags.key.text: The key portion of a key-value tag assigned to the AWS Organizations account, enabling you to categorize and manage the account for cost allocation, access control, or operational purposes.

aws_organizations_account.tags.value.text: The value of a key-value tag assigned to the AWS Organizations account.

aws_organizations_organizational_unit.ta.text: The user-defined key (name) of a tag attached to the organizational unit, used to identify and categorize the unit for resource management.
The value for a tag key attached to the organizational unit, used to assign metadata for management and tracking purposes.

aws_organizations_policy.tags.key.text: The key of a tag that is attached to the AWS Organizations policy, used to identify the tag's purpose or category.

aws_organizations_policy.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag assigned to the AWS Organizations policy, used to organize and identify the policy.

aws_organizations_resource_policy.tags.k.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Organizations resource policy.

aws_organizations_resource_policy.tags.v.text: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the AWS Organizations resource policy, used to organize and identify the policy.

aws_osis_pipeline.log_publishing_options.text: The name of the CloudWatch Logs log group where the OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline publishes logs.

aws_osis_pipeline.resource_policy.text: The IAM resource policy that grants other AWS services permissions to send messages or data to the OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline.

aws_osis_pipeline.resource_policy.policy.text: The `policy` field specifies the JSON resource-based policy document that defines permissions for the OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline to access specified AWS resources, such as the source and sink data stores.

aws_osis_pipeline.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag to attach to the OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline.

aws_osis_pipeline.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline, used to store metadata such as environment, owner, or cost center for resource identification and management.

aws_osis_pipeline.vpc_endpoints.vpc_endp.text: The unique identifier of a VPC endpoint that clients can use to access the OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline within its VPC.

aws_osis_pipeline.vpc_endpoints.vpc_id.text: The ID of the VPC in which the VPC endpoint for the OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline is automatically created, allowing the pipeline to be accessed within that VPC.

aws_osis_pipeline.vpc_endpoints.vpc_opti.text: VPC configuration for a VPC endpoint, specifying the subnet IDs and security group IDs associated with the endpoint in the pipeline's VPC.
Specifies the security group IDs to attach to the VPC endpoint for the OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline, controlling network traffic to and from the endpoint within the VPC.
Specifies the subnet IDs within the VPC where the OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline's VPC endpoint will be provisioned.
Configures VPC attachment options for the OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline's VPC endpoint, including whether to attach to a VPC endpoint service and the IAM role used for that attachment.
Indicates whether the OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline's VPC endpoint is attached to a VPC, enabling the pipeline to access resources within that VPC when set to true.
The CIDR block (e.g., 10.0.0.0/16) that defines the IP address range for the VPC attachment of the OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline's VPC endpoint.
Indicates whether the VPC endpoint for this OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline is managed by the customer ('CUSTOMER') or by the AWS service ('SERVICE') in the pipeline's VPC options.

aws_outposts_site.description.text: The description of the Outposts site, an optional string that provides additional context or identifying information about the site.

aws_outposts_site.name.text: The human-readable name assigned to the Outposts site, used to identify the physical location where the AWS Outpost is installed.

aws_outposts_site.notes.text: An optional string that stores additional descriptive notes or information about the Outposts site.

aws_outposts_site.operating_address.text: The physical address of the Outposts site, specified as an object containing street address, city, state, country, and postal code, used for logistics and installation.

aws_outposts_site.operating_address.addr.text: The first line of the street address (e.g., building number and street) for the operating address of the AWS Outpost site, indicating where the Outpost equipment is physically located.
The second line of the operating address for the Outposts site, used for additional address details such as a suite, unit, or floor number.
Specifies the third line of the street address for the operating (physical) address of the AWS Outposts site.

aws_outposts_site.operating_address.city.text: The city portion of the physical operating address where the AWS Outpost site is deployed and operates.

aws_outposts_site.operating_address.cont.text: The name of the contact person associated with the operating address of the Outpost site.
The phone number of the primary contact person responsible for the Outpost site at this operating address.

aws_outposts_site.operating_address.coun.text: The country code of the operating address for the Outpost site, specified as a two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

aws_outposts_site.operating_address.dist.text: The district or county portion of the operating address where the Outpost site is physically located.

aws_outposts_site.operating_address.muni.text: The municipality (city or town) of the operating address for the Outposts site.

aws_outposts_site.operating_address.post.text: The postal code of the operating address for the Outposts site, which AWS uses for shipping equipment and providing on-site service.

aws_outposts_site.operating_address.stat.text: The state, province, or region portion of the physical operating address for the AWS Outposts site, required when specifying the site's location.

aws_outposts_site.rack_physical_properti.text: Defines the physical characteristics of the Outposts rack, including power draw, power feed drop, connector type, phase, voltage, and maximum weight, which AWS uses to plan installation at the site.
Specifies the type of fiber optic cable used by the Outpost rack, either single-mode or multi-mode.
The maximum weight capacity in pounds that the Outpost rack is designed to support, expressed as a string value that defines the physical weight limit for the site's rack.

Specifies the optical standard used for the fiber-optic network connection on the Outpost rack, determining the type of fiber (e.g., single-mode or multi-mode) and associated speed/transceiver standard.
Specifies the type of power connector used for the Outpost rack (e.g., C19 or C21), which influences the physical power infrastructure required at the site.
Specifies the power draw of the rack in kilovolt-amperes (kVA) when defining the physical properties of the AWS Outposts site rack.
Indicates whether the power feed for the rack drops from above (overhead) or below (underfloor), which determines how service cabling is routed to the outpost rack.
The power phase (single-phase or three-phase) of the power connection for the Outpost rack, such as SINGLE_PHASE or THREE_PHASE.
Specifies the number of uplinks per rack for the Outpost site, using a string enum value such as 'UPLINK_COUNT_4' or 'UPLINK_COUNT_8'.
Specifies the uplink speed (in Gbps) for the Outpost rack's network connection, such as '1G', '10G', '40G', or '100G'.

aws_outposts_site.shipping_address.text: The shipping address for the Outpost site, where AWS will deliver the Outpost hardware.

aws_outposts_site.shipping_address.addre.text: The first line of the shipping address for the Outposts site, typically containing the street number and street name.
The second line of the shipping address for the Outpost site, used to provide additional address details such as a suite, unit, or building number.
Specifies the third line of the shipping address used for the Outposts Site.

aws_outposts_site.shipping_address.city.text: The city portion of the shipping address for the Outposts site.

aws_outposts_site.shipping_address.conta.text: Specifies the contact name to use for deliveries to the shipping address of this AWS Outposts site.
The phone number for the primary contact at the Outposts site's shipping address, used to arrange delivery and installation.

aws_outposts_site.shipping_address.count.text: The two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the physical site's shipping address.

aws_outposts_site.shipping_address.distr.text: Specifies the district or county (subdivision) of the shipping address for the Outpost site.

aws_outposts_site.shipping_address.munic.text: Specifies the municipality (city or town) of the shipping address for the AWS Outposts site equipment.

aws_outposts_site.shipping_address.posta.text: The postal code (ZIP code) portion of the shipping address used for delivering Outpost hardware to this site.

aws_outposts_site.shipping_address.state.text: The state or region component of the shipping address for the Outpost site, used by AWS to deliver the hardware.

aws_outposts_site.site_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Outposts site.

aws_outposts_site.site_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the Outposts site, used to reference the site in other resources.

aws_outposts_site.tags.text: A list of tag objects (each with a Key and Value) to assign to the Outposts Site, used for categorizing and managing the site resource.

aws_outposts_site.tags.key.text: The tag key (for example, 'Environment') for a tag attached to this AWS Outposts site.

aws_panorama_application_instance.applic.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this Panorama application instance.
The unique ID of a previously deployed AWS Panorama application instance that this new instance should replace, enabling a replacement deployment.

aws_panorama_application_instance.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Panorama application instance.

aws_panorama_application_instance.create.text: The Unix epoch timestamp in seconds indicating when the AWS Panorama application instance was created.

aws_panorama_application_instance.defaul.text: The ID or ARN of the AWS Panorama device that this application instance is deployed to and runs on.
The name of the AWS Panorama device (appliance) that serves as the default runtime context for this application instance, returned as a computed read-only attribute by CloudFormation.

aws_panorama_application_instance.descri.text: A user-specified description that provides a human-readable label for the application instance, typically used to identify it in the AWS Panorama console and APIs.

aws_panorama_application_instance.health.text: The health status of the application instance on its device, indicating whether the deployed application is operating normally (e.g., HEALTHY, UNHEALTHY, or NOT_AVAILABLE) and populated by AWS after the instance is created.

aws_panorama_application_instance.last_u.text: The Unix epoch timestamp indicating when the application instance was last updated, as reported by the AWS Panorama service.

aws_panorama_application_instance.manife.text: The JSON payload data that overrides the application manifest for this AWS Panorama application instance, enabling device-specific customization of the deployment.
The application manifest payload as a JSON-formatted string, which defines the AWS Panorama application's graph, pipelines, and runtime configuration.

aws_panorama_application_instance.name.text: A user-defined name for the application instance, used for identification in the AWS Panorama console and API.

aws_panorama_application_instance.runtim.text: The ARN of the IAM role that the application instance assumes to access AWS services during runtime.

aws_panorama_application_instance.status.text: The current deployment status of the application instance, indicating whether it is pending, in progress, succeeded, failed, or running on the AWS Panorama device.
Provides a human-readable description of the current status of the application instance, including error details when the instance is in a failed state.

aws_panorama_application_instance.tags.v.text: The value portion of a tag attached to the AWS Panorama application instance, allowing users to assign arbitrary metadata for identification and management.

aws_panorama_package.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Panorama package.

aws_panorama_package.created_time.text: The Unix timestamp automatically assigned by AWS when the Package was created, indicating the creation time of the Panorama package.

aws_panorama_package.package_id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS Panorama package, assigned by AWS when the package is created.

aws_panorama_package.package_name.text: The unique name of the Panorama package that identifies it within your AWS account and is used when creating or referencing the package in the AWS Panorama console and API.

aws_panorama_package.tags.text: A list of tag objects (each with a Key and Value) to attach to the AWS Panorama package, enabling cost allocation, access control, and resource organization.

aws_panorama_package.tags.key.text: Specifies the key of a tag to attach to the AWS Panorama package for resource identification and management.

aws_panorama_package.tags.value.text: The value component of a key-value tag that can be attached to the Panorama package, used for metadata and resource organization.

aws_panorama_package_version.is_latest_p.text: Indicates whether this patch version is the latest available patch for the package version.

aws_panorama_package_version.owner_accou.text: The AWS account ID that owns the package version, used to identify the package owner when registering a package version for a package shared from another account.

aws_panorama_package_version.package_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Panorama package that this package version belongs to.

aws_panorama_package_version.package_id.text: The ID of the AWS Panorama package to which this package version belongs.

aws_panorama_package_version.package_nam.text: The name of the AWS Panorama package to which this package version belongs, uniquely identifying the package within the account.

aws_panorama_package_version.package_ver.text: The package version identifier for the AWS Panorama package, used to distinguish this release from other versions of the same package.

aws_panorama_package_version.patch_versi.text: Specifies the patch version of the Panorama package, which combined with the package name and package version uniquely identifies a specific package version release in AWS Panorama.

aws_panorama_package_version.registered_.text: The Unix epoch timestamp (in seconds) when this Panorama package version was registered by the service, as returned by AWS Panorama.

aws_panorama_package_version.status.text: The service-assigned lifecycle status of the Panorama package version, indicating whether it is registered, active, deleting, or failed, and updated automatically as the package version transitions through its lifecycle.

aws_panorama_package_version.status_desc.text: The package version's status description, providing contextual details about the current state (such as progress or error information) of the AWS Panorama package version.

aws_panorama_package_version.updated_lat.text: Determines whether the package version is updated to the latest available patch version for the specified package, enabling automatic updates to the newest patch release.

aws_payment_cryptography_alias.alias_nam.text: Specifies the friendly name for the AWS Payment Cryptography key alias, which must begin with 'alias/' and is used to reference a key in cryptographic operations.

aws_payment_cryptography_alias.key_arn.text: The ARN of the AWS Payment Cryptography key that this alias is associated with, allowing the alias to serve as a friendly reference to the key for cryptographic operations.

aws_payment_cryptography_key.derive_key_.text: Specifies the intended cryptographic key usage for a derived key generated from this key.

aws_payment_cryptography_key.enabled.text: Indicates whether the key is enabled for use in cryptographic operations.

aws_payment_cryptography_key.exportable.text: Indicates whether the key material can be exported from AWS Payment Cryptography, enabling use of the key outside the service for encryption operations.

aws_payment_cryptography_key.key_attribu.text: Specifies the cryptographic attributes of the key, including the key algorithm, key class, key usage, and key mode of use, which are required when creating or importing a key.
Specifies the cryptographic algorithm for the key (e.g., TDES_2KEY, TDES_3KEY, AES_128, AES_192, AES_256, RSA_2048, RSA_3072, RSA_4096), which determines the key's permitted cryptographic operations.
Specifies the class of the cryptographic key, such as whether it is a symmetric key, asymmetric key pair, private key, or public key.

Defines the set of cryptographic operations (such as encrypt, decrypt, sign, verify, wrap, unwrap, generate, derive key) that the key is restricted to perform, with each operation represented as a boolean flag.
When true, the key may be used for decryption operations.
Indicates whether this key can be used to derive other keys in cryptographic operations.
Specifies whether the key can be used for encryption operations.
When true, this key is permitted to generate message authentication codes (MACs) as part of its allowed modes of use.
If set to true, this key is unrestricted and can be used for any cryptographic operation, bypassing specific mode-of-use constraints in AWS Payment Cryptography.
Specifies whether the key can be used to generate digital signatures.
Indicates whether the key can be used to unwrap (decrypt) data or keys that were previously wrapped.
Indicates whether the cryptographic key can be used to verify digital signatures or message authentication codes.
Indicates whether the key can be used to wrap (encrypt) another key.

Specifies the intended cryptographic function of the key, using TR31 key usage values such as TR31_C0_CARD_VERIFICATION_KEY or TR31_D0_SYMMETRIC_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY, which constrains how the key can be used in payment operations.

aws_payment_cryptography_key.key_check_v.text: Specifies the algorithm (such as CMAC or HMAC) used to generate the key check value (KCV) for the cryptographic key.

aws_payment_cryptography_key.key_identif.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Payment Cryptography key.

aws_payment_cryptography_key.replication.text: Specifies the list of AWS regions to which the key is replicated for cross-region availability and disaster recovery, allowing the key to be used in those regions.
The current replication status of the payment cryptography key, indicating whether key material has been successfully replicated to the configured replica region (e.g., PENDING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED).

aws_payment_cryptography_key.tags.text: Specifies the tags, which are key-value pairs, to associate with the AWS Payment Cryptography key for resource management and cost tracking.

aws_payment_cryptography_key.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag applied to an AWS Payment Cryptography key, enabling categorization, filtering, cost allocation, and access control for the key.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_connector.certificat.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Private CA certificate authority that will issue certificates for the Active Directory connector.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_connector.connector_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the connector created by this resource.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_connector.directory_.text: The identifier of the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory that this connector is associated with.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_connector.tags.text: Tags (key-value pairs) to associate with the PCA Connector for Active Directory resource, used for identifying, organizing, and managing the connector.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_connector.vpc_inform.text: The VPC information for the connector, specifying the security groups that allow the connector to communicate with the Active Directory in your VPC.
Specifies whether the connector uses only IPv4 addresses or both IPv4 and IPv6 (dual-stack) addresses within the VPC, with allowed values IPV4 and DUALSTACK.
Specifies the IDs of the security groups that AWS Private CA Connector for Active Directory uses to securely communicate with your directory in the VPC.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_directory_registrati.text: The identifier of the AWS Managed Microsoft Active Directory that is registered with the Private CA Connector for Active Directory.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this directory registration within AWS Private CA Connector for Active Directory.
Assigns metadata tags to the PCa Connector for AD directory registration, which can be used for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_service_principal_na.text: The ARN of the Active Directory connector to which this service principal name is registered.
The ARN of the directory registration that this service principal name belongs to, linking the SPN to the associated AWS Managed Microsoft Active Directory.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_template.connector_a.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Private CA Connector for Active Directory connector to which this template belongs.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_template.definition.text: The definition object specifies the certificate template's validity, private key attributes, and flags, which are required by the PCA Connector for Active Directory to create and manage the template.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_template.definition..text: Specifies the v2 configuration for the Active Directory connector template, including certificate validity, extensions, key usage, private key attributes, and subject name flags.
Specifies the validity period of certificates issued using this template, including a numeric period and its unit (days, months, or years).
Specifies how long before certificate expiration the issued certificates are automatically renewed, expressed as a period type (e.g., DAYS) and a numeric value.
The numeric duration for the renewal period of certificates issued under this template, interpreted according to the associated renewal_period type (e.g., DAYS or MONTHS).
Specifies the time unit (e.g., DAYS, MONTHS, YEARS) for the renewal period, which determines how far in advance certificates are renewed.
Specifies the duration and unit of time that certificates issued using this Private CA Connector for AD template remain valid.

The numeric length of the certificate validity period, interpreted in units of the associated validity period type (e.g., days, months, or years) for certificates issued from this PCA Connector AD template.
Specifies the unit of time (DAYS, MONTHS, or YEARS) for the certificate validity period in the PCA Connector for AD template.

Defines enrollment behavior flags for the certificate template, such as requiring user interaction, including symmetric algorithms, and removing invalid certificates from the personal store, which are applied during certificate enrollment.

Enables or disables the reuse of an existing cryptographic key when the NT token keyset storage is full, which is an enrollment flag for the certificate template in AWS Private CA Connector for Active Directory.
When set to true, this flag includes symmetric algorithms in the certificate enrollment request for this template.
When true, this enrollment flag causes the CA to omit the security extension from certificates issued by the template; when false, the security extension is included.
This boolean flag controls whether the certificate template instructs the CA to automatically remove an invalid certificate from the user's personal certificate store after enrollment.
Specifies whether certificate enrollment requires the user to interact with the client, such as entering a PIN or approving the request, in the Active Directory environment.
Defines the certificate extension settings, such as application policies and key usage, that are included on certificates issued with this Active Directory connector template.
Specifies the application policies (extended key usage) that define the intended uses of certificates issued with this template, such as client authentication or code signing.
Indicates whether the application policies extension is marked as critical in the Active Directory certificate template.
Specifies the list of application policies (such as Smart Card Logon, Code Signing, or custom OIDs) that are included in the Application Policies extension of the certificate template.
Specifies the object identifier (OID) of an application policy used in the certificate template, such as a numeric OID like 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1 for server authentication.
Sets the application policy type for the certificate, selecting a predefined OID such as ANY_APPLICATION or CLIENT_AUTHENTICATION, or CUSTOM to require a corresponding PolicyObjectIdentifier.

Defines the key usage extension in the template, specifying the intended cryptographic purposes of the certificate's public key, such as digital signature, key encipherment, data encipherment, and whether the extension is critical.
Specifies whether the key usage extension is marked critical in the certificate template, which determines whether clients must strictly enforce the key usage restrictions.

Specifies the set of key usage purposes (such as digital signature, key encipherment, or data encipherment) that the certificate's public key is authorized for in the key usage extension of a version 2 Active Directory template.
Indicates whether the key can be used for data encipherment, permitting the encryption of arbitrary data with the certificate's public key.
Whether the key usage extension includes the digitalSignature purpose, allowing certificates issued under this template to be used for digital signatures such as authentication or message integrity.
Specifies whether the certificate key can be used for key agreement, such as in Diffie-Hellman key exchange, as part of the KeyUsage extension in the template.
Indicates whether the key usage extension permits the certificate's public key to be used for key encipherment, i.e., encrypting symmetric keys or other data for key transport.

Indicates whether the certificate's key can be used for non-repudiation, which proves the authenticity and integrity of a message or transaction in the key usage extension of the AD connector template.
Configures the general flags for the v2 certificate template, such as AutoEnrollment, MachineType, NonexpiringCertificates, and UserType.
When enabled, this flag allows certificates issued from the template to be automatically enrolled by Active Directory clients, enabling auto-enrollment without requiring manual certificate requests.
Specifies whether the certificate template is intended for machine (computer) accounts rather than user accounts in the Active Directory environment.

Defines the private key attributes for the certificate template version 2, including the required minimum key length, key specification (e.g., RSA or ECDSA), and the allowed cryptographic service providers.
Specifies the list of allowed cryptographic service providers (CSPs) that can be used to generate and store the private key for certificates issued from this template.
Specifies whether the private key generated by the template is intended for key exchange (encryption) or digital signatures.
Specifies the minimum length in bits (e.g., 1024, 2048, or 4096) of the private key that certificates requested from this PCA Connector AD template must have.
Specifies the private key flags for the v2 template definition, determining whether the certificate private key can be exported and which Windows client versions are supported.
