Specifies the Windows Server client version (WIN_SERVER_2008 or WIN_SERVER_2012) for the private key flags in the v2 template definition, which determines the key algorithm and security settings for certificates issued by the Active Directory connector.
Indicates whether the private key associated with the certificate can be exported, controlling the exportable key flag in the certificate template's private key flags.
Specifies whether the private key must use strong key protection, requiring the user to enter a password each time they access or use the key.

Controls the subject name flags for the V2 certificate template, determining which fields (such as common name, directory path, DNS, email, and IP) are required or included as subject alternative names in certificates issued by the Active Directory connector.
Requires the Common Name (CN) component to be present in the subject name for certificates issued by this connector template when set to true.

When enabled, this flag requires the certificate's subject name to include the full directory path (distinguished name) of the AD object, causing certificate requests that do not use a subject name with the directory path to be rejected.
When enabled, requires the certificate's subject common name (CN) to be set to the DNS name of the principal, as part of the subject name flags for the template.
Specifies whether the subject name for certificates issued from this template must include the email address of the principal.
Specifies whether the subject alternative name (SAN) must include the directory GUID of the object for the template.
Indicates whether the certificate must include a DNS name in the subject alternative name (SAN) extension.
When enabled, includes the domain DNS attribute of the Active Directory entity in the certificate's subject alternative name (SAN).
If true, the certificate template requires an email address to be included in the subject alternative name (SAN) of issued certificates.
Specifies whether the template requires that a Service Principal Name (SPN) be present in the certificate's subject alternative name (SAN).
Specifies whether the subject alternative name (SAN) of the certificate must include the user principal name (UPN).

This field lists the names of existing Active Directory certificate templates that this template supersedes, so that certificates issued from the superseded templates are replaced by certificates from this new template.
Defines the v3 template definition for the AWS Private CA Connector for Active Directory, including settings for certificate validity, key usage, extensions, and enrollment flags.
Specifies the validity period and renewal period for certificates issued from this template, including the duration and its unit (e.g., days, months, years).
Specifies how long before certificate expiration that the certificate will be renewed, using a period defined by a numeric value and time unit (such as days).
Defines the numeric duration of the renewal period, which combined with the sibling 'type' field specifies how long before certificate expiration a certificate can be renewed.
The unit of time (e.g., DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, YEARS) used to measure the renewal period for the certificate template.
Defines the numeric duration and unit of time (days, months, or years) during which certificates issued using this Active Directory connector template remain valid.

The numeric duration of the certificate validity period in a template v3 definition, interpreted with its associated unit type (e.g., days, months, or years) to determine how long issued certificates remain valid.
The unit of time (DAYS, MONTHS, or YEARS) used with the numeric period value to define the certificate validity duration.
Defines the enrollment flag settings for this v3 template, controlling behaviors such as inclusion of basic constraints and security extensions on certificates issued to AD principals.
When set to true, this flag allows certificate enrollment to reuse an existing key pair when the NT token keyset storage is full, preventing enrollment failure due to storage capacity.
Setting this to true includes symmetric algorithms in the certificate request for the AD CS template.

When set to true, this enrollment flag omits the security extension from certificates issued by this template, which is commonly needed for smart card logon and certificate-based authentication in Active Directory.

When enabled, this enrollment flag removes invalid certificates from the user's personal certificate store during enrollment, as specified by the REMOVE_INVALID_CERTIFICATE_FROM_PERSONAL_STORE flag in the AWS PCA Connector for AD template definition.
Specifies whether the user must be prompted to interact during certificate enrollment (rather than enrolling silently) when using this template.
Configures the certificate extensions applied by the template, including application policies and key usage settings.

Defines the Application Policies (Extended Key Usage) extension for the certificate template, specifying a list of application policy object identifiers (OIDs) that determine the certificate's intended purposes in the resulting certificates.
Indicates whether the application policies extension is critical, requiring certificates to be rejected if a client does not recognize this extension.

Defines the list of application policies (extended key usage purposes) that certificates issued from this template will support, where each policy item is specified by either an object identifier (OID) or a built-in application policy type.
Specifies the object identifier (OID) of an application policy (extended key usage) to include in the certificate template's Application Policies extension.

Specifies the type of application policy (enhanced key usage) for the template, selecting either a predefined usage such as CLIENT_AUTHENTICATION or CODE_SIGNING, or CUSTOM when the policy object must include a separate custom policy OID.

Specifies the X.509 KeyUsage extension, including a critical flag and usage flags (digital signature, key encipherment, data encipherment, key agreement, key certificate sign, CRL sign, encipher only, decipher only) that define the valid cryptographic purposes of the certificate's public key.
Whether the KeyUsage X.509 certificate extension is marked as critical in the template.
Identifies which key usage flags (for example, digital signature, key encipherment, and key agreement) will be included in the certificate's KeyUsage extension for the template.
Determines whether the key usage extension includes the DataEncipherment flag, authorizing the certificate's public key to be used for data encryption.
A boolean that, when set to true, enables the digitalSignature key usage flag, allowing the certificate's public key to be used for verifying digital signatures.
Indicates whether the key usage extension includes the Key Agreement (keyAgreement) flag in the certificate template's usage flags.
Indicates whether the key can be used for key encipherment, enabling a public key to encrypt symmetric keys or other data for key transport.
Indicates whether the key usage extension includes the non-repudiation flag, enabling the key to be used to verify digital signatures that provide non-repudiation.

Specifies the general flags for the certificate template, including MachineType and UserType booleans that determine whether the template is intended for machine or user certificate enrollment in the Active Directory environment.
Indicates whether the certificate template is enabled for automatic certificate enrollment for users or computers.
Specifies whether this certificate template is configured for machine (computer) principals in Active Directory, enabling computer authentication via issued certificates.
Specifies the hash algorithm (SHA256, SHA384, or SHA512) used to sign certificates issued from this Active Directory connector template.

Defines private key attributes such as minimum key length, key specification (RSA or ECC), and cryptographic providers for the certificate template version 3 in AWS Private CA Connector for Active Directory.
Specifies the private key algorithm (RSA or ECDSA) used for the certificate template in AWS Private CA Connector for Active Directory.
Specifies the list of cryptographic service providers (CSPs) and key storage providers (KSPs) allowed for private key generation in this Active Directory certificate template.
Determines the cryptographic algorithm (RSA or ECC) used for private keys generated for certificates issued under this template.

Defines the key usage property for the private key in a version 3 PCA Connector for AD template, specifying the certificate's intended key usages (such as digital signature or key encipherment) through either property flags or a property type.
Defines the set of key usage flags (Decrypt, KeyAgreement, KeyEncipherment, and Sign) that determine which cryptographic operations are permitted for the private key in the certificate template.
When true, the certificate template's private key is allowed to be used for decryption operations, influencing the key usage extension in issued certificates.
Determines whether the private key can be used for key agreement (e.g., Diffie-Hellman) in the key usage extension of the Active Directory certificate template.
Specifies whether the private key can be used for digital signature operations (the Digital Signature bit in the KeyUsage extension of the certificate template).

Specifies whether the key usage property for the private key allows all key usages (KEY_USAGE_PROPERTY_TYPE_ALL) or a custom set defined via the associated property flags (KEY_USAGE_PROPERTY_TYPE_CUSTOM).
Specifies the minimum key size in bits (e.g., 2048, 3072, or 4096) that the private key must have for certificates issued from this template.
Controls the private key flags for the v3 certificate template, including the client version that determines the minimum supported Windows client for certificate enrollment.
Specifies the minimum Windows Server client version (e.g., WINDOWS_SERVER_2008, WINDOWS_SERVER_2012) that the private key is compatible with for this v3 template's private key flags.
Indicates whether the private key associated with the certificate issued by this template can be exported.
Specifies whether the private key must support the alternate signature algorithm, which is required for CNG (Cryptography Next Generation) keys in this v3 template.
If enabled, the certificate template requires strong key protection for the private key, meaning the user must interact with the key (e.g., enter a password) before it can be used.

Specifies the subject name flags for the template v3, which control whether common name, directory path, DNS as CN, email, and auto-enrollment are included or required in the certificate's subject name.
Specifies whether the certificate subject must include a common name (CN) when using template v3 in the PCA Connector for Active Directory template.

Indicates whether the certificate subject name must include the directory path (e.g., the object's distinguished name path) for the principal, as part of the subject name flags in the version 3 template.

When true, forces the certificate's subject common name (CN) to be populated with the DNS name from the certificate request, corresponding to the RequireDNSAsCN flag in AWS PCA Connector for AD template subject name flags.
When set to true, the certificate subject name must include the requester's email address (the Email field) in the subject name.
Specifies whether the certificate's subject alternative name (SAN) must include the Active Directory directory GUID (objectGUID) of the enrolled subject.
Indicates whether certificates issued by this template must include a DNS name in the subject alternative name (SAN) extension.
Indicates whether the domain DNS name must be included in the certificate's subject alternative name (SAN).
Specifies whether the issued certificate's subject alternative name (SAN) must include an email address.
If true, the certificate template requires the subject alternative name (SAN) to include the Service Principal Name (SPN) of the certificate subject.
When enabled, requires the certificate's Subject Alternative Name (SAN) to include the User Principal Name (UPN) of the AD user or computer.
Specifies the list of existing Active Directory certificate template names that this v3 template supersedes, preventing those older templates from being used for new certificate requests.

Defines the configuration for an Active Directory certificate template using schema version 4, including settings for certificate validity, enrollment flags, private key attributes, key usage, and extensions.
Specifies the validity period of certificates issued from this template, including the numeric duration and its unit (days, months, or years), as defined in the version 4 template definition.

Specifies the duration (as a period and time unit) before a certificate's expiration when the CA connector automatically renews the certificate for templates defined in this CertificateValidity object.
The numerical value of the renewal period's duration, interpreted according to the associated unit type (such as DAYS, MONTHS, or YEARS) defined in the renewal_period's 'type' field.
Specifies the unit of time (DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, or YEARS) used for the renewal period of the certificate template.
Specifies how long the certificate is valid, expressed as a numerical period and a unit type such as days, months, or years.

Specifies the numeric magnitude of the certificate validity period, which combined with the associated type (e.g., DAYS, MONTHS, YEARS) determines how long certificates issued from this template remain valid.
Specifies the time unit (DAYS, MONTHS, or YEARS) for the validity period of certificates issued using this template.

Defines the enrollment flags for the v4 certificate template, controlling options such as whether user interaction is required during enrollment, whether auto-enrollment is permitted, and whether the security extension is included in issued certificates.
Enables certificate enrollment to reuse an existing key pair when the NT token keyset storage is full rather than failing.
Indicates whether symmetric algorithms are included in the certificate enrollment request for this template, allowing the client to use symmetric key algorithms for encryption.
When true, the certificate issued by the private CA connector omits the security extension in its enrollment flags.
When enabled, this enrollment flag removes certificates that are invalid or have expired from the personal certificate store of the enrolling user or computer during certificate enrollment.
Indicates whether the certificate requester must be present and interact during enrollment, such as by selecting a cryptographic service provider, when using this template.
Defines the certificate extensions (such as key usage and application policies) that will be included in certificates issued by the private CA based on this AD connector template.

Specifies the application policies extension for the certificate template, defining a list of policy OIDs that indicate the certificate's intended purposes and whether the extension is marked critical.

Indicates whether the application policies extension is marked as critical in the certificate template, causing a certificate with this extension to be rejected if a relying party does not recognize the application policy OIDs.

The list of application policy objects (each containing an object identifier) that defines the extended key usage purposes for certificates issued using this template, such as client or server authentication.
The object identifier (OID) that identifies the application policy (such as server authentication) to include in the certificate template.
Specifies the type of application policy to include, such as 'ANSI_X9_57' for a standard X.509 policy or 'OMIT' to exclude the policy from the template.

Defines the key usage extension for certificates issued by this template, specifying the permitted cryptographic purposes (such as digital signature or key encipherment) for the certificate's public key.
Specifies whether the key usage extension is marked as critical in the certificate template, requiring strict enforcement by certificate consumers.

Specifies the key usage flag values (such as DigitalSignature, KeyEncipherment, DataEncipherment, KeyAgreement, NonRepudiation, etc.) that define the intended cryptographic purposes of the certificate's public key in the KeyUsage extension.
Specifies whether the data encipherment key usage flag is set, indicating that the certificate's public key can be used to encrypt data directly.
Indicates whether the Digital Signature key usage flag is enabled for certificates issued by this template.
Indicates whether the key can be used for key agreement (such as Diffie-Hellman key exchange) in the certificate's key usage extension.
Indicates whether the key can be used for key encipherment, a key usage extension flag in the Active Directory certificate template.
When true, the certificate's key usage extension includes the non-repudiation bit, allowing the key to be used for digital signatures that provide non-repudiation.
Defines the general flags for the v4 certificate template, including whether auto-enrollment is enabled and whether the template applies to machine or user certificates.
Indicates whether the certificate template supports automatic enrollment, enabling client computers to automatically request and renew certificates based on this template.
Determines whether the certificate template is issued to computer (machine) principals, as opposed to user principals.
Specifies the hash algorithm (such as SHA256, SHA384, or SHA512) used for signing certificates issued from this Private CA Connector for Active Directory template.

Defines the private key cryptographic configuration for the certificate template, including the key algorithm, key usage spec, minimal key length, and allowed cryptographic service providers used during AD certificate enrollment.
Specifies the cryptographic algorithm for the private key, with allowed values of RSA, ECDSA_P256, ECDSA_P384, or ECDSA_P521.
Specifies the list of allowed cryptographic service providers (CSPs) or key storage providers (KSPs) that can be used for the private key in this Active Directory template.
Specifies the cryptographic algorithm and key size for the private key, such as RSA_2048 or ECDSA_P256.

Specifies the key usage extension properties, including the set of key usage flags (such as digital signature, key encipherment, or key agreement) and whether the extension is marked critical, for the private key attributes of this template version 4 definition.
Defines the key usage property flags (Decrypt, KeyAgreement, KeyEncipherment, and Sign) for the certificate template, controlling which private key operations the certificate is allowed to perform.
Indicates whether the private key can be used for decryption, controlling the 'Allow private key to be used for decryption' setting in the Active Directory certificate template's key usage flags.

For an Active Directory certificate template definition, this boolean specifies whether the private key's key usage property includes the Key Agreement flag, allowing the key to be used for protocols like Diffie-Hellman key exchange.
Specifies whether the certificate key can be used for cryptographic signing (digital signature), enabling the certificate to sign data.
Sets the key usage property type to 'ALL', which permits all key usages for the private key in the Active Directory connector template.
Specifies the minimum size, in bits, of the private key that can be used to generate certificates for this template.
Specifies the private key flags for the v4 template, defining the minimum client version and whether private keys are stored in the TPM or in software.
Specifies the Windows client version that the private key flags apply to, controlling the minimum operating system version that can use the certificate template in the AD forest.
Indicates whether the private key can be exported from the certificate store after issuance, corresponding to the 'Allow export of private key' option in Windows certificate templates.
Indicates whether the private key generated by this template uses an alternate signature algorithm, which is required for compatibility with certain client operating systems.
This boolean flag specifies whether renewals must use the same key pair as the original certificate, enforcing key continuity for certificates issued under this template.
Determines whether the private key associated with this AD connector template requires strong key protection, meaning a user must provide a password or other approval before the key can be used.
Specifies whether to use the legacy cryptographic service provider (CSP) instead of the Cryptography API: Next Generation (CNG) provider for the private key.
Specifies which subject name components—such as common name, directory path, DNS as common name, email, SPN, and UPN—are required in the certificate's subject name for this template v4.
Requires that the certificate subject include a common name (CN) when this subject name flag is set.
When true, this flag requires the certificate subject name to include the full directory path (Distinguished Name) of the Active Directory object.
When enabled, requires the certificate subject's common name (CN) to be set to the DNS name, as part of the SubjectNameFlagsV4 settings for the AD connector template.
When set to true, this flag requires that the user's email address appear in the certificate's subject name for the Active Directory template.
Specifies whether the subject alternative name (SAN) of the certificate must include the directory GUID of the AD object, enabling directory GUID-based identity in the certificate's SAN extension.
When true, this flag requires the certificate's subject alternative name (SAN) to include the DNS name in the template.
Specifies whether the subject alternative name (SAN) must include the domain DNS name of the subject in the certificate template.
When true, this flag requires that the subject alternative name (SAN) of the issued certificate include the email address of the enrollee.
Indicates whether the certificate's subject alternative name (SAN) must include a Service Principal Name (SPN) for the template.

When true, this flag requires that the certificate's Subject Alternative Name (SAN) includes the User Principal Name (UPN) of the Active Directory principal requesting the certificate, which is often required for smart card or other authentication scenarios.

Specifies the list of existing certificate template names that this template supersedes, causing the CA connector to associate this new template with those older templates for replacement in Active Directory.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_template.name.text: A user-defined name for the certificate template, which must be unique within the connector and identifies the template in AWS Private CA Connector for Active Directory.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_template.reenroll_al.text: When set to true, triggers reissuance of certificates to all existing certificate holders when the template is updated or modified.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_template.template_ar.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Private CA Connector for Active Directory template managed by this resource.

aws_pcaconnector_ad_template_group_acces.text: Specifies the permissions for the group on the certificate template, including which operations are allowed or denied (such as enroll and autoenroll) via nested Allow and Deny blocks.
Specifies whether the group is granted permission to automatically enroll for certificates, with allowed values 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.

Sets whether the associated Active Directory group is allowed to enroll for certificates using the configured certificate template, forming the enroll access right in this template group access control entry.
Specifies the display name of the Active Directory security group that this template access control entry grants certificate enrollment permissions to.
Specifies the security identifier (SID) of the Active Directory group to which this access control entry grants permissions for the associated template.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Private CA Connector for Active Directory template that this group access control entry applies to.

aws_pcaconnector_scep_challenge.challeng.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the SCEP challenge within AWS Private CA Connector for SCEP, assigned by AWS when the challenge is created.

aws_pcaconnector_scep_challenge.connecto.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the connector that this SCEP challenge belongs to, required to create the challenge under that connector.

aws_pcaconnector_scep_connector.certific.text: The ARN of the AWS Private CA (Certificate Authority) that the SCEP connector uses to sign and issue certificates.

aws_pcaconnector_scep_connector.connecto.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the SCEP connector created by PCA Connector for SCEP.

aws_pcaconnector_scep_connector.endpoint.text: The URL endpoint at which devices access the SCEP connector to enroll for certificates from the associated private CA.

aws_pcaconnector_scep_connector.mobile_d.text: This field specifies the mobile device management (MDM) configuration for the SCEP connector, which enables integration with an MDM system like Microsoft Intune by providing the necessary Intune credentials and domain details for challenge password delivery.

aws_pcaconnector_scep_connector.open_id_.text: The OpenID Connect (OIDC) configuration for the SCEP connector, containing the issuer URL and JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint used to authenticate SCEP client requests.
The expected audience (client ID) claim in the OIDC token used for SCEP client authentication, which the connector validates to ensure the token was issued specifically for this connector.
The issuer URL of the OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider (IdP) that the connector uses to validate the JWT tokens presented by SCEP clients.
The subject claim that must be present in the OpenID Connect token used to authenticate requests to the SCEP connector, enabling validation of the token's 'sub' field.

aws_pcaconnector_scep_connector.type.text: The AWS-assigned connector type (e.g., GENERAL_PURPOSE) that describes the intended use mode of the SCEP connector returned after provisioning.

aws_pcaconnector_scep_connector.vpc_endp.text: The ID of the VPC endpoint that this SCEP connector uses to privately receive SCEP traffic within your VPC.

aws_pcs_cluster.endpoints.ipv6_address.text: The IPv6 address assigned to this cluster endpoint, enabling connectivity to the AWS PCS cluster management services over IPv6.

aws_pcs_cluster.endpoints.port.text: The TCP port number used to access the cluster endpoint, returned by the AWS PCS service for connecting to the cluster's scheduler or management interface.

aws_pcs_cluster.endpoints.private_ip_add.text: The private IP address of a Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS) cluster endpoint, such as the Slurm scheduler (Slurmctld) or database (Slurmdbd), used for internal communication within the VPC.

aws_pcs_cluster.endpoints.public_ip_addr.text: The public IP address of the cluster endpoint, which clients use to connect to the cluster's Slurm scheduler.

aws_pcs_cluster.endpoints.type.text: The type of the cluster endpoint, such as Slurmctld or Slurmdbd, indicating the Slurm service the endpoint provides access to.

aws_pcs_cluster.error_info.code.text: The machine-readable error code returned by AWS PCS when a cluster creation or update operation fails.

aws_pcs_cluster.error_info.message.text: The human-readable error message from an error_info entry, describing the error condition reported for this AWS PCS cluster.

aws_pcs_cluster.slurm_configuration.cgro.text: The name of a parameter to add to the Slurm cgroup.conf file, where each custom setting pairs a parameter name with its value.
The value component of a key-value pair in cgroup_custom_settings, used to override or add a custom cgroup parameter in the Slurm configuration of the PCS cluster.

aws_pcs_cluster.slurm_configuration.slur.text: The name of a Slurm configuration parameter (such as a slurm.conf directive) that you want to override with a custom value in the cluster's Slurm configuration.
The value of a custom Slurm configuration key-value pair, applied to the Slurm scheduler configuration of the cluster to set or override a specific parameter.
The Slurmdbd configuration parameter name (corresponding to a slurmdbd.conf setting) that this custom setting overrides in the cluster's SlurmDBD configuration.
The value of a custom SlurmDBD configuration parameter, paired with its parameter_key, that is applied to the Slurm database daemon for the AWS PCS cluster.

aws_pcs_compute_node_group.error_info.co.text: A machine-readable code that identifies the specific error encountered while AWS PCS was provisioning or managing this compute node group.

aws_pcs_compute_node_group.error_info.me.text: The message text that describes the error condition affecting the compute node group.

aws_pcs_compute_node_group.instance_conf.text: Specifies the EC2 instance type (for example, `c5.large`) that the compute nodes in this instance configuration will use within the compute node group.

aws_pcs_compute_node_group.node_lifecycl.text: The list of argument strings passed to the custom node lifecycle action script that runs when a compute node in the group completes its bootstrap process, allowing the bootstrap script to be parameterized with specific values.
The execution policy for the node bootstrapped lifecycle stage, determining whether the compute node continues or fails if the bootstrap script exits with a non-zero code.
Specifies the name of the node bootstrapped stage in the compute node group's lifecycle actions configuration, identifying this lifecycle stage uniquely.
The script or command that AWS PCS runs on a compute node if the node bootstrapping lifecycle stage fails, allowing custom error handling such as logging or node cleanup in the compute node group.
Specifies the source (such as an S3 location or URI) from which the bootstrap script is retrieved and executed on a compute node when it reaches the node bootstrapped lifecycle stage.
The checksum (e.g., SHA256) of the bootstrap script content in the script source, used to verify the integrity of the script during node bootstrapping in AWS PCS compute node groups.
The version ID of the S3 object that supplies the bootstrap script for the node bootstrapped lifecycle stage, used to pin to a specific version of the script.
The Amazon S3 URI of the script that AWS PCS runs during the node bootstrapped stage of the compute node group's lifecycle actions.
The list of command-line arguments to pass to the script executed by the node_ready lifecycle action for compute nodes in this AWS PCS compute node group.
Specifies whether the node-ready lifecycle action is mandatory or optional, controlling how failures of the action script are handled when a compute node transitions to the ready state.

Specifies the error-handling action to take when a node fails to reach the ready state during the node_ready lifecycle stage, with allowed values such as CONTINUE or FAIL, controlling whether the node is retained or removed.
Defines the source of the script to execute when a compute node becomes ready, typically an S3 object reference that AWS PCS retrieves and runs as part of the lifecycle action.
The checksum (typically SHA256) used to validate the integrity of the script fetched from the script source before it is executed during the node-ready lifecycle stage.
The version ID of the S3 object that holds the script to execute when a compute node reaches the ready lifecycle stage within AWS Parallel Computing Service.
Specifies the S3 URI or local filesystem path of the script to execute on compute nodes at the 'node ready' lifecycle stage.

aws_pcs_compute_node_group.slurm_configu.text: The name of a Slurm configuration parameter to apply to the compute node group's slurm_custom_settings.
The value associated with a custom Slurm configuration parameter key for the compute node group, which overrides or augments the default Slurm configuration on the cluster.

aws_pcs_queue.compute_node_group_configu.text: Specifies the unique identifier of the compute node group to which this queue configuration targets, enabling the queue to submit jobs to the resources defined by that compute node group.

aws_pcs_queue.error_info.code.text: The short error code that identifies the type of failure affecting the queue, complementing the error message returned in the same error info object.

aws_pcs_queue.error_info.message.text: The error message that provides details about the failure condition affecting the AWS PCS queue, as reported in the queue's error information list.

aws_pcs_queue.slurm_configuration.slurm_.text: The name of a Slurm configuration parameter to set on the queue's Slurm cluster.
The value assigned to a custom Slurm parameter (identified by its parameter name) in the AWS PCS queue's Slurm configuration.

aws_personalize_dataset.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to an Amazon Personalize dataset, used to organize and identify the dataset in AWS.

aws_personalize_dataset_group.tags.value.text: The value of a tag (key-value pair) attached to the Amazon Personalize dataset group.

aws_personalize_event_tracker.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag assigned to the Amazon Personalize event tracker, used for metadata and cost allocation.

aws_personalize_event_tracker.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the Amazon Personalize event tracker, used for categorizing and managing the tracker resource.

aws_personalize_metric_attribution.metri.text: The type of user event (such as Purchase or Click) that this metric attribution uses to measure how recommendation results influence that activity.
Defines a SQL-like expression that computes the metric from event attributes and event types, for example `SUM(IF(event_type = 'click', 1, 0))`.
The user-defined name for this metric within the Amazon Personalize metric attribution, used to identify it in the configuration and in the output reports.

aws_personalize_schema.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Personalize schema resource.

aws_personalize_solution.solution_config.text: The name of the categorical hyperparameter whose values are tuned during hyperparameter optimization (HPO) for the Amazon Personalize solution.

Specifies the list of allowed categorical values that a categorical hyperparameter (identified by the sibling Name field) can take during hyperparameter optimization (HPO) for the Amazon Personalize solution.
The maximum value for a continuous hyperparameter range used in hyperparameter optimization for the Amazon Personalize solution.
The minimum value of the range for a continuous hyperparameter that Amazon Personalize explores during hyperparameter optimization (HPO) for the solution.
The name of the continuous hyperparameter to tune during hyperparameter optimization (HPO), which matches a hyperparameter defined in the recipe used by the Amazon Personalize solution.
The maximum value allowed for the integer hyperparameter range used in hyperparameter optimization (HPO) for the Amazon Personalize solution.
The minimum value allowed for an integer-valued hyperparameter in the range being tuned by hyperparameter optimization (HPO).
The name of the integer hyperparameter to tune, matching a hyperparameter name supported by the recipe used by the solution.

aws_personalize_solution.tags.key.text: The key part of a user-defined tag attached to the Amazon Personalize solution, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_personalize_solution.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag key-value pair attached to the Amazon Personalize solution resource.

aws_pinpoint_admchannel.application_id.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Pinpoint application to which the ADM channel is associated.

aws_pinpoint_admchannel.client_id.text: The client ID obtained from your Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) project, required to authorize Pinpoint to send push notifications to Android apps.

aws_pinpoint_admchannel.client_secret.text: The client secret from the Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) service that Amazon Pinpoint uses to authorize and send push notifications through the ADM channel.

aws_pinpoint_admchannel.enabled.text: Indicates whether the ADM channel is enabled for sending push notifications through Amazon Pinpoint.

aws_pinpoint_apnschannel.application_id.text: The unique identifier for the Amazon Pinpoint application that the APNS channel is associated with.

aws_pinpoint_apnschannel.bundle_id.text: The bundle ID that uniquely identifies the app to Apple's Push Notification service (APNs), used as part of the APNs channel configuration in Amazon Pinpoint.

aws_pinpoint_apnschannel.certificate.text: The PEM-encoded Apple Push Notification service (APNs) SSL certificate, which is required when authenticating with a certificate instead of a token for sending push notifications through Amazon Pinpoint.

aws_pinpoint_apnschannel.default_authent.text: Specifies the default authentication method for APNs, which must be either 'CERTIFICATE' or 'TOKEN', used to authenticate with Apple Push Notification service for sending push notifications through Amazon Pinpoint.

aws_pinpoint_apnschannel.enabled.text: Specifies whether to enable the APNs (Apple Push Notification service) channel for the associated Amazon Pinpoint application, allowing it to send push notifications to iOS devices.

aws_pinpoint_apnschannel.id.text: The unique identifier assigned to the APNs channel within the Amazon Pinpoint application.

aws_pinpoint_apnschannel.private_key.text: The PEM-encoded .p8 private key file issued by Apple that Pinpoint uses for token-based authentication with the Apple Push Notification service (APNs).

aws_pinpoint_apnschannel.team_id.text: The Apple Team ID used to authenticate with Apple Push Notification Service when the APNs channel uses token-based authentication.

aws_pinpoint_apnschannel.token_key.text: The private key (in .p8 format) used to authenticate with Apple Push Notification service, corresponding to the token key ID and team ID.

aws_pinpoint_apnschannel.token_key_id.text: The Apple Push Notification service key identifier (kid) from the .p8 private key used to authenticate with APNs via token-based credentials, required when using token authentication.

aws_pinpoint_apnssandbox_channel.applica.text: The ID of the Amazon Pinpoint application to which this APNS sandbox channel belongs.

aws_pinpoint_apnssandbox_channel.bundle_.text: The bundle identifier (App ID) of the iOS application that will receive push notifications through this APNs sandbox channel.

aws_pinpoint_apnssandbox_channel.certifi.text: The Apple Push Notification service (APNs) sandbox certificate, provided in .pem or .p12 format along with its private key, used to authenticate the Pinpoint app with the APNs sandbox endpoint.

aws_pinpoint_apnssandbox_channel.default.text: Determines the default authentication method (CERTIFICATE or TOKEN) that Amazon Pinpoint uses to authenticate with the APNs sandbox service for this channel.

aws_pinpoint_apnssandbox_channel.enabled.text: Whether the APNs sandbox channel is enabled for sending push notifications.

aws_pinpoint_apnssandbox_channel.id.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Pinpoint application that this APNs sandbox channel is associated with.

aws_pinpoint_apnssandbox_channel.private.text: The private key (from a .p8 file) used to sign APNs authentication tokens when token-based authentication is enabled for the sandbox channel.

aws_pinpoint_apnssandbox_channel.team_id.text: The Apple Developer Team ID, a 10-character alphanumeric string, used for APNs authentication with the sandbox channel.

aws_pinpoint_apnssandbox_channel.token_k.text: The private key (.p8 file) from Apple used for token-based authentication in the APNs sandbox channel, required when using token credentials instead of a certificate.
The key ID that Pinpoint uses to identify the private token key when authenticating with the APNs sandbox service.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_channel.applicatio.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Pinpoint application that the APNs VoIP channel is associated with.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_channel.bundle_id.text: The Apple-assigned bundle identifier (e.g., com.example.app) for the iOS app that receives APNs VoIP push notifications, used in the Pinpoint APNs VoIP channel configuration.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_channel.certificat.text: The Apple Push Notification service (APNs) VoIP channel certificate (the .pem file content) used for certificate-based authentication with APNs, which must be paired with the PrivateKey to enable sending VoIP push notifications.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_channel.default_au.text: Determines the default authentication method (either certificate-based or token-based) that Amazon Pinpoint uses to authenticate with the Apple Push Notification service (APNs) for sending VoIP messages when both credentials are configured.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_channel.enabled.text: Indicates whether the APNs VoIP (Apple Push Notification service for Voice over IP) channel is enabled for the associated Amazon Pinpoint application.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_channel.id.text: The unique identifier assigned to the APNs VoIP channel by Amazon Pinpoint.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_channel.private_ke.text: The private key from Apple, paired with the certificate, used to authenticate with Apple Push Notification service for sending VoIP push notifications through this channel.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_channel.team_id.text: The Apple Developer Team ID used, along with the token key and key identifier, to authenticate the APNs VoIP channel via token-based authentication for sending push notifications.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_channel.token_key.text: Specifies the token signing key (a .p8 private key from Apple) that Amazon Pinpoint uses to generate authentication tokens for sending VoIP push notifications through the APNs VoIP channel.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_channel.token_key_.text: The key identifier (kid) of the .p8 private token key that Amazon Pinpoint uses to sign APNs authentication tokens for the VoIP channel when the default authentication method is 'token'.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_sandbox_channel.ap.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Pinpoint application that this APNs VoIP sandbox channel is associated with.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_sandbox_channel.bu.text: Specifies the bundle identifier of the iOS app that receives APNs VoIP notifications via the sandbox channel, used when authenticating with APNs token keys.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_sandbox_channel.ce.text: The PEM-encoded Apple Push Notification service (APNs) certificate that Amazon Pinpoint uses to authenticate with APNs for sending VoIP notifications through the sandbox channel.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_sandbox_channel.de.text: Specifies which authentication method (Certificate or Token) Amazon Pinpoint uses when sending messages through the APNs VoIP sandbox channel.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_sandbox_channel.en.text: Specifies whether the APNs VoIP sandbox channel is enabled for the application, allowing it to send VoIP push notifications through Apple's sandbox environment.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_sandbox_channel.id.text: The unique identifier for this APNs VoIP sandbox channel, which is a short system-assigned string (such as 'apns_voip_sandbox') that identifies the channel within its Pinpoint application.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_sandbox_channel.pr.text: The private key from the Apple Push Notification service (APNs) .p12 certificate file, used to authenticate with APNs for the VoIP sandbox channel.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_sandbox_channel.te.text: The Apple Developer Team ID used to authenticate the APNs VoIP sandbox channel's token signing key with Apple's push notification service.

aws_pinpoint_apnsvoip_sandbox_channel.to.text: The private key (from a .p8 file) used for token-based authentication with Apple Push Notification service for the VoIP sandbox channel in Amazon Pinpoint.
Specifies the Apple APNs token key ID (the 10-character key identifier from the .p8 private key) used for token-based authentication with the APNs VoIP sandbox endpoint.

aws_pinpoint_app.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Pinpoint application.

aws_pinpoint_app.id.text: The unique identifier assigned to the Amazon Pinpoint application when it is created.

aws_pinpoint_app.name.text: The display name of the Amazon Pinpoint application.

aws_pinpoint_app.tags.text: Assigns tags (key-value pairs) to the Amazon Pinpoint application, enabling categorization and management via AWS Resource Groups and cost allocation.

aws_pinpoint_application_settings.applic.text: Specifies the unique identifier (ID) of the Amazon Pinpoint application to which these settings apply.

aws_pinpoint_application_settings.campai.text: The campaign hook specifies the Lambda function and invocation mode that Amazon Pinpoint invokes when a campaign sends messages, enabling custom logic like message personalization or filtering during send time.
The name or ARN of the Lambda function that Amazon Pinpoint invokes as the campaign hook for this application's campaigns and journeys.
Specifies whether the associated Lambda function is invoked during campaign filtering (FILTER) or during campaign delivery (DELIVERY).

aws_pinpoint_application_settings.cloud_.text: Specifies whether CloudWatch metrics are enabled for the Amazon Pinpoint application.

aws_pinpoint_application_settings.id.text: This field is the unique identifier of the Amazon Pinpoint application that these settings apply to, equal to the value of the `application_id` argument.

aws_pinpoint_application_settings.limits.text: Defines quotas for campaign messaging, including the maximum number of messages per day, total messages, per-second send rate, and maximum campaign duration.
The maximum number of messages that a campaign or journey can send to users in a 24-hour period.
The maximum number of seconds that a campaign can run before it is stopped.
The maximum number of messages that can be sent per second through the Amazon Pinpoint application, as a rate limit for campaigns and journeys.
The default maximum number of messages that a campaign or journey can send to a single user over the entire duration of the campaign or journey, as configured in the application's limits.

aws_pinpoint_application_settings.quiet_.text: Defines a daily quiet time window with start and end times (in HH:MM format) during which Amazon Pinpoint does not deliver messages to endpoints in the application.
Specifies the time, in 24-hour HH:MM format, when the daily quiet time ends for the application, marking the end of the window during which messages are not sent to users.
Specifies the start time of the daily quiet period, formatted as HH:MM in 24-hour clock using the application's timezone, during which Amazon Pinpoint suppresses sending messages to endpoints.

aws_pinpoint_baidu_channel.api_key.text: The API key from Baidu Cloud Push used to authenticate the Baidu channel with the Baidu Push service.

aws_pinpoint_baidu_channel.application_i.text: The unique ID of the Amazon Pinpoint application to which this Baidu channel belongs and is configured for sending push notifications.

aws_pinpoint_baidu_channel.enabled.text: Indicates whether the Baidu channel is enabled for delivering push notifications to the app.

aws_pinpoint_baidu_channel.id.text: The ID of the AWS Pinpoint application this Baidu channel is associated with (the ApplicationId returned by Ref).

aws_pinpoint_baidu_channel.secret_key.text: The Baidu Cloud Push API secret key, used together with the API key to authenticate Amazon Pinpoint with Baidu's push notification service for this channel.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.additional_treatme.text: Specifies additional A/B test treatment variations for the campaign, each with its own message configuration, schedule, and treatment-specific settings.

The custom delivery configuration for an additional treatment, specifying the SNS topic or S3 bucket used as the destination for custom endpoints and the types of endpoints treated as custom for that treatment.
Specifies the destination URI or ARN (such as an Amazon SNS topic ARN, Lambda function ARN, or webhook URL) that receives the campaign messages for this treatment when custom delivery is configured.
Defines the list of endpoint types (e.g., EMAIL, SMS, PUSH) for which the custom delivery configuration (such as a Lambda function URI) applies for this additional treatment in the campaign.
Specifies the message configuration (such as email, SMS, push, or custom message content and delivery settings) for this additional treatment in the Amazon Pinpoint campaign.
Configures the Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) push notification settings for the treatment, specifying message content like the body, title, action, and media options for ADM-enabled endpoints.
Specifies the action to take when a recipient taps the ADM (Amazon Device Messaging) push notification, with valid values OPEN_APP, DEEP_LINK, or URL.
The body of the ADM (Amazon Device Messaging) message to send for this campaign treatment.
The URL of the image icon to display alongside the ADM push notification sent by this campaign treatment.
Specifies the URL of the small icon image displayed in the ADM (Amazon Device Messaging) push notification for this additional treatment of the campaign.
The URL of the image to display in the push notification for the Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) channel, used in the message configuration of this additional treatment.
The JSON-formatted message body sent to the Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) service, used as an alternative to the 'Body' field when a raw JSON payload is needed.
The URL of the media content (e.g., an image) to include in the ADM (Amazon Device Messaging) push notification message for this additional treatment of the campaign.
Raw, JSON-formatted payload for the ADM push notification message sent for this campaign treatment, overriding all other message body fields when present.
Specifies whether the ADM (Amazon Device Messaging) message is a silent push notification, which delivers the payload without showing an alert or playing a sound on the device.
Specifies the duration (in seconds) that Amazon Device Messenger (ADM) retains and attempts to deliver the push notification before it expires, for this campaign treatment's ADM message settings.
The title of the ADM (Amazon Device Messaging) push notification message sent as part of this campaign treatment.
The URL to open when a recipient interacts with the ADM (Amazon Device Messaging) push notification from this alternate treatment, used for deep-linking into an app.
Configuration for the Apple Push Notification Service (APNs) message sent to iOS endpoints for this additional treatment in the multivariate campaign.
The action to perform when a recipient taps the APNs push notification, with valid values of OPEN_APP, DEEP_LINK, or URL.
The body text of the APNs push notification message for this additional treatment in the campaign.
Specifies the URL of the image icon to be displayed for the iOS push notification sent via this APNs message configuration.
The URL of the small icon image displayed in the notification for Apple Push Notification service (APNs) messages sent by this campaign treatment.
Specifies the JSON-formatted body of the Apple Push Notification service (APNS) message that is sent as part of the additional treatment's message configuration.
The URL of the rich media content (e.g., image, audio, or video) to include in the APNS push notification for this treatment.
Raw JSON payload for the APNs push notification message, overriding structured message properties when provided.

For the APNs message configuration of each additional treatment, this boolean specifies whether the notification is sent as a silent push, suppressing the display of an alert or message on the device.

Number of seconds that an APNs push message in this additional treatment is valid for; if it cannot be delivered before the TimeToLive value expires, Apple Push Notification service discards the message.
The title text that appears in the notification banner for the Apple Push Notification Service (APNs) message sent by this campaign treatment.
The URL that the APNs push notification opens when the user taps it, typically used when the message action is set to URL.
Defines the Baidu push notification settings (such as title, body, action, data, sound, and URL) for the message sent to Baidu endpoints by this campaign treatment.
For a Baidu push notification in an Amazon Pinpoint campaign, this field specifies the action to take when a user taps the notification, and can be set to OPEN_APP, DEEP_LINK, or URL.
The body text of the Baidu push notification message configured for this additional treatment of the campaign.
The URL of the image icon to display as part of the Baidu push notification for the message configured in this additional campaign treatment.
The URL of the small icon image displayed for the Baidu push notification in the additional treatment's message configuration.
The URL of the image to display in the Baidu push notification for this message treatment.
Specifies the JSON payload for the Baidu push notification message in this additional treatment's message configuration.
The URL to the media file (such as an image or video) that is included in the Baidu push notification message for this campaign treatment.
The raw JSON payload delivered to Baidu for the push notification message in this additional treatment, overriding other message fields when specified.
Whether the Baidu push message is sent as a silent push, delivering data without displaying a notification to the user.
Specifies the expiration time, in seconds, for the Baidu push notification message in this additional treatment of the campaign, after which the message is no longer delivered.
The title displayed in the Baidu push notification sent to users for this campaign treatment.
The URL to open when a user taps the Baidu push notification sent as part of this treatment's message configuration.
Configures the custom message for an additional treatment in a Pinpoint campaign, specifying the payload data to be delivered via the custom message.

The string payload (often JSON-formatted) that is delivered as the content of the custom message for this additional campaign treatment, overriding the default custom message data for the A/B test variant.
Configures the default message content (text, subject, and other settings) sent to recipients in this additional treatment of the Amazon Pinpoint campaign.

Sets the action that occurs when a recipient taps the default message of an additional treatment in a Pinpoint campaign, where OPEN_APP launches the app, DEEP_LINK follows a configured app deep link, and URL opens a specified web URL.
Sets the text content of the default message used by this additional treatment's message configuration for the Pinpoint campaign.
The URL of the image icon to display in the push notification for the default message of the additional treatment in the campaign.
The URL of the small icon image displayed in the push notification for the default message of an additional treatment in this Pinpoint campaign.
Specifies the URL of the image displayed in the default message for an additional treatment group of an Amazon Pinpoint campaign.
A JSON-formatted string that specifies the body of the default message for the additional treatment in the Amazon Pinpoint campaign.
This field specifies the URL of media content (such as an image) to include in the default message for an additional treatment of the Amazon Pinpoint campaign.
The raw, unformatted content of the default message for this additional A/B test treatment in the campaign, used when no channel-specific message override is configured.
Indicates whether the default message for this campaign treatment is sent as a silent push notification, suppressing the alert sound and banner on the target device.

The number of seconds that the default push notification message remains valid; if the message cannot be delivered within this time, such as when the device is offline, the push notification service expires it.
The subject line (for email) or notification title (for push) used in the default message for this additional campaign treatment.

Specifies the URL (web link or deep link) to include in the default message delivered for this additional treatment, allowing recipients to be directed to a specific destination when they interact with the message.
Configures the email message for a treatment group, specifying the subject, body, HTML body, and sender address for emails sent by the Amazon Pinpoint campaign.
The body content of the email message for this additional treatment, containing the HTML or plain-text message text.
Specifies the sender's email address from which the email message for this additional treatment is sent.
Specifies the HTML body of the email message sent as part of an additional treatment (variation) in the Amazon Pinpoint campaign.
The subject line of the email message sent for this additional treatment variant in the Amazon Pinpoint campaign.

Configures the GCM (Google Cloud Messaging / Firebase Cloud Messaging) push notification settings, such as the action, message body, and image icon URL, for an additional treatment group within a Pinpoint campaign.
Specifies the action to perform when a user taps the GCM push notification for this campaign treatment; valid values are OPEN_APP, DEEP_LINK, or URL.
Specifies the text body of the push notification sent to Android devices via Firebase Cloud Messaging (GCM) for this additional treatment group in the Amazon Pinpoint campaign.
Specifies the URL of the icon image to display in the push notification sent to Android devices through GCM for this campaign treatment.
Specifies the URL of the small icon image displayed in the Android device's status bar for the GCM push notification of this additional treatment.
The URL of the image to display in the GCM (Android) push notification for an additional treatment of the campaign.
The raw JSON payload of the Google Cloud Messaging (now Firebase Cloud Messaging) push notification message for this additional treatment's override configuration.
The URL of the media (e.g., an image or video) to include in the Google Cloud Messaging (GCM) push notification sent as part of this additional treatment's message configuration.
The raw JSON-formatted message payload (e.g., a Firebase Cloud Messaging notification structure) delivered to Android devices for this additional treatment's GCM message configuration.
For the GCM message in a campaign treatment, sets whether the push is silent, delivering the notification to the app without an audible or visible alert, typically to trigger background work.

Specifies the number of seconds that Firebase Cloud Messaging (GCM) retains the push message for delivery to an offline endpoint device; if the device becomes reachable within this time, the message is delivered, otherwise it expires.
The title text of the Google Cloud Messaging (GCM/FCM) push notification for this additional treatment, displayed as the notification's heading.
The URL to open when a user taps the GCM (Firebase Cloud Messaging) push notification sent by an additional treatment of this Amazon Pinpoint campaign.

The configuration for the in-app message delivered by this treatment, including its content, layout (e.g., top banner, carousel, full-screen), and action buttons, as part of the additional treatment's message configuration.
Specifies the list of content components for the in-app message, including header and body configurations, buttons, image URL, and background color.
Specifies the background color of the in-app message screen as a hex color code (e.g., '#FFFFFF').
The body_config object defines the configuration for the body text of the in-app message, including its alignment, text, and text color.
Specifies the text alignment for the body text of the in-app message, with valid values including LEFT, RIGHT, CENTER, and TOP.
Specifies the body text displayed in the in-app message content for a given additional treatment of the Amazon Pinpoint campaign.
Specifies the hex color code for the body text of the in-app message in the campaign's additional treatment.
HeaderConfig defines the header text, text color, and alignment for the in-app message content of a campaign treatment.
Determines the horizontal alignment of the header text in the in-app message, such as LEFT, CENTER, or RIGHT.
The text displayed as the header of the in-app message content for this campaign treatment.
In this additional treatment's in-app message header configuration, this field sets the color (as a hex color code) of the header text displayed in the message.
The URL of the image displayed in the in-app message content for the additional treatment's message configuration.
Configures the primary button of an in-app message content block, specifying properties such as button text, color, and the action to take (e.g., a deep link or closing the message).
Specifies the Android-specific style and action for the primary button of an in-app message, including attributes like background color, border radius, text color, and button tap behavior.
Defines the action to take when a user taps the primary button on Android within the in-app message content for this additional treatment, with allowed values such as LINK, DEEP_LINK, or CLOSE.
The URL or deep link that the Android primary button opens when a user taps it in the in-app message.

Sets the default click behavior (action type and link) for the primary button of an in-app message, serving as the fallback configuration when no platform-specific (Android, iOS, Web) override is defined.
Specifies the background color of the primary button in the in-app message's default configuration, using a hexadecimal color value (e.g., #FFFFFF).
Specifies the corner radius (in pixels) of the primary button's border in the default configuration of the in-app message content for this additional treatment of the campaign.
Specifies the behavior when a user taps the primary in-app messaging button, such as closing the message, opening a deep link, or launching a web URL (valid values: CLOSE, DEEP_LINK, LINK).
The URL that the primary button in the in-app message opens when tapped, applied as the default action for that button in the additional treatment's message content.
Sets the label (text) shown on the primary button of the in-app message content for the additional treatment of the Pinpoint campaign.
The hexadecimal color code (e.g., #FFFFFF) used for the text of the primary button in the default configuration of an in-app message within a Pinpoint campaign's additional treatment.
Provides iOS-specific configuration for the primary button, including its on-screen position, size, and the action to take when tapped.
Specifies the action to perform when the primary button on the iOS in-app message is tapped, such as closing the message or opening the deep link specified in the button's link property.
The URL or deep link that the primary in-app message button opens on iOS when tapped.
Specifies the configuration for the primary button in an in-app message when rendered on web platforms, including settings such as the button color, link, and action performed when tapped.
Determines the action (such as LINK, DEEP_LINK, or CLOSE) that occurs when a user clicks the primary button of an in-app message on web clients.
The URL that is opened when a user clicks the primary button in the in-app message content on the web channel.
Specifies the secondary (right-most) button of an in-app message, including its text, styling, and action to execute when clicked.

Defines Android-specific settings for the secondary button in an in-app message, specifying the button action (either LINK, which opens a URL, or DISMISS, which closes the message) and the link to open for the LINK action.
Defines the type of action that occurs when the user taps the secondary button of the in-app message on Android, with valid values typically including LINK, DEEP_LINK, and CLOSE.
The URL or deep link to open when a user taps the secondary button in the in-app message on Android devices for this additional treatment.

Specifies the default button configuration (including colors, border radius, text color, size, and position) for the secondary button in an in-app message, which applies when no platform-specific override (Web, iOS, or Android) is provided.
The background color of the secondary button in the in-app message, specified as a hexadecimal color value (e.g., '#000000').
Specifies the border radius in pixels for the secondary button's corners in the default style of the in-app message within a Pinpoint campaign.

Specifies the action a user triggers when tapping the secondary button in an in-app message's default configuration for a campaign treatment, such as closing the message (CLOSE), opening a deep link (DEEP_LINK), or opening a URL (LINK).
The URL that the secondary button opens when a user taps it in the in-app message.

The text label displayed on the secondary button of an in-app message content block within an additional treatment (variant) of an Amazon Pinpoint campaign, used when the in-app message appears in the default (mobile) app environment.
The hex color code (e.g., #000000) for the text of the secondary button in the in-app message's default configuration.

Specifies iOS-specific styling and action settings (such as background color, text color, border radius, and whether tapping the secondary button opens a URL or deep link) that override the default button configuration for in-app messages delivered to iOS devices.
Specifies the action taken when a user taps the secondary in-app message button on iOS devices; valid values are LINK (opens the associated URL) and CLOSE (dismisses the message).
The URL or deep link that the iOS secondary button opens when tapped by the user in the in-app message.

Specifies the web-specific settings for the secondary button of the in-app message content in this additional treatment, such as the button's text, background color, and link action for web endpoints.
Specifies the action to perform when a user clicks the secondary button in the web version of the in-app message, with valid values such as OPEN_URL, DEEP_LINK, or CLOSE.
The URL that the secondary button opens in a web browser when clicked, for the in-app message content of the additional treatment.
Provides a JSON object of custom key-value pairs to be associated with the in-app message, allowing you to pass additional configuration data to the message without altering the standard template.

For a given additional treatment of a Pinpoint campaign's in-app message configuration, this string specifies the layout style (e.g., TOP_BANNER, BOTTOM_BANNER, CAROUSEL, MIDDLE_BANNER, FULLSCREEN) that determines how the message content is visually arranged within the in-app message.
Specifies the content and delivery settings for SMS messages sent by this campaign treatment, including the message body, message type (transactional or promotional), and sender ID.
The text content of the SMS message sent as part of this additional treatment in the Amazon Pinpoint campaign.
The regulatory entity ID (sender ID) required for SMS messages in this campaign treatment when sending to countries that mandate DLT-based compliance, such as India.
The type of SMS message (e.g., TRANSACTIONAL or PROMOTIONAL) that determines the delivery priority and pricing for the SMS message in the campaign's additional treatment.
The phone number or short code from which the SMS message is sent, which must be an origination number associated with the Amazon Pinpoint account.
Specifies the custom sender ID that appears as the originator on recipients' mobile devices for SMS messages sent via this campaign treatment, used for branding or identification.
The unique ID of the SMS message template used by this additional treatment to compose the SMS message sent by the campaign.

Specifies the scheduling settings (start/end times, frequency, quiet time, timezone, and whether to use local time) for when this additional treatment (variant) of the campaign sends messages to its assigned audience.
The end time (in ISO 8601 format) for the schedule of this additional treatment, after which the treatment stops sending messages for the campaign.
Specifies the event filter criteria (such as event type and attributes) that determine when the additional treatment's schedule should trigger the campaign message.

The dimensions that define the event filter criteria for a campaign's scheduled event-based trigger, specifying the event type, attributes, and metrics that determine which events activate the campaign.

Specifies the event attribute key-value pairs that must match in the event for the event filter to trigger this additional treatment's schedule, where keys are event attribute names and values are the accepted attribute values.

Specifies the event type dimension for the event filter, using a SetDimension object that defines a set of event types (e.g., _session.start or custom events) and whether the filter is inclusive or exclusive.
Specifies whether to include or exclude events that match the event type when filtering, with valid values 'INCLUSIVE' or 'EXCLUSIVE'.
Specifies the list of event type names (e.g., 'click', 'open') that the event_type dimension in the event filter matches, allowing the campaign treatment to be triggered by events of these types.

Defines a map of metric names to metric dimension criteria (such as comparison operator and threshold value) used to filter event occurrences based on their metrics within the event filter for this campaign treatment.

Indicates the type of event to filter for, with valid values of SYSTEM (events generated by the system) or ENDPOINT (events from the endpoint), used by the event filter to determine when the scheduled campaign message is sent.
Specifies how often the additional treatment's message is delivered (e.g., ONCE, HOURLY, DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY) when the campaign schedule repeats.
Specifies whether the schedule for this treatment is based on the local time zone of the targeted endpoints rather than UTC.
Configures the quiet time for the schedule of an additional treatment, specifying the daily start and end times during which Amazon Pinpoint suppresses message sending for that treatment.
The end time of the quiet time window for this treatment's schedule, specified in 24-hour HH:MM format, during which the campaign will not send messages.
The start time (in HH:MM format) of the quiet time window, during which the campaign does not send messages to users, for this additional treatment group's schedule.
The start time (in ISO 8601 format) at which this additional treatment's schedule begins, determining when the A/B test variant becomes active for the campaign.
Specifies the time zone for the schedule of this additional treatment, such as 'UTC' or an IANA time zone name (e.g., 'America/New_York'), affecting when the treatment is sent.
The percentage of the target audience segment allocated to this additional treatment, enabling audience splitting across multiple campaign treatments for A/B testing.
For each additional campaign treatment (A/B variant), this object specifies the message template and version to use for delivering the campaign message.
Specifies the email message template (by name and version) that Amazon Pinpoint uses to send email messages for this treatment of the campaign.
The name of the Amazon Pinpoint email template that is used for this additional treatment's email message, allowing each treatment in the campaign to reference a different template.
The version number of the AWS Pinpoint email template that this additional treatment uses in the campaign's template configuration.
Specifies the push notification message template (template name and version) to use for this additional treatment's push messages, overriding the campaign-level push template when set.
The name of the Amazon Pinpoint push notification template (a message template of type PUSH) to use for this additional treatment's push messages.
Specifies the version of the push notification template to use for this additional treatment of the Amazon Pinpoint campaign.
The SMS template configuration for this additional treatment, defining the name and version of the SMS message template to use.
The name of the Amazon Pinpoint SMS template to use for the treatment's message content.
Specifies the version of the SMS template to use for this additional treatment in the campaign; if not specified, the default version of the template is used.
Configures the voice message template (by name and version) that Amazon Pinpoint applies to this additional treatment when sending voice messages.
The name of the Amazon Pinpoint voice template that this additional treatment uses to generate the voice message for its campaign treatment group.
For this additional treatment, specifies the version of the Amazon Pinpoint voice template to use; if not specified, the active version of the template is used.
Specifies the description of an additional treatment (variant) for the campaign, used to identify or explain the treatment's purpose.
The name of the additional treatment, used to identify and reference it within the campaign's A/B testing setup.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.application_id.text: The unique identifier for the Amazon Pinpoint project (application) that contains the campaign.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the campaign, assigned by AWS when the campaign is created.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.campaign_hook.text: Specifies the Lambda function and its invocation mode (e.g., EVENT or FILTER) that Amazon Pinpoint calls during the campaign's journey to perform custom logic or filtering.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.campaign_hook.lamb.text: The name or ARN of the AWS Lambda function that Amazon Pinpoint invokes when the campaign hook is triggered (for example, to customize or track message sends).

aws_pinpoint_campaign.campaign_hook.mode.text: Specifies whether the Lambda function is invoked to filter the destination audience segment (FILTER) or during message delivery (DELIVERY) for the campaign.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.campaign_hook.web_.text: The URL of the web hook that Amazon Pinpoint calls as part of the campaign hook execution.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.campaign_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the Pinpoint campaign, used to reference the campaign in other resources.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.custom_delivery_co.text: Specifies the custom delivery configuration for the campaign, including the delivery URI and endpoint types used to send messages through a custom channel.
The URI of the custom endpoint (such as a webhook or Lambda function) to which Amazon Pinpoint delivers the campaign message when using this custom delivery configuration.
Specifies the endpoint types (such as EMAIL, SMS, or PUSH) that use this custom delivery configuration when sending campaign messages.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.description.text: A human-readable summary of the campaign's purpose or contents, used to identify the campaign in the Amazon Pinpoint console and reports.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.holdout_percent.text: The percentage of recipients in the campaign who are held out from receiving the message, allowing for A/B testing or control groups to measure campaign effectiveness.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.is_paused.text: Specifies whether the campaign is paused, meaning it stops sending messages until resumed.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.limits.text: Configuration limits for the campaign, such as daily send quota, total messages, and maximum send rate (messages per second).

aws_pinpoint_campaign.limits.daily.text: The maximum number of messages that this campaign can send per day, after which message sends are throttled for the day.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.limits.maximum_dur.text: Specifies the maximum amount of time (in seconds) that a campaign can send messages before it stops.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.limits.messages_pe.text: The maximum number of messages that the campaign can send per second, throttling the send rate to control throughput and avoid exceeding limits.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.limits.total.text: The maximum total number of messages that a campaign can send to a single user over the campaign's lifetime.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.message_configurat.text: The `message_configuration` field defines the content and delivery settings for each message channel (e.g., email, SMS, push) used by the Amazon Pinpoint campaign, including the message body, subject, and sender information.
Specifies the configuration for the Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) push notification message sent by the campaign, including the message body, title, and action for Amazon Fire tablet devices.
Specifies the action to take when a recipient taps the ADM push notification, such as opening the app (OPEN_APP), opening a URL (OPEN_URL), or following a deep link (DEEP_LINK).
The body text of the ADM (Amazon Device Messaging) message delivered by the campaign.
The URL of the icon image displayed for the Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) push notification message.
Sets the URL of the small icon image that appears in the notification for the Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) message configured for the campaign.
Specifies the URL of the image to include in the ADM (Amazon Device Messaging) push notification message sent by the campaign.
The JSON-encoded body of the ADM (Amazon Device Messaging) push notification, which overrides the plain-text body when sending to Amazon Fire OS devices in a Pinpoint campaign.
The URL of the media content (such as an image, audio, or video) to include in the Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) push notification.
Specifies the raw, JSON-formatted message content to send as an ADM (Amazon Device Messaging) notification, which overrides the standard message body.
Specifies whether the ADM message is a silent push notification, so the message is delivered without displaying an alert or notification to the user.
The duration in seconds that the Amazon Device Messenger (ADM) service retains a push notification if the target device is offline, after which the message expires.
The title of the ADM (Amazon Device Messaging) push notification message sent by the campaign.
The URL that is opened on the user's device when they tap the ADM (Amazon Device Messaging) notification, used when the campaign message's action is set to URL.
Specifies the Apple Push Notification service (APNs) message properties for the campaign, including the alert title, body, sound, badge, and action for iOS devices.
Specifies the action to take when a recipient taps the push notification sent by this campaign's APNS message, such as opening the app, navigating to a deep link, or opening a URL.
The body text of the push notification delivered to Apple devices via the Apple Push Notification service (APNs).
