Specifies the URL of the image to display as the icon for the push notification sent to Apple devices through the APNS channel.
Specifies the URL of the small icon image displayed in the push notification on supported iOS devices.
The URL of the image to include in the push notification sent to Apple devices through the APNs channel for this campaign's message configuration.
The JSON-formatted payload for the APNS message, containing custom notification data that Amazon Pinpoint sends to Apple Push Notification Service.
The URL of the media content (e.g., an image or video) to attach to the Apple Push Notification service message, enabling rich notifications.
The raw JSON payload to send to Apple Push Notification Service, overriding any other message settings for the APNS channel.

When set to true, this sends the APNS message as a silent push notification, meaning it is delivered without alerting the user via a banner, sound, or badge, allowing the app to process the message in the background.
Specifies the time-to-live (in seconds) for the APNS push notification, controlling how long the message remains valid for delivery before it expires.
The title text of the Apple Push Notification Service (APNS) message sent to iOS devices in the campaign.
The URL to open in the user's app when they tap the push notification on an iOS device.

This object configures the default Baidu push notification message for the campaign, specifying the message body, action (e.g., open app or URL), and other delivery options like message type and silent push.
Specifies the action to be triggered when a recipient taps the Baidu push notification, with supported values including OPEN_APP, DEEP_LINK, and URL.
The body text of the Baidu push notification message sent to Android devices in China.
Specifies the URL of the icon image displayed for the Baidu push notification message.
Specifies the URL of the small icon image displayed in the notification for the Baidu push message.
The URL of the image to display in the Baidu push notification message for the campaign.
The JSON-formatted body of the message sent through the Baidu push notification service in Amazon Pinpoint.
The URL of the media content (e.g., image or video) to include in the Baidu push notification message for this campaign.
Specifies the raw, JSON-formatted payload for the Baidu push notification message, which overrides all other message content when set.
Indicates whether the Baidu push notification is sent as a silent push, meaning it does not alert the user and only delivers the payload to the app in the background.
Specifies how long (in seconds) the Baidu push notification service attempts to deliver the message before it expires.
Sets the title text for the Baidu push notification message displayed to recipients in the campaign.
Specifies the destination URL that a Baidu push notification opens in the user's mobile browser when the message action is set to URL.
Specifies a custom message that Amazon Pinpoint sends to endpoints not associated with a specific channel (e.g., email, SMS, or push), including optional body text and data.
Specifies the payload of the custom message delivered to the Amazon Pinpoint campaign's custom channel.
Defines the default message content (such as body and subject) that is used for all channels in the campaign when channel-specific message settings are not provided.
Specifies the action to occur when a user taps the push notification: OPEN_APP, DEEP_LINK, or URL.
The body text of the default message that is used by the campaign for all channel types unless overridden by a channel-specific message configuration.
Specifies the URL of the image icon displayed in the mobile push notification for the campaign's default message.
The URL of the small icon image displayed in push notifications sent by the campaign's default message configuration.
Specifies the URL of an image to include in the body of the default message that the campaign sends, such as in an email or push notification.
The JSON-formatted body of the default message, used for push notification channels that expect a JSON payload (such as GCM and APNs).
The URL of the media file (such as an image, audio, or video) to attach to the default message for the campaign, used for rich media content in supported channels.
Defines the raw email body content for the default message, applied when the campaign sends email messages.
When set to true, the default push notification is sent as a silent push, meaning it does not display an alert or play a sound on the recipient's device.
Time to Live (in seconds) for the default push notification message configured in the campaign, indicating how long the push service should attempt to deliver the notification before it expires.

For the default message of an Amazon Pinpoint campaign, this specifies the message title, which appears as the subject line for email deliveries and as the notification title for push notification deliveries.
The URL included in the campaign's default push notification message, used to deep link to a webpage or app location when the notification is opened.
Configures the email message delivered by the campaign, including the subject, sender address, and plain-text/HTML body content.
The plain-text body of the email message that is sent to the campaign's recipients.
Specifies the verified email address that appears on the 'From' line of the email message sent by the campaign.
The HTML-formatted body of the email message configured for the campaign, used when the chosen channel is email and message_configuration.email_message is set.
The subject line of the email message sent by the campaign.

This object specifies the settings for the Google Cloud Messaging (GCM) push notification message delivered to Android endpoint recipients of the campaign, including its action, body, image icon URL, and other GCM-specific payload attributes.
Sets the action to take on user tap for the Firebase Cloud Messaging (GCM) push notification, where 'OPEN_APP' (default) launches the app and 'DEEP_LINK' opens a specific deep link within the app.
The body text of the message sent to Android devices through the GCM (Firebase Cloud Messaging) channel for this Pinpoint campaign.
The URL of the icon image to display with the push notification sent to Android devices via Firebase Cloud Messaging (GCM) for this Pinpoint campaign.
Specifies the URL of the small icon image displayed in the status bar and notification drawer of the Android device for the GCM/FCM push message.
The URL of the image to display in the push notification sent through the Google Cloud Messaging (GCM) channel for the campaign.
Specifies the JSON-formatted body of the push notification delivered through the Google Cloud Messaging (GCM/FCM) channel, overriding the campaign's default message body for Android endpoints.
The URL of the media content to be included in the Google Cloud Messaging (GCM) push notification message.
Specifies the raw JSON-formatted payload of the GCM message, which overrides the individual message properties (such as Title and Body) when set.
Specifies whether the GCM message is a silent push notification, which delivers the payload to the app without displaying a visible notification or alert to the user.

For GCM (Google Cloud Messaging) messages in an Amazon Pinpoint campaign, this field sets the time-to-live in seconds, specifying how long the push notification should be retained by the push service for delivery to an offline device before it expires.
The title of the push notification delivered to Android devices via GCM/FCM in the Amazon Pinpoint campaign's GCM message configuration.
The URL that the GCM push message opens on the recipient's device when the message action is set to URL.
Defines the in-app message content, layout, and configuration that Amazon Pinpoint sends to users through the mobile app for this campaign.
Defines the array of content blocks for the in-app message, each specifying header/body text, images, and button actions displayed to users.
Defines the background color (in hexadecimal format) of the in-app message content in the campaign's in-app message configuration.
Defines the body text configuration for the in-app message, including the text content, alignment, and text color.
Specifies the horizontal alignment of the body text in the in-app message (e.g., LEFT, CENTER, RIGHT).
The body text of the in-app message displayed as part of the campaign's in-app message content.
Specifies the text color of the body content in the in-app message, expressed as a hexadecimal color code (for example, `#FFFFFF`).
Configures the header of the in-app message displayed to users, including the header text, its alignment (left, center, or right), and the text color.
Specifies the horizontal alignment (LEFT, CENTER, or RIGHT) of the header text in the in-app message.
The text displayed as the header of the in-app message, set in the header configuration of the campaign's in-app message content.
The hexadecimal color code used for the header text in the in-app message's header configuration.
Specifies the URL of the image to be displayed in the in-app message content for the Amazon Pinpoint campaign.

Configures the primary action button displayed in the in-app message content, including its visual styling (text, color, border) and the action it performs when tapped (e.g., opening a link, deep link, or closing the message).
The Android-specific override configuration for the primary button in an in-app message content, which customizes the button's text, action, and link behavior when rendered on Android devices.
Specifies the action that occurs when a user taps the primary button on Android, such as closing the in-app message, opening a deep link, or opening a URL.
Specifies the URL or deep link that the primary button in the Android in-app message opens when tapped by the user.

The default_config object specifies the default visual style and behavior for the primary button in an in-app message, such as its background color, text, text color, border radius, and the action (e.g., CLOSE or LINK) invoked when the button is tapped, used when no platform-specific override is set.
Specifies the background color of the primary button in the in-app message's default configuration, provided as a CSS-style color value such as a hex code or color name.
The border radius (in pixels) of the primary button's border in the in-app message when using the default button configuration.
Defines the action performed when a user taps the primary button in the in-app message, with valid values CLOSE, DEEP_LINK, or LINK.
The URL or deep link that the default primary button in the in-app message opens when tapped, used as the default destination unless overridden by platform-specific button configurations.
The text label displayed on the primary button in the in-app message when the default configuration is used.
Specifies the hex color code for the text of the primary button in the in-app message, used as the default configuration for that button.
Specifies the iOS-specific button configuration for the primary button of the in-app message, allowing you to override the default text, color, action, and link for iOS devices.

Determines the action performed when a user taps the primary button in an iOS in-app message for a Pinpoint campaign, with supported values of LINK (open a URL), DEEP_LINK (open a deep link), or CLOSE (dismiss the message).
The URL that opens on an iOS device when a user taps the primary button of the in-app message.
Specifies the button action, link URL, and color to use for the primary button when the in-app message is rendered on web browsers, overriding the default configuration.
Determines the action triggered when the web-based primary button is tapped: either opening the specified link ('LINK') or closing the in-app message ('CLOSE').
The URL that the primary button opens when clicked in the web version of the in-app message.
Defines the secondary button's display properties and behavior in the in-app message, such as its text, colors, link destination, and action type.
Specifies the Android platform-specific override configuration for the secondary button in an in-app message content, such as the button action and text.

The action taken when a user taps the secondary button in an in-app message on Android devices in a Pinpoint campaign, such as opening a deep link (DEEP_LINK), opening a web link (LINK), or closing the message (CLOSE).
Specifies the URL or deep link that the secondary button in the in-app message opens when tapped by an Android user.
DefaultConfig defines the default action, link, and text for the secondary button of an in-app message campaign, used when no platform-specific override is provided.
The background color (hex code) of the secondary action button in the default configuration of the in-app message content for the campaign.
The corner radius, in pixels, applied to the border of the secondary button in the in-app message content.
Specifies the action taken when a user taps the secondary button in the in-app message, with valid values CLOSE, DEEP_LINK, or LINK.
Specifies the deep link URL that the secondary button of the in-app message opens when tapped, as defined in the button's default configuration.
The text to display on the secondary button of the in-app message, used when no device-specific button configuration is provided.
Specifies the hex color code for the text of the secondary button in the default configuration of the in-app message.
Configures the iOS platform-specific settings for the secondary button in the in-app message content, including appearance attributes like text, color, and the button's action or link.
Specifies the action to perform when a user taps the secondary button in the iOS in-app message, such as closing the message, opening a deep link, or opening a URL.
The deep link or URL that is opened when a user taps the secondary button in the in-app message on iOS devices.
Defines web-specific settings (such as the link and text) for the secondary button in the in-app message, overriding the default button configuration when displayed on web endpoints.
Determines the action performed when a user clicks the secondary button in the web version of the in-app message, with valid values including LINK, DEEP_LINK, or CLOSE.
Specifies the web URL to open when a user clicks or taps the secondary button in the in-app message content on the web channel.
Specifies custom key-value data delivered to the user's device as part of the in-app message payload.
The layout template that controls how the in-app message is presented on the device, such as BOTTOM_BANNER, TOP_BANNER, MIDDLE_BANNER, FULL_SCREEN, or CAROUSEL.
Configures the SMS message for the campaign, including its body content, sender ID, and other SMS-specific delivery settings.
The text content of the SMS message delivered to recipients by this campaign.
Specifies the registered entity ID (or sender entity ID) required by telecom regulators in certain countries, such as India, for sending SMS messages within a Pinpoint campaign.
Sets the SMS message type to either TRANSACTIONAL or PROMOTIONAL, which determines how Pinpoint handles delivery priority and rate limits for the campaign's SMS messages.
The dedicated long code or short code phone number that the SMS message is sent from, which must be provisioned for your Amazon Pinpoint account.
The custom sender ID displayed on the receiving device for SMS messages sent by the campaign, used to identify the sender instead of a phone number.
The unique identifier of the Amazon Pinpoint message template that supplies the SMS message content for the campaign, replacing static body text.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.name.text: The name of the Amazon Pinpoint campaign, a required user-defined label that identifies the campaign in the console and API.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.priority.text: Sets the priority of the campaign, which determines the order or precedence of message delivery when multiple campaigns target the same segment and are subject to frequency capping.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.schedule.text: Determines the campaign's run timing, including the start and end times, frequency (e.g., ONCE, HOURLY, DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY), and an optional quiet-time window during which messages are not sent.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.schedule.end_time.text: The ISO 8601 timestamp at which the campaign schedule ends and the campaign stops sending messages.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.schedule.event_fil.text: Defines the event-based trigger criteria for the campaign, specifying the event dimensions and filter type that determine when the campaign is sent.
Specifies the event dimensions (including event type and attribute/metric filters) used to match events that trigger the campaign when the schedule's event filter is applied.
Specifies a map of event attribute names to filter criteria that an event must match for the campaign's schedule event filter to trigger the campaign.

Specifies the event types (for example, _session.start or a custom app event) that must match the endpoint-reported event for the campaign's scheduled event filter trigger, using a SetDimension with values and an inclusive or exclusive dimension type.
Specifies whether the event types listed in the event_type dimension should be included (INCLUSIVE) or excluded (EXCLUSIVE) from the campaign's event-based schedule filter.
Specifies the list of event type names (for example, '_session.start' or '_custom.events') that the event filter matches to determine when the campaign is sent based on the campaign schedule.
Specifies the metric name-value pairs that the triggering event must match for the campaign schedule, e.g., session count or other custom event metrics.
In the campaign schedule's event filter, specifies whether the filter type is `EVENT` (custom application event) or `SYSTEM` (system event), which controls which events trigger the campaign.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.schedule.frequency.text: Specifies how often the campaign is delivered (e.g., ONCE, HOURLY, DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY) as part of the schedule controlling when the campaign runs.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.schedule.is_local_.text: Indicates whether the campaign schedule uses the recipient's local time zone for message delivery instead of the campaign's configured time zone.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.schedule.quiet_tim.text: Defines the quiet time window (start and end times in HH:MM format) during which the campaign cannot send messages.
End time (in HH:mm format) of the daily quiet time window during which the campaign will not send messages.
The start time (in 24-hour HH:MM format) of the quiet time window during which the campaign does not deliver messages to recipients.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.schedule.start_tim.text: The ISO 8601 date and time when the campaign is scheduled to start sending messages.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.schedule.time_zone.text: Specifies the ISO 8601 time zone offset (e.g., 'UTC+05:00') used for interpreting the campaign schedule's start and end times.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.segment_id.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Pinpoint segment that the campaign targets for sending messages.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.segment_version.text: The version of the segment to use for the campaign, allowing you to target a specific revision of the segment.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.tags.text: Specifies a map of key-value tags to attach to the Amazon Pinpoint campaign, enabling resource organization, cost tracking, and IAM-based access control.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.template_configura.text: Defines the message template configuration for the campaign, specifying the name and version of templates to use for each supported channel (email, push, SMS, voice).
Provides the name and version of the email template that the campaign uses to send email messages.
The name of the email template to use for the campaign's email messages.
Specifies the version of the email template to use for the campaign's email messages, matching an existing version of the referenced email template.
Specifies the push notification message template to use for the campaign, enabling the campaign to reference a previously defined Amazon Pinpoint push template by name or ARN.
The name of the Amazon Pinpoint push notification template to use for the campaign's push messages.
Specifies the version of the push notification message template to use for the campaign; if not provided, Amazon Pinpoint uses the default (active) version of the template.
Specifies the SMS message template used for the campaign's SMS messages, including the template name and optional version.
The name of the Amazon Pinpoint SMS template that the campaign references for its SMS message content.
Specifies the version of the SMS message template to use for the campaign; if omitted, Amazon Pinpoint uses the default version of the template.
Specifies the voice message template (by name and version) used by the campaign for sending voice messages via the voice channel.
The name of the Amazon Pinpoint voice message template that this campaign uses to send voice messages.
Specifies the version of the voice message template to use for the campaign; if not provided, the default version of the template is used.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.treatment_descript.text: Specifies a user-defined description of a treatment (variant) for a multivariate or A/B test campaign in Amazon Pinpoint.

aws_pinpoint_campaign.treatment_name.text: The name assigned to a message treatment (variant) in an A/B test for the Amazon Pinpoint campaign, used to identify and manage that treatment.

aws_pinpoint_email_channel.application_i.text: The unique identifier for the Amazon Pinpoint application (project) that the email channel is associated with.

aws_pinpoint_email_channel.configuration.text: The name of the Amazon SES configuration set that is applied to emails sent through this Amazon Pinpoint email channel.

aws_pinpoint_email_channel.enabled.text: Specifies whether the email channel is enabled for the Amazon Pinpoint application.

aws_pinpoint_email_channel.from_address.text: The verified email address that Amazon Pinpoint uses as the sender for emails sent through this channel.

aws_pinpoint_email_channel.id.text: The `id` field stores the ApplicationId of the Amazon Pinpoint application associated with this email channel, as returned by the Pinpoint API.

aws_pinpoint_email_channel.identity.text: Specifies the Amazon SES identity (a verified email address or domain) that Amazon Pinpoint uses to send email through this channel.

aws_pinpoint_email_channel.orchestration.text: The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon Pinpoint assumes to submit email through Amazon SES on behalf of your account for orchestrated sends, such as messages sent via journeys or campaigns on this email channel.

aws_pinpoint_email_channel.role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon Pinpoint assumes to send email through Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) on behalf of the application's email channel.

aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set.del.text: Configures delivery options for emails sent from this configuration set, including the dedicated IP pool (SendingPoolName) and the TLS policy (TlsPolicy).
The name of the dedicated IP pool that Amazon Pinpoint uses to send email for this configuration set.

aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set.id.text: The unique identifier of the configuration set, which corresponds to the configuration set name in Amazon Pinpoint Email.

aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set.nam.text: The unique name of the Amazon Pinpoint email configuration set, used as its identifier when you send email or attach event destinations to it.

aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set.rep.text: Configures reputation metrics tracking for this configuration set, determining whether Amazon Pinpoint publishes email reputation data such as bounce and complaint rates to Amazon CloudWatch.
Enables or disables the publishing of reputation metrics (such as bounce and complaint rates) for email messages sent using this Pinpoint email configuration set.

aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set.sen.text: Defines the email sending options for the configuration set, specifically whether email sending is enabled via the SendingEnabled sub-property.
Enables or disables email sending for the configuration set when set to true or false, respectively.

aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set.tag.text: A list of key-value pairs (Tag objects) to attach to the Amazon Pinpoint email configuration set for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource, including for cost allocation reporting.
The key of a tag attached to the Amazon Pinpoint email configuration set, used to identify and categorize the configuration set for management, cost tracking, and resource organization purposes.
The value of an individual tag key on the Amazon Pinpoint email configuration set, used to store metadata for resource identification, organization, and cost allocation.

aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set.tra.text: Specifies the custom redirect domain used for open and click tracking in emails sent using this Pinpoint email configuration set.
Defines the custom domain that Amazon Pinpoint uses to rewrite links in emails for tracking opens and clicks, overriding the default tracking domain.

aws_pinpoint_email_configuration_set_eve.text: The name of the Amazon Pinpoint configuration set that this event destination is associated with.

Defines the event destination for the email configuration set, specifying where Amazon Pinpoint publishes email event data (such as deliveries, bounces, and complaints) based on matching event types and the chosen destination type (e.g., CloudWatch Logs, Kinesis Data Firehose, or SNS).
Configures the CloudWatch Logs destination for the event destination, including dimension configurations that define how email event metrics are grouped and published to CloudWatch.

Specifies the list of dimension configurations that define how Pinpoint adds custom dimensions (with a dimension name, value source, and default value) to the CloudWatch metrics when event destinations publish events to CloudWatch.
The default value to use for the CloudWatch metric dimension when the source event does not provide a value for the dimension configuration, so the metric always has a dimension value.
The name of the CloudWatch dimension to attach to the event destination's metrics for this dimension configuration.
Specifies the source of the dimension value (e.g., MESSAGE_TYPE or EVENT_TYPE) that determines which email event metadata is used to populate the CloudWatch metric dimension.

Determines whether the event destination is active, controlling whether Amazon Pinpoint delivers event data (such as sends, bounces, or complaints) to the associated destination like an SNS topic, CloudWatch Logs, or Kinesis Firehose.
Configures the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream settings that Amazon Pinpoint uses to send event data when this event destination is triggered.
The ARN of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that Amazon Pinpoint publishes event data to for this event destination.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon Pinpoint assumes to send event data to the specified Kinesis Firehose delivery stream.
Specifies the email event types (such as OPEN, CLICK, BOUNCE, COMPLAINT, DELIVERY, REJECT, or RENDER_FAILURE) that trigger this event destination to process events.
Specifies the Amazon Pinpoint application ID (ApplicationId) that will receive event notifications from this configuration set.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Pinpoint application (project) to which the email configuration set's event destination sends event data.
Specifies the Amazon SNS topic (via its TopicArn) that receives email event notifications from this event destination.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic where the event destination publishes email event notifications for the Amazon Pinpoint configuration set.
The name of the event destination, which uniquely identifies it within the Amazon Pinpoint email configuration set.

aws_pinpoint_email_dedicated_ip_pool.id.text: The unique identifier assigned to the dedicated IP pool, which is the same as the pool name.

aws_pinpoint_email_dedicated_ip_pool.poo.text: The name of the dedicated IP pool in Amazon Pinpoint, which serves as the unique identifier when referencing the pool in sending configurations.

aws_pinpoint_email_dedicated_ip_pool.tag.text: A key in a key-value tag assigned to the Amazon Pinpoint email dedicated IP pool, used to label the pool for cost allocation and resource management.
The value portion of a key-value tag applied to the Amazon Pinpoint dedicated IP pool, used for labeling, organization, and cost allocation.

aws_pinpoint_email_identity.dkim_signing.text: Specifies whether DKIM signing is enabled for the email identity, allowing emails sent from the identity to be signed with the associated DKIM key.

aws_pinpoint_email_identity.feedback_for.text: Enables or disables feedback forwarding for the email identity, causing Amazon Pinpoint to send bounce and complaint notifications to the Return-Path address when enabled.

aws_pinpoint_email_identity.id.text: The email address or domain name that serves as the unique identifier for this Pinpoint email identity.

aws_pinpoint_email_identity.identity_dns.text: The first DNS record name that must be added to your domain's DNS settings to verify ownership of the Amazon Pinpoint email identity.
The name of the second DNS record (typically a DKIM record) required for email identity verification in Amazon Pinpoint.
The third DNS record name returned for the email identity, which must be added to your domain's DNS configuration to verify domain ownership.
This read-only attribute provides the value of the first DNS TXT record that Amazon Pinpoint requires you to add to your domain's DNS settings to verify the email identity for sending email.

The second of the three CNAME record values that Amazon Pinpoint provides for a domain-based email identity; you must publish this value in your DNS to verify domain ownership and enable DKIM email signing.
The value of the third DNS record (TXT record) that must be created in the domain's DNS settings to verify ownership of the email identity in Amazon Pinpoint.

aws_pinpoint_email_identity.mail_from_at.text: Specifies the custom MAIL FROM domain and the behavior (use the default value or reject the message) to take when the MAIL FROM domain is not available for this Pinpoint email identity.
Determines whether Pinpoint uses the default MAIL FROM domain or rejects the message when the custom MAIL FROM domain's MX record is missing or misconfigured (USE_DEFAULT_VALUE or REJECT_MESSAGE).
The custom MAIL FROM domain that Amazon Pinpoint uses as the envelope MAIL FROM address for emails sent from this email identity.

aws_pinpoint_email_identity.name.text: The email address or domain name that serves as the Amazon Pinpoint email identity for sending email.

aws_pinpoint_email_identity.tags.text: Assigns a list of key-value tags to the Amazon Pinpoint email identity to help organize, identify, and manage the resource (e.g., for cost allocation and access control).

aws_pinpoint_email_identity.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a tag attached to the Amazon Pinpoint email identity, used to categorize, manage, and track the resource according to your tagging conventions.

aws_pinpoint_email_identity.tags.value.text: Specifies the value of a tag key-value pair to be associated with the Amazon Pinpoint email identity.

aws_pinpoint_email_template.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS Pinpoint email template.

aws_pinpoint_email_template.default_subs.text: Defines a JSON object of key-value pairs that specify default values for message variables in the email template, used as fallback substitutions when a send request does not provide them.

aws_pinpoint_email_template.html_part.text: The HTML body of the email template, used by Amazon Pinpoint to render the email content in rich text format for recipients.

aws_pinpoint_email_template.id.text: The unique name assigned to the email template in Amazon Pinpoint, which identifies it within the AWS account and region.

aws_pinpoint_email_template.subject.text: The subject line of the email message, which is required and appears on all emails sent using this template.

aws_pinpoint_email_template.tags.text: Assigns key-value pairs to the Amazon Pinpoint email template for organizing and identifying it, with each tag consisting of a key and a value.

aws_pinpoint_email_template.template_des.text: A user-defined description of the email template, used to document the template's purpose or content.

aws_pinpoint_email_template.template_nam.text: The name of the email template, used as the unique identifier for the template in Amazon Pinpoint.

aws_pinpoint_email_template.text_part.text: The plain-text body of the email message defined by this template.

aws_pinpoint_event_stream.application_id.text: The unique identifier (ID) of the Amazon Pinpoint application that the event stream is associated with.

aws_pinpoint_event_stream.destination_st.text: The ARN of the Amazon Kinesis Data Stream or Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream that receives the Pinpoint event stream data.

aws_pinpoint_event_stream.id.text: The application ID of the Amazon Pinpoint application that this event stream is associated with.

aws_pinpoint_event_stream.role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that authorizes Amazon Pinpoint to write event data to the configured Amazon Kinesis stream.

aws_pinpoint_gcmchannel.api_key.text: The Google API key used to authorize Amazon Pinpoint to send push notifications through Firebase Cloud Messaging (GCM) to Android apps.

aws_pinpoint_gcmchannel.application_id.text: The unique identifier for the Amazon Pinpoint application that the GCM channel is associated with.

aws_pinpoint_gcmchannel.default_authenti.text: Specifies the default authentication method for the GCM channel, either 'TOKEN' or 'KEY', which determines how Amazon Pinpoint authenticates with Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) when sending push notifications to Android apps.

aws_pinpoint_gcmchannel.enabled.text: Enables or disables the Google Cloud Messaging (GCM) channel for the associated Amazon Pinpoint application, controlling whether push notifications can be sent to Android devices.

aws_pinpoint_gcmchannel.id.text: The identifier of the GCM channel, equal to the associated Pinpoint application ID.

aws_pinpoint_gcmchannel.service_json.text: A JSON string containing the Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) service account credentials (service account key) that Amazon Pinpoint uses to send push notifications through the GCM channel; when specified, it is used instead of the deprecated API key.

aws_pinpoint_in_app_template.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the in-app message template.

aws_pinpoint_in_app_template.content.text: The list of content objects for the in-app template, each defining the message's header, body, background color, media URL, and optional action buttons.

aws_pinpoint_in_app_template.content.bac.text: The hexadecimal color code (e.g., #FFFFFF) used as the background color of the in-app message.

aws_pinpoint_in_app_template.content.bod.text: The `content.body_config` field configures the in-app message body's text, text color, and alignment (e.g., left, center, or right) for the AWS Pinpoint in-app template.
Specifies the horizontal alignment of the body text in the in-app message (e.g., LEFT, RIGHT, or CENTER).
Specifies the text to display as the body of the in-app message, shown within the message overlay in the mobile app.
Sets the hex color code (for example, #000000) used for the body text in the in-app message content's body configuration.

aws_pinpoint_in_app_template.content.hea.text: Configures the header of an in-app message by specifying the header text, text color, and alignment (left, center, or right).
Specifies the horizontal alignment (LEFT, CENTER, or RIGHT) of the header text in an in-app message template.
The text displayed in the header section of the in-app message.
The hex color code applied to the header text in the in-app message template.

aws_pinpoint_in_app_template.content.ima.text: Defines the URL of the image displayed in the in-app message content of the Amazon Pinpoint in-app template.

aws_pinpoint_in_app_template.content.pri.text: Defines the primary action button for the in-app message content, including its text, link, and platform-specific styles (iOS, Android, web) that dictate the main user interaction.

This object defines the Android-specific override for the primary button in an in-app message, specifying the button action (such as closing the message, opening a deep link, or navigating to a URL) and the link to use for that action, which takes precedence over the default button settings.
Determines what happens when a user taps the primary button on Android, either opening a web URL (LINK), opening an app deep link (DEEP_LINK), or closing the in-app message (CLOSE).
The URL or deep link that the Android client opens when the user taps the primary button in the in-app message.

Specifies the default configuration for the primary button in the in-app message, including its background color, border radius, text, text color, and the action taken when the button is tapped (e.g., opening a link or closing the message).
Specifies the background color of the primary button in the in-app message, provided as a hex color code (e.g., #FF0000).
Sets the pixel value for the corner rounding (border radius) of the primary button in the default state of an in-app message template for Amazon Pinpoint.
Specifies the action performed when a user taps the default primary button in the in-app message, such as opening a link (LINK), a deep link (DEEP_LINK), or closing the message (CLOSE).
The URL or deep link that the user is taken to when they tap the primary button in the in-app message.
The button label text shown on the primary button in the in-app message's default configuration.
Specifies the hexadecimal color code for the text displayed on the primary button in the default configuration of the in-app message template.

The iOS-specific configuration for the primary button in the in-app template's content, customizing the button's appearance (e.g., text color, background color, border radius) and action on iOS devices, overriding the default configuration.

Specifies the action taken when the primary button is tapped on iOS devices in the in-app message, with valid values such as LINK (opens the URL specified in the link property), DEEP_LINK (opens a deep link), or CLOSE (dismisses the message).
The URL or deep link that the primary button opens when tapped on iOS devices, overriding the button's default link for iOS.
Configures how the primary in-app message button behaves on web clients, including the button action (e.g., opening a link, deep link, or closing the message) and the destination URL.
The action to perform when the primary button is clicked in the web (browser) context of the in-app message, such as LINK, DEEP_LINK, or CLOSE.
The URL that the primary button opens when clicked in the web version of the in-app message.

aws_pinpoint_in_app_template.content.sec.text: Configures the optional secondary button of the in-app message, including its enabled state and the action (such as opening a URL or closing the message) that occurs when a user taps it.
The `android` object defines platform-specific override settings for the secondary button, applied when the in-app message is rendered on Android devices.
Sets the action performed when the secondary button is tapped on Android, such as opening a URL (LINK), a deep link (DEEP_LINK), or dismissing the in-app message (DISMISS).
The URL or deep link that the secondary button opens on Android devices when tapped by the user.

The default configuration for the secondary button in the in-app template message, specifying its background color, border radius, action type (e.g., CLOSE or DEEP_LINK), link URL, text, and text color.
Sets the background color (as a hexadecimal color code) of the secondary button in its default state within the in-app message content.
Specifies the border radius (in pixels) for the secondary button in the default configuration of the in-app message content.
Determines what happens when a user taps the secondary button in the in-app message, such as navigating to a URL or deep link, or closing the message.
The URL or deep link that the secondary button opens when tapped, as defined in the button's default configuration.
The text displayed on the secondary button of the in-app message when using the default button configuration.
Sets the text color (as a hex color code) for the default configuration of the secondary button in an Amazon Pinpoint in-app message template.
The iOS-specific override settings for the secondary button in the in-app message, including its appearance and click behavior on iOS devices.
Specifies the action performed when a user taps the secondary button in an iOS in-app message, such as opening a link (LINK), opening a deep link (DEEP_LINK), or closing the message (CLOSE).
The URL that the secondary iOS button opens when tapped, as part of the in-app message content for AWS Pinpoint.
Specifies the Web-platform-specific settings for the secondary button in the in-app message template, including its button action (e.g., close or deep link) and destination link URL.
Specifies the action performed when the user clicks the secondary web button, which can be LINK, DEEP_LINK, or DISMISS.
The URL that the secondary button opens when a user taps it in the web version of the in-app message.

aws_pinpoint_in_app_template.custom_conf.text: Specifies custom key-value pairs (as a map of strings) that are attached to the in-app template, enabling personalized or supplementary data to be used with the message.

aws_pinpoint_in_app_template.layout.text: Sets the layout style for the in-app message, determining how and where the message content is displayed (e.g., top banner, bottom banner, or centered).

aws_pinpoint_in_app_template.tags.text: A map of key-value pairs that can be assigned to the in-app template to help organize, identify, and manage the resource.

aws_pinpoint_in_app_template.template_de.text: Specifies a user-friendly description for the in-app message template, which is displayed in the Amazon Pinpoint console.

aws_pinpoint_in_app_template.template_na.text: The name of the in-app message template, which must be unique within the Amazon Pinpoint project and is used to identify and reference the template in API operations and the console.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.adm.text: Defines the Amazon Device Messenger (ADM) push notification settings, such as the action, title, body, and URL, used for delivering messages to Fire OS devices.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.adm.action.text: Specifies the action that occurs when a user taps the push notification delivered via ADM, with valid values OPEN_APP, DEEP_LINK, or URL.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.adm.body.text: The message body text that is sent to Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) endpoints as the push notification content.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.adm.image_ico.text: For Amazon Device Messenger (ADM) push notifications, this is the URL of the icon image to display in the notification.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.adm.image_url.text: The URL of the image to display in the push notification sent to ADM (Amazon Device Messenger) endpoints.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.adm.small_ima.text: The URL of the small icon image to display in the status bar or as a small icon in notifications sent through Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) from this push template.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.adm.sound.text: For Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) push notifications, this field specifies the name of the sound file to play when the message is received.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.adm.title.text: This field specifies the title of the push notification that Amazon Pinpoint sends to Amazon Device Messaging (ADM) endpoints using this template.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.adm.url.text: Specifies the URL to open when a user taps the push notification delivered through Amazon Device Messaging (ADM).

aws_pinpoint_push_template.apns.text: The Apple Push Notification Service (APNs) settings for this push template, defining the notification content and behavior for iOS devices.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.apns.action.text: The action to take when a user taps the notification sent via APNs; valid values are OPEN_APP, DEEP_LINK, or URL.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.apns.body.text: Specifies the message body (the text content) of the push notification sent to Apple devices through the APNs channel.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.apns.media_ur.text: The URL of the image, video, or other media file to include in the push notification delivered to Apple Push Notification Service (APNS) endpoints.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.apns.sound.text: The name of the sound file to play when an APNs push notification is received, such as 'default' or a custom sound file.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.apns.title.text: The title of the push notification message sent to Apple Push Notification Service (APNS) endpoints.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.apns.url.text: The URL to be opened when an iOS user taps the APNS push notification, applicable when the message action is set to URL.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the push notification template in AWS Pinpoint.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.baidu.text: Specifies the push notification settings for the Baidu channel, including message body, title, action, and other platform-specific options for Android devices in China.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.baidu.action.text: Specifies the action to take when a user taps a push notification sent via the Baidu channel, with supported values including `OPEN_APP`, `DEEP_LINK`, and `URL`.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.baidu.body.text: The message body of the push notification delivered through the Baidu channel (Baidu Cloud Push) for Android devices in China, used in the push template.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.baidu.image_i.text: Specifies the URL of a large image icon to display for Baidu push notifications when using this template.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.baidu.image_u.text: The image_url field specifies the URL of the image to display in the Baidu push notification.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.baidu.small_i.text: The URL of the small icon image that appears in notifications delivered through the Baidu channel for this push template.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.baidu.sound.text: The sound to play on the device when the Baidu push notification is delivered.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.baidu.title.text: The title text for the Baidu push notification message, which appears as the message's headline or subject.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.baidu.url.text: The URL that the Baidu push notification opens in the app when tapped, used when the notification Action is set to open a URL rather than the app or a deep link.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.default.text: The default message data that applies to all message types and platforms, including the message title, body, and other push notification settings.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.default.actio.text: Specifies the action to occur if a recipient taps the push notification, such as opening the app, opening a deep link, or opening a URL.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.default.body.text: Sets the body text of the push notification message, which is the main content displayed to the user when the notification is delivered.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.default.sound.text: Specifies the sound file name or audio resource to play when the app receives the push notification, interpreted according to the mobile platform (for example, an iOS sound filename or an Android notification sound resource).

aws_pinpoint_push_template.default.title.text: The default title of the push notification, used when no platform-specific override is provided.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.default.url.text: In the default push notification template for an AWS Pinpoint push template, this URL specifies the web address that is opened when the user taps the notification, typically used when the notification's action is set to 'URL'.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.default_subst.text: A JSON string defining the default key-value pairs that map message template variables to their default substitution values for the push notification template.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.gcm.text: Specifies the push notification template settings for Android devices via the Google Cloud Messaging (GCM) channel, including message content, action, and Android-specific delivery options.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.gcm.action.text: Determines the action that occurs when a user taps a push notification sent via GCM (Android), with possible values OPEN_APP, DEEP_LINK, and URL.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.gcm.body.text: The message body of the push notification delivered to GCM (Google/Firebase Cloud Messaging) recipients.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.gcm.image_ico.text: The URL of the image icon to display in the push notification for the GCM (Google) channel.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.gcm.image_url.text: The URL of the image to display in the push notification for the GCM (Firebase Cloud Messaging) channel of the PushTemplate.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.gcm.small_ima.text: The URL of the small icon image displayed for Google Cloud Messaging (GCM) push notifications in the AWS Pinpoint push template.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.gcm.sound.text: Specifies the sound to play when the push notification is received on an Android device, either as 'default' or the file name of a sound resource bundled with the app.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.gcm.title.text: The title of the push notification sent to GCM (Google Cloud Messaging / Firebase Cloud Messaging) recipients for this Pinpoint push template.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.gcm.url.text: The URL to open when a recipient taps the push notification delivered to Android devices through the GCM/FCM channel.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.id.text: The id is the name of the push template, which uniquely identifies it within the AWS account.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.tags.text: Assigns metadata to the Amazon Pinpoint push notification template in the form of key-value pairs that can be used to categorize and manage the template.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.template_desc.text: A description of the push notification template, used to identify the template in the Amazon Pinpoint console.

aws_pinpoint_push_template.template_name.text: The name of the push notification template, which uniquely identifies it within your AWS account and must be unique among all templates in your Amazon Pinpoint project.

aws_pinpoint_segment.application_id.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Pinpoint application (project) that the segment belongs to.

aws_pinpoint_segment.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Amazon Pinpoint segment.

aws_pinpoint_segment.dimensions.text: Defines the criteria (such as demographic, behavioral, location, and metrics filters) that determine which endpoints are included in the segment.

aws_pinpoint_segment.dimensions.attribut.text: Specifies attribute-based criteria for the segment, where each key is a custom endpoint attribute name and the value defines the dimension filter (such as inclusion or exclusion type and matching values) used to include or exclude endpoints.

aws_pinpoint_segment.dimensions.behavior.text: Defines the behavior-based criteria for the segment, such as how recently or how often users have used your app, including metrics like session count and session duration, to target endpoints based on their engagement patterns.
Configures the recency dimension for a behavior-based segment, filtering users by how recently they were active (e.g., active or inactive within a specified number of days).
The number of days that defines the recency window (e.g., '30' for the last 30 days) used to include or exclude users in the segment based on their activity recency.
Specifies whether the segment is based on users who are active (ACTIVE) or inactive (INACTIVE) within the specified recency duration.

aws_pinpoint_segment.dimensions.demograp.text: Defines the demographic criteria for the segment, where each key is a demographic attribute (e.g., age, gender, platform) and each value contains inclusion/exclusion rules (AttributeDimension) to filter endpoint membership.
Specifies the set of app version(s) used to include or exclude devices in the segment based on the installed version of your mobile app, with a comparison operator and an array of version strings.
Determines whether the specified app version values are included in (INCLUSIVE) or excluded from (EXCLUSIVE) the segment's demographic filter.
Defines the set of app version strings (for example, '1.0.0') used by the app_version demographic dimension to match devices for the segment.

Defines the demographic dimension for the segment by specifying which contact channels (such as SMS, email, or push) to include or exclude, using a set dimension with a dimension type (inclusive or exclusive) and a list of channel values.
Specifies the dimension type for the channel attribute, either 'INCLUSIVE' to include users on the specified channel or 'EXCLUSIVE' to exclude them, determining how the channel filter is applied.
Specifies the list of app channels (such as GCM, APNS, SMS, or EMAIL) to match in the demographic segment dimension, restricting the segment to devices using those channels.
Defines the device-type demographic criteria used to include or exclude endpoints from a segment, specifying an attribute type (INCLUSIVE or EXCLUSIVE) and a list of device type values to match.
Determines whether the device types specified in the associated Value list are included (INCLUSIVE) or excluded (EXCLUSIVE) when defining this demographic dimension of the Amazon Pinpoint segment.
Specifies the list of device type values (e.g., 'iPhone', 'Android') that serve as matching criteria for this demographic segment dimension in the Pinpoint segment.
Configures the device make (manufacturer, e.g., Apple, Samsung) dimension for the segment, with a set of allowed values and a dimension type to include or exclude matching devices.
Specifies whether to include or exclude the specified device manufacturers from the segment demographic, with a value of 'INCLUSIVE' or 'EXCLUSIVE'.
Specifies the device makes (e.g., Apple, Samsung) to include in the demographic segment dimension.
Defines the demographic device-model filter for the segment, using a set dimension (with values and include/exclude type) to match or exclude devices by model name.
Determines whether the demographic model dimension includes (INCLUSIVE) or excludes (EXCLUSIVE) the specified device models when evaluating the segment.
Specifies the device model names (such as iPhone or Samsung Galaxy) that the demographic model dimension of the segment should match.
Configures the demographic platform filter for a Pinpoint segment, specifying the device platforms (such as iOS, Android, etc.) that endpoints must match to be included in the segment.
Specifies whether the platform dimension is inclusive (matching the specified platforms) or exclusive (excluding the specified platforms).
Specifies the device platforms (such as iOS or Android) that an endpoint must match when the demographic platform dimension is applied to the segment.

aws_pinpoint_segment.dimensions.location.text: Specifies location-based criteria for the segment, such as the country code or GPS coordinates that endpoints must match to be included in the segment.
Defines the country criteria for the location segment dimension, using a set of country codes with an include/exclude filter type to target or exclude devices in those countries.
Specifies whether the country values in this location dimension are included (INCLUSIVE) or excluded (EXCLUSIVE) when matching users for the segment.
Specifies the list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to match endpoints against for the location country dimension of the segment.
Defines a circular geographic area for matching endpoints, using a latitude and longitude coordinate as the center and a radius measured in kilometers.
The coordinates object within the GPS point specifies the latitude and longitude values used to define the location-based segment dimension for AWS Pinpoint.
The latitude of the GPS coordinate that defines the center of a circular location-based segment.
The east-west geographic coordinate (in decimal degrees) of the GPS point used to define the location-based segment's dimension criteria.
The radius in kilometers around the GPS point's latitude and longitude that defines the circular geographic area used to match devices for the segment.

aws_pinpoint_segment.dimensions.metrics.text: Specifies a map of metric names to metric dimension criteria, where each criterion defines a comparison operator and threshold value that endpoint metric values must satisfy to be included in the segment.

aws_pinpoint_segment.dimensions.user_att.text: Specifies filters for including or excluding endpoints based on custom user attribute values, where each key is a user attribute name and its value defines the matching criteria.

aws_pinpoint_segment.name.text: The name of the segment, which is used as a friendly identifier in the Amazon Pinpoint console and API operations.

aws_pinpoint_segment.segment_groups.text: Defines the segment groups, including their dimensions and source segments, that specify the criteria for which endpoints are included in the Amazon Pinpoint segment.

aws_pinpoint_segment.segment_groups.grou.text: A list of group definitions that make up the segment group, where each group specifies the dimensions or source segments used to define the segment's targeting criteria.
Defines the endpoint criteria (attributes, metrics, and user attributes) used to determine which endpoints belong to this segment group.

Defines attribute-based criteria for the segment, mapping each endpoint attribute name to a set of values and match type (e.g., INCLUDED or EXCLUDED) that determine whether an endpoint belongs to the segment.

Defines the behavior-based criteria for segmenting users, including rules for how frequently users launch the app and how recently they were active, used to target audiences based on engagement patterns.
Defines the recency criteria for behavior-based segment dimensions, specifying whether users are targeted based on their activity status (active or inactive) within a specified number of days.
The number of days that defines the recency window for user activity, used to segment users based on when they last performed an activity in Amazon Pinpoint.
Specifies whether the recency dimension targets users who were active ('ACTIVE') or inactive ('INACTIVE') within the time period defined by the associated recency_duration value.
Specifies demographic-based criteria (such as app version, device make, model, and platform) used to filter endpoints into the Pinpoint segment.
Defines the app version matching criteria for the demographic segment, using a set dimension object that specifies whether the listed app versions are included or excluded from the segment.
Specifies whether the app version dimension includes or excludes users based on the listed app version values, using INCLUSIVE or EXCLUSIVE.
The values for the app_version demographic dimension, which are the specific app version strings used to target users based on the version of your app they have installed.
Specifies the demographic dimension for the communication channel (such as EMAIL, SMS, or PUSH) used to reach an endpoint, matching segment members based on that channel attribute.

Controls whether the segment's demographic channel dimension includes or excludes endpoints whose channel attribute (e.g., GCM, APNS) matches the specified values, using a DimensionType of INCLUSIVE or EXCLUSIVE.
In a Pinpoint segment, this list specifies the engagement channel names (e.g., EMAIL, PUSH, SMS) used as criteria to filter endpoints according to the demographic channel dimension.
Specifies the device type dimension used to filter segment members by their device type (such as phone or tablet), with an inclusion/exclusion type and a list of device type values.
Sets the dimension type for the device type demographic filter, either INCLUSIVE to include matching devices or EXCLUSIVE to exclude them.
Specifies the list of device type strings (e.g., 'iPhone', 'Android') that define the device-type demographic dimension for matching endpoints in this segment group's dimension.
Filters a segment's demographic dimensions to target users with a specific device manufacturer, such as Apple or Samsung.
Specifies whether the device make demographic dimension is inclusive (targets the specified makes) or exclusive (excludes the specified makes), with valid values INCLUSIVE or EXCLUSIVE.
Specifies the device manufacturers (makes) to include or exclude in the segment's demographic dimension, such as 'Apple' or 'Samsung', depending on the group's dimension type.
Specifies the device model (such as 'iPhone' or 'Samsung Galaxy S4') that a user's mobile device must match for the user to be included in the segment.
Specifies whether the device model values for this demographic dimension are included in the segment (INCLUSIVE) or excluded from it (EXCLUSIVE).
The list of device model names (such as iPhone 12 or Galaxy S21) that the demographic model dimension matches against when defining an Amazon Pinpoint segment.
Defines the device platform (e.g., iOS, Android) that an endpoint must match for the demographic segment group, including a list of platform values and the include/exclude match type.

Specifies whether endpoints matching the specified platforms (e.g., iOS or Android) are included in or excluded from the segment when using this demographic platform dimension, with allowed values of INCLUSIVE or EXCLUSIVE.
Defines the list of device platform names (such as iOS, Android, or web) that a user endpoint's platform must match to be included in the segment's demographic dimension filter.
Specifies location-based criteria such as country, region, or postal code used to filter endpoints for the segment.
Defines the country used by the location-based criteria within a segment group's dimensions, allowing the segment to target users whose devices are located in the specified country.
Determines whether the country-based filter includes (INCLUSIVE) or excludes (EXCLUSIVE) the countries listed in the `values` field of the same `country` dimension.
The list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to filter segment members by country in the location-based segment dimension.
Defines a GPS coordinate (latitude and longitude) along with a radius in kilometers to include endpoints in the segment based on their proximity to that location.
Specifies the latitude and longitude (as an object) that define the GPS point used for location-based targeting within a Pinpoint segment dimension.
The latitude of the GPS coordinate used to define a location-based segment dimension in Amazon Pinpoint.
The east-west coordinate (in decimal degrees) of a GPS point that defines the center of a geographic area used to match endpoints in a location-based segment dimension.
The radius in kilometers around the GPS coordinates that defines the circular geographic area used to match endpoints for the segment.

Specifies metric-based criteria for the segment dimension, mapping metric names to metric dimensions that define a comparison operator and threshold value for including or excluding endpoints in the segment.

Specifies custom user attribute dimensions for the segment, where each key is a user attribute name and its value defines the matching conditions (attribute type and acceptable values) used to include or exclude endpoints.
Specifies the source segments used by this segment group to define its audience, where each entry references an existing segment by its ID and version.
The ID of an existing Amazon Pinpoint segment used as a source to build this dynamic segment group.
Specifies the version number of the source segment that this segment imports for building the segment group.
Determines whether endpoints must match all (ALL_TARGETING) or any (ANY_TARGETING) of the criteria defined in the segment group's dimensions or source segments.
Specifies whether a segment group must match all of its dimensions (ALL) or any one of its dimensions (ANY) to be included in the segment.

aws_pinpoint_segment.segment_groups.incl.text: Controls how the segment groups are evaluated to include or exclude endpoints, with typical values like ALL, ANY, or NONE for combining multiple groups.

aws_pinpoint_segment.segment_id.text: The unique identifier assigned to the segment in Amazon Pinpoint.

aws_pinpoint_segment.tags.text: Assigns key-value tags to the Amazon Pinpoint segment, which can be used to categorize, organize, and manage the segment.

aws_pinpoint_sms_template.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the SMS template in Amazon Pinpoint.

aws_pinpoint_sms_template.body.text: The actual text content of the SMS message that Amazon Pinpoint sends to recipients when this template is used in a campaign or journey.

aws_pinpoint_sms_template.default_substi.text: Specifies the default substitution variables for the SMS template, provided as a JSON object (string) of key-value pairs that Pinpoint uses to replace message variables when no custom values are supplied.

aws_pinpoint_sms_template.id.text: The template name, which serves as the unique identifier for the AWS Pinpoint SMS template.

aws_pinpoint_sms_template.tags.text: A map of key-value pairs to assign as metadata tags to the SMS template, which can be used to categorize the template for cost allocation and management.

aws_pinpoint_sms_template.template_descr.text: A description of the SMS template, used to provide additional context or details about the template's purpose or content.

aws_pinpoint_sms_template.template_name.text: The name of the SMS message template, which must be unique within your AWS account and is used to identify the template in the Pinpoint API.

aws_pinpoint_smschannel.application_id.text: The unique identifier for the Amazon Pinpoint application (project) that the SMS channel is associated with.

aws_pinpoint_smschannel.enabled.text: Specifies whether the SMS channel is enabled for sending text messages through the Amazon Pinpoint application.

aws_pinpoint_smschannel.id.text: The `id` is the unique identifier for this SMS channel, set to the Amazon Pinpoint application ID.

aws_pinpoint_smschannel.sender_id.text: A custom alphanumeric sender ID that appears on recipients' devices when they receive SMS messages sent from this Pinpoint SMS channel.

aws_pinpoint_smschannel.short_code.text: The registered short code to use for sending SMS messages with the Amazon Pinpoint SMS channel.

aws_pinpoint_voice_channel.application_i.text: The unique identifier for the Amazon Pinpoint application that the voice channel is enabled for.

aws_pinpoint_voice_channel.enabled.text: Specifies whether the voice channel is enabled for sending voice messages through Amazon Pinpoint.

aws_pinpoint_voice_channel.id.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Pinpoint application that this voice channel belongs to (same value as the ApplicationId).

aws_pipes_pipe.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this pipe, assigned by AWS and used to reference the pipe in IAM policies and other AWS services.

aws_pipes_pipe.creation_time.text: The timestamp of when the pipe was created, represented as a string in ISO 8601 format.

aws_pipes_pipe.current_state.text: The current lifecycle state of the pipe, such as RUNNING or STOPPED, as reported by AWS after the pipe is created or updated.

aws_pipes_pipe.description.text: The description field is an optional user-defined text description for the AWS Pipes pipe, used to identify the pipe's purpose or distinguish it from other pipes.

aws_pipes_pipe.desired_state.text: Sets the pipe to either RUNNING or STOPPED after creation or update, controlling whether it actively processes events.

aws_pipes_pipe.enrichment.text: The ARN of the enrichment resource (such as an AWS Lambda function, AWS Step Functions state machine, or API destination) that EventBridge Pipes invokes to transform or enrich the event before sending it to the target.

aws_pipes_pipe.enrichment_parameters.text: Specifies the configuration for the pipe's enrichment stage, including the input template that controls how the source event is transformed before being passed to the enrichment target (e.g., a Lambda function, Step Functions state machine, or API destination).

aws_pipes_pipe.enrichment_parameters.htt.text: Specifies the HTTP request parameters (including headers, query strings, and path parameter values) for a pipe's enrichment step when the target is an API destination.
Specifies the HTTP headers to include in the enrichment request, mapping each header name to its value (which may be a static string or a dynamic expression).
Specifies the list of values to substitute for each path parameter placeholder in the enrichment HTTP endpoint's URL, in the order the placeholders appear.
Specifies the key-value pairs to be included as query string parameters in the HTTP request when the pipe invokes the enrichment endpoint defined by http_parameters.

aws_pipes_pipe.enrichment_parameters.inp.text: Specifies the input template, a JSON string with dynamic references, that determines the payload delivered to the enrichment target for each event.

aws_pipes_pipe.kms_key_identifier.text: Specifies the ARN, ID, or alias of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt data in the EventBridge Pipe.

aws_pipes_pipe.last_modified_time.text: The timestamp indicating when the pipe was last modified.

aws_pipes_pipe.log_configuration.text: Configures the destination (such as CloudWatch Logs, Amazon Data Firehose, or Amazon S3) and the log level for the pipe's execution activity, capturing invocation and error logs.

aws_pipes_pipe.log_configuration.cloudwa.text: Specifies the CloudWatch Logs log destination (including the log group ARN) for this pipe, used when log_configuration is configured to send execution logs to CloudWatch Logs.
The ARN of the CloudWatch Logs log group that receives the pipe's execution logs.

aws_pipes_pipe.log_configuration.firehos.text: Specifies the Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream (via its ARN) to which AWS Pipes delivers execution and diagnostic logs.
The ARN of the Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream to which the pipe's execution logs are delivered when Firehose is selected as the log destination.

aws_pipes_pipe.log_configuration.include.text: Controls which pipe execution data fields (such as the input payload, output payload, or metadata) are included in the log records written to the configured log destination for an AWS Pipes pipe.

aws_pipes_pipe.log_configuration.level.text: The log level for the pipe's logging configuration, such as OFF, ERROR, INFO, TRACE, or WARN, controlling the granularity of log entries emitted by the pipe.

aws_pipes_pipe.log_configuration.s3_log_.text: Configures the Amazon S3 bucket, and optionally a prefix, that acts as the destination for logs emitted by the pipe when S3 is selected as the log delivery mechanism.
The name of the S3 bucket where AWS Pipes delivers execution logs when the pipe's log configuration uses an S3 log destination.
The AWS account ID of the Amazon S3 bucket owner, used to validate ownership when the destination bucket is in a different account.
Controls whether the logs delivered to the S3 bucket are formatted as JSON or as plain text, based on the value of this output format field.
The object key prefix to prepend to log files delivered to the S3 bucket when logging is configured for the pipe.

aws_pipes_pipe.name.text: The name of the EventBridge pipe; if not provided, CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_pipes_pipe.role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that the pipe assumes to read from the source, invoke the enrichment, and deliver to the target.

aws_pipes_pipe.source.text: The ARN of the source resource (such as a Kinesis stream, DynamoDB stream, SQS queue, or EventBridge event bus) from which the pipe reads data.

aws_pipes_pipe.source_parameters.text: Defines source-specific configuration for the pipe's integration, including filtering criteria and service-specific settings (e.g., batch size or stream starting position) for sources like SQS, Kinesis, or DynamoDB.

aws_pipes_pipe.source_parameters.active_.text: Specifies the parameters for an Amazon MQ ActiveMQ broker used as the event source, including the queue name, batch size, and credentials for consuming messages.
The maximum number of records to include in each batch when reading from the ActiveMQ broker source.
Defines the authentication credentials required to connect to the ActiveMQ broker, supporting either basic authentication with a username and password or client certificate TLS authentication.
Specifies the ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the basic authentication credentials (username and password) used to connect to the ActiveMQ broker source.
Specifies the maximum number of seconds that EventBridge Pipes waits when gathering events from an ActiveMQ broker source before invoking the target with a batch.
Specifies the name of the ActiveMQ queue from which the pipe reads messages.

aws_pipes_pipe.source_parameters.dynamo_.text: Specifies the DynamoDB stream source parameters, including the stream's starting position and batch size, used when the pipe's source is a DynamoDB stream.
The maximum number of records to read from the DynamoDB stream in a single batch when using DynamoDB as a pipe source.
Specifies the ARN of an SQS queue or SNS topic where records that fail processing from the DynamoDB stream are sent, serving as a dead-letter target for the pipe source.
The ARN of the Amazon SQS queue or Amazon SNS topic that receives events when AWS Pipes fails to deliver them from the DynamoDB stream source.
Specifies the maximum number of seconds that AWS Pipes will wait to gather records from the DynamoDB stream before sending a batch to the target, allowing you to control the batching behavior.
Sets the maximum age in seconds that a record from the DynamoDB stream source can be retained before the pipe considers it expired and discards it from processing.
Specifies the maximum number of retry attempts AWS Pipes will make to deliver an event from a DynamoDB stream source to the pipe's target before giving up.

Determines how the pipe handles a partial batch failure from the DynamoDB stream, either by discarding the failed batch and continuing (SEND_AND_FORGET) or by sending the failed batch to a destination specified by its ARN.
Sets the maximum number of shards processed concurrently for a DynamoDB stream source, allowing you to scale the pipe's throughput by increasing parallel shard consumption.
Determines the point in the DynamoDB stream from which the pipe starts reading, with valid values including LATEST, TRIM_HORIZON, and AT_TIMESTAMP.

aws_pipes_pipe.source_parameters.filter_.text: Defines the event filter patterns (a list of JSON matching patterns) that select which source events are passed through the pipe for processing.
Specifies the list of event patterns used to filter which source events are processed by the pipe, where each filter defines a JSON pattern that an incoming event must match.
Defines the EventBridge event pattern (as a JSON string) that determines which incoming events from the source are matched and processed, based on the source's filter criteria.

aws_pipes_pipe.source_parameters.kinesis.text: Specifies the parameters for consuming records from an Amazon Kinesis data stream as the pipe source, such as the batch size, starting position, and retry/dead-letter settings.
The maximum number of records to read from the Kinesis stream in a single batch, which controls how many records are processed at once by the pipe.
Configuration for sending events that fail processing from the Kinesis stream to a specified Amazon SQS queue or Amazon SNS topic for dead-letter handling.
The ARN of the dead-letter queue (SQS) or topic (SNS) that receives events from the Kinesis stream that cannot be processed by the pipe.
Specifies the maximum number of seconds that EventBridge Pipes accumulates records from the Kinesis stream before sending the batch to the target, with a maximum allowed value of 300 seconds.
Specifies the maximum age in seconds that a record from the source Kinesis stream can be before it is considered expired and skipped, so that stale data is not delivered to the pipe.
Specifies the maximum number of retry attempts AWS Pipes will make for a batch of Kinesis stream records that fail to be delivered to the target, before invoking dead-letter queue or error handling.
The ARN of a Lambda function that AWS EventBridge Pipes invokes to handle records that fail processing from a Kinesis stream.
Specifies the number of batches to process concurrently from each shard of the Kinesis stream, allowing you to increase throughput by processing multiple batches in parallel per shard (values 1-10).
Specifies the position in the Kinesis stream from which to start reading records, with valid values including LATEST, TRIM_HORIZON, and AT_TIMESTAMP.
The timestamp (in milliseconds since Unix epoch) in the Kinesis stream from which to start reading records when the source's starting position is set to AT_TIMESTAMP.

aws_pipes_pipe.source_parameters.managed.text: Specifies the parameters that configure an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK) stream as the event source for the pipe, including the topic name, starting position, consumer group ID, and batch settings.
The maximum number of records to include in a single batch when reading from the managed Kafka topic used as the source of the pipe.
The consumer group ID that the pipe uses to consume messages from the Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK) topic.
Specifies the Secrets Manager secret ARN(s) used for client authentication (either TLS client certificate or SASL/SCRAM) when connecting to the Amazon MSK stream source.
The ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the client certificate and private key used for mutual TLS authentication to the MSK cluster.
Specifies the ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the SASL/SCRAM-512 credentials used to authenticate to the managed Kafka stream configured as the pipe source.
The maximum number of seconds that AWS Pipes will wait to collect records from the managed Kafka stream before sending a batch to the target, allowing for batching of incoming messages.
Specifies the starting position in the Kafka stream from which the pipe begins consuming records, with valid values being LATEST (default) or TRIM_HORIZON (earliest available).
The name of the Kafka topic in the Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK) cluster from which the pipe reads messages.
