aws_pipes_pipe.source_parameters.rabbit_.text: Specifies the parameters for using an Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ broker as the pipe's event source, including the queue name, virtual host, credentials, batch size, and batching window.
The maximum number of messages from the RabbitMQ broker that can be read in a single batch, before the batch is sent to the target.

This object holds the basic authentication parameters for connecting to the RabbitMQ broker, specifically the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a Secrets Manager secret that stores the broker username and password.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the basic authentication credentials (username and password) used to access the RabbitMQ broker.

The maximum amount of time in seconds that EventBridge Pipes waits to gather messages from a RabbitMQ broker into a batch before invoking the target, even if the configured batch size has not been reached.
Specifies the name of the RabbitMQ queue that the pipe consumes messages from when using an Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ broker as the source.
The name of the RabbitMQ virtual host from which the pipe reads messages.

aws_pipes_pipe.source_parameters.self_ma.text: Defines the parameters for using a self-managed Apache Kafka stream as the pipe's event source, including broker connection details, topic name, and authentication credentials.
Specifies additional Kafka bootstrap server addresses that the pipe may use to connect to the self-managed Kafka cluster, supplementing the primary bootstrap servers for broker discovery.
The maximum number of records to read from a self-managed Kafka topic and include in each batch sent to the pipe target.
Specifies the consumer group ID that the AWS Pipes pipe uses when consuming messages from the self-managed Apache Kafka topic, allowing you to manage offsets and consumer group coordination.
Specifies the authentication credentials (basic auth, client certificate TLS, or SASL/SCRAM) required to connect to the self-managed Apache Kafka cluster source.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that contains the username and password used for basic authentication to the self-managed Kafka cluster.
The ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the client certificate and private key for mutual TLS authentication with the self-managed Apache Kafka cluster.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the SASL SCRAM256 credentials used to authenticate against the self-managed Kafka cluster that is the source of the pipe.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the SASL/SCRAM-512 username and password used to authenticate to the self-managed Apache Kafka cluster.
The maximum number of seconds that EventBridge Pipes will wait to accumulate records from the self-managed Apache Kafka source before sending them in a single batch to the target.
Specifies whether the pipe starts reading messages from the beginning (TRIM_HORIZON) or from the latest offset (LATEST) in the self-managed Kafka topic.
The name of the Kafka topic from which the pipe consumes messages when using a self-managed Apache Kafka source.
The VPC configuration (subnets and security groups) that the pipe uses to connect to your self-managed Kafka brokers.

aws_pipes_pipe.source_parameters.sqs_que.text: This configures the polling behavior for an SQS queue used as the event source in AWS Pipes, allowing you to set properties such as the batch size and the maximum batching window in seconds.
The maximum number of messages that can be polled from the SQS queue in a single batch and then passed as a batch to the pipe's target.
Specifies the maximum amount of time (in seconds) that EventBridge Pipes accumulates records from the source SQS queue before sending a batch to the target.

aws_pipes_pipe.state_reason.text: The reason why the pipe is in its current state, such as an error message when the pipe is in a failed state.

aws_pipes_pipe.tags.text: Specifies the key-value metadata tags to attach to this EventBridge Pipes pipe for resource identification and management.

aws_pipes_pipe.target.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the target resource (for example, an SQS queue, Lambda function, or EventBridge event bus) to which the pipe delivers events.

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.text: Specifies the target-specific configuration for the pipe, including the input template, input transformation, dead-letter configuration, and parameters tailored to the destination service (such as Lambda, SQS, SNS).

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.batch_j.text: Specifies the configuration for an AWS Batch job when it is the target of the pipe, including the job definition, job name, and optional array, retry, and container override settings.
Configures the array size for the AWS Batch job target, determining how many parallel child jobs are submitted as an array job.
Specifies the number of child jobs to run when the pipe targets an AWS Batch job as an array job, allowing multiple parallel task executions.
Overrides the container properties (command, environment, memory, vCPUs, etc.) of the AWS Batch job that the pipe targets when invoking the job.
Overrides the command executed by the container in the AWS Batch job configured as the pipe target, providing a list of strings that replace the default container command.
Specifies a list of environment variable overrides (each with a `Name` and `Value`) to apply to the container when the pipe's target AWS Batch job is executed.
The name of the environment variable to set in the container when the AWS Batch job is run by the pipe target.
The value of the environment variable to set in the container override for the AWS Batch job target of the pipe.
Specifies the instance type to use for the AWS Batch container when the pipe runs a batch job, overriding the default instance type in the job definition.
Defines the resource requirements (such as GPU count) to override for the AWS Batch container when the pipe sends events to the Batch job target.
The type of resource the container override applies to, such as MEMORY, VCPU, or GPU, controlling how the resource requirement is interpreted.

The value of the resource requirement (e.g., number of vCPUs or memory in MiB) applied as a container override for an AWS Batch job, corresponding to the type specified in the resource_requirements entry.
Defines the AWS Batch job dependencies for a Pipes target job, listing prior jobs that must complete successfully before this job can start.
The job ID of a Batch job that must complete before the job submitted by this pipe target can start, used to define job dependencies in the AWS Batch target.
Specifies the type of dependency for the AWS Batch job (e.g., N_TO_N or SEQUENTIAL), defining how the target job's start is conditioned on other jobs in the depends_on list.
The name or ARN of the AWS Batch job definition used to run the target job.
The name to assign to the AWS Batch job that this pipe submits when targeting AWS Batch.
A map of parameter names to values that are passed to the AWS Batch job when the pipe invokes the target, overriding or supplying the job's parameter values.
Specifies the retry strategy for the AWS Batch job, including the number of attempts and the conditions under which the job retries based on exit codes.
The number of times to retry the AWS Batch job target when it fails, as part of the retry strategy.

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.cloud_w.text: Specifies the CloudWatch Logs target parameters, including the log stream name and an optional timestamp that is added to each event sent to the log stream.
The name of the CloudWatch Logs log stream where the pipe writes the event data, overriding the default log stream for the target log group.
The Unix timestamp (as a string) to use as the timestamp for the log event sent to CloudWatch Logs, overriding the event's original time.

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.ecs_tas.text: Specifies the parameters for running an Amazon ECS task when the Pipe target is an ECS service, including task definition, count, launch type, network configuration, and placement settings.
Defines the capacity provider strategy for the ECS task launched by the pipe target, specifying capacity providers and their base and weight values for task placement.
The minimum number of tasks to run on the specified capacity provider as part of the ECS task placement strategy.
The name of the Amazon ECS capacity provider to use when running the task as part of the capacity provider strategy.
The relative weight of this capacity provider in the ECS task's capacity provider strategy, which AWS Pipes uses when placing the task on the target ECS service or cluster.
Specifies whether to enable Amazon ECS managed tags on the ECS task launched as the pipe's target, so that AWS automatically applies system tags to the task.
Enables Amazon ECS Exec (execute command) for the ECS task when the pipe invokes the target.
Specifies the ECS task group, a customizable identifier for a set of related tasks, used for task filtering and grouping.
Specifies the launch type (e.g., FARGATE or EC2) to use when the pipe runs the target Amazon ECS task.
Specifies the VPC network configuration for the ECS task target, including subnets, security groups, and whether to assign a public IP address.
Specifies the VPC configuration (subnets, security groups, and whether to assign a public IP) for the ECS task when its network mode is awsvpc.
Determines whether the ECS task's elastic network interface is assigned a public IP address when using the specified VPC configuration, with values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
A list of security group IDs to attach to the ECS task's elastic network interface when the task uses awsvpc network mode as the target of the pipe.
The IDs of the subnets in which the ECS task will run when using the awsvpc network mode.
Specifies the ECS task and container overrides (such as command, environment variables, CPU/memory limits, task role, and ephemeral storage) applied when the pipe runs the target task.
Defines a list of container overrides to apply to the ECS task launched by the pipe, allowing per-container changes to command, environment variables, and resource limits during the invocation.
In the ECS task overrides for an AWS Pipes target, this list of strings specifies the container command to run, replacing the default command defined in the container image.
Overrides the number of CPU units reserved for the container in the ECS task, as part of the ECS task override for the pipe target.
Specifies the environment variables (as name/value pairs) to set for the container when the ECS task is run, overriding the values from the container definition.
The name of the environment variable to set in the ECS container when the pipe invokes the ECS task target, as part of the container environment overrides.
Sets the value of an environment variable override for a container in the ECS task launched by the pipe target.
Specifies a list of environment files (typically from Amazon S3) that inject environment variables into the container when the ECS task is the pipe target.
The type of environment file to use in the ECS container override, either 's3' for an Amazon S3 object or 'ssm' for an AWS Systems Manager parameter.
The ARN of the S3 object (or the SSM parameter name for the ssm type) that identifies the environment file whose variables are injected into the container as part of the ECS task override.
Specifies the hard memory limit in MiB for the container, overriding the memory value set in the task definition for this ECS task override.
The soft memory limit in MiB to reserve for the container, overriding the memoryReservation value from the container definition.
Specifies the name of the container in the ECS task definition that this override applies to.
Specifies the resource requirements (such as GPU or InferenceAccelerator) to override for the container in the Amazon ECS task when the pipe target is an ECS task.
The type of resource requirement (such as GPU or InferenceAccelerator) applied to the container override in the ECS task target of the AWS Pipes pipe.
Specifies the numeric value for the resource, such as the number of GPUs to allocate, corresponding to the resource type in the resource requirement for the container override in the ECS task target.
The number of CPU units to reserve for the ECS task, overriding the CPU value specified in the task definition.

Specifies the ephemeral storage size override (in GiB) applied to the ECS task when this pipe triggers an ECS task, allowing adjustment of the task's ephemeral storage beyond its registered task definition.
Specifies the amount of ephemeral storage (in GiB) for the ECS task, overriding the task definition's ephemeral storage configuration when the pipe runs the task.
The ARN of the IAM execution role that Amazon ECS uses to run the task, overriding the execution role defined in the task definition when the pipe targets an ECS task.
Overrides the inference accelerator devices for the ECS task launched by this pipe, allowing you to specify a custom device name and type that supersede the task definition's settings.
Specifies the device name of the inference accelerator whose settings are overridden in the ECS task definition.
The device type of the inference accelerator override to apply to the ECS task when the pipe invokes the target, such as 'eia1.medium' or 'eia2.large'.
Specifies the total memory (in MiB) override for the ECS task executed by this pipe, replacing the memory limit defined in the task definition when the target is invoked.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the Amazon ECS task uses as its task role when the pipe triggers the task.
Specifies the placement constraints (e.g., distinctInstance or memberOf) that control how the ECS task is placed on container instances when the pipe target runs the task.

The placement constraint expression (using Amazon ECS placement constraint syntax, such as a cluster query language expression like 'attribute:ecs.instance-type =~ t2.*') that applies when the placement constraint type is 'memberOf'.
Specifies the type of ECS task placement constraint (e.g., distinctInstance or memberOf) that governs how the task is placed on container instances.
Specifies the placement strategy (e.g., spread, binpack, random) used for the ECS task targeted by the pipe, including the strategy type and optional field on which to base it.
Specifies the field to apply the placement strategy against (e.g., 'instanceId' or a custom attribute like 'attribute:ecs.availability-zone') when scheduling the ECS task.
Specifies the type of ECS task placement strategy (e.g., random, spread, or binpack) used when placing the task that the pipe invokes.
Specifies the ECS platform version on which the task runs (e.g., 'LATEST' or a specific version like '1.4.0') when the AWS Pipes target invokes an Amazon ECS task.
Specifies whether tags from the ECS task definition or service are propagated to the ECS task started when the pipe invokes the target, with valid values being TASK_DEFINITION or SERVICE.
A reference identifier you assign to the ECS task, which is passed to the RunTask API as the referenceId to ensure idempotent task creation and to aid in identifying the task in logs.
The tags to apply to the ECS task when the pipe invokes the ECS target.
The key of a tag to apply to the ECS task that the pipe launches as its target.
The value portion of a key-value tag that is attached to the ECS task when the pipe runs the task.
The number of ECS tasks to launch for this target.
Specifies the ARN of the ECS task definition that EventBridge Pipes uses to run a task when the pipe's target is an Amazon ECS task.

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.event_b.text: Configures the parameters used by the pipe when sending events to an Amazon EventBridge event bus target, including the event source, detail type, and optional resources.
Specifies the DetailType value that AWS Pipes assigns to the event when it is delivered to the EventBridge event bus target, allowing the event to be categorized by its type.
The ID of an EventBridge global endpoint used to route the event to an EventBridge event bus in a different AWS Region.
Specifies the list of ARNs that identify the resources associated with the event, which are included in the event sent to the EventBridge event bus target.
Sets the source of the event sent to the EventBridge event bus, identifying the service or application that produced the event.
The timestamp to assign to the event when sending to the EventBridge event bus target; if omitted, the current time is used.

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.http_pa.text: Specifies the HTTP parameters, including header, query string, and path parameter values, used when the Pipe targets an HTTP endpoint such as an API destination.
Specifies the HTTP headers to include in the request sent to the target when using an HTTP endpoint as the pipe target.
The list of values that are substituted, in order, for each path parameter placeholder (such as {param}) in the target endpoint's URL path when the pipe invokes an HTTP target.
Specifies the query string parameters (key-value pairs) to append to the HTTP request made to the target when using an HTTP endpoint or API destination.

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.input_t.text: The template used to transform the input event before it is sent to the target, allowing you to map and extract fields from the original event using JSONPath expressions.

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.kinesis.text: Specifies the parameters for a Kinesis stream target, including the partition key that determines the shard to which the event is delivered.
The partition key value used by the pipe to route the record to a specific shard of the target Kinesis data stream.

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.lambda_.text: Defines the target-specific parameters for a Lambda function target in an AWS Pipe, including the invocation type (e.g., 'Event' or 'RequestResponse') that controls how the pipe invokes the function.
Specifies the invocation type for the Lambda function target, either 'RequestResponse' for synchronous invocation (default) or 'Event' for asynchronous invocation.

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.redshif.text: Defines the configuration for invoking the Amazon Redshift Data API, including the SQL statement, database details, and credentials, when the pipe's target is an Amazon Redshift cluster or serverless workgroup.
When set to true, this flag includes the original event payload in the request sent to the Redshift Data API by the pipe.

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.sage_ma.text: Configures the parameters for invoking an Amazon SageMaker pipeline as the pipe's target, specifying the list of pipeline parameters to pass to the pipeline execution.
Provides a list of name/value pairs that are passed as input parameters to the SageMaker pipeline execution when this pipe targets a SageMaker pipeline.
The name of a SageMaker pipeline parameter to override when the pipe invokes the pipeline, matching the parameter name defined in the SageMaker pipeline.
The value for a single SageMaker pipeline parameter in the list of name-value pairs passed to the target SageMaker pipeline when the pipe executes.

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.sqs_que.text: Specifies the parameters for sending events to an SQS queue as the pipe target, including optional message group ID and message deduplication ID for FIFO queues.
The deduplication ID used for messages sent to the SQS queue, which ensures exactly-once delivery for FIFO queues.
Specifies the message group ID for messages sent to an Amazon SQS FIFO queue, which groups messages to be delivered in a strict order and within a single consumer at a time.

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.step_fu.text: The target parameters for a Step Functions state machine, specifying how the pipe invokes the state machine, including the invocation type such as synchronous (REQUEST_RESPONSE) or asynchronous (FIRE_AND_FORGET) execution.

Specifies whether the pipe invokes the Step Functions state machine synchronously (`REQUEST_RESPONSE`) and waits for the execution to complete, or asynchronously (`FIRE_AND_FORGET`) without waiting for the result.

aws_pipes_pipe.target_parameters.timestr.text: Specifies the Amazon Timestream target configuration, including the database and table names, time column type, and dimension mappings used to write event data from the pipe.
Defines the list of dimension mappings that specify how source data is mapped to Timestream record dimension names and values when the pipe target writes to Timestream.
The name of the Timestream dimension to which the mapped value is written when the pipe sends data to Amazon Timestream.

Specifies the value for the Timestream dimension, which can be a literal string or a JSONPath expression (such as `$.detail.region`) that extracts a value from the event data being sent to the target.
Indicates the value type (VARCHAR or BIGINT) for the mapped dimension, used to cast the incoming event value before sending it to Amazon Timestream.
Specifies the unit of measure for the epoch timestamp value used in the Timestream target's time column, such as MILLISECONDS, SECONDS, MICROSECONDS, or NANOSECONDS.

Defines the multi-measure mappings for the Timestream target, specifying a list of measure names and their associated attribute mappings (including attribute value, measure value, and measure value type) to write multi-measure records.
Defines the list of mappings that specify how source data is assigned to each attribute (measure) within a multi-measure record written to Amazon Timestream.
Specifies the literal value or JSONPath expression used to populate the multi-measure attribute value in the Timestream record written by this pipe target.
Specifies the data type of the measure attribute in the Timestream multi-measure record (e.g., DOUBLE, BIGINT, BOOLEAN, VARCHAR, TIMESTAMP) so that Timestream correctly interprets the incoming value.
In an AWS Pipes Timestream target, this defines the name of an individual multi-measure attribute, which becomes the measure name in the Timestream record when using multi-measure mappings.
Specifies the name of the multi-measure record to write to Amazon Timestream when using multi-measure mappings in the pipe target.
Defines a list of single-measure mappings that specify how source data maps to Timestream measure records, including the measure name, value, and value type.
The name of the measure (column) in the Timestream table to which the source record field is mapped.
Provides the value of a single measure in a Timestream record, which can be a literal string or a dynamic JSON path expression (such as '$.field') resolved from the event payload.

Specifies the data type of the measure value for this single measure mapping, such as DOUBLE, BIGINT, VARCHAR, or BOOLEAN, which determines how the source data is interpreted when written to Amazon Timestream.
Specifies whether the value in the time field is interpreted as a Unix epoch timestamp (seconds since epoch) or as a formatted timestamp string when writing to Amazon Timestream.
Specifies the static timestamp value (as a string) used for the time column when writing the pipe's data to an Amazon Timestream target table.

Specifies the format string used to parse the source event's timestamp field when TimeFieldType is set to TIMESTAMP_FORMAT, determining how AWS Pipes converts the event time into the Timestream record's timestamp.
Provides the value for the version attribute of each record written to the Timestream table, used to enforce record versioning and support upserts.

aws_placement_group.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a user-defined tag applied to the placement group, used to categorize and identify the resource in AWS.

aws_proton_environment_account_connectio.text: The current lifecycle status of the environment account connection, which can be PENDING, CONNECTED, or REJECTED.
Identifies a tag key assigned to the AWS Proton environment account connection resource.
The value of a tag assigned to the Proton environment account connection, used for categorizing and managing the resource.

aws_proton_environment_template.name.text: The name of the environment template, used to identify it within AWS Proton.

aws_proton_environment_template.provisio.text: The provisioning engine used for the environment template, which can be either 'CLOUDFORMATION' or 'TERRAFORM'.

aws_proton_environment_template.tags.val.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS Proton environment template, which can be used to categorize and identify the template for cost allocation and management within AWS.

aws_proton_service_template.name.text: The unique name of the Proton service template.

aws_proton_service_template.pipeline_pro.text: Determines whether the service instance pipeline is provisioned by AWS Proton or by the customer, with valid values CUSTOMER and PROTON.

aws_proton_service_template.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Proton service template, used to identify and categorize the template for operational and cost management purposes.

aws_qbusiness_application.application_ar.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Q Business application, assigned by AWS when the application is created.

aws_qbusiness_application.application_id.text: The unique identifier that AWS QBusiness automatically assigns to the application when it is created.

aws_qbusiness_application.attachments_co.text: Configures whether users can attach files to conversations in the Q Business application, controlled by the AttachmentsControlMode setting (either ENABLED or DISABLED).
Determines whether users can use attachments in the application's chat sessions, with a required value of either ENABLED or DISABLED.

aws_qbusiness_application.auto_subscript.text: Determines whether new users are automatically subscribed to the Amazon Q Business application and, if enabled, specifies the default subscription type (ENTERPRISE or STARTER) assigned to them.

Determines whether AWS Q Business automatically subscribes new users to a default subscription tier (e.g., Q Business Lite or Pro) configured via the default_subscription_type field, with allowed values ENABLED or DISABLED.
Specifies the default subscription type (either 'PLUS' or 'ENTERPRISE') that AWS QBusiness automatically assigns to users when auto-subscription is enabled for the application.

aws_qbusiness_application.client_ids_for.text: Specifies the list of OAuth 2.0 client IDs that an Amazon Q Business application accepts from its OIDC identity provider for authenticating users.

aws_qbusiness_application.created_at.text: The timestamp of when the QBusiness application was created, computed by AWS.

aws_qbusiness_application.description.text: Specifies a user-provided description for the Amazon Q Business application, used to convey its purpose or context to administrators.

aws_qbusiness_application.display_name.text: The display name for the Amazon Q Business application, which is a user-friendly identifier shown in the AWS Management Console and used when referencing the application.

aws_qbusiness_application.encryption_con.text: Specifies the encryption configuration for the Q Business application, including whether to use a customer-managed KMS key and which key to use, for encrypting data at rest.
Specifies the AWS KMS key used to encrypt application data at rest, provided as a key ID or ARN.

aws_qbusiness_application.iam_identity_p.text: The ARN of the IAM identity provider used by Amazon Q Business to authenticate federated users and authorize their access to the application.

aws_qbusiness_application.identity_cente.text: The ARN of the AWS IAM Identity Center application that is automatically created and associated with this Amazon Q Business application when identity center integration is enabled.
The ARN of the AWS IAM Identity Center instance that this Q Business application uses for user provisioning and single sign-on.

aws_qbusiness_application.identity_type.text: Specifies the identity provider protocol used by the QBusiness application to authenticate users, with allowed values including AWS_IAM, SAML, and OIDC.

aws_qbusiness_application.personalizatio.text: Configures whether Amazon Q Business personalization is enabled for the application, with a PersonalizationControlMode setting that turns personalization on or off.
Controls whether personalization is enabled for the Amazon Q Business application, accepting values such as 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED' to turn the feature on or off.

aws_qbusiness_application.qapps_configur.text: Configures whether Q Apps are enabled for the Amazon Q Business application by specifying the QAppsControlMode as ENABLED or DISABLED.
Controls whether Q Apps are enabled or disabled for the Amazon Q Business application, with valid values ENABLED or DISABLED.

aws_qbusiness_application.quick_sight_co.text: Specifies the Amazon QuickSight integration configuration for the QBusiness application, including the QuickSight client namespace used for user groups.
The Amazon QuickSight namespace (e.g., 'default') that the Amazon Q Business application uses to access QuickSight data and assets.

aws_qbusiness_application.role_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an IAM role that the QBusiness application assumes to access and manage AWS resources and data sources on the customer's behalf.

aws_qbusiness_application.status.text: The current lifecycle status of the QBusiness application (e.g., CREATING, ACTIVE, UPDATING, FAILED), set by the service and read-only.

aws_qbusiness_application.tags.text: The tags field specifies a list of key-value pairs attached to the Amazon Q Business application for resource organization, cost tracking, and access control.

aws_qbusiness_application.updated_at.text: The timestamp indicating when the Amazon Q Business application was last updated.

aws_qbusiness_data_accessor.action_confi.text: Specifies the list of allowed actions for this Q Business data accessor, each with an action type and optional filter configuration that constrains which data the accessor can access.
Specifies the name of a QBusiness action that this data accessor is allowed to perform, as part of a configured list of actions within the data accessor.

Defines the document-level filtering for an individual action, using attribute filters (e.g., equals, contains, or range conditions) to restrict the data the action can access within the data accessor.

Defines the attribute-based filter that determines which documents the data accessor action can access, using expressions like equals, contains, range, and logical AND/OR/NOT combinations on document attributes.
Defines a list of document attribute filters that must all match (logical AND) for the data accessor's filter configuration to apply.
Specifies a filter condition that matches documents when the document attribute specified by the key contains all of the values listed in the value field of this object.

The name of the document attribute that the containsAll filter condition applies to, requiring the attribute to contain all specified values for a document to match in the action configuration's document attribute filter.

Specifies the list of attribute values that a document's attribute must contain all of for a containsAll filter condition to match, within an action configuration's filter for an AWS Q Business data accessor.
The date value (in ISO 8601 format) that the contains_all document attribute filter uses to match the value of a date-type document attribute.
This numeric value specifies a long-typed attribute value used in the 'containsAll' document attribute filter condition, requiring the document's attribute to include this value.

The string list value defines the set of document attribute values that must all be present on a document for the containsAll filter to match, thereby controlling which documents the action can access.

In the 'containsAll' condition of a document attribute filter within a data accessor action configuration, this string provides the value that a document attribute must contain for the filter to match.

In an AWS::QBusiness::DataAccessor action configuration filter, this field defines a list of document attribute values; a document matches the filter if its attribute contains any of these values, thereby controlling which documents are accessible for the action.
The name of the document attribute that the 'contains any' filter evaluates, specifying which field in the document is checked against the provided list of values.

In the 'contains any' filter of an AWS QBusiness data accessor, the attribute value object that supplies the list of values (such as a string list) which a document attribute must contain one of for the filter to take effect.

Specifies the date value (as a string in ISO 8601 format) to match against a document attribute of type date when the filter condition uses the `contains_any` operator in the Q Business data accessor action filter.

Specifies a numeric long value that a document attribute must match (as one of the accepted values) for a document to be selected under the containsAny filter condition in this QBusiness data accessor action.
Provides the list of strings used by the `contains_any` filter, matching documents whose attribute list includes any of these strings.

Specifies a single string value used in a containsAny document attribute filter, which determines whether a document's attribute matches any of the provided values to be included in the data accessor's action configuration.
Defines a document attribute filter condition that matches when the specified attribute's value exactly equals the provided value, controlling which documents the data accessor can access.
The name of the document attribute that the equality filter matches against, restricting access to documents with that attribute value.
Defines the document attribute value to be matched exactly in the equalsTo condition of the filter, provided as a DocumentAttributeValue object that can contain a string, long, or date value.

The date value, expressed as an ISO 8601 string (e.g., 2023-12-25T00:00:00Z), used as the value to match exactly in an `equalsTo` document attribute filter within the data accessor's action configuration.
The long (integer) value that the document attribute must equal for the filter to match, used within an equalsTo condition of a document attribute filter.
The list of string values that a document attribute must match (i.e., equal one of the listed values) to satisfy the equalsTo filter in the data accessor's action configuration.
The string value used as the comparison target for the equals-to document attribute filter, which restricts which documents the Q Business data accessor action can operate on.

The greater_than property specifies a greater-than comparison against a document attribute's numeric or date value, so that only documents whose attribute exceeds the given value are included in the data accessor's allowed scope.
The name of the document attribute that is compared against the greater-than value to filter documents accessible to this Q Business data accessor.
The value that the document attribute must exceed in a greater-than comparison, used to filter documents in the AWS QBusiness data accessor action's filter configuration.
Specifies the date (as a string) to compare against a document attribute, used as the right-hand operand when the filter operation is 'greater than' in an AWS Q Business data accessor action filter.
The numeric (long) threshold that the document attribute's value must exceed for the 'greater than' filter condition to match.
Sets the string operand used in the 'greater than' comparison for the document attribute filter, which restricts the documents an action in the AWS Q Business data accessor can operate on.

Sets a comparison condition that matches documents where the specified document attribute value is greater than or equal to a given value, used within the filter configuration to scope the data accessor's access to relevant documents.
The name of the document attribute to compare against in the greater-than-or-equals filter condition.

The value used in a 'greater than or equals' comparison condition on a document attribute, defining the threshold that a document's attribute must meet to be included in the filter applied by the data accessor's action configuration.
Specifies the date value (as an ISO 8601 formatted string) to use as the threshold when the document attribute filter condition is 'greater than or equals'.
Specifies the numeric long value used in a greater-than-or-equals comparison against a document attribute within the filter configuration for an AWS Q Business data accessor.
Specifies the list of string values used as the value in a greater-than-or-equals document attribute filter condition for Q Business data accessor permissions.

In the greaterThanOrEquals filter of a Q Business data accessor's document attribute filter, this string_value specifies the threshold string that a document attribute's value must match or exceed for the document to be accessible through the data accessor.
Defines a less-than comparison on a document attribute value (provided as a key-value pair) to filter documents within an action configuration's data accessor rules.
The name of the document attribute to compare against the specified value using the less-than condition.

The value (as a DocumentAttributeValue object, e.g. stringValue, stringListValue, longValue, or dateValue) that a document attribute is compared against when using the less-than operator in a document attribute filter for the data accessor's action configuration.
The date value (in ISO 8601 format) used as the comparison threshold in a less-than filter for a document attribute in an AWS Q Business data accessor action.

Specifies the long integer threshold used in a 'less than' comparison on a document attribute, controlling which documents the Amazon Q Business data accessor can access based on that attribute's numeric value.
Provides the list of string values used as the attribute value in a 'less than' comparison within a document attribute filter for an Amazon Q Business data accessor action configuration.
The string value used as the comparison operand in a 'less than' condition of an AWS Q Business document attribute filter for a data accessor action.

Specifies a condition in the document attribute filter where the attribute's value must be less than or equal to the provided value, restricting the documents visible to the data accessor based on that attribute.
Specifies the name of the document attribute whose value must be less than or equal to the provided value for the filter to apply.

Defines the comparison value used by the less_than_or_equals condition within a document attribute filter, so that only documents whose attribute value is less than or equal to this value match the filter.

The date_value field specifies a date in ISO 8601 format that serves as the upper bound for a less_than_or_equals comparison on a date-typed document attribute, limiting which documents the data accessor action can access.

The long_value field specifies the numeric long value used as the threshold in a less_than_or_equals comparison on a document attribute within the filter configuration of an action for the AWS Q Business data accessor.

For an AWS::QBusiness::DataAccessor, this field holds the list of strings that serve as the value for a 'less than or equals' document attribute filter condition within an action's filter configuration, determining the attribute values that documents must compare against to be included.

The string value used in a less-than-or-equals comparison for a document attribute filter, determining which documents the data accessor's action can access based on that attribute's value being at most this string.
This field defines a logical NOT filter, matching documents that do not satisfy the nested document attribute filter it contains.
Provides a list of document attribute filter conditions that are combined using a logical OR, so that the overall filter matches if any of the nested filter conditions is satisfied.

aws_qbusiness_data_accessor.application_.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Q Business application to which this data accessor is associated.

aws_qbusiness_data_accessor.authenticati.text: Specifies the authentication configuration for the data accessor, which can be either basic authentication using an IAM role and an AWS Secrets Manager secret (via `BasicAuthenticationConfiguration`) or no authentication (via `NoAuthenticationConfiguration`).
Configures the AWS IAM Identity Center trusted token issuer used for authenticating the Q Business data accessor, including the IAM role ARN and the token issuer endpoint URL.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM Identity Center trusted token issuer used to authenticate the data accessor.
The type of authentication method used by the data accessor to authenticate with the external data source, such as basic authentication, API key, or OAuth 2.0.
Defines the external ID values that AWS Q Business must use when assuming the IAM role specified in the authentication detail, preventing confused deputy attacks.

aws_qbusiness_data_accessor.created_at.text: The creation timestamp of the AWS Q Business data accessor, represented as an ISO 8601 string.

aws_qbusiness_data_accessor.data_accesso.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the data accessor in AWS.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the data accessor.

aws_qbusiness_data_accessor.display_name.text: The display name of the data accessor, which is a user-friendly name used to identify the data accessor in Amazon Q Business.

aws_qbusiness_data_accessor.idc_applicat.text: The ARN of the IAM Identity Center (IDC) application associated with this QBusiness data accessor, used for managing permissions via IAM Identity Center.

aws_qbusiness_data_accessor.principal.text: The ARN of the IAM principal (user or role) that is granted access to the underlying data source through this Q Business data accessor.

aws_qbusiness_data_accessor.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs that define custom tags to associate with the QBusiness data accessor for identity and organization.

aws_qbusiness_data_accessor.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS QBusiness data accessor resource, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_qbusiness_data_accessor.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS Q Business data accessor, used for resource categorization and metadata.

aws_qbusiness_data_accessor.updated_at.text: The date and time at which the QBusiness data accessor was last modified, as determined by AWS.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.application_id.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Q Business application to which this data source belongs.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.configuration.text: The connector-specific configuration for the data source, provided as a JSON object whose keys and values vary by the DataSourceType (for example, S3, Salesforce, or SharePoint).

aws_qbusiness_data_source.created_at.text: The timestamp indicating when the data source was created in AWS QBusiness.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.data_source_ar.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Q Business data source, assigned by AWS upon creation.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.data_source_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS QBusiness to this data source.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.description.text: Provides a user-defined description that helps identify the purpose or content of the data source.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.display_name.text: The human-readable name of the data source, used to identify it in the Amazon Q Business console and APIs.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.document_enric.text: This object configures the document enrichment process for the data source, defining pre-extraction and post-extraction transformations such as inline configuration rules or custom Lambda-based hook functions.
Specifies a list of inline document enrichment configurations that conditionally modify document attributes (e.g., setting, deleting, or altering attribute values) during data ingestion.
Defines the document attribute condition (key, operator, and value) that a document must meet for the associated enrichment action to be applied.
The name of the document attribute that this condition evaluates, such as a metadata field or content property, to determine whether the enrichment action applies.
Determines how the document attribute key's value is compared against the condition's value, with allowed values such as EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, CONTAINS, NOT_CONTAINS, EXISTS, or NOT_EXISTS.

Defines the attribute value (such as a string, string list, number, or date) that the document attribute condition compares against, determining whether the inline document enrichment action is applied.
Provides the date used as the comparison value in the document enrichment condition when the document attribute's value type is DATE, allowing the rule to match documents based on that specific date.

Defines the numeric (long) value to compare against a document attribute in an inline enrichment condition, determining whether the enrichment action applies to documents in the AWS QBusiness data source.

This field provides the list of string values used as the condition value in a QBusiness data source document enrichment inline configuration, allowing multiple attribute values to be matched against when evaluating the condition.
The string value used as the comparison target for a document attribute condition in an inline document enrichment configuration.
Specifies the document attribute that the inline enrichment operation modifies, including the attribute name, the action (such as ADD, DELETE, or REPLACE), and the value to apply.
Specifies whether to overwrite the existing value of the target document attribute with the supplied value or delete the attribute.
The key (name) of the document attribute that the inline document enrichment configuration will update or add for the target in the QBusiness data source.

Specifies the value to assign to the target document attribute in an inline document enrichment configuration, expressed as a DocumentAttributeValue object (which can hold a string, string list, long, or date).
Specifies the date value, in ISO 8601 format, to assign to the document attribute when the inline enrichment target is applied during data source synchronization.
Sets the document attribute to the specified long integer value when the inline enrichment condition is met.
Provides the list of string values to assign to the document attribute (target key) in this inline document enrichment rule, used when the rule's condition is satisfied.
Specifies the string value to assign to the target document attribute in an inline document enrichment action for the AWS Q Business data source.
Defines the Lambda function invoked after document attributes are extracted, enabling custom post-processing and enrichment of the document before indexing.
Specifies the document attribute condition (key, operator, value) that must be satisfied for the post-extraction hook to be invoked during document enrichment.

For the invocation condition of a post-extraction hook, this is the document attribute key (field name) whose value the condition evaluates (e.g., a custom metadata field) to decide whether the hook runs.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, CONTAINS) used to evaluate the document attribute condition that determines whether the post-extraction hook is invoked.
The document attribute value that is compared against the condition key using the operator to determine whether the post-extraction hook is invoked.
Specifies the date value (as a string in ISO 8601 format) that the document attribute must match, per the condition operator, to trigger the post-extraction hook for the data source.
The long integer value used as the document attribute value in the invocation condition that determines whether the post-extraction hook is triggered.

Specifies the list of string values to compare against the document attribute value when evaluating the invocation condition for the post-extraction hook in the data source's document enrichment configuration.

The string value used in the attribute condition that determines whether the post-extraction hook is invoked on a document, compared against the document attribute's value using the specified operator.
The ARN of the Lambda function invoked after document extraction to perform custom post-extraction enrichment on the Q Business data source.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Q Business assumes to invoke the post-extraction Lambda function during document enrichment for this data source.
The name of the S3 bucket where AWS QBusiness stores the extracted documents that are passed to the post-extraction hook's Lambda function for enrichment.
Specifies the AWS Lambda function configuration that is invoked before document extraction to perform pre-extraction enrichment on documents from the data source.
Specifies the condition on a document attribute that determines whether the pre-extraction hook is invoked for a document.

The key (document attribute name) that the invocation condition uses as the attribute to evaluate (with the specified operator and value) to determine whether the pre-extraction hook should be invoked.

This required string specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or CONTAINS) that defines how the invocation condition's value is evaluated against the document attribute, determining whether the pre-extraction hook is triggered.
Provides the attribute value to match in the invocation condition for the pre-extraction hook, using one of several supported value formats (string, string list, long, or date).
The date value used as the attribute value in the hook invocation condition, matched against document attributes to determine whether the pre-extraction hook runs.

Specifies the numeric (long) value that a document attribute must match to satisfy the invocation condition that triggers the pre-extraction hook in the data source's document enrichment configuration.
Defines the list of string values that the document attribute's value is compared against in the invocation condition for the pre-extraction hook.
The string value to match in the document attribute condition that triggers the pre-extraction hook during document enrichment.
The ARN of the AWS Lambda function invoked by the pre-extraction hook to process documents before they are indexed by the Amazon Q Business data source.
The ARN of an IAM role that AWS Q Business assumes to invoke the Lambda function for the pre-extraction document enrichment hook.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that contains the Lambda function code for the pre-extraction hook, which is invoked before document extraction.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.index_id.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Q Business index to which this data source is associated.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.media_extracti.text: Specifies the configuration for extracting text from media files (such as images and audio) in source documents, including whether extraction is enabled for each media type.
Configures whether audio content from media files in the data source is extracted and indexed, typically by enabling or disabling audio transcription for searchable text.
Specifies whether audio extraction from media files in the Amazon Q Business data source is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED).
Configures image extraction for the data source by specifying whether image extraction is enabled or disabled, allowing text and metadata to be extracted from images.
Indicates whether extraction of text from images (such as scanned documents or photos) in the data source is enabled or disabled.
Configures whether AWS Q Business extracts text from video files (e.g., using speech-to-text or optical character recognition) in the data source, based on its enabled or disabled extraction status.
Indicates whether video extraction is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for the QBusiness data source, controlling whether text is extracted from video files.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.role_arn.text: The IAM role ARN that AWS Q Business assumes to access the underlying data source and retrieve documents for indexing.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.status.text: The current status of the data source, indicating whether it is active, being created, updated, deleted, or has failed.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.sync_schedule.text: Specifies the cron expression that defines how often the data source automatically syncs with its source repository.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.tags.text: A list of tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the QBusiness data source, used for resource identification, organization, and management.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.tags.key.text: The key of a key-value tag assigned to the AWS QBusiness data source, used for resource organization and metadata.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.type.text: The connector type (e.g., S3, Salesforce, SharePoint) reported by the service for this Amazon Q Business data source.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.updated_at.text: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) of the most recent update to the data source, returned by the service.

aws_qbusiness_data_source.vpc_configurat.text: Specifies the VPC configuration, including security group IDs and subnet IDs, used by the data source to connect to resources within an Amazon VPC.
The list of security group IDs to associate with the VPC configuration for the AWS QBusiness data source.
Identifies the subnets in the VPC where the Amazon Q Business data source connector runs to access private resources within your network.

aws_qbusiness_index.application_id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS QBusiness application that this index belongs to, required when creating the index.

aws_qbusiness_index.capacity_configurati.text: Specifies the capacity configuration for the index, selecting either the ENTERPRISE or STARTER index type and the number of capacity units to allocate.
The number of capacity units to allocate to the Amazon Q Business index, where each unit adds a fixed amount of storage and query capacity.

aws_qbusiness_index.created_at.text: The ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when this Amazon Q Business index was created.

aws_qbusiness_index.description.text: A description for the Amazon Q Business index.

aws_qbusiness_index.display_name.text: The display name of the Amazon Q Business index, which is a required, user-visible name that identifies the index in the Q Business console and API operations.

aws_qbusiness_index.document_attribute_c.text: Defines which document metadata attributes the index will index and how they can be used for querying and filtering, by specifying each attribute's name, type, and usage configuration.
The unique name of the document attribute that this configuration applies to, used to match metadata fields in ingested documents and reference the attribute in data source schemas.
Determines whether the document attribute can be used in search queries, with allowed values ENABLED or DISABLED.
Specifies the data type of the document attribute in the index configuration, such as STRING, NUMBER, or DATE, which determines how the attribute is indexed and searched.

aws_qbusiness_index.index_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Q Business index, assigned by AWS when the index is created.

aws_qbusiness_index.index_id.text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for the QBusiness index.

aws_qbusiness_index.index_statistics.text: This computed attribute provides usage statistics for the QBusiness index, such as the total number of indexed documents and the combined byte size of the indexed text.

aws_qbusiness_index.index_statistics.tex.text: Contains the total number of text documents and the number of indexed text documents for the AWS QBusiness index.
The total size in bytes of text content that has been indexed for the index.
The total number of text documents that have been indexed in the Amazon Q Business index.

aws_qbusiness_index.status.text: The current lifecycle status of the Amazon Q Business index, such as CREATING during provisioning or ACTIVE when ready to use.

aws_qbusiness_index.tags.text: A list of key-value tag objects to attach to the Amazon Q Business index, used for organizing, managing, and identifying the resource in AWS.

aws_qbusiness_index.tags.key.text: The key of a tag pair attached to the Amazon Q Business index, enabling resource categorization and access management.

aws_qbusiness_index.type.text: Specifies whether the Amazon Q Business index is an ENTERPRISE index for general enterprise search or an ANALYTICS index for analytical and data-intensive workloads.

aws_qbusiness_index.updated_at.text: The timestamp indicating when the QBusiness index was last updated.

aws_qbusiness_permission.actions.text: Lists the Amazon Q Business API actions (e.g., 'qbusiness:Query') that the principal is authorized to perform on the associated Q Business application.

aws_qbusiness_permission.application_id.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Q Business application to which this permission applies.

aws_qbusiness_permission.conditions.text: A list of condition objects, each specifying a condition key (like a user or document attribute) and its allowed values, that restrict the application of the Q Business permission to matching principals and documents.

aws_qbusiness_permission.conditions.cond.text: In an AWS::QBusiness::Permission policy statement, the condition_key field names the contextual key that the permission condition evaluates against the request's context to determine whether the granted actions apply to the principal.
This field specifies the IAM condition operator (such as StringEquals, StringLike, or Bool) used to compare a condition key against its value in a permission policy entry for Amazon Q Business.

For each condition entry in the Q Business permission policy, this list contains the values that must match the condition key to apply the permission, allowing context-based restrictions such as organization IDs or tags.

aws_qbusiness_permission.principal.text: The ARN of the IAM principal (user, role, or group) to which the Q Business application permission is granted.

aws_qbusiness_permission.statement_id.text: The unique identifier for a permission statement that grants the Amazon Q Business application access to a specified action and resource.

aws_qbusiness_plugin.application_id.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Q Business application that this plugin is attached to.

aws_qbusiness_plugin.auth_configuration.text: Specifies the authentication configuration for the plugin, defining whether it uses basic or OAuth 2.0 authentication along with the necessary credentials and endpoint details.

aws_qbusiness_plugin.auth_configuration..text: Specifies the basic authentication settings for the AWS QBusiness plugin by providing the ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the credentials used for authentication.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS QBusiness assumes to retrieve the basic authentication credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the username and password credentials used for basic authentication to the external application configured for the QBusiness plugin.
Configures the QBusiness plugin to require no authentication credentials, indicating that the plugin's external service calls do not need user or API keys.
Defines the OAuth 2.0 client credential settings for the plugin, including the authorization URL, client ID, client secret, and scope, enabling the plugin to authenticate with the external service.
The authorization URL to which users are redirected for authentication when using the OAuth 2.0 client credential configuration for the plugin.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Q Business assumes to retrieve the OAuth2 client credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager for this plugin's authentication.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the client secret used for the OAuth2 client credential authentication flow.
The URL of the OAuth2 token endpoint that the AWS QBusiness plugin calls to exchange its client credentials for an access token.

aws_qbusiness_plugin.build_status.text: The current build status of the Amazon Q Business plugin, indicating whether it is ready to use (e.g., READY), still being created (CREATING), or has failed (FAILED).

aws_qbusiness_plugin.created_at.text: The timestamp indicating when the plugin was created.

aws_qbusiness_plugin.custom_plugin_confi.text: Defines the API schema and source code repository settings for a custom plugin in Amazon Q Business when the plugin type is CUSTOM.
Specifies the OpenAPI 3.0 schema that defines the API operations and data structures for the custom plugin, provided either inline as a JSON/YAML payload or as a reference to an S3 object.
Contains the inline API schema, in JSON or YAML format, that describes the custom plugin's endpoints and operations for Amazon Q Business to invoke.
Configures the Amazon S3 location (bucket and object key) where the OpenAPI schema file for the custom plugin is stored.
The name of the S3 bucket that stores the OpenAPI schema file defining the plugin's API, as referenced by the custom plugin configuration.
The S3 object key (file name) of the OpenAPI schema file that defines the custom plugin's API, stored in the S3 bucket specified by the parent s3 configuration.
Specifies the type of API schema for the custom plugin, either an S3 object or an inline OpenAPI 3.0 payload, with allowed values S3 and OPEN_API_V3.
Provides a description of the custom plugin, helping users understand its purpose and functionality.

aws_qbusiness_plugin.display_name.text: The human-readable name of the plugin, used to identify it in the Amazon Q Business console and APIs.

aws_qbusiness_plugin.plugin_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the plugin in AWS QBusiness.

aws_qbusiness_plugin.plugin_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the plugin in Amazon Q Business when it is created, used to reference the plugin in other APIs and resources.

aws_qbusiness_plugin.server_url.text: The URL of the external server or application that the plugin connects to, serving as the endpoint for its configuration.

aws_qbusiness_plugin.state.text: Indicates the current status of the plugin, such as ENABLED or DISABLED, which determines whether the plugin is active for use in Amazon Q Business applications.

aws_qbusiness_plugin.tags.text: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the QBusiness plugin resource for cost allocation, organization, and identification.

aws_qbusiness_plugin.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the QBusiness plugin, used to store arbitrary metadata for identifying or categorizing the plugin.

aws_qbusiness_plugin.type.text: Specifies the type of the third-party application the plugin integrates with, which determines the required authentication and configuration schema (e.g., SERVICE_NOW, SALESFORCE, JIRA, ZENDESK, or CUSTOM).

aws_qbusiness_plugin.updated_at.text: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the plugin was last updated, set automatically by AWS QBusiness.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.application_id.text: The unique identifier of the Amazon Q Business application to which this retriever belongs.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.configuration.text: Defines the retriever type-specific configuration, which specifies either the Amazon Kendra index configuration (KendraIndexConfiguration) or the native QBusiness index configuration (NativeIndexConfiguration), determining how documents are retrieved.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.configuration.ke.text: Specifies the configuration for using an Amazon Kendra index as the retriever, including the identifier of the Kendra index.
The unique identifier of the Amazon Kendra index to be used as the retriever in the Amazon Q Business retriever configuration.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.configuration.na.text: Configures the retriever to use a native Amazon Q Business index, specifying the index ID and optional metadata handling settings.
Specifies the unique identifier of the Amazon Q Business native index that the retriever is configured to use for performing searches.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.created_at.text: Provides the date and time (as an ISO 8601 string) when the QBusiness retriever was created.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.display_name.text: The human-readable name for the retriever, used to identify it in the AWS Q Business console and API responses.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.retriever_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this QBusiness retriever in AWS.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.retriever_id.text: The unique identifier assigned to the Amazon Q Business retriever.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.role_arn.text: The ARN of an IAM role that grants Amazon Q Business permissions to access the data source associated with this retriever.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.status.text: The current operational status of the Amazon Q Business retriever, such as ACTIVE or INACTIVE, as assigned by the service.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.tags.text: Defines the AWS tags (key-value pairs) applied to the Amazon Q Business retriever resource, which can be used for cost allocation, access control, and metadata organization.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to attach to the Amazon Q Business retriever resource.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.type.text: The type of retriever, either NATIVE_INDEX for the Amazon Q Business native index or KENDRA_INDEX for an Amazon Kendra index.

aws_qbusiness_retriever.updated_at.text: The timestamp indicating when this Amazon Q Business retriever was most recently updated.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.application.text: The unique identifier of the AWS QBusiness application to which this web experience is attached.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.browser_ext.text: Configures the browser extension for the web experience, including whether the extension is enabled and the extension name used to access the QBusiness assistant from a supported browser.
Specifies the browsers (such as Chrome, Firefox, and Edge) for which the AWS Q Business browser extension is enabled in the web experience.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.created_at.text: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the Amazon Q Business web experience was created.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.customizati.text: Specifies the custom CSS and JavaScript URLs used to customize the appearance and behavior of the AWS Q Business web experience.
The URL of a custom CSS file that overrides the default styling of the QBusiness web experience to match your organization's branding.
Specifies the URL of a custom favicon that replaces the default QBusiness icon for the web experience.
Defines the URL of a custom font that replaces the default font for the Amazon Q Business web experience.
The URL of a custom logo image that Amazon Q Business displays on the web experience's chat interface.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.default_end.text: The default endpoint URL of the web experience, automatically assigned by AWS QBusiness when the web experience is created.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.identity_pr.text: Defines the identity provider configuration for the web experience, allowing you to specify either SAML or OIDC settings for user authentication.

Specifies the OpenID Connect (OIDC) configuration for users to authenticate to the web experience, referencing the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores OIDC client credentials and the IAM role used to retrieve them.
The ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the client secret for the OpenID Connect configuration, which the web experience uses to authenticate with the OIDC identity provider.
The ARN of an IAM role that Amazon Q Business assumes to retrieve the OIDC client secret from AWS Secrets Manager for authenticating users to the web experience.
Configures SAML-based single sign-on for the web experience by specifying the IdP metadata document, the IAM role ARN, and optional user/group attribute mappings for authentication.
The URL of the identity provider's authentication endpoint to which users are redirected for SAML single sign-on.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.origins.text: A list of allowed origin URLs (e.g., 'https://example.com') that can embed or access this Amazon Q Business web experience, enabling secure integration with your own web applications while controlling cross-origin access.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.role_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the web experience assumes to access AWS services and resources.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.sample_prom.text: Determines whether sample prompts are shown to users in the AWS Q Business web experience, with allowed values ENABLED or DISABLED.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.status.text: The current lifecycle status of the web experience, such as CREATING, ACTIVE, or DELETING, as assigned by the QBusiness service.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.subtitle.text: The subtitle for the AWS QBusiness web experience, typically displayed under the title in the chat interface.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.tags.text: A list of tag objects (each with a key and value) that are attached to the Amazon Q Business web experience for resource identification, cost allocation, and access management.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.tags.key.text: Defines the tag key for a key-value pair assigned to an AWS Q Business web experience, enabling resource categorization, cost management, and access control through AWS tagging.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.title.text: The title of the web experience, which is displayed to users in the browser tab and as the heading of the web experience interface.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.updated_at.text: The read-only timestamp indicating when the web experience was last updated.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.web_experie.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this QBusiness web experience.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this Amazon Q Business web experience, used to reference it in API calls and other resources.

aws_qbusiness_web_experience.welcome_mes.text: The custom message that Amazon Q Business displays to users when they first open the web experience chat interface.

aws_qldb_ledger.deletion_protection.text: Enables or disables deletion protection for the ledger, preventing the ledger from being deleted when enabled.

aws_qldb_ledger.id.text: The id is the unique name of the QLDB ledger, which serves as the primary identifier for the ledger resource.

aws_qldb_ledger.kms_key.text: The ARN of a customer-managed AWS KMS key used to encrypt the ledger's data at rest; if omitted, AWS QLDB uses an AWS-owned key.

aws_qldb_ledger.name.text: The name of the QLDB ledger to create; if you do not provide one, AWS CloudFormation generates a unique name for the ledger.

aws_qldb_ledger.permissions_mode.text: Sets the permissions mode for the QLDB ledger, which controls whether all IAM principals can access the ledger through IAM policies (ALLOW_ALL) or whether access is restricted by standard QLDB permissions (STANDARD).

aws_qldb_ledger.tags.text: Specifies the list of key-value tags to attach to the QLDB ledger.

aws_qldb_ledger.tags.key.text: Defines the key of a tag applied to the QLDB ledger, which serves as a user-defined label for identifying and managing the ledger resource.

aws_qldb_ledger.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS QLDB ledger, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_qldb_stream.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the QLDB stream, which uniquely identifies the stream within AWS.

aws_qldb_stream.exclusive_end_time.text: The exclusive_end_time specifies the date and time at which the QLDB journal stream stops delivering data; if omitted, the stream continues indefinitely.

aws_qldb_stream.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the QLDB stream when it is created.

aws_qldb_stream.inclusive_start_time.text: The inclusive start time and date (ISO 8601 timestamp) from which the QLDB stream starts capturing journal data, including all revisions committed at or after that exact moment.

aws_qldb_stream.kinesis_configuration.text: Specifies the Amazon Kinesis Data Streams destination for the QLDB stream, including the ARN of the target Kinesis stream and whether aggregation of records is enabled.

aws_qldb_stream.kinesis_configuration.ag.text: Indicates whether to enable aggregation of QLDB stream records before they are delivered to Kinesis Data Streams, which groups multiple records into a single Kinesis record to reduce the number of requests.

aws_qldb_stream.kinesis_configuration.st.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Kinesis data stream to which QLDB writes journal data.

aws_qldb_stream.ledger_name.text: The name of the QLDB ledger from which this stream exports data.

aws_qldb_stream.role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that QLDB assumes to write journal data to the destination Kinesis Data Stream.

aws_qldb_stream.stream_name.text: The user-defined name of the QLDB journal stream, which must be unique within the AWS account and region and is used to identify the stream when creating or managing it.

aws_qldb_stream.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag applied to an Amazon QLDB stream, used to organize, identify, and manage the stream resource within AWS.

aws_qldb_stream.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag attached to the Amazon QLDB stream, used to assign metadata to the stream for identification and management.

aws_quick_sight_action_connector.authent.text: The base endpoint URL of the external API service that the QuickSight action connector communicates with when using API key authentication.

Contains the OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant parameters (such as authorization and token endpoints, client ID, client secret, and scopes) used by QuickSight to authenticate an action connector to an external service.

Contains the OAuth 2.0 client ID and client secret (or a reference to a Secrets Manager secret storing them) used by the QuickSight action connector during the authorization code grant token exchange in its authentication flow.
The URL of the OAuth 2.0 authorization server's authorization endpoint to which users are redirected to grant permissions during the authorization code grant flow for the QuickSight action connector.

The OAuth 2.0 client ID issued to the QuickSight action connector by the external authorization server, used as the public client identifier during the authorization code grant flow to obtain access tokens.
The client secret for the OAuth authorization code grant flow, used by the QuickSight action connector to authenticate with the external service.
The URL of the OAuth 2.0 token endpoint used in the authorization code grant flow to exchange an authorization code for an access token.
The base endpoint (base URL) of the OAuth authorization server to which Amazon QuickSight sends authorization code grant requests for the action connector's authentication metadata.

Specifies the redirect (callback) URL to which the user is redirected after authorizing the OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant, enabling the QuickSight action connector to exchange the authorization code for tokens.
The base endpoint (root URL) of the external service that this basic authentication connection targets, used as the base for all API requests made through the connector.
Specifies the password for HTTP basic authentication to the external endpoint that this QuickSight action connector is configured to call.

This object contains the client credentials (e.g., client ID and client secret) and other details needed to perform the OAuth 2.0 client-credentials grant for authenticating the QuickSight action connector to the external service.
The OAuth client identifier used in the client credentials grant flow to authenticate the QuickSight action connector.
The client secret used to authenticate the application when requesting an access token via the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant for the QuickSight action connector.
Defines the OAuth 2.0 token endpoint URL that the QuickSight action connector calls with the client credentials grant to obtain an access token for authenticating to the external API.
The ARN of the IAM role that QuickSight assumes to authenticate with the external service when using IAM connection metadata for this action connector.

The `noneConnectionMetadata` object is an empty placeholder used within the authentication metadata when the authentication type is set to `none`, indicating that no connection credentials are required for the action connector.
The base endpoint URL that the QuickSight action connector targets when no authentication method (NoneConnectionMetadata) is used.
Specifies the authentication mechanism (such as basic authentication, API key, or OAuth 2.0) that QuickSight uses to authenticate the action connector when invoking the external endpoint.

aws_quick_sight_action_connector.aws_acc.text: The AWS account ID where the QuickSight action connector is deployed, used to scope the resource within the correct account.

aws_quick_sight_action_connector.permiss.text: Specifies the list of Amazon QuickSight actions (e.g., "quicksight:DescribeDashboard", "quicksight:UpdateDashboard") that the principal is allowed to perform on the QuickSight resource.
The ARN of the principal (IAM user, group, role, or QuickSight user/group) that the corresponding actions are being granted to for this QuickSight action connector.

aws_quick_sight_action_connector.type.text: The type of the QuickSight action connector, identifying the external system or service it integrates with (e.g., ServiceNow, Salesforce, or similar supported platforms), required when defining the connector.

aws_quick_sight_action_connector.vpc_con.text: The ARN of the VPC connection that the QuickSight action connector uses to securely access resources within a private VPC.

aws_quick_sight_approval_policy.policy_a.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the QuickSight approval policy, used as a reference in IAM policies and API operations.

aws_quick_sight_approval_policy.policy_i.text: The unique identifier for a QuickSight approval policy that governs whether asset publishing requires approval before the asset is shared.

aws_quick_sight_custom_permissions.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this QuickSight custom permissions resource, automatically assigned by AWS when the resource is created.

aws_quick_sight_custom_permissions.aws_a.text: The AWS account ID in which the QuickSight custom permissions profile is created and associated with this resource.

aws_quick_sight_custom_permissions.capab.text: Specifies the capabilities to enable or disable for the QuickSight custom permissions profile, with each key (e.g., CREATE_AND_UPDATE_DASHBOARDS, ADD_OR_RUN_ANALYSIS) mapped to either 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
