Controls whether the user is granted the ACCESS_APPS_NATIVE_DATA_STORE capability, which permits access to the native data store used by QuickSight applications like QuickSight Q.
Specifies a specific QuickSight capability action (such as EXPORT_TO_CSV or CREATE_AND_UPDATE_DATASETS) that the custom permissions set allows.
Controls whether users in the custom permissions profile can add or run anomaly detection on analyses in Amazon QuickSight, with values typically being ENABLED or DISABLED.
Sets the analysis permission level for the QuickSight custom permissions profile, controlling which analysis actions (e.g., read, create, update) users with these permissions can perform.
Specifies whether users granted this custom permission level are allowed to approve requests to share QuickSight flows.
Controls the Asana action capability, determining whether users with this custom permissions profile can connect to and use Asana as a data source, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Sets the resource status for the box_agent_action capability, controlling whether users with this custom permissions profile can perform Box agent actions in Amazon QuickSight.
Specifies whether users are allowed to build calculated fields using Amazon QuickSight Q, with a value of either 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Controls whether the Confluence integration action is enabled or disabled for these custom permissions, by setting the value to 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Specifies whether the custom permissions include the CREATE_AND_UPDATE_AMAZON_BEDROCK_ARS_ACTION capability, which allows a user to create and update Amazon Bedrock ARS actions in QuickSight.
Determines whether the custom permission allows users to create and update Amazon Bedrock FS actions in Amazon QuickSight.
Determines whether QuickSight custom permissions allow or deny the creation and update of Amazon Bedrock KRS actions, with the value set to 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Sets the state (ENABLED or DISABLED) for the Amazon QuickSight custom permission that controls whether users can create and update Amazon S3 data sources.
Specifies whether users with this custom permission can create and update QuickSight apps; set to 'DENY' to restrict this capability, or 'ALLOW' to permit it.
Specifies whether users with this custom permission can create and update Asana actions in Amazon QuickSight, such as triggering Asana tasks from dashboard insights.
Controls whether the user can create and update Box agent actions in QuickSight, with an allowed value of 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Specifies whether the user has permission to create and update Amazon Comprehend actions in Amazon QuickSight.
Controls whether the QuickSight custom permission allows or denies the create and update action for Amazon Comprehend Medical, with values typically 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Determines whether users can create and update Confluence data source connections, typically set to ENABLED or DISABLED.
Specifies whether users with these custom permissions can create and update dashboard email reports, with valid values 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Specifies whether this custom permissions profile permits or denies the 'CREATE_AND_UPDATE_DATA_SOURCES' capability, controlling whether assigned QuickSight users can create and update data sources.
Determines whether the user can create and update datasets in Amazon QuickSight, with the value set to either 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Determines whether users with this custom permission can create and update QuickSight fact sets, accepting 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.

This field sets the permission status for the 'create and update generic HTTP action' capability within the QuickSight custom permissions profile, using a string value such as 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED' to indicate whether users can create and update these HTTP actions.
Indicates whether the QuickSight custom permissions profile includes the CREATE_AND_UPDATE_GITHUB_ACTION capability, allowing users to create and update GitHub actions.

Indicates whether the custom permissions set includes the CREATE_AND_UPDATE_GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ACTION capability, allowing QuickSight users with these permissions to create and update Google Calendar actions.
This field defines the permission setting (e.g., ALLOW or DENY) for the QuickSight capability to create and update HubSpot actions within custom permissions.
Determines whether the custom permissions allow users to create and update Hugging Face actions in Amazon QuickSight, using a string value that enables or disables this capability.
Specifies whether the custom permission allows ('ALLOW') or denies ('DENY') the user's ability to create and update Intercom actions in Amazon QuickSight.
Determines whether the custom permissions grant or deny the ability to create and update Jira actions in Amazon QuickSight, typically using the values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
This string, with allowed values 'ALLOW' or 'DENY', controls whether a user with these custom permissions can create and update knowledge bases in Amazon QuickSight.
Specifies whether the custom permission allows users to create and update Microsoft Exchange data sources in Amazon QuickSight, typically with a value of 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.

This field specifies whether the Create and update Microsoft Teams action capability is enabled or disabled for the custom permissions, allowing or denying users the ability to create and update Microsoft Teams actions in Amazon QuickSight (with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED').
Controls whether the custom permissions include the CREATE_AND_UPDATE_NEW_RELIC_ACTION capability, granting users the ability to create and update New Relic actions in Amazon QuickSight.
Defines the permission action (ALLOW or DENY) for the QuickSight capability that enables creating and updating Notions (AI-powered natural language narratives) in the QuickSight console.
Controls whether the custom permissions profile allows users to create and update OneDrive actions, with a typical string value of 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Controls whether the custom permissions profile grants the ability to create and update open API actions in Amazon QuickSight, corresponding to the CREATE_AND_UPDATE_OPEN_APIAction capability.
Controls whether users with this custom permissions profile can create and update PagerDuty actions, which are used to set up PagerDuty notifications for QuickSight alerts.
This capability key specifies whether users can create and update Salesforce actions in QuickSight, typically set to either 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Specifies whether users can create and update SAP Business Partner actions in Amazon QuickSight, accepting 'ALLOW' or 'DENY' as the permission value within the custom permissions capabilities.
Determines whether a user can create and update SAP physical inventory actions in QuickSight, typically set to 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Determines whether this custom permission grants the ability to create and update ServiceNow actions (such as data source connections) in Amazon QuickSight.
Controls whether users with this custom permissions profile can create and update Slack actions, which configure how QuickSight reports and dashboards are delivered to Slack channels.
Determines whether the QuickSight user is allowed to create and update Smartsheet data source datasets, with a value of ALLOW or DENY.
Determines whether users granted this custom permission can create and update Amazon Textract actions, with the value specified as 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Specifies whether users with this custom permissions profile are allowed to create and update themes in QuickSight, with accepted values 'ENABLED' or 'DENY'.
Specifies whether users assigned to this custom permission can create and update threshold alerts in Amazon QuickSight.
Controls whether the custom permission set enables the ability to create and update Zendesk actions within Amazon QuickSight, as defined in the capabilities block.
Controls whether users with this custom permissions profile can create and manage chat agents (Amazon QuickSight Q generative AI assistants) in QuickSight.

Toggles the QuickSight capability that lets a user generate an executive summary for a dashboard using QuickSight Q (natural language queries), with the value indicating whether the capability is enabled or disabled.
Controls whether the QuickSight principal with this custom permissions set is allowed to create shared folders, where the value must be 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
This field specifies whether the custom permissions profile permits the user to create spaces in Amazon QuickSight, which are used to organize and manage QuickSight assets and users.
Determines whether principals with this custom permission are allowed to create SPICE datasets, with a value of 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Specifies the permission level for dashboards in this QuickSight custom permissions profile, accepting values such as READ_ONLY, READ_WRITE, or DENY to control user access to dashboards.
Controls whether users with this custom permissions profile can use Amazon QuickSight Q to edit visuals, typically set to ENABLED or DISABLED.
This field indicates whether the custom permissions profile allows (ENABLED) or denies (DISABLED) the ability to export QuickSight data to CSV files.
Enables or disables the ability for users with this custom permissions profile to export data to CSV in QuickSight scheduled reports, using ENABLED or DISABLED.
Specifies whether users assigned to this custom permissions profile may export dashboard or analysis data to Excel, with the value set to 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Specifies whether the export-to-Excel in scheduled reports capability is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for users granted these custom permissions in QuickSight.
Determines whether users assigned these custom permissions can export QuickSight dashboards to PDF, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DENIED'.

The export_to_pdf_in_scheduled_reports capability specifies whether users with this custom permissions profile can export scheduled reports to PDF, with the string value typically being 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
This field specifies whether the user is allowed or denied the Flow capability in Amazon QuickSight, with accepted values 'ALLOW' and 'DENY'.
Controls whether QuickSight users can perform Google Calendar actions, such as creating, updating, or deleting calendar events, with allowed values ENABLED, DISABLED, or ALERT.

This string value toggles whether the QuickSight custom permission grants users the ability to include report content (such as charts or tables) in the emails automatically generated for scheduled reports.
Controls whether users with these custom permissions can access and use Amazon Q knowledge bases in QuickSight, typically set to 'ENABLED' or 'DENIED'.
Controls whether users with this custom permission can manage shared folders in Amazon QuickSight, with a value of either ALLOW or DENY.
Determines whether users with this custom permission are granted or denied the ability to use Microsoft Teams actions in QuickSight, with allowed values `GRANT` and `DENY`.
Specifies whether OneDrive actions (e.g., exporting dashboards or reports to OneDrive) are enabled or disabled for the user, with valid values ENABLED or DISABLED.
Specifies whether the principal has permission to use QuickSight's OpenAPI actions, which allow programmatic access to QuickSight's REST API operations.
Controls whether users are allowed to perform PagerDuty actions (such as sending alerts to PagerDuty), with values 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Determines whether a QuickSight user can perform UI tasks in the Flow feature (a visual data preparation experience), with typical values set to ENABLED or DISABLED.
This field maps to the 'PRINT_REPORTS' capability in Amazon QuickSight, determining whether users with these custom permissions are allowed to print reports, with values like 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Specifies whether users with this custom permissions profile can publish QuickSight dashboards without requiring an approval process.
Specifies whether users assigned this custom permissions profile are allowed to rename shared folders in Amazon QuickSight (e.g., using 'ALLOW' or 'DENY').

Capability that allows or denies the SAP Bill of Material action, controlling whether users with these custom permissions can perform bill-of-material operations on SAP data sources (allowed values: ALLOW, DENY).
Determines whether users with these custom permissions are allowed to perform SAP Business Partner actions in Amazon QuickSight, with the value set to 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Controls whether users with these custom permissions are allowed to perform the SAP material stock action in Amazon QuickSight, typically by setting the value to ALLOW or DENY.

Controls whether users with these custom permissions can perform the physical inventory action (such as counting or posting inventory) against SAP data sources in Amazon QuickSight, with allowed values `ALLOW` or `DENY`.
Determines which ServiceNow actions are permitted (CREATE_UPDATE or READ) for a QuickSight custom permissions profile.

Determines whether the custom permissions include the SHARE_AMAZON_BEDROCK_ACTION capability, granting users the ability to share Amazon Bedrock actions (such as AI-generated insights) with other QuickSight users.
Controls whether users with this custom permission can share Amazon Bedrock KRS actions in QuickSight, with possible values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Determines whether users assigned these custom permissions are allowed to share QuickSight assets directly to Amazon S3, with a value of 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Specifies whether the custom permission allows sharing analyses, with value ENABLED or DISABLED.

Determines whether users with this custom permissions profile are allowed to share QuickSight apps (e.g., Q topics, stories, and other app assets) with other users, with string values ENABLED or DISABLED.
Sets the state ('ALLOW' or 'DENY') of the SHARE_ASANA_ACTION capability, controlling whether QuickSight users with these custom permissions can share analyses/dashboards to Asana.
Controls whether the user is allowed to share QuickSight assets (such as dashboards) with QuickSight Chat Agents, with values typically 'ENABLED' or 'DENY'.
Controls whether the capability to share QuickSight dashboards with Confluence is enabled, using the status value ENABLED or DISABLED.
Determines whether this Amazon QuickSight custom permissions profile allows users to share dashboards with other users.
Controls whether users with this custom permissions profile are allowed to share QuickSight data sources, with the value typically set to 'ENABLED' or 'DENIED'.
Controls whether users with this custom permissions profile can share datasets with other QuickSight users, accepting values 'ENABLED' or 'DENIED'.
Determines whether users with these custom permissions can share fact sets, with value 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Controls whether users with this custom permissions profile are allowed to share QuickSight dashboards or analyses via a generic HTTP action, such as a custom URL or webhook.
Defines whether users assigned this custom permission are allowed to share QuickSight assets to Google Calendar, with the string value typically being 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Controls whether sharing QuickSight assets to HubSpot is allowed or denied, with a value of either 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Controls whether a user can share Hugging Face actions (such as ML models or integrations) within Amazon QuickSight custom permissions.
Controls whether the custom permission set grants the ability to share QuickSight analyses or dashboards via Intercom, with a value expected to be 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Controls whether the custom permissions include the SHARE_KNOWLEDGE_BASES capability, which grants users permission to share Amazon QuickSight knowledge bases.
Controls whether the QuickSight custom permissions allow users to share dashboards and analyses to Microsoft Teams, corresponding to the SHARE_MSTEAMS_ACTION capability.
Determines whether the custom permissions include the ability to share QuickSight notebooks with other users (i.e., the SHARE_NOTEBOOKS capability).
Specifies whether users with this custom permission can share QuickSight dashboards and analyses via OneDrive, with valid values 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Specifies whether users with these custom permissions can share QuickSight dashboards by sending them to PagerDuty, typically set to 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Determines whether users with these custom permissions can share QuickSight dashboards and analyses to Salesforce, with allowed values 'DENY' and 'ALLOW'.

Controls the custom permission for the share-with-SAP-Business-Partner action, where the string value (e.g., ENABLED or DISABLED) determines whether QuickSight users can share assets with SAP Business Partner accounts.
Controls whether users with these custom permissions may share SAP physical inventory actions, typically set to 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED' to allow or deny the action.

This field represents the 'SHARE_SAP_PRODUCT_MASTER_DATA_ACTION' capability in Amazon QuickSight custom permissions, which controls whether users with these permissions can share SAP product master data.
Controls whether the SHARE_SERVICE_NOW_ACTION custom permission capability is enabled or disabled, allowing a user to share QuickSight dashboards through a ServiceNow action.
Controls whether users with these custom permissions can share QuickSight dashboards to Slack, where the string value indicates the allowed or denied status (e.g., 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED').
Sets the ShareSmartsheetAction capability to either 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED', determining whether users with these custom permissions can share Smartsheet data sources in QuickSight.
Indicates whether sharing of Amazon Textract actions is enabled ('ENABLED') or disabled ('DISABLED') for this custom permissions profile in QuickSight.
Determines whether the user can share dashboards with Zendesk, with the value typically set to 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Controls whether users with this custom permission can create and manage QuickSight spaces, with allowed values 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
This field enables or disables the 'SUBSCRIBE_DASHBOARD_EMAIL_REPORTS' capability, granting or denying users the ability to subscribe to dashboard email reports.
Specifies whether the Amazon Textract action is enabled or disabled for the custom permissions profile, controlling whether users can use Textract to extract text from documents in QuickSight.
Controls whether the QuickSight Q Topics capability is allowed or denied for the custom permissions, determining users' ability to create and manage topics.
Controls whether the QuickSight user is permitted to enable agent web search, allowing Amazon Q to incorporate external web results when generating insights and answers.
Determines the permission state for users to invoke Amazon Bedrock actions within QuickSight, typically set to 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Controls whether users with these QuickSight custom permissions can use the Amazon Bedrock KRS action, with the string value typically set to 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.

Controls whether the QuickSight custom permissions profile enables the UseAmazonS3Action capability, which allows or denies users access to Amazon S3 actions such as using S3 data sources, typically set to ENABLED or DISABLED.
Controls whether the custom permission set authorizes the use of BambooHR actions in Amazon QuickSight, typically with a value of 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.

This field controls whether the QuickSight custom permissions profile allows the use of Amazon Bedrock models for generative BI, corresponding to the 'USE_BEDROCK_MODELS' capability in the capabilities list.
Sets the ALLOW or DENY state for the USE_BOX_AGENT_ACTION capability, controlling whether users with this custom permissions profile can use Box agent actions in Amazon QuickSight.
Controls whether the custom permission set includes the ability to use the Canva agent action in Amazon QuickSight, enabling users to leverage Canva's design features for creating or editing visuals.

Specifies whether the custom permission set includes the capability to use Amazon Comprehend actions in QuickSight, such as running text analysis or other natural language processing features on data.

Sets the status of the QuickSight capability 'USE_COMPREHEND_MEDICAL_ACTION' in a custom permissions profile, controlling whether users are allowed or denied the ability to use Amazon Comprehend Medical actions in QuickSight, with valid values 'ALLOW' and 'DENY'.
This string field sets the `USE_CONFLUENCE_ACTION` capability in the QuickSight custom permissions, controlling whether users with these permissions can use Confluence actions.
Specifies whether users with this custom permissions profile are allowed to use fact sets in QuickSight, corresponding to the `UseFactSetAction` capability.
Whether the custom permissions profile allows users to use generic HTTP actions (such as connecting to a custom HTTP endpoint as a data source) in Amazon QuickSight.
Specifies whether the Use HubSpot action capability is enabled or disabled for the custom permissions profile, controlling if users can perform HubSpot-specific actions in QuickSight.

Determines whether users assigned to these custom permissions are allowed to use Hugging Face actions in Amazon QuickSight, such as running Hugging Face machine learning models, by setting the USE_HUGGING_FACE_ACTION capability to ENABLED or DISABLED.
Whether the custom permission set includes the USE_INTERCOM_ACTION capability, which grants users the ability to use the Intercom action in Amazon QuickSight analyses and dashboards.
Controls whether the user can use the Jira integration action in Amazon QuickSight, with values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.

Specifies whether users with these custom permissions can use Microsoft Exchange actions (such as connecting to Microsoft Exchange as a data source) in Amazon QuickSight, typically set to 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.

Controls whether the custom permission allows the use of Microsoft Teams actions (e.g., sharing insights or sending dashboard updates to Teams) in Amazon QuickSight, with values typically 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Controls whether users with these custom permissions can use the OneDrive action (for example, exporting dashboards to OneDrive) by setting this capability to ENABLED or DISABLED.

Specifies whether the user or group with these custom permissions is allowed to use QuickSight OpenAPI actions to programmatically perform operations on QuickSight resources such as creating or updating dashboards and data sources.
Determines whether users with these custom permissions can use the PagerDuty action in QuickSight, with a value of 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Sets the USE_SALESFORCE_ACTION capability to enabled or disabled, controlling whether users can perform Salesforce-related actions in QuickSight.

The `use_sapbill_of_material_action` key in the `capabilities` map sets the permission status (e.g., 'ALLOW' or 'DENY') for the QuickSight SAP Bill of Materials (BOM) action when defining custom permissions for a QuickSight principal.
Controls whether the SAP Business Partner action is enabled or disabled for users assigned these QuickSight custom permissions, where the value is typically 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Sets the custom permission capability to either allow or deny the use of the SAP Material Stock action, with allowed values ENABLED or DISABLED.
Determines whether the SAP Physical Inventory action is allowed or denied for the QuickSight custom permissions capabilities, typically set to 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Determines whether the custom permission allows or denies use of the SAP product master data action in Amazon QuickSight, typically with values like 'ALLOW' or 'DENY'.
Controls whether users with this custom permissions profile can use the SharePoint action in QuickSight, such as exporting or sharing content to SharePoint.
Determines whether the `USE_SLACK_ACTION` capability is enabled in the custom permissions, allowing users to use Slack actions to share QuickSight dashboards and reports.
Controls whether users with this custom permissions profile are allowed to use Smartsheet as a data source in Amazon QuickSight.
Indicates whether the custom permissions set includes the QuickSight `USE_TEXT_EXTRACTOR` capability, which grants users the ability to use Amazon Textract actions to extract text from images.
Determines whether the USE_ZENDESK_ACTION capability is restricted (denied) by the QuickSight custom permissions, affecting users' ability to use Zendesk actions in QuickSight.
Specifies the state (e.g., ENABLED or DISABLED) of the View account SPICE capacity capability in QuickSight custom permissions, controlling whether users can view the account's SPICE capacity usage.

aws_quick_sight_custom_permissions.custo.text: The unique name for the custom permissions profile, used to identify and attach it to QuickSight users or groups within the account.

aws_quick_sight_custom_permissions.tags.text: The tags field attaches key-value metadata to the QuickSight custom permissions resource, enabling cost allocation, resource categorization, and IAM-based access control.

aws_quick_sight_custom_permissions.tags..text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to this QuickSight custom permissions resource for identification and organization.
The value portion of a tag key-value pair assigned to the QuickSight custom permissions resource, used for metadata and resource organization.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.aws_account_id.text: The AWS account ID that owns the data set, defaulting to the account used to make the request if not specified.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.column_groups.g.text: Defines a geospatial column group in a QuickSight dataset, specifying which columns are treated as geographic data and the country code used for map rendering.
The list of column names that are grouped together to form a geographical hierarchy (e.g., country, state, city) for mapping in QuickSight visualizations.
Specifies the two-letter country code (e.g., US, GB) that defines the geographic hierarchy and mapping for the columns in this geospatial column group in the QuickSight dataset.
The name of the geospatial column group, which uniquely identifies the group within the QuickSight data set.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.column_level_pe.text: The list of column names that this column-level permission rule applies to, controlling which columns are visible to the users or groups specified in the rule.
The list of Amazon QuickSight user or group principal ARNs that this column-level permission rule applies to, granting them access to the specified columns.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.data_prep_confi.text: Determines the destination table names for the data set after the data prep transformations are applied, mapping each source table to its corresponding output table within the QuickSight data set.
Defines a mapping of physical table IDs to their corresponding source table definitions, used during data preparation for the QuickSight dataset.

Defines the map of data preparation transform steps for the QuickSight dataset, where each entry maps a user-defined step name to a TransformStep object specifying the transform action (such as filter, project, or rename) to apply.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.data_set_id.text: The user-defined unique identifier for the QuickSight dataset within an AWS Region; if omitted, QuickSight generates one automatically.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.data_set_refres.text: Specifies the retry behavior when a QuickSight dataset refresh fails, defining the maximum number of retry attempts and the wait interval between retries.
Configures email notifications to specified recipients when a dataset refresh fails.
Indicates whether the email alert for data set refresh failure is enabled or disabled, with allowed values such as ENABLED or DISABLED.
Specifies the unit of measurement for the lookback window size (e.g., DAY or HOUR), which determines how much historical data is included in the incremental refresh window.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.dataset_paramet.text: Defines a date-time dataset parameter in Amazon QuickSight, specifying its ID, name, value type (single or multi-valued), optional time granularity, and default values for filtering dataset content.
Specifies the default values for a date-time dataset parameter, which is a container that holds a list of timestamp strings to apply when the parameter is not explicitly provided.
Defines the list of static default date-time values (as strings) for a date time dataset parameter, used when no dynamic default value is provided for the QuickSight data set parameter.
The unique identifier for the date-time dataset parameter within the QuickSight dataset.
The unique name that identifies this date-time dataset parameter, used to reference the parameter within the dataset's queries and when configuring parameter controls.
Specifies the granularity of the date-time dataset parameter (e.g., YEAR, MONTH, DAY, HOUR), which controls how the date-time values are interpreted or aggregated in QuickSight.

Indicates the value type of the date-time dataset parameter, which can be 'SINGLE' for a single date-time value or 'MULTI_VALUED' for multiple date-time values, controlling how the parameter is used in dataset filters and queries.
Defines a decimal (numeric) parameter for the QuickSight dataset, specifying its name and list of numeric values.
Defines the default decimal values for the decimal dataset parameter, which are used when no parameter value is supplied during dataset or analysis operations.
The list of static decimal numbers used as the default values for this decimal dataset parameter when no value is provided by the user.
The unique identifier for the decimal dataset parameter, used to reference this parameter within the QuickSight dataset and in dataset operations such as custom SQL or filters.
A unique name that identifies this decimal dataset parameter within the dataset, which can be referenced in custom SQL or other dataset configurations.
Specifies whether the decimal dataset parameter accepts a single value or multiple values, using the enum values SINGLE_VALUED or MULTI_VALUED.
Defines an integer parameter for the QuickSight dataset, including its name, value type (single or multi-valued), and default values.
The list of default integer values for the integer dataset parameter, used when a value is not supplied during dataset refresh or query runtime.
This field specifies a list of integer values that serve as the static default values for an integer dataset parameter in an Amazon QuickSight data set.
The name of the integer dataset parameter, used to reference and bind the parameter value within the dataset's custom SQL or calculated fields.
Specifies whether the integer dataset parameter accepts a single value or multiple values, with valid values being SINGLE_VALUED or MULTI_VALUED.
Defines a string dataset parameter for a QuickSight dataset, specifying its name and list of string values used in queries or filters.
Specifies the default string values for this string dataset parameter, which are used when the parameter is not provided at analysis runtime.
Defines a list of static default values for a string dataset parameter, used as the parameter's default when no value is supplied at runtime.
The name that identifies this QuickSight dataset string parameter, used to reference the parameter in dataset custom SQL (for example, ${param_name}) and dataset expressions.
Specifies whether the string dataset parameter permits a single value ('SINGLE_VALUED') or multiple values ('MULTI_VALUED').

aws_quick_sight_data_set.field_folders.text: Configures field folders, a map of folder names to objects listing the dataset columns that should be grouped under each folder, enabling organized browsing of fields in QuickSight.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.import_mode.text: The import mode for the dataset, which determines whether data is stored in SPICE (in-memory) for fast analytics or queried directly from the underlying data source; valid values are SPICE and DIRECT_QUERY.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.logical_table_m.text: Maps logical table names to their definitions, enabling custom data views over physical tables with transformations, joins, and filters.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.output_columns..text: A description of the output column, providing additional context about the data contained in that column within the QuickSight dataset.
The name of the output column, which defines the column heading in the resulting dataset schema for Amazon QuickSight.
The sub data type of the output column in an Amazon QuickSight data set, which further refines the column's data type, for instance indicating that a string column carries geospatial data.
Specifies the data type of the output column (e.g., STRING, INTEGER, DECIMAL, DATETIME) in the QuickSight dataset output schema.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.performance_con.text: Defines performance settings for the dataset, specifically a list of unique key configurations used to optimize query performance.

Specifies a list of unique key configurations for the QuickSight dataset's performance configuration, where each unique key defines one or more column names that uniquely identify each row, enabling incremental data refresh and performance optimization.
The list of column names that together form a unique key for the dataset, used by QuickSight to identify unique rows for performance optimization and incremental data refresh.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.permissions.act.text: Specifies the list of QuickSight actions (e.g., 'quicksight:DescribeDataSet', 'quicksight:UpdateDataSet', 'quicksight:DeleteDataSet') allowed for the associated principal on the data set.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.permissions.pri.text: The ARN of the principal (user, group, or role) that the permissions entry grants or revokes actions on the dataset.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.physical_table_.text: Defines the physical tables backing the dataset, mapping each physical table identifier to its source definition (relational table, custom SQL, or S3 source).

aws_quick_sight_data_set.row_level_permi.text: The format version of the row-level security dataset, where VERSION_1 is the legacy format and VERSION_2 is the current format supporting additional features such as multiple role hierarchies.
Specifies whether the row-level permission dataset grants or denies access to the underlying data, with valid values of GRANT_ACCESS or DENY_ACCESS.
Specifies whether the row-level permission dataset is currently enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for the QuickSight data set.
Indicates whether row-level security tag rules are enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for the QuickSight dataset.
The name of the dataset column that this row-level permission tag rule uses to map tag values to rows for access control.
The value that, when the tag key's value equals this string, grants access to all rows in the dataset (bypassing row-level permission filtering).
Defines the tag key that QuickSight matches against a user's tag values to enforce row-level security for the dataset.
The delimiter used to separate multiple values within a single tag rule's tag value for row-level permission tag configuration in this QuickSight dataset.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.semantic_model_.text: Configures the dataset's semantic model properties, providing lists of configured and unconfigured semantic model property configurations that map dataset columns to semantic types for Amazon QuickSight Q.

The semantic_metadata list defines the semantic entities and their field mappings for the QuickSight semantic model configuration, enabling natural language query and other semantic features on the data set.
Specifies a list of custom instruction objects that provide additional business context and guidance to QuickSight's semantic model, enhancing natural language query interpretation for the data set.
Contains the inline text of a custom instruction attached to the dataset's semantic metadata, providing explicit guidance to the QuickSight semantic model for interpreting or using the data.
The actual textual content of an inline custom instruction for QuickSight's semantic model, providing specific guidance on how data should be interpreted or processed in the data set.
For an inline custom instruction in the QuickSight data set's semantic model, this object stores the metadata of a document uploaded to Amazon S3 that contains the instruction's content.
The name of the uploaded document that provides custom instruction content for the QuickSight data set's semantic model.

The description field inside semantic_metadata provides a human-readable explanation of the semantic metadata entry, describing the purpose or meaning of the semantic type assigned to a data path in the QuickSight data set's semantic model.
Specifies the free-form text description for a semantic metadata item (such as a column) in the QuickSight dataset's semantic model, providing human-readable business context.

A map of table names to semantic model table definitions, configuring how each table in the QuickSight dataset is modeled for semantic model features such as natural language querying (Q) by defining measures, dimensions, and hierarchies.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.tags.key.text: Specifies the key of a tag applied to the QuickSight data set, enabling resource identification, categorization, and access control.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.tags.value.text: Value of a tag applied to the Amazon QuickSight data set, used to categorize or filter the resource for management, access control, or cost allocation.

aws_quick_sight_data_set.use_as.text: Determines whether the dataset is used as a visual or as a query in AWS QuickSight.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.alternate_da.text: Defines the Amazon Elasticsearch connection parameters, including the domain name, used when this data source connects to an alternate Elasticsearch cluster.
The domain name (endpoint) of the Amazon Elasticsearch Service domain that the QuickSight data source connects to when used as an alternate data source parameter.
Specifies the Amazon OpenSearch domain connection parameters (such as the domain name) used when this QuickSight data source is configured as an alternate data source.
The name of the Amazon OpenSearch Service domain that this QuickSight data source connects to.

This object configures the Athena-specific connection parameters, including the Athena workgroup and optional IAM role ARN, used when this QuickSight data source connects via an alternate data source definition.

Configures the use of AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO) for authenticating to Athena when this alternate data source is used, typically including an enabled flag and the ARN of the Identity Center instance.
When set to true, this field enables IAM Identity Center identity propagation for the Athena data source, allowing QuickSight user identities to be passed to Athena for fine-grained access control.
The ARN of the IAM role that QuickSight assumes when querying Athena for this alternate data source, used to grant permissions to access Athena and the underlying data.
The name of the Athena workgroup to use for the data source connection.
Provides Aurora-specific connection parameters (such as database, host, and port) for an alternate data source connection in a QuickSight data source.
The name of the Aurora database that the QuickSight data source connects to.
The hostname or endpoint of the Aurora database server to use for the connection when this alternate data source parameter is applied.
The TCP port number used when connecting to the Aurora database, such as 3306 for Aurora MySQL or 5432 for Aurora PostgreSQL.
Specifies the connection parameters (host, port, and database name) for an Aurora PostgreSQL database when used as an alternate data source in a QuickSight data source.
The name of the Aurora PostgreSQL database to use for the QuickSight data source connection.
The hostname or endpoint address of the Aurora PostgreSQL database server for this alternate data source connection.
The TCP port number used to connect to the Aurora PostgreSQL database, typically 5432.
Defines the Databricks-specific connection parameters (including host and port) used when this QuickSight data source is configured with an alternate data source.
The hostname of the Databricks workspace or cluster that the QuickSight data source connects to.
The TCP port number used to connect to the Databricks cluster when this data source is used as an alternate parameter set.
The path to the Databricks SQL endpoint used when connecting to this data source, such as the endpoint identifier portion of the Databricks SQL endpoint URL.
Specifies the connection parameters for a MariaDB database, including the database name, host, and port, when used as an alternate data source in a QuickSight data source definition.
The name of the MariaDB database to use when this alternate data source parameter set is applied to the QuickSight data source.
The hostname or IP address of the alternate MariaDB server to connect to for this QuickSight data source.
The TCP port number used to connect to the MariaDB database.

Specifies the MySQL connection parameters (host, port, database, etc.) for an alternate QuickSight data source, allowing the data source to point to a different MySQL instance or cluster for environment-specific configuration.
The name of the database to connect to for the MySQL data source.
The host name or IP address of the MySQL database server used as an alternate data source.
The TCP port number used to connect to the MySQL database for this alternate data source.
Specifies the Oracle database connection properties (host, port, and database name) used when this QuickSight data source is accessed via an alternate data source parameter set.
The name of the Oracle database used for the QuickSight data source connection.
The hostname or IP address of the Oracle database server that QuickSight connects to for this data source.
The TCP port number on which the Oracle database listens for connections.
Indicates whether the Oracle data source connection uses a service name rather than an Oracle System Identifier (SID).
Configures the host, port, and database name for connecting to an alternate PostgreSQL data source in Amazon QuickSight.
The name of the PostgreSQL database to connect to for this QuickSight data source alternate parameters set.
The host name or IP address of the PostgreSQL server used by this QuickSight data source connection.
The TCP port number on which the PostgreSQL server is listening for connections.
Provides the connection parameters for a Presto data source, including host, port, and catalog, when declared under an alternate data source configuration for a QuickSight data source.
The Presto catalog to use for the data source connection, identifying the default schema namespace for queries.
The host name (endpoint) of the Presto server used by this QuickSight data source connection.
The TCP port used to connect to the Presto instance.
Specifies the connection parameters for an Amazon RDS instance, including the database name and the RDS instance ID.
The name of the database to connect to within the Amazon RDS instance.
The identifier of the Amazon RDS instance used as an alternate data source for the QuickSight data source.

Defines the Redshift-specific connection parameters (such as cluster ID, database name, and authentication) used when this QuickSight data source's alternate data source is an Amazon Redshift cluster.
The cluster ID of the Amazon Redshift cluster to connect to for this alternate data source.
The name of the Redshift database that this alternate data source parameters block uses for the connection.
The hostname of the Amazon Redshift cluster that the QuickSight data source connects to.
Configures IAM-based authentication for the Redshift alternate data source, including the IAM role ARN and optional database user that QuickSight assumes to access the cluster.
When connecting to Amazon Redshift using IAM credentials, this boolean indicates whether QuickSight automatically creates a database user for the IAM identity that is used for authentication.
The list of database group names to which the newly created database user is assigned when IAM-based authentication auto-creates the user for this Redshift data source.
For the alternate data source parameters, this specifies the database user name to use when connecting to the Redshift cluster with IAM authentication in a QuickSight data source.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon QuickSight assumes to access the Redshift cluster when using IAM-based authentication.
Configures AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS Single Sign-On) integration for the Redshift data source, specifically controlling whether identity propagation is enabled for the connection.
Enables IAM Identity Center identity propagation for the Redshift data source, allowing QuickSight to use Identity Center credentials when connecting to Redshift.
The TCP port number that Amazon QuickSight uses to connect to the Amazon Redshift cluster when this alternate data source is used.
Specifies the S3 path and location for an alternate data source, used to provide S3-specific connection details when configuring a QuickSight data source.
Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket and object key (the location) of the manifest file that QuickSight uses to define the files and schema for this S3 data source.
The name of the S3 bucket that contains the manifest file for the S3 data source defined by these parameters.
The S3 object key of the QuickSight data source manifest file, specifying the location within the referenced S3 bucket for the S3 parameters of an alternate data source.
The IAM role ARN that QuickSight assumes to access the S3 bucket for this alternate data source parameter set.
Defines the Amazon S3 Tables connection parameters for this alternate data source, including the target table name.
The ARN of the S3 table bucket that QuickSight connects to for querying the S3 Tables-backed Iceberg table.
Specifies the connection parameters for a Snowflake data source, including host, port, database, and warehouse, when used as an alternate data source.
Determines the authentication mechanism (such as basic user/password or OAuth) when connecting to this alternate Snowflake data source.
Specifies the name of the Snowflake database that the QuickSight data source connects to for queries.
Specifies the database access control role for Snowflake, used by Amazon QuickSight to enforce row-level security when connecting to the Snowflake database.
The hostname of the Snowflake server (e.g., account.snowflakecomputing.com) used to connect to the Snowflake data source in Amazon QuickSight.
Specifies the OAuth authentication configuration for connecting to Snowflake, including token URL, client ID, client secret, and scopes.
Specifies the resource URI of the OAuth identity provider used by QuickSight when authenticating to a Snowflake data source via OAuth.
Specifies the VPC connection properties, including the VPC connection ARN, used for the identity provider when QuickSight authenticates to Snowflake via OAuth.
Specifies the ARN of the VPC connection used to reach the identity provider for Snowflake OAuth authentication in a QuickSight data source.
The OAuth scope requested by QuickSight when authenticating to the Snowflake data source via OAuth, determining the access permissions granted to the OAuth token.
Specifies the URL of the external OAuth token provider endpoint that QuickSight calls to obtain a Snowflake access token when authenticating to this Snowflake data source using OAuth.
The name of the Snowflake warehouse to use when connecting to the Snowflake database for this QuickSight data source.
Specifies the Spark-specific connection parameters (host, port, and database) for this alternate data source, used when the data source is a Spark cluster.
The host name or IP address of the Spark server to use for this alternate data source connection.
The port number used for connecting to the Apache Spark data source.

Defines the connection parameters for a Microsoft SQL Server database (such as host, port, database, and optional instance ID) to be used as an alternate data source parameter set for the QuickSight data source.
The name of the SQL Server database that the QuickSight data source connects to.
The hostname of the SQL Server instance that QuickSight connects to when this alternate data source parameter set is used.
The TCP port number used to connect to the SQL Server database for this QuickSight data source.
Specifies the connection parameters for a Starburst data source, including the host, port, catalog, and product type (Galaxy or Enterprise) when defining alternate data source parameters.
Specifies whether authentication to the Starburst data source uses a stored password or an OAuth token.
The catalog name for the Starburst data source, specifying which catalog within the Starburst cluster to connect to.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that AWS QuickSight assumes to access the Starburst database for this data source.
Specifies the hostname or endpoint of the Starburst server that the QuickSight data source connects to.
Specifies the OAuth client credentials (client ID and secret) required to authenticate to the Starburst data source when OAuth-based authentication is selected.
The URI of the identity provider resource used for OAuth authentication when connecting to a Starburst data source in QuickSight.

The VPC connection properties for the identity provider used during OAuth authentication, containing the VPC connection ARN that QuickSight uses to privately connect to the identity provider when accessing the Starburst data source.
The ARN of the VPC connection that the identity provider uses for OAuth access to the Starburst data source, enabling network isolation.
The OAuth scope that specifies the permissions requested when authenticating to the Starburst data source using OAuth.
The URL of the OAuth token provider endpoint used to obtain access tokens for authenticating to a Starburst data source in Amazon QuickSight.
The TCP port number on which the Starburst database server is listening for connections.
Specifies the Starburst product type (e.g., STARBURST_ENTERPRISE or STARBURST_GALAXY) used for the data source connection.
Contains the connection parameters (such as host, port, and database) for a Teradata database when this data source is used as an alternate data source in QuickSight.
The name of the Teradata database to use for this alternate data source connection.
The host name or IP address of the Teradata server that the QuickSight data source connects to.
The TCP port number on the Teradata server to use for the connection, such as 1025 (the default Teradata port).
Configuration block for Trino connection parameters (host, port, catalog) when this QuickSight data source is specified as an alternate data source.
Specifies the Trino catalog name used by QuickSight to access the data source.
The hostname or IP address of the Trino server that the Amazon QuickSight data source connects to.
The TCP port number on which the Trino server is listening, used by QuickSight to establish a connection to the Trino data source.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.aws_account_.text: The AWS account ID where the QuickSight data source resides; if omitted, the account associated with the current credentials is used.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.credentials..text: Specifies the Amazon Elasticsearch domain connection parameters used as alternate data source parameters in the credential pair for a QuickSight data source.
The domain endpoint (e.g., search-my-domain.us-east-1.es.amazonaws.com) of the Amazon Elasticsearch Service domain to use as the data source.
Specifies the Amazon OpenSearch Service connection parameters, including the domain endpoint, used as an alternate data source within a QuickSight credential pair.
The domain name (endpoint) of the Amazon OpenSearch cluster that this alternate data source parameter set uses for QuickSight to connect to.
Specifies the Athena workgroup and related settings for an alternate Athena data source used within a QuickSight data source credential pair.
Configuration for IAM Identity Center authentication for the Athena data source, which contains a flag to enable or disable using identity center credentials.
Enables or disables identity propagation to Athena using IAM Identity Center, so that row-level access control in Athena can be based on the QuickSight user's identity.
The ARN of the IAM role that QuickSight assumes to query Athena when using these alternate data source parameters.
The name of the Athena workgroup to use when connecting to the Athena data source via the alternate data source parameters specified in the credential pair.
Specifies the connection parameters (host, port, database, etc.) for an Amazon Aurora database when included in the alternate data source parameters of a QuickSight data source credential pair.
The name of the Aurora database to connect to when using these alternate data source parameters.
The host name or endpoint of the Aurora database server that QuickSight connects to for this data source.
The TCP port number on which the Amazon Aurora database is listening, used when connecting via the alternate data source parameters for the credential pair.

Defines the connection parameters, including host, port, and database name, for an Aurora PostgreSQL data source used as an alternate data source within the credential pair of a QuickSight data source.
The name of the Aurora PostgreSQL database to use for the alternate data source connection.
The hostname or endpoint of the Aurora PostgreSQL database that QuickSight connects to for this data source.
The TCP port number that QuickSight uses to connect to the Aurora PostgreSQL database when using these alternate data source parameters.
Specifies the Databricks-specific connection parameters (host, port, and SQL endpoint path) for an alternate data source that can be used with the QuickSight data source's credential pair.
The hostname or endpoint of the Databricks workspace that QuickSight connects to when using these alternate data source parameters.
The TCP port used to connect to the Databricks workspace, typically 443 for HTTPS connections.
Specifies the HTTP path to the Databricks SQL endpoint used for the alternate Databricks data source parameters in the QuickSight data source credential pair.

Specifies the MariaDB connection parameters (host, port, database) used for an alternate data source in the QuickSight credential pair, enabling the same username and password to be applied to a MariaDB database connection.
The name of the MariaDB database that QuickSight connects to when using these alternate data source parameters.
The hostname or IP address of the MariaDB database server for the alternate data source connection.
The TCP port number used to connect to the MariaDB database instance as part of the alternate data source parameters for the QuickSight data source credential pair.

The my_sql_parameters object specifies the MySQL data source connection parameters (including host, port, and database name) used when this credential pair is paired with an alternate MySQL data source.
The name of the MySQL database to use for the alternate data source connection in Amazon QuickSight.
The host name or IP address of the MySQL database server to connect to when using alternate data source parameters in the QuickSight data source credentials.
The TCP port number used to connect to the MySQL server when this alternate parameter set is selected for the QuickSight data source.
The Oracle-specific connection parameters (host, port, and database) used as an alternate data source parameter set within the QuickSight data source credential pair.
The name of the Oracle database (service name/SID) to use for the connection when this alternate set of data source parameters is applied.
The hostname or IP address of the Oracle database server used when connecting through the alternate data source parameters.
The TCP port number on which the Oracle database server listens for connections.
Specifies whether the Oracle connection uses the service name rather than the Oracle SID.
Specifies the PostgreSQL-specific connection parameters (such as host, port, and database) for an alternate data source used within the credential pair of this QuickSight data source.
The name of the PostgreSQL database to use for the alternate data source connection in QuickSight.
Specifies the hostname or IP address of the PostgreSQL database server for the alternate data source connection parameters.
The TCP port number on which the PostgreSQL database server listens, used when connecting via the alternate data source parameters in the QuickSight data source credential pair.
Specifies the Presto connection parameters (host and port) to use when Presto is selected as an alternate data source in the credential pair for this QuickSight data source.
The catalog (database catalog) to use when connecting to the Presto data source.
The host field specifies the hostname or IP address of the Presto server used for the alternate data source parameters within the credential pair of this QuickSight data source.
The TCP port on which the Presto server listens for connections, used here as part of the alternate data source parameters for a Presto data source in QuickSight.
Defines the connection parameters for an Amazon RDS database, including database name, host, and port, used as an alternate data source parameter set for this QuickSight data source credential pair.
The name of the database to connect to on the alternate Amazon RDS data source used for QuickSight credential verification.
The identifier of the Amazon RDS database instance that QuickSight uses when connecting to the alternate data source defined by these RDS parameters in the credential pair.
Defines the parameters required to connect to an Amazon Redshift cluster when Redshift is used as the alternate data source for this credential pair.
The unique identifier of the Amazon Redshift cluster to connect to when using this alternate data source parameter.
The database name to use when connecting to Redshift through the alternate data source parameters in the QuickSight data source credential pair.
Specifies the hostname of the Amazon Redshift cluster used by the alternate data source connection parameters in the QuickSight data source credential pair.
Specifies IAM-based authentication settings for the Redshift data source, including the IAM role ARN and database user details.
Whether to automatically create a database user if the specified user does not exist when connecting to Redshift using IAM credentials.

A list of Redshift database group names that the IAM role/user is associated with, used by QuickSight to apply group-based access control when connecting to the Redshift data source via IAM credentials.
The database user name to use when connecting to Amazon Redshift with IAM credentials in this QuickSight data source.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that grants Amazon QuickSight access to the Redshift cluster for this alternate data source parameter set.
Specifies the IAM Identity Center authentication configuration for the Redshift data source, including whether Identity Center is enabled, when used within an alternate data source parameter set.
When set to true, enables identity propagation so that Amazon QuickSight uses IAM Identity Center credentials to access the Redshift cluster instead of static database credentials.
The TCP port number for the Redshift endpoint, provided in the alternate data source parameters to define the connection when setting up the credential pair for this QuickSight data source.
Defines the S3 bucket and path parameters for an alternate S3 data source that may be used with this credential pair in a QuickSight data source connection.
Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket and key (object path) of the manifest file that defines the S3 data source, used within the alternate data source parameters for the QuickSight data source.
The S3 bucket name that stores the manifest file used by the S3 data source parameters.

The S3 object key (path) of the manifest file, such as 'my-folder/manifest.json', that defines the structure and location of data for the S3 data source, used in conjunction with the bucket name to point to the actual manifest file.
The ARN of the IAM role that QuickSight assumes to access the referenced S3 bucket when using these alternate parameters.
Specifies the S3 Tables parameters (including table name and S3 Tables ARN) used as an alternate data source parameter within a QuickSight credential pair, enabling connection to a specific S3 table.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon S3 table bucket used when this S3 tables alternate data source parameter set is applied to the credential pair for the QuickSight data source.

Specifies the Snowflake-specific connection parameters (such as database, host, and warehouse) used when authenticating with an alternate Snowflake data source for this QuickSight data source's credential pair.
Specifies the authentication method (e.g., PASSWORD or OAUTH) used when connecting to the Snowflake data source through the alternate data source parameters.
The name of the Snowflake database that this QuickSight data source connects to.
The Snowflake database access control role used by QuickSight for the alternate data source connection, specifying a role that controls database access and permissions.
The host name of the Snowflake server to connect to, typically in the form 'account.snowflakecomputing.com'.

Defines the OAuth authentication settings, such as token endpoint and client credentials, used to connect to Snowflake through this alternate data source parameter set in a QuickSight credential pair.

Specifies the resource URI of the identity provider (e.g., Okta or Azure AD) used for OAuth-based authentication to the Snowflake data source, as part of the alternate OAuth parameters for the QuickSight data source credentials.
Specifies the VPC connection properties (including the VPC connection ARN) used to access the identity provider (such as Okta) when authenticating with Snowflake via OAuth.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the VPC connection that QuickSight uses to reach the identity provider (IdP) when performing Snowflake OAuth authentication within the credential pair's alternate data source parameters.
Specifies the OAuth 2.0 scope (permissions) requested for the Snowflake OAuth token, determining what Snowflake resources and actions the authenticated connection can access.
The URL of the token provider used for OAuth authentication when connecting to Snowflake, which QuickSight uses to obtain and refresh access tokens.
The name of the Snowflake warehouse to use for this QuickSight data source connection.
Specifies the Spark cluster connection parameters (host and port) used as an alternate data source within a credential pair, allowing QuickSight to connect to a Spark data source.
The hostname or IP address of the Spark server to connect to when using these alternate data source parameters.
The TCP port used to connect to the Spark server when this parameter set is selected, typically the Spark Thrift server port (for example, 10001).

Specifies the SQL Server connection details (such as host, port, database, and instance) used as an alternate data source parameter set when connecting with the associated credential pair for this QuickSight data source.
The name of the database for the alternate SQL Server data source connection specified in the credential pair.
The hostname or IP address of the SQL Server database server that QuickSight connects to when using these alternate data source parameters within the credential pair for the QuickSight data source.
The TCP port on which the alternate SQL Server database listens, used when specifying a secondary set of connection parameters in a QuickSight data source credential pair.
Provides connection parameters specific to a Starburst data source (including host, port, catalog, and product type) for use as an alternate parameter set within a QuickSight credential pair.
Specifies the authentication type for the Starburst connection, with valid values being 'PASSWORD' or 'TOKEN'.
The name of the Starburst catalog to use for the data source connection.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role used for database access control when connecting to a Starburst data source in QuickSight.
The hostname or IP address of the Starburst server that the QuickSight data source connects to.
Specifies the OAuth 2.0 parameters, including the token provider URL and client credentials, for authenticating the QuickSight data source connection to Starburst.
Specifies the resource URI identifying the identity provider (IdP) that QuickSight uses for OAuth-based authentication when connecting to a Starburst data source.
This object specifies the VPC connection properties required to reach the identity provider when authenticating to a Starburst data source via OAuth in QuickSight.
The ARN of the VPC connection that QuickSight uses to reach the Starburst identity provider when authenticating via OAuth.
The OAuth scope string to request during token exchange when authenticating to the Starburst data source, defining the level of access permissions granted to the OAuth token.
The URL of the OAuth token provider endpoint used to obtain an access token when connecting to a Starburst data source.
The TCP port number that QuickSight uses to connect to the Starburst cluster when using alternate data source parameters.
Specifies the Starburst product type (GALAXY or ENTERPRISE) for the alternate data source parameters in a QuickSight credential pair.
The `teradata_parameters` object defines the Teradata-specific connection settings (host, port, database) for an alternate data source referenced in a QuickSight data source's credential pair.
The name of the Teradata database to use for the alternate data source connection.
The hostname of the Teradata server used in the alternate data source parameters for the credential pair.
The TCP port number used by QuickSight to connect to the Teradata database server.
Specifies the connection parameters (host, port, and catalog) for a Trino data source when used as an alternate data source in a QuickSight credential pair.
The name of the Trino catalog to use for the QuickSight data source connection, identifying the catalog (a named collection of schemas) to query against.
The hostname of the Trino server that QuickSight connects to when using this alternate data source parameter set.
The TCP port number on which the Trino database is listening for connections.
Defines the SSH key pair (private key and user name) used to authenticate to the data source when connecting over SSH, as an alternative to username/password credentials.
The SSH username to use with the key pair when authenticating to the data source, typically the username for accessing an Amazon EMR cluster.
The PEM-encoded private key used for SSH authentication to the data source host when using key pair credentials.
The passphrase required to decrypt the private key used for SSH key-pair authentication when connecting to a data source in Amazon QuickSight.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.data_source_.text: The unique identifier for the QuickSight data source, which is required to reference the data source in other resources and APIs; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique ID.
When true, the Oracle 'database' value is treated as a service name rather than a database/SID, enabling connection by Oracle service name.
Specifies the connection parameters for an Amazon S3 Tables data source, including the table bucket ARN and the table name, enabling QuickSight to access data stored in S3 Tables.
The ARN of the S3 Tables bucket that this Amazon QuickSight data source uses as its storage location for table data.
Specifies the authentication method (e.g., PASSWORD or OAUTH) used by QuickSight to connect to the Snowflake database.
Specifies the Snowflake database access control role used to authorize access to the database when connecting to Snowflake, typically used with OAuth authentication.
Configures OAuth authentication parameters for a Snowflake data source, including the token endpoint URL, scope, and client credentials used to authorize QuickSight access.
The URI of the external identity provider (IdP) that grants OAuth authorization for accessing the Snowflake data source.
The OAuth 2.0 scope (a space-separated list of permissions) that QuickSight requests when using OAuth to authenticate to the Snowflake data source.
The URL of the token provider endpoint used for OAuth-based authentication to the Snowflake database.
Specifies the authentication method for the Starburst data source connection, where valid values are PASSWORD or NO_PASSWORD, determining whether a stored password is used for authentication.
The ARN of the IAM role that QuickSight assumes for database access control when connecting to the Starburst data source.
Specifies the OAuth 2.0 token endpoint and client ID used by QuickSight to authenticate to the Starburst data source.
The URI of the identity provider (IdP) used for OAuth token verification when authenticating to the Starburst data source.

This field specifies the OAuth 2.0 scope(s) that QuickSight requests from the Starburst OAuth authorization server when authenticating to the data source, determining the access permissions granted to the connection.
The token_provider_url specifies the OAuth token provider endpoint URL that QuickSight requests an access token from for authenticating to the Starburst data source.
Specifies the Starburst product type, such as STARBURST_ENTERPRISE or STARBURST_GALAXY, for the data source connection.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.error_info.t.text: Specifies the category of the data source connection error (for example, ACCESS_DENIED or COULD_NOT_PARSE) that is reported in the DataSourceErrorInfo structure.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.folder_arns.text: The list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of QuickSight folders to which this data source is added, organizing it within the folder hierarchy.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.name.text: The display name for the QuickSight data source, which must be unique within the AWS account and is used to identify the data source in the QuickSight console.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.permissions.text: Defines a list of resource permissions that grant specified principals (such as IAM users, groups, or roles) access to the Amazon QuickSight data source, including the allowed actions for each principal.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.permissions..text: Specifies the list of QuickSight actions (e.g., quicksight:DescribeDataSource, quicksight:UpdateDataSource) granted to a principal in a resource-level permission entry for the data source.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM user, group, or role to which the permissions in this entry are granted for the QuickSight data source.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.status.text: Indicates the current lifecycle state of the QuickSight data source, such as CREATION_IN_PROGRESS, CREATION_SUCCESSFUL, or CREATION_FAILED, as reported by the AWS API.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs that act as metadata to identify and organize the QuickSight data source.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.tags.key.text: The tag key portion of a key-value pair used to label and organize the QuickSight data source resource.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag key applied to the QuickSight data source, used to store arbitrary metadata for resource management and cost tracking.

aws_quick_sight_data_source.type.text: The type of the QuickSight data source (e.g., S3, ATHENA, MYSQL, POSTGRESQL), which determines the supported connection properties and how data is accessed.

aws_quick_sight_dlpsetting.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of this QuickSight data protection (DLP) setting, which uniquely identifies the setting and is used to reference it in IAM policies and other AWS services.

aws_quick_sight_dlpsetting.aws_account_i.text: The AWS account ID for which the QuickSight data loss prevention settings are configured.

aws_quick_sight_dlpsetting.dlp_setting_i.text: The required DlpSettingId property specifies a unique, user-defined identifier for the data loss prevention (DLP) setting in Amazon QuickSight.

aws_quick_sight_dlpsetting.enabled.text: Indicates whether the AWS QuickSight data loss prevention (DLP) setting is enabled, which activates the configured data protection policies for the relevant assets.

aws_quick_sight_dlpsetting.provider_conf.text: Specifies the configuration for the data loss prevention (DLP) provider in Amazon QuickSight, including provider-specific parameters required to activate and manage DLP settings.
The `microsoft_purview` provider configuration block defines the connection settings for integrating QuickSight's DLP policy with Microsoft Purview as an external data governance service.

The credentials configuration holds the authentication secrets (such as tenant ID, client ID, and client secret) required for QuickSight to connect to and integrate with Microsoft Purview as the DLP provider.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the credentials (such as the client secret) used to authenticate connections to Microsoft Purview in this QuickSight DLP provider configuration.
Maps Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to configured actions (e.g., masking or blocking) that QuickSight applies to protect data in dashboards and analyses.
The action to apply to data when its Microsoft Purview sensitivity label matches the corresponding label in the mapping, such as denying or allowing access.
The identifier of a Microsoft Purview sensitivity label that is mapped to a DLP action in the QuickSight DLP settings provider configuration.
The label_name specifies the name of a Microsoft Purview sensitivity label that this mapping applies to in the DLP provider configuration.
Controls the action applied to data assets that lack a corresponding Microsoft Purview sensitivity label, determining whether QuickSight allows or blocks access to such unmapped data in DLP policies.

aws_quick_sight_dlpsetting.provider_outa.text: Specifies the action QuickSight takes when its configured identity provider becomes unavailable, used to enforce Data Loss Prevention (DLP) controls during outage events.

aws_quick_sight_dlpsetting.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the QuickSight Data Loss Prevention (DLP) setting, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_quick_sight_dlpsetting.updated_at.text: The timestamp of the last update to the QuickSight data loss prevention setting.

aws_quick_sight_flow.permissions.princip.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM principal (user, group, or role) to which the permissions apply, used to grant or restrict access to the QuickSight resource.

aws_quick_sight_folder.aws_account_id.text: The AWS account ID that owns the QuickSight folder; if omitted, the account ID from the AWS credentials is used.

aws_quick_sight_folder.folder_id.text: Specifies the unique identifier (FolderId) for the QuickSight folder, which AWS uses to reference the folder in API calls and as a component of the folder's ARN.

aws_quick_sight_folder.folder_type.text: Specifies the type of QuickSight folder, with 'SHARED' being the only supported value, determining that the folder can be shared with other QuickSight users.

aws_quick_sight_folder.name.text: The display name of the QuickSight folder, which defaults to the folder's ID if not provided.

aws_quick_sight_folder.parent_folder_arn.text: The ARN of the parent QuickSight folder under which this folder is created, enabling nested folder hierarchies; if omitted, the folder is created at the root level.

aws_quick_sight_folder.permissions.text: Specifies a list of resource permissions for the folder, each granting an IAM principal a set of actions such as quicksight:DescribeFolder or quicksight:UpdateFolder.

aws_quick_sight_folder.permissions.actio.text: Specifies the list of QuickSight actions (e.g., 'quickSight:DescribeFolder', 'quickSight:UpdateFolder') that this permission entry grants to the specified principal on the folder.

aws_quick_sight_folder.permissions.princ.text: The ARN of the QuickSight user or group to which the folder permissions are granted.

aws_quick_sight_folder.sharing_model.text: Determines the sharing scope of the folder, either across the entire AWS account (ACCOUNT) or only within a specific namespace (NAMESPACE), controlling which users can access it.

aws_quick_sight_folder.tags.text: A list of tag key-value pairs to associate with the QuickSight folder, used for managing and organizing resources.

aws_quick_sight_knowledge_base.access_co.text: Specifies how access to the knowledge base is secured, such as by configuring row-level security through an associated dataset.
Enables ACL (access control list) enforcement on the QuickSight knowledge base, which controls data access based on ACL rules defined in the access control configuration.

aws_quick_sight_knowledge_base.created_a.text: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the QuickSight knowledge base was created.

aws_quick_sight_knowledge_base.is_email_.text: Indicates whether email notifications are enabled for failures that occur during the ingestion of documents into the QuickSight knowledge base.

aws_quick_sight_knowledge_base.knowledge.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the QuickSight knowledge base in AWS.
Specifies the Amazon QuickSight template used to initialize and configure the knowledge base.
The unique identifier (knowledge base ID) that must be specified to create and reference the knowledge base within Amazon QuickSight Q.
The total size of the knowledge base content in bytes, as computed by Amazon QuickSight.

aws_quick_sight_knowledge_base.media_ext.text: Specifies the configuration for extracting audio content from media files ingested into the QuickSight knowledge base, enabling downstream processing such as transcription and indexing.
Determines whether audio extraction is enabled or disabled for the media extraction configuration, controlling if audio content from media files is processed and indexed for the knowledge base.
Defines the settings for extracting text and data from images in media files associated with the QuickSight knowledge base, including whether image extraction is enabled.
Determines whether text from images in source documents is extracted and indexed, with a required value of `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`.
Provides the video-specific extraction settings that control how textual content is derived from video files within the knowledge base.
Determines whether video files in the knowledge base are processed to extract text and metadata for Amazon QuickSight Q to use when answering questions, with accepted values `ENABLED` and `DISABLED`.

aws_quick_sight_knowledge_base.name.text: The name of this QuickSight knowledge base.
