aws_quick_sight_knowledge_base.permissio.text: The permissions that control access to the QuickSight knowledge base, consisting of a list of resource permission objects that specify which principals (users, groups, or organizations) can perform certain actions on the resource.
The list of QuickSight IAM actions (for example, quicksight:DescribeKnowledgeBase) that the principal in this permissions entry is authorized to perform on the knowledge base.
The IAM principal (user, group, or role) that is granted the specified permissions on the QuickSight knowledge base.

aws_quick_sight_knowledge_base.primary_o.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the primary owner of the QuickSight knowledge base, typically the IAM user or role with administrative ownership.

aws_quick_sight_knowledge_base.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the QuickSight knowledge base, used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_quick_sight_knowledge_base.updated_a.text: The read-only updated_at field holds the timestamp of the last modification to the QuickSight knowledge base.

aws_quick_sight_oauth_client_application.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the registered OAuth client application, which uniquely identifies it for use in IAM policies and QuickSight APIs.
The OAuth client ID that identifies the third-party client application being registered with Amazon QuickSight for embedded analytics.
The client secret associated with the OAuth client application, used by QuickSight to authenticate the application when requesting access tokens from the OAuth authorization server.
The creation timestamp of the QuickSight OAuth client application, returned as a string in ISO 8601 date-time format.
Specifies the type of the external data source (for example, Salesforce) for which this QuickSight OAuth client application provides authentication.
This object specifies the VPC connection properties that allow Amazon QuickSight to reach the identity provider's OAuth endpoints over a private network.
The ARN of the VPC connection used by the identity provider for the OAuth client application, enabling the app to reach the identity provider over a private network.
The timestamp of the last update to this QuickSight OAuth client application, returned as a read-only string.
The name of the OAuth client application, which is required to identify the external application when registering it with QuickSight.
The URL of the OAuth authorization endpoint to which users are redirected to authenticate for the QuickSight OAuth client application.
The identifier of the OAuth client application being registered with Amazon QuickSight.

Specifies the authentication method used by the OAuth client application, with allowed values such as CLIENT_SECRET or JWT_BEARER, which determines how the client authenticates to QuickSight during token exchange.
The OAuth scopes that define the permissions granted to the QuickSight OAuth client application, specifying which QuickSight API actions it can perform on the user's behalf.
The URL of the OAuth token endpoint where the QuickSight OAuth client application exchanges authorization codes or refreshes tokens to obtain access tokens.
This property defines a list of tag objects (each containing a Key and Value) to attach to the Amazon QuickSight OAuth client application, used for resource management, cost allocation, and metadata.
The key of a tag that can be assigned to this AWS QuickSight OAuth client application for identification and management.

aws_quick_sight_refresh_schedule.aws_acc.text: The AWS account ID that contains the dataset(s) associated with this refresh schedule; if not specified, the provider's default account is used.

aws_quick_sight_refresh_schedule.data_se.text: The unique identifier of the QuickSight dataset that this refresh schedule is associated with and will refresh.

aws_quick_sight_refresh_schedule.schedul.text: The schedule object configures when and how the QuickSight dataset is refreshed, specifying the refresh type (full or incremental), the frequency interval (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly), and the time-of-day and timezone for the refresh.
Specifies whether the scheduled refresh is a FULL_REFRESH or an INCREMENTAL_REFRESH of the QuickSight dataset.
The interval of the QuickSight refresh schedule frequency, which must be one of 'DAILY', 'WEEKLY', or 'MONTHLY', and determines how often the dataset is refreshed.
Specifies the day of the week (for example, SUNDAY) on which the QuickSight dataset refresh runs when the schedule frequency is set to WEEKLY.

aws_quick_sight_space.permissions.action.text: The list of QuickSight actions, such as quicksight:DescribeSpace, that the principal in the containing permission entry is allowed to perform on this QuickSight space.

aws_quick_sight_space.permissions.princi.text: Specifies the ARN of the IAM user, group, or role that is granted the permissions defined in this entry for the QuickSight space.

aws_quick_sight_space.resources.resource.text: The ARN of a QuickSight asset (such as a dashboard, analysis, or dataset) that is associated with and managed within this QuickSight space.
The type of QuickSight asset (e.g., DATASET or DASHBOARD) that is included in this space, indicating which resource the entry refers to.

aws_quick_sight_space.tags.value.text: The value of a key-value tag attached to the QuickSight space, used for cost allocation, access control, and resource identification.

aws_quick_sight_theme.aws_account_id.text: The AWS account ID where the QuickSight theme is created, scoping the theme resource to that specific account.

aws_quick_sight_theme.base_theme_id.text: The ID of the base theme that this theme inherits its default styles from, such as MIDNIGHT or CLASSIC.

aws_quick_sight_theme.configuration.typo.text: Specifies the typography configuration for the theme, including the font families that can be used in visualizations.
Specifies the list of font families used in the theme's typography, where each item is an object that identifies a font by name for use in QuickSight visuals.
Specifies the name of a font family (such as 'Arial' or 'Roboto') to apply to text in the Amazon QuickSight theme's typography settings.

aws_quick_sight_theme.name.text: The display name of the QuickSight theme, used to identify it in the QuickSight console and API.

aws_quick_sight_theme.permissions.text: Specifies the list of access permissions for the theme, where each item grants a principal (user, group, or role ARN) a set of allowed actions such as quicksight:DescribeTheme and quicksight:UpdateTheme.

aws_quick_sight_theme.permissions.action.text: Specifies the list of QuickSight actions (e.g., 'quicksight:DescribeTheme', 'quicksight:UpdateTheme') that the principal is allowed to perform on the theme.

aws_quick_sight_theme.permissions.princi.text: The IAM identity (ARN or name) that is granted the specified actions on the Amazon QuickSight theme.

aws_quick_sight_theme.tags.text: A list of key-value tag pairs to attach to the QuickSight theme for resource management and categorization.

aws_quick_sight_theme.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the QuickSight theme, used to categorize and manage the theme resource.

aws_quick_sight_theme.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag assigned to the Amazon QuickSight theme, used to store arbitrary metadata such as environment or owner.

aws_quick_sight_theme.theme_id.text: The unique identifier for the theme, which must be unique within an AWS account and is used to reference the theme in other QuickSight resources.

aws_quick_sight_theme.version.configurat.text: Defines the typography configuration for the QuickSight theme, including the font families and variants used for text elements in visuals and the interface.
Specifies a list of font family objects, each containing the name of a font family (e.g., 'Arial', 'Times New Roman') to be used in the theme's typography.
The name of the font family (e.g., 'Arial' or 'Times New Roman') that is applied to the QuickSight theme's typography configuration.

aws_quick_sight_theme.version.errors.mes.text: The error message describing why a specific theme version could not be created or updated in Amazon QuickSight.

aws_quick_sight_theme.version.errors.typ.text: The type of error that occurred during the creation or update of a QuickSight theme version, indicating the nature of the failure.

aws_quick_sight_theme.version.status.text: Status of the theme version, representing the current state of creation or update (e.g., CREATION_IN_PROGRESS, CREATION_SUCCESSFUL, CREATION_FAILED, UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS, UPDATE_SUCCESSFUL, UPDATE_FAILED).

aws_quick_sight_theme.version_descriptio.text: Specifies the description of the theme version, providing context about the changes or purpose of this iteration of the QuickSight theme.

aws_quick_sight_topic.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the QuickSight topic, which uniquely identifies the topic within AWS.

aws_quick_sight_topic.aws_account_id.text: The AWS account ID that owns the QuickSight topic; if omitted, defaults to the account where the CloudFormation stack is running.

aws_quick_sight_topic.config_options.text: The config_options property specifies topic-level configuration settings for an Amazon QuickSight topic, such as whether Q Business Insights is enabled.

aws_quick_sight_topic.config_options.qbu.text: Enables Amazon Q Business insights for the topic, allowing natural-language queries to surface relevant insights from the topic's data model.

aws_quick_sight_topic.data_sets.text: Configures the datasets that constitute the QuickSight topic, where each list item provides metadata (e.g., dataset ARN and column details) for a dataset included in the topic.

aws_quick_sight_topic.data_sets.calculat.text: Specifies the calculated fields (computed fields/expressions) defined for each dataset in the QuickSight topic, allowing formula-based transformations of the underlying data.
Specifies the default aggregation (such as SUM or AVERAGE) applied to the calculated field when it is used in visuals in the QuickSight topic.
Specifies the list of aggregation functions (such as SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, COUNT, etc.) that are permitted on this calculated field within the QuickSight topic.
Provides an optional user-defined description that explains the purpose or business meaning of the calculated field within the QuickSight topic's dataset.
The calculated field name is a unique, human-readable string that identifies the calculated field within the dataset, enabling references to it from other parts of the QuickSight topic.
Specifies alternative names or synonyms for the calculated field so that QuickSight can match user natural-language queries to the field.
Defines a list of synonym mappings for cell values in this calculated field, allowing QuickSight to match alternative names for the same value when users ask natural language questions.
The exact string value in the dataset that is represented by a list of synonyms, enabling QuickSight to group equivalent cell values under a single canonical term.
Specifies the list of alternate terms that map to a specific cell value within a calculated field, enabling QuickSight's natural language queries to interpret those terms as referring to that value.
Specifies the data role of the calculated field in the QuickSight topic, indicating whether it is a dimension (DIMENSION) or a measure (MEASURE).

Defines the comparison and ranking rules for this calculated field, including whether to use the default sort order, treat larger or smaller values as better, or specify an explicit list of values to control how they are ordered in QuickSight.
Specifies the ordered list of discrete string values that define the custom comparative sort order for the calculated field within the QuickSight topic.
For a calculated field's comparative ordering, this setting decides whether values that are not in the specified list are treated as the smallest (LEAST) or largest (MOST) when sorting.
Controls whether the comparative ordering settings (including custom column order and sort direction) defined in the parent comparative order object are applied to the calculated field.
Configures the default formatting options (such as number, date, or currency settings) that determine how the calculated field's values are displayed in QuickSight visuals.
Specifies how the calculated field's values are formatted for display in QuickSight, such as AUTO, NUMBER, CURRENCY, PERCENT, or DATE.

Provides the detailed formatting options (e.g., decimal places, currency prefix/suffix, or date time patterns) that define how the calculated field's values are rendered under its default display format.
Specifies the text to display in cells that have no value for this calculated field in the QuickSight topic dataset, overriding the default blank cell representation.
The currency symbol (e.g., '$' or '€') that QuickSight prepends to numeric values when the calculated field's default formatting uses a currency display format.

Specifies the format pattern (e.g., 'yyyy-MM-dd') that controls how date values are displayed for the calculated field when using the date display format, within the default formatting options of a dataset in an Amazon QuickSight topic.
Specifies the decimal separator (e.g., COMMA or PERIOD) to use when displaying the calculated field's formatted numeric values.
Specifies the number of digits to display after the decimal point for numeric values in the calculated field's default formatting.
Specifies the grouping separator (e.g., comma, period, or space) used to group digits in the default numeric display format of the calculated field within the QuickSight topic's dataset.
Specifies the text prefix (e.g., '-' or '(') that is prepended to negative numbers in the display format for this calculated field, when a custom negative format is defined.
The suffix string displayed at the end of a negative number in the calculated field's default number formatting, such as a closing parenthesis for accounting-style negative values.
The prefix is a string prepended to the displayed value of a calculated field (e.g., a currency symbol like '$') when using a custom display format in QuickSight topics.
Specifies the text to append to the formatted value in a QuickSight calculated field's display format, such as a currency symbol or percentage sign.
Determines the scaling factor (e.g., thousands, millions, billions) applied to the display of numeric values for the calculated field.
Determines whether blank cells are formatted according to the blank cell format specified in the display format options for the calculated field.
When set to true, this option applies digit grouping separators (such as commas) to the numeric values of the calculated field in QuickSight displays.
When true, disables semantic search indexing for this calculated field in the QuickSight Topic, so it won't appear in natural language search or autocomplete but remains fully usable in analyses.
The formula or expression used to define the calculated field's value within the QuickSight topic dataset.
Specifies whether the calculated field is included in the QuickSight topic, making it available for end users to use in their analyses.
Specifies whether this calculated field should not be aggregated when used in a filter, giving raw values instead of summarized results.
Specifies whether the calculated field is non-additive, meaning it cannot be summed across multiple records (for example, ratios or distinct counts) and requires special aggregation handling.
Specifies a list of aggregate functions (such as SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX) that are not allowed to be used with this calculated field when it is included in QuickSight analyses.

Specifies the semantic type for the calculated field, including its data type and optionally additional sub-type properties (such as country code), which controls how QuickSight interprets the field's values in analysis.
Specifies the cell value that QuickSight treats as false (falsey) for this calculated field's semantic type, enabling boolean interpretation of non-standard values such as '0' or 'No'.

Specifies a list of alternative string values that are treated as synonyms for the falsey cell value of this semantic type, so that any of these values in a cell are interpreted as false when evaluating the calculated field.
Specifies a finer-grained classification for the calculated field's semantic type, such as 'YEAR' or 'MONTH' for a datetime semantic type, to refine how QuickSight interprets and displays the field.
Specifies the string value (e.g., 'true', 'yes', or '1') that QuickSight should treat as the truthy/true representation when interpreting values of this calculated field's semantic type.
Defines additional string values (besides the primary truthy cell value) that should be treated as true when interpreting this calculated field as a boolean semantic type in Amazon QuickSight.
Sets the semantic type name (e.g., YEAR, QUARTER, MONTH) that defines how QuickSight interprets the calculated field's values, typically enabling date-aware grouping or formatting within the topic.
Defines key-value parameters for the semantic type of a calculated field, allowing customization such as date format or numeric precision.
Specifies the time granularity (e.g., YEAR, MONTH, DAY) for the calculated field, determining how date/time values are grouped or aggregated in QuickSight analyses.

aws_quick_sight_topic.data_sets.columns.text: Defines the list of columns from each dataset that are included in the QuickSight topic, specifying their attributes and semantic roles (e.g., dimension or measure) for analysis.

aws_quick_sight_topic.data_sets.columns..text: Defines the default aggregation (such as SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX) applied to this column within the QuickSight topic, which influences how it is aggregated in analyses.
Specifies the list of aggregate functions (e.g., SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MIN, MAX) that are allowed to be applied to this column in QuickSight topic analyses.

Defines a list of synonym mappings for individual cell values in this column, allowing QuickSight to recognize alternative terms users may type when asking natural-language questions about these data values.
Specifies the actual column value that the associated synonyms refer to, allowing QuickSight to recognize alternative names for that cell value.
A list of alternative names (synonyms) for a specific cell value in the column, used to map those synonyms to the actual value for QuickSight natural language querying.
Specifies whether the column in the QuickSight topic dataset acts as a dimension or a measure for analytical purposes.
Provides descriptive text for a column within a QuickSight topic dataset, giving end users context about the column's meaning and purpose during data exploration.
Specifies a human-readable display name for the column, used in place of the physical column name in QuickSight audiences.
The name of the column in the dataset, used to identify this column when defining semantic rules and relationships in the QuickSight topic.
Defines alternate names (synonyms) for the column, allowing users to reference it with those terms in QuickSight natural language queries.

Defines the custom comparative order (e.g., an explicit ordering of values like high/medium/low) for this column in the QuickSight topic, controlling how its categories are sorted and compared in visualizations.
A list of column values that defines the exact sequence in which the column's values are ordered or displayed in QuickSight when the comparative order is set to a specified (custom) order.
Determines whether values not in the comparative order's specified values are treated as least or most when sorting the column.
Indicates whether the column's comparative ordering uses a custom-defined order from the parent 'ColumnOrder' list, with false meaning the default ordering is applied.
Specifies the default display formatting for the column, such as number, currency, date, or string formatting rules applied when the column is used in visuals.
Determines the default display format for the column's values, controlling how numbers, currencies, percentages, or dates are rendered in QuickSight.

Defines format-specific configuration options (such as decimal places, negative value styling, or date/time patterns) that accompany the chosen display format for a column in the QuickSight topic's default formatting.
The custom string that is displayed in the column's cells when the value is null or blank, for example 'N/A'.
The currency symbol (e.g., '$', '€') used when the column's display format is set to currency in QuickSight topic datasets.
Sets the custom date pattern (e.g., 'yyyy-MM-dd' or 'MM/dd/yyyy') used to display date values for the column when the default formatting is applied.
Specifies the character used as the decimal separator when displaying numeric values in the topic column, such as a period or comma.
Specifies the number of decimal places to display for numeric values when the column's default display format uses a fraction-based numeric format.
Specifies the character used to group digits in numeric values (e.g., the thousands separator) when the column's default formatting is displayed in a QuickSight topic.
Specifies the prefix and suffix used to format negative numbers in the column when the display format is a numeric type, such as displaying them with a minus sign or surrounding them in parentheses.
Specifies the prefix string (e.g., '-') that is placed before negative values when this display format is applied in QuickSight.
Specifies the suffix string (e.g., ')' or ' CR') that is appended after a negative number when the negative format is applied to the column's display formatting in a QuickSight topic.

Specifies the custom string that is placed before the displayed value of a column (e.g., a currency symbol or unit label) when the column's default display format is applied in an Amazon QuickSight topic.
The text that appears immediately after the formatted column value in QuickSight, used to append units (e.g., 'kg') or other suffixes to numeric displays.
Configures the unit scale applied to numeric values in the column's display format, allowing values to be shown as thousands, millions, billions, or trillions (e.g., scaling 1,500,000 to 1.5M).
Indicates whether to apply the configured blank cell format to empty cells in the column's display output.
Specifies whether grouping separators (such as thousands separators) are displayed for numeric values in the QuickSight topic column's default formatting.
When set to true, this column is excluded from the topic's index, preventing it from being used in auto-suggestions or natural language query answering in QuickSight Q.
Indicates whether the column is included in the QuickSight topic, making it available for question answering and dashboard building.
When set to true, this column will never be aggregated when used in a filter within the QuickSight topic.
When true, indicates that the column is non-additive, meaning it cannot be aggregated by summing across dimension values in QuickSight (e.g., ratios or percentages).

Specifies the list of aggregation functions (such as SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, COUNT) that are explicitly disallowed for this column in QuickSight topic-based visuals, preventing those aggregations from being applied to the column.

Defines the semantic type of a column in a QuickSight topic dataset, such as whether it acts as a dimension, measure, date, or geographic field, which determines how QuickSight auto-aggregates and displays it in analyses.
Specifies the custom string value that QuickSight treats as a falsey (null/false) representation when applying the column's semantic type to its data.
Specifies a list of string values that QuickSight should interpret as false (falsey) when applying the semantic type to the column, so that those cell values are treated as boolean false in analyses.

Specifies the sub-type classification of the column's semantic type in the QuickSight topic, refining the semantic type to a more specific format such as a date granularity (e.g., 'MONTH' or 'YEAR') or fiscal period.

Specifies the string value in the dataset column that QuickSight should interpret as TRUE when the column's semantic type is Boolean, enabling non-standard truthy indicators like 'Y' or 'Yes' to be mapped to a true condition.
Specifies a list of string values that are treated as true (synonyms for the truthy cell value) when interpreting a column's semantic type in a QuickSight topic.
Specifies the semantic type name (such as 'DIMENSION', 'MEASURE', or 'DATETIME') that defines how the column is interpreted by the QuickSight topic.
Configuration key-value pairs that customize how QuickSight interprets the column's semantic type, such as date format or geographic spatial settings.
Specifies the time granularity (such as DAY, MONTH, YEAR) used to aggregate date/time values for this column in the QuickSight topic's dataset.

aws_quick_sight_topic.data_sets.data_agg.text: Configures the default data aggregation behavior for a dataset in the QuickSight topic, specifying the column to aggregate and the aggregation function (e.g., SUM, AVERAGE, or COUNT) used for semantic queries in QuickSight Q.
Specifies the date granularity (e.g., DAY, MONTH, YEAR) used to aggregate date fields in the dataset rows for the QuickSight topic.
Specifies the default date column name for the dataset within the QuickSight topic, which QuickSight uses when performing date-based aggregations without an explicit date column.

aws_quick_sight_topic.data_sets.dataset_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the QuickSight dataset that this topic data set references, linking the topic to a specific dataset.
Provides a human-readable description for the dataset, helping topic users understand its content and purpose within the QuickSight topic.
Specifies the name of the QuickSight dataset that this topic's data set configuration references, linking the topic to a specific dataset in your account.

aws_quick_sight_topic.data_sets.filters.text: Defines the filter rules that constrain which rows or columns of the data set are available in the QuickSight topic, enabling row-level or column-level security and data scoping.

aws_quick_sight_topic.data_sets.filters..text: Specifies a category filter configuration for a QuickSight topic dataset, used to filter rows based on categorical field values such as specific category strings or a list of categories.
Specifies the match function (such as EXACT, CONTAINS, STARTS_WITH, or ENDS_WITH) used by this QuickSight topic category filter to evaluate field values.
Specifies whether the category filter is a custom filter (CUSTOM_FILTER) or a namespace filter (NAMESPACE_FILTER).
Defines the fixed list of category values used by the category filter to include or exclude matching data in the QuickSight topic.
Specifies a collective constant for a category filter in a QuickSight topic data set, containing a list of values used to filter categorical data.
The list of values that define the collective constant used in the category filter, specifying the set of categories to include or exclude in the filter.
Specifies whether the category filter's constant is a single value (SINGULAR) or a range of values (RANGE), controlling how the constant value is interpreted.
Specifies a single category value used as the constant in the filter condition, matching items exactly equal to that value.
When true, inverts the category filter so that it matches all categories except those specified in the filter's category values, rather than the ones that match them.
Configures a date range filter on a field in a QuickSight topic dataset, specifying a time interval (start and end dates) that determines which data rows are included.
Specifies the start and end date values that define the range for filtering records in the dataset.
Specifies the type of constant for the date range filter, either SINGULAR (a single date) or RANGE (a start and end date).
This object defines the lower and upper bound dates for the date range filter in the QuickSight topic's dataset filter.
The upper-bound (end) date of the date range constant for the date range filter, provided as a string.

This string value sets the minimum (lower bound) date of the range constant applied by a date range filter to a dataset in an Amazon QuickSight topic, defining the earliest date considered for the filtered data.
Indicates whether the boundary dates of the date range filter are included in the filtered results (true) or excluded (false).
Specifies whether the filter is an enforced value filter or a conditional value filter within the QuickSight topic's data set filter.
A plain-text description that explains the purpose or effect of the filter applied to the dataset in the QuickSight topic.
The unique name that identifies this filter within its parent data set in the QuickSight topic.
Specifies alternative names (synonyms) for the filter, which QuickSight users can use in natural language queries to refer to this filter.
Specifies the type of filter (e.g., CATEGORY_FILTER, NUMERIC_RANGE_FILTER, DATE_RANGE_FILTER) applied to a dataset in the QuickSight topic, determining which nested filter configuration is used.
Configures a numeric equality filter for a QuickSight topic dataset, retaining only rows where the specified numeric field's value equals a given constant or parameter.
Specifies the aggregation function (such as SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, or COUNT) to apply to the numeric field before the equality filter condition is evaluated.
Specifies the singular numeric value or numeric range used as the equal-to condition in the numeric equality filter, containing the constant type and the decimal value(s) to match.
Specifies the constant type for the numeric equality filter, which must be set to SINGULAR to indicate a single numeric value is used for comparison.
The singular_constant defines the single numeric value that the numeric_equality_filter matches against the topic's dataset field.
Defines the numeric range filter settings for a dataset filter in the QuickSight topic, including the column to filter, the minimum and maximum values, and whether the boundaries are inclusive.
Specifies the aggregation function (such as SUM, AVERAGE, or COUNT) to apply to the numeric field before the numeric range filter condition is evaluated.
Defines the constant numeric interval (minimum and maximum) used by the numeric range filter to restrict the topic dataset values.
Indicates the constant type for the numeric range filter, with the value RANGE used to define a lower and upper bound for the filtered numeric values.
Defines the lower and upper bound values (minimum and maximum) for a numeric range filter constant in a QuickSight topic dataset, restricting the data to values within that range.
Specifies the upper bound value of the numeric range for the range constant in a numeric range filter applied to a QuickSight topic data set.
The lower bound (minimum) value of the numeric range filter constant, specifying the start of the range to filter on.
Indicates whether the numeric range filter includes the boundary values (true) or excludes them (false).
Specifies the name of the field in the dataset that the filter operates on (the field whose values are used as the operand for the filter condition).

This object configures a relative date filter for a dataset within an Amazon QuickSight topic, specifying how data should be filtered based on a date range relative to a reference date (such as the current date), e.g., last 30 days or this month.
Defines the constant date value and its type (e.g., singular or range) used by the relative date filter to resolve the filter's date reference within the QuickSight topic dataset.
Specifies whether the constant for the relative date filter is a single value (SINGULAR) or a range of values (RANGE).
The singular constant value (e.g., a specific ISO date or a keyword like 'TODAY') that defines the reference point for evaluating the relative date filter in a QuickSight topic dataset.
The relative date function (such as PREVIOUS, NEXT, THIS, or YEAR_TO_DATE) that defines how the relative date filter calculates the date range to include in the QuickSight topic filter.
Specifies the date granularity (e.g., DAY, MONTH, YEAR) used by the relative date filter to compute the relative time range in the QuickSight topic's data set filter.

aws_quick_sight_topic.data_sets.named_en.text: Defines the named entities (semantic business concepts) within each dataset of the QuickSight topic, which are used by Amazon QuickSight Q for natural language question answering.
Specifies the list of named entity definitions that map dataset fields to the semantic properties, roles, and types of a named entity in a QuickSight topic.
The name of the dataset field that this named entity refers to, used to link the entity's semantic definition to a specific column in the data source.
Defines a metric-based named entity by specifying the aggregation (e.g., SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT) and the dataset field it applies to, enabling quantitative measures in a QuickSight topic.
Specifies the aggregation function (e.g., SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT) applied to the metric in the relevant Amazon QuickSight topic's named entity definition.
Specifies the named parameters required by the metric's aggregation function (for example, the percentile value for PERCENTILE) as a map of parameter names to values.
The physical name of the dataset property (column) that this named entity definition references, used when the named entity is defined directly from a property.
Determines whether the property is treated as a dimension (categorical) or a measure (numeric) in the QuickSight topic's named entity definition.

Specifies the semantic usage of a property in a QuickSight topic's named entity definition, indicating whether the property acts as a DIMENSION (categorical attribute), MEASURE (numeric metric), or INHERIT (use the dataset's default property usage).
A human-readable description of the named entity, used to clarify the entity's business meaning within the QuickSight topic.
Specifies the name of a named entity within a dataset of a QuickSight topic, which represents a business concept for analysis.
A list of alternate names or aliases for a named entity, used to match user natural language queries to the entity in Amazon QuickSight Topics.
Defines the semantic classification of the named entity, such as whether it acts as a dimension or a measure, along with an optional subtype for finer categorization within the QuickSight topic.

Specifies a secondary classification that further refines the primary semantic entity type (defined by type_name) for the named entity in an Amazon QuickSight topic, enabling more granular categorization of the underlying data asset.
Sets the semantic type name for the named entity (e.g., 'QUANTITATIVE' or 'DIMENSION'), defining how QuickSight interprets and analyzes the field in the topic.

Defines a map of key-value pairs that customize the semantic entity type for a named entity in a QuickSight topic, for example by setting a date format for a DATETIME type or an aggregation method for a measure type.

aws_quick_sight_topic.description.text: The description of the QuickSight topic, providing user-friendly context about the topic's purpose or contents.

aws_quick_sight_topic.folder_arns.text: The Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the folders that this QuickSight topic is associated with.

aws_quick_sight_topic.name.text: The display name for the QuickSight topic, which is a human-readable label shown in the QuickSight interface.

aws_quick_sight_topic.tags.text: A list of key-value tag pairs to attach to the QuickSight Topic for metadata management, resource organization, and access control.

aws_quick_sight_topic.tags.key.text: This is the key of a tag assigned to the QuickSight topic, which together with the tag value forms a metadata label used for resource identification, access control, and cost allocation.

aws_quick_sight_topic.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag key-value pair attached to the Amazon QuickSight topic, used for metadata management like cost allocation or environment identification.

aws_quick_sight_topic.topic_id.text: The unique identifier for the QuickSight topic, used to reference the topic in other resources and API operations; if omitted, AWS generates a default topic ID.

aws_quick_sight_topic.user_experience_ve.text: Specifies the user experience version for the QuickSight topic, which controls the feature set and UI, such as NEW_UX for the latest experience.

aws_quick_sight_topic_v2.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the QuickSight topic, assigned by AWS when the topic is created.

aws_quick_sight_topic_v2.aws_account_id.text: The AWS account ID in which the QuickSight topic is created or managed; defaults to the account associated with the provider credentials if not specified.

aws_quick_sight_topic_v2.custom_instruct.text: The textual content of the custom instruction to associate with the QuickSight topic, which is displayed to users as guidance when they interact with the topic.

aws_quick_sight_topic_v2.data_set_relati.text: Specifies the relationships among the datasets associated with the QuickSight topic, enabling the topic to understand how to join or relate data from different sources.
The left-hand dataset reference in a data set relation, which identifies the dataset on the left side of a relationship defined in a QuickSight topic.
The list of column names on the left side of a dataset relation in a QuickSight topic, which are matched to the right-side columns to define the join relationship.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the dataset that acts as the left side of a relationship between two datasets in the QuickSight topic.

The right object identifies the right-side field reference in a dataset relation, containing the dataset ARN and field name needed to link that dataset to the left-side field in the QuickSight topic semantic model.
The list of column names on the right-side dataset that are used as join keys to establish a data set relation in a QuickSight topic.
The ARN of the right-side dataset participating in a data set relation within an Amazon QuickSight topic.

aws_quick_sight_topic_v2.data_sets.text: Defines the list of datasets that comprise this QuickSight topic, with each dataset object specifying the dataset ARN and name (and other optional attributes) that the topic uses to build its semantic model.

aws_quick_sight_topic_v2.data_sets.data_.text: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the QuickSight dataset to include in the topic's data set collection.
The name of the QuickSight dataset that the topic's data set definition refers to, used to identify the dataset among the topic's data sets.

aws_quick_sight_topic_v2.description.text: The human-readable summary of the Amazon QuickSight topic, describing its purpose or the data it represents.

aws_quick_sight_topic_v2.folder_arns.text: The folder_arns field specifies the list of Amazon QuickSight folder ARNs to which this topic is associated, allowing the topic to be organized within folders.

aws_quick_sight_topic_v2.name.text: Sets the display name of the QuickSight topic, which is the human-readable label used to identify the topic in the QuickSight console.

aws_quick_sight_topic_v2.permissions.text: A list of resource permissions that grant or revoke access to the QuickSight topic for specific principals (users, groups, or folders), each specifying allowed actions.

aws_quick_sight_topic_v2.permissions.act.text: The list of IAM QuickSight actions (e.g., quickSight:DescribeTopic, quickSight:UpdateTopic, quickSight:DeleteTopic) that the permission entry grants to the specified principal.

aws_quick_sight_topic_v2.permissions.pri.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the principal (QuickSight user, group, or IAM role) that the associated permission actions apply to for this QuickSight topic.

aws_quick_sight_topic_v2.topic_id.text: The unique identifier for the QuickSight topic, used when importing an existing topic or to reference the topic in other resources.

aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection.availabili.text: Indicates the current availability status of the QuickSight VPC connection, using values such as AVAILABLE, UNAVAILABLE, or PARTIALLY_AVAILABLE, which reflects whether the connection is ready for use in SPICE data ingestion.

aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection.aws_accoun.text: The AWS account ID where the VPC connection is being created, allowing you to specify a different account than the one the credentials belong to.

aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection.dns_resolv.text: Specifies the IP addresses of the private DNS resolvers used to resolve domain names for resources in the VPC connection.

aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection.name.text: The display name for the QuickSight VPC connection, used to identify it in the QuickSight console and APIs.

aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection.network_in.text: The Availability Zone where the network interface used by the QuickSight VPC connection is deployed.
The error message returned by AWS when a network interface associated with the QuickSight VPC connection is in an error state, providing details about why that interface is unhealthy.
The AWS-generated ID of the network interface that QuickSight creates and attaches to the VPC connection to route traffic to resources in your VPC.
The current provisioning state of the network interface created in the customer's VPC for the QuickSight VPC connection, such as whether it is available, creating, or deleting.
The ID of the subnet where the QuickSight VPC connection's network interface is created, enabling QuickSight to reach resources within that subnet.

aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection.role_arn.text: The ARN of the IAM role that grants Amazon QuickSight the permissions required to access the VPC and its resources.

aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection.security_g.text: Specifies the list of security group IDs associated with the VPC connection that control network access to the Amazon QuickSight VPC resources.

aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection.status.text: The current lifecycle status of the QuickSight VPC connection, such as CREATION_IN_PROGRESS, CREATION_SUCCESSFUL, CREATION_FAILED, UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS, UPDATE_SUCCESSFUL, or UPDATE_FAILED (read-only).

aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection.subnet_ids.text: The list of subnet IDs within the VPC where the QuickSight VPC connection is deployed, used to route network traffic for the connection.

aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection.tags.text: The tags to assign to the QuickSight VPC connection, consisting of key-value pairs that help identify, organize, and manage the connection within AWS.

aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the QuickSight VPC connection, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to this AWS QuickSight VPC connection, used to assign metadata or categorize the resource.

aws_quick_sight_vpcconnection.vpcconnect.text: Specifies a custom, user-defined identifier for the QuickSight VPC connection, unique per AWS account and Region, which AWS uses to refer to the connection instead of generating one automatically.

aws_ram_permission.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS Resource Access Manager permission, including the AWS account, region, permission name, and version (e.g., arn:aws:ram:us-east-1:123456789012:permission/MyPermission/1).

aws_ram_permission.permission_type.text: Indicates whether the RAM permission is AWS-managed or customer-managed.

aws_ram_permission.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs to associate with the custom RAM permission, used for tagging and categorizing the permission in AWS Resource Access Manager.

aws_ram_permission.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to attach to the AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) permission, used for organizing and filtering the permission in AWS.

aws_ram_resource_share.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the resource share.

aws_ram_resource_share.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS RAM resource share, used for cost allocation and resource categorization.

aws_ram_resource_share.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS RAM resource share, used for categorizing and managing the resource share.

aws_rbin_rule.exclude_resource_tags.reso.text: Specifies the tag key used to identify resources that should be excluded from the retention rule's cleanup (i.e., resources with this tag key will not be affected by the rule).
The value of a resource tag that, when matched on a resource, excludes that resource from the retention rule's effect.

aws_rbin_rule.lock_configuration.text: The lock configuration for the Recycle Bin rule, specifying the lock mode ('governance' or 'compliance') that determines whether the rule can be modified or deleted after creation.

aws_rbin_rule.resource_tags.resource_tag.text: The tag key that must be present on a resource for the Recycle Bin rule to match it.
The value of a resource tag that a resource must have to be matched by this Recycle Bin retention rule.

aws_rds_cluster_snapshot.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to this RDS cluster snapshot, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the snapshot within AWS.

aws_rds_cluster_snapshot.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key assigned to the RDS cluster snapshot, used for resource categorization and cost allocation.

aws_rds_custom_dbengine_version.database.text: The S3 object keys of the database installation files located in the specified S3 bucket (and optional prefix) that define the installation files for this custom DB engine version.

aws_rds_custom_dbengine_version.dbengine.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to this custom DB engine version by AWS, used to reference the resource in IAM policies and other AWS services.

aws_rds_custom_dbengine_version.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to this AWS RDS Custom DB engine version, used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_rds_dbcluster.associated_roles.featu.text: The name of the database feature (such as S3_INTEGRATION or LAMBDA) for which the associated IAM role is enabled, allowing the DB cluster to use that feature through the role.

aws_rds_dbcluster.associated_roles.role_.text: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an IAM role to associate with the DB cluster, enabling the cluster to access other AWS services such as Lambda or IAM database authentication.

aws_rds_dbcluster.dbcluster_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the DB cluster, automatically assigned by AWS when the cluster is created.

aws_rds_dbcluster.dbcluster_resource_id.text: The AWS-generated, Region-unique, immutable resource identifier for this DB cluster (e.g., cluster-XXXXXXXXXXXXXX), used in IAM policy condition keys and resource-level permissions.

aws_rds_dbcluster.storage_throughput.text: Storage throughput in MiB/s for an Aurora DB cluster that uses io1 or gp3 storage, governing the I/O performance of the cluster's storage volumes.

aws_rds_dbcluster.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the RDS DB cluster, used to organize and identify the resource in AWS.

aws_rds_dbcluster_parameter_group.tags.k.text: The key of a tag applied to the DB cluster parameter group, used to organize and identify the resource within AWS cost allocation and management.

aws_rds_dbcluster_parameter_group.tags.v.text: The value of a tag applied to the DB cluster parameter group, used to categorize the resource for cost tracking, access control, and operational management.

aws_rds_dbinstance.additional_storage_vo.text: The amount of storage, in gibibytes (GiB), to allocate for this additional storage volume attached to the RDS DB instance.
The number of provisioned IOPS to allocate for the additional storage volume on the RDS instance, applicable when the volume's storage type is a provisioned-IOPS type such as io1 or io2.
The maximum storage size, in gigabytes, to which this additional storage volume can be automatically scaled when automatic storage expansion is enabled for the DB instance.
Specifies the storage throughput in MiB/s for the additional storage volume when using the gp3 storage type.
Specifies the name of an additional storage volume for the DB instance, which must be unique among all additional storage volumes on the instance.

aws_rds_dbinstance.associated_roles.feat.text: The name of the feature (e.g., S3_INTEGRATION) that the associated IAM role enables for the DB instance, such as allowing Amazon S3 integration.

aws_rds_dbinstance.associated_roles.role.text: The ARN of the IAM role to associate with the DB instance, enabling the instance to make API calls to other AWS services like S3 or Lambda on your behalf.

aws_rds_dbinstance.dbi_resource_id.text: The AWS-generated unique identifier for the RDS DB instance, used for IAM resource-level permissions and other AWS service integrations.

aws_rds_dbinstance.dbinstance_arn.text: Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the RDS DB instance.

aws_rds_dbinstance.dbinstance_status.text: The current lifecycle status of the RDS DB instance, e.g. 'available', 'creating', 'modifying', or 'deleting'.

aws_rds_dbinstance.instance_create_time.text: The timestamp indicating when the DB instance was created, typically in ISO 8601 format.

aws_rds_dbinstance.is_storage_config_upg.text: Reports whether an available storage configuration upgrade (e.g., from gp2 to gp3 storage type) exists for the DB instance.

aws_rds_dbinstance.latest_restorable_tim.text: The latest time, in UTC, to which the DB instance can be restored using point-in-time recovery, returned as a timestamp string (e.g., 2023-12-01T18:00:00Z) that updates as new backups are taken.

aws_rds_dbinstance.percent_progress.text: The progress, as a percentage, of a major version upgrade or database restoration for the DB instance, as reported by the AWS RDS API.

aws_rds_dbinstance.processor_features.na.text: The name of the processor feature to configure for the RDS DB instance, such as 'coreCount' or 'threadsPerCore', used to set the desired CPU core count and threads per core.

aws_rds_dbinstance.processor_features.va.text: Specifies the value for a processor feature (e.g., enabling or disabling Intel Turbo Boost) for a supported DB instance class.

aws_rds_dbinstance.read_replica_dbcluste.text: Lists the identifiers of the Aurora DB clusters for which this DB instance is a read replica, as reported by RDS after creation.

aws_rds_dbinstance.read_replica_dbinstan.text: A list of identifiers for any read replicas attached to this RDS DB instance, as reported by the AWS RDS describe-db-instances API.

aws_rds_dbinstance.resume_full_automatio.text: The timestamp indicating when the RDS Custom DB instance will automatically resume full automation mode after a pause, present only when the instance's automation is in a paused state.

aws_rds_dbinstance.secondary_availabilit.text: The Availability Zone of the standby DB instance in a Multi-AZ deployment, automatically populated by AWS and read-only.

aws_rds_dbinstance.status_infos.text: The status_infos field is a read-only list of status information objects for the DB instance, each containing a status type, status value, a descriptive message, and a boolean indicating whether the status is normal.

aws_rds_dbinstance.status_infos.message.text: The status message returned by RDS for a DB instance's status information entry, such as the reason behind a read replica or maintenance status.

aws_rds_dbinstance.status_infos.normal.text: Indicates whether the RDS DB instance is operating normally with no issues for this particular status info entry, as returned by the RDS DescribeDBInstances API's DBInstanceStatusInfo object.

aws_rds_dbinstance.status_infos.status.text: The status of a read replica's replication, as reported in the RDS API's StatusInfos list.

aws_rds_dbinstance.status_infos.status_t.text: Indicates the type of an RDS DB instance status entry (e.g., 'read replication') within the status_infos list, which categorizes a particular status message.

aws_rds_dbinstance.tags.value.text: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the DB instance, used for metadata, cost allocation, and resource management in Amazon RDS.

aws_rds_dbinstance.tde_credential_arn.text: The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) password for an Oracle DB instance, used to encrypt or decrypt the database.

aws_rds_dbinstance.tde_credential_passwo.text: The password that corresponds to the TDE credential ARN, used to access the Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) key for an Oracle DB instance.

aws_rds_dbparameter_group.dbparameter_gr.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the DB parameter group in AWS, automatically assigned by RDS when the group is created.

aws_rds_dbparameter_group.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to attach to the DB parameter group.

aws_rds_dbparameter_group.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag assigned to the RDS DB parameter group, enabling custom metadata such as environment, owner, or cost center.

aws_rds_dbproxy.auth.auth_scheme.text: Specifies the authentication scheme the RDS proxy uses when connecting to the database engine, such as SECRETS for AWS Secrets Manager-based credentials.

aws_rds_dbproxy.auth.client_password_aut.text: Specifies the password authentication method the DB proxy uses for client connections, such as MYSQL_NATIVE_PASSWORD or MYSQL_CACHING_SHA2_PASSWORD for MySQL, or POSTGRES_SCRAM_SHA_256 for PostgreSQL, enabling compatibility with the client's password hashing scheme.

aws_rds_dbproxy.auth.description.text: A user-supplied description for this authentication entry, helping identify the purpose of the IAM role or secret used to connect to the DB proxy.

aws_rds_dbproxy.auth.iamauth.text: Indicates whether IAM authentication is required or disabled for connections to the DB proxy using this authentication configuration, with allowed values 'REQUIRED' or 'DISABLED'.

aws_rds_dbproxy.auth.secret_arn.text: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the database user credentials used by this auth configuration for the RDS proxy.

aws_rds_dbproxy.tags.value.text: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the RDS DB proxy, used for organizing and identifying the resource (e.g., by environment or cost center).

aws_rds_dbproxy_endpoint.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag assigned to the RDS DB Proxy endpoint for identification and resource management.

aws_rds_dbproxy_target_group.connection_.text: Configures the connection pool for the DB proxy target group, including maximum connections percentage, maximum idle connections percentage, connection borrow timeout, and session pinning filters.

aws_rds_dbproxy_target_group.dbcluster_i.text: A list of identifiers of Aurora DB clusters that this RDS Proxy target group is associated with, enabling the proxy to route database connections to the specified clusters.

aws_rds_dbproxy_target_group.dbinstance_.text: Specifies the list of identifiers for the RDS DB instances that are associated with this DB proxy target group.

aws_rds_dbsecurity_group.dbsecurity_grou.text: Specifies the ingress rules (CIDR IP ranges or EC2 security groups) that are granted network access to the DB instances associated with this DB security group.
The CIDR-format IPv4 address range (e.g., 10.0.0.0/24) authorized by this ingress rule to access the associated RDS DB security group.
Specifies the ID of the EC2 security group whose instances are allowed to access the DB instances associated with this DB security group.
The name of the EC2 security group that is allowed to access the RDS database, used in an ingress rule for the DB security group.
Specifies the AWS account ID of the owner of the EC2 security group referenced in the ingress rule, which is required when that security group belongs to a different AWS account.

aws_rds_dbsecurity_group.ec2_vpc_id.text: Specifies the ID of the Amazon VPC in which to create the RDS DB security group, allowing the group to control network access to DB instances inside that VPC.

aws_rds_dbsecurity_group.group_descripti.text: A user-supplied description for the DB security group, which is required and helps identify the group's purpose.

aws_rds_dbsecurity_group.id.text: The unique identifier for the DB security group, which is the security group name.

aws_rds_dbsecurity_group.tags.text: A list of key-value tags to assign to the DB security group for metadata and cost allocation.

aws_rds_dbsecurity_group_ingress.cidrip.text: The CIDR IP range (in the form x.x.x.x/x) that is authorized to access instances in the DB security group.

aws_rds_dbsecurity_group_ingress.dbsecur.text: The name of the DB security group to which this ingress rule is added.

aws_rds_dbsecurity_group_ingress.ec2_sec.text: Specifies the ID of the EC2 security group whose traffic is authorized for ingress to the associated RDS DB security group.
The name of the EC2 security group to authorize for ingress to the RDS DB security group.
The AWS account ID of the owner of the EC2 security group referenced by the EC2SecurityGroupName property, used when the security group belongs to a different AWS account.

aws_rds_global_cluster.global_endpoint.text: The global endpoint of the RDS global cluster, containing the address and port used to connect to the primary (writer) instance for read/write operations.

aws_redshift_cluster.endpoint.text: The endpoint object provides the DNS address and port used to connect to the Redshift cluster.

aws_redshift_cluster.logging_properties.text: Configures Amazon Redshift audit logging to an S3 bucket, specifying the destination bucket and optional key prefix for log files.

aws_redshift_cluster.owner_account.text: The AWS account ID of the owner of the snapshot from which the Redshift cluster is being restored, used when restoring from a snapshot in another account.

aws_redshift_cluster.tags.value.text: Specifies the value component of a user-defined tag attached to the Amazon Redshift cluster, used for resource organization, cost allocation, and access control via the tag key-value pair.

aws_redshift_cluster_parameter_group.tag.text: Specifies the key of a tag to attach to the Redshift cluster parameter group, enabling metadata-based identification and management of the resource.

aws_redshift_cluster_security_group.desc.text: The required description for the Redshift cluster security group, which provides a human-readable explanation of the security group's purpose.

aws_redshift_cluster_security_group.id.text: The unique identifier of the Redshift cluster security group, which is the cluster security group name.

aws_redshift_cluster_security_group.tags.text: A list of tag objects (key and value) used to assign metadata to the Redshift cluster security group for cost tracking and resource management.
The value portion of a tag attached to the Redshift cluster security group, used for labeling and identifying the resource.

aws_redshift_cluster_security_group_ingr.text: The IPv4 CIDR range that is allowed inbound access to the Redshift cluster's security group; you must specify either this value or an EC2 security group.
The name of the Redshift cluster security group to which the ingress rule is being added.

aws_redshift_cluster_subnet_group.tags.k.text: The key of a tag applied to the Redshift cluster subnet group, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_redshift_endpoint_access.vpc_securit.text: The current status of a VPC security group associated with the Amazon Redshift endpoint access, indicating whether the security group association is active, being authorized, or being revoked.
The ID of a VPC security group associated with the Redshift endpoint access, used to control network access to the endpoint.

aws_redshift_endpoint_authorization.acco.text: The AWS account ID of the customer to be authorized to access the Redshift cluster's VPC endpoint.

aws_redshift_endpoint_authorization.gran.text: The AWS account ID that is granted access to the cluster's endpoint, returned as a computed read-only attribute.

aws_redshift_event_subscription.tags.key.text: The key name of a tag assigned to this Redshift event subscription, used for management and identifying the resource.

aws_redshift_event_subscription.tags.val.text: The value of a key-value tag attached to the AWS Redshift event subscription, used for identifying and managing the resource.

aws_redshift_scheduled_action.end_time.text: The UTC date and time after which the scheduled action no longer runs; if omitted, the action continues indefinitely until disabled or deleted.

aws_redshift_serverless_namespace.namesp.text: The 'namespace' attribute is a computed, read-only object containing the fully resolved properties of the created Redshift Serverless namespace, such as its Amazon Resource Name (ARN), namespace ID, and status, as returned by the AWS API.

The date and time when the Redshift Serverless namespace was created, expressed as a string timestamp.
The name of the initial database to create within the Redshift Serverless namespace when it is provisioned, defaulting to 'dev' if not specified.
The ARN of the IAM role to set as the default for the namespace, which Redshift Serverless uses to access other AWS services on behalf of the namespace.
The list of IAM role ARNs that the Redshift Serverless namespace can assume to access other AWS services, such as Amazon S3 for data loading or unloading and Redshift Spectrum queries.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this Redshift Serverless namespace.
The unique identifier (UUID) assigned by AWS to the Redshift Serverless namespace, which is used to reference the namespace in other operations.
Sets the unique name for the Redshift Serverless namespace, which serves as its identifier in the account and region.
The current state of the Redshift Serverless namespace, such as AVAILABLE, MODIFYING, or DELETING, reflecting its lifecycle and operational readiness.

aws_redshift_serverless_namespace.snapsh.text: The customer-managed AWS KMS key ID or ARN that encrypts Redshift Serverless snapshot copies sent to the destination region or account defined in this snapshot copy configuration.

aws_redshift_serverless_namespace.tags.k.text: The key portion of a tag assigned to the Redshift Serverless namespace for resource organization and cost tracking.

aws_redshift_serverless_namespace.tags.v.text: The value part of a key-value tag applied to the Redshift Serverless namespace, used for organizing, tracking, and managing the resource within AWS.

The administrator username for the Redshift Serverless namespace at the time the snapshot was created.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Redshift Serverless namespace that this snapshot is associated with.
The name of the Redshift Serverless namespace from which the snapshot is created, identifying the source namespace whose data is captured in the snapshot.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Redshift Serverless snapshot.
The creation time of the Redshift Serverless snapshot, typically a computed ISO 8601 timestamp returned by AWS.
The user-defined name of the Redshift Serverless snapshot, used to uniquely identify the snapshot within its namespace.
The current lifecycle status of the serverless snapshot, indicating whether it is AVAILABLE, CREATING, DELETING, or in another state.

aws_redshift_serverless_snapshot.tags.ke.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to an Amazon Redshift Serverless snapshot, used to organize and identify the snapshot for cost allocation and management.

aws_redshift_serverless_snapshot.tags.va.text: The value for a tag key assigned to the Redshift Serverless snapshot, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

Sets the numeric price performance target level (0-100) for the Redshift Serverless workgroup, controlling the balance between cost and query performance.
The status of the price performance target for the workgroup, indicating whether the target is currently enabled or disabled.

aws_redshift_serverless_workgroup.tags.v.text: The value of a tag attached to the Redshift Serverless workgroup, used for cost allocation and resource organization.

aws_redshift_serverless_workgroup.track_.text: The name of the track (for example, 'current') that specifies the Amazon Redshift Serverless version or release used by the workgroup.

aws_redshift_serverless_workgroup.workgr.text: The `workgroup` computed attribute contains the full set of properties of the created Redshift Serverless workgroup, including its ARN, ID, status, and configuration details, as returned by the AWS API.

The base data processing capacity of the Redshift Serverless workgroup, specified in Redshift Processing Units (RPUs), which determines the minimum amount of compute resources allocated to the workgroup.
Specifies a list of key-value pairs that configure database parameters for the Redshift Serverless workgroup, such as query and session settings.
The name (key) of a configuration parameter to set on the Redshift Serverless workgroup, identifying the specific setting being applied.
The value assigned to a configuration parameter for a Redshift Serverless workgroup, where the parameter key (e.g., max_capacity) determines the setting being applied.
Represents the creation date of the Redshift Serverless workgroup, stored as a string in ISO 8601 timestamp format.
The JDBC/ODBC connection endpoint (address and port) for the Redshift Serverless workgroup, used by clients to connect to the data warehouse.
The DNS address of the VPC endpoint for the Redshift Serverless workgroup, used to connect to the workgroup's data.
The TCP port number on which the Redshift Serverless workgroup's endpoint listens for client connections.

The identifier of the VPC endpoint (e.g., vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h8) that is attached to the workgroup's endpoint for private connectivity.
The ID of the VPC in which the VPC endpoint providing connectivity to the Redshift Serverless workgroup is provisioned.
When enabled, forces all network traffic between the Redshift Serverless workgroup and other services to route through your VPC instead of over the public internet, enhancing security and isolation.
Specifies the maximum compute capacity for the workgroup, in Redshift Processing Units (RPUs), which determines the maximum amount of compute resources available for query processing.
The name of the namespace to which this Redshift Serverless workgroup is attached, determining the database and data resources the workgroup can access.

Configures the price-performance target for the Redshift Serverless workgroup, where an enabled flag and a level value control how the service balances query performance against cost by automatically adjusting capacity.
Sets the price-performance target level (0-100) for the Redshift Serverless workgroup, controlling the trade-off between cost and query performance where higher levels increase performance and cost.
Specifies whether the price performance target is enabled or disabled for the workgroup, with allowed values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Specifies whether the Redshift Serverless workgroup's endpoint can be accessed from the public internet (true) or is restricted to the associated VPC (false).

aws_refactor_spaces_application.api_gate.text: The read-only identifier of the Amazon API Gateway proxy that AWS Refactor Spaces associates with this application, serving as the endpoint for incoming traffic.

aws_refactor_spaces_application.vpc_link.text: The ID of the VPC link that the Refactor Spaces application uses to connect to the VPC.

The effective availability service level objective (SLO) value expressed as a percentage, computed from the applied resiliency policies for the Resilience Hub application.

The name of the resiliency policy that governs the multi-AZ disaster recovery approach, determining the recovery point objective and recovery time objective for an application when an Availability Zone disruption occurs.
The effective recovery point objective (RPO) value for the multi-availability-zone (AZ) failure domain, resolved from the resiliency policy applied to this service.
The effective Recovery Point Objective (RPO) in seconds for workloads deployed across multiple Availability Zones, as derived from the applied resiliency policy.
The effective Recovery Time Objective (RTO) for a multi-AZ outage, as derived from the resiliency policy applied to the service.
The name of the resiliency policy that defines the recovery time objective (RTO) for multi-AZ deployments.
The effective recovery time objective (RTO) in seconds for a multi-AZ deployment, representing the maximum acceptable downtime for that tier.
Specifies the multi-region disaster recovery approach (e.g., active-active or active-passive) that is applied to the application as defined in the effective resilience policy.
Specifies the recovery point objective (RPO) that the application must meet in the event of a multi-region disruption, representing the maximum tolerable data loss across AWS Regions.
The effective recovery point objective (RPO) in seconds for workloads that rely on failover across multiple AWS Regions, as determined by the applied resiliency policy.

The effective multi-region Recovery Time Objective (RTO) value, an object that defines the maximum allowable downtime for workloads when failing over to another region, as computed from the service's effective policy evaluation.
The name of the resiliency policy that defines the effective recovery time objective (RTO) for multi-region failover for the service.
The effective recovery time objective (RTO) in seconds for multi-region configurations, as calculated by the associated AWS Resilience Hub policy.

aws_resilience_hub_v2_service.input_sour.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudFormation stack that defines the resources for this input source's resource configuration in the Resilience Hub service.
The S3 URL of the design file (e.g., a CloudFormation or Terraform template) that defines the resource configuration for the associated input source in the AWS Resilience Hub service.
Configures an Amazon EKS cluster as an input source for the Resilience Hub service, specifying the cluster to be discovered and included in resilience assessments.
The ARN of the Amazon EKS cluster that this EKS resource configuration refers to, used to identify the cluster for resilience discovery and assessment.
Specifies the list of Kubernetes namespaces within the EKS cluster that are used to scope the resilience assessment for this input source.
Specifies the list of key-value tag objects to associate with the resource configuration of an input source, enabling you to categorize and identify the underlying AWS resource in AWS Resilience Hub.
The tag key that, together with the tag value, forms a resource tag entry used to identify or filter resources within the resource configuration of an input source for the Resilience Hub service.
Specifies the S3 or Git URL of the Terraform state file that AWS Resilience Hub uses to import the resource configuration and assess the resilience of the application.

aws_resilience_hub_v2_service.permission.text: Describes the IAM permission model for how AWS Resilience Hub accesses a protected application's resources, including the model type (e.g., role-based or legacy IAM user), the invoker role name, and optional cross-account role ARNs.
The ARN of an IAM role in another AWS account that AWS Resilience Hub can assume to access and assess resources in that account as part of this permission model.

The external ID that AWS Resilience Hub includes when assuming the cross-account IAM role listed in `permission_model.cross_account_role_arns`, so the role trust policy can verify it via the `sts:ExternalId` condition to prevent confused deputy attacks.

aws_resilience_hub_v2_service.report_con.text: Configures the S3 destination (bucket name and object prefix) where AWS Resilience Hub writes the generated report for this service.
The AWS account ID of the owner of the S3 bucket where resilience assessment reports are delivered.
Specifies the S3 bucket path (key prefix) under which the resilience report output files are stored.

aws_resource_explorer2_default_view_asso.text: The ARN of the Resource Explorer view that will be set as the default view for the account.

aws_resource_explorer2_index.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Resource Explorer index, assigned by AWS when the index is created.

aws_resource_explorer2_index.index_state.text: The current lifecycle state of the index, such as ACTIVE, CREATING, UPDATING, or DELETING, as reported by AWS Resource Explorer.

aws_resource_explorer2_index.type.text: Specifies the index type, either LOCAL (indexes resources in your account and region) or AGGREGATOR (aggregates indices from multiple accounts and regions).

aws_resource_explorer2_view.filters.text: Specifies the query filter string that determines which resources are included in this Resource Explorer view.

aws_resource_explorer2_view.filters.filt.text: The Resource Explorer query string that defines which resources are included in the view, using the same syntax as the Search API (e.g., filtering by resource type, tags, or resource properties).

aws_resource_explorer2_view.included_pro.text: Specifies the list of resource property names (each as an 'IncludedProperty' object) to include in the view, controlling which resource properties are returned for resources in the view's search results.
The name of a single resource property to include in the view's output, such as 'InstanceId' or 'Tags' for an EC2 instance, determining which fields are returned for each resource in the view.

aws_resource_explorer2_view.scope.text: The scope specifies the AWS Region (or the literal value 'global' to include all Regions) whose resources this view can search, defaulting to the Region of the CloudFormation stack when omitted.

aws_resource_explorer2_view.tags.text: The Tags property specifies custom key-value pairs to attach to this AWS Resource Explorer view, which you can use to categorize, identify, and manage the view within AWS.

aws_resource_explorer2_view.view_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this Resource Explorer view.

aws_resource_explorer2_view.view_name.text: The user-specified name for the Resource Explorer view, which uniquely identifies the view within your account and Region.

aws_resource_groups_group.configuration.text: Specifies the configuration items that define the resource group, including the type of query (e.g., TagBased or CloudFormationStackBased) and associated parameters.

aws_resource_groups_group.configuration..text: A list of parameter objects (each with a name and values) that configure a configuration item of the resource group, such as specifying the tag key and value for a tag-based group membership query.

The parameter name (key) in a configuration item for an AWS Resource Group, which identifies what the corresponding values apply to (for example, a tag key or resource-specific filter used by the configuration type).
The list of string values assigned to a parameter key in a resource group configuration item, such as the resource types or query criteria that define the group's membership.
The resource type that the query targets, such as 'AWS::EC2::Instance', used to select which resources are included in the resource group.

aws_resource_groups_group.resource_query.text: Specifies the resource query that defines the membership of the group, including the query type (such as TAG_FILTERS) and the underlying query constraints (e.g., resource type filters and tag filters).

The query string that defines the resource selection criteria for the group, expressed using the AWS Resource Groups query syntax (either a JSON object of tag filters and resource type filters, or a CloudFormation stack identifier).

Limits the resources returned by the resource query to only those whose AWS resource types match one of the specified values (e.g., AWS::EC2::Instance), thereby narrowing the set of resources included in the group.
This field specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the CloudFormation stack whose resources are included in the resource group when the resource query type is CLOUDFORMATION_STACK.
Defines the list of tag filters (each containing a tag key and optional set of tag values) that the resource query uses to determine which AWS resources are included in the resource group.
The tag key used to filter resources when defining the group's resource query.
The list of tag values that, combined with the tag filter's key, determine which resources are included in the resource group's query results.
Specifies the type of resource query used to define the group's membership, such as TAG_FILTERS_1_0 for tag-based grouping or CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_1_0 for grouping by CloudFormation stack.

aws_resource_groups_group.resources.text: Specifies the Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the AWS resources to include in this resource group.

aws_resource_groups_group.tags.text: Specifies the metadata tags to attach to the resource group, which are key-value pairs used for cost allocation, access control, and identifying the group.

aws_resource_groups_group.tags.key.text: Specifies the key portion of a key-value tag that can be applied to the AWS Resource Groups group for identification and cost tracking.

aws_robo_maker_fleet.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the RoboMaker fleet, automatically assigned by AWS when the fleet is created.

aws_robo_maker_robot.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS RoboMaker robot within your AWS account.

aws_robo_maker_robot_application.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this AWS RoboMaker robot application.

aws_robo_maker_robot_application.sources.text: Specifies the processor architecture (X86_64, ARM64, or ARMHF) that the robot application source bundle is built for, as part of the source's S3 location configuration.
The name of the S3 bucket that stores the robot application source archive, which AWS RoboMaker uses to deploy the application to robot devices.
The S3 object key (path) of the robot application source bundle, which combined with the S3 bucket identifies the uploaded application archive for the RoboMaker robot application.

aws_robo_maker_robot_application_version.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or name of the AWS RoboMaker robot application for which this version is created.
The version of the robot application, automatically generated by AWS RoboMaker when the version is created.
The unique Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies this RoboMaker robot application version.

aws_robo_maker_simulation_application.ar.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this RoboMaker simulation application.

aws_robo_maker_simulation_application.so.text: The target processor architecture (X86_64 or ARM64) for the simulation application source bundle, used to match the application with the correct robot simulator architecture.
