The name of the Amazon S3 bucket where the robot application source bundle is stored for this simulation application.
The S3 object key of the robot application bundle stored in the bucket specified by the source's s3_bucket, which is a required component of the source configuration for the simulation application.

aws_robo_maker_simulation_application_ve.text: The name or Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the RoboMaker simulation application for which this version is created.
The version number (e.g., '1', '2') assigned to the newly created RoboMaker simulation application version, returned by AWS after creation.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned by AWS to the newly created simulation application version, uniquely identifying it within the account and region.

aws_roles_anywhere_crl.crl_data.text: The PEM-encoded certificate revocation list (CRL) data that is uploaded to AWS Roles Anywhere, containing the list of revoked certificates.

aws_roles_anywhere_crl.crl_id.text: The system-generated unique identifier (UUID) for the certificate revocation list (CRL) in AWS Roles Anywhere, assigned when the CRL is created and used to reference it in subsequent operations.

aws_roles_anywhere_crl.enabled.text: Indicates whether this certificate revocation list (CRL) is enabled for use in revoking certificates in AWS Roles Anywhere.

aws_roles_anywhere_crl.name.text: Specifies the name of the certificate revocation list (CRL) resource, used to uniquely identify it within AWS Roles Anywhere.

aws_roles_anywhere_crl.tags.text: A list of tag objects (each with a Key and Value) that you can assign to the AWS Roles Anywhere certificate revocation list to help manage, identify, and control access to it, such as through IAM tag-based policies.

aws_roles_anywhere_crl.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Roles Anywhere certificate revocation list (CRL), used to categorize and manage the CRL resource according to your organization's tagging scheme.

aws_roles_anywhere_crl.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the AWS Roles Anywhere certificate revocation list (CRL), used for organizing or identifying the resource.

aws_roles_anywhere_crl.trust_anchor_arn.text: The ARN of the trust anchor that this certificate revocation list is associated with.

aws_roles_anywhere_profile.accept_role_s.text: Specifies whether the profile allows the caller to pass a session name in the AssumeRole request's role session name field.

aws_roles_anywhere_profile.attribute_map.text: Attribute mappings in the AWS Roles Anywhere profile define how to use regular-expression rules to extract values from authenticating X.509 certificate attributes (like the subject or issuer DN) and populate them as session tags on the temporary AWS credentials that the profile grants.
Identifies which X.509 certificate field (such as `x509Subject`, `x509Issuer`, or `x509SAN`) to evaluate when matching mapping rules in an AWS Roles Anywhere profile.

Defines the list of matching criteria (source certificate attribute and value pattern) that must be satisfied for the parent attribute mapping to be applied, controlling how certificate attributes are converted into session names or tags for an IAM Roles Anywhere profile.

Specifies the exact certificate or SAML assertion attribute value (such as a subject field or attribute name) that this mapping rule matches to populate the IAM session tag defined by the parent attribute mapping.

aws_roles_anywhere_profile.duration_seco.text: Defines how long, in seconds, the temporary AWS access credentials issued to a session that uses this profile remain valid.

aws_roles_anywhere_profile.enabled.text: A boolean that indicates whether the Roles Anywhere profile is enabled and can be used to issue temporary credentials.

aws_roles_anywhere_profile.managed_polic.text: Specifies the ARNs of IAM managed policies that are attached to the temporary session credentials when a role is assumed using this AWS Roles Anywhere profile.

aws_roles_anywhere_profile.name.text: The friendly name assigned to the IAM Roles Anywhere profile, used as a human-readable identifier for the profile.

aws_roles_anywhere_profile.profile_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the AWS Roles Anywhere profile.

aws_roles_anywhere_profile.profile_id.text: The unique identifier of the IAM Roles Anywhere profile, assigned by AWS when the profile is created.

aws_roles_anywhere_profile.require_insta.text: Specifies whether a session created with this profile must include instance properties (such as EC2 instance identifiers) when requesting temporary credentials.

aws_roles_anywhere_profile.role_arns.text: The list of IAM role ARNs that this profile is allowed to assume for temporary AWS credentials.

aws_roles_anywhere_profile.session_polic.text: The IAM session policy (as a JSON or YAML policy document) that limits the permissions of the temporary credentials issued by the Roles Anywhere profile.

aws_roles_anywhere_profile.tags.text: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) that are attached to the AWS Roles Anywhere profile, which can be used for cost allocation, access control via IAM policies, and resource organization.

aws_roles_anywhere_profile.tags.key.text: The key of a tag (metadata) assigned to the AWS Roles Anywhere profile, used to organize and identify the profile.

aws_roles_anywhere_trust_anchor.enabled.text: Indicates whether the trust anchor is enabled for use with IAM Roles Anywhere.

aws_roles_anywhere_trust_anchor.name.text: Specifies the name of the IAM Roles Anywhere trust anchor, which is required when creating or updating the resource.

aws_roles_anywhere_trust_anchor.notifica.text: List of notification settings for the trust anchor, each specifying whether to enable notifications for a given event (e.g., CA certificate expiration) and the threshold in days before expiration to send alerts.
Specifies the channel through which notifications are sent for this trust anchor; valid values are ALL (send to all configured channels) or SNS (send only to an Amazon SNS topic).
A boolean that indicates whether notifications for the associated event (e.g., CA certificate expiration) are enabled for this trust anchor.
The number of days before a certificate expires that triggers the notification event defined in this notification setting.

aws_roles_anywhere_trust_anchor.source.text: Specifies the certificate authority (CA) source for the trust anchor, either AWS Private CA (ACM PCA) or a certificate bundle, along with the corresponding source data.

aws_roles_anywhere_trust_anchor.source.s.text: Specifies the certificate authority data for the trust anchor, containing either the X.509 certificate contents in x509CertificateData or the ACM Private CA ARN in acmPcaArn, depending on the sourceType.
The ARN of the AWS Certificate Manager Private Certificate Authority (ACM PCA) that serves as the source of trust for this AWS Roles Anywhere trust anchor.
The PEM-encoded X.509 certificate data used as the trust anchor for AWS Roles Anywhere to validate temporary credentials.
Specifies the type of trust anchor source, either AWS_ACM_PCA or CERTIFICATE_BUNDLE, which determines how the source data (ACM Private CA ARN or PEM-encoded certificate bundle) is interpreted.

aws_roles_anywhere_trust_anchor.tags.text: A list of key-value tags to associate with the trust anchor, which AWS uses to organize, track, and control access to the resource.

aws_roles_anywhere_trust_anchor.tags.key.text: Specifies the key of a tag assigned to the AWS IAM Roles Anywhere trust anchor, used to organize, identify, and manage the resource within AWS.

aws_roles_anywhere_trust_anchor.tags.val.text: The value part of a key-value tag attached to the AWS Roles Anywhere trust anchor, used for metadata and resource identification.

aws_roles_anywhere_trust_anchor.trust_an.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the trust anchor.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the trust anchor when it is created, used to reference the trust anchor in other IAM Roles Anywhere operations.

aws_route53_cidr_collection.locations.ci.text: Specifies the list of CIDR blocks (such as '192.0.2.0/24') that define the IP address ranges for this location within the Route 53 CIDR collection, which are then used for DNS routing policies.

aws_route53_cidr_collection.locations.lo.text: The name of the CIDR location within the CIDR collection, serving as a unique identifier for associating the location's CIDR blocks with routing rules.

aws_route53_global_resolver_access_token.text: The unique identifier automatically assigned to this global resolver access token.

An optional caller-supplied token that ensures idempotent creation of the Route 53 Global Resolver access token by uniquely identifying the Create request, allowing safe retries without duplicating the token.
The creation timestamp of the Route 53 Global Resolver access token, indicating when the token was generated by the service.
Specifies the DNS view ID that this access token is scoped to, which the global resolver uses to authorize DNS resolution requests for that view.

aws_route53_global_resolver_dns_view.des.text: An optional human-readable description that you provide for the DNS view to help manage and identify it.

aws_route53_global_resolver_dns_view.fir.text: Determines whether DNS queries are allowed to pass through (fail open) or are rejected (fail closed) when the Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall cannot evaluate the configured firewall rules due to an internal error.

aws_route53_global_resolver_dns_view.upd.text: A read-only timestamp that records when the global resolver DNS view was last modified.

aws_route53_global_resolver_firewall_dom.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Route 53 Resolver firewall domain list, which uniquely identifies the domain list across AWS.
A caller-supplied token used to ensure idempotent creation of the Route 53 Resolver firewall domain list, preventing duplicates if the create request is retried.
The timestamp of when the Route 53 Resolver firewall domain list was created.
A brief description of the Route53 Resolver firewall domain list, used to record its purpose or what domains it contains.
The number of domains currently in the firewall domain list, as reported by Route 53 Resolver.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the Route 53 Resolver firewall domain list.
The name to assign to the Route 53 Resolver firewall domain list, which serves as its identifier in your AWS account.
The current status of the Route 53 Resolver firewall domain list, such as COMPLETE, UPDATING, or DELETING, indicating the lifecycle state of the list.
A message from Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall that provides additional detail about the current status of the domain list, such as an error explanation or confirmation of successful processing.
The key component of a tag assigned to the Route 53 Resolver firewall domain list, enabling you to categorize and filter the resource by metadata.
The value of a user-defined tag assigned to this Route 53 Resolver firewall domain list, used for metadata and cost allocation.
Indicates the timestamp (as a string) at which the Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall domain list was last modified by AWS, matching the ModificationTime attribute returned by the service.

aws_route53_global_resolver_firewall_rul.text: Specifies the action taken when a DNS query matches the firewall rule's conditions, accepting values ALLOW, BLOCK, or ALERT to permit, block, or log/alert the query respectively.
This value specifies the DNS record type (for example, CNAME) that the DNS Firewall rule returns when the block action is set to override, allowing you to point blocked queries to a custom domain.

Specifies the custom domain name that Route 53 Resolver returns in the DNS response for a blocked query when the firewall rule action is BLOCK and the block override configuration (e.g., block_override_dns_type) is applied.
BlockOverrideTtl sets the time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for the custom DNS record returned when a DNS Firewall rule blocks a query with the OVERRIDE response action.
Specifies the DNS response returned when the firewall rule's action is BLOCK, such as NODATA, NXDOMAIN, or an OVERRIDE response.
This field is an idempotency token that ensures duplicate Route 53 Resolver firewall rules are not created when the same request is retried.

Specifies the minimum confidence threshold (LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH) that a threat intelligence domain list match must meet for the Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rule to apply, filtering which domains are treated as malicious.
The timestamp indicating when the Route53 Resolver firewall rule was created, typically in ISO 8601 format.
Provides an optional description for the Route 53 Resolver firewall rule, used to annotate the rule with its purpose or notes.
The unique ID of the firewall domain list that defines the set of domains this resolver firewall rule applies to, associating the rule with that list.
The unique identifier that Route 53 Resolver automatically assigns to the firewall rule upon creation, returned as a computed read-only value.
The name of the Route 53 Resolver firewall rule, which is a required string that provides a friendly identifier for the rule.
The priority value that determines the evaluation order of this rule within its firewall rule group, with lower numbers evaluated first.

The DNS query type (such as A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, etc.) that this firewall rule matches, allowing the rule to evaluate only queries of that type, while omitting it makes the rule evaluate all supported query types.
The DNS query type (e.g., A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, etc.) that this firewall rule evaluates, where an empty value means the rule applies to all query types.
A timestamp that indicates when the firewall rule was last updated.

aws_route53_global_resolver_global_resol.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that AWS assigns to this Route 53 Global Resolver, used as a unique identifier and in IAM policies and resource references.
The current lifecycle status of the Route 53 global resolver rule, reporting values such as COMPLETE, FAILED, UPDATING, or DELETING to indicate the rule's operational state.

aws_route53_global_resolver_hosted_zone_.text: The ID of the Route 53 hosted zone that is being associated with the global resolver in this resource.
The current status of the association, indicating its lifecycle state with values such as CREATING, COMPLETE, DELETING, DELETED, or FAILED.

aws_route53_health_check.health_check_co.text: For a calculated health check, this field lists the health check IDs that Route 53 evaluates to determine the calculated health check's overall status.
Indicates whether the health check uses Server Name Indication (SNI) when checking an HTTPS endpoint.
The number of consecutive health check failures that Amazon Route 53 must observe before marking the endpoint as unhealthy, as part of the health check configuration.

Specifies the fully qualified domain name of the endpoint (such as 'example.com') that Route 53 sends health check requests to, used when the health check targets a domain name instead of an IP address.
The number of individual health checks that must be healthy for a calculated health check to be considered healthy.
Sets the health check status that Route 53 reports when CloudWatch does not have sufficient data to determine the endpoint's health, with allowed values of Healthy, Unhealthy, or LastKnownStatus.
When true, inverts the health check result so that a failed check is reported as healthy and a successful check is reported as unhealthy.
The IPv4 or IPv6 address of the endpoint that Route 53 health checks, used when the health check is configured to check a specific IP rather than a domain name.
Indicates whether Route 53 should measure latency between health checkers in different AWS regions and include the resulting latency data in the health check report.
Specifies the port on the endpoint that Route 53 performs health checks against, with defaults of 80 for TCP/HTTP and 443 for HTTPS when omitted.
Specifies the list of AWS regions from which Route 53 health checkers will issue requests to the endpoint being checked.
How often Route 53 sends a health check request to the endpoint; can be either 10 or 30 seconds, with 10 enabling fast health checks.
The URL path that Route 53 requests from the endpoint when performing an HTTP or HTTPS health check (for example, '/' or '/health').
The ARN of the Route 53 Application Recovery Controller routing control that this health check is associated with, allowing the health check status to determine the routing control's state.
Specifies the string that must appear in the response body for the health check to pass; used with HTTP/HTTPS health checks where the HealthCheckType is HTTP_STR_MATCH or HTTPS_STR_MATCH.
The type of health check to create (e.g., HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, HTTP_STR_MATCH, or CALCULATED), which determines the protocol or method used to evaluate the endpoint's health.

aws_route53_health_check.health_check_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by Route 53 to the health check.

aws_route53_health_check.health_check_ta.text: The key (name) of a user-defined tag to associate with the Route 53 health check.
The value of a tag on the Route 53 health check, providing arbitrary metadata associated with the resource for identification or categorization.

aws_route53_hosted_zone.hosted_zone_feat.text: Enables accelerated recovery for the hosted zone, which allows Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller to more quickly update DNS records during a failover event.

aws_route53_hosted_zone.hosted_zone_tags.text: The key of a tag assigned to the Route53 hosted zone, used to organize and identify the hosted zone within your AWS environment.
The value of a tag in the HostedZoneTags list, which provides an arbitrary string that, together with the tag key, helps identify and manage the Route 53 hosted zone.

aws_route53_hosted_zone.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by Route 53 to the hosted zone, such as Z1234567890ABCDEF.

aws_route53_hosted_zone.name_servers.text: The list of four authoritative Route 53 name servers assigned to the hosted zone for DNS resolution.

aws_route53_hosted_zone.vpcs.vpcid.text: The ID of the VPC that is associated with this private hosted zone, which authorizes the VPC to use the hosted zone for DNS resolution.

aws_route53_hosted_zone.vpcs.vpcregion.text: Specifies the AWS Region where the VPC that you want to associate with this private hosted zone is located, as required when associating a VPC by ID.

aws_route53_profiles_profile.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Route 53 Profiles profile, used to identify and categorize the profile in AWS.

aws_route53_profiles_profile.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag assigned to the Route 53 Profile, used to organize, identify, and manage access to the profile.

aws_route53_profiles_profile_association.text: The value of a tag (key-value pair) attached to the Route 53 Profile association, used for metadata, identification, and cost allocation of the resource.

aws_route53_record_set.alias_target.text: Specifies alias record properties, enabling the record set to route traffic to an AWS resource (e.g., Elastic Load Balancer, CloudFront distribution, or S3 bucket) by providing the target's hosted zone ID and DNS name, with an optional evaluate-target-health flag.

aws_route53_record_set.alias_target.dnsn.text: The DNS name of the AWS resource (such as an Elastic Load Balancer, CloudFront distribution, or S3 website endpoint) to which this alias record routes traffic.

aws_route53_record_set.alias_target.eval.text: Indicates whether Route 53 evaluates the health of the target resource and uses that health information to determine whether to route traffic to the alias target.

aws_route53_record_set.alias_target.host.text: The hosted zone ID of the AWS resource (such as an Elastic Load Balancer, CloudFront distribution, or S3 website bucket) that this alias record points to.

aws_route53_record_set.cidr_routing_conf.text: Configures CIDR-based routing for the record set by specifying the CIDR collection ID and location name that determine which traffic is directed to this record.
The unique identifier of the CIDR collection whose locations and CIDR blocks are used to determine the applicable routing policy for this record set.
Specifies the name of the CIDR location within the referenced CIDR collection that this record set should be associated with for CIDR routing.

aws_route53_record_set.comment.text: Specifies an optional human-readable comment that provides descriptive information about the record set, useful for identifying the purpose of the record.

aws_route53_record_set.failover.text: Indicates whether this record set is the primary or secondary resource for a Route 53 failover routing policy, controlling which record answers queries based on health check status.

aws_route53_record_set.geo_location.text: Specifies the geographic location (continent, country, or subdivision) that this Route 53 record set serves, enabling geolocation routing so DNS queries from that location are answered with this record.

aws_route53_record_set.geo_location.cont.text: The continent code (e.g., 'NA' for North America) that restricts the DNS record to queries originating from that continent when using geolocation routing.

aws_route53_record_set.geo_location.coun.text: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., 'US') that specifies the country for which this Route 53 record will respond to DNS queries when geolocation routing is used.

aws_route53_record_set.geo_location.subd.text: The two-letter code for the US state or other country subdivision (e.g., 'CA' for California) that determines the geographic region from which this record set should be consulted, used when geo location routing policy is enabled with a country_code.

aws_route53_record_set.geo_proximity_loc.text: Specifies the AWS Region or coordinates and bias used by Route 53 for geoproximity routing, which determines the resource that receives traffic based on the geographic origin of the request.
Specifies the AWS region (e.g., us-east-1) that defines the geographic location for this geo proximity routing rule, used by Route 53 to route traffic based on user proximity to that region.
Specifies a value that biases the size of the geographic region for a geo proximity routing policy, where positive values expand the region and negative values shrink it.
Contains the latitude and longitude values that define the geographic point for geo-proximity routing, used when no AWS region is specified in the geo-proximity location.

Specifies the latitude coordinate (in decimal degrees) of the geographic point used for geoproximity routing, which determines how AWS Route 53 routes traffic based on the user's proximity to this location.
The longitude of the geographic coordinate used by Amazon Route 53 to determine the distance for geo-proximity routing for the record set.
Specifies the local zone group associated with a group of AWS Local Zones used for geoproximity routing, such as 'us-west-2-lax-1'.

aws_route53_record_set.health_check_id.text: The ID of the Amazon Route 53 health check associated with this record set, which Route 53 uses to monitor the health of the resource and determine whether to include the record in DNS responses for failover or latency-based routing.

aws_route53_record_set.hosted_zone_id.text: The ID of the hosted zone in which to create the record set, allowing you to specify the zone by its unique identifier instead of its domain name.

aws_route53_record_set.hosted_zone_name.text: The DNS name of an existing Route 53 hosted zone (such as example.com) in which to create the record set; when provided, it is used as an alternative to the hosted zone ID to identify the zone.

aws_route53_record_set.multi_value_answe.text: When enabled, this record set uses multivalue answer routing, allowing Route 53 to return multiple healthy values (e.g., IP addresses) in response to DNS queries.

aws_route53_record_set.name.text: The DNS record name (fully qualified domain name) such as 'www.example.com', which defines the domain name that the record set answers queries for in Amazon Route 53.

aws_route53_record_set.region.text: Specifies the AWS Region where the resource referenced by this record set resides, which Route 53 uses to route DNS queries to the closest region when the routing policy is set to latency-based routing.

aws_route53_record_set.resource_records.text: The list of values for the record set, such as IP addresses for A records, hostnames for CNAME records, or text strings for TXT records, and cannot be set when an alias target is specified.

aws_route53_record_set.set_identifier.text: Specifies a unique identifier for the record set, used to distinguish it from other record sets with the same DNS name and type when the routing policy is weighted, latency, geolocation, multivalue, or failover.

aws_route53_record_set.ttl.text: The time-to-live (TTL) in seconds that DNS resolvers cache this record before requesting an updated value from Route 53.

aws_route53_record_set.type.text: The DNS record type (e.g., A, AAAA, CNAME, MX) for the Route 53 record set.

aws_route53_record_set.weight.text: The relative weight to assign to this record set when using the weighted routing policy, controlling the proportion of DNS responses that point to this record.

aws_route53_record_set_group.comment.text: A free-form comment that describes the record set group, useful for documenting the purpose or contents of the group.

aws_route53_record_set_group.hosted_zone.text: Specifies the ID of the Route 53 hosted zone in which the record sets defined in this group are created.
The name of the hosted zone (e.g., 'example.com.') in which the record sets are created, serving as an alternative to specifying the hosted zone ID.

aws_route53_record_set_group.id.text: The unique identifier for the record set group, which is the AWS Route 53 hosted zone ID that the group belongs to and is automatically assigned by the provider.

aws_route53_record_set_group.record_sets.text: Defines the list of Route 53 DNS record sets to manage together in this group, where each element specifies a record's name, type, TTL, and resource records or alias target.

Specifies the AWS resource (such as an Elastic Load Balancer, CloudFront distribution, or S3 bucket) to which this alias record points, including the target's hosted zone ID and DNS name, and whether Route 53 should evaluate the health of the target.
The DNS name (hostname) of the AWS resource that this alias record targets, such as an Elastic Load Balancer, CloudFront distribution, or S3 website endpoint.
When enabled, Route 53 evaluates the health of the alias target resource and uses that health status to determine whether to include the alias target in DNS responses for this record set.
The hosted zone ID of the AWS resource (such as a load balancer, CloudFront distribution, or S3 bucket website) that this alias record points to.
Defines the CIDR routing configuration for the record set, specifying the collection ID and location name that determine which CIDR block this record set responds to.
The unique identifier of the CIDR collection that defines the IP ranges used for CIDR routing of this record set.
The name of the CIDR location within the specified CIDR collection that this record set routes traffic to, used when the record set's routing policy is CIDR routing.
Specifies whether this record set is the PRIMARY or SECONDARY record when using Route 53 failover routing policy, determining which resource serves traffic under normal and failover conditions.
Specifies the geographic location for which the record set applies, enabling geolocation routing based on continent, country, or US state.
Specifies the two-letter AWS continent code (e.g., EU, NA, AS) that Route 53 uses to match the geographic continent of the DNS query for geo-location routing.

The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., 'US', 'DE') that specifies the geographic country from which DNS queries originate, used to route traffic to this record set when geolocation routing is enabled.
Specifies the two-letter code for the state or province (subdivision) that, together with the country code, defines the geographic location for Route 53 geo routing.
Specifies the geographic routing parameters (AWS Region, local zone group, or coordinates, plus an optional bias) for a record set using Route 53 geo-proximity routing.
The AWS region code (for example, 'us-east-1') that identifies an endpoint for geo-proximity routing, used to define the location of an AWS resource in the geo-proximity record set.

The bias value for the geoproximity routing location, which expands (positive values) or shrinks (negative values) the size of the geographic region from which traffic is routed to this record set, with values ranging from -99 to 99 and a default of 0.
Coordinates for the geo-proximity routing location, containing latitude and longitude values that define a point on the map for routing traffic based on user proximity.
The latitude of the geographic coordinate for a geo-proximity routing location, specified in decimal degrees (e.g., 37.7749) to determine the resource's position for traffic routing.
The longitude coordinate (in decimal degrees) of the geo-proximity location, used by Route 53 to calculate proximity and route traffic accordingly.

Specifies the identifier of the Local Zone Group (e.g., us-east-1-nyc-1) used as the geo proximity routing location in the record set, which allows traffic to be routed to a set of local zones instead of an individual AWS Region.
Specifies the ID of the Amazon Route 53 health check that you want to associate with this record set, enabling DNS failover based on the health of the endpoint.
The unique identifier of the Route 53 hosted zone in which this individual record set is defined within the record set group.
The DNS name of the hosted zone (e.g., example.com) that contains the record set, used as an alternative to the hosted zone ID to identify the parent zone.
Indicates whether the record set uses multi-value answer routing, which lets Amazon Route 53 return multiple values, such as IP addresses, in response to DNS queries.
The DNS name (fully qualified domain name) of the individual record set within the group, such as 'example.com'.
Specifies the AWS region of the resource that this record set routes traffic to, used for latency-based routing and requiring a corresponding SetIdentifier.
Specifies the list of values for the DNS record set, such as IP addresses for A or AAAA records or canonical names for CNAME records, which the record answers with.
The unique identifier that distinguishes this record set from other record sets in the same group, required for weighted, latency, geolocation, or failover routing policies.
The time-to-live (TTL) value, in seconds, that DNS resolvers should cache the resource record set before requesting an update from Route 53.
Specifies the DNS record type (such as A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, or TXT) for each record set in the aws_route53_record_set_group, controlling how Route 53 answers queries for the record set's name.
Specifies the relative weight (0-255) for this record set when using weighted routing, determining the proportion of DNS queries answered with this record set compared to others in the same group.

aws_route53_recovery_control_cluster.clu.text: The URL of the cluster endpoint for the Route 53 Recovery Control cluster, used to access the cluster's routing control API.
The AWS Region (e.g., us-east-1) where the Route 53 Recovery Control Cluster endpoint is located.

aws_route53_recovery_control_cluster.tag.text: The key for a tag attached to the Route53 Recovery Control Cluster, used to categorize and manage the cluster.
The value of a tag attached to the Route 53 Recovery Control cluster.

aws_route53_recovery_control_control_pan.text: The key of a tag attached to the Route 53 Recovery Control control panel, used to categorize or identify the resource for management, filtering, and cost allocation.
The value component of an arbitrary tag (key-value pair) attached to the Route53 Recovery Control control panel, used to categorize, identify, or manage the resource.

aws_route53_recovery_control_safety_rule.text: The key of a tag applied to the Route 53 Recovery Control safety rule, used to categorize and manage the resource.
The value of an individual tag assigned to the AWS Route53 Recovery Control safety rule, used for metadata-based categorization and management of the rule.

aws_route53_recovery_readiness_cell.tags.text: The key of a tag to attach to the Route 53 Recovery Readiness Cell, used to organize and identify the cell for cost allocation and access control.
The value portion of a key-value tag applied to the Route 53 Recovery Readiness cell, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the cell with custom metadata.

aws_route53_recovery_readiness_readiness.text: The value half of a key-value tag attached to the Route 53 Recovery Readiness readiness check, used to add custom metadata for organizing and identifying this resource.

aws_route53_recovery_readiness_recovery_.text: The key of a user-defined tag applied to the Route 53 Recovery Readiness recovery group, used for identifying and categorizing the group within AWS.
The value of a tag attached to the Route 53 Recovery Readiness recovery group, used to assign custom metadata for identifying, organizing, or managing the recovery group.

aws_route53_recovery_readiness_resource_.text: A unique identifier for this resource within the resource set, used to distinguish and group component resources when configuring Route53 Recovery Readiness checks.

Defines the DNS target (Route 53 record set) resource within a resource set, specifying details such as domain name, hosted zone ARN, record type, and record value that Route 53 Application Recovery Controller monitors for readiness.
The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of the DNS target resource that Route 53 Recovery Readiness monitors to verify DNS routing and determine readiness for failover.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Route 53 hosted zone that contains the DNS record evaluated by this recovery readiness resource set's DNS target resource.
The ID of the Amazon Route 53 record set that this DNS target resource references, uniquely identifying the record set within its hosted zone for the readiness check.
The DNS record type (e.g., A, AAAA, or CNAME) used for the DNS target resource in the Route 53 recovery readiness resource set.

In a Route 53 Recovery Readiness resource set's DNS target resource, the `target_resource` object specifies the underlying AWS resource (such as an NLB or a Route 53 record set) that the DNS target points to for readiness checks.
Contains the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Network Load Balancer that this recovery readiness resource set uses as a failover target.
The ARN of the Network Load Balancer (NLB) that serves as the target resource for this DNS target resource in the Route53 Recovery Readiness resource set.
Configuration for a Route 53 resource target, specifying the domain name and record set ID of the Route 53 record that this DNS target resource points to for readiness checks.
The domain name of the Route 53 record set that the DNS target resource references, used by Route 53 Recovery Readiness to evaluate the resource set's readiness.
The unique identifier of the Route 53 record set within a hosted zone that this resource set uses as its DNS target for readiness checks.
For each resource in the resource set, a list of ARNs of Cells or Recovery Groups whose readiness checks include this resource, determining which scopes the resource's readiness is evaluated against.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS resource to include in this resource set, identifying the concrete resource whose readiness is being monitored for recovery testing.
The value component of each tag applied to the Route 53 Recovery Readiness resource set, used to store arbitrary user-defined metadata for identifying and managing the resource set.

aws_route53_resolver_firewall_domain_lis.text: The key of a tag attached to the Route 53 Resolver firewall domain list, used to assign metadata for identifying and organizing the resource in AWS.

aws_route53_resolver_firewall_rule_group.text: Determines how the firewall rule handles matching DNS queries: ALLOW permits them, BLOCK returns a block response, and ALERT logs the match without blocking.
Determines the DNS record type (CNAME or TXT) for the override domain, used when a firewall rule blocks a query with an OVERRIDE response.
The fully qualified domain name that is returned as a DNS override when the rule's action is BLOCK and its BlockResponse is set to OVERRIDE, replacing the blocked domain's response.
The time-to-live (in seconds) for the DNS record returned when this firewall rule's action is BLOCK with a block response of OVERRIDE, specifying how long resolvers cache the override answer.

Specifies the response that Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall returns when a query matches the rule, using one of the allowed values NODATA, NXDOMAIN, or OVERRIDE (where OVERRIDE uses the rule's block override fields to return a custom response).
Sets the minimum confidence score (LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH) required for a domain from a threat intelligence list to be blocked by this firewall rule.
The ID of the AWS Route 53 Resolver firewall domain list that this rule uses to match domains.

Controls whether Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall inspects the DNS redirection (CNAME) chain to evaluate the ultimate target domain against the rule's domain list, accepting values like INSPECT_REDIRECTION or TRUST_REDIRECTION.

Specifies the advanced content category (such as a threat or content type) that the firewall rule targets when its rule type is based on advanced content, allowing the rule group to match domains in that category.
The name of the advanced content category (e.g., 'MALWARE', 'PHISHING', 'BOTNET') that the firewall rule uses to match DNS queries.

The `firewall_advanced_threat_category` field specifies the advanced threat category (e.g., malware, phishing) used to filter DNS queries when the firewall rule is set to an advanced rule type (ADVANCED_RULE) in a Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rule group.
Specifies the threat category (e.g., malware, botnet) for a Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rule that uses advanced threat protection.

An object that specifies the settings for a Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rule of type PARTNER_THREAT_PROTECTION, enabling the rule to forward DNS queries to an AWS Partner security solution for advanced threat detection.

The unique ID of the Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall threat protection whose managed threat list this rule uses to match DNS queries, used when the rule is based on a threat protection rather than a customer-defined domain list.
The evaluation priority for this firewall rule within the rule group, where lower numbers are evaluated first (range 1-10000).
The DNS query type (QTYPE) that this firewall rule applies to, such as A, AAAA, or MX, where an unspecified value matches all query types.
The key of a tag to assign to the Route 53 Resolver firewall rule group for identifying, organizing, or cost-allocation purposes.

Provides the value portion of a tag entry for the Route 53 Resolver firewall rule group, enabling users to associate custom metadata such as environment or cost allocator with the rule group for management and identification.
The value part of a tag attached to the Route 53 Resolver firewall rule group association, used to attach arbitrary metadata like environment or owner for identifying and managing the association.

aws_route53_resolver_outpost_resolver.ta.text: The key of a tag assigned to the Route 53 Resolver Outpost resolver, used to organize, identify, and manage the resolver within AWS.

aws_route53_resolver_resolver_endpoint.i.text: The specific IP address to assign to the resolver endpoint within the referenced subnet; when not provided, AWS automatically chooses an available IP from that subnet.

Specifies the IPv6 address to assign to the Resolver endpoint's elastic network interface (ENI) for this IP address entry, within the given subnet, enabling IPv6-only or dual-stack resolver endpoints.
The subnet ID where the Route 53 Resolver endpoint's elastic network interface is deployed, defining the VPC subnet from which an IP address is allocated for this resolver endpoint.

aws_route53_resolver_resolver_endpoint.t.text: The key of a tag attached to the Route53 Resolver endpoint, enabling you to label the endpoint for filtering, cost tracking, and access control.

aws_route53_resolver_resolver_query_logg.text: The key of a tag attached to this Route 53 Resolver query logging configuration, used to categorize and identify the resource (for example, 'Environment' or 'Project').
The value part of a key-value tag assigned to the Route53 Resolver query logging configuration.

aws_route53_resolver_resolver_rule.tags..text: The key of a tag to assign to the Route 53 Resolver rule for organizing and identifying the resource.
The value of a tag attached to the Route 53 Resolver rule, used to assign metadata for identifying, organizing, or cost-allocation purposes.

aws_route53_resolver_resolver_rule.targe.text: The IP address to which DNS queries matching this resolver rule are forwarded.
Specifies the IPv6 address of the target Resolver endpoint that this Resolver rule forwards DNS queries to.
The port on the target IP address to which the Resolver Rule forwards DNS queries (defaults to 53 if not specified).
The protocol used to forward DNS queries to the target IP address, either 'Do53' for standard DNS over port 53 or 'DoH' for DNS over HTTPS.
The Server Name Indication (SNI) value to include in the TLS handshake when the resolver forwards DNS queries to this target IP using the DoH or DoT protocol.

aws_route53_resolver_resolver_rule_assoc.text: The unique ID assigned by AWS to this Resolver rule association, returned by the service to identify the association between a VPC and a Resolver rule.

aws_route_table.route_table_id.text: The unique identifier of the route table, assigned by AWS (e.g., rtb-xxxxxxxx).

aws_route_table.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag key associated with the route table, used to organize and identify the route table within AWS.

aws_rtbfabric_inbound_external_link.link.text: In the AWS RTB Fabric inbound external link, the customer_provided_id field within link_attributes is a customer-assigned string identifier for the link, intended for the customer's own tracking and correlation purposes.
Specifies the logging configuration for the inbound external link, including the destination where log records are delivered and the level of detail captured for link activity.
The read-only link_status attribute reports the current lifecycle state of the inbound external link (for example, ACTIVE or INACTIVE) as maintained by the AWS RTB Fabric service.

aws_rtbfabric_inbound_external_link.upda.text: This computed string is the timestamp indicating when the inbound external link was last updated.

aws_rtbfabric_link.link_attributes.respo.text: Specifies a list of responder error masking rules for the link, determining which error responses from the responder endpoint should be masked or sanitized when the link processes bid requests.

aws_rtbfabric_link.link_log_settings.app.text: Defines the percentage (0-100) of error-level application log entries to sample and send to the configured log destination for this RTB Fabric link.

aws_rtbfabric_link.link_status.text: The read-only status of the AWS RTB Fabric link, such as whether the link is active or inactive, which is determined and reported by the AWS RTB Fabric service.

aws_rtbfabric_link_routing_rule.created_.text: A timestamp that records when this link routing rule was created, used for tracking and auditing changes.

aws_rtbfabric_link_routing_rule.gateway_.text: The ID of the gateway (such as an internet gateway or virtual private gateway) that the routing rule uses to direct matching traffic.

aws_rtbfabric_link_routing_rule.updated_.text: The updated_timestamp field captures the date and time when this link routing rule was last modified.

aws_rtbfabric_outbound_external_link.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this AWS RTB Fabric outbound external link.

aws_rtbfabric_outbound_external_link.lin.text: In AWS RTB Fabric, the customer_provided_id field within link_attributes is an optional string that you can set to a custom identifier for the outbound external link, enabling you to associate your own tracking or reference ID with the link.
The unique identifier that AWS RTB Fabric assigns to this outbound external link when it is created.

The numeric sampling rate for error-level application log records generated by the RTB Fabric outbound external link, controlling what proportion of error logs are retained or forwarded to the configured log destination.

aws_rtbfabric_requester_gateway.requeste.text: The current status of the requester gateway, indicating its operational lifecycle state such as Active, Inactive, or Deleting, as managed by the RTB Fabric service.

aws_rtbfabric_responder_gateway.acm_cert.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate used for TLS/SSL termination on the responder gateway's public endpoint.

aws_rtbfabric_responder_gateway.listener.text: Configures the network listener for the responder gateway, specifying the port and protocol (such as HTTP or HTTPS) on which it accepts incoming bid requests.

aws_rtbfabric_responder_gateway.trust_st.text: Configures the trust store used by the responder gateway to validate client certificates during mutual TLS handshakes, enabling secure client authentication.

aws_rum_app_monitor.app_monitor_configur.text: The destination service to which CloudWatch RUM sends the extracted metrics, such as CloudWatch or Evidently.
The ARN of the CloudWatch Logs log group or Evidently project that receives the metrics, used when metric destinations are configured for the app monitor.
The ARN of an IAM role that grants CloudWatch RUM permission to publish metrics to the destination specified in this metric destination definition.

Specifies the list of metric definitions for a metric destination, each defining a metric name and the value expression (such as a JSONPath or regex) used to extract the metric value from RUM event data.
A list of event attribute names (dimension keys) from the RUM event JSON that are used as dimensions for the custom metric defined in this metric definition.
The JSON event pattern that filters which RUM application events are included in this metric definition, used to match event attributes for extracting metric values.
The name assigned to this metric definition, which is used as the metric name when the extracted value is sent to the configured CloudWatch destination.
The CloudWatch namespace where the extracted metric is published, defaulting to 'AWS/RUM' if not specified.
Defines the unit label (e.g., 'Milliseconds' or 'Count') that CloudWatch RUM attaches to the metric generated from this metric definition when it is sent to the destination.
The value_key property specifies the key in the event data that CloudWatch RUM uses to extract the numerical value for the custom metric defined by this metric definition.

aws_rum_app_monitor.custom_events.status.text: Determines whether custom event collection is enabled or disabled for the app monitor, with allowed values 'ENABLED' and 'DISABLED'.

aws_rum_app_monitor.platform.text: Specifies the application platform for the app monitor, such as 'Browser' or 'Mobile', which determines how client-side telemetry is collected.

aws_rum_app_monitor.tags.key.text: The tag key, which is the name of the tag used to categorize and manage the CloudWatch RUM app monitor resource.

aws_rum_app_monitor.tags.value.text: Specifies the value for a tag key in the map of tags associated with the AWS RUM app monitor resource.

aws_s3_access_grant.access_grants_locati.text: Configures the S3 sub-prefix (S3SubPrefix) within the associated access grants location, restricting the access grant's permission scope to that prefix.

aws_s3_access_grant.grantee.text: Defines the entity that receives the access grant, including its type (such as an IAM principal, directory user, or directory group) and its identifier (e.g., an ARN or directory ID).

aws_s3_access_grant.tags.text: Assigns a list of user-defined tag key-value pairs to the S3 Access Grant to help identify, organize, and manage the grant (e.g., for cost allocation).

aws_s3_access_grant.tags.key.text: The tag key attached to the S3 Access Grant, used to organize and manage the grant, and can be referenced in resource-based policies for access control.

aws_s3_access_grant.tags.value.text: Specifies the value for a given tag key applied to the S3 Access Grant, which is used for organizing, identifying, and managing the resource in AWS.

aws_s3_access_grants_instance.tags.text: A list of tag objects (each with a Key and Value) to attach to the S3 Access Grants instance, enabling metadata categorization and cost tracking for this resource.

aws_s3_access_grants_instance.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a tag attached to the S3 Access Grants instance, used to define custom metadata for identification, categorization, or cost allocation.

aws_s3_access_grants_instance.tags.value.text: The value of an individual tag key-value pair assigned to the S3 Access Grants instance, enabling cost allocation and resource classification.

aws_s3_access_grants_location.tags.text: Specifies the list of key-value tags to attach to the S3 Access Grants Location, which can be used for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization.

aws_s3_access_grants_location.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the S3 Access Grants location, used to identify and categorize the tag within the resource's tag set.

aws_s3_access_grants_location.tags.value.text: This field stores the value part of a tag key-value pair attached to the S3 Access Grants Location, which AWS uses to let you organize, identify, and manage the resource through custom metadata such as cost allocation or purpose labels.

aws_s3_access_point.public_access_block_.text: Configuration block that specifies the public access block settings for this S3 access point, controlling whether public ACLs and public bucket policies are blocked and whether the access point can be accessed by public buckets.

aws_s3_access_point.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key-value pair attached to the S3 access point, used for metadata, cost allocation, and tag-based access control through IAM policies.

aws_s3_bucket.analytics_configurations.i.text: A unique identifier for the S3 bucket analytics configuration, used to distinguish it from other analytics configurations on the same bucket.

aws_s3_bucket.analytics_configurations.p.text: The object key prefix used to filter which objects in the bucket are included in this S3 analytics configuration, so only objects with keys starting with this prefix are analyzed.

aws_s3_bucket.analytics_configurations.s.text: Specifies the data export configuration for storage class analysis, defining where and how the analytics results are delivered (destination bucket, prefix, and output format).
Configuration for exporting the results of S3 Storage Class Analysis, defining the destination S3 bucket and the output format (e.g., CSV) for the analysis data.
Specifies the destination S3 bucket (with its ARN, account ID, prefix, and format) to which the storage class analysis data export is delivered.
The AWS account ID of the destination bucket that receives the storage-class analysis data export, which is the account that owns the destination bucket for cross-account exports.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 bucket where the S3 analytics data export file is delivered.
Specifies the file format of the exported storage class analysis data to the destination S3 bucket, with the only supported value being 'CSV'.
The prefix used to store the storage class analysis data export files in the destination S3 bucket.
Defines the version of the output schema used when S3 exports storage class analysis results to the configured destination, with the only supported value being 'V_1'.

aws_s3_bucket.analytics_configurations.t.text: The tag filters that specify which objects with matching tag key-value pairs are included in the S3 analytics export configuration.
The tag key that defines which objects are included in the S3 analytics configuration's tag-based filter.
Specifies the tag value used to filter objects for the S3 analytics configuration; objects with this tag value are included in the analytics export.

aws_s3_bucket.arn.text: The bucket's real ARN, computed, known only after ship.

aws_s3_bucket.bucket.text: The bucket's own globally-unique name. Conflicts with `bucket_prefix`.

aws_s3_bucket.bucket_domain_name.text: The bucket's real S3 domain name.

aws_s3_bucket.bucket_encryption.server_s.text: Whether to enable an S3 Bucket Key for the SSE-KMS encryption rule, which uses a bucket-level key to reduce KMS request costs for all objects encrypted under this bucket.
Specifies the default server-side encryption method applied to objects uploaded to the S3 bucket, including the encryption algorithm (e.g., AES256 or aws:kms) and optional AWS KMS key ID.
Specifies the AWS KMS key ID (or ARN) that Amazon S3 uses to encrypt objects by default when the default server-side encryption is set to aws:kms for this bucket.
Specifies the default server-side encryption algorithm applied to objects written to the S3 bucket, accepting values like AES256, aws:kms, or aws:kms:dsse.

aws_s3_bucket.bucket_name_prefix.text: This prefix is used to generate a unique S3 bucket name by combining the specified prefix with a random suffix, ensuring the bucket name is globally unique.

aws_s3_bucket.bucket_prefix.text: A prefix, with a generated suffix appended. Conflicts with `bucket`.

aws_s3_bucket.bucket_regional_domain_nam.text: The bucket's real, region-specific S3 domain name.

aws_s3_bucket.cors_configuration.cors_ru.text: Specifies the HTTP headers that are allowed in a request to the S3 bucket from a cross-origin origin; each entry can be a specific header name (e.g., 'x-amz-date') or the wildcard '*' to allow all headers.
Specifies the list of HTTP methods (such as GET, PUT, POST, DELETE, HEAD) that are allowed for cross-origin requests to the S3 bucket.
Specifies the origins (scheme, host, and port) that are allowed to make cross-origin requests to the bucket.
Specifies the response headers that are exposed to the client (browser) in the actual S3 CORS response, allowing client-side scripts to access them.
The ID is an optional unique identifier for this CORS rule, up to 255 characters, used to identify the rule within the CORS configuration.
Specifies the time in seconds that the browser caches the response to a preflight (OPTIONS) request.

aws_s3_bucket.domain_name.text: The bucket's DNS domain name, which is the global S3 endpoint of the form `<bucket-name>.s3.amazonaws.com`, exposed as a computed attribute for resource references.

aws_s3_bucket.dual_stack_domain_name.text: The dual-stack domain name for the S3 bucket, which is the automatically generated endpoint that supports both IPv4 and IPv6 connections, typically in the format bucket-name.s3.dualstack.region.amazonaws.com.

aws_s3_bucket.force_destroy.text: Destroy the bucket even if it still contains real objects.

aws_s3_bucket.hosted_zone_id.text: The real Route 53 hosted zone ID for this bucket's region.

aws_s3_bucket.intelligent_tiering_config.text: A unique identifier for this S3 Intelligent-Tiering configuration, used to distinguish it from other configurations on the same bucket.

Specifies an object key name prefix that identifies the subset of objects to which this S3 Intelligent-Tiering configuration applies, so only objects with keys beginning with this prefix are included.
Indicates whether the S3 Intelligent-Tiering configuration is enabled or disabled, with allowed values 'Enabled' and 'Disabled'.

Defines the tag filters (key and value pairs) that determine which objects are eligible for this S3 Intelligent-Tiering configuration, so that only objects with matching tags are included in the tiering behavior.
The tag key that, together with the tag value, defines a filter for objects to include in or exclude from an S3 Intelligent-Tiering configuration.
Defines the tag value in an S3 Intelligent-Tiering configuration's tag filter, used to match objects against the specified tag key for applying the tiering policy.
Defines each S3 Intelligent-Tiering tier (ARCHIVE_ACCESS or DEEP_ARCHIVE_ACCESS) and the number of days after which objects are moved to that tier.
The access tier (either ARCHIVE_ACCESS or DEEP_ARCHIVE_ACCESS) to which objects are transitioned after the specified number of days in this Intelligent-Tiering configuration.
The number of days after object creation when S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves the object to the specified access tier (e.g., ARCHIVE_ACCESS or DEEP_ARCHIVE_ACCESS).

aws_s3_bucket.inventory_configurations.d.text: The destination configuration for an S3 inventory report, specifying where the inventory list is delivered (e.g., the target S3 bucket ARN, optional prefix, and output format).
The AWS account ID that owns the destination bucket where the inventory list is delivered, allowing inventory delivery to a bucket in a different account.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 bucket where the inventory reports are delivered.
Specifies the file format for the S3 inventory results (e.g., CSV, ORC, or Parquet) stored at the destination.
The prefix to prepend to the object keys of the inventory report files stored in the destination bucket, so that all inventory results are written under this key prefix.

aws_s3_bucket.inventory_configurations.e.text: Indicates whether the inventory configuration is enabled for the S3 bucket.

aws_s3_bucket.inventory_configurations.i.text: The unique identifier for this S3 inventory configuration, used to distinguish it from other inventory configurations on the bucket.
Determines whether the inventory report includes all versions of each object ('All') or only the current version ('Current').

aws_s3_bucket.inventory_configurations.o.text: Specifies the list of additional object metadata fields (such as Size, LastModifiedDate, StorageClass, ETag) to be included in the S3 inventory output for the bucket, in addition to the mandatory fields (bucket name and object key).

aws_s3_bucket.inventory_configurations.p.text: Filters the inventory to only include objects whose keys begin with the specified prefix, such as 'documents/' or 'logs/'.

aws_s3_bucket.inventory_configurations.s.text: Specifies how often the S3 inventory report is generated, either Daily or Weekly.

aws_s3_bucket.lifecycle_configuration.ru.text: Specifies the number of days after a multipart upload is initiated that the upload must be aborted, as part of an S3 lifecycle rule.
Specifies the number of days after a multipart upload is initiated that S3 will abort the incomplete multipart upload, based on the upload's initiation date.
Specifies the exact date (in ISO 8601 format) on which Amazon S3 permanently deletes objects matching this lifecycle rule, used as an alternative to specifying a number of days.
The number of days after object creation when Amazon S3 permanently deletes objects that match this lifecycle rule.
Indicates whether Amazon S3 removes expired object delete markers when enforcing this lifecycle rule's expiration action.
A unique identifier for the S3 lifecycle rule, used to distinguish it from other rules in the same bucket's lifecycle configuration.
Specifies the expiration behavior for noncurrent versions of objects in the S3 bucket, including the number of days to keep them and optionally how many newer versions to retain.

The number of newer noncurrent versions of an object to preserve before the oldest noncurrent version becomes eligible for expiration, enabling you to retain a specified number of recent versions while expiring older ones.
The number of days after which a noncurrent version of an object is expired and permanently deleted in the S3 lifecycle rule.
Specifies the number of days after which an object version that is no longer current is automatically deleted by the lifecycle rule.
Specifies when noncurrent versions of an object transition to a different storage class, including the number of days after becoming noncurrent and the target storage class.
The number of newer noncurrent versions to retain before this lifecycle transition applies, allowing the action to skip recent noncurrent versions and only affect older ones.
The storage class that noncurrent object versions are transitioned to, such as GLACIER, DEEP_ARCHIVE, or STANDARD_IA, as defined in the S3 lifecycle noncurrent version transition rule.
The number of days from when an object version becomes noncurrent to when it is transitioned to the storage class specified in the lifecycle rule's noncurrent version transition.
Defines the transition actions for noncurrent versions of objects in an S3 lifecycle rule, specifying when to move them to a different storage class and how many newer versions to consider.
The number of newer noncurrent versions of an object that must exist before S3 applies the transition action to a noncurrent version.
Sets the storage class (e.g., GLACIER, STANDARD_IA, DEEP_ARCHIVE) that noncurrent object versions are transitioned to when an S3 lifecycle rule's noncurrent version transition action triggers.

Specifies the number of days after an object version becomes noncurrent (i.e., no longer the current version) before it is transitioned to the storage class defined in the same noncurrent_version_transitions block.
Specifies the minimum object size in bytes for which the lifecycle rule applies to objects.
Specifies the maximum object size (in bytes) for which the lifecycle rule applies, meaning only objects smaller than this value are eligible for the rule's actions.
Specifies the object key prefix that this lifecycle rule applies to, limiting the rule's effect to objects with keys that begin with this string.

Whether the lifecycle rule is currently active, with allowed values 'Enabled' or 'Disabled', controlling whether Amazon S3 executes the rule's expiration, transition, or other actions on matching objects.
Defines tag key-value pairs that must match an object's tags for the lifecycle rule to apply, thereby scoping the rule to a subset of objects.
The tag key to match in the lifecycle rule's tag filter, used to target objects with that specific tag for lifecycle actions.
The tag value that must match an object's tag for the lifecycle rule to apply, used together with the tag key in the same tag filter.
Defines a lifecycle transition action that moves objects to a specified storage class after a specified number of days or on a specific date.
The S3 storage class to which the objects are transitioned when the lifecycle rule's transition action triggers (for example, STANDARD_IA, ONEZONE_IA, INTELLIGENT_TIERING, GLACIER, or DEEP_ARCHIVE).
Specifies the date (in ISO 8601 format) when objects in the bucket are transitioned to the storage class defined by the same transition object, and is mutually exclusive with the 'days' property.
Specifies the number of days after object creation when the lifecycle transition action (to a specified storage class) takes effect for objects in the S3 bucket.
Defines a lifecycle transition, specifying when objects should transition to a different storage class (such as STANDARD_IA or GLACIER) based on age in days or a specific date.
The Amazon S3 storage class to which the object transitions when the lifecycle rule's transition action is triggered (e.g., STANDARD_IA, GLACIER, or DEEP_ARCHIVE).

Specifies the exact date (in ISO 8601 format) on which Amazon S3 should transition objects to the target storage class defined in the parent transition object, used when the transition is date-based rather than age-based.
Specifies the number of days after object creation when the lifecycle transition moves the objects to the storage class defined in the same transition action.

aws_s3_bucket.metrics_configurations.acc.text: The ARN of the S3 access point whose requests are filtered into this metrics configuration, restricting CloudWatch request metrics to that access point.

aws_s3_bucket.metrics_configurations.id.text: The unique identifier for this S3 metrics configuration, used to reference or manage the configuration.

aws_s3_bucket.metrics_configurations.pre.text: The object key prefix that filters the objects included in the S3 metrics configuration, so metrics are collected only for objects whose keys begin with this prefix.

aws_s3_bucket.metrics_configurations.tag.text: Defines the tag key-value pairs that filter which objects are included in this S3 bucket metrics configuration, so metrics are only collected for objects matching all specified tags.
The object tag key used by this metrics configuration filter to include objects in the S3 bucket's metrics reporting.
The value of the tag key used to filter which objects are included in the S3 bucket's metrics configuration.

aws_s3_bucket.notification_configuration.text: The S3 event type (e.g., s3:ObjectCreated:*) that triggers the Lambda function for this notification configuration.
Defines the object key name prefix and/or suffix filters that determine which S3 object events trigger the associated Lambda function notification.
Specifies the S3 object key filter rules (prefix or suffix) that determine which objects trigger the Lambda function notification.
A list of S3 key filter rules (each specifying a Name of 'prefix' or 'suffix' and a Value) that determine which object key names trigger the Lambda function notification for this configuration.
Specifies whether the filter rule matches the object key by prefix or suffix, with allowed values of 'prefix' or 'suffix'.
The value of a filter rule in an S3 bucket's notification configuration that specifies a prefix or suffix pattern which object key names must match to trigger the Lambda function.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Lambda function that Amazon S3 invokes when the specified event type occurs for this filter.
The S3 event type (e.g., s3:ObjectCreated:*) that triggers the notification to the SQS queue.
Defines the object key name filter criteria (prefix and/or suffix rules) that determine which S3 objects trigger the notification to the configured queue.
Specifies the S3 object key filter (prefix/suffix rules) that determines which object keys trigger the notification to the configured queue.

Specifies a list of filter rules (each a name/value pair with name either 'prefix' or 'suffix') used to match S3 object key names so that only objects whose keys contain the specified prefix or suffix trigger a notification to the configured queue.
The name of the filter rule, which must be either 'prefix' or 'suffix', determining whether the rule matches the object key's prefix or suffix.
Specifies the value of an S3 object key filter rule (such as a prefix or suffix) used to determine which objects trigger the notification sent to the configured SQS queue.
The ARN of the Amazon SQS queue to which the S3 bucket sends event notifications for this queue configuration.
The S3 event type (e.g., s3:ObjectCreated:* or s3:ObjectRemoved:*) that triggers the notification to the SNS topic.
Configures the S3KeyFilter for this SNS topic notification, restricting which object key names (by prefix and/or suffix) trigger the event.
Defines the S3 object key name filter (prefix and/or suffix rules) that determines which object events trigger the SNS topic notification.
The rules specify the object key name filter with prefix and/or suffix matching patterns that determine which S3 object create events send a notification to the configured SNS topic.
The name of the S3 key filter rule, which must be either "prefix" or "suffix" and determines how the Value is matched against the object key.
The value of the filter rule applied to object key names, used as the prefix or suffix to match for notification events.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SNS topic that S3 publishes event notifications to for this topic configuration.

aws_s3_bucket.ownership_controls.rules.o.text: Specifies the object ownership rule applied to new objects in the S3 bucket, with valid values including BucketOwnerPreferred, ObjectWriter, and BucketOwnerEnforced.

aws_s3_bucket.region.text: The real AWS region the bucket was created in. Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints). Defaults to the Region set in the [provider configuration](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs#aws-configuration-reference).

aws_s3_bucket.regional_domain_name.text: The AWS S3 bucket's regional domain name, e.g., 'my-bucket.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com', which is a constructed endpoint for accessing the bucket in the region where it was created.

aws_s3_bucket.replication_configuration..text: Specifies whether delete markers created in the source bucket are replicated to the destination bucket, with Status set to Enabled to replicate them or Disabled to skip them.
Specifies whether S3 replicates delete markers created in the source bucket to the destination bucket; set to Enabled to replicate them or Disabled to prevent replication.

The destination configuration for a replication rule, specifying the target S3 bucket and optional settings such as storage class, account, encryption, access control translation, metrics, and replication time.

Specifies the access control translation settings that change the ownership of replicated objects to the destination bucket's AWS account, used when replicating across different AWS accounts (cross-account replication).
Overrides the replica owner to the destination bucket owner by specifying `Destination`, required when replicating objects across AWS accounts.
The AWS account ID of the destination bucket's owner, required when replicating objects into a bucket in a different AWS account.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 bucket to which objects are replicated as part of this replication rule.
Specifies the encryption configuration for objects replicated to the destination bucket, including the KMS key ID used to encrypt the replicas.
Specifies the AWS KMS key ID (or ARN) used by Amazon S3 to encrypt the replicated objects in the destination bucket when the destination uses SSE-KMS encryption.

Specifies the replication metrics configuration for the destination bucket, including whether S3 emits metrics (Status) and the event threshold in minutes (EventThreshold) after which replication events are emitted.

Specifies the minimum replication time threshold in minutes (via the 'Minutes' property) that an object must meet for the replication event to be counted and reported in the S3 replication metrics for this destination.
The number of minutes after which S3 emits a replication metrics event, used as the event threshold for replication time control (RTC) metrics in the destination bucket.
Specifies whether replication metrics are enabled for this destination bucket, with valid values 'Enabled' or 'Disabled'.
Configures S3 Replication Time Control (RTC) for the destination bucket, including whether RTC is enabled and the replication time threshold in minutes.
Indicates whether S3 Replication Time Control (RTC) is enabled for the replication destination, with valid values 'Enabled' or 'Disabled'.
Specifies the time threshold for S3 Replication Time Control (RTC), defining the number of minutes within which the replicated object is expected to be available in the destination bucket.
Sets the time threshold in minutes (up to 15) for S3 Replication Time Control (RTC) to complete replication of objects, establishing the SLA for replication speed.
The storage class to assign to objects replicated to the destination bucket, overriding the default storage class of the destination bucket; for example, STANDARD, STANDARD_IA, or GLACIER.
The filter that defines the object key prefix, tag, or logical AND combination of conditions that determine which objects in the source bucket are replicated by this replication rule.

Specifies a logical AND combination of filter predicates (typically a prefix and one or more tags) that S3 applies when deciding which objects match the replication rule, requiring all specified criteria to be true.

The object key name prefix that must match for objects to be included in an S3 replication rule when the rule's filter uses an AND combination of predicates, typically paired with at least one tag condition.
Specifies a list of tag key-value pairs that an object must include for the replication rule's filter 'and' condition to match, limiting replication to objects that have all of the specified tags.
Specifies the tag key used in the AND condition of an S3 replication rule's filter, allowing the rule to apply only to objects that have a tag with that key.
The tag value that an S3 object must match in order to be included in the replication rule's filter, used within an AND condition that combines this tag filter with other filters.
The object key prefix that identifies which objects the replication rule applies to, used as a filter condition in an S3 replication rule.

This field specifies the tag key and value (as nested Key and Value properties) that an object must have for the S3 replication rule's filter to apply, defining the tag-based criteria for selecting objects to replicate.
The tag key used to filter which objects are replicated; only objects with this tag key (and matching value) are included in the replication rule.
The value of the tag that, together with the key, determines which objects are replicated; S3 replicates only objects that have this exact tag value for the specified tag key.
A unique identifier for the replication rule, used to distinguish it from other rules within the same bucket's replication configuration.
Specifies the object key prefix in the source bucket that identifies which objects this replication rule applies to, with an empty or omitted prefix matching all objects.
The numeric priority for this replication rule, where higher values take precedence when multiple rules match an object, and it is required when multiple rules exist with filters.
Specifies additional source selection criteria for the replication rule, such as whether to replicate objects encrypted with SSE-KMS.
Specifies whether Amazon S3 should replicate objects that are modified after being replicated to the destination bucket, using a Status property (Enabled or Disabled) to control the behavior.
Specifies whether Amazon S3 replicates modifications made to replicas, with the value set to either 'Enabled' or 'Disabled'.
A filter that, when its Status is 'Enabled', tells S3 replication to replicate source objects encrypted with SSE-KMS, and when 'Disabled', excludes them from replication.
Controls whether S3 replicates objects that are encrypted with SSE-KMS from the source bucket, where the value must be 'Enabled' to replicate those objects or 'Disabled' to exclude them.
Specifies whether the replication rule is enabled (Enabled) or disabled (Disabled).

aws_s3_bucket.tags.key.text: The key component of a user-defined tag applied to the S3 bucket, serving as the identifier for cost allocation, access control, and resource metadata.

aws_s3_bucket.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag attached to the S3 bucket, enabling you to associate arbitrary metadata with the bucket for cost allocation, access control, or operational purposes.

aws_s3_bucket.website_configuration.rout.text: Specifies the redirect behavior for a routing rule, including protocol, host name, port, key replacement, and HTTP redirect code, applied when the rule's condition is met.

Specifies the host name to use in the redirect request for a routing rule in the S3 website configuration; for example, if the rule matches, requests are redirected to this host instead of the original bucket's website endpoint.
Specifies the HTTP redirect code (such as 301, 302, or 307) that S3 returns in the redirect response when this routing rule matches, overriding the default 301.
Specifies the protocol (http or https) to use in the redirect location for requests that match the routing rule's condition.
Specifies the object key prefix to use in the redirect request, replacing the matched prefix from the original request.
Specifies the object key name to use in the redirect request, replacing the entire original key for requests that match the routing rule.
Defines the condition (such as a specific HTTP error code or a key prefix) that must be matched for the S3 website routing rule to take effect.
The HTTP error code (e.g., '404') that the origin must return in order for this routing rule condition to apply.
Specifies the object key prefix that must match for the routing rule condition to apply when S3 serves requests from the website endpoint.

aws_s3_bucket.website_url.text: The website URL endpoint for the S3 bucket when static website hosting is configured, such as http://bucket-name.s3-website-region.amazonaws.com.

aws_s3_express_access_point.public_acces.text: Configures the public access block settings for the S3 Express access point, letting you override account-level Block Public Access settings for this specific access point.

aws_s3_express_access_point.scope.text: Defines an optional prefix scope that restricts the S3 Express access point to only objects whose keys start with the specified prefix; if this object is absent, the access point applies to the entire directory bucket.

aws_s3_express_access_point.tags.key.text: The tag key is the user-defined name (e.g., 'Environment') for a metadata tag attached to the S3 Express access point, used for categorization and cost allocation.

aws_s3_express_directory_bucket.bucket_e.text: Enables or disables an S3 Bucket Key for the directory bucket's default SSE-KMS encryption, reducing per-request AWS KMS costs.

Defines the default server-side encryption configuration for the S3 Express Directory Bucket, choosing either SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS with an optional KMS key ID that is applied to objects written without an explicit encryption header.
The AWS KMS customer master key (CMK) ID or ARN used for default server-side encryption with KMS (SSE-KMS) for the S3 Express directory bucket, effective when the SSE algorithm is set to 'aws:kms'.
Specifies the default server-side encryption algorithm (such as AES256 or aws:kms) for objects stored in the S3 Express directory bucket, used when encryption is not specified at upload time.

aws_s3_express_directory_bucket.inventor.text: Defines the destination Amazon S3 bucket and optional prefix where the inventory report files resulting from this inventory configuration are delivered.
The AWS account ID that owns the destination bucket where S3 Express directory bucket inventory reports are delivered, used to verify the bucket owner during configuration.
