The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the destination bucket where the inventory reports for this directory bucket are delivered.
The output format (e.g., 'CSV') of the inventory report delivered to the destination bucket.
The prefix that is prepended to the keys of the inventory report objects when they are delivered to the destination bucket.
Indicates whether this inventory configuration is enabled, so that the S3 Express directory bucket periodically generates and exports inventory lists to the specified destination.
A unique identifier for the inventory configuration, used to distinguish it from other inventory configurations attached to the same directory bucket.
Specifies whether the inventory report includes all object versions or only current versions, with valid values `All` or `Current`.
Specifies the optional metadata fields (such as Size, LastModifiedDate, StorageClass, or ETag) to include in the inventory output for the S3 Express directory bucket.

Specifies the object key prefix that restricts the inventory report to include only objects whose keys start with this prefix, used to filter the set of objects listed in the directory bucket's inventory configuration.
Specifies how often the inventory report is generated for the directory bucket, with valid values of Daily or Weekly.

aws_s3_express_directory_bucket.lifecycl.text: Defines the lifecycle rules for objects in the S3 Express directory bucket, such as expiration, transition to storage classes, or deletion based on a schedule.
Configures a lifecycle rule action that automatically aborts incomplete multipart uploads after the specified number of days since the upload was initiated.
Specifies the number of days after a multipart upload is initiated before the lifecycle rule aborts that incomplete multipart upload in the S3 Express directory bucket.
Specifies the number of days after object creation when the object expires and is automatically deleted by the lifecycle rule for the S3 Express directory bucket.
A unique identifier for the lifecycle rule, used to reference and distinguish it from other rules in the S3 Express directory bucket's lifecycle configuration.
Specifies the minimum object size in bytes for objects to be eligible for this lifecycle rule, so only objects larger than this threshold are affected.
Specifies the maximum object size in bytes; only objects smaller than this threshold will match the lifecycle rule filter.
The key prefix that filters objects in the S3 Express directory bucket so the lifecycle rule applies only to objects with keys starting with that prefix.
Determines whether the lifecycle rule is active, with allowed values 'Enabled' or 'Disabled'.

aws_s3_express_directory_bucket.metrics_.text: For an S3 Express directory bucket, this access point ARN filters the metrics configuration so that metrics are reported only for requests directed to the specified S3 access point.
The unique identifier for this metrics configuration, which must be distinct within the directory bucket and is used to refer to the configuration when setting up CloudWatch bucket metrics.
Specifies the object key prefix that the metrics configuration applies to, so that only requests for objects with this prefix are included in the emitted metrics.

aws_s3_express_directory_bucket.tags.text: Specifies the list of key-value tags to assign to the S3 Express directory bucket, which are used for cost allocation, access control, and metadata management.

aws_s3_express_directory_bucket.tags.val.text: The value component of a tag attached to the S3 Express directory bucket, used for cost allocation and metadata organization.

aws_s3_files_access_point.access_point_a.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 access point, which uniquely identifies the access point and is used for making requests to S3 through the access point.

aws_s3_files_access_point.owner_id.text: The AWS account ID of the owner that created the S3 access point.

aws_s3_files_access_point.posix_user.text: Defines the POSIX user ID (UID) and group ID (GID) for the S3 on Outposts access point, controlling file-level permissions for NFS access.

aws_s3_files_access_point.root_directory.text: Specifies the root directory path within the S3 bucket that the access point is restricted to, so requests through the access point can only access objects under that prefix (supported for S3 on Outposts buckets).

aws_s3_files_access_point.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the S3 file access point, used for identifying and organizing the resource.

aws_s3_files_file_system.bucket.text: The name of the S3 bucket that stores the underlying file data for this file system.

aws_s3_files_file_system.synchronization.text: Specifies the S3 object key prefix that filters which objects are imported from the source S3 bucket to the file system according to this import rule.
Specifies the maximum file size in bytes for files to be included in the synchronization import, so that only files smaller than this value are imported.

aws_s3_files_file_system_policy.policy.text: The policy field specifies the JSON-formatted resource-based policy that grants or denies access to the associated Amazon EFS file system for specified principals, actions, and conditions.

aws_s3_multi_region_access_point.public_.text: This object configures the Multi-Region Access Point's public access block settings, allowing you to block public ACLs, ignore existing public ACLs, block public bucket policies, and restrict cross-account access to buckets with public policies.

aws_s3_multi_region_access_point.regions.text: The name of the S3 bucket to route requests to in this Region of the Multi-Region Access Point.
The AWS account ID that owns the bucket in the specified Region for the Multi-Region Access Point.

aws_s3_object_lambda_access_point.alias.text: The alias is a read-only, generated unique name for the Object Lambda Access Point, which can be used interchangeably with the access point name when making S3 requests.

aws_s3_object_lambda_access_point.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 Object Lambda access point, uniquely identifying it within AWS.

aws_s3_object_lambda_access_point.object.text: Specifies the list of S3 GET/HEAD object request features (e.g., GetObject-Range, GetObject-PartNumber, HeadObject-Range, HeadObject-PartNumber) that the Object Lambda Access Point is allowed to forward to the Lambda function for processing.
Whether CloudWatch metrics are enabled for the Object Lambda Access Point, allowing request and processing metrics to be published to CloudWatch.
The ARN of the standard S3 access point that this Object Lambda access point uses to access the underlying S3 bucket.

Specifies the list of transformation configurations for the Object Lambda Access Point, where each entry defines the S3 actions (such as GetObject) to intercept and the AWS Lambda function invocation that transforms the requested object.
Specifies the list of S3 API operations (such as GetObject and HeadObject) for which the transformation configuration applies.
Defines the content transformation for an Object Lambda Access Point, specifying the AWS Lambda function (through its ARN) that processes the object for the associated action such as GetObject.

aws_s3_object_lambda_access_point.policy.text: Contains the read-only policy status of the Object Lambda Access Point, including whether the access point's resource policy is publicly accessible (IsPublic).

aws_s3_outposts_access_point.vpc_configu.text: The VPC configuration that specifies the virtual private cloud (VPC) in which the S3 on Outposts access point is accessible, containing the required VPC ID.

aws_s3_outposts_bucket.lifecycle_configu.text: Defines the lifecycle configuration rules for the S3 Outposts bucket, including expiration, transitions, and incomplete multipart upload abort actions, with optional filters and rule statuses.
Specifies the number of days after initiation that an incomplete multipart upload to the S3 Outposts bucket is aborted, as part of a lifecycle rule.
The number of days after a multipart upload is initiated before the S3 Outposts bucket lifecycle rule aborts the incomplete multipart upload.
Sets the specific date (in ISO 8601 format) on which objects subject to this lifecycle rule expire and are permanently deleted by S3 on Outposts.
Specifies the number of days after object creation when objects governed by this lifecycle rule expire and are permanently deleted from the S3 on Outposts bucket.
The filter property of a lifecycle rule specifies the object key prefix, tag, or size criteria that determine which objects in the S3 Outposts bucket the rule applies to.
Defines a logical AND set of conditions (e.g., a prefix and one or more tags) that an object must match for the S3 Outposts bucket lifecycle rule to apply.
Specifies the object key prefix to match, used as part of the AND operator that combines this prefix with other conditions (such as tags) for the lifecycle rule's filter.
Specifies a list of tags (key-value pairs) that, when combined with other conditions in the AND operator, must all match an object for the lifecycle rule to apply.
The key of a tag that, together with its value in the same tag object, defines a condition an object must satisfy for the lifecycle rule's AND filter to match and trigger the configured action.
The value of the tag that, along with its key, is evaluated in the And operator of the lifecycle rule filter for the S3 on Outposts bucket.
The key prefix that identifies which objects in the S3 Outposts bucket the lifecycle rule's expiration or transition actions are applied to via the rule's filter.
Specifies a tag (key-value pair) that an object must have in order for this lifecycle rule to apply to it, acting as the filter condition for objects in the S3 on Outposts bucket.
The key of a tag used to filter objects in an S3 Outposts bucket lifecycle rule, so only objects with that tag key (and matching value) are subject to the rule's actions.
The tag value that, together with the tag key in the same filter, identifies which objects in the S3 Outposts bucket the lifecycle rule applies to.
A unique identifier for this lifecycle rule within the bucket's lifecycle configuration.
Indicates whether the lifecycle rule is enabled (active) or disabled (inactive), with allowed values 'Enabled' or 'Disabled'.

aws_s3_outposts_bucket.tags.key.text: Specifies the key of a key-value tag to assign to the S3 on Outposts bucket.

aws_s3_outposts_endpoint.failed_reason.text: The failure reason for the S3 on Outposts endpoint, providing an error code and message if endpoint creation failed.

aws_s3_outposts_endpoint.network_interfa.text: The unique identifier of the Elastic Network Interface (ENI) provisioned for the S3 on Outposts endpoint.

aws_s3_outposts_endpoint.status.text: The endpoint's current lifecycle status, such as Available, Pending, or Deleting, indicating the operational state of the S3 on Outposts endpoint.

aws_s3_storage_lens.storage_lens_configu.text: Configures the S3 Storage Lens prefix-level storage metrics settings, including whether metrics are enabled and the prefix selection criteria (include/exclude prefixes) for the bucket-level prefix aggregation.
Specifies the list of Storage Lens group names to exclude from the account-level Storage Lens aggregation, so that metrics from those groups are not included in the overall view.
The list of Storage Lens group names or ARNs to include in the account-level metrics aggregation, limiting S3 Storage Lens to collect metrics only for the storage covered by those groups.
The list of S3 bucket ARNs to exclude from the Storage Lens configuration's metrics.
Specifies the AWS Regions to exclude from generating Amazon S3 Storage Lens metrics, meaning buckets in those regions are ignored in the aggregated view.
Specifies a list of S3 bucket ARNs to include in the Storage Lens configuration, so that usage and activity metrics are collected for those buckets.
The regions list specifies the AWS Regions to include in the Storage Lens configuration, so that storage metrics and usage data are aggregated only from the listed regions.

aws_s3_storage_lens.tags.value.text: Specifies the value component of a key-value tag assigned to the S3 Storage Lens configuration, which can be used to categorize, filter, and control access to the resource via IAM and AWS Organizations policies.

aws_s3_storage_lens_group.filter.and.mat.text: Specifies the tag key that objects must have to be included in the S3 Storage Lens group when using the match-any-tag filter condition.
The value of the tag key-value pair that an object must match for inclusion in the Storage Lens group when using the match-any-tag filter.

aws_s3_storage_lens_group.filter.match_a.text: Specifies the tag key of a tag that, when present on an S3 object with any of the configured values in the filter's tag list, qualifies that object for inclusion in the Storage Lens group under the MatchAnyTag filter condition.
The tag value that, in combination with the corresponding tag key, determines whether an object matches the MatchAnyTag criterion and is included in the Storage Lens group.

aws_s3_storage_lens_group.filter.or.matc.text: The tag key that must match one of the specified key-value pairs when the storage lens group filter uses an OR condition to include objects with any of these tags.
The tag value that, together with the associated tag key, defines a tag-based filter for including objects in the S3 Storage Lens group.

aws_s3_storage_lens_group.tags.key.text: The key of a Tag attached to the S3 Storage Lens group, which together with the Value forms a metadata label used for cost allocation, access management, and resource organization.

aws_s3_storage_lens_group.tags.value.text: The tag value associated with a tag key on the S3 Storage Lens group, used to store metadata for identifying and managing the group.

aws_s3_tables_table.iceberg_metadata.ice.text: The unique numeric identifier for this partition field within the Iceberg partition spec, used to reference the field in table metadata and query operations.
The name of the partition field, which corresponds to a column name in the Iceberg table's schema and defines the source column used for partitioning in the partition spec.
The numeric ID of the source column in the table schema that this partition field derives from, as defined in the Iceberg partition spec.
Specifies the partition transform applied to the source column (e.g., identity, bucket[N], truncate[N], year, month, day, hour, or void) when defining this field in the Iceberg partition spec.
The numeric identifier that uniquely distinguishes this schema field from other fields in the table's Iceberg schema.
Specifies the column name for this entry in the Iceberg schema field list, which defines the columns of the S3 Tables table.
Specifies whether this field in the table's Iceberg schema is required, meaning that every record must include a non-null value for the field.
Defines the Iceberg data type for a field in the table schema, such as string, int, long, double, boolean, timestamp, or other supported Iceberg types.
The doc property provides a documentation string that describes the purpose or meaning of the schema field within the Iceberg table's schema v2 definition.
The unique numeric ID assigned to this field within the Iceberg schema v2 definition, used internally to reference the field in table metadata and data files.
The name of a column (field) within the Iceberg schema version 2 for the S3 Tables table, which identifies the field in the list of fields for that schema.
Indicates whether this column is required (non-nullable) in the Iceberg table schema, meaning it must contain a value in every row.

Specifies the Iceberg data type for this column in the table schema, defining how values are stored and interpreted (e.g., boolean, int, long, float, double, decimal, date, time, timestamp, string, uuid, fixed, binary, or nested struct/list/map types).
Specifies the sort direction (ASC or DESC) for a field in the Iceberg sort order, determining whether rows are ordered ascending or descending by this field.
Specifies whether null values are positioned first or last when sorting records by this field in the table's Iceberg sort order.

The source_id field specifies the unique numeric identifier of the column in the Iceberg table's schema that this sort field refers to, defining which column is used for sorting in the table's sort order.
The transform function applied to the column for sorting in the Iceberg sort order, such as identity, bucket[N], truncate[N], or time-based transforms like year, month, day, or hour.

aws_s3_tables_table_bucket.replication_c.text: Specifies the list of destination table buckets that this S3 Tables replication rule uses as targets for replicating the table bucket's data.
The ARN of the destination table bucket to which replication rules send copies of table data.

aws_s3_tables_table_bucket.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the S3 table bucket, used to categorize and identify the resource for management and cost allocation.

aws_s3_tables_table_bucket.tags.value.text: Specifies the value of a tag key attached to the S3 Tables table bucket, used for resource organization, cost allocation, and tag-based IAM access control.

aws_s3_vectors_index.tags.key.text: Defines the user-supplied key of a tag attached to the S3 Vectors Index resource, which is used to organize and identify the index through metadata and cost-allocation tags.

aws_sage_maker_action.metadata_propertie.text: Specifies the metadata properties for the SageMaker action, including the source repository, commit ID, the entity that generated the action, and the project ID associated with it.

aws_sage_maker_action.source.text: Specifies the source location and type that identify where this SageMaker action was defined or triggered, such as an Amazon S3 URI or a pipeline execution ARN.

aws_sage_maker_action.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag associated with the SageMaker action, used to store arbitrary metadata such as cost centers or environment labels for managing and organizing the resource.

aws_sage_maker_algorithm.inference_speci.text: Defines the inference code and container configuration for the algorithm, including the inference image URI and supported input/output content types.
Defines the list of Docker container specifications, each including image and configuration, that SageMaker uses for inference when deploying the algorithm.
Specifies a custom hostname for the container, which other containers in the same SageMaker inference pipeline can use to route requests to it.
Sets key-value environment variables that are passed to the inference container when it is deployed.
The name of the machine learning framework (such as TensorFlow or PyTorch) that the inference container image is built with.

Specifies the version of the machine learning framework (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch, MXNet) that the container image is built with, which SageMaker uses to select compatible instance types and inference behavior, and is required when the Framework property is set.
The Amazon ECR registry path (URI) of the Docker container image used as the algorithm's inference container.
Specifies the SHA256 digest of the container image referenced in this inference container definition, enabling you to pin the exact image version for reproducible deployments.
A boolean flag that marks this inference container as the checkpoint container for multi-container SageMaker inference, enabling state to be saved and passed between chained containers.
Specifies the model input configuration for the container, which includes the data input config string that defines the expected input tensor shape and data format for inference.
Specifies the data input configuration for the model container, provided as a JSON string that defines the expected input format, shape, and other parameters for inference.
Specifies the default model name to use when the container serves inference in a multi-model configuration, enabling proper routing of inference requests to the intended model.
The list of MIME content types the algorithm supports for inference input requests (e.g., 'text/csv', 'application/json').
Specifies the list of Amazon EC2 instance types that are supported for real-time inference with this algorithm.
Specifies the list of MIME types that the algorithm's inference container can return as the response payload, constraining the output formats customers may request when deploying the model.
Specifies the list of SageMaker instance types that can be used with this algorithm for batch transform jobs.

aws_sage_maker_algorithm.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the SageMaker Algorithm resource, used for resource categorization, filtering, and access control.

aws_sage_maker_algorithm.tags.value.text: The value of a tag associated with the SageMaker algorithm, allowing you to attach custom metadata like cost center or environment to the resource for management and identification.

aws_sage_maker_algorithm.training_specif.text: Defines the training configuration for the algorithm, including the training image, input/output channels, hyperparameter ranges, metric definitions, and other settings SageMaker uses to run training jobs.
Defines a list of metric definitions, each with a name and a regex pattern, that extract training metrics from the algorithm's training job logs for monitoring and hyperparameter tuning.
Specifies the name of the metric that the training algorithm emits, used for monitoring and evaluation during training.
The regular expression pattern that SageMaker uses to extract the metric value from the training job's CloudWatch logs.
Specifies the hyperparameters that the algorithm supports for training, including their names, types, allowed ranges, and whether each is required or tunable.
Default value for this hyperparameter, used by training jobs when the user does not explicitly provide a value.
The description of a supported hyperparameter that can be tuned in the SageMaker training job, explaining its purpose, allowed values, or effect on model training.
Indicates whether a hyperparameter is required for training jobs that use this SageMaker algorithm.
Indicates whether this hyperparameter can be tuned by SageMaker hyperparameter tuning jobs, allowing its value to be optimized during training.
The name of the hyperparameter, such as 'batch_size' or 'learning_rate', that the algorithm accepts in its training configuration.
Specifies the allowed values for this hyperparameter, either as a minimum and maximum for integer/continuous types or as a list of categories for categorical types.
Specifies the list of allowed categorical values (as strings) for a hyperparameter when its parameter range type is categorical in a SageMaker algorithm's training specification.
Specifies the list of allowed string values for a categorical hyperparameter in the SageMaker algorithm's training specification, defining the set of choices the hyperparameter can take.
In the SageMaker algorithm's training specification, this object defines the allowed minimum and maximum values of the continuous hyperparameter range, using the MaxValue and MinValue properties.
Specifies the maximum value allowed for a continuous hyperparameter in the SageMaker algorithm's training specification.
The minimum value of the continuous range allowed for the hyperparameter, used to define the lower bound for tuning.
Specifies the minimum and maximum values for an integer hyperparameter supported by the training algorithm.
The maximum value of the integer hyperparameter range, representing the upper bound allowed for tuning this parameter.
Specifies the minimum integer value allowed for the hyperparameter range in SageMaker's integer parameter range specification.
The data type of the hyperparameter, which can be one of Integer, Continuous, Categorical, or FreeText.
Specifies the list of Amazon EC2 instance types on which the algorithm can run training jobs, used by SageMaker to validate and schedule training jobs for this algorithm.

Defines the list of metrics that can be used as the objective metric for hyperparameter tuning jobs when training with this algorithm, where each entry specifies a metric name and the regular expression pattern used to extract its value from training output logs.
The name of the training metric that SageMaker hyperparameter tuning jobs can optimize for this algorithm, as specified in the algorithm's training specification.
Specifies whether the tuning job objective metric should be maximized or minimized (valid values are 'Maximize' or 'Minimize') during hyperparameter tuning.
Indicates whether the algorithm supports distributed training, allowing SageMaker training jobs to use multiple compute instances when enabled.
Defines the list of input channels for training, where each channel specifies its name, whether it is required, supported content types, and supported input modes such as File or Pipe.
Specifies a human-readable description of a training data channel, clarifying the data's format or purpose for SageMaker.
Specifies whether the corresponding training channel must be supplied by the user when using this algorithm to create a training job.
Specifies the name of the training channel (e.g., 'train', 'validation') that the algorithm expects in the input data configuration of a training job.

Specifies the compression types (such as 'None' or 'Gzip') that this training channel supports, so SageMaker can accept input data compressed in one of these formats when launching a training job with the algorithm.
Specifies the list of MIME content types (e.g., 'text/csv', 'application/x-recordio') that the training channel accepts for the algorithm's input data.
Specifies the list of supported data input modes (such as File or Pipe) for this training channel in the algorithm's training specification.
The URI of the Docker container image used for training the algorithm.
The SHA256 digest of the Docker container image used for training, which uniquely identifies the image version in Amazon ECR.

aws_sage_maker_app.resource_spec.text: Specifies the SageMaker image version ARN and the compute instance type used for this SageMaker app.

aws_sage_maker_app.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the SageMaker App, used for organizing, cost allocation, and identity-based access control of the resource.

aws_sage_maker_app.tags.value.text: The value of a tag applied to the SageMaker App, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_sage_maker_app_image_config.code_edi.text: Specifies the name (key) of an environment variable to set in the container environment for the SageMaker Code Editor app image configuration.

Specifies the value portion of a key-value pair environment variable that is injected into the SageMaker Code Editor app's container when it launches, paired with the corresponding Key in the same ContainerEnvironmentVariables entry.

aws_sage_maker_app_image_config.jupyter_.text: The name of an environment variable to set in the container for the JupyterLab app image, as part of the SageMaker AppImageConfig.
The value of the environment variable that is set in the container when running a JupyterLab app from this SageMaker image configuration.

aws_sage_maker_app_image_config.kernel_g.text: The display name of the kernel as shown in the Jupyter UI for the kernel gateway app.
The name of the kernel (for example, `python3`) that the SageMaker KernelGateway app uses to launch the kernel specification.

aws_sage_maker_app_image_config.tags.key.text: The key portion of a tag attached to the SageMaker AppImageConfig resource, allowing you to assign custom metadata for identification and organization.

aws_sage_maker_artifact.metadata_propert.text: The metadata properties (such as commit ID, repository, generated by, and project ID) that are associated with the SageMaker artifact.

aws_sage_maker_artifact.source.text: Specifies the origin of the artifact, including the source type (e.g., S3 or ARN) and a source ID that uniquely identifies the artifact's location.

aws_sage_maker_artifact.source.source_ty.text: Specifies the type of identifier used for the source, selecting from MD5Hash, S3ETag, S3Version, or Custom, for a source type associated with the SageMaker artifact.
The value for a source type entry (such as an MD5 hash, S3 URI, or custom string) that identifies the origin of the SageMaker artifact.

aws_sage_maker_artifact.tags.key.text: The user-defined key for a tag attached to the SageMaker artifact, used for metadata and resource organization.

aws_sage_maker_artifact.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the SageMaker artifact, used to organize and identify the artifact within AWS.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.instance_groups.a.text: Specifies the automatic patching configuration for this instance group in the SageMaker HyperPod cluster, including the patch strategy (e.g., 'Auto' or 'None') and the list of instance groups that should be patched.

Defines the deployment strategy for automatic patching of instances in this instance group, including the rolling update policy (e.g., maximum batch size and wait interval) and optional auto-rollback configuration.
Specifies the list of CloudWatch alarms that, if triggered during an automatic patch deployment on a SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group, cause the deployment to automatically roll back.
The name of an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that triggers an automatic rollback of the SageMaker cluster instance group's patch deployment when the alarm enters the ALARM state.

Specifies the maximum number or percentage of nodes in a SageMaker HyperPod instance group that can be patched at the same time during a rolling deployment, defined as an object with value and unit fields.
Specifies whether the maximum number of instances updated per batch during a rolling update is set as a fixed count or as a percentage of the instance group's total instances.

The numeric value of the maximum batch size (used with the accompanying type, e.g., COUNT or PERCENT) that limits how many instances in the SageMaker HyperPod cluster's instance group are updated at a time during a rolling deployment when auto-patch is enabled.
Specifies the maximum number of instances that can be rolled back simultaneously when a rolling update deployment fails for this SageMaker Cluster instance group's auto-patch configuration.
Specifies whether the rollback maximum batch size is expressed as a fixed number of instances (INSTANCE_COUNT) or as a percentage of the instance group's capacity (CAPACITY_PERCENT).

The numeric value of the rollback maximum batch size, specifying the maximum number of instances (or percentage, based on the sibling Type field) that can be rolled back at once during a rolling update of the SageMaker HyperPod cluster's auto-patch deployment when a failure occurs.
Specifies the wait interval, in seconds, between each batch of instances when SageMaker automatically deploys patches to a HyperPod cluster instance group.
Defines the cron expression-based maintenance window during which automatic software patches are applied to the instances in the SageMaker cluster instance group.

Specifies the next date (in YYYY-MM-DD format) on which the SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group will be automatically patched, used when the patch schedule is set to a specific date rather than immediately or on a recurring cron schedule.

Defines the automatic patching strategy for an instance group in an AWS SageMaker HyperPod cluster, where 'PreserveAll' keeps all nodes available during patching and 'SkipAll' disables automatic patching for the group.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.instance_groups.c.text: Defines the minimum and maximum number of instances for the SageMaker HyperPod instance group, allowing the cluster to automatically scale the instance count between these bounds based on the workload.
Specifies the number of On-Demand instances to allocate to this instance group within the SageMaker HyperPod cluster.
Indicates whether the instance group's capacity requirement uses Amazon EC2 Spot Instances, trading potential cost savings for interruption risk.
This field represents the actual number of instances currently running in the given instance group of the SageMaker HyperPod cluster, as reported by AWS.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.instance_groups.e.text: The IAM role that SageMaker assumes to access AWS services and resources on behalf of the instances within this instance group of the SageMaker HyperPod cluster.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.instance_groups.i.text: Specifies the Amazon ECR image ID used to launch the instances in this SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group, enabling a custom container environment for cluster workloads.
The number of instances of the specified instance type to provision in the SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group.
Specifies the unique name of an instance group within the SageMaker HyperPod cluster, used to identify the group when configuring instance types and counts.

Specifies the minimum and maximum computing requirements (such as vCPUs and memory) that instances in a SageMaker HyperPod instance group must meet, enabling AWS to automatically choose an appropriate instance type for the cluster.
Specifies the list of acceptable EC2 instance types (e.g., ml.c5.large, ml.m5.xlarge) for the SageMaker cluster instance group, from which the service selects one when provisioning instances.
Specifies the Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume configuration, such as volume size in GB, attached to each instance within the SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group for local instance storage.
Specifies the Amazon EBS volume configuration for instance storage in a SageMaker cluster instance group, including the volume size in gigabytes.
Determines whether the configured EBS volume serves as the root volume for the instances in the SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group.
Specifies the AWS KMS key ID or ARN used to encrypt the EBS volumes that back the instance storage for the instance group, enabling customer-managed encryption instead of the AWS default.
Specifies the size in gigabytes of the EBS volume to attach to the instances in this instance group of the SageMaker cluster.
Defines the Amazon FSx for Lustre file system configuration (such as file system ID and mount path) used by the SageMaker HyperPod cluster instances in this instance group.
The DNS name of the FSx for Lustre file system that is used as instance storage for the SageMaker cluster instance group.
The mount name of the FSx for Lustre file system to be attached to the instance group's storage configuration.
Specifies the filesystem path where the FSx for Lustre file system is mounted on the SageMaker HyperPod cluster instances.
Configures an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system to be attached to the instances in this SageMaker HyperPod instance group, specifying the file system ID and mount path.
The DNS name of the FSx for OpenZFS file system that SageMaker uses to mount storage to the instances in this instance group of the cluster.
Specifies the mount path for the FSx for OpenZFS file system attached to the SageMaker HyperPod instance group's instance storage configuration.
Sets the SageMaker instance type (example: ml.m5.large) used for this instance group within the SageMaker cluster.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.instance_groups.k.text: Defines Kubernetes labels and taints applied to the nodes in this SageMaker HyperPod instance group, controlling workload scheduling and node taint restrictions.
Defines key-value labels attached to the Kubernetes nodes in this SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group.
Configures Kubernetes taints for the nodes in this SageMaker cluster instance group, which control pod scheduling by requiring pods to have matching tolerations.
Specifies the scheduling effect (NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, or NoExecute) of a Kubernetes taint applied to the instance group in an Amazon SageMaker HyperPod cluster.
The key of a Kubernetes taint applied to nodes in this instance group, used to control which pods can be scheduled onto them.
The value portion of a Kubernetes taint applied to nodes of the SageMaker HyperPod instance group.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.instance_groups.l.text: Defines the lifecycle configuration for the instances in this group, including the S3 URI of the script and the container entrypoint that runs on startup.
The S3 URI of the on-create lifecycle script that SageMaker HyperPod runs when an instance in this cluster instance group is first launched, as part of the instance group's lifecycle configuration.

In an AWS SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group's lifecycle configuration, the on_init_complete script runs on each node after the node has finished its initialization process, allowing cluster-level post-bootstrap customization via a script specified as an S3 URI.
The Amazon S3 URI of the lifecycle configuration script that SageMaker downloads and runs on instances in this cluster's instance group.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.instance_groups.m.text: Specifies the minimum number of instances for an instance group in this SageMaker HyperPod cluster, serving as the lower bound for auto-scaling the group.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.instance_groups.n.text: Configures the network interface for an instance group in a SageMaker HyperPod cluster, specifying the subnet ID and whether the interface is RDMA (for EFA) or standard ENI.

Specifies the network interface type for each instance group in the SageMaker HyperPod cluster, where setting it to 'efa' enables Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) for high-speed, low-latency inter-node communication, while other values use standard Ethernet.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.instance_groups.o.text: Specifies the deep health checks to run on instances in this instance group when the SageMaker HyperPod cluster starts, with allowed values such as InstanceStatus, InstanceConnectivity, and InstanceStorage.
Specifies a VPC configuration that overrides the cluster-level VPC settings for this instance group, including the security group IDs and subnet IDs used by the instances in this group.
Specifies the security group IDs used by the instance group when its override VPC configuration is applied, replacing the cluster-level VPC security groups for that instance group.

Specifies the list of subnet IDs that override the default VPC configuration for each instance group in the SageMaker cluster, allowing the instance group to launch in different subnets than the cluster's main VPC settings.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.instance_groups.s.text: Specifies the schedule for the rolling update of this instance group, including a cron expression and start time to control when updates are applied.

Specifies the deployment configuration for the scheduled update of the SageMaker cluster instance group, controlling how instances are rolled out (e.g., via a rolling update policy with batch size and concurrency parameters).

A list of auto-rollback configurations for a scheduled deployment to an instance group of an AWS SageMaker HyperPod cluster, specifying CloudWatch alarms that trigger automatic rollback of the update when they are in an alarm state.
The name of the CloudWatch alarm that, when it enters the ALARM state during a scheduled update deployment, triggers an automatic rollback of the update for the instance group.
Specifies the rolling update policy for the instance group, defining the maximum batch size and maximum capacity to control how scheduled cluster updates are applied while preserving availability.

Defines the maximum batch size, as either a fixed count or a percentage (represented by an AWS CapacitySize object), of SageMaker Cluster instances that are updated in a single batch during a rolling update of the instance group's scheduled update configuration.
Specifies whether the maximum number of instances updated in a single rolling batch is defined as a fixed count (COUNT) or as a percentage (PERCENTAGE) of the total instances in the cluster.

The numeric value of the maximum batch size (in instance count or percentage, as defined by the sibling 'type' field) that is allowed to be updated in a single batch during a rolling update of the SageMaker cluster instance group.

Specifies the maximum batch size, as a CapacitySize object, for rolling back a failed update of a SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group, limiting how many instances are reverted per rollback batch.
Specifies whether the rollback maximum batch size is expressed as a count or a percentage, with allowed values 'COUNT' or 'PERCENTAGE'.
The numeric value (count or percentage) that specifies the maximum number of nodes that can be rolled back simultaneously when a rolling update fails on a SageMaker HyperPod cluster.
Determines how long the SageMaker HyperPod cluster waits between each batch of instances during a scheduled rolling update of the instance group.
Specifies the cron expression that defines when updates are automatically applied to this instance group in an AWS SageMaker HyperPod cluster.

Defines the Slurm workload manager configuration for this instance group, including the Slurm queue name that associates the group's nodes with a specific Slurm partition in an AWS SageMaker HyperPod cluster.
The Slurm node type for this instance group ('controller' or 'worker'), which designates the group as either the Slurm controller for the cluster or a compute worker node.
Specifies the list of Slurm partition names that this instance group is assigned to, allowing SageMaker HyperPod to schedule workloads across the defined partitions.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.instance_groups.t.text: Specifies the number of CPU threads per core for instances in the SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group, enabling or disabling simultaneous multithreading (SMT) via a value of 1 or 2.
The ARN of the SageMaker Training Plan that reserves capacity for the instances in this instance group of the HyperPod cluster.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.orchestrator.eks.text: The Amazon EKS configuration that specifies the EKS cluster to use as the orchestrator for this SageMaker HyperPod cluster.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.orchestrator.eks..text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon EKS cluster that SageMaker HyperPod uses as the orchestrator for the SageMaker cluster.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.orchestrator.slur.text: The `slurm` property, when set inside `orchestrator`, configures the SageMaker HyperPod cluster to use SLURM as its workload orchestration engine, specifying SLURM cluster settings and SLURM node group definitions.

Specifies whether SageMaker automatically generates the Slurm configuration files (Auto) or uses pre-existing configuration files you supply (NoAuto) for the Slurm orchestrator on the SageMaker HyperPod cluster.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.restricted_instan.text: The current number of running instances in the SageMaker HyperPod restricted instance group, which is reserved for internal cluster operations rather than user workloads.
Specifies the per-unit storage throughput (in MB/s per TiB) for the FSx for Lustre file system provisioned for the SageMaker cluster's restricted instance groups via this environment configuration.
Specifies the size in GiB of the FSx Lustre file system configured for the environment of a restricted instance group in the SageMaker cluster.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that SageMaker assumes to provide permissions for instances in this restricted instance group to access AWS services and resources.
The number of instances to include in this restricted instance group of the SageMaker cluster.
The name of an instance group designated as restricted in the SageMaker HyperPod cluster, meaning that instances in this group have limited or no internet access for security and compliance purposes.
Defines the list of instance storage configurations (e.g., Amazon EBS volume settings) attached to instances within the restricted instance groups of the SageMaker HyperPod cluster.
Configures the EBS volume for the instance storage of the restricted instance group, specifying the volume size in gigabytes.
This boolean flag indicates whether this EBS volume configuration should be treated as the root volume for the instance group, rather than as an additional storage volume.
The AWS KMS key ID used to encrypt the EBS volume attached to instances in a SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group.
Specifies the size, in gigabytes, of the EBS volume to attach to each instance in a SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group's storage configuration.
Specifies the configuration for an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that is mounted as shared storage for the SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group.
The DNS name of the Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that is mounted as instance storage for the restricted instance group in the SageMaker cluster.
The mount name (subdirectory) of the FSx for Lustre file system used by SageMaker HyperPod cluster instances to mount the shared file system.
The absolute path on the instance where the FSx Lustre file system is mounted, making its storage available to the instance group.

Defines the Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system configuration, specifying the file system ID and mount path, used to attach an OpenZFS file system to instances in this SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group.
The fully qualified domain name (DNS name) of the Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system configured as instance storage for the restricted instance group.
Specifies the local mount path on the instance where the FSx for OpenZFS file system is mounted for shared storage access.
Specifies the ML compute instance type (e.g., ml.g5.xlarge) for each instance in this restricted instance group of the SageMaker HyperPod cluster.

Specifies the list of deep health check types (such as InstanceStress, InstanceConnectivity, and InstanceStorage) that SageMaker runs on nodes in this restricted instance group when they start, to detect hardware issues before workload deployment.
The list of security group IDs for the override VPC configuration applied to restricted instance groups in the SageMaker cluster.
The list of VPC subnet IDs that override the VPC configuration for a restricted instance group in an AWS SageMaker HyperPod cluster, determining where instances in that group are placed.
Specifies the number of threads per CPU core for the instances in this SageMaker HyperPod cluster instance group, allowing control of CPU hyper-threading (e.g., 1 to disable or 2 to enable).
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SageMaker training plan that provides reserved capacity for this restricted instance group in the SageMaker HyperPod cluster.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the SageMaker HyperPod cluster, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the cluster's resources and costs.

aws_sage_maker_cluster.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the AWS SageMaker cluster, used to associate custom metadata with the cluster for organization and cost tracking.

aws_sage_maker_code_repository.code_repo.text: Specifies the name of the SageMaker code repository, which uniquely identifies the repository within an AWS account and Region and is used to reference it in SageMaker operations.

aws_sage_maker_code_repository.git_confi.text: The Git configuration for the SageMaker code repository, which specifies the repository URL and optionally the ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret containing Git credentials.
The branch of the Git repository that SageMaker uses for this code repository.
The URL where the Git repository is located; SageMaker clones this repository for the code repository.
The ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the credentials, such as a username and password, for accessing the private Git repository specified in the Git configuration.

aws_sage_maker_code_repository.id.text: The unique name of the SageMaker code repository, which serves as the resource's identifier in AWS and Terraform state.

aws_sage_maker_code_repository.tags.text: Specifies the list of tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the SageMaker Code Repository, enabling you to categorize and manage this repository resource.

aws_sage_maker_code_repository.tags.valu.text: The value portion of a tag that is applied to the AWS SageMaker Code Repository, allowing you to associate metadata for resource organization and management.

aws_sage_maker_context.tags.value.text: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the SageMaker Context, which stores the user-defined string that, combined with the tag key, enables categorization, access control, and cost tracking for this ML resource.

aws_sage_maker_data_quality_job_definiti.text: Configures the Amazon S3 location (S3 URI, local path, and optional KMS encryption key) where the data quality monitoring job's results are stored.
The local path on the container instance where the data quality monitoring job writes its output files before they are uploaded to the specified S3 destination.
Specifies the S3 upload mode for delivering monitoring outputs, either 'Continuous' to upload data as the monitoring job runs or 'EndOfJob' to upload only after the job completes.
The S3 URI of the bucket where the data quality monitoring job results (e.g., statistics, constraints, and reports) are stored.
The key (name) of a tag attached to the SageMaker Data Quality Job Definition, used to identify, categorize, and manage the resource.
The value of a tag attached to the AWS SageMaker Data Quality Job Definition, used for identifying, organizing, and controlling access to the resource.

aws_sage_maker_device.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag attached to the SageMaker device, used for arbitrary metadata such as environment or cost center.

aws_sage_maker_device_fleet.output_confi.text: Specifies the Amazon S3 location (and optional AWS KMS key) where the device fleet's output data, such as device metrics and heartbeats, is stored.

aws_sage_maker_device_fleet.tags.value.text: The value portion of a tag attached to the SageMaker device fleet, allowing you to assign arbitrary metadata for purposes like cost tracking, access control, or operational organization.

aws_sage_maker_domain.default_space_sett.text: Defines the custom file systems (such as Amazon EFS or Amazon FSx for Lustre) that SageMaker automatically mounts in the default space for users within the domain.
Configures an Amazon EFS file system for the SageMaker domain's default space, specifying the file system ID and mount path.
The ID of the Amazon EFS file system that SageMaker mounts in the domain's default space when using this custom file system configuration.
Specifies the directory path within the referenced Amazon EFS file system that SageMaker mounts for the domain's default space, where leaving it unset uses the file system root ('/').
Configures an FSx for Lustre file system, including its ID and optional mount path, for attachment to the default user's SageMaker Studio environment within the domain's default space settings.
The unique identifier of the FSx Lustre file system to be mounted in the default space of an Amazon SageMaker Domain.
Specifies the path within the FSx for Lustre file system that is mounted for the default space of an Amazon SageMaker Domain, as part of the custom file system configuration.
Specifies the Amazon S3 file system configuration for a custom file system attached to the SageMaker Domain's default space, defining how an S3 bucket is mounted at a particular path.
Specifies the absolute path in the Amazon SageMaker Domain default space where the S3 file system is mounted.
The Amazon S3 URI (e.g., s3://bucket/prefix) that specifies the S3 directory mounted as a custom file system in the default space settings for the SageMaker Domain.
Specifies the custom POSIX user ID (UID) and group ID (GID) applied to apps running in the default space of the SageMaker Domain.
Sets the POSIX group ID (GID) for the custom user in the default space settings of the SageMaker Domain, used to control file system permissions.
The numeric POSIX user ID (UID) for the custom POSIX user configuration used by the SageMaker Domain's default space, controlling file ownership on the custom file system.
Configures lifecycle management for JupyterLab applications in the default space, such as idle timeout settings that automatically shut down idle apps.
Configures idle timeout (in minutes) and lifecycle management mode (e.g., enabled/disabled) to automatically shut down or keep alive JupyterLab apps in the SageMaker Studio default space.
The HTTPS URL of the Git repository that SageMaker clones into the JupyterLab environment for the default space in the SageMaker Domain.
The name of the AppImageConfig associated with this custom JupyterLab image, which defines the kernel and file system settings for the image in the SageMaker domain.
The name of the SageMaker image to use for the JupyterLab application in the domain's default space settings.
The version number of the SageMaker image to use for the JupyterLab app in the domain's default space, allowing selection among multiple registered versions of the same image.
Specifies the default SageMaker image, image version, instance type, and lifecycle configuration used when launching JupyterLab apps for this default space.

Specifies the default compute instance type and SageMaker image (including the image ARN and container configuration) used when launching Jupyter Server apps in the default space of the SageMaker Domain.
The name of the SageMaker AppImageConfig resource that specifies the kernel gateway app's image configuration for this custom image within the domain's default kernel gateway settings.
The name of the custom SageMaker image used for KernelGateway apps in the default space settings of the SageMaker Domain.
The version number of the SageMaker image to use for the kernel gateway app in the domain's default space settings.
Specifies the default compute instance type, SageMaker image, and optional image version or lifecycle configuration used for kernel gateway apps in the domain's default space settings.
Defines the default EBS storage volume size in gigabytes allocated for each SageMaker Domain space.
Specifies the maximum size in gigabytes that a SageMaker Studio space can provision for its attached Amazon EBS storage volume, as part of the default space's EBS storage settings.

aws_sage_maker_domain.default_user_setti.text: Specifies the lifecycle management settings, including idle timeout behavior, for the Code Editor application in the SageMaker Domain's default user settings.
Configures the idle timeout and lifecycle management settings that automatically shut down idle Code Editor applications in the SageMaker Domain for the default user profile.
Specifies the name of the SageMaker AppImageConfig resource that defines the configuration for the custom image used with the Code Editor application for the user.
The name of the SageMaker image used to run the Code Editor app in the default user settings of the SageMaker Domain.
The version number of the custom SageMaker image specified for the Code Editor app in the default user settings.
Specifies the instance type (and optionally the SageMaker image ARN) that SageMaker uses to preconfigure the Code Editor app for the default user profile.
Specifies configurations for custom file systems (such as Amazon EFS) that user profiles in the SageMaker Domain can mount in their Studio apps.

Within a custom file system config for SageMaker Studio's default user settings, the `EFSFileSystemConfig` object specifies the Amazon EFS file system ID and mount path to attach an EFS volume to the user's Studio environment.
The unique identifier of the Amazon EFS file system to attach as a custom file system for the SageMaker Domain default user settings.
The path within the Amazon EFS file system that SageMaker mounts for a user's custom file system in SageMaker Studio, specified as an absolute file system path.
Specifies the Amazon FSx for Lustre file system configuration, including the file system ID and optional mount path, used for a custom file system in the SageMaker Domain user's default settings.
The unique identifier of the Amazon FSx for Lustre file system mounted to the SageMaker Studio user environment through this custom file system configuration.
The path of the exported directory in the FSx for Lustre file system that SageMaker mounts for users' apps in the domain.
Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket (and optional storage path) that SageMaker mounts as a read-only custom file system for users in the domain's default user settings.
The S3 URI (for example, s3://my-bucket/path) that defines the S3 location to be mounted as a custom file system for SageMaker Studio users in the domain's default user settings.
Specifies the custom POSIX UID and GID for the default user in the SageMaker Domain, overriding default user identity for JupyterLab and kernel gateway processes.
The group ID (GID) for the custom POSIX user configuration, which sets the group identifier for users in the SageMaker Domain's default user settings.
The numeric POSIX user ID (UID) assigned to the custom user in the SageMaker Domain's default user settings.
Configures idle timeout behavior for JupyterLab apps in the domain, automatically shutting down idle apps based on the IdleSettings sub-property.
Configures idle timeout and lifecycle management settings (e.g., idle timeout in minutes to automatically shut down idle apps) for JupyterLab applications in this SageMaker Domain.
The URL of the Git repository that SageMaker clones and makes available to users in JupyterLab for this SageMaker Domain's default user settings.
The name of the AppImageConfig that defines the kernel and environment configuration for this custom JupyterLab app image in the SageMaker Domain default user settings.
Specifies the name of the SageMaker custom image to use for JupyterLab apps within the domain's default user settings.
The version number of the custom SageMaker image to use for the JupyterLab app, which together with the image name uniquely identifies a specific image version.
Specifies the compute instance type and SageMaker image (and optionally a lifecycle configuration) used to launch JupyterLab apps for the domain's default user settings.
Configures the default compute resources (instance type, SageMaker image, and lifecycle configuration) used when launching the JupyterServer application for users in the SageMaker Domain.
The name of the AppImageConfig resource that provides the kernel gateway runtime configuration (e.g., container environment and file system settings) for the custom image.
The name of the custom SageMaker image (registered in SageMaker) that the kernel gateway application uses for this user's default settings.
The version number of the SageMaker image to use for this custom kernel gateway image in the domain's default user settings.
Specifies the instance type and optionally a SageMaker image (ImageArn) that is used by default when launching KernelGateway apps for users in the domain.
Specifies the name of the AppImageConfig that defines the kernel and other configuration settings used when launching this custom image for RStudio sessions in the SageMaker Domain.
The name of the SageMaker custom image to be used for RStudio session apps within the SageMaker Domain's default user settings.
The version number of the custom SageMaker image to use for RSession apps, identifying a specific version of the image when multiple versions are available.
Specifies the default SageMaker image (via its ARN) and instance type used when launching RSession gateway apps for users in the domain.
Sets the default size in gigabytes of the Amazon EBS storage volume attached to a user's private space in the SageMaker Domain when no custom size is specified.
Specifies the maximum size, in gigabytes, of the Amazon EBS volume that can be attached to a SageMaker Studio space when using the default EBS storage settings for the domain's user profiles.
The name of the SageMaker image for which the specified version aliases are hidden from the Studio web portal in the SageMaker Domain's default user settings.
A list of SageMaker image version aliases (e.g., '1.0', 'latest') that are hidden in the Studio Web Portal for the SageMaker image defined by the parent 'HiddenSageMakerImageVersionAliases' object.

aws_sage_maker_domain.domain_settings.rs.text: Specifies the default resource specification, including the instance type, SageMaker image ARN, and optional lifecycle configuration, used when creating RStudio Server Pro sessions in the SageMaker Domain.

aws_sage_maker_domain.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the SageMaker Domain, which you can set to any string to associate custom metadata with the domain for purposes like resource organization, access control, and cost allocation.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint.deployment_confi.text: Configures how the SageMaker endpoint is deployed or updated, including rolling update policies such as blue/green or canary deployments.
Defines the CloudWatch alarms that, when triggered during a SageMaker endpoint deployment, automatically roll back the deployment to the previous endpoint configuration.
The name of the CloudWatch alarm that SageMaker monitors during a deployment to trigger an automatic rollback of the endpoint to the previous configuration if the alarm enters an alarm state.

Defines the blue/green deployment strategy for updating the SageMaker endpoint, controlling how traffic gradually or immediately shifts from the previous model variant to the new one during an endpoint update.

Specifies the traffic routing strategy (such as canary or linear) and timing parameters that control how SageMaker shifts traffic from the previous endpoint variant to the new one during a blue-green deployment.
Defines the initial canary step size for shifting traffic to the new endpoint variant during a blue/green deployment, expressed as either an instance count or a capacity percentage.

Specifies the step size for the linear traffic routing strategy in the blue/green deployment, defined as a capacity size (type and value) that determines how much additional traffic is shifted to the new variant at each step.
Defines the rolling update policy for a SageMaker endpoint deployment, specifying parameters like maximum batch size and wait interval that control how instances are updated during a rollout.
Defines the maximum capacity (number of instances or percentage) that SageMaker updates in a single batch during a rolling update of the endpoint's variant configuration.
Specifies the maximum batch size (as a CapacitySize object with type and value) that SageMaker uses when rolling back instances during a rolling update deployment of the endpoint.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint.exclude_retained.text: Specifies the type of variant property ('Desktop' or 'Host') to exclude for a retained variant when updating the SageMaker endpoint.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the SageMaker endpoint, used to organize and identify the resource within AWS.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the SageMaker endpoint, used to organize and identify the endpoint for cost allocation and access control.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint_config.async_inf.text: Specifies the configuration for asynchronous inference on the endpoint, including the S3 output path for results, optional notification settings, and client limits such as maximum concurrent invocations per instance.
Specifies client configuration for asynchronous inference, including the maximum number of concurrent invocations per instance allowed for the endpoint.
Sets the maximum number of concurrent invocations per instance that the asynchronous inference client can send to the model, controlling request parallelism for the endpoint.
Configures the S3 output location (and optionally an SNS notification topic) for storing the results of asynchronous inference on this endpoint configuration.
Specifies the AWS KMS key ID used to encrypt the async inference output data stored in Amazon S3.
Specifies the Amazon SNS topic ARNs to receive success and error notifications for asynchronous inference, and optionally which inference response types to include in those notifications.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic to which SageMaker sends an error notification when an asynchronous inference request fails.
Specifies a list of invocation outcomes (e.g., 'SUCCESS' or 'FAILURE') for which the inference response payload is included in the SNS notification for an asynchronous SageMaker endpoint.
SNS topic ARN to which SageMaker publishes a notification when an asynchronous inference completes successfully.
The S3 URI (bucket and prefix) where SageMaker writes the failure response payload for asynchronous inference requests when the model prediction fails.
The S3 bucket and prefix (path) where the results of asynchronous inference requests are written.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint_config.data_capt.text: Configures capturing of request/response data from the endpoint to an S3 location, including whether capture is enabled, sampling percentage, capture options (input/output), and content type headers for monitoring.
Specifies the lists of CSV and JSON content types that SageMaker captures for requests and responses in the endpoint's data capture configuration.
Specifies the list of CSV content types (e.g., 'text/csv') for which Amazon SageMaker captures request and response payloads as part of the data capture configuration for an endpoint.
Specifies the list of content types (e.g., 'application/json') that are classified as JSON for the purpose of data capture on the SageMaker endpoint.
Specifies which data flows (Request/Input and/or Response/Output) to capture for the endpoint's data capture configuration.
Specifies whether the data capture option applies to the input, output, or both (Input, Output, or InputAndOutput) of the endpoint invocation.
The S3 URI where Amazon SageMaker stores the captured endpoint data (payloads) for the DataCaptureConfig of this endpoint configuration.
Indicates whether data capture is enabled for the endpoint, which controls whether SageMaker captures request and response data for monitoring and debugging.
The percentage of incoming requests (0 to 100) to sample for data capture when the endpoint is initially deployed, determining what fraction of traffic is recorded for monitoring or analysis.
The AWS KMS key ID used to encrypt captured endpoint data at rest in the data capture configuration.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint_config.enable_ne.text: If set to true, the endpoint runs in network isolation mode, preventing containers from accessing the internet and restricting traffic to the VPC configured for the endpoint.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint_config.endpoint_.text: The name for the endpoint configuration, which must be unique within an AWS Region in your account.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint_config.execution.text: The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon SageMaker assumes to access model artifacts and other AWS resources needed to serve the endpoint.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint_config.explainer.text: The explainer configuration for the SageMaker endpoint, specifying the Clarify explainer settings used to generate feature attribution explanations for model predictions.

Specifies the configuration for SageMaker Clarify to generate SHAP-based feature attributions for the endpoint, including the SHAP baseline, number of samples, and text configuration for natural language processing.
Determines whether SageMaker Clarify explanations are enabled for the endpoint, with valid values being 'Enabled' or 'Disabled'.

Specifies the input and output data layout (feature headers, feature attribute, label attribute, etc.) that SageMaker Clarify uses to interpret inference requests and responses when generating explainability explanations.

Defines a template string that determines how feature values are placed into the inference request body for SageMaker Clarify, matching the endpoint's expected input format (e.g., with placeholders like {features}).
Specifies the list of feature names for the model input, enabling SageMaker Clarify to label and interpret features when generating explainability insights for the endpoint configuration.
Specifies the data type (categorical or numerical) for each feature, enabling SageMaker Clarify to apply the appropriate explanation method during inference.
Specifies the name or JSONPath of the features attribute in the input dataset, used by SageMaker Clarify for explanations.
The name of the attribute in the SageMaker model's inference response that contains the predicted label, used by SageMaker Clarify to properly parse outputs for bias and explainability analyses.
Specifies the names of the label columns in the dataset, used by SageMaker Clarify to identify which model output headers correspond to labels during explanation generation.
The index of the label column in the input data, used by the SageMaker Clarify explainer to identify the true label for multi-class classification models.
Sets the maximum payload size (in MB) that SageMaker Clarify permits for the inference requests it sends to the endpoint when generating explanations.
The maximum number of records from the input dataset that SageMaker Clarify's inference configuration uses to generate model explanations for the endpoint.
The attribute name in the model output that contains the probability for the predicted class, used by SageMaker Clarify to compute SHAP explanations.
The index of the model output that contains the probability of the positive class, used by SageMaker Clarify to interpret predictions for binary classification.

Specifies the SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) baseline and sampling parameters for the SageMaker Clarify explainer, which are used to generate feature attribution values for model predictions at the endpoint.
Integer specifying how many samples to use when computing SHAP values for the model predictions, used by SageMaker Clarify to approximate the baseline distribution.
Sets the random seed for the SageMaker Clarify SHAP algorithm to ensure reproducible feature attribution results in the endpoint configuration's explainer config.
Specifies the baseline (background) dataset and its serialization format that SageMaker Clarify's SHAP algorithm uses to compute feature attribution values for endpoint predictions.
The MIME type of the SHAP baseline data (e.g., text/csv or application/json) used by SageMaker Clarify for explainability.
Specifies the baseline data (as a JSON string or S3 URI) used by the SHAP algorithm for explainability in SageMaker Clarify.
The S3 URI of the baseline dataset used as the uniform background data for computing SHAP values in SageMaker Clarify explanations for this endpoint configuration.
This object configures how SageMaker Clarify's SHAP explainer processes text features, including language and granularity settings for computing feature attribution.

Specifies the granularity level for text inputs used by SageMaker Clarify SHAP analysis, either 'token' or 'sentence', determining whether the text is divided into individual tokens or entire sentences for generating explanations.
Specifies the language (e.g., 'en' for English) of the text data for SageMaker Clarify SHAP analysis in the text configuration.
If true, SageMaker Clarify transforms the model's probability output to log-odds (logit) before computing SHAP values, which is appropriate for binary classification problems.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint_config.id.text: The unique name of the SageMaker endpoint configuration, which serves as its primary identifier and is assigned by AWS.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint_config.kms_key_i.text: The AWS KMS key ARN used to encrypt data at rest on the ML storage volumes attached to the ML compute instances that host the SageMaker endpoint.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint_config.productio.text: Production variants define the list of model variants to serve at the endpoint, each specifying the model, compute instance type, and traffic weight (initial variant weight) for routing inference requests.

Capacity reservation configuration for the production variant, specifying the Amazon EC2 capacity reservation target (such as a CapacityReservationId) to reserve compute capacity for the variant's instances.

Specifies the capacity reservation preference for the production variant, which can be set to 'capacity_reservation' to reserve capacity in an Availability Zone or 'none' to not use capacity reservations.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SageMaker ML instance reservation to apply to this production variant, allowing you to leverage committed-use discounts for the endpoint capacity.
The timeout in seconds for the container startup health check, after which SageMaker considers the model in this production variant unhealthy if the container has not reported a healthy status.
Indicates whether to enable AWS Systems Manager (SSM) access to the container running the model for this production variant, allowing remote debugging and management.
The initial number of ML compute instances to launch for this production variant.
The initial weight assigned to a production variant, determining the proportion of inference traffic routed to this variant relative to other variants in the endpoint configuration.

Specifies a list of instance pools for a production variant, where each pool defines an instance type and instance count, enabling the variant to span multiple instance types for capacity and cost optimization.

The SageMaker ML compute instance type (e.g., ml.m5.xlarge) used by the corresponding instance pool in a production variant, determining the underlying compute resource that serves traffic for that pool within the endpoint configuration.

The name of the SageMaker model to serve from this instance pool, overriding the model name specified in the parent production variant so a single endpoint configuration can route traffic to different models across its instance pools.

Indicates the priority of this instance pool within the production variant, where a lower numeric value represents a higher precedence that SageMaker uses when selecting an instance type to provision endpoint capacity.
Specifies the Amazon SageMaker ML compute instance type (for example, ml.m4.xlarge) used to host this production variant.
Specifies settings for managed instance scaling of this production variant, including the minimum and maximum instance counts and whether managed scaling is enabled.
The maximum number of instances that the endpoint's production variant can scale out to when managed instance scaling is enabled.
The minimum number of instances that the SageMaker endpoint production variant can scale down to when managed instance scaling is enabled.
Indicates whether managed instance scaling is enabled or disabled for this production variant, with valid values 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED'.
Specifies the maximum time in seconds permitted for SageMaker to download and extract the model artifacts from Amazon S3 onto the inference instance backing this production variant.
The name of the SageMaker model that this production variant will deploy as part of the endpoint configuration.
Determines how incoming requests are distributed across the compute instances backing this production variant, using either a least-outstanding-requests or random routing strategy.

Specifies the routing strategy for the production variant, controlling how SageMaker distributes inference requests across the variant's instances, with valid values such as 'LEAST_OUTSTANDING_REQUESTS' and 'RANDOM'.
Specifies the serverless inference configuration for this production variant, including memory size and maximum concurrency settings.
Sets the maximum number of concurrent invocations the serverless endpoint can handle, controlling throughput and triggering scaling for this production variant.
Specifies the memory size (in MB) for the serverless endpoint production variant, determining the compute resources allocated for the endpoint.
The number of provisioned concurrency execution environments to pre-warm for the serverless production variant, reducing cold start latency at an additional cost.
Specifies the maximum time in seconds that SageMaker waits for the production variant's instances to be provisioned and become healthy before failing the endpoint deployment.
A unique name for the production variant, used to identify and route traffic to the corresponding model within the SageMaker endpoint configuration.
Specifies the size of the Amazon EBS volume in gigabytes to attach to each SageMaker endpoint instance for the production variant, providing additional local storage for the container.

aws_sage_maker_endpoint_config.shadow_pr.text: Defines a list of shadow production variants, each specifying a model to be deployed alongside the primary production variants, which receives a copy of inference requests for testing and monitoring without serving live production traffic.
The capacity reservation configuration for the shadow production variant, specifying the capacity reservation group where the endpoint instances should be launched and the reservation preference.

Specifies whether the shadow production variant uses a specific capacity reservation (value `capacity_reservation`) or the default capacity reservation preference (value `capacity_reservation_preference`) when allocating inference capacity.

Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SageMaker ML capacity reservation assigned to the shadow production variant's capacity reservation configuration, which allows the endpoint to use pre-purchased reserved capacity for hosting the variant.

Defines the timeout in seconds for the container startup health check of this shadow production variant, controlling how long SageMaker waits for the model container to become healthy after startup before routing shadow traffic to it.

When enabled (true), grants AWS Systems Manager (SSM) access to the SageMaker container for this shadow variant, allowing secure remote shell access for debugging and troubleshooting; disabled by default.
Specifies the version of the inference AMI (Amazon Machine Image) to use for the shadow production variant in the SageMaker endpoint configuration.
The number of Amazon EC2 instances to initially launch for this shadow production variant, which handles the shadow/copied traffic for testing in the SageMaker endpoint configuration.

The initial weight (a value between 0 and 1) that determines the fraction of live inference traffic sent to this shadow production variant for testing, while the primary production variants continue to serve the actual traffic.

Specifies the instance pools for this shadow variant, where each pool defines an instance type and the number of instances to allocate on that type, enabling the variant to use multiple instance types.
Specifies the Amazon EC2 instance type (e.g., ml.m5.large) that the instance pool of this shadow production variant will use in the SageMaker endpoint configuration.
