Specifies the Cognito user group that is allowed to access this SageMaker work team.
The ID of the Amazon Cognito user pool that contains the work team members.
Specifies the OIDC identity provider (IdP) ID and a list of group names that define membership in the SageMaker work team.
Specifies the list of OIDC group names that define the members of the workteam for this OIDC member definition.

aws_sage_maker_workteam.notification_con.text: Specifies the SNS topic ARN (via its `NotificationTopicArn`) that SageMaker uses to send notifications about workteam-related events, such as labeling job updates.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic that SageMaker sends workteam lifecycle notifications to, such as when the workteam is created or updated.

aws_sage_maker_workteam.tags.text: Specifies one or more tags (key-value pairs) to assign to the SageMaker Workteam resource, enabling cost allocation and management of the workforce.

aws_sage_maker_workteam.tags.key.text: The tag key assigned to the SageMaker workteam, used for resource categorization and cost allocation.

aws_sage_maker_workteam.tags.value.text: The value portion of a user-defined tag applied to the SageMaker workteam, used for metadata such as cost allocation or environment identification.

aws_sage_maker_workteam.workforce_name.text: The name of the SageMaker workforce that this workteam is associated with, determining the pool of workers available to the workteam.

aws_sage_maker_workteam.workteam_name.text: The name of the SageMaker work team, which must be unique within your AWS account and region; if not provided, AWS CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_scheduler_schedule.name.text: Specifies the name of the Amazon EventBridge Scheduler schedule, which must be unique within a schedule group; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name for the schedule.

aws_scheduler_schedule.target.ecs_parame.text: The base value in the capacity provider strategy defines the minimum number of tasks that must be run on this capacity provider before the provider's weight is considered for additional task placement.
The short name of the capacity provider that ECS uses for placing the task when the schedule triggers.
Specifies the relative weight of this capacity provider in the strategy, determining the proportional share of tasks placed on it compared to other capacity providers.
The expression, such as attribute:instance-type =~ t2.*, that defines the placement constraint for the Amazon ECS task scheduled by this EventBridge Scheduler schedule.

The type of placement constraint for the ECS task, either 'distinctInstance' to place each task on a different container instance or 'memberOf' to constrain placement using a cluster query language expression.
Specifies the field (for example, `instanceId`, `host`, or an attribute expression) on which the ECS placement strategy operates, matching the ECS `PlacementStrategy.field` property.
Specifies the ECS placement strategy type for the scheduler-targeted task, choosing between random, spread, or binpack to control how tasks are distributed across container instances.

aws_scheduler_schedule.target.sage_maker.text: The name of the SageMaker pipeline parameter to pass to the pipeline execution when the schedule triggers the target.
The value to assign to the specified SageMaker pipeline parameter when the schedule triggers the pipeline.

aws_scheduler_schedule_group.name.text: The name of the schedule group, which must be unique within your AWS account and Region; if omitted, CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_scheduler_schedule_group.tags.key.text: The key portion of a tag attached to an AWS EventBridge Scheduler schedule group, used to identify and organize the resource.

aws_scheduler_schedule_group.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag attached to the AWS EventBridge Scheduler schedule group, used to define metadata for the resource.

aws_scn_dataset.partition_spec.fields.na.text: The name of a partition field (column) used in the dataset's partition specification to define how the dataset data is partitioned.

aws_scn_dataset.partition_spec.fields.tr.text: Defines the target data type (such as STRING, INTEGER, DATE, or TIMESTAMP) that a source field's value is transformed to when generating the partition column for the dataset's partition specification.

aws_scn_dataset.schema.fields.is_require.text: Indicates whether this field must be present in every record of the dataset, affecting data validation during ingestion.

aws_scn_dataset.schema.fields.name.text: The name of a field (column) within the schema of an AWS Supply Chain dataset, serving as the unique identifier for that attribute in the dataset.

aws_scn_dataset.schema.fields.type.text: The data type of the field (column) in the schema for the AWS Supply Chain dataset, such as STRING, INTEGER, DOUBLE, or TIMESTAMP.

aws_scn_dataset.schema.primary_keys.name.text: The name of a column designated as a primary key in the dataset's schema definition.

aws_scn_dataset.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Supply Chain dataset, used to organize, identify, or track the resource.

aws_sdb_domain.id.text: The unique identifier of the SimpleDB domain, which is set to the domain name used to reference the domain in AWS.

aws_secrets_manager_rotation_schedule.ex.text: The key of a key-value pair in the external_secret_rotation_metadata map, which is passed as metadata to an external rotation Lambda function to customize the rotation process.

aws_secrets_manager_rotation_schedule.ho.text: Configuration for a hosted AWS Secrets Manager rotation Lambda function, including the rotation type (e.g., MySQLSingleUser) and optional settings such as VPC configuration and a custom function name, which AWS Secrets Manager provisions and manages automatically to rotate the secret.

aws_secrets_manager_rotation_schedule.ro.text: Defines the rotation schedule for the secret, including how often it rotates (via automatically_after_days or a cron/rate expression) and optionally the rotation window duration.

aws_secrets_manager_secret.id.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the secret.

aws_secrets_manager_secret.replica_regio.text: For a replica of the secret in another region, this specifies the ARN, key ID, or alias of the KMS key used to encrypt the secret in that replica region; if omitted, Secrets Manager uses the default KMS key for that region.
The AWS Region to which the secret is replicated, as part of a multi-Region secret replica configuration.

aws_secrets_manager_secret.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Secrets Manager secret, used to identify the tag within the secret's tag set.

aws_secrets_manager_secret_target_attach.text: The ARN of the secret that serves as the unique identifier for this attachment resource.
The ARN or name of the AWS Secrets Manager secret to attach to the specified target (such as an RDS or Redshift cluster).
The ARN of the AWS service resource (such as an Amazon RDS database instance or Amazon Redshift cluster) that the secret is attached to.
Specifies the AWS service type of the target that the secret is attached to, such as an RDS DB instance or Redshift cluster.

aws_security_agent_agent_space.aws_resou.text: Specifies the ARNs of security groups associated with the VPCs in the agent space's AWS resource configuration, used to control network access for the agent.
Specifies the subnet ARNs associated with each VPC in the agent space's AWS resource configuration, defining the subnets the agent space applies to.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) included in the AWS resources associated with this agent space.

aws_security_agent_agent_space.integrate.text: Controls whether the Bitbucket integration automatically remediates code-level security issues identified by the agent.

A nested object representing a Bitbucket repository configured as an integrated resource provider within the security agent's agent space, containing fields that define the repository connection and integration settings.
The repository name (e.g., 'owner/repo') for a Bitbucket repo listed as a provider resource in the security agent space's integrated resources configuration.
The Bitbucket workspace that owns the integrated repository.
Enables or disables the Confluence provider resource's ability to create documents within the integrated Confluence instance for this agent space.
Configures an Atlassian Confluence document source for the agent space's integrated resources, specifying how Confluence documents are accessed and ingested by the security agent.
The name of the Confluence document that is configured as a provider resource within the integrated resource settings for the agent space.
The page_id specifies the unique Confluence page identifier that identifies the document used as a provider resource in the agent space's integrated resource configuration.
Specifies the title of the Confluence space that the Confluence document provider resource is scoped to, enabling the agent space to reference documents within that specific space.
Specifies the GitHub-specific capabilities and permissions that the security agent can use when integrating with GitHub through the agent space's provider resources.
Determines whether the security agent may leave comments on GitHub pull requests or issues as part of its integrated GitHub capabilities.
The GitHub user or organization that owns the repository to be integrated as a provider resource.
Enables automatic remediation of code vulnerabilities in integrated GitLab repositories.
The GitLab namespace (group or user path) that identifies the owner of the repository, used to locate the repository within the GitLab provider as part of an integrated resource.

aws_security_agent_application.id_cconfi.text: The ARN of the AWS IAM Identity Center (IdC) application that is used as part of the IdC configuration for this security agent application resource.

aws_security_agent_pentest.assets.integr.text: The branch of the integrated repository that the pentest agent will scan, determining which version of the code is evaluated for vulnerabilities.

aws_security_agent_pentest.assets.source.text: Specifies the S3 bucket and object key (URI) where the source code for the asset is stored for the penetration test.

aws_security_agent_security_requirement_.text: Provides a human-readable description of the security requirement, explaining the specific security control or configuration the requirement addresses.

aws_security_group.security_group_egress.text: The IPv4 address range, in CIDR form, that is allowed as the destination for outbound traffic in this security group egress rule.
The destination IPv6 CIDR block for the outbound traffic allowed by this security group egress rule, such as ::/0 for all IPv6 addresses.
A human-readable description for the outbound (egress) rule, used to document the rule's purpose or context.
The ID of the destination prefix list that the egress rule applies to, allowing traffic to the CIDR blocks defined by that prefix list (e.g., for VPC endpoints or managed prefix lists).
The ID of the destination security group for this egress rule, which allows outbound traffic to that security group.
The starting port number of the port range for this outbound (egress) rule, defining the lower bound of destination ports permitted for the specified protocol.
Specifies the IP protocol name or number (such as tcp, udp, icmp, or -1 for all protocols) that this egress rule applies to.
The end of the port range (inclusive) for the destination port in this outbound security group rule; for a single port, set it equal to from_port.

aws_security_group.security_group_ingres.text: The IPv4 CIDR block from which inbound traffic is allowed by this security group ingress rule.
The IPv6 CIDR block (e.g., 2001:db8::/32) that is allowed to send inbound traffic to the security group.
A brief, human-readable description for the security group ingress rule, used to document its purpose or source, with a maximum length of 255 characters.
The starting port number for the inbound rule's port range, or the ICMP type number when the protocol is ICMP.
Specifies the IP protocol name (such as tcp, udp, or icmp), a protocol number, or ' -1 ' to represent all protocols, for the ingress rule.
The ID of an AWS prefix list (such as a managed prefix list for AWS services or VPC endpoints) that serves as the source of the inbound traffic permitted by this ingress rule.

Specifies the ID of the source security group (in the same VPC or a peer VPC) whose instances are allowed to send inbound traffic to this security group, used as the SourceSecurityGroupId property of a security group ingress rule.

The name of the source security group whose members are allowed inbound access by this ingress rule; this is used for EC2-Classic rules, whereas VPC security groups usually reference the source by its `SourceSecurityGroupId` instead.
The AWS account ID of the owner of the referenced source security group, required when the source security group belongs to a different AWS account.
The ending port number of the range for this ingress rule; for a single port, specify the same value as from_port.

aws_security_group.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the security group, used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_security_hub_aggregator_v2.aggregati.text: The AWS Region to which Security Hub aggregates findings from all linked Regions in the cross-Region aggregation configuration.

aws_security_hub_automation_rule.actions.text: Defines the updates to apply to a finding's fields (such as severity, workflow status, or other configurable attributes) when this Security Hub automation rule action is executed.
Sets the finding confidence score (0–100) to the specified value when the automation rule action is applied.
Sets the criticality value (0–100) assigned to the finding when the automation rule's finding fields update action is applied.
The note to add to findings when the automation rule triggers a finding-fields update, including the note text and the updated-by principal.
The text of the note that will be applied to the finding when this automation rule action updates the finding's note.
Specifies the AWS principal (IAM user or role) that is recorded as the updater of the note when a Security Hub automation rule updates a finding's note.

Specifies the new list of related findings (each with product ARN and finding ID) to assign to the finding, overwriting any existing related findings when the automation rule performs the finding-field update.
The unique identifier of a related finding to associate with the finding when the automation rule updates the finding's related findings list.

The ARN of the AWS Security Hub product (e.g., an AWS service or partner solution) that generated the related finding to be attached when the automation rule updates the finding's related findings list.
The severity object in the finding fields update specifies the new severity label and product severity score to be assigned to matching findings.
Specifies the new severity label (e.g., INFORMATIONAL, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL) to apply to a finding when this automation rule action updates finding fields.
Specifies the normalized severity value (0-100) to assign to the finding's severity when the automation rule updates the finding fields.
Defines the numeric severity value (0 to 100) to assign to the finding's product severity field when a Security Hub automation rule updates a finding's severity.
Specifies the list of finding types to set on the finding when this automation rule action updates the finding fields.
Specifies the custom key-value pairs to set as the finding's user-defined fields when this automation rule action updates the finding.
When a finding matches this automation rule, this value sets the finding's verification state to the specified enum value (UNKNOWN, TRUE_POSITIVE, FALSE_POSITIVE, or BENIGN_POSITIVE).
Specifies the workflow status (e.g., NEW, NOTIFIED, SUPPRESSED, RESOLVED) to apply to findings when this automation rule action is triggered.
Specifies the workflow status to apply to the finding when the automation rule triggers, with allowed values such as NEW, NOTIFIED, SUPPRESSED, and RESOLVED.
Defines the type of automation rule action, which determines whether the rule performs a finding update (like changing workflow status or severity) or sends a notification to a chat or custom action.

aws_security_hub_automation_rule.created.text: The AWS Identity and Access Management principal (IAM user or role) that created the automation rule, returned as a read-only attribute.

aws_security_hub_automation_rule.criteri.text: Determines the string matching operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX, SUFFIX, NOT_EQUALS) used to compare the finding's AWS account ID against the value specified in the automation rule criterion.
The exact AWS account ID that a finding's AwsAccountId field must equal for the automation rule to apply.
The comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or PREFIX) that determines how the finding's company name is matched against the configured value in this automation rule criterion.
The value that the automation rule compares against the 'Company' field of a Security Hub finding, which identifies the provider or vendor that generated the finding.

Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS, PREFIX, NOT_EQUALS, or PREFIX_NOT_EQUALS) used to match a finding's compliance associated standards ID (e.g., 'standards/aws-foundational-security-best-practices/v/1.0.0') in an automation rule.

Specifies the ARN of a Security Hub standard (e.g., arn:aws:securityhub:us-east-1::standards/aws-foundational-security-best-practices) that the automation rule uses to filter findings by their associated compliance standards.
Specifies the comparison operator used to match the finding's compliance security control ID against the supplied value, such as 'EQUALS' or 'PREFIX'.
The value of the security control ID (e.g., 'EC2.1') that must match the finding's compliance.securityControlId for the automation rule criteria to be satisfied.
Defines the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS) used to match a finding's compliance status against the specified value in the criteria of a Security Hub automation rule.
The compliance status value (such as FAILED, PASSED, WARNING, or NOT_AVAILABLE) that a finding must match to trigger the automation rule.
The confidence score (0-100) that a finding's Confidence attribute must equal for the automation rule's condition to match.
Matches findings where the confidence score (0-100) is greater than or equal to the specified numeric value.
Specifies the upper bound (less than or equal to) for the confidence score of a Security Hub finding that will trigger this automation rule.
Configures the relative date range (e.g., last 7 days) used by the automation rule to match findings based on their 'CreatedAt' timestamp.
Specifies the time unit (e.g., DAYS or HOURS) used to interpret the value of the relative date range for the CreatedAt criterion, enabling filters such as 'last 7 days' or 'last 24 hours'.

The numeric value that, combined with the associated unit (e.g., DAYS), sets the relative date range for matching a finding's createdAt timestamp in the automation rule, such as 7 for the last 7 days.
The end of the timestamp range for the `created_at` criterion, matching findings created on or before this ISO 8601 date and time.
The start of the ISO 8601 timestamp range used to match findings whose creation time (createdAt) is at or after this value.
Specifies the exact criticality value (0-100) that a finding must match for the automation rule's criticality criterion to apply.
The minimum criticality (0–100) that a finding's criticality attribute must have for the automation rule's criteria to match, using a greater-than-or-equal comparison.
Specifies the upper bound (less than or equal to) for the finding's criticality value, so that findings with a criticality score at or below this number match the automation rule's criteria.
Sets the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match a finding's description against the specified value in the automation rule criteria.
The string value that Security Hub compares against a finding's description field to determine whether the automation rule applies, based on the specified comparison operator.
Defines a relative date range (with a unit and value) that filters automation rules to findings whose first observed timestamp falls within a specified number of days ago, such as the last 7 days.
Specifies the time unit (e.g., DAYS) for the date range used to filter findings by their first observed timestamp in an AWS Security Hub automation rule.

The numeric quantity (e.g., number of days) that, combined with the associated unit, defines the relative date range for filtering findings by first observed timestamp in the automation rule's criteria.
Specifies the end of the date range for the 'first observed at' criterion, filtering automation rule matches to findings first observed on or before this timestamp.
The start of the date range used to match findings whose first observed at timestamp falls within this range, formatted as an ISO 8601 string.
Specifies the comparison operator used to match a finding's generator ID against the configured value, such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS.

The generator ID value to match against a finding's GeneratorId field, used as a string filter criterion in a Security Hub automation rule to target findings from specific security products or services.
Defines the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX) used to match a finding's ID against the specified values in the Security Hub automation rule criteria.
Specifies the finding identifier (Id) value to match when the automation rule evaluates Security Hub findings against the criteria's id filter.
Defines a relative time window (e.g., last N days) using a unit and value to match findings by their last observed timestamp in an AWS Security Hub automation rule.
The unit of time (such as DAYS) paired with the date range value to filter findings by their last observed time in an AWS Security Hub automation rule.
The number of time units (as specified by the associated Unit, such as days) in the relative date range used to filter findings by when they were last observed.
The end of the date range used to match findings based on when they were last observed, so a finding's last observed timestamp must be on or before this value to trigger the automation rule.
The start (lower bound) of a timestamp range used to filter findings by the time they were last observed, matching findings whose last observed time is at or after this value.
Specifies the string comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX, SUFFIX, CONTAINS) used to match a finding's note text against the configured value in the automation rule's criteria.

In a Security Hub automation rule, this string is the value for the note_text criterion, which the rule compares against the text of a note (Note.Text) on a finding to determine whether the rule's actions apply.

Specifies the inclusive start and end timestamps that a finding's note-updated time must fall within for the 'note_updated_at' criterion, enabling the automation rule to match findings whose notes were updated during that period.
Specifies the time unit (e.g., DAYS) used with the date range's value to set a relative period for the note_updated_at finding field when evaluating the automation rule criterion.
The number of units (e.g., days) for the relative date range that defines when the finding's note was last updated, used to match automation rule criteria.
Sets the upper-bound timestamp of the date range used by the note_updated_at criterion to match findings whose note was last updated at or before that time.
The starting date-time (ISO 8601) of the range used to filter findings based on when their note was last updated.
Defines the string comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the principal that last updated a finding's note in the Security Hub automation rule criteria.
The value to match against the principal (user or role) that last updated the note on a finding, used as a filter criterion in the Security Hub automation rule.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the finding's product ARN against the given value in the automation rule criteria.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS service or integrated product that generated the finding, used to match findings from a specific product in the automation rule's criteria.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to evaluate the finding's product name against the supplied value in the automation rule's criteria.
Specifies the name of the AWS service (e.g., 'GuardDuty', 'Inspector') that must match the ProductName field of a finding for this automation rule's criteria to be satisfied.
The comparison operator used to match a finding's record state against the specified value, such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS.
Specifies the finding record state to match (e.g., 'ACTIVE' or 'ARCHIVED') when the automation rule's criteria evaluate a finding.

Specifies the comparison operator used by the Security Hub automation rule to match findings based on the related findings ID value (e.g., whether the finding's related finding ID equals or is prefixed by the provided value).
Specifies the identifier of a related finding that must appear in the finding's RelatedFindings list for the automation rule's criteria to match.
Defines the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) that determines how the related findings product ARN is matched against the specified value in the automation rule.
The ARN of the AWS service that generated the related finding, used as a match condition in the automation rule's criteria.

Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, PREFIX, CONTAINS) for the 'resource_details_other' criterion in the automation rule, determining how the finding's custom resource detail key is matched against the provided value.
The name of a custom resource detail attribute that the automation rule's criteria checks against the resource's 'Other' details map.
The value string to match against a custom 'Other' resource detail attribute in Security Hub automation rule criteria.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match a finding's resource ID against the value provided in this automation rule criterion.
The exact resource ID value that the Security Hub automation rule compares against finding resources when the resourceId criterion is evaluated.

Specifies the operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to compare a finding's resource partition (e.g., aws, aws-cn, aws-us-gov) against a configured value in this Security Hub automation rule criterion.
The value must be a valid AWS partition name (such as aws, aws-cn, or aws-us-gov) that matches the resource's partition to trigger the rule.
Defines the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the resource's AWS Region against the values specified in the resource_region filter of the Security Hub automation rule.
The AWS Region value that the resource must be in for the automation rule's resource-region criterion to match.
The comparison operator (such as EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, PREFIX, SUFFIX, CONTAINS) used to match a resource's tag value against the configured value in the Security Hub automation rule criteria.
The resource tag key that must be present on the affected resource for this automation rule's resource tag criterion to match.
The tag value that must match the resource's tag for a finding to be included in the automation rule's criteria.
Specifies the comparison operator used to match the resource type filter, such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS.
The value of the resource type to match in the automation rule, such as AwsEc2Instance or AwsS3Bucket.
Determines how the finding's severity label is compared with the criterion's value, such as EQUALS or PREFIX.
Specifies the severity label value (e.g., LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL, or INFORMATIONAL) that the Security Hub automation rule matches against findings.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX) used to match the finding's source URL against the configured value in this automation rule criterion.
The exact URL string that a finding's SourceUrl attribute must match (per the associated comparison operator) for the Security Hub automation rule criterion to be satisfied.
Determines how the finding's title is matched against the specified value, using operators such as EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, PREFIX, or NOT_PREFIX.
The string value that a finding's title must match (based on the selected comparison operator) for this automation rule criterion to be satisfied.
Specifies the comparison operator used to match the value of a finding's 'Type' field against the provided value in this Security Hub automation rule criterion.

Defines the exact finding type string (e.g., 'Software and Configuration Checks/Network Reachability/Unprotected Port') that the automation rule matches when filtering findings by the 'Type' criterion.

This DateRange object tells Security Hub to match only findings whose 'UpdatedAt' timestamp falls within a relative window, expressed as an integer value and a unit of time (for example, DAYS), from the current time.
Specifies the time unit (such as days, weeks, months, or years) for the date range used to filter findings based on when they were last updated.
The numeric length of the look-back window (used with the corresponding unit, e.g., days) for filtering findings based on their 'UpdatedAt' timestamp in an AWS Security Hub automation rule.
The end (upper bound) of the timeframe used to match findings whose last updated time falls within a range, when defining an updated_at criterion for a Security Hub automation rule.
The start of the date/time range used to filter findings by when they were last updated in Security Hub.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS) used to evaluate the user-defined field value against the automation rule's criteria.
The key is the name of a user-defined field that the automation rule checks against a finding's UserDefinedFields map to match the criteria.
Specifies the expected string value of a user-defined field on a Security Hub finding that must be matched for the automation rule to apply.
Determines the operator (such as EQUALS) that the automation rule uses to compare a finding's verification state against the configured Value in this criterion.
The exact verification state string (such as TRUE_POSITIVE, FALSE_POSITIVE, BENIGN_POSITIVE, or UNKNOWN) that the Security Hub automation rule uses to match findings in its criteria.
Determines whether the finding's workflow status must equal or not equal the specified value (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) for the Security Hub automation rule criteria to match.
Specifies the workflow status of a finding (e.g., NEW, NOTIFIED, RESOLVED, SUPPRESSED) that the automation rule's criteria must match.

aws_security_hub_automation_rule.rule_ar.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely assigned to the Security Hub automation rule when it is created.

aws_security_hub_automation_rule_v2.acti.text: Contains the configuration for sending findings to an external integration, including the ARN of the external integration defined in Security Hub.
The ARN of the external integration connector (such as a Slack or PagerDuty integration) to which this automation rule action sends findings.
Specifies the finding fields to update when this automation rule action is triggered, allowing changes to values such as severity, note, workflow status, and related findings.
The comment text to attach to the finding when this automation rule action updates the finding's fields (sets the note on the finding).
The numeric normalized severity score (0-100) that will be assigned to the finding's severity when this automation rule action updates the finding.
Specifies the type of automated response action, such as 'FINDING_FIELDS_UPDATE' to update a finding's fields, 'SNS' to publish to an SNS topic, or 'CUSTOM_ACTION' to invoke a custom action.

aws_security_hub_automation_rule_v2.crit.text: This field is the list of BooleanFilter objects within a composite filter group, where each object specifies an OCSF attribute of boolean type and the required boolean value to match in the automation rule's OCSF finding criteria.
Specifies the name of the OCSF finding attribute whose boolean value is compared in this filter, such as whether the finding is a false positive.
Specifies the matching criterion for a boolean OCSF filter in a Security Hub automation rule, including the OCSF field name, operator, and value used to evaluate findings.
Defines the boolean value that the OCSF finding attribute specified in the filter's key must equal to satisfy this boolean filter condition within an automation rule's composite OCSF criteria.
Defines a list of date-based filter conditions used within a composite filter to match OCSF findings in Security Hub automation rules based on date fields like creation or update time.

Specifies the name of the OCSF (Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework) field that the date filter condition evaluates, determining which timestamp field from the OCSF finding is compared to the provided date range or value.
Defines the actual date-based condition (e.g., a numeric timestamp, date range, or relative offset) applied when evaluating OCSF finding criteria in the automation rule's composite filter.
Specifies the start and end date values that define the time window for a date-based filter condition within an OCSF composite criteria in a Security Hub automation rule.
The time unit (DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, or YEARS) that, with the date range value, defines a relative window for matching OCSF finding criteria in the Security Hub automation rule.
The numeric quantity of the relative date range (e.g., number of days) used to match OCSF findings that occurred within a specified timeframe in the automation rule's criteria.
Specifies the upper (end) boundary of a date/time range used in a date filter within a composite filter for matching OCSF-format findings against an automation rule's criteria.

The start of the date range for a DateFilter in a composite filter, specified as an ISO 8601 string (e.g., '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z'), used to match findings with activity timestamps on or after this datetime.

Defines a list of map filter conditions within a composite criteria block that match OCSF findings based on key-value pairs in map-type fields (such as resource tags), used to determine if the automation rule applies.
The name of the specific OCSF finding field that this map filter condition evaluates, used within a composite filter to match against a defined value.

The filter object within a map filter of an OCSF finding criteria defines the condition (key, comparison operator, and value) used to match findings against map-type fields in a Security Hub automation rule.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) that determines how the map filter's value is matched against the finding's map field in the automation rule criteria.
The map key used in a map filter within the composite filter to match on a specific OCSF finding attribute in the Security Hub automation rule criteria.

In the OCSF finding criteria composite filter, this string defines the expected value that the specified map key must match for a finding to satisfy the map filter and trigger the Security Hub automation rule.

Defines numeric filter conditions (such as equals, greater than, less than) for OCSF fields within a composite filter, enabling the automation rule to match findings based on those numeric field values.
Specifies the OCSF finding field (in the finding's OCSF representation) whose numeric value is evaluated against the configured number filter condition, such as a count or score attribute.
Defines a numeric filter for an OCSF finding field, including the field identifier and the comparison operation (e.g., equals, greater than, less than) to match against the finding's numeric value.
Specifies the exact numeric value that the corresponding OCSF finding attribute must equal to satisfy the number filter within a composite filter in the Security Hub automation rule.
Defines the lower bound (greater-than-or-equal-to) value for the numeric filter, so that the automation rule matches OCSF findings whose corresponding numeric attribute is at least this value.

Specifies the maximum (less-than-or-equal-to) numeric threshold for a composite number filter on an OCSF finding attribute, so the automation rule matches only findings whose value is at or below this number.

The logical operator (e.g., `AND` or `OR`) used to combine the multiple OCSF filters within this composite filter, determining whether all or any of the sub-conditions must match for the automation rule's criteria to apply.
Defines a list of string filter conditions, each specifying an OCSF field, a comparison operator, and a value, used to match findings for this automation rule's composite filter criteria.
The name of the OCSF finding field that the string filter evaluates within the composite filter, matching findings where that field contains the specified string value.

Defines a single string filter condition inside a composite filter of an OCSF finding criteria, specifying the OCSF field name, comparison operator, and value used to match security findings for an AWS Security Hub automation rule.
Determines the comparison operator used by the string filter to match the OCSF finding field, such as EQUALS or PREFIX, within a composite filter of an AWS Security Hub automation rule.
The string value to match against the OCSF finding attribute specified by this filter's key in the Security Hub automation rule criteria.

aws_security_hub_configuration_policy.co.text: Defines the map of security control parameter names to their ParameterValue objects (containing ValueType and Value, such as custom or default) for the associated control in the Security Hub configuration policy.
The identifier of the AWS Security Hub security control (e.g., EC2.1) for which the custom parameter values are specified.

aws_security_hub_connector.connector_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned by AWS to uniquely identify this Security Hub connector.

aws_security_hub_connector.connector_id.text: The connector_id is the unique, read-only identifier that AWS Security Hub assigns to the connector upon creation.

aws_security_hub_connector.created_by.text: The AWS principal (account or IAM identity) that originally created the Security Hub connector.

aws_security_hub_connector.provider.text: Specifies the provider configuration for the Security Hub connector, including the provider type (for example, AWS or a partner) that determines how the connector is set up to ingest findings into Security Hub.

aws_security_hub_connector_v2.provider.a.text: Contains the Azure-specific configuration, including tenant ID and client credentials, that enables the Security Hub connector to ingest security findings from Microsoft Azure.
Configures the Azure subscriptions or management groups that the Security Hub connector will monitor, determining which Azure resources' findings are ingested into Security Hub.
Specifies whether the Azure connector scope is a management group or a subscription, defining which Azure resources Security Hub monitors for findings.

aws_security_hub_connector_v2.provider.j.text: This block defines the Jira Cloud connection settings for the Security Hub connector, specifying the Jira instance and authentication parameters so that findings can be exported to Jira Cloud.
The project key of the Jira Cloud project that receives Security Hub findings from this connector.

aws_security_hub_connector_v2.provider.s.text: Configures the ServiceNow integration for the Security Hub connector, specifying the instance endpoint and credentials used to deliver findings to ServiceNow.
The instance name (subdomain) of the ServiceNow tenant that AWS Security Hub connects to for delivering findings, such as 'company' in 'company.service-now.com'.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the credentials used to authenticate the ServiceNow connector.

aws_security_hub_delegated_admin.delegat.text: The AWS account identifier of the delegated Security Hub administrator.

aws_security_hub_delegated_admin.status.text: The current delegation status of the Security Hub delegated administrator account, typically ENABLED or DISABLED.

aws_security_hub_finding_aggregator.find.text: The AWS Region where the finding aggregator is created and where findings from linked Regions are aggregated.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the finding aggregator.

aws_security_hub_hub_v2.subscribed_at.text: The ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when the Security Hub hub was subscribed (enabled) in the account, returned as a computed string.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.aws_acc.text: Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or PREFIX) used to evaluate the AWS account ID filter value in the insight.
The AWS account ID that the insight filter matches against, used to include findings from that specific account.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the AWS account name in this Security Hub insight filter.
Specifies the AWS account name value that findings must match to be included in the insight's filter criteria.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.company.text: The comparison operator used to match the company name for the insight filter, such as EQUALS or PREFIX.
The company name of the security product that generated the finding, used as a filter value to include only findings from that company in the insight.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.complia.text: Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the insight filter's value against a compliance standard's associated standards ID.

The value of the compliance_associated_standards_id filter specifies the ARN (Amazon Resource Name) of an AWS Security Hub standard (such as CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark or PCI DSS) associated with a finding's compliance details, used to include or exclude findings in the insight based on that standard membership.
Defines the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match findings against the specified compliance security control ID value in a Security Hub insight filter.
The value of the compliance security control ID filter, which specifies the exact AWS Security Hub security control identifier (e.g., 'EC2.1') that findings must match to be included in the insight.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the security control parameter name when filtering findings in the Security Hub insight.
The value that specifies the name of a security control parameter to filter findings by, used as the 'Value' for the 'ComplianceSecurityControlParametersName' filter in a Security Hub insight.
The comparison operator (such as EQUALS, PREFIX, or NEQ) used to filter findings by the value of a compliance security control parameter in an AWS Security Hub insight.
Specifies the value of a compliance security control parameter to filter findings on when defining a Security Hub insight filter.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, PREFIX) used to match the finding's ComplianceStatus against the filter value in the Security Hub insight.
The compliance status value to filter findings on (e.g., PASSED, FAILED, WARNING, NOT_AVAILABLE) in a Security Hub custom insight.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.confide.text: Defines the equal-to filter for the Confidence score of a finding, matching findings whose confidence attribute is exactly equal to the specified numeric value.
Specifies the lower bound for the confidence score of a finding, filtering to findings with a confidence value greater than or equal to the specified number.
The confidence filter that matches findings with a confidence score less than or equal to the specified value.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.created.text: Defines a start and end timestamp range that filters findings by their creation time when generating the Security Hub insight.
Specifies the unit of time (DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, or YEARS) used by the date range filter to match findings by their creation date.
The number of time units (e.g., days) in the date range used to filter findings by their creation time.
The end of a date range used to filter findings in a Security Hub insight by the time they were created.
The start timestamp for the created_at date range filter, which specifies the earliest creation time for findings to be included in the Security Hub insight.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.critica.text: Specifies the exact criticality value that findings must match (equal to) for the insight filter, used to narrow results to findings with that specific numeric severity score.
When the filter is applied to an insight, filters.criticality.gte restricts the set of findings to those whose criticality score is greater than or equal to the specified numeric value.
Filters findings whose criticality score is less than or equal to the specified value.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.descrip.text: Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX, NOT_EQUALS) that determines how the insight filters findings based on their description text.
The string value that the insight uses to match against a finding's description field, as defined by the associated comparison operator in the Security Hub insight filters.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.finding.text: Specifies the exact confidence value to match in the finding provider fields, filtering findings to those where the provider's confidence equals this number.
Filters insights to include findings whose provider-defined confidence score is greater than or equal to the specified numeric value.
Specifies the inclusive upper bound for the finding provider confidence score, matching findings with a confidence value less than or equal to this number.
Specifies the numeric value for the finding provider's criticality field that findings must equal to match the insight filter, filtering based on provider-reported criticality.
Filters insights to include only findings whose provider-defined criticality value is greater than or equal to the specified number.
Filters findings to those whose provider-defined criticality score is less than or equal to the specified numeric value.

Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, PREFIX) used by the Security Hub insight filter to match the related finding ID from the finding provider fields against the configured filter value.
For an AWS Security Hub insight, this filter value specifies the related findings ID to match in the finding provider fields when filtering findings.
The comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the product ARN of related findings within the finding provider fields for the insight filter.
Specifies the product ARN used to filter findings whose finding-provider data includes related findings with that product ARN.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match findings against the finding provider's severity label filter.
Specifies the severity label value (such as CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or INFORMATIONAL) reported by the finding provider, which the insight filter uses to match findings.
Determines the condition (e.g., EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS) used to match the finding provider's original severity value in the insight filter.
The value to match against the original severity string provided by the finding provider (e.g., 'Low', 'High', or a custom severity label) when filtering insight results.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, PREFIX, or NOT_PREFIX) used to match the finding provider's type values against the specified value in the Security Hub insight filter.

Defines the value to match for the finding provider field type when filtering findings for the Security Hub insight, allowing inclusion or exclusion of findings based on the provider's reported finding types.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.first_o.text: Defines a relative time window (e.g., the last N days) used to filter findings by their first observed timestamp in the Security Hub insight.
Determines the time unit for the relative date-range filter on whether a finding was first observed, where the only supported value in AWS Security Hub is DAYS.
In an AWS Security Hub insight filter on first_observed_at, this number specifies the length of the date range (e.g., the count of days) for the filter condition.
Specifies the end of a date range (in ISO 8601 format) for filtering findings by their first observed time in the Security Hub insight.
The start of a date range used to filter findings by their first observed time, matching records with a first_observed_at value at or after this timestamp.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.generat.text: Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to filter findings by their generator ID against the value provided in the filter.
The generator ID value to match against findings, identifying the product or service that generated them, as defined by the Security Hub insight filter for the generator_id attribute.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.id.comp.text: Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match a finding's Id field against the provided filter value in the insight.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.id.valu.text: The value for the finding ID filter, used to match findings whose Id field equals or does not equal the specified string when defining an insight.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.keyword.text: The keyword string used by the Security Hub insight filter to match findings in which the keyword appears in a finding field, such as the title or a resource tag.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.last_ob.text: The date range used to filter findings based on when they were last observed, defined by a unit (e.g., DAYS) and a value representing the range length.
The unit of time for the date range used to filter findings by their last observed timestamp, with valid values typically being 'DAYS' or 'HOURS'.
The number of time units (such as days) that the date range spans when filtering findings by their last observed timestamp in a Security Hub insight.
The end of the date/time range used to filter findings by their last observed timestamp in the Security Hub insight.
The beginning of an inclusive time range used to filter findings by their last observed timestamp, specified as an ISO 8601 date/time string.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.malware.text: Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX, NOT_EQUALS, or NOT_PREFIX) used to match the malware name field against the filter value in the Security Hub insight.
The malware name value to match when filtering findings for the insight, based on the malware name attribute of a finding.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to evaluate the malware path filter against the insight's specified value.
The file path of the malware used as the value in the malware_path filter, which matches findings based on the Path field of the finding's Malware object.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the malware state against the filter value in the Security Hub insight filter.
The value of the malware state filter, used to match findings with a specific malware state such as OBSERVED or REMEDIATED.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to filter Security Hub insights by malware type.
The malware type string used to filter findings, matching the malware family or type (e.g., Spyware, Ransomware) reported in the finding's malware details.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.network.text: Specifies the comparison operator (EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the network destination domain against the filter value.
The domain name of the network destination to match in the insight's filter criteria.
The IPv4 CIDR block for the destination IP address of network traffic, used to filter which findings are included in the Security Hub insight.
Filter findings whose network destination IPv6 address falls within the specified CIDR block.
Configures the equality condition for the network destination port filter, so only findings with a destination port equal to this number are included in the insight.
The greater-than-or-equal-to condition for the destination network port number used to filter findings in a Security Hub insight.
The inclusive upper bound for the network destination port value to filter findings on, matching insights where the destination port is less than or equal to this number.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., `eq` or `neq`) used to match the network direction value (such as inbound/outbound) in the Security Hub insight filter.
Specifies the network direction (IN or OUT) used to filter findings for the Security Hub insight.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) for the network protocol filter, used to match findings based on the network protocol value.
The specific network protocol value to match (e.g., tcp, udp, or icmp) when filtering findings by network protocol.
The operator used to compare the network source domain filter value, such as EQUALS or PREFIX, in the Security Hub insight filter.
Defines the source network domain value used to filter findings in the Security Hub insight, matching the domain name associated with the source of the network connection.
The IPv4 CIDR block used to match findings whose network source IP address falls within that range for this Security Hub insight filter.
The IPv6 CIDR block used to filter findings by the source IPv6 address of the network connection.
Defines the comparison operator applied to the network source MAC address filter value, with allowed values of EQUALS, PREFIX, NOT_EQUALS, and PREFIX_NOT_EQUALS.
The MAC address to match against the network source when filtering findings for the Security Hub insight.
The numeric source port value that the insight filter uses to match findings where the network source port exactly equals this number.
In the Security Hub insight filter for network source port, this value sets the lower threshold (greater than or equal to) for the source port of findings to include.
Sets the inclusive upper bound for the source port of network connections used in the insight's filter, matching events where the source port is less than or equal to this value.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.note_te.text: Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the note text of findings against the filter value in the Security Hub insight filter.
The value specifies the text that a finding's note must contain for the insight to include the finding.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.note_up.text: The unit (DAYS or HOURS) for the date range filter that matches findings based on when a note was last updated.
The numeric value for the relative date range filter on the note_updated_at field, representing the number of units (e.g., days) to look back.
Filters findings by the end of a date range for when a note was last updated, matching notes updated at or before this RFC 3339 timestamp.
The start of a date range used to filter findings by the timestamp when a note on the finding was last updated.
The comparison operator for filtering findings by the principal that last updated a note, using allowed StringFilter values such as EQUALS and PREFIX.
Specifies the principal (such as an IAM user or role ARN) that last updated a note on a finding, used to filter which findings are included in the insight.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.process.text: The relative date range (defined by a numeric value and a unit such as DAYS or HOURS) used to filter findings based on when the associated process was launched.
The unit of time (days, weeks, months, or years) for the date range filter that matches findings by when the process was launched.
Specifies the numeric value of the relative date range (combined with the unit field) used to filter Security Hub findings by the process launch time.
The upper bound of a date range used to filter findings by the timestamp when the process was launched, where findings with a process launch time at or before this end date are included.
The start of the date/time range used to filter findings by when the associated process was launched, so only processes launched at or after this timestamp are included.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX) used to match the process name in the Security Hub insight filter.
Specifies the process name value to match when filtering findings for the insight, corresponding to the finding's ProcessName attribute.
Specifies the numeric parent process ID (PID) that a finding's process.parent_pid attribute must equal for the insight filter to match.

Specifies the lower bound for the parent process ID (PID) of the process that spawned the related finding, so that only findings with a parent process ID greater than or equal to this value are included in the insight.
Filters findings to include only those whose parent process ID (PID) is less than or equal to the specified number.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX, NOT_EQUALS, or PREFIX_NOT_EQUALS) for the process path filter, defining how the insight matches process paths.
Filters findings by the process path attribute, specifying the exact path of the executable process associated with the finding.
Filters the insight to include only findings where the process's PID (process ID) exactly matches the specified number.
Specifies the lower bound (greater than or equal to) for the process ID (PID) of the process involved in a finding, used to filter which findings are included in the security insight.

This field sets the less-than-or-equal-to condition for filtering Security Hub findings based on the process ID (PID) of the process associated with the finding, matching findings whose process PID is less than or equal to the specified value.

Specifies the date range for filtering findings by when the process terminated, defined either as absolute start and end timestamps (Start, End) or as a relative range (Value, Unit) like 'last 5 days'.
Specifies the time unit (either 'DAYS' or 'WEEKS') for the relative date range used to filter findings based on when the associated process terminated in the Security Hub insight.
Specifies the numeric amount of the date range unit (e.g., days) used when filtering findings by the process termination time relative to the current date.
The exclusive end timestamp of the date range used to filter security findings by the time the related process was terminated, matching findings whose process terminated at or before this bound.
Specifies the start of the date range used to filter findings for the insight based on when the associated process was terminated.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.product.text: The comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match findings against the specified product_arn filter value when selecting findings for the Security Hub insight.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the product (e.g., an AWS service or a partner solution) that generated the findings, used as a filter value to include or exclude those findings in the Security Hub insight.
The comparison operator used to match the product field value, such as EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, CONTAINS, PREFIX, NOT_PREFIX, SUFFIX, or NOT_SUFFIX.

The key of a product-fields filter entry, identifying a product-specific field name (such as 'aws/securityhub/ProductName') whose value, defined by the entry's value, is used to match findings in the insight.
The value to match against a product-specific field for the filter, used to include findings in the Security Hub insight.
Defines the comparison operator (e.g., 'EQUALS' or 'PREFIX') for the product name filter within the Security Hub insight's filters.
Specifies the AWS service name (product name) to filter findings by, such as 'GuardDuty' or 'Security Hub', so an insight only includes findings from that service.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.recomme.text: Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS, PREFIX, or NOT_EQUALS) used to match a finding's recommendation text against the provided filter value.
Specifies the string to match when filtering findings by the recommendation text (Recommendation.Text) in a Security Hub insight.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.record_.text: The comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used by the record state string filter to match a finding's RecordState against the filter's Value when selecting which findings the insight includes.
Specifies the record state value (e.g., ACTIVE or ARCHIVED) that findings must match for the insight's RecordState filter.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.region..text: Specifies the comparison operator used to filter findings based on the AWS Region, such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS.
Specifies an AWS Region value (e.g., 'us-east-1') that a finding's Region must match for it to be included in the insight's filter criteria.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.related.text: Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the related findings ID filter criteria for the Security Hub insight.
The value of a related findings ID used to filter findings in the Security Hub insight.
Specifies the comparison operator for matching the product ARN of related findings in the insight filter, such as EQUALS or PREFIX.

For the related_findings_product_arn filter in a Security Hub insight, this value specifies the product ARN of related findings that the insight's findings must be associated with to match the filter.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.resourc.text: Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX) used to match a finding's resource application ARN against the filter value in the Security Hub insight.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the application associated with the resource, used as the value for the insight filter to match findings based on that application ARN.
Sets the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX) used to match the resource application name in the Security Hub insight's filter criteria.
Specifies the application name value to filter findings by, matching the `Resource.ApplicationName` attribute of the resource associated with each finding in the Security Hub insight.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to filter Security Hub findings based on the IAM instance profile ARN of the EC2 instance.
Defines the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM instance profile to use as a filter value for matching EC2 instance resources in the Security Hub insight.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the EC2 instance's AMI image ID against the filter value for this Security Hub insight filter.
Specifies an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) ID to match for EC2 instances in the Security Hub insight filter.
Specifies a CIDR block to match against the IPv4 addresses assigned to EC2 instances in the filtered findings.
Filters Security Hub findings based on the IPv6 CIDR block assigned to an EC2 instance's IPv6 address, matching only findings whose resource address falls within the specified CIDR range.
Specifies the comparison operator used to match the EC2 instance key name filter, such as EQUALS, PREFIX, or NOT_EQUALS.
Specifies the EC2 instance key pair name to match when filtering Security Hub findings for the resource.
Defines a start and end date range used to filter findings to those where the associated EC2 instance was launched within that period.
Specifies the time unit (such as days, weeks, months, or years) for the relative date range used to filter EC2 instances based on their launch time in the Security Hub insight.
The numeric value that, together with the unit, defines the date range (e.g., the last N days) used to filter EC2 instances by their launch time in the Security Hub insight filter.
The end date (ISO 8601 format) of the time range used to filter for EC2 instances that were launched on or before this timestamp, within the Security Hub insight's resource filter.
The start of the date/time range used to filter Security Hub insights based on when the associated EC2 instance was launched, specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX, NOT_EQUALS) used to filter Security Hub findings by the EC2 instance's subnet ID.
The subnet ID of the EC2 instance that findings must match for this Security Hub insight filter.
Defines the comparison operator (such as EQUALS, PREFIX, or NOT_EQUALS) that determines how the EC2 instance type filter value is matched in the Security Hub insight.
An AWS EC2 instance type (e.g., t3.micro) that the insight filter matches against to include only resources running that instance type.
Specifies the string comparison operator (for example, EQUALS or PREFIX) used to filter Security Hub insights by the VPC ID of an EC2 instance.
The VPC ID of the EC2 instance to match when filtering findings for this insight.
Defines a relative time range (specified by a numeric value and a unit such as DAYS) used to filter insights for resources whose associated IAM access key was created within that period.
The time unit (e.g., DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, YEARS) applied with the date range value to filter insights based on the creation date of IAM access keys.
The numeric value for the date range filter that selects resources based on when their AWS IAM access key was created, interpreted according to the associated unit (e.g., days).
The end of a date range used to filter findings by the creation timestamp of the AWS IAM access key associated with the resource.
The start date and time of the range used to filter Security Hub findings by the creation date of the associated IAM access key.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., 'equals', 'contains', 'starts_with') used to match the IAM access key principal name in the Security Hub insight filter.
The string value that must match the principal name of an IAM access key resource in a finding for that finding to be included in the Security Hub insight.
Defines the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the IAM access key status filter value when selecting findings for this Security Hub insight.
Specifies the access key status value (such as 'Active' or 'Inactive') used by the 'ResourceAwsIamAccessKeyStatus' filter to match findings in a Security Hub insight's filter criteria.
The comparison operator to apply when filtering insights by the IAM access key user name, such as EQUALS or PREFIX.
Defines the exact user name of the AWS IAM access key to match when filtering findings for the insight's `resource_aws_iam_access_key_user_name` filter.
The comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the IAM user user name of a resource against the value provided in the resourceAwsIamUserUserName filter.
The IAM user name to match when filtering findings for the resource type AWS IAM user, used as the value in the resource_aws_iam_user_user_name filter of the Security Hub insight.
Defines the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used when filtering findings by the S3 bucket owner ID of the resource.
The canonical user ID of the S3 bucket owner to match when filtering findings for insights, used as the value for this filter.

In an AWS Security Hub insight, this string specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) for the resource_aws_s3_bucket_owner_name filter, determining how the S3 bucket owner name is matched against the provided value.

The value specifies the AWS account name of the owner of the S3 bucket to match when filtering findings for the Security Hub insight, corresponding to the 'resource.aws.s3Bucket.ownerName' filter criterion.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used by the Security Hub insight filter to match the resource container image ID against the filter value.
Specifies the container image ID (string) to match against the resource's container image ID when filtering findings for the Security Hub insight.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used by this Security Hub insight filter to match the container image name of a resource.

The string value to match against the container image name of the resource associated with a finding, used as the value for the resourceContainerImageName filter in the Security Hub insight definition.
Defines the relative date range (value and unit, such as days) used to filter insights based on when the related resource container was launched, part of the resource_container_launched_at filter.

Specifies the unit of time (currently only 'DAYS') used by the relative date range filter for resource_container_launched_at, determining the window for when a resource's container was launched in the Security Hub insight.
The number of time units (such as days) to look back when filtering insights by the resource container's launch date, forming a relative date range.
The end of the date range (in ISO 8601 format) used to filter findings based on when the related container was launched.
The start of the date range used to filter findings by when the container was launched, expressed as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX) used to match the resource container name filter for the insight.
The string value used to match the name of the container associated with a finding's resource, filtering findings in a Security Hub insight.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, or CONTAINS) used to evaluate the resource's other detail key-value pair against the filter value in the Security Hub insight filter.
The key (name) of a custom 'Other' resource detail attribute used to filter findings, matching resources that have a non-standard detail with this key and the configured filter value.
The value string to match against a custom resource detail attribute (identified by the corresponding key) when filtering findings for the Security Hub insight.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match findings against the resource ID value when defining the insight's filter.
The value used to filter findings by the AWS resource ID of the affected resource, as part of the resource_id string filter for a Security Hub insight.
The comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the resource partition (such as aws, aws-cn, or aws-us-gov) in the Security Hub insight filter.
Specifies the AWS partition (e.g., aws, aws-cn, aws-us-gov) to filter findings by, matching only findings whose resource partition equals this value.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the resource's AWS Region against the filter value in the insight filter.
The AWS region identifier (such as us-east-1) that a resource must belong to in order to match the insight's resource region filter.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX, NOT_EQUALS) used by the Security Hub insight's resource tag filter to match tag values against the filter value.
The tag key that findings' resource tags must match for the resource tags filter condition in the insight.
The resource tag value that must be associated with a finding's affected resource in order for that finding to match the insight's resource tag filter.
The comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX) used to match resource type values in the insight filter.

Specifies the exact AWS resource type (e.g., AwsEc2Instance, AwsS3Bucket) that the insight's resource type filter matches, determining which findings are included based on the type of resource involved.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.sample..text: Determines whether to include only sample findings (true) or only non-sample findings (false) in the Security Hub insight.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.severit.text: Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match the severity label (such as CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW) in the insight filter.
Specifies the severity label string (e.g., LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or CRITICAL) that the insight uses to filter findings based on their severity label.
Specifies the equality condition for the normalized severity score (0-100), returning findings where severity_normalized equals this exact number.
Matches findings with a normalized severity score greater than or equal to the specified number.
Filters findings whose normalized severity score is less than or equal to the specified value.
Filters insight results to findings where the finding's original product severity (severity_product) equals the specified number.

Defines the greater-than-or-equal-to threshold for the numeric severity score (0–100) assigned by the originating security product, used to include only findings that meet this minimum in the Security Hub insight.

The `lte` value sets the inclusive upper bound for the product severity score in a Security Hub insight filter, causing the insight to include only findings whose product severity is less than or equal to the given number.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.source_.text: Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX) used to match a finding's source URL against the filter's value in the Security Hub insight.
The string value to match against a finding's SourceUrl attribute when this filter is used to include or exclude findings in the Security Hub insight.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.threat_.text: Sets the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the threat intel indicator category filter value in an AWS Security Hub insight's filter criteria.
The threat intelligence indicator category value (e.g., DOMAIN, IP, EMAIL) used by the filter to match findings for the insight.

Configures a relative time window (e.g., last 7 days) for the threat_intel_indicator_last_observed_at filter, limiting results to insights whose threat intelligence indicators were last observed within that period.
Defines the unit of measure for the relative time window (for example, DAYS or HOURS) used to filter Security Hub insights based on when a threat intelligence indicator was last observed.
The number of units (e.g., days) in the relative date range used to filter findings by when a threat intelligence indicator was last observed.
The end of the date range used to filter findings by the last observed timestamp of a threat intelligence indicator.

Sets the inclusive start of the date range for the threat_intel_indicator_last_observed_at filter, so the insight includes findings whose threat intelligence indicator was last observed at or after this timestamp.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match the threat intelligence indicator source value when filtering findings for the Security Hub insight.
Specifies the threat intelligence indicator source to match when filtering findings for this insight, corresponding to the finding's ThreatIntelIndicatorSource attribute.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or PREFIX) used to match findings against the threat intelligence indicator's source URL in a Security Hub insight filter.
The value of this filter specifies the source URL of a threat intelligence indicator that findings must match to be included in the insight.
Defines how the threat intelligence indicator type filter matches findings, using a comparison operator such as EQUALS or PREFIX against the specified indicator type value(s).
The threat intelligence indicator type value to match in the insight filter, such as DOMAIN, IPV4_ADDRESS, or URL, used to include findings whose indicator type equals the specified value.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, or PREFIX) used to match a finding's threat intelligence indicator value against the filter's value.
Filters findings by the value of a threat intelligence indicator, matching the ThreatIntelIndicator.Value field of a finding.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.title.c.text: The comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, PREFIX) used to filter findings by their title field within the Security Hub insight's filter criteria.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.title.v.text: The title text to match against finding titles when filtering findings for the Security Hub insight, used with a comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS) defined in the corresponding filter condition.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.type.co.text: Determines the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or PREFIX) used when matching the finding type filter for the Security Hub insight.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.type.va.text: The exact finding type string (e.g., 'Software and Configuration Checks' or a custom type) that the insight's Type filter matches against when filtering findings.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.updated.text: Specifies a relative date range for the UpdatedAt filter, using a numeric value and a unit (e.g., 7 DAYS), so that the insight only includes findings whose last update occurred within that time window.
Specifies the time unit (e.g., 'DAYS') for the date range used to filter findings by their last updated timestamp in a Security Hub insight.

The number of time units (matching the associated `unit` value, e.g., days) in the relative date range used to filter findings based on when they were last updated (UpdatedAt), such as a value of 7 with unit DAYS to include findings updated in the last 7 days.
The upper bound of the date range for filtering findings by when they were last updated, used in the UpdatedAt date filter of an AWS Security Hub insight.
The start of the date range for filtering findings by their last update time, used in the updated_at filter for a Security Hub insight.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.user_de.text: The comparison operator used to match the value of a user-defined field in the Security Hub findings filter, such as EQUALS, PREFIX, or NOT_EQUALS.
The name of a user-defined field used as a filter criterion for the insight, matching findings that have that field set.
For a Security Hub insight filter on a user-defined (custom) finding field, this is the value that the field must equal for a finding to match the insight filter.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.verific.text: The comparison operator used to match the verification state of findings in the insight filter, such as EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, PREFIX, or PREFIX_NOT_EQUALS.
Specifies the verification state value (e.g., TRUE_POSITIVE, FALSE_POSITIVE, BENIGN_POSITIVE, or UNKNOWN) to filter findings for the insight.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.vulnera.text: Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match findings against the vulnerabilities_exploit_available filter value in a Security Hub insight.
