The value of the string filter for `VulnerabilitiesExploitAvailable`, which specifies the desired exploit-availability state (such as YES or NO) that findings must match to be included in the insight.

Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS) used to match the vulnerability fix availability status against the filter's expected value, enabling the insight to include or exclude findings based on whether a fix is available.
Specifies the string value (e.g., 'true' or 'false') that findings' vulnerability fix availability status must match for the insight filter.

aws_security_hub_insight.filters.workflo.text: Determines whether the workflow state filter matches findings whose workflow state equals the specified value (EQUALS) or does not equal that value (NOT_EQUALS).
The workflow state value of the finding (e.g., NEW, NOTIFIED, RESOLVED, SUPPRESSED) that this insight filter matches against when selecting findings.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to match a finding's workflow status against the value defined in this insight filter.
Specifies the Security Hub workflow status (such as `NEW`, `NOTIFIED`, `RESOLVED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, or `DEFERRED`) that findings must match to be included in the insight's filter.

aws_security_hub_security_control.parame.text: A map of parameter names to their configurations (with value type and actual value) that customize the behavior of the security control.

aws_security_hub_security_control.securi.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Security Hub security control to which this resource's settings (such as parameters or enablement) apply.
The unique identifier (e.g., 'ACM.1') of the AWS Security Hub security control to configure, which targets that control for parameter updates.

aws_security_hub_standard.disabled_stand.text: The user-supplied reason for disabling the specified Security Hub standard control in the DisabledStandardsControls list of the AWS::SecurityHub::Standard resource.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the specific Security Hub standard control that is disabled for this standard membership.

aws_security_hub_standard.standards_subs.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the subscription to a Security Hub standard.

aws_security_lake_data_lake.lifecycle_co.text: The number of days after object creation that the lifecycle transition moves the data to the storage class defined in the parent transition rule.
The S3 storage class (e.g., STANDARD_IA, GLACIER) that this lifecycle transition moves the data lake's objects to after the specified transition_days.

aws_security_lake_data_lake.tags.text: A list of tag objects (each with a key and value) assigned to the AWS Security Lake data lake, used for metadata organization, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_security_lake_data_lake.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a tag in the Tags map that attaches user-defined metadata to the AWS Security Lake data lake, commonly used for cost allocation and resource organization.

aws_security_lake_data_lake.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag assigned to the AWS Security Lake data lake, used to attach arbitrary metadata for resource management and identification.

aws_security_lake_subscriber.resource_sh.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) resource share that grants the subscriber access to the Security Lake data lake.
The name of the AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) resource share automatically created to grant the subscriber access to Security Lake data.

aws_security_lake_subscriber.s3_bucket_a.text: For S3 subscribers, the ARN of the S3 bucket where Security Lake delivers data, computed and returned after the subscriber resource is created.

aws_security_lake_subscriber.subscriber_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Security Lake subscriber, automatically assigned by AWS when the subscriber is created.
The ARN of the IAM role that the subscriber uses to access the data lake, assigned by Security Lake when the subscriber is created.

aws_security_lake_subscriber.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Security Lake subscriber, used to define the tag's name for organizing and identifying the subscriber resource.

aws_security_lake_subscriber_notificatio.text: Configuration specifying how to notify the subscriber of new data, either via an SQS queue or an HTTPS endpoint.

aws_service_catalog_app_registry_applica.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AppRegistry application, which uniquely identifies it within AWS and is assigned on creation.
The unique identifier (ApplicationId) of the AppRegistry application, assigned by AWS and used to reference the application in other AppRegistry resources.
Assigns AWS resource tags to the Service Catalog AppRegistry application to help identify, organize, and manage it.

aws_service_catalog_app_registry_attribu.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the attribute group, assigned by AWS upon creation.

The attributes field is a required JSON object of key-value pairs that defines the actual attribute data stored by this AppRegistry attribute group, which can be used to associate metadata like environment, project, or owner with AWS applications and resources.
The unique identifier assigned to the AppRegistry attribute group when it is created, used as the primary reference to this resource.
A map of key-value pairs to attach to the attribute group for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource in AWS Service Catalog AppRegistry.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the application associated with the attribute group in this AppRegistry attribute group association.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the attribute group that is associated with the application in AWS Service Catalog AppRegistry.

aws_service_catalog_app_registry_resourc.text: The ARN of the AWS Service Catalog AppRegistry application that this resource association links the associated resource to, which is automatically set by AWS and read-only.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the resource associated with the AppRegistry application, returned by AWS Service Catalog AppRegistry after the association is created.

aws_service_catalog_cloud_formation_prod.text: Provides a user-friendly description of this provisioning artifact (a version of the product's CloudFormation template), which is displayed to end users in the AWS Service Catalog console when they view or launch the product.

If set to true, disables AWS Service Catalog's validation of the CloudFormation template associated with this provisioning artifact, allowing the product to be created without the service checking the template's syntax or resource definitions.
Specifies the template source information for the provisioning artifact, such as the S3 URL (via the LoadTemplateFromURL key) where the CloudFormation template is stored.

Specifies the physical ID (such as an Amazon S3 object ARN) of an existing CloudFormation template to import as the provisioning artifact, used instead of a template URL to reference the template directly by its resource identification.
Specifies the URL from which the CloudFormation template for this provisioning artifact is loaded.
The name of the provisioning artifact, displayed as the version name for this CloudFormation product in Service Catalog.

The type of provisioning artifact, which can be CLOUD_FORMATION_TEMPLATE, MARKETPLACE, or TERRAFORM, and dictates whether the product template is a CloudFormation template, AWS Marketplace artifact, or Terraform configuration.

Defines the connection to an external source repository (such as AWS CodeStar or GitHub) from which the CloudFormation template for the product is retrieved, including repository details, branch, and folder.

Provides the CodeStar-specific connection details (such as the CodeStar connection ARN, repository branch, and repository path) used by the Service Catalog product to import its template from a source repository.
The key of a tag to assign to the Service Catalog CloudFormation product.
The value of a tag attached to the AWS Service Catalog CloudFormation product, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_service_catalog_cloud_formation_prov.text: Specifies the language code (such as en or jp) used by AWS Service Catalog for localized responses, error messages, and documentation when managing the provisioned product.
The ARN of the CloudFormation stack that AWS Service Catalog provisions for this provisioned product.
Specifies the Amazon SNS topic ARNs to which AWS Service Catalog sends provisioning event notifications for this provisioned product.
The unique identifier of the launch path within AWS Service Catalog that determines which portfolio and constraint combination is used to provision this product.
The name of the Service Catalog provisioning path that identifies the specific product-portfolio association and launch constraints used to provision this product.
The unique identifier of the Service Catalog product from which this provisioned product is created.
The name of the Service Catalog product to provision, used as an alternative to specifying the product ID when provisioning a product.
The unique identifier (e.g., pp-xxxxxxxx) assigned by AWS Service Catalog to the provisioned product, used to reference and manage the provisioned resource.
The user-friendly name of the provisioned product within AWS Service Catalog.
The identifier of the provisioning artifact (product version) to use when provisioning the Service Catalog product.
The name of the Service Catalog provisioning artifact (product version) to use when provisioning the product.
Provides a list of key-value pairs that supply the values for parameters defined in the AWS CloudFormation template of the Service Catalog product being provisioned.
Specifies the name of a provisioning parameter for the Service Catalog product, matching the parameter key defined in the product's CloudFormation template or provisioning artifact.
The value associated with a provisioning parameter key that is supplied to the AWS CloudFormation template during product provisioning.
Specifies provisioning preferences for the product, including StackSet accounts and regions, failure tolerance counts, and maximum concurrent operation counts for stack set deployments.
Specifies the list of AWS account IDs where the associated AWS CloudFormation StackSet deploys when provisioning this Service Catalog product.
Specifies the number of accounts, per Region, for which stack set operation failures are tolerated before the operation is aborted.
Specifies the percentage of accounts, per Region, for which a stack set operation can fail before AWS CloudFormation stops the operation and rolls back the stack.
The maximum number of accounts in which AWS CloudFormation StackSets can create stacks concurrently during stack set provisioning.
Specifies the maximum percentage of accounts in which stack instances are created or updated concurrently when AWS Service Catalog provisions the product using a StackSet.
Specifies whether the AWS CloudFormation StackSet operation performed during provisioning is a create or update operation.
Specifies the AWS Regions where CloudFormation StackSet instances are created when the provisioned product is deployed as a stack set.
The unique identifier of the provisioning record for the provisioned product, which tracks the provisioning operation's status and details in AWS Service Catalog.
Specifies the list of tags (key-value pairs) to associate with the provisioned product, which are applied to the provisioned CloudFormation stack and its resources.
A user-specified key for a tag that AWS Service Catalog applies to the provisioned product.
Specifies the value of a tag key-value pair that AWS Service Catalog applies to the provisioned product.

aws_service_catalog_launch_notification_.text: Specifies the language code (e.g., 'en') used for responses from the AWS Service Catalog API when managing this launch notification constraint.
A free-form text description of the Service Catalog launch notification constraint, which specifies an SNS topic that receives notifications for provisioning and termination events.
The list of Amazon SNS topic ARNs that receive stack event notifications when the associated product is launched via this Service Catalog launch notification constraint.
The identifier of the Service Catalog portfolio to which the launch notification constraint applies.
The identifier of the Service Catalog product to which this launch notification constraint is associated, controlling which product's stack events trigger the configured SNS notifications.

aws_service_catalog_portfolio.accept_lan.text: Specifies the language code (such as 'en' or 'jp') that AWS Service Catalog uses for localized text when returning portfolio details, ensuring the portfolio's description and related metadata appear in the requested language.

aws_service_catalog_portfolio.descriptio.text: A user-friendly description of the Service Catalog portfolio, providing additional context about its purpose and contents.

aws_service_catalog_portfolio.display_na.text: The name of the portfolio, as displayed in the AWS Service Catalog console.

aws_service_catalog_portfolio.id.text: The unique Service Catalog portfolio identifier (e.g., 'port-xxxxxx') assigned by AWS when the portfolio is created, used to reference the portfolio in other resources and API calls.

aws_service_catalog_portfolio.portfolio_.text: The name of the AWS Service Catalog portfolio, automatically populated from the portfolio's DisplayName attribute when read from AWS.

aws_service_catalog_portfolio.provider_n.text: The name of the person or organization that owns and manages the Service Catalog portfolio.

aws_service_catalog_portfolio.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Service Catalog portfolio, used to organize and identify the portfolio for cost allocation and management.

aws_service_catalog_portfolio.tags.value.text: The value (a string) of a key-value tag that can be assigned to the AWS Service Catalog portfolio for organizational purposes.

aws_service_catalog_service_action.accep.text: Specifies the language code (e.g., 'en' for English) used for localized text such as the service action's name and description when interacting with AWS Service Catalog.

aws_service_catalog_service_action.defin.text: Specifies the definition of the Service Catalog service action, including the AWS Systems Manager automation document name, version, IAM assume role, and parameters.
The key of a definition entry, which specifies the service action definition parameter being set, such as Name, Version, AssumeRole, or Parameters.
Specifies the value of the service action definition, such as the ARN of an AWS Systems Manager automation document or an AWS Lambda function that the action invokes.
Specifies the type of service action definition, which for AWS Service Catalog service actions must be set to SSM_AUTOMATION to reference an AWS Systems Manager automation document.

aws_service_catalog_service_action.descr.text: A user-defined, human-readable description of the Service Catalog self-service action, displayed in the AWS Management Console to help users understand the action's purpose.

aws_service_catalog_service_action.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the Service Catalog service action, used to reference it across the AWS service.

aws_service_catalog_service_action.name.text: The human-readable name of the AWS Service Catalog service action, required to uniquely identify and display the action in the Service Catalog console and API.

aws_service_catalog_service_action_assoc.text: The ID (or identifier) of the AWS Service Catalog product to which the self-service action is associated.
The ID of the provisioning artifact (product version) that the service action is associated with.
The ID of the AWS Service Catalog service action that this association attaches to the specified provisioning artifact.

aws_service_discovery_http_namespace.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the HTTP namespace in AWS.

aws_service_discovery_http_namespace.des.text: Provides an optional human-readable description for the HTTP namespace, helping to identify its purpose or distinguish it from other namespaces in service discovery.

aws_service_discovery_http_namespace.id.text: The ID of the HTTP namespace, assigned by AWS Cloud Map when the namespace is created.

aws_service_discovery_http_namespace.nam.text: The name of the HTTP namespace, which must be unique within the AWS account and can contain up to 1024 characters.

aws_service_discovery_http_namespace.tag.text: Specifies a list of key-value tags to associate with the HTTP namespace, enabling you to organize, identify, and manage cost allocation for the namespace.
Specifies the key (name) of a tag applied to the AWS CloudFormation Service Discovery HTTP namespace, forming the key half of a key-value tag pair.

aws_service_discovery_instance.instance_.text: This field is a required map of key-value pairs that define the instance's attributes for AWS Cloud Map service discovery, including standard keys like AWS_INSTANCE_IPV4, AWS_INSTANCE_IPV6, and AWS_INSTANCE_PORT, as well as any custom attributes you need to associate with the instance.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS Cloud Map to the instance when it is registered within the service.

aws_service_discovery_instance.service_i.text: The ID of the AWS Cloud Map service that this instance is registered with, used as the parent service for the instance's health and discovery configuration.

aws_service_discovery_private_dns_namesp.text: Defines the DNS properties for the private namespace, specifically the SOA (Start of Authority) record settings that control the default DNS behavior for the namespace.
Configures the start of authority (SOA) record settings for the private DNS namespace, allowing you to set the time-to-live (TTL) for the SOA record.
Specifies the time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for the SOA (Start of Authority) record of the private DNS namespace, controlling how long DNS resolvers cache the SOA information.

aws_service_discovery_public_dns_namespa.text: The `properties` object contains the configuration attributes of the AWS Cloud Map public DNS namespace, including the required `Name`, optional `Description`, and optional `DnsProperties` (which defines SOA record settings).
Configures DNS behavior for the public namespace, specifically the SOA record TTL that controls how long resolvers cache the namespace's authoritative data.
This object configures the Start of Authority (SOA) record settings for the public DNS namespace, including the TTL value that determines how long DNS resolvers cache the namespace's SOA record.
The time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for the Start of Authority (SOA) record of the public DNS namespace, controlling how long DNS resolvers cache that record.
The key of a tag assigned to the public DNS namespace, used to organize and identify the resource for cost allocation and management.

aws_service_discovery_service.dns_config.text: The time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for the DNS record, controlling how long resolvers cache it before querying AWS Cloud Map again.
Specifies the DNS record type (A, AAAA, SRV, or CNAME) for the service's DNS records.

aws_service_discovery_service.tags.key.text: This key identifies a tag attached to the AWS Cloud Map service, allowing you to assign metadata for cost tracking, access control, or resource organization.

aws_service_discovery_service.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the AWS CloudFormation service discovery service, used to organize, identify, or manage the resource through key-value pairs.

aws_ses_configuration_set.sending_option.text: Indicates whether email sending is enabled for the configuration set.

aws_ses_configuration_set.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Amazon SES configuration set.

aws_ses_configuration_set.tags.value.text: Specifies the value part of a tag assigned to the SES configuration set, used for metadata and resource management.

aws_ses_configuration_set_event_destinat.text: The event destination object that specifies which event types (such as send, bounce, or complaint) to publish and to which destination (Amazon SNS, CloudWatch, or Kinesis Firehose).
Specifies the fallback value for the CloudWatch dimension when the dimension value source (message tag or email header) is not present in the email.

Sets the name of the CloudWatch dimension that Amazon SES attaches to the metrics it publishes for this configuration set's event destination, allowing the metric to be filtered by that dimension in CloudWatch.

The dimension_value_source field specifies whether the dimension value is derived from an email header ('emailHeader') or from a message tag ('messageTag') when publishing SES event data to CloudWatch.
The ARN of the Amazon EventBridge bus to which the SES event is delivered.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic that Amazon SES publishes event notifications to when an email event such as send, bounce, complaint, or delivery occurs.
The unique identifier for this resource, composed of the configuration set name and the event destination name separated by a colon (e.g., 'my-set:my-destination').

aws_ses_contact_list.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to this Amazon SES contact list, used for metadata and resource identification.

aws_ses_contact_list.tags.value.text: The value of a key-value tag attached to the SES contact list, used for metadata and resource management.

aws_ses_contact_list.topics.default_subs.text: The default subscription status (OPT_IN or OPT_OUT) that applies to contacts added to the contact list for this topic when they do not specify an explicit preference.

aws_ses_contact_list.topics.description.text: Specifies a description of the topic in the contact list, providing additional context about the purpose of the topic.

aws_ses_contact_list.topics.display_name.text: The human-readable name for the topic, displayed to contacts when they manage their subscriptions.

aws_ses_contact_list.topics.topic_name.text: The unique, required name for a topic in the SES contact list, used to identify it when configuring subscription preferences and list management.

aws_ses_custom_verification_email_templa.text: The key part of a tag attached to the Amazon SES custom verification email template, used to categorize or identify the template.

aws_ses_dedicated_ip_pool.tags.key.text: The key (e.g., 'Environment') of a tag assigned to this SES dedicated IP pool, used to categorize or identify the resource.

aws_ses_dedicated_ip_pool.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag assigned to the Amazon SES dedicated IP pool, providing user-defined metadata for resource organization and management.

aws_ses_email_identity.dkim_dnstoken_nam.text: The first CNAME record name (DKIM DNS token name) that you must publish in your DNS configuration to complete Easy DKIM setup for this Amazon SES email identity.
The second of three DNS record names (CNAME route) generated for Easy DKIM, which must be added to the domain's DNS settings to complete identity verification.
For the third Easy DKIM token generated for this SES identity, this is the DNS CNAME record name that you must publish in your domain's DNS settings to complete DKIM verification.

aws_ses_email_identity.dkim_dnstoken_val.text: This read-only value is the first of three DKIM DNS token values that must be published as a CNAME record in your DNS to enable DKIM signing for the SES email identity.
The second of three DNS CNAME record values that must be published to complete Easy DKIM verification for the SES email identity.
The third DKIM DNS token value, automatically generated by Amazon SES for this email identity, which is used as the record name in the CNAME record required for Easy DKIM authentication.

aws_ses_email_identity.tags.key.text: The key of a tag applied to the SES email identity, used for organizing and managing the identity via metadata.

aws_ses_email_identity.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the SES email identity, used for metadata and resource management.

aws_ses_mail_manager_addon_instance.addo.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned by AWS that uniquely identifies this Mail Manager add-on instance.
The unique identifier assigned to this addon instance by AWS SES Mail Manager.
The name of the add-on (such as Spamhaus) that this addon instance provides, determined by the addon subscription and returned as a read-only attribute.
The ID of the addon subscription that this addon instance is associated with.

aws_ses_mail_manager_addon_instance.tags.text: Specifies the list of tag objects (key and value) to assign to the SES Mail Manager add-on instance for metadata management and cost allocation.
The key of a tag attached to the SES Mail Manager Addon Instance, used for metadata and resource organization.
The value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS SES Mail Manager add-on instance, used for organization, cost allocation, and access control as an arbitrary string.

aws_ses_mail_manager_addon_subscription..text: The name of the third-party email security or spam filtering add-on that this SES Mail Manager add-on subscription subscribes to, enabling its features for the associated mail managers.
The unique Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned by AWS to this add-on subscription, used to reference the subscription in IAM policies and other AWS services.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this addon subscription, used to reference the subscription in other resources.
Specifies the tags to apply to the SES Mail Manager Add-On Subscription, where each tag object contains a key and value pair for resource metadata and cost allocation.

Specifies the value component of a tag assigned to the SES Mail Manager Add-On Subscription, allowing you to associate arbitrary metadata with the resource for purposes such as cost tracking or resource organization.

aws_ses_mail_manager_address_list.addres.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this address list within AWS SES Mail Manager.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the address list resource, generated upon creation and used to reference this address list in Mail Manager policies and configurations.
Sets the name of the address list, which identifies it in the SES Mail Manager console and API.

aws_ses_mail_manager_address_list.tags.text: Specifies the key-value tags to attach to the SES Mail Manager address list resource, enabling organization, identification, and cost allocation within AWS.

aws_ses_mail_manager_address_list.tags.v.text: The value component of a tag attached to the SES Mail Manager address list, used to store arbitrary metadata for resource identification, cost allocation, and access control.

aws_ses_mail_manager_archive.archive_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the SES Mail Manager archive.

aws_ses_mail_manager_archive.archive_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the mail manager archive upon creation.

aws_ses_mail_manager_archive.archive_nam.text: The friendly name assigned to this SES Mail Manager archive, used to identify and distinguish it within the account.

aws_ses_mail_manager_archive.archive_sta.text: The lifecycle state of the archive, such as active or pending deletion, as maintained by AWS SES Mail Manager.

aws_ses_mail_manager_archive.kms_key_arn.text: The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the email archive.

aws_ses_mail_manager_archive.retention.text: Configures the retention period for archived emails, specifying how long messages are stored in the archive before being automatically deleted.

aws_ses_mail_manager_archive.retention.r.text: Specifies how long email messages are kept in the archive before being automatically deleted, using a duration string such as '30d' for 30 days or '1y' for one year.

aws_ses_mail_manager_archive.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs (tags) to associate with the archive, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the Mail Manager archive resource in AWS SES.

aws_ses_mail_manager_archive.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the SES Mail Manager Archive, used to categorize and identify the archive for management and cost-allocation purposes.

aws_ses_mail_manager_archive.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag (key-value pair) applied to the SES Mail Manager archive, used to organize, identify, or track costs for this archive resource.

aws_ses_mail_manager_ingress_point.areco.text: The A record (DNS A record) automatically provisioned for the SES Mail Manager ingress point, used as the endpoint for inbound email routing.

aws_ses_mail_manager_ingress_point.ingre.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this SES Mail Manager ingress point.
Specifies the SMTP authentication configuration for the ingress point, containing the ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the credentials used for SMTP client authentication.
The ARN of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the SMTP password used to authenticate to the ingress point's SMTP endpoint.
The SMTP password used for authenticated SMTP connections to the SES Mail Manager ingress point, provided directly in the configuration as an alternative to referencing a Secrets Manager secret ARN.
Defines the mutual TLS authentication settings for the ingress point's TLS endpoint, such as the certificate authority used to verify client certificates.

The `trust_store` block supplies the Amazon Resource Name of the AWS SES Mail Manager trust store that holds the CA certificates against which client certificates are verified for mutual TLS authentication on the ingress point.
Provides the PEM-encoded content of a CA certificate to be included in the trust store used for TLS client authentication for the ingress point.
Specifies a PEM-encoded certificate revocation list (CRL) that the ingress point uses to check that client certificates presented during mutual TLS authentication have not been revoked.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the trust store that holds the CA certificates for TLS client authentication in the ingress point's configuration.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this ingress point.
Specifies a friendly name for the ingress point, which is the endpoint through which incoming email is received for the SES mail manager.

aws_ses_mail_manager_ingress_point.netwo.text: Specifies the network configuration for the ingress point, determining whether the endpoint is public or private (VPC-based) and including the relevant VPC and subnet details.

Specifies the VPC and subnet settings that enable the ingress point to receive email traffic over a private network, allowing mail to be delivered from within a private Amazon VPC rather than over the public internet.
The ID of the VPC interface endpoint that enables private access to the ingress point from within your VPC.
Configures the ingress point to be publicly reachable over the internet, accepting incoming mail without requiring a VPC connection.
Specifies whether the public ingest point uses IPv4 or IPv6 addressing, with allowed values 'IPV4' or 'IPV6'.

aws_ses_mail_manager_ingress_point.rule_.text: The ID of the rule set that is associated with this ingress point and is applied to incoming email.

aws_ses_mail_manager_ingress_point.statu.text: The current provisioning status of the ingress point, such as ACTIVE, PROVISIONING, or DELETING.
Defines the desired operational status (e.g., ACTIVE or INACTIVE) that the ingress point should be updated to, enabling you to start or stop inbound email processing through this endpoint.

aws_ses_mail_manager_ingress_point.tags..text: The key of a metadata tag that can be applied to this SES Mail Manager ingress point to help organize, identify, and manage the resource.

aws_ses_mail_manager_ingress_point.tls_p.text: Specifies the TLS enforcement for connections to the ingress point, with allowed values 'REQUIRE' (forces TLS) or 'OPTIONAL' (allows both TLS and non-TLS).

aws_ses_mail_manager_ingress_point.traff.text: The identifier of the traffic policy attached to this ingress point, which defines the rules for processing and routing incoming email.

aws_ses_mail_manager_ingress_point.type.text: Determines the protocol for receiving incoming email at the ingress point, with valid values being SMTP (standard email over SMTP) or API (ingress via the SES API).

aws_ses_mail_manager_relay.authenticatio.text: Specifies the authentication mechanism and credentials used by this SES Mail Manager relay to connect to the destination SMTP server, such as basic authentication or no authentication.
Indicates that the relay does not require any authentication when connecting to the destination SMTP server, as represented by an empty no-authentication configuration.
The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret containing the SMTP credentials (username and password) used for authentication when the relay connects to the remote mail server.

aws_ses_mail_manager_relay.relay_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SES Mail Manager relay, assigned by AWS when the relay is created.

aws_ses_mail_manager_relay.relay_id.text: The unique identifier automatically assigned by AWS to this Mail Manager relay, used to reference the relay in other resources.

aws_ses_mail_manager_relay.relay_name.text: An optional friendly name that identifies this SMTP relay to make it easier to manage within the SES Mail Manager configuration.

aws_ses_mail_manager_relay.server_name.text: The hostname or IP address of the destination SMTP server that this relay uses to forward email.

aws_ses_mail_manager_relay.server_port.text: Sets the TCP port number on the destination mail server that the SES Mail Manager relay uses for SMTP email relaying.

aws_ses_mail_manager_relay.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the SES Mail Manager Relay resource, used to identify and organize the relay within AWS.

aws_ses_mail_manager_rule_set.rule_set_a.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this SES Mail Manager rule set.

aws_ses_mail_manager_rule_set.rule_set_i.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS SES Mail Manager to the rule set, which is automatically generated and used to reference the rule set in other configurations.

aws_ses_mail_manager_rule_set.rule_set_n.text: A unique, user-defined name that identifies the Mail Manager rule set within your AWS account.

aws_ses_mail_manager_rule_set.rules.text: The rules list defines the ordered set of processing rules for the rule set, where each rule specifies conditions and the actions to execute when those conditions are met within the Mail Manager pipeline.

aws_ses_mail_manager_rule_set.rules.acti.text: Specifies the list of actions to execute when a rule's conditions are matched, such as delivering the email to a mailbox or forwarding it.
Adds a custom header with a specified name and value to the email message when the rule's conditions are met.
The name of the email header that this action adds to the message, used in the add_header action of an SES Mail Manager rule set.
The value of the email header that will be added to the message when this AddHeader action is invoked by the rule set.
Configures the rule action to archive the incoming email to the specified SES Mail Manager archive.
Specifies the policy for handling a message when the archive action fails, with valid values CONTINUE (process subsequent actions) or DROP (stop processing and drop the message).
Specifies the ARN of the SES Mail Manager archive to which the email message is archived when this action is triggered.
Defines a bounce action that rejects the incoming email and sends a bounce response back to the sender, with optional bounce code and message parameters.
Determines how the rule set handles an email when the bounce action fails, accepting CONTINUE to proceed with subsequent actions or DROP to stop processing.
Specifies the custom diagnostic message that is included in the bounce notification sent to the original sender when the bounce action is invoked.
The custom message text to include in the bounce email that is sent back to the original sender when this rule's bounce action is triggered.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon SES Mail Manager assumes when executing this bounce action to send a bounce email to the original sender.
The email address used as the envelope sender (Return-Path) when the bounce message is sent by this bounce action in a rule set.
Specifies the three-digit SMTP reply code (e.g., 550, 551) used in the bounce response sent to the sender when an email matches this rule.
The SMTP status code to return in the bounce response, used to specify the rejection reason when a message is bounced.
Specifies the deliver-to-mailbox action for a rule, which forwards the incoming email to a chosen mailbox managed by SES Mail Manager, using the mailbox ARN to determine the destination.
Determines whether the rule set continues processing the next rule or drops the email when the deliver-to-mailbox action fails, with valid values CONTINUE or DROP.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the mailbox to which the email will be delivered by this action.
The role_arn specifies the IAM role ARN that AWS SES Mail Manager assumes to deliver messages to the target mailbox identified by the corresponding mailbox_arn in the deliver_to_mailbox action.
Specifies that the rule action should deliver the email message to an Amazon Q Business application, using an IAM role to grant access to the application.
Specifies whether the rule set continues processing subsequent rules (CONTINUE) or stops and drops the email (DROP) if delivering the email to Amazon Q Business fails.
The ARN of the Amazon Q Business application to which SES Mail Manager delivers the email message when the DeliverToQBusiness action is invoked.
The ID of the Amazon Q Business index to which the email content is delivered when the rule set's action is triggered.
Specifies the ARN of an IAM role that the SES Mail Manager rule action assumes to deliver the email message to the configured Amazon Q Business application.
Terminates rule evaluation and silently discards the message, preventing delivery without generating a bounce or complaint.
Invokes a Lambda function with the email message and its metadata as the event payload, enabling serverless custom processing of matched emails within the rule set.
Specifies the policy for handling a failed Lambda invocation in the rule action, determining whether email processing continues with the next action or the email is dropped.
The ARN of the Lambda function that Mail Manager invokes when a rule with this action matches an inbound email.
Specifies whether the Lambda function is invoked synchronously ('SYNC') or asynchronously ('ASYNC'), controlling whether the rule set execution waits for the Lambda response.
Specifies the number of minutes to retry invoking the Lambda function if the initial invocation fails, after which the action is considered failed.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS SES Mail Manager assumes to invoke the specified Lambda function when this action is triggered.
Configuration for the PublishToSNS action, which sends the email content to the designated SNS topic for further processing.
Determines the behavior when the SNS publish action fails, with 'CONTINUE' allowing subsequent actions to run and 'DROP' causing the email to be rejected.
Specifies the encoding (BASE64 or TEXT) applied to the email content when it is published to the SNS topic.
Specifies whether the email delivered to the SNS topic contains the raw MIME content or a JSON object representation of the message metadata.
The ARN of the IAM role that SES Mail Manager assumes to publish email event data to the configured Amazon SNS topic when this action is triggered.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic to which the email is published when the rule's conditions are met.
Configures the relay action for a rule, which forwards an incoming email to a specified SMTP relay destination via AWS SES Mail Manager.
Determines the behavior when the relay action fails, either continuing with subsequent rule set actions (CONTINUE) or discarding the message (DROP).
Specifies the email address to use as the MAIL FROM (envelope sender) when the message is relayed to the destination SMTP server.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SES Mail Manager relay to which the email is forwarded when this relay action is invoked.
Configuration for the SES Mail Manager ReplaceRecipient action, which overrides the email's original destination with a specified replacement recipient address.
The list of email addresses that replace the original recipient when the replace recipient action is applied.
Specifies a Send action within a mail manager rule, which directs the incoming email to a designated destination using the configured IAM role and determines behavior on delivery failure.
Sets the action failure policy for the send action, indicating whether rule processing should continue with subsequent actions or stop if sending the email fails.
The ARN of the IAM role that Mail Manager assumes to allow the Send action to deliver the message through Amazon SES.
The write_to_s3 property of a rule action specifies the S3 bucket (and optional key prefix) where the email message should be stored as part of the rule set's processing.
Determines whether processing continues or stops when the write-to-S3 action fails, with allowed values 'CONTINUE' or 'DROP'.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS SES Mail Manager assumes to write messages to the specified S3 bucket for this rule action.
The name of the S3 bucket where the incoming email message content is stored when this WriteToS3 action runs.
Specifies the prefix to prepend to the S3 object key when this write-to-S3 action stores the email message in the specified bucket.
The AWS KMS key ID used for server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) of the email message when it is written to the S3 bucket by this action.

aws_ses_mail_manager_rule_set.rules.cond.text: Specifies the list of conditions that an incoming email must satisfy (for example, matching the recipient, sender, or attachment presence) for the rule's actions to be executed.
The boolean_expression object specifies a rule condition that evaluates a boolean email attribute (e.g., whether the message was sent over TLS) to determine if the rule's actions should be applied.
Defines the email attribute (e.g., IsDeliveryReceipt or IsSpam) that the boolean expression condition inspects to determine whether the condition is satisfied.
An object that specifies the analysis to perform using a trained analyzer, including the analyzer ARN and the result field to evaluate against.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS SES Mail Manager analyzer resource to use for evaluating the boolean expression in the rule condition.
Specifies the key in the analysis result payload (from the referenced analyzer) whose value is compared in this boolean condition.
Specifies the email metadata attribute (such as sender, recipient, subject, or authentication result) that the boolean expression evaluates against a configured value in the rule condition.

This object specifies the 'is in address list' evaluation, defining which email attribute (such as sender or recipient) must be present in the referenced address list for the condition to evaluate to true.

The address_lists field provides the list of address list IDs to check the incoming email address against; if the address matches any entry in one of these lists, the containing rule condition evaluates to true.
Specifies which email header or envelope attribute (e.g., From, To, or Recipient) is inspected to determine membership in the referenced address list.
Defines the comparison operation applied when matching a boolean attribute against a boolean value in the rule condition; the only supported operators are EQUALS and NOT_EQUALS.

Evaluates the DMARC policy of the inbound email, matching when the email's DMARC authentication result (such as PASS, FAIL, NONE, or QUARANTINE) satisfies the specified operator and value in this condition.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used to evaluate the DMARC authentication result against the values listed in the same DMARC expression.

Specifies the DMARC verdict values (such as PASS, FAIL, NONE, TEMPERROR, or PERMERROR) that the rule condition compares against the incoming email's DMARC authentication result using the condition's operator.
Specifies an IP-based condition for a rule, matching the source IP address of the email against a list of CIDR ranges or exact IP addresses to determine whether the rule's actions are applied.
Specifies the email attribute (such as the message's source IP address) that the IP expression condition evaluates against the rule's configured IP address ranges.
The operator (CIDR or IP) that defines how the IP expression condition matches the source IP address against the provided values.
The list of IP addresses or CIDR blocks that the rule's IP condition matches against the message source.

Defines a number-based matching condition that compares a numeric email attribute (e.g., message size or recipient count) to a specified value using an operator such as EQUALS, LESS_THAN, or GREATER_THAN.

In an SES Mail Manager rule set, this object identifies the message attribute from which the numeric value used in the number expression condition is extracted before the operator and value comparison are applied.
Specifies which numeric attribute of the email (such as message size or recipient count) the number expression condition evaluates.
Specifies the comparison operator (for example, EQ, NE, GT, LT, GE, LE) used to evaluate the numeric value in a number expression condition within a Mail Manager rule set.
The numeric value that the NumberExpression condition compares against the email attribute to determine whether the rule condition is met.
Specifies a condition for a rule that compares a designated email string attribute (e.g., SENDER, RECIPIENT, MAIL_FROM) to a string value, allowing the rule to trigger when they match.

Specifies the email attribute to evaluate for the string expression condition, such as the sender address, recipient address, a message header, or a MIME part, which is then compared against a value using the condition's operator.
Defines how to use an external analysis result as the evaluation source for the string expression condition, enabling the rule to match on analyzed email data rather than a direct attribute.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the analyzer that the rule set invokes to perform analysis on the email and produce a value to be matched in the string expression condition.
Specifies the field name in the analysis result produced by an AWS SES Mail Manager analyzer, which is used as the value for the string expression condition.
Specifies the email attribute (such as FROM, TO, or SUBJECT) that the string expression condition evaluates against.
Specifies which attribute of the TLS client certificate (for example, subject or issuer) the string condition evaluates against the incoming connection's certificate data.
The name of the MIME header (such as 'Subject' or 'From') whose value the string expression condition evaluates.
Specifies the string comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, CONTAINS) used by the string expression condition to compare the selected email attribute against the configured value.
The list of string values to match against the email attribute (e.g., From, To, Subject) when evaluating a string expression condition in an SES Mail Manager rule set.
Defines a condition that evaluates an email verdict (such as SPF, DKIM, or DMARC) against a specified value using an operator.

The `evaluate` object in a verdict expression condition specifies which email verdict attribute (e.g., SPF, DKIM, DMARC) the rule condition will inspect, typically by providing an attribute name in a nested structure.
The ARN of the AWS SES Mail Manager analyzer whose verdict is evaluated by this rule condition's verdict expression, such as an analyzer that provides spam or virus analysis results.
Specifies the result field from the analysis output that the verdict expression evaluates to determine the condition match.

In an AWS SES Mail Manager rule set verdict expression condition, this attribute specifies which email authentication or verdict attribute (such as SPF, DKIM, or DMARC) is being evaluated against the defined value.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) used by this verdict expression condition to match the message's verdict attribute against the configured value.
The list of email verdict values (such as SUSPECT, BULK, or OK) that this condition matches against; the condition is satisfied when the incoming message's verdict equals any one of these values.

aws_ses_mail_manager_rule_set.rules.name.text: A user-defined name that identifies an individual rule within the SES Mail Manager rule set.

aws_ses_mail_manager_rule_set.rules.unle.text: List of conditions that, if any are met, cause the rule to be skipped (i.e., the rule does not apply to the email).
Specifies a boolean expression that defines an exclusion condition for a rule: when the expression evaluates to true for a given email attribute (such as DKIM, SPF, or TLS), the rule is not applied.
Defines the email message attribute (such as FROM, TO, or SUBJECT) that the boolean expression's operator inspects in this 'unless' exclusion condition.

Configuration for the analysis evaluation type, which compares the value of a message field against the result of an Amazon SES Mail Manager analyzer, allowing rule conditions based on analyzed content.
The ARN of the Amazon SES Mail Manager analyzer used to perform the email content analysis evaluated by this boolean expression condition.

Within an 'unless' condition, this is the name of the result field from the referenced Mail Manager analyzer output that the boolean expression evaluates to determine whether the rule's actions are skipped.

Specifies the email message attribute (such as 'From' or 'SubjectHeader') that is evaluated in the boolean expression of an 'Unless' condition, causing the rule to be skipped if the comparison against the given value yields true.

This evaluation object tests whether the email address associated with the specified message attribute (e.g., sender or recipient) is present in the address list identified by its AddressListId, enabling conditional rule behavior based on address-list membership.
The list of AWS SES Mail Manager address list IDs that the email address is checked against for the 'is in address list' boolean condition inside this rule's 'unless' clause.
Specifies the email attribute (for example, the sender or recipient address) that is checked against the address list to determine whether the condition matches.
Specifies the boolean comparison operator for the 'unless' condition's boolean expression, indicating whether the rule should match when the evaluated attribute is true (IS_TRUE) or false (IS_FALSE).

Specifies a DMARC expression (operator and value such as 'PASS' or 'FAIL') that, when it matches the email's DMARC result, prevents this rule's actions from being executed because it is listed in the 'unless' block.
Determines whether the DMARC verdict must equal the specified value (EQUALS) or not equal it (NOT_EQUALS) for the unless condition to apply.
Specifies the DMARC verification outcomes (such as PASS or FAIL) that the incoming message's DMARC check must match for this 'unless' condition to be evaluated in the Mail Manager rule set.
Defines the source IP address (or CIDR range) matching condition used in the rule's 'unless' clause, so the rule is not applied when the email originates from an IP that matches this expression.
Defines which IP address attribute (e.g., SOURCE_IP or RECIPIENT_IP) to evaluate for the IP expression condition in a mail manager rule set.
Specifies which IP address attribute (such as SOURCE_IP) the unless condition's IP expression checks to determine whether to bypass the rule.
The operator to apply when evaluating the source IP address against the provided CIDR blocks, either CIDR_MATCHES for a match or NOT_CIDR_MATCHES for a non-match.
A list of IP addresses or CIDR blocks used by the 'unless' IP expression condition, so a rule is not applied when the source IP of the email matches any of these values.

Defines a numeric comparison condition that evaluates a specified email attribute (such as recipient count or a header value) against a configured number using an operator like 'equals' or 'greater-than', and is applied in the rule's 'unless' block to exclude matching messages.

Specifies the numeric email attribute (e.g., MESSAGE_SIZE or RECIPIENT_COUNT) that the number_expression evaluates against the configured threshold using its operator, determining whether the rule's 'unless' condition is met.
This field selects the email attribute (e.g., MESSAGE_SIZE or RECIPIENT_COUNT) that the Mail Manager rule evaluates in the numeric comparison of the 'unless' condition.
Determines the relational operator used to compare the numeric value in this 'unless' condition, such as 'eq', 'neq', 'gt', 'gte', 'lt', or 'lte'.
The numeric value to compare against the selected email attribute when the rule's 'unless' condition uses a number expression, such as a message size threshold.

Configures a string-based condition inside an 'unless' clause of a rule, defining the data source (e.g., a header), comparison operator, and value used to exclude matching emails from the rule's actions.

This nested block inside a string_expression in an unless condition of an SES Mail Manager rule set specifies which email attribute (e.g., sender or recipient) to evaluate and the optional fallback value to use when that attribute is missing, serving as the data source for the string comparison.
Specifies the email analysis type (such as VIRUS or SPAM) that the string expression evaluates against in the rule's 'unless' condition.
The ARN of the Amazon Comprehend or Textract analyzer used by the SES Mail Manager rule set to analyze the email content for this string expression condition.
Within this 'unless' string expression, the result_field names the key in the output of the referenced email analysis add-on whose value is evaluated against the condition.
The email attribute (such as From, To, Subject, or a custom header) that the string expression evaluates against in the rule set's unless condition.
Selects the specific client certificate attribute (e.g., Subject, Issuer, Fingerprint) to evaluate in the string expression condition.
Defines the MIME header name to check when the rule's 'unless' condition uses a string expression evaluation.

Specifies the comparison operator (such as EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, or CONTAINS) used to evaluate the email attribute against the string value in a string-based 'unless' condition, determining whether the condition matches and prevents the rule from applying.

The list of string values that the specified email attribute in the 'unless' string expression is compared against; if the attribute matches any of these values, the rule condition is considered true and the rule is not applied.

The verdict_expression object, nested within an 'unless' rule condition, specifies a boolean expression against email authentication verdicts (such as SPF, DKIM, or DMARC) that, when true, prevents the rule's actions from executing.

This object specifies the verdict value (including the verdict type such as SES_VERDICT or SMTP_VERDICT and the specific value to match) that the rule evaluates in a negative (unless) condition to determine whether the rule actions should be skipped.
Defines the analysis condition in the rule's verdict expression, specifying the analyzer and the expected analysis result (e.g., PASS/FAIL) that must match for the condition to apply.
The name of the field in the analysis result (from the configured analyzer) that the unless condition evaluates against a specified value in the verdict expression.
Specifies the email authentication attribute (such as SPF, DKIM, or DMARC) whose verdict is evaluated in this condition.
The operator for the verdict expression, indicating whether the message's verdict must equal (EQUALS) or not equal (NOT_EQUALS) the specified verdict value.

Specifies the list of verdict values (for example, PASS, FAIL, or STALE) that, when matched by the message's specified verdict type, cause the 'unless' condition to be true and therefore skip the rule.

aws_ses_mail_manager_rule_set.tags.text: Specifies the list of key-value tags to attach to this AWS SES Mail Manager rule set, which are used for cost allocation, access control, and operational metadata management.

aws_ses_mail_manager_rule_set.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the SES Mail Manager Rule Set, used for identifying and categorizing the resource.

aws_ses_mail_manager_rule_set.tags.value.text: The value of a tag (key-value pair) applied to the SES Mail Manager rule set, used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_ses_mail_manager_traffic_policy.defa.text: The default action (ALLOW or DENY) that the traffic policy applies to incoming messages that do not match any of the policy's statements.

aws_ses_mail_manager_traffic_policy.max_.text: Sets the maximum incoming email size in bytes that this SES Mail Manager traffic policy will accept, rejecting any message larger than the specified limit.

aws_ses_mail_manager_traffic_policy.poli.text: The list of statements in this traffic policy, where each statement defines a set of conditions and an action (such as allow or deny) for email matching those conditions.
Defines whether messages that match all conditions of this traffic policy statement are allowed through ('ALLOW') or rejected ('DENY').
A list of conditions that determine when a traffic policy statement applies, matching on message attributes such as sender, recipient, or connection properties.
Defines a logical combination of sub-conditions using operators such as AND or OR, which must evaluate to true for an email to match this traffic policy condition.

For an AWS SES Mail Manager traffic policy boolean condition, this object specifies the email attribute (such as the message sender, recipient, or authentication status like DMARC) that will be evaluated to determine if the policy statement's condition matches.
Specifies the analyzer ARN for email content analysis, defining the analysis result that the boolean expression condition evaluates against the configured value.
The ARN of the analyzer that defines the email content analysis service (e.g., Amazon Textract or Comprehend) used to evaluate the boolean expression condition in the SES Mail Manager traffic policy.
Specifies which field in the analysis result the boolean expression evaluates to make a condition decision.
This object identifies the SES address list to test for membership, providing the AddressListId that the email's recipient address is compared against.
Specifies the address lists that the evaluated email address is checked against for the 'is_in_address_list' condition, determining a match if the address appears in any of the specified lists.
Specifies which email address attribute (such as the envelope sender or recipient) the IsInAddressList condition evaluates against the address list.
The boolean operator (e.g., EQUALS or NOT_EQUALS) that defines how the evaluated email attribute is compared to the expected boolean value in this traffic policy condition.

Defines an IP-based condition that matches the source IP address of incoming email against a list of CIDR address ranges using an operator (e.g., CIDR) to determine whether the traffic policy statement applies.
The evaluate property of the IP expression condition defines which IP address (for example, the source IP address of the email) is checked against the specified values in the traffic policy.
Specifies which message attribute (e.g., the connecting client's IP) is evaluated against the IP set in this traffic policy condition.

In an IP address condition of a traffic policy statement, this operator specifies the matching logic—such as CIDR_MATCHES or NOT_CIDR_MATCHES—that determines whether the source IP address is compared against the CIDR values in the expression's values list.
List of IP addresses or CIDR ranges to match against the source IP address in the traffic policy's IP condition.
Specifies an IPv6 address or CIDR range match condition, using an operator such as CIDR_MATCHES, that an email's source or destination IP must satisfy to trigger the traffic policy statement.
The `evaluate` object selects the IPv6 address attribute of the incoming message to compare against the CIDR values in `ipv6_expression.value`, with the supported attribute being `SOURCE_IP`.
Specifies whether the IPv6 address condition evaluates the sender's IP address or the recipient's IP address of the inbound message.
Specifies the matching operator for the IPv6 expression (e.g., 'CIDR_MATCHES' or 'NOT_CIDR_MATCHES'), determining whether traffic originates from within or outside the listed IPv6 CIDR blocks.
The list of IPv6 addresses or CIDR blocks that the traffic policy condition matches against for IPv6-based allow/deny decisions.

This object defines a string-based condition in an SES Mail Manager traffic policy statement, specifying an email attribute (such as envelope sender or recipient) and an operator/value pair to match against for traffic filtering.
Specifies which email attribute (such as the envelope sender, recipient, or TLS status) the string expression condition evaluates in an SES Mail Manager traffic policy statement.

Specifies an email analysis (such as a rule set or add-on) whose result is used as the string value to evaluate in this traffic policy condition, rather than directly evaluating a raw email attribute.
The ARN of the SES Mail Manager analyzer that examines the email content and provides the result used for comparing in this string expression condition.
Specifies the name of the field in the analysis output (e.g., a key from Amazon Comprehend) whose value the string expression should evaluate for the traffic policy condition.
Specifies the email attribute (e.g., FROM, TO, SUBJECT, or RECIPIENT) that the string expression evaluates against in the traffic policy condition.

Determines how the string in the 'to_evaluate' property is compared to the data source value in a string expression condition, with allowed values such as EQUALS, STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, and CONTAINS.

The list of string values to match against the selected message attribute (e.g., the envelope recipient or sender) in a string expression condition, determining whether a traffic policy statement applies to an email.
Defines a TLS condition for the traffic policy statement, used to match inbound email connections based on characteristics such as the TLS protocol version or cipher suite.
Defines which TLS attribute (protocol or cipher) is evaluated by this TLS expression in the traffic policy condition.
The specific TLS connection attribute (such as SNI hostname or TLS protocol version) that the condition evaluates against the expected value.
Specifies the comparison operator (such as Equals, StartsWith, or EndsWith) used to evaluate the TLS handshake property against the value in the tls_expression condition.
Specifies the TLS protocol version (e.g., 'TLSv1.2') that the incoming connection must use to match this traffic policy condition.

aws_ses_mail_manager_traffic_policy.tags.text: A key of a tag attached to the SES Mail Manager traffic policy, used to categorize and manage the resource.

The value part of a key-value tag attached to an AWS SES Mail Manager traffic policy, used to store custom metadata for organizing, identifying, and managing the policy (e.g., cost center or environment).

aws_ses_mail_manager_traffic_policy.traf.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this SES Mail Manager traffic policy, used to reference the policy in IAM policies and other AWS services.
The unique identifier assigned to the SES Mail Manager traffic policy by AWS.
A friendly, human-readable name assigned to this traffic policy to identify it within SES Mail Manager.

aws_ses_multi_region_endpoint.details.ro.text: The AWS Region targeted by this route in the multi-region endpoint's route configuration.

aws_ses_receipt_filter.id.text: The name of the SES receipt filter, which serves as the unique Terraform identifier and matches the filter's `name` attribute.

aws_ses_receipt_rule.rule.actions.add_he.text: Specifies an action that adds a header to an incoming email when the receipt rule matches, using the provided header name and value.
The name of the custom header that this action adds to the incoming email, such as 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value to be included in the custom header that the receipt rule adds to incoming email messages.

aws_ses_receipt_rule.rule.actions.bounce.text: Configures a bounce action that rejects an incoming email and sends a bounce response to the sender, with configurable message text and optional notification to an SNS topic.
The message text to include in the bounce response sent to the original sender when the receipt rule's bounce action triggers.
The email address that the bounce message is sent from when this bounce action is triggered.
Defines the three-digit SMTP reply code (e.g., '550') that SES returns to the sender when a bounce action is triggered for a received message.
The SMTP reply code to return to the sender when the email is bounced by this rule, specified as a three-digit numeric string (e.g., '550').
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic that SES publishes a notification to when the bounce action is applied to a received message.

aws_ses_receipt_rule.rule.actions.connec.text: The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon SES assumes to grant access to the specified Amazon Connect instance when delivering an email through the Connect action of this receipt rule.
The ARN of the Amazon Connect instance that the SES receipt rule's ConnectAction connects the incoming email to.

aws_ses_receipt_rule.rule.actions.lambda.text: Specifies a Lambda action that invokes an AWS Lambda function when the receipt rule matches an incoming email, with properties for the function ARN, invocation type (Event or RequestResponse), and an optional SNS topic for error notifications.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Lambda function that Amazon SES invokes when the receipt rule matches an incoming email.
Specifies whether the Lambda function is invoked asynchronously (Event) or synchronously (RequestResponse) when the SES receipt rule matches an incoming email.
The ARN of an Amazon SNS topic that Amazon SES notifies when the Lambda action is invoked by a receipt rule.

aws_ses_receipt_rule.rule.actions.s3_act.text: Configures the S3 action for a receipt rule, which saves the incoming email message to an Amazon S3 bucket.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket where the received email message is stored when this S3 action is invoked.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon SES assumes to write to the S3 bucket specified in this S3 action of the receipt rule.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the object stored in Amazon S3 by the S3 action of this SES receipt rule; if not provided, Amazon SES uses the default AWS-managed key for the account.
The key prefix to prepend to the object name when storing the received email into the S3 bucket specified by the S3 action of this receipt rule.
The ARN of an Amazon SNS topic that Amazon SES publishes a notification to when the message is successfully saved to the S3 bucket by this action.

aws_ses_receipt_rule.rule.actions.snsact.text: Defines an SNS action that publishes the received email notification to an Amazon SNS topic when an incoming email matches the receipt rule.
Specifies the encoding (UTF-8 or Base64) used for the email content in the Amazon SNS notification sent by this action.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic to which the receipt rule publishes a notification when an incoming email matches the rule.

aws_ses_receipt_rule.rule.actions.stop_a.text: Terminates the receipt rule's action chain, causing SES to stop evaluating subsequent actions and rules for the incoming email.
Specifies the scope of the SES receipt rule stop action, which must be set to `RuleSet` to stop evaluating the entire receipt rule set.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic to which the SES receipt rule's stop action publishes a notification when the rule set evaluation is terminated.

aws_ses_receipt_rule.rule.actions.workma.text: Configures the WorkMail action for a receipt rule, specifying the Amazon WorkMail organization ARN (and optional SNS topic) that receives the incoming email.
The ARN of the Amazon WorkMail organization that receives the email when the receipt rule's WorkMail action is invoked.
The ARN of an Amazon SNS topic to notify when the WorkMail action is triggered by a receipt rule.

aws_ses_template.id.text: The id of the aws_ses_template resource is the template name, which uniquely identifies the SES template within the AWS region.

aws_ses_template.tags.key.text: The key of a tag applied to the Amazon SES email template.

aws_ses_template.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag assigned to the SES email template, used for metadata organization and cost allocation in AWS.

aws_shield_drtaccess.account_id.text: The AWS account ID of the account that has configured the Shield Response Team (DRT) access, automatically populated with the current account ID.

aws_shield_proactive_engagement.account_.text: The AWS account ID that the Shield Advanced proactive engagement configuration applies to; this is automatically resolved to the current account and is read-only.

aws_shield_proactive_engagement.emergenc.text: A free-form note field attached to an emergency contact, used to record additional context such as the contact's role or best time to reach them.
The email address where AWS Shield Advanced sends proactive engagement notifications and alerts for this emergency contact.
The phone number of the emergency contact for AWS Shield Advanced proactive engagement notifications.

aws_shield_protection.application_layer_.text: When present, this marker block selects 'block' as the Shield Advanced automatic application-layer response action, causing the detected malicious request to be blocked.

Sets the automatic application-layer DDoS mitigation action to 'Count', causing AWS Shield Advanced to count matching requests without blocking them so you can observe traffic before enforcing a block.

aws_shield_protection.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag key-value pair attached to an AWS Shield Advanced protection resource, used to store metadata such as owner, environment, or cost center for resource organization and identity.

aws_shield_protection_group.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag attached to the AWS Shield Protection Group, used to store custom metadata that helps identify, organize, and manage the protection group.

aws_signer_profile_permission.action.text: Specifies the AWS Signer operation (such as 'signer:StartSigningJob' or 'signer:GetSigningProfile') that the principal is allowed to perform on the signing profile.

aws_signer_profile_permission.principal.text: The AWS account ID or IAM principal (such as an IAM role or user ARN) that is granted signing-profile access by this profile permission.

aws_signer_profile_permission.profile_na.text: The name of the AWS Signer signing profile to which the permission is granted.

aws_signer_profile_permission.profile_ve.text: The version of the signing profile to which this cross-account permission is scoped; when omitted, the permission applies without version-specific restriction.

aws_signer_profile_permission.statement_.text: A unique identifier for this signing profile permission statement, used to reference the setting in later updates or removal operations.

aws_signer_signing_profile.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this signing profile in AWS Signer.

aws_signer_signing_profile.platform_id.text: The platform ID that determines the signing platform (e.g., AWSLambda or Notation) and the cryptographic algorithm used by the signing profile.

aws_signer_signing_profile.profile_name.text: The unique name of the signing profile, as returned by AWS Signer after the profile is created.

aws_signer_signing_profile.profile_versi.text: The version identifier of the signing profile, which automatically changes each time the profile is updated and is used to reference a specific revision of the profile.
Computed after creation, this attribute holds the ARN (Amazon Resource Name) of the specific version of the signing profile, which uniquely identifies that version for use in signing jobs.

aws_signer_signing_profile.signature_val.text: Specifies the time period for which signatures generated with this signing profile remain valid, using a period type (days, months, or years) and a numeric value.
Specifies the time unit (DAYS, MONTHS, or YEARS) for the validity period of signatures generated by this signing profile.
The numeric value that, together with the signature_validity_period.type (e.g., DAYS, MONTHS, YEARS), defines how long signatures created with this profile remain valid.

aws_signer_signing_profile.tags.key.text: A tag key that, with its corresponding value, assigns a user-defined label to the signing profile for easier identification and management.

aws_signer_signing_profile.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the signing profile, used for categorization and access control in AWS Signer.

aws_sim_space_weaver_simulation.schema_s.text: Specifies the Amazon S3 location (bucket and key) of the JSON schema that defines the entities and components for the simulation.

aws_sim_space_weaver_simulation.snapshot.text: The Amazon S3 bucket and key location of a simulation snapshot that SimSpace Weaver uses to initialize the simulation from a saved state.

aws_smsvoice_configuration_set.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the configuration set in AWS.

aws_smsvoice_configuration_set.event_des.text: The CloudWatchLogsDestination object within an event destination of an AWS::SMSVoice::ConfigurationSet specifies the Amazon CloudWatch Logs destination for voice message events, including the IAM role ARN and log group ARN to which the events are delivered.
The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon CloudWatch Logs assumes to publish event logs for the configuration set's event destination.
The ARN of the Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group where the configuration set delivers event notifications.
Specifies whether the event destination is enabled to receive event notifications for the configuration set.
Specifies the name of the event destination, which uniquely identifies this destination within the configuration set.
The Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream destination for this event destination, specifying the delivery stream ARN and IAM role ARN that AWS SMS Voice uses to deliver event notifications.
The ARN of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to which the configuration set sends event notifications (e.g., message delivery and response events).
The ARN of the IAM role that authorizes AWS SMS Voice to write event notifications to the associated Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream.

This field specifies the voice call events (e.g., INITIATED_CALL, RINGING, ANSWERED, COMPLETED, BUSY, FAILED, or NO_ANSWER) that must occur for the associated event destination to send notifications to its target SNS topic.
Configures the Amazon SNS topic to which event notifications are published for this event destination in the SMS voice configuration set.
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic where the configuration set sends event notifications for this event destination.

aws_smsvoice_opt_out_list.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key-value pair assigned to the AWS SMS Voice opt-out list, used for categorizing or identifying the resource.

aws_smsvoice_phone_number.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the phone number resource in Amazon Pinpoint SMS Voice.

aws_smsvoice_phone_number.mandatory_keyw.text: The message that the phone number automatically sends to an SMS sender when it receives the mandatory HELP keyword, configuring the help response required for compliant phone numbers.
The message that Amazon Pinpoint SMS Voice v2 automatically sends in reply when a sender texts the mandatory 'STOP' keyword to this phone number.

aws_smsvoice_phone_number.optional_keywo.text: Defines the opt-in/opt-out behavior (REGISTER or UNREGISTER) that is applied when an inbound SMS message matches the associated optional keyword on this phone number.
Defines a custom keyword that, when received as an inbound SMS message to the phone number, triggers the pre-configured two-way messaging response associated with that keyword.
The auto-reply text sent when the associated keyword from the same `optional_keywords` list entry is received by this phone number.

aws_smsvoice_phone_number.phone_number.text: The E.164-formatted phone number assigned by AWS for this resource, used as the caller ID for sending voice messages.

aws_smsvoice_phone_number.phone_number_i.text: The service-assigned unique identifier for the phone number, returned by AWS SMS Voice (AWS End User Messaging) after provisioning, used to reference the phone number in API operations and other resources.

aws_smsvoice_phone_number.tags.key.text: The key of a key-value tag that you associate with the phone number to help organize and manage it.

aws_smsvoice_phone_number.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the SMS voice phone number.

aws_smsvoice_pool.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to the SMS voice pool when it is created, which uniquely identifies the pool and is used to reference it in IAM policies and other AWS services.

aws_smsvoice_pool.mandatory_keywords.hel.text: The help message displayed to users who send a HELP message for this mandatory keyword.

aws_smsvoice_pool.mandatory_keywords.sto.text: The custom SMS message that the pool automatically sends back to a mobile subscriber who texts the mandatory keyword 'STOP' to a phone number in the pool.

aws_smsvoice_pool.optional_keywords.keyw.text: For each optional keyword configured on the SMS voice pool, this is the actual word or phrase (e.g., 'HELP' or a custom term) that a user can text to a pool phone number to trigger a predefined response.

aws_smsvoice_pool.optional_keywords.mess.text: The message text that is sent to the sender when they send an SMS containing the associated optional keyword to a phone number in this pool.

aws_smsvoice_pool.pool_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the created pool.

aws_smsvoice_pool.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to an SMS voice pool, which defines the tag's name within the pool's AWS resource tags for organizational and cost-allocation purposes.
