aws_smsvoice_protect_configuration.count.text: Defines the per-country rules for the protect configuration, where each key is a two-letter country code and the value is a rule object containing Boolean flags for Sms, Voice, and Send that control whether messages can be sent to that destination.
Defines a list of MMS messaging rules for a given country in the protect configuration, where each item in the list specifies an action to apply to MMS messages for that country.
The country code to which this MMS rule in the AWS SMS Voice protect configuration's country rule set applies, controlling MMS messaging restrictions for that country.
Determines whether MMS messages are allowed or blocked for the specified country rule set within the protect configuration.

The `sms` list under `country_rule_set` defines country-specific SMS protection rules for the protect configuration, allowing you to set per-country settings such as daily spend limits and opt-out behavior for SMS messages.
The two-character country code (such as 'US') that defines the country to which this SMS rule applies in the protect configuration's country rule set.
Determines whether outbound SMS messages to the associated country are allowed or blocked by this protect configuration's country rule set for the SMS channel.
The voice property contains a list of voice-specific rule objects that control whether voice calls to and from the listed country are allowed or blocked in the protect configuration.
The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., 'US') for which the associated voice rule in the protect configuration's country rule set is defined.
Determines whether voice calls to numbers in the associated country are allowed or blocked, with valid values 'ALLOW' or 'BLOCK'.

aws_smsvoice_registration.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to an AWS SMS Voice registration, which you can use to store arbitrary metadata such as environments, cost centers, or owners for the registration.

aws_sns_topic.delivery_status_logging.fa.text: The IAM role ARN that Amazon SNS assumes to write delivery status logs for failed message deliveries to CloudWatch Logs.

aws_sns_topic.delivery_status_logging.pr.text: Specifies the protocol (e.g., http, https, sqs, lambda) for which this delivery status logging configuration applies in the SNS topic subscription delivery status logging settings.

aws_sns_topic.delivery_status_logging.su.text: Specifies the ARN of an IAM role that Amazon SNS uses to write CloudWatch Logs for messages that were successfully delivered to subscribed endpoints for this topic.
The percentage of successfully delivered messages (0-100, as a string) that Amazon SNS samples for delivery status logging to CloudWatch Logs.

aws_sns_topic.subscription.endpoint.text: The endpoint that receives notifications from the SNS topic, such as an email address, phone number, or URL, depending on the subscription protocol.

aws_sns_topic.subscription.protocol.text: The protocol specifies the type of endpoint that will receive messages from the topic, such as http, https, email, sqs, lambda, etc.

aws_sns_topic.tags.key.text: The tag key that, together with the corresponding tag value, assigns a user-defined metadata label to the SNS topic for purposes such as cost allocation and access control.

aws_sns_topic.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the SNS topic, used for metadata and cost allocation.

aws_sns_topic.topic_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SNS topic, automatically assigned by AWS when the topic is created and used to reference the topic in other services.

aws_sns_topic_policy.id.text: The ARN of the SNS topic that this policy is attached to, which serves as the unique identifier for the aws_sns_topic_policy resource.

aws_sqs_queue.arn.text: The queue's real ARN, computed, known only after ship.

aws_sqs_queue.attributes.text: The queue's read-only attributes as returned by the SQS API (for example ApproximateNumberOfMessages, QueueArn), keyed by attribute name.

aws_sqs_queue.content_based_deduplicatio.text: FIFO only: derive the deduplication ID from message content.

aws_sqs_queue.delay_seconds.text: Delivery delay for every message. `0` to `900`.

aws_sqs_queue.fifo_queue.text: Whether this is a FIFO queue.

aws_sqs_queue.id.text: The queue's own URL, its real identifier.

aws_sqs_queue.kms_data_key_reuse_period_.text: How long a data key is reused before re-calling KMS.

aws_sqs_queue.kms_master_key_id.text: A KMS key for server-side encryption, instead of SQS-managed keys.

aws_sqs_queue.max_message_size.text: Largest allowed message, in bytes. `1024` to `262144`.

aws_sqs_queue.message_retention_seconds.text: How long a message is kept if never deleted. `60` to `1209600` (14 days).

aws_sqs_queue.name.text: The queue's own name. Conflicts with `name_prefix`. For a FIFO queue, must end in `.fifo`.

aws_sqs_queue.name_prefix.text: A prefix, with a generated suffix appended. Conflicts with `name`.

aws_sqs_queue.policy.text: An IAM policy document controlling access to the queue.

aws_sqs_queue.queue_url.text: The URL identifying the created SQS queue.

aws_sqs_queue.redrive_allow_policy.text: Which source queues may use this queue as their dead-letter target.

aws_sqs_queue.redrive_policy.deadLetterT.text: ARN of the dead-letter queue to send failed messages to.

aws_sqs_queue.redrive_policy.maxReceiveC.text: How many times a message may be received before moving to the dead-letter queue.

aws_sqs_queue.region.text: Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints). Defaults to the Region set in the [provider configuration](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs#aws-configuration-reference).

aws_sqs_queue.tags.key.text: The key (name) of a user-defined tag assigned to the SQS queue, used to categorize and manage the queue.

aws_sqs_queue.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the SQS queue.

aws_sqs_queue.visibility_timeout_seconds.text: How long a received message is hidden from other consumers.

aws_sqs_queue_policy.id.text: The ID of the SQS queue policy is the URL of the queue to which the policy is attached.

aws_ssm_association.apply_only_at_cron_i.text: When true, the SSM association is applied only at the interval specified by its cron schedule, and it will not also run during a configured maintenance window.

aws_ssm_association.automation_target_pa.text: Specifies the name of the parameter in the Automation document that receives the target instance IDs or resource identifiers defined in the association's Targets property.

aws_ssm_association.calendar_names.text: Specifies the names or ARNs of Change Calendar resources that define the schedule window during which the SSM association is allowed to run.

aws_ssm_association.compliance_severity.text: Sets the compliance severity level for the association, which determines how the association's compliance status is reported in Systems Manager Compliance.

aws_ssm_association.max_concurrency.text: Specifies the maximum number or percentage of targets that can run the association concurrently, used to control the rate at which state manager applies the document to instances.

aws_ssm_association.max_errors.text: Specifies the maximum number of errors (or, when expressed as a percentage, the maximum portion of the target set) that can occur before the SSM association stops sending requests to run on additional targets.

aws_ssm_association.output_location.text: Specifies the S3 bucket location where the execution output of the SSM association is stored, allowing log and result data to be saved to a user-defined S3 bucket.

aws_ssm_association.output_location.s3_l.text: Specifies the S3 bucket, key prefix, and AWS region for storing the output of the association's command execution.
The name of the S3 bucket where the output (such as execution logs) from the SSM association is stored when an output location is configured.
Specifies the S3 key prefix under which the association's output files are stored in the output S3 bucket, enabling logical grouping or folder structure for the results.
Specifies the AWS Region where the output S3 bucket resides, so that the association's execution results are written to the correct regional bucket.

aws_ssm_association.schedule_offset.text: Specifies the number of minutes to wait after the scheduled time before the association runs, allowing you to delay execution from the cron or rate schedule defined for the association.

aws_ssm_association.sync_compliance.text: Indicates whether compliance for the association is automatically synced with AWS Systems Manager (AUTO) or manually synced (MANUAL).

aws_ssm_association.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag assigned to the SSM association, used to organize, identify, and filter the association within AWS Systems Manager.

aws_ssm_association.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS Systems Manager association, which aids in organizing, identifying, and managing the association through AWS tagging policies.

aws_ssm_association.targets.key.text: Specifies the key of the target filter (e.g., 'InstanceIds' or a tag key) used to select the managed instances to which the SSM association applies.

aws_ssm_association.targets.values.text: Values for the target key, such as EC2 instance IDs when the key is 'InstanceIds' or tag values when the key is a tag-based key like 'tag:Environment'.

aws_ssm_association.wait_for_success_tim.text: Specifies the maximum time in seconds that the provider will wait for the SSM association to reach a successful state after creation or update, after which it returns an error.

aws_ssm_cloud_connector.configuration.az.text: The display name of an Azure subscription targeted by the SSM Cloud Connector's Azure configuration, identifying the subscription by its human-readable name.
The unique Azure subscription ID that the SSM Cloud Connector is configured to manage as part of its Azure connection targets.

aws_ssm_document.attachments.key.text: The key name of an attachment entry, such as 'SourceUrl' or 'Script', that specifies the attachment's purpose within an Automation document.

aws_ssm_document.attachments.values.text: Provides the list of source URLs (such as Amazon S3 file URLs) that define the actual content locations for an SSM document attachment, matched with the attachment's key to specify the type of source.

aws_ssm_document.requires.name.text: The name of the AWS Systems Manager document that this document requires as a dependency.

aws_ssm_document.requires.version.text: The version of another SSM document that this document requires as a dependency, specified in the 'requires' block of the aws_ssm_document resource.

aws_ssm_document.tags.key.text: The tag key to assign to the SSM document, used for identifying and managing the document in AWS Systems Manager.

aws_ssm_document.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to an SSM document, used to add metadata that supports resource identification, organization, and access control in AWS Systems Manager.

aws_ssm_maintenance_window.tags.value.text: Specifies a user-defined value for a tag that can be used to categorize and manage this Systems Manager maintenance window, such as by project or environment.

aws_ssm_maintenance_window_target.target.text: Specifies the type of target, such as 'InstanceIds' to match EC2 instance IDs or a tag key in the format 'tag:key' to match instances by tag, which determines how the associated Values are interpreted.
Specifies the values for the maintenance window target key, such as EC2 instance IDs when the key is 'InstanceIds' or resource group names when the key is 'ResourceGroup'.

aws_ssm_maintenance_window_task.logging_.text: Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket, region, and prefix where the maintenance window task execution logs are stored.
The AWS Region where the S3 bucket that receives the maintenance window task logs is located.
The name of the S3 bucket to which the maintenance window task's execution logs are written, as part of the LoggingInfo configuration for this AWS::SSM::MaintenanceWindowTask resource.
The S3 key prefix (folder path) in the logging bucket where the maintenance window task's output logs are stored.

aws_ssm_maintenance_window_task.targets..text: The key field specifies the type of target for the maintenance window task, such as InstanceIds, ResourceGroupNames, or WindowTargetIds, determining how the corresponding values are interpreted.
Specifies the values for the maintenance window task target key, such as EC2 instance IDs, resource group names, or tag values, that define which resources the task runs on.

aws_ssm_maintenance_window_task.task_inv.text: Defines the parameters that AWS Systems Manager uses to run the maintenance window task, including for Run Command, Automation, Step Functions, or Lambda invocation types.

Specifies the information needed to run an Automation workflow as the maintenance window task, including the document version and the runtime parameters (a map of key-value pairs) that the Automation document requires.
The version of the SSM Automation document to use when the maintenance window task runs, such as a specific document version or '$LATEST'.
The parameters to pass to the AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook (SSM document) when the maintenance window task is executed, specified as a map of parameter names to one or more values.
Configures how the maintenance window invokes an AWS Lambda function, specifying optional client context, function version qualifier, and invocation payload.
Base64-encoded client context data to pass to the Lambda function invoked by the maintenance window task.
The JSON string that is passed as the input payload to the Lambda function when the maintenance window task invokes it.
The Lambda function version or alias to invoke for this maintenance window task.

Specifies the parameters for an AWS Systems Manager Run Command task within a maintenance window, including settings like command timeout, S3 output location, IAM service role, and parameters passed to the SSM document.
Configures the destination CloudWatch Logs log group and whether the AWS Systems Manager Run Command task output is written to CloudWatch Logs.
The user-specified comment (a friendly description) that is included with the Run Command when the maintenance window task invokes the command.

Specifies the SHA-256 hash of the content of the Systems Manager command document to be run, which SSM validates to ensure the document hasn't been altered before executing the maintenance window task.
Specifies the hash algorithm (either Sha256 or Sha1) used by SSM Run Command to validate the integrity of the document content referenced by the maintenance window task.
The version of the SSM document to use when the maintenance window task runs the specified command, such as '1' or '$DEFAULT' or '$LATEST'.

Specifies an Amazon SNS notification configuration for the Run Command task, including the ARN of the SNS topic, the events that trigger notifications (e.g., All, InProgress, Success, TimedOut, Cancelled, Failed), and the notification type (Command or Invocation).
The ARN of the Amazon SNS topic that receives notifications about the status of the Run Command task executed by the maintenance window.
Specifies the Run Command task events (such as Success, Failed, or TimedOut) that trigger a notification to the configured Amazon SNS topic.
This value indicates whether the SNS notification is for the entire command (Command) or for each instance's invocation (Invocation).
Specifies the name of the S3 bucket where the output of the Run Command will be stored for the Maintenance Window Run Command task.
Specifies the S3 key prefix under the output S3 bucket where the Run Command invocation output is stored, acting as a subdirectory for the output files.
A map of parameter names to values that are passed to the SSM Run Command document when the maintenance window task is executed.
The ARN of the IAM service role that AWS Systems Manager assumes to publish Amazon SNS notifications for the Run Command task invoked by this maintenance window.
The maximum number of seconds the command is allowed to run before being stopped and marked as timed out.
Specifies the input and execution name for a Step Functions state machine when the maintenance window task invokes a STEP_FUNCTIONS target.
The JSON input string passed to the Step Functions state machine execution when this maintenance window task runs.
The name to assign to the Step Functions execution when the maintenance window task invokes the state machine.

aws_ssm_ops_item.tags.key.text: Key of a user-defined tag attached to the OpsItem, which can be used to categorize, search, and manage operational work items in AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter.

aws_ssm_ops_item.tags.value.text: The user-defined value for a tag key on the OpsItem, used to add metadata for identifying, organizing, or filtering the OpsItem in AWS Systems Manager.

aws_ssm_parameter.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to the parameter, which uniquely identifies it within AWS.

aws_ssm_patch_baseline.approval_rules.pa.text: A list of patch rules that define which patches are approved for the baseline, including patch filters, approval delay, and compliance level.
Specifies the number of days after a patch's release date that it is automatically approved for installation in the patch baseline.
The date (in YYYY-MM-DD format) after which the patch is no longer automatically approved for this rule.
Specifies the compliance severity level (e.g., CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFORMATIONAL, or UNSPECIFIED) assigned to patches that match this rule for reporting and compliance purposes.
Indicates whether this approval rule also applies to patches that are not classified as security updates, allowing non-security patches to be approved based on the same schedule and filters.

The patch_filter_group object within a patch rule defines the set of patch filter criteria (e.g., product, severity, classification) that a patch must match for the rule to approve it, with all specified filters required to match (AND logic).
Defines the patch filters (each with a key and values) that determine which patches this approval rule applies to, such as by product, severity, or classification.
The name of the patch attribute to filter on, such as PRODUCT, CLASSIFICATION, or MSRC_SEVERITY, for the approval rule's patch filter group.
The list of values used to match patches for the associated patch filter key (e.g., product, classification, or severity) in an AWS SSM patch baseline approval rule.

aws_ssm_patch_baseline.global_filters.pa.text: Defines the list of patch filters that determine which patches are included or excluded from the patch baseline, with each filter specifying a key (e.g., PRODUCT, CLASSIFICATION, MSRC_SEVERITY) and a list of values.
The key of the patch filter (e.g., PRODUCT, CLASSIFICATION, MSRC_SEVERITY) that identifies which patch attribute is used for filtering globally across the patch baseline.

Specifies the list of allowed values for the corresponding patch filter key (such as product, classification, or severity), which is used to match patches that are included in or excluded from the patch baseline.

aws_ssm_patch_baseline.sources.configura.text: Specifies the repository configuration string (such as a yum repository configuration for Amazon Linux) that defines the patch source location for this patch baseline.

aws_ssm_patch_baseline.sources.name.text: The name of the patch source, such as 'Amazon Linux 2' or 'Ubuntu', which identifies the repository configured for this patch baseline.

aws_ssm_patch_baseline.sources.products.text: Specifies the operating system product versions (e.g., 'AmazonLinux2012.03', 'RedhatEnterpriseLinux7') that this patch source repository applies to in the patch baseline.

aws_ssm_patch_baseline.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the patch baseline, used to organize and identify the baseline for cost, environment, or operational purposes.

aws_ssm_resource_data_sync.bucket_name.text: The name of the S3 bucket used as the destination for the resource data sync, where Systems Manager delivers the synced configuration and inventory data.

aws_ssm_resource_data_sync.bucket_prefix.text: The prefix (folder path) within the S3 bucket where Systems Manager Inventory data is delivered by this data sync.

aws_ssm_resource_data_sync.bucket_region.text: The AWS Region where the S3 bucket specified as the destination for the resource data sync is located.

aws_ssm_resource_data_sync.kmskey_arn.text: The ARN of an AWS KMS key that encrypts the synced data stored in the destination Amazon S3 bucket.

aws_ssm_resource_data_sync.s3_destinatio.text: Configuration for the S3 bucket where the resource data sync stores synced operational data, including bucket name, region, optional prefix, KMS key, and sync format.
The name of the S3 bucket where Systems Manager Resource Data Sync stores the synced resource data.
Specifies the S3 object key prefix (path) within the destination bucket where the SSM resource data sync stores its synchronized data.
Specifies the AWS Region in which the S3 bucket that receives the synchronized SSM inventory data is located.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt data in the S3 destination bucket for the resource data sync.
Specifies the format for the System Manager data written to the S3 destination, with valid values of JsonSerDe or Incremental.

aws_ssm_resource_data_sync.sync_format.text: Specifies the serialization format (either JsonSerDe or DelimitedText) used when writing Systems Manager data to the Amazon S3 destination for the resource data sync.

aws_ssm_resource_data_sync.sync_name.text: The name of the resource data sync configuration, which must be unique within the AWS account and Region and is used to identify the sync.

aws_ssm_resource_data_sync.sync_source.text: The sync_source field defines the configuration for the source of the resource data sync, specifying the source type (e.g., 'AwsOrganizations' or 'SingleAccount'), the source regions, and optionally AWS Organizations details to determine where inventory and configuration data is collected from.

aws_ssm_resource_data_sync.sync_source.a.text: The AWS Organizations source configuration for the resource data sync, specifying the organization source type and the organizational units whose resource data will be synchronized.

For the AWS Organizations source of an SSM Resource Data Sync, this required string specifies whether the sync applies to all accounts in the organization ('EntireOrganization') or only to accounts within specified organizational units ('OrganizationalUnits').
Limits the data sync to only the specified organizational units (OUs) in the AWS Organization, so resources from accounts within those OUs are included in the sync.

aws_ssm_resource_data_sync.sync_source.i.text: Indicates whether the resource data sync automatically includes new AWS Regions as they become available, allowing it to begin collecting data from those regions without additional configuration.

aws_ssm_resource_data_sync.sync_source.s.text: Specifies the list of AWS Regions from which Systems Manager collects data for the resource data sync.
Specifies the type of source that the resource data sync aggregates data from, such as S3, a single account across multiple regions, or all accounts in an AWS organization.

aws_ssm_resource_data_sync.sync_type.text: Determines the type of AWS Systems Manager Resource Data Sync, either 'SyncFromSource' to aggregate data from multiple AWS accounts and Regions or 'SyncToDestination' to sync data to an S3 bucket, and controls whether the configuration uses a sync source or an S3 destination.

aws_ssmcontacts_contact.plan.duration_in.text: The number of minutes to wait for the contact to acknowledge an alert before moving to the next stage of the contact's engagement plan.

aws_ssmcontacts_contact.plan.rotation_id.text: The list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the rotations to include in the contact's plan, defining the rotation schedules used for on-call coverage.

aws_ssmcontacts_contact.plan.targets.text: Specifies the list of targets to engage during a stage of the contact's plan, where each target can be a contact channel (e.g., email, SMS, voice) or another contact, defined using ChannelTargetInfo or ContactTargetInfo.

aws_ssmcontacts_contact.plan.targets.cha.text: Identifies the contact channel that Incident Manager engages for a given plan target, along with the optional retry interval before escalation within that stage of the contact's engagement plan.
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the contact channel (such as an email, SMS, or voice channel) that is contacted when this plan target is triggered during an incident.
The number of minutes to wait before retrying the contact channel if the previous attempt to reach it fails.

aws_ssmcontacts_contact.plan.targets.con.text: Specifies the target contact for an engagement plan stage, including the contact's ARN and whether it is an essential target that must acknowledge an incident before escalation proceeds.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the contact that Incident Manager engages when the engagement plan reaches this target.
Determines whether this contact is an essential target in the engagement plan, meaning that if this contact does not acknowledge an engagement, the engagement is considered failed.

aws_ssmcontacts_contact.tags.text: Specifies a list of key-value tag objects to associate with the contact for resource identification and cost tracking.

aws_ssmcontacts_contact.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the SSM Contacts contact, used for categorizing and managing the contact resource.

aws_ssmcontacts_plan.stages.duration_in_.text: The duration, in minutes, for which this stage of the engagement runs before moving to the next stage or ending the engagement.

aws_ssmcontacts_plan.stages.targets.text: Specifies the contacts or contact channels that are notified when this stage of the on-call escalation plan is reached, based on the escalation time.

aws_ssmcontacts_plan.stages.targets.chan.text: Specifies the target as a contact channel rather than a contact, detailing the contact channel's identifier and the retry interval in minutes to wait before re-contacting it during the escalation stage.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the contact channel to notify when this stage is triggered.
The number of minutes to wait before retrying the contact channel if the previous attempt fails, as part of the channel target configuration in an SSM Contacts plan stage.

aws_ssmcontacts_plan.stages.targets.cont.text: Identifies an SSM Contacts contact as a target for the stage, using its contact ID and an IsEssential flag that determines whether the contact must be reached for the on-call handoff to continue.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS SSM Contacts contact that this stage targets when the escalation plan is executed.
A boolean that, when true, marks this contact as essential so that if the contact cannot be reached during an incident, the escalation plan stops and does not continue to subsequent targets.

aws_ssmcontacts_rotation.recurrence.mont.text: Specifies the day of the month on which the monthly rotation shift begins, used in monthly recurrence settings for an AWS Systems Manager Incident Manager contacts rotation.
Specifies the time of day (in HH:MM format) when the shift handoff occurs for the monthly rotation schedule, within the monthly recurrence settings.

aws_ssmcontacts_rotation.recurrence.shif.text: Specifies the list of time ranges (each with start and end time) during which on-call coverage is active for a particular day of the week in the rotation's shift coverage schedule.
The time (in HH:MM format) when the shift coverage window ends for the associated day in the rotation recurrence.
The start time of the daily coverage window, in 24-hour HH:MM format, that defines when this shift's on-call coverage begins.
The day of the week (e.g., Monday, Tuesday) that this shift coverage applies to within the rotation's recurrence schedule.

aws_ssmcontacts_rotation.recurrence.week.text: Specifies the day of the week (using a three-letter abbreviation such as MON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, SAT, or SUN) on which the rotation's weekly on-call shift occurs.
The time of day, in 24-hour HH:MM format, when the on-call shift hands off to the next shift on the scheduled day of the week for the rotation recurrence.

aws_ssmcontacts_rotation.tags.text: Specifies the tags to attach to the rotation, where each tag is an object containing a Key and Value, used to identify, organize, and manage the rotation resource.

aws_ssmcontacts_rotation.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the SSM Contacts rotation, used to store metadata such as ownership, environment, or cost center for organizing and managing the rotation resource.

aws_ssmgui_connect_preferences.connectio.text: The name of the S3 bucket used as a destination where connection recording sessions are stored.

aws_ssmincidents_replication_set.regions.text: The regions list specifies the AWS Regions in which incident records are replicated for this replication set, with each object defining a Region name and an optional customer-managed KMS key for encryption.
This object defines the per-region encryption configuration for the replication set, specifying the AWS KMS key ARN used to encrypt incident data replicated to that region.
The ARN of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the replication set data in this region.
The name of an AWS Region to include in the Incident Manager replication set, determining where incident data will be replicated.

aws_ssmincidents_replication_set.tags.ke.text: The key of a tag assigned to the AWS SSM Incident replication set, used to identify and organize the resource.

aws_ssmincidents_replication_set.tags.va.text: The value of a key-value tag attached to the replication set, used to organize, identify, and manage the resource within AWS Systems Manager Incident Manager.

aws_ssmincidents_response_plan.actions.s.text: Specifies the AWS Systems Manager (SSM) automation document to execute as an action when an incident is created, including the document name, the role assumed for execution, and any input parameters.
The name of the SSM automation document (runbook) that the response plan executes as part of the automation action.
Specifies the version of the SSM Automation document (runbook) to run when the response plan triggers this automation action.

Defines dynamic parameter key-value pairs to pass to the SSM automation document run as part of the response plan, with each value dynamically derived from incident context (e.g., incident ARN) rather than a static value.

In the SSM automation action of an Incident Manager response plan, the key in a dynamic_parameters mapping identifies the name of the automation document parameter whose value will be dynamically set from incident data.
The runtime value assigned to a specific SSM automation document parameter, allowing the response plan to pass incident details or other dynamic values into the automation execution.
Specifies the dynamic incident variable (such as an incident ARN or severity) that will be resolved at runtime and used as the value for this SSM automation document parameter.
Specifies the input parameters to pass to the SSM automation runbook when this response plan action is executed.
The name of the parameter to pass to the SSM automation document when the response plan triggers the runbook.
The list of values to assign to the corresponding SSM automation document parameter when the response plan triggers the automation run.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Systems Manager Automation assumes when executing the automation runbook as part of this response plan's SSM automation action.

Specifies which AWS account the SSM automation document should run in, either the account that was impacted by the incident (IMPACTED_ACCOUNT) or a different, specifically selected account (SPECIFIC_ACCOUNT).

aws_ssmincidents_response_plan.chat_chan.text: The list of Amazon SNS topic ARNs that AWS Chatbot uses to send notifications to the configured chat channel for the incident response plan.

aws_ssmincidents_response_plan.incident_.text: The key of a tag to apply to the incident when it is created, as defined in the incident template of the response plan.
The value of the tag assigned to the incident created from this response plan.
The ARN of the SNS topic that receives incident notifications when a matching incident is created or updated.

aws_ssmincidents_response_plan.integrati.text: Defines the PagerDuty settings (including a name and the ARN or secret ID of an AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the PagerDuty API token) that Incident Manager uses when triggering a PagerDuty incident for this integration.
The name of the PagerDuty configuration, used to identify this integration within the response plan.
The PagerDuty incident configuration that specifies the ID of the PagerDuty service where the incident will be created.
The service_id specifies the unique identifier of the PagerDuty service where incidents will be created when this response plan is executed.
The ID or ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the PagerDuty API token used for the PagerDuty integration in the response plan.

aws_ssmquick_setup_configuration_manager.text: A computed list of configuration definitions that were applied to this SSM Quick Setup Configuration Manager, each specifying the setup operation (such as install or update), the configuration type, and associated parameters.
The ARN of the IAM role that AWS Systems Manager Quick Setup assumes to deploy and manage the configuration in the local AWS account.
Specifies the name of the IAM role that AWS Systems Manager assumes to execute the configuration locally in the target account for this configuration definition.

Specifies the configuration parameters (key-value pairs) that customize the settings for each configuration definition in the Quick Setup configuration manager, as required by the underlying configuration type.
Specifies the type of configuration definition, which determines which AWS service's configuration is being managed by the Quick Setup Configuration Manager.
The version of the configuration type's schema to use when applying the quick setup configuration definition.
The timestamp indicating when the configuration manager was created.
A user-provided free-form description for the SSM Quick Setup configuration manager.
The timestamp of the most recent modification to the configuration manager.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SSM Quick Setup configuration manager, used to uniquely identify and reference the manager resource.
An optional friendly name for the Systems Manager Quick Setup configuration manager, used to identify and reference the configuration in the AWS Management Console and API operations.
Returns a list of status summaries for this configuration manager, where each summary includes a status type (such as Deployment) and the corresponding status (such as Success).
The timestamp (as a string) indicating when the status summary for the SSM Quick Setup configuration manager was last updated.
The current status of the configuration manager, indicating whether the configuration setup succeeded, failed, or is still in progress.

The status message is a human-readable string that provides detailed information about the current status of the configuration manager, including any errors or issues encountered during its deployment or operation.

Identifies the specific aspect of the configuration manager's operation (for example, Deployment or Execution) that the status summary applies to, so the status value is interpreted in the correct context.

aws_ssmquick_setup_lifecycle_automation..text: A map of key-value pairs to assign to the SSM Quick Setup lifecycle automation resource for tracking and management.

aws_sso_application.tags.text: Specifies the tags to attach to the SSO application, which are key-value pairs that help you identify, organize, and manage the application in AWS IAM Identity Center.

aws_sso_application.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to be attached to the AWS SSO application.

aws_sso_instance_access_control_attribut.text: The list of access control attributes that define the user attributes (such as email or department) used in attribute-based access control (ABAC) rules for the AWS SSO (IAM Identity Center) instance.
Specifies the name of the user attribute (such as email or department) that this access control attribute entry defines for use in attribute-based access control (ABAC) in IAM Identity Center.
Represents the list of values for an access control attribute key, which AWS IAM Identity Center uses to enable attribute-based access control (ABAC) for the instance.

For a given access control attribute in this AWS SSO (IAM Identity Center) instance's ABAC configuration, the `source` field lists the identity provider attribute names (e.g., 'email') that are mapped to the attribute key and supply the values used for attribute-based access control.
Defines the list of user attribute key-value pairs (such as email or department) that AWS SSO uses for attribute-based access control (ABAC) in the instance.
The attribute key (name) of an access control attribute that maps to a user identity attribute (such as `email` or `username`) used by IAM Identity Center for permission management.

Holds the source configuration for the access control attribute value, where you provide one or more source strings (e.g., '$${path:user.email}') that define how the attribute value is resolved from your identity source for permission boundaries.
The list of identity source attribute paths (for example, 'user.email') that define the source values for this access control attribute.

aws_sso_permission_set.customer_managed_.text: Specifies the customer-managed IAM policies (identified by name and path) that are attached to this AWS SSO permission set.
The name of the customer managed policy to reference in the permission set.
The IAM path of the customer managed policy, which together with the policy name uniquely identifies the policy to attach to the permission set.

aws_sso_permission_set.managed_policies.text: The list of AWS managed policy ARNs to attach to the permission set.

aws_sso_permission_set.permissions_bound.text: Specifies the permissions boundary for the permission set, which can be either a customer-managed policy reference or an AWS managed policy ARN that limits the maximum permissions of the permission set.
Provides the customer managed policy's name and optional path used to set a permissions boundary on the permission set.
The name of the customer managed IAM policy to use as the permissions boundary for this permission set.
The path of the customer managed IAM policy referenced by the permissions boundary, which defaults to '/' if omitted, used to limit the maximum permissions for the permission set.

aws_sso_permission_set.tags.text: A list of key-value tags to assign to the AWS SSO permission set, which can be used for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization.

aws_sso_permission_set.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to an AWS SSO Permission Set, which is used to categorize, identify, and manage the permission set within AWS SSO.

aws_sso_permission_set.tags.value.text: The tag value (the non-key component of a key-value pair) attached to the AWS SSO PermissionSet, used to label or categorize the resource.

aws_step_functions_activity.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this AWS Step Functions activity, which is used to reference the activity in state machine definitions.

aws_step_functions_activity.encryption_c.text: Specifies the maximum duration, in seconds, that AWS Step Functions will reuse a customer-managed data key from AWS KMS before requesting a new one for encrypting activity data.
The AWS KMS key ID or ARN used to encrypt the activity's data when encryption is configured for the Step Functions activity.
Specifies the type of encryption key used for the activity's data, distinguishing between a customer-managed AWS KMS key (CUSTOMER_MANAGED_KMS_KEY) and an AWS-owned key (AWS_OWNED_KEY).

aws_step_functions_activity.name.text: The name of the Step Functions activity, which must be unique within the AWS account and region.

aws_step_functions_activity.tags.text: Specifies the key-value pairs used to tag the Step Functions activity, enabling you to categorize and manage the activity's resources within AWS.

aws_step_functions_activity.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the AWS Step Functions activity, used to categorize and manage the activity resource.

aws_step_functions_activity.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the Step Functions activity.

aws_step_functions_state_machine.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the Step Functions state machine.

aws_step_functions_state_machine.definit.text: The Amazon States Language definition, a JSON or YAML string that specifies the state machine's states, transitions, and execution logic.
Specifies the S3 bucket and key (and optional version) from which the Amazon States Language definition of the state machine is loaded.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that contains the state machine definition file (the JSON or YAML file referenced by the Key in the same DefinitionS3Location property).
The S3 object key of the state machine definition file, located within the bucket specified by the sibling 'bucket' field of the same 'definition_s3_location' object.
The version ID of the S3 object that contains the state machine definition.
Specifies the Amazon States Language (ASL) definition of the Step Functions state machine as a JSON string.
Provides key-value pairs that substitute variables in the state machine definition string, allowing the same definition to be reused across environments by replacing ${key} placeholders.

aws_step_functions_state_machine.encrypt.text: Configures encryption for the state machine's data, allowing you to specify either an AWS-owned key or a customer-managed AWS KMS key via the `kmsKeyId` and `type` properties.
Specifies the maximum time, in seconds, that Step Functions reuses a KMS data key before it must request a new one from the customer managed key for encrypting state machine data at rest.
Specifies the AWS KMS key ID, ARN, or alias used to encrypt state machine data when you enable a customer-managed encryption key for the state machine.
Determines whether the state machine uses AWS-owned encryption or a customer-managed KMS key for encrypting execution data at rest.

aws_step_functions_state_machine.logging.text: Specifies the logging configuration for the Step Functions state machine, including the log level (e.g., ALL or ERROR), whether execution data is included in logs, and the destination CloudWatch Logs log group for capturing execution history.
Specifies the list of log destinations, such as CloudWatch Logs log groups, where execution history logs for the state machine are delivered.
Specifies the CloudWatch Logs log group (via its ARN) to which the state machine sends execution history and execution-level logs when logging is enabled.
The ARN of the CloudWatch Logs log group where Step Functions writes execution history and runtime output for the state machine.
Specifies whether the state machine's execution data (input and output) is included in the CloudWatch Logs log entries for the logging configuration.
Specifies the verbosity level of execution data recorded in CloudWatch Logs, with valid values OFF, ALL, ERROR, and FATAL.

aws_step_functions_state_machine.name.text: The name of the Step Functions state machine, which is automatically generated by AWS if not explicitly configured and must be unique within the AWS account and region.

aws_step_functions_state_machine.role_ar.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that AWS Step Functions assumes to execute the state machine's tasks.

aws_step_functions_state_machine.state_m.text: Specifies the name of the state machine, which must be unique within your AWS account and region and is used to identify the state machine in AWS Step Functions.
The revision identifier for the state machine, which changes each time the state machine definition is updated.
Specifies whether the state machine is a STANDARD or EXPRESS workflow type.

aws_step_functions_state_machine.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs that you can associate with the Step Functions state machine to help categorize, manage, and control access to the resource, such as for cost allocation or IAM policies.

aws_step_functions_state_machine.tags.ke.text: The key (name) of a user-defined tag applied to the AWS Step Functions state machine, used to organize, identify, and control access to the resource.

aws_step_functions_state_machine.tags.va.text: The value of a user-defined tag assigned to the Step Functions state machine, which can be used for cost allocation, access control, and operational grouping.

aws_step_functions_state_machine.tracing.text: Configures AWS X-Ray tracing for the state machine by setting the 'Enabled' flag, which controls whether trace data is collected for executions.
When set to true, enables AWS X-Ray tracing for the state machine execution, allowing you to trace and analyze the execution steps.

aws_step_functions_state_machine_alias.d.text: The ARN of the state machine version to be deployed as the target of the alias's traffic-shifting deployment preference, to which traffic is gradually shifted according to the selected deployment strategy.

aws_step_functions_state_machine_alias.r.text: The ARN of the state machine version to which a portion of execution traffic is routed when using the alias's routing configuration.

The percentage of traffic (a weight between 0 and 100) routed to the corresponding state machine version in the alias's routing configuration, where all weights in the routing configuration sum to 100.

aws_step_functions_state_machine_alias.s.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Step Functions state machine that this alias refers to.

aws_step_functions_state_machine_version.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this state machine version, including the state machine name and version number.
An optional description of the state machine version, used to provide a human-readable label for the version.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the state machine for which this version is created.
Specifies the revision ID of the state machine to create the version from; if omitted, the version is created from the latest revision.

aws_storage_gateway_tape_pool.tags.key.text: The tag key (e.g., 'Environment') that names a metadata tag attached to the tape pool.

aws_storage_gateway_tape_pool.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag associated with the Storage Gateway tape pool, used to organize and identify the resource in AWS.

aws_subnet.block_public_access_states.text: The effective Block Public Access configuration for the subnet, reporting the current state (`allow` or `block`) for both inbound and outbound traffic via `inbound` and `outbound` keys.

aws_subnet.ipv6_cidr_blocks.text: The list of IPv6 CIDR blocks associated with the subnet, automatically populated by AWS as read-only values.

aws_subnet.network_acl_association_id.text: The unique identifier of the network ACL association attached to this subnet, which represents the association between the subnet and its network ACL (either the default or a custom ACL).

aws_subnet.private_dns_name_options_on_l.text: Indicates whether to enable Resource Name DNS AAAA (IPv6) record for instances launched in this subnet, affecting how instance hostnames resolve in the VPC's private DNS.

Specifies whether to enable the automatic creation of an A record for the resource-based name (private DNS name) of instances launched in this subnet, mapping that name to the instance's private IPv4 address within the VPC's private hosted zone.

Specifies the type of hostname (ip-name or resource-name) that EC2 instances launched in this subnet will receive for their private DNS hostnames, as part of the subnet's PrivateDnsNameOptionsOnLaunch configuration.

aws_subnet.subnet_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS when the subnet is created (e.g., 'subnet-1234567890abcdef0'), which is used to refer to the subnet in other resources.

aws_subnet.tags.key.text: The case-sensitive key of a tag applied to the subnet, used to identify and categorize the resource for cost allocation, access control, and operational management.

aws_synthetics_canary.artifact_config.text: Specifies the S3 encryption configuration for artifacts generated by the canary, such as screenshots, logs, and HAR files.

aws_synthetics_canary.artifact_config.s3.text: Specifies the S3 encryption settings (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS, including the KMS key ARN) applied to the artifacts the canary writes to its S3 bucket.

aws_synthetics_canary.browser_configs.br.text: Sets the browser engine (such as Chrome or Firefox) that the canary uses to run its browser-based test scripts.

aws_synthetics_canary.code.text: The `code` attribute provides the details of the canary's script, including the handler and the source location as an S3 bucket/key/version or an inline zip file.

aws_synthetics_canary.code.handler.text: The name of the JavaScript handler function within the canary script that AWS Synthetics invokes when the canary runs.

aws_synthetics_canary.code.s3_bucket.text: The name of the S3 bucket that contains the canary script to be executed.

aws_synthetics_canary.code.s3_key.text: The S3 object key (path to the script or zip file) in the bucket specified by `code.s3_bucket`, used to retrieve the canary's source code.

aws_synthetics_canary.code.s3_object_ver.text: Specifies the version ID of the S3 object that contains the canary script, allowing you to reference a specific version of the script when multiple versions exist.

aws_synthetics_canary.code.script.text: The inline script (Python or Node.js) that the canary runs to perform synthetic monitoring checks, defining the exact steps and assertions for each run.

aws_synthetics_canary.code.source_locati.text: Provides the ARN of a Lambda layer version that contains the canary's script, as an alternative to inline script or S3 bucket/key properties.

aws_synthetics_canary.replicas.last_modi.text: In an AWS Synthetics canary, this numeric field records the last modification timestamp (Unix time) of a canary replica, which is a copy of the canary deployed to another AWS Region.

aws_synthetics_canary.replicas.vpc_confi.text: Set to true to allow the canary replica's VPC configuration to support IPv6 in dual-stack subnets, enabling the canary to use IPv6 addresses alongside IPv4 when running in the replica's VPC.
The security group IDs applied to the canary's VPC configuration, which control network traffic for the Synthetics canary when it runs in your virtual private cloud.

aws_synthetics_canary.run_config.text: Configure the canary's execution settings, including the amount of memory allotted, the timeout duration for each run, and environment variables passed to the canary script.

aws_synthetics_canary.schedule.text: Specifies how often the canary runs, using a rate or cron expression and optionally a fixed duration in seconds for the run window.

aws_synthetics_canary.schedule.duration_.text: Defines how long (in seconds) the canary is allowed to run for each execution before it is stopped, allowing you to override the default timeout.

aws_synthetics_canary.schedule.expressio.text: The rate or cron expression (e.g., 'rate(5 minutes)' or 'cron(...)') that defines how frequently the canary runs its test script.

aws_synthetics_canary.schedule.retry_con.text: Configures the number of retry attempts for a canary run after a failure, before the run is marked as failed.

aws_synthetics_canary.tags.text: A list of key-value pairs that are attached to the Synthetics canary to help manage, identify, and categorize the resource in AWS.

aws_synthetics_canary.tags.value.text: The value of a tag assigned to the Synthetics canary, used for organizing, identifying, and managing the resource.

aws_synthetics_canary.visual_reference.text: Configuration for visual monitoring, which captures screenshots of the canary's UI and compares them against baseline images to detect visual regressions.

aws_synthetics_canary.visual_reference.b.text: Specifies a list of screenshot coordinates (as comma-separated x,y string values) that are excluded from the visual comparison against the baseline screenshot.
Specifies the name of a baseline screenshot that the canary uses as a reference for visual regression testing.

aws_synthetics_canary.visual_references..text: The ID of the canary run whose screenshots are used as the baseline for visual monitoring comparisons.
Defines the list of base screenshots (each with optional ignore coordinates) that serve as the visual regression baseline for the canary's visual reference.
Specifies the pixel coordinates (as "x,y" strings) on the base screenshot that are excluded from visual comparison during canary runs.
The name of the base screenshot used by the canary's visual monitoring to compare against the live application screen.

aws_synthetics_canary.vpcconfig.text: Configures the canary to run inside a customer-managed VPC by specifying the subnet and security group IDs, which enables the canary to access resources in a private network.

aws_synthetics_canary.vpcconfig.security.text: Specifies the security group IDs that the canary uses to connect to resources in your VPC.

aws_synthetics_canary.vpcconfig.subnet_i.text: The list of subnet IDs in the VPC where the Synthetics canary's execution Lambda will run, giving the canary network access to resources within that VPC.

aws_synthetics_canary.vpcconfig.vpc_id.text: The ID of the VPC in which the canary runs, allowing it to access resources within that VPC by using the provided subnets and security groups.

aws_synthetics_group.resource_arns.text: Specifies the ARNs of the Synthetics canaries to associate with this group, making them members of the group.

aws_synthetics_group.tags.text: Tags are metadata labels (key-value pairs) that you can assign to the Synthetics group to help organize, identify, and manage it, with each tag defined by a key and optional value.

aws_synthetics_group.tags.key.text: The key part of a key-value tag, used to assign metadata to the canary group for identification and resource management.

aws_synthetics_group.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the Synthetics canary group, which is a user-defined string that helps manage and identify the group.

aws_systems_manager_sap_application.appl.text: The unique identifier of the SAP application to register with AWS Systems Manager for SAP.
The type of the SAP application being registered under Systems Manager for SAP (e.g., ABAP, JAVA, or HANA), which determines how the resource is managed and which components are applicable.

aws_systems_manager_sap_application.comp.text: Specifies the type of the SAP component (e.g., HANA or NetWeaver) that this component info entry describes for the AWS Systems Manager for SAP application.
The ID of the EC2 instance that hosts this SAP application component.
This field specifies the SAP System Identifier (SID) for an SAP component associated with the application, which AWS Systems Manager for SAP uses to identify and manage the component.

aws_systems_manager_sap_application.cred.text: A list of credential objects specifying the authentication details (credential type, secret ID, and optional database name) used by the SAP application to connect to SAP systems.
Specifies whether the credential is for administrative access (ADMIN) or system-level access (SYSTEM) to the SAP application.
The name of the SAP database (e.g., an SAP HANA database) that this credential is used to access for the registered SAP application.
The secret ID of the AWS Secrets Manager secret that stores the database credentials for this SAP application.

aws_systems_manager_sap_application.inst.text: The instances field lists the EC2 instance IDs that host the SAP application components that are registered and managed by this Systems Manager for SAP application.

aws_systems_manager_sap_application.sid.text: Specifies the SAP System Identifier (SID) for the SAP system associated with this application, a three-character code that uniquely identifies the SAP system (e.g., `H20`).

aws_systems_manager_sap_application.tags.text: A user-defined key within a tag assigned to the SAP application, used to categorize and filter the resource in AWS Systems Manager.
The value of a tag assigned to the AWS Systems Manager for SAP application, enabling custom metadata for organization, cost tracking, and resource management.

aws_timestream_database.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Timestream database, which uniquely identifies it within AWS.

aws_timestream_database.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the Timestream database, used to organize and identify the resource.

aws_timestream_database.tags.value.text: The value part of a tag applied to the Timestream database, which holds an arbitrary string for resource categorization and management.

aws_timestream_influx_dbcluster.tags.key.text: The key of a tag to assign to the Timestream InfluxDB cluster, used to categorize and manage the resource.

aws_timestream_influx_dbcluster.tags.val.text: The value component of a key-value tag assigned to the Timestream for InfluxDB DB cluster, used for metadata management, cost tracking, and access control.

aws_timestream_influx_dbinstance.tags.ke.text: The tag key (name) for a metadata tag attached to the Timestream for InfluxDB database instance, used to identify, categorize, and manage the resource.

aws_timestream_influx_dbinstance.tags.va.text: Specifies the value of a tag attached to the Timestream for InfluxDB DB instance, used for cost allocation, resource categorization, and access control.

aws_timestream_scheduled_query.tags.key.text: The tag key, which is the name of the tag assigned to the Timestream scheduled query.

aws_timestream_scheduled_query.tags.valu.text: The value string associated with a tag key for the Timestream scheduled query, used for organizing and identifying the query resource.

aws_timestream_scheduled_query.target_co.text: Specifies the data type (VARCHAR or BIGINT) of the dimension value in the dimension mapping for the Timestream target of the scheduled query.
Specifies the name of the dimension in the target Timestream table that the scheduled query result column maps to.
The measure name to assign to this mapping in the target Timestream table when the scheduled query writes mixed measures.
Specifies the data type (e.g., DOUBLE, BIGINT, BOOLEAN, VARCHAR, TIMESTAMP) for a measure value in a mixed measure mapping in the target Timestream configuration of a scheduled query.

Defines the list of attribute mappings that specify which query result columns map to each attribute in a multi-measure record written to Timestream, including the source column and target multi-measure attribute name.
Specifies the data type (e.g., BIGINT, BOOLEAN, DOUBLE, VARCHAR, TIMESTAMP) of the multi-measure attribute's value when mapping query results to a Timestream multi-measure record.
Specifies the source column in the scheduled query result whose value is mapped to the corresponding multi-measure attribute in the Timestream target table.
Specifies the target multi-measure attribute name in the Timestream table to which the source column is mapped for a scheduled query using mixed measure mappings.
The source column in the scheduled query result that is mapped to a specific measure when writing to the Timestream target table.

Sets the name of the measure column in the scheduled query's target Timestream table that receives the mapped measure value, enabling the query to store mixed-measure results under a custom measure name.
The data type of the measure value for this attribute in the multi-measure record written to Timestream (e.g., DOUBLE, BIGINT, VARCHAR, BOOLEAN, TIMESTAMP).
The name of the column in the query results that supplies the value for this multi-measure attribute.
The name of the target multi-measure attribute in the Timestream table where the mapped source column data will be written for the scheduled query.

aws_timestream_table.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this Timestream table.

aws_timestream_table.schema.composite_pa.text: Specifies whether this partition key must be present in every record, with allowed values 'REQUIRED' or 'OPTIONAL'.
Specifies the name of the dimension attribute used as the composite partition key for an AWS Timestream table when the partition key type is DIMENSION.
Specifies the type of the composite partition key, either DIMENSION for a dimension column or MEASURE for the measure name, controlling how Timestream partitions the table's data.

aws_timestream_table.tags.key.text: The key portion of a tag applied to the Timestream table, used to define the tag's name for identifying and organizing the table in AWS.

aws_timestream_table.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag attached to the Timestream table, allowing you to assign an arbitrary string to help categorize, identify, or manage the resource (e.g., for cost allocation).

aws_transcribe_vocabulary_filter.tags.ke.text: The key name for a tag assigned to this Amazon Transcribe vocabulary filter, allowing you to categorize and manage the resource by purpose, owner, or environment.

aws_transcribe_vocabulary_filter.tags.va.text: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the Amazon Transcribe vocabulary filter for organizing and managing the resource.

aws_transfer_agreement.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to an AWS Transfer Family agreement, used to categorize or identify the resource.

aws_transfer_certificate.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the AWS Transfer Family certificate, used for identifying and categorizing the resource.

aws_transfer_connector.as2_config.async_.text: Configures asynchronous Message Disposition Notification (MDN) handling for the AS2 connector, specifying the destination URL, the Secrets Manager secret ARN used to sign the HTTPS request, and whether to send the original message with the MDN (BOTH or NONE).
Specifies the list of AS2 server IDs that are used as the intended recipients for asynchronous MDN (Message Disposition Notification) responses in this connector's AS2 configuration.

aws_transfer_connector.egress_config.text: Specifies the S3 access point that acts as the source location from which the AWS Transfer Family connector reads files to send to the remote server.

aws_transfer_connector.egress_config.vpc.text: Specifies the VPC Lattice configuration used by the AWS Transfer Family connector for routing outbound connections, allowing integration with a VPC Lattice service network to securely reach remote hosts.

aws_transfer_connector.egress_type.text: Specifies the protocol type for the connector (either 'AS2' or 'SFTP') to use for outbound file transfers.

aws_transfer_connector.status.text: The current lifecycle status of the Transfer Family connector, such as ACTIVE or INACTIVE, indicating whether the connector is enabled for file transfers.

aws_transfer_connector.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Transfer Family connector, used for metadata such as cost allocation or organizational identification.

aws_transfer_profile.tags.key.text: A user-defined string that serves as the key in a tag attached to an AWS Transfer Family profile, enabling resource categorization and cost allocation.

aws_transfer_profile.tags.value.text: Specifies the value part of a tag attached to this AWS Transfer Family profile, allowing you to categorize and manage the profile with custom metadata.

aws_transfer_server.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) assigned to the Transfer Family server, which uniquely identifies it across AWS.

aws_transfer_server.certificate.text: The ARN of an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate used to secure FTPS connections for the AWS Transfer Family server.

aws_transfer_server.domain.text: The storage service (S3 or EFS) that this AWS Transfer Family server is configured to use for file storage and management.

aws_transfer_server.endpoint_details.text: Specifies the endpoint configuration for the Transfer Family server, including the endpoint type (PUBLIC, VPC, or VPC_ENDPOINT) and VPC-related settings such as subnet IDs, security group IDs, and Elastic IP allocation IDs.

aws_transfer_server.endpoint_details.add.text: Specifies the list of Elastic IP allocation IDs to associate with the server's VPC endpoint, allowing the Transfer server to have static IP addresses for its endpoint when the endpoint type is VPC.

aws_transfer_server.endpoint_details.sec.text: Specifies the security group IDs attached to the VPC endpoint used by the AWS Transfer Family server, controlling the network traffic allowed to and from the endpoint.

aws_transfer_server.endpoint_details.sub.text: Specifies the subnets in your VPC where the AWS Transfer Family server's endpoint is deployed (for VPC or VPC_ENDPOINT endpoint types), allowing the server to be accessed from within your private network.

aws_transfer_server.endpoint_details.vpc.text: The ID of the VPC endpoint that the AWS Transfer Family server is associated with when the server's endpoint type is set to VPC.
The ID of the VPC in which the AWS Transfer Family server's endpoint is hosted when the endpoint type is set to VPC.

aws_transfer_server.endpoint_type.text: Specifies the type of endpoint for the AWS Transfer Family server, which can be PUBLIC (default), VPC, or VPC_ENDPOINT, determining how clients connect to the server.

aws_transfer_server.identity_provider_de.text: Specifies the configuration details for the identity provider that AWS Transfer Family uses to authenticate users on this server, including the invocation role ARN and either the API Gateway URL, AWS Lambda function, or AWS Directory Service directory ID.
The identifier of the AWS Directory Service directory used as the identity provider for this AWS Transfer Family server, required only when the identity provider type is AWS_DIRECTORY_SERVICE.
The ARN of the AWS Lambda function that AWS Transfer Family invokes for user authentication and authorization when using the AWS Lambda identity provider type.
The IAM role that AWS Transfer Family assumes to invoke the Lambda function for user identity management when using a custom identity provider.
Configures which SFTP authentication methods (such as PASSWORD and PUBLIC_KEY) are permitted for the AWS Transfer Family server when using the specified identity provider details.
The URL of the identity provider endpoint that the Transfer server invokes to authenticate users, such as an API Gateway invocation URL or a ServiceNow instance URL.

aws_transfer_server.identity_provider_ty.text: Specifies the type of identity provider for the Transfer Family server, such as SERVICE_MANAGED, API_GATEWAY, AWS_DIRECTORY_SERVICE, or AWS_LAMBDA, which determines how user authentication is handled.

aws_transfer_server.ip_address_type.text: Specifies whether the Transfer server uses a public IP address or a private IP address within a VPC, with allowed values PUBLIC and VPC.

aws_transfer_server.logging_role.text: The ARN of the IAM role that grants AWS Transfer Family permission to write logs for this server to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.

aws_transfer_server.post_authentication_.text: This field specifies the text of a banner that is displayed to users after they successfully authenticate to the AWS Transfer Family server, appearing after the login process completes.

aws_transfer_server.pre_authentication_l.text: A text banner that AWS Transfer Family displays to users before they authenticate to the server, used for security or informational messages.

aws_transfer_server.protocol_details.text: Specifies protocol-specific settings for the AWS Transfer server, including options such as passive IP, TLS session resumption mode, and AS2 transport settings.

aws_transfer_server.protocol_details.as2.text: Specifies which transport protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, or both) are supported for AS2 message exchange on an AWS Transfer Family server, controlling the network paths allowed for AS2 traffic.

aws_transfer_server.protocol_details.pas.text: The IP address that the AWS Transfer Family server advertises for passive (PASV/EPSV) FTP connections when using FTPS.

aws_transfer_server.protocol_details.set.text: Controls whether the SFTP server performs the SETSTAT operation on the client's behalf (DEFAULT) or responds with a success without actually changing file attributes (ENABLE_NO_OP), affecting how file modification times and permissions are handled during SFTP transfers.

aws_transfer_server.protocol_details.tls.text: Controls whether TLS session resumption is enforced, enabled, or disabled for FTPS connections to the Transfer Family server, with allowed values ENFORCED, ENABLED, and DISABLED.

aws_transfer_server.protocols.text: Specifies the list of file transfer protocols (SFTP, FTP, FTPS) that the AWS Transfer Family server will support.

aws_transfer_server.s3_storage_options.text: Configures S3 storage options for the Transfer Family server, including the directory listing optimization setting that controls whether the server uses optimized directory listing for large S3 directories.

aws_transfer_server.security_policy_name.text: The name of the security policy that defines the TLS protocol versions and cipher suites used to secure SFTP connections to the server.

aws_transfer_server.server_id.text: The unique server identifier assigned by AWS for this Transfer Family server (e.g., s-1234567890abcdef), used to reference the server in API calls and other resources.

aws_transfer_server.state.text: The state of the AWS Transfer Family server, such as ONLINE or OFFLINE, indicating its lifecycle status.

aws_transfer_server.structured_log_desti.text: Specifies the list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of destinations, such as Amazon CloudWatch Logs log groups or Amazon S3 buckets, where structured logs from the AWS Transfer Family server are delivered.

aws_transfer_server.tags.text: Tags are custom key-value labels that you can assign to the AWS Transfer Family server to help organize, identify, and manage it, and they can also be used in resource-level IAM policies to control access to the server.

aws_transfer_server.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS Transfer Family server, used for resource organization and cost tracking.

aws_transfer_server.workflow_details.text: The workflow_details field configures the AWS Transfer Family workflows to execute when files are uploaded to the server, including the on-upload and on-partial-upload workflow steps.

aws_transfer_server.workflow_details.on_.text: A list of workflow steps that AWS Transfer Family executes when a file upload to the server fails partway through, allowing you to run custom actions like copying, tagging, or deleting the partially uploaded file.
The IAM role ARN that AWS Transfer Family assumes to execute the workflow steps when a file transfer is only partially uploaded (e.g., when the upload session ends before the file is fully received).
The unique identifier of the AWS Transfer Family workflow to execute when a file upload is partially completed.
A list of workflow details that specify the workflows to run when a file is uploaded to the server, each containing a workflow ID and execution role.
The IAM role that AWS Transfer Family assumes to execute the workflow when a file is uploaded to the server.
The unique identifier of the AWS Transfer Family workflow that is automatically executed when a file is successfully uploaded to the server.

aws_transfer_user.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the AWS Transfer Family user, assigned by AWS when the user is created.

aws_transfer_user.home_directory.text: The landing directory (folder) for the user when they log in to the Transfer Family server, specified as an absolute path or a virtual path that can include the {Transfer:UserName} variable.

aws_transfer_user.home_directory_mapping.text: Specifies a set of logical directory mappings that translate a user's home directory path to a target S3 or EFS location, allowing different storage paths to be presented as a single virtual path.
For each home directory mapping of an AWS Transfer Family user, this field specifies the logical directory path that the user will see, which is paired with a target path to define the mapping.
Specifies the destination absolute or relative path in the Amazon S3 bucket or Amazon EFS file system to which the 'Entry' logical directory is mapped for this AWS Transfer Family user.
Specifies whether the home directory mapping entry maps to a file ('FILE') or a directory ('DIRECTORY') in AWS Transfer Family.

aws_transfer_user.home_directory_type.text: Determines whether the user's home directory is defined as a logical directory (LOGICAL) or a direct file system path (PATH), with PATH being the default when this property is not specified.

aws_transfer_user.policy.text: A JSON string specifying an IAM scope-down policy that restricts the permissions of the AWS Transfer Family user, allowing multiple users to share the same IAM role with different access levels.

aws_transfer_user.posix_profile.text: Specifies the POSIX user profile, including the UID, GID, and secondary group IDs, used by the AWS Transfer Family user for file system permissions and ownership when operating over SFTP, FTPS, or FTP.

aws_transfer_user.posix_profile.gid.text: Specifies the POSIX group ID (GID) that maps to the user's group on the file transfer server's backing storage, determining file ownership and access permissions for the associated AWS Transfer Family user.

aws_transfer_user.posix_profile.secondar.text: Specifies the secondary group IDs (GIDs) for the user's POSIX profile, granting additional group memberships that affect file and folder access on the AWS Transfer server.

aws_transfer_user.posix_profile.uid.text: Defines the numeric POSIX user ID (UID) that AWS Transfer Family uses to set file ownership and permission checks for this user on the underlying file system (e.g., Amazon EFS).

aws_transfer_user.role.text: The IAM role that AWS Transfer Family assumes to define the user's permissions for accessing the underlying storage (e.g., Amazon S3) and other resources.

aws_transfer_user.server_id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS Transfer Family server to which this user is associated.

aws_transfer_user.tags.text: Assigns customizable metadata tags to the AWS Transfer Family user, enabling categorization, cost allocation, and access-control scoping across AWS resources.

aws_transfer_user.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag applied to an AWS Transfer Family user, used for identifying, organizing, and managing the user resource within AWS.

aws_transfer_user.tags.value.text: The value of a tag key-value pair applied to the AWS Transfer Family user, used for resource organization and access control.

aws_transfer_user.user_name.text: Sets the unique login name for the user in the AWS Transfer Family service, which must be unique within the associated server and is used to identify and authenticate the user during file transfer sessions.

aws_transfer_web_app.endpoint_details.text: Specifies the configuration for the web app's endpoint, including whether it is public or hosted within a VPC and the associated network settings such as VPC ID, subnets, and security groups.

aws_transfer_web_app.endpoint_details.vp.text: List of security group IDs applied to the VPC endpoint for the web app, controlling inbound and outbound traffic to the endpoint.
Specifies the subnets within the VPC where the AWS Transfer Family web app's endpoint is deployed, defining the network locations for private accessibility.
The ID of the VPC to which the Transfer Family web app endpoint is attached, used when the endpoint is VPC-backed rather than public.

aws_transfer_web_app.identity_provider_d.text: The ARN of the AWS Directory Service directory that serves as the identity provider for user authentication for this AWS Transfer Family web app.

aws_transfer_web_app.tags.value.text: The user-defined value of a key-value tag attached to the AWS Transfer Family web app, used for metadata such as cost allocation or environment identification.

aws_transfer_web_app.vpc_endpoint_id.text: The unique identifier of the VPC endpoint that the web app is associated with, used when the web app is deployed within a VPC.

aws_transfer_web_app.web_app_customizati.text: Customizes the branding of the AWS Transfer Family web app by specifying an optional logo and title for the web app's interface.

aws_transfer_web_app.web_app_endpoint_po.text: Specifies a JSON endpoint policy that controls access to the web application's endpoint, allowing you to restrict access to specific IP addresses or VPC endpoints.

aws_transfer_web_app.web_app_units.text: Determines the scaling capacity of the AWS Transfer Family web app by specifying the number of provisioned web app units (via its 'Provisioned' sub-property), which affects the application's performance and concurrency limits.

aws_transfer_web_app.web_app_units.provi.text: The number of provisioned web app units for this AWS Transfer Family web app, which determines the capacity and concurrency of the web app's endpoints.

aws_transfer_workflow.on_exception_steps.text: Configures the destination Amazon S3 bucket, key prefix, and optional overwrite behavior for copying a file when this step runs as part of the workflow's on-exception path.
Defines the target S3 bucket/prefix or EFS path to which the file is copied when this copy step executes as part of the workflow's exception handling.
Specifies the S3 destination bucket and key prefix for the copy step within an exception handler of an AWS Transfer Family workflow, defining where the file will be copied when an error occurs.
The name of the S3 bucket that serves as the destination for the file copy operation in this exception step of the Transfer Family workflow.
Specifies the S3 object key (file path) used as the destination location for the copy step when a workflow executes in its on-exception path.
The user-defined descriptive name for this copy step in the exception handler branch of the AWS Transfer Family workflow.
Specifies whether the copy step overwrites an existing destination file (TRUE) or does not overwrite it (FALSE) when executed as part of an on_exception_steps path in an AWS Transfer Family workflow.
Specifies the source file path for a copy step, which can be a literal path or a workflow variable (e.g., ${original.file}) that identifies the file to copy from the source server.
