The custom_step_details object specifies the AWS Lambda function target and an optional name for a custom step within an exception-handling branch of an AWS Transfer Family workflow.
The `name` property specifies a descriptive name for a custom step (which invokes an AWS Lambda function) in the on-exception steps of an AWS Transfer Family workflow.
Specifies the source file location (relative to the user's home directory) that is used as input to this custom step in an AWS Transfer Family workflow.
The ARN of the AWS Lambda function invoked by this custom step when it runs as part of the workflow's on-exception branch.
The maximum time in seconds that a custom step in the exception path is allowed to run before the workflow times out.

Specifies the decryption configuration for a copy/decrypt step in the workflow's error-handling branch, including source and destination file locations, the decryption key type (e.g., PGP), and whether to overwrite existing files.
For a decrypt step in an AWS Transfer Family workflow exception path, this object defines the destination (either an S3 bucket/prefix or an EFS file system path) where the decrypted file is written.
The EFS file system location (file system ID and path) where the decrypted file is written as the destination for the decrypt step.
The unique identifier of the Amazon EFS file system to which the decrypted file is written as part of the workflow step.
The EFS filesystem path (directory) to which the decrypted file is written when this decrypt step runs as part of the workflow's exception handling steps.
Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket and object key that serve as the destination location for files after the decryption step in an exception handling path of an AWS Transfer Family workflow.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that receives the decrypted file when this decrypt step runs as part of the workflow's exception handling.

The S3 object key (or key prefix) under which the decrypted file is stored in the destination S3 bucket when this decrypt step is executed as part of the on-exception (failure) path of the AWS Transfer Family workflow.
Sets a descriptive name for the decrypt step when it is included in the workflow's on-exception steps.
Specifies whether to overwrite an existing file with the same name or rename the existing file when the decrypted file is written to the destination.
Specifies the source file location (such as an S3 object key or EFS path) that the decrypt step in the workflow operates on.
Specifies the decryption type to use, such as PGP, for the file processed in this workflow step.
Specifies the details of a delete step (such as the source file location and file name) that runs when this workflow's on-exception branch is triggered.
The name field in the delete step details assigns a descriptive identifier to the delete step within the workflow's on-exception branch, used to recognize the step in logs and operational monitoring.

The source file location (path) of the file to delete in the delete step, which can be a static path or a workflow variable such as ${original.file}, resolved against the user's home directory on the AWS Transfer Family server.

Specifies the tag key (Name) and value (Value) for a TAG step in the onExceptionSteps list of an AWS Transfer Family workflow, which are applied to the transferred file when a prior step in the workflow fails.
Specifies the tag key (the name of the tag) to assign to the file when this tag step runs as part of the workflow's exception handling.
Specifies the file path or workflow variable that identifies which uploaded file this tag step (on an exception branch) applies tags to, defaulting to the original file if omitted.
The key-value tags that are applied to a file when a tag step runs as part of the on-exception path (exception handling) of an AWS Transfer Family workflow.
The key of a tag to attach to the file when this tag step runs in the on-exception branch of the Transfer Family workflow.
The value of a user-defined tag to apply to the file when the tag step runs as part of the workflow's exception handler.
The type of workflow step to run when an exception occurs, such as COPY, CUSTOM, DELETE, TAG, or TRANSFORM.

aws_transfer_workflow.steps.copy_step_de.text: Configures a copy step in the workflow, specifying the destination file location (S3 bucket and key or EFS file system) and whether to overwrite existing files.
This object defines the destination for a copied file in an AWS Transfer Family workflow Copy step, specifying either an Amazon S3 file location or an Amazon EFS file location.
Specifies the Amazon S3 bucket and optional key prefix that define the destination location for a file copied by the workflow's copy step.
The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that serves as the destination for the file copied by this workflow copy step.
The S3 object key (file name) under which the copied file is stored in the destination bucket, which can be static or include variables such as `${file_name}` for dynamic naming.
The user-defined name that identifies this copy step within the AWS Transfer workflow.
Determines whether the copy step overwrites an existing file at the destination, with allowed values 'TRUE' or 'FALSE'.
Specifies the source file path (or a variable) to use as the source for the copy operation in a Transfer Family workflow copy step.

aws_transfer_workflow.steps.custom_step_.text: For a workflow step of type CUSTOM, this object specifies the AWS Lambda function to invoke (via its ARN in the `Name` property) and the optional `TimeoutSeconds` setting for the invocation.
The name of the custom step in the AWS Transfer Family workflow, used to identify the step.
Specifies which file the custom Lambda step should process, either the original uploaded file or the output from a previous workflow step.
The ARN of the AWS Lambda function that this custom workflow step invokes.

The maximum time in seconds (defaulting to 900) that the custom Lambda step is allowed to run before the workflow step is marked as failed, as defined in the CustomStepDetails of an AWS Transfer Family workflow step.

aws_transfer_workflow.steps.decrypt_step.text: Provides settings for a workflow step that decrypts files, including the decryption type (such as PGP), the destination S3 location, and options like overwriting existing files.
Defines the target location (an Amazon S3 bucket and key prefix or an Amazon EFS file system path) where the decrypted file is written after the workflow's decrypt step completes.
Specifies the EFS file system ID and path on the destination where the decrypted file is stored.
The unique identifier of the Amazon EFS file system to which the decrypted file is written in this transform step.
The path within the specified Amazon EFS file system where the decrypted file is stored as the destination of the decrypt step in the Transfer Family workflow.
Specifies the S3 bucket and key (file location) to which the decrypted file is written after the decrypt step in the Transfer Family workflow executes.
The name of the S3 bucket where the decrypted file is stored as the destination in the decrypt step of an AWS Transfer Family workflow.
The S3 object key (file path) where the decrypted file is stored after the decrypt step in the AWS Transfer Family workflow.
The descriptive name for the decrypt step in an AWS Transfer Family workflow, used to identify the step in the console and API operations.
Indicates whether the decrypt step overwrites an existing file with the same name in the destination location.
Specifies the location of the source file to be decrypted by the decrypt step in an AWS Transfer Family workflow.
Specifies the encryption type used for the decryption step, with 'PGP' as the only supported value in AWS Transfer Family workflows.

aws_transfer_workflow.steps.delete_step_.text: Specifies the details of a DELETE step in the AWS Transfer workflow, including the step name and the source file location (such as ${original.file}) that identifies which file to delete.
Specifies a human-readable name for the delete step, which AWS Transfer Family uses as a unique identifier for the step within the workflow.
Specifies the location of the file to delete, given as either a static path relative to the user's home directory or a workflow variable such as `${source}`.

aws_transfer_workflow.steps.tag_step_det.text: Provides the configuration for a workflow step that adds tags to a file, including the step name, source file location, and the tags to apply.
The user-defined name for this tag step in the AWS Transfer Family workflow, used to identify the step within the workflow definition.
Specifies which file to use as the source for the tagging operation, either 'ORIGINAL' (the initial uploaded file) or the unique ID of a previous workflow step whose output file should be tagged.
The list of tag key-value pairs that this workflow step applies to the transferred file.
The key of a tag to assign to the transferred file as part of the workflow's tag step.
The value of the key-value tag that this tag step in the AWS Transfer Family workflow assigns to the target resource.

aws_transfer_workflow.steps.type.text: Specifies the type of the workflow step, determining the operation performed on the transferred file (e.g., COPY, DELETE, TAG, or CUSTOM).

aws_transfer_workflow.tags.key.text: The tag key (e.g., 'environment') assigned to the AWS Transfer Family workflow as part of a metadata tag for resource identification and cost allocation.

aws_transfer_workflow.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the AWS Transfer Family workflow, which is a user-defined string that metadataizes the resource for identification, categorization, and access control.

aws_translate_parallel_data.tags.key.text: The key of a tag (e.g., a name like 'purpose') to associate with the Amazon Translate parallel data resource for managing and categorizing it.

aws_translate_parallel_data.tags.value.text: The value component of a key-value tag attached to the AWS Translate parallel data resource, used to categorize or manage the resource.

aws_verified_permissions_identity_source.text: Specifies the identity provider configuration for the identity source, such as Amazon Cognito user pool details (UserPoolArn, ClientId) or an OpenID Connect provider (issuer, client ID, etc.), which Amazon Verified Permissions uses to authenticate and authorize principals.
Configures an Amazon Cognito user pool as the identity source for AWS Verified Permissions, specifying the user pool ARN and associated client application IDs.
The list of Amazon Cognito app client IDs that are allowed to use this identity source for authentication.

Defines the optional group configuration for the Amazon Cognito user pool identity source, specifically setting the GroupEntityType that maps Cognito user pool groups to an entity type used in Cedar policies for group-based authorization.
The Cedar entity type that Cognito user pool groups are mapped to when groups are converted into principal entities for authorization.
The ARN of the Amazon Cognito user pool that this Verified Permissions identity source is associated with, used to validate and authorize user identities within the policy store.

Configuration object that defines the OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider settings, including the issuer URL, entity ID prefix, group configuration, and token selection rules for the identity source.
The entity ID prefix that is prepended to the subject claim of the OIDC identity token to create the unique principal entity ID used by Amazon Verified Permissions.
Specifies the OIDC token claim (via its group_claim field) that contains group membership information for the identity source.
Specifies the name of the claim in the OIDC token that contains the user's group memberships, used by AWS Verified Permissions to determine group assignments for authorization.
Specifies the entity type (e.g., "MyApp::Group") that represents groups in the identity source, used to map OIDC group claims to Cedar group entities.
The URL of the OpenID Connect issuer, which identifies the OIDC provider and is used to verify the issuer claim in access tokens.

Defines how Verified Permissions extracts the principal identifier from an OIDC-issued token by selecting whether to use the access token or the identity token and optionally specifying which token claim to use as the principal's identity.
Configures the OIDC identity source to use only the access token for principal identification, including the claim used to extract the principal ID.
The list of allowed audience (aud) claim values that an access token must contain for it to be accepted by the identity source.
Specifies the claim in the access token that should be used as the principal identifier for the identity source.
Defines the configuration for accepting only the OIDC identity token for authorization, optionally specifying the list of client IDs that are allowed to use this token.
Specifies the list of OIDC client IDs that are allowed to use the identity token, restricting authentication and authorization to tokens issued for those client applications.
Specifies the OIDC claim (e.g., 'sub' or 'user_id') from the identity token that is used as the unique principal identifier for the identity source.

`details` returns the computed configuration details of the identity source, including the Amazon Cognito user pool client IDs and group configuration settings, as resolved by AWS Verified Permissions.
Specifies the client IDs of the identity provider (such as a Cognito user pool app or OIDC application) that are allowed to use this identity source for Amazon Verified Permissions.
The URL of the OpenID Connect discovery endpoint for the identity provider, which Verified Permissions uses to automatically fetch the provider's configuration.
The issuer URL of the OpenID Connect provider used for this identity source, which AWS Verified Permissions uses to discover and validate tokens issued by that provider.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Cognito user pool that acts as the identity provider for this identity source.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the identity source.
The unique identifier of the policy store to which this identity source is attached.
Specifies the principal entity type (e.g., 'User' or 'Group') that identities from this identity source are mapped to for use in Cedar policies.

aws_verified_permissions_policy.definiti.text: Contains the policy's definition, either a static statement written in Cedar policy syntax or a template-linked reference to a policy template with a principal.

The 'definition.static' object defines a static policy for AWS Verified Permissions, containing the Cedar policy statement text (Statement) and an optional AdditionalDetails field for supplementary information.
Provides a human-readable description of the static Cedar policy, documenting its purpose or intended effect within the AWS Verified Permissions policy definition.
The Cedar policy statement text (in Cedar syntax) that defines the authorization rules for this static policy.
Defines a policy that is created from a policy template, specifying the template ID and the principal and resource entities to which the template's placeholders are applied.
Specifies the unique identifier of the policy template from which this template-linked policy is created, allowing the policy to inherit the template's statements and placeholders.
Specifies the principal (e.g., a user or group) to which the template-linked policy applies, identified by its entity type and ID, or the special value 'ANY' to match all principals.
Specifies the unique identifier of the principal entity (within its entity type) to which the template-linked policy applies.
Specifies the entity type (e.g., 'User' or 'Group') of the principal to which the template-linked policy applies, used to bind the principal placeholder in the policy template.
Specifies the resource entity (by type and ID) that the template-linked policy applies to, filling in the resource placeholder from the Cedar policy template.
Specifies the unique ID of the resource entity (such as an application resource or a user) that this template-linked policy applies to as the resource of the policy.
Sets the entity type of the resource to which the template-linked policy applies, constraining the policy's resource scope to Cedar entities of that type.

aws_verified_permissions_policy.policy_i.text: The unique identifier assigned by Amazon Verified Permissions to the policy when it is created, used to reference and manage the policy.

aws_verified_permissions_policy.policy_s.text: The unique identifier of the policy store in AWS Verified Permissions where this policy is created and to which it belongs.

aws_verified_permissions_policy.policy_t.text: The type of the policy (STATIC or TEMPLATE_LINKED), indicating whether the policy was defined directly or linked to a policy template.

aws_verified_permissions_policy_store.ar.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying the policy store, assigned by AWS when the policy store is created.

aws_verified_permissions_policy_store.de.text: Whether deletion protection is enabled for this policy store, which prevents the policy store from being deleted until the setting is disabled.
Specifies whether deletion protection is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for the policy store, controlling whether the policy store can be deleted.
Provides a free-form, human-readable description of the policy store to help identify its purpose or manage it among other stores.

aws_verified_permissions_policy_store.en.text: Specifies the AWS KMS key (customer-managed or AWS-managed) used to encrypt the policy store's data; if omitted, the store is encrypted with an AWS-managed key.
Specifies the default encryption configuration for the policy store, choosing between AWS-managed encryption and a customer-managed AWS KMS key to protect the policy store's data.
Specifies the customer-managed AWS KMS key configuration used to encrypt the policy store, including the KMS key ARN.

Specifies a map of encryption context key-value pairs that are included as authenticated data in the KMS encryption operation when a customer-managed key encrypts the policy store, providing an extra layer of integrity and auditability.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the customer managed AWS KMS key used to encrypt the policy store when KMS encryption is configured.

The computed encryption_state object describes the policy store's current encryption configuration, distinguishing between AWS-managed encryption and customer-managed KMS encryption and including the KMS key ARN when applicable.
The KMS encryption state configuration for the policy store, containing a status field that indicates whether AWS KMS customer-managed key encryption is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED).
Specifies the encryption context (a set of key-value pairs) used as additional authenticated data when encrypting the policy store with AWS KMS.
The `key` attribute specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the customer-managed AWS KMS key used to encrypt the Verified Permissions policy store under the KMS encryption configuration.

aws_verified_permissions_policy_store.po.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the policy store when it is created.

aws_verified_permissions_policy_store.sc.text: Defines the Cedar schema for the policy store, specifying entity types, their attributes, and actions, which determines the valid policies and authorization requests.
The Cedar schema for the policy store, expressed as a JSON string that defines the entity types and actions used in authorization policies.

aws_verified_permissions_policy_store.ta.text: The key of a tag that can be assigned to the AWS Verified Permissions policy store to help organize, identify, and manage the resource.

aws_verified_permissions_policy_store.va.text: Configures the validation mode (OFF or STRICT) for the Cedar policies stored in the policy store, determining whether and how strictly policies are validated.
Specifies whether the policy store validates policies against its schema, with OFF disabling validation and STRICT enabling strict validation.

aws_verified_permissions_policy_store_al.text: The alias name provides a friendly, user-defined identifier for the policy store, allowing it to be referenced in authorization requests instead of the raw policy store ID.
The unique identifier of the Amazon Verified Permissions policy store to which this alias belongs.

aws_verified_permissions_policy_template.text: Specifies an optional text description for the policy template, used to provide context about the template's intended purpose.
The ID of the policy store in which this policy template is created, associating the template with a specific Cedar policy store.
The unique identifier (UUID) assigned by Amazon Verified Permissions to the policy template, used to reference the template in policies and API operations.
The Cedar policy statement, written in the Cedar policy language, that defines the authorization rules for this policy template, optionally using placeholders like ?principal and ?resource.

aws_voice_id_domain.description.text: Specifies a description for the Voice ID domain.

aws_voice_id_domain.domain_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the Voice ID domain, used to reference the domain in other services.

aws_voice_id_domain.name.text: Sets the name of the Voice ID domain, which is a required, user-friendly identifier for the domain.

aws_voice_id_domain.server_side_encrypti.text: Defines the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the domain's data, required when creating a Voice ID domain.
The ARN or ID of the AWS KMS key used to encrypt the Voice ID domain's data at rest.

aws_voice_id_domain.tags.text: A list of key-value tag objects to assign to the Voice ID domain for resource identification and management.

aws_voice_id_domain.tags.key.text: The key of a metadata tag attached to the Amazon Voice ID domain, used to categorize and identify the domain for resource management and access control.

aws_voice_id_domain.tags.value.text: Value of a user-defined tag attached to the Voice ID domain.

aws_vpc.arn.text: The VPC's real ARN, computed, known only after ship.

aws_vpc.cidr_block.text: The real IP address range for this VPC, in CIDR notation.

aws_vpc.cidr_block_associations.text: This computed field contains the list of IPv4 CIDR block associations for the VPC, including the primary CIDR block and any secondary CIDR blocks attached to the VPC.

aws_vpc.default_network_acl.text: The ID of the default network ACL that AWS automatically creates for the VPC.

aws_vpc.default_network_acl_id.text: The real, automatically-created default network ACL.

aws_vpc.default_route_table_id.text: The real, automatically-created default route table.

aws_vpc.default_security_group.text: The ID of the default security group that AWS automatically creates for the VPC.

aws_vpc.default_security_group_id.text: The real, automatically-created default security group.

aws_vpc.enable_dns_hostnames.text: Whether instances get real, public DNS hostnames.

aws_vpc.enable_dns_support.text: Whether real DNS resolution works inside this VPC.

aws_vpc.ipv6_cidr_blocks.text: The IPv6 CIDR block(s) assigned to the VPC, computed by AWS and returned as a list of strings.

aws_vpc.main_route_table_id.text: The real ID of the main route table.

aws_vpc.region.text: Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints). Defaults to the Region set in the [provider configuration](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs#aws-configuration-reference).

aws_vpc.tags.key.text: This field represents the key of a user-defined tag applied to the VPC, forming the key-value pair in the VPC's tag set.

aws_vpc.vpc_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the VPC when it is created, used to reference the VPC elsewhere.

aws_vpc_lattice_access_log_subscription..text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this VPC Lattice access log subscription, automatically assigned by AWS upon creation.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the destination (an S3 bucket, CloudWatch Logs log group, or Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream) to which VPC Lattice access logs are delivered.
The unique identifier assigned to the VPC Lattice access log subscription upon creation.
The ARN of the service network or service that this access log subscription is associated with.
The unique identifier assigned by AWS VPC Lattice to the access log subscription, used to reference the subscription in API calls and other resources.
Specifies the ID or ARN of the service network or service that the access log subscription is associated with, determining which resource's access logs are delivered to the destination.
A list of tag objects (Key and Value) to attach to the VPC Lattice access log subscription, used for organization, cost tracking, and resource management.
The key of a tag attached to this VPC Lattice access log subscription, used to identify, categorize, and manage the subscription alongside other VPC Lattice resources.

The value of a user-defined tag attached to the AWS VPC Lattice access log subscription, used for organizing and identifying the subscription through key-value metadata such as environment, owner, or cost center.

aws_vpc_lattice_auth_policy.policy.text: The JSON policy document that defines the authentication and authorization rules for the associated VPC Lattice service or service network, specifying allowed principals, actions, and conditions.

aws_vpc_lattice_auth_policy.resource_ide.text: The resource identifier specifies the ID or ARN of the VPC Lattice service or service network that this auth policy is associated with.

aws_vpc_lattice_auth_policy.state.text: Returns the current state of the VPC Lattice auth policy, indicating whether the policy is active or inactive.

aws_vpc_lattice_domain_verification.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this VPC Lattice domain verification resource.

aws_vpc_lattice_domain_verification.doma.text: The custom domain name that AWS VPC Lattice will verify to prove ownership before it can be associated with a service network.

aws_vpc_lattice_domain_verification.stat.text: The current state of the domain ownership verification for the VPC Lattice service network, indicating whether the domain has been successfully verified (e.g., IN_PROGRESS, SUCCESS, FAILED).

aws_vpc_lattice_domain_verification.txt_.text: This read-only object contains the TXT record details (such as record name and value) that AWS VPC Lattice generated for verifying ownership of the specified domain.
Specifies the TXT record name (hostname) used for DNS-based verification of domain ownership in VPC Lattice.
The TXT record value that must be added to the domain's DNS configuration to verify ownership for AWS VPC Lattice domain verification.

aws_vpc_lattice_listener.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the VPC Lattice listener, assigned by AWS to uniquely identify the listener resource.

aws_vpc_lattice_listener.default_action.text: The default action defines how the listener handles requests that do not match any other rule, such as forwarding them to a target group or returning a fixed response.

aws_vpc_lattice_listener.default_action..text: Defines a fixed-response action for the listener's default action, which returns a specified HTTP status code (e.g., 404) without forwarding traffic to a target group.
The HTTP status code (for example, 200 or 404) that VPC Lattice returns in the fixed-response action when a request matches this listener's default action.

Configures the listener's default action to forward incoming requests to one or more VPC Lattice target groups with weighted distribution, where this object holds the list of target groups and their respective weights.
Defines the list of target groups and their relative weights for the forward action, specifying how incoming traffic is distributed when the listener's default action is a forward.
The identifier (Amazon Resource Name or ID) of the VPC Lattice target group that this forward action routes traffic to.

Specifies the relative weight assigned to this target group in the listener's forward action, controlling the proportion of traffic it receives compared to other target groups in the weighted distribution.

aws_vpc_lattice_listener.id.text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for this VPC Lattice listener, used as the Terraform resource ID.

aws_vpc_lattice_listener.name.text: The name of the VPC Lattice listener, which is optional and defaults to an AWS-generated name if not provided.

aws_vpc_lattice_listener.port.text: The port number on which the VPC Lattice listener receives incoming traffic, defaulting to 80 for HTTP or 443 for HTTPS when omitted.

aws_vpc_lattice_listener.protocol.text: Specifies the network protocol (HTTP, HTTPS, or TCP) that the VPC Lattice listener uses to accept incoming traffic, as defined by the AWS::VpcLattice::Listener resource.

aws_vpc_lattice_listener.service_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the VPC Lattice service that this listener is associated with, assigned by AWS.

aws_vpc_lattice_listener.service_id.text: The unique identifier of the VPC Lattice service that this listener is attached to, assigned by AWS when the service is provisioned.

aws_vpc_lattice_listener.service_identif.text: The ID or Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the service that owns this listener.

aws_vpc_lattice_listener.tags.text: Specifies a list of tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the VPC Lattice listener, used for identifying and organizing the listener.

aws_vpc_lattice_listener.tags.key.text: The key of a user-defined tag to attach to the VPC Lattice listener, used for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_vpc_lattice_listener.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag assigned to the VPC Lattice listener, used to categorize the resource for cost allocation, access controls, and operational management.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_configuration.a.text: Specifies whether this resource configuration can be associated with a service network that is shared across AWS accounts, typically via AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM).
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the VPC Lattice resource configuration, automatically generated by AWS.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_configuration.c.text: Specifies a custom DNS domain name for the resource configuration, allowing the associated resource to be accessed through that hostname via VPC Lattice.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_configuration.d.text: The domain_verification_id supplies the token that you add as a CNAME record in your DNS provider to prove ownership of the custom domain name for the VPC Lattice resource configuration.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_configuration.g.text: The domain name of the resource configuration group to which this resource configuration belongs.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_configuration.i.text: The unique, system-generated ID that identifies the VPC Lattice resource configuration.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_configuration.n.text: The name of the VPC Lattice resource configuration, which must be unique within the AWS account and Region and serves as the identifier when managing the configuration.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_configuration.p.text: The port ranges (for example, "80-80" or "443") that the resource configuration allows for inbound traffic to the associated resource.
Specifies the protocol type (TCP or TLS) used by the resource configuration to communicate with the resource gateway.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_configuration.r.text: Specifies the authentication type for the resource configuration, either NONE to allow open access or AWS_IAM to require AWS Identity and Access Management authentication.

This object configures how the resource is defined for the VPC Lattice resource configuration, either through an ARN resource (specifying a resource ARN) or a DNS resource (specifying a domain name and IP address type).
Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the resource when you define the resource configuration using an ARN-based resource definition.
The dns_resource object defines a DNS-based resource for the VPC Lattice resource configuration, containing the domain name and optional IP address type for the target resource.
The domain name of the DNS resource that this VPC Lattice resource configuration associates with.
Specifies the IP address type (IPV4, IPV6, or DUALSTACK) for the DNS resource configuration in VPC Lattice, controlling which address family the domain name resolves to.
Specifies the IP address (e.g., 192.0.2.1) for an IP-based resource configuration in AWS VPC Lattice, defining a single target IP for service access.
The ID of the resource configuration group that this resource configuration is associated with in VPC Lattice.
Determines the kind of resource configuration being defined (such as a resource group, subnet, single ARN, or multiple ARNs) and therefore the expected shape of the resource configuration definition.
The ID of the VPC Lattice resource gateway that provides network connectivity for this resource configuration.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_configuration.t.text: Attaches the specified list of tag objects to the Amazon VPC Lattice resource configuration, allowing you to assign key-value metadata for identifying, organizing, and managing the resource.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_gateway.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this VPC Lattice resource gateway, which is automatically generated by AWS when the gateway is created.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_gateway.ip_addr.text: Specifies the IP address type (IPv4 or IPv6) that the resource gateway uses for network traffic to and from its associated resources.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_gateway.name.text: Specifies the name of the VPC Lattice resource gateway, which must be unique across all resource gateways in the same AWS account and region.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_gateway.resourc.text: Specifies the DNS resolution type for the resource gateway's resource configuration, controlling whether DNS names resolve to IPv4, IPv6, or both address types.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_gateway.tags.text: Specifies the tags (key-value pairs) to attach to the VPC Lattice resource gateway, enabling categorization, cost allocation, and access control for the gateway.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_gateway.tags.va.text: The value component of a tag assigned to this VPC Lattice resource gateway, providing user-defined metadata used to identify and organize the gateway.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_gateway.vpc_ide.text: The ID of the VPC in which the resource gateway is deployed.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_policy.policy.text: The JSON policy document that defines the permissions for the VPC Lattice resource, such as a service network or service, controlling which principals can access the resource.

aws_vpc_lattice_resource_policy.resource.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the VPC Lattice resource (such as a service or service network) to which this resource policy is attached.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.action.text: Defines how the rule handles matching traffic, such as forwarding to a target group with weighted targets or returning a fixed HTTP response.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.action.fixed_respon.text: The fixed_response block configures a fixed-response action for the rule, allowing you to specify a custom HTTP status code and an optional response body to be returned when the rule's conditions are met.
The HTTP status code (e.g., 200, 404) returned by the fixed-response action of the VPC Lattice rule.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.action.forward.text: The forward action of the VPC Lattice rule, which specifies the target groups to which matching traffic is forwarded.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.action.forward.targ.text: Specifies the list of target groups and their weights to which the forward action distributes traffic.
The identifier of the target group to which the VPC Lattice rule forwards matching traffic.
Sets the relative traffic weight (0-999) for this target group in a VPC Lattice rule's forward action, so that higher weights receive a proportionally larger share of matched traffic.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this VPC Lattice rule.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.id.text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for this VPC Lattice rule.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.listener_identifier.text: The ID or ARN of the VPC Lattice listener that this rule is associated with, defining the listener on which the rule's match conditions and actions are applied.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.match.text: The match criteria, such as HTTP method, path, headers, query parameters, or TLS Server Name Indication, that define which incoming traffic this rule evaluates.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.match.http_match.text: Defines the HTTP matching criteria (such as method, path, headers, and query parameters) used by the VPC Lattice rule to determine which requests it applies to.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.match.http_match.he.text: Specifies a list of HTTP header match criteria for the rule, including header name, value, and match type (exact, prefix, or contains) used to determine whether incoming traffic matches.
Specifies whether the header value comparison in this HTTP header match is case-sensitive, meaning that when set to false, the matching ignores casing in the header value.
Specifies the match type (e.g., exact, prefix, or contains) and the value used to match the HTTP header value in the VPC Lattice rule.
When the match type is 'contains', specifies the substring that the header value must include for the rule to match.
The exact string value that the HTTP request header must match for this header match condition in a VPC Lattice rule.
Specifies the prefix string that the header value must begin with for the HTTP header match to succeed in the VPC Lattice rule.
The name of the HTTP header to match (e.g., Content-Type, Authorization) in a VPC Lattice rule's HTTP header match condition.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.match.http_match.me.text: The HTTP request method (such as GET, POST, PUT) that incoming requests must use in order for this VPC Lattice rule to match.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.match.http_match.pa.text: Specifies the path matching configuration for the HTTP request in a VPC Lattice rule, including the match type (e.g., PREFIX_MATCH or EXACT_MATCH) and the path value to match.
Determines whether the HTTP path match pattern is case-sensitive, meaning request paths must match the configured path exactly in letter case.
This field defines the path matching pattern (exact, prefix, or wildcard) used to determine whether an incoming HTTP request matches the rule.
The exact path string that the incoming HTTP request's path must match for this rule to apply.
The URL path prefix that incoming requests must match for the VPC Lattice rule to apply.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.name.text: Specifies a friendly name for the VPC Lattice rule, which must be unique within its listener.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.priority.text: The priority assigned to the rule, where lower numbers take precedence over higher numbers when multiple rules match a request.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.service_identifier.text: The identifier (ID or ARN) of the VPC Lattice service that owns the listener and rule, used to scope the rule to a specific service's traffic.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.tags.text: Assigns a list of tags (key-value pairs) to the VPC Lattice rule to help identify and categorize the resource.

aws_vpc_lattice_rule.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to this VPC Lattice rule, used to identify and organize the rule.

aws_vpc_lattice_service.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the VPC Lattice service.

aws_vpc_lattice_service.auth_type.text: Specifies the authentication type for the VPC Lattice service, which can be either NONE (no authentication) or AWS_IAM (requiring IAM-based authentication for requests).

aws_vpc_lattice_service.certificate_arn.text: ARN of the certificate used for TLS encryption on the VPC Lattice service's custom domain.

aws_vpc_lattice_service.created_at.text: The timestamp indicating when the VPC Lattice service was created, in ISO 8601 format.

aws_vpc_lattice_service.custom_domain_na.text: Specifies a custom domain name for the VPC Lattice service, allowing you to use your own domain instead of the default generated DNS name.

aws_vpc_lattice_service.dns_entry.text: The automatically generated DNS entry for the VPC Lattice service, containing the service's domain name and the hosted zone ID that serves its DNS records.

aws_vpc_lattice_service.dns_entry.domain.text: The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) assigned to the VPC Lattice service's DNS entry, used for routing traffic to the service (e.g., service-id.vpc-lattice-svcs.region.on.aws).

aws_vpc_lattice_service.dns_entry.hosted.text: The ID of the Amazon Route 53 hosted zone that contains the DNS record for the VPC Lattice service's domain name, returned by the service after it is created.

aws_vpc_lattice_service.id.text: The unique service ID assigned by AWS when the VPC Lattice service is created.

aws_vpc_lattice_service.idle_timeout_sec.text: Specifies the idle timeout (in seconds) that a connection to the service may remain inactive before it is closed, with a default of 900 seconds.

aws_vpc_lattice_service.last_updated_at.text: Indicates the most recent time at which the VPC Lattice service was modified, expressed as a string in ISO 8601 date-time format.

aws_vpc_lattice_service.name.text: A user-friendly name for the VPC Lattice service; if you don't provide one, AWS CloudFormation generates a unique name for the service.

aws_vpc_lattice_service.status.text: The current lifecycle status of the VPC Lattice service (for example, ACTIVE or CREATE_IN_PROGRESS), which is computed by AWS and indicates whether the service is available or still being provisioned.

aws_vpc_lattice_service.tags.key.text: The key component of a tag pair attached to an AWS VPC Lattice service, allowing you to assign custom metadata for organizing and managing the service.

aws_vpc_lattice_service_network.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the VPC Lattice service network, automatically assigned by AWS upon creation.

aws_vpc_lattice_service_network.auth_typ.text: Determines the authentication method for the service network, accepting either NONE to allow open access or AWS_IAM to require IAM authentication for client requests.

aws_vpc_lattice_service_network.created_.text: The date and time when the service network was created.

aws_vpc_lattice_service_network.id.text: The unique identifier of the VPC Lattice service network (e.g., sn-0123456789abcdef0), assigned by AWS upon creation.

aws_vpc_lattice_service_network.last_upd.text: The timestamp indicating when the VPC Lattice service network was most recently updated, returned as a read-only string.

aws_vpc_lattice_service_network.name.text: Specifies the name of the VPC Lattice service network, which must be unique within the account; if omitted, AWS CloudFormation generates a unique name.

aws_vpc_lattice_service_network.sharing_.text: Defines the sharing configuration for the service network, with an 'enabled' toggle that allows the network to be shared with other AWS accounts through AWS Resource Access Manager.
Whether the service network can be shared with other AWS accounts via AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM).

aws_vpc_lattice_service_network.tags.text: Specifies the tags to associate with the service network, which can be used for cost allocation and resource management.

aws_vpc_lattice_service_network.tags.key.text: The tag key (along with the tag value) used to attach metadata to the VPC Lattice service network for identification and organization.

aws_vpc_lattice_service_network.tags.val.text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the VPC Lattice service network, used for cost allocation, resource organization, and IAM-based access control.

aws_vpc_lattice_service_network_resource.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) uniquely identifying this service network resource association.
The unique AWS-assigned identifier for the VPC Lattice service network resource association.
When enabled, this generates a private DNS hostname for the associated resource within the VPC Lattice service network, allowing it to be accessed via DNS resolution from associated VPCs.
The unique identifier of the resource configuration (such as a VPC or AWS service) to associate with the service network.
The unique ID of the VPC Lattice service network that this resource association attaches the specified resource to.
Specifies a list of key-value tag objects to attach to the VPC Lattice service network resource association, which can be used for resource identification, cost allocation, and access control.
The key of a tag attached to the VPC Lattice service network resource association, used to organize and identify the resource.
The value portion of a tag key-value pair attached to a VPC Lattice service network resource association, used to provide user-defined metadata for identifying or managing the association.

aws_vpc_lattice_service_network_service_.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the VPC Lattice service network service association.
The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) indicating when the service network service association was created.
The generated DNS entry for the service within the VPC Lattice service network, containing the service's domain name and the hosted zone ID where the association's DNS record is configured.
The DNS domain name of the service that is exposed through the VPC Lattice service network association, used by clients in associated VPCs to reach the service.
The ID of the Route 53 hosted zone that contains the DNS record for the service network service association's DNS entry.

The unique AWS-assigned identifier for the VPC Lattice service network service association (for example, an `snssa-` string) that is returned after creation and can be used to reference the association in other resources or API calls.
The ARN of the service that is associated with the service network through this association.
The ID of the service that is associated with the service network, returned as a read-only attribute.
The ID or Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the VPC Lattice service that is associated with the service network.
The name of the VPC Lattice service that is associated with the service network, returned as a read-only attribute after the association is created.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the service network that this service network service association links to a service, uniquely identifying the service network within AWS VPC Lattice.
The unique identifier of the VPC Lattice service network to which the service is associated, assigned by AWS.
The ID or Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the service network that the service is associated with.
The name of the VPC Lattice service network that the associated service is connected to, populated automatically by AWS.
The current status of the service network service association, such as 'ACTIVE', 'CREATE_IN_PROGRESS', or 'DELETE_IN_PROGRESS', reflecting its lifecycle state in VPC Lattice.
Specifies a list of tag objects (key-value pairs) to attach to this VPC Lattice service network service association for metadata and cost tracking.
The key of a tag assigned to the VPC Lattice service network service association, used for organizing and managing the resource in AWS.

aws_vpc_lattice_service_network_vpc_asso.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the VPC association, assigned by AWS when the association is created.
The timestamp indicating when the VPC Lattice service network VPC association was created.
DNS options for the VPC association, specifying the DNS type (IPv4 or IPv6) used to resolve service network domains within the associated VPC.
Determines whether private DNS resolution is enabled for the VPC associated with the service network, accepting values 'enabled' or 'disabled' to control the private DNS preference.

The `dns_options.private_dns_specified_domains` field specifies the list of private DNS domain names that the associated VPC will use to resolve service endpoints in the service network, enabling private DNS resolution for the association.
The unique AWS-assigned identifier for this service network VPC association.
Indicates whether private DNS is enabled for the VPC association, allowing service network endpoints to be resolved using private DNS in the associated VPC.
Specifies the list of security group IDs to optionally associate with this VPC Lattice service network VPC association, which control traffic between the VPC and the service network.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the service network to which the VPC is associated.
The unique identifier of the VPC Lattice service network that this association connects to the specified VPC.
The ID or ARN of the Amazon VPC Lattice service network that the VPC association targets.
The name of the VPC Lattice service network that the VPC is associated with, automatically returned by AWS after the association is created.
The current lifecycle status of the VPC association, such as CREATE_IN_PROGRESS, ACTIVE, or DELETE_IN_PROGRESS, as reported by AWS VPC Lattice.
Assigns a list of key-value tags to the service network VPC association to help manage and identify it.
The value component of a tag attached to the AWS VPC Lattice service network VPC association, used for metadata, identification, and cost allocation.
The ID of the VPC that is associated with the service network.
The ID of the VPC that is associated with the service network.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the VPC Lattice target group, automatically assigned by AWS upon creation.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.config.text: Config specifies the target group's configuration settings, such as the protocol, port, VPC identifier, and health check parameters.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.config.heal.text: Specifies the health check configuration for the VPC Lattice target group, including protocol, port, path, matcher, interval, timeout, and threshold counts used to determine target health.
Indicates whether health checks are enabled for the target group; when set to false, the target group does not perform health-check probing on its registered targets.
The time in seconds between each health check of a target in the VPC Lattice target group, with a default of 30 and a valid range of 5 to 300.
Specifies the number of seconds to wait for a target's health check response before considering it unhealthy.
The number of consecutive successful health checks that must occur before a target is marked as healthy.
Defines the expected HTTP response status codes (e.g., '200' or '200-299') that indicate a healthy target for the health check, structured as an object containing the 'httpCode' property.
Specifies the HTTP status code or range (e.g., '200' or '200-299') that a target must return in response to a health check request for it to be considered healthy for this VPC Lattice target group.
The destination path for HTTP/HTTPS health check requests, used to determine target health, such as '/health'.
The port number on the target that the health check requests are sent to, which overrides the target's traffic port if specified.

Specifies the protocol (HTTP, HTTPS, or TCP) used by VPC Lattice for health checks on targets in this target group, where TCP performs a connection check and HTTP/HTTPS send a request to the configured health check path.
Determines whether health check requests to targets use HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 when the health check protocol is HTTP or HTTPS.
The number of consecutive failed health checks required to mark a target as unhealthy in the VPC Lattice target group's health check configuration.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.config.ip_a.text: Determines the IP address version (IPv4 or IPv6) used for targets when the target type is IP, with IPv4 as the default if omitted.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.config.lamb.text: Specifies the version of the event structure (V1 or V2) that VPC Lattice uses when invoking the Lambda target for this target group, controlling the format of the event payload delivered to the function.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.config.port.text: The port number on which the VPC Lattice target group's targets listen for traffic, specified within the target group's configuration.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.config.prot.text: Specifies the network protocol used by the target group to route traffic to its targets (e.g., HTTP, HTTPS, or TCP).
The HTTP protocol version (HTTP1 or HTTP2) that the target group uses for routing requests to its targets.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.config.vpc_.text: The ID of the VPC in which the target group's targets are located, required for target groups of type IP or ALB but not for Lambda targets.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.created_at.text: The timestamp (in ISO 8601 format) representing when the target group was created.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.id.text: The unique VPC Lattice target group identifier assigned by AWS upon creation, a string with a 'tg-' prefix (e.g., 'tg-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890') used to reference the target group in VPC Lattice operations.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.last_update.text: The timestamp indicating when the target group was last updated.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.name.text: The name of the VPC Lattice target group, providing a friendly identifier for the resource.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.status.text: Indicates the current lifecycle status of the target group, such as ACTIVE or DRAFT, reflecting whether the target group is ready for use.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.tags.text: Defines the tags to associate with the VPC Lattice target group, where each tag is an object with a Key and Value, used to manage, identify, and categorize the target group.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.tags.value.text: The value of a user-defined tag applied to the VPC Lattice target group, used for organizing or identifying the resource.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.targets.text: Specifies the list of targets (by ID or IP address) to register with this target group, optionally with a port.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.targets.id.text: The ID of the target resource, such as an EC2 instance ID, an IP address, or a Lambda function ARN.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.targets.por.text: The network port on which the target receives traffic; if omitted, the target group's default port is used.

aws_vpc_lattice_target_group.type.text: Determines whether the target group routes traffic to IP addresses ('IP'), Lambda functions ('LAMBDA'), or Application Load Balancers ('ALB').

aws_waf_byte_match_set.byte_match_tuples.text: Define the set of byte match conditions (e.g., the request part, target string, positional constraint, and text transformation) that determine whether a web request matches this WAF byte match set.
Specifies the part of the web request in which to search for the target string, such as a specific header, query string, URI, or body.
The name of the HTTP header to match when the field_to_match type is set to HEADER, such as 'User-Agent' or 'Referer'.
The type of the part of the web request to inspect (e.g., HEADER, METHOD, QUERY_STRING, URI, or BODY), which determines how the byte match condition is applied.
Specifies how AWS WAF searches for the target string within the text, such as EXACTLY, STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, CONTAINS, or CONTAINS_WORD.

The literal text that AWS WAF searches for in the specified part of the web request; CloudFormation automatically base64-encodes it when calling the WAF API, and non-ASCII characters should be provided via the separate base64 field.

The Base64-encoded representation of the target string that AWS WAF searches for in web requests, used instead of the plain-text target_string when the match content is binary or contains non-printable characters.
Specifies how AWS WAF transforms the request text before evaluating it against the byte match tuple, such as converting to lowercase, decoding HTML entities, or compressing white space.

aws_waf_byte_match_set.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS WAF to the byte match set, used to reference it in other resources.

aws_waf_byte_match_set.name.text: A friendly name or description that identifies the ByteMatchSet, and is required when creating the resource.

aws_waf_ipset.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to this IP set, used to reference it when associating with AWS WAF rules or updating the set.

aws_waf_ipset.ipset_descriptors.text: Defines the list of IP addresses or CIDR ranges for the IPSet, where each descriptor object specifies an IP version (IPv4 or IPv6) and a value representing the address or range.

aws_waf_ipset.ipset_descriptors.type.text: Specifies the IP address version (either IPV4 or IPV6) for the CIDR value in this IPSet descriptor.

aws_waf_ipset.ipset_descriptors.value.text: The IP address or CIDR range to include in the WAF IPSet, such as 192.0.2.0/24 or 10.0.0.1.

aws_waf_ipset.name.text: The friendly name of the IP set, which cannot be changed after the IP set is created.

aws_waf_rule.id.text: The unique identifier (RuleId) assigned by AWS WAF when the rule is created, used to reference the rule in other resources.

aws_waf_rule.metric_name.text: The name of the CloudWatch metric that AWS WAF publishes for this rule, used for monitoring and setting CloudWatch alarms.

aws_waf_rule.name.text: A friendly name for the WAF rule, which must be unique within the account and is used to identify the rule when it is created and referenced by WebACLs.

aws_waf_rule.predicates.text: Specifies the set of conditions (e.g., IP matches, string matches, SQL injection match) and whether each condition is negated, which together determine the requests that this AWS WAF Classic rule will match.

aws_waf_rule.predicates.data_id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS WAF entity (such as an IP set, byte match set, SQL injection match set, or XSS match set) that this predicate references, matching the predicate's Type.

aws_waf_rule.predicates.negated.text: Whether to invert the match result for this predicate, making the rule match when the specified WAF condition does NOT match.

aws_waf_rule.predicates.type.text: The type of the predicate in an AWS WAF rule, indicating which kind of match condition (such as IPMatch, ByteMatch, or SqlInjectionMatch) the rule uses to block or allow requests.

aws_waf_size_constraint_set.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS WAF to the size constraint set.

aws_waf_size_constraint_set.name.text: The name of the WAF size constraint set, which must be unique within your AWS account and region, and is used to identify this set in web ACL rules.

aws_waf_size_constraint_set.size_constra.text: Specifies the size constraints for the set, each defining the part of a request (FieldToMatch), the transformation to apply, comparison operator, and byte size limit that AWS WAF checks for.
Specifies how the size of a request component is compared to the target size in the size constraint (allowed values: EQ, NE, LE, LT, GE, GT).
Specifies the part of the web request to inspect for the size constraint, such as a header, query string, URI, body, or method.
When the field-to-match type is HEADER or QUERY_STRING, this specifies the header name or query string key to inspect in the web request.
Specifies the part of a web request to inspect, such as a header, the HTTP method, the query string, the URI, or the body, for the size constraint rule.
The size, in bytes, to compare against the inspected portion of a web request when evaluating this size constraint, using the constraint's comparison operator (e.g., EQ, GT).

For an AWS WAF Classic size constraint set, this field specifies the text transformation to apply to the request content before checking its size, with valid values including NONE, COMPRESS_WHITE_SPACE, HTML_ENTITY_DECODE, LOWERCASE, CMD_LINE, and URL_DECODE.

aws_waf_sql_injection_match_set.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS WAF to this SQL injection match set, used to reference the match set in other resources such as a WebACL.

aws_waf_sql_injection_match_set.name.text: Specifies a unique, immutable name for the WAF SQL injection match set, used as its friendly identifier in the AWS WAF console and API.

aws_waf_sql_injection_match_set.sql_inje.text: A list of SQL injection match tuples, each defining a FieldToMatch and TextTransformation that CloudFormation uses to identify SQL injection patterns for the WAF match set.
Specifies the part of the web request (such as a header, body, query string, or URI) that AWS WAF Classic inspects for SQL injection patterns in this SQL injection match tuple.
The name of the HTTP header to inspect when field_to_match's Type is HEADER; it is empty for other types such as METHOD, QUERY_STRING, BODY, or URI.
Specifies the type of web request component to inspect, such as HEADER, QUERY_STRING, BODY, URI, or METHOD, for the SQL injection match condition.
Specifies how the text in the web request is transformed (for example, URL_DECODE or HTML_ENTITY_DECODE) before the SQL injection pattern is checked.

aws_waf_web_acl.default_action.text: Determines the action (ALLOW or BLOCK) that AWS WAF takes for web requests that do not match any rule in this web ACL.

aws_waf_web_acl.default_action.type.text: Specifies the default action, either ALLOW or BLOCK, that AWS WAF applies to web requests that don't match any rule in this web ACL.

aws_waf_web_acl.id.text: The unique AWS-assigned ID of the web ACL, used to reference the web ACL in other resources (e.g., aws_waf_association) and in API calls.

aws_waf_web_acl.metric_name.text: The name of the Amazon CloudWatch metric used to monitor the Web ACL, which must be unique within the region and is displayed in the WAF console and CloudWatch.

aws_waf_web_acl.name.text: The user-defined name of the web ACL, used as its unique identifier within the AWS WAF service.

aws_waf_web_acl.rules.text: A list of rule overrides, each specifying a priority, AWS WAF rule identifier, and action (allow, block, or count) that together define the evaluation order and handling of matching requests.

aws_waf_web_acl.rules.action.text: Specifies the action (ALLOW, BLOCK, or COUNT) that AWS WAF takes when a request matches the associated rule in this web ACL.

aws_waf_web_acl.rules.action.type.text: Specifies how the rule handles matching web requests, with values such as ALLOW, BLOCK, or COUNT.

aws_waf_web_acl.rules.priority.text: The evaluation order for the rule, where lower numbers are evaluated first and each rule in the web ACL must have a unique priority value.

aws_waf_web_acl.rules.rule_id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS WAF rule that this web ACL action applies to within the rules list.

aws_waf_xss_match_set.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the XSS match set, used to reference the set in other WAF resources.

aws_waf_xss_match_set.name.text: A friendly name or description of the XssMatchSet, which is required and cannot be changed after creation.

aws_waf_xss_match_set.xss_match_tuples.text: Specifies the parts of the web request to inspect for cross-site scripting attacks and the text transformations to apply, where each tuple consists of a FieldToMatch and a TextTransformation.

aws_waf_xss_match_set.xss_match_tuples.f.text: Specifies the part of a web request to inspect for cross-site scripting attacks, such as the URI, query string, body, or a named header, via the type and optional data subfields.
The name of the header or query argument that AWS WAF inspects, used when the field-to-match type is HEADER or SINGLE_QUERY_ARG.
Specifies the type of web request component (such as HEADER, METHOD, QUERY_STRING, URI, or BODY) that AWS WAF inspects for cross-site scripting attacks.

aws_waf_xss_match_set.xss_match_tuples.t.text: Specifies how AWS WAF transforms the text component of the web request before inspection for XSS patterns, such as converting to lowercase, decoding HTML entities, or compressing white spaces.

aws_wafregional_byte_match_set.byte_matc.text: Specifies the list of byte match tuples that define the filter criteria (the part of a web request to inspect, the target string, and text transformation) for the AWS WAF Regional byte match set.
Specifies the part of a web request (such as a header, query string, or URI) that AWS WAF Regional inspects for the byte match tuple's search string.
Specifies the name of the HTTP header to match when field_to_match.type is 'HEADER'; for all other field types this must be an empty string.
Specifies the type of web request component (e.g., HEADER, METHOD, QUERY_STRING, URI, or BODY) that the byte match tuple inspects, as defined in the field_to_match object.

This field specifies how the target search string in the byte match tuple must align with the inspected text, using values such as EXACTLY, STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, CONTAINS, or CONTAINS_WORD, to determine whether an AWS WAF Regional rule matches a request.

Specifies the literal string (e.g., a URL or plain text) that AWS WAF Regional searches for in the web request component defined by the containing byte match tuple; for non-ASCII or binary values, you would instead use the tuple's base64-encoded target property.

The base64-encoded representation of the string that AWS WAF Regional searches for in the specified part of a web request, used when the target string cannot be specified directly due to non-printable or binary characters.
Specifies the text transformation AWS WAF applies to the request content before evaluating the byte match condition, such as converting to lowercase or decoding URL-encoded characters.

aws_wafregional_byte_match_set.id.text: The AWS-assigned unique identifier (ByteMatchSetId) for the WAF Regional byte match set.

aws_wafregional_byte_match_set.name.text: A friendly name for the byte match set, which is used as a unique identifier within the AWS WAF Regional service.

aws_wafregional_geo_match_set.geo_match_.text: Defines the list of geographical constraints (country codes) that this WAF Regional geo match set matches against, with each constraint specifying a country to include in the match set.
Specifies the type of geographic constraint, currently only supporting the value 'Country' for a WAF Regional geo match set.
The two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., 'US' for United States) that the geographic match constraint matches when the constraint's type is 'Country'.

aws_wafregional_geo_match_set.id.text: The unique identifier (ID) of the WAF Regional Geo Match Set, as assigned by AWS when the set is created.

aws_wafregional_geo_match_set.name.text: A friendly name for the geo match set, used as a unique identifier when referencing it in AWS WAF Regional.

aws_wafregional_ipset.id.text: The unique identifier (IPSetId) assigned by AWS to this WAF Regional IP set, used to reference the IP set in AWS WAF rules and other resources.

aws_wafregional_ipset.ipset_descriptors.text: Lists the IP addresses and CIDR ranges in the IPSet, where each descriptor specifies a Type (IPV4 or IPV6) and a Value in CIDR notation.

aws_wafregional_ipset.ipset_descriptors..text: Specifies the IP address type (IPV4 or IPV6) for the IP set descriptor.
The IP address or CIDR block to match, such as 192.0.2.0/24 or 2001:db8::/32.

aws_wafregional_ipset.name.text: Sets the friendly name that identifies this AWS WAF Regional IP set, used as a unique label for the set within the AWS WAF service.

aws_wafregional_rate_based_rule.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS WAF Regional to the rate-based rule, used to reference the rule in other resources.

aws_wafregional_rate_based_rule.match_pr.text: Specifies the list of predicates (such as IP match, byte match, SQL injection, or XSS match conditions) that determine which requests are counted toward the rate limit for blocking in this rate-based rule.
The ID of the AWS WAF Regional entity (such as a ByteMatchSet, IPSet, SqlInjectionMatchSet, or XssMatchSet) that this rate-based rule predicate uses to inspect web requests.

Whether the predicate's match condition is inverted, so that a True value causes the rate-based rule to match requests that do NOT satisfy the predicate's criteria (e.g., requests not from the specified IP set), while False matches requests that do satisfy them.

The type of the match predicate (e.g., IPMatch, ByteMatch, SqlInjectionMatch), which indicates the kind of pattern to match; for a rate-based rule this is typically IPMatch because the rule matches based on IP addresses.

aws_wafregional_rate_based_rule.metric_n.text: The CloudWatch metric name for the rule, which must be unique within the web ACL and is used to monitor the rate-based rule's traffic in CloudWatch.

aws_wafregional_rate_based_rule.name.text: The friendly name assigned to the AWS WAF Regional rate-based rule, required to identify the rule in the console and API.

aws_wafregional_rate_based_rule.rate_key.text: Specifies the field (always 'IP' for this resource type) that AWS WAF uses to determine the source of web requests for rate limiting, controlling how requests are counted against the rule's rate threshold.

aws_wafregional_rate_based_rule.rate_lim.text: The maximum number of requests from a single IP address in a 5-minute period that triggers the rate-based rule's action, which for AWS WAF Regional is fixed at 2000.

aws_wafregional_regex_pattern_set.id.text: The unique identifier automatically assigned to this WAF Regional regex pattern set, used to reference it in other resources such as rules and WebACLs.

aws_wafregional_regex_pattern_set.name.text: A unique, user-defined name for the regex pattern set, used to identify it in AWS WAF Regional.

aws_wafregional_regex_pattern_set.regex_.text: Specifies the regular expression patterns to include in this set, where each string is a distinct pattern that AWS WAF Regional uses to match against web requests.

aws_wafregional_rule.id.text: The unique rule ID assigned by AWS WAF Regional when the rule is created, used to reference the rule in other resources such as WebACL rules.

aws_wafregional_rule.metric_name.text: The CloudWatch metric name associated with the rule, which is required and must be unique within the region for monitoring rule-level metrics.

aws_wafregional_rule.name.text: The friendly name for the WAF Regional rule, which is required at creation and cannot be changed after creation, used to identify the rule.

aws_wafregional_rule.predicates.text: A list of predicates that define the conditions under which the rule matches requests, each specifying the match type, the data ID of the associated AWS WAF Regional object, and whether the match condition is negated.

aws_wafregional_rule.predicates.data_id.text: The unique identifier of the AWS WAF Regional resource (such as a ByteMatchSet, IPSet, or SqlInjectionMatchSet) that this predicate references for match evaluation.

aws_wafregional_rule.predicates.negated.text: Specifies whether to negate the condition defined by the referenced rule, causing the WAF rule to match when that underlying condition is false.

aws_wafregional_rule.predicates.type.text: Specifies the type of the WAF Regional rule predicate, indicating the kind of match condition being evaluated, such as IPMatch, ByteMatch, SqlInjectionMatch, XssMatch, SizeConstraint, GeoMatch, or RegexMatch.

aws_wafregional_size_constraint_set.id.text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for the WAF Regional Size Constraint Set, used to reference and manage the resource in Terraform.

aws_wafregional_size_constraint_set.name.text: A friendly name used to identify the size constraint set in AWS WAF Regional, which must be unique within the account.

aws_wafregional_size_constraint_set.size.text: Defines the size constraints that the set enforces, where each constraint specifies a part of the request (such as a header or body), a comparison operator, a size in bytes, and an optional text transformation.
Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQ, NE, LT, LE, GT, GE) used to compare the size of the request part against the configured threshold for this size constraint.
Specifies the part of a web request that the size constraint inspects, such as a header, query string, body, or URI.
The name of the HTTP header to match when the field_to_match type is HEADER; it is ignored for all other types.
Determines which part of the web request (e.g., URI, query string, header, method, or body) the size constraint applies to, as specified by the WAF FieldToMatch type.

Specifies the size (in bytes) of the web request component (such as a query string, header, or body) that AWS WAF Regional inspects, which is compared against the defined comparison operator for this size constraint.
Specifies the text transformation to apply to the web request before evaluating the size constraint, such as NONE, CMD_LINE, HTML_ENTITY_DECODE, LOWERCASE, or URL_DECODE.

aws_wafregional_sql_injection_match_set..text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for this SQL injection match set.
The required friendly name of the SQL injection match set, used to identify it within AWS WAF Regional.

Specifies a list of SQL injection match tuples, each containing a field to match (such as URI or query string) and a text transformation, that together determine which requests are flagged for SQL injection in this AWS WAF Regional match set.
Identifies the specific portion of the web request (e.g., query string, header, body, or method) that the SQL injection match tuple will inspect for malicious patterns.
The name of the HTTP header to inspect when the field_to_match type is HEADER, as used in the SQL injection match tuple.
Specifies the part of the web request to inspect for SQL injection patterns, such as HEADER, QUERY_STRING, BODY, or URI.
Specifies how the web request component (e.g., the query string or header) is transformed before WAF inspects it for SQL injection patterns, such as 'NONE', 'URL_DECODE', or 'BASE64_DECODE'.

aws_wafregional_web_acl.default_action.text: The action AWS WAF takes when a web request doesn't match any rule in the web ACL, specified as an object with a Type property that can be ALLOW, BLOCK, or COUNT.

aws_wafregional_web_acl.default_action.t.text: The action that AWS WAF takes when a request doesn't match any rule in the web ACL, either 'ALLOW' or 'BLOCK'.

aws_wafregional_web_acl.id.text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for the Web ACL, used as the resource ID.

aws_wafregional_web_acl.metric_name.text: The name of the Amazon CloudWatch metric associated with the web ACL, used for monitoring its activity in CloudWatch.

aws_wafregional_web_acl.rules.text: Defines the ordered list of rules for the web ACL, where each rule specifies the rule's ID (referencing an aws_wafregional_rule or aws_wafregional_rule_group resource) and the action (allow, block, or count) that AWS WAF Regional takes when a request matches the rule.

aws_wafregional_web_acl.rules.action.text: Determines the action (ALLOW, BLOCK, or COUNT) that AWS WAF Regional applies to a web request when the corresponding rule matches.

aws_wafregional_web_acl.rules.action.typ.text: Specifies the action that AWS WAF takes when a web request matches the conditions of the rule, such as ALLOW, BLOCK, or COUNT.

aws_wafregional_web_acl.rules.priority.text: Determines the evaluation order of the rule within the web ACL, where rules with lower priority values are evaluated first.

aws_wafregional_web_acl.rules.rule_id.text: Specifies the unique identifier of the AWS WAF Regional rule to associate with this web ACL's rule list.

aws_wafregional_web_aclassociation.resou.text: The ARN of the AWS resource (such as an Application Load Balancer or Amazon API Gateway stage) to associate with the Web ACL.

aws_wafregional_web_aclassociation.web_a.text: The unique identifier of the AWS WAF Regional Web ACL that is associated with the specified resource, such as an Application Load Balancer or Amazon API Gateway stage.

aws_wafregional_xss_match_set.id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the WAF Regional XSS match set.

aws_wafregional_xss_match_set.name.text: The friendly name or description of the XSS match set, required to create the resource in AWS WAF Regional.

aws_wafregional_xss_match_set.xss_match_.text: Specifies the parts of web requests to inspect for cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks, each tuple defining a field to match and a text transformation.
Specifies the part of a web request (such as a header, query string, or body) that AWS WAF Regional inspects for cross-site scripting attack patterns.
The value of the `field_to_match` that defines the specific part of the web request to match, such as the header name when `type` is `HEADER`; it is empty for types like `URI` or `QUERY_STRING`.
Specifies the part of the web request (for example, QUERY_STRING, URI, or BODY) that AWS WAF Regional inspects for cross-site scripting (XSS) attack patterns.
Specifies how the text in the web request component is transformed (e.g., URL_DECODE, LOWERCASE) before the XSS match rule is evaluated.

aws_wafv2_ipset.tags.text: A list of key-value tags to associate with the WAFv2 IP set, used for resource identification, organization, and access management.

aws_wafv2_ipset.tags.key.text: The key of a tag attached to the WAFv2 IP set, used to identify and organize the resource within AWS.

aws_wafv2_ipset.tags.value.text: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the AWS WAFv2 IP set resource.

aws_wafv2_logging_configuration.logging_.text: Specifies whether to keep or drop logs for matching requests, with valid values `KEEP` or `DROP`.

A list of conditions for this logging filter, where each condition pairs a KEEP/DROP action with a label name to match, determining whether matching web requests are included in or excluded from the WAF logs.
Specifies the web request action (e.g., ALLOW, BLOCK, COUNT) that must match for the logging filter condition to apply, allowing log filtering based on the action taken by AWS WAF.
Specifies the WAF action (ALLOW, BLOCK, or COUNT) that must match the action taken by AWS WAF on a request, as part of an action condition in a logging filter.
Defines a condition that matches when a web request carries a label with the exact name specified, allowing the WAFv2 logging filter to include or exclude requests from logging based on that label.
The name of the AWS WAF label that a web request must have for the logging filter condition to match, thereby including or excluding that request's logs.
Determines whether the filter's conditions must all match (MEETS_ALL) or any one must match (MEETS_ANY) for the filter to apply.

aws_wafv2_logging_configuration.redacted.text: Redact the HTTP method (e.g., GET, POST) from the logs for web requests matching the logging configuration.
This field specifies whether to redact the query string of web requests from the logs produced by the WAFv2 logging configuration.
Specifies the name of a single request header whose value WAF will redact in the logging configuration.
The name of the HTTP header whose values are redacted (masked) from the logs delivered by this WAFv2 logging configuration.
