The immunity time in seconds assigned to a successful CAPTCHA token, controlling how long the client can bypass the CAPTCHA challenge for this rule's requests.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.challenge_config.text: Configures challenge action settings, including the immunity time (in seconds) that a successfully challenged client's token remains valid in the web ACL rule.
Specifies the duration (in seconds) that a client that successfully passes a challenge is granted immunity from subsequent challenges, controlling how long the challenge response remains valid.
Specifies the number of seconds an issued challenge token remains valid, during which a client that passed the challenge is not challenged again by this rule.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.name.text: The friendly name of the rule, which must be unique within the web ACL.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.override_action.text: Specifies the override action for a rule that is part of a rule group, which can be set to Count to only count matching requests or None to retain the rule group's original action, and is valid only for rule group rules.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.override_action..text: When configured (as an empty block), this sets the override action for the referenced rule group to Count, so that all rules in the group are evaluated but only counted, bypassing their original actions.
Specifies that the rule's action is not overridden, so the rule uses its original action as defined in the rule group.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.priority.text: The integer priority that determines the evaluation order of this rule among all rules in the web ACL, with lower values evaluated first, and each rule requiring a unique priority.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.rule_labels.text: The rule_labels blocks define custom labels to attach to matching web requests for this rule, allowing later rules in the same web ACL to reference these labels via label match statements.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.rule_labels.name.text: The name of the label that is attached to matching web requests, which can be referenced by other rules or in logging.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.text: Specifies the matching logic for a rule in the AWS WAFv2 web ACL, defining which web requests (based on attributes such as IP addresses, geographic region, or request content) the rule evaluates to determine whether to apply its action like allow, block, or count.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.and_st.text: Represents an AND rule statement that requires all nested statements inside its Statements list to match for the rule to match.
The list of sub-statements that are logically combined with AND, so all must match for the rule's statement to evaluate to true.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.asn_ma.text: Defines an ASN match statement, which matches requests based on the Autonomous System Number (ASN) of the client IP address by comparing it against a specified list of ASNs.

Specifies the list of autonomous system numbers (ASNs) that the client's address must match for the ASN match statement to trigger, with a match occurring if the request's ASN is present in this list.
Specifies how AWS WAF inspects the forwarded client IP address from an HTTP header for an ASN match statement, including the header name and fallback behavior when the header is absent.
Determines whether the ASN match statement matches (MATCH) or does not match (NO_MATCH) a request when the IP address in the specified forwarded header is missing or invalid.
The name of the HTTP header that holds the client IP address to use for ASN matching when traffic is forwarded through a proxy (e.g., X-Forwarded-For).

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.byte_m.text: Configures a byte match rule statement that matches a specific string or binary pattern in a selected component of the web request (e.g., header, query string, body) using a defined positional constraint and optional text transformations.
Specifies the web request component (such as a header, query string, URI path, body, or HTTP method) that the byte match statement inspects for matching strings.
Configures the byte match statement to inspect the entire query string of the web request, thereby matching against all query arguments.
This object configures matching on the raw request body for the byte match statement, optionally specifying oversize handling behavior.
Specifies how AWS WAF treats a request body that exceeds its inspection size limit, with CONTINUE to process normally, MATCH to count as a match, or NO_MATCH to count as no match.
Specifies the cookie match settings for the byte match statement, including the cookie filter pattern, match scope (key or value), and oversize handling behavior.

Specifies the CookieMatchPattern that determines which cookies in the request to inspect for the byte match condition, supporting all cookies, a specified list of included cookies, or all cookies except a list of excluded cookies.
When this configuration block is present, it instructs AWS WAF to inspect all cookies in the request, as opposed to only included or excluded cookies.
In a byte match statement inspecting cookies, specifies the list of cookie names to exclude from inspection, so that the statement only examines cookies not listed here.
Specifies the list of cookie names to include in the cookie match pattern, so AWS WAF inspects only those cookies in the request's cookie header when evaluating the byte match statement.

Inspects the cookie values in a web ACL rule, with match_scope determining whether WAF checks the entire cookie, only the cookie name, or only the cookie value (ALL, KEY, or VALUE) when inspecting cookies for a byte match statement.

Specifies how AWS WAF handles oversized cookies in the request when inspecting cookie fields, with allowed values CONTINUE (continue inspecting without the oversized cookie), MATCH (treat the request as matching the rule), or NO_MATCH (treat the request as not matching).

Specifies the order in which header names are considered when inspecting HTTP headers for the byte match statement, ensuring consistent evaluation even when headers appear multiple times in the request.
Controls the action that AWS WAF takes when the size of the header order exceeds the oversize limit for the byte match statement's field-to-match, allowing CONTINUE, MATCH, or NO_MATCH.
Configures the inspection of HTTP request headers for the byte match, specifying the header name and match pattern to match against.

In an AWS WAFv2 web ACL rule, this object defines the set of request headers that the byte match statement will inspect, supporting options for all headers, a specific list of included headers, or a list of excluded headers.
When this object is present, the match pattern matches all header names in the web request.
The list of HTTP header names to exclude from inspection when the byte match statement's header match pattern is set to exclude those headers, meaning all other headers are examined.
Specifies the names of the headers to include when inspecting request headers in the byte match statement, so only the listed headers are considered for the match pattern.
Specifies whether the byte match rule inspects the entire header, the header name (key), or only the header value when evaluating header fields in a web request.
Specifies how AWS WAF handles oversized header keys or values when inspecting request headers for this byte match statement, with valid values of CONTINUE, MATCH, or NO_MATCH.

Specifies that the WAFv2 rule inspects the JA3 fingerprint of the TLS client as the request part to match, with a configurable fallback behavior (match or no_match) for when the fingerprint is unavailable.
Specifies how AWS WAF should treat a request when it cannot detect a JA3 TLS fingerprint for the connection, causing the byte match statement to match (MATCH) or not match (NO_MATCH).
Indicates that the JA4 fingerprint of the client's TLS connection is the field to match in the byte match statement.
Controls how AWS WAF evaluates the rule when a request does not include a JA4 TLS fingerprint, setting whether such requests are treated as matching or not matching (values: MATCH or NO_MATCH).
Specifies the JSON body of a web request as the location to inspect, allowing the rule to match on the structure and values of the parsed JSON payload.
Specifies whether to treat a request as matching or not matching the rule when the request body is not valid JSON, with allowed values 'MATCH' and 'NO_MATCH'.
Determines which parts of the request's JSON body are inspected by defining either all JSON content or a set of included/excluded JSON paths for the byte match statement.
When present, this property declares that the match pattern applies to all JSON paths within the request body, rather than only to the paths listed in 'IncludedPaths'.
Specifies the list of JSON paths (e.g., '/foo/bar') within the request body that are inspected for the byte match condition; only values at these paths are matched.
Specifies whether AWS WAF inspects the entire JSON request body, only its keys, or only its values when evaluating byte match conditions.
Determines how AWS WAF handles a JSON request body that exceeds the size limit, either continuing without matching, or treating it as a match or non-match.
Specifies that the byte match statement inspects the HTTP request method (such as GET or POST) for matching.
Specifies that the byte match statement inspects the raw query string of the web request, excluding the leading '?', as the field to match.
Defines a single HTTP header to inspect by its name, so the byte match statement evaluates the header's value against its search string.
The name of the HTTP header to inspect, such as 'User-Agent' or 'Referer', that the byte match statement checks against.
Specifies that the match condition inspects a single query string argument by its exact name, allowing you to target a specific query parameter.
The name of the single query argument (e.g., 'foo' in '?foo=bar') whose value is inspected as the field to match in a byte-match statement.
Specifies that the rule inspects the URI fragment (the part of the web request URI that appears after the '#' character) for byte match conditions.
Controls whether requests that lack a URI fragment are treated as a match (MATCH) or no match (NO_MATCH) for this byte match statement.
Specifies that the byte match statement should inspect the URI path of the web request (e.g., the /products/shoes portion, not including the query string).
Defines how AWS WAF searches for the specified match string within the web request component, accepting values like EXACTLY, STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, CONTAINS, or CONTAINS_WORD.
Determines the order in which this text transformation is applied relative to other pre-parse text transformations, with lower values executed first.
Specifies the type of text transformation (e.g., LOWERCASE, HTML_ENTITY_DECODE, COMPRESS_WHITE_SPACE) applied to the web request content before the byte match statement evaluates it.
Specifies the literal string (or base64-encoded byte sequence) that AWS WAF searches for in the request component inspected by this rule's byte match statement.
The base64-encoded string that the byte match statement searches for in the web request, used as an alternative to the plaintext search string.

Specifies the ordered list of text transformations (e.g., LOWERCASE, HTML_ENTITY_DECODE, COMPRESS_WHITE_SPACE) that are applied by priority to the inspected request component before the byte match statement compares it against the search string.
The priority integer defines the order in which this text transformation is applied relative to other text transformations in the same rule, with lower values applied first.
Specifies the type of text transformation to apply to the inspected value before byte matching, such as NONE, LOWERCASE, or HTML_ENTITY_DECODE.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.geo_ma.text: Specifies a geographic match statement that filters requests by the country of the origin IP address, using an array of two-letter country codes.
Specifies the two-character country codes (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) that the geo match statement uses to match requests originating from those countries.
Specifies how to inspect the IP address in a forwarded header for geo matching, including the header name and the fallback behavior when the header is absent or invalid.
Determines whether the geo match action matches or does not match when the client IP address is not found in the forwarded IP header, where 'MATCH' returns a match and 'NO_MATCH' returns no match.
The name of the HTTP header (e.g., X-Forwarded-For) from which the geo match statement reads the client IP address when forwarded_ipconfig is configured.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.ipset_.text: Defines a rule statement that matches web requests against the IP addresses contained in a referenced AWS WAF IP set, triggering when the request's source IP falls within the set's CIDR ranges.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS WAFv2 IP set that this rule statement references to match traffic based on its IP addresses.

Defines how to derive the client IP from a forwarded header (such as X-Forwarded-For) for inspection against the referenced IP set, including the header name, fallback behavior, and the position (e.g., FIRST, LAST, or ANY) to select.
Determines whether a request that lacks a valid forwarded IP header should match the IP set (MATCH) or not match (NO_MATCH).
The name of the HTTP header from which AWS WAF extracts the client IP address when using the forwarded IP configuration for an IP set reference statement.
Specifies whether AWS WAF should use the first IP address (FIRST) or the last IP address (LAST) from the X-Forwarded-For header when evaluating the IP set reference statement.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.label_.text: Configures a label match statement that checks whether the request carries a specific label (or label in a namespace) set by a previous rule, enabling rule chaining based on prior label matches.
The string label name or label namespace prefix that the label match statement checks for, used to match labels added to web requests by other rules.
Determines whether the label match key is interpreted as an exact label (`LABEL`) or as a namespace prefix (`NAMESPACE`) to match against labels applied to the web request or rule.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.manage.text: Defines a rule statement that uses a preconfigured managed rule group from a vendor (e.g., AWS or AWS Marketplace), specifying the group by name and optionally excluding rules from that group.
Specifies the rules within the managed rule group that you want to exclude from being evaluated for web requests, using a list of objects each containing the rule name to exclude.
The name of a rule within the AWS Managed Rules rule group to exclude from the web ACL's evaluation.

Specifies additional configuration for the managed rule group, such as the login path and password/username field indicators, which AWS Managed Rules for Bot Control or Account Takeover Prevention use to inspect request payloads.

Configures the AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet for the managed rule group, defining the account creation request paths and field identifiers (such as email, phone, and login paths) that AWS WAF inspects to detect and block fraud.
The URI path of the account creation endpoint (for example, /signup) that the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set inspects to detect account creation fraud.

Controls whether the path values (such as the login or sign-up path) in the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set are evaluated as regular expressions rather than literal strings when inspecting request paths.
Specifies the JSON path in the request body that identifies the registration page for the AWS Managed Rules account creation fraud prevention (ACFP) rule set to extract and use in its analysis.

Defines the request inspection configuration, including the payload type and the location of username, password, phone number, and email fields in the web request, for the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set.

Specifies the identifiers of the address fields in the incoming request that AWS WAF extracts and inspects for the AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet, enabling account creation fraud prevention to evaluate the customer's address data.
The name of the request component (such as a JSON body field or form field) that contains the address value, used by the AWS WAF ACFP managed rule set to inspect address-type fields.
Specifies the request component (such as a header or query parameter) from which the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set extracts the email address for account creation fraud prevention.

Specifies the name of the form field or JSON key in the web request that holds the email address, used by the AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet request inspection to parse the email for account creation fraud prevention.

Specifies the request field identifier that contains the password for the AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet, enabling WAF to locate and inspect the password value in the request payload during account creation fraud prevention.

The name of the password field in the request payload, such as the JSON key or form field name, that the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set uses to identify and inspect the password for account creation fraud prevention.
Specifies whether the AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet request inspection inspects the request payload as JSON or as form-encoded data (allowed values: JSON, FORM).

Specifies the request fields (such as JSON body fields, headers, or query strings) that contain the phone number, which the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set inspects to identify phone numbers in incoming requests for account creation fraud prevention.

Specifies the JSONPath expression that identifies the phone number field in the inspected web request, used by the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set to extract the phone number for account creation fraud prevention.
Identifies the request component (such as a JSON body field or header) that contains the username, which the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set uses to inspect account creation requests for fraud.
Specifies the name or JSON path of the request field that contains the username for AWS Managed Rules ACFP (Account Creation Fraud Prevention) inspection.

Configures how the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set inspects the HTTP response from the protected resource to identify successful account creation or login attempts, using criteria like status codes, headers, or body content.

Defines the response body inspection for the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set, specifying the success and failure strings that the WAF service looks for in the response body to determine whether an account creation attempt succeeded or failed.
Specifies the list of strings that must appear in the response body for the login attempt to be considered a failure, used by the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set's response inspection.

Specifies the strings that the AWS WAF account creation fraud prevention (ACFP) managed rule group searches for in the response body, so that the response is considered successful if any of these strings are present.

Configures AWS WAF to inspect the HTTP header in the response from the protected application, using the specified header name and success values, to determine whether the account creation fraud prevention rule set should treat the request as successful.
Specifies the list of string values that, when found in the configured response header, are treated as a failure signal by the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set, causing the request to be blocked.

Specifies the name of the HTTP response header that AWS WAF inspects for the token value used in the AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet's response inspection for the account creation fraud prevention rule group.

In the response inspection configuration for the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set, the success_values under the header inspector defines the list of header values that, when present in the specified response header, cause the account creation attempt to be classified as successful.

Specifies the JSON response body field (identifier) that AWS WAF inspects within the response from an account creation attempt to determine whether it succeeded, for the AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet managed rule group.
A list of string values that, when present in the JSON response body, indicate a failed authentication or account-creation request, causing the AWS managed rule group to apply its configured action.
The name of the JSON field in the response body that AWS WAF checks for the account creation success or failure value, as configured in the ACFP rule set's response inspection.

A list of string values that, when found in the JSON response body, indicate a successful account creation attempt, allowing the AWS Managed Rules ACFP rule set to override its default success/failure evaluation.

Specifies the expected HTTP status codes in the response that indicate a successful or failed token challenge for the AWS Managed Rules Account Creation Fraud Prevention rule set, used to determine whether to allow or block the request.

Specifies a list of HTTP status codes (e.g., 403) that the AWS WAFv2 AWSManagedRulesACFPRuleSet treats as failure indicators when inspecting the origin response status code to classify a request as bot traffic.

Defines the list of HTTP status codes that the AWS WAF managed rule group for account creation fraud prevention (ACFP) treats as successful when inspecting the response status code, as part of its response inspection configuration.

Specifies the configuration for the AWS Managed Rules Anti-DDoS rule set (AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet), an empty object that enables the AWS WAF managed DDoS protection rules when associated with a managed rule group statement.
Specifies the client-side action (such as Challenge or CAPTCHA) and the list of custom token domains that AWS WAF uses to verify client requests for the AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet.

The `challenge` object configures the challenge action for the client-side action of the AWS Managed Rules anti-DDoS rule set, determining that AWS WAF presents a CAPTCHA-style challenge instead of blocking when the rule set flags a request.
Specifies a list of regular expression patterns for URI paths that are exempt from the challenge action in the client-side action configuration of the AWS Managed Rules Anti-DDoS rule set.
The regular expression pattern that matches request URIs to exempt from the client-side challenge action in the AWS WAFv2 anti-DDoS managed rule group configuration.
Specifies the sensitivity level (LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH) for the challenge action in the AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet managed rule group, controlling how aggressively clients are challenged.

Specifies whether the challenge action is used as a count action (observing traffic without blocking) or a block action (applying the challenge) for the AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet managed rule group.
Sets the sensitivity threshold for the AWS Managed Rules Anti-DDoS rule set, controlling how aggressively it identifies and blocks potential DDoS traffic (accepting values such as HIGH and LOW).
Configures the AWS Managed Rules ATP (Account Takeover Protection) rule set's settings, such as the login request path and the password field, to detect account takeover attempts.
When set to true, the ATP rule set interprets the login path as a regular expression pattern instead of a literal string.
The URI path of the application's login endpoint (e.g., /login) that AWS Managed Rules for Account Takeover Protection (ATP) inspects for anomalous login activity.

Configures how AWS WAFv2 inspects incoming requests for account takeover attempts, specifying the login path and the location of username and password fields in the request, for the AWS Managed Rules Account Takeover Protection rule set.
Specifies the password field in the request body that the AWS Managed Rules ATP rule set inspects for account takeover attempts, using its Identifier sub-field.

The identifier for the password field, specifying the name of the field in the request payload (for example, a JSON key or form field name) that AWS WAF uses to locate the password when evaluating requests against the AWS Managed Rules ATP rule set.
Specifies the format of the request body payload that AWS WAF inspects for the AWSManagedRulesATPRuleSet, either JSON or form data.
Specifies the location (such as a JSON body field or form field) in the web request from which the AWS Managed Rules ATP rule set extracts the username for account takeover protection.
The name of the request field (e.g., form parameter or JSON property) that contains the username, used by AWS Managed Rules for account takeover prevention to identify the user in the request.
Configures how AWS WAF inspects the login response to determine whether a login attempt succeeded for the AWS account takeover prevention (ATP) managed rule group.

Specifies the response body inspection settings for the AWS Managed Rules ATP rule set, which checks the response body for defined success and failure strings to determine whether an account takeover attempt was successful.
The list of strings that, when present in the response body, indicate a failed authentication attempt for the AWS WAFv2 Account Takeover Protection managed rule group's response inspection.

Lists the strings that, when found in the response body of a login request, cause the AWS Managed Rules ATP rule set to classify the attempt as successful as part of the response inspection body_contains configuration.
This field specifies the response header to inspect for the AWS Managed Rules ATP rule set, along with the header values that map to successful and failed login attempts.
Specifies the response header values that indicate a failed login attempt, used by the AWS Managed Rules ATP rule set's response inspection to trigger the rule.
The name of the HTTP header in the response that AWS WAF inspects for the account takeover prevention managed rule group's response inspection.

In the AWS WAFv2 AWSManagedRulesATPRuleSet response inspection configuration, these success values are the strings that, when found in the specified response header, cause the rule to treat the login attempt as successful for account takeover protection monitoring.

Configures the JSON body inspection used by the AwsManagedRulesATPRuleSet to identify login success or failure markers by specifying a JSON identifier (such as a JSONPath expression) in the protected resource's response body.

Defines a list of string values which, when found in the specified JSON path of the login response, indicate a failed authentication attempt for the AWS Managed Rules ATP rule set's response inspection.
Specifies the JSON field name within the response body that the AWS WAF account takeover prevention (ATP) managed rule group inspects to identify a successful or failed login attempt.
Specifies the string values in the JSON response body that the AWS Managed Rules ATP rule set treats as indicating a successful authentication attempt.
This object configures the status-code-based response inspection for the AWS Managed Rules ATP rule set, allowing you to define which HTTP status codes indicate success or failure of the request.
Specifies the HTTP status codes in the response that indicate a failed login attempt, used by AWS WAF to inspect responses for the account takeover prevention (ATP) managed rule group.

Specifies the HTTP status codes (such as 200) that the AWS Managed Rules ATP rule set's status code response inspection treats as successful login responses, used to identify and block account takeover attempts.

Configures the AWS Managed Rules Bot Control rule set within the managed rule group, enabling you to set its inspection level (Common or Targeted) and optionally enable machine learning for bot detection.
When set to true, enables machine learning for the AWS Managed Rules Bot Control rule set, allowing AWS WAF to use ML models to improve the accuracy of bot detection and classification.
Sets the inspection level for the AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet, either COMMON or TARGETED, to control the depth of bot detection rules applied.
The URL path of the application's login endpoint, used by the managed rule group (e.g., AWS WAF Bot Control) to identify login attempts for token management and rate-based rules.
Specifies the name of the form field in the request body that contains the password, used by the AWS Managed Rules ATP rule set for account takeover protection analysis.
The name of the request field (such as a form field name) that contains the password, used by the AWS WAF account takeover prevention managed rule group to locate the password for inspection.

Specifies whether the request body payload inspected by the managed rule group is JSON or form-encoded (FORM_ENCODED), enabling AWS WAF to parse the data for the account takeover prevention or account creation fraud prevention rule sets.

Specifies the request field (by its name/identifier) that contains the account username, used by AWS-managed rule groups for account takeover prevention (ATP) and account creation fraud prevention (ACFP) to inspect login or sign-up attempts.

Identifies the name of the form field (e.g., 'username') in the login web request body that contains the user's login identifier, used by AWS WAF managed rule groups such as the Account Takeover Protection (ATP) rule set to inspect login attempts.
The name of the AWS managed rule group to use in this statement, such as AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet or AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet.

Overrides the action for specific managed rules inside the managed rule group by mapping each managed rule's name to a new action (such as Allow, Block, Count, Captcha, or Challenge) that replaces the rule group's default behavior.

Specifies the action (Allow, Block, Count, Captcha, or Challenge) to apply to a specific rule in a managed rule group, overriding that rule's default action within the rule_action_overrides configuration.

The 'allow' action in a rule action override changes the action of the specified managed rule to allow the matched web request, so it is not blocked or subjected to challenge/captcha and processing continues with subsequent rules or the resource's default action.
Defines custom request handling, such as inserting additional headers, for requests that are allowed by this rule action override in the managed rule group statement.
A list of HTTP headers to insert into the forwarded web request when the rule action is overridden to Allow and custom request handling is enabled.
The name of the HTTP header to insert into the web request when the override action is set to Allow.
The value of the HTTP header that AWS WAF inserts into the request when the associated managed rule group action override uses an 'allow' action with custom request handling.
Defines the block action to apply when overriding the action of a specific rule in the managed rule group, causing matching requests to be blocked.
Specifies a custom HTTP response (status code and optional custom body) that AWS WAF returns instead of the default 403 when the block action is taken for this managed rule group override.
The key that identifies the custom response body to use for the block action's custom response, matching the keys defined in the WebACL's CustomResponseBodies map.
The HTTP status code (e.g., 403) that AWS WAF returns to the client when the managed rule's action is overridden to block the request with this custom response.
Specifies custom HTTP headers to include in the block response when a managed rule group rule is overridden to block, as part of the custom response configuration for the block action.
The name of a custom HTTP response header that AWS WAF includes in the blocked response when this action override applies, such as 'X-Custom-Header'.
Specifies the value for a custom HTTP response header that AWS WAF includes in the response when the overridden managed rule action is set to block with a custom response.
When overriding the action of a rule in a managed rule group, this defines the CAPTCHA action, which challenges the request with a CAPTCHA puzzle to verify human users.
Defines the custom request handling to apply when the CAPTCHA action is taken, allowing you to insert custom headers or cookies into the request that is sent to the protected resource.
Specifies the headers to insert into the web request when the managed rule group rule's action is overridden to CAPTCHA and custom request handling is configured.
The name of the HTTP header to insert into the request when custom request handling is applied to the CAPTCHA action override in a managed rule group statement.
The value to assign to an inserted HTTP header when a managed rule group rule override uses the CAPTCHA action with custom request handling.
Specifies that the rule's action is overridden to Challenge, which requires the client to complete an AWS WAF CAPTCHA-style challenge before the request is allowed to proceed.
Specifies the custom request handling configuration for the Challenge action, allowing custom headers to be inserted into the request that AWS WAF forwards after the challenge succeeds.

Defines the list of custom headers to add to the request that AWS WAF forwards to the protected resource after a successful Challenge action, enabling you to pass session or context information to the application.
The name of the HTTP header to insert into the request when this rule action override is applied.
Specifies the value of a custom header to insert into requests that match the rule when the challenge action is used as an override in the managed rule group rule action override.
Overrides the referenced managed rule's action so that matching requests are only counted (recorded in WAF metrics) rather than allowed or blocked.
Defines custom request handling, such as inserting additional HTTP headers, to apply to matching requests when this managed rule group rule's action is overridden to Count.
Defines the list of custom HTTP header name/value pairs to insert into the web request when the rule action override is set to Count with custom request handling for a managed rule group statement.
The name of the custom header to insert into the request when the managed rule group rule's action is overridden to Count with custom request handling.
The value of the custom header that AWS WAF inserts into the request when a rule in the managed rule group is overridden to Count and custom request handling is enabled.
Determines the price multiplier that AWS WAF applies to the base monetization price when the rule's action is overridden to Monetize, controlling the amount charged for matched requests.
The name of the specific rule inside the referenced AWS Managed Rules group whose action is being overridden by the paired action_to_use value.
A nested statement that limits the managed rule group to inspect only requests that match this scope-down condition, so the group's rules run only when this additional statement is satisfied.
The name of the vendor that provides the managed rule group, such as 'AWS' for AWS managed rule groups or partner vendors like 'Fortinet' or 'Imperva'.
Specifies the version of the managed rule group to use; when omitted, AWS WAF uses the vendor's default version.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.not_st.text: Negates the nested statement, matching web requests that do not match the enclosed statement.
The WAFv2 statement that is logically negated by the enclosing not_statement, allowing the rule to match when the nested statement evaluates to false.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.or_sta.text: An OR statement that matches a request if any of the nested statements match, allowing you to combine multiple match criteria in a single rule.
A list of nested WAFv2 statements that are combined with OR logic, meaning the OR statement matches if any one of these sub-statements matches the web request.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.rate_b.text: Configures the rule as a rate-based statement, which counts matching requests from a given source (such as an IP address or custom key) over a specified time window and triggers the rule's action when the count exceeds the configured limit.

Specifies how to aggregate requests for rate limiting in the WAFv2 rate-based rule, with valid values including IP (default), FORWARDED_IP (using the forwarded IP address from a header), or CUSTOM_KEYS (using custom key components like labels or headers).

Defines the request characteristics (such as header, cookie, query argument, label, or IP) used to aggregate requests for rate limiting, so the rule counts and limits requests grouped by distinct values for those keys instead of just the client IP.

This field defines a custom key for the rate-based statement that uses the client's ASN (Autonomous System Number) to aggregate requests, so all requests from networks managed by the same ASN count together toward the rate limit.
Specifies the cookie to use as a custom request aggregation key for a rate-based rule, including its name and text transformations.
The name of the cookie whose value will be used as the custom key for aggregating requests in the rate-based rule's custom key configuration.

This list specifies the ordered text transformations (each with a priority and type, e.g., LOWERCASE, URL_DECODE) that are applied to the cookie value before it is used as a key for rate-based rule aggregation, enabling normalized matching for rate limits.
Defines the processing order for this text transformation on the cookie value, where a lower number means the transformation is applied earlier in the sequence.
Specifies the type of text transformation to apply to the cookie value (e.g., LOWERCASE, HTML_ENTITY_DECODE) in a custom key for the rate-based statement of the web ACL.

Configures the forwarded IP custom key for the rate-based statement, which uses the client IP from a specified header (such as X-Forwarded-For) as the aggregation key for rate limiting and requires a `header_name` argument.

Configures a request header as a custom key for the rate-based statement, so AWS WAF can aggregate and rate-limit requests based on the value of that header after applying any specified text transformations.
The name of the request header used as a custom key for aggregating and rate-limiting requests in this rate-based rule.

Specifies the text transformations to apply to the header value used as a custom key in a rate-based rule (e.g., lowercase, URL decode, or command-line processing) before that value is used to aggregate and rate-limit requests.
Specifies the order in which this text transformation is applied to the header value, with lower numbers executed first and each priority unique among transformations in the same custom key.
Specifies the text transformation type (such as NONE, LOWERCASE, or URL_DECODE) applied to the header value used as a custom key for the rate-based rule's rate limiting aggregation.
Defines the HTTP method (e.g., GET, POST) as a custom key in a rate-based statement, so that requests with the same method are grouped together when counting requests for rate limiting.
Specifies that the originating IP address of the web request is used as a custom key for aggregating requests in the rate-based rule.
Configures the client's JA3 TLS fingerprint as a custom key for the rate-based rule's request aggregation, containing the fallback behavior to apply when the fingerprint is unavailable.

Determines how AWS WAFv2 constructs the rate-based rule aggregation key for requests that lack a JA3 fingerprint (e.g., non-TLS traffic), using the client IP address when set to 'ORIGIN' or a constant placeholder when set to 'AWS_WAF'.
Sets the JA4 fingerprint as a custom key for the rate-based statement, making AWS WAF aggregate requests by the client's JA4 TLS fingerprint when rate limiting.

Determines how AWS WAF handles requests that lack a JA4 TLS fingerprint when this custom key is used in a rate-based rule's custom key aggregation, with allowed values such as MATCH or NO_MATCH to either include such requests in the rate count or exclude them.
Specifies the label namespace used as a custom key in a rate-based rule, so requests with labels from that namespace are grouped together for rate limiting decisions.

Specifies the label namespace used to aggregate requests for a rate-based rule when using a label_namespace custom key, such that all requests carrying a label that begins with this namespace count toward the rate limit.
Defines the query argument (query parameter) whose value AWS WAF uses as a custom key for aggregating requests in a rate-based rule statement.
The name of the query argument that AWS WAF uses as the custom key to aggregate requests for the rate-based rule.
Specifies the text transformations to apply to the query argument value before it is used as a custom key for rate limiting, such as lowercasing, URL decoding, or HTML entity decoding.
Specifies the order in which this text transformation is applied relative to other transformations in the same list, with lower numbers processed first (starting at 0).
Specifies the text transformation type (e.g., NONE, LOWERCASE, URL_DECODE) to apply to the query argument value before rate-based evaluation.
This object configures the request's query string as a custom key for rate-based aggregation, with an optional list of text transformations to preprocess the query string before it is counted.

Defines the list of text transformations (each with a priority and transformation type) that are applied to the query string value when it is used as a custom key in the rate-based statement's aggregation.

Specifies the execution order for this text transformation applied to the query string, with lower-numbered priorities running first, determining how the query string is processed before rate-limit aggregation.
Specifies the text transformation type (e.g., NONE, LOWERCASE, URL_DECODE) applied to the query string value used as a custom key in the rate-based statement.
Configures the request's URI path as a custom key for the rate-based rule, with optional text transformations applied to the path before counting.
Specifies the text transformations to apply to the URI path value of the custom key before it is used in the rate-based rule's rate limiting aggregation.
Defines the execution order for the text transformations applied to the URI path custom key in a rate-based rule, with lower priority numbers processed first.

Specifies the type of text transformation to apply to the URI path value being used as a custom key in the rate-based rule, such as LOWERCASE, URL_DECODE, or HTML_ENTITY_DECODE, to normalize the path before the rate aggregation.
The evaluation window (in seconds) used to calculate the request rate for the rate-based rule, with allowed values of 60, 120, 300, 600, 1200, or 1800.

Defines the HTTP header (such as X-Forwarded-For) and fallback behavior used to extract the originating client IP address for rate-based rule evaluation when the request origin IP is masked by a proxy or load balancer.

Specifies how AWS WAF handles requests when it cannot determine the originating IP address from the configured forwarded IP header, setting the action to either match the request (MATCH) or treat it as not matching (NO_MATCH).
The name of the HTTP header to use as the source IP address for rate-based rule evaluation when requests are forwarded through a proxy or load balancer.
The maximum number of requests permitted within a rate-based rule's evaluation window (default 5 minutes) before the rule's action is triggered.
Narrows the rate-based rule's rate limiting to only those web requests that match this nested statement, so requests that do not match are excluded from the rate count.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.regex_.text: Defines a rule statement that matches a request component against a specified regular expression pattern, including the pattern string, the component to inspect (such as a header, query string, or body), and any text transformations to apply before evaluation.
Specifies the part of the web request (such as a header, query string, body, or URI path) that the regular expression pattern is matched against.
Inspect all query arguments of the web request.
This object configures the request body as the part of the web request the regex pattern inspects, and optionally specifies how WAF handles requests whose body exceeds the configured size limit.
Specifies how AWS WAF handles the request body when its size exceeds the inspection limit for regex matching, with allowed values CONTINUE, MATCH, or NO_MATCH.

Specifies the cookies in the web request to inspect against the regex pattern, with options to select all cookies or a subset by name and to match the entire cookie, its key, or its value, along with handling for oversized cookie content.
Defines which cookies in the request are inspected by the regex match statement, either all cookies or a set of cookie names to include or exclude.
Indicates that the regex match should inspect all cookies in the request, rather than a specified subset.
Defines the list of cookie names to exclude from the regex pattern inspection, meaning the rule's regex applies only to cookies not listed in this field.
Specifies the list of cookie names to include in the match pattern for the cookie field to match, so that the regex statement is evaluated only against the cookies whose names appear in this list.
Specifies whether to match all cookies, the cookie name, or the cookie value when inspecting a request's cookies in an AWS WAF v2 rule.
Specifies how AWS WAF handles requests when cookie inspection exceeds the size limits, with possible values CONTINUE, MATCH, or NO_MATCH.
Controls how AWS WAF handles a request when the header order (the full header section) exceeds the size limit WAF can inspect, with valid values CONTINUE, MATCH, and NO_MATCH.
Configures inspection of HTTP request headers for the regex match, defining which headers to check and whether the regex is applied to the header name or its value.
Defines which header names the regex match statement inspects, either by listing included headers, excluded headers, or matching all headers in the web request.
When set to true, this field makes the header match pattern match all headers, so the regex is applied to every header in the request.
The list of header names to exclude from the set of headers to inspect when applying the regex pattern in this regex match statement.
Specifies the names of the headers to include in the header match pattern, so the regex pattern is applied only to the listed headers.

Determines whether the regex pattern is matched against all of the selected header content (ALL), only the header names (KEY), or only the header values (VALUE), for the header matching configuration of a regex match statement in an AWS WAFv2 web ACL.
Determines how AWS WAF handles oversized header values when inspecting headers in the regex match statement, accepting values like CONTINUE, MATCH, or NO_MATCH.
This field specifies the JA3 TLS fingerprint of the client connection to inspect and match against the regex pattern, enabling the rule to filter traffic based on the client's TLS fingerprint.

Determines whether a request should be treated as matching or not matching the regex pattern when the JA3 fingerprint is unavailable for the request (e.g., non-TLS traffic), with valid values being 'MATCH' or 'NO_MATCH'.
Specifies the JA4 fingerprint of the client's TLS connection as the field to match within the regex pattern statement, enabling inspection of the TLS client fingerprint for the request.
Specifies how AWS WAF should treat a request when the JA4 fingerprint is not available, returning either a match or no-match result for the regex match statement.

Defines that the regex match should be performed against the JSON body of the request, including options for specifying which part of the JSON (e.g., all values or specific keys) and how to handle invalid or oversized JSON payloads.
Specifies how the regex pattern is applied when the request body is not valid JSON: setting it to MATCH treats the body as a match and NO_MATCH treats it as not a match.
Specifies which JSON paths within the body to inspect for regex matches, either all content, an array of included paths, or an array of excluded paths.
When true, the regex match statement inspects the entire JSON request body; otherwise, use the IncludedPaths match pattern to limit inspection to specific JSON paths.
The list of JSON paths (e.g., /foo/bar) within the request body that specify the values to which the regex pattern is applied when inspecting the JSON body.
Specifies the part of the JSON body (ALL, HEADERS, COOKIES, or BODY) to inspect for the regular expression pattern.
Determines how AWS WAF handles a request whose JSON body exceeds the maximum inspection size, setting whether to continue processing, match the rule, or not match the rule.
When this method object is present, the regex match statement inspects the HTTP request method (e.g., GET, POST) as the field to match.
When configured, this field makes the regex match statement evaluate the regex pattern against the query string of the incoming HTTP request.
Specifies the single HTTP header (by its Name property) that the regex match statement inspects in the web request.
The name of the HTTP header to inspect against the regular expression pattern.
Specifies that WAF should inspect only a single query string argument in the request, where the argument's name is defined by the `name` field of this nested object.
The name of the query argument (parameter) in the request's query string that you want AWS WAF to inspect against the regular expression pattern.
Configures the regex match to inspect the URI fragment (the portion of the request URI after '#') of the web request.

Determines whether a web request that has no URI fragment (the portion of the URL after '#') is treated as matching the regex pattern (via 'MATCH') or not matching (via 'NO_MATCH') for this field-to-match configuration.
Instructs WAF to inspect only the URI path of the web request (the path component following the host, before any query string).

A list of text transformation objects with priorities that are applied to the inspected web request content before the regex match statement's standard text transformations, enabling decoding or normalization (e.g., Base64 or HTML entity decoding) prior to pattern matching.
Defines the text transformation type (such as LOWERCASE or URL_DECODE) applied during the pre-parse phase before the regex match statement processes the request component.
The regular expression pattern that AWS WAFv2 uses to inspect the specified web request component (such as a header or query string) for a match in the regex match statement.

Defines the ordered list of text transformations that AWS WAF applies to the web request content before it is evaluated against the regular expression in this regex match statement, for example by lowercasing or HTML-decoding the input.

In an AWS WAFv2 regex match statement, this priority number determines the order in which the associated text transformation (e.g., lower-case, html-decode) is applied to the request component, with lower values executed first.
Specifies the type of text transformation to apply to the web request component before evaluating the regex pattern, such as LOWERCASE, URL_DECODE, or HTML_ENTITY_DECODE.
A rule statement that references an AWS WAFv2 regex pattern set by its ARN and defines the web request component (like headers, body, or query string) to inspect for regex matches.
ARN of the AWS WAFv2 regex pattern set that this statement references, used to match web request components against the regex patterns.
Specifies the part of the web request (such as a header, the body, or the query string) that AWS WAF inspects for the regex pattern set.
Specifies that the WAF rule should match on all query arguments in the request, causing the regex pattern set to be evaluated against each query argument in the request.

This field configures the regex pattern set reference statement to inspect the body of the web request, and can optionally include oversize handling settings for bodies that exceed the maximum allowed size.
Specifies how AWS WAF handles a request body that exceeds its size limit when evaluating the body against the regex pattern set in this statement.
Defines how to inspect all cookies in the web request for the regex pattern set reference statement, including the cookie match pattern, match scope (key or value), and oversize handling.
Defines which cookies in the web request are inspected, using an All match or lists of included/excluded cookie names for the regex pattern set reference statement.
Specifies that the rule inspects all cookies in the request, rather than only a named list of included or excluded cookies.

In an AWS WAFv2 web ACL rule using a regex pattern set reference statement, this list specifies the names of cookies to exclude from inspection when the field-to-match is cookies, so those cookies are not evaluated against the regex patterns.
Lists the cookie names that the rule inspects, so only these cookies are matched against the regex pattern set.
Specifies whether AWS WAF inspects all cookie content (ALL), only cookie keys (KEY), or only cookie values (VALUE) when evaluating the regex pattern set against cookies in the web request.
Specifies how AWS WAF handles a request when the cookie header in the inspected component exceeds its size limit, using one of CONTINUE, MATCH, or NO_MATCH.
Specifies that the rule inspects the order of HTTP headers in the request, with optional configuration for how to handle oversized header sections.
Specifies how AWS WAF handles oversized header order when the field-to-match is header_order in a regex pattern set reference statement, with allowed values CONTINUE, MATCH, and NO_MATCH.

Configures how AWS WAF inspects the request headers for the regex pattern set reference statement, specifying the header match pattern (all, included, or excluded headers), the match scope (entire header, key, or value), and the handling of oversized headers.
Defines the match pattern for a header field to match, such as matching all headers or only a specified set of included/excluded header names in the regex pattern set reference statement.
When set to true, this boolean flag tells the WAFv2 header match pattern to match all request headers, rather than only a specified list of header names.

The list of HTTP header names excluded from inspection when the regex pattern set reference statement's field-to-match is set to match against headers, meaning the rule's regex pattern will not be evaluated against these specified headers.
Lists the exact header names that the AWS WAFv2 rule inspects when the field-to-match is a set of request headers, so that only requests containing those headers are matched.
Specifies whether the regular expression pattern set matches against the header name, header value, or both, controlling which part of the HTTP header is inspected for the WAF rule.
Specifies how AWS WAF handles request header sections that exceed the size limit, using values CONTINUE (continue processing), MATCH (treat as match), or NO_MATCH (treat as no match).

Specifies the JA3 fingerprint of the client's TLS connection as the match target for the regex pattern set reference statement, with an object that defines fallback behavior (such as MATCH or NO_MATCH) when the fingerprint is unavailable.
Specifies how AWS WAF handles a web request that doesn't have a JA3 fingerprint, where 'MATCH' treats it as matching the rule condition and 'NO_MATCH' treats it as not matching.
Specifies that the WAF should inspect the JA4 fingerprint of the client's TLS handshake, which is a computed hash representing the client's TLS characteristics, for the regex pattern match.
Specifies how WAF should handle requests that lack a JA4 TLS fingerprint, with 'MATCH' causing such requests to be treated as a match and 'NO_MATCH' treating them as a non-match.
Defines how AWS WAF inspects the JSON-encoded body of the request, including the JSON match pattern and how to handle invalid or oversized bodies.
Specifies whether an invalid JSON body should be treated as a match (MATCH) or no match (NO_MATCH) for the rule statement when AWS WAF cannot parse the request body.

Specifies which parts of the request's JSON body to inspect for the regex pattern set, either the entire body (when All is true) or a defined set of JSON pointer paths (via IncludedPaths) such as '/foo/bar'.
When set, specifies that the regex pattern set should be evaluated against the entire JSON body of the request, rather than only specific JSON paths.
Specifies the JSON path expressions for the parts of the request body to include in inspection, so that the regex pattern is applied only to those paths.
Controls which part of the JSON body the regex pattern set inspects, with allowed values `ALL`, `KEY`, or `VALUE` to target the entire body, only its keys, or only its values.
Determines how AWS WAF handles the request body when it exceeds the maximum size allowed for JSON inspection, with valid values CONTINUE, MATCH, or NO_MATCH.
This setting configures the field-to-match to inspect the HTTP method (e.g., GET or POST) of the web request for the regex pattern set reference statement.
Specifies that the regex pattern set reference statement should inspect the query string of the web request, including the URI query parameters.
Specifies that the regex pattern set reference statement inspects a single HTTP header, identified by the Name property within this object.
The name of the HTTP header to inspect, such as 'User-Agent' or 'Referer', for the regex pattern set reference statement.
This object tells AWS WAF to inspect only a single named query string parameter, with the parameter name defined in its Name property, instead of all query arguments.
The name of the query argument to inspect when using a single query argument as the field to match in a regex pattern set reference statement.
When present as an empty object, this field configures the rule to inspect the URI fragment (the part of the request URI after the '#') against the referenced regex pattern set.
Determines whether the WAF rule matches or does not match when the request URI fragment is absent (missing or empty), with valid values `MATCH` and `NO_MATCH`.
When set, the regex pattern set is evaluated against the path component of the request URI (e.g., /index.html).
Applies a list of text transformations to the selected request component before the regex pattern set is evaluated, allowing normalizations like lowercasing or HTML decoding to be performed first.
The priority number that determines the order in which pre-parse text transformations are applied to the web request before the regex pattern set is evaluated.
Specifies the type of text transformation to apply to the input before the regex pattern set is evaluated, such as LOWERCASE, URL_DECODE, or COMPRESS_WHITE_SPACE.

Specifies the ordered list of text transformations (for example, lowercase, URL decode, or HTML entity decode) that are applied to the web request component before it is evaluated against the associated regex pattern set.
The priority number that determines the order in which this text transformation is applied relative to others in the same rule statement, with lower numbers processed first.
The type of text transformation to apply to the web request component before inspecting it against the regex pattern set, such as LOWERCASE or URL_DECODE.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.rule_g.text: Defines a statement that includes all rules from a referenced rule group by its ARN, optionally overriding actions for specific rules.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS WAFv2 rule group that this statement references, which identifies the rule group to include in the web ACL's rule evaluation.
The name of a rule within the referenced rule group that should be excluded from evaluation by this web ACL.

Specifies a list of actions to override for specific rules within the referenced rule group, allowing you to change the action (e.g., Allow, Block, Count) of individual rules without modifying the rule group itself.
Defines the override action (allow, block, or count) that AWS WAF applies to matching requests for the referenced rule in the rule group, replacing the rule's original action.

When specified as the value of action_to_use, this overrides the action of a rule in the referenced rule group to allow the matching request, so the request is permitted to continue without being blocked or counted.
Defines custom request handling (like inserting headers) that AWS WAF applies to matching requests when the rule's action is overridden to allow.
The list of custom HTTP headers to insert into the request when a rule action override is set to Allow and custom request handling is configured for the referenced rule group.
The name of the custom HTTP header that AWS WAF inserts into the request when the rule action is overridden to Allow with custom request handling.
Specifies the value of the custom HTTP header to insert into the request when the rule action is overridden to Allow and custom request handling is configured.
Overrides the action of the referenced rule with a block action, optionally including custom response settings.
Specifies the custom response (status code, headers, and response body) that AWS WAF sends to the client when the override `block` action is applied to a matched request in the referenced rule group.
The key that identifies the custom response body to use for the block action, matching a key defined in the web ACL's custom_response_bodies map.

The HTTP status code (among WAF-supported values like 200, 403, and 429) that AWS WAF returns in the custom response when the block action override is applied to a rule from the referenced rule group.
Specifies a list of custom HTTP header names and values to include in the block response when this rule group rule's action is overridden to block with a custom response.
The name of the custom HTTP header to include in the block action's custom response when overriding the action of a rule in the referenced rule group.
The value of a custom response header that AWS WAF adds to the HTTP response when the rule group rule action is overridden to Block with a custom response.
Specifies that the rule action override should use AWS WAF CAPTCHA, which presents a CAPTCHA puzzle to the user to verify that the request is human.
Defines custom request handling options, such as custom headers, to insert into the request when the rule action is CAPTCHA.
Defines the custom header name-value pairs to insert into the web request when AWS WAF applies the CAPTCHA action as part of a rule action override for a rule in a referenced rule group.
The name of the custom HTTP header that AWS WAF inserts into the web request when the overridden rule action is handled as a CAPTCHA challenge, as part of the custom request handling configuration.

Specifies the value for a custom HTTP header that AWS WAF inserts into the request when the CAPTCHA action override from the referenced rule group is applied, as part of the custom request handling for that rule.

Specifies that the overridden rule's action is AWS WAF Challenge, which issues a silent JavaScript challenge to the client to verify it is not a bot, with no additional configuration properties for this action object.
Specifies custom request handling, including headers to insert, for requests that pass the challenge initiated by the Challenge action.

This field defines the list of custom HTTP headers (each containing name and value) that AWS WAF adds to a matching request when the rule action override is set to Challenge and custom request handling is enabled.
The name of the HTTP header that AWS WAF inserts into the request when applying the Challenge action as an override for a rule in a referenced rule group.
The value of the HTTP header that AWS WAF inserts into the request when the challenge action override's custom request handling is applied.

When specified, this empty struct overrides the referenced rule group's rule action to 'Count', which records matching requests without blocking or allowing them, commonly used for testing and monitoring.
Defines the custom request handling (such as inserting headers) that AWS WAF applies to matching requests when this rule action override is set to count.
Specifies a list of HTTP headers to insert into the request when an overridden rule in the referenced rule group uses the Count action, where each header defines a name and a value.
The name of the HTTP header to insert into the web request when the action is Count and custom request handling is enabled.
Specifies the value for a custom header that AWS WAF inserts into the web request when the rule action override is set to Count, within the rule_action_overrides of a rule group reference statement.
The price multiplier that is applied to the standard request price when the rule's action is overridden to Monetize, determining the adjusted amount to charge for matching requests.
The name of a rule within the referenced rule group whose action is being overridden by this rule action override.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.size_c.text: This rule statement checks the size of a specified web request component (such as a header, body, or query string) against a defined size limit and comparison operator, matching requests that violate the size constraint.

Specifies the comparison operator (e.g., EQ, GE, LT) used to compare the actual size of the inspected web request component against the declared Size in the size constraint statement of an AWS WAFv2 web ACL rule.
Specifies the part of the web request to inspect for the size constraint, such as a header, the query string, the body, or the URI.
Indicates that the size constraint statement should match against the entire set of query arguments, which are combined into a single string, rather than a specific query argument, header, or body.
Specifies that the size constraint statement inspects the request body, with an optional oversize handling configuration for bodies that exceed the web ACL's limits.

This value determines how AWS WAF responds when the request body exceeds the maximum size allowed for inspection: CONTINUE to inspect the available portion, MATCH to treat the rule as matching, or NO_MATCH to treat it as not matching.

Specifies the cookies in the web request to inspect for the size constraint, including the cookie match pattern (all or a subset), whether to compare cookie keys or values, and how to handle oversized cookie names or values.
Specifies which cookies to inspect in the web request for the size constraint statement, by matching all cookies, only included cookie names, or all except excluded cookie names.
Specifies that all cookies in the request match the pattern when inspecting cookies as part of a size constraint statement.
A list of cookie names that AWS WAF must exclude from size evaluation for the cookies field to match, meaning the size constraint applies to all other cookies in the request.
The list of cookie names to include in the match pattern, so only the size of these cookies is evaluated for the size constraint.
Specifies which portion of the cookie to inspect in the size constraint rule (e.g., ALL, KEY, or VALUE), controlling whether the match is evaluated against the entire cookie, its name, or its value.
Defines the action AWS WAF takes (CONTINUE, MATCH, or NO_MATCH) when the request's cookies exceed the maximum size AWS WAF can inspect in a size constraint statement.
Specifies that the size constraint statement matches against the order in which HTTP headers appear in the request, evaluating the size of that header order sequence.
Determines how AWS WAF handles the web request when the total size of the inspected headers in the specified order exceeds the size constraint limit, with allowed values CONTINUE, MATCH, or NO_MATCH.
Specifies the request headers to inspect for the size constraint, including the header match pattern (all or specific names) and the match scope (e.g., key, value, or both).
Specifies the header match pattern for a size constraint statement, defining whether to inspect all headers or a specific set of included or excluded header names.
When true, the rule inspects all HTTP headers for the size constraint, rather than a specific set of included or excluded headers.
Specifies the names of HTTP headers to exclude from the size constraint check, so the rule evaluates only the remaining headers when the match pattern is configured to exclude these headers.
Specifies the names of the headers to include in the match pattern when inspecting header values for a size constraint rule in AWS WAF V2.
Specifies whether the size constraint checks all header values, only header names (keys), or only header values within the selected headers.

Determines how AWS WAF handles requests that exceed the maximum header size that can be inspected by this size constraint statement, with options to continue processing (CONTINUE), treat as a match (MATCH), or treat as not a match (NO_MATCH).
Specifies that the size constraint statement should inspect the JA3 fingerprint of the client's TLS handshake, a hash derived from the Client Hello packet that identifies the client application.

Specifies whether requests that lack a JA3 fingerprint (for example, non-TLS traffic) should be treated as matching or not matching the size constraint statement, with allowed values 'MATCH' and 'NO_MATCH'.
Specifies that the rule matches on the JA4 TLS fingerprint of the client request, with a configured fallback behavior for requests that lack a JA4 fingerprint.
Determines the match action when a web request lacks a valid JA4 fingerprint, with valid values 'MATCH' to treat the request as matching and 'NO_MATCH' to treat it as not matching.
Defines how AWS WAF parses and matches against the JSON body of the request, specifying the JSON inspection pattern (e.g., all or specific JSON paths) and match scope (e.g., keys, values, or both).
Specifies how AWS WAF should handle a request when the request body is not valid JSON, either treating it as a match ('MATCH') or a non-match ('NO_MATCH') for the size constraint rule.
Specifies the JSON body match pattern, defining whether to inspect the entire JSON document or a set of JSONPath expressions.
Set to true to have the size constraint match against the entire JSON body, ignoring any specific paths listed in the `included_paths` option of the same `match_pattern` block.
Defines a list of JSONPath expressions that identify which properties within the JSON body should be inspected by the size constraint statement.
Specifies how the size constraint is applied to the request's JSON body, using values ALL, KEY, or VALUE to indicate whether the size limit checks the entire body, each key, or each value.
Specifies how AWS WAF handles a JSON request body that exceeds the configured size limit, with valid values CONTINUE, MATCH, or NO_MATCH.
Specifies that the size constraint applies to the HTTP method (e.g., GET, POST) of the request.
When set, this field tells AWS WAF to inspect the request's query string (the part of the URL after the question mark) for the size constraint check.
Configures the rule to inspect a single HTTP header (specified by its Name property) in the web request for the size constraint.
Specifies the name of the HTTP header that AWS WAF inspects for the size constraint check.
Specifies the name of a single query argument (e.g., 'token') whose value the size constraint statement inspects for length limits.
The name of the single query argument (e.g., 'token' or 'user') whose value AWS WAF inspects and applies the size constraint statement's length limits to.
Specifies that the size constraint should be evaluated against the URI fragment, which is the portion of the request URI that appears after the '#' delimiter.
Specifies whether the size constraint statement matches (MATCH) or does not match (NO_MATCH) when the request's URI fragment is absent from the web request.
When specified, this makes the WAFv2 size constraint statement evaluate the request's URI path (the part of the URL after the domain) against the configured size limit.
Specifies the list of text transformations (such as lowercase, HTML decode, or normalize path) to apply to the request component before the size constraint check evaluates it.
Defines the order in which AWS WAF applies this text transformation relative to others in the list, with lower numbers processed first.
The size, in bytes, that the inspected request component is compared against for the size constraint statement.

A list of text transformations that are applied to the inspected content before the size constraint is evaluated, each specifying a transformation priority and type (e.g., NONE, LOWERCASE, COMPRESS_WHITE_SPACE).
The priority field specifies the order in which each text transformation is applied within the size constraint statement, with lower values processed first.
Specifies the text transformation type (e.g., NONE, LOWERCASE, URL_DECODE) to apply to the request component being inspected in the size constraint statement.

aws_wafv2_web_acl.rules.statement.sqli_m.text: Defines a statement that inspects a specified part of the web request (such as body, query string, or URI) for SQL injection patterns, including configurable text transformations to apply before the inspection.
Specifies the part of the web request (such as headers, query string, body, or URI path) that AWS WAF Classic should inspect for SQL injection attack patterns.
When specified, this setting makes the SQL injection match statement inspect all query string parameters of the web request.

Specifies that the request body is the part of the request to inspect for SQL injection, with an optional 'oversize_handling' setting in the object to control how the body is handled when it exceeds WAF limits.
Determines how AWS WAF handles the request body when its size exceeds the body inspection limit, with allowed values CONTINUE, MATCH, or NO_MATCH.
Configures inspection of the web request's cookies for the SQL injection match statement, defining which cookies to examine and whether to match on cookie keys, values, or both.
Defines which cookies to inspect in the SQL injection match statement, allowing you to specify all cookies or a set of included or excluded cookie names.
When set, matches all cookies in the web request, causing every cookie to be inspected by the SQL injection rule.
Specifies the names of cookies to exclude from inspection when the WAFv2 SQL injection match statement evaluates the cookie header, so these cookies are ignored in the attack detection.
The list of cookie names to include in the inspection, so that only these cookies are examined for SQL injection patterns.
Specifies which parts of the cookies to inspect (ALL, KEY, or VALUE) when evaluating the request against the SQL injection match statement.
Specifies how AWS WAF handles a request when the total size of the inspected cookies exceeds the size limit, allowing you to continue processing, treat it as a match, or treat it as no match.
This field sets the `HeaderOrder` match type, which inspects the order in which HTTP request headers appear, but it is not a valid `field_to_match` type for a `sqli_match_statement` in AWS WAFv2.
Controls the action AWS WAF takes when the request's header order exceeds the maximum size that can be inspected, with valid values CONTINUE, MATCH, or NO_MATCH.

Specifies which web request headers to inspect for SQL injection patterns, including the header name match pattern (all, included, or excluded), the match scope (key or value), and how to handle oversize headers.
Specifies which headers (all, a list of included header names, or a list of excluded header names) in the web request to inspect for SQL injection patterns when the field to match is set to headers.
Specifies whether to inspect all headers in the web request, rather than only the included or excluded headers defined in the match pattern.
Specifies the names of headers to exclude from inspection when the match pattern defines which headers to check for SQL injection attacks.

Defines the specific HTTP request header names to be included for inspection when the SQL injection match statement uses the headers field-to-match option, so only those listed headers are evaluated for SQL injection patterns.
Determines whether AWS WAF inspects the entire header, only the header name (key), or only the header value when performing SQL injection matching against the header.
Determines how AWS WAF handles requests when the header set exceeds the size limit in an SQL injection match, using values like 'CONTINUE', 'MATCH', or 'NO_MATCH'.
Configures the rule to inspect the client's JA3 TLS fingerprint as the matching attribute for the SQL injection match statement.

Determines how AWS WAF handles requests that lack a JA3 fingerprint (such as non-TLS traffic) when this setting is used as the field to match in an SQL injection rule, using either 'MATCH' or 'NO_MATCH'.
Specifies that the SQL injection match statement should inspect the JA4 fingerprint of the client's TLS handshake, a value that identifies the TLS client's characteristics.
Specifies the fallback behavior for the JA4 fingerprint field, determining whether the rule matches (MATCH) or does not match (NO_MATCH) when the client's JA4 fingerprint is not available.

Specifies that WAF inspects the JSON body of the request, configuring how to parse and match the payload via properties like match patterns, match scope, invalid fallback behavior, and oversize handling.

Determines whether a request should be treated as a match or non-match for the SQL injection rule when the request's JSON body is invalid (cannot be parsed as JSON), accepting values like 'MATCH' or 'NO_MATCH'.
Specifies the JSON path pattern (all or included/excluded paths) that determines which parts of the request body's JSON structure are inspected by the SQL injection match statement.
When present (typically as an empty object), this flag makes the SQL injection inspection match all JSON paths in the request body, so every JSON field is inspected.
Defines the list of JSONPath expressions indicating which parts of the JSON request body are inspected for SQL injection, so only matching paths are evaluated.
Determines whether the SQL injection match rule inspects all JSON content, only JSON keys, or only JSON values when evaluating the request body.

Specifies how AWS WAF handles the JSON request body when its size exceeds the maximum allowed for inspection, with values CONTINUE, MATCH, or NO_MATCH determining whether the oversize body is treated as a match for the SQL injection rule.
Specifies that the rule inspects the HTTP method of the web request (e.g., GET, POST, PUT) for SQL injection patterns.
When set to true, directs the WAFv2 SQL injection match rule to inspect the entire raw query string of the request (the part of the URL after the question mark).
Specifies a single named HTTP header in the web request to inspect, set via its required Name property.
The name of the HTTP header to inspect for SQL injection attack patterns, for example 'User-Agent'.
