aws_work_spaces_web_portal.portal_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this WorkSpaces Web portal.

aws_work_spaces_web_portal.portal_custom.text: Specifies the custom domain name (e.g., portal.example.com) that users will use to access the WorkSpaces Web portal, replacing the default portal URL.

aws_work_spaces_web_portal.portal_endpoi.text: The URL endpoint for accessing the WorkSpaces Web portal, assigned by AWS and available only after the portal is created.

aws_work_spaces_web_portal.portal_status.text: The current operational status of the portal, which is a read-only service-assigned value indicating whether it is `Incomplete`, `Pending`, or `Active`.

aws_work_spaces_web_portal.renderer_type.text: The renderer type of the portal, a read-only attribute set by AWS to indicate the rendering engine used to deliver web content (such as 'AppStream').

aws_work_spaces_web_portal.service_provi.text: The SAML 2.0 metadata XML document for the portal acting as a service provider, automatically generated and returned by AWS so that external identity providers can configure federation trust with the portal.

aws_work_spaces_web_portal.session_logge.text: Specifies the ARN of the Kinesis data stream (session logger) that captures session logs from the web portal.

aws_work_spaces_web_portal.status_reason.text: Provides a description of why the portal is in its current status, typically when the status is 'Failed'.

aws_work_spaces_web_portal.tags.text: Specifies a list of tag objects (each containing a key and value) that are attached to the WorkSpaces Web Portal, enabling you to categorize and manage the resource by cost, environment, or other criteria.

aws_work_spaces_web_portal.tags.value.text: The user-defined value portion of a tag assigned to the AWS WorkSpaces Web portal, used to provide metadata and support resource categorization and cost allocation.

aws_work_spaces_web_portal.trust_store_a.text: The ARN of the trust store that the WorkSpaces Web portal uses to validate the certificate of the identity provider (IdP) for SAML-based authentication.

aws_work_spaces_web_portal.user_access_l.text: The ARN of the user access logging settings associated with this WorkSpaces Web portal, which controls the capture and delivery of user access logs.

aws_work_spaces_web_portal.user_settings.text: The ARN of the user settings resource to associate with this WorkSpaces Web portal.

aws_work_spaces_web_session_logger.addit.text: A map of key-value pairs that serve as additional encryption context for the KMS key used to encrypt session log data, providing extra authenticated data to the encryption/decryption process.

aws_work_spaces_web_session_logger.assoc.text: The ARNs of the WorkSpaces Web portals to which this session logger is associated.

aws_work_spaces_web_session_logger.creat.text: The date and time when the WorkSpaces Web session logger configuration was created, returned as an ISO 8601 formatted string.

aws_work_spaces_web_session_logger.displ.text: Specifies the display name for the session logger, providing a human-readable identifier for this logging configuration in the AWS Management Console and CloudFormation stacks.

aws_work_spaces_web_session_logger.event.text: The list of event type strings that the session logger should include in its log output, filtering out any session events not matching these values.

aws_work_spaces_web_session_logger.log_c.text: Configures the S3 bucket and key prefix that serves as the destination for WorkSpaces Web session logs when S3 is the selected log output type.
The name of the S3 bucket that receives WorkSpaces Web session logs.
Specifies the AWS account ID of the S3 bucket owner, used to validate access when delivering session logs to an S3 bucket owned by a different account.
Specifies the hierarchical folder layout used to store session log files in the S3 bucket, typically a date-based pattern (e.g., yyyy/MM/dd/HH/) that controls how logs are partitioned in the bucket.
The S3 object key prefix under which session logger log files are stored in the configured S3 bucket.
Specifies the file format (TEXT or JSON) for WorkSpaces Web session logs delivered to the configured Amazon S3 bucket.

aws_work_spaces_web_session_logger.sessi.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this WorkSpaces Web session logger and is used to attach the logger to a WorkSpaces Web portal for session logging.

aws_work_spaces_web_session_logger.tags..text: The value of a user-defined tag attached to the WorkSpaces Web session logger, used to organize and manage the resource.

aws_work_spaces_web_trust_store.associat.text: The list of ARNs of the WorkSpaces Web portals that are associated with this trust store.

aws_work_spaces_web_trust_store.certific.text: A list of PEM-encoded certificates to include in this WorkSpaces Web trust store, used to establish trust for web sessions.

aws_work_spaces_web_trust_store.tags.text: Specifies a list of tags (key-value pairs) to attach to this WorkSpaces Web trust store, supporting resource organization and cost allocation.

aws_work_spaces_web_trust_store.trust_st.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the WorkSpaces Web trust store.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_access_logging_.text: The ARNs of the WorkSpaces Web portals that are associated with this user access logging settings resource.
A list of key-value tags to assign to this user access logging settings configuration.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this user access logging settings resource, used as a reference for attaching the settings to a WorkSpaces Web portal.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.additi.text: Specifies a map of up to five key-value pairs that are passed as additional encryption context to AWS KMS when the WorkSpaces Web user settings are encrypted using a customer managed key.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.associ.text: The list of ARNs of the WorkSpaces Web portals that are associated with these user settings, populated automatically by AWS.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.brandi.text: The read-only branding configuration currently applied to the WorkSpaces web portal, specifying the portal's branding name, logo URL, and support email contact details.
The color theme (e.g., Light or Dark) applied to the WorkSpaces Web portal's branding configuration.
The favicon URL used in the branding configuration for the WorkSpaces Web portal, which is displayed in the browser tab.

Holds the metadata (a map of key-value pairs) for the custom favicon image specified in the branding configuration of the WorkSpaces Web user settings, which is used to customize the browser tab icon in the portal.
The file extension of the custom favicon image (e.g., .png, .jpg) for the WorkSpaces Web portal branding, used in conjunction with the base64-encoded file content to display the icon.
The timestamp of when the favicon image was last uploaded for the branding configuration of the WorkSpaces Web user settings.
The MIME type of the favicon image (e.g., image/png) used in the custom branding for the WorkSpaces Web portal.
Provides locale-specific branding strings (e.g., branding name, display name, support email, and support phone) used to tailor the WorkSpaces Web portal for different language or regional audiences.
The URL of the logo image displayed on the WorkSpaces Web portal when branding is configured.
The `logo_metadata` object specifies the Amazon S3 bucket, key, and optional version ID for the custom logo image that WorkSpaces Web displays in the user portal branding.

Specifies the file extension (e.g., 'png' or 'jpeg') of the logo image used in the branding configuration of WorkSpaces Web user settings, required for identifying the logo's image format when uploading logo metadata.
The timestamp of when the branding logo was last uploaded, used to track the version or freshness of the logo metadata in WorkSpaces Web user settings.
Specifies the MIME type of the logo image file used in the WorkSpaces Web portal branding, such as image/png or image/jpeg.
Specifies the terms of service text that is displayed to end users in the WorkSpaces Web portal as part of the branding configuration.
The URL of a wallpaper image to display in the background of the WorkSpaces Web user portal, used to customize the branding shown to end users.
The wallpaper_metadata object specifies the URL of the wallpaper image used in the branding configuration for the WorkSpaces Web user settings portal.
Specifies the file extension of the wallpaper image (e.g., 'png', 'jpg') used in the branding for WorkSpaces Web user settings.
The timestamp of the last time the wallpaper image was uploaded.
The MIME type (e.g., image/png) of the wallpaper image that is applied to the WorkSpaces Web portal as part of the branding configuration.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.cookie.text: Configuration for cookie synchronization across web portal browser sessions, specifying a list of domains that are blocked from having their cookies synchronized.
Specifies the allowed cookies that are synchronized across browser sessions, where each item identifies a cookie by name (and optionally domain) to control which cookies are kept in sync.
Specifies a domain that is allowed for cookie synchronization in the WorkSpaces Web user settings, meaning cookies for that domain will be shared across browser sessions.
The name of the cookie that is allowed to be synchronized for the associated domain and path in the cookie synchronization allowlist for the WorkSpaces Web user settings.
Specifies the URL path within the domain for which cookies are synchronized, as part of an allowlist entry in the cookie synchronization configuration for WorkSpaces Web user settings.
Lists the cookie specifications that are blocked from being synchronized between the user's local browser and the WorkSpaces Web session, so cookies matching these specifications will not be shared.
The domain name for which cookies are blocked from synchronization across browser sessions in the WorkSpaces Web user settings cookie synchronization configuration.
The name of the cookie on the blocklist, preventing its value from being synchronized between the user's local browser and the WorkSpaces Web streaming session.
The URL path that the cookie applies to, identifying a cookie in the blocklist of cookies excluded from synchronization for the WorkSpaces Web user settings.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.copy_a.text: Specifies whether users are allowed to copy content in the web portal, with allowed values 'Enabled' or 'Disabled'.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.custom.text: The ARN of the customer-managed KMS key used to encrypt sensitive data in the user settings.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.deep_l.text: Specifies whether users can access the WorkSpaces Web portal via deep links that bypass the initial login page.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.discon.text: Specifies the length of time, in minutes, after which a user's WorkSpaces Web session will be disconnected due to inactivity (default is 60).

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.downlo.text: A string enum (Enabled/Disabled) that specifies whether users can download files from the WorkSpaces Web portal, controlling the download permission for the user settings.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.idle_d.text: Specifies the length of time, in minutes, that a user can remain idle in a WorkSpaces Web session before being automatically disconnected.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.paste_.text: Controls whether users are permitted to paste content into the web browsing session, where the string value is set to 'Enabled' to allow paste operations or 'Disabled' to forbid them.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.print_.text: Specifies whether users can print from the web portal, with allowed values of 'Enabled' or 'Disabled'.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.tags.text: Specifies the key-value tags to attach to this WorkSpaces Web UserSettings resource for identifying, organizing, and managing access and costs.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.tags.v.text: The value of a tag assigned to the WorkSpaces Web User Settings resource, used to store the content associated with a tag key for organizing and identifying the resource.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.toolba.text: Defines the toolbar appearance and behavior for the end-user browser in WorkSpaces Web, including options like toolbar type (floating or docked), pinning, and maximum display resolution.
Specifies the list of toolbar items that are hidden from the user's web portal toolbar in the WorkSpaces Web user settings, allowing administrators to control which tools are visible to end users.
Specifies the maximum display resolution, such as '1920x1080', for the WorkSpaces Web browser streaming session.
Specifies the toolbar display type for the WorkSpaces Web browser toolbar, with allowed values 'Floating' or 'Docked'.
Determines whether the web toolbar is displayed in a minimized or docked state for WorkSpaces Web users.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.upload.text: Indicates whether users can upload files from their local device to the remote web session, with allowed values 'Enabled' or 'Disabled'.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.user_s.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the WorkSpaces Web user settings resource, assigned by AWS when the resource is created.

aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings.web_au.text: Controls whether WebAuthn (e.g., security keys or platform authenticators) is allowed for user authentication in the WorkSpaces Web session.

aws_work_spaces_workspace.bundle_id.text: The ID of the WorkSpace bundle that defines the operating system, software, and compute resources for the WorkSpace.

aws_work_spaces_workspace.directory_id.text: The identifier of the AWS Directory Service directory in which the WorkSpace is registered.

aws_work_spaces_workspace.id.text: The unique AWS-assigned identifier for the WorkSpace, typically in the form ws- followed by a string, used to reference the workspace within the account.

aws_work_spaces_workspace.root_volume_en.text: Specifies whether the root volume (C: drive) of the WorkSpace is encrypted for this WorkSpace.

aws_work_spaces_workspace.tags.text: Specifies key-value tags to associate with the WorkSpace, enabling you to organize, identify, and track the resource for cost allocation and management.

aws_work_spaces_workspace.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the WorkSpace, used to categorize and identify the resource.

aws_work_spaces_workspace.user_name.text: The login name of the user in the directory, for whom the WorkSpace is provisioned and associated.

aws_work_spaces_workspace.user_volume_en.text: Indicates whether the user volume (the D: drive on Windows or /home on Linux) of the WorkSpace is encrypted.

aws_work_spaces_workspace.volume_encrypt.text: The AWS KMS key ARN or ID used to encrypt the user and root storage volumes of the WorkSpace, which is required when volume encryption is enabled.

aws_work_spaces_workspace.workspace_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the WorkSpace, such as 'ws-12345678'.

aws_work_spaces_workspace.workspace_prop.text: Specifies the runtime and storage configuration for the WorkSpace, including compute type, running mode, auto-stop timeout, and root/user volume sizes in GiB.

The name of the compute type for the WorkSpace (e.g., VALUE, STANDARD, PERFORMANCE, POWER, GRAPHICS), which determines the hardware specifications such as CPU, memory, and storage resources allocated to the virtual desktop.
Specifies the size of the root volume (C: drive on Windows, / on Linux) for the WorkSpace, in GiB.
Controls whether the WorkSpace runs continuously (ALWAYS_ON) or automatically stops when idle (AUTO_STOP), affecting billing and availability.
The number of minutes a WorkSpace in AUTO_STOP running mode remains running after the user disconnects before it is automatically stopped, with valid values from 60 to 720 minutes.
The size, in GiB, of the user volume (persistent storage for user data) for the WorkSpace.

aws_work_spaces_workspace_ip_group.tags..text: The value portion of a key-value tag attached to the WorkSpaces IP group, used for metadata and cost allocation.

aws_work_spaces_workspace_ip_group.user_.text: Specifies the IP address range in CIDR notation (e.g., 203.0.113.0/24) that defines which client IP addresses are permitted or denied access to WorkSpaces in this IP access control group.
A human-readable description for the IP access rule, used to label or explain the purpose of the rule within the WorkSpaces IP group.

aws_workspaces_instances_volume.tag_spec.text: The tags block within a tag specification, used to define key-value pairs that are attached to the WorkSpaces instance volume for identification and resource management.
The value of a tag assigned to the WorkSpaces volume within the tag specification, used to categorize and manage the volume.

aws_workspaces_instances_workspace_insta.text: Provides the read-only details of the EC2 instance that AWS WorkSpaces automatically manages for this workspace instance.
The EC2 instance identifier for the underlying compute resource that AWS fully manages for this WorkSpace instance.

Specifies the Amazon EBS volume configuration (such as volume size, type, IOPS, encryption, snapshot ID, and delete-on-termination behavior) for the block device mapping attached to the managed instance.
Specifies whether the EBS volume for the managed instance's block device mapping is encrypted at rest, enabling AWS EBS encryption for that volume.
The KMS key ID used to encrypt the EBS volume defined in the block device mapping of the managed instance for this WorkSpace instance.
The size of the EBS volume (in GiB) for the block device mapping on the managed instance, determining the storage capacity of the device.
When set, this field suppresses the block device mapping, preventing the specified device from being exposed to the managed instance.

Specifies the EC2 Capacity Reservation targeting options for the underlying managed instance of the WorkSpace, such as launching into a specific Capacity Reservation or using the default on-demand preference.

Specifies whether the managed EC2 instance should launch into an open Capacity Reservation (value 'open') or ignore open reservations (value 'none'), controlling how existing reserved capacity is used.
Defines the target capacity reservation (by its ID or resource group ARN) that the WorkSpace's managed instance will use to reserve compute capacity.
Specifies the ID of the EC2 Capacity Reservation that the WorkSpace's managed instance should be launched into, ensuring the instance uses reserved capacity.
The ARN of the resource group whose Capacity Reservation the managed instance will target, enabling the instance to use reserved EC2 capacity from that group.
Specifies the CPU options, such as core count and threads per core, for the underlying managed EC2 instance that runs the WorkSpace.
Specifies the number of threads per core for the managed instance's CPU options, with a value of 1 disabling Intel Hyper-Threading for the WorkSpace's underlying EC2 instance.

When set to true, this prevents the underlying managed EC2 instance for the WorkSpace from being stopped through the EC2 StopInstances API operation, allowing it to be stopped only by a user shutdown from within the operating system.
When enabled, assigns an IPv6 address to the primary network interface of the managed WorkSpace instance.
Specifies the Nitro Enclaves options for the underlying managed EC2 instance of this WorkSpace, controlling whether enclaves are enabled on that instance.
When enabled, this boolean enables AWS Nitro Enclaves for the underlying managed EC2 instance that backs this WorkSpace, allowing the instance to run isolated enclave environments.
Configures the hibernation option for the WorkSpace instance, specifically enabling or disabling hibernation of the instance.
Specifies whether hibernation is enabled for the WorkSpace instance, allowing it to be stopped and later resumed with its memory contents preserved.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM instance profile attached to the managed instance, granting it the permissions defined by the profile's IAM role.
The name of the IAM instance profile to attach to the managed instance, which determines the IAM role and permissions granted to that instance.
The unique identifier of the Amazon WorkSpaces image used to create the WorkSpace instance, determining its operating system and preinstalled software.
The compute type for the managed WorkSpace instance (e.g., STANDARD, PERFORMANCE, POWER, GRAPHICS) that determines the CPU, memory, and GPU capacity allocated to the virtual desktop.
The name of the EC2 key pair that encrypts the WorkSpace user's password when the WorkSpace is created.
A list of license configuration ARNs that are associated with the managed instance for license tracking and compliance.
Specifies the ARN of an AWS License Manager license configuration to attach to the WorkSpace's managed instance, enabling license tracking and management for the software running on that instance.

Specifies the auto-recovery behavior for the WorkSpace's maintenance options, accepting 'ENABLED' to allow AWS to automatically restart the instance after a failure or 'DISABLED' to turn off this automatic restart.
Controls the Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) on the managed instance, including whether HTTP requests are allowed, whether IMDSv2 tokens are required, and the maximum hop limit.
Specifies whether the HTTP endpoint for the instance metadata service is enabled or disabled on the managed instance's metadata options.
Controls whether the IPv6 endpoint of the instance metadata service (IMDS) is enabled or disabled for the managed instance, permitting or blocking access to instance metadata over IPv6.

Specifies the maximum number of network hops allowed for the instance metadata service (IMDS) HTTP PUT responses, controlling the token's reachability to prevent unauthorized access to instance metadata.
Specifies whether the managed instance can retrieve the instance's tags through the instance metadata service (allowed values are typically 'enabled' or 'disabled').
Provides a list of network interfaces attached to the managed EC2 instance, including their IP addresses and network configuration.
The zero-based device index of the elastic network interface attached to the WorkSpace's managed instance, where 0 represents the primary network interface.
The list of security group IDs attached to the network interface of the managed WorkSpace instance, controlling inbound and outbound traffic.
The ID of the subnet in your VPC where the Workspace's managed network interface is deployed.

Specifies the network performance options for the managed instance, mirroring EC2's NetworkPerformanceOptions object which typically includes a bandwidth-weighted ENA flag to optimize network throughput.

Determines the bandwidth weighting for the managed instance's network performance options, where 'default' uses the instance's baseline network bandwidth and 'vpc-only' restricts network traffic to the VPC and may reduce the available bandwidth.
Sets the Availability Zone in which the underlying managed instance of this WorkSpace is launched, allowing the workload to be placed in a specific AWS data center.

Specifies the ID of the EC2 placement group into which the WorkSpace's managed instance is launched, enabling low-latency, high-bandwidth network communication with other instances in the same placement group.
Controls whether the WorkSpaces managed EC2 instance's private DNS name gets a resource name DNS AAAA record (IPv6), enabling IPv6 DNS resolution for that resource name.

When enabled, this creates a DNS A record in the VPC's private hosted zone for the resource name of the managed instance, allowing its private DNS name to resolve to the instance's IPv4 address via the resource name.

Specifies the hostname type (either 'ip-name' or 'resource-name') used for the private DNS name of the managed WorkSpaces instance, determining whether the private DNS record is based on the instance's IP address or its resource name.
The ID of the subnet in which the WorkSpace's underlying managed EC2 instance is launched.
Identifies the AWS resource type that the tag specification applies to, such as 'instance' for tagging the managed EC2 instance backing a WorkSpace.
The key of a tag to apply to the managed WorkSpace instance within its tag specification.
Defines the user data script executed on the WorkSpace's managed instance during provisioning, enabling automated setup like software installation or registry changes.
Assigns a list of key-value tags to the WorkSpace instance for resource identification, cost tracking, and access management.
The key of a tag attached to the WorkSpaces instance, used for categorizing, cost tracking, and access control.
The value of a tag applied to the WorkSpace instance, used for resource metadata, organization, and cost tracking.

aws_workspaces_pool.application_settings.text: Determines whether persistent application settings are enabled for the pool and, if so, specifies the settings group name that stores user application preferences.
The name of the settings group that defines which application settings are persisted and applied for users of this WorkSpaces Pool.
The status of application settings for the WorkSpaces pool, required to be either 'ENABLED' or 'DISABLED' to control whether persistent app settings are active for users in the pool.

aws_workspaces_pool.bundle_id.text: The unique identifier of the WorkSpaces bundle that defines the operating system, applications, and hardware configuration for the virtual desktops in the pool.

aws_workspaces_pool.capacity.text: Configures the desired and maximum number of user sessions for the WorkSpaces pool, controlling how many concurrent sessions the pool can support and its auto-scaling limits.

aws_workspaces_pool.capacity.desired_use.text: Specifies the desired number of concurrent user sessions for the WorkSpaces pool, which the service uses to determine how many instances to run to support the expected load.

aws_workspaces_pool.created_at.text: The `created_at` attribute specifies the timestamp when the WorkSpaces pool was created.

aws_workspaces_pool.description.text: Specifies a user-defined description for the WorkSpaces pool to help identify its purpose.

aws_workspaces_pool.directory_id.text: The identifier of the AWS Directory Service directory that the WorkSpaces pool uses for users and authentication.

aws_workspaces_pool.pool_arn.text: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies this WorkSpaces pool.

aws_workspaces_pool.pool_id.text: The unique identifier assigned by AWS to the WorkSpaces pool, used to reference the pool in other resources and API calls.

aws_workspaces_pool.pool_name.text: The name of the WorkSpaces pool, which uniquely identifies the pool within the AWS account and region.

aws_workspaces_pool.running_mode.text: Specifies whether the WorkSpaces in the pool are always running (ALWAYS_ON) or stop automatically when not in use (AUTO_STOP).

aws_workspaces_pool.tags.text: Defines the tags (key-value pairs) to associate with this WorkSpaces pool resource.

aws_workspaces_pool.tags.value.text: The value of a tag attached to the WorkSpaces pool, used for categorizing, identifying, and managing the resource.

aws_workspaces_pool.timeout_settings.text: Defines the session timeout settings for the WorkSpaces pool, including the disconnect timeout, idle disconnect timeout, and maximum user duration in seconds.

aws_workspaces_pool.timeout_settings.dis.text: Specifies the maximum time in seconds a user can remain disconnected from a pool WorkSpace before AWS automatically stops the WorkSpace.

aws_workspaces_pool.timeout_settings.idl.text: Specifies the length of time, in seconds, that a WorkSpaces Pool session can remain idle before a user is automatically disconnected from their streaming session.

aws_workspaces_pool.timeout_settings.max.text: Specifies the maximum time, in seconds, that a user session can remain active before it is automatically disconnected.

aws_xray_group.insights_configuration.text: Configures whether X-Ray Insights is enabled for the group, and whether email notifications for insight events are sent.

aws_xray_group.tags.key.text: Specifies the key of a tag assigned to the AWS X-Ray group, enabling you to categorize and manage the group within your AWS environment.

aws_xray_sampling_rule.sampling_rule.text: This object defines the X-Ray sampling rule's configuration, including priority, reservoir size, fixed rate, and matching criteria such as host, service, HTTP method, URL path, resource ARN, and attributes.

aws_xray_sampling_rule.sampling_rule.sam.text: Specifies the sampling-rate boost configuration for this X-Ray sampling rule, including whether the boost is enabled, the conditions that trigger it, and the boosted sampling rate to apply when those conditions are met.

aws_xray_sampling_rule.sampling_rule_rec.text: The sampling_rule_record field contains the complete sampling rule record, including the rule name, ARN, creation and modification timestamps, and the sampling rule's configuration details such as priority, reservoir size, and fixed rate.
The sampling rule configuration (including rule name, priority, reservoir size, fixed rate, and service matching attributes) embedded within the sampling rule record.

aws_xray_sampling_rule.sampling_rule_upd.text: Sampling rule update configuration for an existing AWS X-Ray sampling rule, specifying the desired changes such as reservoir size, fixed rate, and rule attributes.

aws_xray_sampling_rule.tags.key.text: The key of a tag assigned to the AWS X-Ray sampling rule, used to categorize and manage the rule.

aws_xray_sampling_rule.tags.value.text: The value component of a tag assigned to an AWS X-Ray sampling rule, used for metadata, identification, and cost allocation.
